courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.

courses.title: Dermatology Emergencies: They Do Exist!
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program will review common dermatologic conditions that may result in a patient presenting on emergency. In addition, this program will focus on serious conditions that are considered dermatologic emergencies. This course was previously presented live and RACE-approved (#20-1099652) and this version will be accessible anytime online on medvet.com.

courses.title: Advanced Abdominal Surgery
courses.description: In this course you will learn about advanced abdominal surgical procedures from engaging and relevant recorded lectures that include detailed discussion of diagnostics, tools for prognostication, preoperative patient stabilization, surgical anatomy and surgical techniques. In addition to the didactic lectures, you will have access to a combination of intraoperative video clips and detailed, narrated cadaveric demonstrations of gastrectomy using a stapler, splenectomy (demo of traditional ligatures AND use of a vessel sealant device) and cholecystojejuno-duodenostomy. Management of acute abdomen including septic peritonitis, hemoabdomen and diseases of the pancreas are comprehensively discussed.

courses.title: Every Day Acupuncture For Veterinarians: Mastermind Series (Anytime Version)
courses.description:
This program is an 8-session mastermind series, including an orientation and 7 learning modules, created to bridge the gap between obtaining an education in veterinary acupuncture and effectively applying this modality in a clinical setting to improve patient lives every day. The protocols and processes delivered in this program are designed to help veterinarians who have already completed basic training in veterinary acupuncture take their learning and skills to the next level. The series will provide templates, quick reference guides and mentorship geared toward moving the veterinarian into action, making everyday use of acupuncture possible and efficient even if time is short and intensity is high.
In the first module, participants will learn how to set the patient and the practice up for success, including systems to reduce patient stress and strategic outlines for scheduling and charging. The next four modules will focus on acupuncture strategies, from both the Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) and Western science perspective, to achieve improved patient outcomes when facing common conditions that afflict our companion animals. The conditions of focus are as follows: osteoarthritis and chronic pain, canine allergic dermatitis, feline cystitis and urinary tract inflammation, and feline inflammatory bowel conditions. The sixth module is dedicated to approaching senior patients with multiple medical problems and TCVM patterns, including how to prioritize and treat the patient with a focus on comfort and quality of life. The last module is designed to help the veterinarian develop best business practices around acupuncture and the integrative medical model, including goal setting strategy, to ensure long term success and sustainability. The overall purpose of this program is to improve patient care with acupuncture while achieving a healthy return on investment for the veterinarian and the practice.

courses.title: FUNDAMENTALS OF VETERINARY DENTISTRY (622-42486)
courses.description: This hands-on program was designed to quickly bring practitioners with little or no previous experience with oral disease recognition and treatment "up to speed." Combining the essential disciplines over 3 days: Radiology, Oral Surgery and Periodontal disease treatment will be taught through interactive lectures and focused wet-labs. Doctors will learn clinical anatomy, the complete dental exam with charting, oral prophylaxis in addition to open curettage and bone augmentation.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: 10 Top Medical Record-Keeping Deficiencies
courses.description: You've completed the two-hour course on "Veterinary Medical Records" and are ready to advance your knowledge OR you need a quick refresher. Either way, this condensed one-hour course will break down ten common medical record-keeping errors as evidenced by state veterinary medical board license disciplinary actions. The case examples will allow us to dive deeper into specific scenarios that may land veterinarians in trouble and highlight how to avoid these common mistakes. The course will reinforce how to draft a legally defensible medical record and incorporate best practices for improved patient care.

courses.title: Dry Eye in Canine Patients
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program will review keratoconjunctivitis sicca (dry eye), one of the most common diseases in veterinary ophthalmology. Learn the types of dry eye, how to diagnose other than the STT, and ways treatments have and are advancing for dry eye in dogs. This course was previously presented live and RACE-approved (#20-940581) and this version will be accessible anytime online on medvet.com.

courses.title: New Approach to Respiratory Distress: High-Flow Oxygen Therapy
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program will review pertinent respiratory physiology, traditional oxygen supplementation techniques, physiology of high-flow oxygen therapy, and evidence available in veterinary medicine regarding its use and limitations. Guidelines will be suggested for the use of high-flow oxygen in the intensive care unit (ICU). This course was previously presented live and RACE-approved (#20-1035804) and this version will be accessible anytime online on medvet.com.

courses.title: Compassion Fatigue - Recognition Treatment and Prevention
courses.description: This program will provide veterinary professionals the education and understanding on how Compassion Fatigue impacts the veterinary industry and how we can work together to recognize, treat, and prevent. It provides tips on combatting compassion fatigue including the QPR tool that aids in effective intervention in a crisis situation. With a high prevalence of suicide in veterinary medicine it is critical that we have the education and resources to support our colleagues. This presentation will also teach PAWS -- practice mindfulness, assess your self-care, work together, and say something.

courses.provider: SAN DIEGO ZOO WILDLIFE ALLIANCE ACADEMY - SAFE CAPTURE
courses.title: Chemical Immobilization of Animals
courses.description: This training provides the most complete, up-to-date instruction available on chemical immobilization and anesthesia of domestic animals and wildlife, presented in an easy-to-understand manner that is applicable to all experience levels. The instructors are veterinarians who specialize in remotely-delivered anesthetic agents. This program, which has historically been considered by many to be the gold-standard in chemical immobilization training, is now part of San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Academy.

courses.title: Introduction to Veterinary Oral Surgery and Periodontal Treatment
courses.description:
The Introduction to Veterinary Oral Surgery and Periodontal Treatment class is for doctors only and is limited to 10 veterinarians with two instructors and two assistants. This class is RACE approved for 8 hours of continuing education credits.
This class is for veterinarians only and will cover the common techniques needed to deliver the bulk of all dental care required for your patients. Simulated lesions are created on cadaver specimens, and the participants then treat the pathology. Each participant has their own work station equipped with everything needed for the class, and will receive a brand new dental instrument set. No more sharing dull bent instruments in lab. This class focuses on oral surgery, covering surgical extraction technique, easy retrieval of fractured roots, repair of oronasal fistulas and introduction to periodontal treatment. Discussions in this class are far-ranging and usually include in-depth discussion of dental economics in veterinary practice. Two instructors and two assistants for ten participants ensures a high level of individual attention. The doctors are never more than a few minutes away from overseeing your work.

courses.title: Common, Painful, Ignored: Osteoarthritis in Cats
courses.description:
Osteoarthritis (OA) pain is the most common condition affecting cats. The effects of pain are devastating. They are cat-astrophic! They destroy an individual's personality, enjoyment of life, and ability to interact positively with others.
This course offers practical strategies for identifying and managing OA pain in cats, with a focus on interpreting feline-specific behaviors and using available diagnostic tools effectively. The session will also explore current treatment options and how to prioritize them based on efficacy, safety, and the individual needs of each patient.

courses.title: Managing FCGS in Practice: What Every Technician Should Know
courses.description:
Feline chronic gingivostomatitis (FCGS) is a severe, painful inflammatory disease that affects about 10% of cats and can significantly impact a cat's quality of life. Veterinary technicians play a critical role in veterinary care: from assisting with diagnostic evaluation and administering medications to supporting client communication and education. Because of this, it is essential that technicians are equipped with practical knowledge to recognize this debilitating condition and support appropriate patient care.
This lecture is designed for veterinary technicians and provides a practical, science-based overview of FCGS, including its clinical signs, cause of the disease, and underlying immune-mediated nature. The session will review current treatment strategies, including surgery, medical management, and the emerging use of mesenchymal stromal cell therapy for cats with refractory FCGS.

courses.provider: VETERINARY EMERGENCY AND CRITICAL CARE SOCIETY
courses.title: IVECCS 2025 - On-Demand
courses.description: In conjunction with IVECCS 2025, a selection of sessions from the live conference in San Diego, CA from September 4-8th will be available for attendees to view on-demand for 30 days following the conference. The theme of this year's conference is Cardiovascular System. By providing state-of-the-art education, VECCS continues to raise the standards of how to provide the best care for critically ill and emergent large and small animal patients. The comprehensive scientific program will provide a variety of topics at all levels of interest and experience to meet the attendees' needs. Topics discussed will include anesthesia and analgesia, cardiovascular, endocrinology, exotics, infectious disease, neurology, acid-base and electrolytes, point of care ultrasound, SIRS/sepsis, surgery, toxicology, and technician specific sessions.

courses.provider: SUNSHINE BOOKS, INC., DBA KAREN PRYOR CLICKER TRAINING
courses.title: BETTER VETERINARY VISITS (692-34784)
courses.description: This course is designed for any veterinary professional, including technicians, veterinarians, and veterinary assistants. Trainers who work with vets, or pet owners who would like to improve their pets behavior during veterinary visits will also benefit. No previous training experience is necessary.

courses.title: Localizing Dyspnea (DRIP115)
courses.description: This course will take you through the fundamentals of localizing dyspnea. The physiological process of localizing dyspnea will be discussed along with the diagnostic approach and treatment for the dyspneic patient.

courses.title: Foundations in Veterinary Anesthesia and Simulation Workshop
courses.description: After a half day review of anesthesia & monitoring best practices, clinical teams will participate in an anesthesia skills simulation lab that will test competence in overcoming common anesthetic complications. As participants suspend their disbelief, each scenario is designed to facilitate enhanced team communication, critical thinking and sound medical response to common situations encountered by your clinical team that include equipment failure, hypotension, hypercapnia and cardiac arrhythmia.

courses.title: Principles of Wound Closure & Suturing Techniques
courses.description: Join Dr. Lynetta Freeman in this webinar discussing suture selection and suturing techniques in soft tissue surgery.

courses.provider: CORNELL UNIVERSITY, COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: Oral Examination and Periodontal Charting in the Anesthetized Dog and Cat
courses.description: Dentistry is a fast-growing field in veterinary care. Many health providers are interested in improving their knowledge and practical skills in this area. In this 90-minute online course, we teach how to perform a systematic oral examination under general anesthesia and record clinical findings. Using up-close 4K videos, detailed animations, 3-D models, and high-quality clinical photos, participants will learn the importance of patient positioning and clinician ergonomics, understand the tools needed and how to use them, review oral and dental nomenclature, become familiar with dental charting, and appreciate the need for a systematic and repeatable approach to oral examination. This course is designed for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and veterinary students who want to cultivate their knowledge of the complex anatomy and disease processes of the oral cavity.

courses.title: Optimizing Dermatology Diagnoses: A Practical Guide with SOAP-Based Software
courses.description: In this webinar, discover how to provide relief for the vast number of pets suffering from skin and ear issues using SOAP-based practice management software. Dr. Lauren Jones will take a deep dive into how to revolutionize the workflow for those frustratingly difficult cases. Learn how your team can provide effective solutions that deliver the best possible outcomes through efficient documentation and client communications, diagnostic accuracy, and streamlined workflows. Don't miss this opportunity to optimize your veterinary practice with cutting-edge software that eliminates frustrating redundancies and is built to work the way you work.

courses.title: Small Animal Soft Tissue Immersion Program Session 1
courses.description:
This program is structured for the attendee to become a proficient, confident soft tissue sonographer, by immersing them in soft tissue ultrasound in 3 sessions spread over a 3 to 4 month period. The student will be with us for 3 days a week, every 6 to 8 weeks, spread over 4 months. Each session will build upon the prior session. Knobs, measurements, labeling, scan technique of the abdomen, scanning protocol, artifacts, normal and abnormals, of the liver, gall bladder, spleen, kidneys, bladder, adrenal glands, pancreas, Gi tract., lymph nodes, and reproductive tract will be covered. Case submissions will be required weekly between sessions, for critique. Referral to a telemedicine service or specialist may still be necessary, as this is a skill set that requires continuing practice allowing proficiency to become excellence.
This is a Medicine class delivered in a lecture/wetlab format.

courses.title: DENTAL RADIOGRAPH POSITIONING, CLEANING, PROBING, AND CHARTING BEST PRACTICES WORKSHOP
courses.description: Full day lab to teach best practices for dental radiograph positioning, cleaning, probing and charting for oral health.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2022 ACVIM Forum, In Person
courses.description: The ACVIM Forum is a veterinary healthcare event with thousands of attendees from around the world. The ACVIM Forum consistently boasts a diverse range of the best and brightest speakers, engaging sessions, medical discoveries and innovative exhibitors to keep veterinary practitioners current with the latest trends in veterinary internal medicine, and provides practical information that can be used by specialists, residents, veterinarians and technicians in daily practice. This 4-day program will focus on in person presentations, including Special Interest Groups sessions.

courses.title: Management of Feline Diabetes: A Review of Current Best Understanding
courses.description: In this session, Dr. Patty Lathan will discuss how to begin treatment of cats newly diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. Attendees will learn which diets to use for these feline diabetics and which insulins work best for various clinical scenarios.

courses.title: From Imaging to Diagnosis: Harness the Full Potential of Ultrasound-Guided FNA
courses.description: Join us to elevate your skills in ultrasound-guided fine needle aspirate (FNA) cytology. Learn best practices for lesion selection, sample collection, preparation, and staining to maximize the diagnostic yield of your aspirates. Real clinical cases will be presented to highlight the correlation between ultrasound imaging and cytology findings, leading to accurate diagnosis. We will also discuss the importance of effective collaboration between clinicians and clinical pathologists to ensure a team-based approach to diagnosis. Enhance your practical skills and improve patient outcomes through ultrasound-guided FNA

courses.title: Veterinary CE at Sea 2025
courses.description: Veterinarians and veterinary support staff can earn 16 hours of continuing education onboard Royal Caribbean's Oasis of the Seas February 16-22, 2025 with speakers sponsored by Elanco.

courses.title: Suturing Techniques & Surgical Knots: Tips & Tricks for the Veterinary Team to Optimize Wound Closure
courses.description: No two wounds are the same. For some wounds, surgical closure can provide an incredible benefit to the patient. Join us in this webinar geared toward veterinary technicians to learn all the tips and tricks on how your veterinary team can optimize wound healing by perfecting their suturing techniques.

courses.title: Fear Free Veterinary Certification Course
courses.description:
As veterinary professionals, we understand the emotional demand of the veterinary field, and we know the impact that stress and anxiety can have on our patients, our team, and our practices. Our goal: Provide veterinary professionals with the tools and knowledge to address different levels of fear, anxiety, and stress; improve client communication; and increase workplace safety.
Fear Free veterinary visits reduce fear, anxiety, and stress and create an experience that is more enjoyable and safer for all involved, including your patients, clients, and team. Learning how to implement Fear Free visits means veterinary teams will see their patients more often, and pet owners will seek advice from them as a trusted source.
This program consists of eight modules, which will need to be taken in consecutive order.
Each module will end with an exam which needs to be successfully completed prior to moving on to the next module. Progress on work can be saved at any time, giving participants the flexibility to self-pace throughout the program. When all eight modules have been completed, the participant will be awarded with a Fear Free certificate.
The purchase of the Fear Free Veterinary Certification Program provides you with an annual membership for the program, which requires an annual renewal fee and completion of additional annual CE to maintain your membership. Be sure to familiarize yourself and your team with the full renewal details for the Fear Free Veterinary Certification Program here.
As a Fear Free Certified Professional, you will:
- Reduce or remove anxiety triggers that can cause pets to become fearful at home, in transport, and at the veterinary hospital
- Help owners deliver calm pets to your hospital
- Enhance the quality of medicine in your practice
- Increase compliance
- Improve safety for the veterinary team

courses.title: Secrets of Success in Veterinary Dentistry
courses.description: Comprehensive On-Demand Online Course that shows you how to Create the Veterinary Dentistry Service that you, your staff, and your patients deserve. Dr. Beckman guides you through overcoming all obstacles and achieving the ultimate success in your practice.

courses.title: Management of the Broodmare
courses.description:
The presenter will discuss the routine care the mare requires throughout the year.
Topics will include preparing the mare through anestrus to managing her cycle
to conception. The medications and tools used in the breeding shed will be discussed along
with maintenance considerations for the pregnant mare from conception to foaling.

courses.title: Veterinary Dental Extraction Weekend Wet Lab
courses.description: This lecture and wet lab is extremely practical, providing the veterinarian with the skills needed to treat the majority of dentistry cases seen in practice daily. This Live course includes a full day of practical general Veterinary Dentistry topics and a full day of hands on intense instruction to master canine and feline extractions where equipment, specimens, PPE is provided.

courses.provider: SHARK REEF AQUARIUM AT MANDALAY BAY
courses.title: Shark Reef Aquatic Medicine Seminar
courses.description: The Shark Reef Aquatic Medicine Seminar is a two to three -day live presentation that focuses on the veterinary care and husbandry primarily of elasmobranch fish as well as teleost fish and reptiles. The presentations are led by specialty experts in the field primarily from AZA accredited Zoos and Aquariums. Topic include, surgery, diagnostics, restraint, anatomy and histopathology

courses.title: Integrating a Balanced Anesthesia Protocol in Your Practice
courses.description:
Ensuring optimal patient care and safety in veterinary practices demands the ability to craft personalized anesthetic drug protocols tailored to each patient. This presentation aims to equip veterinary professionals with a systematic approach to developing a well-balanced anesthesia drug protocol, including information on the common anesthetic drugs used during premedication, induction, and maintenance phases. VetSnap has decided to sponsor this webinar to bring valuable information to our followers. We understand the need of using controlled drugs in veterinary medicine, and the headaches that logging can cause, which is why VetSnap is here to help with this time consuming process.
By attending this presentation, participants will gain valuable insights into the art and science of anesthesia management, which will enhance their ability to provide optimal care for their animal patients. The goal of this presentation is to empower veterinary practitioners with the knowledge and confidence to create safe, effective, and tailored anesthesia drug protocols, resulting in better patient care and improved surgical outcomes.

courses.title: Critical Findings on Thoracic and Abdominal Radiographs in the Emergency Patient
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program will review case presentations and radiographic diagnoses that if not immediately detected may have negative consequences for the patient. This course was previously presented live and RACE-approved (#20-947995) and this version will be accessible anytime online on medvet.com.

courses.title: Level 1 Clinical Dentistry Lab for Veterinarians
courses.description: This lecture and hands on lab introduces foundational knowledge and skills for performing oral surgery and regional nerve blocks.

courses.title: From Bowels to Bile: Supplements & the Gut-Liver Connection in Dogs & Cats
courses.description: The gut-liver axis describes the relationship and crosstalk between the gastrointestinal tract and the liver in both health and disease states. Essential in this crosstalk are signals arising from dietary, genetic, and environmental factors. The portal vein transports nutrients and gut-derived antigens to the liver, while bile acids, proteins, lipids, and immune components are delivered back to the intestinal tract. The health of this interaction depends on a healthy immune response, intestinal barrier integrity, a balanced microbiome, and normal functioning of major gut luminal metabolic regulators, notably bile acids. This session will review the anatomy and function of the gut-liver connection, along with clinical signs that may be overlooked when this balance is disrupted. Attendees will explore how the gut-liver axis can help direct therapies, including diet interventions, medications, and supplements that can modulate and support the intestinal mucosal barrier, intestinal microbiota, and liver regeneration and repair.

courses.title: CBC Interpretation: Easy as 1, 2, 3!
courses.description: In this engaging session, participants will gain a deeper understanding of how to interpret CBC results in the context of various clinical scenarios to help ensure accurate and informed decisions in patient care. Dr. Austin Viall will delve into the intricacies of RBC analysis and explore the fundamental parameters of RBCs, including hematocrit, hemoglobin concentration, and red cell indices. Participants will also gain an understanding of WBC counts and distribution patterns to better assess the immune system's response to various conditions and to help the practitioner in identifying and interpreting WBC abnormalities.

courses.title: Canine Otitis Externa: Diagnosis, Management, Success
courses.description: Canine otitis externa is one of the most frequently encountered conditions in small animal veterinary practice. This presentation explores the causes of canine otitis externa including the predisposing, primary and perpetuating factors, the importance of otic cytology, and the essential treatment modalities to help ensure clinical resolution. The development of a long-term maintenance cleaning and allergy management plan will also be discussed.

courses.title: Common Hurdles in the Treatment of Urinary Incontinence
courses.description: Managing urinary sphincter mechanism incompetence in dogs is fairly straightforward in most cases, but there are times when patients do not respond as expected or practitioners have to modify the "usual" treatment in the face of comorbidities. In this presentation, Dr. Julie Byron will cover the various medical options for managing this condition, their pros and cons, and the most appropriate patient population for each option. Dr. Byron will also review how to handle medication transitions and situations when alterations in care may be needed, such as in patients with comorbid conditions, patients that are challenging to medicate, and those experiencing side effects. The presentation will conclude with a discussion of alternatives for dogs that do not respond to standard medical management.

courses.title: Conservative Management of Canine Cruciate Injuries
courses.description: Cruciate issues are a common presenting complaint in companion canines. Although the gold standard for management is surgical intervention, some clients may favor more conservative, less invasive, alternative management approaches. This presentation will describe the conservative management plan a primary care veterinarian can follow in conjunction with their local rehabilitation veterinarian. Dr. Lisa Mason will provide a detailed description of the pathology of cruciate injury and will review conservative management options, including orthotics, regenerative medicine, rehabilitation techniques, and long-term multimodal joint health management, with a brief mention of surgical interventions.

courses.title: Zennovation in Sedation: Rethinking What is Possible
courses.description: In this educational presentation, we will discuss sedation in dogs. The foundation will be set by reviewing the basic physiology behind commonly used sedatives in dogs. We will discuss the most commonly used sedatives and reversal agents, and introduce the novel sedative Zenalpha (medetomidine and vatinoxan hydrochlorides).

courses.title: STELFONTA (tigilanol tiglate injection): Practical aspects, Case reports and Tips from a veterinarian who is using it
courses.description: In this course, information will be provided about mode of action, indications, dosing, administration, adverse events and safe use of STELFONTA. The majority of the presentation will be focused on case experience provided by a general practice veterinarian and will illustrate patient selection and client communication tips for discussing the tumor destruction and wound healing journey as well as information on the pet owner experience.

courses.title: NC State Small Animal Abdominal Ultrasound Course
courses.description: The NC State Small Animal Abdominal Ultrasound Course provides lectures and hands-on laboratories for practitioners who wish to become more competent at abdominal ultrasonography in the small animal patient. It will provide a solid foundation in ultrasound physics, anatomy, and many case examples. In addition, this course allows hands-on experience for the practitioner.

courses.title: Navigating Controlled Substances in Veterinary Practice
courses.description: Strengthen your understanding of controlled substance management in veterinary practice! DEA regulations can feel complex, but this webinar led by PharmD Dr. Tara Marmulak simplifies the process. Explore the details of the Controlled Substances Act, prescribing rules for different controlled substance schedules, and crucial recordkeeping obligations outlined in the DEA Practitioner's Manual. Learn how to navigate these regulations with confidence and ensure compliance in your practice. This informative session is a must-attend for veterinary professionals seeking to stay up-to-date on controlled substance management.

courses.title: Destination Success: How to Get from Where You Are to Where You Want to Be
courses.description:
Remember that spark of excitement when you first chose veterinary medicine? That feeling that you could change the world? Sometimes along the way, even after building a successful career, that spark can dim. You might wake up wondering, Is this all there is? or What happened to those big dreams?
You have worked hard and built a successful career. But maybe you are feeling restless, or your day to day work is not quite what you imagined it would be. Instead of letting life just happen, or staying stuck in a role that does not excite you anymore, why not take time to think about what you really want?
In this interactive mini workshop, you will learn how to create a clear picture of your ideal future and map out steps to get there. We will start by exploring what truly matters to you, your values, dreams, and goals. Then we will look at where you are now and where you want to be, bridging that gap with practical planning.
Together, we will turn big dreams into realistic goals and then break those goals into smaller, doable steps. Using proven goal setting techniques, you will create your own workbook filled with your vision, goals, and action plans for the future.
This is not just about dreaming, it is about doing. You will leave with a practical plan and clear next steps to move toward a future that energizes and fulfills you.

courses.title: When Bandages Go Wrong: Managing slips, sores, and owner conversations
courses.description:
This lecture dives into the most common complications that can occur with veterinary bandages, from slipping and unraveling to pressure sores and moisture damage. Attendees will learn how to identify early warning signs, correct mistakes, and effectively communicate with pet owners when issues arise. Practical tips and real-world case examples will help veterinary technicians feel more confident in preventing and managing bandage failures, ensuring better outcomes for both patients and clients.
Learning Objectives:
* Recognize and troubleshoot common bandage complications such as slipping, pressure sores, and moisture-related damage through early detection and intervention.
* Apply practical correction strategies to improve bandage security, comfort, and effectiveness, using real-world case examples and technician-focused techniques.
* Develop effective communication skills for guiding pet owners in monitoring bandages at home, addressing concerns, and ensuring compliance for better patient outcomes.

courses.title: From Diagnosis to Care: Comprehensive Oral Health in General Practice
courses.description: This course will walk participants through performing a comprehensive oral health assessment and treatment (COHAT). We will discuss evaluating individual patient variables such as age, comorbidity, and severity of disease. We will discuss techniques to maximize positive patient outcomes, as well as techniques to successfully perform dental extractions.

courses.title: From Comfort to Closure: Designing Palliative Care Plans and Navigating End-of-Life Decisions
courses.description:
This webinar is designed exclusively for veterinarians seeking to enhance their approach to quality of life assessments and palliative care planning. Led by a mobile practitioner specializing in euthanasia and quality of life consultations, this session will provide practical tools for creating personalized care plans tailored to each patients unique needs.
Participants will explore strategies for assessing quality of life, implementing effective palliative care protocols, and recognizing the critical signs that indicate when end of life care should be considered. Gain confidence in guiding families through these emotionally charged decisions while maintaining compassionate, ethical, and professional care.
Perfect for veterinarians dedicated to providing exceptional support during the most challenging stages of their patients lives.

courses.title: Management of Fulminant Liver Failure in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This lecture will cover the basic pathophysiology of liver failure based on current veterinary literature, including some of the scoring systems used to help prognosticate these cases for practitioners. We will place special emphasis on the most common liver toxins in cats and dogs and on the management of hepatic encephalopathy. Finally, we will discuss the common treatments for acute liver failure as well as some individual therapies for specific toxins.

courses.title: When the Tinkle Gets Tough: How to Manage a Critically Ill Patient with Urethral Obstruction
courses.description: In this lecture, we will examine the less common complications of a common disease, feline urethral obstruction. We will discuss the management of hyperkalemia, post obstructive diuresis, uroabdomen, urethral tear, and patients that you struggle to catheterize. We will discuss the mechanisms behind atrial standstill and how to manage it, and why some hyperkalemic patients may in fact be tachycardic.

courses.title: Spot the signs. Change the outcome: a case-based approach to equine osteoarthritis
courses.description:
Equine osteoarthritis is a progressive, long-term condition that rarely follows a linear
path. In this collaborative webinar, we take a practical, case-based approach to
understanding how equine OA develops, how it responds to intervention, and how
ongoing monitoring can support better clinical decision-making.
Through real clinical cases presented by Dr Beau Whitaker (US) and Dr Stefan Cokelaere (Europe), we will
explore early and subtle signs of OA, discuss treatment and training adaptations, and
examine how different management strategies influence outcomes over time.

courses.title: Acute Kidney Injury in Dogs and Cats
courses.description:
This lecture will cover the basic pathophysiology of kidney failure based on current veterinary literature, including some of the scoring systems used to help prognosticate these cases for practitioners. Special emphasis will be placed on the most common nephrotoxins in cats and dogs. Finally, we will discuss the common treatments for AKI as well as some individual therapies for specific toxins and in cases of oliguria or anuria.
* Learning Objectives:
* Know some of the most common nephrotoxic pathophysiology in dogs and cats
* General treatment of AKI
* Treatment of AKI where the patient develops oliguria or anuria

courses.title: Acid-Base Disturbances - A Case Based Approach
courses.description: Do you have a blood gas analyzer but dread using it? Does the base excess make you weak in the knees and the anion gap bewilder you? In this session, a simple, clinically relevant step-by-step approach to evaluation of acid-base status using arterial or venous blood gas samples will be presented. Clinical cases will be used to illustrate the utility of this approach. By the end of this session, you'll be ready to take on anything that the analyzer throws at you.

courses.title: Locoregional Blocks of the Oral Cavity
courses.description:
This webinar will discuss the pharmacokinetics of local anesthesia and its applications for use in the oral cavity. Areas of application, such as the infraorbital, middle mental, caudal maxillary, and inferior alveolar blocks, will be discussed, as well as the pros and cons of each.
Learning Objectives:
How to calculate your local blocks and administer them.
How local regional blocks work.
Complications of local regional blocks.

courses.title: Cardiac Emergencies in Veterinary Patients
courses.description: In this course, participants will learn how to triage and stabilize common cardiac emergent patients. Congestive heart failure in both cats and dogs will be discussed, as well as pericardial effusion, aortic thromboembolism and caval syndrome.

courses.title: CANINE DENTISTRY WEBINAR (588-36287)
courses.description: This course focuses on canine dentistry, oral surgery and radiology. Periodontal disease, surgical and non surgical extractions and disease of canine oral cavity are discussed in a case by case format.

courses.title: Medication Frustration Begone! Tips to Improve Compliance for Pet Parents and Minimize Patient Stress
courses.description:
If you are a relief veterinarian, you likely prescribe multiple medications a day to patients. But do you ever stop and think about what happens when the client gets home and needs to give that first dose? Administering meds can be one of the most stressful activities for both pets and pet parents, impacting emotional wellbeing and preventing pets from getting the medical care they need.
In this webinar, we will discuss why it is so important to consider the emotional health of both the pet and the pet parent when prescribing. We will also cover tips and tricks to communicate to caregivers to minimize stress during the medication process, with a particular focus on oral meds.

courses.title: Diabetic Complications: A Criticalists Practical Approach to These Not-So-Sweet Cases
courses.description: Diabetes mellitus in canine and feline patients presents a spectrum of challenges, with complications such as diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), euglycemic DKA (eDKA) and hyperosmolar hyperglycemic syndrome (HHS) requiring rapid recognition and intervention. Attendees will gain knowledge of fluid therapy, insulin protocols, electrolyte corrections, and comorbid condition diagnoses crucial to stabilization of these cases for referral or managing these cases in house. By the end of this lecture, attendees will have a clear, systematic approach to diagnosis and management of patients with diabetic crises.

courses.title: Lifestyle Medicine Habits to Support Veterinary Mental Health
courses.description:
This Mental Health Awareness Month, join us for an engaging lecture that dives into how lifestyle medicine can support your mental well being and help you thrive as a veterinary professional. We will cover the science of habit and behavior change, including tools like the Habit Loop, and explore how habits like better nutrition, movement, sleep, and stress management connect to your mental health. Discover the essentials of lifestyle medicine and how simple, evidence based habits can make a big difference.
You will leave with practical, easy to implement strategies tailored for busy veterinary professionals, empowering you to build habits that stick and support your well-being for the long haul. It is time to put yourself and your well-being at the top of your priority list.

courses.title: 2025 IGNITE Online Summit on Orthobiologics, Translational Sports Medicine and Pre/Rehabilitation.
courses.description:
Regenerative medicine and orthobiologics are rapidly changing the way care is being delivered to human, equine and canine athletes. Veterinarians are often too busy to sort through the current and sometimes conflicting research and clinical applications on these topics let alone engage in discussions with colleagues and hear the perspectives of human physicians and researchers.
The 2025 IGNITE Online Summit on Orthobiologics, Translational Sports Medicine and Pre/Rehabilitation is dedicated to helping attendees make informed decisions based upon the most current research and clinical experiences in these fields using a standardized evaluation process. The wide scope of topics offered is done by partnering with international groups and associations focused on these subjects and working with different species and humans.
This is a truly translational medicine approach.
This is a truly holistic approach since we also include prevention and rehabilitation programs with physiotherapists.
Every day ends with a moderated panel discussion that includes speakers, selected panelists and input from the audience, and is aiming at having the following questions answered:
- What is in the product?
- Are the contents of product quantified and tested? If so, how often and how?
- What is the intended physiologic effect?
- Summarize research that has been conducted/published to validate use of the product.
- Approximately how many horses and human patient have been treated with product?
- Have adverse reactions (pain, swelling, negative result) been tracked? If so, what are results and how are they tracked?
- What is short-term and long-term follow-up data regarding efficacy?
- Describe ideal indication for this product and why. Are they indications to avoid use?
- Describe protocol for treatment and aftercare; NSAIDS? Series of treatments, etc.?
- What property/component makes this product unique?
- What can we learn from each other?

courses.title: It Takes a Team: Evidence-based Communication Tools for the Veterinary Team
courses.description: Delivery of quality healthcare requires highly skilled teams that can remain effective in the complex, unpredictable environment that is the modern veterinary practice. Drawing on the evidence-based TeamSTEPPS system developed for human health care, this session will introduce the VetTEAMS framework, a series of team competencies and simple communication tools that can be integrated into your practice to reduce medical errors, and improve team performance, and enhance staff satisfaction. Delivery of high-quality veterinary care requires extraordinary team work. Learn how you can help your team reach the next level of efficiency, quality, and safety.

courses.title: Exotic Mammal Euthanasia for the General Practitioner
courses.description: Presented by Dr. Céline Leheurteux, DMV, this session provides practical guidance on euthanasia for exotic mammals in a general practice setting. Attendees will explore preferred injection techniques and learn pre-euthanasia sedation tips and protocols tailored for rabbits, ferrets, and rodents. Gain confidence in delivering compassionate care during this sensitive process.

courses.title: Demystified Anesthetic DOGma and Avoiding CATastrophes
courses.description:
This 1 hour presentation investigates common Dogma that circulates veterinary anesthesia and analgesia, perhaps even adjacent topics. Wonder which way is best for inflating endotracheal tubes and perhaps how we likely doing it, isn't best? Wonder why people say no Ketamine for exotic cat breeds? What about morphine mania in cats? Or opioids in horses, or nail polish for surgery, or acepromazine in boxers, or the origins of a Doppler value in a cat is the MAP not SAP? I have done the literature review and will share the evidence so you are empowered to make the best judgement call. Bring your DOGma's and possible CATastrophes, and lets get to the bottom of it, scientifically and move beyond the 'this is what I was taught'.
Learning Objectives:
* Enhance critical thinking and investigate skills researching common anesthetic related dogma,
* Learn the origin of common anesthetic misconceptions
* Broaden anesthetic knowledge and ability to perform critical review of literature to determine bets practice for the individualized patient.

courses.title: Diabetic Emergencies
courses.description: Diabetic patients often present to the ER in various crises. As a technician your ability to recognize the type of emergency and monitor your patient appropriately will help the patient get the best treatment possible and support a quick recovery. This lecture will review the most common and life threatening diabetic emergencies. The physiology of the endocrine pancreas and the pathophysiology of Hypoglycemia, Diabetic Ketotic Acidosis and Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar Syndrome will be reviewed. Stabilization, treatment and nursing care will be discussed.

courses.title: Taming the Student Debt Monster
courses.description: Student loans have been a moving target recently, with frequent changes and challenges to repayment plans. We will discuss the latest updates on income-driven repayment programs and how to incorporate student loans into your overall financial plan. Being intentional about your repayment strategy is worth the time and effort, since choosing the wrong plan can be a costly mistake.

courses.title: Kirbys Rule of 20. A Checklist for Routine Assessment of the Critically Ill Patient
courses.description: Routine assessment of hospitalized patients is important to monitor key subjective and objective physical examination parameters to assess the patients response to treatment in the hospital as well as early detection of possible complications. Kirbys rule of 20 was written by Rebecca Kirby, DVM, DACVIM, DACVECC and is a checklist of twenty important parameters to monitor in patients at least once per day.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Dentistry for the General Practitioner
courses.description:
A detailed review of fundamental information that all GP doctors should know about Veterinary dentistry in dogs and cats.
Learning Objectives:
* Know the basic anatomy of the tooth and mouth, learn the normal and be able to recognize the abnormal.
* Learn how to perform an oral exam on awake patients and be able to recognize disease.
* Recognize common oral diseases: periodontal disease, fractured teeth, gingival masses, tooth resorption, non vital teeth, missing teeth, malocclusions.
* Be able to recommend appropriate treatment based on oral exam findings.
* Be able to assess the level of disease and get an accurate estimate based on the oral exam and also other factors like breed, size and age of the patient.

courses.title: Stabilizing the Patient with Non-Traumatic Hemoabdomen
courses.description: In this lecture, we will take a case-based approach on managing the non-traumatic canine hemoabdomen patient, from initial triage and stabilization, through diagnostics, and into the operating room. Participants will gain an understanding of common cardiovascular and hemostatic disturbances in these patients and how to manage them. Beyond the physiology, we will discuss the overall approach to these patients and how to manage owner conversations and expectations.

courses.title: Harnessing AI for Veterinary Medical Records
courses.description: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing the landscape of veterinary medicine, offering new ways to reduce burnout, improve accuracy, and enhance patient care. In this session, Dr. Kat will share practical insights from her work developing and refining AI driven medical record tools. Attendees will learn how AI can be leveraged to make their lives easier without compromising the art and science of veterinary practice.

courses.title: Triage and Common Presentations in Exotic Companion Animals
courses.description: Exotic patients are fragile and often mask illness until advanced. This lecture reviews efficient, low-stress triage techniques, key history elements, and species-specific stabilization steps. Common emergency and appointment presentations in ferrets, rabbits, small mammals, birds, and reptiles are outlined with practical, actionable protocols to improve outcomes and client education.

courses.title: The RECOVER 2024 CPR Guidelines: Basic and Advanced Life Support
courses.description: When patients experience cardiopulmonary arrest (CPA), seconds count. A well-trained and prepared veterinary health care team can mean the difference between life and death when a patient experiences CPA. This lecture will explain key concepts from the newly updated RECOVER 2024 evidence evaluation process in the domains of Basic and Advanced Life Support, including the evidence-based approach to providing optimal chest compressions and ventilation in dogs and cats, as well as monitoring, drug and defibrillation therapy.

courses.title: Common Arrhythmias and their Treatments
courses.description:
In this course, participants will review how to interpret an ECG tracing, rate and
rhythm, and then advance their skills into correct arrhythmia diagnosis. We will discuss
antiarrhythmic medication classes, mechanism of action and which drugs to select for each type of common arrhythmia.

courses.title: Aortic Thromboembolism in Cats
courses.description:
In this course, participants will review the pathogenesis of thromboembolic disease in cats. We will describe the risk factors that preclude cardiac cats to this particular complication, prevention mechanisms and treatment courses.
Learning Objectives:
* Identify how to prevent aortic thromboembolism in cats
* Determine prognostic indicators that help dictate client conversation and expectations
* Learn various courses of treatments for aortic thromboembolism cases

courses.title: To Text or Not To Text: Navigating the Multigenerational Team
courses.description:
In the diverse landscape of in-person, virtual and hybrid teams, multi-generational teams and clients bring unique perspectives, communication styles, and expectations. This presentation explores strategies for effectively navigating this generational diversity by fostering collaboration, understanding and enhancing connections.
Throughout this workshop, participants will learn the differences of each current and future generation in the workforce. By the end of the session, participants will have gained an understanding of how we can be different and still cohesive when working alongside people of other generations.

courses.title: Elevate Your Veterinary Career: Mastering Your Own Engagement and Job Satisfaction
courses.description:
As a veterinary professional, your job satisfaction and overall well-being are essential to providing top-notch care. This webinar will empower you to take control of your employee experience and foster a fulfilling career. Discover how to uncover your core values, understand what truly matters to you, and align your work with your passions.
Identify your growth and safety needs, determine your professional development goals and create a supportive work environment. Master effective communication by learning how to communicate your needs clearly and build strong relationships with colleagues.
By the end of this webinar, you'll have practical strategies to enhance your job satisfaction, increase your engagement, and thrive in your veterinary career.

courses.title: 2026 MPA Breeder Hatchery Seminar
courses.description: The 2026 Breeder-Hatchery Seminar is a one-day educational program designed to provide poultry industry professionals with current information and practical management strategies related to breeder flock performance, hatchery operations, biosecurity, flock health, and production efficiency. Presentations will focus on fertility management, hatchery sanitation, egg collection and handling, feed distribution, egg turning, flock health, biosecurity practices, and emerging industry issues. The seminar provides attendees with science-based information and practical field applications that can be implemented within breeder and hatchery operations to improve bird welfare, production outcomes, and operational efficiency.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Dentistry, Level 2
courses.description:
This class is available to DVMs who have completed one of the Introduction to Canine and Feline Dentistry and Oral Surgery classes. This 8-hour class will consist of 4 hours of lecture followed by 4 hours of hands-on wet lab. The topics discussed in lecture will include periodontal disease, dental fractures, an introduction to endodontic pathology, and common extraction complications.
The lab will include the basics of open and closed root planning, application of perioceutic products, odontoplasty with bonded sealants of uncomplicated crown fractures, difficult extractions, and surgical removal of root tips.
This class will be presented by Steven Honzelka, DVM, DAVDC.

courses.title: Stewardship Starts Here: The Power of Veterinary Technicians in Protecting Antibiotics
courses.description: Participants will gain a practical understanding of antimicrobial resistance, AMR, and the veterinary technician's role in antimicrobial stewardship. This session provides actionable strategies in infection prevention, sample collection, medication handling and client communication to support responsible antibiotic use. Attendees will leave equipped to improve patient outcomes and help preserve antimicrobial effectiveness.

courses.title: The Future of Veterinary Surgery - On Demand
courses.description: The goal of this webinar is to highlight upcoming techniques/technologies that may represent future directions in veterinary surgery. Panelists will discuss their personal experiences with new technology as it pertains to surgical treatments in small and large animal patient populations. Participants will learn about computer-guided surgical techniques, uses for stealth navigations systems, and applications for robotic surgical systems in both small and large animal surgical settings.

courses.title: Tiny Teeth, Big Trouble: Feline Periodontal Disease
courses.description: Periodontal disease affects more than 80 percent of adult cats. This disease often goes unnoticed in cats until progression is severe enough to cause significant oral and systemic health issues. Effective prevention and treatment is a combination of professional intervention and consistent oral hygiene in the cat's home environment. This presentation will review the prevalence, pathophysiology, and treatment of periodontal disease in cats, with a focus on recommending effective home care to clients.

courses.title: Surgical Approach to the Ear, Head, and Neck On-Demand
courses.description: Ear, head, and neck surgery is performed commonly in small animal soft tissue surgery, although challenges and complications may arise. This seminar discusses novel and creative ways of enhancing the surgeon's approach to the head, neck, and ear. Additionally, this seminar reviews tips and tricks for revision and reconstruction surgeries of the ear, head, and neck that aim to augment a surgeon's approach to certain complicated procedures.

courses.title: Upper Gastrointestinal Tract Reconstruction
courses.description: During this hybrid lab, participants will learn the standard techniques to reconstruct the upper gastrointestinal tract: Y-U pyloroplasty, Billroth I, and Billroth II. Then, participants will be exposed to the Roux-en-Y principles that are used to replace the Billroth II to reconstruct the upper gastrointestinal tract and /or to avoid cholecystoduodenostomy in dogs and cats.

courses.title: African Vet Conservation
courses.description:
Step into the world of wildlife veterinary medicine with this intensive, hands-on training course in South Africa. Designed for veterinarians, vet students, and vet nurses, this program covers all essential skills needed for a career in wildlife medicine.
Learn about chemical immobilization, darting techniques, including from a helicopter, field anesthesia, and emergency wildlife care; All while working up close with Africa's iconic species.
From tracking and safely relocating animals to understanding the role of wildlife conservation in veterinary medicine, this course offers real-world experience in the heart of the African bush.

courses.provider: THE EQUINE CUSHING'S AND INSULIN RESISTANCE GROUP, INC.
courses.title: NO! LAMINITIS CONFERENCE 2025
courses.description:
Recent estimates indicate that between 10% and 15% of horses experience laminitis each year. Endocrine disease is the cause in approximately 80% to 90% of these cases, affecting 1 million horses annually in the US alone. For 25 years, the ECIR Group has supported education designed to prevent equine metabolic laminitis with these four basic tenets: Diagnosis, Diet, Trim, and Exercise. Past conference attendees welcomed the latest in research and specific protocols used to improve the welfare of equines in their care. The 2025 NO Laminitis! Conference will continue to build on that mission. When: October 31 through November 2, 2025 Where: ECIR Virtual Conference Room (Zoom) at the location of your choice. Speakers include, Eleanor Kellon, VMD, Robert Bowker, VMD, PhD, Kathleen Gustafson PhD, Harold Schott, DVM, PhD, Isabelle Kagan, PhD, Elaine Norton, DVM, PhD, Priska Darani, PhD, Jo Ireland, BVMS, PhD, David Rendle, BVSc, Tania Sundra, BSc, BVMS, Kathleen Sullivan, PhD, Suzanne Gottschang, PhD, and Johan Brojer, DVM, PhD, recipient of the inaugural 2024 ECIR Group Inc research grant. Ticket Pricing (USD): Veterinary Professionals seeking 21 hours AAVSB RACE CE; $350, Full Lecture Admission $300, Early-Bird (Registration prior to October 10, 2025) $275, Veterinary Student with proof of University enrollment required $175. Full course description and registration can be found at https://www.nolaminitis.org/
Approved for 21 hours of AAVSB Continuing Education.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: The Stigma of Addiction for Veterinarians
courses.description: This non-interactive, on-demand, continuing education program provides veterinary professionals with a comprehensive examination of addiction stigma and its impact on clinical decision-making, client care, and the well-being of veterinary practitioners themselves. Participants will gain foundational knowledge in opioid training, controlled substance prescribing, and the identification and reduction of addiction stigma in veterinary practice settings. The course uses a one health approach to addresses substance use disorder through the lens of person-first language, medication-assisted treatment, prescription monitoring programs, and compassionate care strategies for clients and colleagues alike. Veterinary professionals concerned with compassion fatigue, veterinary mental health, and the culture of silence surrounding addiction within the profession will find targeted, evidence-based guidance and actionable resources throughout this program. This course was designed to satisfy state license CE requirements on pain management, opioids and other controlled substances and change how veterinarians practice.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: Upper Airway Surgical Diseases On-Demand
courses.description: Managing diseases that contribute to upper airway obstruction continues to be an evolving and challenging aspect of veterinary surgery. Complex anatomy and function, along with limitations in diagnostics, contribute to these challenges. This seminar focuses on challenging cases and innovative solutions. Specialists in this field discuss approaches to these cases, including the work-up, surgery, and post-operative care.

courses.title: Degenerative Lumbosacral Stenosis
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will examine the pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings of degenerative lumbosacral stenosis (DLSS) in canine patients. This course will also review and compare treatments including surgical decompression, epidural steroid injections, and medical management to optimize patient outcomes.

courses.title: The Rapidly Changing Landscape of Feline HCM, Diagnostic and Therapeutic Updates
courses.description: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a common feline disease with severe disease outcomes. In this one-hour webinar we will break down a practical approach to feline medicine for diagnosing the often-silent disease of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. We will highlight advances in diagnostics, methods of assessing HCM severity and prognosis, and new treatment opportunities available.

courses.title: The RECOVER Newborn Resuscitation Guidelines: A Tour Through the Algorithm
courses.description: The RECOVER initiative's most recent clinical guidelines revolve around the unique aspects of resuscitation of newborn dogs and cats immediately after birth. This session will go over the newborn resuscitation algorithm. This algorithm provides a step-by-step approach to essential resuscitation measures for puppies and kittens as they transition from intra- to extrauterine life. Key questions addressed in this presentation are: Which newborns need resuscitation? How does the heart rate guide resuscitation measures? What monitoring should be used during resuscitation? Should oxygen always be supplemented? What is the single most important intervention to save non-vigorous newborn puppies/kittens? I will further point out how different newborn resuscitation is from CPR in adult dogs and cats.

courses.title: Locoregional Anesthesia On-Demand
courses.description: This webinar series provides a comprehensive overview of locoregional anesthesia, exploring its benefits and practical applications through detailed discussions of epidural, sacrococcygeal, transversus abdominis plane (TAP), saphenous, and sciatic nerve blocks. Participants will gain knowledge of pertinent anatomy, procedural techniques, and strategies for integrating these blocks into effective postoperative pain management plans, particularly for abdominal and hind limb procedures.

courses.title: Mountain to Sea Veterinary Leadership Retreat - Greece
courses.description:
This eight session, hands-on leadership course empowers veterinary
professionals to delegate with intention, build trust, and develop leadership capacity within their teams. Many leaders struggle to let go of tasks and decisions due to fear, identity, or a lack of clear frameworks. The result is bottlenecks, burnout, and missed growth opportunities for the team. Across four days, participants will explore the emotional and strategic barriers to delegation, learn proven delegation and coaching models, and apply tools to foster a culture of accountability and ownership. Through real-time practice, feedback, and collaboration, attendees will leave with a customized action plan to confidently empower their teams.

courses.title: Decade One Meeting Four
courses.description: This course covers professional communication skills including effective communication, negotiation, conflict resolution, gender roles in communication, and difficult conversations.

courses.title: Tiny Teeth, Big Trouble - Feline Periodontal Disease
courses.description: Periodontal disease affects more than 80% of adult cats. This disease often goes unnoticed in cats until progression is severe enough to cause significant oral and systemic health issues. Effective prevention and treatment is a combination of professional intervention and consistent oral hygiene in the cat's home environment. This presentation will review the prevalence, pathophysiology, and treatment of periodontal disease in cats, with a focus on recommending effective home cat to clients.

courses.title: Management of Urgent and Emergent Cases in General & Urgent Care Practice
courses.description: Some of the most common sick and urgent emergencies that present a diagnostic or therapeutic challenge to general practitioners are anaphylaxis, endocrine emergencies including hypoadrenocorticism, and urinary obstruction cases. With practical diagnostic tips, treatment guidelines and clinical examples, the lecture is presented from the perspective of a Criticalist that has years of experience working in general practice, urgent care and multispecialty referral hospitals, and currently provides 24/7 specialty consultations to veterinarians through DVM STAT Consulting.

courses.title: Equine Osteoarthritis and Chondroprotective Therapies
courses.description: The presenter reviews equine osteoarthritis (OA) and chondroprotective therapies. Focus areas include basic anatomy of the joint, articular cartilage composition and function, pathophysiology of OA including histologic progression, and types of chondroprotective therapies. The types of therapies discussed will include hyaluronate sodium (HA), glycosaminoglycan (PSGAG), and pentosan polysulfate (PPS), which are all currently indicated for OA and/or degenerative joint disease in horses. Additionally a meta-analysis of current research with regards to equine OA treatments will be analyzed

courses.title: Becoming a Veterinary SuperCommunicator
courses.description:
Veterinary medicine is filled with emotionally charged conversations with clients, colleagues, and team members. When communication breaks down, it often leads to conflict, complaints, stress, and burnout.
But when communication skills improve, everything changes.
The Becoming a Veterinary SuperCommunicator Program is a 4-week interactive learning experience designed to help veterinary professionals navigate difficult conversations with confidence and clarity.
In this program, participants will learn practical, evidence-based communication strategies to:
build stronger client relationships
manage emotionally charged conversations
resolve workplace conflict
regulate their internal response to challenging interactions
foster healthier and more supportive team dynamics
Through four focused live interactive sessions and an optional 1-on-1 coaching session, participants will gain tools they can apply immediately to improve communication, strengthen relationships, and support both personal and workplace wellbeing.

courses.title: Veterinary Spinal Manipulative Therapy (Postgraduate & State-Approved Certification)
courses.description: The curriculum consists of a minimum of 226 hours of supervised instruction (both didactic & hands-on practicum lab, divided into 5 (five) Modules. Each class has a maximum of twenty students per class, providing an excellent faculty-to-student ratio. As this is a postgraduate certification program, each student must set time aside to study, practice, and integrate the said information. Time to study and practice varies between 10 and 15 hrs. per week. Please note that all clinical and practical work included in the program is under direct supervision, with NO external externships required. In addition, each student must present two (2) cases in a SOAP format during Modules IV or V. All attendees receive an in-depth syllabus.

courses.title: Advanced Fracture Repair 3: Pelvic Fractures and SI Luxation
courses.description:
This is an advanced level course designed for practitioners that have completed the Principles of Fracture Repair course (or equivalent) and have experience with fracture repair. The course is one of three advanced courses designed to train veterinarians to reach a high level of expertise in veterinary orthopedics. These techniques are difficult and quite demanding. They require a firm understanding of orthopedic principles, tissue handling, use of power equipment, locking plate technique, and use of bone clamps and other orthopedic instrumentation.
Fractures of the pelvis are common in dogs and cats. Pelvic fractures are also commonly accompanied by sacroiliac luxation or hip dislocation. This course will discuss decision-making, surgical approach, reduction techniques and surgical repair of fractures of the ilium and acetabulum as well as repair of sacroiliac luxation and hip dislocation.
This course is designed to take the general practitioner to a higher level in pelvic injury repair. We will teach reliable techniques and give valuable practical tips useful in repairing challenging pelvic fractures, sacroiliac luxation and hip dislocation. New implant designs have made fracture repair much simpler and more affordable. In addition, postoperative management of patients has also been simplified and complications are rate if the principles of fracture repair are followed.
This course will familiarize participants with repair techniques through lecture and clinical case presentations. Following lecture and case review, participants will repair fractures and luxation on plastic bone models and cadavers. Postoperative radiographs will be taken to evaluate the participants repair technique.

courses.title: Surgical Management of Chylothorax
courses.description: The presentation will discuss the latest concepts in surgical management of canine and feline chylothorax with a focus on the important practical aspects of intraoperative decision-making and the latest data on outcomes.

courses.title: Separation Related Distress in Dog: 5 Steps to Success
courses.description: This course discusses and defines separation related distress and its subtypes. It is also important to differentiate SRD from other behavior disorders that may show similar or overlapping signs. The evaluation and treatment process is laid out in five steps to enable practitioners to adequately evaluate and address the problem.

courses.title: Navigating the Feline CKD Mosaic: From Early Intervention to Emerging Therapies.
courses.description:
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects nearly one-third of senior cats, yet no two patients experience the disease in exactly the same way. Advances in our understanding of feline CKD are reshaping how veterinarians approach diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment, moving beyond a one-size-fits-all strategy toward more individualized care.
This webinar will explore the diverse clinical trajectories that characterize feline CKD and discuss practical approaches for tailoring management to the needs of individual patients. Through case-based examples, attendees will review emerging concepts in early intervention, including management of anemia, phosphorus homeostasis, and acid-base balance, as well as the growing recognition of interactions between the gastrointestinal tract and the kidneys. The session will conclude with a look toward the future of feline nephrology, highlighting promising areas of ongoing research and therapeutic innovation that may further transform care for cats with kidney disease.

courses.title: Anesthesia: Equipment Maintenance
courses.description: This program is meant to give the veterinary staff member basic knowledge of how an anesthesia machine functions, how to maintain and troubleshoot such equipment, and bad habits to avoid.

courses.title: The future of proactive veterinary care
courses.description:
What would you do for every patient if you had unlimited time? Most vets have an instinctive answer and almost no way to act on it. This session is about the technology that's finally closing that gap. Digitail CEO Sebastian Gabor and Dr. Laila Proenca lay out a vision for AI in veterinary medicine. Not scribes and summaries, but a complete proactive intelligence layer that pulls together PIMS data, pet parent app activity, and clinic communications to tell you in real time what every patient needs before they walk through the door. Anchored in fresh findings from the 2026 AAHA State of the Industry study and grounded in Dr. Proenca's own experience running this kind of system in her clinic, you'll see what proactive care actually looks like day-to-day: the conversations it enables, the cases it surfaces, and the membership and wellness models it makes possible for the first time.
Key Takeaways
- Understand how AI is evolving beyond documentation tools into proactive patient intelligence, and what that shift means for day-to-day clinic operations.
- Learn how integrating PIMS data, pet parent app activity, and clinic communications can surface patient needs before the appointment begins.
- See real-world evidence from a practitioner already running a proactive care model, anchored in findings from the 2026 AAHA State of the Industry study.
- Discover how proactive AI infrastructure enables membership and wellness plan models that were previously too operationally complex to sustain.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: Hand Skills and Headspace: The Science of Surgical Coaching - On Demand
courses.description: As surgeons, we have all experienced a variety of mentorship and coaching styles throughout our training. What defines a great surgical coach, and how is this different from a professional mentor? How can we improve our own coaching of students, interns and residents, so that the next generation of surgeons possesses both the technical skillset and the mindset required to achieve surgical excellence? Drawing from principles of adult educational psychology, coaching in human surgery and mindset tools from high performers in other industries, the webinar will provide practical strategies to improve clinical coaching, foster a growth mindset in adult learners and create an environment of psychological safety. Whether you are involved in coaching veterinary students, nurses, house officers or practicing veterinarians, we hope that you will find meaningful guidance that benefits your own surgical growth as much as your learners.

courses.title: Women IN Surgery - Vet (WINS-Vet)
courses.description:
This two-day Women in Surgery (WINS) forum is designed to bring veterinary surgeons together to advance clinical expertise, strengthen professional resilience, and foster a supportive community within orthopedic surgery. Through a combination of expert-led lectures, case-based panel discussions, and hands-on laboratory training, participants will explore the principles and practical application of joint arthrodesis across the forelimb and hindlimb.
The program features focused sessions on carpal and tarsal arthrodesis, including tips, techniques, and decision-making strategies for procedures such as partial versus pancarpal arthrodesis. Attendees will engage in interactive panel discussions and case reviews that emphasize clinical reasoning, fixation selection, and postoperative management. Dedicated ArthroLab experiences provide the opportunity to apply these concepts in a hands-on setting using current plating systems and instrumentation.
In addition to technical training, the forum highlights professional development and peer collaboration through resident abstract presentations and facilitated group discussions. Topics include protecting surgical repairs, managing complex trauma cases, and cultivating strength and perspective in challenging clinical environments. The program culminates in collaborative case-sharing sessions, encouraging participants to exchange insights and build lasting professional connections.

courses.title: Staff retention: The power of positive practice culture
courses.description: Weve brought together some of the most respected figures in the veterinary wellness space to explore one of the most pressing issues facing the veterinary industry. Join Chankia Berry, Marie Holowaychuk, Olivia Oginska, Andy Green and Sarah Hoggan for a lively discussion on the staff shortage crisis and how cultivating a positive work environment can help practices attract and retain talent in an ultra-competitive labor market. Expect fresh insights and proven strategies you can start using immediately to elevate your workplace culture and increase staff retention.

courses.title: Updates on Plasma Cell Pododermatitis and Immune Complex Mediated Glomerular Nephritis (ICGN)
courses.description: This session will share recent research regarding the clinical presentation of plasma cell pododermatitis (PCP) and associated immune complex mediated glomerular nephritis (ICGN) in cats, an uncommon but serious condition traditionally associated with a poor prognosis. Familiarity with these disease processes and their potential association may facilitate earlier diagnosis and improve outcomes for young cats affected by these conditions.

courses.title: Self-Compassion for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description:
This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will focus on self-compassion. We are often our own worst critics, especially when we are passionate about our work. This can negatively impact our mood, mental health, and work performance. This program will provide tools and techniques to practice to protect our wellbeing, plus the reasoning behind why these methods work.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1242038.)

courses.title: CANINE MASSAGE FUNDAMENTALS (1419-37823)
courses.description: Canine Massage is a valuable modality that veterinary professionals should add to their existing skill set to accompany the care provided by the veterinarian. Massage benefits dogs physically and emotionally, including reducing stress and anxiety as well as decreasing pain and discomfort as a result of age, illness, surgery, or injury. Massage can help improve outcomes by supporting the healing process, reducing healing time, and generally improving quality of life. Effective canine massage involves much more than applying massage techniques to the body. In addition to learning the techniques in this 3-day workshop, participants will learn the essential skills of palpation, which include understanding the basics of skeletal anatomy, proper body mechanics, and how to engage your "thinking fingers" in order to assess the dog's body.
