Participants will also learn how to use passive range of motion (PROM) as part of the assessment process. By the end of the workshop, participants will have gained the tools necessary to provide a dog with an effective and safe massage to promote relaxation and wellness. Prerequisites: Trust and Relationship-Building with Dogs (Parts 1 and 2), Canine Massage Fundamentals Part 1 (online), or instructor permission.

courses.title: Large Animal Keynote Lecture: Complications: Talking About Something We'd Rather Not Discuss On-Demand
courses.description: Complications are an unfortunate part of veterinary surgery. While the complication rate in most instances is quite low, it is still something the surgeon has to deal with. Complications affect not only the patient but also the surgery team, the animal care team, and the animal owners. This keynote lecture reviews a series of cases and the complications arising from them. This lecture focuses on how to discuss surgical complications with the surgery team and the owners.

courses.title: Introduction to Quantitative Risk Analysis for Animal Health and Food Safety
courses.description: This CE course provides a practical introduction to risk analysis and quantitative risk assessment for animal health and food safety. Veterinarians (specifically those in food safety, regulatory animal health and research) will learn what risk analysis is and how it is used to support decision-making in animal health and food safety. We will introduce organizations that govern international standards, will explain the main components of quantitative risk analysis in animal health and food safety, and discuss similarities and differences. We will review published examples to illustrate how quantitative risk assessments supports decision-making and inform policies.

courses.title: Competency, Quality, and Growth: Redefining Surgical Residency Education On-Demand
courses.description: This seminar covers key issues relevant to surgical training that are essential to prepare veterinary students to be successful in the practice of surgery upon graduation. Lectures explore innovations in pre-clinical skills training, how to maximize the clinical learning experience to foster practice-ready veterinarians and develop future surgeons, the use of collaborative partnerships to support the educational program, and strategies for building a sustainable faculty workforce. An interactive panel discussion allows expert speakers and interested learners to discuss complex topics critical for ensuring the future of a high-quality surgical education and maintaining the art of surgery in practice.

courses.title: Decade One 2.0 Year Two
courses.description:
Decade One 2.0: Year Two builds on the foundational business and branding concepts taught in Year One and transitions participants into deeper professional skills essential for long-term sustainability in equine practice.
This year focuses on leadership development, emotional intelligence, communication frameworks, burnout prevention, negotiation skills, and workplace culture dynamics. All content is directly applied to the daily realities of equine veterinary work.
The curriculum is delivered through a combination of pre-recorded, noninteractive video lessons taught by Dr. Amy Grice, and monthly live interactive Zoom sessions facilitated by Drs. Cordivano, Gray, and Zeytoonian. Each monthly module includes a blend of lectures, reflection exercises, practical tools, and real-world case applications.
Participants gain immediately applicable strategies to strengthen their leadership, communicate more effectively with clients and colleagues, navigate conflict, and sustain a healthy career in the demanding world of equine veterinary practice.

courses.title: Inside and Out
courses.description:
Welcome to Inside and Out, the veterinary mystery series where dermatology and internal medicine team up to solve clinical puzzles that refuse to follow the textbook rules. In this fun, fast-paced, on-demand talk show style course, board-certified veterinary dermatologist Dr. Joya Griffin and board-certified internal medicine specialist Dr. Forrest Cummings take you inside some of the most challenging small animal cases in practice, the ones where the skin says one thing, the body says something else, and diagnostic detective work becomes the name of the game.
Each 20-minute episode drops you straight into a real-world mystery case. Instead of passive learning, you follow along as the specialists think out loud, debate differentials, and work through diagnostic strategies just like they would during a referral consultation. The goal is to make high-level clinical reasoning feel accessible, practical, and actually entertaining.

courses.title: Self-Compassion for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description:
This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will focus on self-compassion. We are often our own worst critics, especially when we are passionate about our work. This can negatively impact our mood, mental health, and work performance. This program will provide tools and techniques to practice to protect our wellbeing, plus the reasoning behind why these methods work.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1242038.)

courses.title: Effect of a heated anesthetic circuit on body temperature of anesthetized New Zealand white rabbits (Oryctolagus cuniculus)
courses.description: Participants will learn ways to limit hypothermia in clinical rabbit patients, as well as why this is important. Several active warming methods are discussed, with emphasis on the heated anesthetic circuit used in this research study.

courses.title: Anaesthesia of Exotic Animals: Part 1
courses.description: This lecture, presented by Dr Sonya Miles BVSc CertAVP(ZM) CertAqV MRCVS, introduces the core principles of anaesthesia in exotic species, emphasising the anatomical, physiological, and behavioural adaptations required to ensure patient safety. The session covers pre-anaesthetic assessment, stabilisation strategies, species-specific risk factors, and fundamental anaesthetic techniques used in exotic mammals, birds, and reptiles. Delegates will learn how to minimise peri-anaesthetic stress, select appropriate premedication and induction methods, and perform intubation safely using equipment suitable for small and anatomically unique species. The content provides a structured foundation for practitioners looking to develop confidence in delivering anaesthesia to non-traditional companion animals.

courses.title: Equine Toxicology Review
courses.description: Review of Top Equine Toxicoses

courses.title: Canine and Feline Clinical Pathology Part 3: Kidneys and Urinalysis
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive review of small animal clinical pathology with a focus on kidney function, azotemia classification, proteinuria, and urinary tract disease management. Participants learn to interpret laboratory findings, including urinalysis and serum chemistries, while exploring common diseases such as chronic kidney disease, protein-losing nephropathy, urethral obstruction, and feline lower urinary tract disease. The program combines case-based learning with diagnostic and treatment strategies to enhance clinical practice.

courses.title: Canine Juvenile Bone Disease
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of juvenile orthopedic diseases and dysplasias affecting dogs (primarily) and cats. Participants explore the clinical presentation, pathophysiology, diagnostic techniques, and management strategies for conditions such as panosteitis, hypertrophic osteodystrophy, osteochondrosis, hip dysplasia, avascular necrosis of the femoral head, elbow dysplasia, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, and craniomandibular osteopathy. This program emphasizes radiographic interpretation, breed-specific considerations, and both surgical and medical interventions to optimize patient outcomes.

courses.title: Switchback Foundation
courses.description: If you feel like you've lose your passion that you once had for being a practicing veterinary professional, or struggle in a toxic workplace, you are not alone. We have a skill set which will unlock your potential as a leader, resurrect passion and change toxic team traits into switched-on, synergistic and cohesive team momentum.

courses.title: Dental Radiographs Made Easy - Webinar
courses.description: Dental radiographs are an essential part of the oral exam. The crown is just the tip of the iceberg. Approximately 42 percent of dental pathology is found below the gumline. Radiographs will help diagnose pathology that is not visible from the surface, confirm suspect pathology, and help demonstrate the pathology to the client. Dental radiographs can improve the standard of care in your practice and increase your clinic revenue.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: V.I.P. Veterinary Introductory Pathology- A System-Based Review
courses.description: This monthly webinar series will present a systems-based introduction to veterinary histopathology. Each month, a different body system (Integument, Urinary, Reproductive, Cardiovascular, Endocrine, Pulmonary, Musculoskeletal, Digestive, Hemolymphatic, Nervous, and Special Senses [Eye and Ear]) will be introduced in a way that participants of any level of experience (veterinary students, interns, residents and/or anatomic pathologists) will be able to comprehend and further expand their knowledge of veterinary pathology. Each webinar will introduce the normal tissue architecture, histological features of each anatomic structure and highlight the response to injury of different tissues and cell types found within each system. Cumulatively, by the end of the series, participants will have learned about the embryologic development, structure, function, and response to injury of twelve body systems - As well as received an introduction to some species specific variations of different systemic components. Additionally, these webinars will introduce unique patterns and types of injury that are seen in certain organ systems (such as patterns of pneumonia and zonal patterns of hepatocyte injury). Presentations will give a comprehensive introduction that illus

courses.title: Chronic Pain Symposium 2026 - On Demand
courses.description: The third annual Chronic Pain Symposium, hosted by Canine Arthritis Management, was a three-day global online event featuring continuing education for veterinary professionals. The virtual symposium presented lectures and engaging panel discussions with world-renowned experts on a wide range of topics relating to chronic pain in companion animals. The lecture recordings from this revolutionary learning event are now available to access on demand, with a select number of lectures featuring RACE approval; delegates are required to complete a minimum of 1 credit hour.

courses.title: When the Tinkle Gets Tough: How to Manage a Critically Ill Patient with Urethral Obstruction
courses.description: In this lecture, we will examine the less common complications of a common disease, feline urethral obstruction. We will discuss the management of hyperkalemia, post obstructive diuresis, uroabdomen, urethral tear, and patients that you struggle to catheterize. We will discuss the mechanisms behind atrial standstill and how to manage it, and why some hyperkalemic patients may in fact be tachycardic.

courses.title: Practice Proactive Wellness for Consistently Better Patient Outcomes
courses.description:
The demographics of our veterinary clients has changed drastically over the last few years. Clients are more informed and want to have a healthy pet. They view their pets as their starter children and demand excellent veterinary care.
This course will assist attendees in developing a proactive wellness program of care allows clients a visual understanding of their pet's issues and a way for them to be directly involved in the treatment thereof.
Infrared thermal imaging (IRTI) provides a way of identifying problems before the onset of clinical signs. IRTI identifies anatomical areas that would benefit from further evaluation and possibly diagnostics, objectively monitors any therapeutic rehabilitation regime to maximize patient care and is a client education tool that increases client compliance with clinical recommendations.
With expanding uses in pain management, wound healing, and rehabilitation, laser therapy has become a critical addition to the continuum of care. Laser therapy resolves inflammation and encourages vasodilation activation of the lymphatic drainage system to provide analgesia. Photobiomodulation can be helpful in managing fractures, post-operative pain, osteoarthritis, otitis, stomatitis, wounds, ligament injuries in small animals and horses and corneal ulcers, just to mention a few.
One of the steps we will discuss is incorporating a laser therapy rental system in your clinic. This will provide clients with a direct involvement in their pet's treatment regimen.
After IRTI identifies all the areas where it would be the most beneficial, a loading photoceutical dose of photonic energy is administered in the clinic. The client is then sent home with a copy of the IRTI to guide them in their home application of laser therapy. After a specified time, the animal is brought back to the clinic to reimage. The change in the temperatures within the regions of interest are a very objective monitor as to the progress of the patient.
Utilizing infrared thermal

courses.title: Antimicrobial Stewardship Made Practical
courses.description:
Companion animal veterinarians are increasingly confronted with patients suffering from antimicrobial resistant (AMR) infections. AMR is a problem across health sectors, though the focus has largely been on human and agricultural animals. Cats and dogs share our environments, and sometimes our ice cream cones, and we prescribe the same antibiotic drug classes as those used in human health. Recently, more attention is being payed to this oft ignored population in regards to AMR.
Antimicrobial stewardship (AS) is the actions that prescribers take to improve patient outcomes while minimizing unintended consequences of antibiotic use, such as drug toxicity and the development of AMR. The American Veterinary Medical Association has outlined five core concepts of AS in veterinary medicine.1 The AVMA has charged veterinarians, in service to our patients the community, to evaluate our antibiotic use practices and commit to use antibiotics judiciously.
In human outpatient practice, it is estimated that at least 30% of antibiotic prescriptions are unnecessary.2 It has been postulated that inappropriate and over-prescribing in small animal medicine is at least as prevalent.3 In fact, one publication reports that 40% of dogs receiving an antibiotic prescription in a single hospital had no clinical evidence of infection.4 Often too veterinarians empirically prescribed antibiotics with a broader than needed antimicrobial spectrum or those of critical importance to human medicine. This means that there is much low hanging fruit and easy opportunities to take small steps towards AS in our practices.
The need for enhanced antibiotic stewardship efforts in small animal medicine is clear to those of us who treat dogs and cats. The question for many is how? This webinar will provide an overview of AMR and AS in companion animals. It will offer simple steps and accessible tools so that every veterinary practice can start small with AS and make meaning change.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: 2026 AAVLD Annual Meeting Davis Thompson Foundation Pre-Meeting Workshop: Molecular Diagnostics for Pathologists
courses.description: Join us for the 2026 AAVLD-Davis Thompson Foundation Pre-Meeting Workshop where we will help you navigate the development, interpretation, strengths, and limitations of modern molecular tests. Our esteemed speakers are ready to guide you through a colorful array of fluorescent and stained slides, illuminate the dark shadows of next generation sequencing, and even help you reach peak amplification of your PCR expertise.

courses.title: Hyperbilirubinemia
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary professionals will provide an overview of the pathophysiology of hyperbilirubinemia and how to apply these to a diagnostic work-up for hyperbilirubinemic patients.
(This course was previously presented live in 2025 and was RACE-approved # 20-128-5031.)

courses.title: Anesthetic Plans: A Practical Approach
courses.description: The lecture is 1 hour and focuses on how to design anesthesia protocols for everyday patients. The lecture covers everything from patient preparation to drug selection and maintenance.

courses.title: Challenges and Updates in Equine Arthroscopic Surgery - On-Demand
courses.description: This seminar covers innovative arthroscopy and bursoscopy techniques in equine joint disease. Difficult cases are presented with discussion on fracture repair, condylar cysts, and navicular disease.

courses.provider: ASSOCIATION OF REPTILE AND AMPHIBIAN VETERINARIANS (ARAV)
courses.title: HerpVet
courses.description: HerpVet is a week-long intensive course geared to providing new exotic animal practitioners with essential knowledge and practical skills in amphibian and reptile medicine.

courses.title: WSAVA Scientific Programme 2024
courses.description: WSAVA World Congress 2024 will feature its trademark high quality, evidence-based lectures on clinical and non-clinical topics delivered by global experts. Given growing demand for knowledge on dermatology and oncology in Asia, these topics will feature in dedicated streams, while the program also includes a range of lectures on dentistry, diagnostics, cardiology, internal medicine, nutrition and surgery.

courses.title: 2026 Wildlife Care Conference
courses.description: This virtual conference is geared toward wildlife rehabilitators, veterinary professionals, keepers, wildlife educators, and anyone interested in a professional career working with wildlife. There will be broadly applicable medical topics such as triaging patients, wound management, fracture stabilization, wildlife diseases, along with talks directed at specific species groups. Talks will cover a variety of avian, mammal, and herptile species.

courses.title: Infection in Large Animal Fracture-On Demand
courses.description: 90 minute webinar reviewing the implications, treatment options, and clinical decision making of infection in large animal orthopedic surgery. Discussion will focus on the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of infection in large animal orthopedic patients with internal fixation for fracture repair or arthrodesis.

courses.title: Stallion Frozen Semen
courses.description: Lectures will include the advantages and disadvantages of frozen semen, principles of cryopreservation, importance of a test freeze, laboratory equipment and supplies required to freeze semen, detailed instructions on how to process and freeze semen, how to evaluate the quality of a frozen semen sample, methods to store and transport frozen semen, optimal management strategies for mares being bred with frozen semen and procedures for insemination of mares with frozen semen. In addition, a video overview of the entire process from initial evaluation of a stallion semen sample through the freezing and storage process is provided. An appendix of videos describing important background techniques such as how to determine sperm concentration using a hemacytometer and a NucleoCounter, how to centrifuge stallion semen and safety procedures when working with liquid nitrogen are also provided. Finally, a series of charts, worksheets, how-to guides, data logs and protocols are included in the course material. There is no prerequisite for this course.

courses.title: Communication Skills of Offering Partnership, Pausing, and Unconditional Positive Regard in Veterinary Practice.
courses.description: This continuing education course teaches three advanced relationship centered communication skills for veterinary professionals offering partnership, strategic pausing, and unconditional positive regard. Participants will learn how to use partnership language to reduce (doctor vs. client) dynamics, use pauses intentionally to improve listening and decision quality, and communicate respect and nonjudgment even during challenging interactions. The course emphasizes practical exam room scripts and repeatable workflows for emotionally charged situations, differing client preferences, and treatment plan resistance. By applying these tools consistently, veterinary teams can improve trust, reduce conflict, increase client adherence, and create calmer, more collaborative consultations.

courses.title: Communication Skills of Signposting, Ask-Tell-Ask, and Asking Permission in Veterinary Consultations.
courses.description: This continuing education course teaches three high-impact communication tools that improve clarity, collaboration, and client confidence in veterinary care: signposting, Ask-Tell-Ask, and asking permission. Participants will learn how to map the consultation, so clients know what to expect, assess baseline understanding before providing information, and invite consent before sensitive questions, physical exam steps, diagnostics, and treatment discussions. The course focuses on practical language and exam-room workflows that reduce confusion, improve information retention, and strengthen shared decision-making. These tools help veterinary teams communicate more efficiently while preserving trust, dignity, and partnership with clients.

courses.title: Decade One Meeting Five
courses.description: This course is a small business primer covering topics including inventory management, HR- hiring, firing, disability and pregancy laws, employment manuals, OSHA requirements, and DEA criteria.

courses.title: The Oral Examination and Common Oral Pathology
courses.description: Being able to identify oral pathology and anomalies is essential. A thorough dental examination includes a conscious and an anesthetized examination to identify pathology and anomalies and to aid in developing treatment plans. This presentation will discuss the most commonly found pathology in the oral cavities of canines and felines.

courses.title: TPLO WebInHour Series
courses.description: During this four-part webinar series, attendees will review all stages of the TPLO procedure, from pre-op planning to managing complications should they arise.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: VETERINARY MEDICAL RECORDS (1078-37545)
courses.description:
The oft-repeated adage among healthcare professionals "if you didn't document it, you didn't do it," creates an unfortunate perception that the only reason to maintain good medical records is to stay out of trouble. In this course, you will learn how to create a legally defensible medical record in order to improve patient care and enjoy benefits the extend far beyond preventing a license discipline or malpractice action.
If you are looking for additional medial records training we also offer the following related CE topics: 10 Top Medical Record-Keeping Deficiencies; Client Consent & Communication; Medical Record-Keeping-Beyond the SOAP; Medical Record-Keeping for Controlled Substances and Prescribing Medications; and Medical Record-Keeping to Meet the Standard of Care. All of these additional offerings will on build this foundational course.

courses.title: Radiological Identification of the Challenging Total Hip Replacement On-Demand
courses.description: Critical radiological preview of the total hip replacement candidate is essential in order to determine the practicality of THR, and plan modifications to standard surgical technique. While templating for implant size and type is an important element of this preview, the philosophy of the use of templating to initiate rehearsal of surgery will be presented with clinical examples. The advantage of CT based 3-D modeling in specific cases will also be discussed.

courses.title: Emergency Ophthalmology
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will review ophthalmic emergencies, including triage and presentation, patient history, exam, and ocular diagnostics. In addition, specific disease processes including ulcers, glaucoma, uveitis, and others will be presented.

courses.provider: KARL STORZ VETERINARY ENDOSCOPY - AMERICA LTD
courses.title: DIAGNOSTIC ENDOSCOPY: AN IMMERSIVE GUIDE (online course)
courses.description: The KARL STORZ Veterinary Endoscopy DIAGNOSTIC ENDOSCOPY - AN IMMERSIVE GUIDE online course provides in-depth online training in small animal internal medicine endoscopy. This course consists of an online only course (20 CE Hours). This course provides in-depth online training in flexible and rigid scope anatomy, handling and cleaning; laser physics, handling and safety; intracorporal laser lithotripsy; cystoscopy, rhinoscopy, bronchoscopy, upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy, laparoscopy and associated advanced procedures. Information covered includes equipment required, case selection and anesthetic considerations, procedural techniques, tips & tricks, and complications.

courses.title: Critical Checkpoints in Planning and Performing Pastern Arthrodesis - On Demand
courses.description: This presentation outlines the critical checkpoints in the planning and surgical execution of proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint arthrodesis in horses. Emphasis is placed on meticulous joint preparation, precise implant positioning, and biomechanical principles required to achieve optimal compression and stability. Practical surgical tips, including plate contouring, screw orientation, and intraoperative strategies to improve accuracy and efficiency, will be discussed to enhance clinical outcomes and postoperative comfort.

courses.title: Enhancing Recovery: Advancements in Rehabilitation for the Equine Surgeon On-Demand
courses.description: This webinar will explore the latest advancements and techniques in equine rehabilitation that are relevant to equine surgeons, aimed at enhancing outcomes for equine athletes. Topics will include strategies for recovery following laparotomy and laparoscopy, targeted treatments for neurologic conditions and post-cervical vertebral fusion, and cutting-edge approaches to improving outcomes in musculoskeletal disease.

courses.title: Oncologic Emergencies: What To Do When Cancer Bites Back
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinarians and veterinary technicians will provide an overview of systemic complications seen in the cancer patient, with a specific focus on emergent illness. This program will highlight practical examples for veterinary practitioners to provide strategies to aid in effective initial triage, patient assessment, and appropriate stabilization, while facilitating a final cancer diagnosis. In addition, this course will review common cancer therapeutic complications and how the primary care team can help in patient care and treatment monitoring, with the goal of improving overall quality of life.
(This course was previously presented live on March 20, 2025 and was RACE-approved # 20-1281339.)

courses.title: Recognizing and Managing Feline Acromegaly as a cause of Insulin Resistant Feline Diabetes
courses.description: Feline diabetes mellitus (DM) is estimated to impact approximately 1 out of 4 diabetic cats in North America. However, achieving treatment success appears challenging in a number of diabetic cats. Managing diabetic cats is not always straightforward. For many of these more difficult cases, what had been found is that the diabetes' etopathogenesis is not necessarily type 2, but a classification of an underlying disease process referred to as "other specific types of diabetes." One such type of "other diabetes" is hypersomatotropism, which results in acromegaly. Feline acromegaly is characterized by excessive growth hormone secretion leading to a wide array of clinical signs caused by the hormone's effects on multiple organ systems. Utilizing a case-based approach, this presentation will review the etiology/pathophysiology, history and clinical signs, diagnosis and medical and nutritional management of insulin resistant diabetes resulting from feline acromegaly.

courses.title: Internal Medicine in Real Life: Practical Strategies for Your Toughest Chronic Cases
courses.description:
Internal Medicine in Real Life: Practical Strategies for Your Toughest Chronic Cases
This three-part CE series is designed for general practitioners who want practical, confidence-building approaches to liver disease, hyperadrenocorticism, and chronic kidney disease. Across three interactive 2-hour sessions, you'll learn how to diagnose these conditions efficiently, avoid common mistakes, and implement treatment strategies that actually move the needle for your patients. Each session blends evidence-based guidelines with real-world tips, case examples, and communication strategies you can put to use the next day in practice.
Session 1 - Demystifying Liver Disease in Dogs and Cats
Confused about feline cholangiohepatitis? Unsure how aggressively to pursue diagnostics in the icteric cat? Curious how to apply ACVIM guidelines to canine chronic hepatitis? This session breaks down the most common hepatopathies you see in practice - clearly, simply, and practically. Learn streamlined diagnostic pathways, treatment strategies that make a difference, and case-based pearls that demystify these often frustrating conditions.
Session 2 - Is This Cushing's and Do I Care?
Cushing's is one of the most confusing and sometimes frustrating diseases in veterinary medicine. This session gives you a practical, evidence-based roadmap for when to test, how to test, and - most importantly - when to treat. We'll tackle the gray areas, the unexpected complications, the borderline test results, and the realistic conversations you need to have with clients to keep expectations aligned with outcomes.
Session 3 - Chronic Kidney Disease: Moving the Needle
CKD is one of the most common - and manageable - conditions in older cats and dogs. This session focuses on early recognition, IRIS-guided treatment, and practical strategies that improve longevity and quality of life. Learn how to identify progression earlier, manage complications proactively, and use nutritional therapy as a powerful tool in s

courses.title: Masterclass: Intra-articular Approaches to OA Management in Dogs
courses.description:
Canine osteoarthritis (OA) is a complex, whole-body disease - and intra-articular therapies offer a way to directly target joint disease and pain. This practical, evidence-based course taught by Dr. Joao Alves, DVM, MSc, PhD, gives veterinary professionals the skills to understand OA pathology, select the right cases, and confidently, safely, and effectively integrate joint-specific treatments as part of a multimodal management plan.
Attendees will gain a practical understanding of osteoarthritis pathogeneis and where intra-articular interventions can influence disease and clinical signs. Through real clinical cases, veterinary professionals will learn how to select the right candidates, how to choose the most appropriate intra-articular options through evidence-based decision making, and integrate intra-articular treatments in personalized long-term rehabilitation plans. The course also covers navigating challenging joints, recognizing treatment response, and adjusting plans based on outcomes.

courses.title: Articular Fracture Management: Optimization of Results and Novel Treatment Options On-Demand
courses.description: Articular fractures occur commonly in dogs and cats. The goal of treatment is to allow a return to pain-free motion and ameliorate the inevitable development of osteoarthritis. Adherence to certain principles is critical in giving the patient the greatest opportunity of maintaining a healthy joint. Principles of treatment include obtaining an accurate diagnosis, early treatment, achieving anatomical reduction, providing rigid fixation, restoring the functional axis of the limb, and appropriate use of postoperative physical rehabilitation. During this seminar, the speakers explore these principles and the underlying evidence base and provide guidance for their application. Unfortunately, despite adherence to such principles, high morbidity remains commonly associated with articular fracture treatment, particularly with pathologic articular fractures where an incomplete understanding of the associated pathogenesis likely contributes to suboptimal results. Later talks in this seminar explore specific mechanisms of dealing with such pathologic fractures and explore when minimally invasive techniques, including fracturoscopy, may become applicable. In the final lecture, speakers consider when total joint replacement may be considered for articular fracture management, the challenges associated with this, and how the technique can be adapted to optimize outcomes.

courses.title: It Takes a Team: Evidence-based Communication Tools for the Veterinary Team
courses.description: Delivery of quality healthcare requires highly skilled teams that can remain effective in the complex, unpredictable environment that is the modern veterinary practice. Drawing on the evidence-based TeamSTEPPS system developed for human health care, this session will introduce the VetTEAMS framework, a series of team competencies and simple communication tools that can be integrated into your practice to reduce medical errors, and improve team performance, and enhance staff satisfaction. Delivery of high quality veterinary care requires extraordinary team work. Learn how you can help your team reach the next level of efficiency, quality, and safety.

courses.title: Laryngeal tie-forward: Tips and Tricks - On-Demand
courses.description: This presentation will focus on the pertinent surgical anatomy and technique for performing a laryngeal tie-forward. Intra-operative and post-operative complications and management strategies will also be discussed.

courses.title: Canine Total Hip Replacement: Patient Selection and Evaluation, Hip Dysplasia, plus Other Rule Outs to Consider
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will review basic aspects of practical and efficient orthopedic plus neurologic patient evaluation for total hip replacement. In addition, this course will review the most common disease rule outs that might preclude a total hip replacement procedure, plus ancillary therapies if it is contraindicated. This course was previously RACE-approved program # 20-1323067.

courses.title: Small Animal Keynote Lecture: Defining Success in Veterinary Surgery On-Demand
courses.description: Are you a SUCCESS story in veterinary surgery? Yes. Is it possible to be even more successful? How are we doing compared to our peers? Are we the sole determinant of our success, or do we need help from others? A surgeon has many duties and achievements long before picking up a scalpel. This keynote lecture discusses attaining success, failure that can lead to success, and some challenges we meet to reach goals. We can continue to be even more successful in our specialty for self-satisfaction, for the well-being of animals, and for animal owners happiness.

courses.title: Feline Liver Diseases: A Simplified Clinical Approach
courses.description: This one hour lecture discusses common feline liver diseases (hepatic lipidosis, cholangitis, and neoplasia) as well as their subtypes. Differentiation using biochemistry and CB results, ultrasound, aspirates and biopsies will be discussed, as well the treatment options for these conditions. An emphasis will be placed on practical, in clinic tests and treatments.

courses.title: Decision-making for TPLO with InternalBrace(TM) Ligament Augmentation
courses.description: During this webinar, faculty review the biomechanics and literature behind the InternalBrace(TM) Ligament Augmentation technique for instability post-TPLO, indications for its application, and surgical technique.

courses.title: 28947 - ONE-DAY BAT REHABILITATION BASICS WORKSHOP (1131-35646)
courses.description: In this class, rehabilitatorparticipantss learn the basic skills that are essential to successfully rehabilitating orphaned and injured bats and returning them to their natural habitat. The class format is a combination of lecture, discussion, and hands-on activities designed to provide students with key information and experience.

courses.title: The Allergic Cat Course
courses.description: The Allergic Cat Course is an 8-hour, self-paced online course designed to empower, engage, and enlighten the general practitioner in the recognition, diagnosis, and management of feline allergic skin and ear disease. Comprised of five structured modules, this course offers in-depth instruction on disease pathogenesis, diagnostic workflows, therapeutic strategies, and case-based application, all with a focus on Feline Atopic Skin Syndrome (FASS). Updates to terminology, clinical standards, and treatment recommendations are thoroughly reviewed. Designed as a comprehensive and accessible non-interactive learning experience, this course equips practitioners with the knowledge and tools to manage feline allergy cases in general practice confidently.

courses.title: Joints, Implants, Infections: Orthopedic Infections,Responsible Antimicrobial Use in Livestock, Equine, and Small Animal
courses.description: This seminar brings together experts in farm animal, equine, and small animal orthopedics to explore the prevention, diagnosis, and management of orthopedic infections across veterinary species. Special emphasis is placed on evidence-based clinical decision-making, with speakers providing practical and scientific insights into antimicrobial stewardship, regulations, antimicrobial alternatives, and guidelines for cases without definitive microbial data. While each speaker addresses species-specific challenges during their individual lectures, the panel concludes with a discussion on the shared role of veterinary orthopedic surgeons in advancing responsible antimicrobial use while optimizing patient outcomes.

courses.title: Introduction to Brachycephalic Obstructive Airway Syndrome
courses.description: A brief overview of the clinical presentation, diagnosis, and treatment of laryngeal airway problems in dogs diagnosed with BOAS. The focus will be on practical and newer techniques for the rhinoplasty, palatoplasty comparing the cut-and-sew, use of a vessel sealing device, and bipolar amputation

courses.title: Dermpath 101: Demystify Dermpath (recorded version of 20-1279131)
courses.description: This course covers the basics of how to master dermatopathology vocabulary and confidently approach complex cases. We will build diagnostic skills with guided pattern recognition techniques. We will also learn the difference between primary and secondary skin lesions and when, where, and how best to biopsy them. Additionally, this knowledge will include application to real-world cases for better patient outcomes.

courses.title: Anesthesia Monitoring: The Basics
courses.description: A basic introduction into anesthesia monitoring with multiparameter monitors including: heart rate, pulse oximetry, blood pressure, ecg, and capnography.

courses.title: THRIVE: mental health, relationship management and career development
courses.description: This 7-day continuing education focused on mental health and professional development. Delegates will be resident for 7 days at a 5* safari lodge in the Victoria Falls National Park, Zimbabwe, Africa. Here you can be immersed in nature with the goal of stepping out of your normal environment and developing new mental health, self-awareness, and relationship skills that will benefit career satisfaction, growth, and longevity. This course mixes retreat-style relaxation and safari experiences, with immersive and interactive teaching. The course runs with a maximum of 16 people at a time, for an exclusive and tailored experience. What you will learn: - The Enneagram: typing your personality, understanding opposite personalities, and how to use this to develop team relationships - Conflict management and embracing differences - Intruder syndrome and how to combat it - Self-awareness. how to combat stress - Burnout: why it happens and how to prevent it - Self-forgiveness: Techniques to prevent self-blame and utilise perceived failure to develop your career - Emotional IQ ACCOMMODATION Delegates will enjoy their own luxury lodge room with king-size bed (shared rooms can be accommodated) with cool luxurious white linen, large sweeping mosquito nets, warm evening lighting and safari chic design. Rooms are ensuite with showers as well as outdoor showers to enjoy the African night sky. Each room has its own private deck overlooking the river. LOCATION The lodge is set in the Victoria Falls National Park, a big 5 wildlife area. You can expect to be serenaded with calls of the wild at breakfast and supper, elephants trumpeting and lions roaring into the night. In the evening, you can enjoy sunsets igniting the horizon and then kicking back around the fire, under a sky of stars.

courses.title: Radiology
courses.description: This interactive session will focus on the identification and interpretation of common thoracic and abdominal radiographic abnormalities through a case-based approach. Attendees will engage in the systematic review of representative cases, gaining practical insights into key disease processes and radiographic patterns.

courses.title: Integrative Neuromodulation: Basic Skills in Dry Needling and Photomedicine
courses.description: This immersive 3-day program covers the scientific foundations and clinical applications of dry needling and photomedicine for small animal patients. Through lectures, demonstrations, hands-on laboratories, clay modeling, palpation practice, movement assessment, neurologic localization exercises, and case-based discussions, participants will build practical skills for evaluating and supporting musculoskeletal, neurologic, chronic pain, and geriatric patients.

courses.title: Self-Compassion for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description:
This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will focus on self-compassion. We are often our own worst critics, especially when we are passionate about our work. This can negatively impact our mood, mental health, and work performance. This program will provide tools and techniques to practice to protect our wellbeing, plus the reasoning behind why these methods work.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1242038.)

courses.title: CPR Clinical Guidelines: RECOVER & BEYOND
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary professionals will provide a CPR didactic review of the rationale behind and logistics of delivering hands-on psychomotor skills imperative to CPR readiness. This course is designed to both introduce these skills to novice providers and to serve as a review for more experienced doctors/staff to prevent the decay in CPR knowledge/skills. The CPR course includes three modules: Introduction, Basic Life Support-BLS and Advanced Life Support-ALS. Modules focus on the necessary cognitive skills required to provide high-quality CPR as outlined in the current RECOVER CPR guidelines for BLS and ALS.
(This course was previously presented live in 2025 and was RACE-approved # 20-911755.)

courses.title: Advancements in Orthobiologics: New Techniques and New Evidence On-Demand
courses.description: Join us for an engaging webinar exploring the latest advancements in orthobiologic therapy. This webinar covers cutting-edge innovations, clinical applications, and research insights into regenerative treatments for musculoskeletal conditions. Whether you're a healthcare professional or researcher, gain valuable knowledge to enhance patient care and drive the future of orthobiologics.

courses.title: 13th Annual Veterinary Business Symposium
courses.description: PSIvet's two-day, in-person veterinary business symposium designed to educate veterinarians and veterinary staff to more effectively manage several aspects of the business of veterinary medicine, led by leading national experts and educators, for improved financial, business, and clinical outcomes of independent veterinary practices.
courses.location: Hyatt Regency St. Louis at The Arch

courses.title: Caring for Exotic Species in Hospital: Part 1
courses.description: This lecture, delivered by Dr Sonya Miles BVSc CertAVP(ZM) CertAqV MRCVS, introduces the specialised environmental, behavioural, and physiological considerations involved in hospitalising exotic species. Focusing on exotic mammals and birds, the session outlines how to create appropriate inpatient environments, manage stress, ensure biosecurity, and safely house species with unique needs. Delegates will learn how to configure species-specific housing (including vivaria, avian enclosures, and mammal kennels), recognise essential environmental parameters, and integrate Vetario incubators into routine care to support temperature regulation, humidity control, and oxygen supplementation. Through practical examples and real-world clinical experience, this lecture equips clinicians with the foundational skills needed to deliver safe, consistent, and welfare-focused hospital care to exotic patients.

courses.title: Surgical Management of Chylothorax - On Demand
courses.description: The presentation will discuss the latest concepts in surgical management of canine and feline chylothorax with a focus on the important practical aspects of intraoperative decision-making and the latest data on outcomes.

courses.title: Improving the Euthanasia Experience; Medical Offerings
courses.description: This series explores the veterinary professional's experience with euthanasia, offering ways to avoid common mistakes and bringing improved methodology to light. This series will combat the dreaded compassion fatigue and burnout by showcasing compassionate measures that can be taken efficiently and with the care of the pet, pet owner and veterinary staff in mind. A special focus is taken to cover the soft skills that Euthanasia requires, but veterinarians often lack training in. Resources for both the veterinary staff members and pet owners will be provided.

courses.title: The FAS Scale and PreVisit Pharmaceuticals
courses.description: This presentation describes the FAS (Fear, Anxiety, Stress) scale and its use during veterinary visits. We also discuss the phenotypes of stress (fight, flight, freeze, faint, fidget) and how these are used to help tailor medication choices. Classes of PVP medications are covered and some detail provided on the mechanism of action and use for each class as well as common side effects. These include SARIs, alpha-2 agonists, gabamimetics, and benzodiazepines among others. Guidelines are discussed to help attendees choose specific medications within each class for certain patients.

courses.title: How Platelet Rich Plasma Works in Osteoarthritis
courses.description: This course will begin by explaining WHAT is Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP). It will cover HOW PRP is made. It will cover different TYPES of PRP. And it will highlight WHAT PRP actually does to address osteoarthritis.

courses.title: Dermatology Secrets with Dr. Joya Griffin
courses.description:
You went to vet school to help animals. But somewhere between the pruritic dogs and the mystery skin masses, dermatology started feeling like a subject you were just getting through rather than actually mastering.
Dr. Joya Griffin gets it and she is here to change that.
A board-certified veterinary dermatologist with a genuine passion for teaching, Dr. Griffin has designed this three-part series specifically for the veterinarian who wants to feel more confident walking into skin cases, not just survive them. In three focused 30-minute sessions, she shares the clinical knowledge, practical frameworks, and real-world perspective that took her years to develop -- and delivers it in a way that is warm, clear, and immediately useful.
This is the kind of CE that actually makes your next appointment better.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Neurology Part 2: Key Spinal Column Conditions
courses.description: This course explores the diagnosis and management of common neurologic and spinal diseases in small animals, including intervertebral disc disease, fibrocartilaginous embolism, atlantoaxial subluxation, and feline aortic thromboembolism. Participants learn practical approaches to diagnostic imaging, surgical interventions, and medical management, with a focus on improving patient outcomes.

courses.title: Advances in Wound Healing On-Demand
courses.description: Speakers present current treatment options for minimizing morbidity and mortality associated with difficult wounds. The seminar focuses on discussion of innovative techniques being utilized to optimize wound healing including various surgical techniques, topical medications, and negative pressure wound therapy.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: Client Consent and Communications
courses.description: Communication is critical to ensuring valid client consent. It is more than a form, and is rather a shared decision-making process between the veterinarian and the client. Learn how veterinarians can enhance their ability to communicate with clients to determine the best course of action for their animals while respecting the veterinarian-client-patient relationship and the human animal bond.

courses.title: Advanced Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Wet Lab
courses.description: This two-day course will discuss advanced oral and maxillofacial surgeries, with an emphasis on use of maxillofacial miniplates for repair of mandibular and maxillary fractures. Utilizing a mixture of lecture and wet lab, the event will provide 12 hours of education provided by a fellow of the AVDC Oral and Maxillofacial Fellowship. Participants will leave with an understanding of techniques and equipment needed for application of miniplates in dogs and cats.

courses.title: Switchback Vet Clinic Essentials: Core Principles for Transforming Clinic Culture
courses.description: Discover the tools and strategies to reshape your clinics culture and build a resilient cohesive team Switchback Vet Clinic Essentials: Core Principles for Transforming Clinic Culture introduces veterinary professionals to the foundational concepts of the Switchback Vet Framework emphasizing neuroplasticity team dynamics and sustainable leadership This six module course equips you to identify and address the root causes of burnout compassion fatigue and team dysfunction while fostering a front-brain success-driven mindset Learn how to harness the power of collective growth improve communication and create a clinic environment where staff and clients thrive With practical insights tailored to veterinary practice this course is your gateway to a transformative leadership journey setting the stage for long-term personal team and organizational success

courses.title: The RECOVER 2024 CPR Guidelines: Basic and Advanced Life Support
courses.description: When patients experience cardiopulmonary arrest (CPA), seconds count. A well-trained and prepared veterinary health care team can mean the difference between life and death when a patient experiences CPA. This lecture will explain key concepts from the newly updated RECOVER 2024 evidence evaluation process in the domains of Basic and Advanced Life Support, including the evidence-based approach to providing optimal chest compressions and ventilation in dogs and cats, as well as monitoring, drug and defi brillation therapy.

courses.title: Lymphatic Massage - The Common Denominator
courses.description: In addition to mastering the fundamental massage techniques, every canine massage therapist and veterinary rehabilitation specialist should understand how to effectively use lymphatic massage protocols as they are an essential skill that can benefit dogs in any situation. In this advanced workshop, participants learn specific lymphatic massage techniques that can be used after deep tissue work to help clear metabolic wastes from the body; after surgery or injury to reduce swelling; and during palliative and hospice care to help sick and convalescing dogs by boosting the immune system and clearing out toxins, which when accumulated can cause nausea, fatigue, and pain. These techniques are gentle, nuanced, and effective, and the relaxation effects are profound. Lymphatic massage can truly be used in just about every situation and in every session with a dog, making it the common denominator in canine massage.

courses.title: Canine Leptospirosis: Current Insights and Practical Approaches for Veterinarians
courses.description: In this 60-minute presentation, we will provide an in-depth overview of canine leptospirosis, focusing on recent advancements in its pathophysiology, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. We will begin with an update on the bacterial strains involved, their modes of infection, and immune responses, followed by a discussion of the wide-ranging clinical manifestations of the disease. The second half will cover diagnostic innovations, including new testing methodologies, as well as the latest treatment protocols for managing leptospirosis, including antimicrobial therapy, supportive care, and handling complications and knowing when to refer. The presentation will conclude with an update on prevention strategies, including vaccination, biosecurity measures, and emerging public health concerns.

courses.title: Symposium on Therapeutic Advances in Animal Rehabilitation (STAAR)
courses.description: STAAR Conference for veterinarians and animal rehabilitation professionals aims to bring to you the most advanced courses in rehabilitation, sports medicine, and fitness taught by industry leaders and pioneers. Wetlabs are intensive and designed for the serious veterinary practitioner. Our unique method of education focuses on hands-on, practical experience using live canines. Wetlabs include live dogs (approximately 1 animal for every 3-4 participants) so that learned skills and techniques can be directly and immediately implemented into practice. Classes are intimate, informal, and small to maximize learning (maximum 20 participants/class). STAAR provides education that cannot be found at national or specialist conferences because of its integration of the many sub-professions involved in veterinary rehabilitation, sports medicine, and fitness and the focus on specific and sometimes difficult topics.

courses.title: The Drug Deal: Mirtazapine
courses.description: The Drug Deal: Mirtazapine is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Brachycephalics: The Nose is Just the Tip (of the Iceberg)
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program will review the anatomy of brachycephalic breeds and the associated disease processes and surgical options available. (This course was previously presented live and was RACE-approved # 20-1108336.)

courses.title: Unconventional Arthroscopies On-Demand
courses.description: This three presentation webinar series will consist of case based discussions highlighting tricks and tips for using effectively in areas where arthroscopy is not commonly utilized including: assessment of the tarsus for treatment of OCD lesions and as part of the decision making for ankle replacement; to guide fracture reduction in the elbow and carpal joints; and to assess the hip as part of the decision making process prior to performing pelvic osteotomy surgery.

courses.title: Improving Dairy Calf Performance from Birth to Lactation
courses.description:
Development of dairy calves presents unique challenges compared to beef calves. This presentation will present and review common management methods of reducing morbidity and mortality in calf rearing operations.
Understanding the impact gastrointestinal development and immune development during the neonatal period and its effect on performance throughout the animals life.
Understanding the importance and process of rumen development. While beef calves typically receive milk from the dam for the first 6 to 8 months of life, most dairy calves have 6 to 8 weeks for sufficient development to allow continued growth and development without a liquid diet.. In addition, the rumen is a dynamic organ continually changing based upon the calfs diet. Proper acclimation is important for optimum performance.
Understanding the role of Megasphaera elsdenii, as an aid in rumen development and rumen function.
Understanding the importance of trace minerals in supporting the immune system. This includes the function of trace minerals in innate immunity as well as in the adaptive immune system and response to vaccine.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: V.I.P. Veterinary Introductory Pathology- A System-Based Review
courses.description: This monthly webinar series will present a systems-based introduction to veterinary histopathology. Each month, a different body system (Integument, Urinary, Reproductive, Cardiovascular, Endocrine, Pulmonary, Musculoskeletal, Digestive, Hemolymphatic, Nervous, and Special Senses [Eye and Ear]) will be introduced in a way that participants of any level of experience (veterinary students, interns, residents and/or anatomic pathologists) will be able to comprehend and further expand their knowledge of veterinary pathology. Each webinar will introduce the normal tissue architecture, histological features of each anatomic structure and highlight the response to injury of different tissues and cell types found within each system. Cumulatively, by the end of the series, participants will have learned about the embryologic development, structure, function, and response to injury of twelve body systems - As well as received an introduction to some species specific variations of different systemic components. Additionally, these webinars will introduce unique patterns and types of injury that are seen in certain organ systems (such as patterns of pneumonia and zonal patterns of hepatocyte injury). Presentations will give a comprehensive introduction that illus

courses.title: Decade One Meeting Three
courses.description: This course covers professional social and emotional skills topics including leadership, emotional intelligence, work-life balance, boundaries, and recognizing and coping with emotional blackmail.

courses.title: Reptile Nutrition
courses.description: This presentation is a thorough review of reptile nutrition, including information on carnivores, omnivores, and herbivores. It will include limitations of commercially available invertebrate prey and how to improve their nutritional status through gut-loading and powder supplementation for commonly kept insectivores. Herbivore feeding strategies will be reviewed, including the nutritional content of common store-bought greens and correlating this to the natural feeding strategies of commonly kept herbivores. Different methods of water provision will be reviewed. This presentation will include a thorough literature review of the last 5 years.

courses.title: (On Demand) Updates on the Diagnosis and Management of Equine Endocrinology Cases
courses.description: In this on demand webinar, participants will gain valuable insights into the latest updates and advancements relevant to the diagnosis and management of PPID, Insulin Dysregulation (ID), and Laminitis. Led by globally recognized experts at the forefront of research and clinical applications, these lectures and Q&A sessions are tailored to provide Veterinarians and Horse owners with the most current, practical, and actionable insights.

courses.title: Decade One 2.0 Year One
courses.description:
Year One focuses on building a professional brand and developing financial literacy for equine veterinarians. Topics include Mission, Vision, and Values, Marketing & Branding, Financial Foundations, Practice Performance Evaluation, Fraud & Embezzlement Prevention, and Revenue Capture & Pricing Strategies.
This course is delivered through a combination of interactive live Zoom meetings and on-demand virtual content, spread over the course of a year in monthly installments. Pre-recorded materials are accessed through the ThriveCart platform, with enrollment granted upon payment of an annual membership fee.

courses.title: Small Animal Wound Management
courses.description: This course covers management of wounds in dogs and cats: initial stabilization, wound assessment and debridement, decision-making in wound closure (including definitive debridement and primary closure, open wound management, and second intention healing), bandaging, and key points for closure and use of drains.

courses.title: Conjunctivitis to Crisis: A Stepwise Approach to the Red-Eyed Patient
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) program is a recording of a live virtual webinar. This medical program for veterinary professionals reviews the common ocular disease conditions that cause pet owners to report a red eye. This session includes a general overview of many common conditions plus focuses on the disease presentation, diagnostics, and treatments for ocular diseases.

courses.title: Top 10 Essential Things to Become a Better Stifle Surgeon
courses.description: This webinar will review the ten things faculty see as essential items to set yourself up as a better stifle surgeon. Additionally, faculty will provide examples of their application and explain how these things can make you more efficient.

courses.title: Canine Top Emergency Room Presentations
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of emergency and critical care topics in veterinary medicine, focusing on practical approaches to managing respiratory distress, trauma, acute abdomen, toxicoses, seizures, and other urgent conditions. Participants gain actionable knowledge and clinical techniques to address these conditions effectively in both general practice and emergency settings.

courses.title: ORAL PATHOLOGY / RADIOLOGY (622-42487)
courses.description: Interactive lectures covering the indications for oral radiography and the proper technique in getting the images are covered in the morning session. In the afternoon participants will be actively taking radiographs on skull and cadaver specimens of both the cat and dog. In addition, interactive case studies are presented which cover the initial oral pathology seen on physical examination and the associated radiographic images and the diagnosis.

courses.title: Small Animal Clinical Pathology Part 4: Electrolytes and Blood Gas
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of clinical pathology and acid-base analysis in veterinary medicine. Participants learn to interpret blood gases, serum chemistries, and acid-base disturbances through real-world case studies. Key topics include metabolic and respiratory disorders, electrolyte imbalances, and advanced diagnostic techniques.

courses.title: Setting Up for Success: Exam Room Design, Professional Appearance, Medical Record Preparation, and the Exam Room Flow Model.
courses.description: This continuing education course teaches veterinary professionals how to optimize the clinical environment and personal preparation to improve communication, efficiency, and client confidence. Participants will learn practical strategies for exam room design, professional appearance/uniform standards, and pre-visit medical record review, then apply these foundations within a structured Exam Room Flow Model. The course emphasizes how preparation before entering the room influences trust, time management, case clarity, and the quality of clinical decisions. Learners will leave with a repeatable system that helps teams reduce preventable communication errors, improve consistency across appointments, and create a calmer, more effective client experience.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Neurology Part 1: Localize the lesion
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of neurological disorders in canine and feline patients, focusing on neurological exam techniques, lesion localization, and clinical reasoning. Topics include upper and lower motor neuron disorders, neuroanatomy, proprioceptive deficits, vestibular ataxia, and cranial nerve assessment. Participants gain practical skills for diagnosing and managing neurological conditions through detailed explanations and clinical case examples.

courses.title: Surgical Trauma and Traumatic Surgery On-Demand
courses.description: Naturally occurring trauma, as well as the trauma resulting from invasive surgical procedures, result in systemic responses that follow similar physiologic pathways and affect patient outcomes. In this context, surgical goals include not only correcting the original traumatic injury but also minimizing the "second hit" resulting from the applied surgical intervention. During this seminar, speakers discuss the pathophysiology of both naturally occurring and surgically inflicted trauma, and optimal timing of surgical intervention in trauma management. Case-based discussions present the current standards of trauma management, and the seminar culminates in a fast-paced morbidity and mortality rounds centered on surgical trauma.

courses.title: Skin Flaps in Small Animal Reconstructive Surgery: Head, Trunk, Extremities On-Demand
courses.description: Skin flaps remain as one of the most versatile methods to close problematic defects secondary to trauma and tumor resection. This webinar will discuss the clinical application of local flaps, axial pattern flaps, and compounds flaps in small animal surgery.

courses.provider: SIR JAMES DUNN ANIMAL WELFARE CENTRE, ATLANTIC VETERINARY COLLEGE, UNIVERSITY OF
courses.title: Sir James Dunn Animal Welfare Centre 2024 Webinar Series
courses.description: This webinar series will present participants with current knowledge about veterinary behavioural medicine with a focus on animal welfare. We will discuss how the early life environment and experiences affects canine behaviour, as well as how behavioural indicators can provide insight into neurobehavioral development in feline. New and exciting research in the area of veterinary behavioural medicine will also be included in the program, including highlights from the literature on the welfare of dogs and cats under our care. The focus of the program will be on the role of the veterinarian in helping to resolve welfare concerns in companion animals.

courses.title: OrthoLine(TM) System Overview
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Sean Murphy, DVM, DACVS-SA, provides an overview of the OrthoLine(TM) Fracture Management System, reviewing biomechanics, system features, and clinical cases.

courses.title: Situations That Challenge Us: Abuse, Neglect, and Limited Resources
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will review our legal and ethical obligations in instances of suspected cruelty, abuse, and neglect. This course will include related client communication strategies and reporting mandates, distinguish between neglect and lack of access to resources, and what to do with each type of challenging situation.

courses.title: Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency
courses.description: This lecture aims to provide referring veterinarians with an overview of canine and feline exocrine pancreatic insufficiency from pathophysiology through management and common comorbidities. Real-world case examples are provided.

courses.title: The Stifle Joint: Effective Evaluation
courses.description: In this one-hour webinar, Dr. Nina Kieves, DVM, DACVS-SA, DACVSMR, CCRT, discusses the pathophysiology of stifle joint disease in canines, early vs. late diagnosis, guidelines for treatment, and recovery expectations.

courses.title: Equine Facial Fractures On-Demand
courses.description: This webinar discusses diagnostics for equine head trauma and various methods and considerations for repairing equine facial fractures.

courses.title: Management of Post-Operative Cranial Cruciate Ligament Disease (CCLD)
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary professionals will review the basics of cranial cruciate ligament disease (CCLD). This program will focus on the diagnosis of cranial cruciate ligament rupture (CCLR), surgical and non-surgical treatment options, post-operative complications, and rehabilitation following CCLR surgery.
(This course was previously presented live in 2025 and was RACE-approved # 20-1299596.)

courses.title: 3D Modeling and Printing in Orthopedics On-Demand
courses.description: Why are surgeons so excited about 3D printing? Is it the next step in your career and practice? This webinar will span from the basics of 3D printing to cutting-edge developments in veterinary orthopedics. This includes information on what cases should be considered and how to get started with 3D guides, to applications in arthrodesis and joint replacement by leaders in the field.

courses.title: Symposium on Therapeutic Advances in Animal Rehabilitation (STAAR)
courses.description: STAAR Conference for veterinarians and animal rehabilitation professionals aims to bring to you the most advanced courses in rehabilitation, sports medicine, and fitness taught by industry leaders and pioneers. Wet labs are intensive and designed for the serious veterinary practitioner. Our unique method of education focuses on hands-on, practical experience using live equines. Wet labs include approximately 1 horse per every 3-4 participants so that learned skills and techniques can be directly and immediately implemented into practice. Classes are intimate, informal, and small to maximize learning (maximum 15 participants/class). STAAR brings its signature hands-on practical model to equine education and integrates many professions involved in comprehensive equine care.

courses.title: Airway Management using veterinary specific supra-glottic airway devices
courses.description: This presentation is designed to give delegates the facts about using veterinary specific supra glottic devices and when to use the correct airway devices in a clinical situation.

courses.title: Feline Liver Diseases: A Simplified Clinical Approach
courses.description: This one hour lecture discusses common feline liver diseases (hepatic lipidosis, cholangitis, and neoplasia) as well as their subtypes. Differentiation using biochemistry and CB results, ultrasound, aspirates and biopsies will be discussed, as well the treatment options for these conditions. An emphasis will be placed on practical, in clinic tests and treatments.

courses.title: Mastering Pelvic and Femur Traumatology
courses.description:
Participants will take a deep dive into complex trauma cases, including sacroiliac (SI) luxation, hip luxation, and complex fractures of the femur and pelvis. Refine techniques in fluoroscopy-guided procedures in the state-of-the-art ArthroLab, equipped with multiple C-arms to support and maximize hands-on learning in a realistic surgical environment.
Master percutaneous repairs using fluoroscopy: Optimize positioning and improve accuracy with guided pin placement to simplify approaches to SI injuries, capital physeal and femoral neck fractures. Reduce surgical time with real-time imaging strategies.
The wet labs will also cover:
- Surgical Hip arthroscopy and arthroscopic hip luxation stabilizations
- Minimally invasive hip joint exploration using Nanoneedle technology
- Open surgical approaches to master repairs using the newest canine-specific anatomical plates designed for pelvic and femur fractures, enhancing surgical precision and confidence.
As part of the immersive format, participants will engage in:
-Live surgical demonstrations
-Case-based discussions
-Collaborative problem-solving with peers and faculty
During interactive case presentation sessions, attendees are encouraged to bring their own cases to explore different scenarios and discover innovative solutions.

courses.title: Canine Respiratory Emergencies
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review recognition and stabilization of patients presenting in respiratory distress. This course will also include point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) diagnostics with a focus on lung ultrasound, plus diagnostic interpretation and interventional strategies for critically ill patients.

courses.title: Self-Compassion for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description:
This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will focus on self-compassion. We are often our own worst critics, especially when we are passionate about our work. This can negatively impact our mood, mental health, and work performance. This program will provide tools and techniques to practice to protect our wellbeing, plus the reasoning behind why these methods work.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1242038.)

courses.title: Small Animal Keynote Lecture: Optimizing Artificial Chordae Length and Annuloplasty Sizing for Enhanced Mitral Valve Repair
courses.description: In mitral valve repair, it is essential to determine the optimal length of the artificial chordae tendineae and the size of the annulus during surgery. In this lecture, we will discuss the methods of estimating the appropriate length of the chordae tendineae and the size of the annuloplasty using transesophageal echocardiography - the technique of chordal replacement and annuloplasty based on this measurement, and the resulting findings.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: Medical Records: Beyond the SOAP
courses.description: This one-hour continuing education program examines how veterinary medical records affect patient care, client communication, and legal risk in practice. Using case examples, the session focuses on practical documentation strategies for NSAIDs, compounded and extra-label drug use, referrals, consultations, and emerging issues such as AI in veterinary medicine. We will also include ethical considerations for both patient care and professional interactions.

courses.title: ECC Topics for the General Practitioner
courses.description:
ECC in veterinary medicine provides urgent and life-saving care for animals. This course will cover the following Emergency and Critical Care topics for the general practitioner:
Identifying shock and developing a fluid therapy plan
Fluid therapy is a mainstay of emergency and critical care. We need to know how to develop a fluid therapy plan when we reach for a bag of fluids or a blood product. In this lecture, we will talk about identifying shock in dogs and cats then how to tailor your fluid therapy plan to each patient. We will have examples of cases to work through as part of our discussion.
Emergency respiratory techniques and anesthesia considerations
We are often faced with patients that have respiratory compromise in practice, regardless of if the practice is small animal general practice or an ER. Because of that, we should have an awareness of the techniques available we can use to stabilize and treat patients when needed. Anesthesia options and complications will be discussed. Even if you are not doing the procedure, it is helpful to have awareness and talking points for clients if referral is warranted. We will cover nasal oxygen catheter placement, thoracocentesis, tracheostomy, and chest tube placement.
Interpreting ECGs in the ER
ECGs and their interpretation is commonplace in any small animal practice. In this lecture, we will review common ECG abnormalities in small animal emergency patients, using point of care testing to aid in diagnosis as well as treatment options for these situations. We will use case examples as a guide to developing a triage and stabilization plan for our canine and feline patients in the ER and ICU.
Gastric dilatation volvulus
Gastric dilatation volvulus is a life threatening disease that can affect any dog, but overrepresented in large or giant breed dogs. While you may not see many in a day
practice, you have an opportunity to treat if they do before referral. Our goal today is identification, stabilization, surgical opti

courses.title: Complications in Large Animal Surgery On-Demand
courses.description: This on-demand seminar focuses on surgical complications of large animal surgery.

courses.title: Whats New, Pussycat? An Update on Feline Heart Disease
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinarians and technicians will review newer issues in feline cardiology, including an update on phenotypic descriptions, available diagnostics, and treatments. This course was previously presented live and RACE-approved (#20-1099646) and this version will be accessible anytime online on medvet.com.

courses.provider: TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY OFFICE OF VETERINARY CONTINUING EDUCATION
courses.title: Veterinary Opioids: Texas Board Rules & Federal Laws Concerning Controlled Substances
courses.description: This online module is designed to equip the participant with a basic understanding of opioid abuse and controlled substance diversion, as well as inventory recordkeeping and security requirements. The course meets the 2 hours of opioid training requirements of the Texas Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners (TBVME). Federal regulations concerning labeling, use, compounding, recordkeeping, and security of prescription of controlled drugs are addressed.

courses.title: Clots! Bleeding! Coagulation! Oh my! Thromboembolic Disease and Its Management in the ER
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary professionals will review coagulation physiology, with a primary focus on hypercoagulability and thromboembolic disease. This program will highlight common presentations for thromboembolism in the emergent patient, diagnostic tools for the general practitioner, as well as the specialist when available, potential underlying etiologies, plus management strategies. In addition, the course will briefly review disseminated intravascular coagulation and its relationship to thromboembolic disease, as well as underlying causes (specifically neoplasia). (This course was previously presented live in 2025 and was RACE-approved # 20-1281338.)

courses.title: M2S 6 Hour Wellness Bundle
courses.description: This evidence-informed educational series provides veterinary professionals with a comprehensive framework for understanding and improving personal wellbeing, resilience, and long-term career sustainability.
