Participants will explore the distinctions between true wellbeing, pseudo-wellbeing, and poor wellbeing, examine the physiology of the autonomic nervous system and its role in stress, anxiety, and emotional regulation, and learn practical tools to restore balance through breathwork, mindfulness, grounding, movement, and cognitive reframing. Additional topics include present-moment awareness, intentional prioritization of time and energy, and the concept of making small, high-impact investments in one's future self. Attendees will develop practical strategies to align daily choices with their most important values and create a more sustainable and fulfilling life in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: Notable Equine Soft Tissue and Orthopedic Articles from the Last Year - On Demand
courses.description: This webinar will highlight impactful research published over the past year in equine soft tissue and orthopedic surgery. Attendees will receive a clinically focused overview and discussion of new findings.

courses.title: Updates on Plasma Cell Pododermatitis and ICGN
courses.description: This session will share recent research regarding the clinical presentation of plasma cell pododermatitis (PCP) and associated immune complex mediated glomerular nephritis (ICGN) in cats, an uncommon but serious condition traditionally associated with a poor prognosis. Familiarity with these disease processes and their potential association may facilitate earlier diagnosis and improve outcomes for young cats affected by these conditions.

courses.provider: TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY OFFICE OF VETERINARY CONTINUING EDUCATION
courses.title: 2026 Vet-KU - Texas A&M Internal Medicine Conference: Endocrinology
courses.description: This 25-hour program will provide attendees with current practically relevant information on small animal endocrinology. To this end, several sessions will outline a logical diagnostic approach to challenging but common problems, such as polyuria/polydipsia, while others will help attendees formulate better treatment plans for common but challenging conditions, such as diabetes mellitus. The program will cover a wide range of important disease entities including diabetes mellitus in cats and dogs, canine hypercortisolism, canine hypoadrenocorticism, hypothyroidism in dogs and cats, hyperthyroidism in cats, and endocrine neoplasia. Special emphasis will be paid to major new developments in the treatment of diabetes mellitus. The final hour of each day will be an interactive session, covering complex and controversial topics. The 4 speakers are all recognized experts in this field: Andrew Bugbee (Texas A&M University), Sean Hulsebosch (University of California Davis), Daniel Langlois (Michigan State University), Jocelyn Mott (University of Florida).

courses.title: Current Advances in Large Animal Analgesia - On-Demand
courses.description: This seminar focuses on current pain management strategies and advances in large animal veterinary medicine, including multimodal analgesia therapy using current pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical options.

courses.title: Vascular Anomalies: Interventional Radiology Management of Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunts, Arteriovenous Malformations OD
courses.description: During these talks, the management of hepatic vascular anomalies will be discussed in detail with particular focus on pre- and post-treatment management, advanced diagnostics, and intravascular therapeutic techniques.

courses.title: Caring for Exotic Species in Hospital: Part 2
courses.description: In this continuation of Part 1, Dr Sonya Miles BVSc CertAVP(ZM) CertAqV MRCVS explores advanced concepts in exotic species hospital care, including temperature control, humidity management, oxygen therapy, and the safe use of Vetario incubators. The lecture focuses on clinical reasoning behind incubator use, particularly for debilitated, hypothermic, post-anaesthetic, and respiratory-compromised patients. Delegates will learn how to assess thermoneutral ranges, avoid thermal injury, provide species-appropriate humidity, administer supplemental oxygen, and implement nebulisation therapy for respiratory disease. The session also covers the limitations of incubators for reptiles and highlights alternative housing solutions for poikilothermic species. By the end of the lecture, clinicians will be able to confidently deliver tailored supportive care, recognise species-specific vulnerabilities, and implement protocols that promote safe and effective recovery for exotic patients.

courses.title: Gonadectomy in Dogs- Pros and Cons
courses.description: This program will discuss the pros and cons of gonadectomy in dogs.The surgeon will review sterilization options for female and male dogs and the literature on gonadectomy(primarily focusing on decreased risk of oncologic and orthopedic conditions when remaining hormonally intact) and will review how to pick a surgical option for your specific patient.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: Regulation of the Profession
courses.description: A perceived failure of veterinary medical care may lead an animal owner to pursue legal recourse, including a professional negligence or veterinary malpractice suit or a license complaint, which may result in serious repercussions for a veterinarian. This course will review the rules and regulations that govern veterinary conduct; steps in a state license disciplinary action; elements of a veterinary malpractice claim; and strategies to help prevent legal and ethical issues from arising in clinical practice.

courses.title: Things That Twist: A Surgical Approach
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary professionals will provide an overview on organs that can torse in the body, how they present, and the surgery to repair them. This presentation will review various types of torsion including mesenteric, colonic, splenic, lung lobe, liver, and testicle.
(This course was previously presented live in 2025 and was RACE-approved # 20-1283840.)

courses.title: GI Surgery in Cattle-On Demand
courses.description: This webinar reviews common diseases requiring GI surgery in cattle and the surgical techniques used to correct them.

courses.title: Antimicrobial Stewardship for Surgeons: Prophylactic Use and Other Considerations - On Demand
courses.description: The panelists in this webinar will discuss the use of prophylactic antibiotics, including evidence for/against, and evidence based recommendations. Other topics will include how to inspire change in your practice and a global view of antimicrobial use.¿

courses.title: Canine Coughing
courses.description: This course provides an exploration of canine respiratory and cardiovascular disorders, including collapsing trachea, heartworm disease, and infectious tracheobronchitis. Participants will learn the pathophysiology, diagnostic modalities, and treatment protocols for these common conditions. Through case studies, clinical insights, and evidence-based guidelines, attendees will enhance their ability to diagnose, treat, and manage these diseases effectively.

courses.title: Canine Pruritus
courses.description: This course provides an exploration of diagnosing and managing pruritic skin diseases in dogs. Participants will learn to differentiate between ectoparasites, allergic conditions, and secondary infections, such as Staphylococcus pseudintermedius pyoderma and Malassezia pachydermatis dermatitis. With an emphasis on practical diagnostic techniques and treatment protocols, attendees will acquire knowledge about zoonotic implications, flea prevention, and multimodal approaches to atopic dermatitis.

courses.title: Tough Pain Problems Symposium
courses.description: A symposium geared to strengthen pain assessments, diversify treatment options, and improve clinical outcomes with evidence-based integrative medicine and rehabilitation. We have leading researchers and clinicians present research and discuss scientific, integrative medicine and rehabilitation approaches for short- and long-term pain problems in veterinary patients large and small. We promote evidence-based, safe, and restorative treatment options for animals in pain.

courses.title: Chronic Pain Symposium 2025
courses.description: The second annual Chronic Pain Symposium, hosted by Canine Arthritis Management, is a four-day global online learning event for canine and veterinary professionals, with the aim to ENGAGE, EDUCATE, ENABLE, and EMPOWER every attendee to become a competent advocate of chronic pain management. Delegates can immerse themselves in the lecture recordings from this virtual event, featuring knowledge sharing, discussion, and a tight network of clinicians and therapists where the primary goal is welfare through excellent pain management. Over the course of this four-day symposium, three days will be offering RACE-approved lectures; attendees are required to attend a minimum of 1 credit hour.

courses.title: Gastric Dilatation Volvulus
courses.description: This course will be a brief but thorough review of gastric dilatation volvulus in dogs: risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical findings, diagnostics, medical stabilization, and surgical treatment will be discussed in detail, with emphasis on current best practice recommendations.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Neurology Part 3: Intracranial Disease and Epilepsy
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of neurological diseases in dogs and cats, emphasizing intracranial diseases, their diagnosis, and treatment. Participants learn about common conditions such as idiopathic epilepsy, infectious encephalitis, neoplasia, and systemic hypertension. The program explores diagnostic tools like neurologic exams, MRI, CSF analysis, and fundic exams, while covering therapeutic strategies including antiepileptic drugs, immunosuppression, and management of hypertensive emergencies.

courses.title: Osteopathic Medical Massage for Small Animals Certification (CVMM)
courses.description: The 2026 Medical Massage program includes instructional videos, hands-on coursework at home and onsite, expanded sections on anatomy, myofascial dysfunction, osteopathic and Swedish massage techniques, and the neurophysiology of soft tissue manual therapy. Certification for veterinarians is based on the successful completion of online modules, hands-on practice at home, the in-person Clinical Intensive, and a case report documenting the clinical implementation of medical massage.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: The Veterinarian Client Patient Relationship
courses.description: The veterinarian-client-patient relationship (VCPR) is the basis for interaction among veterinarians, their clients, and their patients. Most states and federal law require a valid VCPR to provide patient care and prescribe medications. Learn about the qualifying characteristics of the VCPR; steps to establish, maintain and terminate the relationship; the resulting duties this relationship creates; and about the potential to delegate these duties.

courses.title: Contract Negotiation and Renegotiation On-Demand
courses.description: Webinar aimed at demystifying the intricate landscape of employment agreements, retention bonuses, non-competes, and corporate contracts. In this session, we will delve into the purpose of employment agreements and clarify who should sign them, shedding light on their significance in fostering employee-employer relationships. Furthermore, we will explore the nuances of retention bonuses and their role in talent retention strategies, as well as the implications of non-compete clauses for both employees and employers. Additionally, we will discuss corporate contracts and highlight key elements that are crucial for employees to understand, empowering them to make informed decisions about their professional engagements. Whether you're an employee seeking clarity or an employer aiming to enhance your workforce management practices, this webinar promises valuable insights into optimizing the employee experience within the realm of contractual obligations.

courses.title: Diaphragmatic and Thoracic Body Wall Reconstruction and Hernias-On-Demand
courses.description: This seminar explores principles and current best practices in diaphragmatic and thoracic body wall reconstruction techniques, including recent advances in minimally invasive approaches to diaphragmatic hernia repair.

courses.title: Trace minerals in cattle reproduction and immune function
courses.description: The objective of this course is to fully understand the role of Trace minerals in the reproduction and immune function in ruminants. We will also explore the impact of imbalances and how these imbalances can be diagnosed and corrected. You will also fully understand the role of trace minerals in the reproductive systems (breeding males and females) and how the immune system functions in ruminants. The impact of imbalances and how these imbalances occur, are diagnosed and correctly managed.

courses.provider: THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE SPECIALISTS NORTH SCOTTSDALE
courses.title: The Specialists Exchange Deconstructing Primary Care Inquiries through Multi Disciplinary Case Review
courses.description: This interactive 60 minute, multi-session, series serves as a bridge between frontline primary care and advanced specialty medicine. Rather than a traditional lecture, each event is built around a curated selection of complex clinical questions and "mutual cases" submitted by primary care veterinarians. A panel of specialists will guide participants through a deep-dive analysis of cases, examining the evolution of medical standards (past vs. future) and the physiological "why" behind specific diagnostic and treatment choices. Attendees will gain a clearer understanding of the rationale behind specialist protocols, helping to refine their own clinical decision-making and improve the continuity of care for shared patients.

courses.title: NAVDF 2026 - North American Veterinary Dermatology Forum
courses.description: Inspired by a passion for the specialty, the American Academy of Veterinary Dermatology (AAVD) and the American College of Veterinary Dermatology (ACVD) created the North American Veterinary Dermatology Forum (NAVDF) in 2011 to provide state-of-the-art continuing education paired with outstanding social events and networking opportunities. An interactive exhibit hall with innovative products and services to elevate the practice of veterinary dermatology is also a feature of the Forum.

courses.title: Top 5 Feline Emergency Presentations
courses.description:
Covers the top 5 feline emergency presentations:
1) Respiratory distress
2) Urethral obstruction
3) Vomiting due to gastrointestinal causes
4) Vomiting due to non-gastrointestinal causes
5) Trauma

courses.title: Overcoming Imposter Syndrome in Vet Med: A Positive Intelligence Approach
courses.description: This 1-hour interactive webinar empowers veterinary professionals with effective tools for transcending self-doubt, perfectionism, and people-pleasing, the roots of imposter syndrome. Participants will discover how self-sabotaging behavior patterns called 'Saboteurs' contribute to this hurtful self-image. Attendees will learn how to build resilience and self-compassion using science-based tools to overcome the insidious damage of imposter syndrome.

courses.title: Webinar: Feline-Focused Care: A Review of the AAHA Diabetes Management Guidelines for Cats
courses.description: Diabetes management in cats calls for a different approach than in dogs especially with SGLT2-inhibitor drugs now expanding feline treatment options. This webinar presents the 2026 AAHA Diabetes Management Guidelines for Cats, offering primary care teams practical, step-by-step guidance on diagnosing, treating, and monitoring diabetes mellitus in feline patients. Participants will leave with actionable strategies to improve glycemic control, support client adherence, and deliver confident, evidence-based care for their diabetic feline patients.

courses.title: A Proven Addition to Biosecurity Protocols
courses.description:
Most veterinary biosecurity protocols focus on what teams can see and touch surfaces, instruments, textiles. But the air circulating through your facility carries its own pathogen load, and what's airborne inevitably resettles on the surfaces you just cleaned. This invisible gap in infection prevention can contribute to hospital-acquired infections, increase costs, and undermine even the most rigorous manual cleaning protocols.
Join Dr. Dan Dreyfuss, DVM, MA, for a practical, evidence-informed session examining the role of air quality in veterinary biosecurity and what practices can do about it. Dr. Dreyfuss will walk through the science behind Dry Hydrogen Peroxide technology, a continuous decontamination approach that actively reduces airborne and surface-level pathogens in occupied spaces without disrupting daily operations.
This session goes beyond theory. Participants will explore how DHP technology is already being deployed in human healthcare environments, why those applications translate to veterinary settings, and how this approach layers rather than replaces existing cleaning and disinfection workflows. Whether your practice is a high-volume general hospital, a specialty referral center, or a shelter environment managing dense populations, this webinar offers a framework for evaluating and integrating air-based pathogen reduction into your biosecurity strategy.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: Steps to a COHAT - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Performing a Complete Oral Health Assessment and Treatment (COHAT) entails much more than removing plaque and calculus from the teeth. A thorough dental prophylaxis consists of educating the client, an oral examination, charting disease process, pathology and anomalies, radiographs, both supra and sub-gingival plaque and calculus removal, hand scaling, polishing, irrigation, and home care instructions. Each step is vital to prevent or halt disease progression.

courses.title: Megasphaera elsdenii and its effect on cattle health
courses.description: This program is designed to give veterinarians and technicians a review of the anatomy and physiology of the bovine rumen. This overview will include a detailed explanation of the impact of the rumen micro flora on the health and production of cattle. The rumen microbe Megasphaera elsdenii will be discussed in further detail for its ability to control and maintain the pH of the rumen due to its preferential consumption of lactic acid.

courses.title: Mountain to Sea Veterinary CE and Wellness Retreat - Costa Rica August 2025
courses.description: This program covers subject matter focused in small animal neurology and anesthesiology and is suitable for the general practitioner. We will discuss anesthesia for brachycephalics, monitoring updates, hypotension in anesthesia, feline anesthesia, and ketamine. For neurology, we will discuss the neurologic exam, seizure management, CBD in canine epilepsy, canine cognitive dysfunction, and IVDD. This program will also include 6 hours of online coursework through Get MotiVETed University on topics of wellbeing and suicide prevention basics as veterinary professionals, which will be part of the overall program but will be taken through GMU (these 6 hours are already RACE approved and GMU will provide certificates).

courses.title: CPR Refresher Series: Annual Training & RECOVER 2.0 Updates
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinarians and technicians will provide a CPR refresher training is a didactic review of the logistics of delivering hands-on psychomotor skills imperative to CPR readiness. The course is designed to review essential BLS/ALS skills and knowledge, while providing RECOVER 2.0 2024 updates.

courses.title: Taking Veterinary Dentistry to the Next Level 201
courses.description: Oral disease is one of the most prevalent diseases in dogs and cats and it is also the most preventable disease. This five-session (1 hour each) course will help take your dental skills to the next level. Improve your skills by discovering the steps of a thorough oral examination and appreciate the progression of periodontal disease if left untreated. Learn the importance of each step of a Comprehensive Oral Health Assessment and Treatment procedure. Acquire tips and tricks to take diagnostic dental radiographs. Understand the need for anesthesia, pain management, and how to place dental nerve blocks in dogs and cats. Learn when to refer a patient to a specialist and understand advanced dental procedures to discuss options with clients better.

courses.title: Steps to a COHAT
courses.description: Performing a Complete Oral Health Assessment and Treatment (COHAT) entails much more than removing plaque and calculus from the teeth. A thorough dental prophylaxis consists of educating the client, an oral examination, charting the disease process, pathology and anomalies, radiographs, both supra, and sub-gingival plaque and calculus removal, hand scaling, polishing, irrigation, and home care instructions. Each step is vital to prevent or halt disease progression.

courses.title: Decade One Meeting Six
courses.description: This business course covers compensation methods, benefit offerings, and employment agreements. In addition, transitions of ownership, corporate acquisitions, practice valuation, and partners' operating agreements are discussed.

courses.title: The Foundations of Wildlife Chemical Capture
courses.description: This independent online course is the most current and extensive training chemical immobilization of non-domestic animals. This course will benefit veterinary professionals, such as veterinarians, LVTs, and CAETs, who provide veterinary support for zoos, sanctuaries, wildlife research and management programs, exotic game farms, rehabilitation, and animal control. The course covers in detail all of the essential elements needed for a successful, safe, and effective chemical capture program including legal responsibilities, record keeping, the veterinarian/client/patient relationship, drug delivery, immobilizing drugs, animal patient monitoring, veterinary emergencies, and human safety.

courses.provider: SAN DIEGO ZOO WILDLIFE ALLIANCE ACADEMY - SAFE CAPTURE
courses.title: Chemical Immobilization of Animals E-LEARNING Module
courses.description: This training provides the most complete, up-to-date instruction available on chemical immobilization of animals, presented in an easy-to-understand manner that is applicable to all experience levels. The instructors are veterinarians and biologists who specialize in remotely-delivered anesthetic agents. This program has historically been considered by many to be the standard in chemical immobilization training. San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Academy now offers this training in self-paced, online learning modules.

courses.title: Essential Oils For Pets
courses.description:
4 hours of Training from top Veterinarians in the Animal Aromatherapy field in person on September 18th, 2024 starting at 9 am at the Gallivan Center in Salt Lake City, Utah. Gain a wealth of knowledge and practical skills to support your own pets and in your practices.
Dr. Mia Frezzo (DVM) will cover Easing Anxiety and Stress in our dogs and cats. Discover how essential oils can be a natural remedy to ease anxiety and stress in your pets and patients. Learn about specific oils and application techniques that can create a calming environment for both dogs and cats. This session will equip you with practical knowledge to enhance your pets' emotional well-being, helping them feel more relaxed and secure in their daily lives.
Dr. Janis Fisher, (DVM, CVA, CCRT, CAC) will cover Using Essential Oils to Support Mobility Through All Life Stages. Learn which essential oils can support a pet's mobility from birth to old age. For anyone caring for a pet with mobility issues, this lecture will help to equip the care giver and practitioner with practical uses of essential oils for the most common injuries or diseases that can affect a pets mobility.
Dr. Jeannette Yamamoto (DVM) will cover The Use of Essential Oils in Managing Osteoarthritis in Dogs and Cats. Explore the therapeutic benefits of essential oils in managing arthritis in pets. This session will cover how certain oils can alleviate pain and improve joint health in dogs and cats. You'll gain valuable insights into integrating these natural solutions into your pets' care routines, enhancing their comfort and overall quality of life.
Dr. Janet Roark with cover Essential Oil Safety with Pets and Managing Difficult Cases. Essential oils can be wonderful tools to use around and with pets. Safety is key of course, which we will cover. Essential Oils can be very useful in the management of difficult situations, such as itchy dogs with complex allergies or cats that need kidney or liver support. We will discuss several cases w

courses.title: The Art of Bandaging: Hands-on Skills for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians and veterinary technicians will include a hands-on bandaging lab and practical demonstrations, plus present a comprehensive overview of general bandaging techniques and the most effective applications. In addition, a special focus of the program will be on distal limbs, including soft padded bandages, splints, and fiberglass cast applications.

courses.title: B-line to Feline CHF: Point of care ultrasound to diagnose feline congestive heart failure in the emergency room
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) program is a recording of a live virtual webinar. The program uses a case example to demonstrate how point of care ultrasound (POCUS) can help differentiate congestive heart failure from other causes of feline lower respiratory disease in the emergency room. The POCUS findings are supported by a discussion of recent literature.
This course was previously RACE-approved program # 20-897488. (It just expired on 3/2/24.)

courses.title: CAM Veterinary Practitioner
courses.description: CAM Veterinary Practitioner is a comprehensive overview of canine osteoarthritis (OA) and its evidence-based management. Despite being classed as a welfare concern and recognized as one of the leading causes of elective euthanasia, OA is an often overlooked and poorly managed disease. This course will provide the veterinary professional with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to successfully manage OA in their patients. Through case-based learning, the attendee will be given an in-depth look at the identification, diagnosis, and multimodal management of the disease, as well as palliative/end of life care considerations. Emphasis is placed on following an evidence-based multimodal approach to management, with consideration of the biopsychosocial care model and focus on improving client compliance through enhanced communication and owner education. The course is designed to allow the veterinarian or veterinary technician to immediately incorporate their new understanding into their professional role.

courses.title: Master Course in Urgent Care
courses.description: Master urgent care with this 8-module program led by veterinary criticalist Dr. Natosha Richardson. Learn triage, CPR, supportive care, diagnostics, and treatments through a systems-based approach. Explore CNS, GI, respiratory, and integumentary emergencies to confidently assess, diagnose, and treat critical cases. Build expertise and improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: The Basics of Veterinary Dentistry 101
courses.description: Oral disease is one of the most prevalent diseases in dogs and cats, and it is also the most preventable disease. This five-session course will be a basic refresher on veterinary dentistry. The lessons will help improve your understanding of oral anatomy and the disease process, performing and charting a thorough oral examination, recognizing common oral pathology, the importance of maintaining dental equipment and discussing effective home care options with pet owners.

courses.title: Thriving through the power of self-awareness
courses.description: This webinar will introduce participants to the topic of cognitive and emotional self-awareness, both of which build the foundation of emotional intelligence (EQ). Emotional intelligence involves being able to recognise our own capabilities and emotions, managing them for the sake of ourselves and others around us, removing our blind spots, as well as recognising emotions of there people and building relationships in a healthy, agile way. Becoming deeply and wisely self-aware allows veterinary professionals to develop strong sense of confidence and self-efficacy, achieve the state of flow more easily, grow in a dynamic and healthy way and protect their own mental health. What is more, if we set up the foundation of realistic self awareness and remove our blind spots, we are more able to shape positive intra-team dynamics, build psychologically safe workplace culture and manage conflicts. In this session, participants will learn what self-awareness truly means, what the benefits of it are and how they can take the first steps towards developing it.

courses.title: Endocrinology Secrets with Dr. Forrest Cummings
courses.description:
Endocrinology is one of those areas where having a strong internal medicine mentor changes everything. Dr. Forrest Cummings is that mentor.
He has been managing these cases at the referral level for nearly two decades, has presented on canine diabetes and Cushing's disease to veterinary audiences across the country, and has a genuine gift for making the complex feel manageable. This series is designed to give you the clinical confidence to walk into your next endocrine case with a real plan, not just a hope.
Master Diabetes in Dogs and Cats, plus Cushing's and Addison's Disease and come away with practical tools you can put to work immediately.

courses.provider: SIR JAMES DUNN ANIMAL WELFARE CENTRE, ATLANTIC VETERINARY COLLEGE, UNIVERSITY OF
courses.title: Sir James Dunn Animal Welfare Center Spring 2022 Webinar Series
courses.description: This webinar series will present participants with current knowledge about the welfare of dogs used for breeding as well as their offspring. We will discuss methods used to assess the welfare of dogs used for breeding using reliable indicators from the animal themselves and their housing environments. We will also discuss the animal welfare problems associated with breeding for certain traits, such as conformations that result in brachycephaly. Current policies on these topics will be discussed from both a North American and an international perspective, as well as recommendations for how best to mitigate some of the animal welfare problems currently associated with dog breeding. The focus of the program will be on the role of the veterinarian in helping to resolve some of these concerns.

courses.title: CAMadvocate Level 1 - A Canine Professional's Introduction to Canine Osteoarthritis
courses.description:
CAMadvocate Level 1 is an initiative to improve canine welfare globally. Canine Osteoarthritis (OA) was reclassified by Vet Compass as a welfare concern in April 2018. Extensive analysis of first opinion veterinary caseload identified OA as a leading cause of elective euthanasia, as well as the disease which negatively impacted the dog for the longest time and brought with it the most severe clinical signs. The new understanding highlights that we need to do more for our canine companions such as increased awareness, earlier identification and improved management.
Every canine professional has a duty of care to increase their knowledge regarding this overlooked and often terminal disease.
The course aims to:
Develop the canine professional's knowledge of the disease.
Impart an understanding of the recognised evidence-based approach to identification and diagnosis..
Explain, clarify and detail the structure of a multimodal management plan with case-based learning.
Provide and evidence-based understanding to tackle the multitude of interventions sold as effective for OA.
Create a passion for further learning and action against canine OA.
Course design:
10 modules with each module consisting of a recorded presentation based lecture, online learning resources and downloadable tools and multiple- choice examination.
Intentions of the course:
Identify and feel confident to action beneficial changes to current practice for improved canine welfare.
Understand OA affects dogs of all ages and identify the disease.
Comprehend the underlying causes and influences on disease development and progression.
Understand that multiple valuable actions can be taken throughout a dog's life to reduce the likelihood of OA shortening a dog's lifespan.
Be able to recite prevalence of OA, describe the progression of the disease and simplify how chronic pain is expressed.
Identify the difference between chronic and acute pain and the global impact OA has on the body and mind.
Understand and ac

courses.title: THE PROBLEM MARE (1478-44063)
courses.description: The goal of the course is to provide a broad review of reproductive issues in the non-pregnant mare. The course will start with an overview of techniques for reproductive evaluation of the problem mare and subsequently transition to discussions of issues with ovarian function, oviductal problems, uterine abnormalities, problems with the cervix, vagina and vestibule, and finish with discussions on behavioral abnormalities and finally problems associated with the mammary gland and lactation.

courses.title: Surgical Extractions in Canines and Felines
courses.description: This 9 hour course will be 2.5 hours of interactive lecture and 6.5 hours of hands-on laboratory. The lecture will cover the indications for surgical extractions in both cats and dogs and the appropriate surgical techniques for exodontia. Each participant will be working at their own stations with their specimens, equipment and instrumentations at specially designed dental training tables. Specific teeth in both Canines and Felines will be assigned to practice surgical exodontia. This will involve making the appropriate muco-gingival flaps, bone reduction and teeth elevation techniques. Utilizing videography, the procedures for each tooth will be illustrated throughout the laboratory portion.

courses.title: EQUINE EMBRYO TRANSFER (1478-44714)
courses.description:
The goal of the course is to provide up-to-date, clinically relevant information on equine embryo transfer. Lectures will include donor mare management, embryo collection procedures, embryo evaluation, recipient mare management, the art of transferring embryos, cooled transport of embryos, problems encountered in equine embryo transfer, and embryo vitrification (cryopreservation).
Colorado State University has a long history of research, clinical service and continuing education in the field of equine reproduction and more specifically in the area of embryo transfer.

courses.title: Animal Aromatherapy Specialist Certification - Online
courses.description:
Learn Exactly How, When, and Why We will use Essential Oils, Exactly Which Oils to Use, and How to Use Your New-found Knowledge to Help Animals and Their Owners. Join hundreds of others who have learned how to use essential oils safely and effectively with animals - straight from Dr. Janet Roark, a trusted veterinarian and leader in the field of animal aromatherapy.
Get answers to the most common (and most important!) animal aromatherapy questions asked over the past five years. These recorded Q&A sessions are packed with real-life examples, practical tips, and expert guidance. They are all available for immediate access during this self-paced course. You will get interactive transcripts of every Training and Q&A Session, a downloadable Student Workbook PDF, and one year of access to all course content. Plus, you'll get personal feedback on every assignment & case study to help you get the most out of your certification.
BONUS: Essential Oils A-Z Workshop - Jump right in with instant access to the 2-hour Essential Oils for Animals A-Z workshop replay - plus the full set of presentation slides to follow along or reference anytime.
BONUS: 12+ Additional Resources
12+ Bonus Resources & Downloads including Sample Wording for Setting up Appointments, Carrier Oil Reference Guide, Dilution Guide, EO Benefit Charts and more.

courses.title: External Coaptation Principles: Casting and Splinting 101
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will be presented as a hands-on lab focusing on splinting and casting techniques for fracture stabilization. This course will include indications for external coaptation, proper application methods, and complication prevention strategies to optimize patient outcomes.

courses.title: Radiobiology and Radiation Protection for the Veterinary Profession
courses.description:
This course is presented to familiarize Veterinarians and their associates with the principles of protection from radiation in diagnostic imaging.
Atomic Structure is outlined briefly and an introduction to cell biology is presented. This continues through the cell components and their sensitivity to radiation damage to the conclusion of whether the cell can be repaired or die.
The fundamentals of electricity follows to outline how radiation is produced in the electronic circuit. The fundamentals of the xray tube and the heterogeneous nature of radiation produced within the xray tube is discussed.
The effects of overexposure to radiation are outlined and methods of protection are presented for both the patient and the operator.
Finally the various laws and regulations are outlined for International, USA and Canada.

courses.title: Tips and Tricks to Great Dental Rads
courses.description: Dental radiographs are an essential part of the oral examination. The crown is just the tip of the iceberg. Approximately 42 percent of dental pathology is only found on radiographs. Radiographs help diagnose pathology that is not visible from the crown, confirm pathology, and demonstrate pathology fo the pet owner. Dental radiographs can improve the standard of care in your practice and increase your clinic revenue. This presentation will help veterinary professionals produce diagnostic dental radiographs.

courses.title: 2025 AAHA Con Conference
courses.description: The annual conference for the American Animal Hospital Association in Chicago, September 11-13, 2024 at the Chicago Marriott Downtown Magnificent Mile Hotel. This September, join the best of the best in veterinary medicine in Chicago, Illinois for a few days of networking, hands-on learning, and industry thought leadership. If you are a veterinarian, practice manager, technician, or part of the staff at a clinic, AAHA CON is the place to refresh and reinvigorate your passion for the industry. When you join us, you'll be up close and personal with internationally known experts.

courses.title: The Space We Create (please see attachment for full title)
courses.description: This course provides education on the core OARS communication skills of Motivational Interviewing (MI), an evidence-based therapeutic modality that has demonstrated success with human medical providers on improving communication with clients/patients, and improving client/patient compliance. This course also provides education and skills practice in both the MI OARS skills and co-regulation/nervous system regulation techniques from Polyvagal Theory (PVT), an evidence-based therapeutic modality that can be highly effective for nervous system regulation and co-regulation during stressful situations, including conflict between the veterinary professional and their client. PVT regulation skills also contribute to the veterinary professional's skill set for effective self-care, both outside and during work hours.

courses.title: A Year in Review: Evidence-Based Advances in Gastrointestinal and Hepatobiliary Surgery - On Demand
courses.description: This webinar will highlight the most impactful papers published over the last 12-18 months regarding gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary disease in small animals, emphasizing their clinical application and how they challenge or reinforce current surgical practices. Topics will include updates in surgical management of intestinal obstruction, gallbladder mucoceles and cholecystectomy outcomes, advances in minimally invasive approaches, and perioperative care strategies affecting morbidity and survival. Discussion will focus on interpreting evidence for daily decision-making, identifying areas where further research is needed, and integrating emerging techniques into practice.

courses.title: Arthroscopy of the Canine and Human Shoulder Webinar Series
courses.description: This webinar series is a translational medicine discussion of the human and canine shoulder. Faculty will review anatomy, biomechanics, common injuries, and treatment protocols in both species.

courses.title: Successful OR and Patient Preparation for Orthopedic Surgery
courses.description: During this one-hour webinar, faculty discuss numerous tips and tricks for operating room setup, patient preparation, and improving efficiency in one's practice.

courses.title: Custom Implants in Small Animal Surgery On-demand
courses.description: The use of custom implants is becoming increasingly common in small animal surgery as 3D surgical planning and 3D metal printing technology become more widely available and less costly. This seminar consists of several lectures from veterinary surgeons with experience in the development and implantation of custom implants in veterinary patients. The goal of the seminar will be to increase small animal surgeons' awareness of the potential of custom implants in the field of small animal surgery.

courses.title: Beyond Trazodone: Making Tailored Medication Choices in Behavior Therapy
courses.description: This session covers common classes of medications used in behavior therapy in dogs and cats. This includes serotonin reuptake inhibitors (e.g. fluoxetine, paroxetine, citalopram), serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (e.g. venlafaxine), serotonin antagonist-reuptake inhibitors (e.g. trazodone), benzodiazepines, gabamimetic drugs, and alpha agonists (e.g. clonidine, Sileo Oral Gel). Mechanism of action of each class will be discussed briefly as well as indications and side effects. Additionally, the presenter will discuss behavioral symptoms and breed differences that will assist practitioners in choosing one medication over another to individualize therapy for common behavior problems such as aggression, separation anxiety, storm/noise phobia, and compulsive/repetitive behaviors.

courses.title: Surgery of the Small Colon
courses.description: This webinar discusses management of various small colon diseases. Highlights include surgical techniques specific to the small colon and post-operative management.

courses.title: Fangs on the Farm: The Chupacabra Files
courses.description: When cattle at a Connecticut fair turn up drained of blood, rumors of the legendary Chupacabra spread like wildfire, but the truth is even more shocking. In this comedy dramatic podcast you will join veterinarians on a gripping investigation that blends forensic science, tick biology, and myth-busting detective work. Discover how to identify Asian longhorned tick infestations (hint: they clone themselves!), manage outbreaks, and calmly debunk "monster panic" with clients. With expert interviews, this is a front-row seat to a veterinary mystery you will not forget.

courses.title: Connecting with Empathy to Clients Under Stress
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary professionals will review how to have difficult conversations with pet families in crisis to communicate information. This course provides guidance regarding the neurological implications of stress and strategies for the best way to communicate.

courses.title: A Joint Venture Webinar Series
courses.description:
This robust, four-part series of lectures focuses on canine cruciate surgery. From intraoperative decision-making to appropriate perioperative management, this online event is designed to help you improve patient outcomes and post-operative comfort.
Lecture Topics Include:
- General Approach of Stifle Arthroscopy (Part 1)
- Intraoperative Decision Making for TPLO (Part 2)
- Internal Brace-Augmented TPLO (Part 3)
- Perioperative Management for Stifle Surgery (Part 4)

courses.title: Performing an Effective Forelimb Exam
courses.description: During this webinar, Dr. Nina Kieves, DVM, DACVS-SA, DACVSMR, CCRT, will review tips and tricks for performing a forelimb lameness exam. She will describe her examination process and decision-making algorithm for forelimb lameness.

courses.title: Beyond the Bottle: Understanding and Preventing Pentobarbital Exposure Risks
courses.description:
Euthanasia is one of the most delicate and compassionate aspects of veterinary medicine. However, what happens next is just as important and often overlooked. Pentobarbital, the most commonly used euthanasia drug, poses significant legal, ethical, and environmental risks when pet remains are sent home.
Despite best intentions, improper aftercare can lead to wildlife toxicosis, domestic pet exposure, and environmental contamination. In this session, Dr. Celine Leheurteux DMV will explore the hidden dangers of pentobarbital residues and why responsible aftercare should be a priority in every practice.
Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of pentobarbital related risks, an overview of the AVMA Companion Animal Aftercare Policy, and practical strategies for educating clients on responsible options. As veterinary medicine continues to evolve, it is time to rethink aftercare practices and ensure we are protecting animals, the environment, and our profession.
What You Will Learn
Pentobarbital Toxicosis and Environmental Impact
Literature review on pentobarbital residues and contamination risks
The real world consequences of improper aftercare
AVMA Companion Animal Aftercare Policy
Key takeaways and implications for veterinary practices
Understanding professional responsibilities in post euthanasia care
Client Education and Responsible Aftercare
How to communicate aftercare risks to pet owners
Practical guidance for implementing safer protocols in your clinic

courses.title: Master Course in Respiratory Disease Management
courses.description:
Join Vet Candy's Respiratory Disease Management Master Course, led by Dr. Anthony Gonzalez, a board-certified critical care specialist and featuring veterinary technician, Alyssa Mages. This comprehensive program dives deep into the science and clinical skills needed to expertly diagnose, treat, and manage respiratory conditions, while enhancing client communication strategies.
Course Highlights:
In-depth training on respiratory disease diagnosis and management
Evidence-based treatment approaches
Practical client counseling techniques

courses.title: Stabilizing the Patient with Non-Traumatic Hemoabdomen
courses.description: In this lecture, we will take a case-based approach on managing the non-traumatic canine hemoabdomen patient, from initial triage and stabilization, through diagnostics, and into the operating room. Participants will gain an understanding of common cardiovascular and hemostatic disturbances in these patients and how to manage them. Beyond the physiology, we will discuss the overall approach to these patients and how to manage owner conversations and expectations.

courses.title: Common Arrhythmias and their Treatments
courses.description: In this course, participants will review how to interpret an ECG tracing, rate and rhythm, and then advance their skills into correct arrhythmia diagnosis. We will discuss antiarrhythmic medication classes, mechanism of action and which drugs to select for each type of common arrhythmia.

courses.title: Chronic Canine Respiratory Diseases
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review signalment, clinical signs, diagnostics, and treatment of the most common canine chronic respiratory diseases that can lead to respiratory emergencies and pulmonary hypertension.

courses.title: Masterclass: Chronic Pain in Our Feline Patients
courses.description: Dr. Sarah Caney, BVSc, DSAM(Feline), PhD, MRCVS, hosts a series of webinars with a focus on chronic pain in cats. Senior cats are especially vulnerable to chronically painful conditions, but feline behaviour and coping strategies often make it difficult for caregivers and clinicians to identify pain. This masterclass will enable veterinary professionals to become more proficient at recognizing and clinically assessing pain in senior cats and developing tailored diagnostic and management strategies incorporating both medical and supportive care.

courses.title: Exotic Vet Med Essentials 2026
courses.description: This is a 12-week course introducing veterinarians to the basics of exotic animal veterinary care. Modules cover Avian, Reptile/Amphibian and Exotic companion mammal anatomy and physiology, husbandry, physical exam and restraint, preventative care and basic techniques, and recognition, diagnosis, and treatment of common diseases. The lectures will be pre-recorded and participants will have access to support materials including anatomy illustrations, diagnostic algorithms, and drug tables. Participants will receive credit after passing post-course quizzes after each module.

courses.title: Surgical Interventions for Equine Tendon and Ligament Disorders - On-Demand
courses.description: This seminar comprehensively discusses evidence-guided surgical interventions for equine tendon and ligament disorders with an emphasis on case-based scenarios frequently encountered in our clinical practices. Advanced surgical techniques for treating congenital and acquired flexural contractures/deformities will be presented. Current and upcoming surgical (and post-surgery) interventions that are guided by advanced diagnostic imaging for enhancing intra- and extra-synovial tendon and enthesis healing will be covered.

courses.title: Improving the Euthanasia Experience; Non-Medical Offerings
courses.description: This series explores the veterinary professional's experience with euthanasia, offering ways to avoid common mistakes and bringing improved methodology to light. This series will combat the dreaded compassion fatigue and burnout by showcasing compassionate measures that can be taken efficiently and with the care of the pet, pet owner and veterinary staff in mind. A special focus is taken to cover the soft skills that Euthanasia requires, but veterinarians often lack training in. Resources for both the veterinary staff members and pet owners will be provided.

courses.title: CORA Based Leveling Osteotomy (CBLO)
courses.description:
CORA based leveling osteotomy (CBLO) is a unique procedure that modifies the tibial
plateau angle in order to prevent cranial translation (cranial drawer) and tibial thrust in the cranial cruciate deficient
stifle. Advantages of the technique include ease of the osteotomy, non-articular osteotomy, and rapid healing of the
osteotomy. Rapid healing and early return to function are the result of complete bone contact along the surface of
the osteotomy and ability to apply compression at the osteotomy. Numerous advantages of the technique have been
identified and will be presented in lecture format. In vitro and in vivo outcome studies will be presented as well as
complications and their management.

courses.title: A Positive Spin on Imposter Syndrome - On Demand
courses.description: In "A Positive Spin on Imposter Syndrome,"¿panelists recognize imposter syndrome as a natural response to challenges and as an opportunity for professional and personal growth. Panelists also evaluate strategies for reframing self-doubt into constructive moments that support learning and resilience, and apply practical techniques to transform imposter feelings into building confidence, adaptability, and long-term success.

courses.title: ADVANCED SKILLS BAT REHABILITATION WORKSHOP (1131-35648)
courses.description: In this one-day class, participants learn how to manage more complex cases, including long-term care, closed fracture stabilization, open fracture reduction and repair, wound care, anesthesia, and pain management.

courses.title: Dog Bite Prevention in the Home and Baby/Toddler Safety
courses.description: Human pregnancy, infant, and toddler phases are very different and present unique challenges, risks and solutions. Veterinarians, as part of the family health care team and as public health providers, are frequently called upon after a dog behaves aggressively or bites a child. Dog bites are a symptom of a larger, usually chronic problem that may have been avoided with proper education, intervention, and management. This 4-part series serves to inform veterinary professionals on how to better educate and support families with dogs and children. Through a better understanding of the dog as a canid species, their developmental stages and impacts on behavior, we can guide families in how to prevent childhood bites and decrease the chances of a dog being relinquished.

courses.title: Equine Distal Interphalangeal Joint Arthrodesis On-Demand
courses.description: This hybrid laboratory discusses an open dorsal approach to the distal interphalangeal joint, debride the articular cartilage, and prepare the dorsal surface of the middle phalanx and the dorsal proximal surface of the distal phalanx for application of a custom arthrodesis plate. Under radiographic guidance the plate will be applied along with transarticular screws in lag fashion. The custom designed plate will be applied through a single skin incision without penetration of the hoof wall.

courses.title: Upper Airway Abnormalities On-Demand
courses.description: This webinar will cover step-by-step how to do a thorough upper airway examination. Abnormalities will be discussed as well as methods to recognize the abnormalities.

courses.title: Wound Management: Choosing the Primary Layer
courses.description: This course reviews the wound healing process, discusses clinical evaluation strategies to help guide wound management, and specifically describes several different primary wound dressings. Indications for use of each are discussed, and case examples are provided.

courses.provider: UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: A stepwise guide to antibiotic stewardship in small animal practice
courses.description:
Small animal veterinarians are increasingly confronted with patients suffering from antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) infections. AMR infections in cats and dogs have an impact on human health and vice versa due to close contact and shared environments. Additionally, antibiotics of human health importance are used commonly in companion animal medicine.
Antibiotic stewardship (AS) aims to optimize patient outcomes and minimize unintended consequences of antibiotic use (AU), including AMR. The American Veterinary Medical Association has outlined five core principles of AS in veterinary medicine.
This one-hour webinar, presented by Dr. Jennifer Granick, DVM, MS, PhD, DACVIM (SAIM) - associate professor of small animal internal medicine at the University of Minnesota College of Veterinary Medicine, provides a brief overview of AMR in small animals, as well as an accessible approach to development of AS practices within small animal veterinary clinics.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Clinical Pathology Part 1: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Coagulation
courses.description: This course provides a detailed exploration of small animal clinical pathology, focusing on hematologic evaluation, coagulation disorders, and the application of case-based learning. Participants will gain a practical understanding of interpreting complete blood counts (CBCs), coagulation profiles, and their clinical implications for anemia, leukograms, and hemostatic abnormalities. The course includes discussions on diseases like immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA), rodenticide toxicity, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and anemia of chronic disease. Designed for veterinary professionals, this course emphasizes diagnostic reasoning and clinical application to improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: Internal Medicine in Real Life: Practical Strategies for Your Toughest Chronic Cases
courses.description:
Internal Medicine in Real Life: Practical Strategies for Your Toughest Chronic Cases
This three-part CE series is designed for general practitioners who want practical, confidence-building approaches to liver disease, hyperadrenocorticism, and chronic kidney disease. Across three interactive 2-hour sessions, you'll learn how to diagnose these conditions efficiently, avoid common mistakes, and implement treatment strategies that actually move the needle for your patients
Session 1- Demystifying Liver Disease in Dogs and Cats
Confused about feline cholangiohepatitis? Unsure how aggressively to pursue diagnostics in the icteric cat? Curious how to apply ACVIM guidelines to canine chronic hepatitis? This session breaks down the most common hepatopathies you see in practice - clearly, simply, and practically. Learn streamlined diagnostic pathways, treatment strategies that make a difference, and case-based pearls that demystify these often frustrating conditions.
Session 2 - Is This Cushing's and Do I Care?
Cushing's is one of the most confusing and sometimes frustrating diseases in veterinary medicine. This session gives you a practical, evidence-based roadmap for when to test, how to test, and - most importantly - when to treat. We'll tackle the gray areas, the unexpected complications, the borderline test results, and the realistic conversations you need to have with clients to keep expectations aligned with outcomes.
Session 3-Chronic Kidney Disease: Moving the Needle
CKD is one of the most common - and manageable - conditions in older cats and dogs. This session focuses on early recognition, IRIS-guided treatment, and practical strategies that improve longevity and quality of life. Learn how to identify progression earlier, manage complications proactively, and use nutritional therapy as a powerful tool in slowing disease progression.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: Telehealth and Telemedicine: Legal and Ethical Considerations
courses.description: While telemedicine is a different means of care delivery than in-person veterinary care, it is subject to the same legal and ethical considerations. This course will increase the participants knowledge of the state and federal regulatory landscape, explain the legal and ethical challenges that may arise with the use of telehealth and telemedicine, help you use your professional judgment to determine if using a telehealth tool is appropriate for you, and provide tips to employ best practices for quality care and patient safety.

courses.title: Medical and Surgical Management of Otitis Media in Rabbits
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review the diagnosis and treatment of otitis media in rabbits. This course will cover how to identify clinical signs, apply advanced imaging techniques, and surgical management approaches to optimize patient outcomes in exotic practice.

courses.title: Innovative Approaches to Providing 24/7/365 Clinical Service On-Demand
courses.description: This webinar features a panel discussion with specialist veterinarians, discussing innovative or unusual approaches to the provision of continuous specialist care in practice. Practitioners working in different setups will discuss the details of their approach, including pros and cons, followed by an open discussion with the audience and time for questions.

courses.title: Spanish for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: Spanish for Veterinary Professionals is an online Spanish language provider for people in the animal care industry. The complete four-module program covers the initial consultation, clinical signs and symptoms, diseases, anatomy, diagnostic tools, prescriptions, home care instructions, finance and billing vocabulary. With a maximum of three Spanish learners in each live course, practice talk time is maximized and provided in an engaging manner.

courses.title: Stifle Arthroscopy Webinar Series
courses.description: During this three-part webinar series, faculty review all aspects of stifle arthroscopy: OR setup and patient preparation, joint evaluation, meniscal evaluation and treatment, and challenging cases.

courses.title: Intravenous Potassium Supplementation in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This course will cover the basic and advanced aspects of potassium supplementation as well as treatment of hypokalemia in stable and critically-ill feline and canine patients. It will provide an in-depth overview of step-by-step approach to potassium calculations (for parenteral supplementation and refractory hypokalemia). Each lesson contains numerous clinical examples and post-lesson quiz that is intended to re-enforce students' learning. All participants will be able to download unique and comprehensive step-by-step protocols on treatment of hypokalemia.

courses.title: Catupuncture Advanced Certification
courses.description: This course educates veterinarians on the consideration and implementation of science based integrative medicine for feline patients. It covers five disciplines medical acupuncture, photomedicine, medical massage, rehabilitation, and botanical medicine. Prerequisites Enrollees must have graduated or be currently enrolled in Medical Acupuncture for Veterinarians or have satisfied acquired sufficient knowledge in science-based veterinary medical acupuncture, as deemed by Dr. Narda Robinson, in order to qualify.

courses.title: The Pregnant Mare
courses.description: The goal of the course is to provide up-to-date, clinically relevant information on pregnancy diagnosis, problems of early pregnancy, management of twins, complications of mid- to late term pregnancy, care of the pregnant mare, prediction of foaling, normal foaling, induction of labor, evaluation and management of dystocia and complications of the post-partum mare including options for management of retained fetal membranes. Colorado State University has a long history of applied research and clinical service in the field of equine reproduction as well as a dedication to continuing education for horse owners and veterinarians.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: V.I.P. Veterinary Introductory Pathology- A System-Based Review
courses.description: This monthly webinar series will present a systems-based introduction to veterinary histopathology. Each month, a different body system (Integument, Urinary, Reproductive, Cardiovascular, Endocrine, Pulmonary, Musculoskeletal, Digestive, Hemolymphatic, Nervous, and Special Senses [Eye and Ear]) will be introduced in a way that participants of any level of experience (veterinary students, interns, residents and/or anatomic pathologists) will be able to comprehend and further expand their knowledge of veterinary pathology. Each webinar will introduce the normal tissue architecture, histological features of each anatomic structure and highlight the response to injury of different tissues and cell types found within each system. Cumulatively, by the end of the series, participants will have learned about the embryologic development, structure, function, and response to injury of twelve body systems - As well as received an introduction to some species specific variations of different systemic components. Additionally, these webinars will introduce unique patterns and types of injury that are seen in certain organ systems (such as patterns of pneumonia and zonal patterns of hepatocyte injury). Presentations will give a comprehensive introduction that illus

courses.title: Spontaneous Ventilation Under Anesthesia and Monitoring Techniques
courses.description:
This course will review basic respiratory physiology and how anesthesia affects
ventilation in dogs and cats. Common terminology pertaining to ventilation will be defined with an emphasis on hypoventilation and atelectasis and how that affects the patients and their anesthetic plane. Each commonly used anesthetic drug will be identified as well as their effects on ventilation. A comparison and contrast of the pulse oximeter and the capnograph will be discussed and a brief introduction to capnography and capnogram waves will be presented. Attendees do not have to have current knowledge or experience with capnography to appreciate this lecture.

courses.title: Equine Fracture Complications and Trauma - On-Demand
courses.description:
This seminar focuses on the identification, understanding, and management of fracture complications in large animal trauma, with emphasis on equine patients. The seminar opens with a 30 minute expert lecture by Dr. Anton Furst reviewing common surgical complications associated with fracture fixation. The next lecture is an interactive, case based 1 hour panel discussion centered on mechanical failures.
Panelists present selected clinical cases to stimulate discussion on possible causes, intraoperative decision making, and what might have been done differently. When appropriate, cases are supported by biomechanical interpretation and premodeled 3D analyses to help link clinical observations with underlying mechanical principles. The aim of this seminar is to provide practical insights to improve recognition, prevention, and management of complications in large animal fracture repair.

courses.title: Fracture Management in Farm Animals On-Demand
courses.description: Fracture management in farm animals can be both challenging and rewarding. Determining the best management strategy is often not only based on the fracture itself but also on regulatory concerns, costs, owner expectations, and animal use, which can range from pet to production. This webinar will provide a summary of a few management strategies and the ideal circumstances for their implementation.

courses.provider: FECAVA - FEDERATION OF EUROPEAN COMPANION ANIMAL VETERINARY ASSOCIATIONS
courses.title: FECAVA Certificate in Small Animal Anaesthesia and Analgesia
courses.description:
The FECAVA Certificate in Small Animal Anaesthesia and Analgesia lectures apply clinical and current knowledge of anaesthesia, pain management and fluid therapy. This course provides a foundation for clinical rotations in later parts of the programme. We want to provide a dynamic experience using bite-sized webinars that practitioners can work through at their convenience provided by the world's best clinical anaesthesiologists.
The certificate consists of four modules: Module I: Introduction (fundamentals, behaviour, patient safety, ethics, pharmacology); Module II: Acute Pain Management (assessment, analgesia, case discussions); Module III: Foundations of Anaesthesia (drugs, monitoring, complications); Module IV: Special Patients: case discussions.
Small animal anaesthesia/analgesia is covered using a sequential approach to performing an anaesthetic procedure, with a focus on drug protocols and choices, safety, monitoring and ultimately patient welfare. Clinical reasoning skills are developed as "special patient" case discussions are presented during the last module of the certification.
Acute pain management is approached from a clinical viewpoint to ensure the practicioners will be equipped with skills to recognise and treat acute pain appropriately in a range of situations. The basics of local anaesthetic techniques are discussed to ensure best-practices and evidence-based approach to multimodal analgesia.
This Certification also provides an overview of fluid therapy, acid-base balance and the impact of electrolytes disturbances on anaesthesia. Fluid therapy education is presented in a practical way with case discussions.
Each lecture includes short multiple-choice quizzes (5 questions). Participants must achieve at least 80% correct answers (4 out of 5) to proceed to the next lecture.The Certificate is available in English for the moment.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: V.I.P. Veterinary Introductory Pathology- A System-Based Review
courses.description: This monthly webinar series will present a systems-based introduction to veterinary histopathology. Each month, a different body system (Integument, Urinary, Reproductive, Cardiovascular, Endocrine, Pulmonary, Musculoskeletal, Digestive, Hemolymphatic, Nervous, and Special Senses [Eye and Ear]) will be introduced in a way that participants of any level of experience (veterinary students, interns, residents and/or anatomic pathologists) will be able to comprehend and further expand their knowledge of veterinary pathology. Each webinar will introduce the normal tissue architecture, histological features of each anatomic structure and highlight the response to injury of different tissues and cell types found within each system. Cumulatively, by the end of the series, participants will have learned about the embryologic development, structure, function, and response to injury of twelve body systems - As well as received an introduction to some species specific variations of different systemic components. Additionally, these webinars will introduce unique patterns and types of injury that are seen in certain organ systems (such as patterns of pneumonia and zonal patterns of hepatocyte injury). Presentations will give a comprehensive introduction that illus

courses.title: Dermpath 101: Demystify Dermpath
courses.description: This course covers the basics of how to master dermatopathology vocabulary and confidently approach complex cases. We will build diagnostic skills with guided pattern recognition techniques. We will also learn the difference between primary and secondary skin lesions and when, where, and how best to biopsy them. Additionally, this knowledge will include application to real-world cases for better patient outcomes.

courses.title: VetVine Pet Cancer Summit
courses.description:
Changes in the world of cancer diagnosis and treatment are evolving at lightning speed - so much so that even oncologists themselves can have a hard time keeping up!
We are convening specialists in companion animal cancer care who will be sharing their practical perspectives and valuable insights who will inspire hope and drive change in how you care for dogs and cats diagnosed with cancer.
Throughout this series of webinars we'll highlight several types of cancer that impact dogs and/or cats including lymphoma, mast cell tumors, melanoma, osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and more! We'll talk about advances in diagnostic testing as well as emerging or novel therapies that are improving outcomes for pets with cancer.

courses.title: ENDODONTICS 1 (622-42484)
courses.description: This 3-day introductory course in Endodontics will cover radiographic indication for endodontic disease and it's treatment. Materials, instrumentation and therapy will be covered in treating fresh fractured or crown amputated teeth, versus those requiring root canal therapy. Root canal access preparations, canal debridement and obturation will be practiced. Final restoration materials and usages will be demonstrated and practiced to finish the complete root canal.

courses.title: Decade One Meeting Two
courses.description: This course covers financial topics including understanding financial reports, 100 Pennies, the 1% difference, revenue & profitability, and rational price setting.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: 2022 ACVP/DTF Pre-Meeting Workshop Getting into the Hard Stuff: Tumors of Bone, Cartilage, and Dental Tissues (on-demand)
courses.description: This lecture will target veterinary students, interns, residents, and anatomic pathologists involved in diagnostics. The conference will be organized into presentations and case-based interactive discussions with digital microscopy files available to registrants prior to the meeting. The presentations will cover preparation of bone and hard tissue sections, integration of immunohistochemistry, radiology and cytology into diagnosis, and key features of common bone, cartilage and hard tissue tumors. Case presentations will be used to illustrate the approach and diagnostic features of different bone and dental tumors. Course Objectives: This workshop will allow participants to identify tumors of bone, cartilage, and other hard tissues, highlighting the normal reactions of bone to injury, recognize neoplasia and use current nomenclature, principles and guidelines for hard tissue tumor diagnosis and reporting. Attendees will recognize the importance of combining clinical, diagnostic imaging, and gross and microscopic interpretation for diagnosis. The presenters will share their approach on hard tissue pathology. These presentations will cover normal bone and responses of bone to injury, preparation of bone and hard tissues sections, integration of immunohistochemistry, diagnostic imaging and cytology into diagnosis, and key diagnostic features of common bone, cartilage, and hard tissue tumors. Finally, there will be an interactive case-based discussion with digital microscopy files available to registrants prior to the workshop. These case-based discussions will be used to illustrate the approach used by the presenters, highlighting the diagnostic features of bone and dental tumors. keywords: bone, cartilage, dental tissues, neoplasia

courses.title: Applied Acupressure Fundamentals
courses.description:
Acupressure, a bodywork technique based in Traditional Chinese Medicine, is a non-invasive approach to preventive care and pain management. Providing acupressure to your own dog and to the dogs in your care will allow you to play an important role in their overall mental and physical health and well-being. Acupressure, which is not a substitute for regular veterinary care, can be used alone or combined with other modalities and is ideal for any dog at any stage of life. This workshop will provide participants with the basic tools to immediately give the dogs in their care a simple, but effective, acupressure session using acupoints that deliver a boost to the immune system and specifically focus on musculoskeletal soreness, calming, and overall relaxation and comfort care.
This is a Continuing Education course that can be taken at any time. No prerequisites.

courses.title: Cannabidiol (CBD) in Canine Epilepsy
courses.description:
Description:
The learning objectives of this seminar are for veterinary medical professionals: 1. To review idiopathic epilepsy, and understand: a. the prevalence of idiopathic epilepsy in canines, b. frequency of refractory epilepsy, c. therapeutic options for refractory epileptics. 2. To learn about Cannabis sativa and the endocannabinoid system, and review: a. the origin of the plant cannabis sativa, b. function of the endocannabinoid system, c. the two most prominent cannabinoids, tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD), d. target endogenous cannabinoid receptors present in the body, namely CB1 and CB2, e. neuroprotective, anticonvulsant, and anxiolytic properties of CBD. 3. To learn about the use of cannabinoids in human epilepsy, and understand: a. history of cannabinoids in humane medicine, b. history of use in adult and pediatric epilepsy, 4. To review the available literature on CBD in canine epilepsy, and understand: a. pharmacokinetics of CBD in dogs, b. reported side effects, c. reported safety and efficacy in refractory epileptics. 5. To learn to educate owners about CBD use in dogs, specifically: a. products available on the market, b. quality controls concerns in reference to formulation, c. legal limitations for producing and prescribing CBD products.

courses.title: Mastering the Greeting Process: Communication Skills for the First Moments of the Veterinary Visit
courses.description: This continuing education course focuses on the Greeting Process, the first phase of the veterinary consultation where trust, rapport, and visit tone are established. Participants will learn practical, repeatable communication behaviors for the opening moments of the appointment, including professional introduction, use of client/pet names, rapport-building language, body language awareness, and clear transition into the medical interview. The course emphasizes how first impressions influence client confidence, cooperation, and overall appointment efficiency. Through exam-room scripts and workflow integration, learners will develop a consistent greeting approach that reduces tension, strengthens relationships, and improves the quality of the entire visit.

courses.title: Pre-Operative and Conservative Management of Fractures
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary professionals will focus on the general approach, diagnosis, stabilization, and splinting of fractures. The course will review how to best prepare patients prior to surgery, coaptation techniques, and which patients are eligible for management entirely with coaptation. In addition, case presentations will demonstrate the techniques and management strategies that are featured. Key components of conversations with pets families regarding fracture management will also be highlighted.
(This course was previously presented live in 2025 and was RACE-approved # 20-1290425.)

courses.title: Does Another One Really Have to Bite the Dust
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will be presented as a hands on lab highlighting how outdated habits, team communication gaps, and drug protocol missteps can turn a survivable code into a tragedy. Participants wont just review the latest reassessment campaign on veterinary resuscitation initiative updates, they will perform them on canine and feline manikins to build the muscle memory and confidence needed to deliver high quality chest compressions, master the single dose atropine rule, and run a coordinated code. This course will provide the skills to give patients the best possible shot at the return of spontaneous circulation.

courses.provider: KARL STORZ VETERINARY ENDOSCOPY - AMERICA LTD
courses.title: Diagnostic Endoscopy: An Immersive Guide (Live Course)
courses.description:
