Program objective is to provide training on minimally invasive endoscopy courses designed to meet the varied needs of small animal veterinarians and specialists desiring in-depth training in small animal internal medicine endoscopy.
Course Design. Two types of courses. One is an online course only, and the other is an integrated course consisting of an online and the in-person live course. Attendees of the Live Course must first successfully complete the Diagnostic Endoscopy: An Immersive Guide (online course) which provides the foundation for the in-person training course. Training covers flexible and rigid endoscope anatomy, handling, cleaning, laser physics, safety, laser lithotripsy, cystoscopy, rhinoscopy, bronchoscopy, upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy, laparoscopy and associated advanced procedures.
Onsite laboratories focus on maximizing practice with lectures. A mixture of dry, cadaveric and live animal labs is used to facilitate the mastery of presented materials, with the expectation that participants will be ready to perform endoscopy upon course completion.
This in-person training course includes 5 days, approximately 44 hours of onsite training. Attendees cultivate proficiency in flexible and rigid endoscopes, handling, cleaning, laser physics, safety, laser lithotripsy, cystoscopy, rhinoscopy, bronchoscopy, laparoscopy, upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy, and advanced procedures.

courses.title: Cant Walk or Wont Walk
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review common presentations of mixed orthopedic and neurologic conditions, in addition to awkward metabolic systemic disorders. This course will also highlight front limb and rear limb examination findings plus treatments options for non-ambulatory patients.

courses.title: Orthobiologics: The What and The How
courses.description: During this 1-hour webinar, faculty will review the application of biologics in veterinary medicine. Starting with a broad overview of what biologics are and the different types available, discuss joint injection technique, and bring everything together with case examples.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: 2026 ACVP/Davis-Thompson Foundation Pre-Meeting Workshop - Pathology of the Respiratory System
courses.description:
Course Description: Pathology of the respiratory system, especially of the interstitial lung diseases, creates considerable difficulty for diagnostic pathologists due to the complexity of lesions, overlapping histologic features of the many conditions that affect the respiratory tract, and development of new knowledge of these diseases. Our speakers will present a workshop based on their extensive experience in respiratory pathology which include authorship of book chapters and scholarly articles on respiratory diseases.
This meeting is suitable for veterinary students, interns, residents, graduate students and anatomic pathologists. The workshop will be organized into presentations and case-based interactive discussion with digital microscopy files available to registrants prior to the meeting. The presentations will focus on the diagnostic approach to diseases of the respiratory tract of domestic mammals.
Course Objectives: At the end of this workshop, participants will have the ability to outline the approach to and identify normal anatomy of the lung in domestic species, identify patterns of lung disease, and define the terminology associated with pulmonary pathology. Participants will also be introduced to mechanisms of disease in specific interstitial lung diseases and recognize/diagnose interstitial lung diseases specific to small and large animal species.
Attendees will review the anatomy of the respiratory system and to the patterns of diseases affecting the respiratory system. Focusing on interstitial lung diseases, they will develop insights into the diverse morphologic patterns of interstitial lung diseases, and differences in their pathogenesis and cause, followed by a review of specific interstitial lung diseases affecting companion and food-producing domestic mammals. Finally, there will be an interactive case-based discussion with digital microscopy files available to registrants prior to the workshop. These case-based discussions will be used to ill

courses.title: Ophthalmic Surgery
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will be presented as a lecture plus hands-on lab focusing on ophthalmic surgery for eyelid mass removal, laceration repair, entropion correction, and pocket imbrication for cherry eye. This course will include a review of surgical indications for these conditions, pre-operative testing, client communication strategies in preparation for the procedures, plus post-operative recommended care. The hands-on lab portion will feature step-by-step demonstrations on porcine cadaver eyes with eyelids for participants to practice surgical techniques. In addition, live patient surgical videos will be featured.

courses.title: TightRope or SwiveLock CCL Repair: Which do I choose?
courses.description: During this one-hour webinar, faculty review the indications and techniques for TightRope and SwiveLock CCL stabilization, discussing equipment, landmarks, and tips & tricks.

courses.title: THRIVE: mental health, relationship management and career development
courses.description: This 7-day continuing education focused on mental health and professional development. Delegates will be resident for 7 days at a 5* safari lodge in the Victoria Falls National Park, Zimbabwe, Africa. Here you can be immersed in nature with the goal of stepping out of your normal environment and developing new mental health, self-awareness, and relationship skills that will benefit career satisfaction, growth, and longevity. This course mixes retreat-style relaxation and safari experiences, with immersive and interactive teaching. The course runs with a maximum of 16 people at a time, for an exclusive and tailored experience. What you will learn: - The Enneagram: typing your personality, understanding opposite personalities, and how to use this to develop team relationships - Conflict management and embracing differences - Intruder syndrome and how to combat it - Self-awareness. how to combat stress - Burnout: why it happens and how to prevent it - Self-forgiveness: Techniques to prevent self-blame and utilise perceived failure to develop your career - Emotional IQ ACCOMMODATION Delegates will enjoy their own luxury lodge room with king-size bed (shared rooms can be accommodated) with cool luxurious white linen, large sweeping mosquito nets, warm evening lighting and safari chic design. Rooms are ensuite with showers as well as outdoor showers to enjoy the African night sky. Each room has its own private deck overlooking the river. LOCATION The lodge is set in the Victoria Falls National Park, a big 5 wildlife area. You can expect to be serenaded with calls of the wild at breakfast and supper, elephants trumpeting and lions roaring into the night. In the evening, you can enjoy sunsets igniting the horizon and then kicking back around the fire, under a sky of stars.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.provider: SIR JAMES DUNN ANIMAL WELFARE CENTRE, ATLANTIC VETERINARY COLLEGE, UNIVERSITY OF
courses.title: Sir James Dunn Animal Welfare Centre 2025 Webinar Series
courses.description: This webinar series will present participants with current knowledge about the care and welfare of small companion animals, with a focus on rabbits and rodents. Three experts in the field will discuss best practices for the care of these animals, including what we know about their natural behaviors and strategies that can be used to improve their affective states, such as proper housing and management. The webinar will also include information about common health problems in these animals, and ways to mitigate these challenges. The program will focus on the role of the veterinarian in providing care to these animals as well as guidance to their clients about how best to house and manage them.

courses.title: Maxillofacial Fractures in the Juvenile Skeleton - On Demand
courses.description: This presentation will go over the principles of maxillofacial trauma repair, with a specific focus on juvenile trauma cases. Case descriptions will highlight pertinent anatomy involved, imaging findings, and discuss the choices between invasive and non-invasive techniques.

courses.title: At the Intersection of Surgery and Regenerative Medicine: The Quest for Optimizing Musculoskeletal Sport Horse Injuries
courses.description: Complications are an unfortunate part of veterinary surgery. While the complication rate in most instances is quite low, it is still something the surgeon has to deal with. Complications affect not only the patient but also the surgery team, the animal care team, and the animal owners. This keynote lecture reviews a series of cases and the complications arising from them. This lecture focuses on how to discuss surgical complications with the surgery team and the owners.

courses.title: The Equine Spine On-demand
courses.description: The diagnosis and management of disease of the equine cervical and thoracolumbar spine has dramatically evolved in recent years. During this webinar, speakers discuss recent advances in imaging the cervical and thoracolumbar spine and how imaging findings relate to surgical case selection. The innovative intervertebral foraminotomy procedure and advances in cervical stabilization techniques are discussed through presentations and case discussion. This webinar also presents surgical options and outcomes for management of thoracolumbar pain.

courses.title: Pulmonary Hypertension: What Is It and Where Does It Come From
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review the pathophysiology, clinical signs, diagnosis, and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. This course will also include case-based examples to distinguish between pulmonary disease with hypertension and cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

courses.title: We Need to Talk: Resolving Case Complications With Communication Between Primary Care Veterinarians and Diplomates On-Demand
courses.description: Case complications happen and are often unavoidable. Collaboration between ACVS Diplomates and primary care veterinarians (PCV) is essential for addressing complications and maintaining ideal patient care. Consistent and clear communication among all members of the veterinary care team and clients is paramount to managing complications. This interactive session will present complications and work through how they can be managed by the Diplomate and the PCV communicating as a collaborative team to obtain the best results.

courses.title: Cracking the Cruciate Code: From Diagnosis to Treatment
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will provide an overview of the anatomy and pathophysiology of the cranial cruciate ligament plus feature physical exam findings associated with complete and partial tears. In addition to highlighting key points for client education, this course will review diagnostic approaches, radiographic interpretations, technique tips for extracapsular repairs, plus treatment options for cruciate ligament disease.

courses.title: Research Grant Application Workshop
courses.description: This instructional presentation contains a brief introductory segment and four distinct components (hypothesis and specific aims, background and preliminary studies, experimental approach, and statistical methods and references) focused on preparation of surgery resident and Diplomate proposals for funding consideration by the ACVS Foundation. Content is patterned after the publicly accessible instructions for ACVS grant proposals but in greater depth and detail. The presentation is intended to serve as a helpful tool to guide proposal preparation.

courses.title: Veterinarian of Record Relationship Training Course
courses.description: This course will explore how to establish and maintain a successful veterinarian of record relationship (VORR) between a licensed veterinarian and an animal welfare organization (AWO) for the benefit of shelter animals and both partners

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: Mammary Tumors in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: This program will discuss everyone's favorite topic: mammary tumors! This course will cover the histologic criteria of malignancy, established grading schemes for both canine and feline mammary tumors, and the current subclassifications. The final part of the course will present examples of real cases via scanned digital slides.

courses.title: Arthrodesis and Long Bone Fracture Repair On-Demand
courses.description: This seminar focuses on innovative approaches and current updated knowledge in the areas of arthrodesis/facilitated ankylosis and long bone fracture repair in the horse. Lectures cover topics including but not limited to carpal/tarsal/proximal interphalangeal/metacarpophalangeal arthrodesis along with metacarpal/tarsal and phalangeal fractures in racing and performance horses. Speakers discuss cutting edge approaches, surgical planning techniques, treatment challenges, and outcomes. A case-based panel discussion with audience participation encouraged provides valuable insight into the best practice for managing these challenging cases.

courses.title: The future of proactive veterinary care
courses.description:
What would you do for every patient if you had unlimited time? Most vets have an instinctive answer and almost no way to act on it. This session is about the technology that's finally closing that gap. Digitail CEO Sebastian Gabor and Dr. Laila Proenca lay out a vision for AI in veterinary medicine. Not scribes and summaries, but a complete proactive intelligence layer that pulls together PIMS data, pet parent app activity, and clinic communications to tell you in real time what every patient needs before they walk through the door. Anchored in fresh findings from the 2026 AAHA State of the Industry study and grounded in Dr. Proenca's own experience running this kind of system in her clinic, you'll see what proactive care actually looks like day-to-day: the conversations it enables, the cases it surfaces, and the membership and wellness models it makes possible for the first time.
Key Takeaways
- Understand how AI is evolving beyond documentation tools into proactive patient intelligence, and what that shift means for day-to-day clinic operations.
- Learn how integrating PIMS data, pet parent app activity, and clinic communications can surface patient needs before the appointment begins.
- See real-world evidence from a practitioner already running a proactive care model, anchored in findings from the 2026 AAHA State of the Industry study.
- Discover how proactive AI infrastructure enables membership and wellness plan models that were previously too operationally complex to sustain.

courses.provider: TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY OFFICE OF VETERINARY CONTINUING EDUCATION
courses.title: Veterinary Opioids: Texas Board Rules and Federal Laws
courses.description: This online module is designed to equip the participant with a basic understanding of opioid abuse and controlled substance diversion, as well as inventory recordkeeping and security requirements. The course meets the 2 hours of opioid training requirements of the Texas Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners (TBVME). Federal regulations concerning labeling, use, compounding, recordkeeping, and security of prescription of controlled drugs are addressed.

courses.title: Early Career Financial Planning: For Those Who Want to be Financially Free On-Demand
courses.description: The seminar focuses on providing veterinarians with actionable strategies to achieve financial freedom. Topics covered include: student debt, practice management, contract negotiations, mindset around money, investing, and overall physical and mental health. Attendees will leave with the baseline tools and resources needed to set themselves and their families up for success.

courses.title: Cardiac Emergencies in Veterinary Patients
courses.description: In this course, participants will learn how to triage and stabilize common cardiac emergent patients. Congestive heart failure in both cats and dogs will be discussed, as well as pericardial effusion, aortic thromboembolism and caval syndrome.

courses.title: Advanced Small Animal Laparoscopy On-Demand
courses.description: This hybrid laboratory will include¿a brief¿introduction¿to¿equipment,¿discussion¿of indications¿and¿contraindications¿for¿specific minimally¿invasive¿procedures,¿and instruction regarding¿abdominal¿procedures¿(intracorporeal gastropexy,¿herniorrhaphy, cholecystectomy,¿adrenalectomy, nephrectomy).¿

courses.title: We Need to Talk, Resolving Case Complications with Communication - On Demand
courses.description:
Surgical complications are an unavoidable part of practice, but the way they are discussed among all parties often determines whether a challenging case becomes a source of collaboration, conflict, or fractured trust. This interactive lecture uses real-world large and small animal surgical scenarios to explore the difficult conversations that arise among surgeons, primary care veterinarians, clients, and clinical teams. Rather than focusing on the technical details of each case, the session invites residents to step back from the clinician cap and examine the communication decisions that shape client perception, referral relationships, case continuity, and professional collegiality.
Residents in both large and small animal surgery will gain practical strategies for navigating situations when expectations diverge, outcomes are imperfect, or communication is delayed, incomplete, or misunderstood. Emphasis will be placed on using the ACVS Collaborative Relationship Communication Tool to proactively clarify roles, timelines, follow-up responsibilities, client messaging, and shared decision-making between the specialist and primary care veterinarian. By examining difficult cases through a communication lens, this lecture aims to help residents build the professional habits needed to preserve trust, reduce conflict, and improve patient outcomes through stronger teamwork.

courses.title: Anaesthesia of Exotic Animals: Part 2
courses.description: In this second instalment, Dr Sonya Miles BVSc CertAVP(ZM) CertAqV MRCVS expands on the practical aspects of anaesthetic management in exotic species. Building on foundational principles, this session explores maintenance anaesthesia, ventilation strategies, advanced monitoring, thermal support, and safe recovery techniques. Delegates will develop an understanding of species-appropriate anaesthetic depth assessment, airway management challenges, and common complications. The lecture also discusses pain recognition in prey species, fluid therapy, nutritional support, and the role of equipment such as incubators in achieving optimal outcomes. This session equips clinicians with the applied skills required to safely manage the entire anaesthetic period in a wide range of exotic taxa.

courses.provider: NORTH AMERICAN VETERINARY COMMUNITY (EASTERN STATES VETERINARY ASSOCIATION)
courses.title: VMX Virtual 2026
courses.description: This program is comprised of select content from VMX 2026 (live virtual program) that was presented live, and then converted to on-demand courses for 60 days after January 17th, 2026.

courses.title: Challenging Forelimb Cases On-Demand
courses.description: In this webinar, speakers discuss their approaches to forelimb lameness cases, which can often be difficult to localize. Discussion involves various diagnostic options and when to utilize each, as applied to specific cases provided by the speakers. Approximately 3-4 cases are shared.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Clinical Pathology Part 2: Liver, Proteins, Pancreas
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of serum biochemistry as it pertains to small animal clinical pathology, focusing on three primary organ systems: the liver, pancreas, and plasma proteins. Attendees gain practical insights into interpreting biochemical profiles, diagnosing underlying conditions, and applying these findings to clinical decision-making. This course features case-based discussions highlighting common and complex presentations in cats and dogs, with topics including hepatic dysfunction, portosystemic shunts, protein-losing enteropathy, and pancreatitis.

courses.title: Small Animal Clinical Pathology Part 5: Endocrine
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive review of diagnostic approaches to common endocrine disorders in small animals, focusing on diabetes mellitus, hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, hyperadrenocorticism, and hypoadrenocorticism. Attendees will gain hands-on case interpretation experience using clinical pathology data, diagnostic algorithms, and evidence-based tools for distinguishing between primary disease and concurrent illness.

courses.title: Gonadectomy in Dogs- Pros and Cons
courses.description: This program will discuss the pros and cons of gonadectomy in dogs.The surgeon will review sterilization options for female and male dogs and the literature on gonadectomy(primarily focusing on decreased risk of oncologic and orthopedic conditions when remaining hormonally intact) and will review how to pick a surgical option for your specific patient.

courses.title: Euthanasia & Hospice Services (Certificate Program Part 2)
courses.description: This program is a comprehensive course designed for veterinary professionals seeking to enhance their skills and knowledge in providing compassionate and effective end-of-life care for companion animals. This program, led by Dr. Kathleen Cooney, engages learners into modern best practices, including euthanasia techniques, palliative care, and communication strategies with pet owners. The introduction begins with reading the AAHA / IAAHPC's End of Life Care Guidelines to set the foundation of understanding and concepts at the core of practicing Hospice & Palliative Care in veterinary medicine. Euthanasia and Hospice Services (modules 1-8) covers in detail the clinical goals of our patients while addressing the emotional, social, and spiritual needs of the caregiver.

courses.title: Recognizing and Managing Feline Acromegaly as a cause of Insulin Resistant Feline Diabetes
courses.description: Feline diabetes mellitus (DM) is estimated to impact approximately 1 in 4 diabetic cats in North America. However, achieving treatment success appears challenging in a number of diabetic cats. Managing diabetic cats is not always straightforward. For many of these more difficult cases, what has been found is that the diabetes etipathogenesis is not necessrily type 2,, but a classificationof an underlying disease process referred to as "other specific types of diabetes." One such type of "other" is hypersomatotropism, which results in acromegaly. Feline acromegaly is characterized by excessive growth hormone secretionleading to a wide array of clinical signs caused by the hormone's effects on multiple organ systems. Utilizing a case based approach, this presentation will review the etiology and pathophysiology, history and clinical signs, diagnosis, and medical and nutritional management of insulin resistant diabetes resulting from feline acromegaly.

courses.title: Great Lakes Veterinary Conference (GLVC)
courses.description: This multi-day in-person veterinary conference brings together industry leaders and practitioners for an engaging mix of professional development, clinical education, and networking. Kicking off with an inspiring opening session by Dr. Betsy Charles, attendees will explore leadership, culture, and innovation in veterinary medicine. The program features concurrent tracks on oncology, preventive care, cytology, microbiology, hematology, and diagnostics led by renowned experts and supported by industry partners. In addition to hands-on workshops and in-depth lectures, participants can connect with peers during social events, receptions, and shared meals, creating a well-rounded experience focused on advancing both clinical skills and practice success.

courses.title: Canine Extraction Techniques I Laboratory
courses.description: This hands on introductory course is designed for the veterinarian wishing to learn or improve their basic dental extraction technique. Participants will be able to practice the using a high speed hand piece and extraction instruments. Participants will perform single and multi-rooted tooth extractions. Emphasis will be placed on sectioning of teeth, tissue handling, gingival flap preparation, and the use of bone graft materials. Incisors, maxillary canines and premolar teeth extraction techniques will be broken down step by step. Local nerve blocks will be discussed and the correct sites for placing those nerve blocks will be identified.

courses.title: Basic Dental Radiograph Interpretation
courses.description: Dental radiographs are an essential part of the oral examination. You are now taking diagnostic rads but what are you seeing? Learn how to properly position dental radiographs to identify the correct teeth. Understand what are normal findings vs. pathology. The basics of dental radiology interpretation will be presented along with a series of What is that? slides to help better understand dental radiology.

courses.title: Good Grief
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will provide an overview on grief theories and how they can be applied at various stages of the veterinary care process. In addition, this program will review specific strategies to use when working with clients through their grief process. (This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1184250.)

courses.title: Veterinary Dentistry Intensive: Hands-On In-Situ Workshop for Faster, More Effective Veterinarians.
courses.description: In-person learning workshop of essential veterinary Comprehensive Oral Health Assessment and Treatment (COHAT) in the dental suite. Participants shall receive interactive training in combination with classroom setting, case studies and hands-on application using cadaver heads and/or anesthetized patients if available to provide without risk to patient safety. Program also includes emphasis on essential tips with dental procedures to ease staff stressors while increasing efficiency and effectiveness. Small group limit of no more than ten (10) doctors to one (1) dental trainer provides intensive mentorship opportunities.

courses.title: Complications in Stifle Surgery. When reconstruction fails, how can we achieve success with total knee replacement? On Demand
courses.description: This presentation reviews possible failure after reconstructive surgeries and how total knee replacement can address those in select cases. The different total knee replacement implants available and expected outcome are presented. As well as case based discussion with experts in joint replacement focusing on stifle complications and revision with total knee replacement.

courses.provider: SIR JAMES DUNN ANIMAL WELFARE CENTRE, ATLANTIC VETERINARY COLLEGE, UNIVERSITY OF
courses.title: Sir James Dunn Animal Welfare Centre 2026 Webinar Series
courses.description: This webinar series will present participants with current knowledge about the care and welfare of small companion animals, with a focus on rabbits and rodents. Three experts in the field will discuss best practices for the care of these animals, including what we know about their natural behaviors and strategies that can be used to improve their affective states, such as proper housing and management. The webinar will also include information about common health problems in these animals, and ways to mitigate these challenges. The program will focus on the role of the veterinarian in providing care to these animals as well as guidance to their clients about how best to house and manage them.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: MICHIGAN MEDICAL RECORDS & VETERINARY LAW (1078-37548)
courses.description: This Michigan specific course has been approved by the Michigan Veterinary Medical Association to satisfy state continuing education license requirements related to medical records, and one hour related to state veterinary law and or federal or state controlled substance laws. *If you have already taken this course or need additional credits and/or more in-depth knowledge we also offer the following related CE topics: 10 Top Medical Record-Keeping Deficiencies; Client Consent & Communication; Medical Record-Keeping-Beyond the SOAP; Medical Record-Keeping for Controlled Substances and Prescribing Medications; and Medical Record-Keeping to Meet the Standard of Care. All of these offerings will on build this foundational course.

courses.title: Mastering the Medical Interview: Communication Skills for Accurate History, Trust, and Clinical Clarity.
courses.description: This continuing education course teaches veterinary professionals how to conduct a structured, efficient, and client-centered medical interview in the exam room. Participants will learn communication strategies that improve history-taking accuracy, uncover client concerns earlier, and create a collaborative tone for the rest of the visit. The course emphasizes practical use of open-ended and close-ended questions, reflective listening, empathy statements, signposting, and summarizing to improve interview flow and reduce missed information. Learners will apply a repeatable interview framework that strengthens client trust, supports better clinical reasoning, and improves adherence to diagnostic and treatment plans.

courses.title: Effective Prioritization
courses.description: This non-medical On Demand program will teach veterinary professionals who struggle with how to effectively prioritize their work, especially given the pace and changing nature of what we do. It will focus on how you can more effectively prioritize your day by doing the right things first, planning your work so you can do it well, being as efficient as you can with the time that you have. We know that you can't get more hours in the day, but after this program, you should be able to use those hours even better. You might even improve your work/life effectiveness!

courses.title: Lower Back Pain and Conservative Management of Lumbosacral Disease
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinarians will review the diagnosis and conservative management of lower back pain and lumbosacral disease in canine patients. This course will include common etiologies, physical examination techniques for differentiating spinal from orthopedic pain, and the role of biomechanics in spinal compression.

courses.title: Small Animal Electrolyte and Acid-Base Mastery: Certification Course
courses.description:
This comprehensive online training program encompasses a wide range of topics related to the physiology, diagnosis, and treatment of potassium, sodium, and acid-base disorders in small animal patients. It also provides a comprehensive exploration of traditional acid-base analysis, complemented by numerous practical case examples to facilitate skill development. The core of this course is composed of meticulously designed modules focusing on potassium, sodium, and acid-base management. Each module is thoughtfully structured with a series of concise 5-15 minute video lessons, followed by engaging case scenarios and interactive quizzes. As a part of this program, all participants will gain exclusive access to a sophisticated Excel-based calculator. This tool simplifies the calculation of potassium, sodium, phosphorous, and magnesium supplementation rates, in addition to enabling a thorough analysis of acid-base parameters. Enrolled learners will become part of the course community where they can engage in discussions and share insights on personal cases involving electrolyte and acid-base disorders, fostering collaborative learning and professional development.
Your bundle purchase includes everything you need to master small animal electrolyte and acid-base disorders:
- Lifetime access to 80 in-depth video lessons divided between 3 modules: Potassium, Sodium, and Acid-Base Disorders.
- Lifetime access to numerous real-life case scenarios.
- 2-year membership to the exclusive VETEMCRIT community platform.
- Excel-based electrolyte and acid-base calculator for enhanced productivity.
- Comprehensive electronic workbook (PDF) with the written course material for convenient learning
- 12.5 RACE-approved credits to advance your professional development and fulfill your license requirements.
- Certificate of completion to showcase your expertise.
- 7-day 100% Money Back Guarantee (No questions asked).

courses.title: QPR: Question, Persuade and Refer: Three Steps Anyone Can Learn To Help Prevent Suicide
courses.description: This program will provide veterinary professionals the QPR tool that aids in effective intervention when someone you know is suicidal or in a crisis situation. With a high prevalence of suicide in veterinary medicine it is critical that we have the education and resources to support our co-workers.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: VETERINARY ETHICS & LEADERSHIP
courses.description: The primary objective of this course is to enhance your ethical literacy. We will identify resources to support ethical decision-making; compare legal and ethical duties; and review case scenarios (to include euthanasia, prescribing medications and antibiotic stewardship, client-directed care and spectrum of care) to help inform emotionally intelligent strategies for problem-solving that decrease moral stress; strengthen veterinary leadership capabilities; and improve the well-being of veterinary professionals and their patients. VHMA Approved Course ID #20-48.

courses.title: Masterclass: Psychopharmacology
courses.description: Dr. Katrin Jahn, a double-board certified specialist in veterinary behaviour medicine, hosts this practical, case-based masterclass focusing on the recognition, assessment, and treatment of clinical behaviour cases that may include a pain component as part of their presentation. Four cases with different presentations will be examined, using Dr. Jahn's "7 Ms" treatment approach to give veterinary professionals a framework to use on their own patients to ensure that all angles have been addressed to support better outcomes. The underlying physiological and pathophysiological processes that contribute to these cases will be addressed, and evidence-based best practices and approaches that can make significant changes in these patients' outcomes will be considered. The masterclass is underpinned by physiology and neurobiochemistry and their respective pathologies, enabling attendees to make the connections between presentations, underlying causes, and treatment approaches.

courses.provider: SWINE MEDICINE EDUCATION CENTER AT IOWA STATE UNIVERSITY
courses.title: Antimicrobial Stewardship In Swine Medicine
courses.description: This course will serve as an in-depth examination of the five pillars of antimicrobial stewardship with a focus on the swine industry. Antimicrobial stewardship is increasingly important to both veterinary and human medicine. There is a heightened scrutiny of how these antimicrobials are used, combined with increased regulations on drug use and a sparcity of new drug production. Veterinarians will need skills to judiciously use antimicrobials to preserve their useage and prevent antimicrobial resistance. Therefore, the aim of this course is to review antimicrobial stewardship principles and provide the tools to carry them out in veterinary practice.

courses.title: Equine Massage Certification
courses.description: Therasage Equine Massage provides a highly educational opportunity for students to broaden their knowledge of equine massage, develop business skills that lead to a promising career path, and earn certification in Equine Massage to be able to gain employment.

courses.title: Flexible Gastrointestinal Endoscopy
courses.description: This two-day introductory GI endoscopy course will include 7 hours of lectures covering indications, basic technique, and disorders diagnosed via endoscopy and a total of 9 hours of laboratory time for key hands-on experience. Day one laboratory will use GI models and fresh cadavers to learn basic endoscopic manipulation, biopsy techniques, foreign body removal, and PEG tube placement. Day two laboratory will involve live dogs performing basic upper GI endoscopy to perfect manipulation skills. Bring your technician; they can attend lectures and individual training on endoscopic instrumentation and set up, biopsy management and assist during the laboratory.

courses.title: Small Animal Abdominal Surgery
courses.description: This course will focus on basic abdominal surgical procedures performed in general practice. A strong emphasis will be placed on basic surgical principles related to gastrointestinal surgery and urinary surgery. This course includes 4 hours of lecture and 12 hours of lab using fresh intestinal and canine cadavers. During the cadaver labs basic gastrointestinal surgery (gastrotomy, gastrectomy, gastropexy, enterotomy, enterectomy), cystotomy, partial cystectomy, urethrostomy and splenectomy will be demonstrated by instructors and then performed by participants. At the end of this course participants will be comfortable performing the techniques mentioned above.

courses.title: A Complete Intro to Bone Plating: Principles, Surgical Approaches, Stabilization of Common Diaphyseal Fractures & Autogenous
courses.description:
We get it, not all clients are able to accept a referral for fracture repair, but,
Are you tired of amputating limbs that you know you can save?¿

Are you interested in learning simple techniques designed for the general practitioner to stabilize the most common fractures seen in dogs and cats?¿¿¿
¿
This blended, online + hands-on, plating course is like NONE other!¿ If you are going to be successful with your fracture repairs, you do not want just SOME of the important principles, you want ALL of them and this is THE course to put you on right path right from the very start! courses.description: This two-day introductory GI endoscopy course will include 7 hours of lectures covering indications, basic technique, and disorders diagnosed via endoscopy and a total of 9 hours of laboratory time for key hands-on experience. Day one laboratory will use GI models and fresh cadavers to learn basic endoscopic manipulation, biopsy techniques, foreign body removal, and PEG tube placement. courses.title: Otitis Externa: How Cytology Can Unlock the Mystery
courses.description: Three cases of otitis externa in dogs are used to demonstrate the value of ear swab cytology. The technical details for obtaining good samples and the basics of slide analysis will be covered for both dogs and cats. Interpretation of cytology in combination with otoscopic and other dermatologic examination findings will be illustrated with each of the cases. And finally the role of ear swab cytology in antimicrobial stewardship will be discussed.

courses.title: Introduction to Small Animal Laparoscopy
courses.description: With just 2 veterinarians per lab station and LOTS of hands-on lab time, you are sure to develop your new skills rapidly! This course is for the veterinarian (& veterinary technician) interested in developing skills in minimally invasive abdominal organ biopsy, other diagnostics and surgical procedures. You will learn all about laparoscopic instrumentation, basic techniques and procedures so that you can make the most of your many laboratory experiences. You will develop your new skills on the laparoscopic trainer before progressing to cadaveric training that includes portal placement, tissue biopsy (liver, pancreas, kidney), cholecystocentesis, ovariectomy, cryptorchidectomy and basic laparoscopy-assisted techniques including intestinal biopsy, jejunostomy tube placement, gastropexy, and cystoscopic removal of bladder stones.

courses.title: Dietary Management: Recent Updates to a Classic Approach
courses.description: In this session, Dr. Adam Rudinsky, DACVIM reviews dietary approaches to vomiting and diarrhea management. Once a patient is diagnosed, how are we going to choose a diet? Should it be part of multi-modal management? Are there more effective and beneficial approaches? We will specifically focus on the application of paradigm shifting research published in the past few years which changes our approach in these patients. Join in to get a clinical update on the most effective treatment of vomiting and diarrhea.

courses.title: Feline Diabetes and the SGLT2-Inhibitor, Velagliflozin: Monitoring & Troubleshooting
courses.description: Using case study examples, this presentation will review monitoring and troubleshooting for a cat on a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor and how to address complications. We'll also discuss when and how to transition to traditional insulin therapy.

courses.title: 4 Tactics that Make Financial Failure Virtually Impossible
courses.description: When a veterinarian starts the doctorate journey, the primary concern is care for animals and others, and money is not the motivation. However, once out of school and practicing as an associate or practice owner, the reality becomes obvious that personal financial success is the only way a veterinarian can stay in the game of helping animals and others. The more financial success, the more help can be provided. However, there are barriers and pitfalls to be aware of along the journey that make financial success seem impossible. What if every veterinarian knew how to handle to financial problems proactively. The truth is, nearly every problem can be predicted to some degree and planned for to make financial failure virtually impossible for a veterinarian.

courses.title: The Importance of Hypertension in Proteinuria in Dogs and Cats with CKD
courses.description: Systolic hypertension and renal proteinuria are common complications of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in dogs and cats, and both are associated with progressive loss of nephrons. Control of these complications can lead to improved quality of life and prolonged survival. Angiotensin receptor blockers are the current treatment of choice for hypertension and proteinuria in both dogs and cats.

courses.title: From Chaos to Control: The Financial Reset Every Practice Owner Needs
courses.description:
Private healthcare practice owners often experience strong practice growth while still feeling uncertain about their personal financial progress. This educational session examines common financial challenges faced by practice owners, including cash flow unpredictability, rising expenses, debt management, and the difficulty of coordinating business and household financial decisions.
Participants will explore how financial disorganization and disconnected decision-making between the practice and the household can create inefficiencies that impact long-term financial stability. The session introduces a structured framework for organizing financial information, integrating practice and household financial planning, and establishing measurable financial indicators that support informed decision-making.
Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how to evaluate their current financial structure, identify potential inefficiencies, and apply practical principles that support improved financial clarity, organization, and long-term planning.

courses.title: Words Matter: How Language Shapes Pet Obesity Care, Compliance, and Outcomes
courses.description: Effective obesity care in companion animals depends as much on our words as on our medical plans. This session translates current evidence on implicit weight bias, stigma, and client communication into practical steps veterinary teams can apply immediately. Attendees will learn why medical framing and pet-first language improve acceptance and adherence, how to differentiate overweight, pre-clinical obesity, and clinical obesity, and how to shift conversations from scale numbers to body condition and body composition. We will review research linking obesity to reduced quality of life and the improvements seen with even modest fat loss, outline a step-weight-loss method that sets realistic timelines and targets for dogs and cats, and discuss when and how to use visual aids, BCS images, and basic diagnostics to personalize care. The course closes with ready-to-use phrases, communication templates, and team roles that reduce blame, normalize the challenge of weight loss, and celebrate small wins. The goal is a consistent, stigma-free approach that strengthens trust, supports behavior change, and improves health outcomes for pets and families.

courses.title: Stem Cell Therapy for Oral Diseases
courses.description: This lecture will review the normal oral immunology in dogs and cats and discuss how oral dysbiosis and several oral conditions result in immune dysregulation. The potential opportunity for stem cell therapy in these conditions will be discussed. Oral conditions to be reviewed include feline chronic gingivostomatitis, periodontitis and aggressive periodontitis, gingivitis and early onset gingivitis, canine ulcerative chronic stomatitis, and oral cancers.

courses.title: A Fresh Perspective: a discussion on feeding fresh
courses.description: This course provides veterinary professionals with a balanced, evidence-based look at fresh pet food diets compared to fresh-homemade and traditional dry food. Topics include a review of pet food safety; effective strategies for navigating popular nutrition trends; the practical benefits of fresh feeding; and key considerations for tailoring to a patient's needs. Attendees will leave equipped to objectively counsel clients on fresh versus dry feeding options.

courses.title: Practical Dermatology for the Every Day Veterinary Professional Part 2
courses.description: Step inside a real-world dermatology practice and experience how dermatologists approach ear and skin disease--from diagnostics to treatment decisions- in a dynamic, case-based format. This interactive CE session brings cytology to life, breaking down practical workflows, common pitfalls, and how to confidently translate findings into targeted therapy. Drs. Julia Miller, Joya Griffin and Jeff Tinsley share real world clinical cases with you in real time. Learn how you can improve compliance, outcomes while practicing antimicrobial stewardship. Designed for the entire veterinary team, this program delivers key takeaways you can immediately implement to elevate patient care and client communication. If you want to sharpen your diagnostic skills, streamline your treatment protocols, and stay ahead in dermatology, this is a session you don't want to miss! Welcome to "Inside the Clinic!"

courses.title: How to Expedite Your Retirement Goals in 10 Years or Less
courses.description: Many Veterinarians delay serious retirement planning while focusing on running and growing their businesses or being a valuable associate in a practice. Unfortunately, this often leads to inefficiencies, missed opportunities, and financial uncertainty as they approach their desired exit timeline. In this webinar attendees will learn how to take control of their financial future by identifying the right metrics to monitor, correcting operational inefficiencies, and aligning business income with personal wealth goals. This program provides practical financial strategies tailored to the unique circumstances of private practice owners, with a focus on optimizing cash flow, protecting profitability, and creating a sustainable plan for long-term success.

courses.title: Alternative Modalities in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: The use of alternative therapies have always been divided by an eastern versus western perspective, with some veterinarians being identified as an integrative utilizing theories and protocols from both areas of medical practice. With the increasing awareness of the intrinsic role of the gut microbiome on patient health and the ongoing concern of antimicrobial resistance, veterinarians are searching for alternative science based modalities. Pharmacognosy is the study of medicines or crude drugs produced from natural sources such as plants, microbes, and animals. While this may include drugs like morphine, the use of microbes has become a staple of animal health through the use of probiotics. Veterinary professionals may use this research to improve patient health without the use of conventional medications and therapies. This panel will discuss alternative therapies they have found effective based on the panels advanced training, experience, and research in alternative therapies.

courses.title: Rewriting Practice Workflow Technology Solutions for Short-Staffed Hospitals
courses.description: Veterinary practices continue to face unprecedented staffing shortages that impact efficiency, client service, and overall team well-being. This session will explore how thoughtful workflow redesign combined with technology solutions can help hospitals operate more effectively with limited staff. Participants will gain insights into practical, non-commercial strategies and tools that support communication, scheduling, medical recordkeeping, client interactions, and team collaboration. By leveraging technology and rethinking traditional processes, practices can reduce administrative burdens, increase efficiency, and create more sustainable work environments during staffing challenges.

courses.title: Fetch Nashville on Demand
courses.description: This online non-interactive distance education program offers learners a wide array of medical and nonmedical continuing education options. Learners will gain a comprehensive understanding of the principles, techniques, and best practices across various veterinary disciplines. They will be equipped with the knowledge to accurately diagnose, treat, and manage a wide range of conditions, ensuring improved patient outcomes and advancing their clinical skills. Leaners are expected to receive actionable insights into both common and complex veterinary issues, emphasizing evidence-based approaches and practical applications that can immediately enhance clinical practice.

courses.title: Itchy and I Won't Eat That! Navigating Feline Dermatoses in the Picky Eater
courses.description: This program will cover the ins and outs of navigating the cat diet trial. From case selection (both owner and patient) to diet selection to what to do with the finicky feline palate, you will leave feeling confident about how to approach these cases.

courses.title: K9 & Kitty in the Coalmine? Dogs & Cats as sentinels for human infectious disease risk
courses.description:
This case-based session will summarize key clinical aspects of tick-borne and GI parasite infectious agents of veterinary and One Health concern- plus inform on the ability of human's 4-legged best friends (dogs and cats) to act as sentinels for human exposure risk to parasites. Recent peer-reviewed literature, and evidence- and expert-based guidelines, will be discussed.
By the end of the session participants should feel comfortable and confident facing off against these increasingly common infectious diseases, and well-equipped with expert- and evidence-based resources to assist with case management, prevention, and pet-owner communication, along with addressing One Health concerns.

courses.title: TREATING DIABETES IN DOGS AND CATS: How to get started on the right foot
courses.description: The treatment of diabetes in dogs and cats is complex and requires a great deal of patience. Many presentations about diabetes focus on the long term treatment and monitoring of our patients. As owner survey's have confirmed that the first few weeks of treatment can make or break an owner's wiliness to continue treatment. This presentation will focus on the beginning of treatment instead with the goal of leaving attendees confident that they will be able to lead owners smoothly into the treatment of this complex disease.

Learners will gain a comprehensive understanding of the principles, techniques, and best practices across various veterinary disciplines. They will be equipped with the knowledge to accurately diagnose, treat, and manage a wide range of conditions, ensuring improved patient outcomes and advancing their clinical skills. Learners are expected to receive actionable insights into both common and complex veterinary issues, emphasizing evidence-based approaches and practical applications that can immediately enhance clinical practice. courses.title: Mastering the Money Side of Your Exit Strategy: The Science of Practice Valuation
courses.description: Most practice owners assume that when they're ready to sell, the numbers will speak for themselves. The truth? Your financial independence after the sale depends on far more than what a buyer offers - it depends on how you've planned, structured, and protected your exit. The exit planning starts earlier than you think. Eric Mill will unpack the financial blind spots that cause practice owners to settle for deals that don't truly secure their future. Whether you're 2 years or 10 years away from selling, you'll gain the clarity and confidence to align your practice value with your long-term wealth goals - and walk away on your terms, not the buyer's.

courses.title: Non-Pharmaceutical Treatment of Osteoarthritis
courses.description: Have you ever been frustrated when treating a chronic OA patient when pharmaceuticals are not enough or contraindicated? Is OA preventable in at-risk patients? This presentation will focus on nutraceutical use in OA cases and alternative strategies for preventing and managing osteoarthritis (OA) in cats and dogs,. The most current evidence for these strategies will be presented.

courses.title: Safety Shows Respect: OSHA compliance as a way to boost morale and bond teams
courses.description: In addition to a requirement by law, OSHA training signals to team members that their wellbeing matters and that employees are valuable. Done regularly, it can be both informational and inspirational as it fosters stronger relationship between leaders and team members while simultaneously keeping employees safe from harm. Safety training is proven to lower accidents and to address rising concerns by both AAHA and OSHA that veterinary professionals need more focused attention on safety.

courses.title: HIRING RIGHT THE FIRST TIME (637-35354)
courses.description: The lecture is 1 hour and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on hiring the right staff for a veterinary practice. The speaker includes information about checking references, interview styles, and improving the application process.

courses.title: Stem Cell Therapy for Dermatological Diseases
courses.description:
The skin is a complex immune organ whose function depends on the integrated performance of the epidermal barrier, innate and adaptive immune cells, and a resident microbiome. Disruption of any one of these components destabilizes the others, and most dermatological diseases reflect coordinated failure of this immune-barrier-microbiome triad.
Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and their secretome are uniquely suited to address these immune-driven processes because they act simultaneously on all three axes. Multiple stem cell delivery routes have been explored for dermatological diseases. The strongest veterinary evidence base exists for canine atopic dermatitis and chronic wound management; however several other conditions may show promise based on human and rodent data.
This lecture will review potential stem cell therapy applications in veterinary dermatological diseases.

courses.title: The Oral Microbiome across Oral Sites in Cats with Chronic Gingivostomatitis, Periodontal Disease, and Tooth Resorption Compa
courses.description: Feline chronic gingivostomatitis (FCGS) remains a poorly understood clinical condition with significant impact on the quality of life of affected cats. An understanding of the pathogenesis of this inflammatory disease will enable the development of improved and targeted therapeutics beyond full-mouth extractions. Here, we collected sterile noninvasive plaque samples at ten distinct sites within the oral cavity in cats with FCGS (n =12), healthy cats (n =9), or cats with other oral conditions (n =11). We used 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V1-V9) to profile bacteria in the oral microbiome. We found that the microbiomes of cats with FCGS were distinct from those of healthy cats at multiple oral sites, indicating that dysbiosis is present throughout the oral cavity. The microbiomes of cats varied depending on their oral diagnoses, confirming that the various dental diseases impact the microbiome in different ways. Lastly, microbiome data obtained from swabs of the oral cavity were similar to those obtained using endodontic paper point plaque samples, suggesting this approach as another valuable method of sampling. Given these additional insights, future studies can focus on targeted therapeutics so that extraction of healthy teeth will no longer be the standard of care for this challenging condition.

courses.title: Evolution of Pet Food formats and their impact on Pet Nutrition and Health
courses.description: In the past there were basically two types of pet food formats, dry and canned, made by a few known pet food manufacturers. This presentation will address today's complex diversity in pet foods formats, new processing methods, new preservation systems and variety of nutritional compositions. New research is appearing comparing how traditional and new product formats can impact pets' health and nutrition. Understanding the differences between pet formats will help veterinary professional manage nutritional risks better, provide information and facts to clients and make sound dietary decisions for the benefit of the pet.

courses.title: Nutrition and Stem Cell Therapy in Dogs and Cats: Optimizing for Better Outcomes
courses.description: Stem cell therapy is an exciting part of regenerative veterinary medicine, but the patient's nutritional and metabolic state may influence how well these therapies perform. This webinar reviews the biologic links between nutrition, inflammation, microbiome function, and stem cell behavior, with a practical focus on dogs and cats. Participants will learn how veterinary teams can help support the patient's biological environment before, during, and after regenerative treatment, while exploring where the scientific evidence is well established and where it continues to emerge.

courses.provider: AMERICAN KENNEL CLUB CANINE HEALTH FOUNDATION
courses.title: Environmental chemicals and lymphoma risk in dogs
courses.description: Lymphoma, a cancer of the lymphoid cells of the immune system, is one of the most frequently diagnosed cancers in dogs. While genetic mutations are known contributors, environmental exposures are also suspected to play a role in disease development. With support from the AKC Canine Health Foundation, researchers at the University of Wisconsin, Madison explored how genetic susceptibility and exposure to environmental chemicals, such as water chlorination byproducts and proximity to industrial facilities, may influence lymphoma risk, particularly in Boxers. This webinar will review their findings, including key insights on glutathione-S-transferase (GST) enzyme function and the geographic factors linked to higher lymphoma incidence in dogs. The results contribute to a better understanding of cancer risk and inform future strategies for prevention.

courses.title: The Role of JAK Inhibitors in Treating Pruritus Associated with Allergic and Atopic Dermatitis in Canines
courses.description: This podcast will cover the causes of allergic and atopic dermatitis as well as outline various treatment options available on the market. We will take a close look at various treatment solutions based on the presentation of symptoms in an individual dog.

courses.title: Creating a Calmer Clinic
courses.description: In this 1-hour virtual webinar the audience will be walked through a general practice and demonstrate the value of Reducing Fear, Anxiety and Stress with a Calmer Clinic atmosphere. Begins by reviewing the prevalence of fear, anxiety, and stress for many patients and pet parents today at veterinary hospitals, as well as the ongoing mental health challenges for veterinary professionals. Attendees will learn how practical and appropriate use of pheromones and other stress-reducing techniques within veterinary clinics can lower fear and anxiety scores in patients, pet parents, and veterinary teams. Specific examples will be given within each section for logistical placement, workflow implementation, and expected outcomes. The moderator will tour the hospital and interview key stakeholders within the practice.

courses.title: Beyond What the Eye Can See, Magnification and Lighting for Veterinary Dentistry
courses.description: Providing professional dental care requires a sharp sense of vision during the procedure. Attempting this without magnification and proper lighting hinders our ability to deliver the necessary level of care, preventing us from accurately observing our actions and increasing the risk of causing harm through poor head, neck, and back postures. This lecture aims to outline the essential factors for making informed decisions about purchasing and using magnification and personal lighting systems for professional veterinary dentistry, as well as the risks associated with poor postures and inadequate lighting.

courses.title: Dog Longevity 101: Aging Fundamentals That Every Vet Should Know
courses.description: This course will cover the basic elements of aging biology in dogs, focusing on mechanisms that lead to aging-associated disease and potential targets for therapeutic interventions. We will explore the concept of aging as a modifiable risk factor for common diseases occurring in older dogs and look at existing and future preventive medicine options that can slow the aging process and extend healthy lifespan by delaying disease and preserving good quality of life.

courses.title: Setting calves up for success! - Scours prevention from management to vaccine and specific polyclonal antibody strategies.
courses.description: This course will be an overview of current challenges when it comes to neonatal calf diarrhea as well as strategies of how to prevent scours. This course will cover best management practices, vaccine strategies as well as the use of specific polyclonal antibodies. The course will also describe in detail the unique characteristics polyclonal antibodies (maternal bovine colostrum antibodies) have and why they are an effective way to increase immunity in the neonatal calf. The course will support claims with peer reviewed published data as well as internal data.

courses.title: Sit, Stay, Learn - An Introduction to Canine Behavior
courses.description: This program will cover the basics of canine behavior. Through a thorough overview, the learner will gain a deeper understanding of how to apply the basics of canine behavior in general practice and home environment settings. This will allow the learner to promptly recognize and prioritize behavioral situations and prepare appropriate behavioral modifications. The learner will have a general understanding of how to approach certain cases and provide initial supportive care.

courses.title: Flip the Script: How an Online Pharmacy Strengthens Your Practice
courses.description: In this informative webinar, Dr. Caitlin DeWilde explores how integrating an online pharmacy can be a powerful tool for veterinary practices. The session addresses how online pharmacies can work alongside traditional in-clinic pharmacy services, driving higher engagement, improving client satisfaction, and enhancing revenue. Dr. DeWilde will cover the challenges of competing with big-box retailers and how marketing and streamlined workflows can effectively differentiate your pharmacy services. By the end of the session, participants will understand the importance of integrating an online pharmacy to elevate both the client experience and the practice's business model.

courses.title: Chat FecalGPT? Using AI For Revolutionary Parasite Diagnostics and Prevention
courses.description: In this 30-minute live presentation, Dr. Natalie Marks will discuss how practices can utilize artificial intelligence to improve parasite diagnostics and prevention. It will begin with an overview of the sensitivity of more traditional fecal floats and centrifugation and how this can cause clinical disease in our patients and increase the risk of zoonotic transfer. We will then shift to what artificial intelligence is in association with parasite diagnostics. We will close with the benefits of AI fecal technology, including improved efficiency, cost savings, improved work culture, precise results and treatment, and financial stability for the practice.

courses.title: Tumor microbiome in domestic cats affected by oral squamous cell carcinoma
courses.description:
Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) accounts for a clinically significant proportion of feline tumors and is associated with late diagnosis, limited therapeutic options, and a poor prognosis. Despite growing recognition of feline OSCC as a potential spontaneous animal model for human head and neck cancer, critical gaps remain in understanding its underlying pathogenesis. In particular, the contribution of the oral microbiome (a factor increasingly implicated in cancer development and progression in humans) has not been well characterized in cats.
This presentation aims to define the oral microbial landscape associated with feline OSCC and compare it to that of clinically healthy cats. Oral swab samples were collected from multiple sites in cats diagnosed with OSCC, including tumor surfaces and distant clinically normal mucosa, as well as from the gingival margin of healthy control cats. Full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing was used to characterize microbial composition, diversity, and community structure.The study demonstrated that feline OSCC is associated with marked oral microbial dysbiosis, including reduced alpha diversity, distinct beta-diversity clustering, and consistent taxonomic shifts relative to healthy controls. These findings provide the first comprehensive characterization of oral microbiome alterations in feline OSCC and establish a critical foundation for future mechanistic studies.
By elucidating microbial changes associated with feline oral cancer, this study strengthens the relevance of feline OSCC as a spontaneous translational model for human head and neck cancer and opens new avenues for biomarker discovery, early detection strategies, and microbiome-targeted interventions.

courses.title: Program Title: The Heart of the Matter: Managing complex congestive heart failure
courses.description: This lecture will review management of congestive heart failure secondary to common cardiac diseases in dogs and cats. The lecture will also peel back the curtain on why that twice a day dosing of oral furosemide is no longer managing your patient's advanced heart failure signs and some new medications/therapies that may be more effective.

courses.title: Unlocking the Potential of Blood Microbiome for Enhanced Prevention and Diagnosis in Cats and Dogs
courses.description:
Recent advances in microbiome research have unveiled a new frontier in veterinary medicine. Blood, as well as urine and other body tissues, have been traditionally considered to be sterile environments but recent findings are suggesting that they can be populated by microbes. "Unlocking the Potential of Blood Microbiome for Enhanced Prevention and Diagnosis in Cats and Dogs," presents cutting-edge insights and practical applications for veterinarians.
This webinar will commence by elucidating the fundamental principles underlying the blood microbiome, exploring its composition, dynamics, and significance in and significance in prevention and diagnosis of diseases. Through a comprehensive review of current literature and ongoing research endeavors, attendees will gain an understanding of how alterations in the blood microbiome can serve as early indicators of various pathologies. Moreover, it will showcase pioneering methodologies for profiling the blood microbiome, providing a less invasive alternative for detecting gut inflammation. Attendees will acquire valuable insights into sample collection protocols and data interpretation strategies tailored specifically for studying the blood microbiome in cats and dogs.
This lecture underscores the translational potential of blood microbiome research, elucidating how insights gleaned from preclinical studies can be translated into clinical practice to enhance preventive care, refine diagnostic approaches, and optimize treatment modalities for companion animals.
In summary, the webinar will offer a unique opportunity to explore the frontier of veterinary microbiome research, empowering attendees to harness the transformative potential of the blood microbiome in advancing feline and canine healthcare.

courses.title: CONTROLLED SUBSTANCES 101: HOW & WHY YOU MUST COMPLY! 1 HOUR COMPREHENSIVE OVERVIEW (1356-36182)
courses.description: Controlled Substances 101: How & Why You Must Comply! one hour course is an intensive recordkeeping overview of the DEA's controlled substance regulations that impact the primary care, specialty, emergency, urgent care, equine, relief and mobile veterinary practices every day.

courses.title: Microscopic Heroes: Innovative Probiotics for Happier Guts
courses.description: As our understanding of the gut microbiome evolves, so do the therapeutic tools available to veterinarians. This webinar dives into the exciting world of innovative microbiome therapies and their potential to transform gut health in veterinary patients, including Saccharomyces boulardii, bacteriophages, and microbial cocktails. Learn how these cutting-edge microbiome modulation therapies influence the gut microbiome, improve digestive health, and open new doors for treating gastrointestinal and metabolic disorders in veterinary patients.

courses.title: Podcast: Tick Tidbits: Ticking off the 5 W's on These Tiny Troublemakers
courses.description:
Ticks pose a significant health risk to companion animals, both as blood-feeding parasites and as vectors for numerous pathogens. Over the past few decades, tick populations have expanded and intensified due to factors such as increased globalization, greater movement of humans and animals, and climate change. In the United States, common tick species - including the blacklegged tick, lone star tick, American dog tick, and brown dog tick - have the potential to transmit a range of bacterial, protozoal, and viral pathogens.
Serological data indicate that tick-borne pathogens are a persistent challenge for dogs, with U.S. canines frequently testing positive for agents of anaplasmosis, Lyme disease, and ehrlichiosis. Many of these same ticks and pathogens also pose a public health risk, as the tick species that commonly bite dogs can also transmit these same pathogens to humans. As a result, dogs can serve as valuable sentinels for tick-borne disease risks of their human families.
Despite awareness of the risks ticks pose to pets, ticks are often and easily overlooked. Given that ticks are a year-round threat in most regions, annual testing and the routine use of fast-acting tick control products play a critical role in protecting pet health by killing ticks and reducing pathogen transmission risk.

courses.title: Beyond the Bite: Transmission, Testing, and Treatment of Tick-Borne Infections in Dogs
courses.description: This presentation reviews current data on time to transmission of tick-borne infections in dogs. Feeding by common hard ticks is complex, and each tick requires several days to complete the feeding process. We will review current understandings of the mechanism of transmission for different tick-borne pathogens of dogs, including Borrelia burgdorferi, Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Ehrlichia spp., Rickettsia spp., and Babesia spp., and discuss studies designed to determine minimum transmission times and the effect of acaricides on this process. We will also go over testing strategies for canine tick-borne infections and strategies to effectively protect dogs from ticks and tick-borne diseases.

courses.title: Probing into parasites and protection
courses.description: This program will cover common myths related to parasites and their prevention and treatment in dogs and cats. Discussion will include common misconceptions, hurdles to compliance, updates on prevalence, and the impact of parasites persisting post-treatment.

courses.title: Feline Fine: The Value of Wellness Testing and Parasite Prevention in Cats
courses.description: In this podcast, Dr. Michelle Evason will discuss topics related to spectrum of care and feline care, and practical tips for communicating with pet owners about these topics.

courses.title: Satisfying Diet Trials: Improving Client Education on Food Allergies
courses.description: If only it were as easy as submitting a test to know which foods a pet is allergic to. Because reliable serum tests for food allergies have not been developed and because adverse food reactions are chronic and frustrating, veterinarians must partner with pet owners to successfully complete an elimination diet trial to rule out, diagnose, and manage this lifelong condition. Decreasing a pet owner's fear, anxiety and stress surrounding diet trials through communication and education can make a world of difference for the whole family's quality of life in just two months. This discussion will provide veterinarians and support staff with an understanding of food allergies, elimination diet trials, and communication tools to successfully partner with clients in diagnosing and managing food allergic pets.

courses.title: How to use IRIS Kidney Guidelines in practice
courses.description: This presentation will review the latest IRIS Staging information and published veterinary research focused on chronic kidney disease (CKD). Patient management involves more than medications alone. The benefits of incorporating targeted nutritional support as part of the CKD patient's management plan will be discussed. Diet options that can best manage the changes in kidney function as well as strategies to introduce nutritional support intervention to your CKD patients will be shared. Participants will access a comprehensive list of recommended commercial diets and insight into specific diet similarities and differences which will assist you in making patient-appropriate diet recommendations.

courses.title: Communicating choices: Supporting informed decisions in veterinary emergencies
courses.description: Whether you practice in a general, urgent, or emergency setting, you undoubtedly see pets presenting for unexpected health problems. Research suggests that 1 in 3 pet families would struggle to pay for an unexpected veterinary bill of $500 or less. At the same time, the cost of care continues to rise as pet families face economic uncertainty leading many to delay care or make difficult decisions under stress. But how do we really know what the options are, and how can we discuss the trade-offs as we offer treatment and diagnostic choices across a range from basic to advanced? We'll also explore ways to incorporate financial options that help make care more accessible without compromising patient outcomes.

courses.title: Skin Health At The Gut-Skin Axis: Development And Clinical Application Of Skin Rescue For Atopic Dermatitis In Cats And Dogs
courses.description:
Atopic dermatitis (AD) in cats and dogs is a common, multifactorial disease characterized by immune dysregulation, barrier dysfunction, and recurrent microbial imbalance. While traditional management strategies focus on anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory therapies, emerging research highlights the critical role of the gut microbiome in the onset, progression, and recurrence of inflammatory skin conditions.
This session provides a comprehensive overview of the scientific rationale, research, and formulation strategy behind Skin Rescue, an innovative supplement designed to act at the gut-skin axis to support patients with AD and other inflammatory, microbiome-associated dermatologic conditions.
Attendees will explore how coordinated support of gut barrier function, immune regulation, and oxidative balance can disrupt self-perpetuating inflammatory cycles and shift patients toward long-term skin stability.
Key clinical and scientific research informing the development of Skin Rescue will be reviewed to illustrate how targeted microbiome modulation may reduce pruritus, improve skin condition, and support long-term management of allergic dermatitis. The session will also provide practical guidance on integrating Skin Rescue into multimodal treatment plans alongside conventional therapies, including corticosteroids, biologics, and dietary management.

courses.title: Inside the Itchy Dog: A Real-World, Team-Based Dermatology Approach
courses.description:
This pending RACE approval CE session is an immersive, clinic-based program inviting attendees into a real-world dermatology setting (Dr Andrew Rosenberg and team) to explore a comprehensive, team-driven approach to the diagnosis and management of canine pruritus. Filmed at Animal Dermatology Clinic in Wayne, New Jersey, this educational program will follow the patient journey from the front desk to diagnosis and treatment, offering insights from client service representatives (CSRs), veterinary technicians, a board-certified veterinary dermatologist, and even the pet owner.
Through expert interviews, practical demonstrations, and case-based discussions, this program will focus on the implementation of a multimodal, diagnostic-first strategy for managing chronic dermatologic cases. Viewers will walk away with actionable tips on utilizing the dermatologic database, communicating more effectively with clients, maximizing technician involvement, and incorporating new therapeutic innovation including Zenrelia into clinical practice.

courses.title: The Gut-Brain Axis and its Relevance to Canine Cognitive Dysfunction
courses.description: There is increasing evidence that the gut microbiota is involved in the function and dysfunction of the brain.
