Dysbiosis, or an abnormal percentage of pathogenic gut bacteria, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of human Alzheimer's disease (AD). Canine cognitive dysfunction (CCD) is the dog version of human AD, having similar pathologic features. The gastrointestinal system is in constant contact with the brain via several conduits, collectively referred to as the gut-brain axis. There is evidence in rodent AD models and a few small human AD clinical trials, that correcting or improving dysbiosis can lead to improved cognitive function. This presentation will provide an overview of the gut-brain axis in health and disease. In addition, the potential role of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in the treatment of CCD will be discussed, including case examples.

courses.title: Money Talks: How to Have Better Cost Conversations and Improve Access to Care
courses.description: "What are my options, doc?" Whether you practice in a general, urgent, or emergency setting, you undoubtedly serve pet families concerned about the cost of veterinary care. Research suggests that 1 in 3 pet families would struggle to pay for an unexpected veterinary bill of $500 or less, making it more important than ever for veterinary teams to adapt the ways they approach conversations with clients about the cost of care. Using clinical case examples, including conditions like lameness that are often seen several times per day in both the ER and general practice, this session will help teams effectively set clear client expectations and successfully navigate financial conversations. Attendees will gain practical strategies to prepare pet families for healthcare costs, set realistic expectations for treatment options, and empower clients to make informed decisions that align with their goals and resources.

courses.title: A Fresh Perspective on Human Grade Pet Food Manufacturing and Safety
courses.description: This continuing education program provides veterinarians with a clear, science-based overview of fresh pet food, including how it is manufactured, regulated, and differentiated from other formats. It equips clinicians to confidently interpret safety, nutrition, and labeling claims so they can guide client conversations with accuracy and practical relevance.

courses.title: Updates on FIC: Practical Approaches to Diagnosis and Care
courses.description: Feline idiopathic cystitis (FIC) is the most common cause of feline lower urinary tract (LUT) signs. Despite a presentation primarily associated with LUT signs, FIC represents a health condition that involves more than the urinary bladder, linking the nervous system, adrenal system, husbandry practices, and the environment in which the cat lives. In this seminar, we will outline strategies to augment FIC diagnosis and explore how to identify key triggers for FIC. Attendees will gain an understanding of basic feline essential needs and how correcting deficiencies in husbandry practices and the environment can contribute to better disease management.

courses.title: Practical Dietary Solutions for Chronic Enteropathy in Dogs: A Case-Based Discussion
courses.description: Gastrointestinal disorders are highly prevalent in veterinary practice. This case management-focused presentation will delve into the complexities of diagnosing and managing these conditions in dogs, emphasizing the importance of a structured, patient-centered approach. We will discuss case assessment techniques and diagnostic strategies including localizing the problem within the gastrointestinal system, relevant workup, and a "multi-modal" treatment approach. The session will highlight appropriate diet selection and nutritional management including diet trials and supplements that can be tailored to the individual dog. In addition, we will examine the impact of microbiome health on patient outcomes, including the role of antibiotics and their effects on gut flora. The goal of the presentation is to provide actionable insights and strategies to optimize case management, client communications and improve the health and quality of life for dogs with gastrointestinal disorders.

courses.title: Optimizing Value in Multi-Doctor Veterinary Practice Transitions
courses.description: This educational webinar examines the complex factors involved in valuing and selling multi-doctor (2+ DVM) veterinary practices with annual revenues between $2-$10 million. Participants will explore proven approaches to practice valuation, financial optimization, and transition planning. The program will cover current valuation methodologies, strategies for enhancing practice profitability, risk assessment and mitigation in practice sales, and critical factors to be aware of in the negotiation process. To summarize, participants should come away from this presentation with a comprehensive understanding of the practice sale process, a better sense of what their practice may be worth, and more confidence around what is needed for informed decision-making as it pertains to selling one's practice.

courses.title: Rapid Relief: Managing Canine Allergic Itch in Practice
courses.description: Managing canine atopic dermatitis (cAD) can be difficult, lifelong and frustrating for the owner and clinician as well as uncomfortable for the pet. It is crucial to consider factors that can increase pruritus in dogs such as secondary infections, allergies and ectoparasites. As a member of the veterinary team, we also need to consider logistics such as finances, caregiver burden and physical limitations. This podcast episode will review medical options to relieve allergic itch and how to consider medication administration when prescribing treatments.

courses.title: Medication use in companion animals and its impact on the microbiome of domestic cats and dogs
courses.description: Since antimicrobial agents were first developed to treat disease in the early 20th century, these drugs quickly became indispensable tools in combating diseases and ensuring the health and well-being of humans and companion animals. This webinar, titled "Medication Use in Companion Animals and Its Impact on the Microbiome of Domestic Cats and Dogs," delves into the essential role medications play in treating many health conditions. However, the focus shifts to the unintended consequences of these therapeutic interventions, particularly antibiotics but also non-antibiotic drugs, on the gut microbiome of companion animals. It is highlighted how such medications, while critical for disease management, can inadvertently eliminate beneficial commensal bacteria, leading to dysbiosis, a state of microbial imbalance that can harm pet health. The lecture will also briefly explore the issue of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), a growing concern exacerbated by the overuse and misuse of drugs. Through internal research examples, the webinar illustrates how this overreliance on medications contributes to the emergence and spread of resistant pathobionts, complicating infection management and posing significant challenges in veterinary medicine. The webinar aims to impart knowledge on the dual nature of drug use in companion animals, balancing the necessity for disease treatment against the risks of disrupting the microbiome and fueling AMR. It emphasizes the need for prudent medication practices to safeguard pets' health while mitigating the rise of drug-resistant pathogens.

courses.title: Sutures Basics and Applications
courses.description: In this webinar, we will review the basics of all things suture related as well as clinically useful applications of this information with a special focus on the most commonly used suture patterns in anatomic structures commonly operated by general practitioners and surgeons alike.

courses.title: Unlocking Opportunity: A Conversation About Veterinary Practice Ownership and Finding Your Path
courses.description:
What does it really take to own a veterinary practice today? In this engaging and real conversation, Dr. Jennifer Bruns sits down with Dr. Vernard Hodges to explore the highs and lows of veterinary practice ownership through the lens of lived experience.
Together, they'll unpack:
The biggest wins and most rewarding aspects of owning a practice- from professional freedom to financial opportunity.
- Common pitfalls and "watch outs," and how to proactively avoid or manage them.
What to do if you feel stuck, scared, or unsure about taking the leap into ownership.
- The best career advice Dr. Hodges has received- and what he wishes more veterinarians knew early on.
This program is for veterinarians and veterinary professionals at all stages of their careers. The goal of this webinar is to offer practical insight, suggestions, and motivation to help attendees think differently about what's possible in veterinary medicine. Whether you're ownership-curious or already on the path, you'll leave with clarity, confidence, and actionable next steps.

courses.title: They Are NOT Too Old for Dental Procedures! (Usually)
courses.description: The incidence of periodontal disease increases with aging pets, and while a lifetime of care may decrease serious issues in later life, many seniors need significant care. With 'pet-alized' assessment and analgesia/anesthesia protocols, you can minimize the risk factor to get them the care they need. Educating the owner as to the benefits of managing this chronic periodontal state can help convince them of the necessity of treatment.

courses.title: Fetch Charlotte On Demand 2025
courses.description: This online non-interactive distance education program offers learners a wide array of medical and nonmedical continuing education options. Learners will gain a comprehensive understanding of the principles, techniques, and best practices across various veterinary disciplines. They will be equipped with the knowledge to accurately diagnose, treat, and manage a wide range of conditions, ensuring improved patient outcomes and advancing their clinical skills. Leaners are expected to receive actionable insights into both common and complex veterinary issues, emphasizing evidence-based approaches and practical applications that can immediately enhance clinical practice.

courses.title: State of The Veterinary Industry -Trends and Myths
courses.description: The topic of the event will be about the state of the veterinary industry and how it will evolve over the next 2-3 years. It will address what factors and conditions will impact the growth, profitability, and practice valuation. We will discuss the top six dynamics that will impact and disrupt the industry. We will discuss the top six myths that prevent a practice owner from achieving their maximum practice valuation. Finally, we will give practice owners strategies to address the six dynamics and myths that can undercut the decades of hard work in building their livelihood and retirement.

courses.title: Why 2+DVM practices are at risk Today? Myths are Guiding Decisions...Not FACTS!
courses.description: This webinar examines how technological advancements, workforce trends and consumer habits - as well as the current buying landscape - are affecting multi-doctor veterinary practices today. The webinar explores the greatest threats and opportunities for these practices, aiming to dispel common myths that often guide practice owners' decision making that affect their present and their future. Participants can expect to learn fact-based strategies for navigating the evolving veterinary landscape, putting them in stronger positions to overcome ownership challenges and reap optimal results when selling.

courses.title: Straight Talk about Marketing and Communication. Let's get real!
courses.description: This course will equip you with insights and practical tools to manage marketing and customer communication, bringing common sense to digital marketing with real examples and data-driven analysis. It will help you put together strategies to attract new customers and stay top of mind with existing ones. You will learn about websites, social media, online reputation, SEO, digital advertising, email, and text marketing to help you prioritize resources and investments effectively. As a result, you will be able to refine your strategy and messaging, set clear communication goals, and manage your website or marketing partners to deliver most impactful programs for your practice.

courses.title: Anesthetic Management of Dogs with Diabetes Mellitus
courses.description: Dogs with diabetes mellitus present unique anesthetic challenges due to alterations in glucose metabolism, electrolyte balance, hydration status, and the physiologic stress response associated with anesthesia and surgery. Appropriate perioperative management is essential to minimize complications such as hypoglycemia, hyperglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis, electrolyte disturbances, and delayed recovery. This presentation reviews the pathophysiology of diabetes mellitus relevant to anesthesia, preanesthetic patient assessment and stabilization, perioperative insulin and blood glucose management, anesthetic drug selection, monitoring strategies, and postoperative care. Emphasis will be placed on practical clinical decision-making, including perioperative insulin adjustments, glucose supplementation, anesthetic protocol selection, and recognition and treatment of perioperative complications. Attendees will gain a systematic approach to anesthetizing diabetic dogs safely while optimizing patient stability and recovery.

courses.title: Perfect Timing: protecting dogs from tick-borne infections
courses.description: This presentation reviews current data on time to transmission of tick - borne infections in dogs. Feeding by common hard ticks is complex, and each tick requires several days to complete the feeding process. Once an attachment site is selected and established, physiologic changes in the tick occur that both facilitate acquisition of a blood meal and initiate maturation and replication of pathogens. When tick feeding is allowed to continue normally, pathogen transmission may follow hours to days after initial tick attachment. We will review current understanding of the mechanism of transmission for different tick-borne pathogens of dogs, including Borrelia burgdorferi, Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Ehrlichia spp., Rickettsia spp., and Babesia spp., and discuss studies designed to determine minimum transmission times. We'll also go over testing strategies for canine tick- borne infections and outline next steps when dogs test positive. Join us to learn more about protecting dogs from ticks and tick-borne diseases.

courses.title: Fetch Coastal On Demand 2024
courses.description: This online non-interactive distance education program offers learners a wide array of medical and non medical continuing education options. Learners will gain a comprehensive understanding of the principles, techniques, and best practices across various veterinary disciplines. They will be equipped with the knowledge to accurately diagnose, treat, and manage a wide range of conditions, ensuring improved patient outcomes and advancing their clinical skills. Learners are expected to receive actionable insights into both common and complex veterinary issues, emphasizing evidence-based approaches and practical applications that can immediately enhance clinical practice. They may highlight the value of the program in improving patient care and expanding

courses.title: The Cat Friendly Experience: From Meet to Treat
courses.description:
Despite overall declines in U.S. veterinary visits, feline care continues to grow, with rising cat adoptions and increasing clinical visits. Yet cats remain one of the most underserved patient populations, often due to the stress and anxiety associated with veterinary visits. This webinar presents a practical, evidence-based approach to improving both the feline exam experience and caregiver satisfaction through the principles of Cat Friendly Practice. Attendees will gain insight into the physiologic and emotional effects of stress in cats, the influence of the clinical environment on behavior, and how caregiver perception impacts compliance.
With a focus on creating a feline friendly clinic environment, adopting feline-specific handling techniques, and navigating the expanding options of products licensed for cats, this session equips veterinary professionals to reduce fear, improve diagnostic accuracy, and foster stronger client relationships. The result is a calmer, more compassionate approach to feline care that supports increased visits, better preventive medicine, and earlier disease detection

courses.title: The Ownership Move: Rethinking the Path from Associate DVM to Boss
courses.description:
a. According to the American Veterinary Medical Association, approximately 35% of associate veterinarians are considering starting their own practice. Practice ownership offers numerous benefits, both financially and emotionally, and veterinarians who work for themselves consistently rate their satisfaction higher than those who do not. Veterinarians who own their practices report lower rates of burnout, according to the AVMA.
b. This program is designed for veterinary professionals seeking to explore practice ownership. Participants will gain comprehensive insights into various ownership structures and operational strategies that align with modern demands and personal goals. The course will cover a range of topics, offering practical knowledge and inspiration for creating a veterinary practice that enhances quality of life and overall wellbeing

courses.title: Breed-Specific Derm and Nutrition Plans: Tailoring Diets for Pets with Genetic Dermatologic Predispositions
courses.description: This course reviews common breed-specific dermatologic disorders and focused nutrition approaches to help manage these patients. Nutrient needs to address metabolic, physiologic and clinical manifestations of these disorders will be discussed. Recommendations regarding diet and nutrient supplementation options will be provided.

courses.title: Grain of Truth: Sorting Facts from Fables in Pet Nutrition
courses.description:
This course addresses prevalent nutrition myths affecting veterinary practice and clinical
dietary recommendations. Veterinarians will learn evidence-based clarifications to common misconceptions about
pet food ingredients, formulation principles, and nutritional adequacy. Topics include digestibility myths, protein
requirements, ingredient quality (by-products, grains, legumes, oils), human-grade standards, supplement necessity,
raw feeding claims, weight management strategies, and a clearer understanding of the different nutrition
credentials.

courses.title: Advancements in Calf Scour Prevention: New Data on USDA-Labeled Polyclonal Bovine Colostrum Antibody Technology for On-Label
courses.description: This course delves into the critical role of scour prevention and explores the various prevention strategies currently available. The primary emphasis will be on the use of bovine-derived maternal colostrum antibodies to prevent neonatal calf scours. Participants will gain comprehensive insights into the production process of these antibodies, the scope of available data both published and unpublished and the level of protection they offer against scours and other neonatal calf diseases. The course will also address both on-label and off-label uses, alongside a thorough review of internal and external data sources.

courses.title: Harnessing the Power of Laser Therapy for Canine and Equine Health
courses.description: Join Dr. Tom Walsh, a distinguished rehabilitation veterinarian from Myrtle Beach, SC, and Dr. Wendy Coren, a renowned equine veterinarian from Ocala, FL, for an insightful webinar exploring the transformative benefits of laser therapy in veterinary medicine. Tailored for veterinarians and veterinary industry professionals, this collaborative session will delve into the science and practical applications of laser therapy for dogs and horses. Key topics include its efficacy in pain relief, inflammation reduction, arthritis management, and tissue healing. Learn how this non-invasive modality can enhance patient outcomes, improve mobility, and elevate quality of life for canine and equine patients. Discover cutting-edge protocols, case studies, and evidence-based insights from two leading experts in their respective fields. Don't miss this opportunity to advance your practice with innovative therapeutic approaches.

courses.title: Microbiome Responses to Oral Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in a Cohort of Domestic Dogs
courses.description: Fecal microbiota transplants (FMTs) Fecal microbiota transplants (FMTs) have been successful at treating digestive and skin conditions in dogs. In this webinar, we will uncover groundbreaking research that examines the impact of FMTs on the microbiome of fifty-four dogs suffering from chronic diarrhea, vomiting, or constipation. Utilizing cutting-edge 16S rRNA gene sequencing technology, we meticulously track the transformations in the microbial landscape before and after FMT administration. During the session, participants will gain an understanding of how bacterial genera enriches after FMT to participate in various metabolic processes crucial for gut health, insights into how host diet, recent antibiotic use, and body condition score significantly influence the fecal microbiomes of FMT recipients, and the dynamics of bacterial engraftment in oral FMTs, including engraftment rates influenced by the diversity of the donor's microbiome.

courses.title: Bioactive Peptide Supplements: Breaking the Itch/Scratch Cycle
courses.description: Pruritus (itch) can result from many different mechanisms that are not always mutually exclusive. These include allergic reactions, inflammatory reactions, infections, insect bites, drug reactions, food reactions, reactions secondary to systemic disease or due to the presence of neurologic disease. This makes itch a complex and recurring issue to deal with for veterinarians, pet parents and the pets themselves, that has a direct impact on the quality of life of the pet and the pet parent. This presentation explores the emerging role of bioactive peptide supplements as a natural, adjunctive approach to help break the itch/scratch cycle in companion animals. We'll examine how these naturally occurring compounds can support skin health, modulate inflammatory responses, and offer a complementary strategy alongside conventional therapies. Special attention will be given to understanding the mechanisms of pruritus, the value of nutraceuticals in clinical practice, and practical guidance for incorporating peptide-based supplements into individualized wellness plans

courses.title: Animal Cruelty Investigations: Evidence Collection Fundamentals
courses.description: The University of Florida Veterinary Forensic Sciences Laboratory and the Humane Society of the United States will be hosting an animal cruelty investigations workshop. This workshop is open to law enforcement, crime scene investigators, evidence technicians, animal control officers, veterinarians, and prosecutors interested in advancing their knowledge of both small and large-scale animal cruelty investigations. The course will be a mixture of lecture format and hands-on activities. Topics will include fundamentals for evidence collection with both large- and small-scale animal crimes, including an overview of how to utilize veterinary forensic sciences and unique considerations for large-scale investigations.

courses.title: Effectiveness of USDA-Approved Scour Vaccines: Insights from Research and Practical Applications in Neonatal Calf Care
courses.description: This course provides an overview of scour prevention strategies for neonatal calves, with a particular emphasis on scour vaccines and the available data on disease prevention. It serves as a comprehensive refresher, blending established approaches to scour prevention with insights from recently published studies.

courses.title: A New Category of Care: A Practitioner's Guide to Proactive, Non-Invasive Screening of Lumps and Bumps
courses.description: In this one-hour lecture, Dr. Natalie Marks will discuss why early disease detection is vital for the best pet outcomes. While most clinicians would agree with this tenet, more than half of dermal and subcutaneous masses in dogs go undiagnosed mainly due to the cost and invasiveness of traditional tests. This lecture will discuss how a non-invasive cancer screening tool using heat diffusion imaging and artificial intelligence can screen dermal and subcutaneous masses safely. It will also discuss how this technology does not compete with traditional strategies like FNA, biopsy, or surgery but instead helps reinforce the need for these clinically indicated tests. The lecture will finish with a deeper dive into the technology itself, its accuracy, and workflow implementation

courses.title: Tick Tidbits: Ticking off the 5 W's on These Tiny Troublemakers
courses.description:
Ticks pose a significant health risk to companion animals, both as blood-feeding parasites and as vectors for numerous pathogens. Over the past few decades, tick populations have expanded and intensified due to factors such as increased globalization, greater movement of humans and animals, and climate change. In the United States, common tick species-including the blacklegged tick, lone star tick, American dog tick, and brown dog tick-have the potential to transmit a range of bacterial, protozoal, and viral pathogens.
Serological data indicate that tick-borne pathogens are a persistent challenge for dogs, with U.S. canines frequently testing positive for agents of anaplasmosis, Lyme disease, and ehrlichiosis. Many of these same ticks and pathogens also pose a public health risk, as the tick species that commonly bite dogs can also transmit these same pathogens to humans. As a result, dogs can serve as valuable sentinels for tick-borne disease risks of their human families.
Despite awareness of the risks ticks pose to pets, ticks are often and easily overlooked. Given that ticks are a year-round threat in most regions, annual testing and the routine use of fast-acting tick control products play a critical role in protecting pet health by killing ticks and reducing pathogen transmission risk.

courses.title: A Modern Approach to Canine Atopic Dermatitis: is there a better way?
courses.description: In this informative session, Dr. Sheinberg will explore evidence-based strategies for managing Canine Atopic Dermatitis (CAD). This lecture will provide practical insights and actionable recommendations for veterinarians, with a focus on integrating cutting-edge therapies such as topical treatments, systemic management, and allergen-specific immunotherapy. Through a case-based approach, attendees will learn how to optimize treatment plans tailored to individual patients, address common challenges, and improve client communication to ensure better outcomes.

courses.title: Fetch Kansas City on Demand
courses.description: This online non-interactive distance education program offers learners a wide array of medical and nonmedical continuing education options. Learners will gain a comprehensive understanding of the principles, techniques, and best practices across various veterinary disciplines. They will be equipped with the knowledge to accurately diagnose, treat, and manage a wide range of conditions, ensuring improved patient outcomes and advancing their clinical skills. Leaners are expected to receive actionable insights into both common and complex veterinary issues, emphasizing evidence-based approaches and practical applications that can immediately enhance clinical practice.

courses.title: The Roadmap to Osteoarthritis Success
courses.description: Canine osteoarthritis is a complex disease that impacts the quality of life for many of our canine patients. Treatment decisions can be intimidating with the numerous options available, leaving veterinarians confused about how they should manage their patients. A recent survey revealed that many veterinarians see osteoarthritis as a prevalent issue in their patients, but they would appreciate some guidance or a protocol to better manage their patients. After discussing the survey findings, the program will reveal the roadmap for osteoarthritis management based on where a patient may be in the course of the disease.

courses.title: Power Up Your Team With Meetings That Inspire: Build Culture, Boost Engagement, Drive Results
courses.description: Transform your veterinary practice team meetings from dreaded time wasters into powerful culture-building tools that boost engagement, retention, and practice success. This session reveals how to create meetings people want to attend through 5 evidence-based principles: making them interactive, psychologically safe, fun, educational, and productive. Designed for veterinary practice managers, owners, and team leaders, participants will learn practical strategies to facilitate meaningful discussions, encourage balanced participation, and connect daily tasks to practice mission. Attendees will leave with concrete tools including delegation strategies, meeting planning templates, and facilitation techniques. Topics include psychological safety, team engagement, leadership development, communication strategies, and practice culture.

courses.title: Love no matter who you are - understanding the spectrum of Pet Parents
courses.description: This course explores the intersection of LGBTQIA+ identity and pet ownership, emphasizing the critical role veterinary professionals play in fostering inclusive, affirming, and culturally competent care. Participants will examine how diverse lived experiences within the LGBTQIA+ community impact access to veterinary services and how the profession can better uphold the human-animal bond through inclusive practices. The webinar will provide practical strategies for creating safe, welcoming spaces in clinical settings, supporting pet owners through affirming partnerships, and ensuring pets receive the highest quality of care.

courses.title: Utilizing the Nu.Q Vet Cancer Test in Practice
courses.description: This course covers challenges and unmet needs in the diagnosis of canine cancer, shares clinical data from studies of the Nu.Q Vet Cancer Test, how to process the sample and interpret results, how to integrate the use of the test in YOUR clinical practice and provides Case Study examples to illustrate how the test may / may not be used. The presenter is a leading light in the veterinary oncology field, Dr Sue Ettinger aka, Dr Sue Cancer Vet.

courses.title: Practical Dermatology for the Every Day Veterinary Professional
courses.description: Step inside a real-world dermatology practice and experience how dermatologists approach ear and skin disease--from diagnostics to treatment decisions- in a dynamic, case-based format. This interactive CE session brings cytology to life, breaking down practical workflows, common pitfalls, and how to confidently translate findings into targeted therapy. Drs. Julia Miller, Joya Griffin and Jeff Tinsley share real world clinical cases with you in real time. Learn how you can improve compliance, outcomes while practicing antimicrobial stewardship. Designed for the entire veterinary team, this program delivers key takeaways you can immediately implement to elevate patient care and client communication. If you want to sharpen your diagnostic skills, streamline your treatment protocols, and stay ahead in dermatology, this is a session you don't want to miss! Welcome to "Inside the Clinic!"

courses.title: The Importance of Hypertension in Proteinuria in Dogs and Cats with CKD
courses.description: Systolic hypertension and renal proteinuria are common complications of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in dogs and cats, and both are associated with progressive loss of nephrons. Control of these complications can lead to improved quality of life and prolonged survival. Angiotensin receptor blockers are the current treatment of choice for hypertension and proteinuria in both dogs and cats.

courses.title: Understanding how and when to utilize AI in imaging
courses.description: In this podcast interview, Dr. Lisa Ziemer provides an overview of Antech RapidRead, the AI-assisted radiographic interpretation tool, what the tool does, how veterinarians can utilize AI-powered tools in practice, and looks at a RapidRead case study.

courses.title: Managing Canine Obesity: Calories, consequences, and difficult conversations
courses.description: Canine obesity is a common and clinically significant nutritional disorder with far-reaching implications on health and longevity. Attendees will review risk factors for the development of obesity as well as evidence-based dietary strategies for safe, effective weight loss and long-term weight maintenance.

courses.title: A Total Wound Care Approach: Improving the Physical and Emotional Health of Patients
courses.description: In this 1-hour RACE-approved lecture, attendees will start with a refresher on the pathophysiology around wound healing in dogs and cats. This will include both gross and microscopic descriptions. Attendees will then discuss different pain points around treating wounds with a heavy focus on fear, anxiety, and stress in both patients and clients. This moves into physical factors that impede wound healing (immune suppression, inflammation, etc.) Understanding what creates an ideal healing environment takes attendees towards an introduction to a new standard of wound care that considers our patients' physical and emotional health. The final section of the lecture will include case-based discussions with strategies for general and emergency practices around workflow implementation and client communication.

courses.title: Fetch Encore - Cardiology -Mastering the Heart of the Matter
courses.description: Heart disease cases can feel intimidating, but they don't have to be! This Fetch Encore virtual symposium simplifies cardiology into clear, practical decision making you can apply immediately. Start making stronger calls with case-based learning, including: A comprehensive view, from heart murmurs to congestive heart failure Clarity for diagnosing, staging, and managing cardiac patients When to treat, when to refer, how to optimize outcomes

courses.title: Advancing the Spectrum of Care in Canine Parvovirus (CPV): Emerging Therapies Using FMT and CPV Monoclonal Antibody
courses.description: Canine parvovirus (CPV) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in dogs despite advances in supportive care. This session reviews emerging therapeutic strategies, including fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and CPV-specific monoclonal antibody therapy. Data from a recent prospective, randomized clinical trial demonstrate that FMT significantly accelerates clinical recovery and reduces hospitalization time, while new retrospective data highlight improved clinical outcomes with monoclonal antibody use. Participants will learn how to integrate these therapies into a spectrum-of-care approach to improve clinical and economic outcomes in CPV management.

courses.title: CKD: New and Old Management Options
courses.description: This lecture presents current ways to manage chronic kidney disease in dogs and cats. It examines what is new and what is on the horizon to improve quality of life for patients. The lecture will review how we should think about chronic kidney disease and its progression, and how new management techniques may influence progression of disease.

courses.title: Non-Surgical Management of Canine Degenerative Joint Disease
courses.description: This 1-hour lecture discusses diagnosis and medical management of canine osteoarthritis. Multimodal management and treatment options are discussed. Surgery is briefly touched upon. This is for all small animal practitioners who see these cases on a daily basis.

courses.title: The Cat Friendly Experience: From Meet to Treat
courses.description:
Despite overall declines in U.S. veterinary visits, feline care continues to grow, with rising cat adoptions and increasing clinical visits. Yet cats remain one of the most underserved patient populations, often due to the stress and anxiety associated with veterinary visits. This webinar presents a practical, evidence-based approach to improving both the feline exam experience and caregiver satisfaction through the principles of Cat Friendly Practice. Attendees will gain insight into the physiologic and emotional effects of stress in cats, the influence of the clinical environment on behavior, and how caregiver perception impacts compliance.
With a focus on creating a feline friendly clinic environment, adopting feline-specific handling techniques, and navigating the expanding options of products licensed for cats, this session equips veterinary professionals to reduce fear, improve diagnostic accuracy, and foster stronger client relationships. The result is a calmer, more compassionate approach to feline care that supports increased visits, better preventive medicine, and earlier disease detection.

courses.title: A Peek Behind the Curtain: Taking a Better Approach to HCM in Your Feline Patients
courses.description: In this one-hour live, interactive virtual webinar, attendees will start with a review of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in cats, covering known prevalence, the pathophysiology of the disease, predisposed breeds, and current limitations in diagnostics. The webinar will then explore the staging of this disease based on ACVIM guidelines, the opportunities and challenges of current workups, and the latest developments in diagnostics and therapeutics. The session will conclude with a summary of a current workup strategy, along with discussion points for clinicians and veterinary teams to share with pet parents.

courses.title: 5 Investments That Should Be Part of Every Owner's Portfolio
courses.description:
Are you confident your retirement plan is on the right track? Most practice owners rely on traditional financial advice that doesn't account for the unique challenges and opportunities of running a healthcare practice. This can leave you underprepared for the future a practice owner deserves. A practice owner needs more than a 401k to secure their financial future, yet many have that and the sale of the practice as their main plans for retirement.
This webinar will explore 5 Investments that should be part of every practice owner's portfolio.

courses.title: Adjunctive Analgesic Drugs
courses.description: Adjunctive drugs are often shrouded in confusion, misunderstanding and anecdotal evidence that may or may not have bearing on the drugs true capabilities in treating pain. This session looks at only the facts of what we know about the most common analgesic drugs.

courses.title: Authentic Marketing: Building Lifelong Client Connections
courses.description:
In a digital-first world, authentic connection is the ultimate differentiator in veterinary care. This session redefines marketing, not as advertising, but as an extension of the compassion veterinarians already provide.
Through real-world examples and actionable insights, attendees will learn how to build trust, increase visibility, and create a lasting reputation through local marketing fundamentals like Google optimization, social storytelling, and community engagement. We'll also share how PetSmart Veterinary Services helps scale these efforts through a partnership model that blends personal storytelling with professional marketing reach.

courses.title: When the Itch Won't Quit - Cultivating Compliance in Your Derm Cases
courses.description: This 30-minute program, presented by board-certified Veterinary Dermatologist Dr. Julia E. Miller, will cover how to maximize clinical communication strategies to improve compliance in your dermatology cases. A whole-clinic approach, from client service representatives, the nursing care team, to the doctors, will be emphasized. Let's tackle how to approach our itchy patients and get our clients on board for continued care and better outcomes.

courses.title: Current Evidence for Regenerative Medicine in Canine and Feline Osteoarthritis
courses.description:
This course helps veterinarians navigate the when, why, and how of using regenerative medicine to treat osteoarthritis (OA) in dogs and cats.
We explore the evolving understanding of OA as a disease of immune dysfunction and tissue degeneration, and how early regenerative intervention can shift the entire trajectory of the disease.
Attendees will gain step-by-step, practical protocols that combine pain optimization (to reveal true therapeutic response) with product preparation, injection technique, recovery-to-rehab progression, and long-term care planning.
A concise clinical case illustrates real decision points and outcomes using regenerative tools, including Gallant's off-the-shelf stem cell therapy.

courses.title: Canine Osteoarthritis: Current Concepts and Advances in Treatment
courses.description:
Canine osteoarthritis is one of the most common causes of chronic pain and reduced mobility in dogs, significantly impacting quality of life. There are many underlying factors behind this condition, and treatment options and prognosis may vary depending on the root cause.
The webinar provides an evidence-based review of osteoarthritis (OA) in dogs and explores the underlying factors of the disease. The webinar will also cover current and emerging treatment options for canine OA and how to select the appropriate treatment strategy based on the patient's underlying condition.

courses.title: Save More Teeth with ReGum Vet
courses.description: This talk is intended to review the incidence of periodontal disease, the differences in treatment based on bone levels, and the indication for the use of ReGumVet in patients with advanced periodontal disease. Attendees will learn tips for ultrasonic cleaning as well as hand instrumentation to prepare the surface for the application of ReGumVet in general practice. The steps for placement as well as flap closure are discussed to allow the attendee to be able to save more teeth with ReGumVet.

courses.title: Supporting Gastrointestinal Health in Dogs and Cats with Supplements: A Science-backed Approach
courses.description:
Gastrointestinal upset is one of the most common presentations in small animal general practice. As understanding
of antibiotic stewardship and the gut microbiome continues to evolve, veterinarians are increasingly seeking
supportive, evidence-informed approaches for managing uncomplicated gastrointestinal cases in dogs and cats.
This course will review key differences between supplements and pharmaceuticals and outline common
presentations gastrointestinal upset in dogs and cats. Participants will explore foundational gastrointestinal
physiology and mechanisms commonly targeted by dietary and supplemental support, including barrier function,
microbial balance, immune signaling, and appetite support.
The program will also review current evidence and emerging data related to gastrointestinal supplements, including
formulation considerations, species-specific probiotics, immunoglobulin-based ingredients, and palatability.
Emphasis will be placed on appropriate clinical positioning, regulatory considerations, and transparent interpretation
of available data to support confident, responsible recommendations in practice.

courses.title: Cobalamin status in patients with chronic GI disease and management
courses.description: Cobalamin is a water-soluble vitamin that is plentiful in most commercial diets. However, dogs and cats with chronic intestinal disease or exocrine pancreatic insufficiency are frequently cobalamin deficient. This session will summarize the physiologic role of cobalamin, the consequences of cobalamin deficiency, as well as its diagnosis. The session will focus on the management of cobalamin deficiency through cobalamin supplementation.

courses.title: Fetch Charlotte On Demand
courses.description: This is the On Demand version of our Fetch conference in Charlotte. Fetch, a dvm360 conference, at Charlotte, NC is a live interactive, in-person conference with a combination of both medical and nonmedical programs created for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and practice managers to achieve their continuing education in veterinary medicine. Educational content tracks include: Anesthesiology, Artificial Intelligence, Behavior, Cardiology, Critical Care, Dermatology, Exotics, Feline Medicine, Hands-On Lab, Integrative Medicine , Internal Medicine, Keynote, Laser Therapy, Legal Matters, Marketing, Nutrition, Oncology, Ophthalmology, Orthopedics, Parasitology, Peer to Peer Breakfast, Sponsored CE, Practice Management, Peer to Peer Luncheon, Sponsored CE, Practice Management, Practice Management, Practice Ownership, Surgery, Technician Critical Care, Technician Feline Medicine, Technician Medicine, Toxicology, Workshop; Ophthalmology

courses.title: Nutrition and Stem Cell Therapy in Dogs and Cats: Optimizing for Better Outcomes
courses.description: Stem cell therapy is an exciting part of regenerative veterinary medicine, but the patient's nutritional and metabolic state may influence how well these therapies perform. This webinar reviews the biologic links between nutrition, inflammation, microbiome function, and stem cell behavior, with a practical focus on dogs and cats. Participants will learn how veterinary teams can help support the patient's biological environment before, during, and after regenerative treatment, while exploring where the scientific evidence is well established and where it continues to emerge.

courses.title: A Fresh Perspective: a discussion on feeding fresh
courses.description: This course provides veterinary professionals with a balanced, evidence based look at fresh pet food diets compared to fresh homemade and traditional dry food. Topics include a review of pet food safety; effective strategies for navigating popular nutrition trends; the practical benefits of fresh feeding; and key considerations for tailoring to a patient's needs. Attendees will leave equipped to objectively counsel clients on fresh versus dry feeding options.

courses.provider: WESTERN UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES, COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: Advanced Laparoscopy Course for Small Animal General Practitioners
courses.description: This one-day advanced course is designed for veterinarians with prior experience in laparoscopic surgery. The program focuses on advanced laparoscopic procedures, including laparoscopic-assisted gastropexy and Single-Incision Laparoscopic Surgery (SILS). Participants will receive both theoretical instruction and hands-on surgical training on live animal models. This course emphasizes mastery of advanced techniques, complication management, and practical integration of laparoscopic gastropexy and SILS into clinical practice.

courses.title: Make or Break: How the Right Mentorship Program Can Define Your Veterinary Career
courses.description: Petco Chief Veterinarian, Dr. Whitney Miller, DVM, MBA, DACVPM and Dr. Ashlee Redmond, DVM, Director of Medical Special Programs at Petco will explore research that supports the profound impact early career mentorships can have on the wellbeing, success, and longevity of veterinarians. But all mentorship programs are not created equal. Dr. Miller and Dr. Redmond will help you identify and understand the attributes of high-quality, effective mentorship programs to help new veterinarians make the right choice for their new careers.

courses.title: Can I help my Client's Cruciate Ligament-Deficient Dog when TPLO/TTA isn't an Option?
courses.description: Tibial osteotomies like Tibial Plateau Leveling Osteotomy (TPLO), Tibial Tuberosity Advancement (TTA) and others have significantly advanced our profession's ability to effectively treat a large spectrum of dogs with cranial cruciate ligament disease (CrCLD) even when the athletic performance outcome expectations are lofty. Nonetheless, geographical and /or economic constraints can limit the availability of these procedures for some pets. In this session, Dr. P will describe how you can select patients who are likely to benefit from extracapsular (ExCap) suture stabilization of the stifle and some important pre-, intra-, and post-operative nuances to maximize your chances of success.

courses.title: Success Strategies for Canine Allergic Dermatitis: Pearls to Help during Itchy Dog Season
courses.description: Allergy season is here- learn new dermatology tips and pearls based on science so you are ready to treat all of your itchy canine patients. Keys to treatment success will be shared including case examples that demonstrate how to best use fast, effective and safe anti-pruritic medications to maximize treatment success and compliance. A simplified diagnostic approach for acute and chronic cases of allergic itch will be shared. Studies on owner preferences and compliance with chewable vs. film-coated tablets and how to maximize treatment success with Cytopoint through additional injections will be presented. We will review the safety of Apoquel's (oclacitinib tablet) new 10-year pharmacovigilance data, and will describe how the safety of a drug is determined and how vaccine response study results and labels can differ among currently approved JAK inhibitors for dogs.

courses.title: Mastering Atopic Dermatitis: Multimodal Management for Holistic Control
courses.description: o This 50-minute webinar will be presented by Dr. Joya Griffin, DVM. Dr. Griffin will review the pathogenesis of canine atopic dermatitis and how to implement a systematic approach to achieve an accurate diagnosis. Dr. Griffin will also explore how to manage each atopic case based on the specific needs of the patient and how to control disease by implementing evidence-based treatments to reduce pruritus and prevent allergic flare.

courses.title: Is Osteoarthritis a Disease of Young Dogs? Rethinking Risk Across All Life Stages
courses.description:
Osteoarthritis is often framed as a condition of older dogs - but the evidence challenges that assumption. Nearly 40% of dogs across all ages, breeds, and body weights show signs of OA pain, yet fewer than half are ever diagnosed and only a third are treated.
Emerging data from dogs as young as 8 months, combined with what we know about the unique genetic history of domestic breeds, reveals that OA risk begins far earlier than most practitioners expect.
This session examines the biological and epidemiological evidence supporting OA as a disease of all life stages, reviews the pain physiology driving clinical signs, and applies key concepts through a real-world case study. Attendees will leave with a practical screening framework to identify, assess, and address OA pain across every canine patient in their practice.

courses.provider: WESTERN UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES, COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: Basic Laparoscopy Course for Small Animal General Practioners
courses.description: This two-day, hands-on course provides veterinarians with foundational knowledge and practical experience in minimally invasive laparoscopic surgery. Designed for practitioners with little to no previous experience, the program includes lectures, videos, and extensive wet-lab training. Participants will begin with laparoscopic models and simulators and advance to performing live-animal laparoscopic procedures, focusing on abdominal exploration and ovariectomy.

courses.title: Say Yes To Dentistry!
courses.description: Hidden in the mouth it is difficult for clients to understand the full impact dental disease has on their pet's quality of life. If they will not accept and move forward with the doctor's recommendations, they cannot help their patient. This lecture focuses on language, analogies and tips to help the whole hospital team increase client compliance and have dentistry thrive at their practice.

courses.title: Updates in Nutritional Management of Feline Diabetes
courses.description: This course touches on general nutritional management of feline diabetes mellitus and covers recent scientific publications on this topic. A proposed new classification system and nutritional guidelines for feline diabetes mellitus will be reviewed, as well as the results of a recent clinical trial evaluating a new nutritional innovation in insulin-treated overweight diabetic cats.

courses.title: Planning for Pruritus: Allergic Triggers and Management Strategies for Allergy Season
courses.description: In many parts of the United States, summer is the start of allergy season. Allergic dermatitis is one of the most common reasons for pet owners to bring their dog to the veterinarian. Itch and secondary infection can be both frustrating and challenging to diagnose and treat. This case-based discussion will work through several patients, highlighting anti-pruritic therapies, secondary problems like skin and ear infections, and common primary triggers of allergic dermatitis that should be identified and minimized for long term control of allergies.

courses.title: Healing Light: Photochemical Therapy How is it Different and Where does it shine in Private Practice
courses.description: This 1-hour seminar will be an overview of the low-level laser technology and its use in small animal medicine. A basic overview of the physics and understanding of how light energy works in the patient and how photochemical lasers are unique. Attendees will see the practical application and potential outcomes. Dr. Huff will share several case studies & case history through videos and photos. Finally, ample time for questions and answers will be provided to ensure a complete understanding.

courses.title: Chasing the Cause: identifying triggers and applying dietary solutions in canine otitis
courses.description: Otitis externa is a prevalent complaint in patients presented to small animal practices. This inflammatory disease of the external ear canal and/or pinna can have an acute or chronic presentation. Diagnosis and management of otitis externa depend on identifying the type of infection. However, it is essential to figure out the underlying cause of the infection. Learn how to identify the primary cause of canine otitis and how nutritional changes to help manage them long-term even for atopic dermatitis.

courses.title: Fetch Charlotte On Demand 2026 Part 2
courses.description: This is the On Demand version of our Fetch conference in Charlotte. Fetch, a dvm360 conference, at Charlotte, NC is a live interactive, in-person conference with a combination of both medical and nonmedical programs created for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and practice managers to achieve their continuing education in veterinary medicine. Educational content tracks include: Anesthesiology, Artificial Intelligence, Behavior, Cardiology, Critical Care, Dermatology, Exotics, Feline Medicine, Hands-On Lab, Integrative Medicine , Internal Medicine, Keynote, Laser Therapy, Legal Matters, Marketing, Nutrition, Oncology, Ophthalmology, Orthopedics, Parasitology, Peer to Peer Breakfast, Sponsored CE, Practice Management, Peer to Peer Luncheon, Sponsored CE, Practice Management, Practice Management, Practice Ownership, Surgery, Technician Critical Care, Technician Feline Medicine, Technician Medicine, Toxicology, Workshop; Ophthalmology

courses.title: Just Bust a Myth!: Canine Food Allergies Demystified
courses.description: In this one-hour on-demand podcast, dermatologists Dr. Julia Miller and Dr. Joya Griffin, and Dr. Natalie Marks will start by reviewing canine food allergies, including historical clues such as the age of onset and seasonality in the patient, physical examination findings, including the minimum derm database, and other subtle findings that might suggest food allergy. They will then dive deeper into the dos and don'ts of diet trials, focusing on the client conversation, the different types of diets (novel protein hydrolyzed, prescription vs. OTC, home-cooked vs. commercial), the duration, if we need to challenge, and finish with guidance on how to proceed with the canine patient that may have both food allergy and atopy. The remainder of the podcast will feature questions from the audience pertinent to food allergy and diet trials.

courses.title: Inside the Clinic--Parvo Perspectives, Strategies, Stories & CPMA Solutions
courses.description: This program provides an overview of canine parvovirus (CPV) and associated treatment. This discussion follows a parvo case from initial call to the clinic through diagnosis and treatment, including impact of the latest therapeutic options on case management. The discussion highlights how a parvo case impacts all areas of the clinic and how every member of the team can help the owners navigate treatment options for the best choice for their family and pet. An introduction and overview of Elanco's Canine Parvovirus Monoclonal Antibody will be discussed.

courses.title: Alternative Pet Foods: From Formulation to Bowl
courses.description: This course reviews alternative feeding formats ("minimally processed diets") -- what comprises these diets, why clients are seeking them, what challenges are present and ways to overcome them.

courses.title: 5 Ways to Help Pet Families Say Yes to Care: Case-Based Strategies for a High-Cost World
courses.description:
Veterinary healthcare teams are seeing more pets present sicker and later as the cost of veterinary services continues to rise faster than overall consumer prices, and roughly one in three pet families would struggle to pay an unexpected $500 veterinary bill. In daily practice, this often shows up as challenging cost of care conversations, delayed decision-making, increased team stress, and patients receiving less care. This 30-minute, case-based medical CE session focuses on practical, time-efficient strategies to support access to care while maintaining clinical quality and trust.
Using common canine and feline scenarios such as urethral obstruction, arthritis, and acute surgical presentations, this session will walk through five actionable approaches that fit real exam-room constraints. Attendees will see how to introduce financial considerations early, present guideline-informed care pathways using a spectrum of care framework, apply clinical empathy techniques, and incorporate pet insurance and payment options.
This webinar is designed for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and practice managers in general, urgent, and emergency practice, with a focus on practical language, clinical decision frameworks, and team habits that support clearer communication and access to care.

courses.title: Chronic Allergic Dermatitis Essentials: Dermatologist-Endorsed, AAHA-Approved Strategies
courses.description:
Chronic allergic dermatitis can be a real headache for clients and their furry friends. It's uncomfortable, frustrating, and often totally preventable. Join us for a power-packed session where we dig deep into the reasons behind annoying flare ups and reveal how to tackle them head-on. Andrew Simpson, DAVCD, will share practical, science-backed strategies that will transform your approach and help your team manage allergic dermatitis.
We'll kick things off with a quick tour of the current AAHA Allergic Dermatitis Guidelines and the brains behind them setting the stage for a deeper understanding of chronic allergic dermatitis. From there, we'll unpack the usual suspects: seasonal shifts, secondary infections, food allergens, and those ever-persistent parasites. We will also explore how each one fans the flames of inflammation.
Cytology? Nonnegotiable. Year-round parasite control? Absolutely. We'll show you how to build a proactive plan that anticipates flares before they start, including: Prepping for seasonal transitions, Tackling secondary infections head-on,Locking down diet and parasite control with zero wiggle room
You'll also gain tools to empower pet owners, such as medicated topicals, clear instructions, and early intervention strategies that work. We'll cover referral red flags and the studies that support timely specialist involvement, so you know when it's time to call in the dermatology cavalry.

courses.title: Practical Corneal Ulcer Management for General Practitioners
courses.description: Reviewing corneal anatomy and how that pertains to our understanding of ulcer management. This program will delve into the specifics of recognizing and treating corneal ulcers from superficial to deep in your practice in a digestible manner.

courses.title: From Clinic to Curbside: Lessons Learned on my journey as a Mobile Veterinarian
courses.description: Ride along with Dr. Allie McPhee during her journey of building a successful mobile veterinary practice. This honest and sometimes humorous presentation outlines key steps in building a successful business, from defining your unique service model and securing financing to selecting equipment, insurance, and staffing. Ultimately, it encourages veterinarians to confidently pursue mobile practice as a fulfilling and viable career path.

courses.title: Understanding Microbiome Variability in Healthy Dogs: Implications for Microbiome Testing
courses.description:
Advances in canine microbiome research have transformed our understanding of gastrointestinal health, revealing associations between microbial community structure and a wide range of digestive, metabolic, and immune-mediated conditions. As microbiome testing becomes increasingly integrated into veterinary practice, clinicians are often faced with interpreting changes in bacterial abundances and determining whether those changes represent disease, dysbiosis, or normal biological variation.
One of the most important unanswered questions in companion animal microbiome science has been the degree to which the microbiome naturally fluctuates over time in healthy individuals. While cross-sectional studies have identified bacterial taxa associated with health and disease, comparatively little attention has been paid to the temporal stability of these organisms or the extent to which healthy microbiomes vary from month to month.
This course reviews recent longitudinal research evaluating the fecal microbiomes of 35 healthy dogs sampled monthly over one to two years using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Participants will explore how microbial communities change over time despite consistent diets, and the absence of antibiotics or medications. Findings demonstrate that temporal variability is an inherent characteristic of the healthy canine gut microbiome and that fluctuations occur both at the community level and among individual bacterial taxa.
The session will examine which bacterial species exhibit relatively stable patterns and which taxa are especially dynamic. Particular attention will be given to bacterial groups that commonly generate concern during microbiome testing, including Streptococcus spp., Escherichia coli, and Clostridium perfringens.
Beyond reviewing study findings, the course emphasizes practical clinical application. Participants will learn how temporal variability influences microbiome test interpretation, the limitations of single time-point test

courses.title: Veterinary Induction Agents, Making the Safest Choice
courses.description: This continuing education webinar is designed for veterinary professionals involved in anesthesia who want to strengthen their understanding of available anesthetic induction agents. The session will review the pharmacology, physiologic effects, and clinical applications of commonly used agents, including propofol, alfaxalone, ketamine-based combinations, and etomidate. Participants will learn how to evaluate patient status, species-specific responses, and concurrent disease considerations when formulating an induction plan. The presentation will emphasize practical, evidence-based selection and dosing strategies to improve anesthetic safety, quality of induction, and transition to maintenance anesthesia. Case examples will reinforce your clinical decision-making and highlight troubleshooting tips for challenging anesthetic inductions.

courses.title: Stem Cell Therapy for Neurological Diseases
courses.description: This lecture will discuss the immunological dysregulation at the root of many neurological diseases in humans and animals, and how stem cells are being explored for these conditions. There are several animal models for human conditions that may drive clinical research to benefit cross-species.

courses.title: Advanced Modalities in Wound Management: Evidence- Based Strategies Through the 4 Stages of Wound Repair
courses.description: Wound management is no longer just a clinical task it's a strategic opportunity to elevate patient outcomes while driving meaningful practice growth. This session goes beyond traditional bandaging techniques to explore how modern wound care protocols, product selection, and workflow design can be optimized for both medical excellence and financial performance. Attendees will learn how to streamline wound care processes, improve client compliance, and integrate advanced therapies into everyday practice without disrupting efficiency. By aligning clinical decision making with operational strategy, veterinary teams can reduce complications, accelerate healing, and create a more predictable and profitable service line. This session delivers practical, real world approaches to harmonizing high- quality wound care with measurable return on investment.

courses.title: Modulating Immunity: Mushrooms, Oats, and Colostrum
courses.description: This course will review the rationale for, and benefits of, incorporating nutrients from mushrooms as well as oats and colostrum into a veterinary healthcare management plan.

courses.title: Advancing FMT in Veterinary Medicine: Viability and Diversity in Lyophilized Microbiota
courses.description: This webinar explores the clinical and practical advancements in fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) for companion animals, with a focus on the development of lyophilized (freeze-dried) fecal material. Attendees will gain insights into how this process enhances safety, stability, and ease of administration in veterinary settings. The session will review methods used to assess bacterial viability- such as culturability, metabolic activity, and membrane integrity- and present findings on the diversity and survival of bacterial species in lyophilized samples from healthy cats and dogs. This evidence supports the clinical relevance and reliability of powdered FMT formulations in small animal practice.

courses.title: Veterinary Laser Therapy in Clinical Practice Subtitle: Science, Safety, and Applications in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description:
Photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) is a type of laser therapy increasingly utilized in veterinary medicine as an adjunctive modality in a variety of situations, including pain management, inflammatory conditions, wound healing, and rehabilitation. This continuing education course provides a practical overview of PBMT and its clinical application in veterinary patients.
Participants will review the biologic and physics of PBMT, including wavelength, power density, energy dosage, and proposed mechanisms of action at the cellular and tissue levels. Current veterinary literature will be discussed to evaluate the indications and therapeutic effects of PBMT across common clinical scenarios.
The course will address practical considerations for clinical use of PBMT, including patient selection, treatment protocols, safety standards, and contraindications. Common applications such as musculoskeletal pain, osteoarthritis, wound management, and post-operative care will be presented to illustrate appropriate integration into veterinary practice. Additionally, the course shares newer modalities for the use of PBMT, including internal medicine usage, allergic dermatitis, as well as dental disease.
Designed for both veterinarians and veterinary technicians, this course emphasizes safe, ethical, and informed use of PBMT while supporting interprofessional collaboration within the veterinary healthcare team.

courses.title: Vet Teams 2.0: The Next Generation! Preparing veterinary teams for the future of client care, technology, & teamwork.
courses.description:
Veterinary practices are under pressure like never before. Pet owners expect faster communication, easier scheduling, and a seamless experience that blends compassion with convenience. Meanwhile, staff shortages and burnout are straining teams, leaving front desks overwhelmed. Technology and AI present opportunities to ease this burden - but only if they're implemented thoughtfully.
This session will cut through the hype and focus on what matters most: how veterinary teams can leverage technology to reduce stress, improve client communication, and preserve the human-animal bond. Attendees will first engage with framing questions on AI, communication tools, and client expectations, then steer the conversation through live polls and Q&A.
The goal: practical, resourceful strategies to help veterinary leaders prepare their practices for the next generation of care without losing the empathy that defines the profession.

courses.title: Gilvetmab: A Novel Immunotherapy in the Fight Against Cancer
courses.description: Veterinary oncology has seen significant advancements in immunotherapy, offering novel treatment approaches for companion animals diagnosed with cancer. Immunotherapy aims to harness the body's immune system to recognize and attack cancerous cells, reducing reliance on traditional treatments such as chemotherapy and radiation therapy. This lecture discusses the novel class of agents called "checkpoint inhibitors," focusing on the first in veterinary medicine, Gilvemab.

courses.title: Puppy Socialization or Infectious Disease Prevention - Can't We Have Both??
courses.description: The first 12 weeks of a puppy's life are prime time for socialization. Failure to adequately socialize puppies during this time is arguably the most common reason for the development of major, often life- threatening behavioral concerns in adult dogs. Many serious problems can be prevented if appropriate care is given during these early, sensitive weeks of a puppy's life. One major challenge to adequate socialization is a puppy's simultaneous vulnerability to infectious diseases. As maternal antibodies wane and immune systems lag in their full response to immunization, many in the veterinary community advise against early contact with dogs and environments outside the safety of home. So how do we navigate these competing risks and promote overall behavioral and physical health? This talk will review key concepts in puppy socialization AND infectious disease prevention, providing a practical approach to safe and effective socialization practices.

courses.title: The Vet Economy Exposed: Where We Are, What's Next, and What to Do Now
courses.description: Is the veterinary economy truly recession-resistant? This course presents findings from a peer-reviewed study in Frontiers in Veterinary Science that models and forecasts the veterinary medicine business cycle using 25 years of industry-specific data. Participants will learn why the industry entered a recessionary phase in late 2024, what the forecast suggests through 2026, and - most importantly - what practice owners and managers should be doing right now. Phase-specific management strategies covering cost containment, workforce planning, client retention, and capital positioning are discussed for each stage of the veterinary economic cycle.

courses.title: All things allergies! From nose to tail and ear to paw...
courses.description: Managing canine atopic dermatitis (cAD) can be difficult and require multimodal therapy. The International Committee of Allergic Diseases of Animals (ICADA) is a group of board-certified veterinary dermatologists that arranges publications of critical reviews on allergic diseases of domestic animal species. Recently, ICADA has updated the guidelines and knowledge available regarding the pathogenesis and treatment of cAD. This lecture will review these updated guidelines and how to apply them to daily clinical management of cAD including skin barrier treatment, microbiome, immunotherapy, genetic factors, etc.

courses.title: Grain of Truth: Sorting Facts from Fables in Pet Nutrition
courses.description:
This course addresses prevalent nutrition myths affecting veterinary practice and clinical
dietary recommendations. Veterinarians will learn evidence-based clarifications to common misconceptions about
pet food ingredients, formulation principles, and nutritional adequacy. Topics include digestibility myths, protein
requirements, ingredient quality (by-products, grains, legumes, oils), human-grade standards, supplement necessity,
raw feeding claims, weight management strategies, and a clearer understanding of the different nutrition
credentials.

courses.title: When less is more: Is once-daily insulin possible in diabetic dogs?
courses.description: This webinar unites the patient, the pet owner, and the healthcare team to achieve the best possible outcomes in managing the many changes associated with diabetes mellitus. At the center are once-daily treatment options that simplifies care for most pets. In this talk, attendees will learn how a once-daily insulin protocol can be a practical reality for most diabetic dogs using case examples to show how to successfully start, regulate, and maintain patients to optimize patient and owner quality of life.

courses.title: Save More Teeth with ReGum Vet Podcast
courses.description: This talk is intended to review the incidence of periodontal disease, the differences in treatment based on bone levels, and the indication for the use of ReGumVet in patients with advanced periodontal disease. Attendees will learn tips for ultrasonic cleaning as well as hand instrumentation to prepare the surface for the application of ReGumVet in general practice. The steps for placement as well as flap closure are discussed to allow the attendee to be able to save more teeth with ReGumVet.

courses.title: Personalized Care: Adapting Your Approach for Breed and Age
courses.description:
Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Personalized Veterinary Care in Action
Join us for a practical webinar on delivering personalized veterinary care by adapting your approach to each patient's unique needs. Using case studies, you will learn how a simple tool can help you recognize breed- and age-specific risks for a wide range of conditions, from orthopedic issues like cruciate tears and arthritis to heart disease and cancer. You will enable your team to refine your diagnostic and treatment recommendations while building trust with pet families. Discover how this personalized, data-driven approach enhances efficiency, strengthens client relationships, and ensures a deeper level of care, no matter what comes through your door.

courses.title: Fetch Nashville on Demand 2026
courses.description: This is the On Demand version of our Fetch conference in Nashville. Fetch, a dvm360 conference, at Nashville, TN is a live interactive, in-person conference with a combination of both medical and nonmedical programs created for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and practice managers to achieve their continuing education in veterinary medicine. Educational content tracks include: Anesthesiology, Animal Welfare, Artificial Intelligence, Behavior, Cardiology, Emergency Medicine, Feline Medicine, General Practice, Geriatrics , Hands-On Lab, Infectious Diseases, Integrative Medicine, Internal Medicine, Laser Therapy, Marketing, Nutrition, Oncology, Ophthalmology, Pain Management, Parasitology, Peer to Peer Breakfast, Sponsored CE, Practice Management, Peer to Peer Luncheon, Sponsored CE, Practice Management, Practice Management, Practice Ownership, Shelter Medicine, Surgery, Technician Anesthesiology, Technician Critical Care, Technician Feline Medicine, Technician Medicine, Technician Pain Management, Toxicology, Veterinary Crossfire , Wellness

courses.title: Canine Lymphoma Treatment - Never a One Size Fits All
courses.description: This CE will discuss how Laverdia CA-1 (verdinexor tabs) fit into treatment of dogs with lymphoma. We will discuss the mechanism of action, dosing, adverse events and efficacy of this novel agent. Finally discussing why Laverdia CA-1 should be utilized in the primary care setting.

courses.title: The Current Ins and Outs of Cellular Therapies for Gastrointestinal Disease
courses.description: This webinar will discuss the current information around the use of cellular therapies including mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) therapy to treat chronic gastrointestinal disease (i.e. chronic inflammatory enteropathy (CIE), previously known as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)). Attendees will gain an evidence-based understanding of the rationale, specific therapies and applications, opportunities, and challenges.

courses.title: 3 Reasons Smart Practice Owners are Selling Sooner
courses.description: This presentation will explore the top three reasons why today's savvy veterinary practice owners are choosing to sell their practices sooner rather than later. We'll discuss how the right sale can lead to increased job satisfaction, financial freedom, and a more fulfilling life beyond the clinic doors. Attendees will learn how selling a practice at the right time can not only elevate their professional experience but also enable them to pursue personal aspirations and spend more quality time with family. Importantly, for those concerned about "losing their identity" as a veterinarian or practice owner, this session will reveal how selling - if engineered precisely - can actually enhance their sense of self, allowing them to integrate new identities, such as parent, traveler, hobbyist, without losing their professional legacy. Transitions Elite will guide participants through key strategies and practical steps for planning a successful exit no matter their age.

courses.title: Veterinary MRI Training Course with John Posh
courses.description: This innovative and comprehensive online course features 13 videos created by John Posh, R.T. (R)(MR), Director of the MRI Internship Program at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. The course is designed for veterinarians, licensed veterinary technicians as well as human trained technicians. The course consists of 13 video lessons. Each video lesson is followed by a short exam. Students must complete and pass all 13 exams and complete the technical portion to receive 14.5 CE credits approved by RACE.

courses.title: C15:0 (Pentadecanoic Acid): Newly Discovered Essential Fatty Acid to Support Longevity
courses.description: This course covers the science behind C15:0 (pentadecanoic acid) as a newly discovered essential fatty acid, the first essential fatty acid to be found in over 90 years.
