Specific topics to be covered include understanding the mechanisms of action of C15:0; demonstrated efficacy of C15:0 related to metabolic, heart, liver, immune, and red blood cell health; pathophysiology of a newly discovered nutritional C15:0 deficiency syndrome (Cellular Fragility Syndrome); blood tests to detect and treat nutritional C15:0 deficiencies; specific mechanisms and optimal C15:0 levels to enhance multiple mammalian longevity pathways; cell-based performance and safety of pure C15:0 supplementation compared to leading longevity molecules, including rapamycin.

courses.title: It Takes a Village: Who You Need in Your Corner When Opening a Practice
courses.description: Opening a veterinary practice is an exciting milestone, but no one does it alone. Success comes from surrounding yourself with the right team of advisors, mentors, and partners who can help you navigate the challenges of ownership. In this session, we'll explore the "village" every new practice owner needs to thrive, from financial and legal experts to operational support and trusted veterinary peers. You'll gain insight into how to build your dream team, avoid common pitfalls, and set yourself up for long-term success.

courses.title: The Business of Veterinary Supplements
courses.description: This program examines the role of veterinary supplements within modern clinical practice, focusing on how supplement recommendations influence patient care, client trust, and practice sustainability. Participants will explore current trends in the veterinary supplement market, common points where adherence and continuity of care are lost, and practical systems that support consistent, medically grounded recommendations. The course emphasizes staged care models, pricing as a trust signal, team alignment, and refill pathways that help clinics maintain continuity of care while strengthening the veterinarian-client-patient relationship. Keywords include veterinary supplements, nutraceuticals, practice management, client adherence, preventive care, and clinical consistency.

courses.title: Two Day Fracture Course
courses.description:
This course is designed for small animal practitioners seeking practical, effective methods to manage long bone fractures in dogs and cats. Participants will learn simplified techniques suitable for both straightforward and comminuted fractures, using modern implants that enhance surgical efficiency and reduce costs. By following key principles of fracture repair, complications can be minimized and outcomes improved.
Through a combination of lectures, clinical case discussions, and hands-on practice, attendees will gain confidence in choosing appropriate fixation methods and performing repairs. Practical sessions include fracture repair on plastic bone models and cadavers, followed by postoperative radiographs to assess technique and reinforce learning.
Learning Objectives
Understand the biology of bone healing and differentiate between primary and secondary healing
Review fracture classification systems and fixation strategies
Learn direct and indirect fracture reduction techniques and when to apply each approach
Apply the biomechanics of intramedullary pins, cerclage wires, bone screws, and plates, including compression, neutralization, and bridging methods

courses.title: Investigating Animal Cruelty: A Scientific Approach
courses.description: Animal cruelty is a crime that knows no boundaries. Veterinarians and veterinary technicians need to be able to document the injuries victims of animal cruelty have, be able to collect medical evidence, get evidence analyzed, and must be able to convey their findings in written reports, and verbally. Participants of this workshop will learn how to work-up different types of animal cruelty cases and how to document cases using best practices.

courses.title: Patella Luxation Online Course
courses.description:
Theoretical Part
01 Welcome
02 About Patellar Luxations
03 Clinical Examination
04 Case Evaluation
05 Realignment by TTT
06 The Rapid Luxation Approach
07 Special Cases
08 Surgery Equipment
09 The Surgery in Theory (Animation)
Practical Part
10 Surgery Preparation
11 Sulcoplasty
12 Rapid Luxation Surgery
Advises
13 How to begin
14 Exam
Finally you will have the chance to do an exam with multiple choice questions and get a certificate in order to get Training Points from your veterinary association.

courses.title: Catch It Before It Counts: The New Era of Canine Cancer Screening
courses.description: This course educates veterinary professionals on the critical role of early cancer detection in canine patients. Participants will learn how IDEXX's specialized cancer screening blood tests can enhance diagnostic accuracy, support clinical decision-making, and lead to improved patient outcomes through proactive care.

courses.title: From Diagnosis to Lifelong Care: Advancing Feline Chronic Kidney Disease Management
courses.description: This talk will cover key aspects of improving the lives of cats with chronic kidney disease (CKD), including the pathogenesis and staging of CKD, dietary complications, and management of conditions such as azotemia, acidosis, hypokalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypertension, anemia, dehydration, and anorexia. It will also address the latest treatment breakthroughs, including new therapies for anemia and strategies for managing complications like intestinal dysbiosis. Attendees will gain comprehensive insights into the diagnosis and holistic management of CKD in feline patients.

courses.title: Is Osteoarthritis a disease of Young Dogs?
courses.description: This program explores the evolving understanding of osteoarthritis (OA) in dogs, challenging the traditional view that it is solely a disease of older animals. Through current research and clinical insights, it highlights how OA affects dogs of all ages, breeds, and sizes, emphasizing the importance of early diagnosis and proactive pain management. Attendees will gain a deeper appreciation of the genetic and developmental factors contributing to OA and learn practical approaches to better identify and treat this common yet often underdiagnosed condition in canine patients.

courses.title: How to Ensure you are Ready to Exit Your Practice With Plenty of Wealth
courses.description: Selling your practice might be the biggest financial decision you ever make, but most owners wait too long or plan too little only to exit under stress, with less money than they should. In this webinar, we will share the core financial and emotional strategies every practice owner needs to understand to exit successfully, protect their wealth, and retire confidently.

courses.title: Mitral Valve Disease: Managing Clinical Signs & Extending Life
courses.description: This session provides an overview of recent clinical trials evaluating pharmacologic treatment of heart disease in dogs with clinical signs, emphasizing strategies for the primary care veterinarian. The clinical recognition, stabilization, and long-term management of congestive heart failure in dogs will be explored using case vignettes and a question-and-answer approach between speakers- from signs of cough to the first hospitalization to the patient with advanced, refractory disease.

courses.title: The Must-Know Deets on Canine Diabetes
courses.description: In this one-hour lecture, Dr. Natalie Marks will start with a quick review of the pathophysiology of canine diabetes, its similarities to human juvenile diabetes, and the differences between canine and feline manifestations of this disease. Attendees will be presented with common and uncommon clinical signs, as well as clinicopathologic abnormalities, that help identify co-morbidities. The diagnostic strategy will be quickly reviewed, allowing more time to be spent on treatment and monitoring options. Innovations and strategies will conclude the lecture for attendee consideration.

courses.title: Hot Topics in Dairy Calf Research: What Does the Industry Need to Know?
courses.description: Veterinarians play a critical role in calf health and development, and staying current with the latest research is essential for guiding clients and improving outcomes. This course will explore emerging science and key trends in dairy calf management, focusing on findings presented at the 2024 American Dairy Science Association annual meeting.

courses.title: Pet Food Labels: What You Need to Know and Understand to Discuss Them with Confidence
courses.description:
Pet food labels contain a wealth of regulated information, but interpreting that information accurately requires knowing the rules behind it. This continuing education program gives veterinary professionals a practical, evidence-based framework for reading and explaining pet food labels, so they can guide client conversations with clarity rather than hesitation.
Participants will move through the full anatomy of a pet food label: from the legal and regulatory structure governing what must appear on the label (and who enforces it), to the Nutritional Adequacy Statement, ingredient list, Guaranteed Analysis, and product claims. The course addresses common client misconceptions head-on, including why ingredient list position is not a reliable proxy for dietary quality, what "by-products" and "meal" ingredients actually mean under AAFCO definitions, why Guaranteed Analysis values are minimums and maximums rather than actuals, and how to convert nutrients across dry matter, as-fed, and energy bases for meaningful diet comparisons. The WSAVA Global Nutrition Committee guidelines are introduced as a practical tool for evaluating pet food manufacturers beyond the label itself.
By the end of this program, participants will be equipped to shift the conversation in the exam room from ingredient-list anxiety to nutritional science, meeting clients where they are while grounding recommendations in regulatory reality.

courses.title: Heart Failure! Heart Failure? What to do when they're not responding
courses.description: This webinar will review important considerations when managing a suspect heart failure patient that is not initially responding to conventional heart failure therapy. First you must ask yourself - do I have a correct diagnosis? If so, then the next questions is how do I escalate or add drugs or implement other strategies to relieve the congestion. We will review the various presentations or phenotypes of heart failure and how to optimize therapy for a successful outcome.

courses.title: Restoring Bile Acid Metabolism After Antibiotic-Induced Dysbiosis in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Peptacetobacter hiranonis is emerging as one of the most clinically important commensal bacteria in companion animal gastrointestinal health. This course provides a comprehensive overview of its evolutionary history, functional role in bile acid metabolism, and association with dysbiosis in dogs and cats. Participants will gain a deep understanding of how P. hiranonis and its closely related cat species, Peptacetobacter felis convert primary to secondary bile acids - metabolites essential for maintaining microbial balance, regulating mucosal inflammation, and inhibiting opportunistic pathogens. The session will expand on how antibiotic exposure, even months prior, reduces or eliminates P. hiranonis and P. felis, leading to impaired bile acid metabolism and a cascade of dysbiotic changes manifesting as chronic diarrhea, recurrent GI signs, and reduced microbiome resilience. We will review the phylogenetic context of the Peptacetobacter group, its susceptibility to antibiotics, and the implications for clinical decision-making. The session includes a review of recent placebo-controlled field studies evaluating targeted Peptacetobacter restoration strategies in dogs and cats. Findings from one such investigation will be presented as an example of how live biotherapeutic approaches may influence microbial and metabolic recovery. This investigation was a placebo-controlled field trial in 72 dogs and 65 cats evaluating a targeted live probiotic containing P. hiranonis or P. felis, respectively. Attendees will learn how supplementation restored microbial and metabolic balance, improved clinical outcomes, and showed sustained benefits after treatment cessation. Species-specific factors, age, and antibiotic-recency effects will be discussed, along with guidance for integrating Peptacetobacter restoration into common clinical scenarios. This course equips clinicians with evidence-based strategies to identify P. hiranonis and P. felis deficiencies, support bile acid recovery,

courses.title: That's not my job!: Practical solutions for workplace toxicity
courses.description: With the shortage of veterinary staff and high caseloads, team members are struggling with burnout. Unfortunately, workplace toxicity contributes to employee burnout and dissatisfaction, which can lead to a vicious cycle of turnover and burnout for those team members left behind. Recent studies and focus groups have served to highlight the components of a toxic workplace, in which toxic attitudes are ignored or not addressed. This session will describe the causes and consequences of a toxic veterinary work environment and introduce some strategies for mitigating workplace toxicity.

courses.title: Fetch National Harbor On Demand, Part 1
courses.description: Fetch, a dvm360 conference, at National Harbor, MD is a live interactive, in-person conference with a combination of both medical and nonmedical programs created for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and practice managers to achieve their continuing education in veterinary medicine. Educational content tracks include: Anesthesiology, Bandaging, Behavior, Cardiology, Clinical Pathology, Critical Care, CSR Receptionist Track ,Dentistry, Dermatology, Feline Medicine, Feline Nutrition, Gastroenterology, General Practice, Hands-On Lab, Integrative Medicine, Internal Medicine, Keynote, Laser Therapy, Marketing, Neurology, Nutrition, Oncology, Ophthalmology, Orthopedics, Pain Management, Parasitology, Peer to Peer Lunch, Practice Ownership, Pharmacology, Practice Management, Rehabilitation, Spectrum of Care; Ophthalmology, Surgery, Technician Cardiology, Technician Critical Care, Technician Emergency Medicine, Technician Internal Medicine, Technician Medicine, Technician Radiology, Toxicology, and Wound Management

courses.title: Risks, Rewards, and Regulation: Getting Comfortable With Compounding
courses.description: Whether your patient is a picky pug or a carsick kitty, this interactive session will equip you with the necessary compounding knowledge and tools to customize care and understand liability. You'll learn about the evolution of compounding and regulations before diving into strategies for maximizing benefits, minimizing risk, and mitigating common prescription errors.

courses.title: Diagnosing OA & IA Treatments: A Focus on Synovetin OA
courses.description: This lecture explores the clinical diagnosis of canine osteoarthritis (OA), including the use of physical exams, imaging, and diagnostic tools. It also reviews intra-articular (IA) treatment options, their mechanisms, indications, and evidence for effectiveness in managing canine OA.

courses.title: You Asked, We Answered: The Most Commonly Asked Questions About the Future of Stem Cell Therapy in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This lecture addresses the most commonly asked questions about stem cell therapy in veterinary medicine including where they are sourced from, their mechanisms of action, their safety profiles, and how the new way of sourcing stem cells from healthy donors differs from the old way of sourcing stem cells from the patient.

courses.title: Chronic Disease Management in Practice: Enhancing Care Through Personalized Recommendations
courses.description: Chronic conditions like kidney disease and lymphoma make up a significant portion of visits, yet every patient and pet family are unique and could benefit from a personalized care plan. This presentation utilizes a case-based approach to demonstrate how evidence-based medicine can be paired with pet family-centered communication to help teams tailor recommendations across the spectrum of care. Participants will level-up their navigation of difficult conversations with pet parents, applying proven clinical empathy and nonjudgmental communication strategies, incorporating breed - specific risks based on the latest data, and developing care plans that align with each pet family's goals and finances.

courses.title: Stem Cell Applications in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Stem cell therapy is being explored for a variety of conditions in companion animals, including refractory feline chronic gingivostomatitis, osteoarthritis, atopic dermatitis, asthma, inflammatory bowel disease, and immune-mediated encephalitis. While most other treatments target symptom management, stem cell therapy targets the root cause of disease, working with the body's own cells to promote healing. The basics of how stem cells modulate the immune system and promote tissue repair will be discussed. We will review how stem cell therapy is being explored in veterinary medicine and how it can ultimately be incorporated into daily veterinary practice.

courses.title: Fetch On-Demand--Kansas City 2024
courses.description:
This online non-interactive distance education program offers learners a wide array of medical and non medical continuing education options. Learners will gain a comprehensive understanding of the principles, techniques, and best practices across various veterinary disciplines. They will be equipped with the knowledge to accurately diagnose, treat, and manage a wide range of conditions, ensuring improved patient outcomes and advancing their clinical skills.
Learners are expected to receive actionable insights into both common and complex veterinary issues, emphasizing evidence-based approaches and practical applications that can immediately enhance clinical practice. They may highlight the value of the program in improving patient care and expanding

courses.title: When less is more: Is once-daily insulin possible in diabetic dogs?
courses.description: This webinar unites the patient, the pet owner, and the healthcare team to achieve the best possible outcomes in managing the many changes associated with diabetes mellitus. At the center are once-daily treatment options that simplifies care for most pets. In this talk, attendees will learn how a once-daily insulin protocol can be a practical reality for most diabetic dogs using case examples to show how to successfully start, regulate, and maintain patients to optimize patient and owner quality of life.

courses.title: A comparative look at pet food formats: Making informed choices for our pets
courses.description: This presentation explores the evolving landscape of pet food formats, comparing the nutritional profiles and impacts of dry kibble, wet food, treats, supplements, and fresh food options. Dr. Nolan Frantz, a leading expert in companion animal nutrition with extensive industry experience, will present data from two original studies comparing extruded kibble to fresh and human-grade diets in beagles. These studies investigated the effects of different food formats on fecal characteristics, microbiome composition, serum profiles, hematology, gene expression, and skin/coat health. Additionally, the presentation will discuss the pros and cons of each pet food format, considering factors such as cost, convenience, palatability, nutritional content, and long-term health implications. Further research is needed to fully understand the long-term effects of different pet food formats on canine health and to identify the key drivers of any health implications. The presentation concludes with a discussion of the significant growth of the pet food industry and the increasing consumer demand for fresh and human-grade options.

courses.title: Strategically Planning How to Set Up Your Finances for a Banner Year
courses.description:
Are you ready to make 2025 your most successful year yet? This engaging and actionable webinar is designed to help professionals like you set clear goals, evaluate growth opportunities, and optimize your practice for efficiency and success.
We'll start by focusing on goal setting and production targets to ensure you're aligned with your financial and professional objectives. Next, we'll explore whether expansion is the right move for your practice, using a proven checklist to guide your decision - making process.
Discover how to make your practice more efficient by analyzing key metrics, updating systems, and making strategic financial adjustments. We'll also cover collaboration with your professional team to review essential plans and insurance policies, keeping your business and personal finances on track.
Whether you're looking to grow, streamline, or solidify your operations, this webinar will provide practical strategies and tools to help you thrive in 2025 and beyond.

courses.title: Munching with Microbes: Gut-Ready for Nutrition
courses.description: Nutrition provides energy to patients, and the microbes inhabiting the biome in the large intestine. The GI or gut microbiome is becoming recognized by general practitioners as playing a role in patient health and the nutrients fed to sustain host life, can also influence these microbes and their functions. This session will offer insight into the factors associated with gut dysbiosis, and how intestinal physiology maintains a healthy balance for the patient and the microbiome. Looking at key nutrition factors, and utilizing research associated with nutrition focused on the state of the gut microbiome, we will explore how to complete a diet assessment improving microbe balance. Additionally, how to calculate energy requirements and transition nutrition will be discussed to ensure a slow and beneficial change occurs. Finally, supplementation including vitamin, mineral, and biotics will be briefly discussed as considerations when managing patients with gut dysbiosis.

courses.title: Unleashing the Secrets of the Canine Gut: The DoggyBiome Study
courses.description: Despite considerable interest and research in the canine fecal microbiome, our understanding of its species-level composition remains incomplete, as the majority of studies have only provided genus-level resolution. This study used full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing to analyze the fecal microbiomes of 286 healthy dogs in North America. We identified 23 core bacterial species, including Collinsella intestinalis and Prevotella copri, which comprised 75% of the microbiome on average. Factors like diet, sex, neuter status, age, and body weight influenced microbiome variation. Notably, dogs fed kibble had more core taxa and were enriched in species like C. intestinalis and P. copri compared to those on raw or cooked diets. Dogs on raw diets had higher levels of Bacteroides vulgatus and Enterococcus faecium. The findings highlight the species-level composition and factors affecting the canine fecal microbiome.

courses.title: Beyond GI Disease: Expanding the Clinical Potential of FMT in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This webinar highlights the expanding potential of Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) in veterinary medicine beyond gastrointestinal disease. By exploring the complex connections between the gut microbiome and other organ systems, this session examines how FMT may influence and support treatment for a range of non-GI related conditions. A panel of experienced veterinarians will share clinical case applications where FMT has been incorporated into the management of disorders such as atopic dermatitis, hepatic disease, chronic kidney disease, metabolic and behavioral disorders, immune-mediated diseases, pancreatic dysfunction, and cancer. The discussion will emphasize both scientific understanding and practical experience, offering insight into patient selection, treatment protocols, outcome tracking, and integrative care approaches. The session concludes with an open Q&A to foster clinical dialogue and critical thinking among participants.

courses.title: Chronic Pain Management: Looking beyond NSAIDs
courses.description: This webinar is designed for veterinary professionals seeking to enhance their understanding and skills in treating chronic pain in their patients. We will explore the benefits of a multimodal approach to pain management, integrating both pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions. Attendees will gain insights into the latest evidence-based practices for using medications, physical therapy, acupuncture, environmental modifications, and other strategies to improve patient outcomes and quality of life. Join us for an in-depth discussion on how to create and implement individualized pain management plans that address the unique needs of each patient.

courses.title: 5 Ways to Build Better Patient-Client Relationships with AI: Strengthening Care and Connection in Veterinary Practice
courses.description: This course, designed for veterinarians and veterinary practice managers, explores five key strategies for enhancing patient-client relationships through the integration of AI technology in clinical practice. Participants will learn how to leverage AI scribes to improve documentation efficiency, reduce administrative burdens, and enhance client communication, allowing for more personal, attentive care during appointments. Topics include AI-driven documentation, creating comprehensive medical records, delivering clear discharge summaries, and strategies for fostering trust and loyalty. This course will also cover practical applications for using AI tools to reclaim time for both patient care and work-life balance.

courses.title: FELINE DENTISTRY AND ORAL SURGERY (789-36990)
courses.description:
Feline dentistry can be frustrating for some veterinarians. The goal of this course is to help veterinarians get more comfortable with cat dentistry and is for veterinarians only.
The course curriculum will focus on anatomy, oral pathology, regional anesthesia, a step-by-step approach on extractions and extraction complications. There is a 3-hour lab section of the course will focus on the steps of surgical extraction in cats, including mucogingivial flap design, tooth sectioning, bone removal, use of a dental elevator and luxator, alveoplasty, periosteal releasing incisions, and tension-free closure.
We will cover extraction complications that arise in feline dentistry, including retained roots, mandibular fractures and displaced tooth roots. Additionally, we will review best practices in educating clients about feline dentistry and how to improve client compliance.
There will be two instructors and 1 assistant to ensure that participants will have a high level of attention. Each participant will have a brand-new, sharp, extraction instrument set designed specifically for feline dentistry to use and then take home with them. Magnification is extremely helpful for this course. Please bring your own if you have it. We will provide magnification for those who do not.

courses.title: Equine Upper Airway Symposium
courses.description: This three-and-a-half-day symposium offers lectures and wet labs designed to present in-depth, current scientific information regarding pathophysiology, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis for upper airway (UA) conditions in the horse. The target participants for the meeting are veterinarians in resident training programs and clinicians who have not had the desired exposure to UA conditions in the horse.

courses.title: Early Diagnosis and Improved Management of CKD in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Early diagnosis of CKD gives us the best opportunity to slow the progressive nature of the disease and buys time for client education about kidney function and disease which will increase client compliance. The International Renal Interest Society (IRIS) CKD Staging System will be used to tailor CKD treatments to patients based on their stage of disease. How to monitor FGF-23 concentrations to improve control of serum phosphorus will be addressed

courses.title: Phoenix Landing Wellness Retreat 2026: How Can I Help?
courses.description: A 2-day conference addressing health issues related to parrots. Veterinarians and other speakers will address common illnesses, preventative measures, diagnostics, case studies, approaches to physical and mental health, as well as conservation strategies for wild parrots that can teach us so much about the needs of captive parrots.

courses.title: Navigating the Allergy Journey: Managing Acute Flares of Allergic Dermatitis
courses.description: As allergy season approaches, veterinary professionals must be equipped with effective strategies to manage acute flares of allergic dermatitis in dogs. This session, Navigating the Allergy Journey: Managing Acute Flares of Allergic Dermatitis, offers practical, science-based insights into diagnosing and treating pruritic patients. Participants will explore a simplified diagnostic approach, learn how to optimize the use of fast-acting therapies like Apoquel and Cytopoint, and understand the importance of client communication and compliance. With a focus on real-world cases and current research, this course empowers clinicians to deliver rapid relief and long-term success for their allergic patients.

courses.title: Updates on the Staging & Management of Mitral Valve Disease in Dogs
courses.description: Current management of mitral valve disease (MVD) in dogs is guided by consensus panel guidelines based on cardiac staging. This session covers recently updated staging guidelines for MVD with clinical case examples from patients in different stages of disease. Practical use of cardiac drugs at various stages of heart disease are considered, including subclinical disease, the initial presentation of heart failure, and long-term management of advanced disease.

courses.title: Dental Radiograph Positioning Training
courses.description: Dental Radiography Positioning Training will provide hands on training for veterinarians and technicians on proper radiograph acquisition technique, and the operation of and care for their equipment.

courses.title: SDEP ECHO PROGRESSION (802-37652)
courses.description: With this 2 credit online program, you will learn to perform a complete echo from start to finish while implementing the SDEP SonoPath's Diagnostic Efficiency Protocol scanning techniques. The program includes SDEP ECHO Progression, bonus aortic outflow velocity in felines, and the post-test to earn your CE credits. The SDEP Echo progression also utilizes a numbering system to optimize every region of the heart to evaluate functions, velocities, pressures and chamber sizes. SDEP Echo includes three separate measurements for the left atrial measurements and all standard Doppler velocities. Alternative views image the right atrium and auricle to ensure visualization of heart base masses. This protocol affords the most complete image set for evaluation of the heart from acquired to congenital disease.

courses.title: SDEP 17 PT. ABDOMEN PROGRESSION (802-37651)
courses.description: With this 2 CE credit, online program you will learn how SDEP utilizes a 3-second cine loop approach in a 17-point protocol that produces a full abdominal scan, from the deep pelvic urethra to the diaphragm and everything in between. Image shunts, bile duct obstruction, renal and bladder pathology, gastrointestinal obstruction, pancreatitis, masses, peritonitis, mucocele, ascites, pericardial effusion, built-in redundancy of image angles ensures, multiple views of every organ and organ system, minimizes the potential for missed lesions. Each step is numbered for easy reference, reinforcing communication between instructor, sonographer, and specialist. The sonogram is performed consistently and repeatedly in both traditional scanning scenarios and emergency situations.

courses.title: SIMPLE & SURGICAL EXTRACTIONS OF THE DOG & CAT (588-35742)
courses.description:
Simple & Surgical Extractions for the Dog & Cat
This Non Interactive-distance course for 7 CE hours provides examples and indications for simple and surgical extractions, addresses complications, provides detailed images and video describing the correct technique to ensure maximum success.

courses.provider: UNIVERSITY OF DENVER, DANIELS COLLEGE OF BUSINESS
courses.title: VMG 1.0 Leadership Academy
courses.description: VMG 1.0 Leadership Academy is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Happy Endings: Not Just a Fairy Tale
courses.description: This video course will feature four sections, through which we'll learn how to make end of life care an enjoyable and rewarding component of veterinary practice. Discover ways to create happy memories for your clients, your patients, and your staff. We will explore end of life care from both a medical perspective and an interpersonal, relationship-building perspective.

courses.title: WORKING THROUGH ASCITES (802-41332)
courses.description:
Changes to the normal abdominal anatomy when effusions are present in the midst of pathological processes will be demonstrated along with the degrees of change and how they correlate to certain pathologies.
Course Objectives:
Hemoabdomen
Transudate
Modified transudate
Exudative processes
A deductive process from the sonographic and medical perspective regarding the cause for effusion formation will be explained and demonstrated with various case presentations
Sampling pathological organs causing effusions by FNA and drainage procedures from an ultrasound-guided process

courses.title: Finding Hidden Opportunities in Your P&L: Using Data-Driven Strategies to Strengthen Clinic Finances
courses.description:
This course is designed to provide a practical guide to revenue optimization for Veterinary Practice Owners and Hospital Managers looking to offset rising operating costs. We will discuss some of the hidden savings opportunities found in a veterinary practices Profit and Loss statement, the hidden costs associated with missed forward bookings and examine opportunities like surcharging that can be used to protect the bottom line of a veterinary practice.
Learning Objectives
Analyze the hidden financial impact of missed forward bookings, specifically regarding staffing inefficiencies and recapture expenses.
Identify high-churn clients using ROI modeling and modern software tools and how to leverage the latest technology to streamline this analysis and improve retention
Optimize profit margins by auditing card processing fees, understanding the real margin impact and how to successfully implement surcharging to offset rising credit card processing costs.

courses.title: Finding Hidden Opportunities in Your P&L (On-Demand)
courses.description: This on demand webinar course is designed to provide a practical guide to revenue optimization for Veterinary Practice Owners and Hospital Managers looking to offset rising operating costs. We will discuss some of the hidden savings opportunities found in a veterinary practice profit and loss statement, the hidden costs associated with missed forward bookings and examine opportunities like surcharging that can be used to protect the practice bottom line.

courses.title: Co-occurring of Animal Cruelty and Human Interpersonal Violence
courses.description: The Link Between Animal Abuse and Human Interpersonal Violence: A Veterinary Perspective. In January of 2014 NYPD formally became the responding law enforcement agency for all complaints of animal cruelty in New York City. Because NYPD has always been the responding law enforcement agency for domestic violence in New York City adding the animal component to their work has resulted in the identification of many cases where there is both animal abuse and human interpersonal violence. This presentation will provide the attendee with medical and legal information about these types of cases and illustrate important points by looking at actual cases.

courses.title: Getting Cats to Eat: It is More Than Pouring Food in a Bowl (TECH391)
courses.description: The veterinary healthcare team should be the preferred, expert source of the best nutritional information for cats. Proper nutritional management is one of the most important factors in maximizing health, performance, and longevity in cats, in addition to managing disease conditions. This session will review the physiology and behavior of feeding cats, and the importance of recognizing the unique needs of an obligate carnivore. We will also discuss tips to ensure cats are getting the nutrients they need, recognizing and avoiding food aversion and fixed taste preferences, to the bowls they eat out of, to those housed in multi-cat homes.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Early Life Stressors and the Behavior and Physiology of Rescue Kittens (On Demand)
courses.description:
Across species, early-life stressors, such as inadequate nutrition, maternal separation, unreliable access to shelter, threats/abuse, and disease, profoundly affect brain development and behavior. Research has shown these stressors can impair cognitive, emotional, and social functions as well as alter the body's stress response systems, particularly the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. In kittens specifically, early nutritional stress and maternal separation have been linked to learning deficits, abnormal fear responses, increased aggression, and altered play behavior.
Our study examined how early-life stress affects the behavior and physiology of 50 homeless rescue kittens. The kittens in this study were placed into foster homes under the care of the Prince Edward Island Humane Society. The kittens then underwent behavioural testing at 8-, 10-, and 12-weeks of age. Hair samples were collected at the 8-week testing and used to measure hair cortisol concentration (HCC), an assay for cumulative stress over the previous 3 months. Blood samples were collected when the kittens were neutered and used to measure relative telomere lengths (RTL), an assay for epigenetic changes from prenatal and early-life stress. The results of the study revealed complex and sometimes unexpected patterns. As expected, kittens separated from their mothers had significantly higher HCC, but against expectations, they had longer RTL. Similarly, as expected, kittens approached a novel human more readily at the 10- and 12-week testing compared to the 8-weeks testing but in contrast to the initial hypothesis, they became less tolerant of being held by a novel human as they got older. Interestingly, kittens who did not approach a novel human during testing had significantly lower HCC, suggesting a blunted stress response, rather than simple shyness. These findings demonstrate the complicated nature of the relationships between early-life stress, physiological responses, epigenetic changes

courses.title: Keys to Accessible Cytology Screening: How AI Is Bridging the Gap
courses.description: Explore the impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven cytology in veterinary diagnostics. In this webinar, Drs. Eric Morissette and Kristin Owens will review cytology sample preparation and how the Vetscan Imagyst's AI Masses indication can quickly identify cancer-suggestive cells and help veterinarians make timely treatment decisions and improve patient care.

courses.title: Hypotension During Anesthesia (ANES201)
courses.description: This course discusses hypotension during anesthesia, focusing on its causes and management in small animal patients. We will discuss the underlying causes as well as the merits and limitations of various blood pressure monitoring methods. Finally, we will discuss a systematic approach to managing hypotensive episodes from a mechanistic viewpoint.

courses.title: The Basics of Trans-Neuronal Degeneration: Understanding When Enough Is Enough
courses.description: This course will provide attendees with: 1) A basic understanding of mechanotransduction and the cellular change that occur as a result of soft tissue and peripheral nerve stimulation. 2) How the understanding of mechanotransduction guides treatment protocols 3) Provide definitions for Central Integrative state, Transneuronal or neuronal degeneration (TND/ND), and Functional Neurology and understanding why these are important to implementing a multimodality approach to rehabilitation.

courses.title: Wound Management
courses.description:
The purpose of this course is to provide tools and knowledge on wound management to aid in the successful rehabilitation of wildlife.
Developed specifically for wildlife care professionals, Wound Management provides a systematic review of the physiology and treatment of the most common types of soft-tissue wounds seen in injured mammalian and avian species.

courses.title: VET Expo 2026, Sydney
courses.description: The VET Expo is Australia largest veterinary event with close over 1000 registered attendees, 120 speakers, and 100 exhibitors. Vet Expo compared to traditional style conferences, is faster paced with 20 or 60 minute presentations with innovative sessions including technical demos and a pitch fest and is free to attend. The event is specifically designed for the whole veterinarian profession including vet specialists, general practices, vet nurses, practice managers, clinic owners, technicians, researchers, government, and other animal health professionals. Speakers are from a wide range of backgrounds include vets, vet nurses, academics and researchers, animal behaviorist's, animal welfare professionals, and practice managers.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Use and Care of Surgical Equipment: Pulse Oximeter, Clippers, and Infusion Pump
courses.description: This level one course from ASNA explains basic operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of some common surgical equipment. The equipment discussed includes the pulse oximeter, clippers, and infusion pump. The course can be taken at your own pace, but most learners will complete it in 30-45 minutes.

courses.title: TIBIAL PLATEAU-LEVELING OSTEOTOMY PART 2: BIOMECHANICS, PATIENT SELECTION, AND PLANNING (195-36635)
courses.description: This online lecture includes a discussion on the biomechanics of the TPLO technique. Attendees will learn about preoperative radiographs, planning, and implant selection. Attendees will also gain an understanding of patient assessment and the selection of candidates for TPLO.

courses.title: Practitioner's Program
courses.description: Equine specific, clinically and practically based lectures for the equine veterinarian encompassing medicine, surgery, reproduction, neonatology, anesthesia, lameness and sports medicine, internal medicine, equine dentistry, parasitology, toxicology, practice management and other topics relevant to equine practice. Lectures are delivered by specialists, diplomates and experts in their field

courses.title: Utilizing the Nu.Qr Vet Cancer Test in Practice
courses.description: This course covers challenges and unmet needs in the diagnosis of canine cancer, shares clinical data from studies of the Nu.Qr Vet Cancer Test, how to process the sample and interpret results, how to integrate the use of the test in YOUR clinical practice and provides Case Study examples to illustrate how the test may / may not be used. The presenter is Dr Tom Butera, DVM.

courses.title: Practice CEnts Module 1: Building Wealth - Basic Accounting (PRAC113)
courses.description:
Most education geared toward a veterinary hospital is centered on medicine. Although that is very important, we must not forget a veterinary hospital is also a BUSINESS. The financial success of a veterinary hospital has more to do with being a success business man or woman than being a successful veterinarian. This course is designed to help either a veterinarian or practice manager learn how to manage the BUSINESS of the veterinary practice. By doing so, the practice should become more profitable and less stressful for the owner.
This is the first of several planned non-interactive courses in a Practice CEnts management series geared towards improving profits for a veterinary practice and thereby creating wealth for the owner.
In this course, the participant is provided a working knowledge of the accounting that will be used in the future Practice CEnts courses. In the intermediate and advanced courses participants will learn more tools and structures so they can make better management and financial decisions and thus more profitable decisions for the practice.

courses.title: LafeberVet Corcoran-Grosset April 2025 Non-Interactive Program
courses.description: The April 2025 Non-Interactive Program consists of two webinar recordings. Respiratory Disease in Chelonians by Mike Corcoran, DVM, DABVP (Reptile and Amphibian Practice), CertAqV and Clinical Approach to Fish Medicine by Claire Grosset, DMV, IPSAV, CES (Avian Pathol), DACZM.

courses.title: KYON An Introduction to Total Hip Replacement Online Course
courses.description: KYON An Introduction to THR Online Course is designed to provide surgeons with essential information for understanding of the KYON THR system, case selection, and postoperative care. Additionally, learners will gain an understanding of radiography requirements, and the primary steps of the surgical procedure. Upon completion, participants will have gained familiarity with the system, preoperative and postoperative radiograph requirements, and postoperative care.

courses.title: Kidney Function and the Gut Microbiome
courses.description: This interactive course will help you gain knowledge pertaining to the gut microbiome and how it can support cats and dogs with compromised kidney function. You will gain a deeper understanding of kidney function, the incidence and challenges of Chronic Kidney Disease, and how nutrition can be used by the veterinary healthcare team to work with the pet parents as they work to slow the disease progression. Additionally, you will gain knowledge of the gut microbiome, pre and probiotics, and how these elements can work together to supporting the health of cats and dogs with Chronic Kidney Disease.

courses.title: Ratite Medicine and Surgery - The Basics (EXOT328)
courses.description: This course will introduce participants to the wonderful world of ratite birds. The species within this broad group, their relevant anatomy and physiology, handling and restraint methods, sedation, anesthesia and a variety of disease infectious and non-infectious problems will be discussed; all of which are present in the current literature.

courses.title: Avian Anatomy Basics (EXOT326)
courses.description: This course is an introduction to pet bird anatomy.

courses.title: Behavior Belongs in Shelter Medicine: The Shelter Vet's Role in Behavioral and Emotional Health (On Demand)
courses.description:
This continuing education program reviews the role of the shelter veterinarian in assessing, supporting, and managing behavioral and emotional health in dogs and cats housed in shelter environments. The session will examine how behavioral presentation intersects with medical conditions, welfare considerations, and legal scope of practice, with emphasis on the veterinarian's responsibility to diagnose behavior-related conditions and develop appropriate treatment plans.
Participants will explore evidence-informed approaches to identifying behavior changes attributable to medical or environmental factors; applying behavioral and psychopharmacological interventions within a shelter's operational constraints; and collaborating effectively with shelter staff, volunteers, and community practitioners to support continuity of care. The program also addresses risk assessment, safety considerations, and the veterinarian's role in guiding outcome decisions and aftercare planning for animals with behavioral concerns.

courses.title: All About Fascia
courses.description: This course covers the role fascia plays in a healthy musculoskeletal system. The participant will learn :1) about fascial make up and characteristics. 2) why fascia is essential in supporting mechanical systems 3) about some common ways fascial disfunction presents clinically 4) how to diagnose and treat fascial disfunction.

courses.title: Cannabis in Veterinary Medicine: The Basics (PHAR114)
courses.description: With cannabis science and the legal environment rapidly changing throughout the country, if not the world, we are excited to offer this first of its kind introduction to veterinary cannabis course. This course will provide up-to-date information on medical and legal topics pertaining to cannabis in veterinary medicine. It will review the endocannabinoid system, the cannabis plant itself and all its components. Discuss the toxicologic aspects of cannabis, through a review of the pertinent seminal cannabis articles. Take a look at the clinical application of cannabis. And finally review the federal and state laws and regulations and how they pertain specifically to veterinary medicine.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2025 New Insights on Feline Infectious Disease On Demand
courses.description:
Morning sessions will provide state-of-the-art updates on the current outbreak of feline infectious peritonitis in Europe, and the potential risk of spread further afield. The role of diagnostics, and importance of diagnostics in this disease, and the current treatment options-how these are progressing and the outlook for a newly diagnosed case. The panel discussion will include experts from the United Kingdom and the United States, discussing the global impact of this disease, the variations in treatments offered and sharing their experiences in treating this disease.
During the afternoon, the focus will be on growing evidence for infectious causes of neoplasia in cats, with sessions focused on both viral and bacterial causes of neoplasia. These will be followed by a panel discussion with experts from around the world, discussing potential considerations in cases of neoplasia, when diagnostics and treatment for infectious diseases should be considered and the implications to the cat.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Common Infectious Diseases of Dogs & Cats
courses.description: This level one course discusses common canine and feline diseases, as well as internal and external parasites and prevention strategies found in high-quality, high-volume spay/neuter (HQHVSN) environments, shelters, and other veterinary facilities. It can be completed at your own pace, but most learners will complete the course in 1-1.5 hours.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Feline Fix by Five
courses.description: The American Veterinary Medical Association has endorsed spay/neuter for cats by the age of five months, recognizing that pregnancy can occur by that age and there are no adverse effects to early-age sterilization. Early spay/neuter will significantly reduce the number of unwanted pregnancies, in turn reducing relinquishment of kittens to animal shelters and the burden on shelter resources and staff and increasing the number of lives saved.

courses.title: Canine Inflammatory Bowel Disease: How to Approach Challenging Cases
courses.description: We've all had difficult cases of chronic gastrointestinal signs that have been difficult to diagnose, leaving the veterinary team unsure of next steps. Join Dr. Myles McKenna for this 1-hour, case-based webinar as he talks about the challenges of diagnosing canine inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and offers 10 steps to troubleshooting difficult cases.

courses.title: Science of Tissue Management: Sutures, Polymers & Needles
courses.description: This free webinar will discuss wound closure principles and the phases of wound healing by tissue type, as well as how to select the best polymer for the different tissue type.

courses.title: CVM Conference November 2026
courses.description: The CVM Conference will offer attendees the chance to earn 20 CE hours from over 130 sessions, over many topics such as radiology, toxicology, ophthalmology, field medicine, equine and bovine sessions, and other professional topics as well.

courses.title: Nonsurgical Management of Canine Degenerative Joint Disease
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Michael H. Jaffe will review the diagnosis and nonsurgical management of canine degenerative joint disease (DJD), including multimodal management. Emphasis will be placed on how different multimodal approaches work and which options to consider for an individual patient. Many commonly used prescription and nonprescription products and their roles in multimodal management will also be explored.

courses.title: The wonderful world of cannabinoids in small animal practice
courses.description: This session discusses what veterinarians should be looking for when recommending CBD- rich hemp-based products. The focus is on the information that the veterinarian should be looking for on a certificate of analysis (COA) of marketed products. Discussion around the cannabinoid analysis when companies do third party testing, as well as microbiologics, mycotoxins, solvent residues, heavy metals, pesticides and terpenes is covered. More importantly, understanding if companies have validated utility of the product through pharmacokinetic testing in the species intended, as well as safety data with a deeper examination of current safety data around long-term supplementation. As there is increasing evidence on the efficacy of CBD rich hemp products on a variety of conditions, these studies will be examined surrounding the growing evidence for chronic osteoarthritis pain. Further evidence-based medicine will be examined around the growing number of trials surrounding seizures with a focus not only on efficacy, but potential drug interactions. Similarly, neurological implications of CBD-rich hemp use in anxiety are slowly emerging suggesting that dosing is very important in mitigating situational behavioral issues and can be used effectively. Lastly, evidence around pruritic diseases and the immune system will be examined particularly around the atopic dermatitis, and cannabinoids as potential immune system regulators.

courses.title: Muscle Health: Strengthening Animal Healthspan
courses.description: Maintaining muscle health is one of the most critical, and often overlooked, factors in extending both the lifespan and quality of life for companion animals. Muscle loss impacts mobility, immune function, recovery from illness or injury, and overall vitality. For veterinarians and their teams, understanding the role of muscle in aging pets opens the door to earlier intervention, better outcomes, and improved client satisfaction. This course examines the science behind muscle health and options to help preserve and rebuild muscle. The role of Fortetropin, an all-natural advanced nutritional supplement, in addressing preservation of muscle health is shared. The course offers practical insights participants can apply to patient care and client education, ultimately supporting longer, healthier lives for pets.

courses.title: KYON An Introduction to ALPS TPLO Online Course
courses.description: ALPS TPLO Introduction Course is designed to review how to diagnose a cranial cruciate ligament rupture and consider TPLO and other treatments options. It also reviews how to plan and apply the TPLO procedure and the important steps of preoperative and postoperative care.

courses.title: FLUTD: Whats All the Stress? (TECH381)
courses.description: This presentation will focus on causes of FLUTD (feline lower urinary tract disease), evidence based management, the veterinary technicians role in producing a positive outcome, and communication with the cat owner. New nutrients and nutritional management options, specifically relating to FIC (feline idiopathic cystitis) and stress in cats, will be discussed.

courses.title: New Techniques in Tumor Removal Approaches to Cryotherapy Utilization
courses.description: This program will cover the basics of using cryotherapy to treat tumors in veterinary settings. We will review the history of cryotherapy in veterinary medicine and also discuss the cellular, humoral, and immune response to cryotherapy. An introduction to the Kubanda cryoprobe will also be given along with the procedure and selection criteria for using the device in a veterinary setting. We conclude with future possibilities for cryotherapy in the veterinary market and a quick quiz to test comprehension of material.

courses.title: Introduction to Radiology (DIAG415)
courses.description: This course will cover the discovery and history of the first radiographs, basic radiology concepts, radiology safety and physics as well as evaluation of different x-ray systems used in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: Introduction to Traumatic Brain Injury (DRIP151)
courses.description: This course will cover an introduction to traumatic brain injury focusing on practical information that can be utilized by all practitioners.

courses.title: UNIVERSAL HIP WORKSHOP (407-36907)
courses.description: Developed in cooperation with experienced industry-leading surgeons, this two-day workshop consists of a comprehensive online educational component, supplemental classroom instruction, and extensive hands-on laboratory experience. This multi-faceted approach to education is designed to offer participants the necessary resources and support to sufficiently familiarize themselves with the procedure, and reliably offer an advanced orthopedic service to their clientele. Participants will learn proper technique for use of the Universal Hip system, focusing on preoperative planning, surgical technique, and clinical follow-up, with opportunity to use the instruments to gain an understanding of the surgical objectives.

courses.title: Three Behavior Lessons You'll Use Every Day
courses.description:
In this video course, Veterinary Behaviorist, Dr. Amy Pike, will help us understand the cues our patients are giving us through their body language and behavior. Through videos and discussion, we'll learn to differentiate medical, environmental, and psychological causes of unwanted behaviors.
In session one, we'll learn how to read dog and cat body language, focusing on tails, ears, eyes, facial expressions, and body positioning. In session two, through video examples and understanding of basic training principles, we'll learn how to train dogs and cats to accept medical care, including bathing, eye drops, ear medications, and oral medications. In session three, we'll study the classical signs of separation anxiety, learn how to differentiate separation anxiety from similar disorders, and how to treat.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2026 Monitoring Drug Therapy On Demand
courses.description: Morning sessions will provide state of the art updates on immunosuppressive therapy, anticonvulsant therapy, drug therapy for patients with liver disease, and drug therapy for patients with renal disease, with an emphasis on both pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic monitoring, accompanied by a panel discussion to probe deeper into areas of interest. Afternoon sessions will cover topics such as monitoring trilostane therapy, monitoring mineralocorticoid therapy in patients with Addisons disease, antimicrobial therapy and avoiding antimicrobial resistance, and pharmacogenomics, again accompanied by a panel discussion. Presenters will have focused research expertise and clinical experience in monitoring drug therapy, and attendees will be exposed to deep and up to the minute information on the practical aspects of advanced therapeutic drug monitoring.

courses.title: Current Trends in Wildlife Forensic Science
courses.description: Wildlife trafficking continues to be a major threat to many species throughout the world. While once rare, the use of forensic science to combat such illegal activity in now commonplace. The field continues to develop rapidly with the emergence of new technologies and data analysis capabilities. Examples of these current trends will be discussed, along with thoughts about the future of wildlife forensic science. This course is free for IVFSA members.

courses.title: Introduction to Abdominal Ultrasound Online Course
courses.description: This online course¿aims to give you the confidence to perform an ultrasound examination of the abdominal cavity and optimise your images using the equipment you have available in practice. Through a combination of text, videos, animations and interactive content, we will cover a logical and methodical approach to ultrasonography which will enable you to identify and fully evaluate all the major abdominal organs. As artefacts are common in ultrasound, we will help you to recognise them and explore the root causes for each. Additionally, we will begin to explore the interpretation and reporting of changes seen on ultrasound examination. This online course is the equivalent of 6 hours of CPD and the theory material is available for 180 days from first access.

courses.title: Avian Enrichment : What, Why and How
courses.description:
Caring for birds means more than meeting their basic needs; it requires understanding their natural behaviors and providing enrichment that supports both physical and mental wellbeing.
Cassie Malina, CPBT-KA, CPBC, will help you explore ways to create engaging, species-appropriate environments for birds and share practical strategies to support their natural behaviors every day.

courses.title: Veterinary Abdominal Ultrasound Training Camp
courses.description: This hands-on, small-group veterinary abdominal ultrasound training program is designed for veterinarians and veterinary technicians of all skill levels, from beginners to advanced practitioners. Participants will gain practical experience performing diagnostic-quality abdominal ultrasounds using a structured, protocol-based approach. Over three immersive days, attendees will master core organ imaging, systematic scanning workflows, and advanced techniques for the liver, pancreas, adrenal glands, and gastrointestinal tract. The program includes interactive lectures, live-patient scanning labs, and 30 days of personalized feedback through mentored teleradiology, ensuring participants leave with confidence, improved efficiency, and skills that translate directly to clinical practice. This course emphasizes hands-on learning, real-world applications, and long-term clinical success.
courses.location: COVE - The Center of Veterinary Excellence

courses.title: Social Behavior and Implications for Bonded Pairs in Group Housed Shelter Cats
courses.description: Little is known about the social behavior of cats living in group housing at shelters. In a series of studies, we recorded all the social behavior occurring between cats living in group housing and compared cats who were introduced at the shelter versus those who were surrendered together. We then followed up by specifically examining social behavior between cats who were labeled as bonded pairs or adopted together. Cats who were labeled as bonded pairs had a longer time to adoption, but the relationship between this designation and social behavior was weak. Recommendations will be provided for identifying bonded pairs.

courses.provider: SUSTAINABILITY IN EQUINE PRACTICE SEMINAR AND RETREAT
courses.title: The Sustainability In Equine Practice Seminar 2026
courses.description:
The Sustainability in Equine Practice Seminar & Retreat 2026 is a 2.5-day continuing education program designed specifically for equine veterinarians seeking practical strategies to build sustainable, successful, and fulfilling careers in equine practice. Hosted jointly by Sustainability in Equine Practice Seminars (SEPS) and Decade One, this retreat-style meeting combines business education, leadership development, wellness, communication skills, legal and financial guidance, and community connection in an immersive learning environment.
This program addresses many of the non-clinical challenges that directly impact career longevity, professional satisfaction, and practice sustainability within equine veterinary medicine. Through lecture-based presentations, facilitated discussions, and interactive learning opportunities, participants will gain actionable tools to improve personal well-being, strengthen leadership and communication skills, enhance financial literacy, increase practice profitability, navigate legal and ethical issues, and foster healthier workplace and client relationships.

courses.title: Maddies Insights Helping the helpers Improving shelter staff well-being
courses.description: In 2023 Best Friends launched a survey of shelter staff wellbeing in the U.S. the largest survey of its kind to date. This presentation will focus on how struggling shelters and rescues can apply the lessons learned from work in the veterinary wellbeing field to improve the wellbeing of their staff and volunteers.

courses.title: BOAS in the ER (TECH415)
courses.description: Brachycephalic Obstructive Airway Syndrome (BOAS) is a condition that is caused by the conformation of the upper respiratory system in brachycephalic dogs and cats. BOAS can exacerbate other emergencies and make treating brachycephalic patients difficult. This presentation will review the pathophysiology of BOAS and discuss recognition, management, and treatment.

courses.title: Responsiveness Leverage Software. Improve Efficiency. Rekindle Joy
courses.description:
Do you remember why you joined the veterinary industry in the first place? I assume it was because you found joy in helping animals, not because you loved the endless paperwork and administrative tasks that go into running a successful practice. Wheres the balance?
In this presentation, we will explore how software technology can help veterinary professionals reduce daily stressors and reclaim their joy in the field. We will discuss the latest advances in software and how they can be used to streamline daily tasks, improve patient care, and enhance the overall veterinary experience. By the end of this presentation, youll better understand how the right veterinary software can relieve your administrative burden so you can stay true to your core values and have more time to focus on providing exceptional patient care.

courses.title: EVCC's February CE Event
courses.description: EVCC's February CE Event is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: American College of Veterinary Pharmacists 2026 Annual Veterinary Pharmacy Conference
courses.description: The 2026 Veterinary Pharmacy Conference provides an interdisciplinary, practice-focused program designed to equip pharmacists, veterinarians, pharmacy technicians, and veterinary technicians with advanced competencies in veterinary pharmacotherapy and compounding. Through sessions spanning species-specific formulation strategies, novel and emerging therapeutics, and nontraditional patient populations, including wildlife, aquatic species, and invertebrates, attendees will strengthen their ability to apply evidence-informed, patient-centered care across diverse clinical scenarios. Emphasis is placed on optimizing medication delivery, overcoming administration challenges, and enhancing safety and adherence through innovative approaches such as tailored compounding and fear-free techniques. Collectively, the conference fosters collaborative, One Health-aligned practice by integrating cutting-edge science with practical, real-world application across the veterinary care continuum .

courses.title: ETCO2 And You-A guide to Capnography and ETCO2
courses.description: This lecture will cover the monitoring parameter end tidal carbon dioxide. In this lecture we will discuss how the exchange in gas occurs in mammals, what it means for our patient under anesthesia, how we monitor it, and how to troubleshoot waveforms.

courses.title: Understanding the Powerful Impact of Ashwagandha on Pet and Horse Health
courses.description:
Lauded by human health professionals for its many clinically-proven adaptogenic healing properties, ashwagandha is now starting to appear in a variety of animal health supplements and functional treats. How does this natural ally for human health, which has been used successfully for more than 3000 years, benefit companion animals?
This course looks at the multiple issues ashwagandha can address, and the effects this ayurvedic herb has for animal patients in practice. It starts by unpacking what ashwagandha is, how this adaptogenic herb works to safely address and improve animal health challenges, and how carefully controlled production, harvesting and management, as well as complete compliance, transparency, and sustainability can affect quality and efficacy. The course then moves on to take a closer look at these peer-reviewed, published studies, which utilize KSM-66 Ashwagandha root extract, as a jumping off point:
1. Adaptogenic and immunomodulatory activity of Ashwagandha Root Extract: an experimental study in an equine model
2. Efficacy and safety of standardized Ashwagandha Root Extract (Withania somnifera) on stress and anxiety in domestic dogs
3. Adaptogenic Ashwagandha Root Extract modulates inflammatory markers in feline stress management
4. Effects of Ashwagandha Root Extract on aging-related changes in healthy geriatric dogs
Each study will be covered in depth, looking at an overview, parameters assessed, and conclusive results.
It ends with a look at ongoing research related to ashwagandha root extract for animal health, which other natural ingredients it works well with, and how it can be added to pet health regimens, routines, ingredient profiles, and treatment protocols.

courses.title: Corneal Ulcers
courses.description:
A CE talk covering diagnosis and management of simple, indolent and
complicated corneal ulcers in dogs and cats

courses.title: Antibody testing for Vaccine preventable disease
courses.description:
Antibody testing for patient response to core vaccines is a significantly underutilized resource in veterinary practice. The recent introduction of Point-of-Care Tests kits provides clinicians the opportunity to objectively assess the need for, and response to, core vaccines in both dogs (Distemper-Parvovirus-Adenovirus) and cats (Panleukopenia [with limited availability for herpesvirus and calicivirus]) and do so within minutes.
This presentation addresses the 3 most fundamental issues facing veterinarians regarding the decision to implement antibody testing in practice:
1) Are test results a valid indication of protective immunity?
2) What are the indications for testing individual patients? and
3) How do test results (+ vs -) impact patient management decisions?

courses.title: AAAP 2025 Annual Meeting
courses.description: The American Association of Avian Pathologists (AAAP) Annual Meeting is the premier U.S. scientific meeting focused on poultry health, welfare and food safety for poultry veterinarians and scientists. The meeting facilitates member collaboration to advance science-based knowledge, expertise, and education, and is attended by poultry veterinarians and scientists from the United States and internationally. The 2025 AAAP scientific program incorporates 109, 15-minute oral presentations in the following 22 sessions: Welfare, Wealth of Knowledge, Virology, Vaccinology, Salmonella, Reovirus, Parasitology, Other, Newcastle Disease Virus, Mycoplasma, Marek's Disease, Infectious Bursal Disease, Infectious Bronchitis Virus, Immunology, Epidemiology, Diagnostics, Coccidiosis, Case Report, Bacteriology, Avian Metapneumovirus, Avian Influenza, and Antimicrobial/Antibiotic Resistance. Additionally, the 2024 AAAP scientific program incorporates 136 poster presentations in the following 15 sessions: Wealth of Knowledge, Virology, Vaccinology, Reovirus, Newcastle Disease Virus, Mycoplasma, Infectious Bursal Disease, Infectious Bronchitis Virus, Enteric Health, Diagnostics, Coccidiosis, Case Report, Bacteriology, Avian Metapneumovirus, and Avian Influenza. Meeting attendees will engage with these posters daily over the course of the 3-day meeting. The focus of this year's keynote presentation by Dr. Mike Donohue is How Continuous Incremental Advances in Broiler Performance Have Affected Costs of Production and Broiler Availability Over the Last Forty-Five Years. Searchable keywords: AAAP, poultry, veterinarians, scientists, poultry health, poultry welfare, food safety.

courses.title: LafeberVet Ferret-Parrot Spring 2026 Non-Interactive Program
courses.description: The LafeberVet Ferret-Parrot Spring 2026 non-interactive program consists of one new webinar recording "Clinical Medicine of the Domestic Ferret" by Christal Pollock, DVM, DABVP (Avian Practice) plus recordings of two live webinars "The Geriatric Collapsing Ferret: More than Insulinoma" by Cathy Johnson-Delaney, DVM and "Reproductive Disease in Psittacine Birds" by Don Harris, DVM

courses.title: All The Wrong People Have Imposter Syndrome
courses.description: Imposter Syndrome is a psychological condition that affects a large portion of the veterinary field. I have it, you likely have it, and many of your co-workers have it. It is characterized by self-doubt and the worry of being exposed as a "fraud" despite proof of accomplishments and validation. This presentation will empower veterinary technicians by giving them the information and resources they need to identify, address, and work towards overcoming imposter syndrome. We can be more resilient and self-assured by establishing a supportive environment and encouraging self-awareness within ourselves and our colleagues. Imposter syndrome can hold you back from achieving your full potential in this field. Together, we can defeat impostor syndrome and realize that we are worthy of being here, we are not frauds, and we are highly valuable in this profession.

courses.title: Specialsts update online
courses.description: This will be recorded sessions from our already RACE approved specialists update series. They will be avaliable for on demand viewing. We will be providing medical CE from our specialsts in anesthesia and dentistry. The offerings are cutting edge but practical.

courses.title: Veterinary Medical Terminology-The Basics (STAF208)
courses.description: Veterinary staff must be able to interpret client and layman terms and translate to veterinary terms and vice versa. As such, a clear understanding of medical terminology is an important part of daily activities in any veterinary practice. Correct use of terminology in the veterinary workplace enhances client education and practice-wide communication. This course will introduce the concept of breaking down medical terms into their component root words, prefixes and suffixes for ease of understanding. Terminology by body system will be introduced, and the participant will be able to "decode" medical terms, as well as demonstrate the correct medical terms for many signs and symptoms. Medical terms for the body parts, as well as terms for diseases, pathologies, diagnostics and treatments for each body system will be covered. This is a terminology course and will not branch into the physiology of various diseases and conditions.

courses.title: Press Pause on the Parvo Panic: Preventing a Case from Becoming an Outbreak
courses.description: Have you ever had a parvovirus case turn into a parvovirus outbreak? Do you want to expand your ability to manage canine parvovirus cases without putting the rest of the population at risk? This webinar will explore current recommendations and new tools for managing canine parvovirus in shelter environments. Shelter medicine expert Dr. Brian DiGangi will share how to plan for safe and successful case management by refining preventive care and biosecurity practices. Techniques to prevent the disease from spreading through the population and move affected animals through the shelter systems quickly, including exciting new treatment options, will also be highlighted.

courses.title: Stress Management in Vet Med
courses.description:
Overview
This 2 hour course is designed to provide veterinarians, technicians, and practice managers with effective strategies to manage stress. By understanding the root causes of stress and adopting the practical techniques in this course, participants will learn how to reduce stress 'in the heat of the moment', and enhance their overall well-being.
Key Objectives
1. Identify Stress Sources: Participants will learn to recognize the primary sources of stress, including self-generated stressors and external factors.
2. Understand Thought Patterns: The course introduces the concept of thought patterns that exacerbate stress. Participants will learn to identify and manage these patterns.
3. Practice Mindfulness Techniques: Participants will be taught mindfulness techniques to shift brain activation from a stress-prone state to a calm and focused state.
4. Apply Cognitive Behavioral Techniques: The course includes exercises based on Cognitive Behavioral Psychology to help participants change negative thought patterns and improve emotional responses.
5. Enhance Resilience: By practicing daily mindfulness and understanding how to reframe negative thoughts, participants will develop greater resilience and faster recovery from stressful situations.
Course Structure
* Introduction to Stress: Define stress and its impact on physical and mental health.
* Understanding Thought Patterns: Explore how thought patterns contribute to stress and learn strategies to manage them.
* Mindfulness Techniques: Teach participants how to use mindfulness to shift brain activation and reduce stress.
* Cognitive Behavioral Techniques: Introduce the "think/feel/act" framework to change negative thought patterns.
* Practical Applications: Provide examples and exercises for applying these techniques in real-world scenarios.
* Conclusion and Next Steps: Summarize key takeaways and encourage ongoing practice for sustained stress management.
Learning Outcomes
Upon completing this course, participants

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Exploring Efficacy, Barriers, and Best Practices of Companion Animal Foster Caregiving (OnDemand))
courses.description: Foster care is a unique form of human-animal interaction that is increasingly understood to be an effective tool for improving the welfare of shelter-living animals. Even brief stays in foster care can allow animals to escape the stressors of the shelter, provide an environment that allows for greater social interaction, and offer opportunities for improved health and behavior. In this presentation, we will highlight the key takeaways revealed in the 42 published articles evaluating companion animal foster care programs that are included in our recent review paper: Companion animal foster caregiving: A scoping review exploring animal and caregiver welfare, barriers to caregiver recruitment and retention, and best practices for foster care programs in animal shelters.
