During our discussion, we will examine a variety of foster care programs that have been studied, explore the evidence of their effects on human and animal welfare, evaluate the successes and challenges in supporting shelter foster care programs, illuminate discrepancies in equity and diversity of caregiver engagement that offer opportunities for recruitment, and recommend best practices for lasting programmatic success.

courses.title: Webinar - Common Non-Orthopaedic Surgical Conditions of the Foal
courses.description: This webinar will cover common non-orthopaedic conditions of the foal which may require surgical intervention, such as umbilical infections, patent urachus, ruptured bladder and hernias. It will focus on case selection, timing of surgery and pre- and post-surgical considerations and prognosis as well as an introduction to the surgical techniques.

courses.title: LafeberVet Winter 2025 Non-Interactive Program
courses.description: The Winter 2025 Non-Interactive Program consists of two new webinar recordings Pet Poultry Basics by Marcie Logsdon, DVM and The Intersection of Medical and Behavioral Issues in Avian Health by Yvonne van Zeeland, DVM, MVR, PhD, DECZM as well as two preexisting programs. Program 840790 includes Rabbit and Large Herbivorous Rodent Dental Disease by Krista Keller, DVM, DACZM, Routine Veterinary Care of the Miniature Pig by Kristie Mozzachio, DVM, DACVP, CVA, and Basic Wildlife Rehabilitation Triage by Renee Schott, DVM, CWR. Program 934611 consists of one webinar recording A Clinicians Perspective on Avian Ganglioneuritis and Avian Bornavirus by Brenna Fitzgerald, DVM, DABVP.

courses.title: Tales from the Crit: Interactive Hematology Case Studies with the Laboratory Retrievers-Module 4
courses.description: The Laboratory Retrievers - Purdue continuing education (CE) program is an online learning experience for veterinary professionals, created by the Laboratory Retrievers LLC and Purdue University College of Veterinary Medicine. These highly interactive, case-based modules help veterinarians and technicians confidently interpret CBC data, analyze cytograms and recognize key blood film cell morphology in minutes.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: The Nose Knows, Or Does It?
courses.description: More dogs every day are being used by government agencies to find drugs, explosives, human remains and other animal species. At the same time, pet owners have discovered the sport of canine nose work and are enjoying the benefits of this engaging and stimulating activity. There is much we don't know about the canine olfaction system and what factors may influence a dog's ability to perform scent work appropriately. This lecture is going to examine the canine olfaction system and look at various drugs that may or may not affect scenting ability.

courses.title: Small Animal Programme 2025
courses.description: This programme includes 13 hours of world-class CPD, delivered by experts in the field. The main objective is to keep veterinarians up to date with the latest insights into small animals. The Programme will outline the typical approach to investigating and managing cases in order to optimise the outcome. Topics covered range from cardiology, oncology, behaviour, dermatology, among others.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Obesity Management (NUTR125)
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss health risks associated with obesity in dogs and cats; nutritional assessments for obese and overweight patients, including dietary history, body condition score, and muscle condition score; and a step-by-step approach to the overweight or obese patient. We will also discuss case examples.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Fur-Ever Starts Now: Supporting Dogs and Adopters Post Adoption (On Demand)
courses.description:
Globally, thousands of dogs are relinquished to rehoming organizations each year (Coe et al., 2014) to be adopted into new homes (Weiss et al., 2015). Similarly to the general dog-owning population, new adopters often experience health and behavior concerns in their dogs (Neidhart & Boyd, 2002). However, for adopted dogs, these concerns can lead to them being returned to the rehoming organization they were adopted from (Powell et al., 2022). To try and address this, in 2018, Dogs Trust, the largest dog welfare charity in the UK, launched its post-adoption support project. Individuals adopting a dog from any UK Dogs Trust Rehoming Centre are eligible to receive phone calls regarding their dog's health and behavior at specific timepoints after adoption (2 days, 2 weeks, 4 months).
In this presentation, we will explore the post-adoption support project. Starting with describing the methodology and cohort of adopters and dogs, we will go on to delve into the common health and behavior concerns reported by adopters in their newly adopted dogs before examining the uptake of behavior support and the reasons for declining the support. Finally, we will end by looking at return to kennel rates during the project and comment on the common reasons and time points at which dogs are returned.

courses.title: Orthobiologic Therapies for Canine Musculoskeletal Disease
courses.description: Orthobiologic therapies are being increasingly used in veterinary medicine, but they are not one-size-fits-all solutions. This webinar will clarify how platelet-rich plasma, conditioned serums/autologous protein solutions, and cell-based therapies differ in their biological mechanisms and clinical applications. Attendees will learn how accurate diagnosis and staging and understanding pathology of musculoskeletal disease can drive appropriate selection of orthobiologic therapies and why they are most effective when integrated into a comprehensive treatment plan rather than used in isolation.

courses.title: When Behavioral Problems are Actually Medical Problems
courses.description:
In this video course, Veterinary Behaviorist, Dr. Amy Pike, will help us understand the cues our patients are giving us through their body language and behavior. Through videos and discussion, we'll learn to differentiate medical, environmental, and psychological causes of unwanted behaviors.
In session one, we'll move body-system by body-system to understand how medical disorders can present as behavioral problems. Case examples will be utilized in each lesson, to demonstrate how behaviors resolve when the underlying medical issue is treated. By the end of the course, attendees will understand the importance of the mantra - behavior medicine is always medical first, behavior second.

courses.title: BioMedtrix Universal Hip: Cementless and Cemented THR Online Course
courses.description: The BioMedtrix Universal Hip online course is designed to provide surgeons with an in-depth understanding of the BioMedtrix Universal Hip System and the surgical procedure.

courses.title: The Rez Clinic Manifesto: Delivering High Volume Spay/Neuter Veterinary Care on Native American Reservations
courses.description: This course will teach students how to create and deliver high volume spay/neuter veterinary care on Native American reservations. In this course we examine key decision in service delivery, with an emphasis on ASPCA Spay/Neuter Alliance protocols and real world experience. We rely on our experience with our First Nations Veterinary mobile unit where we deliver six clinics a year on the multiple reservations. Specific topics will include: defining clinic values, mechanisms for controlling bite, flight and mortality risks, implementation of fear free techniques, pain and stress mitigation through selection of drug protocols, client communication, cultural sensitivity, clinic inventory, start up and consumable cost estimates, soliciting volunteers, marketing clinics, and aftercare considerations.

courses.title: 2024 Therapeutic Update & Year-in-Review with Dr. Jim Budde
courses.description: 2024 saw the debut of several novel drugs and therapeutic options in veterinary medicine, revolutionizing our approach to how we treat and manage some of the most common clinical conditions seen in practice. Join veterinary pharmacist Dr. Jim A. Budde in this webinar powered by Plumb's as he recaps these new drugs and therapeutics introduced to the veterinary profession in 2024- from pregabalin and pimobendan to methimazole and beyond. Dr. Budde will be joined by clinical experts Dr. Matthew Kornya and Dr. Daniel J. Fletcher as they discuss the impact of these drugs and share updates from various key guidelines, including veterinary CPR guidelines, new American Heartworm Association guidelines, and more.

courses.title: LIVE Surgery Event: NIR Fluorescence Technology - Giving you the green light!
courses.description: The overall objective of the Webinar is to identify when NIRF Technology can help in tumour resection, skin reconstruction and as a guide for sentinel lymph node resection. Specifically, a surgical procedure will be performed for the removal of a skin tumour with a reconstructive technique, guided by indocyanine green (ICG) in the isolation of the reconstructive flap. During the same procedure, the neoplastic sentinel lymph node will be located using an ICG tracer and will be removed with a laparoscopic technique if identified intra-abdominally, or, conversely, thoracoscopically if intrathoracic.

courses.title: Low Stress Handling and Restraint of Difficult Dogs and Cats (BHVR902)
courses.description: Do you routinely find yourself scruffing, stretching, or struggling with cats? Do you have difficulty with hyperactive, fearful, or aggressive dogs? This course teaches Low Stress Handling techniques that work even with the most fearful animals. You will learn how to create a calm, inviting environment, how to use towel wrap techniques, and several methods for handling pets of different sizes and dispositions. These are principles and techniques you can adjust to each animal's needs. Put it all together, and you will create a more low stress, pet friendly facility where animals, clients, and staff all benefit.

courses.title: Pain Pathways and Analgesia (TECH435)
courses.description: Discover the art and science of pain management in both companion and large animals in this comprehensive course. This journey will take you from the basics of pain terminology to advanced, real-world understanding of how pain works in the body and how to treat it effectively. Instead of simply memorizing drug lists, you'll learn why each medication works by exploring pain pathways and receptor-level pharmacology in an engaging, easy-to-understand way. You'll gain practical insight into how different analgesic drugs work together to provide safer, more effective pain control and better patient outcomes.

courses.title: Diagnosis of Hypoadrenocorticism
courses.description: The presenter reviews the diagnosis of hypoadrenocorticism. Focus areas include disease pathogenesis, types of hypoadrenocorticism, clinical signs and physical exam findings, and the various diagnostic options. The tests discussed include the minimum database, ECG, imaging, and specific endocrine testing. Caveats for performing an ACTH stimulation test and interpretation are also discussed.

courses.title: TIBIAL PLATEAU-LEVELING OSTEOTOMY PART 3: INSTRUMENTATION AND SURGICAL TECHNIQUE (195-36636)
courses.description: This course is designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn/refine the tibial plateau-leveling osteotomy technique and to understand the major advantages of PAX Polyaxial Locking TPLO Plate System. The TPLO technique will be taught in a step-by-step fashion. This online lecture will discuss surgical instrumentation, surgical approach, jig placement, performing the tibial osteotomy, and plate and screw osteosynthesis. After attending this lecture, attendees will be prepared to practice the technique on cadavers during the recommended hands-on workshop.

courses.title: Separation Anxiety: Putting a Stop to the Intimidation
courses.description: This webinar will review the importance of therapy for a dog that is suffering from anxiety when left alone. This webinar will walk the average person, or even the most experienced veterinarian or medical staff member, through the foundational skills to focus on for dogs experiencing distress when they are left alone. This can often be an "intimidating" area when talking with an owner whose dog is struggling through departures. After this webinar, you should feel confident about discussing the specific therapy activities for a dog struggling with separation anxiety.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2024 A Comprehensive Approach to Enteral Feeding: Why, When and How On Demand
courses.description:
In this on-demand course, we will provide an encompassing view of enteral feeding. This will include reasons to implement it, how to best select the patients to benefit from it, and how to develop and implement a feeding plan.
This offering will include tips on communication with clients as well as guidance for making and troubleshooting diet slurry formulas, to provide a well-rounded approach to enteral feeding. Panel discussions focused on the practical implementation of enteral feeding will be led by experts in the field.
This course will provide valuable information for all SAIM clinicians and residents in a variety of practice settings, including nutritionists looking to supplement their base knowledge on this topic.

courses.title: Advanced Small Animal Medicine: Case-Based Insights and Innovations
courses.description: This course is designed for the experienced small animal practitioner who wishes to develop their approach to the diagnosis and management of some of the more complex small animal medical cases. Using real-life clinical case examples, a wide range of disorders will be covered, including those of the gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, endocrine, urogenital, haematological and immune systems. Background theoretical knowledge and helpful practical tips on performing diagnostic techniques will also be interspersed amongst cases. The current recommended management of these conditions will be discussed, drawing from experience on the speaker and the veterinary literature.

courses.title: ECG Interpretation for Veterinary Technicians & Veterinarians
courses.description: A course designed for veterinarians, technicians or other support staff to aid in interpreting ECGs during triage, ICU hospitalization, and under general anesthesia. The aim of this lecture is to establish a systematic approach to ECG interpretation and the criteria for identifying common arrhythmias.

courses.title: Access to Veterinary Care: A National Family Crisis
courses.description:
Lack of access to veterinary care is a complex societal problem with multiple causes but it is primarily associated with low socioeconomic status. Simply stated, millions of pets do not receive adequate veterinary care because the costs are beyond the family's ability to pay -- making lack of access to veterinary care the most significant animal welfare crisis affecting owned pets in the United States.
This webinar shares the results of a national study of barriers to veterinary care that pet owners face, and what veterinarians know about the problem and their attitudes and practices regarding it. In addition, AlignCare, a research and development project of One Health Veterinary care, funded by Maddie's Fund, will be presented. AlignCare improves access to veterinary care by aligning family support social services and public health entities with veterinary service providers, using charitable donations from foundations, businesses, and private citizens.

courses.title: Focus on GI (a 2 lecture series) (Non Interactive)
courses.description:
Lecture 1: Acute Diarrhoea in Dogs: When to choose probiotics, prebiotics or antibiotics
LECTURE ABSTRACT:
Acute diarrhoea in dogs is a common clinical presentation that can arise from a variety of causes, ranging from dietary indiscretion to infectious diseases. This lecture will explore the decision-making process behind the use of probiotics, prebiotics, and antibiotics in managing acute diarrhoea in canine patients. Attendees will learn to differentiate between cases that benefit from supportive care versus those requiring targeted antimicrobial therapy. Through case studies and evidence-based guidelines, veterinarians will gain confidence in choosing the most appropriate treatment to ensure optimal patient outcomes.
Lecture 2: Chronic Diarrhoea in Dogs: A Practical Approach
Lecture Abstract:
Chronic diarrhoea in dogs presents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge, often requiring a systematic and practical approach to identify underlying causes and implement effective treatments. This lecture will guide veterinarians through the step-by-step process of evaluating and managing chronic diarrhoea in canine patients. Emphasis will be placed on the importance of thorough history-taking, diagnostic testing, dietary management, and the appropriate use of medications. Through case discussions and clinical insights, participants will be equipped to develop comprehensive treatment plans tailored to each patient's unique needs.

courses.title: American College of Veterinary Ophthalmologists Conference - On-Demand
courses.description: The ACVO hosts an annual scientific international conference for its Diplomates and general practitioners for the purpose of providing continuing educational course credit. This year's conference will be the 54th annual scientific meeting. All C.E. content will be in on-demand format November 15, 2025 - November 15, 2026. The on-demand platform will provide question and answer requirements at 70% or higher pass rate to earn credit. All the speakers are minimally licensed DVMs who present recent research findings and masters level education for the attendees. All of these speakers submitted their research for presentation that was reviewed and approved by Diplomate members of the ACVO planning committee, who are also on the ACVO Board of Regents. Conference attendees will gain expanded knowledge of ophthalmological disease and treatment techniques.

courses.title: Practical Applications of Recent Veterinary Forensic Advances for Documenting Suspected Cases of Organized Dogfighting
courses.description: Documenting animals suspected of being involved in organized dogfighting can be a daunting and overwhelming request. This 1-hour lecture will provide participants with an overview of organized dogfighting, discuss best practices for documenting animals as evidence in this particular case type, and highlight recent literature providing evidence-based patterns of injury to assist veterinarians in rendering an expert opinion as to the cause(s) of injuries that may be observed in these cases. This webinar is free for IVFSA members.

courses.title: KYON: An Introduction to Tibial Tuberosity Advancement TTA Online Course
courses.description: Tibial Tuberosity Advancement (TTA) is used to treat dogs with a ruptured Cranial Cruciate Ligament (CrCL). KYON: An Introduction to Tibial Tuberosity Advancement TTA Online Course is designed to give background on CrCL disease, understand the range of treatment options, acquire foundational knowledge in when, why, and how to offer TTA, and provide surgeons knowledge in preparation of attending a hands-on workshop.

courses.title: Dispensing Legend Drugs in Florida (PHAR108)
courses.description: This course addresses handling and concerns within the Florida veterinary setting when dispensing drugs products. Topics include license and registration requirements, proper handling of controlled and non-controlled substances, and violations and penalties associated with deviations.

courses.title: Advanced Hematology: Dissecting the Data & Blood Film Review
courses.description: Accurate interpretation of diagnostic blood work is vital in diagnosing and managing sick patients. In this case-based webinar, Dr. Holly Brown will highlight practical strategies for identifying key changes in the CBC. Dr. Brown will review how to evaluate anemia, how obtaining accurate WBC differentials can aid in recognizing and monitoring inflammation, and best practices in evaluating thrombocytopenia. By pairing cytograms with blood film findings and ancillary diagnostics, Dr. Brown will demonstrate how to turn automated data into actionable insights that can help guide patient diagnosis and management.

courses.title: Gastric Dilatation-Volvulus (TECH453)
courses.description: Anesthesia on healthy patients is not without complications, and is too often taken for granted and performed without adequate planning or preparation. However, with any emergency presented to triage, a thorough pre-operative assessment must be performed, and patient assessment begins with the first step inside the door. The stressed and ill emergency patient will have altered physiological responses that will in turn alter the pharmacokinetics of the agents commonly used to provide anesthesia. This course is designed to assist you in your management of Gastric Dilation-Volvulus (GDV).

courses.title: Advanced Equine Veterinary Manual Therapy Online Course
courses.description: This course will be offered for those veterinarians who have been practicing some form of Veterinary Spinal Manipulation for at least 3 years. This course is intended both as a stand-alone course for those unable to travel, but also as a pre-requisite to an completely hands-on in-person class demonstrating techniques and coaching better results for veterinary manipulation and improving equine health through body work. Veterinarians will learn about Veterinary Manual Therapy, including an online lecture of fascia and descriptions of myofascial release. Integrating Veterinary Tui-na into adjusting will be mentioned, as well as the integration of Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine into equine health through body work. This online lecture series involves 5 hours of lecture on the topics of 1) basic chiropractic neurology; 2) the science of fascia and description of fascial release techniques; 3) patterns of chiropractic findings and how ther relate to lameness; 4) limb conformation as it relates to hoof balance; and 5) how advanced farrier techniques can affect the upper equine body and adjusting. There will also be 3 hours of video showing 1) equine veterinary manual therapy, integrating chiropractic techniques with veterinary Tui-na and myofacial release; 2) how to assess stressors on the equine hoof; and 3) how to work with farriers to adjust hoof balance and create better upper body biomechanics and improve athletic performance with integration.

courses.title: Getting the Most Out of Thoracic Radiography & Ultrasonography in the Diagnosis & Management of Heart Failure
courses.description: Imaging of the heart, lungs, and pleural space can help increase clinician confidence in the diagnosis of heart disease and heart failure. Traditionally, thoracic radiography has been the most common imaging modality used in the diagnosis of heart disease and heart failure; however, as quality ultrasound machines have become more affordable, point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) has become more commonly available in general practices and emergency settings, with thoracic POCUS also having gained acceptance in the diagnosis and monitoring of congestive heart failure. In this lecture, Dr. Teresa DeFrancesco will expand on the advantages and disadvantages of each of these imaging modalities in the diagnosis and management of heart failure and share tips on how to optimally use these important diagnostic tools in practice.

courses.provider: JOHNS HOPKINS P.O.E. TOTAL WORKER HEALTH CENTER IN MENTAL HEALTH
courses.title: Total Worker Health for Veterinary and Animal Care Workers
courses.description: This continuing education session provides an overview of Total Worker Health (TWH) principles and their application within veterinary medicine and the animal care workforce. Participants will explore the integration of occupational safety and health promotion strategies to improve worker well-being. The course will introduce the P.O.E. framework, highlight key tools used to assess workforce well-being, and discuss practical strategies to support the mental health, safety, and overall resilience of veterinary professionals.

courses.title: Veterinary Forensics: Non-Accidental Injury Self Study (MULT230)
courses.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI) tracks four different types of animal abuse, one of which is Intentional Abuse and Torture, what is commonly referred to as physical abuse or non-accidental injury (NAI). In this course, we will do a deep dive into the various signs of the different types of NAI: blunt force trauma, sharp force trauma, gunshot/projectile wounds, asphyxiation and drowning, burns, intentional and malicious poisoning, and Munchausen syndrome by proxy. Discussions will include signs of NAI, mimics of NAI, documentation, and a little bit on evidence collection. Examples from actual cases will be included.

courses.title: Preventive Care: Digging into the Data
courses.description: This webinar will investigate current trends in preventive care diagnostics in North America. Drs. Elizabeth Schooley and James Marshall take a deep dive into the most common abnormalities found on wellness panels and discuss how a comprehensive understanding of each patient can help veterinarians support the long-term health of their patients.

courses.title: Expert Level Cannabinoid Science, Part 3
courses.description: The Expert Level Cannabinoid Science, Part 3 presentation will explore additional applications of the cannabinoids and discuss some potential future developments. Again, reviewing the evidence base, we will largely focus on the role of cannabinoids in the skin and dermatological disease states. We will explore various data sets evaluating systemic versus topical use of these molecules. Again, reviewing available data, we will demonstrate that use of cannabinoids is considered safe, with a particular emphasis on the superiority of the acidic molecules. The potential for cannabinoids as adjuncts in the control of antimicrobial resistance is appraised and presented, including use in oral hygiene.

courses.title: VOM Hands On Short Course
courses.description: Veterinary Orthopedic Manipulation (VOM) is an instrument-based animal adjusting course that is precise and effective at rebalancing neurovascular imbalances to enhance healing and performance.

courses.title: American College of Veterinary Ophthalmologists Conference - On-Demand
courses.description: The ACVO hosts an annual scientific international conference for its Diplomates and general practitioners for the purpose of providing continuing educational course credit. This year's conference will be the 54th annual scientific meeting. All C.E. content will be in on-demand format November 15, 2024 - February 15, 2025. The on-demand platform will provide question and answer requirements at 70% or higher pass rate to earn credit. All the speakers are minimally licensed DVMs/MDs who present recent research findings and masters level education for the attendees. All of these speakers submitted their research for presentation that was reviewed and approved by Diplomate members of the ACVO planning committee, who are also on the ACVO Board of Regents. Conference attendees will gain expanded knowledge of ophthalmological disease and treatment techniques.

courses.title: Wound Closure Academy: Veterinary Suturing Techniques & Surgical Knots
courses.description: This webinar will educate on wound closure suturing and advanced knot-tying techniques used in veterinary surgical cases.

courses.title: Financial Clarity = Hospital Stability
courses.description: There are very few who enjoy managing practice finances, but it remains an essential part of creating and maintaining a stable practice. In this webinar, Dr. Duffy Jones will review why proper management of practice finances is essential. Plus, he'll provide insights to help attendees better understand some of the key metrics of practice finances, and he'll share a straightforward tool to make interpreting clinic finances as easy as reading patient blood work.

courses.title: Tips, Tricks, & Hacks: The Essential Guide to Feline Aggression
courses.description: Feline aggression is a complex and often misunderstood behavior, but it doesn't have to be. In this webinar, Dr. Lisa Radosta will provide you with the essential guide to understanding and managing feline aggression. Dr. Radosta will review the importance of recognizing early warning signs, how to identify the underlying motivations for aggression, and how to develop a multimodal management approach. Attendees will also explore common aggression types, diagnostic and management strategies, and communication techniques to best equip their teams to effectively support feline patients and their owners.

courses.title: Bearded Dragon Basic Medicine (EXOT511)
courses.description:
As bearded dragons become one of the most popular pets in the trade, we must ensure that we are educating clients on how to appropriately take care of their cute spiked reptilian pets.
In this course, we will dive into the basic husbandry, welfare, and nutritional needs of bearded dragons. The clinician will be able to understand the performance of basic clinical techniques to obtain diagnostic information for the bearded dragon patient including veterinary common medical conditions, diagnosis, and treatment.
To earn a certificate of completion, the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 95 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025, to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Farm Animal Parasitology (TECH440)
courses.description: Parasites have pestered our farm animals and us since before the dawn of the agricultural revolution. The primary purpose of this course is to develop an understanding of farm animal parasite life cycles, public health issues, proper sample processing, evaluation, and identification of internal and external parasites of horses, ruminants, pigs, and poultry. Techniques to improve ova recovery, life cycles, microscopic and gross identification techniques will be covered. (Diagnosis or treatment options will not be covered in this course.)

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Toxins on the Horizon: What Every Veterinarian Needs To Know
courses.description: This course covers information on four newer toxins in veterinary medicine: oclacitinib, acrylamide, GLP-1s and 7-Hydroxymitragynine. We will discuss background information, clinical signs, diagnostics and treatments for each of the toxins

courses.title: Parasitology for Wildlife Rehabilitators
courses.description: This course is designed to give wildlife care professionals a basic understanding of veterinary parasitology within a One Health framework. The course provides foundational knowledge on vocabulary, diagnostics, and the natural history of parasite species in mammals, avians, and herptiles. Topics include diagnostic techniques, biosecurity, endoparasites, ectoparasites, One Health, and treatment. Lab Included.

courses.provider: ZERO PAIN PHILOSOPHY - ACE VETS LIMITED
courses.title: A US perspective on opioids for pain management
courses.description:
The use of opioids has a firm place in analgesic provision. Across the globe access to opioids varies, according to local availability from a manufacturing perspective but also regulatory frameworks also play a role.
The US perspective is rooted in years of experience both in the clinical and research setting. Dr Khursheed Mama is an anaesthesiologist with a wide reaching reputation. We are honoured to have Dr Mama present this webinar and bring you a different view on a common topic

courses.title: Myth 3 and 4: Wrapping, Packaging and Labeling.
courses.description:
A significant responsibility of veterinarians is to minimize patient risk. In the operating room this is particularly important regarding surgical wound infection. In Myth 3 and 4: Reusable vs Disposable Sterile Wrapping and The Art of Sterile Packaging you will learn the guidelines for evaluation and use of packaging systems. You will also learn about the loading of the steam sterilizer, and how to select the appropriate labelling method to ensure accuracy without jeopardizing the sterilization process.
Expected time to complete this course is 2 hours.

courses.provider: VETERINARY EMERGENCY AND CRITICAL CARE SOCIETY
courses.title: Online Tech MDR from IVECCS 2023
courses.description: The Technician MDR series is designed for veterinary technicians advancing their expertise in emergency and critical care. Ideal for those pursuing or maintaining specialty certification, these sessions cover essential topics such as fluid therapy, CPR, cardiology, pharmacology, oncology, toxicology, sepsis, and hepatology. Highlights include precise fluid therapy techniques, RECOVER CPR updates, endocardiosis and heart failure management, anesthetic pharmacology, hypercalcemia of malignancy, toxin management, sepsis treatment, and liver disease insights. Attendees will gain practical, specialty-level knowledge to enhance their critical care skills.

courses.title: Rhinebeck Equine Clinical Perspectives in Equine Practice
courses.description:
This continuing education program provides clinically relevant updates for equine practitioners. The program features nine 50-minute lectures delivered by specialists and experienced equine veterinarians who previously completed internships at Rhinebeck Equine. The event is part of the Rhinebeck Equine Internship Program 20th Anniversary celebration and alumni reunion. Presenters represent alumni of the Rhinebeck Equine internship program who have returned to share clinical updates and perspectives with regional practitioners.
This continuing education program is hosted by Rhinebeck Equine and provided by Cavalcade Management Group, an AAVSB RACE-approved continuing education provider.
The target audience is licensed veterinarians involved in equine clinical practice, including general practitioners and equine specialists. The program may also be of interest to veterinary interns, residents, and technicians.

courses.title: Don't Give Up on Allergy Patients
courses.description: Owners of pets with atopic dermatitis can frequently feel emotionally, physically, and financially drained due to their pet's condition, leading to a lack of compliance and straining the veterinarian-client-patient relationship. Frequently, clients are quick to want to discontinue therapy, whether oral or topical, resulting in flare-ups and more subsequent frustration. Knowing the pathogenesis of this condition can help the practitioner better prepare the client for the anticipated treatment path. This 1-hour webinar will review the pathogenesis and treatment of atopic dermatitis, with a special focus on communicating with clients to help veterinarians feel more confident in their recommendations and treatment plan.

courses.title: Managing Shelter Overcrowding: Strategies for Timely, Appropriate Outcomes and Harm Reduction (On-Demand)
courses.description:
Veterinarians and veterinary technicians play critical roles in navigating the current crisis of shelter overcrowding. In many communities, the number of animals entering shelters far exceeds the capacity of staff, housing, and resources. This situation compromises animal welfare, increases staff stress, and delays decision-making. Operating within Capacity for Care (C4C) is the long-term solution, ensuring every animal receives an appropriate outcome in a timely manner. However, most shelters must also address how to mitigate harm while operating beyond their ideal capacity today.
This session provides practical strategies for veterinary professionals to influence both animal care and operational flow during crowding. Participants will examine how intake and outcome balance affects welfare, the role of daily monitoring and pathway planning, and the importance of timely euthanasia decisions when no safe live outcomes exist. The session emphasizes quick, realistic actions that reduce harm to animals, protect staff and volunteer well-being, and support sustainable practices even under pressure.
By linking operational principles with welfare-focused decision-making, this session equips DVMs and RVTs to support shelters in both immediate harm reduction and long-term capacity goals.

courses.title: Vaccine Technologies: Deciding What's Best for Your Patients
courses.description: Today, unlike any time in the past, the selection and use of vaccines in clinical practice have become significantly more challenging with the availability of multiple vaccine technologies designed to target the same pathogen. In this webinar, Dr. Richard Ford, coauthor of the AAHA Canine Vaccination Guidelines, will discuss the spectrum of vaccines currently licensed for administration to companion animals and the complex factors that guide clinical decision-making with regard to vaccination of individual animals. Dr. Ford will review available vaccine technologies, their dosing strategies and rationale, and their advantages and potential adverse effects.

courses.provider: THE AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF FISH VETERINARIANS
courses.title: 2025 AAFV Conference- On Demand
courses.description: The 2025 Annual American Association of Fish Veterinarians Conference will be held at the Long Island Aquarium, Riverhead, NY from Oct 12-15. This is the recorded, on demand version.

courses.title: Imaging of Young Dog Skeletal Diseases
courses.description: This presentation by a board-certified veterinary radiologist is intended for veterinarians and veterinary technicians in general practice. The most common congenital and acquired osseous abnormalities of skeletally immature canine patients, including pertinent history, signalment, and diagnostic imaging findings, will be reviewed.

courses.title: Chronic Hepatitis in the Dog: More Common Than You May Think
courses.description: Copper-associated chronic hepatitis and idiopathic (immune) hepatitis are 2 of the most common types of hepatitis and require specific management. In this webinar, Dr. David C. Twedt will review how to identify and manage these conditions, as well as how to determine their etiology. Attendees will learn how copper chelation, low-copper diets, and antioxidant multimodal management factor into the treatment of copper-associated hepatitis and how diet, anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive therapy, and antifibrotic and liver nutraceuticals can be used to manage cases of idiopathic chronic hepatitis.

courses.title: A Fear Free Approach for Humans from Intake to Discharge
courses.description: By the end of the webinar, participants will be able to identify common stressors faced by veterinary team members and clients throughout the patient visit process and apply practical strategies to foster calm, communication, and collaboration from intake to discharge.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Coagulopathy in the ICU - Parts 1 & 2
courses.description:
Coagulopathy in the ICU - Why Care about Clots & How to Stop Them?
This practical and case-based exploration of coagulopathy will open with a review of human and veterinary data on thrombi, highlighting their common - but often overlooked - occurrence and profound impact on case outcomes. From there, we will explore the cell-based model of clot formation, its distinct activation, maturation, and fibrinolysis phases, and how the cascade is shifted towards hypercoagulability by trauma, sepsis, tumors, cardiac and autoimmune diseases. Virchow's triad and clinicopathologic tests (CBC, PT aPTT & thrombo elastogram (TEG) will be applied to clinical cases to identify patients at risk for thrombus formation. Now equipped to detect hypercoagulability, we will explore established and emerging thromboprophylaxis and therapeutic strategies, including antiplatelet and anticoagulant medications, to develop a rational approach to case management. The following conditions will be discussed: Cat with aortic-thromboembolism, dog with pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) and acute kidney disease/acute neurological disease. Special guests will share novel insights on current literature and emerging therapies.
Why Care about Clots? Epidemiology of Coagulopathy & How Clots form
Treating the HYPER-Coagulable State - How can we break down Thrombi?
Coagulopathy in the ICU - HYPO-Coagulability Matters!
Though hyper-coagulability can be devastating, equally challenging are patients who can't form clots. The cell-based model of clot formation and diagnostic tools will be used to separate acquired bleeding disorders into those of platelets, clotting factor deficiencies, and hyperfibrinolysis. Particular attention will be given to trauma, the lethal triad, and how initial stabilization can contribute to the development of trauma coagulopathy. From there, we will move into practical treatment decisions: When should you give plasma vs. cryoprecipitate? What are the transfusion triggers and how much blo

courses.title: FarmResponse
courses.description: FarmResponse is a 3.5-hour continuing education module developed by national experts from the AgriStress Response Network. This course addresses farm and ranching cultural competencies, financial stress, land ownership and legacy issues, and the work of agriculture. This knowledge is critical to effectively care for a farmer's total health (health of the body and mind). FarmResponse improves cultural competencies and understanding of the stressors affecting agricultural producers, workers, and their families.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Ideal age of spay and neuter in dogs and cats
courses.description: The debate over when to recommend sterilization in pet dogs and cats has been under increased scrutiny over the past 5-10 years. With some veterinary professionals promoting pediatric spay/neuter, and others recommending waiting or foregoing sterilization altogether for some breeds, how should we be basing our decisions/recommendations?

courses.title: IACUC 101 PLUS
courses.description: IACUC 101 PLUS program is two six-hour days of didactic and interactive educational opportunities for both new and seasoned IACUC members, IACUC affiliates and others who contribute to their institution's animal care and use program. The "Plus" portion of this 2-day program includes additional Occupational Health and Safety, Wildlife and Post Approval Monitoring modules, as well as updates from USDA and OLAW. Didactic sessions address institutional responsibilities, IACUC charges, relevant informational resources, animal welfare laws, regulations and policies, and best practices. Students also are challenged to consider, deliberate, and develop action plans for a variety of potential IACUC scenarios. The course includes Q&A sessions with representatives from USDA and OLAW. This highly interactive, advanced program provides multiple opportunities to engage in real life applications of the basic concepts with the goals of learning new approaches and gaining new perspectives for managing issues that many animal care and use programs face.

courses.title: Chronic Nasal Discharge Anytime
courses.description: This course focuses on chronic nasal discharge found in modern veterinary practice and the logical way to handle it.

courses.title: How To Start A Veterinary Practice (PRAC117) Self-Study
courses.description: This course is specifically designed for Veterinarians who are thinking of starting a new practice. (Optionally: a Practice Manager or Office Manager can also gain insight on running a profitable practice from taking this course.) The authors take you from the ''I think I want to start my own practice'', to opening your doors. We have 6 industry experts who will guide you along the way from conceptual idea, to finding the ''right'' location; developing a Business Plan; obtaining financing; legal decisions; building / remodeling your facility; buying equipment; hiring staff; to opening day; and finally operating and maintaining a profitable practice. Yes, it is a lot! But you need this information before taking on the largest amount of debt you will have in your career. You need to know ahead of time if you have a good chance of success not just hope it all works out in the end.

courses.title: Feeding the Healthy Senior Dog: Nutrition Strategies for Proactive Aging Care
courses.description: The dietary needs of our veterinary patients evolve with aging. The veterinary team can proactively address some of these changes throughout the pet's lifespan. This lecture will discuss a complete nutritional assessment and individualized dietary recommendations for aging pets.

courses.title: Panel Discussion: Mandibular & Maxillary Fracture Repair
courses.description:
Utilizing cases from their practices, the international panel of world-renowned equine surgical specialists will discuss various aspects of management of common fractures of the mandible and the maxilla, including but not limited to:
Diagnostic imaging for mandibular and maxillar fractures
- When is CT required?
Tips & tricks to avoid intraoperative complications
New minimal invasive techniques for mandibular fracture repair using wires or cables, LCP-Technique and External fixators
Decision making for implant selection.
Recognizing & dealing with intra- and postoperative complications

courses.title: Veterinary Feed Directive and Other US Regulations (PHAR304)
courses.description: This course will cover the regulatory landscape of using antibiotics in food animals. It is designed to be a companion course to the food animal antimicrobial resistance webinar. The course will cover applicable United States regulations as well as the history of how we got to where we are today. There will be a detailed discussion of the Veterinary Feed Directive (VFD) regulations and a walk-through of how to write a VFD.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: Respiratory Emergencies for Internists On Demand
courses.description: Advanced continuing education course designed for boarded small animal internists, with a focus on the initial assessment and treatment of dogs and cats with urgent respiratory disease. The focus will be on a practical approach to common emergency respiratory presentations. The course will consist of a mix of didactic lectures, case-based presentations, and expert group discussions.

courses.title: Gut Check: What's Going on in the World of Intestinal Parasites?
courses.description: Intestinal parasites, particularly roundworms and hookworms with their seasonal trends and increasing prevalence, pose a growing challenge to veterinary professionals. In addition, environmental contamination in parks and public spaces remains a significant risk factor for pets and their owners. However, regular parasite testing and clear client education can not only help combat these challenges but also build trust and strengthen practice growth. In this webinar, Dr. I. Craig Prior will review why advanced diagnostics like PCR testing are becoming essential for accurate detection and treatment, especially with the emergence of multidrug-resistant hookworms. He'll also discuss why consistent year-round prevention, routine fecal testing, and proactive client communication are critical for protecting both animal and public health.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Gastrointestinal Disorders
courses.description: The Gastrointestinal Disorders course is designed to give you an overview of key factors affecting pet gastrointestinal (GI) health. The course discusses diagnosis of common GI conditions in cats and dogs, related key nutritional factors, and nutritional management strategies to help minimize GI distress.

courses.title: Acute Pancreatitis in Dogs: Updates in Diagnosis & Management Strategies
courses.description: In this webinar, strengthen your clinical approach to diagnosing and managing acute pancreatitis in dogs. Through a case-based discussion of challenging cases, often with comorbidities, Dr. Sue Yee Lim will tackle discordant diagnostic test results and provide a practical framework for deciding when a patient truly has pancreatitis. The presentation will also explore emerging and evolving management strategies that are reshaping how veterinarians approach this age-old disease.

courses.title: Advances in Heartworm Management: Clinical Takeaways From the 2025 AHS Triennial Heartworm Symposium
courses.description: This webinar will summarize the key takeaways from the 2025 Triennial Heartworm Symposium. Drs. Andrew Moorhead and Marisa Ames will share highlights on the latest research in heartworm disease, its management, and the practical applications of these insights into clinical practice. Whether you were unable to attend the Triennial Heartworm Symposium or you attended and want a refresher course on the primary findings this webinar is for you!

courses.title: Clinical Approach to Canine Immune-Mediated Anemia: Benefits and Risks of Transfusion
courses.description:
On-demand webcast: Immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA) remains one of the most challenging emergencies encountered in small animal practice. This case-based session will guide participants through a practical and clinically relevant approach to diagnosis and management, blending personal clinical experience with current evidence and consensus recommendations.
The presentation will examine transfusion therapy in IMHA, balancing its benefits and risks, and will share practical guidance on anticoagulant treatment and on adjusting immunosuppressive therapy to improve patient outcomes. Attention will be given to establishing effective monitoring and follow-up protocols that are financially realistic and that help reduce the risk of relapse and long-term complications. This session is designed to provide veterinarians with clear, experience-based guidance for managing IMHA patients more confidently from acute stabilization to long-term care.

courses.title: First-of-its kind and the best Early Cancer Diagnostics test in veterinary medicine available for cats and dogs!
courses.description:
Pet Preferred Diagnostic offers a new universal highly specific and sensitive serological test for the detection eleven specific onconeural antibodies against intracellular neuronal antigens that are associated with twenty two different tumors and fourteen neurological diseases. These antibodies, called onconeural or highrisk antibodies, can be found in patients with paraneoplastic neurological syndromes PNS which are well defined as cancer associated neurological diseases and characterized by severe and progressive neurological degeneration, remote from the tumor. Depending on the type of tumor, tumor cells express several antigens that can stimulate the formation of specific autoantibodies that are involved in the development of PNS, which precedes a tumor diagnosis.
Its important to note that these onconeural antibodies can also be detected without a neurological syndrome and are specific for malignancy rather than for a particular neurological syndrome.
This test is the only one on the veterinary market that differentiates twenty-two different tumors and fourteen neurological diseases and is available for felines too. Dogs and cats with and without clinical signs should be screened for these diseases to detect possible tumours at a treatable stage. The test is an excellent tool to confirm or decline suspicion of having one of 22 tumors, to initiate a timely treatment and to monitor post-treatment.

courses.title: Opioid 411 in 2023 1-Hour Self-Study On-Demand
courses.description: This course has been designed to fulfill the continuing education requirements for all states that have mandated CE on the topic of controlled substances. It provides students with a broad range of expert-level knowledge on subjects including federal controlled substance laws, best practices for prescribing and management of controlled substances including benzodiazepine and opioid medications, use of electronic PDMPs, recognition of substance abuse, signs of opioid abuse, addiction, and diversion, opioid use and dependency in-office staff, clients and co-workers, and treatment of chronic pain.

courses.title: GX Aug - Dec 2024
courses.description: individual on demand 1 hr webinars for vets and nurses

courses.title: Canine Lab 4: Desensitization and Counterconditioning: Teaching Dogs to Willingly Accept Medical Procedures
courses.description: Many dogs dislike or are fearful of various types of handling for procedures such as toenail trims, injections and venipuncture. While it may seem faster to use force-restraint, this type of handling frequently makes the patient worse and takes more time. Techniques for training dogs to enjoy procedures are straightforward, but there are important nuances. In this lab you'll learn the detailed steps that will lead to quick and efficient success. Your patients will now be happy and your clients will be, too.

courses.title: MMPC Learniverse - The 4 Rights - The Right Place
courses.description: Online Self paced course. How do you determine the Right Place for an animal at risk of entering the shelter? In this course, you will learn the framework that allows you to remove decision fatigue and get animals where they need to be, or help them right where they are. The Five Key Initiatives of the Million Cat Challenge have expanded to include other species at risk in shelters and evolved into the Four Rights. Within the Four Rights, every element works in concert to support one another. Animals and people are treated as individuals, empowering shelter staff to make the best decisions for everyone; community safety net services are in place and flourishing, and humane care within the shelter is provided, with appropriate outcomes for the animals that do come in, allowing shelters to deliver the Right Care, in the Right Place, at the Right Time, to the Right Outcome. As part of the Maddies Million Pet Challenge Learniverse program, subject matter experts from the UC Davis Koret Shelter Medicine Program will discuss guiding principles that animal welfare professionals can use to make decisions, train their staff and engage the public. You'll also learn about programs you can use at your shelter to lead animals to the right outcome while making the best possible use of your resources and reducing the burden on your staff. Finally, you'll see how other animal shelters have successfully implemented these programs. Learning Objectives include: Describe the Four Rights concept, Describe the Right Place concept, List potential consequences of not choosing the Right Place, Explain principles that should be considered when determining the Right Place for an animal, Discuss what should be considered when determining the right place for kittens, cats, and dogs, List questions that should be asked when helping finders determine the best place for found kittens, Explain the importance of communicating kitten best practices to your community, Describe strategies you can use t

courses.title: Infectious Disease Control: Pathogens & Disease Transmission
courses.description: This course explores several zoonotic pathogens common to animal care settings discussing routes of transmission and clinical signs in order to explore mechanisms for prevention. Common questions such as "Can I or my pet get it?" or "Can we give it to each other?" can be answered only after the team fully understands the pathogens causing the disease. This course also looks at the difference between quarantine and isolation and when each is appropriate. In addition, this course introduces standard mechanisms for controlling disease transmission in a clinical setting.

courses.title: Infectious Disease Control: Infection Prevention
courses.description: Epidemiological concepts fundamental to infection prevention, such as the "epidemiological triangle", establish the need for infection control in animal care settings. Types of pathogens and key features of each are explored with those commonly encountered in animal care settings specifically discussed. The importance of general pathogen classifications to infection control plans is also explored.

courses.title: TIBIAL PLATEAU-LEVELING OSTEOTOMY PART 4: BONE MODEL DEMONSTRATION AND COMPLEX CASES (195-36647)
courses.description: This online lecture discusses the modified TPLO approaches for specific patient conditions, such as tibial torsion, tibial varus, tibial valgus, and medial patellar luxation. The lecture includes a review of complex TPLO case studies and a demonstration of the TPLO technique on a bone model.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Advanced Mare Reproduction - Investigating the Problem Mare
courses.description:
As part of our Lecture Series on Advanced Mare Reproduction Drs. Angus McKinnon, James Crabtree, Jonathan Pycock & Juan Samper are covering the following topics:
Management of Cycling Problems in Mares - transitional mares, anovulatory hemorrhagic follicles; dioestrus follicle
The repeat Breeder - What to do next?
Examining the Barren Mare (incl. use of ultrasonography in the subfertile mare
Sampling Techniques for Problem Breeders
Risk Factors for Non-Pregnancy in Mares
Management of the Fluid Producing Mare

courses.title: Webinar Series - Advanced Mare Reproduction Artificial Insemination
courses.description:
As part of our Lecture Series on Advanced Mare Reproduction Drs. Jonathan Pycock and Juan Samper are covering the following topics:
Routine Management of Mares for chilled and frozen Insemination
Managing Semen for Deep Horn Insemination (DHI)

courses.title: Webinar Series - Advanced Mare Reproduction - The Pregnant Mare
courses.description:
As part of our Lecture Series on Advanced Mare Reproduction Drs. Angus McKinnon & Jonathan Pycock are covering the following topics:
Twin Management - including Tips & Tricks
Foetal Sexing - 56 - 75 days
Foetal Sexing - Day 110 & Beyond

courses.title: Webinar - One thousand stifle arthroscopies - What have I learnt?
courses.description: European & RCVS Specialist in Equine Surgery, Graham Munroe has been treading the boards of equine referral practice for over forty years. In this webinar he analyses the results of more than one thousand stifle arthroscopic procedures, performed by the same surgeon over a 30-year period. Clinical histories, signs, diagnostic imaging and surgical findings, post-operative care and rehabilitation regimes are all discussed together with the results of the surgical interventions and their relation to long-term prognoses for a range of stifle diseases and injuries.

courses.title: Postural Rehabilitation Professional
courses.description: Postural Rehabilitation Professional is a 6 week, high contact program designed to teach equine professionals how to evaluate and remediate equine abnormal compensatory posture (ACP). Participants will learn about how standing posture is generated and controlled by the CNS, the peripheral structures critical to posture that tend to become distorted by domestication, how to recognize and remediate abnormal anatomic structures (distal limb/hoof, stomatognathic system) and function of the cervical spine to restore normal neutral posture to equine patients. We will also teach team-building among equine professionals, professional communications and how to apply injury forensics to chronic cases.

courses.title: Shock (DRIP110)
courses.description: This course will take you through the fundamentals of the patient in shock. The physiological process of shock will be discussed along with the diagnostic approach and treatment of the patient in shock.

courses.title: Oncology and Emergency Critical Care with Brianna Keller and Katie Osekavage
courses.description: Earn Veterinary Continuing Education on Oncology and Emergency Critical Care
courses.location: Bar Harbor Maine Acadia National Park

courses.title: GAIN - Advanced Ultrasonography
courses.description:
This course is designed for veterinarians who want to master their ultrasound techniques. The name is a clever play on words, referencing both the "gain" control on an ultrasound machine to enhance specific structures you are scanning and the opportunity to gain cutting-edge clinical knowledge in diagnostic ultrasound.
D.V.M., Ph.D., DACVR, DECVDI, Dominique Penninck and Dipl. ECVDI Emmelie Stock will guide you through five modules in which you will learn to optimize scanning technique and refine your diagnostic skills. It is the perfect way to amplify your expertise and provide better care for your patients

courses.title: LafeberVet Stahl-Latney-Lennox + Fall 2025 Non-Interactive Program
courses.description: The LafeberVet Fall 2025 Non-Interactive Program consists of three new webinar recordings plus three preexisting programs: two expired (#924392 and #903638) and one eligible for submission (#963814). Courses cover avian, exotic animal, and herptile medicine. A range of topics are addressed including anatomy and physiology, emergency and critical care, nutrition, sedation and anesthesia, pediatrics, cardiology, diagnostic techniques, such as cytodiagnosis and venipuncture, restraint and handling, euthanasia techniques, as well as clinical concerns, from feather destructive behavior and reproductive disease to gastrointestinal stasis and rabbit hemorrhagic disease, and . One webinar recording also covers the mechanics of flight as well as animal welfare and ethics related to wing trims.

courses.title: Explainable AI for Disease Prediction in Pets
courses.description:
Predictive AI only generates value when people trust it enough to act upon it. In regulated, data-heavy industries such as insurance that trust isn't assumed. It has to be built, methodically, long before any model ships. In this webinar, we will walk attendees through the real engineering and collaboration process behind Fetch Health Forecast, a live AI product that accurately predicts the likelihood of 45 disease categories based on data collected on nearly 800,000 dogs over 17 years of insurance claims to show why AI explainability (XAI) is a discipline you build from the first line of model design, not a feature you add at the end.
The session will cover:
-Why explainability starts with the domain expert in the room: How the collaboration between data scientists and veterinary specialists shaped every stage of the Fetch Health Forecast model.
-The case for building deliberately simple models first: How baseline "stupid models" catch data leakage, validate signals, and create a shared language between data scientists and domain experts before complexity is introduced.
-Translating model outputs into real-world decisions: How feature importance and partial dependence plots were used to surface insights a veterinarian, an insurer, or a pet owner could actually act on.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Backpack Hazards: Protecting Pets from Hidden Toxins
courses.description: August and September are just around the corner, and that means it's almost time for the beginning of the new school year! Come learn about common back-to-school toxins - from school supplies to common items found in backpacks and lunchboxes. Come learn about the list of potential pet toxins and dangers to be extra cautious for the coming school year.

courses.title: Controlled Drugs: Recordkeeping and Diversion Prevention in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description:
All veterinary team members with access to controlled drugs must be aware of the DEA's expectations regarding controlled substance recordkeeping. The course provides examples of documentation methods for keeping track of controlled drugs. Why and how cycle counting should be incorporated and what to do when discrepancies are found are covered. It is heavy on examples regarding how to apply DEA regulations in practice.
Preventing drug diversion requires vigilance, education, and clear policies. Both human and veterinary healthcare professionals play a crucial role in ensuring controlled substances are properly managed to protect patients, workers, and organizations. This course explores the issue of drug diversion in healthcare and veterinary settings, focusing on risks, prevention strategies, and response protocols.

courses.title: When Patients Ain't Doing Right: Team Treatment Plans to Improve Sick Pet Examinations
courses.description: Do you dream about improving the workflow for sick pet examinations to alleviate the strain on the entire veterinary healthcare team? Join Dr. Shannon Sura to gain tips and tricks on how to do just that. In this webinar, Dr. Sura will review the process on how to improve sick pet examinations, including defining the minimum diagnostic database and building out protocols. Attendees will learn the value of engaging and training all members of the veterinary healthcare team to improve client compliance and clinic workflows, as well as how to monitor the success of team training and how enhancing the use of practice information management systems can streamline the development of treatment plans. The webinar will conclude with a patient journey to demonstrate how these recommendations can be realized in an everyday sick pet appointment.

courses.title: Navigating Difficult Client and Colleague Interactions
courses.description:
Difficult interactions are inevitable, but you can improve the outcome of some of these interactions, which will improve your day-to-day work life as well as the experiences of your clients and team.
During this Colleague Consult episode, we will explore strategies for improving difficult client and team interactions that you can begin implementing right away in your practice.

courses.title: FELINE LOWER URINARY TRACT SIGNS (297-43061)
courses.description: The Feline Lower Urinary Tract Signs (feline LUTS) course is designed to give an overview of a group of conditions that can affect the bladder and urethra of cats. The course discusses diagnosis of feline LUTS, introduces related key nutritional factors, and provides nutritional management strategies for cats with LUTS.

courses.title: Camp Maddie: Behavior Edition (OnDemand, Modular)
courses.description: The free, virtual event will consist of two half-days that will include presentations, short videos and Q&A sessions. At Camp Maddie: Behavior Edition, we will talk about determining which dogs are safe to rehome, keeping dogs happy and healthy while in your care, and finding them homes.

courses.title: Finder Foster Legal Considerations with Shelter PALS
courses.description: What is a Finder Foster program? How does it work, how long do finders need to hold an animal and what are other important legal aspects of these programs? Please see attached document for full description and learning objectives.

courses.title: Got a Team? Here is How to Seriously Empower the Women on It
courses.description: Empowering the women on your team isnt just about checking boxes its about creating a real culture of support and growth. In this webinar, we will break down some simple but powerful ways to help the women you work with thrive. From understanding what truly motivates each person to giving them the confidence and tools to speak up, we will explore how you can make a tangible impact on their careers. Plus, we will talk about how to boost their earning potential, show recognition in meaningful ways, and champion their long term goals. If you are ready to make a real difference and help the women on your team reach their full potential, this webinar is for you!

courses.title: WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management - Module III Pain Management in Practice
courses.description: This course includes Module III of the WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management. The course was developed with the vision that veterinary professionals (veterinarians and nurses and veterinary technicians) across the globe understand the importance of adequate pain management for small animal health and welfare, and are empowered to 1) Frequently assess pain in small animals with knowledge of pain-related behaviors and validated pain scales 2)Prevent pain and other negative emotions such as fear, discomfort, nausea and anxiety 3)Treat pain using drug and non-drug therapies in which the analgesic plan is developed on a case-by-case basis and adapted to their own reality. The WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management includes pre-recorded lectures in addition to mandatory and suggested reading materials, and quizzes at the end of each lecture. The educational content is primarily based on the recently published 2022 WSAVA guidelines for the recognition, assessment and treatment of pain, and on additional topics not covered by that document, but considered to be important and relevant for professionals working with companion animal health and welfare globally. Lectures are given by the authors of the Guidelines and other invited experts in the field. The WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management is divided into three Modules. The Module III Pain Management in Practice has 16 hours of content (32 recorded lectures of 20 -30 mins each and 2 hours of mandatory reading). It includes lectures focused on the following topics to put the gained knowledge from Module 1 and 2 into practice while considering the challenges they might face such as limited access to analgesic drugs. For example, tiered analgesic protocols are presented for the management of numerous painful conditions; from state-of-the-art protocols to those with limited analgesic options.

courses.title: Streamlining Client Education: How PupWise Supports Veterinarians in Proactive Pet Care
courses.description:
Veterinary teams are on the front lines of pet care, often spending valuable time addressing repetitive client questions, correcting misinformation, and explaining basic wellness concepts. These challenges stress already busy practices and leave less time for addressing critical patient needs.
In this webinar, Vail Weymann will introduce PupWise, a learning and wellness platform that helps dog parents take a more proactive approach to their pets health and wellbeing. Youll learn how PupWise can become a trusted partner for veterinarians by providing expert powered education that lightens the educational load, fosters proactive care habits, and enhances client loyalty.
Well share actionable strategies for integrating PupWise into practice workflows, from pre-appointment resources to post visit follow ups. This webinar will also highlight the platform's potential to streamline appointments and strengthen client relationships, enabling veterinarians to focus on what they do best providing exceptional care.

courses.provider: NORTH CAROLINA STATE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: 2024 Honey Bee Veterinary Consortium Virtual Conference (On-Demand)
courses.description:
The Honey Bee Veterinary Consortium (HBVC) is made up of students and professionals from all segments of veterinary medicine and animal science who care about bees and beekeeping.
As of January 2017, if a beekeeper needs to administer antibiotics to their honey bees, they are required to have a prescription or feed directive from a licensed veterinarian. Part of our mission at HBVC is to provide an avenue for beekeepers to locate a veterinarian that is willing to work with bees.
The 2024 HBVC Virtual Conference will provide lectures on a variety of topics, including beginner sessions for veterinarians wanting to learn the basics about honey bees and more advanced sessions for seasoned veterinarians wanting to learn more about honey bees.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Consult with Prof Virginia Reef - Latest Developments in Equine Ultrasound
courses.description:
The hunt for neoplasia using ultrasound will focus primarily on exploring the thorax and abdomen, but also its use in identifying soft tissue masses. The sonographic characterization of obvious masses and the identification of more subtle abnormalities, consistent with neoplasia, will be discussed. Evaluation of blood flow to and in the mass is valuable. The use of ultrasound-guided fine needle aspirates and biopsies are an integral part of confirming the diagnosis.
While normal arrhythmias and murmurs in horses abound, determining their significance in the prepurchase setting can be challenging. ECG (resting and exercising) and echocardiography are the mainstays of determining the significance of an arrhythmia or murmur, respectively. Obtaining ECG, auditory and POCUS recordings on a smart phone, which can be emailed to a specialist, aid the practitioner in determining when to refer. This session will focus on cardiac abnormalities detected in the prepurchase setting and determining their significance.
This session will explore diagnosing and managing the more uncommon and challenging cardiac diseases. We will delve in depth into pericardial diseases, endocarditis and complex congenital cardiac diseases. Also, recognizing myocardial diseases can be challenging when obvious changes in myocardial echogenicity is lacking. We will explore advanced methods of assessing myocardial function. Extensive case discussions will round off this session and give attendees the opportunity to expand their experience on how to apply the theory on horses with challenging cardiac problems.

We will delve in depth into pericardial diseases, endocarditis and complex congenital cardiac diseases. Also, recognizing myocardial diseases can be challenging when obvious changes in myocardial echogenicity is lacking. We will explore advanced methods of assessing myocardial function. Extensive ca

courses.title: Fluid Therapy Update (DRIP101)
courses.description: A course set up to review updated principles of fluid dynamics, and the development of an effective fluid therapy plan. It touches on current controversies with synthetic colloids, and serves as a wonderful transition to more complicated disease processes.

courses.provider: HIGH GOAL VETERINARY SERVICES AND DIAGNOSTIC IMAGING
courses.title: Is It Surgical? A Practical Guide to GI Radiology for the General Practitioner
courses.description: This course provides general practitioners, relief veterinarians, and emergency clinicians with a systematic framework for interpreting gastrointestinal radiographs in small animal patients. Using real case examples, participants will learn to evaluate the stomach, small bowel, and colon for findings that require surgical intervention versus medical management. Topics include gastric displacement and dilation (including GDV variants), pyloric obstruction, foreign bodies, mesenteric volvulus, functional ileus, intussusception, colonic torsion, and infiltrative disease.

courses.title: Uncovering the Depths of the Utility of Ultrasound
courses.description:
This 50-minute advanced lecture examines the versatility of abdominal ultrasound in canine and feline patients and emphasizes conditions that are commonly overlooked or underutilized indications for ultrasonography. The session reviews ultrasound evaluation of major abdominal organs including the urinary bladder, lymph nodes, reproductive tract, kidneys, adrenal glands, spleen, liver, stomach, pancreas, small intestine, and abdominal vasculature.
Clinical examples will highlight how ultrasound can identify conditions such as cryptorchidism, paraprostatic cysts, congenital reproductive anomalies, obstructive and ectopic ureters, splenic torsion, unusual splenic presentations, peritoneopericardial diaphragmatic hernia (PPDH), hepatic congestion, gallbladder disease, free abdominal gas, and gastrointestinal pathology including intussusceptions and foreign bodies.
Participants will also learn how subtle ultrasonographic clues, including vascular changes, organ positioning, and ultrasound artifacts, can indicate pathology even when obvious structural abnormalities are not present. Additional discussion will focus on interpretation of abdominal lymph nodes and practical techniques for improving diagnostic sampling during ultrasound-guided procedures. The goal is to broaden the differential diagnoses and demonstrate how ultrasound can serve as a primary diagnostic modality for a wider range of disease processes in small animal patients.

courses.title: Elite Practice Leadership Academy
courses.description: This 7-session course is designed to help veterinary professionals develop effective leadership skills to enhance team performance, improve workplace culture, and support long-term sustainability. Participants will explore topics including practice culture, multigenerational leadership, performance reviews, coaching and counseling, change management, and professional wellbeing. Through interactive sessions and actionable strategies, attendees will gain tools to lead with confidence, reduce burnout, and drive team engagement. Ideal for veterinary practice owners, managers, and team leads seeking growth in communication, staff development, and organizational success.

courses.title: Basic Fish Medicine (EXOT213)
courses.description: The first module of this course focuses on basic husbandry and water quality. How to access and methods to quantify the most important parameters, as well as, how to identify poor water quality and how to improve it. The second module of the course is designed to provide veterinarians, technicians and nurses with fundamental knowledge of aquatic veterinary nursing, divided into emergency nursing, client communication, medical nursing, and surgical nursing. The topics will include triage, restraint, sample collection techniques, water analysis, post-mortem examination, advanced imaging, patient management, therapeutic techniques, anesthesia, and more. The third module focuses on common presenting signs and diseases of ornamental fish and some diagnostic and treatment options.

courses.title: guidED 2025 | Victoria, BC
courses.description: guidED 2025 | Victoria, BC is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Intracardiac Pet Euthanasias; Your Heart's in the Right Place
courses.description: Euthanasia is an intimate experience for many veterinary practitioners. They know which techniques they like and those they don't. While it's been known for quite some time that intracardiac injections are nerve wracking to perform, a recent study showed that 82% of veterinarians prefer not to do them with clients present, and would just as soon avoid them altogether if given the chance. There are times when an intracardiac euthanasia injection is the best option for the patient, and it's up to all veterinarians to gain the confidence and skills to perform them, especially in front of clients. In this session, we take a closer look at this euthanasia injection method and why it's so effective. Want to make it a safe and dare-we-say pleasant experience for your patient, clients and team? Join us to learn how.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: ACVIM Principles of Cancer Immunotherapy
courses.description: Immunotherapy is now recognized as the 'fourth pillar' of cancer therapy.
