As immunological approaches are translated into the clinic for human and veterinary cancer patients, it is essential for oncologists and other health care professionals to have a thorough understanding of immunophysiology and immunopathology, as this will allow them to appreciate the balance between the potential benefits and the considerable risks of immunotherapy. This lecture will emphasize general principles of immunotherapy, describe several approaches that have been or are being translated from the laboratory to the clinic, and provide selected examples of how gains in immunotherapy are being translated to companion animals with cancer. The presentation is divided into five sections. The first section will present a brief primer of immunophysiology and immunopathology. The viewer is strongly encouraged to watch the previous lecture in this series entitled, 'Building the Immune Environment of Cancer.' The second section will review mechanisms whereby the immunosuppressive barrier can be disrupted and through which the immune system can attack the tumor. The third section will cover a brief history of immunotherapy, illustrating the centuries-old interest in this field. The fourth section will review general approaches to immunotherapy with select examples of their application in companion animals. The fifth and final section will introduce the emerging area of cancer Immunoprophylaxis, which represents the next frontier for cancer immunotherapy.

courses.title: An Introduction to Radiation Therapy for Distinguished Older Canines
courses.description: An Introduction to Radiation Therapy for Distinguished Older Canines

courses.title: The Storm Before the Calm: Supporting Behavioral Health in Cats & Dogs
courses.description: This webinar will review the rationale for incorporating compounds that can beneficially modulate clinical signs of fear, anxiety, and stress into a management plan for dogs and cats to help provide calm and comfort, improve quality of life, and enhance the emotional bond for both pets and their owners.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Equine Emergency & Critical Care for Advanced Practitioners
courses.description: This practically oriented webinar was designed for equine practitioners and veterinary technicians with good working knowledge in the field of equine emergency and critical care. The world-renowned specialists will report on new developments and share invaluable tips and tricks on how to efficiently diagnose and treat critically ill patients in a private clinic setting. Each of the following hot topics will be addressed via well-illustrated, interactive case discussions providing a platform for the panel to also share pitfalls and erroneous clinical conclusions:

courses.title: Canine Weight Management
courses.description: An introductory course focused on canine weight management including the importance of proper nutrition and nutrient balance when developing a weight management program. The modules in this course provide a deeper understanding of many aspects of weight management including an overview of the disease condition, factors involved in diagnosing a weight issue, recommendations for treatment plans as well as communication tips for engaging the pet parent to ensure successful outcomes.

courses.title: Managing Cats With Subclinical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Joshua Stern will discuss the diagnosis and management of subclinical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). The presentation will focus on understanding disease progression and identifying cats that are at increased risk for cardiovascular conditions such as congestive heart failure, thromboembolism, and sudden cardiac death. Through case discussions, Dr. Stern will review how to develop a treatment plan for these patients and discuss potential future therapies and ongoing clinical research in this evolving and exciting clinical landscape.

courses.title: Nutritional Support for Cognitive Health and Joint Care in Cats and Dogs
courses.description:
This course focuses on the benefits of proper nutrition for supporting both brain and joint health in cats and dogs. Participants will learn about the pathogenesis, clinical signs and evidence for nutritional management of feline and canine cognitive dysfunction syndrome (CDS) and degenerative joint disease (DJD).
Successful completion of this course provides insights into managing senior patients using nutritional support for these common co-conditions.

courses.title: The Clinical Approach to the Neurologic Exam (DRIP148)
courses.description: This course focuses on the typical presentation, differential diagnosis, treatments and prognosis of the common veterinary neurologic exam.

courses.title: Feed Real Summit 2026
courses.description:
Discover Practical Paths To Dog Longevity
Food is the basis of wellness, but even the best diet can be outdone by toxic chemicals found in everyday dog products, including shampoos, bedding, flea and tick topicals, and supplements. FRS26 is designed to provide 2.0 dog parents, veterinary professionals, and other canine professionals, including aspiring wellness coaches, trainers, and groomers, with practical and actionable tips for promoting dog longevity.
Speaker presentations, workshops, and the panel discussion will cover the following topics: The Basics of Ayurveda for Canine Longevity, Vaccines and Titers, Entangled Presence: Healing, Connection, and Longevity, Silver Muzzles, Golden Hearts: Understanding Your Aging Dog, Pets and Their Light Environments: Why Light is the Foundation to Health, Stem Cells as Secret Agents, DIY Fresh Food: Save Money and Make Your Dog's Food at Home, Mushroom Treats for Dogs: Sneaking Nutrition into Every Bite, Creating Herbal Tinctures and Infusions, and The Future of Canine Wellness Beyond the Veterinary Clinic.

courses.title: Pre-Trilostane, Baseline, or Stim: Which is the best method to check cortisol levels?
courses.description: Hyperadrenocorticism (HAC) can be a costly disease for which to monitor treatment success. This module explores the various types of monitoring tests, including current knowledge, caveats, and clinical value of each test. The ACTH stimulation test has been the standard test used to monitor treatment in the US, but it is expensive and time-consuming. The newest test, the pre-pill cortisol test, is also discussed; this test has been adopted as the EU test of choice, but not as of yet in the US. This monitoring tool would be much less costly and time-consuming than traditional tests, leading to improved client compliance and patient outcomes.

courses.title: Large Animal Myofascial Practitioners Course
courses.description: This course covers the role of the myofascial system in equines, the relationship between muscle and trigger points, and fascia and its role and function in the body. This course is designed to educate students about the muscular and fascial systems, how to differentiate normal tissue from dysfunctional tissue and discuss the various diagnostic and treatment techniques regarding myofascial pain in detail. The course includes an online and practical component covering twenty different muscles. Students will learn the theory of myofascial pain, the function of muscle and fascia, how to identify myofascial pain, palpation, diagnostics, and in-depth treatment options. At the end of the course, the student should be able to locate myofascial dysfunction and treat myofascial trigger points effectively with good results.

courses.title: Circle of Care: Amputation Pain Solutions & Home Recovery Insights for Amputee Pets & Their People
courses.description:
Amputations are major surgeries that are painful not only intraoperatively, but can also be painful for a fairly long time post-operatively. The longer recovery time from pain is due to the large areas of soft tissue involvement at the surgery site and the severing of numerous, some fairly large, nerves. The latter initiates neuropathic pain, which can be difficult to control. If the amputation is done because of a painful lesion, the pre-existing pain will exacerbate the intra- and post-operative pain. Dr Grubb will discuss pre-, intra- and post-operative analgesic strategies.
Attendees will learn about the most immediate concerns that pet parents have when their dog or cat has had a limb amputation. The goal is to encourage discussion before and after surgery, in order to facilitate a smoother recovery with less emotional burden on the pet parent as well as the veterinary team.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Introduction to Spaying and Neutering
courses.description: This course describes the goals a high-quality, high-volume spay/neuter (HQHVSN) clinic advocates for, as well as a view of the surgical procedures in their entirety. We will discuss the history of HQHVSN, its continued pursuit of a high standard of quality patient care, and how that relates to increasing access to veterinary care for dogs and cats in need.

courses.title: How to Keep Infectious Disease at Bay at Your Shelter
courses.description: This webinar will include a discussion of common infectious diseases in animal shelters and information on mitigating the risk of these diseases occurring in and spreading through an animal shelter population.

courses.title: There are no bad cats, just cats with high FAS
courses.description: Cats often have increased FAS in the veterinary setting, over the years this has driven them out of the clinic and perpetuated biases towards this purrfect species. We will discuss ways to improve feline care by decreasing their FAS.

courses.title: BioMedtrix Introduction to THR for Surgical Residents Workshop
courses.description: The BioMedtrix Introduction to THR for Surgical Residents Workshop was developed in cooperation with experienced industry-leading surgeons. This one-day course is designed for second and third-year residents and consists of a comprehensive online educational component, classroom instruction, and hands-on laboratory experience. Our multi-faceted approach to education is designed to offer participants a thorough supply of resources, reinforcement, and support to familiarize themselves with the Total Hip Replacement procedure.

courses.title: Reap What you Sow: Applying Positive Reinforcement to Horse Health Care
courses.description: This Equine Behavior program provides information about the use of positive techniques to reduce distress and promote voluntary cooperation in horses, which in turn improve the safety of veterinary professionals. The techniques are based on scientifically validated principles of learning and behavior that have proven effectiveness and are recognized as being humane. The focus of the program is on horses and the objective will be to provide detailed information and illustrative examples about how to apply these techniques in a veterinary practice.

courses.title: Canine Chroic Enteropathy - Non Interactive
courses.description: "This course provides a comprehensive review of diagnosis, treatment and long-term management of chronic GI disease in dogs, with a focus on using dietary management. Participants will take away practical management strategies and approaches to aid in long-term management of dogs with GI disease. "

courses.provider: CAREFREE DENTISTRY AND ORAL SURGERY FOR ANIMALS
courses.title: 2025 Annual Stomatology Symposium
courses.description: Join Carefree Dentistry and Oral Surgery for Animals at the Phoenix Zoo on February 12, 2025, for the 2nd Annual Stomatology Symposium, a full-day event covering essential topics in veterinary dentistry. Gain expert insights into dental radiograph interpretation, managing salivary gland disorders, advanced periodontal therapies, and performing high-quality COHATs. Learn best practices in anesthesia and pain management, and explore the latest approaches to diagnosing and treating oral tumors in animals. Expect interactive discussions, networking with leading professionals, and practical takeaways to elevate your clinical practice in animal dental care.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2026 Advanced Equine Endocrinology
courses.description: Equine endocrinology is rapidly evolving, with new discoveries shaping how we diagnose and manage diseases. This 2-day ACE course offers an advanced, evidence-based update on endocrine disorders in equids from the neonatal to geriatric periods. Topics include nutrition, pharmacologic therapies, and both emergent and long-term management strategies. Interactive Q&A panels with leading experts will ensure participants leave with practical tools they can apply immediately in clinical practice.

courses.title: Monitoring of Small Animal Diabetes
courses.description: Diabetes remains one of the most challenging conditions in small animal practice, with 33 porcent of diabetic patients not surviving beyond the first year. How can we change this statistic and help diabetic pets live longer, healthier lives? Join us for this essential webinar, Monitoring of Small Animal Diabetes, where we will explore advanced strategies to extend diabetic patients' lives and improve outcomes. We will cover effective approaches to easing the initial shock of a diabetes diagnosis for pet owners and dive into the latest advancements in diabetes management, equipping you with the tools to provide comprehensive, compassionate care in todays veterinary landscape.

courses.title: CCAT II: Biophysical Agent Modalities & Therapeutic Exercises
courses.description:
This course will provide the participant with the didactic material for selected biophysical agent modalities used in canine physical rehabilitation. Superficial heating and cooling agents, therapeutic ultrasound, extracorporeal shockwave treatment, PEMF, laser therapy, and electrical stimulation will be covered as well as theoretical clinical applications with cases.
This course also provides the participant with the necessary skills necessary to prescribe and provide therapeutic exercise programs. Benefits and risks associated with therapeutic exercise programs will be covered along with outcome assessment of exercise programs. Topics covered include joint biomechanics, exercise physiology, range of motion and stretching, gait training, strengthening exercises, balance and proprioceptive exercises, aquatic exercises, and exercises for wellness/prevention. Outcome measures (goniometry, circumferential measurements, etc.) will also be covered in this course.

courses.title: Small Animal Dentistry - Virtual
courses.description: Small Animal Dentistry For The Everyday Practice. This course is designed for the every day practitioner to expand their knowledge of small animal dentistry. This course will provide the necessary knowledge to properly diagnose oral pathology, provide instruction on extractions, radiology and complications that may arise.

courses.title: Meatlys cultivated chicken for pet food: safety, regulation, nutritional quality, digestibility, palatability and feeding tr
courses.description: Pet food is responsible for around 20% of global meat consumption, and cultivated meat (also known as lab-grown meat) is a promising alternative protein source to address the public health, environmental and animal welfare challenges of conventional meat production. In July 2024, Meatly obtain the first ever global regulatory approval to sell cultivated meat as an ingredient for pet food. This was the result of both technological progress and extensive data collection about the use of cultivated meat in pet nutrition. In this webinar, Meatlys CEO and their veterinary nutritionist will share all current safety and nutritional information and answer your questions on cultivated meat. This will allow veterinarians to answer pet owners questions on the topic in the framework of evidence-based nutrition.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Avian Nutrition, Ophthalmology Dermatology, Behaviour and Welfare of Parrots
courses.description: This webinar series has been designed for veterinarians in practice, working with avian cases, wishing to gain a higher level of expertise in their approach to avian nutrition and its impact on bird well-being, avian ophthalmology and dermatology as well as emergency and critical care of birds in general and behavioural issues and management of parrots in particular.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2024 Updates on Neuromuscular Disorders On Demand
courses.description: Over the past several years, the number and characterization of neuromuscular diseases affecting companion animals has greatly expanded. Neuromuscular diseases can be diagnostic challenges. This course is designed to bring the attendee up to date on the correct approach to the diagnosis of neuromuscular diseases. Classifications of muscle and peripheral nerve diseases have changed, as mutations for genetic diseases are identified and the pathogenesis of these diseases defined. This course will enable recognition of the common clinical phenotypes, understanding of the rationale and need for diagnostic testing, and awareness of new genetic tests. Optimal treatments are still lacking for most neuromuscular diseases. Thus, a well-designed approach to clinical trials is required to aid in the discovery of new and effective therapies.

courses.title: The Future Is Four: Dive Into The 4 Rights - The Right Care in the Right Place at the Right Time to the Right Outcome - Webin
courses.description: The foundation of the Million Cat Challenge rested on Five Key Initiatives, refined, and adapted to shelters of every size and type throughout North America, which together represented a holistic approach that addressed the before, during, and after for any cat at risk of shelter entry. These initiatives were proven by over 3.5 million more cat lives saved by over 1500 Challenger Shelters. Now, ThanksToMaddie, we are thinking bigger. With the Maddie Million Pet Challenge, the Five Key Initiatives of the Million Cat Challenge have expanded to include other species at risk in shelters and evolved into the Four Rights. Within the Four Rights, every element works in concert to support one another: animals and people are treated as individuals, empowering shelter staff to make the best decisions for everyone, community safety net services are in place and flourishing, and humane care within the shelter is provided, with appropriate outcomes for the animals that do come in, allowing shelters to deliver the Right Care, in the Right Place, at the Right Time, and to the Right Outcome. As part of the Maddie Million Pet Challenge Learniverse program, subject matter experts from the UC Davis Koret Shelter Medicine Program will discuss guiding principles that animal welfare professionals can use to make decisions, train their staff, and engage the public. To get a complete overview of the series, watch an introduction presented by Dr. Kate Hurley, The Future is Four.

courses.title: Soft Tissue Level 2: Intermediate to Advanced Online Class
courses.description: This course is designed for the attendee to learn the normal and abnormal appearance of all abdominal organs, including pancreas, adrenal glands, and lymph nodes. In addition, scanning technique, machine controls necessary to create a high quality diagnostic image, measurements, and following a consistent scanning protocol will be emphasized. Ultrasound guided aspiration and biopsy technique will be covered. Taught by a Board Certified Veterinary Radiologist. The format is a Non-interactive Distance Class.

courses.title: Introduction to Veterinary Resilience
courses.description: This on-demand program will introduce participants to the basic concepts of applied veterinary resilience. Through concise, small-bite modules, students will gain a foundational understanding of how our brains manage adversity and discover practical tools for turning challenges into opportunities for growth. This awareness can create behaviors that empower veterinary professionals to create a supportive work environment, encourage one another, encourage engagement in the profession, and promote overall flourishing. Students will learn evidence-based resilience concepts and some simple tools to apply skills and knowledge "in the real world". This 7-module program is self-paced and includes brief quizzes to assess student learning.

courses.title: The Acid Test: HPP and Lactic Acid For Raw Food Safety
courses.description: Considering the health risks associated with raw meat pet foods to pets and humans, High Pressure Processing (HPP) has shown promise in significantly reducing pathogens like Salmonella, E. coli STEC, and L. monocytogenes refrigeration. Since L. monocytogenes is more resistant to HPP, further formulation and process optimization are needed to ensure long-term safety. Chicken based raw diet pet food was inoculated with 7-8 log CFU/g cocktails of Salmonella spp., E. coli STEC or L. monocytogenes and stored at 4*C for 24 hours before the addition of either 0.7% or 1.0% w/v lactic acid fermentate (LAF) and HPP treated at 586 MPa for 2, 3 and 4 min after 24 or 72 hours storage at 4*C. HPP treated products were stored frozen up to 21 days and analyzed microbiologically. This study clearly demonstrates that when both LAF and HPP are employed, a full 5-log reduction of Salmonella spp., E. coli STEC, and L. monocytogenes is consistently achieved. The use of LAF appears to be instrumental in enhancing the lethality of the treatment. Qualitative enrichment further highlights that LAF not only boosts the immediate log reduction but also contributes to a more comprehensive inactivation profile during post-HPP frozen storage. The optimal combination in this study was found to be 1% LAF with HPP at 586 MPa for 4 minutes. The combo hurdles not only maximize pathogen inactivation but also provide both formulation and processing controls, serving as a robust strategy against potential re-growth during storage.

courses.title: Virtual Care Master Class Level 2
courses.description: Level Two of this virtual care master class guides veterinarians through the complete virtual exam process. Participants learn how to effectively take a remote history, maximize their video patient exams, develop a clinical impression, create a treatment, general advice, or triage plan, and complete their medical records. Additional modules cover how to connect clients with prescription, OTC, and wellness products using VetsterRx, and how to apply professional communication skills in challenging situations. Conflict resolution, de-escalation, and maintaining boundaries are emphasized to support successful, stress-free virtual interactions.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Human Medications
courses.description: Human medications remain one of the ASPCA Poison Control's most common calls each year. During this webinar, we will provide the audience members with a better understanding of the mechanism of toxicity, common clinical signs, and the most current approach to treating toxicities from the most common human medication exposures.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Exotics vs Toxins: Common ingestions in our uncommon species
courses.description: This course will cover some of the most common exotic species-related calls that we take at APCC, involving reptiles, rabbits, guinea pigs, ferrets, and more. We will discuss both common and unique toxin ingestions in exotic species, and discuss important species differences from dogs and cats. Lastly, clinical management of toxin ingestions will be discussed.

courses.title: OPTIMAL AGE FOR SPAY / NEUTER (Anytime)
courses.description: Recent veterinary literature related to spay neuter has caused veterinarians to question the traditional approaches to sterilization of dogs and cats. Some in the profession advocate delaying spay neuter later than the traditional age of 6 months, others advocate early age or pediatric spay neuter. Who is correct? Is there a single recommendation that can be made for all dogs and cats related to the age of ovariohysterectomy or castration? We will discuss several of the articles that have contributed to the confusion. The goal is to analyze confusing and often conflicting reports in the veterinary literature to help veterinarians understand the pros and cons of spay/neuter and the most appropriate age to perform these surgeries in male and female dogs and cats.

courses.title: Low Stress Handling Certification Silver Level
courses.description: The purpose of this Certification in Low Stress Handling is to provide the teaching content needed to understand and improve the individual's or hospital's ability to create a low stress environment and handle animals in a less stressful manner. Coursework for this Certification goes beyond the teaching available from Dr. Sophia Yins textbook/DVD Low Stress Handling, Restraint and Behavior Modification of Dogs & Cats and related training videos. While those sources include improvements to the hospital's design, to its preparation of and for the patient prior to a visit, and to its use of tools and sedative agents, a large portion of Low Stress Handling relies on the development of hands on skills.

courses.provider: VETERINARY EMERGENCY AND CRITICAL CARE SOCIETY
courses.title: Online Tech MDR from IVECCS 2024
courses.description: The Technician MDR course is designed for veterinary technicians seeking to explore focused areas of clinical knowledge at the depth appropriate for those pursuing specialty certification. These sessions are particularly suited for technicians preparing for emergency and critical care specialty certification, as well as for those wishing to maintain and advance their professional competency. Topics addressed may include coagulation disorders, cardiogenic shock, the RAAS (renin angiotensin aldosterone system), hyperglycemic hyperosmolar syndrome, electrolyte disturbances, and advanced acid base and blood gas interpretation.

courses.title: Gut Instincts: How the Gut Brain Axis Shapes FAS and Pain
courses.description: Join us for an informative webinar on how the gut brain axis shapes FAS and pain in your patients. Robin SAAR RVT, VTS (NUTRITION), MSC CANDIDATE will teach you how the bacteria in the gut can affect your patience pain and FAS. You will learn about the endocannabinoid system, the pathways of bacterial translocation, the neurotramsitters that bacteria produce, and the dysbiosis influence on pain.

courses.title: CN3000: Caninology Canine Body Worker Certification Course
courses.description: The CN3000 Certification program is designed for students who wish to pursue a career in canine bodywork, and is regularly attended by veterinarians, veterinary technicians, physical therapists, human massage therapist and chiropractors who wish to enhance their skills or continue their education.

courses.title: March Fourward: The Future is Four
courses.description: The foundation of the Million Cat Challenge rested on Five Key Initiatives, refined and adapted to shelters of every size and type throughout North America, which together represented a holistic approach that addressed the before, during and after for any cat at risk of shelter entry. These initiatives were proven by over 3.5 million more cat lives saved by over 1,500 Challenger Shelters. The Five Key Initiatives have expanded to include other species at risk in shelters and evolved into the Four Rights, with community safety net services, humane care within the shelter, and appropriate outcomes for the animals that do come in all working in concert to support one another.

courses.title: Superior - The Decisive Surgery Course
courses.description:
Surgery is a specialized field of medicine that requires not only extensive technical knowledge but also a high degree of personal strength. In this webinar series, three top-class surgeons will share their insights.
Theresa Fossum looks at the classic GDV from an interesting practical perspective and opens in her second webinar the doors way for surgical treatment of cardiac diseases for general practitioners.
Pieter Nelissen will give insight into the modern surgical approach of the brachycephalic obstructive syndrome and will explain in his second webinar the effective way of how to manage and treat laryngeal paralysis in dogs and cats.
Rachel Hattersley will cover in her webinar the interesting topic of surgical oncology.
All three of our brilliant speakers will pass on their expertise and experience and take you into the fantastic world of high-class surgery.
This course is suitable for both beginners and advanced veterinarians. The only requirement is enthusiasm and fascination for surgery.
Be part of this fantastic experience and dive with us into a world full of excitement, precision and passion.

courses.title: Dynamic Discussion of Practical Pearls in Ophthalmology, Orthopedics, Dentistry, and Dermatology
courses.description: The interactive lectures will focus on recognition of both common and species/breed specific ophthalmic, dermatologic, and orthopedic disease processes. Case studies will be emphasized in an informal game show format with the attendees able to test their own knowledge and recognition of disease. Diagnostic results and clinical signs that are unexpected will also be highlighted to widen the learners ability to diagnose and treat. Discussion of diagnosis and therapy will follow recognition of the disease. State of the art updates will be included specific to diseases.

courses.title: An Introduction to CORA Based Leveling Osteotomy (CBLO)
courses.description:
This course is designed to provide foundational knowledge of CORA Based Leveling Osteotomy (CBLO). This course reviews when and why to conduct a CBLO procedure and gives theory behind why CBLO has been highly successful in repairing anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears in canines. After reviewing the procedure from preoperative care to postoperative care, this course reviews current research and provides next steps.
CORA based leveling osteotomy is a procedure where the tibial plateau slope is modified by centering the saw blade (ACA) at the location of the CORA (center of rotation of angulation). In doing so there is no secondary translation; the proximal anatomic axis and distal anatomic axis are aligned.
The expected time to complete this course is 3 hours.

courses.title: Pathogenesis of Atopic Dermatitis: Clinical Applications
courses.description: Atopic dermatitis is a complex, multifactorial disease that can be frustrating to manage in general practice. In this webinar, Dr. Sara Ramos will review the pathogenesis of atopic dermatitis through a clinical application lens and compare and contrast canine and feline atopic dermatitis to human atopic dermatitis. Attendees will leave with a new sense of confidence in how to clinically take the pathogenesis of atopic dermatitis into account when designing an individualized treatment plan.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Can Trauma-informed Care Support Behavior Modification Efforts for Dogs? (On Demand)
courses.description: This talk will explore the aspects of Trauma-Informed Care for humans which might be applied in dogs, focusing on the assessment of shelter dogs or those presented for problematic behaviors, and the potential for protecting puppies from adverse early experiences.

courses.title: Certificate in Cultivating Positive Team Communication (for Veterinary Professionals)
courses.description: This highly interactive, evidence-based program will introduce participants to the art, science, and application of positive communication skills. Participants will gain a deep understanding of the interconnected nature of positive communication, high-quality relationships, and the basics of conflict management in the workplace. They will master the skills of cultivating and strengthening interpersonal capital within teams by way of applied positive communication and conflict management approaches. The program leverages a mixed-methods approach to learning including asynchronous materials, supportive resources, small-bite live lectures, interactive "safe space" practice sessions, real-world skill-enhancing challenges, professional coaching, and more in an intimate cohort-style setting.

courses.title: American College of Animal Welfare Short Course 2026
courses.description: The American College of Animal Welfare (ACAW) is the AVMA-approved veterinary specialty college for veterinarians with advanced training and expertise in animal welfare. The mission of ACAW is to advance animal welfare through education, certification, and scientific investigation. ACAW is pleased to invite veterinarians and veterinary students interested in animal welfare to ACAW Short Course 2026. This conference includes scientific sessions about important issues in animal welfare (this year focusing on animals used in research and education), an optional field trip to a local research facility to assess the welfare of their animals, a poster session, and multiple opportunities for socializing and networking with ACAW diplomates, residents, and other veterinarians interested in animal welfare.

courses.title: Breathing Space: Controlling Canine Respiratory Disease Amid Shelter Crowding -- On Demand
courses.description:
In the face of rising intake numbers, shelters need some breathing space to keep infectious diseases at bay. This webinar focuses on managing canine respiratory disease when your facility is stretched to its limits. You'll discover how a combination of reduced crowding, improved ventilation, and stress reduction can dramatically lower the risk of CIRD outbreaks.
In this 60-minute discussion, we'll outline actionable steps to implement effective isolation and quarantine protocols while leveraging foster homes to decompress overcrowded kennels and halt disease spread. Attendees will also get up to date on vaccination strategies to boost immunity in the population, including guidance on when diagnostic testing is warranted to identify the culprit behind an outbreak. Equally important, we'll discuss antibiotic stewardship -- recognizing when a cough just needs supportive care versus when a serious secondary infection calls for treatment.
By applying these tools, your team can find room to breathe and ensure more dogs stay healthy and ready for adoption.

courses.title: EXTRACAPSULAR (EXCAP) LATERAL FABELLO-TIBIAL SUTURE STABILIZATION OF THE STIFLE: WET LAB (195-41366)
courses.description: This hands-on workshop is one part of a series of programs designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn/refine the extracapsular (ExCap) lateral fabello-tibial suture stabilization technique and to understand the major advantages of PowerX Crimping System. Participants will perform the ExCap suture stabilization technique on canine cadavers under faculty supervision using a step-by-step high-resolution video demonstration. This laboratory will include arthrotomy for stifle exploration, removal of the CrCL remnants, inspection of the medial meniscus, proper placement of the ExCap suture and use of a precise crimping system and critique of your repair.

courses.title: Clinical Uses of Amnion in Veterinary Regenerative Medicine: An Introductory Course
courses.description: This introductory continuing education program provides veterinarians with an evidence-informed overview of amnion-derived products used in veterinary regenerative medicine. The course includes a brief historical perspective on the use of amniotic membrane in wound care, followed by discussion of its biological properties, proposed mechanisms of action, and current clinical applications in conditions such as osteoarthritis, soft tissue injury (including tendon and ligament), fractures, wound management, and ocular surface conditions in small animal and equine patients. The program will review product types, including amniotic membrane allografts and fluid or particulate amnion-derived preparations, along with safety considerations and practical approaches to case selection and administration (e.g., topical application, ocular surface use, and local placement within or around affected tissues). Species-specific sourcing considerations, including allogeneic use in equine patients and xenogeneic use in canine patients, will be addressed. Case-based examples are included to support clinical decision-making, along with discussion of current evidence limitations and variability among available biologic products.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: The Hemoabdomen Patient
courses.description: Hemoabdomens during spays are a concerning ordeal. This presentation will lead the attendee through practices that can help in identifying signs of a hemoabdomen, diagnosis, and treatment during routine spays.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: ACVIM North American Neuroscience Course (Brain Camp): Advanced Veterinary Neuroscience Week 2
courses.description: This 5-day offering is the second installment of this 10-day module and is designed to offer an intense, high-level review of clinical veterinary neurology aimed at the neurology resident. Topics will range from neuroanatomy and neuropathology all the way through diagnostic imaging and surgical interventions. This is a broad review of clinical neurology with the goal of preparing for the specialty examination and clinical practice.

courses.title: AO VET NA Blended Course: AO PEER Level 2 Course--Publication Writing
courses.description:
AO VET North America is partnering with ACVS to offer the AO Program for Education and Excellence in Research (AO PEER).
This Level 2 course is designed to introduce participants to the principles, workflow, and challenges of preparing a scientific manuscript for publication. The experienced faculty will offer insights and guidance into how best to define content, illustrate, write, and edit a scientific article. Participants will learn about the review process that is undertaken by journals, how to avoid common pitfalls in scientific writing, and how to use reviewers' comments to improve their manuscript.
Prior to meeting at the Surgery Summit, participants will complete a self-directed online course beginning September 22, 2025. An interactive forum will be available during the online course work to give participants an opportunity to exchange thoughts and discuss challenges.
Following the completion of the online self-paced portion of the course, participants will gather in person on Wednesday, October 22, 2025, at the ACVS Surgery Summit.

courses.title: Best Practices for Rescue Horses
courses.description: This program with Dr. Stacie Boswell, a Board-Certified Large Animal Surgeon, focuses on caring for equines in transition who have medical issues, particularly starvation. An attendee should be able to appropriately manage a horse's return to health after starvation or prolonged caloric deficiency. Attendees should be able to identify additional health needs for an individual neglected horse, and learn how to triage health and behavioural considerations for optimum well-being. Refeeding syndrome and considerations for euthanasia will be discussed.

courses.title: Introduction to Laser Therapy
courses.description:
Learn the latest laser therapy treatment concepts and techniques. Content will include recommended target doses, how to calculate them manually and automatically, general protocols for laser therapy case management, proper delivery and treatment techniques, preparation of the client, patient, and laser therapist for treatment sessions, and creation of an appropriate treatment environment.
Learn how to use your therapy laser to treat every-day acute and chronic conditions as well as less common conditions you may have not yet thought of. Broaden the range of patients benefiting from your use of laser therapy with this case and results-based webinar.
This presentation focuses on the importance of identifying, measuring, and treating pain. The consequences of pain are assessed as is the use of photobiomodulation laser therapy as an important component to pain management support. The role of analgesic drugs and their site of action in the Pain Pathway will be reviewed and how the unique properties of laser therapy may be used in perioperative, acute, and chronic pain management. Case reports illustrate laser uses for patients with abdominal/visceral pain, oral/dental pain, musculoskeletal pain, and urinary tract pain.
The science of laser therapy has evolved from early low level laser therapy, through laboratory experience with cold lasers, to today's widespread use in veterinary medicine of efficient, high powered devices. This introductory webinar will look at laser therapy 2017 the science, the evidence, the potential clinical applications and the safety guidelines.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2024 Updates on Urothelial Carcinoma On Demand
courses.description:
Urothelial carcinoma is a notoriously difficult cancer in veterinary oncology for which reliably effective therapies are still needed. In this day-long virtual course, panelists¿will first discuss available data exploring the biologic basis of this cancer and the development and clinical integration of novel diagnostics. The course will continue with the clinical application of surgery, non-surgical interventional procedures, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapies, and multi-modal therapies that are currently available or emerging for veterinary cancer patients. A keynote speaker from physician-based medicine will present information from the human urothelial carcinoma landscape.
Successes, potential opportunities, and challenges associated with this cancer will be discussed in depth with significant opportunity for open Q&A with speakers.

courses.title: Combating Antimicrobial Resistance with Stewardship: A One Health Approach
courses.description: The Chicago Department of Public health will be hosting a free one-day continuing education event. Attendees across a spectrum of settings will learn how to maximize their organization's capacity to take actionable steps and combat the problem of antimicrobial resistance. Local and national leaders in antimicrobial stewardship will guide participants on how they can use limited resources to have the biggest impact, how they can use their facility's data to prioritize activities, and how they can motivate patients or clients and colleagues to invest in antimicrobial stewardships.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Tox Trends: Emerging Toxins & Updates in Clinical Veterinary Toxicology
courses.description: In this one-hour session, learn how to identify and treat the toxic syndromes currently on the rise in companion animals. The first portion of the lecture will include discussion on psychedelic mushrooms, delta-8 THC, oclacitinib, illicit xylazine, and SGLT inhibitors. The second half of the hour will feature recent updates in clinical toxicology. We will cover extracorporeal elimination, grape and raisin exposures, induction of emesis with ropinirole, and fluid diuresis.

courses.title: Canine Cognitive Dysfunction
courses.description: We will cover senior dog problems, focusing on canine cognitive dysfunction. We will also consider special considerations for treating behavior concerns in the geriatric population.

courses.title: Bleeding Disorders and Hemostasis (DRIP144)
courses.description: This course focuses on relevant pathophysiology and diagnostic testing regarding bleeding disorders and hemostasis and discusses potential therapies.

courses.title: The View on Procedural Sedation from A to Zenalpha
courses.description: In this talk-show style panelist discussion, Dr. Jane Quandt, Dr. Tannetje' Crocker, and Darci Palmer will share their views on procedural sedation, from A to Zenalpha. They will discuss the goals of procedural sedation, define what procedural sedation really means in veterinary practice, and examine what drug selection factors the veterinary team should consider when sedating dogs, including healthy dogs and aging dogs with cardiovascular issues. They will also explore what drug options are available in our toolbox for procedural sedation and share a closer look at the innovative alpha-2 combination drug, Zenalpha (medetomidine and vatinoxan hydrochlorides).

courses.title: Double Your Dentistry Online
courses.description: This online module will discuss the Midmark dental study, its results and the "5 Keys to Success" exhibited by the veterinary practices who participated

courses.title: 2026 Veterinary CE at Sea
courses.description: Veterinary professionals can earn up to 12 hours of continuing education while onboard Royal Caribbean's Anthem of the Seas sailing roundtrip from Seattle with stops in Alaska and Canada.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Concurrent Fat & Food Sensitivities
courses.description: This course is focused on the benefits of optimal nutritional management for dogs with adverse food reactions. This includes developing an understanding of adverse food reactions, the role of the microbiome and nutrition, and how the veterinarian healthcare team can work with the pet parent to address adverse food reactions with nutritional management.

courses.title: Heartworm Prevention: Closing the Gap with Spectrum of Care
courses.description: In the session, we'll review the medical knowledge needed in order to effectively communicate about heartworm disease, including lifecycle, preventive options, and treatment options. Then we'll discuss increasing efficacy of heartworm prevention compliance. We'll present common barriers to preventive compliance, through case-based scenarios, and provide dialog and facts to help guide veterinary staff in their communications with clients and achieve better compliance.

courses.title: COMPREHENSIVE BOVINE EMBRYO TRANSFER TRAINING COURSE (1484-39132)
courses.description: The 5-day Comprehensive Embryo Transfer Training Course teaches the student: superovulation techniques, estrous synchronization methods, collection, recognition, manipulation, classification, freezing, thawing and transfer of bovine embryos.
courses.location: International Embryo Technology School Training Facility

courses.title: An update on managing common feline problems in practice
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage the feline patient who are presented to their clinic with a variety of clinical problems. The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: The Weight They Carry Screening and Panel
courses.description: According to the CDC, those in veterinary medicine are more than twice as likely to die by suicide than the general population. The veterinary industry is currently experiencing a nationwide mental health crisis. Overworked and understaffed, veterinary workers often find themselves struggling with long hours. The national shortage of veterinarians and technicians caused by the pandemic exacerbated the situation, leading to chronic stress and burnout. Although as Kathy and other veterinarians we interviewed mentioned, it really the difficult conversations with owners about their beloved pets that take the most toll on them. Together with owners they often have to make heartbreaking decisions due to financial constraints and decide when to take a life. Meanwhile, very few veterinarians have spoken openly about the impact on their mental health due to lack of awareness and longstanding stigma.

courses.title: Chronic Small Intestinal Diarrhea: Cat versus Dog
courses.description:
As veterinarians we see dogs and cats with diarrhea on a daily basis. In many cases it is due to harmless infections, food changes etc and will resolve quickly without need for intensive further investigations or treatment. However, when the diarrhea is persistently present for more than 3 weeks it has become chronic and it is advised to pursue further diagnostics and possible trial treatments to figure out what the underlying cause of the diarrhea is.
In this lecture we will present 2 clinical cases, one of a dog and one of a cat with chronic diarrhea and we will focus on some important differences that exist between dogs and cats when it comes to chronic small intestinal diseases

courses.title: Advanced Global FAST Point of Care Ultrasound course with ultrasound guided procedures lab and scanning session
courses.description: The course covers AFAST and its image acquisition, its target-organ approach for obvious soft tissue abnormalities, and its abdominal fluid scoring system with case-based applications; TFAST and its image acquisition, its echocardiography views, its use for the accurate diagnosis of pleural and pericardial effusion and pneumothorax, its target-organ approach of the heart and pleural space for obvious soft-tissue abnormalities; and Vet BLUE and its image acquisition, its regional, pattern-based approach integrating its B-line scoring system, and 6 lung ultrasound signs. The course includes 2 days: On Day 1, there are 5 hours of lecture and 3 hours of dry lab covering Fundamentals of Imaging, Knobology, and Ultrasound Guided Procedures. On Day 2, there are 4 hours of lectures and 4 hours of a scanning session covering image acquisition for (AFAST, TFAST, and Vet BLUE).

courses.title: Incident Debriefing Training for Mental Well-Being: Supporting Teams in Exotic and Zoo Environments
courses.description: This webinar aims to equip staff and volunteers in the Exotic Animal Industry (EAI) with tools to process difficult or traumatic incidents (e.g., animal death, escape, injury, public event), to support each others' mental health after critical events, and to reinforce a culture of safety, compassion, and accountability.

courses.title: BioMedtrix THR Skills Workshop: Refining Technique to Reduce Complications
courses.description:
The THR Skills Workshop is intended for surgeons who have an established caseload in BioMedtrix THR, or who have matriculated through the BioMedtrix Mentorship Program.
The goal of this two-day workshop is to present impactful refinements of the THR technique, particularly related to cementless (BFX) implants. In the classroom, there will be a heavy emphasis on case review and delegates will be invited to submit challenging or complicated cases for discussion.
Seminars will be reinforced by demonstration and rehearsal of surgical techniques in a wet lab.

courses.title: Fresh Feeding Basics for Dogs
courses.description: Course Name: Fresh Feeding Basics for Dogs. This one-hour webinar will cover the basics of why and how to feed real fresh food to dogs. Complete transitioning to a fresh food diet or using fresh food as kibble toppers will be covered. Topics will include reasons to switch or add fresh food, fresh feeding models, an introduction to each recommended component, tips on sourcing whole food ingredients, and how to use food supplements for specific diseases.

courses.title: Advanced Oral Techniques for the Horse
courses.description: The Advanced Oral Techniques for the Horse course is designed for a practitioner at any career level. This course will contain the vital information needed to successfully perform equine dentistry. It will cover pertinent anatomy of the teeth and oral cavity, regional anesthesia, radiography, sinus anatomy and straightforward extractions of the incisors.

courses.title: HMR LAB #1: ESSENTIAL EXERCISES FOR MOVING DOGS FROM PLACE TO PLACE (22-35462)
courses.description: Are you uncomfortable handling large, hyperactive, or seemingly aggressive dogs? Did you know that if you're unaware of how the dog perceives every interaction, you could be giving unclear or conflicting cues which can cause him to become confused, fearful, and even aggressive? Learn the Low Stress Handling techniques that will allow you to provide clear direction and hence have good control to improve both your confidence in handling and the dog's confidence in you.

courses.title: Patient Safety: Checklists, Yes! But So Much More (ANES202)
courses.description: This presentation explores the concept of safety culture within veterinary healthcare organizations, focusing on its evolution and importance in reducing medical errors. It examines various strategies for improving safety, including the use of checklists and standardized procedures, with a focus on communication and teamwork.

courses.title: PATELLAR LUXATION PART 4: SOFT TISSUE TENSION BALANCING, SURGICAL INSTRUMENTATION, AND POSTOPERATIVE (195-41364)
courses.description: Attendees will enjoy high resolution video footage from Dr. Palmer's operating room as they learn about capsular release, quadriceps release, and imbrication surgical techniques. You will then benefit from Dr. P's discussion of 'tools of the trade' that are useful in each component of patellar luxation corrective surgery. Finally, Dr. P (aka 'the Patella Fella') will provide attendees with a lively discussion of the goals and "how to" techniques of postoperative care and lifelong joint support following patellar luxation surgery.

courses.title: Feline Obesity (TECH444)
courses.description: In this non-interactive course, we will discuss the diagnostics, management, and treatments used in feline obesity patients. Our guest case will be Gimli, an obese M/N DSH. Key Nutritional Factors, disease, and nutritional management including client communication and follow up will complete the course.

courses.title: Seizures: Medical management strategies
courses.description: Presented by Dr. Elizabeth Meiman, a board-certified Neurologist, this is a basic review of seizure medications & management for Veterinary professionals. This is part one of a two-part series that contains practical medication strategies and sets a foundation for the second lecture. Includes a review of common anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs)

courses.title: PATELLAR LUXATION PART 3: TROCHLEOPLASTY AND TIBIAL CREST TRANSPOSITION (195-41363)
courses.description: In this module, you will learn how to determine if your patient requires a trochleoplasty and how to perform abrasion, wedge, block and trochlear chondroplasty techniques. Liberal use of video demonstration will provide the attendee with great insight in how to effectively perform wedge and block trochleoplasty techniques including some tips that you won't find in the textbooks! Next you will learn how to determine if your patient requires a tibial crest transposition before learning new surgical techniques such as the "temporary door stopper needle" that simplify the procedure for the novice (and 'not-so-novice') surgeon.

courses.title: CAM- Canine Arthritis Management Practitioner
courses.description: CAM Veterinary Practitioner is a comprehensive overview of canine osteoarthritis (OA) and its evidence-based management. Despite being classed as a welfare concern and recognized as one of the leading causes of elective euthanasia, OA is an often overlooked and poorly managed disease. This course will provide the veterinary professional with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to successfully manage OA in their patients. Through case-based learning, the attendee will be given an in-depth look at the identification, diagnosis, and multimodal management of the disease, as well as palliative/end of life care considerations. Emphasis is placed on following an evidence-based multimodal approach to management, with consideration of the biopsychosocial care model and focus on improving client compliance through enhanced communication and owner education. The course is designed to allow the veterinarian or veterinary technician to immediately incorporate their new understanding into their professional role.

courses.title: Navigating the World of Pet Supplements: Evidence, Safety, and Recommendations
courses.description: This course provides veterinarians and veterinary technicians with evidence-based guidance on pet supplement regulation, quality assessment, and clinical recommendations. The presentation addresses the unclear regulatory landscape involved with supplement manufacturing, production, and marketing. Veterinarians will learn to identify high-quality supplements through label evaluation, third-party testing indicators, and manufacturing standards while recognizing regulatory and marketing red flags. The course covers common supplement categories including skin and coat support, gastrointestinal health, allergy and immune support, hip and joint products, and multivitamins, with emphasis on evidence-supported ingredients and appropriate dosing. Trending ingredients are examined such as algae oil, fibers, biotics, CBD, and herbs, with critical review of peer-reviewed evidence, contraindications, and clinical applications. A clinical framework guides supplement selection based on therapeutic goals, patient safety, drug interactions, and realistic expectations for outcomes.

courses.title: CCAT I: Introduction to Companion Animal Rehabilitation Therapy
courses.description:
The CCAT I course provides an up-to-date overview for the field of companion animal rehabilitation. Similarities and differences between human and animal rehabilitation will be discussed. And a review of the regulatory issues involved in this field of practice from the perspective of both physical therapists and veterinarians will be covered. The principles of veterinary sports medicine will also be included in the CCAT I course, as well as the role of team members.
An overview of basic comparative anatomy will be reviewed, as well as commonly seen orthopedic and neurological conditions. Collaboration between the veterinary and physical therapy professions will be emphasized to enhance the learning experience. Patient, orthopedic, and neurologic evaluations are also covered.
How to get started in the field of animal rehabilitation and protocol development will be reviewed, and also the importance of a team approach to animal rehabilitation.

courses.title: The Technology of Shockwave Therapy
courses.description: Course Summary This course will provide attendees with: 1) A basic understanding of the various applications and techniques for delivering therapeutic shockwave treatments 2) A review of the indications and contraindications for use for Shockwave Therapy 3) An introduction and review of the use of the PiezoWave Vet shockwave system 4) An overview of the piezoelectric technology used in the PiezoWave2 shockwave device 5) A review of conditions treated with Shockwave Therapy and specific positioning of the device and patients Course Objectives Upon completion of the course, attendees should have a basic understanding of : 1) The application and rationale for the use of Shockwave Therapy in Veterinary Medicine 2) The various conditions treated with therapeutic shockwave 3) Review of proper treatment protocols for indicated conditions and pre and post treatment approaches

courses.title: Understanding Medical Conditions and Pain
courses.description: Although animal trainers can typically recognize the external signs of an animal in serious pain or distress, they are not necessarily aware of what's going on inside the animal's body and how it can affect their behavior. This module will discuss common conditions as well as take an in-depth look at pain management strategies and the effects of pain and stress on an animal.

courses.title: Foster Care and the Human-Animal Bond (OnDemand)
courses.description: It is commonplace among those who provide foster care for animals to have a recurring conversation with those who do not. Upon hearing that one is an animal foster parent a frequent response is, Oh, I could never do that. I would not be able to give the animal up. But this is precisely what those caring for animal fosters are called to do. The ability of animal shelters and rescues to provide critical care through foster homes depends on volunteers who willingly and temporarily take animals into their homes and lives. Studies of foster volunteers has indicated that they find taking care of animals with medical, and particularly behavioral, issue to be stressful. And volunteers that do not feel that their shelter is providing them sufficient emotional support are more likely to think about quitting. Given these two realities it becomes important for shelter staff to understand the emotional aspects of providing foster care and to identify ways to better support volunteers so that they are satisfied and more likely to continue to provide this service.

courses.title: Making the World a Better Place for Horses: Awareness of the Ridden Horse Pain Ethogram and how to apply it
courses.description: Understanding unwanted behavior in horses can reduce the risk of coercive and punishment based training. Dr. Dyson discusses how behavior is communication and should not be interpreted as naughty. Pain can compromise performance, trainability, rider safety and confidence. Often horses try to conceal musculoskeletal pain by gait modifications. Using the validated Ridden Horse Pain Ethogram (otherwise known as the Ridden Horse Performance Checklist) can assist veterinary professionals in their evaluation of equines. Its use in the real world by owners, equine professionals from all disciplines and veterinarians will be reviewed.

courses.title: Chronic Coughing in Dogs (DRIP121)
courses.description: This course focuses on relevant pathophysiology and diagnostic testing regarding chronic coughing in dogs and discusses potential therapies.

courses.title: Foundations of Surgical Exodontia: Anatomy, Sectioning, and Flap Design
courses.description:
This 3-hour continuing education course focuses on the fundamental principles of surgical tooth extraction in veterinary patients. This course provides a comprehensive, clinically focused approach to foundational surgical principles in veterinary dentistry. Emphasis is placed on understanding oral anatomy, alveolar bone characteristics, and regional blood supply, and how these factors influence extraction technique and healing outcomes. Participants will develop a strong understanding of extraction socket biology, atraumatic technique, and the role of surgical decision-making in preventing complications.
The course further explores tooth sectioning principles, including indications, biomechanics, and execution, followed by an in-depth review of mucoperiosteal flap design and instrumentation. Through practical instruction and clinical integration, attendees will gain the knowledge necessary to perform extractions more efficiently, safely, and predictably.

courses.title: Ask Me Anything: Hypoadrenocorticism in Dogs With Dr. Daniel Langlois
courses.description: In this "Ask Me Anything"-style webinar, Dr. Daniel Langlois will provide an overview of canine hypoadrenocorticism, review the pathophysiology of adrenal insufficiency, identify the most effective diagnostic screening and confirmatory tests, and outline long-term management strategies.

courses.title: Tales from the Crit: Interactive Hematology Case Studies with the Laboratory Retrievers (Module 2)
courses.description: The Laboratory Retrievers - Purdue continuing education (CE) program is an online learning experience for veterinary professionals, created by the Laboratory Retrievers LLC and Purdue University College of Veterinary Medicine. These highly interactive, case-based modules help veterinarians and technicians confidently interpret CBC data, analyze cytograms and recognize key blood film cell morphology in minutes.

courses.title: Seizures, Solutions, & the Human-Animal Bond With Dr. Platt
courses.description: Seizures are one of the most emotionally challenging presentations in small animal practice, often leaving veterinarians navigating both urgent medical decisions and distressed owners. In this episode, Dr. Simon Platt joins Dr. Beth to discuss how to approach first-time seizure cases, differentiate idiopathic epilepsy from cases requiring advanced diagnostics, and better support the client experience. Plus, discover where once-daily potassium bromide can fit into long-term seizure control and treatment adherence, and find out how you can earn CE for listening to this podcast!

courses.title: EXTRACAPSULAR (EXCAP) LATERAL FABELLO-TIBIAL SUTURE STABILIZATION OF THE STIFLE: WET LAB (195-41366)
courses.description: This hands-on workshop is one part of a series of programs designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn/refine the extracapsular (ExCap) lateral fabello-tibial suture stabilization technique and to understand the major advantages of PowerX Crimping System. Participants will perform the ExCap suture stabilization technique on canine cadavers under faculty supervision using a step-by-step high-resolution video demonstration. This laboratory will include arthrotomy for stifle exploration, removal of the CrCL remnants, inspection of the medial meniscus, proper placement of the ExCap suture and use of a precise crimping system and critique of your repair.

courses.title: Acute Kidney Injury - Special focus on Leptospirosis (DRIP126)
courses.description:
This course focuses on relevant pathophysiology and diagnostic testing regarding Acute Kidney Injury and discusses potential therapies.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 61 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Peek Before You Pick: How to Select a Dog Trainer
courses.description: Have you ever wondered how to select a dog trainer to whom you are comfortable sending your clients? If so, you are not alone in the minefield of alphabet soup and overpromised results. In this talk, we review learning theory and the responsibilities that veterinary professionals have when referring their clients for training and behavior modification for their dogs. With real-life examples, we will go over how to best identify trainers that utilize humane and scientifically-sound methods, along with how to identify misleading verbiage that some trainers use in order to help you best support your patients.

courses.title: Veterinary Abdominal Ultrasound Training Camp
courses.description: This hands-on, small-group veterinary abdominal ultrasound training program is designed for veterinarians and veterinary technicians of all skill levels, from beginners to advanced practitioners. Participants will gain practical experience performing diagnostic-quality abdominal ultrasounds using a structured, protocol-based approach. Over three immersive days, attendees will master core organ imaging, systematic scanning workflows, and advanced techniques for the liver, pancreas, adrenal glands, and gastrointestinal tract. The program includes interactive lectures, live-patient scanning labs, and 30 days of personalized feedback through mentored teleradiology, ensuring participants leave with confidence, improved efficiency, and skills that translate directly to clinical practice. This course emphasizes hands-on learning, real-world applications, and long-term clinical success.
courses.location: COVE - The Center of Veterinary Excellence

courses.title: Monoclonal Antibodies
courses.description:
Monoclonal antibodies are not our grandparents drugs. Monoclonal antibodies (mAb) offer discreet, directed therapeutic interventions for a variety of diseases. Target antigens range from infections organisms to cellular structures to mediators of inflammation. The characteristics of mAb favor general safety and efficacy. Their large molecular size removes many of the risks for adversity that characterize small drug molecules, with the most likely side effects reflecting allergies. However, as large proteins, many of the principles of pharmacology that we learned do not apply , at least in the way we were taught.
Currently, six monoclonal antibodies are approved for use in animals in the United States. These include mAb that target parvovirus, an immune checkpoint cancer protein immune checkpoints (gilvmetmab) and mAb that target inflammatory mediators. These include lokivetmab, which targets IL-31 and the antinerve growth factor drugs frunevetmab (cats) and bedinvetmab (dogs).

courses.title: LafeberVet Forbes-Ozawa Spring 2025 Non-Interactive Program
courses.description: The Spring 2025 Non-Interactive Program consists of two new webinar recordings: "Antimicrobial Stewardship in Exotic Animal Medicine" by Neil Forbes, BVetMed DECZM FRCVS and "Hazardous Habitats: Protecting Exotics From Everyday Toxins" by Sarah Ozawa, DVM, DACZM. These recordings will be based on RACE-approved live events (program #1284824).

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Common Misconceptions in Clinical Toxicology
courses.description: In this webinar, we will discuss common misconceptions in clinical toxicology. We will discuss in detail different myths related to toxins themselves, as well as to the management of toxin ingestions. Lastly, recent updates to best practice treatment recommendations will be reviewed.

courses.title: Cytology After Dark
courses.description: In this webinar, discover the impact of point-of-care cytology and hematology techniques in the management of sick patients. The case-based presentation will also explore how to utilize cytology to make clinical decisions regarding surgical intervention and how to identify infectious agents, along with how a well-prepared blood smear can impact achieving a diagnosis.

courses.title: From Test to Treatment: How Cytology Screening Can Improve Access to Care for Patients
courses.description: Delve into the revolutionary impact of AI-driven cytology in veterinary diagnostics. This course will guide you through the process of sample preparation and demonstrate how integrating AI insights with specialist expertise can overcome barriers and improve access to cytology. Drs. Mollyann Holland and Cory Penn will discuss the Vetscan Imagyst system, focusing on the AI Masses indication, which helps identify cells suggestive of cancer quickly and accurately1,2 within a clinical setting and supports veterinarians in making timely and informed treatment decisions, improving care for patients that might otherwise face barriers to critical diagnostic services.

courses.title: Ask Me Anything: Feline Infectious Peritonitis with Dr. Matthew Kornya
courses.description: In this dynamic "Ask Me Anything"-style webinar powered by Standards of Care, one of the industry's top experts in feline medicine will discuss the diagnosis and treatment of feline infectious peritonitis (FIP). Dr. Matthew Kornya will review current and emerging diagnostic tools for FIP, explore the groundbreaking antiviral therapies that have transformed treatment (including GS-441524 and remdesivir), and provide practical guidance on how to help clients legally access these treatments and manage costs.

courses.title: PiezoWave2 Shockwave Therapy Clinical Applications in Small Animal Rehab
courses.description: This course will provide attendees with: 1) A basic understanding of the various applications and techniques for delivering therapeutic shockwave treatments 2) A review of the indications and contraindications for use for Shockwave Therapy 3) An introduction and review of the use of the PiezoWave Vet shockwave system 4) An overview of the piezoelectric technology used in the PiezoWave2 shockwave device 5) A review of conditions treated with Shockwave Therapy and specific positioning of the device and patients Course Objectives Upon completion of the course, attendees should have a basic understanding of : 1) The application and rationale for the use of Shockwave Therapy in Veterinary Medicine 2) The various conditions treated with therapeutic shockwave 3) Review of proper treatment protocols for indicated conditions and pre and post treatment approaches.

courses.title: Traumatic Brain Injury and Spinal Fractures (DRIP150)
courses.description: This course focuses on the typical presentation, differential diagnosis, treatments and prognosis of traumatic brain injury and spinal fractures.

courses.title: Intermediate TPLO and Meniscal Management Online Course
courses.description: Intermediate TPLO and Meniscal Management Online Course reviews the anatomy, function, and pathology of the menisci, along with current diagnostic and treatment approaches for meniscal injury. Additional topics include TPLO modifications for quadriceps alignment, adjunctive techniques for medial patellar luxation, and the integration of extracapsular suture stabilization using the OrthoSta system.

courses.title: Veterinarians are the heart: Your role in addressing animal cruelty in your community
courses.description: Veterinary teams are uniquely positioned to identify, report, and address cases of animal cruelty and their involvement is vital for the well-being of animals and society. With a responsibility underscored by the veterinarian's oath to protect the welfare of animals, the veterinary profession must turn its attention to proactively gaining the skills and training required to fulfill that promise. This presentation will introduce attendees to the important ways the veterinary team may become aware of and assist in animal cruelty cases and prevent animal suffering. With an emphasis on measures that can be implemented in private practice, we will address the concerns and answer the questions many veterinarians raise when considering their participation in animal cruelty investigations and empower them to be more effective advocates for animal welfare, active participants in recognizing and reporting cruelty, and valuable contributors to the broader effort to combat animal neglect and abuse in their community. The knowledge of: What to do? What to document? What to report? and Why? allows you to go forward and confidently pursue justice on behalf of mistreated animals. We will cover the basics of animal cruelty law, how to report concerns to law enforcement, and will provide practical, practice-ready information to prepare the team to participate in this important work. Case examples are used to illustrate the content and learning objectives.

courses.title: Capnography (ANES204)
courses.description: This course will give attendees a detailed guide to capnography. The lecture reviews the physiology of CO2, rationale for clinical monitoring CO2, recognition and treatment of common aberrations in CO2. Multiple case examples are used to illustrate the value of end-tidal CO2 monitoring. Also included are several Frequently Asked Questions. The goal of this lecture is to inspire implementation of capnography, enhance application and understanding of this incredibly important monitoring tool for elevating anesthesia safety.

courses.provider: CENTER FOR FOOD SECURITY AND PUBLIC HEALTH COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE IOWA S
courses.title: Cleaning and Disinfection in Animal Settings (Basic Course)
courses.description:
Cleaning and disinfection- often referred to as C&D- is an essential process for the prevention of disease in animal settings. Destroying microorganisms in the environment and on surfaces reduces exposure risks and the spread of disease, and protects animal and human health. Understanding how to properly conduct C&D procedures helps to obtain optimal results.
This is a basic course that overviews key principles of cleaning and disinfection. It will explain the steps for the basic C&D process, tips when performing C&D procedures, and factors that can affect disinfection success. Safety considerations during C&D efforts will also be discussed.

courses.title: Intro to Minimally Invasive Surgery in Small Animals
courses.description: You know Halsted's surgical principles, but how do they vary when it comes to minimally invasive surgery? In this webinar, learn the indications, patient benefits, and equipment needed for invasive procedures in small animals. Plus, learn when to convert to an open procedure.

courses.title: Hands-Free Radiology: Safer, Calmer Imaging for Pets and Teams
courses.description: Hands-free radiology is more than a positioning technique -- it is a mindset shift. In this Fear Free--aligned webinar, participants will learn how reducing manual restraint improves patient emotional wellbeing, decreases occupational radiation exposure, and enhances diagnostic quality. Through practical demonstrations and real-world discussion, attendees will leave with clear, achievable strategies to create safer, calmer imaging experiences for pets and veterinary teams.

courses.title: IVUSS 2025 Annual Meeting - On Demand
courses.description: The annual conference of the International Veterinary Ultrasound Society. The goals of the lectures at this conference are to improve the knowledge base, skills, and diagnostic ability of small animal sonographers in the fields of abdominal sonography and echocardiography.

courses.title: Fear Free Injections for Equine Patients
courses.description: In this course, we will be building on the subjects discussed in the Fear Free Veterinary Certification Program for Equines, and we will delve into specific, proactive, learning-theory based techniques to help our equine patients experience Fear Free injection procedures. Multiple options for techniques will be discussed in detail, to allow you to thoughtfully match the horse's FAS level and history to an appropriate technique.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Mushroom Mystique- Which ones are magic and which ones are tragic
courses.description: This course covers recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of toxic exposures in cats and dogs to mushrooms. While there are too many mushrooms species to cover them all, this presentation will discuss the main categories of toxic mushrooms that can be found in the United States and Canada. This presentation will cover diagnosis and treatment of different types of toxic mushrooms, including tips on how to get mushrooms identified, as well as how to treat unknown mushroom exposures. Come join us for a virtual foray into the wonderful world of fungi!

courses.title: Practical Fish Radiography (EXOT215)
courses.description: This course is designed to give the veterinarian a practical and comprehensive understanding of the techniques used in fish radiography and an approach to interpreting fish radiographs. Topics will include fish anatomy, and the preparation, technique and positioning required to achieve good diagnostic images. Although mainly based on commonly kept pet species such as koi and goldfish, the techniques can be applied to any fish species.
