Examples of the most common uses of radiography in fish will be illustrated and include abnormal buoyancy and swimming behaviour, body deformity due to abdominal swelling and skeletal lesions, and foreign bodies. In many cases, the radiographic features will be compared to the gross findings at necropsy. Advice on improving image quality for posting on VIN will be offered and illustrated by previous examples from the Aquatic Animal Medicine board.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Toxins That Keep Toxicologists Up At Night
courses.description: This course will cover agents that cause more severe poisonings in companion animals. Agents of concern include those that are fast acting, cause significant or life-threatening clinical signs, or are complicated to manage. Agents discussed will include ethylene glycol, baclofen, cholecalciferol, 5-fluoruracil, 5-HTP, and amlodipine. Mechanisms of toxicity, clinical signs, diagnosis, and treatment will be discussed.

courses.title: Updates on the Clinical Applications of Zenalpha
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Kris Kruse-Elliott will review the pharmacology and clinical use of alpha-2 agonists and antagonists in dogs. She will discuss the clinical use of Zenalpha (medetomidine and vatinoxan hydrochlorides injection) in canine sedation, including its advantages, limitations, and unique clinical applications as an alternative option for canine sedation and how it differs from medetomidine or dexmedetomidine alone. Dr. Kruse-Elliott will also share practical guidance for selecting sedation protocols and establishing parameters for safe sedation regardless of drug choice.

courses.title: Do You Know JAK? How Janus Kinase Inhibitors Have Been Game-Changers in the Treatment of Canine Atopic Dermatitis
courses.description: There are a multitude of Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor medications in human medicine, and with these types of medications currently playing the biggest role in the treatment of canine atopic dermatitis, more will be on the way in veterinary medicine. As this drug class increases, it is important to understand how they really work and what they can and cannot do. This webinar will explore the clinical uses of JAK inhibitors, review what safety regarding this drug class looks like, and discuss how to differentiate the available options.

courses.title: Potential Hazards of Surgical Smoke
courses.description: During surgical procedures that involve a laser or electrosurgical or ultrasonic unit, the thermal destruction of tissue creates a smoke byproduct. Research has confirmed that this smoke plume can contain toxins.

courses.title: Social Behavior and Implications for Bonded Pairs in Group Housed Shelter Cats
courses.description: Little is known about the social behavior of cats living in group housing at shelters. In a series of studies, we recorded all the social behavior occurring between cats living in group housing and compared cats who were introduced at the shelter versus those who were surrendered together. We then followed up by specifically examining social behavior between cats who were labeled as bonded pairs or adopted together. Cats who were labeled as bonded pairs had a longer time to adoption, but the relationship between this designation and social behavior was weak. Recommendations will be provided for identifying bonded pairs.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: Novel Oncology Therapeutics: Targeting Hope - On Demand
courses.description:
Immunotherapies and personalized medicine offerings are rapidly becoming more widely available to the field of veterinary oncology. Remaining current on these newly available therapies can be challenging particularly when clinical use may outpace systematic reporting of efficacy and toxicity.
In this on-demand course, panelists will discuss available data supporting clinical application of immunotherapies, targeted therapies, and combination therapies that are currently available or on the horizon for veterinary cancer patients. Successes, potential opportunities, and challenges of clinical integration of these therapies will be discussed in depth with significant opportunity for open Q&A

courses.title: Webinar Series - Elevate Your Anesthetic Practice with Dr. Khursheed Mama
courses.description:
Keeping the Calm: Optimizing Sedation Protocols
Rapid advances in pharmacology have put the days of holding frightened or struggling patients down for nail trims, imaging, and other procedures firmly in the past. Wading through the wide range of affordable options now available can sometimes feel overwhelming. In this interactive session, we will briefly review traditional and adjunctive options then apply them to different clinical scenarios using a case-based approach.
Fact or Fiction? Breed Related Anesthesia Challenges
Patient breed and conformation often take starring roles in anesthetic risk assessment. Valid concerns will be separated from hype using a case-based exploration of breed-related drug sensitivities, anatomic considerations, and the influence of breed-specific co-morbidities on drug selection, supportive care, and monitoring. Time will be reserved at the end of the session to address participant questions.
Keep on Beating: Anesthetic Considerations for Cardiac Cases
Weighing the risk of anesthesia against potential benefits of dental prophylaxis and other anesthetic procedures for patients with heart disease can be tricky! In this session, we will review the pathophysiology and anesthetic implications of common cardiac diseases. Case examples will be used to develop appropriate sedative and anesthetic protocols, discuss hemodynamic support, and tailor monitoring for patients with heart disease and common co-morbidities.

courses.title: Ultrasound-Guided Orthopedic Injection Techniques & Therapies
courses.description: Ultrasonography has become a crucially important diagnostic imaging modality in Equine Orthopedics and most Equine Practitioners nowadays have access to the necessary equipment. A growing number of equine orthopedic specialists have furthermore extended the use of ultrasonography creatively to assist with injection techniques and to facilitate minimally invasive surgery. This 1 1/2 - day practical course has been developed to provide equine and mixed animal practitioners who have experience with ultrasonography, with the theoretical knowledge and the practical skills of performing ultrasound-guided orthopedic injections and ultrasound-assisted surgical techniques, covering all regions of the musculoskeletal apparatus of the horse. Whole horses will be used to recreate a scenario as it might be encountered in live horses. A review of conventional and biologic treatment modalities for orthopedic conditions will round the course up.

courses.title: Hill's Global Symposium 2025 - Strong Science, Long Lives
courses.description:
An insightful online gathering of veterinary professionals as we discover a deeper understanding of the ageing process and support of healthy ageing for dogs and cats in your care. Join online to learn about new research on ageing topics including:
* Innovations for treating Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome
* Evolving strategies for Osteoarthritis Pain Management
* Addressing comorbidities in cats and dogs
* Why hospice and how it is not sad

courses.title: Home alone: An update on canine separation-related disorders
courses.description: Separation-related disorder (SRD) remains one of the most common behavioral problem in the canine population, affecting up to 40% of canine patients in veterinary behavior specialty practices. They can be taxing to the human-animal bond by restricting the guardian's ability to leave the home without their dog. This webinar gives an update on terminology and most recent research on the different types of SRDs. It will also discuss different treatment options, including medications and behavior modification.

courses.title: Senior Dog Veterinary Certification Level 1
courses.description: This multisession program focuses on the fundamentals of senior and geriatric canine care to prepare veterinary practitioners for the unique needs of their elderly canine patients. Topics include the foundation of canine geroscience and aging, prepping for successful visits to the hospital, implementing senior dog care programs to better support their needs and identifying client communication challenges with senior dog parents.

courses.provider: VETERINARY EMERGENCY AND CRITICAL CARE SOCIETY
courses.title: Online VET MDR from IVECCS 2024
courses.description: The Veterinary MDR Program offers practitioners an opportunity to engage in advanced, in-depth study of critical topics relevant to emergency and critical care medicine. This program is designed for both small and large animal residents preparing for specialty certification exams, as well as for practicing veterinarians seeking to strengthen their clinical expertise.Course content includes focused sessions on Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), Pathophysiology of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) and Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic Syndrome (HHS), Essential Equations, Acid-Base Disorders, Cardiac Arrhythmias, Intravenous Fluid Therapy, Lactate Metabolism, and Hepatic Physiology. Upon completion of this program, participants will have gained the knowledge and skills necessary to apply evidence-based principles in the diagnosis and management of critically ill veterinary patients, enhancing their proficiency and confidence in emergency and critical care practice.

courses.title: It's Not You, It's Your Unconscious Programming: Uninstall Hustle & Diet Culture Malware For Sustainable Health & Success
courses.description: This masterclass teaches veterinary professionals how unconscious programming, shaped by cultural pressures like hustle and diet culture, impacts decision-making, well-being, and long-term success. Through a science-based, heart-centered approach, participants will learn how nervous system patterns, mindset, and behavioral conditioning ("malware") influence boundaries, habits, and career satisfaction. The session combines education with practical tools, guided reflections, and nervous-system resets to help attendees identify and "uninstall" unhelpful programming, restore clarity, and create sustainable habits that support personal well-being, leadership, effectiveness, and professional performance. Topics include burnout prevention, stress physiology, behavior change science, mindset, emotional resilience, and strategies for cultivating healthy, sustainable success in veterinary medicine and life.

courses.title: Infusing Sustainability into Veterinary Medical Practice
courses.description: Climate change, biodiversity loss, and other environmental hazards present significant and growing risks to the health of animals worldwide. As trusted messengers within their communities, veterinary teams have great potential to drive a more sustainable and healthier future. This presentation will examine the health impacts affecting animals, outline professional actions that support both mitigation and adaptation efforts, and introduce a practical framework and tools to guide the veterinary team on their sustainability journey.

courses.title: MMPC Learniverse - Community Cat Programs - Legal Considerations with Shelter PALS
courses.description:
This course will define Community Cats, discuss what Community Cat Programs are, explain why Community Cat Programs are needed, and describe how effective Community Cat Programs operate. You'll learn how your shelter can help address the cat overpopulation problem by implementing humane, evidence-based Community Cat Programs.
This course was adapted from a webinar by Bruce Wagman, Lead Counsel for the San Francisco SPCA's Shelter Policy and Legal Services (Shelter PALS) program and hosted by the California Animal Welfare Association (CalAnimals).

courses.title: It's About Time! Mainstreaming Veterinary Herbal Medicine for Healthy Aging
courses.description: Discover the practical role of veterinary herbal medicine in supporting healthy aging in pets. This webinar will highlight how specific herbs can help support physiologic resilience and mitigate the cumulative effects of oxidative stress and inflammation on multiple body systems. Clinically relevant herbs and evidence to support their use will be reviewed, with attention to safety, contraindications, and benefits. Dr. Barbara Fougere and Dr. Nancy Loes will also discuss how herbs can be safely integrated into mainstream veterinary care to enhance health and quality of life in aging patients.

courses.title: The Serum Biochemical Profile (DIAG223)
courses.description: Playing the numbers game: Gaining confidence with interpretation of the serum biochemical profile. This course offers veterinarians a unique perspective on chemistry case interpretation from both an internist and a clinical pathologist teaching in tandem. Participants will gain confidence interpreting abnormalities of the serum biochemical profile using real life cases focusing on dogs and cats.

courses.title: Clarifying Misconceptions About Bone
courses.description: Clarifying Misconceptions About Bone Grafts in Veterinary Practice Online Course is designed to clarify misconceptions about bone grafts by familiarizing learners with primary and secondary bone healing, the properties of bone grafts, bone graft use, and types of bone grafts.

courses.title: Conscious Leadership
courses.description:
These sessions explore the foundations of conscious leadership -- how awareness, energy, and internal patterns shape our experience of stress, communication, and wellbeing.
Participants will learn how compassion fatigue and burnout exist on a continuum, how to identify early warning signs in themselves and others, and how a leader's energy influences psychological safety and team culture.
Through practical tools and reflective insights, attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how to shift from reactivity toward grounded, intentional leadership.
These sessions will also focus on applying conscious leadership to real-world team dynamics. Participants will explore how to create psychological safety, support team members who are struggling, and communicate in ways that build trust rather than defensiveness.
We'll look at the everyday leadership behaviors that cultivate resilience, shared ownership, and a healthy culture. Attendees will leave with actionable strategies for leading with presence, navigating difficult conversations, and empowering teams to thrive -- even in high-pressure environments.

courses.title: Practical Thoracic Radiograph Interpretation for General Practitioners
courses.description: Thoracic radiographs are among the most commonly performed diagnostic imaging studies in small animal practice. This webinar provides a practical framework for evaluating canine and feline thoracic radiographs using principles commonly employed by veterinary radiologists. Participants will review thoracic anatomy, projection-specific considerations, roentgen signs, pulmonary pattern recognition, cardiac assessment, pleural space disease, and common interpretation pitfalls. The session is designed to improve diagnostic confidence and support more consistent clinical decision-making in everyday practice.

courses.title: Cardiology FAQ - Non-Interactive
courses.description: This course reviews some of the most commonly asked cardiology questions from referring veterinarians. Participants should be more comfortable with interpreting heart murmurs in puppies, proBNP interpretation, usage of furosemide, and diet recommendations.

courses.title: Feline Low Stress Handling Algorithm and Towel Wrap (CDPS123)
courses.description: This newly updated course provides veterinary and non-veterinary professionals with critical thinking skills for handling cats using Low Stress Handling methods. The curriculum includes Dr. Sophia Yin's original towel wrap techniques, as well as new and updated information on interpreting feline body language to determine appropriate handling strategies. The course focuses on practical skills and decision-making tools, equipping participants to create positive experiences for cats in their care.

courses.provider: VETERINARY EMERGENCY AND CRITICAL CARE SOCIETY
courses.title: IVECCS 2026 - Savannah, GA
courses.description: IVECCS 2026 will be held in person in Savannah, GA from September 14-17th. Through state-of-the-art education and collaborative learning opportunities, VECCS continues its mission of advancing the standards of care for critically ill and emergent large and small animal patients. The comprehensive scientific program is designed to meet the needs of attendees across all levels of experience and areas of interest. Educational sessions will be tailored for veterinarians, veterinary specialists, veterinary technicians and nurses, veterinary technician specialists, support staff, and practice or hospital managers with an interest in small and large animal emergency, critical care, and specialty medicine. Lecture-based sessions will cover a wide range of topics, including emergency medicine, surgery, critical care, anesthesia and analgesia, gastrointestinal and hepatic disease, renal care, urgent care, ICU management, and leadership development. In addition to lectures, hands-on workshops and small-group forums will provide practical training in advanced monitoring and surgical techniques, RECOVER CPR, VetATLS, POCUS, physical medicine modalities, and communication skills. These interactive educational experiences are designed to equip attendees with both the clinical knowledge and practical skills necessary to enhance patient care and outcomes in veterinary emergency and critical care settings.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: How Multi-Vitamins Can Mean Multi-Problems for pets
courses.description: The presentation will cover the most common human dietary supplements and their potential toxicity to animals, mechanism of action, clinical signs, and treatment plans.

courses.title: Family Paws Education for Fear Free Professionals
courses.description: The goal of this course is to equip veterinary professionals with the knowledge and practical strategies needed to support families with dogs and children, prevent conflict and dog bites, and strengthen the human animal bond through Fear Free and Family Paws principles.

courses.title: Maddies Insights: Benefits of Pair-Housing Dogs on Welfare Measures and Length of Stay - OnDemand
courses.description: Dogs are often housed alone in shelter settings to reduce injury and disease spread. However, social isolation can be a stressor for dogs. Most prior studies have focused on laboratory dogs or shelter dogs that have been kenneled for several months. Thus, those results might not necessarily generalize to shelter dogs, many of which have shorter lengths of stay than those dogs studied to date and might be co-housed soon after intake. We investigated the behavioral and physiological effects of single- or pair-housing shelter dogs, most of which had recently entered the shelter, as well as the impact of pair-housing on length of stay. In this talk, we will review the literature on cohousing dogs, go into detail on our study methods and results, and discuss the benefits of pair-housing dogs, as well as practical considerations for pair-housing dogs.

courses.title: Before Four Weeks: Updated Vaccination Recommendations for Neonatal Puppies and Kittens (On Demand))
courses.description:
Neonatal and juvenile puppies and kittens are uniquely vulnerable to infectious disease, particularly when housed in high-density, high-turnover environments such as animal shelters or foster care systems with suboptimal biosecurity. Historically, core vaccination protocols have recommended delaying vaccine initiation until 4-6 weeks of age due to concerns about maternal antibody interference and immature immune response. However, in high-risk environments, this delay may result in critical gaps in protection during a period of heightened susceptibility.
This session will present an evidence-based rationale for updated recommendations on the early administration of core vaccines in neonates and juveniles exposed to meaningful disease risk. Participants will receive a concise review of the immunological principles governing vaccine response in young animals, followed by an overview of the relevant literature informing the revised protocols. Practical implementation strategies will be discussed for both shelter and non-shelter environments where early exposure to infectious pathogens is a concern.
This webinar is designed to support veterinarians, shelter medicine professionals, and allied animal care providers in tailoring vaccine protocols to match environmental risk-enhancing both individual animal protection and population-level disease control.

courses.title: Amphibians 101 (EXOT902)
courses.description: This course is exactly what it sounds like - amphibians 101, or a beginner's guide to the basics of amphibian medicine. The focus is on frogs, most specifically, pet frogs that might be likely to present in practice - however, the techniques discussed would be appropriate for application to most sick amphibians. The approach to basic husbandry, taking a good history, performing a physical exam, and an introduction to diagnostics, common diseases, and therapy options are included. The hope is to take someone with minimal frog experience to being able to work through a sick frog case with confidence.

courses.title: Tales from the Crit: Interactive Hematology Case Studies with the Laboratory Retrievers (Module 3)
courses.description: The Laboratory Retrievers - Purdue continuing education (CE) program is an online learning experience for veterinary professionals, created by the Laboratory Retrievers LLC and Purdue University College of Veterinary Medicine. These highly interactive, case-based modules help veterinarians and technicians confidently interpret CBC data, analyze cytograms and recognize key blood film cell morphology in minutes.

courses.title: Indications for Extracorporeal Therapy
courses.description: Attendees will learn about the application for extracorporeal therapy in dogs and cats including both dialysis and TPE. We will cover the basic concepts of ECT, renal indications, immunomodulatory indications, toxic/overdose indications as well as cover some case examples.

courses.title: How Client Communication Tools Can Strengthen the Human-Animal Bond
courses.description: In veterinary practice, client communication tools can help ensure that pet owners feel connected to their pets' healthcare journey and are equipped to provide the best care possible. In this webinar, learn how integrating client communication tools into veterinary practice information management systems can improve the bond between clients and their pets by fostering timely care, continuous engagement, and accessible guidance. By enhancing appointment management, nurturing engagement, educating pet owners, facilitating telemedicine, and simplifying financial processes, these tools can help pet owners focus on what matters most: their relationship with their pet.

courses.title: Essentials of Gastrointestinal Diseases By Dr Betty Chow BVM&S, MRCVS, DACVIM
courses.description: Essentials of Gastrointestinal Diseases By Dr Betty Chow BVM&S, MRCVS, DACVIM is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Top OSHA Violations for Animal Health Facilities
courses.description: This 1 hour course is presented by Karson L. Carpenter, President of Compliance Training Partners, and will review top OSHA violations seen over the past year. The course will allow participants to see areas in which they may be vulnerable to citation and fine and provide practical solutions for preventing them. Participants will receive access to a Detailed Compliance Audit App that will allow them to evaluate their facility and formulate a plan for achieving full compliance.

courses.title: Mealtime as Medicine: Using Fresh Food for Clinical Outcomes
courses.description: Nutrition is a powerful yet often underutilized clinical tool, particularly for patients experiencing pain, inflammation, or recovery challenges. This course explores how fresh food diets, when used appropriately, can support healing, comfort, and overall well-being. Learners will gain practical guidance on indications and contraindications, safe transition strategies, and team-based implementation of feeding protocols in real veterinary settings. Grounded in evidence-based nutrition and aligned with Fear Free principles, this course equips veterinary professionals with clear, actionable tools to support patient comfort and clinical outcomes through mealtime decisions.

courses.title: Small Patients, Big Procedures: Weighing Pediatric Spay & Neuter Considerations (On-Demand)
courses.description:
Pediatric spay and neuter surgeries are a cornerstone of population management and animal welfare strategies in both shelter and community practice. Historically, veterinarians were trained to delay sterilization until six months of age, but current evidence supports safe and effective procedures at a much earlier age and lower body weight. Early-age spay/neuter -- commonly performed at 6-16 weeks of age -- has been endorsed by major veterinary organizations, including the Association of Shelter Veterinarians (ASV) and the American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA), and is increasingly utilized in high-quality, high-volume spay/neuter (HQHVSN) programs as well as private practice.
This session will review the current recommendations for pediatric spay/neuter of dogs and cats, including key considerations around surgical candidacy, anesthesia and analgesia, tissue handling, and perioperative care. Presenters will highlight practical adjustments needed for pediatric patients -- such as appropriate fasting protocols, thermoregulation strategies, and multimodal pain management -- and will discuss evidence showing that pediatric patients often experience shorter surgical times, quicker recoveries, and lower complication rates than their adult counterparts.
In addition to clinical techniques, the session will examine the broader implications of pediatric spay/neuter for shelters and access-to-care programs. By reducing length of stay, decreasing disease exposure, and preventing unplanned litters, pediatric sterilization supports organizational capacity for care while advancing population-level welfare outcomes. Presenters will also discuss staff and community considerations, common myths and concerns, and case-based examples illustrating how pediatric spay/neuter can be successfully integrated into both shelter medicine and HQHVSN practice models.

courses.provider: CENTER FOR PUBLIC VETERINARY MEDICINE (CPVM), VAMD COLLEGE OF VET
courses.title: Virtual Veterinary Career Transition Workshop - Industry Focus
courses.description: This veterinary career transition workshop, hosted by the Center for Public Veterinary Medicine with the Virginia-Maryland College of Veterinary Medicine, is designed to help veterinarians understand the breadth of opportunities in veterinary medicine, and how to create a new career path. This online workshop includes information on career opportunities in public veterinary practice, with a particular emphasis on careers in industry. Topics covered also include career and self-assessment, resume building, professional networking, job searching, and other key career transition issues. It is conducted with a format of short lectures, individual and group activities, group discussions, and expert panels. While the program emphasizes career opportunities within industry, it also addresses key aspects of federal, state, and alternative career paths. Invited speakers include federal and state veterinarians, corporate and industry veterinarians, and more.

courses.title: Upper Airway Disorders (DRIP133)
courses.description: This course focuses on upper airway disorders found in modern veterinary practice and the logical way to handle them.

courses.title: Bring Your Ultrasound Back to Life! - Improve Patient Care with Global FAST Point of Care Ultrasound
courses.description: The webinar will cover an introduction to AFAST, abdominal ultrasound format for soft tissue, free fluid, and free air, TFAST, thoracic ultrasound format for pericardial and pleural effusion, and fundamental echocardiography, and Vet BLUE, a lung ultrasound format with a regional, pattern-based approach, a B-line Scoring System for wet lung, and its visual lung language for its easily learned signs of consolidation. These FAST ultrasound formats are reviewed in a case-based, practical, and achievable for the non-radiologist, non-cardiologist practitioner.

courses.title: AFAST Point of Care Ultrasound Online Course
courses.description:
The Updated AFAST Online Course Curriculum: The course covers AFAST and its image acquisition, target organ approach for obvious soft tissue abnormalities, and the abdominal fluid scoring system with case based applications.
Module 01 - History and Overview of FAST
Module 02 - Clinical Applications of AFAST and Its Fluid Scoring System
Module 03 - The Diaphragmatico-Hepatic View - Image Acquisition, Pearls, Pitfalls and Artifacts
Module 04- The Spleen-Renal View - Image Acquisition, Pearls, Pitfalls and Artifacts
Module 05 - The Cysto-Colic View - Image Acquisition, Pearls, Pitfalls and Artifacts
Module 06 - The Small Intestinal- Umbilical View - Image Acquisition, Pearls, Pitfalls and Artifacts
Module 07 - Incidental and Unexpected Case Studies - AFAST and Its Target-Organ Approach
Supplemental Module - How to Do AFAST and Its Target-Organ Approach
Course Objectives
Image Acquisition
Understand the Pitfalls and Artifacts at Each AFAST View
Know How to Calculate the Abdominal Fluid Score
Know How to Use the Abdominal Fluid Scoring System for Decision-Making
Know How to Assess Volume Status
Know How to Diagnose Pericardial and Pleural Effusion during AFAST via the Diaphragatico-Hepatic View
Understand the AFAST Target-Organ Approach and Its Limitations
Apply AFAST and a Fluid Score to Multiple Patients on a Daily Basis
The AFAST Online Course is a self-paced, recorded course, that requires a passing grade of 80% on each Module's Quiz prior to being able to move on to the next Module.

courses.title: Foundational Knowledge of Performing TPLO
courses.description: Tibial Plateau Leveling Osteotomy (TPLO) is used to treat dogs with a ruptured Cranial Cruciate Ligament (CCL). Foundations of Performing TPLO is designed to give background on CCL disease, understand the range of treatment options, acquire foundational knowledge in when, why, and how to offer TPLO, and provide surgeons knowledge in preparation of attending a hands-on workshop.

courses.title: Canine Lab 3: Handling and Restraining Small and Medium-sized Dogs with Skill and Ease
courses.description: People tend to restrain small and medium-sized dogs with force due to their size, which causes them to struggle defensively. The result: procedures take longer and patients become more difficult with each visit. In this lab, you'll learn a variety of holds and be able to identify the directions of movement they control. This will allow you to adapt quickly to the situation and to the dog's response. Patients who otherwise would be difficult to handle will now be calm and cooperative.

courses.title: Triage for Veterinary Technicians (TECH448)
courses.description: Triage is an essential skill for all veterinary technicians and nurses working in emergency, critical care, and general practice settings. This self study course introduces the foundational concepts of veterinary triage, including how to perform a primary survey, identify abnormalities, and apply triage classification systems to prioritize patient care. Students will learn how to put triage concepts into action with practical steps for clinical practice and improved patient outcomes.

courses.title: Gastric Dilatation-Volvulus (GDV)
courses.description: Gastric Dilatation-Volvulus (GDV) is one of the most important medical and surgical emergencies in small animal medicine. It leads to severe hemodynamic decompensation, as well as tissue death and respiratory difficulty. The signs escalate fast and may lead to death in a matter of a few hours, so being able to identify the signs fast is essential for a clinician. The final diagnosis is given by radiography, with the pattern being pathognomonic. This course aims to discuss clinical signs, risk factors, radiographic findings, and treatment options in a dynamic flow, including preview questions, radiographic interpretation exercises, in-depth explanations, and a test to apply what was learned in the course.

courses.title: Practical Approaches to Wound Care and Management for Referring Veterinarians -Non Interactive
courses.description: This course offers a practical overview of wound care and management for small animal patients, covering wound classification, stabilization, lavage, debridement, closure techniques, and bandaging strategies. Emphasis will be placed on the use of drains, appropriate antibiotic selection, and collaborative approaches to optimize healing and patient outcomes.

courses.title: Derm Trifecta: Essential Steps for Managing Small Animal Dermatology (TECH408)
courses.description: Dermatology conditions in our canine and feline patients are very common and many diseases are not curable. Skin conditions can look similar and this session will enable you to recognize the important aspects with obtaining the patient history and learn proper techniques along with helpful hints to perform dermatologic procedures accurately. Dermatology cases can be frustrating for the veterinary team and the owner; we can play a vital role in client education to help improve owner adherence and lead to a more successfully managed patient.

courses.title: Cracking the Code on Lumps & Bumps: Fast, Efficient Diagnosis in Everyday Practice
courses.description: Lumps and bumps are among the most common concerns in general practice, but getting quick, reliable answers is anything but simple. In this webinar, Dr. Natalie Marks is joined by 2 top oncologists, Drs. Craig Clifford and Gillian Dank, for a practical conversation about the most efficient, cost-effective, and conclusive techniques for ruling out benign masses or, alternatively, catching malignancies early. Together, they'll review the most used diagnostic strategies for skin and subcutaneous masses, including where current tools fall short and how to overcome barriers like the limitations of fine-needle aspiration, delays in receiving cytology results, and economic constraints. Attendees will also explore new diagnostic technologies that can help improve speed of receiving results, objectivity, and client communication and the latest updates in the most practical intervention strategies for dermal and subcutaneous cancers.

courses.title: Brumation Non-Interactive
courses.description:
The Brumation Non-Interactive Program consists of one webinar recording Brumation in Turtles and Tortoises by Joanna Hedley BVM&S DZooMed (Reptilian) DECZM (Herpetology) MRCVS.
Brumation is a natural state of dormancy or inactivity that occurs in response to colder temperatures. In the wild, many chelonian species enter brumation as a survival strategy, relying on stored glycogen and fat as metabolic processes slow down. While brumation is a normal physiological process in nature, replicating this process in captivity presents a number of challenges.
Despite limited scientific evidence to guide best practices for brumation in captive chelonians, there is no shortage of strong opinions on the topic. Complicating matters further, brumation-associated health issues are not uncommon in practice, underscoring the need for a clearer understanding of the process to help mitigate risks.
This web-based seminar will examine the numerous factors that influence brumation and outline key considerations when preparing to brumate a chelonian in a controlled environment. First, the chelonian should undergo a comprehensive health assessment to determine the suitability of brumation for this individual. Dr. Hedley will then review critical preparatory steps, including bathing, withdrawal of food, and a gradual reduction of both environmental temperature and photoperiod. Various brumation techniques will be discussed, including outdoor housing, traditional box methods, and refrigerator or chiller methods. Strategies for effective monitoring during brumation, as well as appropriate rewarming protocols, will also be covered.

courses.title: On-Demand: The Portion Prescription: Treating Pet Obesity with Precision and Compassion
courses.description: Pet obesity isn't just a nutrition issue; it's a chronic disease that requires structured, individualized treatment. In this webinar, veterinary professionals will learn how to implement effective weight loss plans using clinical tools like calorie calculations, portion control, and macronutrient tailoring. We'll cover how protein, fat, fiber, and L-carnitine can support lean muscle mass and promote fat loss, as well as how to utilize commercial products to simplify feeding plans. Communication tips and client-friendly visuals will help teams discuss obesity in a non-judgmental manner, support compliance, and debunk myths surrounding "fresh" and "raw" food trends. This is practical, evidence-based medicine for one of today's most common and overlooked medical conditions in dogs and cats.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Beyond Clean & Jerk - Advanced Management of Periodontal Disease
courses.description: Webinar Series - Beyond Clean & Jerk - Advanced Management of Periodontal Disease is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Infectious Disease Control: Implementation & Communication
courses.description: Knowledge without implementation is knowledge underutilized. Implementation itself requires a separate set of skills and accessible resources that will lead to the creation of a formal infection control program, or to refining an existing one. In addition, once the protocols have been determined, they must be communicated to all members of the animal care team as well as to clients. The creation of effective infectious disease control protocols is not the final step. Rather, practices need to set in place a robust and continuing assessment and compliance evaluation process to ensure success, resulting in a safer workplace for team members, clients, and animals. This course will provide the key actionable steps and resources needed to create, assess, refine, and communicate effective infection control protocols to optimize success.

courses.title: Triage, Stabilization and Endpoints of Resuscitation (DRIP143)
courses.description:
This course focuses on triage systems that can be utilized by all practitioners. With practical information to help stabilize your emergency and critical care patient.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 125 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: A Whiter Shade of Pale: What Anemia Means for Patients
courses.description:
This grand-rounds style webinar will approach anemia from a case-based perspective. Explore signs of
regenerative anemia with boarded internist Dr. Adam Gow and boarded clinical pathologist Dr. Corry
Yeuroukis. Discover tips and tricks to optimize blood smears in anemic patients, then hit the rewind
button and explore how a similar clinical presentation reflects nonregenerative anemia.

courses.title: WSAVA Certificate in Professional Development and Personal Wellbeing
courses.description: In the face of an increasingly challenging working environment for companion animal veterinary professionals globally, the WSAVA's Certificate in Professional Development and Personal Wellbeing offers veterinary team members a practical, structured learning experience and an opportunity to build a roadmap for success in both their personal and work lives. Content for the Certificate is delivered via video lectures, delivered by an expert in veterinary professional development. They are supported by case studies, a downloadable workbook, space for reflection and links to further resources. Engagement with the course is assessed by quizzes at the end of each module. The content has been designed to be accessible by those with neurodiversity and is underpinned by the principles of wellbeing and self-care as set out in the WSAVA's Global Guidelines on Professional Wellbeing.

courses.title: Musculoskeletal Ultrasonography (DIAG431)
courses.description: This course is part of an extensive series on continuing education related to the use of ultrasonography in veterinary medicine. The course will focus on utilizing ultrasound imaging for orthopedic and musculoskeletal presentations in practice, and how the use of ultrasound can assist in diagnosis, confirm diagnoses from radiographs, stage surgical interventions, and monitor healing. The course highlights how to position the patient and probe for optimal imaging and demonstrates an understanding of the images by using imposing radiographic images and illustrations for context. Case studies are discussed, offering real-world examples on how to maximize the use of ultrasound units in your practice beyond aspirates and POCUS (Point-of-Care Ultrasound).

courses.title: Mindful Veterinary Practice: Reducing Stress for Teams and Patients
courses.description: Veterinary care is emotionally and physically demanding, and stress can impact both patient welfare and team performance. Mindful Veterinary Practice: Reducing Stress for Teams and Patients gives veterinary professionals practical, in-shift strategies to stay calm, focused, and effective. Through recognizing early signs of stress in animals and people, applying quick mindfulness techniques, and making simple environmental adjustments, learners will discover how their presence, behavior, and surroundings influence patient experiences. This course provides actionable tools that integrate seamlessly into daily workflows, helping to create a more compassionate, low-stress culture for every patient visit.

courses.title: Understanding Patient Safety: Reducing Risk and Harm in Veterinary Practice (PRAC163)
courses.description:
We all want our patients to be safe and to reduce the risk of harm, but what does 'safe' really mean and what contributes towards a positive safety culture within veterinary practice? What have other industries such commercial aviation, healthcare, nuclear power and rail got to do with reliably achieving positive outcomes within your clinics? How do we respond to unexpected outcomes and errors in a way that supports learning and improvement? What does systems thinking mean and why does this matter for your team? What is the relationship between psychology, behaviour science, ergonomics and reducing risk to veterinary patients?
We will explore these questions and many more throughout this course and provide you with the underlying knowledge, supporting science as well as some tangible guidance and tools.

courses.title: LafeberVet June 2025 Non-Interactive Program Doss + Three Courses
courses.description: The June 2025 Non-Interactive Program consists of three teaching modules and 19 webinar recordings. The "Hedgehog Anesthesia & Surgery" webinar recording by Dr. Grayson Doss is new. All other courses are being resubmitted from preexisting programs #1100164, 1083090, and 1094766: Avian Anesthesia: Practical Applications by Jody Nugent-Deal, RVT, VTS (Anesthesia), VTS (Exotic Companion Animal), Chelonian Shell Repair by J. Stoewen DVM, MSW, RSW, PhD, Rabbit Basics Level 2 Teaching Module by Christal Pollock, DVM, DABVP (Avian Practice), Rabbit Nutrition and Critical Care Feeding by Kara Burns, MS, Med, LVT, VTS (Nutrition), Reptile and Amphibian Nutrition by Thomas H. Boyer, DVM, DABVP (Reptile and Amphibian

courses.title: Pet Wellness and Life Stages Nutrition
courses.description: The Pet Wellness & Life Stages Nutrition is designed to provide a fundamental understanding of the nutritional needs of dogs and cats as they move through the various phases of growth, development and aging. This course will provide an overview of the various stages and related nutritional needs of each stage, as well as recommendations to consider when providing pet owners with your nutritional recommendations for the dogs and cats that visit your practice.

courses.title: The Clinical Approach to Seizures (DRIP149)
courses.description: This course focuses on the typical presentation, differential diagnosis, treatments, and prognosis of seizures.

courses.title: Shelter Clinic Management (self-paced course)
courses.description: Austin Pets Alive! has developed a comprehensive medical program that addresses each animal in a way that allows them to conserve resources so they can help as many animals as possible while also ensuring that every animal receives treatment that meets or exceeds their standards of care. This course will teach you to systematize medical treatment and implement lifesaving protocols in your shelter's medical clinic, balancing quality care with the capacity to care for a large volume of animals. This course is authored by Jordana Moerbe, Maddie's Medical Program Director at American Pets Alive!.

courses.title: TIBIAL PLATEAU-LEVELING OSTEOTOMY PART 1: AETIOPATHOGENESIS, CLINICAL EXAMINATION, AND X-RAY (195-36634)
courses.description: This online lecture focuses on the biomechanics of the cruciate ligament deficient stifle and tibial plateau levelling osteotomy, TPLO. The lecture includes a discussion regarding clinical presentation, stifle palpation, instability tests and stifle radiography.

courses.title: Behavioral Management Strategies: Psychotropic Medications, Training, and Beyond
courses.description:
In this video course, Veterinary Behaviorist, Dr. Amy Pike, will help us understand the cues our patients are giving us through their body language and behavior. Through videos and discussion, we'll learn to differentiate medical, environmental, and psychological causes of unwanted behaviors.
In session one, we'll learn "the six M's" of behavior care. Through addressing each "M" systematically, avoid overlooking or misdiagnosing the problem. In session two, hear communication strategies to help clients understand why referral to a veterinary behaviorist is important. Communication scripts and examples will be provided. Also review the SOCRATES method of history taking and learn how to apply it to behavior care. In session three, review all the nutraceutical and pharmaceutical therapeutic options available for treatment of behavioral disorders. Understand the mechanisms of action, indications for use, risks, drug interactions, and indications of efficacy.

courses.title: Senior and Geriatric Dog Society Veterinary Certification Level 2
courses.description: This multisession program focuses on the foundations of senior and geriatric canine medicine within specialized topics including anesthesia, healthy senior dog nutrition, cognitive dysfunction, ocular disease, chronic pain, dentistry and end of life. Establishing foundations in these areas of senior dog medicine will enhance the ability of veterinary practitioners in meeting the unique needs of their elderly canine patients.

courses.title: COMPREHENSIVE BOVINE EMBRYO TRANSFER TRAINING COURSE (1484-39132)
courses.description: The 5-day Comprehensive Embryo Transfer Training Course teaches the student: superovulation techniques, estrous synchronization methods, collection, recognition, manipulation, classification, freezing, thawing and transfer of bovine embryos.
courses.location: International Embryo Technology School Training Facility

courses.title: Beyond Animal Shelter Walls: Using Community Data to Understand Intake Diversion of Owner Surrendered Animals (OnDemand)
courses.description: How do we reduce relinquishment to animal shelters? In the U.S. and Canada, approximately 25-30% of animals that enter shelters are surrendered by owners. However, despite many shelters and rescues providing various pet support services for the past few decades, there has been little demonstratable reduction in owner surrendered animals. Currently, many animal shelters use data collected at intake, such as surrender reasons, to create programs that aim to support pet owners to keep their pets. This presentation will outline research into animal shelters, pet owning communities, self-rehoming platforms, and pet owners to demonstrate the complex system of pet surrender. By the end of this presentation, participants will learn how community data can complement animal shelter data to help divert animals from shelters.

courses.title: Emergency Veterinary Care: Making Decisions and Thriving Under Pressure (PRAC164)
courses.description:
Are you thriving...or just surviving? Many of us work in the ER because we thrive in the high-pressure environment created by multiple traumas, dyspneic or septic patients. With multiple time-critical patients at once, we need our stress levels to be low to moderate to perform at our best - but overwhelming stress reduces cognitive function, leading us to survive rather than thrive.
If this sounds familiar, how can you tip yourself, or your team, back to thriving - and why is it important?
A thriving team member has maximum cognitive bandwidth to make appropriate clinical decisions, communicate effectively and be adaptable, which increases patient safety, strengthens client relationships, and improves their own wellbeing.
This course will give you the tools to recognize when and why your cognitive bandwidth decreases, how to recognize it in others, and how to support individuals and teams to widen it again.

courses.title: The Fungus Among Us: Preventing, Diagnosing, and Treating Ringworm (On Demand)
courses.description: In a shelter setting, ringworm can be a significant, yet manageable challenge. New and ongoing research continues to inform our understanding of dermatophytosis (aka ringworm) and improve the management of this infectious disease. In this webinar, we'll hear from veterinarians who have used this research to successfully diagnose and treat many, many cats who were diagnosed with ringworm. They'll share their experiences, learnings, and tips to help you develop a consistent and effective strategy to prevent and manage this disease while ensuring that BOTH the physical and mental well-being of animals and shelter staff are upheld during treatment.

courses.title: Small Animal Programme 2023 part 2
courses.description: This programme includes 17 hours of world-class CPD, delivered by experts in the field. The main objective is to keep veterinarians up to date with the latest insights into small animals. The Programme will outline the typical approach to investigating and managing cases in order to optimise the outcome. Topics covered range from surgery, gastroenterology, ophthalmology, oncology, among others.

courses.title: Byers Hyperadrenocorticism and Hypoadrenocorticism in 2023 Anytime
courses.description: Learners will explore relevant physiology, logical diagnostic investigations, and appropriate therapies for hypoadrenocorticism and hypoadrenocorticism in the fields of emergency/critical care and internal medicine diseases that affect cats and dogs.

courses.title: Impact of Classical Counterconditioning (Quiet Kennel Exercise) on Barking in Shelter Dogs (OnDemand)
courses.description: A major welfare concern in animal shelters is excessive barking from kenneled dogs. This contributes to noise pollution, can cause hearing damage, and has a negative impact on all animals within earshot. This study demonstrated that by implementing a simple classical counterconditioning exercise, consisting of instructing all ward passers-through to toss treats to each dog regardless of behavior exhibited, could change the emotional state of dogs from negative to more positive, thus reducing fear and frustration that often leads to excessive barking. Data analysis showed that implementation of this simple exercise did reduce barking at clinically relevant levels even with a changing shelter population. Additionally, for each percent increase in compliance rate, there was an average decrease of 17.3 dB in the maximum decibel reading. Moreover, an overall positive change in attitude from most dogs towards visitors further showed the positive effects of the study.

courses.title: EQ1200: Equine CranioSacral Therapy - Level 1
courses.description: This 5-day class will train students in the theory, concepts and practice of Craniosacral Therapy as it pertains to the equine population, while giving them the opportunity to integrate this knowledge with the Nervous System and Fascial System. This course is designed to teach participants the skills involved in evaluating and helping neuromusculoskeletal/fascial dysfunction in horses.

courses.title: Importance of Taste in Foods for Pets with Cancer
courses.description: This course will give you an understanding of why complete and balanced nutrition and great taste are needed in foods for cats and dogs and how both can be achieved. You will also develop a greater understanding of the special nutritional needs of cats and dogs living with cancer and why these pets are at an increased risk of malnutrition. You will gain knowledge and confidence in discussing nutritional recommendations with pet parents. You will be able to guide pet parents through implementation of a new feeding program to help avoid the malnutrition and weight loss often seen in cancer patients. Ultimately, this will help you improve quality of life for your cancer patients.

courses.title: Concierge Vet Mastermind
courses.description: The Concierge Vet Mastermind is an advanced professional development program designed specifically for veterinarians running or building house call and concierge practices. Through an exclusive combination of live coaching, in-depth curriculum, peer collaboration, and personalized mentorship, participants gain actionable strategies to elevate business and practice ownership skills, streamline operations, enhance client communication, and scale revenue. Graduates emerge ready to deliver exceptional concierge-level care, backed by a supportive network and proven business frameworks grounded in real-world veterinary experience.

courses.title: Unleashing Progress: Taming Perfectionism in Vet Med (STAF205)
courses.description:
Perfectionism can feel like a strength in veterinary medicine. Our patients rely on us, and our clients trust us. But when "never making a mistake" becomes your personal standard, the pressure can be overwhelming. Over time, perfectionism can drain your energy, increase anxiety, and make it harder to feel satisfied with the work you do.
In this two-part course, we'll explore perfectionism through a personal lens-how it shows up in your daily work, how it impacts your mental and emotional well-being, and how to break free from the constant cycle of "never good enough". You'll gain insights and practical tools to quiet your inner critic, set realistic expectations, and care for yourself while still providing exceptional patient care.

courses.title: Gastroesophageal Reflux: An Under Recognized Source of Pain (DRIP106)
courses.description: Based on new data, the incidence of gastroesophageal reflux is too often under recognized and addressed, especially in canine patients. This course will briefly review the relevant pathophysiology of GERD, and focus on diagnosis, and effective current therapies.

courses.title: Pain Scales in Dogs and Cats for Veterinary Technicians - Weighing the Options (TECH457)
courses.description: Identifying the symptoms of pain in dogs and cats is an important but oftentimes difficult part of a veterinary technician's job. Furthermore, differentiating acute pain signs from fear, anxiety and stress (FAS) can be perplexing to even the most astute observers. We'll explore the pros and cons of a variety of pain scoring tools for both acute and chronic pain. Interpreting body language as it relates to pain versus FAS will also be discussed.

courses.title: Euthanasia Team Support (Online)
courses.description: In this module, we will outline euthanasia-related factors affecting the health and overall well being of the veterinary team. We will focus on standardizing protocols for efficiency and consistency, review team training procedures, and discuss use of the CAETA team training manual. Attention will also be given to help personnel cope with euthanasia-related stress and reduce compassion fatigue.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2026 North American Neuroscience (Brain Camp) Course
courses.description: Preparation lectures to support the learning during Brain Camp. Brain Camp is a week-long immersive experience designed primarily for veterinary neurology and neurosurgery residents and early-career neurologists. This offering is also beneficial for non-specialists looking to develop their foundational neurology expertise. Through interactive lectures, panel discussions, and table-top workshops, participants have the opportunity to strengthen their clinical knowledge base, reasoning, and decision-making in a supportive, high-energy environment. Team-based competitions will reinforce key concepts in a fun, low-stakes format. Social events and networking sessions will bring together generations of neurologists from around the world.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Pediatric and Geriatric Toxicology: Age Matters in Poison Response
courses.description: This 1-hour continuing education course explores the unique toxicological risks facing pediatric and geriatric small animal patients. Participants will examine how age-related physiological differences alter susceptibility to toxin exposure, clinical presentation, and treatment response. The course is designed for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and students seeking to strengthen their approach to toxicology cases in age-specific canine and feline patients. Topics include developmental stage and aging impact clinical signs, diagnostic interpretation, treatment selection, and prognosis in toxicology cases. Practical case-based examples will highlight adjustments in diagnostic evaluation, medication use, fluid therapy, and supportive care for young and elderly patients

courses.title: Managing Mitral Valve Disease in General Practice
courses.description: This webinar will provide an overview of myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD). Common patient signalment and history, physical examination findings, and diagnostic and treatment recommendations for each stage of disease according to the ACVIM guidelines will be discussed.

courses.title: FOCUS ON ENDOCRINE ( A 3 LECTURE SERIES)
courses.description:
Lecture 1: Keep Calm and Treat Addison's: A Guide to Canine Hypoadrenocorticism
SUMMARY: This presentation will cover the varied clinical signs of Addison's, its diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring - hopefully preventing you from stressing out over Addison's.
Lecture 2: Unraveling Cushings: Correctly Identifying Canine Hyperadrenocorticism
SUMMARY:
While canine hyperadrenocorticism is a more common diagnosis than hypoadrenocorticism, it is not without its pitfalls in diagnosis. Learn about the different presentations of the disease and how to avoid erroneous diagnosis.
Lecture 3: The Diagnostic Puzzle of Canine Hypothyroidism: Getting It Right
LECTURE ABSTRACT:
This is one endocrine disease that can be easily misdiagnosed. This presentation will focus on the correct pathway to diagnosis and how best to ascertain whether you have the correct diagnosis.

courses.title: TELEMEDICINE: EXTENDING CARE BEYOND YOUR WALLS (Anytime)
courses.description:
Veterinary medicine today is changing rapidly. Pet owners are expecting more and more from their veterinarian. The COVID-19 outbreak changed the way your clients look for health information for themselves and their pets. These growing expectations, combined with changing consumer habits, can put new strains on hospitals and their bottom line. Adding a flexible telehealth platform as an additional tool to deliver care can help veterinary teams adapt to the new demands through improved communication and client engagement, streamlined team-based workflows, and the creation of new revenue opportunities. To fully realize the benefits of telehealth, veterinarians must understand best practices, legal and regulatory implications, and how to adopt them in their own offices.
This webinar uses real-world data and case examples to demonstrate how virtual care can be used to improve practice efficiency and productivity, expand care to underserved populations (during and after the pandemic), and help mitigate both the direct and indirect effects of the virus in your practice.

courses.title: The Basics of Exotic Companion Mammal Anesthesia (EXOT110)
courses.description: Have you ever wondered where to start when that rabbit with overgrown teeth needs to be anesthetized? How about the hamster that needs a mass removed? This course is for you! We will discuss the basics of anesthetizing any companion exotic mammal that comes into your practice, starting with the core physical exam findings and working all the way through to monitoring in surgery. This class will focus on the aspects of sedation and anesthesia, and will not heavily discuss the medical or surgical conditions commonly seen in the species under discussion. We'll cover sedation and anesthesia for ferrets, rabbits, guinea pigs, chinchillas, hamsters, mice, rats, gerbils, and sugar gliders - and principles that can be applied to a wide variety of other companion exotic mammals.

courses.title: Animal Echo Collection: Comparative Echo in Human & Nonhuman Primates
courses.description: Veterinarian Echo Collection is a new collection of modules that provide learners with access to various echo topics where speakers discuss the similarities and differences in human and nonhumans. Modules include a combination of lectures, animated videos, questions and case discussions.

courses.title: Front Desk Exceptional Client Skills (STAF209)
courses.description: Outstanding client service is the cornerstone of every successful veterinary practice. Most clients cannot evaluate your practice's medical expertise and unfortunately, base their decision to return on their experience at the front desk. Clients are your most important asset, and it takes only one negative encounter to lose a long-time or potential client. A client will always remember his/her first few minutes at your practice along with the last few. During this course, emphasis will be placed on creating a client's overall positive experience, building client loyalty, increasing a client's perception of value, and making the front desk member a valuable contributor to the hospital team.

courses.title: Overview of intervertebral disc disease The Down Dog
courses.description: Overview of intervertebral disc disease. The "Down" Dog Anatomy / Pathophysiology 1. Intervertebral disc 2. Type I vs Type II 3. Disc degeneration 4. Clinical IVDD Clinical Presentation 1. Grades 2. Progression Plan 1. When to refer 2. What is an emergency 3. Deep pain 4. Conservative management vs surgery 5. Myelomalacia

courses.title: Adrenal Ultrasonography (DIAG430)
courses.description: Early in our ultrasound journey, some operators likened looking for an adrenal gland to finding the proverbial needle in a haystack. But what if that needle had a GPS tracker attached to it to pinpoint its location? In this course, we will show you how to consistently locate the left adrenal gland and discuss the findings and challenges of the right adrenal gland. The course will review adrenal hormone production and compare histology with ultrasound findings. Findings on the abdominal ultrasound expected when suspecting Cushing's, Addison's, or neoplasia are discussed.

courses.provider: NIAMRRE - NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE RESEARCH AND EDUCATION
courses.title: Antibiotic Stewardship and Science Communication for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description:
The World Health Organization has classified antimicrobial resistance a top global public health concern that requires a one health approach. As a vital link between animal and human health, veterinarians serve as guardians of responsible antibiotic use and stewardship practices, preserving the efficacy of medically important antibiotics used for pets and food-producing animals. It is therefore crucial that they be equipped with the communication skills required to educate their clients on appropriate antibiotic use. The goal of this self-paced, online course is to increase veterinary professionals knowledge and skills for effective science communication to help mitigate the threat of antibiotic resistance.
The course comprises of four online modules of interactive learning. These are:
1. Antibiotic Resistance in Professional and Social Settings
2. Communication Strategies in Clinical Settings to Assist in Mitigating Antibiotic Resistance
3. Common Challenging Scenarios and
4. Future Communication Strategies for Antibiotic Stewardship
Each module will take approximately 15 - 20 minutes to complete (total time 60 minutes)
Learning Objectives: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
1. Explain key concepts related to antibiotic resistance and its impact on animal and human health.
2. Discuss principles of antibiotic stewardship and identify practical steps to implement stewardship practices for better health outcomes.
3. Identify essential elements of strong science communication and practical approaches (such as SODAPOP and GETSMART) to engage clients in a conversation about antibiotic use.
4. Recognize communication barriers in client interaction about antibiotic treatment and address their root causes
5. Practice applying contrasting communication approaches to challenging scenarios encountered in veterinary practice and evaluate their effectiveness in meeting communication goals.
6. Integrate learned principles of science communication and antibiot

courses.title: The Geriatric Ferret (EXOT019)
courses.description: Did you ever think that just treating ferrets was complicated enough? How about the geriatric ferret, with multiple medical conditions? In this course, we will break down the most common diseases seen in the older ferret, and provide some structure to figuring out what is priority and how to go about maximizing quality of lift for these complicated little senior citizens so beloved by their owners!

courses.title: Off to the Right Start: Nutrition for Your Kitten
courses.description:
A strong nutritional foundation supports the growth and development of a kitten throughout the first year of life. Kittens are normally dependent¿on the queen to provide food during the neonatal or nursing period so if the queen cant or wont provide sufficient maternal care for survival from birth to weaning, veterinary teams need to be prepared to step in and provide essential education for kitten caregivers.
A host of physiologic¿needs normally provided by the queen must be met to ensure¿survival of neonates: heat, humidity, nutrition, immunity, elimination,¿sanitation, security and social stimulation. A foster¿queen or the caregiver must meet these needs for orphaned kittens and manage the gradual process of weaning from queens milk to solid food.
In this course, you'll learn how to feed nursing kittens, feed orphaned¿kittens, and integrate the weaning process. We will also discuss nutritional assessment, key nutrients for a healthy kitten, and feeding¿to achieve healthy growth, optimize trainability and immune function, and minimize obesity.¿

courses.title: I Deworm But I Can't Get Rid of Hookworms: Are These Hookworms Resistant?
courses.description: Resistance to dewormers has emerged as a serious concern in Ancylostoma caninum, one of the hookworms of dogs. This course discusses how anthelmintic resistance arises, what we know about the prevalence of resistance in hookworms in the United States, how to diagnose cases of resistance, and how to manage these cases.

courses.provider: CENTER FOR FOOD SECURITY AND PUBLIC HEALTH COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE IOWA S
courses.title: Introduction to Farmed Cervid CWD Programs for Veterinarians
courses.description: Chronic Wasting Disease (CWD) is a fatal disease affecting many members of the Cervidae family. Veterinarians play a vital role not only in helping cervid producers succeed but also in protecting the health of the cervid industry. Understanding the biology and surveillance of CWD will allow veterinarians to promote animal health and support the U.S. cervid industry. This course will cover general information about CWD, current U.S. CWD surveillance and response activities, and details regarding participation in state CWD programs.

courses.title: Equine Euthanasia
courses.description: Horses and other equids are companion animals. They are loved and revered in our society and deserve the same attention given to their end-of-life story as all other beloved pets. Equine euthanasia is considered by many to be the most challenging type of euthanasia there is; their size, strength, and the nature of the bond around them makes it necessary for us to increase our skillset and ensure a safe and gentle death each time. Written by David Shuey, LVT, CHPT, a long-standing advocate for ideal standards in equine euthanasia, this module will explore many parameters around equine euthanasia; safety, proper techniques, restraint/handling, maintaining the bond, and more. Join us for an enlightening session sure to make you better prepared to work with these majestic creatures.

courses.title: From Missile-Guiding Pigeons to Spy Dogs: How to Use Applied Behavior Analysis to Drive Huge Improvements in Your Training
courses.description: Harness the power of science in your training! Whether you're a trainer, veterinary behaviorist, pet owner, police, military, or scent work trainer, training methods based on the science of animal behavior can get you astonishingly fast and consistent results. In this second of two fascinating, live-recorded lectures, Dr. Sophia Yin veterinarian, animal behaviorist, and author explains clearly and vividly the essential foundations and practical applications of the science of animal learning.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2024 Evaluating Manuscripts for Clinical Practice, Residency Training and Peer Review On Demand
courses.description: Have you ever skipped the statistics section of a manuscript because you did not feel confident about evaluating it. Do you wonder how journal policy affects manuscript quality. If so this course is for you. It begins with the presentation of a foundational biostatistical toolbox to help clinicians accurately pose and analyze research questions. Effective approaches for evaluating literature will be presented and modeled. The course concludes with sessions on how artificial intelligence and editorial policy may impact manuscript content and quality. This course is tailored for Candidates and Diplomates seeking to more accurately review and apply published research.

courses.title: Rapid Reversal of Fear and Aggression in Dogs and Cats (BHVR901)
courses.description: Flooding, desensitization, classical counterconditioning and operant counterconditioning are the 4 methods of behavior modification; but which one should you use? Many people are familiar with the terms and techniques but may lack the full knowledge needed to apply them appropriately. Improper or unskilled application can cause an animal's behavior to worsen rather than improve. This course shows how understanding the underlying principles and learning to read and respond to the animal's reactions in real time can increase both your level and your speed of success when reversing fear and aggression. You will see these techniques applied in real veterinary, training, and shelter settings, and learn how to use them safely so animals can be examined, treated, and handled without force.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Nutritional Tools (NUTR124)
courses.description: This course is intended to review tools used in nutrition practice, as well as basic principles of canine and feline nutrition. This two-hour course will focus on nutritional assessment tools, differences between canine and feline nutrition, a brief overview of pet food label interpretation, and a discussion of dietary options for dogs and cats.

courses.title: CPR - A Team Approach (TECH449)
courses.description: This course provides a focused, evidence-based overview of small-animal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) aligned with the RECOVER 2024 guidelines. Participants will learn how to prepare their hospital and respond effectively as a coordinated veterinary team during cardiopulmonary arrest events. Core topics include patient recognition, high-quality basic and advanced life support, post-arrest patient stabilization, and newborn resuscitation. The course emphasizes practical, team-centered skills that enhance confidence, communication, and patient outcomes in emergency situations.

courses.title: The use of Settle in the mare: Q&A
courses.description: Dr. Carleigh Fedorka provides an overview of reproductive immunology, including immunity of the uterus and the effects of breeding and pregnancy, along with potential complications. She then discusses Settle immunotherapy, a formulation of Mycobacterium cell wall fraction for the treatment of endometritis, including a review of research data and future directions for the product.

courses.title: Anemia in Cats and Dogs (DRIP114)
courses.description:
This course will cover the pathology, diagnostic approach and treatment options of the anemic veterinary patient.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 57 minutes.

courses.title: Allround Starter/Refresher program companion animals
courses.description:
The Allround Starter/Refresher program is a one-year online continuing education program for veterinarians in general practice seeking to strengthen or refresh their clinical foundation in small animal medicine. The program is designed for early-career veterinarians, experienced veterinarians seeking a structured refresher, and veterinarians transitioning into companion animal practice.
Participants complete a predefined sequence of 10 modules, each focused on a core discipline within small animal medicine, namely internal medicine, infectious diseases, anesthesia and analgesia, emergency and critical care, clinical pathology, medical imaging, neurology, cardiology, dermatology, surgery and orthopedics. The program provides approximately 70 hours of online learning material over one year. Through structured online webinars, written materials, quizzes and clinical cases, participants review practical concepts that support confident decision-making in everyday small animal practice.
The course covers broad foundational knowledge across companion animal medicine and is intended to help participants consolidate clinical reasoning, recognize common presentations, review diagnostic and therapeutic principles, and apply evidence-informed approaches in general practice. Participants may submit questions to instructors by email during the course.
The course is taught by board-certified diplomates and residents in their respective veterinary disciplines. This ensures that the content is delivered by clinicians with in-depth subject-matter expertise and practical experience relevant to companion animal medicine.

courses.title: Crisis - Cardiorespiratory Emergencies
courses.description: This e-learning course provides a comprehensive guide to managing life-threatening cardiorespiratory emergencies in veterinary medicine through five specialized modules. It is designed to replace anxiety with confidence by equipping clinicians with the tools for rapid stabilization of the patient and further decision-making.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Avian Toxicities
courses.description: This course will cover the most common toxicities called into the ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center, along with recommended treatments and stabilization of the Avian patient.

courses.title: Endocrinology Refresher Course
courses.description: Are you ready to elevate your expertise in endocrinology and become a master in managing diabetes and hormonal disorders in dogs and cats? An intensive series of 4 webinars designed to refresh and enhance your knowledge in feline and canine endocrinology. Don't miss this opportunity to refine your skills and stay at the forefront of endocrine veterinary care.

courses.title: Nutritional Support of Oral Health in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: This course will advance your understanding of dental care and oral health in cats and dogs. You will gain an understanding of the benefits of proper dental care, and how proper nutrition and food texture can support oral health. You will gain knowledge and confidence in discussing dental related nutritional recommendations that with pet parents. You will be able to guide pet parents through implementation of a new feeding program to help avoid periodontal disease, particularly for those pets in higher-risk groups.

courses.title: Examining the Relationship between BIPOC Communities and Their Companion Animals
courses.description: Catherine Kisavi-Atatah Ph.D. will share the findings of her publication, Examining the Relationship between BIPOC Communities and Their Companion Animals. This study explored the relationship between BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Color) communities with their companion animals, using Attachment Theory as a lens of analyses. Findings suggest that public and private policy decision-makers should develop and implement holistic, across-the-board, companion animal policies that are user-friendly to all, which will and could bring some positive social changes to all owners in the state of Texas and possibly beyond.

courses.title: The Influence of Field Trip and Sleepover Programs on Shelter Dog Welfare (OnDemand)
courses.description: Animal shelters can be stressful for dogs, but human interaction, such as foster caregiving, can improve their experience. In this webcast, I will discuss multiple studies we have carried out as part of the Arizona State University and Virginia Tech Maddie's Nationwide Fostering Study in which we studied the effects of field trip and sleepover programs on the welfare of dogs living in shelters.
