Our initial studies investigated the physiological impacts of these programs, and our recently published study examined how field trips and sleepovers influenced dogs' likelihood of adoption and length of stay. We also explored factors related to the performance of these programs. Overall, our findings support the implementation of these programs, and I will discuss how we can use short-term fostering programs to improve the welfare of dogs in shelters as they await adoption.

courses.title: Clinical Approach to the Icteric Patient (DRIP160)
courses.description:
This course focuses on relevant pathophysiology and diagnostic testing regarding the icteric patient and discusses potential therapies.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test.

courses.title: Feline Ultrasound: The Vomiting Cat (DIAG433)
courses.description:
It's an often-repeated adage - "cats are not little dogs", and this is especially true with feline medicine and ultrasound. Cats have many unique diseases that require feline-specific knowledge to diagnose and treat. Ultrasound is one of the most useful tools feline clinicians have in their arsenal to diagnose diseases in cats, who often present with very vague and non-specific clinical signs.
This is one of four courses in the Feline Ultrasound collection. Each course will consist of a single 2-hour session that will focus on the normal ultrasound appearance of an organ system and then present changes observed that are associated with specific diseases. These courses are independent of each other and can be taken in any combination.
This course will cover using ultrasound to diagnose the underlying causes of vomiting in cats. The normal ultrasound appearance of the feline gastrointestinal tract will be reviewed and then contrasted with such topics as feline chronic enteropathies, gastrointestinal neoplasia, mechanical obstructions, functional ileus and pancreatitis.

courses.title: Proptosis (TECH454)
courses.description: Anesthesia on healthy patients is not without complications, and is too often taken for granted and performed without adequate planning or preparation. However, with any emergency presented to triage, a thorough pre-operative assessment must be performed, and patient assessment begins with the first step inside the door. The stressed and ill emergency patient will have altered physiological responses that will in turn alter the pharmacokinetics of the agents commonly used to provide anesthesia. This course is designed to assist you in your management of proptosis.

courses.title: VETERINARY STRESSORS: KEEP THE COMPASSION, KICK THE FATIGUE ( Anytime)
courses.description: Veterinary professionals experience death at a rate five times higher than our human physician colleagues. The bond between our patients and their humans can run the gamut from pathological attachment to disposable companions, and anywhere in between. Our workdays are hectic and the pressure from other aspects of our lives can pile on. Learn the triggers for and effects of compassion fatigue, and healthy ways to manage stress.

courses.title: Separating Fact, Fiction, and Uncertainty: Canine Respiratory Illness
courses.description: This course was created in response to continued reports of an upswing in respiratory illnesses impacting dogs across North America, Trupanion invites you to join this webinar hosted by a panel of global veterinary authorities to discuss this topic. Originally aired live on November 30, 2023.

courses.title: WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management - Module I - Understanding and assessing pain
courses.description:
The WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management was developed for veterinary professionals across the globe to understand the importance of adequate pain management for small animal health and welfare. This course includes Module I (out of three Modules) of the WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management .
With this Certificate, the student will be empowered to:
1) Frequently assess pain in small animals with knowledge of pain-related behaviors and validated pain scales
2) Prevent pain and other negative emotions such as fear, discomfort, nausea and anxiety
3) Treat pain using drug and non-drug therapies on a case-by-case basis
The WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management includes pre-recorded lectures in addition to mandatory and suggested reading materials, and quizzes at the end of each lecture. The educational content is primarily based on the recently published 2022 WSAVA guidelines for the recognition, assessment and treatment of pain, and on additional topics not covered by that document, but considered to be important and relevant for professionals working with companion animal health and welfare globally. Lectures are given by the authors of the Guidelines and other invited experts in the field.
The entire educational content is available at no cost following registration. A fee will be charged to those who would like to receive the actual Certificate and recognition of continuing education credits. The WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management is divided into three Modules. The Module I - Understanding and assessing pain has 8 hours of content (12 recorded lectures of 30 minutes each and 2 hours of mandatory reading). It includes lectures focused on the following topics: animal welfare; ethics in pain management; pain pathophysiology; the role of emotions on pain perception; clinical assessment of pain in dogs and cats; human-animal bond; client communication; stakeholders and the importance of nurses/technicians; and sustainability.

courses.provider: ZERO PAIN PHILOSOPHY - ACE VETS LIMITED
courses.title: Zero Pain Philosophy Local Anaesthesia Course
courses.description:
The Zero Pain Philosophy Local Anaesthesia course gives the learner the knowledge required to start using local anaesthesia in their practice. Each webinar describes the technique, highlighting where the learner would use that particular technique. Each webinar is complemented with videos that explain the technique visually so the learner can easily review the video immediately before attempting the technique.
A mix of content is provided, with webinars, podcasts, pain updates and reflective learning assignments. The pain updates and reflect articles present a topic for review, along with references for the learner to read.

courses.title: Short-Term Foster Programs for Shelter Cats: Beneficial or Problematic?
courses.description: This webinar was presented by Dr. Kristyn Vitale, the lead author on a new study exploring shelter cat foster programs. Every year millions of cats enter animal shelters in the U.S. alone. Interventions are greatly needed that have the potential to reduce cat stress and increase cat welfare while in the shelter environment. Although dog foster programs have become commonplace for many animal shelters, cat foster programs are relatively uncommon, potentially due to the belief that cats may be at risk of unnecessary stress from the fostering experience. In the study, researchers examined the social behavior and stress levels of cats that stayed in the shelter to cats that left the shelter for short-term foster, either for 1-night or 1-week. The results of the study indicate that shelter cats placed in foster care were not at a disadvantage. These findings can benefit both cats and animal shelters alike. Tune into the webinar to learn more about the study and how to apply the results in an animal shelter setting.

courses.title: Copper Storage Disease (DRIP123)
courses.description: This course focuses on copper storage disease in dogs found in modern veterinary practice and the logical way to handle it.

courses.title: Guidelines for Surgical Infection Control: Small Steps Make a BIG Difference
courses.description: Guidelines for Surgical Infection Control: Small Steps Make a BIG Difference is designed to provide an overview of surgical wound management and infection control in veterinary science. Topics include categorizing surgical wounds, classifying surgical site infections (SSIs), identifying common bacteria, adhering to recommended standards for patient and instrument preparation, implementing infection control in the operating room (OR), and postoperative wound care.

courses.title: Fear Free: Behavioural Euthanasia
courses.description: This webinar will teach you to develop compassion and empathy for your clients who are facing the difficult decision of behavioural euthanasia. You will learn ways to determine the severity of the behavioral concern and resources to offer them to remedy the situation. Understanding the risk of patients is also important as well as having realistic expectations of outcomes.

courses.title: Certification in Veterinary Integrative Therapeutic Nutrition
courses.description: This course was originally developed by Barbara Fougere, DVM, Barbara Royal,DVM, Susan Wynn, DVM, DACVN and Natasha Lilly, DVM. Their background combines experience in clinical work and cases, pet food industry collaborations, nutrition software development, study, research and literature publications, authorship and pioneering work in nutrition, international university affiliations and professorships and worldwide leadership in progressive and effective therapeutic veterinary nutrition. Integrative therapeutic nutrition provides a bridge between conventional veterinary commercial food options, supplements and pharmaceuticals, and fresh food nutrition options, and assesses both commercially available and individual recipe options for health conditions. With a clinically relevant approach to the effect of food on health from the microscopic to macroscopic, current research is incorporated, along with species specific metabolic information, and a growing database of clinical successes to describe best practices in an integrative nutritional prescription. Relevant data on both macro- and micro-nutrients and practices for each medical condition will be evaluated and discussed.

courses.title: TPLO for Veterinary Technicians Online Course
courses.description: TPLO for Veterinary Technicians is designed to prepare veterinary technicians to assist in the TPLO procedure. First it reviews diagnostics for CrCL disease, then reviews the preoperative steps such as radiography and patient preparation. Next it gives an overview of commonly used instrumentation, and the surgical technique from the view of a veterinary technicians. Finally it gives an overview of client communication and postoperative radiography and postoperative care.

courses.title: L.E.G.S. Applied Ethology Family Dog Mediation Professional Course
courses.description: Dogs & People in the Modern World, Dog Training as a Broken Model, The Need for Evolution in the Dog Behavior Industry, The "Pet" Industry, Ethology (L.E.G.S.) & Applied Ethology, Fundamentals of Evolution (to appreciate disconnect we have with dogs as it relates to nature), Captivity & Welfare - Broken L.E.G.S., Quickstart L.E.G.S. Assessments, SELF Antecedents, GENETICS Antecedents (deep dive into all ten genetic working groups history and "behavior problems", ENVIRONMENT Antecedents (ultimate to proximate, including social environment), LEARNING Antecedents & Element Within and Beyond ABA, using ethology in dog behavior and welfare work, working with dogs and people, Kim's top dog hacks (practical solutions and interventions using applied ethology)

courses.title: Ask Me Anything: Corneal Ulceration with Dr. Andrew Lewin
courses.description: This exclusive "Ask Me Anything"-style webinar powered by Plumb's will provide expert guidance on the clinical challenges associated with corneal ulceration. In this presentation, Plumb's Pro author Dr. Andrew Lewin will share new insights into the diagnosis and management of this condition and answer all your burning questions related to corneal ulceration.

courses.title: Guinea Pig Basics (EXOT012)
courses.description: This course covers the basics of guinea pig ownership and husbandry, as well as an overview of a general clinical approach to the species, discussing common diseases and their treatments.

courses.title: Effective Decontamination Techniques for Toxicant Exposures (PHAR205)
courses.description: Acute exposures of veterinary patients to potential toxicants requires immediate attention to determine the risk of toxicosis developing and to take appropriate measures to minimize harm from the toxicant. Decontamination should only be performed when the risk from the toxicant is greater than the risks inherent in the decontamination technique being performed. This course will present rational approaches to patient decontamination including risk assessment, indications and contraindications of decontamination, and explanation of various decontamination techniques to employ depending on individual circumstances.

courses.title: VSPA Spring Conference 2026
courses.description: The VSPA Fall Conference 2026 is a 2.5-day event for owners and teams of non-competing, independent specialty and emergency veterinary hospitals. In-person attendees will engage in lectures, discussions, and socials aimed at bolstering sustainable practices in HR, strategic planning, and finance, all while nurturing team engagement and psychological safety. Attendees will leave re-energized and ready to lead; attendance records will be provided for in-person participants.

courses.title: FIP / GS-441524 Treatment Webinar
courses.description:
The mysterious FIP: diagnosis, treatment, and management of complicated cases, relapses and comorbidities in cats with FIP.
This lecture will cover diagnosis of FIP and the complexities in FIP diagnosis. This lecture will focus on managing complicated cases of FIP, what to do if cats are not responding to medications, relapses of FIP as well as cats that develop comorbidities such as IMHA, sepsis, pneumonia etc. We will also address questions about trending cats with FIV/FeLV. We will discuss relapses of FIP as these are not so common, and making sure we do not over diagnose FIP relapse and avoid both unnecessary antiviral treatments as well as provide appropriate therapy.

courses.title: The practical application of canine procedural sedation for a busy practice --- a roundtable discussion
courses.description: In this educational presentation, we will introduce the concept of procedural sedation in veterinary practice. This includes a review of the basic physiology behind sedation in dogs, commonly used sedatives, and the use of a reversal agent. Lastly, we will discuss a novel sedative, Zenalpha --- a combination of the alpha-2 agonsist, medetomidine, and the peripheral alpha-2 antagonist, vatinoxan --- and how it can improve your clinical practice.

courses.title: Laparoscopy CE training program
courses.description: Provide laparoscopy training to veterinarians and their veterinary technical staff. This training will be done on-site at a Veterinary Hospital for hands-on training with actual patients. The course will cover the use of a otoscope, rhinoscope, cystoscope and laparoscope along with their respective equipment, procedures and anatomy. The course will cover the most common endoscopy, laparoscopy, cystoscopy, otoscopy & rhinoscopy procedures. We will review anatomy along with teaching minimally invasive surgical techniques.

courses.title: 2025 AHVMA Annual Conference On-Demand
courses.description: American Holistic Veterinary Medical Association Annual Conference On-Demand. These are the recordings of the face-to-face seminar/lectures from the in-person AHVMA Annual Conference offered from September 6-9, 2025, providing an On-Demand option. Post course assessments will be provided at the end of each lecture. Our main objective is to increase knowledge and skills of CAVM techniques, topics, and procedures.

courses.title: Chronic Snorkers aka Feline Rhinitis (FELI104)
courses.description: Practically every practice has at least one of them - the "chronic snorker", those lovely cats who return visit after visit with respiratory signs, seemingly no matter what you do for them. Frustrated with sending home round after round of antibiotics? Learn in the course why this isn't working - and what the other treatment and diagnostic options might include. This course is for every single person who has ever been frustrated by an upper respiratory feline patient.

courses.title: Backyard Poultry Basics (EXOT317)
courses.description: In recent years, more people are starting to raise small flocks of poultry in backyard urban settings. Because of the small numbers of birds involved, they are often viewed more as pets than as production animals, even though they are being kept primarily for eggs or meat. When these birds become injured or ill, the owners are turning to their local family veterinarian for assistance, even though many small animal practitioners have very little to no experience with poultry or with how to treat animals that are being used in food production. This course is intended to help those veterinarians and their technicians/technologists become more familiar with the handling and care of poultry commonly encountered in the backyard setting.

courses.title: Pruritus Simplified: A Step-by-Step Approach to the Allergic Dog
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Joya Griffin will present a practical, step-by-step clinical approach to evaluating the pruritic dog, beginning with the initial diagnostic investigation and progressing through evidence-based treatment selection. Participants will learn how to systematically rule out common differential diagnoses and identify allergic skin disease. In addition, Dr. Griffin will discuss how to assess pruritus severity and inflammatory skin lesions to aid in the development of individualized treatment plans. Emphasis will be placed on practical decision-making to improve patient outcomes and client satisfaction.

courses.title: Anesthetic Monitors-Understanding Their Use & Limitations (TECH336)
courses.description: Technicians interpret data from anesthetic monitors on a routine basis. This 1-hour presentation covers various monitoring modalities used in assessing the anesthetized patient, as well as common pitfalls and precautions that should be taken while interpreting the data provided by them. Monitoring modalities discussed include esophageal stethoscope, ECG, blood pressure, pulse oximetry, capnography and temperature.

courses.provider: OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY - CARLSON COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: Oops, They Bit it Again: Diagnosis and Management of Fractured Teeth
courses.description: This presentation will cover diagnosis and assessment of dentoalveolar trauma and approach to treatment planning for general practice. We will discuss this commonly identified condition and when diagnostics and intervention are indicated, including how to discuss these examination findings with clients, assessment and determination of treatment options, including when to consider dentin bonding for enamel-dentin fractures. An overview of the process of dentin bonding will be included.

courses.title: Feline Ultrasound: The Feline Urinary Tract (DIAG432)
courses.description:
It's an often-repeated adage - "cats are not little dogs", and this is especially true with feline medicine and ultrasound. Cats have many unique diseases that require feline-specific knowledge to diagnose and treat. Ultrasound is one of the most useful tools feline clinicians have in their arsenal to diagnose diseases in cats, who often present with very vague and non-specific clinical signs.
This is one of four courses in the Feline Ultrasound collection. Each course will consist of a single 2-hour session that will focus on the normal ultrasound appearance of an organ system and then present changes observed that are associated with specific diseases. These courses are independent of each other and can be taken in any combination.
This course will cover the use of ultrasound to assess the feline urinary tract, including the normal ultrasound appearance of the feline kidney and bladder, deviations from normal that are not clinically relevant, and the ultrasound appearance of diseases that affect the feline kidney and bladder. In addition, there will be a review of ultrasound-guided cystocentesis.

courses.provider: AMERICAN INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL LASER APPLICATIONS
courses.title: INTRODUCTION TO LASER THERAPY FOR THE VETERINARY TECHNICIAN, VETERINARY ASSISTANT, & VETERINARY NURS (554-44074)
courses.description:
The use of therapeutic lasers within the veterinary profession has multiplied exponentially in the last few years. Unfortunately, they are not being utilized to their potential. This is due to a lack of understanding of how photobiomodulation works, what occurs within the tissue to which it is applied, proper application techniques, and how versatile this therapy can be to each practice.
In most practices, the veterinary technician, assistant, or nurse endures the everyday task of applying laser therapy.
This course will allow these colleagues to understand not only the science and research supporting this modality but also application techniques and actual cases, which supply the foundation allowing extrapolation to each practice environment.

courses.title: Strategic Planning: The Magic of Intention
courses.description: In this course, participants will be guided through every step of the strategic planning process for veterinary practices. They will learn how to effectively prepare for an impactful and effective strategic planning weekend and identify where their practice currently stands. From there, they will define clear goals, map out actionable steps to achieve those goals, and establish methods to track progress. By the end, participants will have a solid framework to propel their practice toward its vision and long-term success.

courses.title: An Overview of New World Screwworm
courses.description: New World Screwworm is not present in the United States. This webinar will provide information from USDA to allow zoo and exotic animal industry stakeholders to understand current geographic distribution of the fly, eradication strategies, and early recognition. In addition, the webinar will provide resources for when facilities are faced with concerns for NWS.

courses.title: Victim to Verdict: The Veterinarian's Role in Animal Cruelty Investigations Online Course
courses.description: See attachment.

courses.title: How Fish Breathe
courses.description:
Understanding how fish breathe is important to how we provide care for them. In this course we will review the anatomy and physiology of the fish respiratory system. We will compare and contrast it to terrestrial (land) mammal breathing. As we journey through the basics of fish oxygenation and ventilation, we'll talk about how this impacts how we handle these amazing creatures, and touch on the anesthesia of fish too.
We will also cover how to measure oxygen in a body of water or aquarium, as well as how to measure oxygenation and ventilation in a fish. The measurement of carbon dioxide will be discussed. Lastly, we will talk about how to revive a fish that is near death due to hypoxemia (low levels of oxygen in their bloodstream).

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Insights and Implications from Housing-Related Animal Shelter Intake Data (On-Demand)
courses.description:
The lack of affordable and available rental housing in the US is an epidemic, impacting a majority of American renters -- not just low-income renters, although they're the most burdened. Housing insecurity for tenants has increased in severity in the last several years as rents have skyrocketed and eviction rates have, in many cities, climbed higher than even pre-pandemic levels (Harvard, 2024). Today, more renters than ever are experiencing at least moderate rent burden as unaffordability in the rental market hit an all-time high in 2022 (Harvard, 2024). The impact of the lack of available, affordable rental housing, and housing insecurity more broadly, is not felt race-neutrally. A 2024 report by Harvard University's Joint Center for Housing Studies reported that over half of Black and Hispanic renter families were moderately or severely housing cost burdened, compared to only 41.9% of white renter families (Harvard, 2024).
Housing insecurity directly impacts peoples' ability to acquire and keep pets for life. Already dismal options for affordable housing are likely to be worse for those families also searching for pet-inclusive housing, which I define as housing free from pet breed, size, or weight restrictions and nonrefundable pet fees or rents. In fact, a 2021 report from Michaelson Found Animals found that only approximately 8% of rental housing surveyed was free of breed, weight, or size restrictions. Distressingly, a 2003 FIREPAW study also found that only 7% of housing was pet-friendly, indicating that the rental housing market may not be significantly more "pet-friendly" than it was 20 years ago. There is a small, but growing body of research to better understand the impact of rental housing conditions on pets, pet owners, and animal shelters in the U.S. and how this issue relates to broader affordable housing and tenants' rights social justice advocacy.
The purpose of this presentation is to share the results of three research projects, co-authored by th

courses.title: Gait Analysis for the Performance Dog
courses.description: Locomotion is the movement of the body that allows it to move from one point to another location. Gait analysis can be considered an art, as the viewer needs to have a good understanding of the normal gait patterns and issues associated with abnormal movements. It is the intent of this course to build upon the information provided in the functional anatomy course and the biomechanics course and utilize this knowledge in an applicable manner. This is very helpful when the professional is developing a conditioning program, identifying performance deficiencies, or making decisions related to a rehabilitative program. Dogs and other animals cannot talk like the human subjects. So, it can be very hard to understand how a dog is feeling, their aches or pains, or any other underlying issues they may be experiencing. Analyzing canine motion is very complex in its nature, but it can be used as a helpful tool to assess musculoskeletal health, identify areas that may benefit from conditioning programs and used as a basis for building rehabilitation programs.

courses.title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Cats (DRIP103)
courses.description: Diabetic ketoacidosis in felines brings a shiver to most practitioners. Therefore, let us explore the relevant pathophysiology, current diagnostic testing, and logical, effective therapies to provide confidence in medical intervention, and the greatest probability for success in treating these complicated cases. Concurrent disease factors, electrolyte derangements, and when to get patients started on long acting insulin, as well as suggestions for client compliance, such as at home monitoring are addressed. Feline patients are highlighted, but canine patients are also discussed.

courses.title: Canine Postural Rehabilitation Professional
courses.description: This course examines the CNS mechanisms and integration of postural control, the structures and functions of anatomic regions (cervical spine, distal limb, stomatognathic system) that are principal informants of proprioceptive information used to generate and control posture in dogs, how to recognize normal neutral posture (NNP) and abnormal compensatory posture (ACP), why they are commonly distorted and/or compromised in domestic dogs, the common chronic lameness and performance problems associated with ACP, and how to enact therapeutic changes that will restore normal neutral posture.

courses.title: Certification in Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine
courses.description: The Certification in Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine enables practitioners to develop competency in utilising Western herbal medicine and Western herbal medicine principles in the assessment, treatment and management of animals in their care. Successful completion of this course will enable practitioners to safely and effectively integrate a core group of 40 important herbs into a veterinary practice. The course is orientated towards applied theory, which can be implemented in a veterinary practice almost immediately. Practitioners will be able to develop confidence and competence over time during the course, with continuous case support, guidance and feedback from tutors with both simulated and active case forums and subsequently their own clinical cases.

courses.title: Mushrooms & More: Modulating Immunity
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Nancy Loes will review the rationale for and benefits of incorporating nutrients from mushrooms, oats, and colostrum into an overall veterinary healthcare management plan.

courses.title: Improving Access to Care: Financial Triage in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: One of the most common and distressing barriers to veterinary care for both clients and veterinary teams is finances. When confronted with client financial constraints many practices are forced to provide care at no charge, heavily discount their services, or even turn pets away. There is a better way! Join us to learn about practical tools and sustainable solution-oriented financial resources that can be easily implemented by veterinary teams. Help clients say "yes" to your recommended treatment plans and free yourself to work on what matters most: your patient.

courses.title: Vector-Borne Diseases: What's Emerging With Direction & Magnitude Near You?
courses.description: In this webinar, Drs. Michael Lappin and Michelle Evason will share clinical veterinary updates on emerging detection of vector-borne diseases in dogs and cats, including trypanosomiasis (ie, Chagas), cytauxzoonosis (ie, bobcat fever), Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and others. The webinar will review the role of dogs and cats as sentinels and their contribution to the surveillance of vector-borne pathogens in the United States and Canada, along with how veterinarians and their teams can raise awareness, educate, and communicate on One Health risks.

courses.title: Where's the Lesion? A Guide to Neurolocalization
courses.description: This course is intended to review the components of the neurological examination and improve neurolocalization skills for general practitioners and emergency medicine veterinarians.

courses.title: Ask Me Anything: Urinary Tract Infections in Dogs With Dr. Shannon Palermo
courses.description: In this "Ask Me Anything"-style webinar powered by Standards of Care, Shannon Palermo, VMD, DACVIM, will discuss accurate diagnosis of UTIs in dogs, review how to identify predisposing factors for recurrent infections, and outline strategies for effective antimicrobial use and prevention of resistance.

courses.title: What the Cluck? Backyard Poultry Medicine
courses.description: Chickens make the best patients! Backyard poultry represents a growing segment of the companion animal veterinary market. As pet chickens are classified as food animals, it behooves the clinician to be aware of laws surrounding drug use in these patients. This lecture will cover the basics of backyard poultry husbandry and medicine and prepare you for adding these fabulous creatures to your appointment schedule.

courses.title: When Is Low Too Low? Hematology Abnormalities in the Cancer Patient
courses.description: Even if you are not the one administering chemotherapy, managing cancer patients requires a keen eye for hematology abnormalities. In this case-based session, Dr. Sue Ettinger will guide you through the essentials of monitoring neutrophils, lymphocytes, and platelets in cancer patients, whether you're performing a nadir CBC or assessing a patient that is not feeling well posttreatment. Attendees will learn when intervention is necessary versus when careful monitoring is sufficient and will also explore a new hematology technology that can help enhance patient care, giving you the confidence to interpret and act on your hematology results.

courses.provider: VETERINARY EMERGENCY AND CRITICAL CARE SOCIETY
courses.title: Online Vet MDR from IVECCS 2023
courses.description: The Veterinary MDR program provides practitioners with the opportunity to explore specific topics in depth, suitable for those pursuing specialty certification. Designed for both small and large animal residents preparing for emergency and critical care exams, as well as veterinarians seeking to enhance their knowledge, the program includes sessions on systemic inflammation, the interplay between coagulation and inflammation, glycemic control in sepsis, core principles of medical statistics, gastrointestinal motility and hormonal control, ischemia-reperfusion injury, glycosaminoglycans, and antimicrobial resistance. This program equips veterinarians with essential knowledge and skills to excel in emergency and critical care.

courses.title: Triage and resuscitation of the canine and feline neonate
courses.description: Presented by a board-certified criticalist, Meghan Harmon, DVM, DACVECC, this presentation focuses on a case-based approach to learning successful triage and resuscitation of the canine and feline neonate. First, Dr. Harmon will outline how to take a good history when working with critical neonates before reviewing how to perform a thorough physical examination (including normal and abnormal exam findings). By focusing on 2 critical care cases, you will then be introduced to the most common causes of morbidity and mortality in neonates. In working through these cases, you are invited to evaluate normal and abnormal laboratory findings and learn how to properly treat these conditions.

courses.title: Cliff Notes for the World of SGLT2 Inhibitors: Where Are We Now?
courses.description: In 2022 and 2023, veterinary medicine saw the release of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors for the treatment of feline diabetes mellitus. This drug class increases glucose and sodium excretion into the urine, thereby reducing hyperglycemia independent of insulin secretion. This presentation will share real-life clinical cases to provide the audience with a "cliff notes" version of everything there is to know about SGLT2 inhibitors in treatment of cats with diabetes, including appropriate patient selection and screening, indications, monitoring, and adverse effects. Future applications of SGLT2 inhibitors in other species and diseases will also be addressed on.

courses.title: The Development of, and Research on, the Family Bondedness Scale (OnDemand)
courses.description: The presentation will cover the development and use of, and research to date on, the Family Bondedness Scale when measuring equivalence between cat and dog owners. In the presentation Dr. Nugent will go over the rationale for the scale, what it is intended to measure, how it was developed, how scores on the scale should be interpreted, and how it should be scored and used. He will also discuss current research on the scale and the implications of the results of this research.

courses.title: Unresponsive Behavior: A Guide to Evaluation & Compassionate Choices for Refractory Behavior Problems in Companion Animals
courses.description:
Refractory behavior problems are something we have all seen in practice. These cases are often highly charged emotionally, and we know that owners who feel they have come to the end of their ability to care for a challenging pet are heartbroken and often guilt ridden. During this important webinar we will consider how to evaluate these cases.
Ruling out medical reasons for behavior issues and referring to professional experienced behaviorists before euthanasia is important, however it is not the focus of this particular webinar.

courses.title: The Pruritic Cat: Managing Itchy Felines
courses.description: This course will guide attendees through a practical, case based approach to the itchy cat. This course will teach veterinarians how to recognize and identify common causes of itch to the more challenging, how to identify or chronic conditions. Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how to identify the underlying cause, relieve discomfort, and improve the quality of life for the patient and their families.

courses.title: Adrenal Gland Ultrasound Masterclass: A Structured Approach to Reliable Identification and Interpretation in Dogs and Cats
courses.description:
This practical veterinary ultrasound webinar masterclass focuses on improving clinician confidence and accuracy when imaging the adrenal glands in dogs and cats.
Drawing on the presenter's background in education, this course introduces a structured, repeatable approach to adrenal imaging using the L.A.D.R. and R.A.D.R. protocols. These are frameworks specifically developed by the presenter to simplify adrenal localisation and reduce cognitive overload during scanning. These protocols are designed to be easy to remember, clinically applicable and immediately implementable in practice.
Participants will learn how to reliably locate and assess adrenal glands using anatomical landmarks, alongside alternative techniques for challenging cases. The course covers adrenal anatomy, scanning techniques, normal ultrasonographic appearance, measurement guidelines, and interpretation of abnormal findings including adrenal enlargement, nodules, mineralisation and small glands.
The program incorporates high-quality, professionally filmed ultrasound footage, including detailed visualisation of probe positioning and hand movements, to enhance practical understanding and replicate real-world scanning techniques.
Designed for general practitioners and emergency clinicians, this webinar masterclass emphasises clinical application, troubleshooting and integration of ultrasound findings with patient history and laboratory data.

courses.title: LafeberVet Heatley 2025 Non-Interactive Program
courses.description: The webinar recording, Clinical Pathology of Herptiles, will be presented by J. Jill Heatley, MS, DVM, DABVP (Avian Practice, Reptile & Amphibian Practice), DACZM. Clinicopathologic evaluation of reptiles is useful for health assessment and monitoring. There are specific considerations when evaluating data from this taxonomic group, including sex, age, time of year/season, reproductive status, diet, captive versus wild, geographic location, methodology, and anticoagulant. This webinar describes hematology, biochemistry, and urinalysis features of reptiles and amphibians as well as clinical relevance.

courses.title: Essentials of Raw Feeding for Veterinary Professionals and Canine Nutritionists
courses.description: Program Description: This course will review the basics of dog digestive anatomy and physiology, nutritional requirements, including macronutrients, micronutrients, and trace minerals, and the basics of fresh feeding. It aims to familiarize veterinary team members with the concepts of fresh feeding for dogs and give them the confidence to partner with owners to provide a balanced, fresh food diet. Successful participants will receive a certificate as a Certified Professional Canine Nutritionist.

courses.provider: SUNSHINE BOOKS, INC., DBA KAREN PRYOR CLICKER TRAINING
courses.title: PUPPY START RIGHT FOR INSTRUCTORS (692-35009)
courses.description:
This course is for anyone who wants to begin teaching puppy socialization classes or for those who already teach but would like to up their game. If you are a veterinary professional, a dog trainer, or another animal care professional, this course will help you improve puppies lives as well as expand your client services.
This course was written and is taught by Debbie Martin, RVT, VTS (Behavior), CPDT-KA, KPA CTP, and Kenneth M. Martin, DVM, Diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Behaviorists, the authors of Puppy Start Right: Foundation Training for the Companion Dog.

courses.title: Veterinary Orthopedic Manipulation VOM Modules 1-4 with Certification
courses.description:
Veterinary Orthopedic Manipulation is an instrument-based technology to provide precise animal adjusting for exacting rehabilitation to each pet, maximizing recovery in every situation. Veterinary Orthopedic Manipulation VOM is a healing technology that locates areas of the animals nervous system that has fallen out of communication, and re-establishes neuronal communication and thus induces healing. This course will introduce Veterinary Orthopedic Manipulation VOM TM, provide detailed, in-depth information, instruction, demonstrations and all forms and data needed to expand you practice to include this modality into your practice. Videos as well as literature, images, and in-person contact throughout ensures a full understanding and ability to perform this in your practice to greatly enhance the services you provide to get to optimal health in each of your pets.
A second course, Veterinary Orthopedic Manipulation VOM Hands-on Course, 20 1211572 is available to get in-depth hands on experience once this course has been completed.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Beyond Doing Better: Using Behavior Data to Monitor Well-Being in Cats (OnDemand)
courses.description: Safeguarding the well-being of cats is essential to the mission of any responsible animal shelter. Environmental enrichment and behaviour modification are often key to this goal. Measuring response to these interventions is essential to ensure strategies are successful. This webinar will present 4 ordinal rating scales designed to evaluate different expressions of cat behaviour/welfare on a 0-5 scale (modified Fear, Anxiety, and Stress score; Response to Petting score; Participation in Play score; and Food Intake Summary score) that have excellent interobserver agreement and reliability, and a few other tools to describe behaviour in a quantitative way. These tools are exceptionally useful to evaluate the response individual cats have to specific interventions, make decisions about which interventions should be tried first by looking at what was effective in cases presenting similarly in the past, and evaluating the efficacy of different interventions across a population of similar cats in a research project.

courses.title: Veterinary Equine Acupuncture
courses.description: Certification in Equine Acupuncture is a 12-month, part-time, fully on-line course oriented towards applied theory, both traditional and scientific which can be applied to clinical practice. You will be able to develop your confidence and competence during the course with continuous case support from tutors and case forums. You begin your clinical training with simulated cases but rapidly transform to discussion of your own patients and your treatment progress.

courses.title: V&T - Fluid Therapy for Urgent and Emergency Feline & Canine Patients
courses.description: The theme is to have a veterinary specialist and RVT co-present to share relevant and practical knowledge that would appeal to both veterinarians and RVTs in general practice. The goal is to help empower RVTs, as well as showcase how the veterinarian and RVT can best work together and leverage each other's skillsets and expertise. 1) 50-minute plenary session (all attendees are veterinarians and RVTs) providing an overview of critical care. 2) Attendees would then be sent to one of two break-out rooms for a 50-minute workshop (Part 1) -Virtual Breakout Room #1 (this workshop is aimed at GP veterinarians) -Virtual Breakout Room #1 (this workshop is aimed at RVTs) 3) Break, followed by a second 45-minute workshop (Part 2) -Virtual Breakout Room #1 (this workshop is aimed at GP veterinarians) -Virtual Breakout Room #1 (this workshop is aimed at RVTs) 4) Wrap-up plenary session (all attendees) for a 15-minute closing session with q&a

courses.title: Cat Superhighway: The Right Outcome for Every Cat (self-paced course)
courses.description: This course will equip veterinarians and other animal shelter professionals with the tools to implement or enhance pathway planning for cats and kittens, streamlining their journey to the best possible outcome. The course presents research-backed strategies to reduce length of stay, decrease intake and ensure positive outcomes for all cats. The superhighway model enhances community cat programs and increases lifesaving capabilities but also includes flexible "offramps" for unique cases, ensuring that every cat -- whether a friendly community cat or a litter of neonates -- receives the most appropriate care. Participants will learn to confidently navigate challenging decisions with ease, using this model to efficiently manage every cat's pathway to the best available outcome.

courses.title: Purebred Paradox: Disease Risks in Purebred Dogs and the Welfare Implications of Dog Breeding
courses.description: A scientific analysis of breed specific problems and conditions that are of greatest concern to veterinary professionals are discussed in this webinar. Ideas for educating clients who breed dogs or are considering acquiring a purebred puppy are also introduced.

courses.title: Byers AKI and CKD 2023 Anytime
courses.description: Learners will explore relevant physiology, logical diagnostic investigations, and appropriate therapies for AKI and CKD in the fields of emergency/critical care and internal medicine diseases that affect cats and dogs.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: The Only Solution is Fat Infusion: Intralipid Therapy
courses.description: This one-hour presentation will include a comprehensive review of Intravenous Lipid Emulsion (ILE) Therapy, also known as Intralipid Therapy.

courses.title: Two Sides of the Same Coin: Insights from a Specialist & Generalist on Diagnosing & Managing Canine Osteoarthritis Pain
courses.description: Osteoarthritis pain affects around 40% of canine patients yet remains underdiagnosed and undertreated. Because the signs can be subtle and often go unnoticed by pet owners and veterinarians, these dogs suffer in silence, leading to decreased quality of life, disruption of the human-animal bond, and, potentially, premature death. In this webinar, Drs. Melina Zimmerman and Brian Neuman will provide a framework for improving the diagnosis and treatment of canine OA pain and discuss the benefits of a team approach for the clinic, the patient, the pet owner, and the profession.

courses.title: Panel Discussion: Dry Eye Disease - Not just a Schirmer tear test & cyclosporine
courses.description:
Tear film diseases are one of the most common ocular surface problems in practice. There are several types of presentations of Dry Eye Disease (DED), and therefore numerous ways exist to approach diagnosis and treatment, some of which are more controversial. An international panel of world-renowned veterinary ophthalmologists with a special interest in DED will be using an evidence-based approach to discussing the causes, presentations, diagnosis and therapeutic options for companion animals affected by DED.
This session's topic is aimed at general practice veterinarians including those with a special interest in ophthalmology and advanced practitioners.

courses.title: PMP State Reporting for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: This course provides veterinary professionals with essential knowledge and skills for effectively utilizing and complying with Prescription Monitoring Programs (PMPs). Participants will gain a clear understanding of the importance of PMPs in controlled substance management, their specific applicability to veterinary practice, and the procedures for navigating state-specific reporting regulations. The course will cover how to find and interpret data submission guidelines and specifications, ensuring attendees can confidently fulfill their PMP responsibilities and maintain regulatory compliance.

courses.title: A Guide to DEA Compliance in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This comprehensive on-demand course provides veterinary professionals with the knowledge they need to navigate DEA regulations surrounding controlled substance use in veterinary practice. The course covers the legal landscape of controlled substances, DEA compliance responsibilities, proper record-keeping and reconciliation procedures, and strategies for diversion prevention. It is designed for both new professionals and those seeking to refine their knowledge of DEA compliance in their practice. The course takes approximately 1.5 hours to complete and includes multiple quizzes to reinforce key concepts.

courses.title: HPAI Updates for the Exotic Animal Industry
courses.description: This webinar will provide an update to the ongoing highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreak in the United States. On February 8, 2022, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) confirmed Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) A H5N1 virus in a commercial poultry flock in the United States. Since then, USDA has worked swiftly with states and poultry producers to identify and respond to HPAI H5N1 detections. The outbreak of HPAI H5N1 has been widespread globally in wild and domesticated birds; sporadic H5N1 virus infections in mammals have also been reported across the continents of Asia, North America, South America, and Europe. Since late March 2024, USDA, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and state veterinary and public health officials have been responding to detections of H5N1 virus in dairy cows. This webinar will provide a general update on HPAI, along with information pertinent to those within the exotic animal industry space.

courses.title: WEIGHT MANAGEMENT (297-43059)
courses.description: The Weight Management course is designed to give an introduction to canine weight management, the issues caused by poor weight management and strategies for dealing with dogs who may be overweight. An understanding of weight management for dogs, identifying weight management issues particular to the individual pet and the scale of those issues, finding strategies for dealing with overweight and general health and nutrition advice. This course will give you the confidence to engage with owners of pets with weight management issues and give you strategies to help address the weight management issues to improve the health of the pet.

courses.title: Urgent care medicine update
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian with practical information on the current thoughts on the initial management of patients that require urgent but not emergent care. Dr's Butler and Hackett will discuss their approach to deciding on the initial management of these patients along with deciding when to transfer to emergency care.

courses.title: Wellness testing in senior dogs: What to test for and when.
courses.description: This course will take an evidence-based look at screening in healthy senior dogs: what testing to do, how often, and how to use the results. Wellness testing is different from testing to identify disease, and we will look at principles and guidelines for both clinical lab testing and other types of assessments, such as imaging and tools for assessing pain, mobility, cognitive health, and more.

courses.title: HANDLING PUPPIES AND KITTENS TO BE STRESS FREE AS ADULTS (Anytime)
courses.description: Renowned behaviorist Dr. Ian Dunbar discusses the importance of, and techniques for, handling and socialization of puppies and kittens to ensure that they are stress-free as adults, including during clinic visits. Puppies and kittens that have been handled by and socialized with numerous people prior to 12 weeks of age, especially neonatally, thoroughly enjoy being hugged and handled, i.e., restrained and examined, as adults. However, as adults, confident cats and dogs do not require time-consuming, stress-free, egg-shell handling techniques, or physical means of restraint.

courses.title: Home Euthanasia (Online)
courses.description: Home euthanasia has a very different feeling to it than the hospital setting. There are more variables like location, who is present, distractions, and troubleshooting without the support of the full veterinary team. It requires greater flexibility, time management, and client communication skills. This module will outline the top 10 unique components to home euthanasia and help our students build confidence in providing it.

courses.title: PLE-ease: Just Change the Diet? A Practical Approach to Chronic Enteropathies and Protein-Losing Enteropathy
courses.description: Chronic enteropathies (CE) and protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) remain among the most common yet diagnostically challenging gastrointestinal disorders encountered in small animal practice. This lecture provides an evidence-based, practical framework for approaching patients with chronic gastrointestinal disease, emphasizing the recently published 2026 ACVIM Consensus Statement on chronic enteropathies. Attendees will learn how to localize gastrointestinal disease, prioritize diagnostic testing, recognize disorders that mimic PLE, and determine when dietary therapy alone is appropriate versus when advanced diagnostics are warranted. The lecture concludes with a practical discussion of nutritional management, lymphangiectasia, thrombosis prevention, and treatment strategies for dogs with protein-losing enteropathy.

courses.title: THESE TOES WERE MADE FOR MORE THAN SCRATCHING:THE CASE AGAINST FELINE TOE AMPUTATION (Anytime)
courses.description: As a specialist in pain management, Dr. Downing has a unique, expert perspective on issues related to cat declawing (feline toe amputation) and why it should not be performed on cats. During this webinar, Dr. Downing addresses the chronic maladaptive pain and pathologic changes in biomechanics that can result from feline toe amputation, the bioethical violations involved in feline toe amputation and strategies to share with cat owners to encourage cats to use their claws in ways that are acceptable to their human caregivers.

courses.provider: CENTER FOR FOOD SECURITY AND PUBLIC HEALTH COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE IOWA S
courses.title: Zoonoses: Protecting People and Animals in Rural Communities
courses.description:
The Zoonoses: Protecting People and Animals in Rural Communities web-based course provides any animal health, human health, public health professional or student with an overview of zoonoses related to cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, horses and poultry. Lessons focus on key zoonotic diseases, ways to identify disease exposure risks for people and animals, and how to communicate prevention with clients, including those that may be immunocompromised. Lesson material is delivered in 3 formats: short, narrated presentations (videos), podcasts (audio only), or printable lecture transcripts (PDF). The course incorporates scenarios (e.g., case-based situations) to highlight specific zoonotic disease prevention measures, and demonstrate methods for effectively communicating risks in rural community settings.
This course will help participants
1. Explain the impacts of zoonotic diseases on animal and human health in rural communities
2. Recognize the areas for increased risks for zoonoses in farm settings
3. Understand the role of veterinary personnel in zoonotic disease prevention
4. Gain confidence assessing zoonotic risks and communicating key prevention measures and strategies with your clients and community

courses.title: Where Will the Good Dogs Come From? (Anytime)
courses.description: In this talk, we will explore the current and future landscape of the acquisition of dogs. An increase in demand for dogs has made finding a good dog challenging, and this looming crisis has come to a head as demand has spiked during the pandemic. A lack of puppies or behaviorally sound adult dogs in shelters, irresponsible breeding, multi-year waiting lists, and dog breeds riddled with genetically mediated health issues are among the many concerns that make finding an acceptable dog, let alone a good dog, very challenging. In a culture where an owner's expectations of what a "good" dog means may differ from what breeders and shelters think is reasonable, how can a dog owner feel confident that they will find a healthy, long-lived dog who will make a behaviorally sound pet or sport dog? Many social rules define appropriate and ethical breeding, but how might these rules change in the future to make it easier for ethical breeders to produce healthy, behaviorally sound dogs destined for pet homes?

courses.title: Controlling Controlled Drugs (TECH163)
courses.description: Are you sure the controlled drug policies for your practice comply with DEA regulations? This course provides practical guidance on controlled substance accountability in the veterinary hospital. Get an overview of current DEA regulations, including registration, ordering, security, dispensing, accountability, inventories, and common problem-resolution scenarios in a veterinary practice setting.

courses.title: Spinal Cord Trauma (EMRG220)
courses.description: This course will cover emergency stabilization, management and analgesia for acute spinal trauma patients, neurological evaluation, diagnostic procedures and prognosis for animals suffering from spinal trauma injuries and best anesthesia practices for those patients requiring advanced diagnostic imaging and/or surgery.

courses.title: Managing the trauma patient
courses.description: Veterinarians who participate in this course will learn from our Trauma Team comprised of an emergency critical care specialist, a soft tissue surgeon and an orthopedic surgeon. They will be guided thru life-saving care to wound care to abdominal surgery and to basic care for fractures & luxations. This team uses real life clinical cases, video examples, practical tips and audience response devices to keep the discussion lively, interactive, relevant and fun. Upon completion of the seminar, the participant should have a better understanding of what is involved in the initial diagnosis and management of the trauma patient along with further knowledge of how to manage the patient that then requires surgical intervention.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Ergonomics for Veterinary Staff
courses.description:
The goal of ergonomics is to improve the interaction between people and their environments by reducing physical strain, mental stress, and the risk of injury.
In this course, we will explore the importance of ergonomics in the veterinary profession and how it can be applied to ensure the health and safety of those who care for the animals.

courses.title: Managing Behavior Cases in Primary Care
courses.description:
We will explore how to best manage behavior cases in primary care practices.
https://vvbm.vet/events/

courses.title: Advanced glycation end products in differently processed pet foods and the implications for companion animal disease
courses.description: Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) are a group of heterogenous compounds formed during heat driven non-enzymatic reactions between simple sugars and any compounds containing an amide group such as protein or nucleic acids. These are a subset of Maillard reaction products (MRPs) that have been identified in ultra-processed human foods and have been associated with several degenerative and inflammatory diseases. These AGEs may be divided into dietary (dAGEs) that are exogenous as they come from food or described as endogenous when they are formed as part of normal physiologic processes in the body. The receptor for AGEs (RAGE) has several isoforms which mediate cellular and serum AGE activity. Cellular RAGE binds to AGEs to initiate and sustain inflammation within cells while soluble RAGE acts as a scavenger to remove circulating AGEs. The objective of this study was to quantify AGEs in differently processed pet foods (two ultra-processed- canned and kibble; one moderately processed- air-dried; and one mildly cooked), determine the effect on serum and urine AGE concentration when these foods were fed to healthy dogs and investigate the effect on serum RAGE concentration in response to the different processed diets. All AGE concentrations were measured using ultra-high performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry and RAGE was quantified using a commercially available kit. Total dAGEs was highest in the canned food and in the serum of dogs when this food was fed. There was no difference in total urine AGEs or serum RAGE concentration. This study was exploratory in nature, serving as the foundation for future prospective studies and identifies the domestic dog as a proposed animal model for human diseases related to consumption of differently processed foods.

courses.title: Evidence Based Equine Rehabilitation (EBER) & Examination
courses.description:
This is a unique online Evidence based Equine Rehabilitation course from the Academy of Animal Sport Science (AASS). Accessible to everyone who wants to learn, this 67 hour, 37 lecture course is presented by the worlds leading specialists.
Eligible licensed equine professionals may continue with the residential practical course and pursue the AASS Animal Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation certificate.
This course takes 67 hours to complete all lectures in full including the guided study, self quizzes at the end of each lecture as well as the final exam. Students have 1 year to complete all 37 lectures, guided study and sefl-quizzes. The final exam is complete within 1 month of the final lecture.

courses.title: Coaching, Reviews, and Feedback (STAF194)
courses.description:
When do we give coaching, reviews, or feedback, and how can we tell the difference between them?
In this course, we'll focus on how to nurture a perfect-10 superstar employee. We will discuss how and when to use coaching sessions, performance reviews, and feedback meetings appropriately to outline expectations and deliver information to employees. You'll learn how to calculate and give raises based on goal achievement, enhanced skill development, or positive behavior. We'll also address how to correct substandard performance - and when to call it quits and steer a substandard performer right out the front door of the practice for good.

courses.title: Reporting Suspected Abuse: A Roadmap for the Veterinary Community
courses.description: Veterinary professionals are often the first to detect animal abuse as you interact with your clients and patients. Therefore, it is critically important that you have the skills and tools needed to recognize and report abuse. This special three-part webinar series covers all aspects of veterinary involvement in an abuse case, from recognition and documentation, hospital procedures, and the veterinarian's role in the legal case.

courses.title: Obesity & Laminitis: Keep the horse's mind and body healthy while restricting diet
courses.description:
Weight management of the modern equid is a challenge for many horse, mule and donkey owners. Obesity and the associated health-related impacts are well-documented with equine laminitis being the consequence of greatest welfare concern.
Equine laminitis is a common and debilitating condition resulting in pain and lameness in the affected feet. Laminitis has been found to affect between 1.5% and 34% of horses worldwide and it is estimated that 1 in 10 horses in Britain will develop an episode every year. The majority of laminitis episodes are considered to be endocrinopathic in nature; specifically linked with the inability of the horse to properly regulate their insulin levels in the blood, resulting in hyperinsulinaemia (referred to as insulin dysregulation [ID]). Insulin dysregulation is a key component of Equine Metabolic Syndrome (EMS) and while not all animals with EMS will be overweight, most EMS horses will have general and/or regional adiposity.
Management changes which induce weight loss (usually dietary restriction alongside exercise where possible) have been shown to improve or even reverse ID and are important in the management of horses with EMS and ultimately help reduce the risk of laminitis.
However, common methods of dietary restriction can be at odds with the innate behaviours and physiology of a horse i.e. a herd animal that needs to move and trickle feed on high fibre forage (including both grazing and browsing-type behaviours) for up to 18 out of 24 hours.
This webinar takes a holistic approach to the subject of obesity and laminitis, particularly focusing on how we can provide horses with options to promote loss of excess fat, maintain a healthy body condition and reduce the risk of laminitis while still enabling them to be a horse and live a rich life.

courses.title: EQ100: Equinology Equine Body Worker Certification Course
courses.description:
The unique Equinology Equine Body Work approach is a hands-on system that addresses the whole body, implementing specific manual palpation methods to assess soft tissue and symmetry of muscle and structure. Students will learn how to utilize detailed static and dynamic evaluation strategies to inform their sessions. Students will be shown how to combine a range of body work techniques, including sports massage, soft tissue mobilization, stretching, range of motion and positioning exercises as well as focal point work (stress and trigger points) to provide optimal support for horses working in every discipline.
The EQ100 Certification program is designed for students who wish to pursue a career in equine body work, and is regularly attended by veterinarians, veterinary technicians, physical therapists, human massage therapists, and chiropractors who wish to enhance their skills or continue their education.
The subject matter for this course is presented in a variety of mediums. The classroom lectures (incorporating discussions, visual presentations, illustrations, videos, bones and specimens) will prepare the student for the hands-on practical labs (both in the classroom and on the horse). The lab practicals vary depending on the topic and are supported by templates, labelling sessions, gait analysis sessions, muscle and surface anatomy identification and hands-on sessions. Additional independent study is required in the evenings, which is evaluated through self-assessments and quizzes.
This course also requires pre-course distance study in skeletal anatomy and a post-course externship demonstrating the skills and techniques learned in class. The EQ100 has been recognized by the International Veterinary Chiropractic Association and counts for 50 CE Hours for the National Certification Board for Therapeutic Massage & Bodywork (the maximum number of hours allowed).

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Five Domains Model for Animal Welfare Assessment (On Demand)
courses.description:
Animal well-being represents how an animal experiences their life. It characterizes the overall mental experiences of an animal and is a subjective concept that cannot be directly measured. Instead, well-being indicators are used to cautiously infer mental experiences from resource provisions, management factors and a range of animal-based measures. The Five Domains Model is a holistic and structured framework for gathering together these indicators and assessing animal well-being. It is used to systematically assess the well-being of animals in a range of contexts and explicitly focuses on an animal's mental experiences.
The Five Domains Model is used internationally to assess animal well-being in a range of contexts. The Model also represents a framework that could be used to advance animal care -- by drawing attention to a wide range of areas where we can make improvements. While animal well-being is an animal-centered concept ( i.e., the focus is on assessing an animal's mental experiences), animal care is human-centered (i.e., the focus is on what we can provide for animals). Animal care encourages those responsible for animals to consider providing them with a range of opportunities so that they can have a good life. The aim of this presentation is to demonstrate how the Five Domains can be used to scientifically assess animal well-being and how they also provide a means of considering how best to care for animals.

courses.title: Small Animal Programme 2021
courses.description: This programme includes 37 hours of world-class CPD, delivered by experts in the field. The main objective is to keep veterinarians up to date with the latest insights into small animals. Topics covered range from internal medicine, ophthalmology, oncology, internal medicine and much more.

courses.title: Making Your Practice Feline Friendly (PRAC150)
courses.description: Whether you are an assistant, a technician, a new grad vet, or a seasoned practitioner - we've all seen cats that cause us to groan when they appear on the schedule. There are often tips and tricks to deal with these problematic kitties and the sometimes-difficult owners that accompany them! This course is a compilation of ideas, concepts, practical tips, and tricks aimed to help you evaluate your practice and look for ways to improve the experience of working with cats for the entire staff, clients, and of course - the cats themselves.

courses.provider: CENTER FOR FOOD SECURITY AND PUBLIC HEALTH COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE IOWA S
courses.title: Biosecurity in Livestock and Poultry Production: Basic
courses.description: Veterinary personnel must be trained in biosecurity to protect the health of U.S. livestock and poultry. This 3-hour program provides a comprehensive biosecurity education that is not affiliated with a particular species, industry, or program.

courses.title: Is there more to this than behavior?
courses.description: This course covers the work-up of behavioral cases with regard to medical differential diagnoses. It includes a discussion of behavioral clinical signs that may indicate an underlying medical disorder as well as approach to diagnosis of both the medical and behavioral disorder as well as a brief discussion on treatment of behavioral disorders that involve medical diagnoses.

courses.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound and the Diagnosis of Congestive Heart Failure
courses.description: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) examination of the heart, lungs and pleural space are becoming well accepted for the rapid diagnosis of congestive heart failure in dogs and cats. In this lecture, we will further expand on the specific POCUS findings together with other clinical assessments that will increase your confidence of diagnosis for left-sided and right-sided congestive heart failure.

courses.title: Periodontal Disease: Treatments, Adjuncts, and an Exciting New Option
courses.description: Periodontal disease is the most common illness in our companion animals, and it can be deadly. We will provide a quick review of what periodontal disease is, why it's such a problem for companion animals, as well as how to diagnose it, treat it, and prevent it in dogs and cats. From there, we will provide an overview of available adjunctive therapies, including a novel product containing hyaluronic acid alongside its supporting data.

courses.title: Whiskers Underwater: A Deep Dive into Feline Medicine
courses.description: This program contains eight lecture hours on various topics in feline medicine and practice. Topics include dentistry, lower urinary tract diseases and surgery, dermatology, GI diseases, cat friendly practice, and behavioral medicine including inappropriate elimination.

courses.title: Occlusal Equilibration & Diagnostic Module 1
courses.description: Occlusal Equilibration & Diagnostic Module 1 is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: The Neuropsychology of Resilience: Polyvagal Practices for Sustainable Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Veterinary professionals work in high-stakes environments where emotional resilience is essential for sustainable practice. This workshop provides science-based education on the neuropsychology of stress and resilience, tailored for veterinarians and veterinary technicians. Participants will learn practical strategies to recognize nervous system states, regulate emotional responses, and integrate micro-recovery practices into their daily workflow. Designed as professional skills training, this program equips attendees with actionable tools to prevent burnout and maintain effectiveness in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: Managing refractory allergic dermatitis and otitis externa in dogs
courses.description: This lecture will cover the diagnostic approach to complex canine allergy cases, and we will discuss multimodal management strategies for more successful outcomes.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Not All Cats Want a Couch: Using Research for Decisions on Working Cat Placements (On Demand)
courses.description:
Recent research published in the Journal of Shelter Medicine and Community Animal Health highlights an important truth: not every cat is suited for life in a traditional home. Using the Feline Spectrum Assessment (FSA), the study revealed that cats least likely to be socialized were more fearful, less affectionate, and less amenable to handling post-adoption (even by their primary caretaker) compared to their more socialized counterparts. Adopters of these cats were also more likely to report their cat would have been happier outside, underscoring the need for shelters to carefully match cats with appropriate placement pathways. This evidence helps confirm what many in sheltering already know -- while adoption is an ideal outcome for many cats, it is not the right outcome for every cat.
In the case of cats for which a traditional adoption pathway would not be appropriate and TNR/RTF is not possible, working cat or barn cat programs provide a humane and practical alternative. But careful consideration must be given to ensure the cat is medically appropriate, the placement site is suitable and safe, and that the transition into a new environment is conducted in a thoughtful, stepwise way. At Toronto Humane Society, cats identified as barn cat candidates are selected using the FSA alongside behavioral history and ongoing monitoring of in-shelter behavior modification progress, then integrated using a structured acclimation process: a period of crate confinement, followed by exploration in a secure space such as a tack room, before eventual free-roam. This approach maximizes welfare and sets both the cat and placement site up for long-term success.

courses.title: 51st Annual IVAS Congress On Demand
courses.description:
The objective of the 51st Annual IVAS Congress is to provide top quality continuing education which advances the knowledge and skills of veterinarians in the areas of acupuncture, acupuncture related and East-Asian medical therapy, including Chinese herbal medicine, laser and Chinese Food & Tui-Na therapies.
Continuing education is provided through online on-demand lectures led by presenters known as experts in veterinary acupuncture medicine. Session tracks include small animal and large.
Each presentation is given live first and recorded for viewing later on-demand, through our online learning platform. For each hour of an on-demand presentation the RACE required 5 questions are provided and each attendee must receive a 70% or above to receive RACE hours and the grades are recorded for each attendee through our learning platform quiz application.

courses.title: Increasing Comfort Level with Behavior Cases
courses.description: This training module focuses on enhancing the ability to effectively address behavioral health concerns by covering several key areas. Participants will learn to differentiate between prevention and intervention behavior cases through the use of behavioral triage, allowing for more accurate and timely responses. The course also emphasizes the importance of establishing a standard operating procedure for strategically inquiring about a patient's behavioral health, tailored to different life stages. Additionally, attendees will be introduced to the essential components of a behavior treatment plan, gaining insight into how these elements support patient outcomes. The module further highlights the value of creating a dedicated behavior team, with clearly defined roles for each member to ensure coordinated care. Finally, it underscores the necessity of knowing when to refer cases to other professionals, particularly when situations extend beyond one's expertise or comfort level, thereby promoting ethical and effective practice.

courses.title: Safe & Successful Sedation: Every Patient, Every Procedure
courses.description: Whether to facilitate a minor laceration repair, obtain radiographs, or perform an otoscopic examination on a fractious dog, veterinarians often rely on sedation to safely perform many clinical procedures. But with so many sedative drugs in the toolbox, how do we choose the best protocol for our patient and the intended procedure? Using a case-based approach, this webinar will review how best to utilize different drugs to produce a safe sedative experience. Because unstable pets present a unique sedative challenge, each case will feature a hemodynamic, respiratory, neurologic, or attitude challenge. Clinical pearls will ensure the learner is prepared to anticipate and address complications for different comorbidities and drug combinations.

courses.title: CANIS Conference
courses.description: Brought to you by Aggressive Dog and APDT International, the CANIS Conference (Canine Advocacy, Networking, Innovation, and Science) is not your average industry event. It is a celebration of all things dog. Over four energizing days, trainers, behavior consultants, veterinarians, shelter and rescue workers, sport dog handlers, and pet care professionals come together to learn, connect, and spark new ideas. With five engaging educational tracks, live demonstrations, and extensive networking opportunities, CANIS is where science meets passion, innovation sparks ideas, and the future of dog welfare takes center stage.

courses.title: Introduction to Saddle Fitting
courses.description:
This course is for veterinarians, equine professionals and interested owners.
It is an in-depth look at the evidence-based principles of saddle fit for English and Western saddles, with practical evaluating and fitting techniques.

courses.title: Taking the Fear out of Bottle Feeding and Basic Kitten Care
courses.description: Did you know healthy neonatal kittens do NOT need to be fed every two hours? Learn about the latest guidelines for kitten feeding and other kitten care in this course. The course was developed by the Kitten College at the Animal Welfare League of Arlington in Arlington, VA to help their foster caregivers raise happy, healthy kittens. The first kitten nursery of its kind, Arlington went from saving 92 kittens a year in 2016 to over 1500 kittens in 2023. Since its inception, the Kitten College program has been implemented in a growing number of shelters and rescues across the country.

courses.title: Foot-and-Mouth Disease Emergency Preparation Course for Canada
courses.description:
