This comprehensive four-week, seven-module, hybrid live webinar and online virtual course is designed to equip veterinarians with the necessary skills to diagnose and investigate outbreaks of Food-and-Mouth Disease (FMD), emphasizing their pivotal role in implementing emergency disease control measures (biosecurity, contingency planning and vaccination), involving one, three-part scenario and a final knowledge assessment.
This course is also open to other personnel in animal agriculture (including epidemiologists, veterinary technicians and technologists, and other animal health and welfare emergency management specialists).
After completing this course, participants will have increased knowledge of how to:
- Diagnose FMD through clinical and laboratory examination;
- Conduct an epidemiological enquiry for FMD;
- Enter and leave infected premises in a biosecure manner to prevent the potential introduction and spread of FMD virus; and
- Advise livestock owners on the control measures involved in regaining FMD-free status.

courses.title: Kellogg West Symposium 2026
courses.description: During this full day symposium AALAS members and non-members come together to experience lectures and networking. The program is designed to have topics relevant to the entire membership.

courses.title: Mental Fitness Training For Vet Med
courses.description:
This course combines the Positive Intelligence 7-week Foundations program with 7 live private sessions with the course instructor to help veterinarians and technicians build the skills and habits needed for sustained personal and professional growth.
Grounded in neuroscience, cognitive behavioral psychology, and positive psychology, this program empowers participants with the skills for:
*Enhanced self-awareness, resilience, and emotional intelligence
*Reduced self-judgment and greater confidence
*Improved relationships at work and at home
*Improved mental focus and performance
*Sustained stress-reduction, improved happiness, faster recovery-time from negative experiences.
This is an evidence-based, science-backed, globally proven program that has achieved results for more than 1,000,000 participants in 50 countries.
To receive Continuing Education Credit for this program, participants must complete all 7 teaching modules, attend 7 live sessions with the course instructor, and document 5-10 minutes of daily practice using the PQ app.
Who Should Enroll?
This program is ideal for veterinarians, practice managers, and technicians committed to improving performance, reducing stress, and building lasting positive mental habits. It is especially beneficial for professionals seeking a science-based, structured approach to mental well-being.

courses.title: Neuroradiology Basics (DIAG422)
courses.description: This course will cover common neuroradiology concepts and techniques. First through identifying normal anatomy structure and then introducing common abnormal presentations. Covering the skull, brain, vertebral column and intervertebral disc diseases and neoplasia.

courses.title: Cockfighting Investigations
courses.description: This 1 hour webinar covers the basics of forensic investigation of cockfighting and is geared towards veterinary and law enforcement professionals. The basics of cockfighting, including related paraphernalia, will be discussed as well as crime scene analysis and handling of both live and dead birds.

courses.title: 2026 BARC Behaviour and Rehabilitation Conference: Diagnosing & Treating Lameness and Behaviour Like A Pro
courses.description: This inaugural Canadian conference featuring the latest diagnostics, treatment options, and research for veterinarians interested in all aspects of behaviour or musculoskeletal issues, including those with certification in rehabilitation, acupuncture, chiropractic care, or those who focus on post-injury recovery, surgery, lameness, neurological issues, and arthritis. It will be held in person, in British Columbia, Canada, on Saturday, September 12 and Sunday, September 13, 2026. The CE sessions will cover new research, trends, and treatment plans for lameness, pain, rehabilitation, and behaviour, including behaviour affect on post-injury and surgery, neurological issues, and arthritis, providing attendees with immediately usable information. There are 11 sessions on two individual streams for rehabilitation and behaviour, as well as 3 dual stream sessions bringing together behaviour specialists, rehabilitation specialists, and general practitioners who will learn new ways of working together.

courses.title: CRANIAL CRUCIATE LIGAMENT DISEASE PART 3: EXTRACAPSULAR STIFLE STABILIZATION TECHNIQUE (195-41359)
courses.description: This lecture is designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn/refine the lateral suture technique and to understand the major advantages of PowerX Crimping System. The ExCap Lateral Fabello-Tibial Suture technique will be taught in a step-by-step fashion. This lecture will discuss isometric points for suture placement, proper approach to the stifle, removal of the cruciate remnants, identification of the proper placement of the suture, and how to secure the ExCap suture using a precise crimping system. courses.title: The Business of Canine Rehabilitati
courses.description:
The Business of Canine Rehabilitation course was designed to assist professionals with the knowledge and skills to establish and run a successful canine rehabilitation facility. Canine rehabilitation can look many different ways inclusive of stand alone facilities, mobile practices, or adjuncts to hospital programs. Participants will learn about market trends, effective business strategies, facility planning and advanced treatment modalities. Through interactive case studies, real world applications, and the latest industry insights, this course will prepare you to thrive in the competitive field of canine rehabilitation.
Our lead instructor, Dr. Deb Torraca, created the original Business of Canine Rehabilitation Course in 2013. Much has changed in the world of canine rehabilitation, including the business considerations of owning and operating a canine rehabilitation practice. As a successful canine rehabilitation practice owner, Dr. Torraca has been at the forefront of these changes.
She has teamed up with Anthony Schena to provide the most up to date and relevant information for the business side of canine rehabilitation. This course is a valuable resource for those that own their own canine rehabilitation practice, future rehabbers/owners, and those that are affiliated with an existing practice that offers canine rehabilitation.

Attendees will learn practical instructions for operating circle and non-rebreathing systems, performing pressure checks of each system, and understand steps in troubleshooting common problems. courses.title: Getting to Know Yourself (VCAS108)
courses.description: There are individual personal preferences in daily life and clinical practice, affecting ourselves, colleagues, and clients. courses.title: Communication and Conflict Resolution for Thriving Workplaces

Effective communication among teams is a reliable predictor of job satisfaction and is also associated with lower burnout scores. During this webinar, the different forms of conflict will be described with practical strategies for addressing conflict with others. Methods for engaging in compassionate (non-violent) communication with colleagues and team members will also be shared with examples of statements and phrases that will foster collaboration rather than confrontation. All members of the veterinary team will benefit from learning these tools for the betterment of their personal and professional wellbeing.

courses.title: THE FINAL JOURNEY GUIDING PET PARENTS THROUGH END OF LIFE DECISION MAKING
courses.description:
THE FINAL JOURNEY
This is an in depth course designed to assist veterinarians and veterinary technicians with communications and situations involving euthanasia, end of life decisions, death and grief. Confidence in navigating this area increases professional career satisfaction and personal life satisfaction.

In this on-demand course, we will provide an update on various scientific, technical, and clinical aspects of transfusion medicine. Experts in the field will share their take on recent or interesting literature, as well as their valuable experience, on new usage of blood components, the role of transfusion medicine in conditions such as immune-mediated hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia, transfusion reactions, blood compatibility and challenges in feline blood transfusion including xenotransfusion.

courses.title: Fear Free Rehab: Reducing FAS in Canine & Feline Patients During Therapy
courses.description: To equip veterinary rehabilitation professionals with the knowledge and strategies to recognize, prevent, and reduce Fear, Anxiety, and Stress (FAS) in canine and feline patients during therapy, ensuring improved patient welfare, cooperation, and clinical outcomes.

courses.title: Isn't That Just Medicine? Spectrum of Care
courses.description:
Veterinarians are in the unique and challenging position of balancing the medical needs of their patients with the emotional, physical, and financial needs of their clients and their own moral and legal obligations to both. Embracing the spectrum of care can help to accomplish this delicate balancing act.
Spectrum of care is the idea that in every situation there is a range of options - both diagnostically and therapeutically - for patients and clients. More invasive, extensive, and expensive options fall on one end of the spectrum while less invasive, more cost-effective options fall on the other, with a wide range of middle ground options in between. Within this range is the best fit for each individual patient and client. The right choice will maximize the patient's quality of life within the client's limitations.

courses.title: Ultrasound-Guided Regional Anesthetic Techniques - Case-Discussions and Q&A
courses.description: The series consists of 7 on-demand modules that can be worked through at your leisure and is taught by the organizers of the 'Cornell Regional Anesthesia Boot Camp'. Each session will introduce different ultrasound-guided regional anesthetic techniques that can be used to provide anesthesia and analgesia for commonly performed surgical procedures in small animals.

courses.title: Applied Biomechanics for the Performance Dog
courses.description:
Biomechanics is the study of the mechanics of biological activity. It can be used by the an owner, trainer, handler or Veterinarian to optimize, improve, enhance canine performance or diagnose performance issues. Biomechanics and its application to athletic or work performance is called Kinesiology. Kinesiology is the study of human and animal movement, performance, and function. It is made up kinematics and kinetics. Kinematics is the branch that studies the geometry of motion. It describes motion in terms of how far something moves (e.g. stride length), how fast something moves (e.g. speed), how long something moves (e.g. stride time), and how consistently something moves (e.g. stride rate). The motion described may be linear (in a straight line) or angular (in a circular path). Kinetics is the branch that studies the forces of movement. It describes the causes of motion, or the forces involved. Static states are where all of the forces are balanced and the body is in equilibrium. Dynamic states are where the forces are not balanced and the body changes or moves in relation to the resulting force variance. This information is helpful when describing or communicating about how a dog moves. It can be used to establish normal movement parameters, identify movement alterations or to determine optimal movement patterns related to activity or performance.
It is the intent of this course to introduce the applications of Kinesiology (Biomechanics) to the student in a functional manner. This is very helpful when the professional is developing a training regimen, conditioning program, identifying performance deficiencies, or making decisions related to a rehabilitative program.

If you only ever attend one webinar series about how legal guidelines can be used to your advantage to decrease unnecessary intakes, shorten shelter stays and improve outcomes, let this be the one. courses.title: Feline Tooth Resorption: What to Extract, What to Amputate, What to Leave, and Why
courses.description:
Feline tooth resorption is one of the most prevalent oral pathologies in cats and represents a significant source of chronic oral pain. Despite its frequency, the condition is often underdiagnosed due to subtle clinical presentation and reliance on visual examination alone. Many affected patients exhibit minimal outward signs despite advanced pathology, making accurate diagnosis dependent on a systematic approach that includes full-mouth intraoral radiography. Appropriate treatment planning requires a thorough understanding of disease classification, radiographic interpretation, and surgical decision-making.
On physical examination, clinicians may observe gross changes that raise suspicion for tooth resorption, including gingival migration along the crown of the tooth, focal areas of gingival inflammation, or visible crown defects. In some cases, teeth may appear clinically absent due to advanced resorption, despite retained root structures within the alveolus. These findings, even in the absence of overt pain behaviors, support the need for anesthetized oral examination and diagnostic imaging. The course will emphasize how these clinical findings can be used to justify general anesthesia to clients as both a diagnostic and therapeutic necessity.
This course provides a comprehensive review of feline tooth resorption, including current understanding of pathophysiology, classification systems, and disease progression. Emphasis is placed on case-based learning, application of extraction techniques, and critical evaluation of the limitations of dental radiography in diagnosis and treatment planning. While radiography remains essential, its limitations in early lesion detection and interpretation are addressed. The multifactorial and incompletely understood etiology is discussed in the context of current veterinary literature, including proposed roles of odontoclastic activity, chronic inflammation, periodontal disease, and age-related changes.

Join Dr. Terry W. Fossum, world-renowned veterinary surgeon and author of the best-selling textbook Small Animal Surgery, as she unveils her groundbreaking research on oleander (Nerium indicum) in veterinary medicine. courses.title: The Science & Clinical Application of Serum Amyloid A

courses.title: Introduction to wildlife forensic entomology and the application of insect biology to animal welfare cases
courses.description: Forensic Entomology is a multifaceted discipline of forensic science that is focused on the application of insect biology toward legal matters. The primary focus of the discipline has historically been centered on death investigations, especially the application of insect development to estimation of portions of the postmortem interval (PMI) or timing of insect colonization (TOC). Various species of necrophagous flies are the 'stars' of forensic entomology, with several recognized for their keen sense of olfaction, resulting in detection and arrival on a corpse or carrion within minutes of death. The same volatile compounds of death serve as attractants, albeit far less concentrated, to flies in instances of lesions or wounds associated with neglect or abuse. Insects developing on a decedent can also serve as matrices for toxicological or DNA analysis, as well as in detection of gunshot or explosives residues. This presentation will introduce the basic principles of forensic entomology and discuss the major uses of entomological evidence toward medicolegal investigations. A specific focus will be on wildlife forensic entomology, emphasizing the types of cases relevant to veterinary and wildlife forensics and the insects that commonly serve as evidence in animal welfare cases.

courses.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors & the Diabetic Cat: What We've Learned So Far
courses.description: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have emerged as an exciting new treatment option for feline diabetes mellitus. The SGLT2 inhibitor drug class controls hyperglycemia by promoting glucosuria via selective blockade of renal glucose reabsorption, and several recent veterinary publications have added to the collective knowledge of the importance of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy for diabetes treatment. With US approval of these drugs having occurred only recently, it is equally important to remain abreast of new information gleaned from veterinarians' experiences with the clinical use of these drugs. To provide listeners with a comprehensive update of SGLT2 inhibitor use in cats, this presentation will integrate the pharmacologic and physiologic basis for SGLT2 inhibitor use, results from recent research, and input from veterinarians who have used these drugs in clinical patients.

courses.title: LafeberVet Barron Sea Turtle Program Application
courses.description: Presented in conjunction with the Wildlife Disease Association, this webinar will outline the regulatory, anatomical, diagnostic, and therapeutic considerations involved in sea turtle rehabilitation. Sea turtle rehabilitation in the United States emphasizes the need for compliance with state and federal rules, often requiring special licensure. Seven sea turtle species are typically threatened or endangered, with anthropogenic threats driving conservation and clinical care efforts. Anatomy details cover the carapace, plastron, and shell structure, including scute patterns and bone derivation. Diagnostics prioritize a thorough physical exam, baseline temperature, imaging, blood work, and fecal analysis, with careful choice of sampling sites and anticoagulants to minimize stress. Critical care stresses graded fluid therapy, rewarming, analgesia, and cautious antibiotic use, while supportive care emphasizes rehydration, nutrition, and, if needed, enteric or parenteral feeding. Therapeutics discuss anesthesia protocols, multimodal analgesia, and a broad empiric antimicrobial/antifungal plan. Common presentations include fibropapillomatosis, plastic ingestion, buoyancy disorders, and trauma from human activities, all of which influence prognosis and potential euthanasia.

courses.title: Balancing CKD Management with GI and Dermatological Comorbidities
courses.description: This course covers important information around chronic kidney disease in dogs and cats, specifically when other comorbidities are present, such as gastrointestinal and dermatological issues. In this course, you will learn about the tug of war that is present when looking to manage CKD nutritionally while taking the other concurrent conditions into account. We will also cover the recommendations for nutritional management for both dogs and cats with CKD and GI and Dermatological issues. You will come away with a better understanding of the crucial nutritional balance needed for successful management of these diseases.

courses.title: Sepsis and Septic Shock (DRIP105)
courses.description: This course will begin with a review of relevant pathophysiology. Diagnostics and tips for accurately identifying patients with sepsis and septic shock will be discussed, along with important points on treatment options.

courses.title: Role of the Veterinary Surgical Scrub Technician (TECH458)
courses.description: Often described as the surgeon's primary assistant, veterinary surgical scrub technicians (VSSTs) play a vital role on the surgical team. To be a great scrub tech, you need to be familiar with the surgical procedure and the surgeon's preferences and needs, and you must be able to anticipate, even when things go wrong. VSSTs can also help clients understand and follow the veterinarian's recommendations surrounding their pet's surgical procedure and can assist with client education during all phases of care, from pre-operative preparation through full recovery.

courses.title: Pharmaceuticals in a Multimodal Behavior Plan: Strategic Use in the Treatment of Fear, Stress, & Anxiety
courses.description: The use of pharmaceuticals in veterinary behavioral medicine extends far beyond suppression of clinical signs, serving as a critical tool for improving patient welfare, facilitating learning, and interrupting maladaptive emotional cycles. In this webinar, Dr. Christopher Pachel will explore how medications fit within a multimodal treatment framework for fear-, stress-, and anxiety-related disorders, with an emphasis on thoughtful, case-specific decision-making. Dr. Pachel will also review how untreated behavioral conditions can impact patient safety and quality of life and increase risk for relinquishment, reinforcing the importance of timely and appropriate intervention. Attendees will also explore the major classes of psychotropic medications, including their mechanisms of action, clinical applications, and roles as maintenance or situational supports. Practical guidance will be provided on aligning medication strategies with behavior modification plans and caregiver capacity. Throughout, the focus will remain on improving patient outcomes through integrated, ethical, and evidence-informed care.

courses.title: KYON: An Introduction to Patellar Groove Replacement (PGR) Online Course
courses.description: KYON: An Introduction to Patellar Groove Replacement (PGR) Online Course is an online course designed to review the partial knee replacement procedure used to treat patella luxation in dogs of and cats of all sizes by reducing arthritic pain associated with chronic knee luxation. KYON: An Introduction to PGR is designed to review when, why, and how to use PGR to treat patella luxation. Further course topics are case studies and relevant research.

courses.title: Treatment of Hypoadrenocorticism
courses.description: The presenter reviews the treatment of hypoadrenocorticism. Focus areas include emergency management, maintenance and monitoring, and troubleshooting and frequently asked questions. Prioritization of issues for the critically ill patient are discussed, including addressing hyperkalemia and bradycardia. Fluid resuscitation and cortisol replacement are also discussed. The multiple treatment options available for maintenance treatment are discussed as well.

courses.title: Medicinal Plants (ALTM401)
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss some of the plants found in nature which might have medicinal applications, as well as some harvesting and preparation techniques that can be used for these plants. This course is not meant as a complete tutorial on medicinal herbs, nor does it heavily cover the diagnosis and treatment of disease entities rather it is meant as an aid in the identification of medicinal plants, proper preparation, their chemical properties and potential indications.

courses.title: Knowledge is Power - Strengthening the Regulatory Veterinarian's Clinical and Scientific Expertise
courses.description: RegVet CE is designed with content specific to the responsibilities assigned to and skills required of racing regulatory veterinarians who often are tasked with overseeing the safety, welfare, and integrity if the horseracing industry, specifically its equine athletes. This continuing education program is designed to provide clinical and scientific tools to aide regulatory veterinarians in accomplishing their day-to-day responsibilities, the theme of this meeting is "Knowledge is Power - Strengthening the Regulatory Veterinarian's Clinical and Scientific Expertise". The content of this meeting will focus on a deep dive into the use of diagnostics, covering cardio-pulmonary and musculoskeletal systems, as a tool to aide decision making, review of new research into emerging technologies to identify risk factors with the possibility of preventing exercise associated sudden death, a review of how to clinically recognize lameness in the context of the pre-race exam using case videos, review of case histories to use as tools for risk assessment strategies, communication workshop and how to have the difficult conversation, overview of human sport approach to anti-doping, review of climate smart competition protocols and their application to racing, USDA's perspective on recent Equine Infectious Anemia outbreaks. The overall learning objective is to foster enhanced and uniform standards or practice among regulatory veterinarians across all domestic and international racing jurisdictions.

courses.title: No More Cat Wrangling: Techniques for Feline-Friendly Handling
courses.description: Many cats experience fear, anxiety, and stress during handling and veterinary visits, leading to various negative consequences for both the cats and their human caretakers. These effects may include reduced quality of life for the cats, increased risks of injury to veterinary staff, lower quality care during visits, and potential surrender of cats by caregivers due to broken bonds. It is essential to limit fear, anxiety, and stress in cats by providing positive and gentle human-to-cat interactions. This session focuses on recognizing signs of fear, anxiety, and stress in cats and provides participants with practical, effective handling strategies.

courses.title: Seminar on Canine Reproduction 2025 On Demand
courses.description: 5 Hours of virtual live lectures that will then be available for on demand viewing for 3 months. Aimed at veterinarians, Vet Techs, and Interns/Residents.

courses.title: The Team Approach to Dental Procedures: How to Provide Comprehensive Preventive Dental Care in Practice
courses.description: Periodontal disease is one of the most common diseases diagnosed in companion animal patients. Comprehensive dental care within a veterinary practice encompasses treatment of the disease when diagnosed but should also place emphasis on prevention. This requires the entire veterinary team, from client service representatives to technicians and doctors, to understand their role in providing consistent recommendations to clients. In this webinar with veterinary dental expert Dr. Naomi Hoyer, explore how an effective comprehensive dentistry program starts before the patient walks in the door and continues well after the patient is discharged from an anesthetized procedure.

courses.title: Suicide Prevention, Mental Health and Well-Being for Veterinarians Anytime
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth understanding of the need to address veterinarians' mental health and well-being. Learn about the importance of suicide awareness prevention and find out how to get help for someone in crisis.

courses.title: Canine Cognitive Dysfunction: Can we improve the lives of affected dogs?
courses.description: Veterinary neurologist, Dr. Curtis Dewey and veterinary surgeon, Dr. Theresa Fossum present a 1 hour course on Canine Cognitive Dysfunction including new therapies. They take a deep dive into the causes, symptoms and treatments that are available.

courses.title: Graduate Diploma in Veterinary Acupuncture
courses.description: The Graduate Diploma in Veterinary Acupuncture, is a 24-month, part-time, fully on-line course oriented towards applied theory, both traditional and scientific, designed for veterinarians who desire to further enhance their skills and knowledge in integrative veterinary medicine. You will be able to start using acupuncture within the first module. The course consists of basic and advanced instruction in veterinary acupuncture as the teaching components; the development of a reflective case logbook of personal experience of the skills practiced, demonstrated professional ability and competence and preparing material and evidence for assessment of competencies. Confidence and competence is developed during the course with continuous case support, guidance, and feedback from tutors, regular live case forums, and then your own clinical cases. IVAS recognizes the CIVT Acupuncture courses. CIVT Graduates of the Graduate Diploma in Veterinary Acupuncture course can join IVAS as Credentialed members.

courses.title: Increasing Comfort Level with Behavior Cases
courses.description: Creating a behavior plan can be stressful in itself, but it doesn't have to be this way! Debbie Martin shares her thoughts and methodology on how to identify, plan, and assess behavior cases to better treat your clients.

courses.title: Level Up Your Hematology Skills
courses.description: This session will focus on the diagnostic power of a comprehensive CBC. Using cased-based examples, Dr. Eric Morissette will explore advances in artificial intelligence (AI) technology that can help make blood smears easier than ever and will share expert insights on how to leverage automated hematology analyzers with AI blood smear technology.

courses.title: Understanding Canine Valvular Heart Disease: Classification, Diagnosis & Management
courses.description:
Join Dr Matt Miller, a board-certified veterinary cardiologist, as he explains valvular heart disease in dogs and its impact on canine heart health In this comprehensive veterinary cardiology lecture, Dr Miller breaks down the ACVIM classification scheme, covering Stage A at-risk dogs to Stage D end-stage heart failure and explaining how to identify early signs of heart disease in dogs
Learn about essential diagnostic tests for heart disease, including thoracic radiography chest X-rays, echocardiography heart ultrasound, and NT-proBNP testing, and how they help assess heart failure in dogs
Dr Miller also discusses treatment for canine heart disease, including
Pimobendan Vetmedin
ACE inhibitors enalapril benazepril
Diuretics furosemide spironolactone
Cardio-supportive supplements
This video is ideal for veterinarians vet techs and pet owners who want to better understand dog heart disease symptoms treatments and prognosis Discover how to differentiate between asymptomatic heart disease and congestive heart failure in dogs and why early detection and treatment are key to improving quality of life in dogs with heart disease

courses.title: MMPC Learniverse - Animal Intake Requirements and Holding Periods - Legal Considerations with Shelter PALS
courses.description:
When it comes to daily shelter activities, the most common questions, and greatest confusion, revolve around intake (if, when, who) of animals, and the applicable holding periods once intake occurs.
This course will discuss the laws that shape intake and holding periods for animals in shelters in the state of California (but the basic concepts and discussion points will apply to all states). You'll learn the California-specific state mandates and requirements surrounding intake, exceptions surrounding holding periods, and how to determine holding periods in various situations. If you're not in California let this information guide you in what to research in your own state.
Knowing which animals should enter the shelter and how long they must stay is crucial to prioritizing intake of the animals who truly need to be at your shelter and minimizing length of stay in shelters for those animals.
The specific information in this course is applicable to and based on considerations of California state law, subject to modifications necessitated by state or local laws. Shelters in other states are encouraged to check their state, county, city, and local laws to determine intake and holding procedures.
This course was adapted from a webinar by Bruce Wagman, Lead Counsel for the San Francisco SPCA's Shelter Policy and Legal Services (Shelter PALS) program and hosted by the California Animal Welfare Association (CalAnimals).

courses.title: Continuous Glucose = Continuous Confidence
courses.description: Diabetes mellitus in dogs and cats is a complex, lifelong condition requiring precise monitoring, timely intervention, and a meaningful veterinarian-client-patient relationship. In this webinar, Dr. Jocelyn Mott and Dr. Natalie Marks will put their internist and generalist expertise together to review the pathophysiology of canine and feline diabetes, the real-world limitations of conventional monitoring, and how technology is reshaping diabetic care with continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices. They will also explore what continuous glucose data look like, what those data reveal that spot checks miss, and how integrating glucose readings with activity and feeding events can transform the clinical picture and improve diagnostic confidence. Dr. Mott and Dr. Marks will provide expert insights on how to implement a whole-practice diabetes system, including how to apply sensors in less than 60 seconds, interpret blood glucose data, adjust insulin doses based on trend data, improve workflows in ways that reduce client and team anxiety, increase client compliance, and lower the risk for hypoglycemic emergencies.

courses.title: OrthoSta: Knotless Ligament Reconstruction System Online Course
courses.description: The OrthoSta: Knotless Ligament Reconstruction System Online Course provides a comprehensive overview of CrCL injuries and how they can be effectively managed using the OrthoSta Knotless System. Through this online course, participants will explore the surgical technique, the concept of isometry, interarticular structures, and gain insights into postoperative care management.

courses.title: Emergency Management of the Cardiac Patient
courses.description: To review strategies for managing common cardiac emergencies. Presented by a board-certified cardiologist

courses.title: Opioid 411 in 2022 2-Hour Anytime
courses.description:
This course has been designed to fulfil the continuing education requirements
for all states that have mandated CE on the topic of controlled substances. It provides students with a
broad range of expert level knowledge on subjects including federal controlled substance laws, best
practices for prescribing and management of controlled substances including benzodiazepine and
opioid medications, use of electronic PDMPs, dispensing controlled substances, recognition of
substance abuse, signs of opioid abuse, addiction and diversion, opioid use and dependency in office
staff, clients and co-workers, use, misuse, documentation, safeguarding and monitoring controlled
substances, controlled substance diversion, inventory and security, treatment of chronic pain, and
controlled substance prescribing for chronic pain management.

courses.title: Canine Lab 1: Essential Exercises for Moving Dogs from Place to Place
courses.description: Are you uncomfortable handling large, hyperactive, or seemingly aggressive dogs. Did you know that if you're unaware of how the dog perceives every interaction, you could be giving unclear or conflicting cues which can cause him to become confused, fearful, and even aggressive. Learn the Low Stress Handling techniques that will allow you to provide clear direction and hence have good control to improve both your confidence in handling and the dog's confidence in you.

courses.title: Chronic Small Intestinal Diarrhea : Cat versus Dog
courses.description: In this RACE-approved veterinary CE presentation, one of BBVSHs board-certified Internal Medicine Specialists, Dr. Geert Paes, will delve into the condition of chronic diarrhea in small animals specifically, cats and dogs

courses.title: Rest Easy Anesthesia: Basic Monitoring for a Busy Practice
courses.description: Anesthesia can be scary sometimes! But have no fear, appropriate monitoring can help us provide an optimal anesthesia experience for the patient (and the anesthetist). In these educational modules, we'll explore how monitoring ventilation, oxygenation, circulation and a few other vital parameters can help you and your patients have a positive anesthesia experience. We'll also review the most current research on anesthesia monitoring. You'll walk away with tips and tools to share with your team and implement in practice tomorrow. Let's get ready to have some fun.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Sterility & Packs in Spay/Neuter Clinics
courses.description: This level one course describes the cleaning and sterilization of surgical instruments commonly used in high-quality, high-volume spay/neuter (HQHVSN), as well as the proper methods for pack preparation, autoclave use, and maintenance.

courses.title: On-Demand: Clients Keep Asking About Fresh - What Does the Science Say?
courses.description:
Fresh pet food has become one of the most talked about trends in both the veterinary and pet owner communities. But is it just a temporary shift or does it represent a meaningful evolution in how we approach nutrition, chronic disease, and clinical outcomes?
This lecture invites veterinary professionals to take a closer look at the science, client trends, and clinical rationale behind the rise of fresh cooked pet food. Whether you are a firm believer in the benefits of fresh food or still skeptical about its role in clinical nutrition, we will objectively review the data on digestibility, palatability, hydration, nutrient bioavailability, and inflammation, as well as how different processing methods like high heat cooking can influence nutritional quality and health markers such as advanced glycation end products.
Veterinary professionals will walk away with clear evidence that can inform an understanding of when and why fresh food may offer benefits and how to confidently discuss its role in patient care.

courses.title: Utility of C-Reactive Protein in Clinical Practice
courses.description: Join Dr. Alicia Mastrocco in this webinar focusing on the utility of C-reactive protein (CRP) in clinical practice. This presentation will provide an overview of CRP, evaluate its role in the inflammatory disease, and explore how to interpret test results in a variety of clinical scenarios.

courses.title: Practical Behavior Information for Veterinary Practitioners
courses.description:
This seminar comprises just about all that veterinary practitioners need to know about dog behavior and training. It consists of over 6 hours of video, plus detailed notes and supplementary dog training resources that can be downloaded and distributed to your clients.
The scope of the information is certainly not huge but it's hugely time-sensitive and critically important for the quality of life of dogs, owners and practitioners. Dogs develop only a limited number of problems, the problems are utterly predictable and their prevention or resolution is by and large, pretty straightforward.
These predictable and preventable behavior problems are the single biggest reason why owners surrender or abandon their dogs. Owners do not want to live with a dog that soils the house, barks excessively, chews destructively, misbehaves when left at home alone, or is hyperactive or unfriendly. The pet loses its life, the owner loses a companion and the veterinarian loses an animal client. It makes good sense, therefore, for veterinarians to consider pets' psychological and behavioral health as well as physical health, i.e., to educate your clients how to educate their pets.
The veterinary profession holds the key, since practitioners enjoy the unique position of seeing every puppy a number of times while he/she is still young and impressionable and at a time when the owners are enthusiastic about training. This seminar will provide effective resources for veterinarians to disseminate necessary time-sensitive educational materials to their clients.
Animal behavior has a crucial impact on the veterinary profession. Mannerly, well-behaved and good-natured dogs allow the practitioner to get on with their job. Behavior, temperament and training problems waste time and generally make life unpleasant for the practitioner, owner, and animal client.

courses.title: FOCUS ON JOURNALS ( A 2 LECTURE SERIES) On Demand
courses.description:
Lecture Title 1: What's New in Small Animal Surgery
Speaker: Dr Julian Lunn BVSc MACVSc (Small Animal Med) MACVSc (Small Animal Surgery) MVetClinStud (Neurology)
Lecture Abstract: Small animal surgery is a continuously advancing field, with innovations in surgical techniques, perioperative care, and postoperative rehabilitation being driven by ongoing research. Recent literature has provided valuable insights into new surgical techniques, optimising surgical outcomes, reducing complication rates, and improving patient recovery and quality of life. Lecture 2: What's New in Emergency Medicine
Speaker: Speaker: Dr Philip Judge BVSc MVS PG Cert Vet Stud MACVSc (Vet. Emergency and Critical Care; Medicine of Dogs)
Lecture Description
Small animal emergency medicine continues to evolve rapidly, with new evidence shaping both diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. Staying abreast of the latest research is essential for veterinarians to provide optimal, evidence-based care in high-pressure, time-critical situations. This lecture will present a review of recent literature, highlighting key developments in areas of acute trauma management, resuscitation and monitoring. The focus will be on translating cutting-edge research into practical strategies that can be implemented in clinical practice immediately.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Equine Endocrinology - Improving the Approach to Common Disorders & Awareness of the Rarer Ones
courses.description: This lecture series is intended to fill in the gaps for practitioners dealing with potential endocrine cases. The series will include a large amount of discussion as well as lecture-based information, and will primarily cover EMS and PPID including the important principles that might have been forgotten as well as approaches to more challenging scenarios. Rarer endocrine disorders such as thyroid disorders, disorders of calcium homeostasis and hyperlipidaemia will also be covered.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Consult with Prof Derek Knottenbelt - Equine Neoplasia
courses.description:
The following Sessions are included in this Webinar Series:
Cancer and how it develops - Lecture & Interactive Case-Discussions
Sarcoid - Lecture & Interactive Case-Discussions
Melanoma - Lecture & Interactive Case-Discussions
Carcinoma - Lecture & Interactive Case-Discussions
Other tumours and tumour like conditions of the of the skin - Lecture & Interactive Case-Discussions
Paraneoplastic syndromes - Lecture & Interactive Case-Discussions
Internal neoplasitic disease - Lecture & Interactive Case-Discussions

courses.title: The Veterinary Cardio Club
courses.description:
The Veterinary Cardio Club is an international online continuing education platform dedicated to improving the knowledge and clinical competence of veterinarians in small animal cardiology. The program delivers structured educational content through live webinars, recorded lectures, and case-based discussions focused on cardiovascular diseases in dogs and cats.
Educational activities emphasize practical clinical application, enabling veterinarians to improve diagnostic reasoning, interpretation of diagnostic tests, and evidence-based management of cardiac patients in daily practice. Topics include electrocardiography, thoracic radiography, echocardiography, congenital and acquired heart disease, cardiac pharmacology, and emergency management of cardiovascular conditions.
The program combines theoretical foundations with real clinical cases to promote active learning and practical decision-making. Sessions are led by experienced veterinary cardiologists and clinicians with expertise in cardiovascular medicine. Interactive discussion and participant engagement are encouraged to enhance learning outcomes.
The overall goal of the Veterinary Cardio Club is to support veterinarians in developing greater confidence and competence in the diagnosis and treatment of cardiac diseases in companion animals, ultimately improving patient care and clinical outcomes.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Neurotoxins in Practice: Recognizing and Managing Nervous System Poisons
courses.description: This course will address commonly encountered exposures that result in notable neurologic effects.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Ultrasound-Guided Regional Anesthetic Techniques for Small Animals
courses.description:
The first of its kind anywhere, this exciting webinar series will familiarize you with a range of topics within the relatively new and rapidly evolving field of ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia. Taught by world-renowned experts, each session will introduce you to different ultrasound-guided regional anesthetic techniques that can be used to provide anesthesia and analgesia for commonly performed surgical procedures in small animals. Topic areas include epidural anesthesia, peripheral nerve blocks of the thoracic and pelvic limbs, and fascial plane blocks of the abdomen and thorax. Pertinent literature will be considered; however, the main focus of each session will be to introduce you to these ultrasound-guided techniques and how to successfully incorporate the use of these blocks into clinical practice. Through in-depth discussions of anatomy, drug selection, required equipment, what are the desired ultrasound images to obtain, and expected effects and contraindications, you will develop a working understanding of these important new techniques and how you can use these blocks to contribute to multimodal pain management and balanced anesthesia in your own small animal patients.
This series covers the following 7 topics that have conveniently been split up into 2 1/2 hour weekly sessions that cover:
Introduction to Ultrasound-guided Regional Anesthetic Techniques
Stifle & Distal Pelvic Limb Surgery
Proximal Pelvic Limb Surgery
The Thoracic Limb
Epidural Anesthesia
Interfascial Plane Blocks and the Abdomen
The Trunk

courses.title: LEO - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE CAT WITH ASYMPTOMATIC HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY (930-35079)
courses.description: LEO - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE CAT WITH ASYMPTOMATIC HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY (930-35079) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Hill's Global Symposium 2024 - Nourish the Gut, Nurture the Future (online learning version)
courses.description: Groundbreaking insights from some of the most prominent experts in the field of gut microbiome and organ connection. View the sessions from the 2024 Hill's Global Symposium 2024 for an insightful gathering of veterinary professionals as we uncover the secrets of gut-organ connection. Topics include: Gut Microbiome Support; Solving Gut-Kidney Mysteries; Stress & the Gut-Brain Link and Secrets of Gut-Skin Synergy.

courses.title: Itchy, red, stinky patients? What topicals do you prescribe and when?
courses.description: The speaker will discuss how to assess patients with skin inflammation and the advantages and disadvantages of using topical therapy. He'll focus on the various types of inflammatory skin conditions and their treatment, including bacterial pyoderma, Malassezia dermatitis, skin-fold infections, atopy, and seborrhea.

courses.title: Introduction to Cooperative Care for Dogs (self-paced course)
courses.description:
This course introduces learners to the key principles of cooperative care to minimize fear, anxiety and stress, and improve safety for staff and dogs during medical care in the shelter and other environments, such as foster homes. Cooperative care training originated in zoos and other institutions involved in the husbandry of wild animals and is considered standard practice in modern accredited zoos and aquariums worldwide. The techniques taught here are helpful for all dogs, but learners should practice with dogs who are generally tolerant of mild handling and restraint to develop your skills and comfort level with cooperative care.
There is often an immediate need for medical handling for dogs upon intake into a shelter. The examples in this course reflect "real world" shelter situations, where dogs who are unfamiliar with cooperative care require immediate treatment. While some procedures will likely require the dog to be muzzled or sedated, many less invasive procedures can be successfully performed with cooperative care. Additional safety measures, like muzzles, should be employed for dogs exhibiting escalated levels of fear, anxiety and stress during medical handling.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2025 Bridging ECC and Internal Medicine: Advanced Knowledge for Urgent Patient Care On Demand
courses.description: This advanced continuing education course is designed for veterinary specialists seeking to enhance their expertise in managing critically ill patients at the intersection of emergency and internal medicine. Through interactive lectures, case-based discussions, and expert panels, participants will gain cutting-edge knowledge on respiratory emergencies, shock resuscitation, electrolyte disturbances, and metabolic crises. This course will emphasize practical, evidence-based approaches to diagnosis and treatment, equipping attendees with the skills to optimize urgent patient care.

courses.title: Introduction to Ultrasound-Guided Cystocentesis (TECH461)
courses.description:
Urine collection and analysis may be part of a complete healthy pet screening panel or performed in patients with clinical signs associated with upper urinary tract or lower urinary tract. Ultrasound-guided cystocentesis increases the likelihood of obtaining a sterile urine sample in obese pets or pets with small bladders compared to manual palpation techniques. In addition, it provides an opportunity to assess the urinary bladder for common abnormalities. Because this procedure is often performed by veterinary technicians, they are often the first person on the medical team to evaluate a patient's bladder with ultrasound and should be aware of common abnormalities.
This course will review the normal ultrasound appearance of the canine and feline bladder, and contrast normal with common abnormalities, such as stones, wall masses or wall thickening. It will also review potential risks and complications of the procedure, and review in a step-by-step manner how to perform the procedure safely.

courses.title: Endocrine Emergencies: What Is New in Management?
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Elizabeth Rozanski will review how to investigate and treat endocrine emergencies, with a particular focus on diabetic ketoacidosis and concurrent pancreatitis, hypoadrenocorticism, and thyroid and calcium abnormalities. Participants will also explore monitoring strategies for these conditions, including how to be cost-conscious while still providing high-quality care.

courses.title: Panel Discussion: Wobbler Syndrome - Diagnostic & Therapeutic Challenge
courses.description: Wobbler Syndrome or Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (CSM) continues to represent a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. Recent advances in diagnostic imaging and therapeutic procedures have improved the management of affected dogs. The multidisciplinary international panel of world-renowned leaders in this field will consist of a neurologist, surgeon, and a rehabilitation specialist. They will debate how to best approach Wobbler cases and discuss the most valuable diagnostic tests, decision-making in regard to treatment, rehabilitation, and what prognosis owners should expect. The panel discussion will be moderated by a highly respected neurologist.

courses.title: Basic Cardiac Radiology (DIAG417)
courses.description:
This course will cover common cardiac radiology concepts and techniques. First through identifying normal anatomy structure and then introducing common abnormal presentations. Common congenital diseases as well as acquired heart disease will be discussed.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 147 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Prudent Use of Antimicrobials (PHAR305)
courses.description: Antimicrobial resistance is an increasing problem in both human and veterinary medicine. Whenever an antimicrobial is used, it inadvertently selects for resistance by killing or inhibiting sensitive bacteria and leaving behind resistant organisms. As a result, medicines become ineffective and infections persist, increasing hospital times, cost and morbidity. Inappropriate antibiotic use can lead to superbugs that are difficult or impossible to treat with our current antibiotic options. This course will discuss the mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance, the use of "best" practices to avoid the emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance.

courses.title: Practice CEnts Module 4: Wealth Creation - Advanced Accounting (PRAC413)
courses.description:
This is our final Practice CEnts Module and we have arrived at the Wealth Creation summit. Now it is time to develop your Millionaire Plan! This module takes everything you learned in the basic accounting Modules 1 & 2, plus using Module 3 to apply your accounting knowledge and improve your practice profits. From these additional profits, you will develop your own Millionaire Plan (using YOUR numbers) to achieve financial independence. As a bonus, we also include a spreadsheet so you can monitor your ACTUAL progress with your GOALS.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 229 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Postural Rehabilitation Professional
courses.description: Postural Rehabilitation Professional is a 6 week, high contact program designed to teach equine professionals how to evaluate and remediate equine abnormal compensatory posture (ACP). Participants will learn about how standing posture is generated and controlled by the CNS, the peripheral structures critical to posture that tend to become distorted by domestication, how to recognize and remediate abnormal anatomic structures (distal limb/hoof, stomatognathic system) and function of the cervical spine to restore normal neutral posture to equine patients. We will also teach team-building among equine professionals, professional communications and how to apply injury forensics to chronic cases.

courses.title: Graduate Diploma in Veterinary Chinese Herbal Medicine
courses.description:
This course provides you with the resources, support and opportunity to become a master of your own practice as a Veterinary Chinese Herbalist.
It is pragmatic, straightforward and integrates science with tradition. The course includes an overview of Traditional Chinese Medicine and classical formulas, with clinical strategies integrating TCM and western medicine. Your readings offer an opportunity to cover subjects in more depth while your lectures, videos and assessments are the core of the course.
Our goal is to have you Certified as a competent and confident practitioner.

courses.title: Small Animal Anesthesia Monitoring: Pulse Oximetry, Capnography & Electrocardiography
courses.description: In this lecture, Molly Allen, DVM, DACVAA presents the physiological basis, principles of operation and interpretation for pulse oximetry, capnography and electrocardiography. Case examples are included to demonstrate specific abnormalities detected with pulse oximetry, capnography and electrocardiography.

courses.title: INTEGRATING ACUPUNCTURE INTO PRACTICE (991-41384)
courses.description: This online recorded webinar consists of 3 interactive modules with each module focusing on a different aspect of integrating acupuncture into your veterinary practice. The goal is to help close the gap that often occurs between obtaining an education in acupuncture and Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine and putting it into real world practice successfully from a business standpoint. Once you have completed the webinar and exercises you will have a user-friendly, efficient system for integrating acupuncture, as well as a plan for achieving your ideal version of an integrative veterinary practice. Because you essentially have a road map to follow, you will be on the fast track to success!

courses.title: Maddies(R) Million Pet Challenge Shelter Consultation Mentorship - Foundational Course
courses.description:
Objective Statement: The purpose of this class is to teach mentees the most effective and holistic approach to shelter assessments. Mentees will learn the significance of research prior to the assessment that includes review of state statutes and local public policy, historical statistics and the infrastructure of the organization. Learning objectives focus on strategies to help shelters work more efficiently and strategically in the areas of admissions, Safety Net, population management, and live outcome programs. The class includes 1.5 hours of video learning and 1.0 hour of reinforcement materials, including self-test quizzes and activities.
Target Audience: Veterinarians, veterinary technicians engaged in animal shelter management
Concepts/skills for participants: Mentees will learn how to influence decision makers and build a foundation that creates an efficient sheltering system. Guiding principles are based on compliance with Association of Shelter Veterinarians Guidelines for Standards of Care in Animal shelters for maintenance of animal physical and behavioral health, facility design to promote animal welfare and proper sanitation, and One Health community programs to protect public health and safety.

courses.title: Ellevet Academy
courses.description: This course aims to provide information on the use of cannabinoids in veterinary species. It will encompass the history of cannabinoid use in human and veterinary medicine, pharmacology and chemistry of cannabidiol, relevant clinical research, and indications for use. The course will consist of 5 distinct modules, with each increasing in complexity and detail. The modules will each provide 1 hour of CE for veterinarians and veterinary technicians. Detail on each module will be provided on the required attachment. Each module will be delivered in an online, non-interactive format accessed through ElleVet Science's education portal on the company website.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Exploring Factors That Influence Public Engagement of Adoptable Pets on Social Media - OnDemand
courses.description: The use of social media platforms to advertise adoptable animals has increased throughout the years. The content of these posts (e.g., photos, videos, text) may increase post engagement (eg., likes and shares) and ultimately animal adoptions. Few studies have examined which characteristics of post content successfully increase engagement. This talk will give background information regarding the online promotion of adoptable animals and will focus on the results of our recent study that analyzed the Facebook posts of several rural animal shelters to determine whether certain types of content (e.g., style/features of photos and videos, subject/tone of text, type/sex of animal, etc.) influenced engagement. We also had the opportunity to compare differences between posts in 2019 (pre-pandemic) and 2020 (post-pandemic). The results of this study suggest that the type of animal and the environment in which the animals were depicted can influence likes and shares of posts. It was also discovered that posts in 2019 received more likes, while posts in 2020 received more shares. Although the findings of this study support the use of social media to increase the engagement of posts depicting adoptable animals, more research is needed to determine how the content of posts directly influence adoption rates.

courses.title: EQ900: Equine Anatomy Discovery Workshop - Clay & Hands-On
courses.description: This course utilizes the brilliant system developed by Jon Zahourek, founder of ANATOMY IN CLAY Learning Systems. It is designed for professionals to help solidify their knowledge of equine anatomy and is regularly attended by veterinarians and veterinary technicians. This comprehensive class allows students to build individual muscles on the Equiken model in clay, as well as palpate (or locate) each muscle on the live horse.
courses.location: Keep Stables at Chapel View Farm

courses.title: OSHA Made Easy for Equine Health Facilities
courses.description: OSHA requires comprehensive safety training for all employees in equine health facilities. This course will fulfill these requirements and update participants on the latest regulatory changes from OSHA, as well as their expectations should your facility be inspected. The course will cover OSHA requirements in the following areas: Means of Egress, Ionizing Radiation, Electrical Safety, Fire Safety , First Aid, Prevention of Zoonotic Disease, Animal Handling, Halogenated Anesthetic Gas Safety, Hazardous Materials, Ventilation, Regulated Waste, Recordkeeping, and General Duty Clause

courses.title: BioMedtrix 2018 Total Joint Conference
courses.description:
BioMedtrix hosted the 2018 Total Joint Conference in Chicago, May 18th-19th. The conference hosted panel discussions and presentations from leading industry professionals about current veterinary orthopedic research.
This course includes 20 lessons. Each lesson consists of a video of the presentation followed by the abstract written by the presenter.

courses.title: Introduction to Pachyderm Medicine: Elephants, Rhinos and Hippos (EXOT617)
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss the basic husbandry, welfare, medical, and nutritional needs of elephants, rhinos, and hippos, including common diseases, anesthesia and sedation techniques, and reproduction.

courses.title: Early Detection with Canine Cancer Screening
courses.description: This course covers challenges and unmet needs in the diagnosis of canine cancer, shares clinical data from studies of the Nu.Q Vet Cancer Test, how to process the sample and interpret results and provides Case Study examples to illustrate how the test may / may not be used. The presenter is a leading light in the veterinary oncology field, Dr Sue Ettinger aka, Dr Sue Cancer Vet.

courses.title: Fluid Therapy for Wildlife Rehabilitators Online
courses.description:
This course provides wildlife professionals a working knowledge of vocabulary and concepts underlying the modern approach to fluid therapy in mammals, birds, and reptiles. Students will learn the physiology of dehydration, its effects on various organs, how to recognize the clinical signs of dehydration, and how to formulate and carry out a fluid therapy plan.
This is an online, asynchronous course, which is designed to be completed at each student's individual pace. Each module is centered around a video lecture supplemented by learning tools such as readings, exercises, case studies, quizzes, and at home labs.

courses.title: Derm Allergies: Which Itch Is It? (TECH419)
courses.description: Pruritus is a common reason pets present to the veterinary hospital. This itching can strain the human-animal bond, in addition to owners thinking that their pet is uncomfortable or suffering. How do veterinary team members know if the pruritus results from a food allergy, food intolerance, atopic dermatitis, or something else? This course will review the causes of pruritus in dogs and cats and determine which itch is which. The veterinary technician plays a significant role in this determination, as well as in the education and communication with the pet owner. Nutritional management clearly affects epidermal turnover, defensive barriers, inflammatory mediators, hair growth, and important features of normal and pathological skin. Thus, nutritional management for the various itch-inducing disease conditions will be discussed, along with details regarding specific nutrients and their role in managing the signs of each type of pruritus. The role of these nutrients will be explored, along with the potential benefits of nutritional modification as part of a multimodal management approach in supporting patients with pruritic dermatological conditions.

courses.title: You Can't Judge Pet Food by the Cover
courses.description:
Choosing the best nutrition for each patient is a detailed clinical task. Pet food production and the methods and standards involved are similarly intricate and important to get right. Exploring the process of making pet food demystifies each stage, starting from meticulous formulation to safe manufacturing and ensuring traceability and safety of the food.
A deeper look in the whole life cycle of pet food empowers veterinary professionals to make informed decisions on how to best nourish their patients. This starts with insight into how board-certified nutritionists formulate the food, select ingredients, and validate adequacy for patients. After it is formulated, food scientists and other experts leverage different processing methods and consider factors such as nutritional preservation, palatability, and sustainability. The NOVA system, an existing scientific classification framework that categorizes food processing methods based on their impact on nutritional quality, helps us understand the nutritional profiles of different foods and the consequences of different types of processing.
WSAVA guidelines for selecting a pet food provide internationally recognized standards that ensure the safety, quality, and nutritional adequacy of pet food. Safety standards can vary among pet food manufacturers, though, and veterinary professionals need the knowledge and tools to confidently advocate for food safety standards and traceability.
This comprehensive review of the making of pet food - from formulation to feeding - will help veterinary professionals navigate the vast market of pet food with confidence, authority, and peace of mind that they are recommending quality nutritional options for their patients.

courses.title: OLD CAT SOULS: AGING, PAIN AND ASSURING COMFORT (Anytime)
courses.description: Our understanding of pain in cats has begun to improve. Because cats manifest pain differently than dogs, it has gone largely unrecognized and untreated until the last decade. The pathways of pain must be understood in order to be successfully addressed. Chronic pain, in particular, has been neglected in large part because its manifestation is unique in the feline species. This webinar will help you better recognize and treat pain in cats, and help your clients recognize the subtle signs of pain that may go unrecognized at home.

courses.title: RETHINKING COMMON SMALL ANIMAL CHRONIC PAIN ISSUES AND THERAPIES (Anytime)
courses.description: This presentation provides a review of the literature and a summary of some important physiologic and pathophysiologic basis for pain in our patients, highlighting the importance of early recognition, prevention and prompt treatment of pain. Therapies discussed for chronic pain will include baseline dietary, complementary, physical medicine modalities, progressing through anti-inflammatory and oral opioids, to more advanced locoregional and infusion therapies. Chronic medical pain conditions such as that resulting from trauma, surgical intervention, degenerative disease (osteoarthritis), and neurologic impairments in cats and dogs will be the focus of the seminar.

courses.title: Opioid 411 in 2024
courses.description:
This course has been designed to fulfill the continuing education requirements
for all states that have mandated CE on the topic of controlled substances. It provides students with a
broad range of expert-level knowledge on subjects including federal controlled substance laws, best
practices for prescribing and management of controlled substances including benzodiazepine and
opioid medications, use of electronic PDMPs, dispensing controlled substances, recognition of
substance abuse, signs of opioid abuse, addiction, and diversion, opioid use and dependency in office
staff, clients and co-workers, use, misuse, documentation, safeguarding and monitoring controlled
substances, controlled substance diversion, inventory and security, treatment of chronic pain, and
controlled substance prescribing for chronic pain management.

courses.title: What Giraffes, Dogs, and Chickens Have in Common Training Techniques that Work for All Creatures
courses.description: Ninety percent of all animal training, regardless of the species or complexity of the task, relies on a strong understanding of the science of learning. Learn what these foundation principles are and how to apply them to everyday training. By the end of this lecture, you'll have the information you need to modify behavior in your dog or cat, as well as your horse, housemates, or even hippos!

courses.title: A New Category of Care: A Practitioner's Guide to Proactive, Noninvasive Screening of Lumps & Bumps
courses.description: In this 1-hour lecture, Dr. Natalie Marks will discuss why early disease detection is vital for the best patient outcomes. Although most clinicians would agree with this tenet, more than half of dermal and subcutaneous masses in dogs go undiagnosed mainly due to the cost and invasiveness of traditional tests. This lecture will discuss how a noninvasive cancer screening tool using heat diffusion imaging can safely screen dermal and subcutaneous masses and is being developed to diagnose and identify malignancies like mast cell tumors. Dr. Marks will also review how this technology does not compete with traditional strategies like fine-needle aspiration, biopsy, and/or surgery but instead helps reinforce the need for these clinically indicated tests. The lecture will finish with a deeper dive into the technology itself, its accuracy, and workflow implementation.

courses.title: The Nutritional Management of Feline Diabetes Mellitus
courses.description: The course will give you an understanding of potential signs of feline diabetes mellitus and which cats are at high risk for developing this disease. You will gain knowledge and confidence in discussing nutritional management strategies for this common feline health concern with pet parents. You will be able to guide pet parents in implementing proven nutritional management to help manage a cat's weight and diabetes symptoms.

courses.title: Reptile Medicine, Anesthesia, Analgesia and Important Infectious Diseases (EXOT503)
courses.description: This course will focus on the clinically relevant anatomy, techniques, and diseases of commonly held reptiles that you may see in your practice, and will cover the basics of reptile anesthesia and analgesia, which drugs to use and how to monitor these patients. We will discuss a new emerging disease in snakes, Ophidiomycosis (SFD), that is rapidly spreading in free-ranging and captive snakes and the conservation significance of this disease. Lastly, we will focus on the top 5 reptile viruses that you might see in your practice.

courses.title: Practice CEnts Module 3: Increasing Practice Profits Through Financial Analysis (PRAC313)
courses.description: This is the heavy weight module where you will see results! We take the information learned in Modules 1 & 2 and apply it using new advanced Financial Tools to directly improve the profitability of your practice. This is where the rubber hits the road. All the accounting information you went through in Modules 1 and 2 is necessary to understand the Advanced Financial Tools supplied in this module. At the end of this course, you can turn your attention to your practice and put the tools to work. Then sit back and watch your practice profits grow.

courses.provider: DR. JUDY MORGAN'S NATURALLY HEALTHY PETS
courses.title: The International Naturally Healthy Pets Experience (Virtual)
courses.description: What happens when Dr. Judy Morgan, DVM, CVA, CVCP, CVFT wants to host a once-in-a-lifetime International Natural Pet Care event? Never before have these esteemed speakers/holistic veterinary experts been together in such an incredible speaker lineup, but Dr. Judy is bringing them to Orlando, Florida from around the globe for The International Naturally Healthy Pets Experience. Course offering already made for in-person and this is for virtual attendees.

courses.title: Compassion Fatigue (STAF183)
courses.description: Have you ever felt numb after a euthanasia, gotten home from a hard day, and picked a silly fight with your partner, or realized you hadn't had a good night's sleep in weeks, but couldn't figure out why? These can all be signs of compassion fatigue, or a gradual state of physical and emotional exhaustion that accumulates over time as we take on the pain, trauma, and distress we see nearly every day as veterinary professionals. Compassion fatigue training is designed to help you recapture and hold onto your sense of purpose, joy, and hope. We will learn the difference between compassion fatigue and burnout, discuss secondary traumatic stress, and introduce evidence-based professional resiliency skills to help you manage stress and the emotional demands of this challenging but beautiful profession.

courses.title: Zennovation in Sedation: Rethinking What is Possible
courses.description: In this educational presentation, we will discuss sedation in dogs. The foundation will be set by reviewing the basic physiology behind commonly used sedatives in dogs. We will discuss the most commonly used sedatives and reversal agents, and introduce the novel sedative Zenalpha (medetomidine and vatinoxan).

courses.title: AAAP 2026 Annual Meeting - Online
courses.description: The American Association of Avian Pathologists (AAAP) Annual Meeting is the premier U.S. scientific meeting focused on poultry health, welfare and food safety for poultry veterinarians and scientists. The meeting facilitates member collaboration to advance science-based knowledge, expertise, and education, and is attended by poultry veterinarians and scientists from the United States and internationally. The 2026 AAAP scientific online program incorporates 31, 15-20 minute recorded sessions presentations in the following 17 topics: Welfare, Salmonella, Enteric Health, Antimicrobial/Antibiotic Resistance, Food Safety, Avian Metapneumovirus, Avian Influenza, Infectious Bursal Disease, Mareks Disease, Vaccinology, Reovirus, Epidemiology, Mycoplasma, Diagnostics, Case Report, Hatchery, and Coccidiosis. The recorded sessions will be grouped into 5 segments. Each segment will have 6-7, 15-20 minute recorded sessions in each. Course participants can choose to take a minimum 1 or maximum 5 segments during this session. Meaning they could earn a minimum of 1.50 CE or a maximum of 8 CE depending on how many segments in the course each person choses to engage with. Meeting attendees will engage with these recorded sessions anytime between August 10th - December 31st, 2026. Searchable keywords: AAAP, poultry, veterinarians, scientists, poultry health, poultry welfare, food safety

courses.title: Food as Medicine: The Power of Functional Nutrition
courses.description: This webinar will introduce functional nutrition as a practical, evidence-informed approach to using food as therapeutic support, offering a way to help patients thrive while avoiding harm from overconditioning and ultraprocessed diets. Through real-world examples, veterinary professionals will explore how to individualize recommendations based on genetics, breed factors, and more and implement clinic-ready strategies, including those on client communication, common nutraceuticals, responsive conditions/body systems, and outcome monitoring.

courses.title: ISELP One Day Seminar Featuring the Hock and Proximal Suspensory
courses.description: The seminar will focus on the Hock and Proximal Suspensory, detailing bone and joint structures, tendons, vessels and nerves. There will be clinical case presentations, lectures, and wet-lab where each attendee will have hands-on instruction led by Dr. Peters and Dr. Oakley. This is a unique opportunity to learn from two experts who specialize in locomotor pathology.

courses.title: Ethical Pet Aftercare (Online)
courses.description: For generations, veterinary teams have assisted with the deceased pet aftercare of patients to facilitate the needs of pet owners. From memorialization to holding pets for pickup, it's been a normal business practice to make arrangements lightening the burden of such things for grieving owners. In today's growing end-of-life specialties, more attention is being directed towards ensuring arrangements are done in the most ethical manner possible. It is common for pet owners to remain unaware of details affecting their pet's care. This module shines light to ideal best practices in pet aftercare, with attention to transparency and aligning with what pet owners themselves have asked for.

courses.title: Veterinary Pain Management
courses.description:
Let Dr. Mark Epstein clear up any and all questions with
your veterinary pain management topics by providing a blueprint for success. Feel at ease with each and
every procedure by incorporating the lessons, tips, and tricks in learning with others online.

courses.title: Chonky Cats: Health Hazard or Hype? How to Communicate the Dangers to Cat Parents
courses.description: Feline obesity. According to the Association of Pet Obesity Prevention (APOP), approximately 60% of US adult cats are categorized as overweight or have obesity by their veterinarian. When does "chonky" convert into disease? What are the health risks of excess weight in cats? How can veterinary professionals more effectively and empathetically communicate the dangers of feline obesity to cat owners? What are the latest findings on the treatment of obesity in cats?

courses.title: Tales from the Crit: Interactive Hematology Case Studies with the Laboratory Retrievers (Module 1)
courses.description: The Laboratory Retrievers - Purdue continuing education (CE) program is an online learning experience for veterinary professionals, created by the Laboratory Retrievers LLC and Purdue University's College of Veterinary Medicine. These highly interactive, case-based modules help veterinarians and technicians confidently interpret CBC data, analyze cytograms and recognize key blood film cell morphology in minutes.

courses.title: Perioperative Management of Gastric Dilation Volvulus Patients (DRIP102)
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss how to prepare and stabilize GDV patients for surgery. Variable degrees of gastric malpositioning will be covered as well as logical and effective therapies for after-surgery care.

courses.title: Managing common gastro-intestinal problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with gastro-intestinal problems The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common gastrointestinal problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.
