courses.title: Indications for Extracorporeal Therapy
courses.description: Attendees will learn about the application for extracorporeal therapy in dogs and cats including both dialysis and TPE. We will cover the basic concepts of ECT, renal indications, immunomodulatory indications, toxic/overdose indications as well as cover some case examples.

courses.title: Veterinary Dental Radiographic Interpretation Online Course
courses.description: Radiographic evaluation has fast become a common facet of veterinary dentistry and only practices that utilize dental radiography can practice quality dentistry. Interpretation of radiographic changes that occur in the tooth and surrounding bone take many forms. Identification of oral pathology in most cases can only be determined by proper radiographic technique and correct interpretation of radiographic findings. A basic understanding of canine and feline oral disease can only be appreciated by matching gross clinical findings with radiographic changes. This 5 part webinar series provides a detailed case approach to radiographic interpretation.

courses.title: Azores - Vet Meet Summer Camp
courses.description: Annual Imaging Conference by Vet Meet

courses.title: International Congress on Infectious Diseases 2024
courses.description: The 20th ICID 2024 is the premier meeting that goes far beyond clinical microbiology and the usual communicable diseases to encompass ALL fields pertaining to infection within a One Health context. This landmark event champions all practitioners from every corner of the globe. The 20th ICID 2024 in Cape Town brings together over 2,500 infectious disease experts from more than 100 countries. The ISID and our many stakeholder partners are working together to create a unique event focused on clinical knowledge and practice, novel translational science, infection prevention protocols and the epidemic intelligence of infectious disease. Every 2 years, the Congress where world-renowned experts share innovative ideas and colleagues spark critical connections is a place for our global industry and medical community to share groundbreaking solutions for prevention, management, and cutting edge treatments for all those impacted by infectious diseases.

courses.title: CERTIFICATION IN CLINICAL INTEGRATIVE CANINE REHABILITATION (682-35924)
courses.description: This course is designed for rapid clinical integration of new skills and knowledge and provides strategies to develop therapeutic programs for frequently occurring conditions that respond well to physical rehabilitation and other integrative therapies, in conjunction with more conventional surgery and pharmacological interventions as required. The aim of integrative rehabilitation is always to optimize outcomes for patients and clients.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Veterinary Surgeon as an Expert Witness
courses.description: Whilst Welfare, Ethics and Law is considered to be a specialist field in its own right, many veterinary clinicians are inadvertently dragged into legal situations as a result of their day-to-day work. This course will prepare colleagues in all veterinary disciplines to carry out this role efficiently and to gain a reasonable understanding of the relevant and essential legislation by giving an overview of the role of the veterinary surgeon as an expert witness. The course also covers the RCVS advice regarding expert witnesses and how to prepare an investigative visit, collect evidence, handle contemporaneous notes, and prepare the statement. There will also be case assessments, using real historic case material and delegates are encouraged to bring their own cases, which will be discussed, criticised, and improved in terms of data collection, tracking and management.

courses.title: Wildlife Medicine Course for Private Practitioners
courses.description: This course is intended to provide veterinary practitioners with an introduction on how to approach wildlife medicine cases for the purpose of stabilizing the animal and subsequent transfer to an authorized wildlife rehabilitator. Further, veterinarians will learn about various wildlife rehabilitation considerations that are important to restore health and welfare of the wild patient. This course is a mix of synchronous and asynchronous online learning. There will be live attendance required for some virtual meetings.

courses.title: DEA Audit Preparedness for Veterinary Practices
courses.description: This comprehensive course provides veterinary professionals with critical knowledge and skills to effectively prepare for and manage DEA audits, ensuring compliance with controlled substance regulations. The program delves into the intricacies of the DEA audit process, covering audit scope, preparation strategies, in-audit conduct, and post-audit recovery. Participants will learn to identify audit triggers, manage essential documentation, implement staff training protocols, and navigate auditor interactions. A key component of the course is an interactive Mock Audit Project, simulating a real-world audit scenario to provide practical application of learned principles.

courses.title: Head Trauma Doesnt Have to be a Headache: Practical Head Trauma Management for Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Head trauma in cats and dogs is a relatively common clinical emergency that can present in isolation or concurrence with systemic trauma. This session will address a brief practical pathophysiology¿of traumatic brain injury and then focus on how to examine these patients. The efficient evaluation of the patient will determine¿the type of therapy that should be instituted in addition¿to the patient's prognosis, both of which will also be discussed

courses.title: Red Light, Green Light: Rapid Triage for Primary Care Practices
courses.description: This presentation covers all aspects of triage from phone triage to rapid assessment. It covers common triage sorting techniques and how to discuss emergency intervention and consent with owners for more critical cases.

courses.title: 2026 Vivarium Operational Excellence Network 4th Annual Virtual Conference
courses.description:
The Vivarium Operational Excellence Network (VOEN) 2026 Virtual Conference brings together laboratory animal science professionals, vivarium leaders, veterinary teams, and research operations staff for a full-day program built around one central conviction: how we work is just as important as the work itself.
This year's conference explores the intersection of operational systems, leadership practice, and animal welfare, examining how smarter workflows, stronger teams, and a deeper commitment to care combine to advance the quality and integrity of laboratory animal research. From artificial intelligence in ethics review to lean management in training programs, from psychological safety frameworks to biosecurity response, the 2026 program reflects the full breadth of challenges and opportunities facing modern vivarium operations.
Sessions are designed to be immediately applicable, grounded in real institutional experience, and relevant across facility types, sizes, and career stages. Whether you are building new systems, navigating workforce challenges, advancing your own leadership, or looking for practical tools to bring back to your team, The VOEN 2026 Conference offers a program built for where the field is headed, and the professionals driving it forward.

courses.title: Panel Discussion: Social Media in Equine Practice - Is digital marketing unavoidable for equine practitioners today?
courses.description:
Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube to name but a few, some of which you wouldn't even recognise. As the age range decreases in the veterinary sector, the number of platforms to which we are signed up increases. Rarely do people not have at least a Facebook and Instagram account nowadays. Social media is now firmly part of our daily lives.
Brand reputation and employer brand are at the top of most companies' minds today, especially as consumerism and competition rise notwithstanding the forever decreasing veterinary manpower available.
What are the motivations behind the use of digital marketing in equine practice and how do we manage to endorse this as busy practitioners? Are there any best practices, rules or risks we should be taking into account? Should digital marketing be taught at vet school or should we all be employing community managers?

courses.title: Tinkering with Anesthesia Machines (TECH452)
courses.description: A gas anesthesia machine is only as reliable as the technician who operates it. In this course, go beyond familiarity with the controls to gain a deeper knowledge of each component and its role in the overall function. You'll feel more confident in testing and troubleshooting when you truly understand how these common machines work.

courses.title: Thoracic Radiology Basics (DIAG418)
courses.description: This course will cover common thoracic radiology concepts and techniques. First through identifying normal anatomy structure and then introducing common patterns of pulmonary disease.

courses.title: Integrative Neuroacupuncture
courses.description: This course explores acupuncture from a modern, evidence-based perspective, with discussion of the use of acupuncture, explained through a neuro-physiological perspective, for a range of common veterinary medical conditions in small animals. In this rapidly developing area, effective evaluation and validation of research is important and will also be discussed.

courses.title: Client Communication 101: Building and Maintaining Positive Relationships
courses.description: This webinar focuses on the foundations of effective client communication, essential for building trust and fostering long-term relationships. Participants will learn techniques to enhance their listening skills, convey empathy, and create clear, consistent messaging that strengthens the client-veterinary team bond. Whether you're new to veterinary practice or looking to refine your skills, this session offers practical strategies for maintaining positive interactions that lead to client satisfaction and loyalty.

courses.title: LafeberVet March 2026 Non-Interactive
courses.description: The March 2026 Non-Interactive Course consists of 15 webinar recordings: two recordings from approved live webinars #1350645 (Caring Beyond Cure) and expired course #776-11130 (Foraging and Enrichment) as well as 13 recordings from non-interactive webinar courses #1160344, #1170116, #1126138, and #1124510 (Amphibian Husbandry, Natural History, and Medicine: A review of important amphibian veterinary information, Avian Nutrition: Practical Applications, Avian Radiology: Basic Principles, Reference Values & Clinical Cases, Bushfires & Australian Wildlife, pt 1 of Australian Wildfire and Wildlife Insights, Australian Wildfire and Wildlife Insights, Decision Making in Rabbit Gastrointestinal Syndrome , Ethics & Wild Animal Welfare in Natural Disasters, Part 2 of Australian Wildfire and Wildlife Insights, Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza, Husbandry and Preventive Medicine in Birds of Prey, Keeping and Treating Mediterranean Tortoises, Reptile and Amphibian Imaging, Reptile Anesthesia and Analgesia , and Ultrasound in Birds).

courses.title: Byers Portal Vein Hypoplasia in 2023 Anytime
courses.description: Learners will explore relevant physiology, logical diagnostic investigations, and appropriate therapies for portal vein hypoplasia in the fields of emergency/critical care and internal medicine diseases that affect cats and dogs.

courses.title: Oral Tumors
courses.description: A presentation on common canine and feline oral tumors including recommended staging and diagnostics tests, tumor types, treatment options, and prognosis.

courses.title: Liver Made Easy: A Simplified Approach to Diagnosing Liver Disease
courses.description: Participants will gain an understanding of the importance of abnormal liver enzymes, as well as the differences between primary and secondary liver disease, in this case-based course on liver disease in dogs and cats.

courses.title: HOARDING: A HUMAN ANIMAL BOND DISORDER (Anytime)
courses.description: This webinar explores the multifactorial issue of hoarding, looking at the role of shelters, private practitioners, animal control, law enforcement, social services and animal welfare organizations. Topics discussed include recognition of potential hoarding situations, who to involve in intervention, understanding when interventions may or may not be successful and understanding challenges faced by shelters.

courses.title: TOXICOLOGY SYMPOSIUYM 2025 (A 3 LECTURE SERIES)
courses.description:
Lecture 1:
PROGRAM TITLE: Top Mistakes Made in the First Five Minutes of a Toxicology Case and How to Fix Them! By Dr Laura Stern
Abstract: The first few minutes at the vet hospital can be critical for toxicology cases. Decontamination and providing stabilizing care should be prompt, but it can be difficult to assess if and when they are needed. We'll explore some of the most common errors that can potentially lead to complications, adversely affect patient outcomes, or simply may be unnecessary. We will discuss the importance of when and how to obtain a thorough toxicologic history and the importance of promptly evaluating toxicology patients, treating serious or life-threatening clinical signs (sometimes even before the toxin is known), and quickly decontaminating these patients when appropriate.
PROGRAM TITLE: How to be a Tox Math Wizard by Dr Jennifer Kendall
Abstract:
In this lecture, we will cover common calculations encountered when managing toxin exposures. Join me as we navigate the mystical world of numbers and become an expert in handling dosage calculations, quick conversions, CRIs, and more!
LECTURE 3:
PROGRAM TITLE: New Meds in Vet Med? Solensia, Librela, Bexacat, etc by Dr Cristine Hayes
Abstract:
Veterinary medicine is evolving rapidly, and new medications are transforming the way we manage chronic conditions in our patients. Solensia and Librela, the first monoclonal antibody therapies for osteoarthritis pain in cats and dogs, offer a novel, targeted approach to pain relief with fewer systemic side effects. Bexacat, the first SGLT2 inhibitor for feline diabetes, provides an insulin-free option for newly diagnosed diabetic cats. But how do these new treatments compare to existing therapies? What are their indications, contraindications, and potential risks? In this lecture, we will explore the mechanisms of action, clinical applications, safety considerations, and practical implementation of these groundbreaking medications. Join us to stay ahead of

courses.title: Reptile Radiography (EXOT509)
courses.description: Not every practitioner has access to ultrasonography or CT, but we ALL have access to radiography, and there is a lot of diagnostic power in x-rays! This course starts with an introduction to why you should be routinely imaging your reptile cases and tackles some of the reptile-specific issues that can cause poor image quality and inferior interpretation. Normal radiographic anatomy is covered before launching into a number of clinical cases involving lizards, snakes, and chelonians.

courses.title: Optimizing antibiotics: Tips for choosing the best drug, dose, route and duration
courses.description: Antibiotics are an important therapeutic modality for bacterial infections in dogs and cats. All use of antibiotics, however, can lead to antimicrobial resistance. Optimization of antibiotic use can help preserve these drugs to treat both animal and human patients. This talk will focus on how to select of empiric antibiotics, choose and interpret diagnostic tests for bacterial infections (including interpretation of antimicrobial susceptibility testing), select dose, route and duration of antibiotic treatment, and improve client compliance. Useful clinical resources will be shared.

courses.title: KYON Mini Total Hip Replacement (THR) System Online Course
courses.description: KYON: Zurich Mini Cementless Small Breeds Total Hip Online Course is designed to provide surgeons with an in-depth understanding of the KYON Zurich Mini Cementless Small Breeds system and the surgical procedure. Upon completion, participants will have the prerequisite information required before attending a KYON Zurich Mini Cementless Hands-on Workshop.

courses.title: The Silent Sufferers: Practical Strategies for Managing Chronic Pain in Geriatric Dogs
courses.description: This lecture will help general practitioners identify subtle signs of chronic pain, build confidence in diagnosis, and implement practical, multimodal treatment strategies that fit into everyday practice. Through real cases, tools, and client communication tips, attendees will walk away ready to improve comfort and quality of life for their senior patients.

courses.title: Medicinal Plants: Tips on Identification, Preparation, and Use (ALTM402)
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss some of the plants found in nature which might have medicinal applications, as well as some harvesting and preparation techniques that can be used for these plants. This course is not meant as a complete tutorial on medicinal herbs, nor does it heavily cover the diagnosis and treatment of disease entities- rather it is meant as an aid in the identification of medicinal plants, proper preparation, their chemical properties and potential indications.

courses.title: Basic Orthopedic Radiology (DIAG419)
courses.description: This course will cover common orthopedic radiology concepts and techniques. First through identifying normal anatomy structure and then introducing common abnormal presentations. Common developmental bone diseases as well as acquired disease will be discussed.

courses.provider: MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY DEPARTMENT OF POULTRY SCIENCE
courses.title: Mississippi State University Layer Seminar
courses.description:
The Mississippi State University Department of Poultry Science will host a two-day Poultry Layer Workshop focused on current production challenges, health management, nutrition, regulatory updates, and management practices in modern commercial egg operations. This in-person program will bring together egg producers, veterinarians, nutritionists, researchers, Extension personnel, and allied industry professionals for practical learning and discussion centered on contemporary layer production systems.
The workshop will begin with onsite registration and welcome remarks from leadership representing Mississippi State University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, the Mississippi Agricultural and Forestry Experiment Station, and the Mississippi State University Extension Service, along with an update from the Department of Poultry Science. Participants will receive an overview of the program, including orientation information and housekeeping details to help ensure a productive and engaging workshop.
Day one will focus primarily on nutrition, disease management, and feed-related considerations for commercial layers. The program will begin with a session on the nutrition of specialty eggs, highlighting dietary strategies used to support specialty egg production and product differentiation. A session on major layer diseases will follow, emphasizing recognition and management of important health challenges including spotty liver disease and infectious coryza. After a scheduled networking break, programming will continue with a discussion on layer nutrition and feed mill quality control, addressing best practices for maintaining feed quality and consistency. The afternoon will conclude with a session examining emerging opportunities for feed additives in layer production. The first day will adjourn in the late afternoon, followed by an optional group dinner that will provide additional opportunities for networking and discussion among attendees.
The second day will beg

courses.title: Wellness testing in senior dogs: What to test for and when.
courses.description: This course will take an evidence-based look at screening in healthy senior dogs: what testing to do, how often, and how to use the results. Wellness testing is different from testing to identify disease, and we will look at principles and guidelines for both clinical lab testing and other types of assessments, such as imaging and tools for assessing pain, mobility, cognitive health, and more.

courses.title: Stressless: How Supplements Can Transform Behavior
courses.description: With a focus on practical applications and scientific research, this case-based lecture will explore how supplements can be integrated into behavior management plans to reduce patient stress and anxiety and improve outcomes. Attendees will gain insights into the mechanisms, benefits, and proper use of supplements to help support more comprehensive care for patients.

courses.title: IVAS Certification Course In Veterinary Acupuncture
courses.description:
The Certification Course in Veterinary Acupuncture taught by the International Veterinary Acupuncture Society (IVAS) has been setting the global standard in veterinary acupuncture since 1974. The curriculum of the course integrates a background of the fundamentals and application of the scientific basis for acupuncture, as well as a background in the fundamentals and applications of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and acupuncture. The educational program provides acupuncture study and clinical applications for small animal, large animal, avian and exotic species. The program prepares the veterinarian for integration of acupuncture into clinical practice.
The curriculum of the course is not limited to the study of TCM theory. The curriculum incorporates current scientific acupuncture theory and biomedical science in its application and approach to patient assessment and treatment. A variety of methods of patient examination and treatment are taught and demonstrated. Students are reminded to always perform a Western medical examination first and obtain all necessary diagnostics prior to integrating acupuncture.
The IVAS certification process requires successful completion of all four sessions of the IVAS Course; attendance of the Mentored Internship; passage of the written exam and either one or two practical examinations depending on their area of focus; submission of a log book documenting 10 cases and a peer-reviewed written case report. Graduates of the IVAS Certification Course in Veterinary Acupuncture will be certified in either Small Animal, Equine or both.
Classroom lecture begin with the anatomic, physiologic, and historical aspects of acupuncture. As the course progresses, patient assessment and diagnosis from both a clinically western scientific perspective and TCM theory approach are introduced. courses.title: General Practitioner Certificate in Feline Practice
courses.description: The General Practitioner Certificate in Feline Practice has been developed to enable veterinary surgeons across the world to access world-class teaching materials. The program is designed to empower veterinary surgeons with comprehensive feline expertise and encourage cat friendly practice in clinic.

courses.title: Interpretation of Feline Dental Radiographs
courses.description: Full mouth intraoral radiographs are required to properly diagnose and treat oral disease. At the end of this online video the participant will be able to interpret feline dental radiographs, identifying normal anatomy and radiographic signs of periodontal disease, endodontic disease, tooth resorption, osseous lesions, and developmental issues.

courses.title: Webinar - Equine Sand Enteropathy - Diagnosis & Treatment
courses.description: Sand enteropathy is a common disease in many parts of the world. This lecture will review the current evidence on the diagnosis, management and prevention of this important disease with a focus on the recent body of evidence that has challenged the validity of many pre-existing practices.

courses.title: Fear(less) Mindset
courses.description: This webinar covers an overview for the veterinary professional looking to help find work/life balance. We address stress, burnout and how to transform stress mindset into something that enables you rather than harms you.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Consentful Contact: Pilot Study on Human-Dog Touch (On Demand)
courses.description:
Understanding and respecting an animal's signals during interactions can significantly enhance their welfare and improve the human-animal interactions. In this presentation, Dr. Amir Sarrafchi will discuss his research on how dogs respond behaviourally when allowed to choose or refuse human contact. Drawing from his work on animal agency and consent, Dr. Sarrafchi will explore how these concepts can be practically applied in everyday animal care, shelter environments, and adoption programs.
Participants will gain insights into how allowing animals to exercise choice, such as initiating or avoiding touch, can reduce stress and support more positive interactions. The session will translate research findings into simple, effective strategies that caretakers, trainers, and shelter staff can use to promote consent-based handling and improve welfare outcomes.

courses.title: VOE-Network Virtual Conference
courses.description:
A live virtual gathering designed to inspired, connect, and equip professionals across the animal care community. This years theme, People, Purpose, Progress, reflects the essential balance between compassionate leadership, strategic innovation, and continuous improvement in animal healthcare operations.
As our field evolves so does the way we lead, care, and collaborate. This conference will explore the vital human element of operational excellence, how to empower teams, thoughtful leadership, and a shared sense of purpose can drive impactful change for both people and animals. Through diverse and insightful abstracts from institutions around the world, the 2025 program offers a dynamic look at the future of animal healthcare management.
All sessions will be presented live and recordings will be available to registered attendees for 90 days following the event, providing flexibility to review sessions or catch up on any that you may have missed.
Learning objective include
- Leadership and Team Empowerment: Explore how modern leadership models are reshaping animal healthcare culture, from building psychological safety and trust, to fostering accountability and growth across roles.
- Digital Transformation and Automation: Discover how facilities are using smart systems, automation, and data to streamline workflows, reduce manual errors, and elevate standards of animal care.
- Compassionate Care for Staff and Animals: Session will emphasize empathy in leadership, workplace wellbeing, and care practices that reflect a deep respect for animals and the professionals who serve them.
- Lean Methodologies and Continuous Improvement: Learn how organizations are applying lean thinking and continuous improvement tools to boost efficiency, minimize waste, and create adaptable high performing teams.
- Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement: Hear how successful partnerships across departments, disciplines, and institutions are unlocking innovation, increasing alignment, and adv

courses.title: VSPA Fall Conference 2025
courses.description: The VSPA Fall Conference 2025 is a 2.5-day event for owners and teams of non-competing, independent specialty and emergency veterinary hospitals. In-person attendees will engage in lectures, discussions, and socials aimed at bolstering sustainable practices in HR, strategic planning, and finance, all while nurturing team engagement and psychological safety. Attendees will leave re-energized and ready to lead; attendance records will be provided for in-person participants.

courses.title: The Field's Practitioner's Guide to Equine Internal Medicine Ultrasonography
courses.description: This 6-hour course covers the most commonly performed internal medicine ultrasound examinations in the horse (abdomen, thorax, cardiac, and vessels). The course will be divided into 3 hours of lecture-based sessions which will include indications for each exam, normal structures and appearances to assess, and abnormalities that may be encountered. The second half of the course will have participants practice ultrasound examinations on live horses, one site at a time. After ultrasounding each site, participants will come together to discuss findings and any difficulties or questions that arose.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2025 Veterinary Nutrition: Past, Present and Future On Demand
courses.description: This course offers clinicians, nutritionists, internists, and technicians a unique opportunity to explore specialized aspects of pet nutrition that are less commonly encountered in daily practice. Provided by experts in the field, topics will include palatability research, novel pet food ingredients, and the development of veterinary diets, among others. Interactive presentations and discussions will address real-world challenges and solutions in both private practice and academia. Engage with leaders in pet nutrition and expand your expertise in this dynamic remote course.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Avian / Exotic Animal Medicine & Soft Tissue Surgery
courses.description: Interest in soft tissue surgery in avian and exotic animals has increased over the last decade due to widespread use of isoflurane anesthesia, the introduction of microsurgical techniques and improvement of microsurgical and bipolar radio-surgical instrumentation. This course has been designed for veterinarians in practice, working with avian cases, wishing to gain a higher level of expertise in their approach to avian respiratory disease, psittacine neonatology and post mortem techniques. The course also includes an insight into PPDS as well as discussions of raptor tendon injuries and their repair. In preparation of the wetlab, the second day starts with an introductory lecture on avian and exotic animal soft tissue surgery and use of radio surgery, followed by an extensive 4-hour wet lab, where all delegates will undertake a variety of techniques required when confronted with injured avian and exotic animal species. This is an invaluable opportunity for delegates to gain real hands-on practical experience under the supervision of specialists, such that they have confidence to undertake all procedures in their own practices.

courses.title: Managing the geriatric patient
courses.description: This course to be presented by Dr's Robertson & Gardner is focused on providing the attendee with updated information on the managing the geriatric patient and end of life care. In this course, the speakers will emphasize how they manage common geriatric problems and provide recommendations on end of life home care management.

courses.title: Are They Grumpy or Do They Hurt? Understanding the Influence of Pain on Behavior Problems
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Margaret Gruen will describe the ways pain can affect behavior and contribute to behavioral problems in dogs. The presentation will review the multidimensionality of pain and the ways that pain can influence learning, motivation, and the display of behaviors.

courses.title: ADVANCED ORAL TECHNIQUES FOR THE HORSE - VIRTUAL (217-44358)
courses.description: The Advanced Oral Techniques for the Horse -Virtual course is designed for a practitioner at any career level. This course will contain the vital information needed to successfully perform equine dentistry. It will cover pertinent anatomy of the teeth and oral cavity, regional anesthesia, radiography, sinus anatomy and straightforward extractions of the incisors.

courses.title: The Science of Resilience: Polyvagal and Cognitive Load Practices for Veterinary Well-Being
courses.description:
Veterinary professionals operate in fast-paced, emotionally demanding environments that place consistent strain on cognitive and nervous system function. This 3-hour workshop explores the neuropsychological underpinnings of stress and resilience in veterinary medicine, with specific focus on cognitive load, autonomic state regulation, and cognitive reframing. Participants will learn evidence-based strategies to recognize signs of overload, apply targeted nervous system regulation tools, and reframe unhelpful thought patterns common in high-pressure clinical settings.
This training is designed for licensed veterinarians and veterinary technicians and integrates scientific frameworks with directly applicable tools to support sustainable well-being. Through structured instruction and guided learning activities, participants will build a toolkit for practical micro-recovery and mental resilience.

courses.title: Pet Loss Support During Euthanasia
courses.description: The human-animal bond is a beautiful part of our humanity. Sharing love and companionship with animals is paramount to our own wellbeing, meaning the loss of a pet can be overwhelming and wrought with personal struggle. In this module, students will explore the depth of the human-animal bond, learn new ways of supporting the bereaved client, and become more familiar with the stages of grief, including pathologic and complicated grief.

courses.title: Chronic Vomiting in Dogs (DRIP158)
courses.description: This course focuses on the problem of chronic vomiting in dogs found in modern veterinary practice and the logical way to handle it.

courses.title: EQUINE VETERINARY PROCEDURES WITHOUT THE DUSTUP (Anytime)
courses.description: The goal of this webinar is to introduce and review techniques that help reduce and/or eliminate fear, anxiety and stress during routine equine veterinary procedures. Creating the most positive experience for the horse, client, veterinarian, and veterinary assistants will help reduce equine distress, increase safety, and set up for future success. The program will also discuss the role of equine behaviorists for educating about behavior modification techniques based on principles of learning that can be used with horses who are extremely fearful or fractious.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Antidotes in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: In this complimentary ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center online webinar, Dr. Justine Lee, DACVECC, DABT, reviews the use of antidotes in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: SURGERY OF THE EAR, AIRWAY, SPLEEN AND LIVER
courses.description: This 4 hour non-interactive course covers Ear, Airway, Spleen and Liver surgery of both the dog and cat. Each surgery listed below discusses indicators, risk, materials needed, anatomy, surgical technique and prognosis and postoperative management of each surgery.

courses.title: IVAS Certification Course in Veterinary Acupuncture - Labs
courses.description:

The program prepares the participant for integration of acupuncture into clinical practice.

The curriculum incorporates current scientific acupuncture theory and biomedical science in its application and approach to patient assessment and treatment. A variety of methods of patient examination and treatment are taught and demonstrated.
