courses.location: Embassy Suites San Antonio Brooks Hotel and Spa

courses.title: The Role of Pet Health Insurance in Pet Health and Wellness
courses.description: This course will give an overview of how pet insurance works, explore the benefits and drawbacks of pet insurance, discuss how to counsel clients about pet insurance, and cover best practices for integrating pet insurance in the private practice setting.

courses.title: Essentials of Emergency By Dr Rebecca Walton DACVECC
courses.description:
Course Format:
A six-week, self-paced online program offering approximately 12 hours of structured video lectures, downloadable notes, drug charts and case workbooks. Learners receive 12 weeks of access and may complete modules at their own pace.
Target Audience:
Veterinarians and final-year veterinary students seeking to improve confidence and competence in small-animal emergency and critical-care management, including general practitioners, emergency clinicians and new graduates.
Course Overview:
Emergency and critical care are among the most high-stakes areas of veterinary practice, requiring rapid decision-making, sound protocols and confident execution. Essentials of Emergency provides a structured, evidence-based approach to key emergency workflows: from triage and shock recognition, through point-of-care diagnostics, fluid therapy and real-world case management. With guidance from a board-certified ECC specialist, the course bridges theory and clinical application via case-based scenarios and practical protocols.
Learning Objectives:
By the end of this course, participants will be able to:
Conduct efficient triage (including phone triage, front-desk screening and in-clinic primary/secondary survey) and identify life-threatening conditions.
Recognise and differentiate types of shock (hypovolaemic, distributive, cardiogenic, obstructive), interpret key clinical signs and initiate appropriate stabilisation.
Apply point-of-care diagnostic tools (PCV/TS, lactate, blood smear, POCUS) to derive rapid, actionable information in unstable patients.
Select and administer appropriate fluid therapy (crystalloids vs colloids, calculate doses and rates, recognise adverse effects) tailored to emergency patients.
Develop and adjust comprehensive emergency plans (fluid/drug/diagnostic strategy) in complex, evolving cases using case-based learning.
Demonstrate safe and effective communication with veterinary clients under emergency conditions and set realistic expectations for

courses.title: Penn Vet Working Dog Practitioner, 3-day CORE Hands-On Workshop
courses.description: Working and performance dogs possess several unique attributes, e.g., higher physical demands, increased injury risks, greater exposure to hazardous substances, more demanding nutritional needs, other, that greatly separates their veterinary needs from that of their pet counterparts. Currently, a critical knowledge gap regarding the working dog's unique needs exists within the veterinary community. The Working Dog Practitioner (WDP) certification program is designed to fill that gap, providing veterinarians with an opportunity to expand their working dog knowledge and skills in order to effectively address the working dogs demands. Penn Vet's WDP is comprised of four sections, thirteen Online Introductory Modules, a 3 day CORE workshop, Electives, and a Preceptorship. The program provides specialized instruction through online and hands on learning taught by instructors that are specialty certified practicing veterinarians with real life working dog experiences and or subject matter experts in one or more of the various disciplines within the working dog field. The 3 day CORE hands on workshop, combines classroom and laboratory learning to build on the core elements of working and performance dog care introduced in the thirteen Introductory On Line modules. The instructor cadre is comprised of renowned industry and academic leaders with practical experience with working dogs in each field of expertise. The 3 consecutive day workshop held at the Penn Vet Working Dog Center (PVWDC) in Philadelphia, PA allows direct interactions with working dogs and experts to enhance the confidence and skill of veterinary professions who care for working and performance dogs. Individuals that seek this training are committed to the highest standard of care for their patients and the best educational experience for themselves.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: ACVIM North American Neuroscience Course (Brain Camp): Advanced Veterinary Neuroscience Week 1
courses.description: This 5-day offering is the first installment of this 10-day module and is designed to offer an intense, high-level review of clinical veterinary neurology aimed at the neurology resident. Topics will range from neuroanatomy and neuropathology all the way through diagnostic imaging and surgical interventions. This is a broad review of clinical neurology with the goal of preparing for the specialty examination and clinical practice.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Springtime Hazards
courses.description: Springtime brings its own set of potential hazards for our pets. This course will cover several springtime watchouts, including springtime plants, fertilizers, insecticides, composting dangers, and more.

courses.title: Caring Beyond Cure: Palliative and Pain Management Strategies for Exotic Animals
courses.description: This webinar explores the veterinarian's role in delivering compassionate, structured palliative care for exotic companion animals. As advances in husbandry and veterinary care extend lifespan, chronic and degenerative diseases are increasingly common, making effective pain recognition and management essential. This presentation will focus on early identification of chronic pain, species-specific assessment tools, and multimodal analgesia techniques while addressing unique physiologic considerations of exotic species. Dr. Kingsley will also discuss client communication, hospice planning, ethical decision-making, and practical medical, environmental, and nutritional strategies to improve quality of life in aging and chronically ill exotic animals.

courses.title: Feline Diabetes Mellitus Nutrition for Veterinary Technicians (TECH443)
courses.description: In this self-study course, we will discuss the diagnostics, management, and treatments used in feline diabetes patients. Our guest case will be Bootsie, an obese F/S DSH. Key Nutritional Factors, disease, and nutritional management including client communication and follow up will complete the course.

courses.title: Molecular Equine Testing: Is it Ever Black and White?
courses.description: Molecular testing for equine pathogens using technologies such as point-of-care PCR is becoming increasingly popular. However, like all testing technologies, the reliability of the result is dependent on a wide range of variables, including: the clinical status of the patient, its shedding status, the location of sampling and the quality of the sample, and the accuracy of the testing technology used. This webinar will dive into those variables and discuss the importance of understanding the testing technologies utilized today.

courses.title: KER Equine Health and Nutrition Conference - On Demand
courses.description: Kentucky Equine Research hosted its 27th Equine Health and Nutrition Conference on February 5-6, 2024, at the Golden Ocala Golf and Equestrian Club in Ocala, Florida. The two-day scientific symposium attracted over 200 delegates from six continents. The conference featured 16 scientific presentations that covered many important topics, including respiratory and cardiovascular physiology, muscle disorders and their genetic basis, management of glandular gastric ulcers, thermoregulation, and exercise conditioning.

courses.title: Veterinary Orthopedic Manipulation Refresher Recertification Online Course
courses.description: This is a review of the basic VOM (Veterinary Orthopedic Manipulation) procedure as well as additional descriptions of Myofascial release techniques, Percussor muscle and adhesion release and frequency specific laser therapy and how these other modalities can build on the benefits of VOM. Additional discussions of medications and supplements that can benefit use with VOM as well as ones that can decrease the diagnostic reflexes of the VOM passes. Reiterating the proper procedures, precautions, prior diagnostics needed to proceed is included. Our goal for this course is to review everything to remind everyone of the proper precise procedures.

courses.title: IVUSS 2026 Annual Meeting - Utrecht
courses.description: The annual conference of the International Veterinary Ultrasound Society. The goals of the lectures at this conference are to improve the knowledge base, skills, and diagnostic ability of small animal sonographers in the fields of abdominal sonography and echocardiography.

courses.title: Anesthesia for the Emergency Small Animal Patient: A Case-Based Discussion (ANES121)
courses.description: This course focuses on anesthesia for emergency surgery in dogs and cats. Not only does this course provide sample anesthetic protocols for emergency surgery, but it also discusses what complications to expect and how to prepare for and treat them. Case examples include stable foreign body, pyometra, C-section, hemoabdomen/splenectomy, GDV, and septic abdomen surgeries. There will also be a brief discussion of how to incorporate local anesthetic techniques for these patients (blind and ultrasound-guided).

courses.title: VETERINARY DENTAL INTERACTIVE CASE WORKSHOP (588-41703)
courses.description:
Efficiently mastering case management while a patient is under anesthesia presents multiple challenges.
Being able to read radiographs, explore pathology and make quick therapeutic decisions frustrates many of my students.
Gain confidence and efficiency learning with others online.

courses.title: Feline Veterinary Suturing Techniques
courses.description: Join Dr. Lynetta Freeman and Dr. Elizabeth Swanson in discussing suture selection, challenges, and suturing techniques in feline soft tissue surgery.

courses.title: Vaccination Protocols: Tailoring Protection for Every Patient (On Demand)
courses.description: In this presentation, Dr. Schumacher will explore the essential role of vaccination to protect vulnerable populations, prevent outbreaks, and improve overall animal welfare. Designed for veterinary medical staff as well as shelter staff interested in improving their understanding of vaccination, this session will cover best practices for vaccine selection and scheduling, as well along with the latest recommendations for vaccination of neonates in high-risk environments.

courses.title: 2026 Hill's Global Symposium - Healthy Skin Starts From Within
courses.description:
Hill's Global Symposium is an insightful collection of presentations from veterinary professionals developed to increase the professional understanding of the dermatologic concerns and the interwoven relationship with the health of the gut microbiome. Topics include
The Gut-Skin Axis: Keeping the barriers intact
Novel Approaches to Dermatologic Patients
Updates in Feline Dermatology and Updates on Canine Atopic Dermatitis
Nutritional Considerations for Supporting Skin Barrier Functions
Multimodal Management of the Chronic Feline Dermatitis Patient

courses.title: How to Win at Skin Cases: Mastering Management of the Pruritic Pet
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Joya Griffin will review the pathogenesis of canine atopic dermatitis and how to implement a systematic approach to achieve an accurate diagnosis. Attendees will learn how to create an individualized treatment plan based on the specific needs of each patient and implement evidence-based treatments to reduce pruritus and prevent allergic flare.

courses.title: SMALL ANIMAL NUTRITION (297-43060)
courses.description: The Small Animal Nutrition course is part of the Putting Nutrition Into Practice Series, designed to give an introduction to nutrition for small animals. This course is designed to help you better communicate with clients regarding the nutritional needs of their pets.

courses.title: TIBIAL PLATEAU-LEVELING OSTEOTOMY PART 5: PAX LOCKING SYSTEM, PERI/POST OPERATIVE MANAGEMENT AND CO (195-36648)
courses.description: This online lecture focuses on post-operative management of patients after TPLO surgery and complications. Attendees will learn how to identify, avoid, and manage potential complications. The lecture will also review the principles of locking plates and the advantage/disadvantages of the PAX Locking System.

courses.title: CARING FOR EXOTIC PETS IN THE SHELTER (631-38160)
courses.description:
Does your shelter have protocols in place for your shelter population other than dogs and cats? These animals make up (on average) around 10% of most shelter's intakes, so having protocols and plans in place for the most common exotic animal intakes can save time, hassle, and promote welfare of these creatures.
Assistant Clinical Professor at Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine Dr. Lena DeTar gives practitioners of shelter medicine the tools they'll need to address the welfare, husbandry, and medical/surgical needs of small mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians that may come into the shelter.

courses.title: Leading Edge for Veterinarians
courses.description: Leading Edge for Veterinarians is a Non Medical, Anytime Program comprising 52 structured training modules delivered digitally over 52 weeks. Each week, students receive a link to a 15 to 20 minute video followed by a set of five questions that confirm their understanding of the content and indicate progress. Leading Edge for Veterinarians is delivered to students via a specialised learning platform. This ensures that students receive their content in a highly engaging way that promotes consumption and knowledge retention. Leading Edge for Veterinarians is optimised for mobile device usage, tablets and smartphones, in line with student preferences. Learning outcomes are consolidated by way of a quiz at the completion of each weekly module. The Leading Edge for Veterinarians interface has exceptional reporting and communication functionality. Student progress and engagement can be easily monitored, and automated reminders are sent to students for any overdue course content, ensuring that they don't fall behind. The intuitive platform also provides for regular and easy communication to and from the veterinarian to facilitate discussion and feedback.

courses.title: Modern Approaches to Canine Mobility and Palliative Care
courses.description: This 1.5 CE credit course will provide on modern approaches to chronic pain management, palliative care and mobility, the use of intra-articular injection, shockwave for palliative patients, new pharmaceuticals for mobility management, and the use of infusion therapies.

courses.title: Dental Dilemmas in Veterinary General Practice: How to Manage Cases with Confidence
courses.description: Dental disease is one of the most frequently diagnosed conditions in companion animals, yet many general practitioners face uncertainty when managing oral health cases beyond routine cleanings. This lecture addresses the most common and challenging dental dilemmas encountered in veterinary general practice, from fractured teeth to staging periodontal disease and deciding when to refer. Emphasizing a practical approach, we will explore diagnostic strategies, treatment planning, pain management, and client communication to build confidence in clinical decision-making. This session will equip you with the tools and knowledge to navigate dental cases with greater skill and confidence.

courses.title: Abdominal Radiology Basics (DIAG416)
courses.description:
This course will cover common abdominal radiology concepts and techniques. First through identifying normal anatomy structure and then introducing common abnormal presentations. The GI system, liver, spleen, kidney, gallbladder, adrenal glands, and urinary system will all be discussed.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 255 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate

courses.title: FOCUS ON EXOTICS ( A 3 LECTURE SERIES) ON DEMAND
courses.description: Lecture Title 1: Foraging Enrichment Foraging is a natural behaviour exhibited by many exotic animals and birds, yet it is often overlooked in captive environments. Lack of appropriate mental and physical stimulation can lead to stress, stereotypies, and behavioural issues in these species. This webinar explores the science and practice of foraging enrichment, focusing on how to create species-appropriate, safe, and engaging foraging opportunities in clinical, zoo, and home settings. Participants will learn about natural feeding behaviours, enrichment planning, and practical applications for birds, reptiles, and small mammals. Through case examples and evidence-based strategies, veterinarians will be equipped to support clients and facilities in improving animal welfare through effective enrichment. Lecture 2: Exotic Palliative and Chronic Pain Management: This presentation explores key principles of palliative care and chronic pain management in exotic animals, including birds, reptiles, and small mammals. It covers recognizing subtle signs of discomfort, using multimodal pain control, and supporting patients through environmental and nutritional strategies-such as assisted feeding and targeted supplementation. The talk also emphasizes effective client communication, compassionate decision-making, and practical tools to improve quality of life through proactive pain management. Lecture 3: Intubation and Tube Feeding Intubation and tube feeding are vital but often challenging procedures in the management of exotic animals and avian patients. Their unique anatomy and physiological responses demand tailored approaches that differ significantly from those used in traditional companion animals. This webinar will guide veterinarians through the principles and practicalities of safe, effective intubation and nutritional support via tube feeding in birds, reptiles, and small mammals. Attendees will gain insight into species-specific anatomical considerations, equipment cho

courses.title: Alpha-2 Adrenergic Agonists & Zenalpha
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Kate Cummings will provide an overview of alpha-2 adrenergic agonists, review their historic uses in veterinary medicine, and highlight key differences among available drugs, including xylazine, medetomidine, and dexmedetomidine. Dr. Cummings will explore the known effects of this drug class on the cardiovascular system, along with other associated side effects, to help clinicians determine when alpha-2 adrenergic agonists are beneficial, when their use should be avoided, and when and how to combine these agents with additional drugs. Attendees will be introduced to Zenalpha (medetomidine and vatinoxan hydrochlorides) Injection and will leave with an understanding of appropriate case selection, dosing considerations, and what differentiates Zenalpha pharmacologically from other sedation options.

courses.title: Anesthesia Emergencies
courses.description: This presentation will go over common anesthesia concerns and emergencies due to equipment failure or negative side effects of drugs. This will go over how to address and trouble shoot them and cover common hypotensive drugs needed

courses.title: Dr. Cooney's Most Challenging Cases: pivoting from panic to peace
courses.description: Someone who performs a lot of euthanasia is going to have challenging cases from time to time. They make everyone nervous during a time when calm and peace is so important. Dr. Cooney is a well-known expert in companion animal euthanasia and has helped over 10,000 animals with the procedure. She has picked out some of her toughest to review with you and help you overcome challenges of your own. When we know better, we do better.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Don't Sweat It: An overview of common toxidromes and their management
courses.description: This course will cover common toxidromes encountered in veterinary medicine, including anticholinergic, cholinergic, sympathomimetic, opioid and hyperthermic toxidromes. An overview of mechanisms, clinical presentations, treatment, and diagnostic testing will be presented as well as a considerations for approaching decontamination and unknown toxic exposures.

courses.title: Management of Controlled Substances
courses.description: This course will review and educate veterinarians on the opioid epidemic in the United States and the management of controlled substances, which is a common required continuing education course for state veterinary medical boards. In this 2-hour session, presented by a clinical veterinary pharmacist and a practicing cardiologist, the attendees with learn about the various schedules of controlled substances, best practicing for prescribing, wasting, and storing these controlled substances and how to recognize signs of abuse or misuse.

courses.title: Environmental Chemicals and Cancer Risks in Dogs
courses.description:
This presentation explains the importance of preventative cancer recommendations for canine patients in the primary care setting. Several common canine cancers have been shown to be related to environmental chemical exposures. This presentation identifies specific environmental chemical exposures associated with specific cancers in dogs, or in people with analogous cancers.
Bladder cancer and lymphoma have strong links to environmental chemical exposures in people, and we are finding that the same may be true for dogs. This session presents the evidence for specific chemical exposures and these cancers in dogs and provide practical recommendations to make to owners of high-risk breeds.

courses.provider: ZERO PAIN PHILOSOPHY - ACE VETS LIMITED
courses.title: Zero Pain Philosophy Acute Pain Management Course
courses.description: The Zero Pain Philosophy Acute Pain Management course gives the learner the knowledge required to ensure optimal analgesia is provided to all patients.

courses.title: Neurology Mini Course
courses.description: This four hour course offering will provide in person, small classroom learning for veterinarians.

courses.title: Let's Beam On: How Radiation is used to Treat Common Oral Tumors
courses.description: This presentation is a review of the three most common oral neoplasia's in dogs (oral malignant melanoma, fibrosarcoma and squamous cell carcinoma) and the single most common oral neoplasia in cats (squamous cell carcinoma). We will review common presentations, biological behavior and risk factors for these diseases and discuss the different types of radiation protocols used for treatment. Using patient cases, we also discuss prognosis, side effects, and outcomes with radiation for each of the four tumor types.

courses.title: Endoscopy & Laparoscopy CE training program
courses.description: Provide endoscopy and laparoscopy training to veterinarians and their veterinary technical staff. This training will be done on-site at a Veterinary Hospital for hands-on training with actual patients. The course will cover the use of a gastroscope, otoscope, rhinoscope, cystoscope and laparoscope along with their respective equipment, procedures and anatomy. The course will cover the most common endoscopy, laparoscopy, cystoscopy, otoscopy & rhinoscopy procedures. We will review anatomy along with teaching minimally invasive surgical techniques.

courses.title: Cushings Disease: Diagnostic Tips & Tricks
courses.description: In this case-based webinar, Dr. Patty Lathan will discuss some of the less common clinical signs that suggest the presence of hyperadrenocorticism (ie, Cushing's disease). Differences in diagnostic tests and which ones to use in various situations will also be reviewed.

courses.title: Redefining the Gold Standard: A New Framework for More Accessible Care - On Demand
courses.description:
This recorded webinar challenges the assumption that the "gold standard" of care is the only acceptable standard. While ideal in some cases, a one-size-fits-all approach can limit access to care, disempower both clients and providers, and create unnecessary barriers, particularly in underserved communities.
Building on principles of spectrum and incremental care, this session introduces contextualized care, a framework that supports clinical decision-making based on available resources, ethical and legal responsibilities, and the needs of the specific animal and community involved.
Originally presented to a standing-room-only audience at the 2025 Animal Care Expo, this session reflects a growing consensus across the profession: it's time to reexamine rigid standards and align care delivery with the realities of diverse practice settings.

courses.title: Focus on Behaviour ( a 2 lecture series)
courses.description:
Lecture 1: Why did the Dog Bite? Understanding Canine Aggression
LECTURE ABSTRACT:
Aggression is a leading cause of the relinquishment of dogs to shelters and is the most common presenting complaint to Veterinary Behaviourists. Like any medical problem, the first step is to understand what is happening and why. With behaviour problems, this means determining the motivation for the performance of the behaviour. This lecture will discuss how clinicians can understand the dog's motivation for the behaviours, review differential diagnoses, and discuss the three main components of a behavioural treatment plan.
Lecture 2: What if they don't come back? Treating Separation Anxiety
LECTURE ABSTRACT:
Separation related-distress results in significant emotional and physical consequences for both the pet and the family. This lecture will review our current understanding of the etiologies of separation anxiety, discuss how to make the diagnosis, and review the components of a comprehensive treatment plan.

courses.title: Raw Diets 101
courses.description: Communication about nutrition is essential for wellness in companion animals, and continuing education about the potential risks and potential benefits of raw diets will improve in-clinic conversations. What are raw diets, and why are they gaining popularity? This talk will cover perceived benefits, anecdotal evidence, and a brief introduction to emerging research, as well as covering essential differences between homemade & commercially prepared raw diets.

courses.title: Veterinary Practice Sales Market Update
courses.description: These sessions provide veterinary professionals with timely, data-driven insights and practical frameworks to better understand the dynamics shaping practice ownership transitions and the current market valuations being applied in an ever-changing landscape. Through discussion of industry trends, valuation principles, and the sales process, attendees will gain knowledge that supports informed decision-making and long-term planning for their practice.

courses.title: Expert Level Cannabinoid Science, Part 4: Felines and Cannabinoid Medicine
courses.description: The Expert Level Cannabinoid Science, Part 4 presentation will explore the unique aspects of cats and how this impacts their dosing and alternative formulation requirements, alongside points of note regarding administration. Reviewing the available evidence including pharmacokinetic data, we will explore appropriate dosing and dose intervals, leading on to an appraisal of current safety data relating specifically to cats. Again, drawing on available literature, we will highlight areas where cannabinoids may have applications in feline clinical medicine, and will also reinforce this through the presentation of several case reports.

courses.title: Treatment of Atopic Dermatitis in 2024
courses.description: This webinar will explore current treatment options available for the management of canine atopic dermatitis. Dr. Thomas Lewis will review the current guidelines from the International Committee on Allergic Disease in Animals and discuss when to use certain therapies and when certain therapeutic options may be suboptimal or even contraindicated.

courses.title: The House Call Vet Academy
courses.description:
This is an on-demand online course for veterinarians who would like
to build their own house call practice, or revamp an existing house call practice. This course includes 1 year of access to the materials as well as once per month group education sessions during the year.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Backyard Poultry Medicine and Surgery
courses.description:
Client interest and commitment to Back Yard Poultry, has mushroomed dramatically in the past 6-8 years. Not only has this created a requirement for clinicians to advance their avian medicine and surgery, an area traditionally not taught at the undergraduate level, but also all the complexities of dispensing medication to food-producing species, maintaining records, etc. This webinar series has been designed for veterinarians in practice, who are working with backyard poultry.
The webinar series includes discussions of common backyard poultry diseases, including etiology, diagnosis, and realistic treatment options as well as traditional poultry medicine and flock health. This webinar series will take attendees a stage further, to include anaesthesia, diagnostics, and common surgical challenges (crop impaction, salpingohysterectomy, fracture repairs).
Chickens are no longer 'an agricultural commodity', but often a much loved family member, with many clients willing to pursue extensive diagnostic and treatment modalities.

courses.title: Functional Anatomy for the Performance Dog
courses.description: Anatomy is a field of veterinary science that goes virtually unnoticed after graduation from Veterinary College. In reality the information does not necessarily change over time. That does not lessen the need for todays veterinary practitioner, dog handler or dog trainer to review this information, especially as it relates to musculoskeletal evaluation and canine performance. Locomotion is a complex interaction of nerves, muscles, tendons, bones and the other associated tissues. It is amazing how the body continually functions in a way that we always take anatomical movement for granted. Any action or non-action involves conscious and unconscious multi-tissue activity. It is a continuous series of intricate actions combined together producing whole body movement. It is the intent of this course to introduce the musculoskeletal anatomy to the student in a functional manner. This is very helpful when the professional is designing a training regiment, developing a conditioning program or making decisions related to a rehabilitative program.

courses.title: Cancer Immunotherapy in Practice: Options and Autologous Cancer Vaccines
courses.description: This presentation will briefly review the interactions between the immune system and cancer, and describe various immunotherapy strategies. Practical options for immunotherapy in clinical practice will be discussed, including metronomic chemotherapy and autologous cancer vaccines.

courses.title: Bringing Care Everywhere: How access to care issues can direct treatment in the field (MULT118)
courses.description:
Access to Care may be the current catch phrase, but in reality there has always been and there is now an ever-growing need for veterinary services to be provided to underserved populations. This can be low income urban areas or isolated rural areas, and it can affect varying degrees of income levels. As clinics become more available through nonprofit and outreach work, it is important to keep in mind that low/no cost clinics do not correlate with decreased quality of care. This course is designed to introduce participants to common factors that can affect decision-making, treatment options, and follow-up plans while providing high quality care to reach the desired patient outcome. We will follow actual cases throughout the course from clinic presentation to discharge as examples.
Please note: COVID-19 has created challenges throughout the veterinary field which requires individualized protocols. For the purposes of this course we will not be discussing COVID-19 precautions and safety measures.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 96 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Essentials of Veterinary Chinese Medicine
courses.description:
This 'Essentials' course is designed to provide students with an introduction to the concepts of prescribing Chinese herbal medicine and some important veterinary Chinese herbal formulas. The approach is simple but effective and built on what they already know by taking a biomedical approach to the herbs. Gastrointestinal and renal disease are then covered from a basic Chinese medicine perspective to get students started with those frustrating cases and so that students can apply what they have learned during the course. We hope this will then inspire you to go on and study veterinary Chinese herbal medicine in more detail with one of our Certification or advanced courses!
This course is evidence-based, self-paced and self-assessed. It is delivered by qualified and experienced practitioners with live tutor support. It is completed over eight weeks and can be started any time. This course is open to veterinarians with no prior training in Chinese herbal medicine.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Opportunities for Barriers & Bias During Off-Site Animal Adoption Events (On Demand)
courses.description: This presentation shares findings from a large survey of 484 U.S. animal shelter and rescue organizations on adoption event practices and adopter screening procedures. Participants will learn about common processes in adoption decision-making, the role of implicit bias in these processes, and how organizational procedures can affect both the speed and equity of pet adoptions. The session will highlight areas for animal shelter professionals to reflect on their own adoption practices and consider strategies for reducing barriers while supporting successful matches between people and pets.

courses.title: Digital Cytopathology: Real-Time Expert Help in Your Everyday Practice
courses.description: In this presentation, learn how digital microscopy and deep learning artificial intelligence (AI) can alleviate challenges surrounding workflows and the time it takes to read samples while also providing practitioners confidence in the accuracy of results for fecal flotations, blood smears, skin impression smears, ear and skin swab cytologic smears, and digital cytology. Plus, become familiar with recommended diagnostic modalities for routine wellness and sick animal examinations. Through case-based examples, Dr. Shannon Sura and Dr. Erica Dumeyer will demonstrate workflows associated with varied uses of digital microscopy.

courses.title: Understanding Tribal Sovereignty and Jurisdiction for Animal Welfare Professionals (On Demand)
courses.description: Effective and respectful partnerships with Tribal Nations require more than good intentions, they demand a foundational understanding of history, law, and culture. This course is designed for animal welfare professionals working alongside and in partnership with Tribal communities. Through the guidance of Karen Diver, former White House Special Assistant to President Obama for Native American Affairs and a national leader in tribal governance, participants will gain critical insights into the historical and legal framework that shapes tribal sovereignty. Participants will explore the government-to-government relationship between Tribal Nations and Federal and State governments, beginning with treaty-making and continuing through key legislation and court decisions that impact jurisdiction and self-determination. The course emphasizes that Tribal Nations are not homogenous; each tribe has its own government structure, laws, and cultural perspectives. Understanding these distinctions is essential for building trust and fostering long-term, respectful collaboration. This webcast will include: - the historical and legal foundations of tribal sovereignty - treaties and the ongoing federal trust responsibility - differences in tribal, state, and federal jurisdiction - the diversity of Tribal Nations and the importance of cultural competence - navigating partnerships in the context of animal welfare, including regulatory and legal considerations - case studies highlighting successful collaboration and common pitfalls

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: The Animal Welfare Assessment Grid (On Demand)
courses.description: The Animal Welfare Assessment Grid (AWAG www.awag.org.uk) is a powerful, cloud-based tool designed to track and visualize the welfare and lifetime experiences of animals. By turning husbandry and veterinary records into clear, easy-to-read graphics, AWAG transforms complex welfare data into compelling visual evidence -- making it easier to communicate with decision-makers, support strategies for change, or substantiate welfare-related marketing claims. Its unique time-based approach looks beyond single moments in time, providing a whole-life perspective that helps animal care professionals plan timely, targeted interventions to improve or safeguard quality of life. Built around the five domains model, AWAG evaluates four key parameters -- physical, behavioral/psychological, environmental, and procedural -- each of which can be tailored to suit different species and animal-use contexts. The tool identifies significant events that impact welfare and calculates a Cumulative Welfare Assessment Score (CWAS) over time, allowing users to see trends in an animal's quality of life at a glance. By highlighting specific areas for refinement, AWAG empowers carers, researchers, and organizations to make data-driven decisions that directly enhance animal welfare. This webcast will explore how AWAG works, its flexibility across settings, and how its lifetime approach to animal well-being sets it apart from other assessment methods.

courses.title: Scratch That! How to Be a Derm Superhero for Your Patients
courses.description: Join Dr. Fiona Bateman for this case-based presentation on how to find solutions for "unresponsive" dermatology patients. You'll learn how new technology for interpreting your most valuable dermatology diagnostic test, cytology, can help improve clinic workflows and accuracy of results, all while generating improved value for clients. This session will also look at how treatment options can help improve the age-old problem of client compliance, leading to improved patient care.

courses.title: Small Animal Programme 2022
courses.description: This programme includes 39 hours of world-class CPD, delivered by experts in the field. The main objective is to keep veterinarians up to date with the latest insights into small animals. Topics covered range from internal medicine, ophthalmology, oncology, gastroenterology, neurology and much more.

courses.title: On-Demand: Nutritional Management of Canine Chronic Gastrointestinal Disease
courses.description: Gastrointestinal disorders are very common in veterinary practice and nutrition is a very important aspect of case management. Over 55-60% of patients with chronic gastrointestinal disorders will be diet responsive. In order to design the best nutrition plan, it is important to do a thorough patient assessment by collecting a thorough diet history, performing a thorough physical examination and completing appropriate diagnostic tests. This will help localize the affected portion of the gastrointestinal tract (small bowel, large bowel, pancreas) and design Thoughtful diet trials. Key nutritional factors for diet selection should be including diet digestibility, protein, fat and fiber as well as calorie density and micronutrients. Many diet options are now available for management of gastrointestinal disorders utilizing different strategies including highly digestible, lower fat, fiber enriched, and novel or hydrolyzed protein. In some cases, supplements or medications are appropriate, but unnecessary antibiotic use should be avoided. Cases will be presented to highlight nutritional assessment, optimal dietary management and recommended follow up.

courses.title: BioMedtrix Universal Hip In-Person Mentorship Opportunity
courses.description: The BioMedtrix Universal Hip In-Person Mentorship Opportunity offers surgeons and their team technical feedback and support required to gain confidence in performing THR as they prepare to perform clinical cases.

courses.title: ONLINE VET NURSE CONFERENCE 2025
courses.description:
Lecture 1: Nursing the Seizuring Patient (by Dr Philip Judge)
Abstract
Seizures are among the most common neurological emergencies encountered in veterinary practice, and effective nursing care is critical to patient outcomes. This webinar will provide veterinary professionals with practical strategies for stabilising seizuring patients, minimising complications, and providing ongoing monitoring and support. From triage and emergency interventions to post-ictal care and owner communication, attendees will gain confidence in delivering comprehensive nursing care during these often-chaotic cases.Lecture 2: Golden Years Reimagined: Unlocking Vitality in Ageing Dogs ( Dy Dr Sarah Robson)
Abstract
As dogs enter their senior years, they often face a unique set of health challenges that require a proactive and compassionate approach. This webinar will explore practical strategies to support ageing dogs and enhance their quality of life. From recognising early signs of age-related disease to implementing tailored nursing care and client communication, attendees will learn how to keep senior patients comfortable, active, and thriving well into their golden years.
Lecture 3: Growing Pains: Brains Under Construction, Behaviour Out of Control ( by Maria Alomajan)
Abstract
Adolescence in dogs is a challenging developmental stage, often marked by unpredictable behaviour, testing boundaries, and a brain still under construction. This webinar will explore the physiological and behavioural changes that occur during this critical period, highlight common problem behaviours, and provide practical strategies for veterinary professionals to support both dogs and their owners. By understanding the science behind teenage turmoil, participants will be better equipped to guide clients through this stage and set young dogs up for long-term success.
Lecture 4: Avian Orthopaedics: From Triage to Discharge ( by Iffy Glendinning)
Abstract: Orthopaedic injuries in birds present unique challenges

courses.title: Rethinking Rabbits: Integrating the New Shelter Housing Guidelines (On Demand)
courses.description:
Domestic rabbits are among the most common small mammals housed in animal shelters, yet until recently, there were no comprehensive, evidence-based guidelines to inform their care and housing. In 2025, the Association of Shelter Veterinarians released the first set of Guidelines for Humane Rabbit Housing in Animal Shelters, developed by a panel of experts in shelter medicine, behavior, and animal welfare.
This session will introduce veterinarians and veterinary technicians to the principles behind these new guidelines, including the scientific foundation, the process by which recommendations were developed, and the core housing elements shown to reduce stress, improve health, and support positive outcomes for rabbits in shelter care. Presenters will highlight both the practical and welfare-driven aspects of rabbit housing design, with emphasis on considerations unique to rabbits as prey species, such as space allocation, flooring, hiding opportunities, enrichment, and group versus individual housing.
By grounding daily practice in these standards, shelters can provide safer, more effective, and more humane housing environments for rabbits, ultimately improving capacity for care and supporting live outcomes.

courses.title: Identifying and Understanding Animal Cruelty and Neglect (On Demand Course)
courses.description: This course will guide attendees through understanding the difference between the two primary types of animal cruelty -- malicious cruelty and neglect. Using definitions, examples of current laws, and lived experience, the instructor will help the attendees understand the spectrum of emotional reaction as well the where the law lies. Attendees will also learn about the types of information that might be needed if they suspect cruelty has taken place and how to gather it for their ACOs.

courses.title: Focus Your Dermatology Diagnosis & Care with Vetscan Imagyst
courses.description: Dermatologic cases, including skin and ear disease, make up a significant portion of a small animal veterinarian's daily caseload. This session will provide an image-rich, case-based review of a concise, practical diagnostic and treatment approach to canine pruritus patients, with a special focus on the importance of cutaneous and otic cytology. Images and videos will demonstrate lesion selection and collection strategies to optimize the efficiency, accuracy, and utility of ear and skin cytology samples. This session will also explore a new and innovative way to obtain efficient cytology results for everyday dermatology cases through the Vetscan Imagyst. Participants will also learn how deep learning AI can alleviate challenges surrounding workflow and the time it takes to read samples while providing practitioners confidence in the accuracy and results for impression and cytologic smears.

courses.title: Diagnostics for Cranial Cruciate Ligament Disease Online Course
courses.description: Diagnostics for Cranial Cruciate Ligament Disease (CrCL) Online Course is designed for general practitioners who are looking to understand how to diagnoses CrCL through describing the history findings consistent with cranial cruciate ligament disease and identifying findings on orthopedic examination that would be consistent with pelvic limb lameness and cranial cruciate ligament disease. Topics discuss are anatomy and pathophysiology, gait examination, standing examination, recumbency examination, cranial drawer test, tibial thrust test, and required radiography with patient positioning.

courses.title: Blood Chemistry in the Canine and Feline (TECH442)
courses.description: Many of us run blood tests and chemistry profiles daily. Do you really understand what each of these tests indicate and what they mean? This class will go through the most common chemistry tests and explain what each one indicates, how they correlate with other tests, and what they really mean. We will also cover some of the more common tests done in-house for viruses and parasites. Common tests sent out to reference labs will be reviewed as well to complete the course.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Fun in the Sun
courses.description: This webinar will cover common exposures in dogs and cats that the ASPCA's Poison Control provides consultations on during the summer months. We will review a variety of substances, their concerning toxicants, resulting clinical signs, diagnostic testing changes, and treatment. Join us as we journey through a summer day and discuss the potential toxicities you may need to manage in small animal clinical practice.

courses.title: Level Up Performance Based Compensation for Your Whole Team
courses.description:
I find that most practice owners struggle with pay scales, starting wages, raises, and promotions. The solution is a performance-based compensation model with tier-based levels. We have used this model successfully in our practice for over a decade, attracting, retaining, and motivating high-performing team members.
This 5-module workshop will walk you through exactly what you need to know and do to design, implement, and maintain a tier-based system for compensating your team members.
Implementing a team member compensation program will be transformational to your practice because you will:
- Empower your team.
- Eliminate the stress of raises and promotions.
- Maintain internal consistency and high-level skills/knowledge.
- Attract, retain, and motivate high performing team members.
- Encourage cooperation and mentoring.
- Recognize and reward self-motivation and performance.
How it Works
Each position in your practice needs to be defined and the duties divided into multiple levels. Each level or tier should have soft skills, hard skills, and knowledge. Some of the skills, like drawing blood from ten cats, can be logged by the team member. Knowledge can be assessed with tests, like medical math or vaccine schedules. The first tier is usually all the stuff that you expect them to be proficient in at the end of their orientation. And then each additional tier level has higher level skills and knowledge.
The biggest benefit is that each team member is empowered and provided the tools to control their career path and their compensation. A benefit to the practice owner/manager is that there is no more confusion around hiring wages and raises. If you want to work alongside self-motivated team members who actively pursue improvement in hard skills, soft skills, and knowledge and help their peers do the same, performance-based compensation may be just the thing for you and your practice.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of the Cancer Patient (TECH396)
courses.description: Cancer is one of the most common diseases of dogs and cats. Recent advances in cancer therapy have resulted in increased survival time for many veterinary patients. Despite these advances, malnutrition remains a common problem in these patients. Cancer-associated malnutrition occurs as a consequence of an imbalance between the nutritional needs of the patient, the demands of the tumor and the availability of nutrients in the body. Nutritional management of veterinary patients with cancer should be specific to each patient based on ongoing nutritional assessment. This course will review how nutritional management influences remission time, survival time, and quality of life of veterinary patients with cancer. We will also discuss the role of the pet owner and how nutrition can help pets feel better while allowing family members to feel they are a part of their pets treatment. Veterinary technicians must ensure that clients understand their pets cancer diagnosis and accept the recommendations made.

courses.title: Back to Stool: Things You May Have Forgotten About Clinical Parasitology
courses.description: Accurate diagnosis is crucial for effectively managing, controlling, and treating parasitic infections in companion animals, but how confident are you in conducting tests and interpreting results? This course covers the principles of most common routine diagnostic tests, identifies their applicability and limitations, breaks down common pitfalls, and explores emerging challenges and advancements in clinical parasitology. It provides practical insights to enhance diagnostic skills and to help participants make informed decisions that directly impact patient care.

courses.title: Foundations of Small Intestinal Surgery
courses.description: Foundations of small intestinal surgery is a dynamic, comprehensive continuing education course designed to make you more confident, capable, and current in the operating room. From mastering the intricacies of the cranial mesenteric artery to choosing the ideal suture for a feline enterotomy, Dr. Sri Jayantha blends evidence-based techniques with practical insights that will elevate your surgical outcomes. You'll explore key topics like intestinal viability, leak testing, and enterotomy planning, all while reinforcing critical decision making through real-world scenarios and expertly crafted quizzes. Whether you're looking to sharpen your technique, stay on the cutting edge of small animal GI surgery, or fulfill CE requirements with something that's actually engaging, this course is your go to. We've packed it with clinically relevant pearls like why the proliferative phase is the most crucial for wound strength, how to handle the tricky duodenum and ileum, and what methods truly minimize contamination during enterotomies.

courses.title: FEAR FREE SHELTER COURSE: CORE MODULES
courses.description: The goal of the Fear Free Shelter Program is to improve the experiences of animals by education shelter, rescue, and animal welfare employees and volunteers like you about their emotional needs. We aim to empower you to apply key strategies and techniques designed to reduce the negative emotional states that are commonly experienced by shelter and recue animals - including fear, anxiety, stress (FAS), and frustration - and increase their enrichment opportunities. The Fear Free Shelter Program provides training suitable for all of the individuals involved in the care and oversight of the shelter and rescue animals - from medical and behavioral staff to intake, reception, kennel, and cattery staff to animal control officers, adoption counselors, foster caregivers, and shelter volunteers.

courses.title: Behavioural approach to rabbit health and welfare - From home to the hospital.
courses.description: On-demand webcast:

courses.title: The Business of Veterinary Supplements
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Ernie Ward will examine the role of veterinary supplements within modern clinical practice, focusing on how supplement recommendations can influence patient care, client trust, and practice sustainability. Participants will explore current trends in the veterinary supplement market, common points where compliance and continuity of care are frequently lost, and protocols that can help support consistent, medically grounded recommendations. Dr. Ward will review staged care models, pricing as a trust signal, strategies to improve team alignment, and refill methods that can help clinics maintain continuity of care while strengthening the veterinarian-client-patient relationship.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Toxicology Dos and Dont's
courses.description: When a pet has been poisoned, we want to act quickly to prevent problems or to treat signs that are already present. It is important to know which methods and treatments are safe and effective, and also, which may cause harm. This presentation will cover some common toxin exposures with unique treatment requirements.

courses.title: Fear Free for Felines: An Introduction
courses.description: This course introduces veterinary professionals to the Fear Free approach specifically tailored for feline patients. Through a series of focused lessons, learners will explore communication strategies, considerate handling techniques, touch gradients, appropriate use of rewards, and gentle control methods. Practical scenarios and case studies will help reinforce strategies for reducing fear, anxiety, and stress (FAS) in cats during veterinary visits. Learners will leave equipped with the knowledge and resources to integrate cooperative care into daily workflows, creating a better experience for cats, clients, and veterinary teams.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Dogs with Osteoarthritis
courses.description: The course provides an understanding of potential Osteoarthritis (OA) signs and which dogs are at increased risk for developing OA. You will gain knowledge and confidence in discussing nutritional management strategies for this common canine health concern with pet parents. You will be able to guide pet parents in implementing proven nutritional management to help manage the progression of OA and provide some symptomatic relief.

courses.title: Animal Echo Collection: Assessment of the mitral valve and quantification of mitral regurgitation in humans and other animals
courses.description:

PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: Animal Echo Collection is a new collection of OnDemand courses that provide learners with access to various echo topics where speakers discuss the similarities and differences in human and nonhumans. The OnDemand courses include a combination of lectures, animated videos, questions and case discussions.
Animal Echo Collection: Assessment of the mitral valve and quantification of mitral regurgitation in humans and other animals.
This OnDemand course will compare and contrast mitral valve structure and function between the species. This complementary approach will add to the knowledge and generation of ideas of any participant whose area is generally confined to one species of patient.

Bri Potter MS, DVM, DACVIM
William Zoghbi MD, FASE

Chris Orton DVM

courses.title: Dental Nerve Blocks (TECH359)
courses.description: This lecture will serve to provide veterinary technicians and veterinarians with instructions on performing safe and effective regional and local nerve blocks for painful dental procedures. Included in this discussion will be information on which drugs to use, drug doses, equipment needed, tissues blocked, and proper placement of the regional nerve block. Photos will be provided for visual aids.

courses.title: Controlling Controlled Drugs(TECH163)
courses.description: This course is designed to provide practical guidance on the administration of a controlled substance accountability program in the veterinary hospital. The course will present an overview of the DEA regulations, including registration, ordering, security, dispensing, accountability, inventories, and problem resolution scenarios that are likely to happen in a veterinary practice setting. **This course will discuss US federal (DEA) laws only. **

courses.title: Tales from the Crit: Interactive Hematology Case Studies with the Laboratory Retrievers-Module 4
courses.description:
The Laboratory Retrievers Purdue continuing education (CE) program is an online learning experience for veterinary professionals, created by the Laboratory Retrievers LLC and Purdue University College of Veterinary Medicine.
These highly interactive, case-based modules help veterinarians and technicians confidently interpret CBC data, analyze cytograms and recognize key blood film cell morphology in minutes.

courses.title: Alone, Afraid, & Misunderstood: Managing Canine Separation Anxiety in Practice
courses.description: Canine separation anxiety is one of the most common behavioral disorders encountered in veterinary practice. Dogs with separation-related distress may be presented with a history of vocalization, destructive behaviors, inappropriate elimination, self-injury, and/or other signs that can strain the human-animal bond and lead to relinquishment if left untreated. This webinar will review the current understanding of separation anxiety, including underlying emotional and behavioral mechanisms, differential diagnoses, and evidence-based treatment strategies. Attendees will explore practical approaches to diagnosis, client communication, behavior modification planning, and the appropriate use of pharmacologic support to improve outcomes for patients and their families.

courses.title: Movora Educations State of the Art Infection Prevention Protecting Your Patients and Practice Online Course
courses.description: Movora Educations State of the Art Infection Prevention Protecting Your Patients and Practice is a detailed explanation of the costs of surgical infections to clinics, doctors, patients, and pet owners. The two greatest risks to infection are discussed and solutions to these risks are considered. This course also includes a lecture from a veterinary surgeon about the similarities and differences between human and animal orthopedics. The final two lessons of the course review preoperative, postoperative and intraoperative strategies for avoiding surgical site infections, and makes a case for reduction of antibiotics in surgery.

courses.provider: CORNELL UNIVERSITY, COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: INTRAORAL RADIOLOGY IN THE DOG (458-43760)
courses.description: In this 4.5-hour online course, we comprehensively cover intraoral radiography in the dog. Our primary objective is to provide the learner with the skills and knowledge to obtain diagnostic images and to be able to interpret them efficiently and accurately in the clinical setting. We will cover the equipment required to take intraoral radiographs, review the normal radiographic anatomy, provide detailed explanations on how to obtain each projection, and how to correct common mistakes. The lessons will ultimately help the participant to systematically interpret pathological processes using real clinical cases. This course is composed of eight lessons covering understanding the benefits of intraoral radiology, radiographic equipment, normal radiographic anatomy refresher, principles of intraoral radiology, obtaining intraoral radiographs: step by step, troubleshooting common mistakes, orienting intraoral radiographs labial mounting, and interpreting intraoral radiographs.

courses.title: Small Animal Case Studies & Suturing Techniques
courses.description: This webinar will provide a hands-on introduction to wound closure suturing and knot-tying techniques through small animal case studies.

courses.title: Essentials of Veterinary Acupuncture
courses.description:
Essentials of Veterinary Acupuncture is designed for veterinarians with no prior experience of acupuncture, or for someone who trained a long time ago and needs a refresher. This course teaches techniques and some of the most powerful acupuncture points to get started in treating musculoskeletal disorders in small animals (also with some application in equines).
The course covers the benefits of acupuncture in Western Medicine terms. Acupuncture improves patient well-being in ways that are easy to understand - influencing autonomic activity, relieving pain and changing blood flow patterns, through techniques and mechanisms that the veterinarian can learn quickly and easily. The positive results with patients treated during this course can inspire you to obtain in-depth training through other more advanced courses.

courses.title: H5N1 Bird Flu: What to Know
courses.description: This course was created in partnership with the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) to provide recommendations and resources to help veterinary teams educate clients about H5N1 Bird Flu and promote safe practices to protect our pets and communities.

courses.title: Feeding Fido & Felix: Navigating the Right Diets for Liver Health
courses.description: This webinar with Dr. John P. Loftus will explore the critical role of diet in managing liver conditions in dogs and cats and offer a comprehensive guide to the best nutritional strategies. Attendees will learn about the different types of therapeutic (and nontherapeutic) diets available to support liver function, including low-protein, highly digestible, and antioxidant-rich options, and the importance of balancing key nutrients, such as amino acids, fats, and vitamins and minerals, to address specific liver-related conditions. Dr. Loftus will also cover how to tailor diets for individual pets based on their specific liver condition, whether it's for liver shunts, copper-associated hepatitis, or other liver conditions.

courses.title: Financially Friendly Clinics: Redefining Access and Trust in Veterinary Care
courses.description:
In todays challenging economic climate, veterinary clinics must rethink how they address clients financial concerns. Being financially friendly doesnt have to be about lowering prices, offering discounted care, or becoming a nonprofit, its really about creating an environment of empathy and collaboration that eases the financial burden of veterinary care. This webinar, Financially Friendly Clinics Redefining Access and Trust in Veterinary Care, explores practical steps clinics can take to support clients without compromising revenue.
From making payment options more visible and rethinking language for presenting treatment plans to fostering open, judgment free conversations about affordability, well outline simple yet impactful strategies to build trust and loyalty. Youll learn how small, easy to implement and low cost changes, such as revising payment signage, using proactive communication, and educating clients about financing options, can create an atmosphere of emotional safety for both clients and the veterinary team, and at the same time positively contribute to financial sustainability.
Join Suzanne Cannon, MS, MA, Co Founder of VetBilling, for a one hour session filled with actionable insights to position your clinic as a trusted partner in veterinary care. Discover how financial friendliness can improve client relationships, reduce stress for your team, and ultimately help more pets receive the care they deserve all without lowering your prices.

courses.title: Webinar Series - In-Depth Equine Ophthalmology with Drs. Dennis Brooks & Brian Gilger
courses.description: Ophthalmology in the horse is progressing rapidly. This in-depth module series will dramatically improve the ophthalmic capabilities of equine veterinarians and veterinary ophthalmologists at all levels of experience by providing knowledge of and insight into the latest diagnostic and therapeutic techniques and treatment options available to speed the healing of simple and complicated eye problems of the horse. Drs. Brooks & Gilger will be sharing invaluable tips and tricks and pearls of wisdom that they have acquired over the decades of experience in equine ophthalmology.

courses.title: STEP-BY-STEP CANINE EXTRACTION TECHNIQUES
courses.description:
The Step-by-Step Canine Tooth Extraction series was created to provide veterinarians with a practical, clinically focused approach to surgical exodontia through detailed educational PDF guides, high-resolution clinical photography, and concise narrated procedural videos.
Each module focuses on a specific extraction procedure, including the maxillary canine tooth, maxillary fourth premolar, mandibular canine tooth, and mandibular molar. The downloadable step-by-step PDF resources provide detailed explanations of surgical technique, instrumentation, flap design, bone removal, luxation mechanics, root elevation, sectioning strategy, tissue handling, and closure principles in a clear and methodical format.
Accompanying narrated videos are designed to reinforce key surgical concepts and demonstrate important procedural steps while guiding viewers through the clinical reasoning behind specific surgical decisions and techniques.
Rather than simply demonstrating how to remove a tooth, these modules emphasize understanding why certain approaches are performed, how to improve visualization and efficiency, how to preserve healthy tissue, and how to minimize surgical complications. The goal is to provide practical educational resources that veterinarians can repeatedly reference and apply directly in clinical practice.

courses.title: Certification in Veterinary Acupuncture
courses.description: Certification in Veterinary Acupuncture, is a 12-month, part-time, fully on-line course oriented towards applied theory, both traditional and scientific, which can be applied to clinical practice almost immediately. Confidence and competence is developed during the course with continuous case support from tutors, regular live case forums, and one-to-one practical sessions and assessments using Skype. Clinical training begins with simulated cases but rapidly transforms to discussion of your own patients and your treatment progress. IVAS recognizes the CIVT Acupuncture courses. CIVT Graduates of the Certificate Veterinary Acupuncture (Small Animal) course can join IVAS as Credentialed members. Students will begin to use acupuncture within the first module (for musculo-skeletal issues initially) and gradually build their skills and knowledge to include more complex internal medicine problems.

courses.title: Ensuring Controlled Substance Compliance in the Veterinary Clinic
courses.description: Controlled substance compliance is critical for all veterinarians, both to comply with federal regulations and to ensure that loss or unauthorized use of controlled substances does not occur. In veterinary practice, there are some common ways noncompliance may occur, potentially leading to theft of controlled substances or even consequences for the practitioner's DEA registration. In this webinar, attendees will explore how having strong policies and procedures, conducting training, and, in some cases, using electronic methods for medication tracking can help enhance their practice's current drug handling protocols to maximize compliance.

courses.title: Team Approach to Developing a Balanced Anesthesia Drug Protocol (TECH456)
courses.description:
A team-based approach to veterinary anesthesia is essential for ensuring patient safety, optimizing anesthetic outcomes, and promoting efficient clinical workflow. Members of the veterinary support team are frequently responsible for monitoring patients during anesthetic events, yet they are often excluded from the planning phase, which includes pre-anesthetic patient assessment, development of patient-specific anesthesia drug protocols, and anesthesia management strategies.
In this course, you'll explore all aspects of developing a balanced anesthesia drug protocol, beginning with pre-anesthetic patient assessment and progressing through commonly used drugs and techniques for premedication, induction, maintenance, and recovery. We'll incorporate weekly case-based discussions and practical applications to reinforce key concepts and promote real-world clinical applications.
By the end of the course, you will have gained the knowledge and confidence to participate actively in anesthesia planning and anesthesia drug protocol development - and you'll be ready to demonstrate to the veterinarians you work with that collaborative anesthesia management means better staff utilization, more efficient workflows, and enhanced patient outcomes.

courses.title: Approach to the Veterinary Oncology Patient
courses.description: This course covers the Approach to the Veterinary Oncology Patient. The course will cover the basics of diagnostics, staging, and treatment options for animal cancer patients. The program will also cover Pearls of Wisdom in Oncology: the dos and donts that apply to diagnostics and treatment of cancer in animals.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Disease Prevention in Spay/Neuter Clinics
courses.description: This level two course will cover disease prevention strategies, including preventing pathogen spread, cleaning and disinfection, and cross-contamination prevention.¿

courses.title: Veterinary Leadership Programme (PRAC165)
courses.description: This solutions-focused course empowers veterinary professionals to positively influence the people around them. Essential for current or aspiring leaders, skills in leadership, communication, and conflict resolution will also benefit every member of the veterinary team. Participants will learn to lead, manage, and motivate their teams effectively, communicate more successfully, and feel confident handling difficult situations.

courses.title: Treatment of Canine Parvoviral Enteritis
courses.description: This presentation will review the current standard-of-care treatment recommendations for canine parvovirus (CPV) using a case-based approach. Dr. Kristin Zersen will discuss fluid therapy, plasma products, antibiotics, and nutrition. Recommendations for outpatient treatment and the most recent literature discussing additional treatment options for puppies with CPV will also be reviewed.

courses.title: Point of Care Ultrasound for Assessment of Volume Status and Fluid Responsiveness
courses.description: POCUS is a valuable tool for assessing volume status and fluid responsiveness in both dogs and cats. Understanding the limitations and proper use of different ultrasound views can enhance diagnostic accuracy and improve patient care. The careful application of these techniques allows clinicians to tailor fluid therapy more precisely, optimizing outcomes for critically ill veterinary patients.

courses.provider: AMERICAN VETERINARY SOCIETY OF ANIMAL BEHAVIOR
courses.title: The Clinical Animal Behavior Conference 2025 (Recorded)
courses.description: The Clinical Animal Behavior Conference is a 2.5-day intensive conference focusing on veterinary behavioral medicine. The theme of this year's conference is "Expanding Your Behavioral Toolkit". Throughout the conference, attendees will learn the science behind various behavioral problems in companion animals and how to recognize, diagnose, and manage these problems. They will also learn strategies to implement change and reach financial success in the veterinary practice. Presentations include topics such as: Animal behavioral analysis and interventions; Understanding the role of antecedents in behavior; Recognition and management of feline elimination problems; Non-elimination behavioral problems in felines; Evidence-based handling of felines; Behavioral prevention for canine patients; Feline psychopharmacology; Cooperative veterinary care; How to implement change in veterinary practices; Business aspects of financial success while meeting patients' needs and more.

courses.title: Canine Cognitive Dysfunction - How to help our aging patients
courses.description: Join us for an informative webinar on Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome (CDS) in aging pets, where we'll explore the brain changes that contribute to this common condition. Learn how to recognize the early signs, utilize key diagnostic tools, and understand the most effective treatment options available. We'll also share practical strategies for preventing and managing symptoms to improve quality of life for senior pets. Don't miss this opportunity to deepen your knowledge and better support your aging patients or companions!

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: CANCER BIOENERGETICS
courses.description: One of the revised hallmarks of cancer is dysregulated energy metabolism. This session will cover the historical and modern concepts of glucose utilization and energy generation in cancer, how it may affect tumor cell behavior, and strategies for intervention.

courses.title: Ferret Basics (EXOT014)
courses.description: This course will cover the basics of ferret ownership and husbandry, as well as an overview of a general clinical approach to the species, discussing common diseases and their treatments.

courses.title: TOXICOLOGY SYMPOSIUM 2026 ( On Demand)
courses.description:
PROGRAM TITLE: Old Dogs, New Tricks: How Do New Toxin Treatments Measure Up? By Dr Karla Smith DVM
LECTURE ABSTRACT:
The lecture will discuss when newer therapies such as intralipids or cholestyramine are indicated for the treatment of toxicity and when established therapies are completely appropriate. Recent journal articles will be discussed, along with firsthand experience from ASPCA Poison Control. We will also touch on why some new therapies that sound exciting may not be useful in the real world.
PROGRAM TITLE: Species Sensitivities in the Toxin Realm by Dr Laura Stern DVM DABVT
LECTURE ABSTRACT:
We all know that cats are not small dogs, but why? This lecture will explore species differences between cats and dogs and how that affects their sensitivity to certain toxins. We will take a deep dive into the fascinating physiology that provides our least favorite complications when treating toxicities in our favorite companion animal species. Highlights include: ABCB1-1D genetic mutations, feline erythrocyte sensitivity to oxidative damage, feline specific metabolism defects, and dog and cat specific toxins.
PROGRAM TITLE: Toxic Top 10: What Australian Pets Are Really Getting Into by Pooja Mehta
Lecture Abstract:
What toxins are Australian veterinarians really encountering in practice? Based on five years of data from the Australian Animal Poisons Centre, Pooja Mehta reveals the most common toxin exposures reported across Australia and New Zealand - and what the AAPC team recommends for managing these cases.
LECTURE 4:
PROGRAM TITLE: Spectrum of Care: Appropriate Management of Toxicology Cases on a Budget by Dr Catherine Dzienisiewski VMD, MLAS, DABT
Lecture Abstract: The spectrum of care in the management of toxicities refers to the range of strategies used to recognize, assess, prevent, and treat adverse effects of toxicities. The primary goal is to ensure patient safety while maintaining treatment efficacy. It is important to establish key goals for veterinary c

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Basics of Extracorporeal Therapy for Toxin Exposures
courses.description: Extracorporeal therapies remove blood from our patients, manipulate or remove a component and then return the blood to our patients. The most common modalities used in veterinary medicine are hemodialysis, charcoal hemoperfusion, and therapeutic plasma exchange. Patients undergoing timely extracorporeal therapy can have a shortened course of intoxication or decreased severity of intoxication. However, these treatments are not without risks and serious adverse events have been reported. We will discuss the basics of each different treatment modality, characteristics of toxins that indicate which modality is most likely to be effective, and how to determine if your case might benefit from extracorporeal therapy. Specifically, we will discuss how to select the correct patient at the correct time with the right dosage and the right clinical signs in order to maximize the chances of a successful outcome.

courses.provider: CAREFREE DENTISTRY AND ORAL SURGERY FOR ANIMALS
courses.title: Introduction to Feline Dentistry and Oral Surgery
courses.description: This course provides comprehensive, hands-on training in feline veterinary dentistry and oral surgery, with emphasis on feline oral anatomy, common dental and periodontal pathology, regional anesthesia techniques, and methodical extraction procedures. Participants will learn evidence-based approaches to feline tooth extractions, including mucogingival flap design, sectioning multi-rooted teeth, alveolar bone removal, use of dental luxators, alveoloplasty, and tension-free closure, as well as strategies for managing common complications. The program combines focused lectures with extensive wet lab experience using feline cadaver specimens, allowing participants to build confidence and technical skill in diagnosing feline dental disease and performing extractions. Designed for DVMs seeking to improve their feline dentistry and oral surgery skills, this course emphasizes practical application, clinical decision-making, and improved patient outcomes in cats.
courses.location: Carefree Dentistry & Oral Surgery for Animals
