courses.title: Nutritional management for cats & dogs with concurrent health conditions affecting multiple organs
courses.description: This course is focused on the importance of nutritional management as part of a multimodal approach to supporting canine and feline patients suffering from concurrent conditions related to the kidneys, heart, pancreas, liver and bladder as well as fat sensitivities. Comorbidities can present a challenge in selecting a nutritional option with the proper balance of key nutrients to aid pets with varied health challenges.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Gatekeeping Pet Ownership: The Impacts of Adoption Discrimination - On-Demand
courses.description: The animal welfare field has been discussing low-barrier adoption processes as a best practice for more than a decade, yet recent research has found that BIPOC families are still more likely than white families to be denied during the adoption process. We conducted focus groups (n = 27) and surveys (n = 311) with BIPOC pet owners to gain a more nuanced understanding of BIPOC families' experiences with getting pets in four U.S. cities (Atlanta, GA; Miami, FL; Minneapolis, MN; Philadelphia, PA). Key findings include that only 28% of survey participants reported being treated with kindness/respect by a shelter/rescue. The remaining 72% reported negative experiences with a shelter/rescue, including being "ghosted", provided with misinformation, experiencing disrespect or embarrassment, and/or being intimidated or treated with hostility. The top three community-led solutions for making pet ownership accessible to all included: provide more services/supplies/information to support the health and well-being of pets after adoption/purchase (46%), eliminate processes that make it more difficult to acquire a pet (45%), and be more understanding about a person's financial situation (42%). These findings highlight the critical need to move discussions from "low-barrier adoptions" to "making pet ownership accessible to all".

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: 10 Things Pets Love to Get Into: Top Toxins for Dogs and Cats at ASPCA Poison Control
courses.description: In this one hour session, learn how to identify and treat the most common toxin exposures in companion animals. These include chocolate, grapes/raisins, xylitol, bromethalin, onions/garlic, lilies, alstroemeria, detergents, ibuprofen, and cholecalciferol. We will cover identifying levels of concern, considerations for approaching decontamination, clinical presentations, treatment, and diagnostic testing.

courses.title: The Endothelial Glycocalyx Targeting Vascular Permeability (DRIP100)
courses.description: The endothelial glycocalyx is not an ivory tower subject! When properly addressed, and therapeutically targeted, it can greatly improve mortality and morbidity in practice. The refresher or introduction of the endothelial glycocalyx will touch on the structure and function, as well as relevant pathology of damage, and potential therapies to support and improve the health of the endothelial glycocalyx.

courses.title: Hepatic Encephalopathy (DRIP108)
courses.description: This course briefly reviews the relevant pathophysiology of hepatic encephalopathy, but will focus on proper tools for diagnosis and most effective and logical therapies for maximum beneficial outcomes in treatment and/or management of patients.

courses.title: PLE-ease: Just Change the Diet? A Practical Approach to Chronic Enteropathies and Protein-Losing Enteropathy
courses.description: Chronic enteropathies (CE) and protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) remain among the most common yet diagnostically challenging gastrointestinal disorders encountered in small animal practice. This lecture provides an evidence-based, practical framework for approaching patients with chronic gastrointestinal disease, emphasizing the recently published 2026 ACVIM Consensus Statement on chronic enteropathies. Attendees will learn how to localize gastrointestinal disease, prioritize diagnostic testing, recognize disorders that mimic PLE, and determine when dietary therapy alone is appropriate versus when advanced diagnostics are warranted. The lecture concludes with a practical discussion of nutritional management, lymphangiectasia, thrombosis prevention, and treatment strategies for dogs with protein-losing enteropathy.

courses.title: Select Cases in Veterinary Neurology (DRIP161)
courses.description:
The course will expose the clinician to atypical presentations of common neurologic diseases through reviewing a few select cases.
To earn a certificate of completion, the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test.

courses.title: The many faces of FIP
courses.description: This session will discuss recent clinical experience with feline infectious peritonitis (FIP), emerging areas of knowledge with this virus, and a focus on the variety of clinical presentations of FIP. The session will utilize case discussions as a starting point for highlighting newly identified clinical manifestations of FIP, when to include FIP on the differential diagnosis list, and logical approaches to FIP diagnostic test selection and interpretation. We will review what is known in the literature and what is still not known, as well as upcoming areas of research to keep an eye on.

courses.title: Veterinary Dentistry Service Jump Start Step by Step
courses.description:
Let Dr. Beckman help you eliminate the stress with your veterinary dentistry cases by providing a blueprint for success. Feel at ease with each and every procedure by incorporating the lessons, tips and tricks learned in this course.
Create the Veterinary Dentistry Service that you, your staff and your patients deserve. Dr. Beckman guides you to overcome all obstacles and achieve the ultimate success in your practice. View the course videos and resources wherever, whenever and as many times as you like 24/7

courses.title: The Clinical Application of Cardiac NT-proBNP
courses.description: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a powerful, evidence-based biomarker that can help clinicians quickly differentiate cardiac from noncardiac causes of respiratory distress and detect occult heart disease before clinical signs appear. Use of NT-proBNP can help provide objective clarity when evaluating patients presented with murmurs, cough, or dyspnea and when interpreting equivocal radiographic findings, supporting confident decision-making in real time. As a follow-up to the previous webinar "The Clinical Utility of Cardiac Biomarkers," Dr. Stacey Hendershott will review the clinical application of NT-proBNP in the context of real-world cases.

courses.title: Aligning Programs with Community Needs to Support Companion Dog Retention (On Demand)
courses.description: Animal sheltering has evolved to focus on community-based services as much as in-shelter care. The philosophy that animal sheltering begins and ends within the community through various support programs is gaining traction. These programs, ranging from food banks and training classes to veterinary services, aim to support pet guardianship and retention in the home. However, there's often a mismatch between the programs offered and the actual needs of the community. In this session, Seana will share research on pre-COVID retention programs focused on companion dogs offered by US animal sheltering organizations, highlighting gaps between these programs and community needs. She will outline a strategic decision-making process for selecting community programs to support pets in homes and discuss different program options.

courses.title: Nutrition and Healthy Aging in Dogs: What Do We Know?
courses.description: Aging is associated with many physiological changes, some of which can be influenced by nutrition, disease status, environment and management, and activity. Senior dogs and cats commonly have a lower metabolism, less efficient digestion and metabolism, and less flexibility with lower resilience to environmental changes as well as health challenges. This talk will cover diet strategies and options for senior dogs including various commercial products in different marketing categories. We will also discuss how we can use nutritional strategies to prolong lifespan, and which nutrients may have benefits or risks for this population.

courses.title: Client Communication (STAF211)
courses.description: This presentation explores the critical role of communication in veterinary client interactions, emphasizing both verbal and nonverbal elements. It highlights that 93% of communication is nonverbal, including body language, tone, and facial expressions, while only 7% is verbal. Building trust and strong client relationships requires consistency, attentiveness, and honesty, as first impressions and positive interactions are vital for client satisfaction.

courses.title: Risks, Ethics, and Data: Practical AI Guidance for Relief Vets
courses.description:
Relief vets move between clinics, teams, systems, and workflows. AI can help make that work easier, but it needs to be used clearly, responsibly, and with the veterinarian in control.
In this webinar, Dr. Mike Mossop talks through the practical realities of AI in relief practice, including client consent, recording, privacy, data ownership, retention settings, documentation risk, and professional accountability.
You'll learn what to ask before using AI in a new clinic, how to think about sensitive client information, and how recordings and transcripts can support clearer records when used thoughtfully.

courses.title: Hamster, Mouse, and Gerbil Basics (EXOT020)
courses.description: This course will cover the basics of hamster, mouse, and gerbil ownership and husbandry, as well as an overview of a general clinical approach to the species, discussing common diseases and their treatments.

courses.title: Foundational Knowledge of Performing THR
courses.description: This course is designed to provide veterinary surgeons with the foundational knowledge needed to understand the full commitment of becoming a skilled, THR surgeon. This course reviews the case load and financial commitment for offering THR at a veterinary clinic. This includes the cost of education, staff, location, and equipment. The course also reviews the skill acquisitions process, and the time needed to complete the online, in-person and mentorship program. Finally, this course gives an overview of the hip systems offered by Movora.

courses.title: Lateral Suture Repair for Cranial Cruciate Ligament Insufficiency: Monofilament Nylon and OrthoZip
courses.description: Lateral Suture Repair for Cranial Cruciate Ligament Insufficiency: Monofilament Nylon and OrthoZip Online Course is designed to give background on when and why to use lateral sutures with cranial cruciate ligament disease. This course reviews how lateral sutures are biomechanically different, surgical approach, meniscal management, and the importance of isometry.

courses.title: Under Pressure: Glaucoma Recognition and Treatment
courses.description: In this lecture with Dr. DJ Haeussler we go over common causes of glaucoma, medical, and surgical management.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Feeling Thorny: Identifying and Treating Common Plant Exposures in Dogs & Cats
courses.description: This 1-hour webinar will cover the basic concepts behind the clinical management of dog and cat plant exposures. We will focus on common landscape and ornamental plants. We will discuss tactics to help the clinician overcome the common obstacles to performing a risk assessment and developing a treatment plan for patients. The management of these cases will be presented in a systems-based fashion to allow us to cover a broad range of toxic plants within the hour. Please note that food plant exposures (grapes/raisins, onion/garlic, avocado, macadamia nut, etc.) will not be discussed in detail.

courses.provider: CAREFREE DENTISTRY AND ORAL SURGERY FOR ANIMALS
courses.title: Introduction to Canine Dentistry and Oral Surgery
courses.description: This course provides comprehensive, hands-on training in veterinary dentistry with a focus on pathology recognition, local anesthesia techniques, and surgical extraction principles. Participants will learn evidence- based methods for retained root retrieval, periodontal flap surgery, and root planing. The program also includes instruction on the clinical use of Doxirobe and the application of bonded sealants for advanced dental case management. Designed for DVMs seeking to improve their practical dentistry skills, this course combines lecture-based learning with guided clinical exercises to build confidence in performing common and advanced dental procedures.
courses.location: Carefree Dentistry & Oral Surgery for Animals

courses.title: Pet insurance claims as a One Health tool to monitor diverse classes of diseases
courses.description: We will examine the usefulness of pet insurance claims for the North American pet insurance company Fetch to monitor diseases in several different classes. We will discuss: giardiasis (a potentially zoonotic protozoan parasite), valley fever (an environmental fungal disease), Lyme disease (a vector-borne disease), and zoonotic dog intestinal worms. Taking these diseases which have very different transmission mechanisms, and comparing them between people and dogs has revealed that pet insurance claims can be an important One Health tool.

courses.title: Growing Pains & Golden Years: Tackling Separation Anxiety & Lookalikes Across Life Stages
courses.description: Separation-related behaviors do not just affect anxious, middle-aged dogs; they can emerge in puppies, resurface in seniors, or even mask other conditions like cognitive dysfunction. In this case-based lecture, Dr. Lisa Radosta will explore how life stage can shape anxiety triggers, treatment needs, and outcomes. Attendees will discover the importance of early intervention, how to distinguish separation anxiety from lookalike problems, and how tools like Reconcile can help improve both treatment success and quality of life. Attendees will leave with practical strategies to keep clients engaged in the conversation and support patients, whether they are a bouncy pup or a golden oldie.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Shelter Practices and Barriers in the Use of Anxiety Medications and Alternatives (On Demand)
courses.description:
Fear, anxiety, and stress are common challenges for cats and dogs in shelter environments, yet little is known about how shelters use psychoactive medications and non-medication alternatives to address these welfare concerns. This presentation will include findings from a recently published study examining which psychoactive medications (such as gabapentin, trazodone, and fluoxetine) and non-medication alternatives (such as pheromones and nutraceuticals) are most commonly used in shelters in North America, how shelter staff perceive their efficacy and of administration, and the barriers such as cost, uncertainty about efficacy, and time constraints that limit their use, when warranted.
In addition to highlighting key differences between cats and dogs in reported treatment frequency, this presentation will explore how factors such as shelter type, intake volume, and staff roles influence anxiety-medication decision-making.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: ACVIM North American Neuroscience Course (Brain Camp): Advanced Diagnostic Imaging
courses.description: This 2-day module is an intense review of advanced neuroimaging, primarily focusing on magnetic resonance imaging. Computed tomography and clinical cases are incorporated into the module. Important points of physics and disease syndromes will be emphasized.

courses.title: From Disaster to Decontamination: Common Toxicities and Advanced Elimination Strategies
courses.description: This lecture reviews a practical, stepwise approach to the toxic veterinary patient, from initial exposure and triage through decontamination and advanced elimination strategies. Participants will discuss common intoxications encountered in small animal practice, including risk assessment, stabilization, gastrointestinal decontamination, antidote use, and supportive care. The session will also introduce advanced extracorporeal toxin removal techniques including carbon hemoperfusion, hemodialysis, and therapeutic plasma exchange, with emphasis on identifying appropriate candidates and understanding when referral is indicated. Attendees will leave with a structured framework for managing toxicity and making informed decisions about advanced toxin elimination.

courses.title: Gall Bladder Disease and Surgery
courses.description: This is a lecture on gall bladder disease and surgery options in small animals, primarily canine and patients.

courses.title: Leveraging Pheromones to Improve Patient Well-being
courses.description: Pheromones are a powerful yet often underutilized tool for improving well-being during interactions with veterinary professionals. This webinar explores how species-specific pheromones can help strengthen the "trust triangle" between pets, owners, and veterinary teams by reducing fear, promoting emotional safety, and supporting smoother exams and procedures. Attendees will learn how to integrate pheromones into real workflow touchpoints--from lobby to exam room to treatment areas--and how to communicate their value to pet owners in a clear, confidence-building way. Participants will walk away with practical guidance they can implement immediately to enhance patient comfort, improve team efficiency, and elevate the overall client experience.

courses.title: Challenges Facing the Front Desk (STAF210)
courses.description: Building client loyalty is an opportunity happening all day, every day. The front office staff member plays the most critical role in the success or failure of a veterinary practice. No matter how competent, capable, or caring you are, at some point clients will be unhappy with you. How your front desk handles these situations may determine whether this client returns or whether you lose that client. Unified front desk staff will create a loyal clientele that will assure compliance with the doctor's recommendations. Your front desk staff will attract new clients and solidify the current clients while creating a positive experience. They generally improve productivity and efficiency in your veterinary practice along with handling the distressed client with ease.

courses.title: Is there Anything Beyond Clinical Work for Veterinary Professionals (VCAS110)
courses.description: In this conversation the many options available to veterinarians beyond clinical practice will be discussed. Strategies for knowing whether to lean into discomfort or recognize it is time to make a change will also be explored. The session will also discuss personal preferences and how they relate to different career options.

courses.title: Peaceful Euthanasia Certification
courses.description: The CAETA Peaceful Euthanasia Certification. was developed to provide students with the most progressive, modern approaches to euthanasia. CAETA goes beyond basic core competencies to ensure the skillful delivery of current techniques and emotional intelligence necessary to protect well being and sustainability. The Program is 10 hours in length.The focus is on small companion animal euthanasia, with attention given to best practices for livestock, horses and exotics. We closely follow the AVMAs Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals document and CAETAs 14 Essential Components of Companion Animal Euthanasia.Those who complete will earn the designation of Certified Peaceful Euthanasia Veterinarian (CPEV) or Certified Peaceful Euthanasia Professional (CPEP)

courses.title: Therapeutic Update & Year-in-Review With Dr. Jim Budde
courses.description: 2025 saw the debut of novel drugs and changes to existing therapeutic options in veterinary medicine. Join veterinary pharmacist Dr. Jim Budde in this webinar powered by Standards of Care as he recaps new drugs that entered the veterinary profession in 2025 and summarizes the updates to existing therapeutics, from sirolimus to ilunocitinib, bedinvetmab to fluralaner, and beyond. Dr. Budde will be joined by clinical expert Dr. Rachel Halpin as they discuss the impact of these drugs on subclinical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in cats, otitis externa in dogs, and more.

courses.title: Rabbit Basics (EXOT016)
courses.description: This course will cover the basics of rabbit ownership and husbandry, as well as an overview of a general clinical approach to the species, covering common diseases and their treatments.

courses.title: Immune Thrombocytopenia (DRIP118)
courses.description: This course will take you through the fundamentals of the immune thrombocytopenic patient. The physiological process of immune thrombocytopenia will be discussed along with the diagnostic approach and treatment of the ITP patient.

courses.title: Webinar - Acid/Base Balance in Horses - Interpreting Arterial Blood Gas Samples
courses.description:
This webinar was devised for veterinarians who need to understand acid base balance and interpret blood gas results related to acid base balance in horses, e.g. equine anaesthetists, equine internal medics, equine surgeons.
It will cover the basics of acid-base balance in the horse and detail the 'traditional' or (Sigaard-Andersen) approach to interpreting blood gases, simple and mixed examples will be given. The focus is to get the attendees to feel confident interpreting blood gas results in their own cases. This webinar is aimed at those with a veterinary undergraduate degree, and or, another degree (e.g. nurses/technicians - who did chemistry at an advanced level at school e.g. equivalent to A-level in the UK).

courses.title: CN1200: Canine CranioSacral Therapy - Level 1
courses.description: This 5-day class will train students in the theory, concepts and practice of Craniosacral Therapy as it pertains to the canine population, while giving them the opportunity to integrate this knowledge with the Nervous System and Fascial System. This course is designed to teach participants the skills involved in evaluating and helping neuromusculoskeletal/fascial dysfunction in dogs.

courses.title: EQ103: Advanced Equine Soft Tissue Techniques, Intro to Spinal Mobilization, Rehabilitation Concepts & Clinical Reasoning
courses.description: This 5-day course has a strong emphasis on the practical application of advanced equine bodywork/soft tissue mobilization (STM) techniques, including sports massage, stretching, mobilization and muscle activation techniques. It is designed for equine healthcare providers to incorporate the use of soft tissue work into their existing practices and elevate their skills to apply the advanced techniques.
courses.location: Keep Stables at Chapel View Farm

courses.title: Safe Knotting & Suturing Techniques
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Ameet Singh will review how to perform and use commonly performed friction knots, including the strangle knot, modified Miller's knot, and the Aberdeen knot, to improve your subcutaneous tissue closures. The presentation will also discuss additional suturing tips and tricks to help avoid complications.

courses.title: Principles of Fracture Repair
courses.description: The Principles of Fracture Repair course covers topics including reliable techniques and valuable, applicable tips for repairing both simple and more challenging comminuted fractures of long bones. In this course learners will familiarize themselves with surgical technique, new implant design, common complications and how to manage them, pre-operative planning, and post operative management.

courses.title: Chronic Vomiting in Cats (DRIP142)
courses.description:
This course focuses on relevant pathophysiology and diagnostic testing regarding chronic vomiting in cats and discusses potential therapies.
.

courses.title: Graduate Diploma for Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine
courses.description: The Graduate Diploma of Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine enables practitioners to develop competency in utilising Western herbal medicine and Western herbal medicine principles in the assessment, treatment and management of animals in their care. Successful completion of this course will enable you to integrate a new therapy into practice. The course is orientated towards applied theory, which you can implement in your work almost immediately. Practitioners will be able to develop confidence and competence over time with continuous case support, guidance and feedback from tutors with both simulated and active case forums and subsequently their own clinical cases.

courses.title: Cardiac Level 2: Color & Spectral Doppler Online
courses.description:
This course will cover two dimensional and left parasternal imaging planes in order to apply the principles of doppler as it applies to image quality and accuracy. Normal and abnormal color flow of MR, TR, RVOT, and LVOT will be taught in order to understand and incorporate spectral doppler and pressure gradients. Echocardiographic features of the common acquired diseases of CVD, PH, DCM, HCM, HOCM, and NSCM will be taught. At completion of this course the attendee will be able to incorporate color and spectral doppler into their echocardiographic exam, and recognize echocardiographic features of some of the common acquired heart diseases.
It is a Medicine class delivered in a lecture format, non-interactive online.

courses.title: Poultry Medicine for Veterinarians
courses.description: This online training program is designed to educate general-practice veterinarians about poultry issues in small-scale commercial and home flocks. The construction of the course is a collaboration between the University of Kentucky, Utah State University, and Michigan State University. The structure involves a series of modules, which allows each participant to advance at their own pace. Each module will be considered autonomously, allowing the participant to accrue CE credit per module.

courses.title: Cats and Calcium: A Review of Feline Hypercalcemia (MULT311)
courses.description: Calcium homeostasis is a complex process involving several hormones and organ systems. Hypercalcemia is increasing recognized in feline practice and is a significant cause of patient morbidity. This course will start with a review the essentials of calcium regulation, with an emphasis on the interactions between the various players. The clinical impact of hypercalcemia will be discussed, with a focus on common clinical signs and those associated with significant morbidity. A logical diagnostic approach based on the most common causes of hypercalcemia will then be outlined. And finally, management options for cats with hypercalcemia will be outlined, with an emphasis on the current evidence to support each approach.

courses.title: Veterinary Technician Utilization: What Does That Mean & How Do We Do It?
courses.description: Veterinary Technicians are an essential part of the veterinary healthcare team. Currently, technicians are in high demand and short supply with demand expected to grow exponentially over the next several years. During this presentation we will discuss the scope of practice for veterinary technicians and the difference between veterinary assistants and technicians. Attendees will learn where to find and interpret the practice act & rules of their state. Proper utilization of professional veterinary technicians can help mitigate the veterinary shortage as well as increase practice revenue and efficiency.

courses.title: Equine Behavior and Handling (TECH450)
courses.description: This course provides students with the foundational knowledge and practical skills required to safely and effectively handle, lead, and restrain horses in a variety of everyday, medical, and emergency situations. Emphasizing equine behavior, body language, and "low-stress" handling philosophies, students will learn to read subtle behavioral cues to anticipate a horse's reactions.

courses.title: Equine Radiology (TECH451)
courses.description:
In the fast-paced world of equine medicine, the Veterinary Technician is the "Chief Image Officer". This course is designed to transform your approach to equine imaging from "just taking pictures" to producing diagnostic-grade radiographs that allow for faster, more accurate diagnoses.
We focus on the unique challenges of the equine patient - unpredictable movement, large anatomy, and field conditions - while prioritizing the safety of the horse, the handler, and yourself.

courses.title: PATELLAR LUXATION PART 2: CASE SELECTION AND SURGICAL APPROACH (195-41362)
courses.description: It has been said that "God's problems become the surgeon's problem as soon as a scalpel touches the patient" ...life is too short to spend lots of time and anguish managing patient complications that could have easily been avoided in the first place! This lecture will utilize an evidence-based approach (supplemented by Dr. Palmer's experience) to guide you in case selection so that you can enjoy more than your share of "surgical successes" and avoid the cases that are at risk of developing complications. You will also learn Dr. Palmer's general step-by-step approach to patellar surgery as well view video demonstrations of a medial and lateral parapatellar arthrotomy.

courses.title: Stabilization of the Emergency Patient for Veterinary Technicians (TECH447)
courses.description: This self study course equips veterinary technicians/nurses with the core stabilization skills essential for emergency patients: rapid triage review and primary survey; venous access and catheter selection; fluid resuscitation planning and shock dosing; oxygen therapy options and FiO2 targets; venous blood gas (VBG) analysis and acid-base interpretation; and practical use of ECG and blood pressure monitoring tools to guide early interventions.

courses.title: Under the Microscope-Cytology for Veterinary Technicians (TECH263)
courses.description: Cytology is a common in-house testing tool in the veterinary practice in which veterinary technicians play a vital role in the collection process, data recording, and evaluation of specimens to aid the veterinarian in the preliminary diagnosis. The primary purpose of this course is to develop an understanding of the proper collection techniques, sample handling, processing, and evaluation of cytological specimens. Techniques to improve the diagnostic value of the specimen, submission to outside laboratories, cellular anatomy, and microscopic identification techniques will be covered.

courses.title: Practical Fluid Therapy: The What, How, and Why!
courses.description: This presentation will update clinicians on the latest approach to fluid therapy in their small-animal patients. The presenter will begin with background information on the various types of fluid loss and the types of fluid available to treat these conditions. He'll review how to develop a fluid therapy plan (route, rate, type) and assess individual patients. The new concept of the endothelial glycocalyx and its clinical importance will also be discussed. The presenter will end with a case example to reinforce his learning objectives.

courses.title: Multi-Cat Households: Updates to Recognizing and Managing Intercat Conflict
courses.description: Although intercat conflict is common in companion cats, it is often unrecognized because of the subtle signs that occur more frequently than hissing or fighting. Without addressing the intercat conflict, feline welfare is impaired. Learn the most recent information to detect intercat conflict, the interplay between mental and physical health and how to manage the distress in these patients. Although psychopharmacology is often recommended, it is most important to address the physical and social environment and identify whether medical management is needed.

courses.title: Increasing Engagement in Kitten Fostering Programs: Lessons Learned from High Kitten Intake Zip Codes in LA County (OnDemand)
courses.description: Debra Olmedo and Greg Miller will provide an overview of recent research aimed at identifying ways to increase awareness and engagement in kitten fostering programs among residents of areas with high intake of kittens to animal shelters. They will discuss the project methodology, what they learned about awareness, interest, and concerns related to fostering, and what opportunities this research highlighted for increasing fostering program engagement.

courses.title: CRANIAL CRUCIATE LIGAMENT DISEASE PART 1: DIAGNOSTIC TIPS AND TRICKS (195-41356)
courses.description: This lecture focuses on techniques for diagnosing cranial cruciate ligament disease (CrCLD) in the canine. The lecture includes a comprehensive discussion of the subtleties of gait observation, stifle palpation, instability tests and stifle radiography. Participants will learn how to position patients for stifle radiographs that will permit detection of CrCD as well as pertinent co-morbidities that can render ExCap Suture stabilization a failure. After attending this lecture, attendees will be better able to diagnose CrCLD and detect important co-morbidities that may influence the best treatment plan as well as the patient prognosis.

courses.title: CY - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE CAT WITH CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE (CHF) WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION. (930-35078)
courses.description: CY - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE CAT WITH CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE (CHF) WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION. (930-35078) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: PET NUTRITION COACH CERTIFICATION (1027-36016)
courses.description: Nutrition is the cornerstone to patient health and well-being and is good medicine. The entire veterinary healthcare team should be the best source of nutrition information for pets. Clients who understand that preventive care preserves and lengthens their relationship with their pets are more likely to use veterinary services regularly, so team members should focus on proper nutrition for every patient that presents to their practice. Good nutrition is not a fad it is good business and good medicine. This course includes a training course and one sitting for the exam.

courses.title: The Master Class Collection (CDPS114)
courses.description:
If you feel insecure with your skills, you could be giving confusing or conflicting cues to dogs, creating fear and even aggression. By learning proper restraint methods and which movements they control, you can adapt quickly to the situation and to the dog's response.
Using counterconditioning and desensitization, you will create cooperative dogs for nail trims, injections, and venipuncture which shortens procedure time and uses fewer staff members. Gaining a dog's consent and reading body language properly can result in fewer bites.

courses.title: Medical Recordkeeping for Veterinarians
courses.description: Medical records are at the core of every successful veterinary practice. Creating good medical records can be integrated into every step of practice without adding any extra workload for associates. This course is designed to increase efficiency in practice, while ensuring compliance with the law. We specifically discuss effective client communication, obtaining client consent, anesthesia records, the SOAP/HEAP process, client handouts and other quality increasing, time-saving techniques. Legally, we will also cover evidentiary standards, legal presumptions, confidentiality and medical records storage.

courses.title: Acute Pancreatitis (DRIP117)
courses.description: This course will cover the physiology of acute pancreatitis in cats and dogs, including diagnosing and developing a treatment plan for pancreatitis patients.

courses.title: Zoonotic Diseases (TECH341)
courses.description: Common bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic zoonoses encountered by the veterinary professional will be covered. Clinical presentation in both animals and humans will be reviewed. Treatment and tests for these diseases will also be discussed. Prevention of transmission and protection of veterinary staff and clients will be explored.

courses.title: As Time Goes By-Aging & the Foundations of Small Animal Geriatric Medicine (MULT121)
courses.description:
This course is intended to introduce the small animal clinician to the principles and practice of canine and feline gerontology (both species will be discussed, but the body of information is considerably greater for dogs, and the course will reflect that).
We begin with the fundamentals of aging, including the core mechanisms and the clinical phenotype of aging in dogs and cats. After developing our understanding of aging as the most important modifiable risk factor for the three Ds of geriatrics- disability, disease, and death-we shift to building a systematic approach to the assessment and management of geriatric canine and feline patients. We review the most important diseases and clinical problems of senior dogs and cats and introduce evidence-based resources, such as formal assessment tools and clinical practice guidelines, to support the diagnosis, assessment, monitoring, and treatment of these conditions.

courses.title: Feline Ultrasound: 10 Ways Cats Are Not Small Dogs (DIAG435)
courses.description:
It's an often-repeated adage - "cats are not little dogs", and this is especially true with feline medicine and ultrasound. Cats have many unique diseases that require feline-specific knowledge to diagnose and treat. Ultrasound is one of the most useful tools feline clinicians have in their arsenal to diagnose diseases in cats, who often present with very vague and non-specific clinical signs.
This is one of four courses in the Feline Ultrasound collection. Each course will consist of a single 2-hour session that will focus on the normal ultrasound appearance of an organ system and then present changes observed that are associated with specific diseases. These courses are independent of each other and can be taken in any combination.
This course will review the ultrasound appearance of 10 diseases/anatomic variations that are unique to cats and were not touched upon during the other Feline Ultrasound courses. There will be time provided at the end of the session for questions regarding feline ultrasound stemming from this or any of the other Feline Ultrasound courses.

courses.title: The Art and Science of Negotiation
courses.description: This course leads the participants through the relationship-based approach to negotiating as taught to professional negotiators and applied to veterinary contract negotiation.

courses.title: Protect What Matters: Leveraging COPAT for Lifelong Oral Health
courses.description: This webinar will introduce veterinary teams to a structured, prevention-focused approach to managing dental disease in dogs and cats using the Comprehensive Oral Prevention, Assessment, and Treatment (COPAT) framework. In this session, Dr. Jan Bellows will emphasize the importance of shifting from episodic dental care to continuous oral protection and integrating client education, risk assessment, and individualized prevention strategies into everyday practice. Attendees will learn how to identify early disease, standardize dental workflows, and improve compliance through clear communication and practical tools. Dr. Bellows will highlight how each component of COPAT can contribute to reducing disease burden and improving patient healthspan. Real-world case examples and team-based protocols will be presented to support immediate implementation, leaving participants feeling equipped to elevate their dental programs from procedure-based care to comprehensive oral health protection.

courses.title: The Electrical System of the Heart: Principles and Applications of ECG Monitoring (TECH459)
courses.description: In practice, ECG rhythms often differ from textbook examples. Interpreting ECGs requires a gentle, detailed understanding of the heart's electrical workings. This engaging four-part course warmly guides you through the basics of conduction, pacing, and arrhythmias, and offers practical tips to help you become more confident in ECG interpretation.

courses.title: Telemedicine and Vaccine Clinics in California: What Shelters Need to Know About Legislative Updates for 2024 (OnDemand)
courses.description: This webinar will provide updates regarding vaccine clinics and telemedicine in veterinary medicine and shelters. Both Senate Bill 669, which expands the ability of Registered Veterinary Technicians to administer vital vaccines, and Assembly Bill 1339, which expands telehealth capabilities, will be covered. In this webinar, you will learn how to Utilize RVTs to run vaccine clinics in California without a veterinarian onsite; provide increased access to veterinary care through vaccine clinics in California; use telemedicine to expand the veterinary care your California shelter can provide; increase access to care for underserved pets in California; and utilize telemedicine to increase veterinary care for your own California shelter and foster animals.

courses.title: ADVANCED CERTIFICATION IN VETERINARY NEUROACUPUNCTURE (682-44688)
courses.description: The advanced certification in Veterinary Neuroacupuncture helps bridge the gap between Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and conventional veterinary medicine through a contemporary exploration and integration of the neurophysiological application of acupuncture in small animal clinical practice. It shows the connection between certain TCM theories and practices and current scientific explanations or theories of acupuncture, and how it works. It incorporates current scientific acupuncture theory and biomedical science in its application and approach to patient assessment and treatment, along with the application of TCM theory. Collaborative learning opportunities are gained through discussion and sharing of information, with a focus on the clinical application of this new knowledge. Problem-solving case studies are included and active forum discussions provide a range of current clinical conundrums for consideration.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: SCIENCE OF ONCOLOGY - ONLINE VIDEO SERIES- Epigenetics of Cancer
courses.description: This lecture describes the common, currently understood epigenetic mechanisms of mammalian cells that contribute to carcinogenesis. It will explain an overall mechanism for each type of epigenetic modification, and give specifics in veterinary oncology where they have been published. The student should be able to describe the effects of these epigenetic modifications on gene expression and cell function after this lecture.

courses.title: Managing common behavioral and neurologic problems
courses.description: Doctors Wininger and Pachel will present a complete discussion of the common neurologic and behavioral problems that they encounter in their individual practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of the problems- both canine and feline. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common behavioral and neurologic diseases and disorders.

courses.provider: AMERICAN INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL LASER APPLICATIONS
courses.title: Optimizing Your Laser Therapy Application Technique: Application Techniques to the Canine Joints
courses.description:
This is the first in a series of courses dedicated to optimizing the use of laser therapy in veterinary practice. This course will focus on the most effective techniques for applying laser therapy to the joints of canine patients. Sara Granburg, DVN, CCRP, and Lauren Bueter, BS, RVT, CCRP, CCMT, owners of Michiana Animal Rehab Services, will present as a team and demonstrate how to use different therapy lasers to target canine joint structures. They will provide both anatomical descriptions and video demonstrations to ensure thorough saturation of all joint structures with photonic energy, resulting in consistent clinical outcomes.
The course includes sections on the fundamentals of laser therapy, various application techniques demonstrating on and off contact, scanning and point-to-point delivery, and safety. Followed by sections on each joint structure unique to the canine patient: the joint structures of the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine, the scapulohumeral joint, the humeral-radial-ulnar joints, the carpal joint, the metacarpal joints, the interphalangeal joints of both the fore and hind limbs, the sacroiliac joint, the coxofemoral joint, the stifle joint, the tarsal joints, and the metatarsophalangeal joints.

courses.title: LafeberVet October 2024 Non-Interactive Program
courses.description:
The October 2024 Non-Interactive Program consists of one new webinar recording plus a preexisting program that includes six webinar recordings and three teaching modules that is eligible for submission (#972022), which includes webinar recordings and teaching modules.
The new webinar recording that will be submitted is "Exotic Companion Mammal Enrichment" by Teresa Bradley Bays, DVM, CVA, DABVP (ECM), CVMMP, CTPEP.
Six webinar recordings are being submitted for renewal: "Exotic Small Mammal Anesthesia Part II" by Jody Nugent-Deal, RVT, VTS (Anesthesia Analgesia) VTS (Clinical Practice Exotic Companion Animal), "Sedation and Pain Management of Exotic Companion Mammals" by Dario d'Ovidio, DVM, DVM, MS, SpecPACS, DECZM (Small Mammals), "What Parrots Want: The Importance and Use of Foraging and Environmental Enrichment for Birds" by Yvonne van Zeeland, DVM, MVR, PhD, DECZM (Avian Practice), "Avian Respiratory Anatomy, Physiology, and Disease: An Overview" by James Morrisey, DVM, DABVP (Avian Practice), "Don't Let It Croak Clinical Approach to Amphibian Emergencies" by Douglas Whiteside, DVM DVSc DACZM DECZM (Zoo Health Management), and
"Introduction to Avian Orthopedics" by David Scott, DVM.

courses.title: A deep dive into Cardiology
courses.description: This program covers fundamental principles of cardiology and applies them to advanced clinical management of patients with complex disease. We emphasize rational therapy based on underlying mechanisms of disease over standard protocol thinking. In addition, we have opportunity for the group to collaboratively assess numerous ECG studies and determine if therapy is indicated at all and, if yes, which approach would be most optimal for the situation.

courses.title: Movora Orthopedic Symposium 2022 Online Course
courses.description: The 2022 Movora Orthopedic Symposium hosted workshops, panel discussions, and presentations from leading industry professionals about current veterinary orthopedic research. This course includes 25 lessons. Each lesson consists of lesson objectives, a recorded presentation, and knowledge check questions. A passing score of 70% is required to complete this course.

courses.title: Updates in Oncology and Geriatric Care
courses.description: This program is designed to provide in-depth information regarding therapies to treat cancer in small animals. One session will discuss the utility of non-invasive cancer screening options as an early diagnostic tool in canine medicine. A second session will discuss how integrative cancer care can help enhance quality of life through the use of functional and physical medicine. A third session will focus on electrochemotherapy and the cancer care spectrum, identifying potential candidates for electrochemotherapy treatment. A fourth session will review common skin ailments in older patients and provide treatment options for each condition as well as how those are specifically applied to a geriatric patient population. A fifth session will review the common causes of urinary incontinence in senior pets and explain how to develop a rational diagnostic and therapeutic plan to help minimize incontinence and its side effects. The final session will discuss the pros and cons of pursuing dental procedures in geriatric and senior patients, focusing specifically on the safety of anesthesia in each case.

courses.title: Canine Chroic Enteropathy
courses.description: "This course provides a comprehensive review of diagnosis, treatment and long-term management of chronic GI disease in dogs, with a focus on using dietary management. Participants will take away practical management strategies and approaches to aid in long-term management of dogs with GI disease. "

courses.title: Bust Your Saboteurs!
courses.description: This interactive 2 hour workshop introduces veterinary professionals to the foundational concept of Positive Intelligence... recognizing and managing self-sabotaging thought and behavior patterns known as Saboteurs. Participants will learn to identify the nine most common Saboteurs that undermine well-being, relationships, and productivity in veterinary practice. Through group exercises, reflection, and hands-on application, attendees will explore the impact of Saboteur dynamics on team and client interactions, and discover strategies to foster resilience, emotional intelligence, and trust within their work culture. Attendees will also experience the PQ Self-Command tool, with evidence-based neuroscience support, to shift from stress-driven reactions to a more calm, focused, and effective mindset. By the end of the workshop, participants will be equipped with actionable skills to reduce burnout, enhance collaboration, and elevate quality of care for themselves, their teams, and their patients.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: SCIENCE OF ONCOLOGY - ONLINE VIDEO SERIES - Canine Cancer Precision Medicine
courses.description: Cancer is a genetic disease. The genomics revolution of the past two decades has provided detailed maps of the underpinnings of many human cancers through the generation of hundreds of thousands of cancer genome sequences. These data are increasingly leveraged to guide development of new clinical diagnostics, prognostics, and targeted treatments that are improving outcomes for human cancer patients. The genomics revolution has now also crossed into veterinary oncology, particularly in pet dogs, where nearly two thousand cancer genomes have been sequenced and published in the past five years alone. Although the path from mapping cancer genome landscapes to clinical translation is still under development, the oncoming flood of genomic data stands poised to transform veterinary oncology. We and others are charting the genomic landscapes of naturally occurring canine cancers in order to develop new clinical tools for veterinary oncology and to establish comparative settings in which clinical hypotheses can be rapidly tested across species. Here we will review cancer's genetic basis across species, summarize the history of and recent developments in naturally occurring canine cancer genomics, and discuss implications of these emerging data for development of new clinical tools in veterinary oncology including opportunities and challenges in leveraging these data.

courses.provider: UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA MAPLES CENTER FOR FORENSIC MEDICINE
courses.title: Euthanasia by Injection: Parts 1 and 2
courses.description:
This online, on-demand course prepares students with the knowledge and clinical skills necessary to seek licensure, or to recertify, as a Certified Euthanasia Technician (CET) for animal shelters. The course is divided into two parts that may be taken separately or together:
Part 1: consists of interactive lecture content about anatomy, pharmacology, proper administration and storage of euthanasia drugs, federal and state laws regulating the storage and accountability of euthanasia solutions, euthanasia technician stress management, and proper disposal of euthanized animals.
Part 2: consists of hands-on, clinical skills competency training where students practice and demonstrate proficiency with animal selection; proper handling of syringes and needles; calculating drug dosage; record-keeping for controlled drug logs; low-stress handling of animals; giving SC, IM, IV, IP, and IC injections; verifying depth of anesthesia; verifying death; and proper body disposal.

courses.title: ARCO - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE DOG WITH DEGENERATIVE VALVULAR DISEASE WITH SEVERE SYSTEMIC HYP (930-35077)
courses.description: ARCO - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE DOG WITH DEGENERATIVE VALVULAR DISEASE WITH SEVERE SYSTEMIC HYP (930-35077) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Fear Free Anesthesia & Surgery: From Intake to Discharge
courses.description:
Anesthesia and surgery are often the most stressful parts of the job for any veterinary professional. As people who are involved in anesthesia and surgery on a daily basis, we often forget that our patients and their owners do not have the same level of understanding and perspective and that can make the experience even scarier. As veterinary staff, we also sometimes get into such a pattern with our process that we stop looking for ways to improve and may miss opportunities to do better for our patients, clients, and to elevate to work we do.
For all our veterinary patients, care is a continuous process and that process begins and ends at home. This is most true when considering patients presenting for anesthesia and surgery. This lecture will cover consideration for improved patient care beginning with potential need for pre-visit pharmaceuticals (PVPs) through to techniques and considerations for less stressful drop-offs and important client communication. We will also discuss techniques, tips, and tricks to maximise sedation, decrease stress levels, and minimize adverse outcomes during the premedication and induction periods. Intra-operative techniques will be discussed to ensure that patients reach recovery as comfortably as possible. Lastly, we will discuss indepth ways to make recovery a smoother, safer, calmer experience for both patients and staff.

courses.title: ONLINE VET NURSE CONFERENCE 2024 ( On Demand)
courses.description:
Scales in Slumber: The Art and Science of Reptile Anaesthesia by Samantha Clutterbuck Anesthesia in reptiles presents unique challenges due to their diverse physiology and varying responses to anesthetic agents. This 1-hour webinar explores the intricacies of reptile anesthesia, blending the art and science required to safely and effectively manage these patients. Attendees will gain insights into the unique physiological considerations of reptiles, learn best practices for anesthetic protocols, and understand how to monitor and manage anesthesia in different species. The webinar will also cover common complications and how to prevent them, ensuring that veterinarians can provide the highest standard of care for their scaly patients Wound Management: 7 Tips to Advance your Nursing Care by Flick Caldwell : Veterinary nurses and technicians provide an essential clinical role in the triage and management of a vast range of wounds in traumatic and emergent patients. This lecture invites you to explore the key stages required for the assessment and treatment of wounds, alongside the care planning required for the wound patient.
We will discuss a wide range of wound dressings and their correct application for a variety of wounds, ranging from sterile surgical incisions to infected and chronic non-healing wounds.
You will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge to patient case studies within this lecture, and gain confidence as a clinical practitioner in wound care.
Elevating Veterinary Nutrition to a Standard of Care: Implementing the 4 Paws Method for Effective Client Communication by Dr Bryony Senic : This presentation will cover the importance of nutrition as the 5th vital assessment. It will introduce the 4 paws method for how we open the door for nutrition conversations and effective client communication. It will cover what are open ended questions, how to obtain a dietary history, effective communication styles and the non verbal communication that we can use.

courses.title: On-Demand: Nourishing Noses and Tails: Using Physical Exams to Decode Nutrition
courses.description: As veterinarians we typically rely on medical history and physical examination to determine health and identify problems in our patients. The nutritional assessment portion of this evaluation usually includes information about diet and feeding plan along with evaluating body weight trends, body condition score (BCS), and muscle condition score (MCS). There is more to a nutrition assessment if we just dig a bit deeper into patient history and include more observations on physical examinations. Questions about appetite/enthusiasm at mealtime, overall energy, stools, breath, and even body odor can give us more insights into nutritional status. The devil is in the details when you closely evaluate coat, skin, nails and oral health. Also, diagnostic labs and/or lab trends can be used as part of an in-depth nutritional assessment. Using more specific history, physical examination, and diagnostic testing will enable you to readily determine if the current diet and feeding plan is providing your patient optimal nutrition. Case examples will highlight the how and why of more in-depth nutritional assessments for our veterinary patients.

courses.title: Vet BLUE Lung Point of Care Ultrasound Online Course
courses.description: The Vet BLUE Lung Point of Care Ultrasound Online course is a self-paced recorded online course that includes 8 modules covering: Introduction to lung ultrasound, image acquisition (how to perform lung ultrasound), wet lung vs. dry lung principles, cased based applications including assessment for pulmonary edema, pneumonia and other wet lung conditions, nodular diseases and pulmonary masses, assessment for pulmonary thromboembolism, and using Vet BLUE for patient monitoring and CPR.

courses.title: Maddies Insights: Benefits of Pair-Housing Dogs on Welfare Measures and Length of Stay - Live
courses.description: Dogs are often housed alone in shelter settings to reduce injury and disease spread. However, social isolation can be a stressor for dogs. Most prior studies have focused on laboratory dogs or shelter dogs that have been kenneled for several months. Thus, those results might not necessarily generalize to shelter dogs, many of which have shorter lengths of stay than those dogs studied to date and might be co-housed soon after intake. We investigated the behavioral and physiological effects of single- or pair-housing shelter dogs, most of which had recently entered the shelter, as well as the impact of pair-housing on length of stay. In this talk, we will review the literature on cohousing dogs, go into detail on our study methods and results, and discuss the benefits of pair-housing dogs, as well as practical considerations for pair-housing dogs.

courses.title: KYON ALPS PAUL-II: Introduction Course Online Course
courses.description: This is an introductory course to ALPS Proximal Abducting Ulnar Osteotomy system, PAUL-II. It provides relevant information about the PAUL-II system, indications for PAUL, pre and post-operative care and the PAUL-II surgical technique.

courses.title: Traditional Chinese Herbal Medicine for Veterinarians: Begining to Advanced, Two Paths to the Summit.
courses.description: This course will take licensed veterinarians from a very basic understanding of Chinese herbal medicine to an advanced knowledge and application. Two Paths To The Summit" is Dr. Chris Besson's textbook on TCVM herbals, and it incorporates not only Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine concepts of the herbs but also biomedical understanding. Utilizing the latest research in both pathways, this text serves as the foundation for educating veterinarians to use herbal formulas, regardless of the path they choose to understand them. This novel approach, which utilizes both biomedical and traditional Chinese veterinary medical understanding of herbal medicine, is unique. In addition to pre-recorded videos, participants have access to weekly calls where they can receive further instruction, ask questions, and receive support in applying what they've learned to their patients.

courses.provider: AMERICAN INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL LASER APPLICATIONS
courses.title: INTRODUCTION TO COMPANION ANIMAL LASER THERAPY (554-44787)
courses.description:
This course provides access to the complete Companion Animal Therapy Certification Course. This course outlines the biological effects of medical lasers for treating common conditions in companion animals. It covers the effects of medical lasers in the promotion of analgesia, acceleration of wound healing, and reduction of inflammation.
There are demonstrations for treating a variety of disorders concerning the oral cavity, ear, cervical region, elbow, lumbar spine, hip, stifle, tarsus, and others.

courses.provider: AMERICAN INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL LASER APPLICATIONS
courses.title: VETERINARY MEDICAL LASER SAFETY OFFICER TRAINING (554-39421)
courses.description: The Veterinary Medical Laser Safety Officer (VMLSO) is an integral member of your team to ensure the safe use of therapy laser in a clinical environment.

courses.provider: DELAWARE VALLEY VETERINARY ACADEMY OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: Real-World Topics in Small Animal Dermatology
courses.description: This course explores various topics in small animal dermatology. We will review the underlying causes, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, and evidence-based treatment strategies for different skin conditions and dermatological issues.

courses.title: Small Animal Myofascial Practitioner - CSMP I
courses.description:
CSMP I: Online Lecture (10 hours)
This program will provide an overview of muscle and fascia, myofascial pain syndromes and trigger points. Palpation, diagnosis, and a wide range of treatment options are then discussed, including treatment technique, legislation, and needle safety. The 25 muscles that we are going to focus on in this course are then covered extensively with an emphasis on location, referral patterns and treatment protocols per muscle group.

courses.title: Introduction to Exotic Felid Medicine (EXOT616)
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss the basic husbandry, medical, and nutritional needs of exotic felids, including common diseases, anesthesia and sedation techniques, and reproduction.

courses.title: Separation Related Problems in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This presentation will cover the clinical signs of separation related problems, diagnosing separation related problems, and treating separation related problems in both dogs and cats.

courses.title: Congreso Veterinario de Leon Florida
courses.description:
For Veterinarian and technicians Professional, 2nd Edition of the congress in Spanish, the conference will held for the second time in Florida, with International and USA speakers. The target audience will be Spanish and bilingual attendees.
The topics will span the full range of veterinary specialties (mainly small animals related).

courses.title: Stay Safe During Equine Emergencies
courses.description: This webinar contains information useful to all veterinary professionals, even those who do not practice on horses. Since horses are often transported to different locations, accidents can happen anywhere. Practitioners are introduced to easy ways to learn the Incident Command model for safe teamwork for daily use in the clinic, as well as response to field emergencies. Choosing the correct end points relevant to various dangerous scenarios, and the difficult decision-making processing for triage, treatment and euthanasia are threaded throughout the presentation.

courses.provider: VETERINARY EMERGENCY AND CRITICAL CARE SOCIETY
courses.title: IVECCS 2026 - On Demand
courses.description: In conjunction with IVECCS 2026, a selection of sessions from the live conference held in Savannah, GA from September 14-17th will be available on-demand for 30 days following the event, allowing attendees extended access to valuable educational content and resources. Through its commitment to delivering state-of-the-art continuing education, the Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Society continues to advance the standards of care for critically ill and emergent large and small animal patients. The comprehensive scientific program is designed to meet the needs of veterinary professionals across all levels of experience and areas of interest, offering a diverse range of sessions led by experts in the field. Educational topics will include toxicology, exotics, fluid therapy, practice leadership, CPR, respiratory medicine, point-of-care ultrasound, surgery, emergency medicine, critical care, anesthesia and analgesia, gastrointestinal and hepatic disorders, renal medicine, urgent care, ICU management, and technician-focused education, as well as professional leadership development.

courses.title: Feline Weight Management
courses.description: An introductory course focused on feline weight management including the importance of proper nutrition and nutrient balance when developing a weight management program. The modules in this course provide a deeper understanding of many aspects of weight management including an overview of the disease condition, factors involved in diagnosing a weight issue, recommendations for treatment plans as well as communication tips for engaging the pet parent to ensure successful outcomes.

courses.title: CRANIAL CRUCIATE LIGAMENT DISEASE PART 4: MENISCUS AND POSTOP CARE (195-41360)
courses.description: This lecture focuses on the pathogenesis and treatment of meniscus tears associated with CrCLD in the canine and postoperative patient care after extracapsular stifle stabilization surgery. This lecture includes a review of the meniscal anatomy, tips for surgical visualization of the meniscus, surgical treatment for meniscal tears, and medial meniscal release. This lecture also discusses the three phases of rehabilitation after extracapsular stifle stabilization surgery.

courses.title: Feline Leukemia Testing: One and Done for Everyone
courses.description: In 2020, the AAFP released new retrovirus testing guidelines that recommend one quality point of care test then moving forward with a live-outcome pathway. In accordance, Austin Pets Alive!, home of the most robust FeLV adoption program in the world, changed its FeLV testing protocols. No more serum testing. No more "confirmation" testing. What does this mean in practice, how do we pathway plan for cats with different diagnoses, and why is this the new recommendation?

courses.title: LafeberVet Fall 2025/Winter 2026 Non-Interactive Program
courses.description: The Fall 2025/Winter 2026 Non-Interactive Course consists of four webinar recordings "A Refresher on Guinea Pig Medicine" and "Clinical Medicine of Bearded Dragons" by Dr. Grayson Doss, "Therapeutic Techniques in Reptile Patients" by Dr. Douglas Mader and "Sunburned! An Evidence-Based Update on UVB Lighting for Captive Exotic Species" by Dr. Mark Mitchell.

courses.provider: THE WORLD SMALL ANIMAL VETERINARY ASSOCIATION (WSAVA)
courses.title: 50th World Small Animal Veterinary Association (WSAVA)
courses.description:
The 50th World Small Animal Veterinary Association World Congress, organised by the Associacao Nacional de Clínicos Veterinários do Brasil, will take place in the vibrant city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, from September 25 to 27, 2025. This landmark event will be held simultaneously with the Brazilian ANCLIVEPA Congress and the FIAVAC Congress, creating a unique opportunity for veterinary professionals to participate in a comprehensive educational experience.
The congress will feature a wide range of sessions on the latest advancements in veterinary medicine, delivered by highly qualified international and local experts. Topics will cover cutting-edge research, emerging treatments, and best practices in small animal care, offering participants the chance to expand their knowledge, engage in meaningful discussions, and collaborate with colleagues from around the world.
In addition to the scientific sessions, attendees will have the chance to explore the local culture, enjoy Rio's iconic attractions, and network with professionals in a welcoming, international environment. Whether you're looking to enhance your clinical expertise or foster new professional connections, the WSAVA 2025 Congress promises to be an unforgettable experience.

courses.title: I have Made a Mistake, Now What? (VCAS109)
courses.description: In this conversation the emotional impact of making a mistake is discussed, including how the individual reactions to mistakes can shape relationship with oneself, colleagues and clients. The concepts of shame, vulnerability and resilience are introduced, as well as practical tips on how to deal with mistakes in the daily job of veterinarians.

courses.title: The Changing Landscape of Veterinary Osteoarthritis: Navigating Established & New Therapies
courses.description: This session will explore the importance of osteoarthritis (OA) management and the role of established and new therapies in companion animals from a practicing clinician's point of view. Dr. Bryan Torres will offer a comprehensive overview of OA management in companion animals and review the current research and evidence for OA therapies, as well as the role of those therapies in current treatment protocols. Dr. Torres will also provide tips on how to translate scientific developments into clinical practice and provide practical insights to improve patient outcomes and inform future care strategies.

courses.title: Zoonotic Disease Prevention, Emergency Care, and Overpopulation Control in a Resource-Limited Environment
courses.description: This course will provide veterinarians and veterinary technicians with a comprehensive understanding of zoonotic diseases and problems stemming from overpopulation in low-resource areas. It will focus on practical strategies for prevention, control and communication/education within local communities. It will, additionally, provide practice and new methods with which to facilitate emergency veterinary care. It will utilize case studies to illustrate the application of these principles. Learning objectives: Understand global/local distribution and importance of zoonotic diseases in low-resource settings. Identify key risk factors for zoonotic disease transmission and appropriate control measures. Learn about parasite prevention and control strategies for common animal diseases. Develop communication skills for effectively conveying health messages and importance of spaying/neutering to non-veterinary, and sometimes non-educated, audiences. Understand how to adapt healthcare approach to culturally diverse/low-resource population. Practice new and existing approaches to providing prompt and successful emergency veterinary care.

courses.title: Small Breeds Total Hip Replacement
courses.description: Now featuring both BFX (biologic-fixation) press-fit acetabular stems and cups, in addition to CFX stems and cups, this full-day course combines online learning with in-depth classroom instruction and extensive hands-on laboratory experience. Our multi-faceted educational approach equips participants with the knowledge and skills needed to confidently perform the procedure and offer advanced orthopedic services to their clients. The course covers proper use of the Small Breeds System, with a focus on preoperative planning, surgical technique, and clinical follow-up. Participants will have the opportunity to work directly with the instruments to gain a practical understanding of the surgical objectives.

courses.title: Here Comes the Sun: Fat-Soluble Vitamin Toxicoses (NUTR122)
courses.description: Fat-soluble vitamin toxicoses are uncommon in a clinical setting. However, these vitamins should always remain on the differential list dependent on patient history or presentation due to their metabolic functionality and possible extremely severe or even deadly consequences if consumed in toxic concentrations. Vitamin A and Vitamin D in particular pose more health risks than other vitamins. These two vitamins will be discussed in depth, reviewing their metabolism, concerns associated with acute or chronic toxic concentration risks, and nutritional interventions. Over-the-counter supplements intended for humans and/or animals will be covered in detail due to these products being a source of possible exposure to these nutrients.

courses.provider: THE VETERINARY SPECIALTY HOSPITAL OF PALM BEACH GARDENS
courses.title: Crisis to Calm: Stabilizing the Airway Patient
courses.description: When seconds matter, confidence and clarity are everything. This lecture takes you step-by-step through the critical process of stabilizing the airway patient, from the moment they arrive in crisis to achieving a controlled and secure airway. We'll begin with a concise review of airway anatomy and key definitions before moving into practical triage strategies and recognition of common causes and mimics. Attendees will learn to identify characteristic patterns, interpret diagnostic findings, and implement effective initial treatments and management plans. The session will also cover essential procedures and techniques for airway stabilization, with real-world case examples discussed as time allows. Perfect for both general practitioners and emergency clinicians, this talk blends physiology, diagnostics, and hands-on application to help you move confidently from crisis to calm in even the most challenging airway cases.

courses.title: Decoding Compliance: What You Need to Know about Controlled Drugs and Premises Permits
courses.description: The goal of this online, self-paced course is to simplify, distill, and deliver the essential knowledge you need to address challenges and navigate the intricate landscape of drug and premises permit regulations. This course was adapted from a webinar by Bruce Wagman, Lead Counsel for the San Francisco SPCA's Shelter Policy and Legal Services program and Cindi Delany, DVM, Director of Online Learning for Maddie's Million Pet Challenge at the UC Davis Koret Shelter Medicine Program hosted by the California Animal Welfare Association.

courses.title: Immune Mediated Hemolytic Anemia (DRIP119)
courses.description: This course will take you through the fundamentals of IMHA patients. The physiological process of IMHA will be discussed along with the diagnostic approach and treatment of the acute abdomen patient.

courses.title: Cushing's: Communication and Compliance
courses.description: Cushing's syndrome can be an expensive and challenging disease to treat, but treatment is important for optimum patient outcome. Dr. Cook discusses important communication points to share with clients, including when to consider Cushing's disease, how to discuss the diagnosis, and how to engage and support clients through treatment and monitoring. Clinically relevant updates about clinical signs, diagnosis, and treatment are included throughout the presentation.

courses.title: How to Make a Difference Without Being the Boss
courses.description: Regardless of your job title, you have the power to make real change in your practice. Even small actions can have a big impact.

courses.title: Myofascial Pain: Mechanism to Management
courses.description: This course will provide attendees with: 1) A better understanding of myofascial trigger points. Their origins, physiological characteristics and role in producing pain 2) A review of the various approaches for diagnosis and treatment of Myofascial Trigger Points 3) A review of the available manual treatment techniques and modalities proven to be effective in treating trigger points Link to course on YouTube https://youtu.be/CYiyoSg5hY4

courses.title: In the Know About Noses: Health Trends in Brachycephalic Breeds
courses.description: With brachycephalic breeds like French Bulldogs, Boxers, and English Bulldogs routinely included in most popular breed lists in the U.S., the only thing more common than treating them in your practice may be strong feelings about their health. But how many of the things we know about brachycephalic breeds are supported by millions of years of pet health data? In 2022, Nationwide started publishing novel evidence-based pet health studies about cancer and diseases of aging pets, leveraging their 40 years of pet health experience and data to provide pet families and veterinary healthcare teams with tangible analysis and insights. This session will provide newly published insights into diseases of brachycephalic dogs, offering a data-informed approach to brachycephalic disease awareness, education, and management.

courses.title: There's Nothing Cute About Acute Pancreatitis in Dogs
courses.description: Acute pancreatitis in dogs is a complex medical condition that can be equally complex to diagnose and treat. In this webinar, Dr. David Twedt will cover the latest information on the diagnosis and management of acute pancreatitis in dogs. A clinical case will be used to review the clinical presentation, risk factors, and pathophysiology of pancreatitis. The diagnostic approach and disease management will be covered in detail, highlighting the diagnostic value of available testing options and the new therapeutic options for disease monitoring.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Pediatric and Geriatric Toxicology: Age Matters in Poison Response
courses.description: This 1-hour continuing education course explores the unique toxicological risks facing pediatric and geriatric small animal patients. Participants will examine how age-related physiological differences alter susceptibility to toxin exposure, clinical presentation, and treatment response. The course is designed for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and students seeking to strengthen their approach to toxicology cases in age-specific canine and feline patients. Topics include developmental stage and aging impact clinical signs, diagnostic interpretation, treatment selection, and prognosis in toxicology cases. Practical case-based examples will highlight adjustments in diagnostic evaluation, medication use, fluid therapy, and supportive care for young and elderly patients.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: Tumor Microenvironment
courses.description: SCIENCE OF ONCOLOGY - ONLINE VIDEO SERIES: This lecture will describe the tumor microenvironment, beginning with the mechanisms that lead to the creation of a tumor niche and continuing through the steps that allow it to evolve to favor tumor growth and dissemination. The tumor microenvironment refers to the complex ecosystem in which tumor cells reside and interact.

courses.title: Animal Echo Collection: Comparative CHD Assessment: Biped vs. Quadruped RVOT Obstructions
courses.description: Many of the same congenital cardiovascular malformations occur in animals and humans.
