In this case-based OnDemand webinar, experts will review specific congenital malformations with an emphasis on their methods of imaging and their clinical decision-making process. Understanding how veterinarians, physicians, and sonographers approach these can provide new information and an additional perspective for attendees of this webinar, regardless of their scope of practice.

courses.title: Companion Livestock and Equine Euthanasia
courses.description: Those of us working with smaller companion animals are sometimes asked to help companion livestock and horses. This module seeks to address the similarities and differences. It's designed for small animal veterinary teams who wish to better understand how to euthanize companion livestock and horses. For those wishing to learn about traditional livestock euthanasia and more information on equine euthanasia, we encourage you to watch those modules to supplement this one. The book Veterinary Euthanasia Techniques; A practical guide pairs well with this material.

courses.title: Logical Problem Solving (VCAS103)
courses.description: This session will help you to become aware of different ways of approaching a medical problem. We will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of 3 commonly used methods: pattern recognition, fishing trip and logical clinical problem solving. The importance of defining medical problems in patients using a carefully taken clinical history and physical examination, then constructing a problem list and order according to the specific nature of the problems and relevance will be covered. Learn to refine a problem list on the basis of newly acquired information and localize the most specific problems of the patient to a body system and define the lesion in the body system.

courses.title: END OF LIFE CARE, QUALITY OF LIFE ASSESSMENT AND HOSPICE (Anytime)
courses.description: Participants will review the human animal bond, as well as human and veterinary end of life care practices, revolving around the core principles of palliative care and goal-centered care at end of life. Participants will receive basic information regarding current veterinary euthanasia guidelines and practices. Participants will be challenged to review human quality of life assessment practices, and how this may cross over into the realm of animal care when euthanasia is an option. Participants will be given information to find quality of life scoring applications for use in their practices. Participants will learn what animal hospice entails, and intricate decision-making regarding this end of life care service. Case examples will be discussed throughout.

courses.title: Assessment and management of the top five health conditions in senior dogs: The 'Cliff Notes' version
courses.description: This course will provide a rapid review of the top five conditions associated with declining quality of life and mortality in senior dogs: neoplasia, musculoskeletal disease, cardiac disease, chronic kidney disease, and cognitive dysfunction. We will cover the most common manifestations of each category and how to identify, assess, and manage them according to the latest expert guidelines. This survey should provide you with the tools and resources you need to approach diagnosing and managing these important health problems in your patients.

courses.title: General Soft Tissue Surgery
courses.description: Detailed videos and descriptions of procedures for the veterinarian in general veterinary practice. Eliminate indecision with Dr. Berg's advice designed to help you confidently conquer these procedures. Organized for Quick Review Prior to Any Procedure

courses.title: Laws and Rules Governing the Practice of Veterinary Medicine in Florida (PHAR109)
courses.description: This course explores the laws and rules governing the practice of veterinary medicine in Florida and gives a basic overview in a modular format. The course begins with licensing, educational requirements, and scope of practice. The veterinarian-client-patient relationship as well as requirements related to medical records will be discussed. Permits, inspections and minimum standards of practice will follow. A brief overview covering advertising applications will be determined. Wellness and impairment of veterinarians will be discussed as well as the opioid crisis. The course ends with an overview of associated violations and penalties. This course focuses heavily on F.S. 455, F.S. 474 and Chapter 61G18.

courses.title: Let's Talk Nutrition: Communicating with Clients About Nutrition Trends (Anytime)
courses.description: Clients have so many questions about pet foods and feeding philosophies for the veterinary healthcare team. Pet owners crave information about what's best to feed their pets. They bring in myths and misconceptions, information from their favorite website or magazine filled with rating systems praising pet food products and trashing others. This webinar will offer nutrition updates, resources and tips for talking with clients about current food trends and FDA investigations.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Respiratory Distress in Acute Care - A Diagnostic & Therapeutic Challenge
courses.description:
Dealing with Obvious Respiratory distress is very uncomfortable and potentially life-threatening. Prompt recognition and targeted therapy are key to a successful outcome. While it's obvious that patients are compromised, identifying and treating the exact cause(s) can make the difference between life and death. This session will cover clinically relevant aspects of pulmonary physiology, respiratory distress recognition/triage, and blood gas analysis.
Treatment of Respiratory Distress - From the Essentials to the Advanced In this session we will discuss the practical management of patients with respiratory distress. We will review essential, potentially lifesaving techniques such as oxygen therapy, thoracocenteses and dive into mechanical ventilation, an advanced but underused salvage procedure.

courses.title: Making the Most of Working in a Team (VCAS111)
courses.description: Other colleagues play an important role in the smooth running of a veterinary practice. We will discuss awareness of different types of personalities and preferences in ways of working and in communicating. Being aware of our own personal preferences and how to work in harmony with different preferences will also be covered. We will also focus on applying self knowledge in choosing the best practice, how to identify if there is a mismatch of needs and preferences between you and your team, and strategies to apply when this occurs.

courses.provider: THE AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF FISH VETERINARIANS
courses.title: 2024 American Association of Fish Veterinarian Conference - Virtual
courses.description: Virtual recording of 2 days of 2024 American Association of Fish Veterinarian Conference in Seattle, Washington. The 2024 American Association of Fish Veterinarians (AAFV) Conference will be held in Seattle, WA October 17-21, 2024. It will provide Veterinarians and Veterinary Technicians with recent concepts, methods and cases for the diagnosis, treatment and practice of fish medicine. We will offer wet labs, presentations focusing on the areas of Fish Board Certification, fish diagnostics, wild fish health, public aquaria, aquaculture and pet fish private practice.

courses.title: New Grad Symposium 2025 (On Demand)
courses.description: Lecture 1: The Emergency Cat - 10 Things You Need To Know Speaker: Dr Philip Judge Lecture abstract: You've been told that cats are not small dogs - but just how different are they? Well, in just about everything, they are significantly different from their canine counterparts! From clinical signs, to physiology and metabolism, we need to consider cats in a very special way, in order to help us diagnose what's wrong in the emergency setting, to administering treatments in a manner that will optimise outcome! Join renowned emergency clinician, Dr. Philip Judge, as he explores 10 things you need to know about cats in an emergency! LECTURE 2: Confidence Unlocked: Embrace Your Potential & Defeat the Impostor Speaker: Olivia Oginska DVM, MRCVS, PGCert SAS, MSc Lecture Abstract: Being a fantastic clinician involves vast amounts of stress, difficult decisions, and, on occasion, self-doubt. In this session, delegates will learn about the power of self-awareness in defeating the impostor feelings and becoming a confident veterinarian and team player. The science of emotional intelligence offers practical advice on managing our thoughts and actions so that we can provide the best patient care while protecting our mental wellbeing. Lecture 3: Safeguarding Your Veterinary Career: Managing Client Complaints and Mental Health Speakers: Cat Walker AMDRAS, RVN, Cert IV VN, BA(Hons)(International Studies), LLB, Grad Dip (Legal Practice) / Lachlan Campbell BVSc(hons) BScApp(hons) BSc Dip.Mgt MANZCVS(Surgery) MICDA Lecture abstract: In the veterinary profession, client complaints are an inherent challenge that can significantly impact mental health and career satisfaction. This presentation explores the intricacies of preventing and coping with such complaints, emphasizing their potential impact on practitioner well-being and workforce sustainability, along with the broader implications for patient safety. Lecture 4: Is that a Foreign Body? A Systematic Approach to Animal Radiographs

courses.title: It's Not Just a Phase Mom: The 4 Phases of Anesthesia Lecture Series
courses.description: This presentation will go over the 4 phases of anesthesia: premedication, induction, maintenance, & recovery. It will go over different patient considerations, pharmacology & drugs used, patient monitoring & analgesia considerations for each phase of anesthesia. We will also go over contraindications for specific anesthesia related situations and anesthesia/analgesia medications. This course will be a series given over 4 weeks in separate sessions. The first three being 1 hour and the final session being 1.5 hrs

courses.title: Vetster Master Class Level 1
courses.description: This course is designed to equip veterinarians with the essential skills needed to excel in virtual care, including telehealth, telemedicine, general advice, and teletriage. It is broken down into six video modules, each with an associated PDF and short quiz. The titles are: What is virtual care and why is it important? What are the benefits of providing virtual care? The role of the VCPR. Getting started. Virtual care excellence. Deep dive on general advice. The goal is to set veterinarians up for success in providing telehealth services via any medium while also showing how to optimize use of the Vetster marketplace.

courses.title: The role of shockwave with Physical Rehabilitation and Surgery
courses.description: This course will provide attendees with; 1) An overview of stifle structure and injury. What does the cruciate do and what happens when injury occurs. 2) A review of surgical and non-surgical approaches to cruciate injury. 3) The role of shockwave therapy in the treatment of the stifle. 4) Review a multimodal approach to treatment approaches and suggested rehabilitation strategies.

courses.title: Feline Heartworm Disease (TECH309)
courses.description: Reports of feline heartworm disease (FHWD) have been published for over 80 years, yet we still do not spend enough time talking to our clients about prevention. For cats prevention is the key, as there is no effective, safe treatment. Learn how cats are different, and how heartworm behaves when infecting cats.

courses.title: Urine Trouble 2.0: Behavioral and Environmental Treatments for House Soiling Cats
courses.description:
In this video course, Veterinary Behaviorist, Dr. Amy Pike, will help us understand the cues our patients are giving us through their body language and behavior. Through videos and discussion, we'll learn how addressing stress and suboptimal living environments can resolve inappropriate eliminations and reduce occurrence of FLUTD symptoms in cats.
We'll discuss standards for history-taking, methods for determining a cat's preferred litter and litter box, ways to reduce inter-cat aggression, and methods for providing enrichment and safe spaces to reduce anxiety and stress.

courses.title: Rabbits, the New Cat? Embrace Treating Rabbits with Confidence
courses.description: Domestic rabbits are the third most popular pet in the United States, and not surprisingly, the third most common pet found in animal shelters. Many general practitioners are not comfortable with rabbit medicine and surgery, however there is a need for expanding these services. This presentation will go over basic rabbit husbandry, some of the more common rabbit diseases, as well as touch on the importance of and techniques for rabbit spay and neuter.

courses.provider: DR. JUDY MORGAN'S NATURALLY HEALTHY PETS
courses.title: The Naturally Healthy Pets Reunion Experience
courses.description:
How can we top the epic International NHP Experience that we held in May, 2025 in Orlando, FL??? We need to go to Texas to have an even BIGGER and BETTER Experience! Take part in the Natural Pet Care event that everyone is talking about! Check out the incredible speaker lineup, that includes Dr. Judy Morgan herself and learn from all of our top experts in the holistic pet care industry.
The demographic will largely be dedicated pet parents, pet professionals, veterinary professionals and students and we will have both human and pet focused brands joining us. We are expecting up to 500 in-person attendees and approx 100 vendors.
With this incredible speaker lineup, the NHP Reunion Experience promises to SELL OUT! So, don't wait to register and secure your spot today.
Be one of the 500 fortunate pet parents and natural pet care professionals to experience these expert speakers plus the 100 or so hand-picked exhibitors with high quality products for the best in holistic pet care. Don't miss out on this paws-itively amazing event!

courses.title: Creating a Pet-Friendly Hospital, Animal Shelter, or Petcare Business (CDPS112)
courses.description: Creating a "pet-friendly" hospital, shelter, or Petcare business is a simple, inexpensive path to improved efficiency, increased staff safety, happy pets, and clients who feel a bond with your business. Learn how in this fun and fascinating series of lectures taken from a half-day seminar given by veterinarian, animal behaviorist, and author, Dr. Sophia Yin.

courses.title: Attacking Periodontal Disease: A Case-Based Approach to Veterinary Dentistry & Oral Surgery
courses.description:
Attacking Periodontal Disease: A Case-Based Approach to Veterinary Dentistry & Oral Surgery is a comprehensive 4-hour continuing education course designed to move beyond traditional periodontal disease lectures and focus on practical, real-world clinical application. This course will succinctly review the foundations of canine and feline periodontal disease while emphasizing clinical reasoning, case-based decision making, and treatment planning in everyday veterinary practice.
Through a series of authentic clinical cases, attendees will learn how to approach varying stages of dental disease, develop practical extraction strategies, perform regional nerve blocks, and apply efficient oral surgery techniques with confidence. The course will also highlight the importance of client communication, managing expectations, balancing ideal versus realistic treatment options, and creating achievable outcomes tailored to each patient and family.
Designed for veterinary professionals seeking a more interactive and applicable approach to dentistry, this course integrates procedural technique, extraction mechanics, periodontal therapy, and oral surgery principles into realistic scenarios clinicians commonly encounter in practice.

courses.title: NORA - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE DOG WITH PATENT DUCTUS ARTERIOSUS (PDA) (930-35080)
courses.description: NORA - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE DOG WITH PATENT DUCTUS ARTERIOSUS (PDA) (930-35080) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: BioMedtrix Universal Hip Small Breeds: Cementless and Cemented THR Online Course
courses.description: The BioMedtrix Universal Hip Small Breeds online course is designed to provide surgeons with an in-depth understanding of the BioMedtrix Universal Hip Small Breeds system and the surgical procedure. Upon completion, participants will have the prerequisite information required before attending a Universal Hip Small Breeds Hands-on Workshop.

courses.provider: THE VETERINARY SPECIALTY HOSPITAL OF PALM BEACH GARDENS
courses.title: Urinary Incontinence: Beyond Proin
courses.description:
The focus of this session will be to help expand the differentials list and in-house
treament options for urinary incontinence while placing a strong focus on formulating
a presumptive diagnosis and highlighting treatment options available at referral
institutions.

courses.title: AAAP 2025 Annual Meeting - Online
courses.description:
The American Association of Avian Pathologists (AAAP) Annual Meeting is the premier U.S. scientific meeting focused on poultry health, welfare and food safety for poultry veterinarians and scientists. The meeting facilitates member collaboration to advance science-based knowledge, expertise, and education, and is attended by poultry veterinarians and scientists from the United States and internationally. The 2025 AAAP scientific online program incorporates 44, 15-minute recorded sessions presentations in the following 18 topics: Antimicrobial/Antibiotic Resistance, Avian Influenza, Bacteriology, Case Report, Coccidiosis, Diagnostics, Epidemiology, Infectious Bronchitis Virus, Infectious Bursal Disease, Marek's Disease, Mycoplasma, Newcastle Disease Virus, Other, Parasitology, Vaccinology, Virology, Wealth of Knowledge, and Welfare.
The recorded sessions will be grouped into 11 segments. Each segment will have 4, 15-minute recorded sessions in each. Course participants can choose to take a minimum 1 or maximum 11 segments during this session. Meaning they could earn a minimum of 1 CE or a maximum of 11 CE depending on how many segments in the course each person choses to engage with. Meeting attendees will engage with these recorded sessions anytime between July 14th - August 14th, 2025. Searchable keywords: AAAP, poultry, veterinarians, scientists, poultry health, poultry welfare, food safety

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2023 Complicated Gastroenterology Cases: Medical and Nutritional Integration On Demand
courses.description: In this on-demand course, we will provide an update on the medical and nutritional approaches to complicated gastrointestinal diseases in the dog and cat. Discussions focused around esophageal, gastrointestinal, and pancreatic diseases will be led by experts in the field of anatomic pathology, gastroenterology, and nutrition. Included in the course is a clinically impactful summary of up-to-date research breakthroughs. The integration of nutrition throughout this course will provide a comprehensive experience for the attendee.

courses.title: The Wonderful World of Hemp Cannabinoids in Small Animal Practice
courses.description: This session will discuss factors for veterinarians to consider when recommending CBD-rich hemp based products. The focus will be on information to look for on a certificate of analysis (COA) of marketed products. Discussion will address the cannabinoid analysis from manufacturer's third party testing, as well as analyses for microbiologics, mycotoxins, solvent residues, heavy metals, pesticides and terpenes. More importantly, an understanding of whether companies have validated utility of the product through pharmacokinetic testing in the species intended will be covered. Safety considerations, with a deeper examination of current safety data around long term supplementation will also be addressed. As there is increasing evidence of efficacy of CBD rich hemp products for a variety of conditions, these studies will be examined with a focus on the growing evidence for chronic osteoarthritis pain, with further foray into acute surgical pain studies. Further evidence-based medicine will be examined around the growing number of trials addressing seizure disorders, with a focus not only on efficacy, but also on potential drug interactions. Lastly, evidence around pruritic diseases and the immune system will be examined, particularly as it pertains to atopic dermititis and cannabinoids as potential immune system regulators.

courses.title: CRANIAL CRUCIATE LIGAMENT DISEASE PART 2: EDUCATING THE PET OWNER AND CASE SELECTION (195-41357)
courses.description: This lecture focuses on educating the pet owner about CrCLD treatment options and their anticipated outcomes and possible complications. Attendees will learn how to select patients who will likely benefit from ExCap Suture stabilization as well as detect those who are at risk of treatment failure. After attending this lecture, attendees will be better able to discuss with the pet owner the cause of CrCLD, surgical and non-surgical treatment options, and risk of complications. Attendees will also be able to judiciously select surgical cases based on breed, tibial plateau angle, patient demeanor, and client/patient compliance.

courses.provider: NORTH CAROLINA STATE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: NC Veterinary Pain Short Course
courses.description: NC State College of Veterinary Medicine is proud to host the sixth international Veterinary Pain Short Course on pain, pain mechanisms and novel therapies in veterinary medicine, June 4 through 6, 2026 NC State College of Veterinary Medicine, Raleigh NC. This meeting is unique in veterinary medicine for its emphasis upon fundamental principles and mechanisms of pain as they pertain to the veterinary patient.

courses.title: Before the Rehabilitator Arrives: How to stabilize emergency wildlife patients (Anytime)
courses.description: Management of wildlife cases is left to licensed rehabilitators in this country. However, Veterinarians and their staff, can and should be trained to stabilize wildlife before the patient can be transferred to the appropriate facility. The presentation will allow practitioners of all kinds to do the following: a. Basic safe animal handling of wildlife. b. Recognize what cases should be treated temporarily and how to do it. c. Recognize when an animal should be given the gift of euthanasia so that the patient does not have to wait unnecessarily for the rehabilitator. d. Understand zoonotic risks and how to stay safe. e. Basic overview of the most common medical interventions required to stabilize wildlife.

courses.title: Introduction to Veterinary Dentistry Online
courses.description: This is an introductory course on veterinary dentistry that covers oral anatomy, instrumentation & equipment, the dental procedure and radiography.

courses.title: Veterinary Forensics (MULT220)
courses.description: More and more, our society is mindful of the connection between people and animals including the connection between animal abuse and interpersonal violence. Because of this, it is imperative that all veterinarians and support staff be able to identify potential animal abuse and know the laws related to their roles in reporting animal abuse. But to report abuse, one must first be able to identify it and document it correctly. Additionally, it may be necessary to collect evidence in a manner that does not compromise the case. This course strives to teach each participant what the Link is, what laws may pertain to animal abuse, how to identify signs consistent with animal abuse, and how to document those signs including writing a report. The focus will be on individual small animals but will also include large-scale cases and briefly touch on large animals and exotics. Finally, there will be a brief discussion of the SARS-CoV2 pandemic and its relation to animal abuse.

courses.title: Raw Food: A Research Review
courses.description: For decades now, we have been advising pet owners and veterinarians that the supposed benefits of feeding raw are not supported by studies. Times are changing and we are seeing increasing interest in the exploration of benefits from feeding minimally processed diets. This talk will cover a range of studies on the possible benefits of raw food diets and explore potential explanations for the differences seen.

courses.title: Ophthalmic Emergencies
courses.description: Emily Conway, BVMS, MS, MRCVS, ACVO will discuss how to diagnosis and treat the following common Ophthalmic Emergencies. Including what recommend equipment, skills, and medications are recommended.

courses.title: Cognitively Inclined: Supporting the Aging Canine Brain
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Nancy Loes will review the rationale for incorporating nutritional and herbal compounds into an overall veterinary healthcare management plan for aging dogs. She will elaborate on how these compounds have been shown to beneficially modulate behavioral disturbances, memory loss, and learning disabilities that can develop over time in aging patients. Attendees will leave with an understanding of how targeted nutritional strategies can support the aging brain and help maintain healthy cognitive function.

courses.title: Approach to the Down Dog (DRIP132)
courses.description:
The lecture focuses on the typical presentation, differential diagnosis, treatments, and prognosis of the acutely down dog, including disease which may mimic IVDD. A small portion of the lecture series will expose the clinician to atypical presentations of common myelopathies.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 58 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Is in-house PCR testing right for my practice? Investing in equine hospital biosecurity
courses.description: Implementing new technologies to your practice can seem daunting. In this webinar, Dr. Jillian Minuto (DVM, DACVIM) of Chaparral Veterinary Medical Center and Eric Mendonsa (Fluxergy) discuss how Chaparral brought rapid PCR to their practice to bolster biosecurity practices. Dr. Minuto shares her experience using the Fluxergy platform and her best protocols for screening patients for infectious disease.

courses.title: New Technologies in Laboratory Testing
courses.description: Holograms, artificial intelligence, and functionalized radio filters, oh my! Diagnostic laboratory technologies are rapidly evolving to improve patient care and clinic operations. Novel biomarkers, expanded test menus, and improved accuracy will be increasingly available at the point of care. This lecture will cover several new technologies coming soon to clinical practice, including holographic cell reconstruction, and surface acoustic wave biosensors, as well as several technologies currently available but not widely used. Learn about the lab of tomorrow today!

courses.title: General Practitioner Certificate in Computed Tomography
courses.description: General Practitioner Certificate in Computed Tomography is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.provider: DBA VETERINARY DENTISTRY EDUCATION AND CONSULTING SERVICES
courses.title: Advanced Dental and Maxillofacial Imaging (Cone Beam Computed Tomography, Conventional Computed Tomography, Magnetic Resonanc
courses.description: Advanced Dental and Maxillofacial Imaging (Cone Beam Computed Tomography, Conventional Computed Tomography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging, Tomosynthesis) in the Dog Cat: The 13 CE hour course is designed for AVDC residents, AVDC Diplomates, and general practitioners, to understand various imaging modalities pertaining to practice of veterinary dentistry and oral surgery. It combines the experience of 2 board-certified radiologists and is supported by a Board-Certified Veterinary Dentist. A brief discussion of the physics of conventional computed tomography (CT), cone beam computed tomography (CBCT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) will be presented. Clinical anatomy and pathology will be presented with the various imaging modalities to understand interpretation of dental, oral, and maxillofacial pathology. The 4-hour CBCT section will include clinical cases (canine and feline tooth resorption, periodontal disease, endodontic disease, trauma, temporomandibular pathology, odontogenic cysts, and oral cancer comparison and corresponding digital intraoral radiographs and clinical photographs to enhance learning between what is visualized with CBCT compared to digital intraoral radiology. Introduction of an emerging technology, tomosynthesis, will be presented as another imaging modality for dental and maxillofacial pathology. An interactive thoracic radiology section is presented for learning assessment of the thoracic cavity as part of patient anesthetic preparation and challenges. The course will enhance dental and maxillofacial pathology for AVDC residents and diplomates as well as the general practitioner adding advanced imaging modalities to their practices. This 13 CE Hour RACE approved course will be submitted for RACE approval and is submitted for AVDC pre-approval to satisfy 12 hours for AVDC residents for specialist in training hours in Radiology/Imaging including 8 hours of dental/oral/maxillo-facial imaging techniques.

courses.title: Immune System: Function and its Impact on Vaccines
courses.description: This program will take a look at an overview of the immune system and how different vaccines work to achieve immunity. This topic provides levels of knowledge that would suit new graduates (learning about different types of vaccines), through to those studying for their VTS (breaking down the different parts of the immune system and what they do).

courses.provider: THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS MEDICAL BRANCH
courses.title: Achieving Data Quality & Integrity in Maximum Containment Laboratories Nonclinical 2026
courses.description: The Achieving Data Quality and Integrity in Maximum Containment Laboratories 2026 course is a four and one half day hybrid training program offered annually utilizing expert faculty from the Food and Drug Administration, government, academia, and business and industry. This is a free, hybrid, virtual and in-person, public educational outreach course hosted annually that teaches veterinarians and other participants how to achieve data quality with high-consequence pathogens, e.g., biosafety levels 3 and 4, according to FDAs Good Laboratory Practice regulations. The course includes laboratory activities conducted in virtual mock Biosafety Level, BSL2 and BSL4 training laboratories to emphasize the differences between biosafety levels and the complexity of conducting laboratory activities in a BSL4 laboratory environment. An online training module on the Good Laboratory Practice, GLP, regulations, 21 CFR Part 58, is included as a course prerequisite. For additional background information, visit official the Course Website in the description page.

courses.title: Canine Heart Disease Stages and the Role of Radiographs in Long-Term Management
courses.description:
Canine heart disease often progresses over months to years, moving from congenital structural malformations and risk status, to asymptomatic structural disease, to congestive heart failure, and, in some patients, refractory disease. This webinar provides a practical framework for using ACVIM canine heart disease stages and thoracic radiographs to support long-term management in small animal practice.
Participants will review Stage A, Stage B1, Stage B2, Stage C, and Stage D myxomatous mitral valve disease , with emphasis on how thoracic radiographs help assess cardiac size, left atrial enlargement, pulmonary vessels, pulmonary edema, and concurrent respiratory disease. The session will also cover the clinical value of vertebral heart score (VHS), vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), serial radiographic comparison, and stage-based monitoring workflows. The program is designed to help veterinary teams improve confidence, consistency, and clinical decision-making when managing dogs with suspected or confirmed heart disease.

courses.title: CANIS Conference
courses.description: Brought to you by Aggressive Dog and APDT International, the CANIS Conference (Canine Advocacy, Networking, Innovation, and Science) is not your average industry event. It is a celebration of all things dog. Over four energizing days, trainers, behavior consultants, veterinarians, shelter and rescue workers, sport dog handlers, and pet care professionals come together to learn, connect, and spark new ideas. With five engaging educational tracks, live demonstrations, and extensive networking opportunities, CANIS is where science meets passion, innovation sparks ideas, and the future of dog welfare takes center stage.

courses.title: Animal Wellness Academy (1516-44156)
courses.description: Through the Animal Wellness Academy, veterinarians, veterinary technicians and veterinary students can access the latest veterinary trends, technologies and treatments. There are a total of 48 hours of CE offered through five tracks: Nutrition & Supplements, Diagnostics & Advancements, Innovative Techniques, Integrative Solutions, and Wellness for You and Your Practice. These tracks have been designed to support and enrich veterinary learning, with the goal of giving general practitioners additional knowledge, options and solutions for optimal healing and wellbeing so they can provide the best possible care for each individual animal. Animal Wellness Academy was created by the publishers of Innovative Veterinary Care Journal, which, since 2010, has presented scientific and evidence-based studies, and helped to bridge the gap between allopathic and integrative healing.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Spectrum of Care: Appropriate management of Toxicology Cases on a Budget
courses.description: The spectrum of care in the management of toxicities refers to the range of strategies used to recognize, assess, prevent, and treat adverse effects of toxicities. The primary goal is to ensure patient safety while maintaining treatment efficacy. It is important to establish key goals for veterinary care, emphasizing the importance of communication, evidence-based medicine, and client-centered decision-making in the treatment of toxicities.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: DNA Deep Dive: Incorporating Genetics into Veterinary Cardiology to Enhance Diagnosis, Prognosis, and Treatment On Demand
courses.description: Through lectures and panel discussions, this course will provide an in depth look at the most common inherited heart diseases and how our patient genetic architecture impacts their response to medical therapies. As our knowledge of veterinary genetics continues to expand, understanding how to incorporate genetic testing and counseling into veterinary cardiology case evaluations and therapeutic management grows more important. Our speakers will address mitral valve degeneration, arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, drug resistance, and the interface between each of these topics and canine and feline genetics. The content will focus on a current understanding of genetic etiology of disease and the practical application of this knowledge in the clinic. Veterinary genetics is a fast moving field and course participants will leave with the most current knowledge and the ability to critically evaluate future discoveries.

courses.title: Navigating Raw Nutrition Conversations
courses.description: Nutrition has become the fifth vital assessment; therefore, confident communication about nutrition and alternative diets has become essential in the clinic. But how do you start a nutrition dialogue in the exam room and how do you navigate conversations with savvy nutrition clients? This talk will improve the practical application of nutrition knowledge about alternative feeding and raw pet foods.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2025 Advanced Endocrinology On Demand
courses.description: 2025 Advanced Endocrinology On Demand is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Rat Basics (EXOT015)
courses.description: This course will cover the basics of rat ownership and husbandry, as well as an overview of a general clinical approach to the species, discussing common diseases and their treatments.

courses.title: Small Animal Programme 2025 part 1
courses.description: This programme includes 23 hours of world-class CPD, delivered by experts in the field. The main objective is to keep veterinarians up to date with the latest insights into small animals. The Programme will outline the typical approach to investigating and managing cases in order to optimise the outcome. Topics covered range from orthopaedics, endocrinology, behaviour, neurology, among others.

courses.title: Introduction to Radiology (DIAG415)
courses.description:
This course will cover the discovery and history of the first radiographs, basic radiology concepts, radiology safety and physics as well as evaluation of different x-ray systems used in veterinary medicine.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 157 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Bridging the Gap: What Oncologists Wish GPs Knew About Veterinary Oncology
courses.description: Ever wonder what the specialists want before referral? This lecture is designed to facilitate a comprehensive understanding of the key aspects of veterinary oncology, focusing on the approach to masses, diagnostic testing, staging, and treatment options, with the aim of improving collaboration between oncologists and general practitioners.

courses.title: Recognizing Brewing Fear and Aggression in Dogs and Cats (BHVR100)
courses.description: Dog and cat bites are among the most common injuries in veterinary hospitals and pet care settings. Failing to recognize subtle signs of fear and anxiety, combined with improper handling, can have lasting behavioral consequences, leaving animals physically better but behaviorally worse. Learning how a more skilled approach to handling these patients keeps them feeling safe while helping you avoid dangerous and stressful situations.

courses.title: Vestibular Disease (DRIP157)
courses.description: The lecture series focuses on the typical presentation, differential diagnosis, treatments, and prognosis of common veterinary neurologic diseases. A small portion of the lecture series will expose the clinician to atypical presentations of common neurologic diseases.

courses.title: Understanding and Implementing Advances in Neonatal Kitten Care - OnDemand
courses.description:
Neonatal kitten care has seen significant advancements over the last decade. At the same time social media had created thousands of influencers sharing information on the best ways to save these little ones. This information is often conflicting. In 2023, several major shelter medicine programs and animal advocacy groups updated their guidelines for caring for neonatal kittens which added even more confusion and debate about the best ways to care underage kittens.
Our goal is to review these changes with industry leaders and answer questions to those caregivers confused by the updated guidelines.

courses.provider: DR. JUDY MORGAN'S NATURALLY HEALTHY PETS
courses.title: The Naturally Healthy Pets Reunion Experience
courses.description:
How can we top the epic International NHP Experience that we held in May, 2025 in Orlando, FL??? We need to go to Texas to have an even BIGGER and BETTER Experience! Take part in the Natural Pet Care event that everyone is talking about! Check out the incredible speaker lineup, that includes Dr. Judy Morgan herself and learn from all of our top experts in the holistic pet care industry.
The demographic will largely be dedicated pet parents, pet professionals, veterinary professionals and students and we will have both human and pet focused brands joining us. We are expecting up to 500 in-person attendees and approx 100 vendors.
With this incredible speaker lineup, the NHP Reunion Experience promises to SELL OUT! So, don't wait to register and secure your spot today.
Be one of the 500 fortunate pet parents and natural pet care professionals to experience these expert speakers plus the 100 or so hand-picked exhibitors with high quality products for the best in holistic pet care. Don't miss out on this paws-itively amazing event!

courses.title: Practical Calicivirus: All You Need to Know from Diagnosis to Adoption (OnDemand)
courses.description: Feline calicivirus (FCV) is a contagious, often severe virus in cats that can be difficult, time-consuming, and expensive to treat. However, standardized protocols help treat these cats efficiently, reduce transmission within the shelter, and get cats moving toward live outcomes. This webcast will cover diagnosing calicivirus without the use of expensive testing; treating the virus and caring for sick cats in the shelter; and clearing and adopting the cats after illness.

courses.title: Big Dog Master Class (On Demand, Modular)
courses.description: With shelter dog populations returning to pre pandemic levels, outcomes slowing, transport destinations drying up, and historic levels of staffing turnover, shelters are struggling with medium and large dogs. The Big Dog Master Class is now available on demand in 8 segments on Maddies University to help staff at all levels better manage big dog populations, maximize organizational efficiencies, utilize technologies, build proven programs, and implement transparent, effective policies based on five components of big dog management: public safety, intake management, live outcomes, humane care, and cost efficiency. We brought the nations top experts together. Among them are veterinarians, epidemiologists, veterinary behaviorists, shelter directors, trainers, and national leaders to give you highly usable programs that do not require special skills or breaking the bank to make positive changes. This free, on demand, virtual conference opportunity is made possible by support from Maddies Fund and organized by the Maddies Million Pet Challenge and Human Animal Support Services.

courses.title: Three Behavior Lessons You'll Use Every Day
courses.description:
In this video course, Veterinary Behaviorist, Dr. Amy Pike, will help us understand the cues our patients are giving us through their body language and behavior. Through videos and discussion, we'll learn to differentiate medical, environmental, and psychological causes of unwanted behaviors.
In session one, we'll learn how to read dog and cat body language, focusing on tails, ears, eyes, facial expressions, and body positioning. In session two, through video examples and understanding of basic training principles, we'll learn how to train dogs and cats to accept medical care, including bathing, eye drops, ear medications, and oral medications. In session three, we'll study the classical signs of separation anxiety, learn how to differentiate separation anxiety from similar disorders, and how to treat.

courses.title: IVAS Certification Course in Veterinary Acupuncture
courses.description:
The Certification Course in Veterinary Acupuncture taught by the International Veterinary Acupuncture Society (IVAS) has been setting the global standard in veterinary acupuncture since 1974. The curriculum of the course integrates a background of the fundamentals and application of the scientific basis for acupuncture, as well as a background in the fundamentals and applications of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and acupuncture. The educational program provides acupuncture study and clinical applications for small animal, large animal, avian, and exotic species. The program prepares the participant for integration of acupuncture into clinical practice.
The curriculum of the course is not limited to the study of TCM theory. The curriculum incorporates current scientific acupuncture theory and biomedical science in its application and approach to patient assessment and treatment. A variety of methods of patient examination and treatment are taught and demonstrated. Students are reminded to always perform a Western medical examination first and obtain all necessary diagnostics prior to integrating acupuncture.
The IVAS certification process requires successful completion of all online content, 3 sessions of hands-on labs; attendance of the Mentored Internship; passage of the written exam and either one or two practical examinations depending on their area of focus; submission of a logbook documenting 10 cases and a peer-reviewed written case report. Graduates of the IVAS Certification Course in Veterinary Acupuncture will be certified in either Small Animal, Equine, or both.

courses.title: Endoscopy Basics (DIAG424)
courses.description: The course will provide an introduction to endoscopy including the indications for performing procedures, an outline of the required equipment for flexible and rigid endoscopy, how to care for/clean/setup the endoscopes and a review of available endoscopic accessories.

courses.title: Confidence with Small Animal Echocardiography
courses.description:
The course is designed to get Vets started with small animal Echocardiography. It walks through anatomy of the animal to help support image acquisition along with structure and function of the heart in order to help with diagnosis.
It is an online course consisting of presentations, live scanning tutorials, demo cases and quizzes to help students understand the content. As designed for beginners it starts with the basics on the different windows to obtain and demonstrations on how to obtain images from these windows with advice on probe position, but also image optimization with your ultrasound system controls. There will examples of normal cases and what to expect to see, but also common pathology to look out for. Aiding the student to be able to make visual assessment of the cardiac function, but also what measurements to use to help their diagnosis.
The focus is on the 2D ultrasound image, but the course does cover colour Doppler, pulsed wave Doppler and Continuous wave Doppler for more advanced techniques to obtain full exams for assessment. Looking at how to examine function of the heart along with any valvular pathology.
There are dedicated modules for cardiomyopathies - common pathology found in cats and dogs for vets.
Whilst a fully online course - the student has access to experts in the field for any advice or if they need more support with their studying

courses.title: Hatching Leadership: Live Better, Work Better (self-paced course)
courses.description:
Living better fuels working better, and working better enriches how you live. This course invites you to reflect on your lived experiences, beliefs and responses to challenges -- guiding you to build emotional and physical awareness. By exploring these areas, you'll uncover new clarity, motivation and purpose that can transform how you connect with others and contribute at work. Whether you're a team member or a leader, this course is designed to help you approach your role with intention and authenticity.
This course is appropriate for both seasoned leaders and those aspiring to leadership positions.

courses.title: Advanced Canine and Feline Clinical Nutrition
courses.description:
This comprehensive online course is designed for veterinarians and veterinary technicians seeking advanced, evidence-based training in canine and feline nutrition. The program offers in-depth instruction on the principles of companion animal nutrition, emphasizing species-specific nutrient requirements, nutrient metabolism, and the role of nutrition in both health and disease.
Delivered in a self-paced format, the course is structured into three modules:
1. Fundamentals of Nutrition: covering core nutrition concepts and metabolic pathways.
2. Applied Canine and Feline Nutrition: focusing on species-specific dietary needs, ingredient evaluation, and formulation principles.
3. Clinical Nutrition: exploring therapeutic nutrition and the dietary management of disease states.
The course includes approximately 60 hours of recorded lectures and is offered three times per year: January, April, and August.
Key Topics Include:
1. Nutrient metabolism and dietary requirements in dogs and cats
2. Pet food ingredients, formulation, and evaluation techniques
3. Evidence-based clinical nutrition strategies
4. Nutritional management of disease conditions
Participants will develop practical skills in formulating and assessing diets, as well as applying therapeutic nutrition in clinical practice. Disease states addressed include:
Diabetes mellitus, Urolithiasis, Dermatologic conditions, Chronic kidney disease, Cancer, Hepatic lipidosis, Gastrointestinal disorders, Cardiac disease, Skeletal disorders, and Obesity.
Throughout the course, emphasis is placed on integrating the latest scientific research with real-world clinical application, empowering participants to confidently manage nutrition-related cases in veterinary settings.

courses.title: The ABCs of Essential Fatty Acids
courses.description: This webinar will review the basics of essential omega fatty acids, including their benefits for multiple body systems and as an integrative component of optimal health. Participants will also learn about a novel omega-3 measurement kit.

courses.title: Deep Dive Into a New Era: Clinical Utility of NT-proBNP & Other Cardiac Biomarkers
courses.description: The scope of veterinary medicine and the landscape of available diagnostics have evolved over the last several decades. As diagnostic options have expanded, so has our ability to detect and manage cardiac conditions earlier and more effectively. In this webinar, Dr. Stacey Hendershott will explore the clinical utility of cardiac biomarkers, with a focus on NT-proBNP and troponin, in the small animal veterinary patient.

courses.title: Innovative Approaches in Small Animal Surgery
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. J. Brad Case and Dr. Jeffrey J. Runge will educate on innovative clinical approaches to veterinary surgical cases using case studies and clinical evidence.

courses.title: Ticks & Other Pesky Parasites: The Guests Your Dog Never Invited But You Can Kick Out!
courses.description: This comprehensive webinar will provide veterinary professionals with a deep dive into the world of canine parasitology, with a special focus on ticks and zoonotic tick-borne pathogens of veterinary and public health importance. Dr. Kathryn Reif will review common and emerging external (ie, ticks and fleas) and internal (ie, hookworms, roundworms, tapeworms, heartworms) canine parasites. Emerging and expanding tick and tick-borne pathogen threats will be highlighted, as will the timing and implications of pathogen transmission by ticks and shared public health concerns. Dr. Reif will also present the results of a recent study on tick speed of kill by isoxazolines and introduce a recently approved broad-spectrum parasite control product for dogs.

courses.title: 20205 (Online) Webinar Series - Part 1/2
courses.description: The American Association of Avian Pathologists will be presenting 2 webinars by 2 of our disease related committees. The 2025 Webinar series will be presented to both AAAP members and non-members. The first webinar will fall under the topic of emerging diseases and the second webinar will fall under the topic of respiratory diseases. Both were live webinars, now recorded, and to be posted online with questions for users to view if they were not able to attend the live sessions.

courses.title: ZORRO - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE DOG WITH MYXOMATOUS MITRAL VALVE DEGENERATION (930-35082)
courses.description: ZORRO - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE DOG WITH MYXOMATOUS MITRAL VALVE DEGENERATION (930-35082) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Status epilepticus Physiology & management strategies in dogs.
courses.description: Presented by Dr. Elizabeth Meiman, a board-certified Neurologist, this is a review of Status epilepticus: Physiology & management strategies in dogs for Veterinary professionals. This is part two of a two-part series that provides practical strategies for treating canine patients in status epilepticus.

courses.title: Tales from the Crit: Interactive Hematology Case Studies with the Laboratory Retrievers (Module 1)
courses.description: The Laboratory Retrievers - Purdue continuing education (CE) program is an online learning experience for veterinary professionals, created by the Laboratory Retrievers LLC and Purdue University College of Veterinary Medicine. These highly interactive, case-based modules help veterinarians and technicians confidently interpret CBC data, analyze cytograms and recognize key blood film cell morphology in minutes.

courses.title: Biosecurity Considerations for Zoological Operations and Wildlife Confiscations in Aquatic and Terrestrial Settings
courses.description: Infectious disease prevention and management are critical considerations in zoological facilities. Veterinary professionals at zoos and aquariums are leaders in establishing biosecurity protocols for routine zoological operations, including pre-shipment testing and quarantine procedures. Biosecurity is particularly essential in practice situations that incorporate the interface between well-established animal collections in managed care, wildlife rehabilitation, and notably, confiscations. Animals confiscated from the illegal wildlife trade present some of the highest biosecurity risks for a rescue facility. Presenting with little or no medical history, potential severe illnesses, and the possible presence of infectious, zoonotic, or foreign animal diseases, these cases require rapid assessment and strict protocols to protect both animal and human health. This lecture will discuss veterinary risk management and biosecurity practices in AZA accredited zoological institutions, focusing on the care of aquatic and terrestrial taxa, respectively. Discussion will include unique examples of risk assessment and applied biosecurity from aquatic and terrestrial species perspectives. The session will also review how to evaluate a facility's capability to manage confiscated wildlife safely, effectively, and with the highest standards of biosecurity, considering resources, staffing, species experience, veterinary capacity, and access to experienced consultants.

courses.title: Veterinary Pain Management Workshop
courses.description: This is a 4 part workshop created with general practice veterinarians in mind to give the blueprint and step-by-step plan to complete your pain management topic with confidence, efficiency and high standard of care for your patients.

courses.title: Focus on Exotics (A 2 lecture series - ON DEMAND
courses.description:
Lecture Title 1: 7 THINGS THAT WILL SAVE YOUR EXOTIC PATIENT: SIMPLE, PRACTICAL STEPS FOR GP AND EMERGENCY VETS IN THE FIRST CRITICAL HOURS
Speaker: Dr Jade Kingsley BA/BSc, BVSc, PgDip (animal physiology), MANZCVS (Avian Health)
Lecture Abstract:
Exotic patients present unique challenges in general practice and emergency settings. As prey species, they often mask clinical signs until disease is advanced, and when they do present, deterioration can be rapid and unforgiving. The goal of this session is to provide a clear, practical framework for managing these patients in the first critical hours. By focusing on a small number of high-yield principles and techniques, clinicians can dramatically improve survival and patient outcomes.
Lecture 2: SMALL INTESTINAL OBSTRUCTIONS IN RABBITS LECTURE DESCRIPTION:
Speaker: Dr Izidora Sladakovic BVSc (Hons I), MVS, DACZM
Lecture Abstract: From diagnosis and misdiagnosis, to debate between medical and surgical management, small intestinal obstructions in rabbits are an ongoing source of confusion. With the correct diagnosis and appropriately selected treatment protocol, this condition carries a good to excellent prognosis. By breaking it down to the basics, the aim of this lecture is to provide clinicians with the foundational knowledge to approach these cases with more confidence.

courses.title: Veterinary Abdominal Ultrasound Training Camp
courses.description: This hands-on, small-group veterinary abdominal ultrasound training program is designed for veterinarians and veterinary technicians of all skill levels, from beginners to advanced practitioners. Participants will gain practical experience performing diagnostic-quality abdominal ultrasounds using a structured, protocol-based approach. Over three immersive days, attendees will master core organ imaging, systematic scanning workflows, and advanced techniques for the liver, pancreas, adrenal glands, and gastrointestinal tract. The program includes interactive lectures, live-patient scanning labs, and 30 days of personalized feedback through mentored teleradiology, ensuring participants leave with confidence, improved efficiency, and skills that translate directly to clinical practice. This course emphasizes hands-on learning, real-world applications, and long-term clinical success.
courses.location: COVE - The Center of Veterinary Excellence

courses.title: Clinical Approach to the Icteric Patient
courses.description: This webinar will highlight new ways to utilize technology to increase our ability to diagnose the icteric patient more efficiently with the help of specialists. The presentation will cover the production of bilirubin in the liver and define the 3 categories of icterus. Through a case-based discussion, appropriate diagnostics for the icteric patient will also be explored.

courses.title: Compassionate Care: Reducing In-Home Treatment Stress for Fearful Felines
courses.description:
Petsitters and mobile vet professionals deliver essential in-home care for cats, ranging from medication administration to husbandry to TLC. But when a cat is fearful of unfamiliar people and handling, a home visit from a provider can significantly increase their fear, anxiety, and stress and prevent them from getting the medical care they need.
In this talk, we'll discuss pre-visit tips to create a Fear Free plan for care, including gathering information about the feline and communicating with the caregiver. We'll also discuss methods to minimize stress when interacting with cats after arrival at the home and when providing common medical treatments.

courses.title: Optimizing Outcomes: A Practitioner's Guide to Using NT-proBNP in MMVD Cases
courses.description: This webinar will review NT-proBNP as a helpful cardiac biomarker and its uses in monitoring the progression of myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) in small-breed dogs and in assessing efficacy of treatment. Dr. Geri Lake-Bakaar will also share insights into an ongoing clinical study measuring NT-proBNP and its correlation with echocardiographic improvement.

courses.title: More Than Manure: VETSCAN IMAGYST & Its Place in Equine Parasite Detection
courses.description: In this presentation, Dr. Cory Penn will take a look at the new equine AI fecal indication on the VETSCAN IMAGYST and how the instrument allows for detection and diagnosis of equine intestinal parasites.

courses.title: Managing osteoarthritis in dogs: A team-based approach to at-home care
courses.description: Osteoarthritis is a non-curative disease that impacts the dog physically, physiologically, cognitively and emotionally. It drives complex clinical presentations which require the knowledge, skills and availability of a team approach to best manage not only the disease but its consequential illness for the rest of that dog's life.

courses.title: Surgical Confidence Online
courses.description: Surgical Confidence Online is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Navigating Access to Care: Veterinarian Roles and Goals Inside and Outside the Shelter (On Demand)
courses.description: Veterinarians wear many hats when it comes to providing access to veterinary care and interact with many invested partners along the way: staff, volunteers, community members, adopters, ACOs, municipalities, administration, board members, and medical teams, to name a few. In this episode, we will center the conversation around the roles and goals of veterinarians who provide services inside and outside the animal shelter and what "access to care" means in these contexts. The discussion will include how to balance goals between medical and operational teams, staff and community members, and shelter medicine and private practice providers. We will review the impacts of services like community vaccine clinics and high-volume surgery practices on shelter medicine and veterinarians working in these spaces and talk about how these efforts influence what services should be prioritized for shelter and community access to care programs.

courses.title: Treating Otitis Externa, not necessarily rinse and repeat!
courses.description: Treating Otitis Externa is not always a rinse and repeat process. In this webinar attendees will understand how cytology is critical to determining treatment plans, long term treatment options for otitis externa with rods, and when to use oral and topical glucocorticoids, ideal therapies for dogs with atopic dermatitis, and understand benefits and limitations of culture and susceptibility with otitis externa.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Cardiovascular Treatment
courses.description: Have a hypotensive, tachycardiac patient secondary to beta-blocker toxicosis? What about a hypertensive, tachycardiac patient secondary to amphetamine toxicosis? Learn how to treat them in this 90-minute course.

courses.title: Sterilization is Instrumental - Beating the Bugs (TECH441)
courses.description: The responsibility of surgical instrument care is often thrust upon veterinary technicians and assistants. During this course you will learn the science behind and importance of proper surgical instrument processing, including discussion on packaging materials, the role of ultrasonic cleaning devices and appropriate use of steam sterilization. Various methods to assure quality control during the sterilization process are also discussed in detail. This information is beneficial for those wanting to ensure they are following industry standards regarding proper sterilization practices or interested in pursuing a surgical specialty through the Academy of Veterinary Surgical Technicians.

courses.title: Dilated Cardiomyopathy & Diet-Associated DCM
courses.description: This presentation will discuss dilated cardiomyopathy and its various causes, as well as typical examination findings and signalments, and treatment recommendations. Particular attention will be paid to diet-associated DCM and our current understanding of this issue.

courses.title: Relationship-Centered Communication
courses.description: Learn relationship-centered communication skills for engaging in meaningful dialogue with your clients so you can overcome their barriers, decrease your moral distress, and increase access to veterinary care. This course is for everyone on the team.

courses.title: Muscle Matters: Identifying At-Risk Patients for Muscle Loss & Understanding the Importance of Early Intervention
courses.description: In this webinar, learn how to confidently identify patients at risk for muscle atrophy and understand the underlying pathology of this condition. Dr. Kara Amstutz will review effective muscle condition assessment techniques, various treatment options, and practical strategies for selecting cases for muscle supplementation. Attendees will also discover how to administer these supplements for optimal results, gain insights into setting realistic expectations for clinical outcomes, and explore how to effectively monitor patient progress.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Common Holiday Toxins
courses.description: In this webinar, veterinarians and veterinary staff will learn about a variety of human foods and other seasonal hazards that may be toxic to pets.

courses.provider: ZERO PAIN PHILOSOPHY - ACE VETS LIMITED
courses.title: Zero Pain Philosophy Cat Pain Course
courses.description: In this course we will discuss the recognition of acute and chronic pain in cats, the use of opioids and NSAIDs to treat this pain and what to do when these drugs fail to alleviate the pain our patient is suffering. The course takes an in depth view of many aspects of feline pain management with reference to the latest literature.

courses.title: Practical Field Anesthesia and Monitoring Techniques for the Equine Patient
courses.description: Practical Field Anesthesia and Monitoring Techniques for the Equine Patient. This course is designed for the every day practitioner to expand their knowledge of field anesthesia and monitoring techniques. Will provide the necessary knowledge to properly perform anesthesia not in a clinical setting, proper monitoring parameters and dealing with complications that may arise.

courses.title: Shockwave Therapy for Treatment of Shoulder Tendinopathy
courses.description: This course will provide attendees with; 1)Multiple strategies to treat shoulder tendinopathy. 2) A basic understanding of the shoulder anatomy and its function. 3) The role of soft tissue injury in lameness 4) Common indicators and identification of shoulder injuries . 5) Presentation of a clinical study on the treatment of shoulder tendinopathy. 6) Review a multimodal approach to treatment approaches and suggested rehabilitation strategies. Link to Course https://youtu.be/E1rcDnIWup8

courses.title: Anaphylaxis for Veterinary Technicians (TECH446)
courses.description: This focused self study course equips veterinary technicians/nurses to rapidly recognize and treat anaphylaxis, an acute, life threatening systemic hypersensitivity reaction. Topics include a concise review of the immune system, pathophysiology (IgE mediated, non IgE immunologic, and non immunologic pathways), body systems affected, clinical presentation, and a step wise approach to treatment and nursing care/monitoring.

courses.title: Fishing for Solutions: Level Up Your Wound Management Skills with Kerecis VET
courses.description:
Join us for an engaging webinar thats set to revolutionize your approach to veterinary wound healing! Introducing Kerecis VET, a groundbreaking product that harnesses the power of Atlantic Cod Fish Skin for unparalleled wound healing and tissue regeneration. Dive into the fascinating journey behind Kerecis VET, where sustainable fish skin, a by-product of Icelands fishing industry, is turned into a healing solution!
During the webinar we will share the scientific rationale behind why Kerecis VET works, share compelling research, and show you exactly where and how to use it for the best results.
Our expert veterinarian will take you behind the scenes with real-life success stories where Kerecis VET made a massive impact. Shes spilling all the secrets; top-tier graft management tips, dressing hacks, and priceless clinical pearls that will elevate your practice.

courses.title: Feline Urethral Obstruction (DRIP120)
courses.description: This course will take you through the fundamentals of managing the feline urethral obstructed patient. The physiological process of urethral obstruction will be discussed along with the diagnostic approach and treatment of the urethral obstructed feline patient.

courses.title: Infectious Disease Control: Cleaning, Disinfection & Sterilization
courses.description: Environmental and equipment cleaning, disinfection, and, in some settings, sterilization are critical to preventing workplace-associated infections. Effective infection control protocols require identifying the steps and correct procedures needed for success. This course reviews the components of an effective protocol along with common disinfection pitfalls and their solutions. Lastly, the course outlines how to adjust the workplace cleaning, disinfection, and sterilization protocols to better protect the health of both animals and people.

courses.title: INTERVERTEBRAL DISC DISEASE IN DOGS: OH, MY ACHING BACK (57-38844)
courses.description: Intervertebral disc disease (IVDD) is the most common spinal problem in dogs. This course will discuss the anatomy and pathophysiology of type I and type II IVDD in the cervical and thoracolumbar regions as well as diagnostics and medical and surgical treatment options. Included are recommendations for obtaining diagnostic radiographs of each spinal region and advice on when to refer these patients. Acute non-compressive nucleus pulposus extrusion will also be described.

courses.title: IVAS Certification in Veterinary Chinese Herbal Medicine
courses.description: The International Veterinary Acupuncture Society (IVAS) Pathways to Excellence in Veterinary Chinese Herbal Medicine (VCHM) offers licensed veterinarians clinically orientated education and skills. All courses are delivered by the government accredited College of Integrative Veterinary Therapies (CIVT). If you want to extend your knowledge and add Chinese Herbal Medicine to your armory, then the IVAS Certification in Veterinary Chinese Herbal Medicine offers you the chance to expand your treatment options in a very rational, effective, and evidence-based way.

courses.provider: AMERICAN VETERINARY SOCIETY OF ANIMAL BEHAVIOR
courses.title: Clinical Animal Behavior Conference 2026
courses.description: The Clinical Animal Behavior Conference is a 2.5-day intensive event dedicated to advancing the field of veterinary behavioral medicine. Centered on the theme Evolving Together: Advancing our Understanding of Behavior, this conference provides veterinary professionals with actionable, compassionate, and science-based strategies to elevate patient care and improve outcomes. Throughout the conference, attendees will learn to identify behavioral disorders, devise treatment plans which include behavior modifications, environmental changes, the use of constructional affection, enrichment and psychoactive medications. In addition, attendees will learn strategies such as fostering a team approach and using inclusive language to build trust and empathy among the health care team and with clients in order to achieve effective and consistent long term behavioral care for patients.

courses.title: Core Strengthening for Optimal Performance
courses.description:
Evidence-based guide to safe and effective horse core conditioning
Part 1: Functional anatomy of the equine core - what lies under the skin?
Part 2: Biomechanics and kinematics - how does the equine spine move?
Part 3: Motor control in core conditioning - the brain-body connection!
Part 4: The nitty-gritty: the how and when of different core activation and strengthening exercises
Part 5: Different therapies and techniques to support horse core conditioning
Part 6: Suggested combinations for static and dynamic core conditioning - what else can I do for my horse?

courses.title: Essentials of Trauma Patient By Dr Franziska Meyer, Dr. med. vet. DACVECC
courses.description: Essentials of Trauma Patient By Dr Franziska Meyer, Dr. med. vet. DACVECC is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Senior Dog Nutrition: A Practical Guide for the Veterinary Practitioner
courses.description: This course will review common age-related conditions in senior dogs and help veterinarians and their healthcare teams recognize when a diet modification is needed.

courses.title: NoodleU Murder Mystery Event May 2025 ON DEMAND
courses.description: Sharpen your investigative skills with NoodleU Murder Mystery 2025, a thrilling and immersive veterinary learning experience where each session is designed to uncover the hidden clues behind common yet complex clinical mysteries. Inspired by classic whodunnit storytelling, this year's NoodleU conference combines engaging content with practical insights to help veterinary professionals elevate their diagnostic and treatment strategies, all with a touch of mystery-solving fun.

courses.title: Panel Discussion: Radiography at Yearling Sales - What really matters?
courses.description:
Interpretation of radiological findings at bloodstock sales can be a minefield for clinicians and may have a huge impact on the realised sale price of yearlings - yet, there is no 'rulebook' and nobody gets it right all of the time. Beyond the 'science', many factors feed into the final determination of relative importance of any given radiological blemish, including variables relating to horse, client, racing jurisdiction and clinician experience. What types of imperfections are most important, and for whom? What weight should be attributed to conformation, physical exam and pedigree when viewing a defect? What are the most appropriate ways to communicate findings in terms of risk? How should one approach quality control of radiographs, and when/how should additional projections be taken? Which are the most important projections?
This panel discussion will draw on the experience of three highly respected vets on the international yearling sales circuit from Europe, North America and Australia. Covered topics will range from key pathologies including imaging nuances, unusual cases, tricky situations and unexpected outcomes. Expect to learn far more than can be found in any textbook!

courses.title: Webinar Series - Update on Equine Gastric Ulcer Syndrome
courses.description: This lecture series, "Update on Equine Gastric Ulcer Syndrome," provides a comprehensive overview of the condition, its management, and prevention strategies.

courses.title: Pet Birds - Common Conditions (EXOT327)
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the avian species. Topics covered include clinical presentation of conditions seen most commonly in pet birds, diagnostic protocols, and treatment.

courses.title: Intervertebral Disc Disease (IVDD) in Dogs
courses.description: This program will go over presentation, diagnosis, treatment and prognosis of IVDD including how to assess a dog's gait, test for proprioceptive deficits, pain, and reflexes. Discussion also includes medical versus surgical management and the prognosis of IVDD.

courses.title: Heatstroke (DRIP107)
courses.description: This session dives into the relevant pathophysiology, as well as highlighting the recognition and assessment of heatstroke. It focuses on logical and effective therapies, and addresses the prognosis, and how to maximize the probability of recovery for patients.

courses.title: Canine Otitis Externa: Diagnosis, Management, Success
courses.description: Canine otitis externa is one of the most frequently encountered conditions in small animal veterinary practice. This presentation explores the causes of canine otitis externa including the predisposing, primary and perpetuating factors, the importance of otic cytology, and the essential treatment modalities to help ensure clinical resolution. The development of a long-term maintenance cleaning and allergy management plan will also be discussed.

courses.title: Cardiac Emergencies (DRIP111)
courses.description: This course will cover the physiology of cardiac emergencies in cats and dogs, including diagnosing and developing a treatment plan for these patients.

courses.title: Vet BLUE Lung Point of Care Ultrasound Online Course
courses.description: The Vet BLUE Lung Point of Care Ultrasound Online course is a self-paced recorded online course that includes 8 modules covering: Introduction to lung ultrasound, image acquisition (how to perform lung ultrasound), wet lung vs. dry lung principles, cased based applications including assessment for pulmonary edema, pneumonia and other wet lung conditions, nodular diseases and pulmonary masses, assessment for pulmonary thromboembolism, and using Vet BLUE for patient monitoring and CPR.

courses.title: Living With Claws: Confidently Provide Guidance to Feline Owners
courses.description: This discussion equips the veterinary team with information and tools to educate pet parents on alternatives to declawing. By ending the elective onychectomy procedure we are protecting the welfare of our feline patients, but we also must know how to help pet parents live in harmony with cats and their claws. With a plethora of information out there, this discussion streamlines what you need to know today to set your pet parents up for success tomorrow.

courses.title: Veterinary Technician Utilization-Hey I Got This! (STAF196)
courses.description: How well is your practice utilizing veterinary technicians compared to other practices and current standards? Placing and utilizing vet techs in the appropriate role within the team is linked to better patient care, staff fulfillment, more manageable workloads, increased practice revenue, and team wellness. This course will identify obstacles to reaching higher standards and discuss how to have difficult discussions within the hospital to aid in increasing vet tech utilization.

courses.title: Point-of-Care Testing: How You Can Improve Patient Care
courses.description: This session will review available point-of-care testing options for evaluation of dogs and cats with a variety of diseases. Dr. Elizabeth Rozanski will share real-life cases, how diagnostic testing can help aid in clinical decision-making, and when further evaluation is needed. Attendees will also explore a cost-effective approach to patient care that can help improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: Perioperative management of brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome Non-Interactive
courses.description: This lecture is targeted at veterinary professionals and support staff. The lecture will cover the pathophysiology of brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome in dogs and cats, and medical and surgical treatment recommendations.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Chronic Kidney Disease in Cats
courses.description: This course provides an overview of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in cats, including disease signs and diagnosis, related key nutritional factors, and nutritional management strategies.

courses.title: Backyard Poultry Basics (EXOT333)
courses.description: With a growing interest in self-sufficiency, the number of people keeping small flocks of backyard poultry is rising. With this rise in flock numbers is a growing expectancy for veterinary care at a level equivalent to what clients have come to expect for other companion animals. The first step for veterinarians to meet these expectations is to acquire the knowledge of the basics, without which it is difficult to understand the hows and whys of disease.
