By completing this course, veterinarians, technicians and students will have a thorough grasp of poultry, their care and nutrition, and the basics of providing veterinary care.

courses.title: Pet Bird Essentials (EXOT325)
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the avian species. Topics covered include basic training, husbandry, handling, physical exam, sample collection and processing, diagnostic protocols, and treatment.

courses.title: Neurodiversity in Veterinary Clients and Team Members: A Fear Free Approach to Inclusive Care
courses.description: Neurodiversity encompasses the natural variations in human brain function and behavior, including conditions such as autism, ADHD, dyslexia, and more. In the veterinary field, understanding neurodiversity is essential for creating inclusive, supportive environments for both clients and team members. This course equips veterinary professionals with the awareness, strategies, and tools to effectively communicate, accommodate sensory and processing differences, and foster a practice culture that values all forms of thinking and interaction.

courses.title: Separating Fact, Fiction, and Uncertainty: Canine Respiratory Illness, Part II
courses.description: This course was developed in response to continued reports of an upswing in respiratory illnesses impacting dogs across North America. Join Trupanion with a panel of global veterinary authorities as they discuss Canine Respiratory Illness and learnings since part I of this series. Originally aired on February 13, 2024.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Advanced Ophthalmology
courses.description: This course was devised for equine practitioners with a good working knowledge in equine ophthalmology and provides an update on recent developments in the field. The speaker panel consisting of 2 of the most highly respected and experienced equine ophthalmologists worldwide will be discussing the current thinking on pathophysiology of different conditions affecting the equine eye and will cover established and recently developed cutting-edge diagnostic / therapeutic techniques and medications.

courses.title: The Digital Rx Shift: Smarter Prescription Workflows for Veterinary Practice
courses.description: This webinar will provide a practical overview of how digital prescription workflows are changing veterinary practices. In this session, Kim Lance will explore how digital prescribing and prescription request management can improve accuracy, reduce administrative burden, support documentation and compliance efforts, and enhance communication with both clients and pharmacies. She will also highlight key workflow and implementation considerations for practices looking to incorporate digital prescription tools into everyday operations.

courses.title: Ask Me Anything: Anal Sacculitis with Dr. Mollie Mesman
courses.description: In this "Ask Me Anything"-style webinar powered by Standards of Care, Mollie Mesman, DVM, DACVD, will provide an overview of canine anal sac health and disease, review the physiology and function of anal sacs, identify primary factors contributing to impaction, and outline treatment and management strategies.

courses.title: Cooperative Care in Practice: Reducing Fear, Anxiety, and Stress Through Partnership
courses.description: By the end of this course, veterinary professionals will be able to apply cooperative care techniques, such as desensitization, counter-conditioning, and low-stress handling, to reduce patient FAS and improve procedure outcomes, while effectively interpreting behavior cues and communicating strategies to clients to support ongoing cooperative care at home.

courses.title: Leading with Limits: Learning to Thrive as a Veterinarian
courses.description: This course is designed to help you create balance, set healthy boundaries, and develop leadership skills that empower you and those around you. Each module offers practical tools to support your well-being, strengthen team dynamics, and enhance patient and client relationships.

courses.title: Mitigating Fear, Anxiety, & Stress in Patients in Isolation & Quarantine Housing
courses.description: Whether animals are being managed in a shelter environment, veterinary clinic, or laboratory setting, the welfare of animals in isolation housing should be considered. How veterinary teams care for these animals is of particular importance, especially for puppies in their sensitive period for socialization. This webinar will review signs of animal stress, how to mitigate stress, and specific tips for promoting good welfare for dogs and puppies in quarantine or isolation.

courses.title: Today's Top Parasite Prevention Tips & Tactics
courses.description: Lurking inside and outside of pets, owners, and homes, parasites never cease to disgust and annoy all parties involved. Prevention through education and proper product utilization are key to achieving a parasite-free existence. Every veterinarian in general practice has their go-to products that are perfectly appropriate for most patients; however, the perpetual addition of new preventive products, changes to existing products, and flooding of advertisements and social media miseducation can confuse clients about their options. In this webinar, get expert tips to help you become empowered when it comes to educating clients on these selections and better understand the ever-changing landscape of parasite prevention and the factors that may make one product more effective than another on a case-by-case basis.

courses.title: Emergency & Critical Care
courses.description: There are lots of ways to make visits Fear Free when there is time for you and the client to discuss the animal's FAS, add pre-visit pharmaceuticals, take your time, and even postpone non-essential procedures. But, what about in an emergency or critical care situation? Even though the procedures are not elective, there are still things you can do to help ease patients' FAS.

courses.title: Updates in Acute Canine Pancreatitis
courses.description: This webinar will explore the latest advancements in the treatment of canine pancreatitis, with a focus on both inpatient and outpatient management strategies. Special attention will be given to the novel therapeutic PANOQUELL-CA1 (fuzapladib sodium for injection), including its mechanism of action, clinical applications, and potential benefits in improving patient outcomes. Attendees will also discover how to integrate this emerging therapy into practice for enhanced pancreatitis care.

courses.provider: CENTER FOR FOOD SECURITY AND PUBLIC HEALTH COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE IOWA S
courses.title: Cleaning and Disinfection in Animal Settings (Advanced Course)
courses.description: Cleaning and disinfection, often referred to as C&D, is an essential process for the prevention of disease in animal settings. Destroying microorganisms in the environment and on surfaces reduces exposure risks and the spread of disease, and protects animal and human health. Understanding how to properly conduct C&D procedures helps to obtain optimum results. This course provides practical examples for livestock production, veterinary clinic and disease outbreak settings.

courses.title: Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis - Can You Identify & Treat This Novel Syndrome - Self-Study
courses.description: In recent months, sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have become available for the treatment of insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus in feline patients. One of the rare potential side effects of this class of medication is euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (eDKA). Learners will review the relevant pathophysiology of, as well as diagnostic testing and therapeutic interventions for cats suspected or confirmed to be living with eDKA.

courses.title: The Journey You Own: Practices for Well-being and Productivity
courses.description: Are you ready to reignite your passion, reclaim your energy, and revolutionize your approach to work? Time to break free from the draining cycle of reactive responses and embrace a more dynamic and fulfilling path. In this immersive introductory course, you will embark on a journey to explore the depths of your reactions, actions, and emotions, while cultivating a sense of stillness in your daily life. Discover practical strategies to create more space, incorporate contemplative practices into your life, and align personal values with your actions and activities, boosting your productivity while maintaining balance. By the end of this learning experience, you will emerge with the tools to become more grounded, whole and fulfilled in your work and your life. This course is authored by Jyothi V. Robertson, DVM, DABVP and the Journey You Own team, with invaluable assistance from Leonard Levy, Video Director of Photography, Cody Flowers of Flowers Camera LLC and Bhavana Learning Group.

courses.title: Webinar -Fluid Therapy for Colic/Diarrhea - IV & Enteral (incl. Cases)
courses.description: The fluid lectures will focus on an initial review of the key principles of fluid therapy and its monitoring. The pros and cons of electrolyte supplementation will be reviewed. A particular focus will be paid to the use of non-conventional fluids including enteral fluids, in both hospital and field settings, Carboy IV fluids, and rectal fluids.

courses.title: COMPREHENSIVE BOVINE EMBRYO TRANSFER TRAINING COURSE (1484-39132)
courses.description: The 5-day Comprehensive Embryo Transfer Training Course teaches the student: superovulation techniques, estrous synchronization methods, collection, recognition, manipulation, classification, freezing, thawing and transfer of bovine embryos.
courses.location: International Embryo Technology School Training Facility

courses.title: AFAST Point of Care Ultrasound Online Course
courses.description:
The AFAST Online Course with Updated Curriculum: The course has been recently updated and covers AFAST which is a point of care ultrasound protocol and its image acquisition, target organ approach for obvious soft tissue abnormalities, and the abdominal fluid scoring system with case-based applications.
Module 01 - History and Overview of FAST
Module 02 - Clinical Applications of AFAST and Its Fluid Scoring System
Module 03 - The Diaphragmatico-Hepatic View - Image Acquisition, Pearls, Pitfalls and Artifacts
Module 04- The Spleen-Renal View - Image Acquisition, Pearls, Pitfalls and Artifacts
Module 05 - The Cysto-Colic View - Image Acquisition, Pearls, Pitfalls and Artifacts
Module 06 - The Small Intestinal- Umbilical View - Image Acquisition, Pearls, Pitfalls and Artifacts
Module 07 - Incidental and Unexpected Case Studies - AFAST and Its Target-Organ Approach
Supplemental Module - How to Do AFAST and Its Target-Organ Approach

courses.title: Managing the stressed out male cat - Feline urethral obstructions
courses.description: During this lecture, management of feline urethral obstruction (UO) from history to emergency stabilization through to discharge and at-home care instructions are presented with a strong focus on evidence-based medicine. Exact medication doses will be provided.

courses.title: Sun City Veterinary Conference 2025-On Demand
courses.description:
Six hours from the 2025 Sun City Veterinary Conference are on demand via streaming.
Pre-recorded RACE approved lectures from the conference are available in the subjects of Behavior Medicine (3 hrs), Internal Medicine (2 hrs), and Practice Management (1 hr):
"Separation Anxiety-Calming the Angst" Dr. Jeff Nichol DVM IAABC
"Aggression Between Family Dogs-When to Intervene" Dr. Jeff Nichol DVM IAABC
"Aggressive/Fearful Pets in the Veterinary Clinic" Dr. Jeff Nichol DVM IAABC
"Leptospirosis-Diagnosis, Complications, and Treatment" Dr. Antu Radhakrishnan DVM, DACVIM(SAIM)
"Addison's Disease-Conquering the Crisis" Dr. Antu Radhakrishnan DVM, DACVIM(SAIM)
"Brave New World: Artificial Intelligence in Veterinary Medicine" Matt Heinlein LVT, MBA, CVPM

courses.title: Strategies for Challenging Ableism in Companion Animal Welfare
courses.description: Many animal shelters and rescues unwittingly perpetuate ableism through their engagements with disabled animals, even when they are trying to help these animals. In this session, we will explore how animal shelters and rescues contribute to problematic representations of disability and engage in practices that harm these animals. We will explore strategies for challenging ableism and better serving disabled animals.

courses.title: There Is No Such Thing as a Dental: How to Communicate With Clients & Staff About Comprehensive Dentistry
courses.description: The word "dental" has been used to describe a procedure that is much more all-encompassing than the name suggests, causing a lack of understanding among clients and staff. In this webinar, Dr. Naomi Hoyer will share how understanding the wide range of dental diseases and using more effective language to describe the anesthetized oral examination, imaging, dental cleaning, and necessary treatments can empower the veterinary team to provide the best care possible for patients.

courses.title: Endocrine Emergencies (DRIP122)
courses.description:
This course focuses on relevant pathophysiology and diagnostic testing regarding endocrine emergencies and discusses potential therapies.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 73 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Navigating IVDD Recovery
courses.description: This course will provide attendees with an overview of IVDD, an understanding of the phases of IVDD recovery, how to optimize pain management with a multimodal approach and how to apply safe, phase-appropriate rehab techniques to reduce pain, promote neuroplasticity, and restore mobility.

courses.title: In Sickness & in Health: Equine Liver Disease Updates
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Erin Pearson will review common equine hepatic disorders, including bacterial cholangiohepatitis, cholelithiasis, pyrrolizidine alkaloid toxicity, and infectious viral hepatitis (equine parvovirus and equine hepacivirus). Focus will be on the clinical and clinicopathologic signs of these diseases and how to formulate diagnostic and treatment plans through case examples. Attendees will also explore how to interpret liver blood work and ultrasonographic findings to guide diagnoses and therapeutic recommendations.

courses.title: A Day in the Life of a Dermatologist
courses.description: This course examines the diagnosis, treatment, and client education of dermatological disorders of the dog and cat. It explores common and uncommon skin diseases such as pemphigus, discoid lupus erythematosus, systemic lupus erythematosus, erythema multiforme, Steven's Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis, and epitheliotropic lymphoma. Allergic dermatitis is rounds out the review.

courses.title: Managing and Treating Canine Hypoadrenocorticism (Addison's Disease)
courses.description: Participants will be updated on all aspects of hypoadrenocorticism (HOC) diagnosis and management. The presentation will include HOC pathophysiology, clinical signs, diagnosis, treatment options, and monitoring. To make the presentation as clinically relevant as possible, multiple case studies will be presented as well.

courses.title: COMPREHENSIVE BOVINE EMBRYO TRANSFER TRAINING COURSE (1484-39132)
courses.description: The 5-day Comprehensive Embryo Transfer Training Course teaches the student: superovulation techniques, estrous synchronization methods, collection, recognition, manipulation, classification, freezing, thawing and transfer of bovine embryos.
courses.location: International Embryo Technology School Training Facility

courses.title: WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management - Module II - Preventing and treating pain.
courses.description:
This course includes Module II of the WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management. The course was developed with the vision that veterinary professionals (veterinarians and nurses and veterinary technicians) across the globe understand the importance of adequate pain management for small animal health and welfare, and are empowered to
1) Frequently assess pain in small animals with knowledge of pain-related behaviors and validated pain scales
2)Prevent pain and other negative emotions such as fear, discomfort, nausea and anxiety
3)Treat pain using drug and non-drug therapies in which the analgesic plan is developed on a case-by-case basis and adapted to their own reality.
The WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management includes pre-recorded lectures in addition to mandatory and suggested reading materials, and quizzes at the end of each lecture. The educational content is primarily based on the published 2022 WSAVA guidelines for the recognition, assessment and treatment of pain, and on additional topics not covered by that document, but considered to be important and relevant for professionals working with companion animal health and welfare globally. Lectures are given by the authors of the Guidelines and other invited experts in the field.
The entire educational content is available at no cost following registration to any veterinarian or nurse or veterinary technician. A fee will be charged to those who would like to receive the actual Certificate and recognition of continuing education credits.
The WSAVA Certificate in Pain Management is divided into three Modules. The Module II Preventing and treating pain has 12 hours of content (12 recorded lectures of 0.5 hour each and 3.5 hours of mandatory reading).
It includes lectures focused on the following topics, Principles of pain management, Analgesic drug delivery techniques and tools, Opioids, Anti-inflammatory, Local anesthetics, Alpha-2 agonists, Adjunctive analgesic drugs, Adjunctive musculoskeletal therapies, non-analgesi

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2025 Considerations for Clinical Implementation of Immunotherapy in Veterinary Oncology On Demand
courses.description: Immunotherapy is revolutionizing cancer treatment in both human and veterinary medicine, expanding the therapeutic toolbox for veterinary cancer patients. This virtual, day-long course will explore immunotherapy's evolution, current state, and future potential within veterinary oncology. Led by an esteemed panel of human and veterinary cancer immunotherapy experts, topics will cover the role of CAR T-cell therapies, immune checkpoint inhibitors, the generation of tumor-reactive activated T cells, and review progress in immunotherapy applications in veterinary applications. Comparative insights from human oncology will provide a bridge to innovative therapeutic strategies in veterinary medicine and help the clinical veterinary oncologist navigate paradigm shifts in the oncologic approach and management of patients undergoing immunotherapy.

courses.title: Parasitology of Dogs and Cats (TECH439)
courses.description: Animals and people have been plagued with parasites since prehistoric times and understanding what youre up against is the first step in knowing how to treat your patients. In this course, youll develop an understanding of canine and feline parasite life cycles, zoonosis, proper sample processing, evaluation, and identification of internal and external parasites of dogs and cats. Youll also learn techniques to improve ova recovery and microscopic and gross identification techniques.

courses.title: Neuromuscular Junction Disease and Peripheral Neuropathies (DRIP128)
courses.description:
This course focuses on Neuromuscular Junction Disease and Peripheral Neuropathies found in modern veterinary practice and the logical way to handle.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 55 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: A Pawsitive Approach to Managing Hyperthyroid Cats
courses.description: Whether animals are being managed in a shelter environment, veterinary clinic, or laboratory setting, the welfare of animals in isolation housing should be considered. How veterinary teams care for these animals is of particular importance, especially for puppies in their sensitive period for socialization. This webinar will review signs of animal stress, how to mitigate stress, and specific tips for promoting good welfare for dogs and puppies in quarantine or isolation.

courses.title: Emotionally Intelligent Euthanasia (Online)
courses.description: Emotionally Intelligent Euthanasia (EIE) is born of the idea that maintaining personal control of emotions is beneficial to one's mental health and well-being. It is useful to understand what we are feeling during euthanasia and what others around us are experiencing. Such knowledge guides our communication with pet owners and makes end-of-life work much more enjoyable and fulfilling. This module explores concepts like self-awareness, social skills, and empathy to build lasting EIE. Ideal for veterinary students, those new to veterinary medicine, and those who may be feeling dissatisfied with euthanasia-related work.

courses.title: Using Distractions: Fear Free Do's and Don'ts
courses.description: Food or toy distractions can be an exceptionally useful tool in Fear Free. But they must be used appropriately, and in the correct situations, to ensure they actually decrease or prevent FAS, rather than inadvertently make things worse. This one-hour course will empower you to know when to use distractions (and when not to use them), how to properly implement them, and what to do "in the moment." Through several video examples and scenarios such as nail trims and vaccines, you will learn what to do "in the moment" as well.

courses.title: Redefining Inflammatory Bowel Disease: The Role of Dysbiosis
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Heather Kvitko-White will review how our improved understanding of the intestinal microbiome is shifting the paradigm in the diagnosis and management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). This presentation will explore the role of the microbiome in patient health, the causes and consequences of dysbiosis in disease, and, most importantly, how this information impacts daily choices in the clinic.

courses.title: One Health: Dogs and Cats as Sentinels for Human Risk
courses.description: This case-based course summarizes key clinical aspects of ehrlichiosis, anaplasmosis, and Lyme, including the One Health concern. It explains how dogs and cats can act as sentinels for human exposure risk to parasites. Recent peer-reviewed literature as well as evidence and expert based guidelines will be shared. This course helps participants feel more comfortable and confident facing off against these increasingly common infectious disease, including communicating with pet owners.

courses.title: The Crying Dog
courses.description: 1. In this lecture with Dr. DJ Haeussler we go over common causes of epiphora in dogs and offer recommendations on recognition and medical and surgical treatment options.

courses.title: Essentials of Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine
courses.description: Essentials of Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine was developed by Dr Barbara Fougere and is taught by the faculty of CIVT. This CIVT course is designed to provide you with confidence and a working knowledge of ten of the most popular herbs for use in practice. The course helps you to address the common questions that clients ask about herbal medicine. It is not designed to make you an herbalist, but it will give you important insights and knowledge that will help in everyday practice. CIVT provides an evidence-based approach bridging science with the tradition of herbal medicine.

courses.title: Ultrasound Modular Course
courses.description:
4 module eLearning course covering ultrasound of the following:
Imaging artifacts in ultrasonography
Ultrasound of the liver and gall bladder
Ultrasound of the spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands
Ultrasound of the gastrointestinal tract and urinary tract

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2023 Clinical Communication for Specialists and Candidates On Demand
courses.description: This three-module, on-demand course explores essential concepts and tools for clinical communication in veterinary medicine for specialists and candidates. Based on the Calgary-Cambridge veterinary communication model, participants will develop an understanding and familiarity with existing terminology and review of the evidence behind clinical communication as a skillset that is both useful and expandable. Modules includes foundational topics for using communication to achieve clinical goals as well as in-depth discussion and application of core communication skills.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Abdominal, Thoracic & Soft Tissue Ultrasound
courses.description: This webinar series was developed to provide attendees with the theoretical knowledge and the practical skills of ultrasound image acquisition and interpretation of Abdominal, Thoracic and soft Tissue Ultrasound. It is suitable for vets from equine or mixed practice who are keen to further develop their equine ultrasound expertise.

courses.title: Canine Lab 2: Handling and Restraining Medium-sized and Large Dogs with Skill and Ease
courses.description: Have you ever had to struggle to get a dog into position or keep him there for an exam or procedure? We often use force to restrain uncooperative dogs when techniques that incorporate finesse would work better. With Low Stress Handling techniques you learn how to control movement in all directions while providing the support and guidance the dog needs to feel secure.

courses.title: Equine Corneal Lacerations
courses.description:
This course covers how to approach an equine corneal laceration in
the field when referral to a specialty hospital is not an option. We will discuss surgical and medical management, as well as ethical components to the case.

courses.title: Trupanion Certification
courses.description: This free, 30-minute certification program is designed to help hospital teams practice their best medicine by reducing stressful conversations about cost of care. By becoming Trupanion Certified, team members broaden their professional development, streamline daily workflows and reduce administrative hassle while learning how to grow their client base and help more pets.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Adverse Food Reactions (NUTR126)
courses.description: Adverse food reactions, including food allergies, have diverse clinical signs with gastrointestinal and/or cutaneous manifestations. In this course we discuss the classification, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and management of adverse food reactions. We will primarily focus on nutritional management and will discuss diagnostic food trials for the different types of adverse food reactions, gastrointestinal and cutaneous. We will review how to identify nutrients of concern for both gastrointestinal adverse food reactions and cutaneous adverse food reactions and how these nutrients of concern impact dietary management. Feeding strategies, diet selection, and case management will also be discussed.

courses.title: Feline Ultrasound: The Yellow Cat and Ultrasound-Guided Fine Needle Aspirates (DIAG434)
courses.description:
It's an often-repeated adage - "cats are not little dogs", and this is especially true with feline medicine and ultrasound. Cats have many unique diseases that require feline-specific knowledge to diagnose and treat. Ultrasound is one of the most useful tools feline clinicians have in their arsenal to diagnose diseases in cats, who often present with very vague and non-specific clinical signs.
This is one of four courses in the Feline Ultrasound collection. Each course will consist of a single 2-hour session that will focus on the normal ultrasound appearance of an organ system and then present changes observed that are associated with specific diseases. These courses are independent of each other and can be taken in any combination.
This course will review two important concepts: scanning the yellow cat and how to perform ultrasound guided fine needle aspirates. We will review the 3 causes of icterus in cats and how to use ultrasound to narrow down the differential list. We will discuss the normal appearance of the feline liver, gallbladder, and pancreas on ultrasound, and review the ultrasound appearance of diseases causing hyperbilirubinemia in cats. The course will review when to perform fine needle aspirates and when to avoid the procedure. There will be a detailed overview of how to perform ultrasound guided FNA and how to prepare and submit slides, considerations and approaches to aspirating individual organs, and ideal case selection.

courses.title: Canine Chagas Disease: An Emergency Perspective
courses.description: The expanding range of Chagas Disease caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is adding to the already challenging aspects of diagnosis and treatment. This course will give an overview and update of Chagas disease including the pathogenesis, identification of clinical signs, diagnostic testing, and treatment in an emergency setting.

courses.provider: AMERICAN SOCIETY FOR THE PREVENTION OF CRUELTY TO ANIMALS (ASPCA)
courses.title: Winter Hazards
courses.description:
This course covers a discussion of several common causes of pet toxicities seen in the winter months. It discusses the concerns associated with these winter toxins and the treatment needed for each of them as well as pitfalls to avoid in treatment of these toxicities.
The toxicities covered will include antifreeze, ice melts and exposures to Holiday time plants and home made ornaments.

courses.title: Emergency Care for Zoomed (exotic) Pets: From Crisis to Success
courses.description:
This online course provides an intensive lecture on a wide array of medicine and emergency critical care of zoomed (exotic) species, including mammals (rabbits, rodents, ferrets, hedgehogs, sugar gliders), birds (with focus on Psittacines) and reptiles (chelonians, snakes and lizards).
It covers aspects of how to set up your practice, medical math, triage, clinical skills, sedation and analgesia, CPR guidelines, assessment and treatment of dehydration and hypovolemia, assessment and treatment of hypotension, common emergencial presentations of zoomed (exotic) species, among other important topics.
The course is aimed at veterinarians and veterinary paraprofessionals (technician, assistant, nurse), as well as respective students with a keen interest in emergency and critical care of zoomed (exotic) species.

courses.title: Getting Through the Day: How to Make it Through the Day in GP Module 3 (SAIM803)
courses.description:
The VIN Foundation (https://vinfoundation.org) is a non-profit organization committed to helping you, and all new graduates, feel supported as you journey into and through our profession. Getting Through the Day is a VIN Foundation resource made possible through individual donations and grants. VIN membership is not required to access the VIN Foundation resources.
In this course different topics will be presented each week and the presentations will include highlights on pathophysiology, case presentation, differentials, diagnostic approach, treatment recommendations, and case examples where appropriate. Important non-technical skills will also be included.

courses.title: Practical Approach to Thoracic Trauma in Cats and Dogs (DRIP104)
courses.description: This course will go into how to stabilize and manage thoracic trauma in cats and dogs. Both penetrating and blunt traumas will be discussed and the logical way to approach treating these patients.

courses.title: Pet Dogs, Problem Dogs, High Performance Dogs: How Science Can Take Your Training to a New Level (CDPS113)
courses.description: Get fast, consistent training results for any species whether you are a trainer, veterinary behaviorist, or pet owner. Learn from Dr. Sophia Yin how science and Applied Behavior Analysis can improve your animal training skills while deepening your understanding of animal behavior.

courses.title: Traumatic Brain Injury (DRIP109)
courses.description: This course will take you through the fundamentals of managing a patient with traumatic brain injury. Topics will include the physiological process of brain injury, as well as the medical assessment of your patient. Monitoring and therapeutic options will also be discussed to ensure optimal care for your traumatic brain injury patient.

courses.title: Exotic Euthanasia (Online)
courses.description: This module demonstrates species-specific euthanasia for companion exotics such as small mammals, reptiles, and birds. The purpose is to introduce the various techniques used in these animals compared to dogs and cats and shed light on the complexities they bring. Attention will be given to predominantly injectable techniques, with some content on physical euthanasia methods. We will review how veterinarians manage these cases respectfully and compassionately.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Rabbit Medicine
courses.description: The webinar series provides a solid grounding in common clinical presentations and pathologies in rabbits such as respiratory conditions It also covers critical care, analgesia and anaesthesia - all of which are vitally important to get sick rabbits better quicker.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Practical Equine Endoscopy - Respiratory, Gastrointestinal & Urogenital Tracts
courses.description: Nowadays most equine practices have an endoscope at their disposal, which might not get used as much as it could. This lecture series is designed to provide vets from equine practice with the theoretical and especially invaluable tips & tricks to help them perform most routine diagnostic and some therapeutic endoscopic procedures currently used in equine practice. A panel of international experts who have dedicated a significant proportion of their careers to equine endoscopy are involved with this course and will be sharing pearls of wisdom. The first part of the lecture series will focus on the upper/lower respiratory tract and sinoscopy and in the second part the gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts will be covered.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Rehabilitation for Equine Neck Conditions
courses.description: Neck problems are commonly encountered in horses of all ages, but especially in middle-aged and older animals, have debilitating consequences and only a limited number of treatment options exist. This lecture series covers the cervical anatomy, joint motion and how to use passive stretches to rehabilitate horses affected by neck conditions. A team consisting of a world-renowned sports medicine and rehabilitation specialist and an equine physiotherapist will be exchanging notes on how they personally approach such challenging cases, when and how they use rehabilitation modalities and what exercises they recommend by extensively discussing cases.

courses.title: Evidence-Based Rehabilitation for Equine Kissing Spines
courses.description:
Part 1 - Functional Anatomy, Biomechanics, and Pathology
Part 2 - Pain, Pain Management, and Core Muscle Function
Part 3 - Brain to Body: Neuromotor Control and Movement Retraining
Part 4 - Electrotherapies for Rehabilitation for Kissing Spines
Part 5 - Conservative versus Surgical Treatment for Kissing Spine: Specialist Q & A
Part 6 - The Nitty-Gritty: Specific Exercises for each Phase of Rehabilitation

courses.title: PATELLAR LUXATION PART 1: PATHOANATOMY, DIAGNOSTIC TIPS AND CLIENT EDUCATION (195-41361)
courses.description: This lecture begins with a discussion of what determines whether the patella tracks normally or it luxates. Understanding of this relevant pathoanatomy guides the veterinarian in their diagnostic methods, client education, case selection, and surgical techniques. Diagnostic tips include a discussion of breeds at risk for medial patellar luxation (MPL) vs. lateral patellar luxation (LPL), gait patterns typical of MPL and LPL, the importance of the standing examination and hip extension, video demonstration of cruciate ligament evaluation and common radiographic errors that you can avoid. This module concludes with a discussion of evidence-based answers to questions commonly asked by pet owners. After attending this lecture, attendees will be better able to understand and diagnose patellar luxation (including the difficult cases) and to educate pet owners with regard to their commonly asked questions.

courses.title: Understanding Myofascial Pain In Small Animals
courses.description:
This course will provide attendees with: 1) A basic understanding of the important role that soft tissue disfunction plays in influencing movement and pain 2) A better understanding of myofascial trigger points their origins, physiological characteristics and role in producing pain 3) A review of neuro pathways and their role in transmitting pain signals 4) A review of the various approaches for diagnosis and treatment of soft tissue disfunction 5) A review of the available treatment modalities proven to be effective in treating soft tissue injuries
Link to course on YouTube https://youtu.be/4gOT3Uc2zpo

courses.title: A Brief Review of Veterinary Toxicology (DRIP125)
courses.description:
This course is a brief review of veterinary toxicology. It will focuses on relevant pathophysiology and diagnostic testing regarding common toxicants encountered by veterinary patients and discusses potential therapies.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Completion of the course will take a minimum of 120 minutes. Participants must complete the participation requirements by April 30, 2025 to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Camp Maddie: Kitten Edition (OnDemand, Modular)
courses.description:
Prepare for Kitten Season with expert guidance! This free virtual event is designed to equip participants with essential skills and knowledge to tackle the challenges of the upcoming kitten season, which is expected to be particularly demanding. Most kittens in the US are born to free-roaming community cats. With shelters already stretched thin, this event will provide critical insights from industry experts to help organizations scale up their responses to meet the needs of more vulnerable kittens in their communities. Topics will include: The role of community cat programs in saving kittens; Developing kitten foster programs that are effective, safe, and fun; Medical protocols tailored for kitten care in shelters and rescues; Behavior and socialization protocols for raising confident, friendly kittens.
Join us for this invaluable opportunity to learn from the best in the field and ensure you are prepared to make a difference in the lives of more kittens this season!

courses.title: Interpretation of Canine Dental Radiographs
courses.description: Full mouth intraoral radiographs are required to properly diagnose and treat oral disease. At the end of this online video the participant will be able to interpret canine dental radiographs, identifying normal anatomy and radiographic signs of periodontal disease, endodontic disease, tooth resorption, osseous lesions, and developmental issues.

courses.title: Influenza: Current Trends, Pathogens, & Prevention
courses.description: In the last year, influenza has reasserted itself as a pathogen of interest for veterinarians, both large and small. With high-path avian influenza (HPAI) having infected a human in the United States for the first time in history, influenza appears to be rapidly evolving and expanding its reach from a species perspective and from a geographical standpoint. It is only a matter of time before dog owners are once again concerned about it as well. Just as the influenza pathogen continues to evolve, so, too, does vaccine technology and our understanding of the immune system and the role of each cell within. Join Dr. Jenifer Chatfield in this webinar for a discussion of replicon technology in vaccine development and the persistent evolution of influenza and where these things collide.

courses.title: Advanced Certification in Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine
courses.description:
This Advanced Certification in Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine course is designed for veterinarians who have already undertaken either the CIVT Certification Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine or a similar course through a recognized herbal school or can demonstrate their experience in Western herbal medicine. The focus of this course is on the Materia Medica from a veterinary perspective and on therapeutics for veterinary conditions at an advanced level. The course is taken over 12 months at your own pace.
The focus of these modules is on the Materia Medica from a veterinary perspective and on therapeutics for veterinary conditions at an advanced level. Western herbal medicine for complaints of the major body systems is covered through examination of both traditional and evidence-based Materia Medica. The Materia Medica covers the actions, indications, constituents and contraindications of herbs and enables the student to develop a working comprehension of the herbs in relation to the different body systems and to become both competent and confident in the use of these herbs for a wide variety of disease states. A minimum of 100 herbs is covered during these modules.

courses.title: Protecting Kittens from Feline Panleukopenia: Essential Strategies for Animal Shelters and Rescues (On Demand)
courses.description: Animal shelter and rescue agencies across the country often struggle to protects cats and in particular kittens from the infectious diseases that tend to rise as 'kitten season' surges each year. This webinar focuses on safeguarding cats of all ages from feline panleukopenia (sometimes also called feline distemper or FPV), a highly contagious and potentially fatal viral disease. Veterinary experts will discuss disease recognition in individuals and within a shelter population, effective prevention methods, and best practices for managing outbreaks in shelter environments and foster homes.

courses.title: Clinical Utility of Cardiac Biomarkers
courses.description: This webinar will help the general practitioner incorporate cardiac biomarkers into their practice and review applicable literature regarding these tests. Dr. Derek Hanes will begin with a brief review of the cardiac biomarkers available for testing and their physiologic properties to best understand under what conditions these markers may become elevated. This will be followed by a review of current literature, with particular emphasis on how evidence-based medicine can help guide when cardiac biomarkers can be helpful. Dr. Hanes will also review additional disease processes that can affect biomarkers, potentially requiring additional diagnostics. Viewers will leave with a better understanding of when cardiac biomarkers can be helpful in both respiratory and cardiac patients and how to determine when and what additional diagnostics and follow-up are appropriate if abnormal results are obtained.

courses.title: Regional Anesthetic Blocks
courses.description: This course covers regional anesthetic dental blocks in dogs and cats, including when to use each block and dosage of anesthetic. It will also cover potential complications and how to avoid them.

courses.title: AHNTI US 2026 (Kisaco Research)
courses.description:
AHNTI US Boston 2026 is a three-day commercial meeting for the animal health value chain, running 26-28 October in Boston. It is not a clinical conference, a trade show, or a policy forum. It is a commercial decision-making environment where capital is allocated, partnerships are formed, pipeline decisions are made, and route-to-market questions are answered.
The event brings together 500+ senior delegates from across the full animal health ecosystem: biopharma, diagnostics, nutrition, technology, distribution, agtech, investors, and - for the first time in 2026 - veterinary practice groups at scale.
AHNTI US 2026 (Boston) is being redesigned as a commercial, value-chain-led meeting for animal health - connecting discovery, development, and delivery through the lens that matters most to sponsors: how innovation turns into scalable revenue in the US market.

courses.title: Revive and Refresh Your TCM Skills; Maximize Your Results
courses.description:
Chinese medicine can be an overwhelming undertaking, seemingly requiring you to sift through hundreds of formulas, thousand of herbs, and thousands of pages of books and binders every time you come to treat a patient. Chinese medicine often seems just too time intensive to be practical, especially in a busy modern practice setting.
This course gives practical solutions to speed up the process, with skills and approaches that are immediately useful and relevant to your practice via invigorating and interactive case-based lectures. It shows how to correlate a patient's history with their biomedical complaints including examination of pulse, tongue and active points, giving a comprehensive understanding of what is going on.
This allows you to immediately choose the treatment most likely to be effective. You'll then learn how to implement those treatments with maximum safety and efficacy, so that you're finally able to rsolve chronic problems for good. You will finally know how to be reassured you know exactly what you're doing when you get back to the clinic.

courses.title: Penn Vet Working Dog Practitioner Program: Introduction to Scent Detection Dogs
courses.description: This is an introduction to the veterinary relationship with handlers and their working dogs, specifically the scent detection canine. In this module you will learn the history of explosive detection, narcotics detection and medical detection specifically with a focus on cancer detection. You will become familiar with the language used to describe the dogs and their training. This section will provide an overview of olfactory function and factors that might interfere with canine performance. You will come to recognize the differences between a veterinary examination of a working dog compared to a pet dog and develop strategies for low stress handling that can be applied to all dogs. You will explore the working environment and potential hazards that these dogs face in their careers, enabling you to work with the handlers to develop preventive care plans and first aid responses.

courses.title: Is That Old Dog Frail? Perspectives from the Dog Aging Project

courses.provider: AMERICAN INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL LASER APPLICATIONS
courses.title: INTRODUCTION TO LASER THERAPY IN THE EQUINE ATHLETE (554-44861)
courses.description:
This course provides access to the complete Equine Therapy Certification Course. This course outlines the biological effects of medical lasers for treating common conditions in horses. It covers the effects of medical lasers in the promotion of analgesia, acceleration of wound healing, and reduction of inflammation.
There are demonstrations for treating a variety of disorders concerning the head (oral cavity & ear), cervical region, shoulder, carpals, metacarpals, fetlock, hoof, back, hip stifle, hock, and others.
Includes the following 3 courses:
1. Medical Laser Safety
2. The Science Behind Medical Lasers
3. Laser Therapy Principles for the Equine Athlete

courses.provider: AMERICAN INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL LASER APPLICATIONS
courses.title: RAISING THE STANDARD OF VETERINARY CARE: A MULTI-MODAL APPROACH TO MANAGING PAIN - ON DEMAND (554-44859)
courses.description: This program features the most current information available on this important facet of patient care presented not only via lectures but in an interactive hands-on curriculum. Our faculty will provide you with an interactive and engaged learning format that includes daily practice applications & hands-on techniques.

courses.title: Veterinary Care in Shelters: Who Can Legally Do What?
courses.description: In this course, you will learn how to fully leverage the veterinary care capabilities of your entire team, not just your designated medical staff, including front office staff, field officers, kennel attendants, volunteers, and fosters. Bruce Wagman, Lead Counsel for San Francisco SPCAs Shelter Policy and Legal Services, will review which shelter tasks team members can perform, from intake related care and running diagnostics to providing treatment, surgery, euthanasia, public veterinary services, and emergency care. After this course, you will be ready to maximize options for providing veterinary care while adhering to the law and practice act requirements.

courses.title: The Science Behind SINE Class Drugs: Novel Small Molecules for Oncology (On Demand)
courses.description: Selective inhibition of nuclear export (SINE) class drugs are small molecules recently introduced to both human and veterinary oncology. This course will explore the mechanism of action, demonstrated in vitro effects, and clinical indications of this novel class of drugs. We will also explore how SINE class drugs introduce a new way to think about managing cancer and how they may be integrated into the treatment of several neoplastic diseases.

courses.title: Veterinary Nutrition Ambassador Program
courses.description: The Veterinary Nutrition Ambassador Program is a multi-level series of highly-focused courses designed to advance the global understanding of the vital role nutrition plays in management of many diseases as well as maintenance of overall health. The major emphasis of this course is to instruct participants in the practical aspects of nutrition. Nutritional aspects of the mechanisms of health and disease are taught primarily at the individual and population level and includes some molecular and cellular level aspects. The program is designed for all veterinary audiences, to support their ability to properly nourish dogs and cats in their care. The use of clinically relevant information in this video-based series facilitates practical application of learning as the participant progresses through the levels in sequence.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: ACVIM Forum 2026 On Demand
courses.description: The ACVIM Forum is a veterinary healthcare event with thousands of attendees from around the world. The ACVIM Forum consistently boasts a diverse range of the best and brightest speakers, engaging sessions, medical discoveries and innovative exhibitors to keep veterinary practitioners current with the latest trends in veterinary internal medicine, and provides practical information that can be used by specialists, residents, veterinarians and technicians in daily practice. Selected sessions will be available pre-recorded and/or content captured for access on-demand.

courses.title: Veterinary Natural Nutrition
courses.description:
This course covers the principles of small animal nutrition including prepared petfoods, alternative feeding approaches and home made diets.
The course provides the knowledge and skills to advise on the advantages and disadvantages of each, as well as being able to assess in a broad way a food or diet from a nutritional standpoint.
Veterinary Natural Animal Nutrition fills in the gap of knowledge from mainstream nutrition philosophy which focuses on prepared pet foods. A balanced viewpoint is taken, along with an evidence based approach in the interests of animal health and wellbeing. Note that individual contributor's opinions do not necessarily reflect those of CIVT.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Practical Management of the Older Athlete
courses.description: Over the past twenty years the number of older horses has increased exponentially as a result of significant advances in equine medicine and horses having increasingly become companion animals. This has led to a plethora of new medical and husbandry challenges for veterinarians dealing with an aging equine population. Aimed at equine practitioners, the webinar series covers the most important areas affecting older horses, such as weight-loss, dental challenges, Cushings, OA, laminitis, shoeing techniques, cardiopulmonary conditions, neoplasia and how to keep the senior sports horse competing etc.

courses.title: Backyard Poultry Medicine and Surgery (EXOT334)
courses.description: Most of us in clinical practice have realized by now that the backyard chicken is increasingly becoming a part of both our clients' lives and ours, as clinicians. But when you look back at your university training, you also realize that learning about commercial poultry and disease management doesn't prepare you for the reality of companion chicken practice, where the value of the patient cannot be measured in just dollars. This course will give you more in-depth knowledge on the medicine and surgery of backyard poultry than you have had to date, giving you the confidence to walk into your examination room, comfortable in your knowledge and abilities to offer the standard of care you believe in.

courses.title: Webinar Series - An Introduction to Advanced Surgical Dental Extraction Techniques (incl. MITR, MTE & Segmentation)
courses.description: Oral extraction techniques have been shown to cause much fewer post-interventional complications in horses compared to surgical extraction techniques. Performing oral dental extractions should however not be taken lightly as complications like dental fractures, retained root tips, collateral damage etc. can easily occur and require in-depth anatomical knowledge, good technical skills and clinical versatility to resolve. This course is aimed at practitioners with a good working knowledge in equine dentistry who want to learn about various oral dental extraction techniques, how to apply them clinically and managing arising complications.

courses.provider: CARE: COMPANIONS AND ANIMALS FOR REFORM AND EQUITY
courses.title: VetREDI: Veterinary Professionals: Racial Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion, Bronze Certification
courses.description: Animal Welfare Expertise collaborates with Veterinary Expertise to deeply evaluate the role of Racial Equity in the professions and how they are deeply linked. By focusing on the awareness of self and culture within our veterinary spaces, all veterinary team members (veterinarians, veterinary technicians and assistants, practice managers, client coordinators, instructors, shelters, etc.) can have critical roles to play in the improvement of access to care through collaboration understanding the marginalization we place on each other and clients/community members without intentional action. We review the implicit biases and privileges we each have and break down some common areas of opportunity while supporting the continued self-awareness journey. This is done in a safe and supportive way, while giving opportunities for further discovery and actual opportunities for change within our individual environments.

courses.title: Hypercalcemia in Cats & Dogs (DRIP152)
courses.description: This course will explore hypercalcemia, a common endocrinopathy in canine and feline medicine. Participants will review real-life case examples to discuss history and clinical presentation, as well as accurate diagnosis and appropriate treatment.

courses.title: Clinical Case Challenge
courses.description: This online module presents the learner with a real veterinary case to simulate optimum management of a patient with Cushing's syndrome. We present the case workflow in the form of quiz questions and the learner is required to make decisions based on the patient's rest results and clinical response. Depending on the learner's decisions throughout the course, they will be presented with 10 to 12 questions to ultimately arrive at a long-term treatment plan for the patients. At the end, Dr. Bruyette describes how he handled the case and provides expert perspective on diagnosing treating, and managing Cushing's syndrome.

courses.title: Autologous Platelet Concentrate and Canine Joint Injections
courses.description: This lecture will help practitioners perform a series of joint injections for the six main diarthrodial joints in the dog.

courses.title: 2024 AHVMA Annual Conference Virtual Extension
courses.description: American Holistic Veterinary Medical Association Annual Conference. This is a face-to-face seminar/lecture and workshop/lab delivery. Our main objective is to increase knowledge and skills of CAVM techniques, topics and procedures.

courses.title: Stitch Happens: How You Can Be a Hero with Emergency Surgery
courses.description: Ready to enhance your skills in both a general practice and emergency surgery setting? Join Dr. Philippa Pavia in this dynamic webinar tailored specifically for emergency veterinarians and general practitioners who are not just performing surgery but also on the first line of defense in triage and initial evaluations. Dr. Pavia will delve into critical aspects of emergency surgery across various body systems, including the thorax, peritoneum, and GI tract. Attendees will get practical tips and techniques to boost their confidence when it comes to diagnosing and managing emergency cases, gaining a better understanding of when to take immediate action, when to wait, and when to consult or refer to a specialist. In addition, attendees will acquire valuable insights into how to effectively communicate with clients and with the veterinary team, which are crucial for successful outcomes in emergency situations.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: 2024 Advanced Equine Neurology On Demand
courses.description:
Taught by world renowned experts in equine neurology, this intensive course will cover current approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of equine neurologic disease.
Lectures will focus on an in-depth review of the neurologic exam, electrodiagnostics, advanced imaging of the brain and cervical spine and diseases including cervical vertebral stenotic myelopathy, equine degenerative myelopathy, neuroborreliosis, seizure disorders, sleep disorders, and equine protozoal myeloencephalopathy

courses.title: Behavioral and Convenience Euthanasia (Recording)
courses.description: Behavioral and convenience euthanasia requests are known to cause moral stress in veterinarians. They are complicated situations that arise from a variety of factors, which veterinary teams must consider before proceeding with euthanasia. This session looks at the types of euthanasia, reviews decision-making tools, shows how to build policies into a euthanasia manual, and gives instruction on how to more safely approach aggression cases.

courses.provider: CANADIAN ANIMAL SHELTER AND COMMUNITY MEDICINE ASSOCIATION
courses.title: Humane Canada Track: Shelter and Community Medicine
courses.description:
As shelters navigate through rising veterinary costs and staffing shortages their role as the first line of support for animals awaiting adoption has never been more vital. But what if we could prevent some of these animals from ever needing to enter the shelter system in the first place?
Join us for a series of deep dive sessions exploring access to care. We'll examine how shelter teams, shelter veterinarians, and local veterinarians can help animals before they enter the shelter, while they're under shelter care, and after they've been adopted.
In the next days, we will provide an educational track focused on advancing the well-being and welfare of shelter animals through innovative approaches to preventive care, thoughtful medical case management, in-house procedures, enhanced capacity for care, and shelter medicine prevention.
Join us to explore real-world strategies and forward-thinking programs that help shelters meet the complex medical needs of animals in their care while paving the way for healthier, happier outcomes for shelter animals.

courses.title: Navicular Syndrome and the Clinical Use of Bisphoshonates in Equine Practice
courses.description: Participants will learn about the mechanism of action of bisphosphonates in both human and equine medicine. They will also review how bone remodeling affects normal horses and those with bone disease. Navicular disease, one of the most common causes of forelimb lameness in the horse, will be discussed in depth, including the causes, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. Finally, a clinical field study showing the efficacy of a bisphosphonate (clodronate) in treating navicular disease will be discussed.

courses.provider: WEST INDIES VETERINARY CONFERENCE BY ROSS UNIVERSITY SCHOOL OF VETERINARY MEDICI
courses.title: West Indies Veterinary Conference 2026
courses.description: The West Indies Veterinary Conference will include medical and non-medical interactive programming focusing on small animal and large animal veterinary care as well as practice management. Topics to include dentistry, small and large dermatology, emergency and critical care, equine sports medicine, gastrointestinal disease, small and large animal microbiology, point of care ultrasound, urgent care, cardiology, and practice management.

courses.title: To re-cut or not to re-cut: Medical and surgical management of spay/neuter complications
courses.description: The most common intra-op and post-op spay/neuter complications will be presented and discussed along with recommended spectrum-of-care management plans. This program is about proactive approaches to manage and minimize complications and how best to prepare your clinic for when they do happen.

courses.title: Maddie's Insights - Behavioral Euthanasia: Just the Facts! (ON DEMAND)
courses.description: Behavioral euthanasia is a sensitive topic, with a wide variety of personal thoughts and emotions. But what do we actually know about it? How often does it happen, and why? Do we have data we can use to make decisions? Where can we turn for information? This talk will walk you through the existing (and pending!) research on behavioral euthanasia to help us separate fact from fiction.

courses.title: Introduction to Canine Musculoskeletal Ultrasound
courses.description:
The participant will be actively engaged in study of canine diagnostic musculoskeletal
ultrasound concepts and techniques, including intense instruction on scanning for
relevant anatomy. Current veterinary and peer reviewed literature on diagnostic musculoskeletal
ultrasound, elastography, and regenerative medicine as treatment for tendinopathies
is incorporated into presentation. Peer-reviewed literature on the subject of diagnostic
musculoskeletal ultrasound is provided upon request of the participant.
Ultrasound physics, ultrasound artifacts, scanning principles, landmark sites and anatomy will be reviewed and explained throughout the region presentations. Relevant scanning principles for these areas will be addressed. Best practices are reviewed. Participants will learn techniques in relevant scanning musculoskeletal anatomy through pre-recorded online-canine diagnostic ultrasound of the shoulder, elbow, carpus, hip, stifle, tarsus, and iliopsoas areas. Instructor and participant will work through a variety of techniques for obtaining the most clinically accurate and precise ultrasound images needed for definitive and superior diagnosis of canine musculoskeletal injuries through course quizzes, assignments, and monthly live, interactive discussion of techniques. Participant will engage the application of musculoskeletal ultrasound as a diagnostic tool to evaluate the injury and healing of sports-related canine conditions as a guide for canine rehabilitation. Diagnosing, treatment and rehabilitation of common conditions (shoulder tendinopathies, carpal and tarsal soft tissue injuries, Achilles tendon injuries, stifle injuries, and iliopsoas tendon strains and region pathology), is also included in each anatomical module. The importance of re-scanning throughout the healing period will also be addressed, as well how ultrasound can be used frequently in patient treatment plans to ensure each stage of the physical rehabilitation process is tailored to the individual

courses.title: The Difference a Measure Makes: Using Science to Decipher Your Animal's Behavior CDPS117
courses.description: This course covers the science behind body language, timing and treat delivery to create an optimal learning environment for the animals in our care. You will learn how adjusting your technique can impact animal training.

courses.title: Myth 1: Cleaning Surgical Instruments and Power Tools
courses.description: Myth 1: Cleaning Surgical Instruments and Power Tools is designed to provide necessary information to decrease infection through detailed, correct cleaning of immersible devices. The course outlines the appropriate chemicals to use and the reprocessing methods for the general surgery instruments, burs, orthopedic instruments, and lumens.

courses.title: Hill's Global Symposium 2025: Strong Science. Long Lives (live broadcast)
courses.description:
An insightful online gathering of veterinary professionals as we discover a deeper understanding of the ageing process and support of healthy ageing for dogs and cats in your care. Join online to learn about new research on ageing topics including:
* Innovations for treating Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome
* Evolving strategies for Osteoarthritis Pain Management
* Addressing comorbidities in cats and dogs
* Why and how hospice is not sad

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY INTERNAL MEDICINE
courses.title: ACVIM Hope vs. Hype in Veterinary Oncology Diagnostics On Demand
courses.description: This on-demand course will provide an intensive, topics-based review of basic science topics pertinent to the clinical practice of veterinary oncology. The diverse and daily expanding field of specialized oncology diagnostics available for dogs and cats makes remaining current on the latest advances challenging. Keeping up-to-date on the latest data is important for presenting case management options to clients along with realistic expectations. In this day-long virtual course, panelists will discuss the available data (or, sometimes, lack thereof) for the somewhat more controversial aspects of veterinary oncology diagnostics, including: Personalized medicine, chemosensitivity assays, liquid biopsy possibilities, and diagnostic/prognostic panels. The potential opportunities and challenges of clinical integration of these diagnostics will be discussed.

courses.title: Acute Abdomen (DRIP112)
courses.description: This course will take you through the fundamentals of the acute abdomen patient. The physiological process of acute abdomen will be discussed along with the diagnostic approach and treatment of the acute abdomen patient.

courses.title: Behavior in Everyday Practice: Step by Step of Managing Behavior Cases in Your Practice Anytime
courses.description: Behavior problems are common in veterinary patients. How to treat them can be a mystery. Many of these cases can be diagnosed and managed in general practice. In this series, you will learn how to recognize common behavior problems in canine and feline patients, collect and analyze a patient's behavioral history, diagnose, and treat behavior problems in a general practice setting.

courses.title: Integrative Veterinary Neurology
courses.description: Neurology may seem complicated, but it doesn't have to be that way. One of the most important goals of this class is to remove the fear from neurology, and help you enjoy treating your small animal neurological patients. Refresh your training and practice fear-free neurology. This course will give you confidence and competence with the clinical neurological exam and help you hone down on the location of the problem.

courses.title: MMPC Learniverse - The Four Rights Courses
courses.description:
With the Maddie's Million Pet Challenge, the Five Key Initiatives of the Million Cat Challenge have expanded to include other species at risk in shelters and evolved into the Four Rights. Within the Four Rights, every element works in concert to support one another. Animals and people are treated as individuals, empowering shelter staff to make the best decisions for everyone. Community safety net services are in place and flourishing. Humane care within the shelter is provided, with appropriate outcomes for the animals that do come in, allowing shelters to deliver the Right Care, in the Right Place, at the Right Time, to the Right Outcome.
As part of the Maddie's Million Pet Challenge Learniverse program, subject matter experts from the UC Davis Koret Shelter Medicine Program will discuss guiding principles that animal welfare professionals can use to make decisions, train their staff and engage the public.

courses.title: Essentials of Canine Endocrinology By Dr. Yi Cui DVM, ECVIM-CA
courses.description:
Course Format
A six-week, self-paced online program offering approximately 12 hours of structured video lectures, downloadable notes, endocrine-specific protocols, and interactive quizzes. Learners have 12 weeks of access and may complete modules at their own pace.
Target Audience
Veterinarians and final-year veterinary students seeking to build confidence and clinical competence in the diagnosis and management of common canine endocrine disorders, particularly those working in general practice.
Course Overview
Endocrine diseases are among the most common and challenging chronic conditions encountered in small-animal practice. Essentials of Canine Endocrinology provides a structured, practical, and evidence-based approach to diagnosing, treating, and monitoring canine endocrine disorders. The course focuses on real-world clinical decision-making, helping veterinarians move beyond algorithms to understand the why behind diagnostic choices and treatment adjustments. Through case-based teaching and step-by-step frameworks, participants learn to confidently manage long-term endocrine patients while avoiding common pitfalls.
Learning Objectives:
By the end of this course, participants will be able to:
Diagnose canine diabetes mellitus using appropriate clinical assessment and laboratory testing.
Develop safe and effective insulin treatment plans, including insulin selection, dosing, handling, and dietary considerations.
Interpret glucose curves, fructosamine levels, and clinical response to troubleshoot poor diabetic control and prevent hypoglycaemia.
Diagnose and manage canine hyperadrenocorticism, including selection and interpretation of screening and confirmatory tests and formulation of monitoring protocols.
Accurately diagnose canine hypothyroidism, interpret thyroid testing in context, and implement appropriate levothyroxine therapy and follow-up.
Apply structured protocols and case-based reasoning to manage endocrine patients in general practice settings.

courses.provider: SALLY SAID SO PROFESSIONAL DOG TRAINING
courses.title: Sally Said So, To The Rescue
courses.description: This course covers everything about rescues. Statistics on why they are there and why they are returned, the importance of proper environmental management and decompression time. Behind the scenes of rescues good and bad, in depth behavior and shaping from environmental stressors that created the behaviors and hope to rehabilitate them in to an amazing family pet.

courses.title: Veterinary Dermatology Lecture
courses.description: Small Animal Dermatology Update Lecture

courses.title: Puppy Socialization or Infectious Disease Prevention: Can't We Have Both?
courses.description: The first 12 weeks of a puppy's life are prime time for socialization. Failure to adequately socialize puppies during this time is arguably the most common reason for the development of major, often life-threatening behavioral concerns in adult dogs. Many serious problems can be prevented if appropriate care is given during these early, sensitive weeks of a puppy's life. One major challenge to adequate socialization is a puppy's simultaneous vulnerability to infectious diseases. Because maternal antibodies wane and immune systems lag in their full response to immunization, many professionals in the veterinary community advise against early contact with dogs and environments outside the safety of home. So how can veterinarians navigate these competing risks while promoting overall behavioral and physical health? This webinar will review key concepts in puppy socialization and infectious disease prevention, providing a practical approach to safe and effective socialization practices.

courses.title: Tales from the Crit: Interactive Hematology Case Studies with the Laboratory Retrievers (Module 2)
courses.description: The Laboratory Retrievers -Purdue continuing education (CE) program is an online learning experience for veterinary professionals, created by the Laboratory Retrievers LLC and Purdue University College of Veterinary Medicine. These highly interactive, case-based modules help veterinarians and technicians confidently interpret CBC data, analyze cytograms and recognize key blood film cell morphology in minutes.

courses.title: DONT MAKE IT WORSE: HANDLING DIFFICULT DOGS IN THE CLINIC (Anytime)
courses.description: Behavioral concerns in dog patients occur on a regular basis in the veterinary clinic. Many dogs present as fearful in the clinic and that fear may trigger aggressive behavior during veterinary exams. There is a push in recent years for veterinary professions to learn more about the emotional component to behavior and to consider the emotional wellbeing of their patients through safe, humane handling practices that reduce fear and improve the dog's behavioral response to veterinary exams.

courses.title: THE RITES OF PASSAGE WITH ANTIMICROBIAL STEWARDSHIP (1500-43316)
courses.description:
This online course will provide a concise lecture on the importance of antimicrobial stewardship. This course centers on a novel acronym for good stewardship of antibiotic prescription, the VETAHEAD's RITES of passage. Clinical examples of the use of RITES of passage will be discussed with emphasis in zoological companion animals.
Additionally, the course will cover aspects of the importance of antibiotic stewardship, the dangers of antimicrobial resistance, will properly define the veterinary patient client relationship, discuss the importance of pursuing diagnostics prior to the prescription of antibiotics, following up, tracking and monitoring the health outcomes post antibiotic therapy. Prevention strategies and proper husbandry techniques, the importance of avoiding excessive use of antibiotics and excessive contamination of the environment, and the importance of basing antibiotic use and prescription on evidence-based medicine and proven scientific methodologies will also be covered during the course.
This course is aimed at veterinarians and veterinary paraprofessionals (technician, assistant, nurse) as well as students with a keen interest in preventing antimicrobial resistance.

courses.title: Join the flock: Incorporating Chickens into your practice
courses.description: This course covers content on a wide array of medicine, surgery, commonly performed techniques and procedures in chickens, including aspects of how to set up a practice, mobile practice, egg abnormalities, common breeds, anatomy, husbandry, handling, preventative medicine, clinical techniques, diagnostic imaging, sedation, common diseases, diagnostic imaging, therapeutics, anesthesia, medicine and surgery, geriatric care, necropsy, reportable diseases, prohibited drugs, extra-label use of drugs and withdrawal times, and legislation.

courses.provider: NEW MEXICO HUMANE CONFERENCE | ANIMAL HUMANE NEW MEXICO
courses.title: New Mexico Humane Conference
courses.description:
The New Mexico Humane Conference is a premier regional gathering dedicated to advancing the care, protection, and well-being of animals through education, collaboration, and innovation. Hosted annually in Albuquerque, NM, the conference brings together professionals and advocates from across the fields of animal welfare, veterinary medicine, public health, social work, and municipal services.
The 2025 conference will offer a multi-disciplinary slate of sessions designed to deepen participants' understanding of animal health, shelter medicine, humane care standards, and the interconnected challenges faced by people and pets. Conference content is developed to reflect emerging trends, evidence-based practices, and real-world scenarios encountered in both clinical and community-based animal care settings.
Topics include, but are not limited to:
-Shelter medicine best practices and innovations
-Strategies for addressing animal hoarding and cruelty investigations
-Public health impacts of companion animal care and community outreach
-Behavioral health for companion animals in shelters and foster homes
-Managing infectious disease outbreaks in shelter environments
-Emergency and disaster response involving animals
-Cultural competence and access to veterinary care
-Interdisciplinary collaborations that strengthen human-animal support systems
Veterinary professionals will benefit from sessions that provide practical, actionable guidance for improving animal outcomes, understanding complex medical and behavioral conditions, and applying trauma-informed, equity-driven approaches in their work. Several sessions are taught by veterinarians, behaviorists, legal experts, and sheltering leaders who bring case studies, data, and field experience to the forefront of learning.
The conference is appropriate for licensed veterinarians, veterinary technicians, shelter medical staff, animal control officers, nonprofit leaders, and students preparing for careers in animal health or shelt

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Pruritic Dogs
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the most common causes of pruritus leading to skin problems in dogs, including disease signs, assessment, related key nutritional factors (KNFs), and nutritional management strategies related to dermatological issues. The course covers adverse food reactions and atopy.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Management of Life-threatening Cardiac Emergencies
courses.description: This lecture will cover in detail common, cardiac life-threatening emergencies in regard to recognizing them, properly diagnosing them and managing/treatment

courses.title: Bacteriuria in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: What is the clinical significance of bacteriuria in veterinary patients? How are appropriate antimicrobials selected for urinary tract infections (UTI). Protocols to classify UTIs aid in diagnosis and treatment. This course looks at the interpretation of culture and susceptibility along with antimicrobial selection. It also reviews follow-up for UTI patients. It is important for all medical members of a veterinary practice to be familiar with the UTI concepts examined in this course, either as an aid to diagnosis and treatment or to provide better nursing care and support.

courses.title: Anesthesia and pain management in practice
