courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian with practical information on the current thoughts on anesthesia along with acute and chronic pain management in their practice. The combination of two Anesthesiologist/pain management specialists will provide a unique approach to the patient management. Dr's Grubb and Robertson will discuss their approach to management of patients requiring anesthesia along with their assessment and management of pain in practice today. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of anesthesia and pain management available for their patients.

courses.title: General Practitioner Certificate in Small Animal Surgery GPCert(SAS)
courses.description: The General Practitioner Certificate in Small Animal Surgery has been developed to enable veterinary surgeons across the world to access world-class teaching materials. Developed by a global team of surgical specialists, this comprehensive two-year program covers both soft tissue and orthopedic/spinal surgeries.

courses.title: Nutrition Poo-pourri: An Intro to Gastrointestinal Diets
courses.description: This lecture is intended to cover the various types of commercial diets available for veterinarians to choose from when managing cases of gastrointestinal disease. We will discuss the 4 main categories of gastrointestinal diets, as well as a few mock cases to help with identifying clinical applications to help veterinarians better cater dietary therapy to improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: Better Living Through Chemistry: Exploring the use of psychopharmacy in the treatment of canine behavior problems
courses.description: We will cover the use of psychopharmacology in the treatment of canine behavior problems.

courses.title: Becoming a Secure Base: Using science to improve human-animal bonds and welfare
courses.description: Many people feel that they have shared a strong bond with a dog, and there is growing scientific evidence that these dogs also form strong bonds with their humans. However, science also tells us that not all bonds are created equal. The kind and quality of attachment relationship shared can influence dog behavior and welfare outcomes. In this talk, Dr. Monique Udell will provide an overview of attachment theory, including what it means to be a Secure Base, and how this knowledge can be applied to better understand and improve dog-human relationships and the relationships shared between humans and other animals.

courses.title: TFAST Point of Care Ultrasound Online Course
courses.description: The TFAST Course is a self-paced recorded online course that includes 8 modules covering: TFAST point of ultrasound examination overview, image acquisition, TFAST right and left echocardiographic views, diagnosis of pericardial effusion, diagnosis of pleural effusion, diagnosis of pneumothorax, and many case-based applications to demonstrate how TFAST can positively impact patient care and optimize case management.

courses.title: CBD IN CLINICAL PRACTICE: WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW (1644-43172)
courses.description: Many veterinarians are being asked about CBD by their clients. Unfortunately, there has been little guidance provided for veterinarians regarding CBD safety or efficacy. Dr. Terry Fossum will walk you through the science of CBD, as well as the CBD regulatory environment for pets. Do you want to feel comfortable recommending CBD to your clients? Are you unsure which CBD brands carry high quality products? Are you concerned about adverse events? If you want to know the answers to these questions, this webinar is for you. Dr. Terry Fossum has been a thought leader in veterinary medicine for the past 30 years and she is forging the path for CBD to become mainstream.

courses.title: The Power of Yes - Removing Barriers to Adoption at Animal Shelters
courses.description: While 70% of US households have a pet, only a fraction of those animals are adopted from animal shelters. This course looks at barriers that typically push potential adopters away from animal shelters and towards other options. In addition to examining adoption barriers and the misconceptions that help them persist, we look at strategies that can lower these hurdles, help more animals reach a live outcome and a happy life, and help animal shelters embrace and welcome all members of their community.

courses.title: SASHA - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE DOG WITH STAGE B2 MYXOMATOUS MITRAL VALVE DEGENERATION (MMVD) (930-35081)
courses.description: SASHA - DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION OF THE DOG WITH STAGE B2 MYXOMATOUS MITRAL VALVE DEGENERATION (MMVD) (930-35081) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.provider: AMERICAN VETERINARY SOCIETY OF ANIMAL BEHAVIOR
courses.title: The Clinical Animal Behavioral Conference 2025
courses.description: The Clinical Animal Behavior Conference is a 2.5-day intensive conference focusing on veterinary behavioral medicine. The theme of this year's conference is "Expanding Your Behavioral Toolkit". Throughout the conference, attendees will learn the science behind various behavioral problems in companion animals and how to recognize, diagnose, and manage these problems. They will also learn strategies to implement change and reach financial success in the veterinary practice. Presentations include topics such as: Animal behavioral analysis and interventions; Understanding the role of antecedents in behavior; Recognition and management of feline elimination problems; Non-elimination behavioral problems in felines; Evidence-based handling of felines; Behavioral prevention for canine patients; Feline psychopharmacology; Cooperative veterinary care; How to implement change in veterinary practices; Business aspects of financial success while meeting patients' needs and more.

courses.title: The first 24 hours
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to present the most current information on the diagnosis and treatment of many emergencies that you are commonly asked to manage in your patients. The main emphasis of the seminars will be to give you practical information that you can readily utilize in your practice. Dr. Grubb will provide an update on anesthesia and pain management of the emergency patient and Dr. Johnson will present a practical discussion on how he manages his patients presented with an urgent or emergency problem. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: SONOGRAPHIC APPROACH TO THE SHUNT HUNT Part 1 & 2
courses.description: Detection of portosystemic shunts and the negative shunt hunt, utilizing the SDEP abdominal scanning protocol; exhaustive review of EHPSS and IHPSS including clinical approaches, medical and surgical management in this 2-part series.

courses.provider: CENTER FOR FOOD SECURITY AND PUBLIC HEALTH COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE IOWA S
courses.title: Biosecurity in Livestock and Poultry Production: Advanced
courses.description: Veterinary personnel must be trained in biosecurity to protect the health of U.S. livestock and poultry. This six-hour course provides a comprehensive biosecurity education that is not affiliated with a particular species, industry, or program.

courses.title: Abdominal Ultrasound: Beyond the Basics
courses.description:
This two-day, clinically focused, hands-on course is designed for practicing veterinarians seeking to advance their ultrasound imaging skills for abdominal diagnostics in general practice settings.
The goal is to deliver a hands-on, practical learning experience focused on real-world applications, enhancing diagnostic accuracy and patient care. With over eight hours of laboratory sessions using live dogs and cats, this course will teach participants how to operate ultrasound machines, optimize image quality, and perform comprehensive abdominal ultrasound examinations. Attendees will gain a deep understanding of normal abdominal anatomy and learn the techniques needed to consistently obtain diagnostic images.
We are proud to partner with Samsung, who will be providing all ultrasound machines for the event and subsidizing the course.
This course is ideal for veterinarians ready to integrate ultrasound more fully into their diagnostic toolset and improve real-time decision-making for their patients.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Advanced Mare Reproduction - Pregnancy Related Problems
courses.description:
As part of our Lecture Series on Advanced Mare Reproduction Drs. Angus McKinnon, Joan Carrick, Jonathan Pycock & Tom Stout are covering the following topics:
Preventing early pregnancy failure in natural and assisted breeding
Placentitis - thinking beyond CUPT
Pre-Partum Reproductive Emergencies
Approach to Dystocia in the Field
Examining the Barren Mare (including use of ultrasonography in the subfertile mare)
Post-Partum Reproductive Emergencies (incl. Retained Fetal Membranes)

courses.title: 101 DENTAL WET LAV (1320-36915)
courses.description: Registrants will have at least 4 hours hands-on practice extracting dog and /or cat teeth. Registrants will also receive at least three hours of lecture on dental anatomy, dental radiography, how to stay out of trouble with extractions and what do with what you see

courses.title: Beyond Fatigue: Wellbeing for the Long Haul
courses.description:
Program Description
A veterinary hospital can be a stressful environment to work in. Combine that with the incredible level of dedication and passion veterinary staff bring to their jobs, and its not difficult to understand why burnout and compassion fatigue are prolific in veterinary medicine. Discover ways to overcome or prevent burnout and compassion fatigue.
Program Agenda
What stresses you out?
- Name it to tame it
When have you prioritized your wellbeing?
- Who at your practice does it well? What can you learn from them?
How is wellbeing achieved?
- It is not a one time event. It takes work and we will help you identify how you can find the time
Finding happiness
- Prioritizing the things that you enjoy doing
- What makes you come alive at work?
Tools to identify a path forward
- Mood journal
- Choosing positivity
- Gratitude exercise
How do you maintain your wellbeing?
Finding time for wellbeing
- The moments are there - see them and take advantage
Inspiring a culture of wellbeing
- What you can do to normalize prioritizing wellbeing at your clinic?
How cost of care and wellbeing are connected
Wellbeing - you have got this
- Veterinary medicine needs you
Learning Objectives
- Recognize opportunities to improve or maintain personal and team wellbeing
- Identify ways to discuss wellbeing with your team
- Identify several actionable steps to improve the wellbeing of yourself and your team

courses.title: From Scan to Stride: The Future of Pet Mobility is Here with 3D Technology
courses.description:
Discover how cutting edge technology is transforming mobility solutions for pets who need extra support. In this webinar, Lydia Mindek of 3DPets and renowned veterinarian Dr. Andrea Looney will share their innovative process for creating custom mobility devices including orthotics, prosthetics, and carts tailored to each pets unique needs.
You will see how advanced 3D scanning and printing technology enables the creation of devices that enhance the lives of pets facing injuries, congenital conditions, or other mobility challenges. Hear inspiring success stories, gain insight into the design and production process, and learn how these devices help pets achieve long-term mobility and a better quality of life.

courses.title: Equine Regenerative Therapy---Autologous Blood Products
courses.description: The presenter reviews equine regenerative therapy. Focus areas include basic principles of regenerative medicine, FDA regulations, and types of autologous blood products. The types of medical devices necessary for processing autologous blood products including centrifugation, filtration, and incubation are all discussed. Additionally a meta-analysis of current research with regards to platelet rich plasma (PRP), autologous conditioned serum (ACS), autologous protein solutions (APS), and alpha 2 macroglobulin will be analyzed.

courses.title: Feline Hypotension (DRIP116)
courses.description: This course will cover the physiology of hypotension in the feline patient, including the diagnostic approach and treatment.

courses.title: KYON Total Hip Replacement Prelearning Online Courses
courses.description: KYON: Total Hip Replacement Prelearning Online Course is designed to provide surgeons with a deeper understanding of the KYON THR hip system and procedure. Participants will learn about the surgical procedure, its main features, and expected outcomes. This course is also designed to provide surgeons with a detailed understanding of the surgical technique and preoperative and postoperative care.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Reptiles in Practice - From Tortoise, to Lizards and Snakes
courses.description: Reptile keeping is becoming more and more popular worldwide. Sadly all too often case presentation is linked to husbandry and management related shortfalls. The webinar series deals with management, husbandry (with a particular emphasis on recent husbandry advances), sex determination, parisitology, common case presentations, anaesthesia, clinical pathology techniques, diagnostic imaging, differential diagnosis, treatment options and therapeutic options (drugs, doses, routes of administration). Conditions of snakes, chelonian, lizards and crocodilians will also be considered.

courses.title: Treatment Options for Canine Fears and Anxiety
courses.description: The presenters will discuss the results of their recent publication concerning optimal treatments for various canine behavior issues related to fear and anxiety. In a previous study, they showed that 44% of all dogs have one or more of such issues, so treatment of these problems, ranging from separation anxiety to storm and noise phobia, to generalized anxiety and PTSD, should be of wide interest. They will detail the odds of improvement in individual problems of this nature that are treated by different types of professionals, along with the programs and techniques they employ, and the success of each.

courses.title: Certificate in Cultivating Positive Team Communication (for Veterinary Leaders)
courses.description: This highly interactive, evidence-based program will introduce participants to the art, science, and application of positive communication team-building skills. Participants will gain a deep understanding of the interconnected nature of positive communication, high-quality relationships, and the basics of conflict management in the workplace. They will master the skills of cultivating and strengthening interpersonal capital within teams by way of applied positive communication and conflict management approaches. The program leverages a mixed-methods approach to learning including asynchronous materials, supportive resources, small-bite live lectures, interactive "safe space" practice sessions, real-world skill-enhancing challenges, professional coaching, and more in an intimate cohort-style setting.

courses.title: FELINE DESTRUCTIVE SCRATCHING (1135-42825)
courses.description: In this one-hour module, you will learn what natural functions scratching serves for cats; common owner responses to scratching and the problems associated with them; and the potential fallout from declawing cats. Most importantly, you'll come away with several safe and effective alternative solutions to the problem of unwanted scratching, and a made-for-owners handout to help guide them in the right direction.

courses.title: Canine Myxomatous Valve Disease - Diagnosis, Staging & Management
courses.description: Mitral regurgitation is the most common cause of heart disease in dogs. This presentation provides an overview of myxomatous valvular heart disease in dogs, including natural history, diagnostic testing, (ACVIM) staging of disease, and therapeutic approaches with a review of the commonly-used cardiovascular medications.

courses.title: Marie Bartling
courses.description:
Note: the lecture title seems to have been replaced with my name an instructor.
The course name submitted is:
Breaking the Barriers to treating arthritis in dogs and cats
This course is a one-day lecture and wet lab focused on observation, diagnostic and therapy skills for treating dogs with osteoarthritis by joint injection.

courses.title: Eyes, ears & beyond
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients presented to their clinic with a dermatologic or ocular problem. The combination of a Dermatologist and an Ophthalmologist will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Fascia101: The Forgotten Organ
courses.description:
Veterinarians are realizing the importance of fascia and fascial treatments for painful patients. This course is designed as an introduction to fascia and myofascial pain syndrome as well as commonly used treatments. Students will receive instruction in the following areas:
Physiology and anatomy of fascia and fascia lines
Muscle functional physiology
Myofascial pain syndromes and identification of Myofascial trigger points
Palpation techniques to identify trigger points and their location
Various techniques used to treat myofascial trigger points

courses.title: Urgent care medicine update
courses.description: In this seminar, Drs. Lee, Pachtinger and Reinstein will present a complete discussion of the common urgent care clinical problems that they encounter in their individual practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of the problems. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common problems in urgent care management. The three specialists will bring case examples highlighting the triage, stabilization and management of these dynamic and challenging cases.

courses.title: ALONE IN THE WILDNERNESS (1135-44501)
courses.description: Are you the only person in your clinic who has a passion for Fear Free? It's easy to get discouraged and frustrated when we are surrounded by obstacles. This course provides tools to achieve your Fear Free goals even when you feel like you are all alone in your work. Learn how to get buy-in, implement strategies from the ground up, and encourage your colleagues to join your heart's work of protecting the emotional welfare of our treasured animal patients.

courses.title: Ophthalmology in the urgent care setting
courses.description: Doctors Maggs and Eaton will present a complete discussion of the common ocular problems that they encounter in their individual practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of the problems- both canine and feline. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the initial and then ongoing management of common ocular problems.

courses.title: Molly Angel
courses.description:
Canine Dentistry and Extractions with Wet Lab
This program consists of 4 hours of lecture presentations followed by 4 hours of wet lab using canine cadavers that will focus on basic oral therapeutics including in-depth instruction with extraction techniques. The lecture presentation will begin with normal anatomy of the canine adult and pediatric patient, normal radiographic positioning of the canine patient, review of principles and positioning of standard imaging including digital radiographic and cone beam computed tomography, general and individual patient care with respect to the anesthetic process, fundamental anesthetic protocols and patient care for the canine dental patient, applications of local anesthesia and techniques appropriate for the canine patient, as well as standard oral surgical flap and extraction techniques. Patient aftercare and follow up recommendations will also be discussed as well as appropriate post operative instructions.
Lecture will also include basic necessities of the dental practice including equipment needs, logistic and regulatory requirements in regard to radiation safety, hand and power instrumentation specific to canine oral surgery suture materials as well as appropriate use and maintenance of the above noted equipment.
The wet lab segment of this day will include the application of the aforementioned lecture topics to be applied to canine cadavers. Participants will practice local nerve block applications, general oral flap techniques, closure of tissues, use of high-speed instrumentation as well as hand instrumentation to complete general therapeutics and extractions on cadaver samples.
The learning objectives of this course should provide the participants with a better understanding of the dental operatory, equipment used, diagnostic procedures and the entire anesthetic dental process for a canine patient. The participants should also expect to have individual instruction during the wet lab portion to assist with improving

courses.title: Laser Therapy in Small Animal Practice: the Science Behind the Right Energy
courses.description: In this one-hour video course, we shine a light on the science and benefits of laser therapy with Dr. Maria Suarez Redondo. After mastering the foundational mechanisms at a cellular level, we'll review a variety of case examples of recoveries enhanced by laser therapy. Then, round the session out with a conversation on safety parameters, appropriate protocols, and indications so you can give patients the best of cutting-edge technology.

courses.title: VLI Trek
courses.description: VLI Trek is a hands-on, immersive program developed by the Veterinary Leadership Institute (VLI) to help veterinary healthcare professionals experience more fulfilling careers. Why Trek? Veterinary professionals work in a vibrant and engaging profession. The same things that capture our hearts and minds can also weigh us down. We can lose our focus, energy and enthusiasm for our professional and personal lives. There are no easy fixes or one-stop shopping solutions to fix these problems. It takes personal work, reflection and a supportive community to help us. VLI Trek is about stepping off the treadmill, and in community with like-minded colleagues, to discover and develop new capacities to engage in our work and in our lives.

courses.title: High-Quality, High-Volume Spay/Neuter Techniques
courses.description: This course will cover the fundamentals of High-Quality, High-Volume Spay/Neuter (HQHVSN) techniques to safely increase spay/neuter efficiency and reduce surgical time. Measurable educational goals and behavioral objectives include learning and understanding new HQHVSN techniques to increase efficiency and reduce surgical time in dog and cat sterilization surgery.

courses.title: Fluid Therapy for Emergency and Urgent Care Patients: A Guide for the General Practitioner
courses.description: The presenter will discuss different types of fluids available for use in veterinary patients with a short review of the types, the differences between the types, and a brief description on the use of crystalloids vs colloids. The presenter will also touch on appropriate fluid therapy types, techniques, and rates for resuscitation, rehydration, and preventing continuing fluid loss. The presentation will be from a criticalists perspective but will be geared to general practice.

courses.title: Ophthalmology for the General Practitioner
courses.description: This course will cover general ophthalmic conditions, ophthalmic emergencies, and glaucoma. We will discuss how to diagnose and treat these conditions, how to manage them long term, and when to consider referral.

courses.title: On Demand: Shake it Off! Relief from Otitis Externa
courses.description: Acute, painful ear infections are common and stressful for pet owners, and chronic, relapsing otitis externa is frustrating for owners and the veterinary team. This discussion will review where many of these frustrations stem from and provide helpful tools for relief, such as Fear Free techniques and communication tools. Addressing and preventing relapse of otitis externa involves a thorough understanding of Primary causes of otitis externa, common Secondary infections and sampling techniques, Perpetuating factors that occur with chronicity which make resolution of infection more challenging, and Predisposing issues that put animals with primary diseases at a higher risk of relapse. Treatments for allergic dermatitis, a common primary trigger for otitis externa, will be discussed to help select the most effective therapy while minimizing risks.

courses.title: House Call & Mobile Vet Virtual Conference 2025
courses.description: This program, hosted by The House Call Vet Academy and Dr. Eve Harrison, VMD, CVA, is a two day virtual conference for house call & mobile veterinarians, vet techs, as well as vets & techs who may be interested in exploring mobile veterinary practice or are house call curious! In this conference, attendees can expect to learn about the logistics of starting, growing, or leveling up a mobile veterinary practice, as well as how to stay safe emotionally and physically while practicing medicine in this special and unique way, in or around the homes of their patients and clients. This virtual conference is for & by house call & mobile veterinarians & staff to give our community a platform to learn about actionable information & resources, find inspiration, network with each other, and lift each other up.

courses.title: Feline One medicine: where feline behavior, lameness and pain management meet
courses.description: The three doctors will present a complete discussion of common problems that they encounter in their individual practices. The combination of a Surgeon, a Behaviorist and Anesthesiologist/pain management specialist will provide a unique approach to the feline patient management. The problems presented will be everyday common clinical disorders that veterinarians manage in their practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of these common problems. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of the clinical diseases and disorders.

courses.title: IV Fluid Therapy: Part 1
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive, clinically relevant overview of intravenous (IV) fluid therapy in small animals. The lecture covers key concepts in assessing hydration status and fluid deficits, evaluating for signs of fluid overload, choosing between IV and intraosseous (IO) access, and selecting the most appropriate type of IV fluid. Through discussion of real case examples and physiology-based reasoning, the speaker walks using isotonic, hypotonic, and hypertonic crystalloids, as well as natural and synthetic colloids, with special attention to when and why to choose each fluid type in various clinical scenarios.

courses.title: A Peaceful Passing: Elevating Veterinary Hospice and Euthanasia Practices
courses.description: This course offers veterinary professionals a thoughtful guide to improving the entire experience of hospice care and euthanasia, both for clients and for their own teams. Learners will explore the role of hospice appointments in preparing families for the decisions and emotions that surround end-of-life care, including the importance of honest conversations and planning. The course covers how to use tools such as consultation forms, quality of life scales, and client handouts to strengthen communication and build trust. Participants will examine the delicate balance between managing medical needs and providing emotional support, learning how to help families make informed, compassionate choices for their pets. By the end of this section, learners will have a clearer understanding of how early preparation can lead to more peaceful outcomes.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Introduction to Birds
courses.description: This course will provide training for individuals working with birds in research. This course will address species that are not poultry. It will cover topics such as research mandates, occupational health, housing, routine care, handling, detecting pain and distress, research procedures, and euthanasia.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Introduction to Swine
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to working with swine in a research environment. The topics covered will include regulatory coverage, zoonotic hazards, housing requirements, anesthesia, pain management, and support care and monitoring. Today pigs are popular models for surgical research and teaching, cardiovascular studies, and xenotransplantation work (transplant of tissues for which the donor is of a different species than the recipient - e.g., pig to man). Three classifications of swine are covered in this course: Domestic pigs, including the common agricultural breeds; Minipigs, including the common research breeds; and Eurasian wild pig (boar).

courses.title: Inclusivity for All: Fair and Impartial Equity for the Deaf & Hard of Hearing
courses.description: This course describes the importance of equity and inclusion for individuals with disabilities, specifically the deaf and hard of hearing, and focuses on adapting new ways to tackle this perceived language barrier.

courses.title: Equine Ophthalmology: Cloudy/Swollen Eyes
courses.description: This course provides an overview of one of the most common equine emergent ophthalmic presenting complaints (swollen/cloudy eye), focusing on conditions such as corneal ulcers and equine recurrent uveitis (ERU). Participants learn to recognize clinical signs of swollen, cloudy, and painful eyes, understand diagnostic techniques including fluorescein staining, tonometry, and ophthalmoscopic examination, and review treatment strategies involving antimicrobials, anti-inflammatories, mydriatics, and surgical interventions. Special emphasis is placed on nerve blocks for examination, the role of systemic disease in ocular conditions, and long-term management to prevent complications such as cataracts, glaucoma, and blindness.

courses.title: Small Animal Congenital Surgical Disorders: Part 1
courses.description: This course reviews the most common surgical congenital anomalies encountered in small animal practice. Attendees will learn about the diagnosis, imaging, and treatment of patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and portosystemic shunts (PSS). The course emphasizes understanding the underlying fetal circulatory changes, clinical presentations, available and best diagnostics, and surgical and minimally invasive treatment options while highlighting potential complications and postoperative management.

courses.title: Septic Foals: Risk Factors, Diagnosis, and Treatment in Equine Neonatology
courses.description: This course provides a discussion of sepsis in neonatal foals, focusing on risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostics, treatment strategies, and prognosis. Attendees learn how to identify early signs of systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), recognize common sites of infection (joints, umbilicus, lungs, GI tract, CNS), and manage critically ill foals in an intensive care setting. The role of failure of passive transfer (FPT), environmental conditions, and maternal health in predisposing foals to sepsis is discussed. Diagnostic modalities include bloodwork abnormalities (neutropenia, azotemia, metabolic acidosis, hyperlactatemia, IgG snap testing), ultrasonography, and radiographic assessment of infected joints and umbilical structures. The session also covers emergency stabilization (IV fluids, plasma transfusions, broad-spectrum antibiotics, anti-endotoxin therapies, and nutritional support), prognosis, and preventive strategies for reducing neonatal sepsis rates in equine breeding operations.

courses.title: Equine Gastrointestinal Parasites
courses.description: This course provides a review of equine gastrointestinal parasitology, focusing on the identification, pathophysiology, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of the common gastrointestinal parasitic infections in horses. Participants learn about parasite lifecycles, host susceptibility, and the challenges posed by anthelmintic resistance. Key parasites include small and large strongyles, ascarids, tapeworms, threadworms, pinworms, Gasterophilus spp., and Habronema species, along with their impact on equine health. The course emphasizes evidence-based parasite control strategies, including fecal egg count reduction testing, selective deworming protocols, and environmental management techniques. Attendees develop practical skills in diagnosing and managing parasitic infections in both adult horses and foals, optimizing parasite control programs to minimize resistance while maintaining equine health.

courses.title: Small Animal Congenital Surgical Disorders: Part 2
courses.description: This course reviews the most common surgical congenital anomalies encountered in small animal practice. Attendees will learn about the diagnosis, imaging, and treatment of persistent right aortic arch (PRAA) and types of diaphragmatic hernias. The course emphasizes understanding the underlying fetal circulatory changes, clinical presentations, available and best diagnostics, and surgical and minimally invasive treatment options while highlighting potential complications and postoperative management.

courses.title: AAHA Management of Allergic Skin Diseases in Dogs and Cats Guidelines Certificate Course
courses.description: AAHA Management of Allergic Skin Diseases in Dogs and Cats Certificate Course provides a comprehensive, yet practical, exploration of allergic skin diseases for veterinary teams. Through competency-based learning objectives based on our trusted, peer-reviewed, 2023 AAHA Management of Allergic Skin Diseases in Dogs and Cats guidelines, dive into the latest evidence-based approaches to diagnosing, treating, and managing a variety of allergic skin conditions, including atopic dermatitis, food allergy, and flea allergy dermatitis. Through interactive modules and case studies, learners will gain a thorough understanding of the clinical presentation and effective management strategies for these common and often challenging skin disorders.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Aseptic Technique for Rodent Survival Surgery
courses.description: Research protocols may require surgical procedures on the rodents in the study. These procedures may be minor or major procedures, but all procedures will require knowledge of aseptic techniques to guard against infection. Surgery in laboratory animal facilities requires technical expertise and planning to ensure that rodents are cared for properly and that the procedure is conducted in accordance with laws and regulations and institutional standard operating procedures.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Post Procedure Care of Mice and Rats in Research: Minimizing Pain and Distress
courses.description: The goal of this course is to provide information on how to minimize pain and distress in mice and rats during and after experimental procedures. The course will discuss strategies for preemptively planning a study to minimize pain, approaches to recognize pain, and treatment modalities to reduce it in rodents. Much of the focus is on surgery and postsurgical pain. However, these strategies can generally be applied to the myriad of nonsurgical procedures that may cause pain in rodents.

courses.title: From Toxic to Terrific - Cultivating Wellbeing in the Veterinary Workplace
courses.description: This month-long immersive online program teaches practice owners, managers, and veterinarians or veterinary technicians in practice leadership or management roles how to resolve toxicity and cultivate workplace wellbeing. All information is evidence-based and includes practical skills for managing effective and coherent teams including tools for effective communication, conflict resolution, fostering psychological safety, and promoting mental health and wellbeing initiatives. Content is in the form of weekly informative emails and webinars, reflection exercises and action plans, peer-to-peer support, and group coaching.

courses.title: AAHA Working, Assistance and Therapy Dog Guidelines Certificate Course RACE Abstract
courses.description: AAHA Working, Assistance and Therapy Dog Guidelines Certificate Course RACE Abstract is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: De-escalation Techniques to Handle Client Complaints and Conflicts
courses.description: As a manager or team member in the veterinary industry, dealing with emotions and difficult situations is inevitable. Every day, we are faced with situations, tasks, people, and animals that cause us to have emotional reactions. It is no surprise that in your position you are bound to come across stressed, emotional, and sometimes irate clients. Every business, no matter the industry, will encounter difficult clients at some point. Sometimes it can be tricky to figure out how to deal with difficult clients effectively. During this webinar, you will learn a few strategies to help you manage and diffuse these situations effectively.

courses.title: Pawsitive Dental Radiology Interpretation Masterclass
courses.description: This 2-hour veterinary dental radiology masterclass provides a systematic approach to dental radiograph interpretation in dogs and cats. Participants will review normal radiographic anatomy, identify periodontal disease, endodontic disease, tooth resorption, and periapical pathology, and apply case-based diagnostic techniques to improve clinical decision-making, treatment planning, and patient outcomes.

courses.title: AAHA Anesthesia Safety and Monitoring Guidelines Certificate
courses.description: AAHA Anesthesia Safety and Monitoring Guidelines Certificate is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Defining the E in DEI: Equity Essentials
courses.description: This course introduces basic concepts related to diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) with an emphasis on the concept of equity. Within the context of veterinary medicine, individuals will deepen their understanding of equity as it relates to similar concepts. The historical context behind many of our modern-day equity issues is provided as a framework for exploring where those issues show up within their own profession. In addition to providing basic concepts and critical historical context, this module utilizes current research to help learners explore the benefits of increased equity in the workplace. The purpose of this module is to not only equip individuals with a strong conceptual foundation but also with strategies to advance equity within their own organizations.

courses.title: Bovine classic conditions: part 2
courses.description:
This course presents a comprehensive overview of common clinical conditions affecting cattle, including displaced
abomasum, bloat, choke, metabolic diseases (such as ketosis, fatty liver, and milk fever), and bovine respiratory disease complex. Through case-based discussions and practical examples, attendees gain a working knowledge of diagnostic techniques, treatment protocols, and management strategies relevant to both dairy and beef cattle operations. The emphasis is on integrating clinical skills with herd-level decision-making to optimize outcomes.

courses.title: Transgender Advocacy and Allyship
courses.description: This course introduces the experience of the transgender community within veterinary medicine. Through personal experience, research, and supportive resources this course teaches students the statics and facts regarding the trans* community within our profession, and how to be a supportive ally both as an individual and an institution.

courses.title: Communicating Across Cultures
courses.description: This course introduces Cross Cultural communication and how to navigate cultural differences in a veterinary setting.

courses.title: Bovine miscellaneous conditions
courses.description: This course provides an overview of bovine leukemia virus (BLV) infection, its association with lymphosarcoma, and the clinical, diagnostic, and preventive implications in cattle herds. It also addresses bovine lameness, including detailed lameness workups, diagnostic techniques, treatment strategies, and welfare considerations. Participants gain practical guidance applicable to both beef and dairy cattle in field and clinical settings.

courses.title: Porcine Toxicities and Deficiencies
courses.description: This course provides a review of common toxicities and nutritional deficiencies in swine, focusing on their clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management. Participants will gain an understanding of key toxic agents, including mycotoxins (aflatoxin, deoxynivalenol (DON), ergot alkaloids, fumonisin, ochratoxin, and zearalenone), tiamulin-ionophore interactions, and hydrogen sulfide gas exposure. The course also explores vitamin and mineral deficiencies, such as vitamin E/selenium, iron, and vitamin D, which contribute to metabolic disorders in pigs. Special emphasis is placed on pathophysiology, gross and histopathologic lesions, diagnostic strategies, and effective intervention methods. By the end of the course, attendees are equipped with practical knowledge to identify, prevent, and manage these critical conditions in swine production systems.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Working Safely with Rodents in Biocontainment
courses.description: Rodents are the most common type of mammal in animal biocontainment facilities. As for all biocontainment work, emphasis must be placed on training and personnel safety. With appropriate training and by following SOPs, personnel can effectively and efficiently work with many different species of rodents. This course is focused on the ABSL-2 or -3 facility and cover preparing animal for biocontainment, occupational health concerns, husbandry and animal care, animal emergencies, and research in biocontainment.

courses.title: Bovine neurologic diseases
courses.description:
This session explores the clinical presentation, differential diagnosis, and treatment strategies for two neurologic
conditions commonly seen in ruminants: polioencephalomalacia (PEM) and lead toxicity. Attendees learn to distinguish between the two based on neurologic and gastrointestinal signs, response to treatment, and environmental risk factors.
Emphasis is placed on supportive care, diagnostic approaches, and management implications for food safety.

courses.title: Epidemiology part 2: reference intervals, false positives, morbidity/mortality, and incidence/prevalence
courses.description: This course focuses on high-yield concepts beyond basic math. This session explores the clinical relevance of reference intervals, diagnostic test interpretation, and common epidemiology terms like incidence, prevalence, morbidity, and mortality. With relatable examples, study questions, and clinical applications, this lecture helps solidify epidemiology concepts that appear in everyday practice.

courses.title: Top 10 Toxins Affecting Dogs and Cats in Practice Today
courses.description: This course offers an exploration of the most prevalent toxins that pose a threat to our canine and feline companions today. Dr. Schmid, Veterinary Toxicologist with Pet Poison Helpline / SafetyCall shares the latest information on challenges in toxicology and common cases in companion animal practice.

courses.title: Veterinary CPR: From Guidelines to Clinical Confidence
courses.description: Veterinary CPR: From Guidelines to Clinical Confidence is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Bovine calving disorders and neonatal calf conditions
courses.description: This course provides an overview of common periparturient and neonatal conditions affecting beef and dairy cattle. Key topics include dystocia management, postpartum complications such as retained placenta and metritis, and common calf diseases like sepsis, omphalitis, and white muscle disease. Attendees learn evidence-based approaches for field diagnosis and treatment, surgical decision-making, and preventive herd health strategies.

courses.title: Equine Myopathies
courses.description: This course provides a review of top equine myopathies, both exertional and non-exertional. Participants learn to differentiate between genetic and sporadic myopathies, recognize clinical presentations such as muscle stiffness, atrophy, weakness, and myoglobinuria, and perform key diagnostic tests including muscle enzyme analysis, genetic testing, and muscle biopsy. The session will also explore treatment protocols for acute and chronic myopathies, including fluid therapy for myoglobinuria, dietary modifications, exercise regimens, and pharmacologic interventions such as dantrolene and corticosteroids. Prognostic factors and breed predispositions, particularly in Quarter horses, are discussed.

courses.title: Breaking Down Barriers and Finding Common Ground - The Culture of Communication
courses.description:
To truly BLEND within the veterinary profession, it's of vital importance we learn how to first talk with one another. The recognition of cultural differences, the impacts of language, ability status, and an overall understanding of what diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging (DEIB), means are crucial to the sustainability of the individuals within our profession and our surrounding communities.
This session will address the defining components of DEIB and communication and how to interweave them both within the fabric of our veterinary team culture.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Animal Protocols: Strategies for Effective Review
courses.description: This course will discuss ways an IACUC can approach protocol evaluation with concern for animal well-being and ethical costs, weighed against objectives and needs of the protocol. The course offers scenarios that illustrate types of issues that can arise during protocol evaluation and provides discussion questions to consider as a way to help to resolve the issues.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: AVMA Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals: 2020 Edition
courses.description: This course is based on the AVMA Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals which was published by the American Veterinary Medical Association in February of 2020. This course focuses on animal euthanasia in the research setting.

courses.title: Equine Neurological Disorders: Part 1
courses.description: This course provides a review of five major equine neurologic conditions, focusing on their clinical presentation, differential diagnoses, diagnostic testing, and treatment options. Participants will explore equine protozoal myeloencephalitis (EPM), cervical vertebral stenotic myelopathy (CVSM), traumatic brain and spinal cord injuries, botulism and tetanus, and the vitamin E-associated conditions (equine degenerative myeloencephalopathy (EDM) and equine motor neuron disease (EMND)). The course emphasizes practical approaches to diagnosing and managing these diseases.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Working with the IACUC
courses.description: To ensure that animal research and teaching is performed according to the highest standards of ethics, scientific rigor and reproducibility, research must take place under the supervision of an IACUC. By assuring that animal research and teaching comply with animal welfare laws and guidelines, the IACUC ensures that animals are not subjected to unnecessary pain and distress. A robust partnership between the researcher and the IACUC also protects both the investigator and the institution. It is essential that all researchers are familiar with how to best interact with their IACUC. This course is designed with the following specific goals in mind: 1) Assist investigators in completing their animal use protocol application and interacting effectively with the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC), 2 Review the basic issues with which IACUC members must become familiar to effectively review animal research and teaching proposals, 3) Provide information on special circumstances that may need to be addressed in an animal protocol form, such as the use of recombinant DNA or select agents, and 4) Provide the training legally required by the Animal Welfare Act and Regulations and Public Health Service Policy.

courses.title: Top Equine Endocrine Disorders
courses.description: This course offers a review of two key equine endocrine disorders - Equine Metabolic Syndrome (EMS) and Pituitary Pars Intermedia Dysfunction (PPID, also known as equine Cushing disease). Participants learn to identify clinical signs of each disorder; understand the underlying pathophysiologies; and review diagnostic protocols (resting insulin vs. resting ACTH and dynamic tests like the oral sugar test and TRH stimulation test). The session also covers treatment strategies including dietary management, exercise protocols, and pharmacologic interventions, along with the importance of supportive care and owner compliance.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Working with Laboratory Zebrafish
courses.description: The goal of this course is to provide information about how to work with zebrafish as a model in laboratory animal research protocols. Zebrafish are increasing in use as a model in biomedical research. Much is still to be learned regarding the care and use of zebrafish in research studies. Therefore, there may be variations among institutions as to the protocols regarding husbandry, nutrition, breeding, etc. This course will focus on the biology of zebrafish, regulatory requirements, husbandry and care, and pain management and anesthesia procedures.

courses.title: Poultry Viral Diseases: Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention for Veterinary Practice
courses.description: Poultry Viral Diseases: Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention for Veterinary Practice is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: The Missing Link: Wellness & Oppression
courses.description: Our understanding of wellness is often shaped by individualistic frameworks that do not address how experiencing discrimination and oppression can directly impact the wellbeing of diverse communities. People with diverse identities working in veterinary medicine face with their own experiences of discrimination as well as the exposure to secondary trauma of those they support including their communities at large. This can result in more nuanced experiences of compassion fatigue which require an intersectional lens. This session will explore how one's wellbeing is directly impacted by discrimination, trauma and oppression, followed by an overview of what those most impacted by discrimination can do to promote their own well-being, what allies can do to foster collective change, and what veterinary practices can do to foster equitable and inclusive wellness change.

courses.title: Professional Series: An Overview of Daily Psychiatric Medication
courses.description:
This 15 minute long online video covers the foundational considerations when working with daily psychiatric medications. It covers indications for use of medications, the time frame for medications to take effect, the timeline for side effects to appear, and guidelines for increasing, decreasing, and discontinuing medications.
Learning Objectives:
1. Indications for the use of daily psychiatric medications.
2. Timeline considerations for the use of daily medications.
3. When side effects can be expected to appear when using daily psychiatric medications.
Program Agenda:
a. Professional Series: An Overview of Daily Psychiatric Medications (single session)
b. 15:05 minutes
c. Dr. Ariel Fagen, DVM, DACVB

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Ethical Decision-Making in Animal Research
courses.description: This course will give you the principles needed to analyze an ethical conflict and to make a decision that best balances the benefits and costs for the individuals and subjects involved. After completing this course, you may practice these principles by working through the case studies that follow in this course series.

courses.title: No Drama, No Trauma: Security and Prevention for Practice
courses.description: Veterinary hospitals are places of healing, but they are not immune to workplace violence risks. This course delivers a thorough exploration of the four primary types of workplace violence that affect veterinary practices: criminal intent, client violence, worker-on-worker conflict, and personal relationship spillover. Through real life case examples, veterinary professionals will gain the knowledge and tools to better assess their clinic vulnerabilities and implement risk reduction strategies.

courses.title: Aquaculture part 2: Environmental Diseases of Fish
courses.description: This course introduces veterinary professionals and students to foundational concepts in aquatic animal health, focusing on environmental factors that influence fish disease. Participants gain an understanding of key components in aquatic systems, including water quality, filtration, and gas exchange, and how imbalances in these systems contribute to clinical disease. The program covers essential topics such as the nitrogen cycle, new and old tank syndrome, waterborne toxins, pH shifts, and gas-related disorders. Emphasis is placed on practical diagnostic approaches and treatment strategies relevant to clinical practice, aquaculture, and aquarium medicine.

courses.title: Performance Horse Medicine
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth study of anatomy, biomechanics, and neuromuscular control in performance horses. The information in this course adds to the veterinarian's knowledge base to enhance lameness and performance evaluation and treatment of equine patients

courses.title: Dentistry and Orofacial Surgery of Exotic Companion Mammals
courses.description:
The Dentistry and Orofacial Surgery of Exotic Companion Mammals online course is an eight-session comprehensive didactic program covering every up-to-date and cutting edge aspect of this broad branch of exotic companion mammal medicine and surgery.
This course includes anatomy, physiology, standard and advanced diagnostic imaging, intraoral treatment, basic and advanced extraoral surgical treatment.
It will provide useful information for those approaching this topic for the first time, as well as for those who already possess basic or intermediate knowledge and desire to pursue more information in this area.
Visually-oriented keynotes include practical sessions with videos of step-by-step dental procedures and surgical cases.

courses.title: AAHA Diabetes Management Guidelines for Dogs and Cats Certificate Course
courses.description: Developed in alignment with the 2018 AAHA Diabetes Management Guidelines for Dogs and Cats, the course offers a real-world, clinical approach to navigating diabetic cases. Through interactive modules and case studies, learners will gain a thorough understanding of the clinical presentation and effective short- and long-term management strategies for these patients. In addition, because a collaborative approach between the veterinary team and pet owner is so important in successfully managing a diabetic patient, this course addresses how to communicate with owners effectively and with empathy when making treatment decisions

courses.title: Building Cultural Competence and Communication Skills with the Latinx Community
courses.description: This course is designed to provide an introductory overview for the need to build cultural competence and understanding of Latinx culture in the context of veterinary medicine. Whether you are a small animal practioner working with Latinx pet owners, or a food animal veterinarian working with Spanish-speaking workers, this course will help you understand the importance of building your cultural knowledge of the Latinx community in order to create trust and provide culturally appropriate veterinary care. This program will discuss the need for Spanish communication courses with an emphasis on cultural understanding at veterinary colleges, the barriers to adequate veterinary care in Latinx communities, the complexity of Latinx culture, the lack of Latinx representation in the veterinary industry and more.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Introduction to Rats
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to working with rats in a research environment. The topics covered will include regulatory coverage, zoonotic hazards, housing requirements, anesthesia, pain management, and support care and monitoring.

courses.title: Active Allyship: The Celebration of Differences & Allyship
courses.description: During this program we will discuss the essential elements of allyship including self-education, leveraging privilege and power, reaffirming that allyship centers on the oppressed, and the power of committing fully. We must speak up with radical candor. We must be active allies. And we must learn how to incorporate these important concepts into our culture and workflow.

courses.title: One Health Perspective: Avian Influenza in Cats & Infection Control
courses.description: This course examines the current landscape of H5N1 avian influenza infections in companion animals, with an emphasis on domestic cats. Participants will engage with real-world case examples, diagnostic and infection control protocols, and One Health collaboration strategies that span clinical practice and public health. Learners benefit from the insight of a multidisciplinary team of experts, including state public health veterinarians, infectious disease researchers, and leaders in veterinary epidemiology and infection control. These professionals bring direct experience managing H5N1 outbreaks, coordinating interagency responses, and guiding clinical decisions in the face of evolving zoonotic threats. Designed for veterinary professionals, public health practitioners, and others involved in animal health or zoonotic disease surveillance, this course supports practical application through a blend of scientific evidence, policy considerations, and operational case management.

courses.title: Leptospirosis Unmasked: Updated Clinical Insights for Every Practice
courses.description: This course, led by Dr. Jane Sykes, delivers the latest updates from the most recent ACVIM Consensus Statement on canine leptospirosis. Veterinary professionals will gain a comprehensive understanding of leptospiral pathogenesis, zoonotic risk, and diagnostic challenges, along with practical clinical recommendations. New molecular insights into the biofilm forming ability of Leptospira spp. and their persistence in renal tissue are discussed in detail, highlighting the disease's potential for subclinical shedding, environmental contamination, and multisystemic involvement. Clinicians will learn to apply current epidemiological evidence, moving beyond outdated geographic and lifestyle assumptions. The course emphasizes the importance of identifying leptospirosis in urban and small breed dogs and supports year-round vigilance regardless of season or setting. Diagnostic methods including MAT titers, PCR, and point-of-care testing are explored with clear guidance on interpretation, including real-world case examples and consensus-based case definitions. Equally important, the course addresses prevention strategies through vaccination, highlighting newly published data supporting the classification of leptospirosis as a core vaccine recommendation. Treatment protocols for acute and chronic presentations are reviewed, along with best practices for antimicrobial use and client education. By the end of this course, veterinary teams will be better equipped to prevent, diagnose, and manage this complex, underrecognized threat.

courses.title: Cyberbullying in Practice: How Veterinary Teams Protect Minds and Mission
courses.description: Cyberbullying is not just an online inconvenience, it is a growing threat to the emotional well-being of veterinary professionals and the operational health of practices. This course explores the definitions, impacts, and strategies surrounding cyberbullying, focusing on how repeated online attacks affect both individuals and teams. Learners will gain a deep understanding of how cyberbullying differs from ordinary criticism, why emotional responses matter, and how distress can impair decision-making. Drawing on veterinary social work expertise and supported by tools like the AVMA Reputation Management Toolkit, the course provides practical guidance for handling cyberbullying incidents with clarity and resilience. By the end, learners will be able to recognize the emotional, psychological, and organizational costs of online harassment and apply meaningful tools to address them.

courses.title: AAHA Community Care Guidelines: Practical Strategies for Inclusive Veterinary Practice
courses.description: The AAHA Community Care Guidelines mark a pivotal step toward redefining how veterinary teams approach access to care. This course unpacks the collaborative work of leaders in shelter medicine, private practice, public health, and veterinary equity, offering veterinary professionals a clear roadmap to provide high-quality care across diverse client and patient populations.

courses.title: Bovine classic conditions: part 1
courses.description:
This course provides an in-depth exploration of several significant infectious conditions affecting cattle: traumatic
reticuloperitonitis and -pericarditis, Actinomyces bovis (lumpy jaw), and Actinobacillus lignieresii (wooden tongue). Through detailed case discussions, clinical signs, diagnostic approaches, and treatment options, participants will gain practical tools for recognizing and managing these diseases.

courses.title: DEA Compliance Made Practical: Protecting Your Practice
courses.description: No one wants a DEA inspection to catch them off guard. This course gives veterinary teams the inside scoop from someone who spent decades with the DEA and now helps clinics stay compliant every day.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Post Procedure Care of Mice and Rats in Research: Minimizing Pain and Distress
courses.description: The goal of this course is to provide information on how to minimize pain and distress in mice and rats during and after experimental procedures. The course will discuss strategies for preemptively planning a study to minimize pain, approaches to recognize pain, and treatment modalities to reduce it in rodents. Much of the focus is on surgery and postsurgical pain. However, these strategies can generally be applied to the myriad of nonsurgical procedures that may cause pain in rodents.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Guide for the Care and Use of Agricultural Animals in Research and Teaching (4th Edition)
courses.description: The Guide for the Care and Use of Agricultural Animals in Research and Teaching (Ag Guide) provides information on the most common agricultural animals under a variety of teaching and research circumstances. This course focuses on the Ag Guide's first five chapters, which address key concepts in the management of agricultural animals: institutional policies, veterinary care, husbandry and housing, biosecurity, environmental enrichment, handling, and transport.

courses.title: Change is Hard: Modern Management of Feline Diabetes with SGLT2 Inhibitors
courses.description: Change is Hard: Modern Management of Feline Diabetes with SGLT2 Inhibitors is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Compassion Fatigue
courses.description: Compassion fatigue is an emotional state that was first recognized in the early 1990s in highly empathetic nurses who had lost their nurturing quality and compassion towards their patients. However, only very recently have we made this association with feelings that many of us have long experienced in the laboratory animal science community. Compassion fatigue can culminate to a point of emotional, physical, and cognitive exhaustion that can come at a great professional and personal toll that impacts our well-being. Because of this cost, it is essential that we continue to discuss this issue openly until awareness, acknowledgment, and established strategies for care are commonplace in our field. It is important to realize that all individuals working in our field can be affected, not only those working directly with animals. The goal of this course is to provide information that will help you cope with feelings and emotions that may arise from your work in the laboratory animal science field.

courses.title: Equine Skin Conditions: Diagnosis and Treatment of Common Dermatologic Disorders
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the most common equine dermatologic conditions, focusing on tumors (squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma, sarcoids, habronemiasis), allergic conditions (culicoides hypersensitivity, onchocerciasis), and infectious skin diseases (dermatophilosis, ringworm). Attendees learn how to identify clinical presentations, differentiate between conditions with similar appearances, and develop treatment plans. Diagnostic approaches, including cytology, biopsy, intradermal allergy testing, and dermatophyte culture, are covered, along with management strategies such as surgical excision, immunotherapy, corticosteroids, anthelmintics, antifungal therapy, and fly control.

courses.title: Porcine Musculoskeletal and Dermatologic Diseases
courses.description: This course provides a review of musculoskeletal and dermatologic diseases in swine, focusing on diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. Participants learn about bacterial, viral, and parasitic conditions that cause arthritis, lameness, septicemia, and skin disorders, including Glaesserella parasuis, Streptococcus suis, Mycoplasma spp., Erysipelas spp., Seneca Valley virus, Staphylococcus hyicus, and sarcoptic mange. The course covers clinical presentations, pathology, zoonotic risks, and regulatory considerations, with an emphasis on vaccination, biosecurity, and diagnostic approaches such as PCR, culture, and histopathology. This course enhances veterinary clinical reasoning to improve swine herd health outcomes and disease management strategies.

courses.title: Equine Neurological Disorders: Part 2
courses.description: This course provides a review of equine herpesvirus-1 myeloencephalopathy (EHM), neonatal encephalopathy, vestibular disease, encephalomyelitis (Eastern and Western equine encephalitis, West Nile virus), and meningitis, with a bonus discussion on neuroborreliosis. Participants learn about the clinical presentation, differential diagnoses, diagnostic testing, treatment approaches, and prognosis for each condition. The course emphasizes practical case-based learning, integrating real-world scenarios to enhance diagnostic and treatment skills.

courses.title: Equine Gastrointestinal Disease: Diagnosis and Management of Colic, Colitis, Gastric Ulcer Syndrome, and Esophageal Obstructi
courses.description: This course focuses on common equine gastrointestinal disorders and emergencies. Participants explore the diagnostic approaches and treatment protocols for a variety of the gastrointestinal conditions most commonly seen in first opinion equine practice, including colic (both medical and surgical), acute colitis (infectious and noninfectious), equine gastric ulcer syndrome (differentiating squamous and glandular disease), and esophageal obstruction (choke). The course emphasizes diagnostic strategies (physical exam, ultrasound, gastroscopy, endoscopy), and evidence based treatment modalities, and key preventive measures such as biosecurity, nutritional management, and dental care.

courses.title: Feline Life Stages Guidelines Certificate Course
courses.description:
Cats are the most popular pets in the United States and are often considered family members. However, many do not receive the preventive healthcare they need and deserve. Why is there such a significant gap in care? Why do owners believe their cats do not need routine veterinary exams? This gap in care stems from two primary reasons: cats' stoic and reclusive nature, and the misconception by owners that cats are self-sufficient and do not need medical attention.
How can we encourage more preventive care visits for cats?
This course aims to address this question head-on by:
Equipping veterinary teams with specific reasons why preventive checkups are essential at every stage of a cat's life
Providing a framework for managing a cat's healthcare throughout their life in a way that resonates with how clients think about their own cats
Emphasizing the distinct health needs at each life stage and the benefits of individualized care
In addition, this course focuses on enhancing the veterinary experience for cats through feline-friendly handling techniques and exploring different aspects of client communication. Participants will learn effective strategies for gathering detailed patient information, enabling earlier and more accurate diagnoses of feline health issues. The course also emphasizes the critical role of ongoing education and training within veterinary teams, ensuring that practices stay current with the latest research and techniques in feline care.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Introduction to Mice
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to working with mice in a research environment. The topics covered will include regulatory coverage, zoonotic hazards, housing requirements, anesthesia, pain management, and support care and monitoring.

courses.title: AAHA Pain Management Guidelines Certificate
courses.description: This course delivers a structured, evidence-informed approach to managing pain in canine and feline patients, based on the AAHA Pain Management Guidelines. It equips veterinary professionals with the tools and clinical reasoning needed to assess, treat, and re-evaluate pain using proactive, multimodal strategies. Participants will learn to distinguish between acute and chronic pain presentations, utilize validated pain assessment instruments - including those tailored for pet owners - and prioritize therapeutic options using a tiered decision-making framework. The course emphasizes preemptive analgesia, effective client education, and whole-team collaboration in building and executing individualized treatment plans. Designed for both seasoned practitioners and those seeking to update their knowledge with current best practices, this course includes practical tools, decision trees, pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic treatment comparisons, and guidance specific to both canine and feline patients.

courses.title: Shiny Isn't Sharp, How to Sharpen Common Dental Instruments
courses.description: This 1-hour on-demand course focuses on veterinary dental instrument sharpening techniques for maintaining optimal performance in clinical practice. Participants will learn to evaluate and sharpen dental curettes, scalers, winged and straight elevators, luxators, and periosteal elevators, while understanding how proper sharpening improves instrument efficiency, ergonomics, and patient safety.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: A One Health Approach to Controlled Substances and the Opioid Crisis
courses.description: Learn how veterinarians can contribute to the interactive effort of multiple disciplines, clients, and local and national associations to combat the deadly opioid crisis. The course will provide continuing education on opioids and other controlled substances awareness to include: the schedule and use of opioids and other controlled substances; integration of treatments; alternative of treatments for pain management; counseling clients on the proper use, storage and disposal practices; the risks associated with using opioids and other controlled substances; the stigma of addiction; state and federal laws pertaining to prescribing and dispensing controlled substances; security features for a safety and compliance plan; and proper disposal requirements for both patient prescriptions and the veterinarian's inventory. This course is also approved by both VHMA and the Texas Veterinary Medical Examiners.

courses.title: Poultry Bacterial and Parasitic Diseases
courses.description:
This course builds upon foundational knowledge of poultry virology by diving into key bacterial and protozoal diseases
that affect both backyard and commercial flocks. Designed to support real-world clinical decision-making, this lecture
provides an in-depth look at major pathogens such as Pasteurella multocida, Mycoplasma gallisepticum, Avibacterium
paragallinarum, Salmonella spp., Eimeria spp., and Histomonas meleagridis. Attendees gain insight into clinical signs,
lesion patterns, diagnostic strategies, treatment options (when applicable), and prevention protocols. With a focus on
North American poultry practices, this course also highlights regulatory considerations and zoonotic risks, emphasizing a
practical approach to poultry health in varied settings.

courses.title: Canine Vaccines in a Vaccine-Hesitant World
courses.description: This segment of the Canine Vaccination Guidelines Certificate Course, presented by Dr. George Moore, discusses the updates and nuances of the 2022 AAHA Canine Vaccination Guidelines. Dr. Moore provides a historical perspective on the development of these guidelines, highlighting their evolution over the past two decades. He emphasizes the importance of clear communication with clients in a vaccine-hesitant world and discusses the considerations for core versus non-core vaccines, the challenges of vaccinating dogs in shelters, and the complexities of interpreting serologic titers. The presentation also covers practical aspects such as vaccine storage, handling, and addressing adverse events, all while maintaining a focus on evidence-based medicine. This insightful discussion is designed to equip veterinary professionals with the knowledge needed to effectively implement these guidelines in their practices, ensuring the best possible care for their canine patients.

courses.title: Fluid Therapy in Dogs and Cats: Precision, Safety, and Best Practices
courses.description: This course, based on the latest AAHA Fluid Therapy Guidelines, provides veterinary professionals with evidence based strategies to individualize fluid therapy for canine and feline patients. Learn how to assess hydration and perfusion status, select the right fluids, prevent fluid overload, and use clinical and ultrasound techniques to guide decision making.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Humane Endpoints
courses.description: The criteria used for intervention in research studies to prevent unnecessary pain and distress are called "endpoint criteria" or "humane endpoints" because they describe when it is time discontinue a painful procedure, remove an animal from a study, provide anesthesia, analgesia, or other supportive care, and euthanize an animal to prevent suffering. The goal of this course is to provide information on how to establish humane endpoint criteria for rodent studies.

courses.title: AAHA Canine Vaccinations Guidelines Certificate
courses.description: In this course, you will learn everything you need to know about canine vaccinations from world-renowned subject matter experts. Get the most up-to-date canine vaccine recommendations, learn how to interpret patient serologic titers and understand the factors associated with post vaccination adverse events and reactions. You will also get the opportunity to dive into the three C's of achieving client compliance: consistency, communication, and connection.

courses.title: The Role of Emotional Intelligence in Your Interactions with Others: An Intro to Social Awareness & Relationship Management
courses.description: Great leaders keep the emotional current of a team moving in a positive direction making their team feel understood and cared for. Throughout this webinar, we'll explore emotional intelligence through the lens of social awareness and relationship management. Improving these two areas will enable you to recognize and respond to emotions in others creating more meaningful relationships. Improving emotional intelligence will allow you to become a more resonant leader, driving a positive practice culture.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Colony Management I: Breeding and Recordkeeping
courses.description: This course provides information for researchers, animal technicians, and facility managers who are getting ready to start a colony, would like to review the basics of mouse breeding, or want to find ways to improve their breeding program. In this course, we have presented the most basic information you will need to manage a mouse colony while adhering to federal and institutional policies and mandates for ethical treatment of the animals in your care. Good recordkeeping in the colony and clear communication with the investigators are both absolutely essential to running an efficient colony, where the production of unwanted mice is minimized while the needs of the investigator are met in a timely fashion.

courses.title: Building A Thriving Dental Practice
courses.description: Over 80% of adult dogs and cats have some form of oral disease. Is your practice currently performing dental procedures on that percentage of your patients? Learn ways to explain and communicate the importance of good oral health to your clients and take dentistry to the next level in your practice, and fill those tables!

courses.title: Mastering Difficult Conversations: Tools for Clear and Compassionate Communication
courses.description: This presentation explores why interactions become difficult, emphasizing the importance of self-awareness and emotional intelligence.
