Attendees will learn actionable strategies like active listening, de-escalation techniques, and the use of assertive language. Real-life scenarios and a communication toolkit provide practical takeaways for improving outcomes in both professional and personal settings.

courses.title: Bridging the Gap: Shelter Medicine, Private Practice, and the Power of Partnership
courses.description: The course highlights the importance of effective communication and partnership between shelter veterinarians and general practitioners, focusing on strategies to improve client education, strengthen the human-animal bond, and create sustainable outcomes for adopted pets. Learners will gain a deep understanding of topics like the five freedoms of animal welfare, pathway planning, no-kill policies, vaccination guidelines, and advanced surgical techniques used in shelter settings.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Animal Protocols: Strategies for Effective Review
courses.description: This course will discuss ways an IACUC can approach protocol evaluation with concern for animal well-being and ethical costs, weighed against objectives and needs of the protocol. The course offers scenarios that illustrate types of issues that can arise during protocol evaluation and provides discussion questions to consider as a way to help to resolve the issues.

courses.title: Mastering Hematology: Beyond the Automated CBC
courses.description: This course offers a deep dive into the essentials of veterinary hematology, with a focus on improving how teams use complete blood counts and blood smear evaluations in daily practice. Participants will review the fundamentals of quantitative and qualitative bloodwork analysis, gaining a sharper understanding of cell counts, morphology, and the importance of confirming automated results. Special attention is given to common barriers such as time, confidence, and workflow pressures, with practical strategies to address these challenges and elevate diagnostic quality. Learners will explore the evolving role of artificial intelligence, specifically through the VetScan Imagyst platform, which enhances blood smear interpretation and streamlines case management. By the end of this section, veterinary professionals will better understand how to combine technology, teamwork, and clinical reasoning for stronger diagnostic outcomes.

courses.title: Pain is a Team Sport: The Vital Role of Technicians in Alleviating Pain
courses.description: Pain is a Team Sport: The Vital Role of Technicians in Alleviating Pain is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Mitral Valve Disease in Dogs: From Early Detection to First-Line Therapy
courses.description: Mitral Valve Disease in Dogs: From Early Detection to First-Line Therapy is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Pain Management in Laboratory Animals
courses.description: The evaluation of pain has become a routine requirement in proper patient care, as important and basic as traditional vital signs of temperature, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and heart rate. As research animals are required to have care that is consistent with veterinary medicine standards, the prevention and alleviation of pain has become an important principle in the humane care of research animals. This course is specifically concerned with the R of refinement; that is, reducing to a minimum the pain and distress experienced by those animals used in research procedures.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Introduction to Horses
courses.description: This course will provide essential information about using horses in research settings. If you are responsible for handling horses or if you must write an animal use protocol that involves horses, this course will provide you with the basic information you need to work with this species.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Introduction to Nonhuman Primates
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to working with nonhuman primates in a research environment. The topics covered will include regulatory coverage, zoonotic hazards, housing requirements, anesthesia, pain management, and support care and monitoring.

courses.title: Equine Lameness Overview
courses.description: This course provides a first-year graduate-level review of equine lameness, covering common causes, diagnostic techniques, and treatment approaches. The course is designed to enhance veterinary professionals' understanding of lameness evaluation, including the use of nerve blocks, imaging modalities, and therapeutic/rehabilitation strategies. Key topics include foot pain conditions (e.g., sole abscesses, laminitis, and navicular syndrome); soft tissue injuries affecting tendons and ligaments; degenerative joint disease; and fractures. Participants gain practical insights into recognizing and addressing lameness in equine patients, making use of advanced diagnostic tools and therapeutic interventions.

courses.title: Equine Reproduction Part 2: Foaling and Post-partum Issues
courses.description: This course provides a review of equine foaling: normal and the most common complications (abortion, dystocia, and red bag delivery) and common postpartum emergencies (uterine artery rupture, retained placenta, and endometritis). Participants learn to diagnose and manage these conditions with discussion of clinical approaches. The course emphasizes rapid decision-making, emergency interventions, and long-term reproductive management strategies for affected mares. This course enhances the ability to prevent, diagnose, and treat life-threatening reproductive emergencies in equine practice.

courses.title: Equine Reproduction Part 1: Overview of Equine Reproduction and Pregnancy
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of equine reproduction, covering fundamental and advanced concepts related to the estrous cycle, breeding management, pregnancy maintenance, and late-term complications. Participants will gain expertise in estrous cycle physiology, hormonal manipulation, pregnancy diagnosis, and the most frequently seen late-reproductive disorders such as placentitis, hydrops conditions, and uterine torsion. This course emphasizes practical approaches to managing equine fertility and reproductive emergencies.

courses.title: Porcine Respiratory Conditions
courses.description: This course provides a review of the most common respiratory diseases in swine, focusing on their pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic techniques, and management strategies. Attendees learn about major viral and bacterial respiratory pathogens, including porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS), influenza A, porcine circovirus type 2 (PCV2), Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae, atrophic rhinitis, and Actinobacillus suis. Special emphasis is placed on differentiating clinical signs, interpreting necropsy findings, and implementing biosecurity and vaccination protocols to mitigate disease impact. The course equips participants with practical knowledge to effectively diagnose, prevent, and manage respiratory diseases in swine herds.

courses.title: Canine Endocrine Disease and Immune-Mediated Hemolytic Anemia
courses.description: This course covers the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management of several key endocrine and hematologic conditions encountered in canine veterinary practice, including immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA), Hyperadrenocorticism (Cushing disease), hypothyroidism, and diabetes mellitus. Participants learn to recognize clinical signs, interpret diagnostic tests, and implement effective treatment strategies. The program also highlights critical considerations for differentiating between overlapping conditions and managing complex cases.

courses.title: Epidemiology part 1: sensitivity/specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value
courses.description:
This course provides an engaging and accessible overview of essential epidemiology concepts used in clinical practice.
Participants gain confidence in performing fundamental epidemiological calculations, including sensitivity, specificity,
predictive values, and prevalence-based problem solving. Using real-life examples, analogies, and simplified methods,
this session helps demystify epidemiology for veterinary professionals.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Working with Controlled Substances
courses.description: The Working with Controlled Substances course is designed for those who will be using controlled substances in the laboratory or animal facility, or for those who will be responsible for their use. The use of controlled substances is highly regulated. The federal Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is authorized to enforce the Controlled Substances Act (CSA) and the controlled substance regulations, which specify the proper use of controlled substances in the medical and research fields. This course will help you understand both the security required to store and dispense these substances, recordkeeping requirements, and how to properly dispose of these substances.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Medical Records
courses.description: Animals used for research, teaching, or testing purposes are regulated by agencies that monitor the welfare of the animals. Appropriate, accurate, and complete medical records are an integral part of ensuring that the animals are treated in a humane and purposeful manner. Application of performance standards within medical record programs allows the research institution to ensure that the research animals receive the highest level of care available. This course will provide a brief overview of medical records for animals used in research and laboratory settings. This course will review important regulations governing animal research and will provide suggestions on how to keep accurate and complete medical records.

courses.title: AAHA Palliative Care Certificate Program
courses.description: AAHA Palliative Care Certificate Program is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: AAHA Nutrition Guidelines Certificate Course
courses.description: AAHA Nutrition Guidelines Certificate Course is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Introduction to Cattle
courses.description: While cattle are more commonly used in agricultural research, they also play a role in biomedical research. Working with cattle may present a challenge to researchers; but with proper training, studies involving cattle can be productive. This course will provide training for individuals working with cattle in research. It will cover topics such as research mandates, occupational health, housing, routine care, handling, detecting pain and distress, research procedures, and euthanasia.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Large Animal Surgery: Aseptic Technique and Anesthesia
courses.description: The Large Animal Surgery course provides information about surgery on larger species, such as goats, sheep, pigs, cattle, and horses. Some principles are the same as for smaller species, e.g., aseptic technique. However, large body size and species-specific physiology present unique challenges for performing surgery.

courses.provider: ANIMAL & VETERINARY LEGAL SERVICES, PLLC, SARAH L. BABCOCK
courses.title: Controlled Substance and Opioid Awareness: Michigan Mandatory CE
courses.description: The course will provide continuing education on opioids and other controlled substances. The comprehensive training includes the specific content needed to satisfy Michigan R. 338.3135 for licensees on opioids and controlled substance awareness in a convenient online and on-demand format. This program offers Michigan veterinarian's, and their support team, online continuing education on the following topics: the schedule and use of opioids and other controlled substances; integration of treatments; alternative of treatments for pain management; counseling clients on the proper use, storage and disposal practices; the risks associated with using opioids and other controlled substances; the stigma of addiction; state and federal laws pertaining to prescribing and dispensing controlled substances; utilizing the Michigan Automated Prescription System (MAPS); security features for a safety and compliance plan; and proper disposal requirements for both patient prescriptions and the veterinarian's inventory. This course is also approved by both VHMA and the Michigan Veterinary Medical Association.

courses.title: Top Ten Reportable Diseases: What Every Veterinarian Should Know
courses.description: This course highlights ten of the most critical reportable diseases encountered in veterinary medicine, with a focus on conditions that are zoonotic, economically significant, or clinically confusing. Participants will learn not only how to recognize these diseases, but also how and when to report them in accordance with North American public health regulation. Key topics include diagnostic clues, legal considerations, and disease control strategies. The course also covers top prohibited drugs in food animals.

courses.title: Equine Respiratory Disease (Upper and Lower Respiratory Tract) and Sinus Disorders: Diagnosis, Treatment, and Case Management
courses.description: This course offers an exploration of commonly seen equine respiratory disorders. The presenter reviews a spectrum of conditions, including viral upper respiratory infections, strangles, guttural pouch conditions, sinusitis, pneumonia, and equine asthma, and helps to differentiate their clinical presentations. Participants gain insight into routine and advanced diagnostics (e.g., PCR, endoscopy, thoracic ultrasound, radiography, CT, tracheal wash, and bronchoalveolar lavage), development of therapeutic strategies (from supportive care and antimicrobials to surgical interventions), and understand key biosecurity and management protocols essential for optimal patient outcomes.

courses.title: Native American and Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: In today's diverse world, it's crucial for veterinary professionals to have a deep understanding of cultural sensitivities and inclusivity to provide the best care for all clients, including Native American communities. This module will explore various facets of this intersection between Native American culture and veterinary medicine. By exploring respectful language and cultural awareness, client engagement techniques and how to build an inclusive practice we will explore best practice for inclusivity and equity for both clients and colleagues.

courses.title: Small ruminant common conditions
courses.description: This course provides an overview of common small ruminant diseases with clinical relevance to field and hospital settings. Key topics include diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of urolithiasis, pregnancy toxemia, contagious skin conditions (contagious ecthyma (orf) and caseous lymphadenitis (CL)), and neurologic diseases (caprine arthritis encephalitis (CAE), polioencephalomalacia, listeriosis). With an emphasis on clinical signs, practical diagnostics, and management decisions, this session is geared toward improving outcomes in both commercial and companion settings.

courses.title: IV Fluid Therapy: Part 2
courses.description: This course focuses on the safe and effective administration of IV fluid therapy in small animal patients, with particular emphasis on assessing fluid responsiveness, adjusting fluid plans based on real-time clinical data, and using tools such as lactate monitoring, PCV/TS, and urine output to guide therapy. Real-world case examples highlight how to manage complex fluid therapy in patients with shock, dehydration, fluid overload, or high ongoing losses. The presenter also discusses special considerations for cats, calculating fluid rates based on ins-and-outs, and the art of making dynamic clinical decisions.

courses.title: Aquaculture part 1: Infectious diseases of fish
courses.description: This course provides an overview of common infectious diseases affecting both freshwater and marine fish, emphasizing practical diagnostic approaches and clinical decision-making. Participants will learn about parasitic, bacterial, and viral diseases, including those most likely to be encountered in aquaculture, aquarium, and zoological settings. Special attention is given to life cycle patterns, diagnostic techniques, zoonotic concerns, treatment limitations, and regulatory considerations.

courses.title: Rabies Compliance Made Clear: Protecting Pets, Clients, and Clinics
courses.description: Rabies remains one of the most consequential diseases for veterinary professionals, carrying profound clinical, legal, and financial implications. In this course, Dr. Richard Ford explores the evolving landscape of rabies vaccination, importation regulations, and public health mandates with clarity and authority.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Colony Management I: Breeding and Recordkeeping
courses.description: This course provides information for researchers, animal technicians, and facility managers who are getting ready to start a colony, would like to review the basics of mouse breeding, or want to find ways to improve their breeding program. In this course, we have presented the most basic information you will need to manage a mouse colony while adhering to federal and institutional policies and mandates for ethical treatment of the animals in your care. Good recordkeeping in the colony and clear communication with the investigators are both absolutely essential to running an efficient colony, where the production of unwanted mice is minimized while the needs of the investigator are met in a timely fashion.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Occupational Health and Safety in the Care and Use of Research Animals
courses.description: Occupational Health and Safety in the Care and Use of Research Animals is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Creating Individualized Feline Vaccine Protocols
courses.description: Creating Individualized Feline Vaccine Protocols is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Top Causes of Canine Vomiting: Pancreatitis, Parvovirus, and Megaesophagus
courses.description: This presentation delves into key diagnostic and treatment challenges associated with vomiting dogs commonly faced in veterinary practice, including differentiating vomiting from regurgitation. The speaker covers the diagnosis and management of pancreatitis, parvovirus, and megaesophagus.

courses.title: Equine Neurological Disorders: Part 3
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of equine vector-borne viral encephalitis, focusing on the four most common causes in the continental United States: West Nile virus, Eastern equine encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalitis virus, and rabies virus. Participants learn about the pathophysiology, epidemiology, and clinical signs of these diseases, as well as differential diagnoses. The course also covers diagnostic approaches, treatment strategies, prognosis, and prevention, including vaccination protocols and vector control. This program enhances diagnostic reasoning and case management skills in equine neurology.

courses.title: The Bottom Line is Color Blind: The Case for Diversity in Veterinary Leadership
courses.description:
When you are a member of a profession in which you are truly a minority and almost invisible, opportunities for leadership are not often seen or offered. Minorities are not often sought after for leadership roles at any level of the profession. This is not only a routine phenomenon of veterinary
medicine but is more pronounced due to diminished representation.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals 8th Edition (2011)
courses.description: This course takes an in-depth look at the Guide and covers its content in detail chapter by chapter. Chapters of the Guide include Key Concepts, Animal Care and Use Program, Environment, Housing, and Management, Veterinary Care, and Physical Plant. The main objective of the Guide is to provide information to institutions in maintaining high-quality research programs, and to enhance animal well-being, the quality of research, and the advancement of science.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Incident Planning and Response within the Animal Biocontainment Facility
courses.description:
This course discusses preparing for, responding to, and recovering from a hazardous incident in the animal biocontainment facility. As with the rest of the courses in the Animal Biosafety Training Program, it focuses on ABSL-2 and ABSL-3 only. An incident could range from a small problem that can be handled quickly to large natural disasters requiring a major response.
When hazardous incidents occur, personnel must first ensure safety of staff working in and around the area, and then be able to intervene quickly to minimize pain and distress to the animals, control or prevent release of biohazardous materials, and minimize or prevent damage to the facility. This course focuses on the special considerations of responding to incidents within the animal biocontainment facility. It does not cover the details of creating a general disaster plan.

courses.title: Purposeful Leadership: Cultivating an environment founded in diversity, equity, inclusion, & belonging (DEIB)
courses.description:
Veterinary medicine is experiencing a turning point - historically our profession has been impactful in providing exceptional medical and surgical care for our patients but in doing so we have overlooked a critical component - it's people. We have not prioritized diversity, equity, inclusion or belonging (DEIB), in our daily practice and that has directly influenced our work norms and culture. Veterinary medicine also continues to be one of the least diverse professions in the United States. We must acknowledge that it leaves us culturally inept to diagnose and treat our patients when barriers exist. In 2021, the AVMA published, "Are we in a veterinary workforce crisis?" which highlighted stressors afflicting veterinary professionals that lead to twice the turnover than medical doctors and other health professions. Veterinary professionals and teams are faced with mental health issues (anxiety, stress, burnout), staggering income:debt ratio and poor work-life balance, which influence their work environments.
A cultural renovation is needed within our profession, and this can begin as early as veterinary school. Academic institutions have the ability to prioritize and infuse DEIB in practice daily within their curricula, additional training, outreach and within their teaching hospitals. This will generate future veterinary professionals that will have the cultural humility to engage with the diversity of the people and animals we serve. Today's students are veterinary medicine's future potential specialists, practice owners, and industry leaders who can intrinsically motivate and positively influence the relationships veterinary medicine will have in our communities when cultivating a DEIB founded environment.

courses.title: Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging
courses.description: In a rapidly evolving world and workforce, promoting diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB) is critical for fostering a vibrant and engaged veterinary community. We will dive into what DEIB looks like in the veterinary space and how an environment of belonging fosters innovation, improves patient care, enhances client satisfaction, and ultimately contributes to the overall success of a veterinary practice.

courses.title: LGBTQIA+ & Allyship
courses.description: This course introduces the breakdown of Gender Identity, Gender Expression, Sexuality, and Biological sex; Pronouns and misgendering; and how to be an active ally.

courses.title: Golden Years: Managing Cognitive Decline in Pets
courses.description: Cognitive dysfunction is an often-overlooked challenge in aging dogs and cats, yet it significantly impacts both patients and owners. This course provides veterinary professionals with a thorough understanding of how to recognize, diagnose, and manage age-related cognitive decline. Learners will explore the clinical signs, differential diagnoses, and validated assessment tools that support accurate evaluation.

courses.title: Shelter Behavior Medicine Journal
courses.description:
This course provides veterinary professionals and certified animal behavior specialists with evidence-informed, practical protocols for managing behavioral conditions in shelter dogs and cats through
psychopharmacology and reward-based behavior modification. Participants will explore behavior modification category classifications (Levels 1-3) for conditions including generalized anxiety, separation anxiety, noise sensitivity, fear, resource guarding, and long-term residency deterioration in both canine and feline patients.
Topics include pharmacological selection criteria (daily vs. situational medications), dosing protocols for commonly used behavior drugs in dogs and cats (including SSRIs, benzodiazepines, Gabapentin, Trazodone, Clonidine, and Acepromazine), nutraceutical supplementation, serotonin syndrome recognition and management, the Chill Protocol, pre-euthanasia sedation considerations, and post-
adoption medication and behavior support. The course also addresses the collaborative responsibilities of veterinary and training/behavior teams, objective behavioral documentation, and adopter communication best practices.
Learning Objectives:
1. Classify shelter animals into appropriate behavior modification categories and levels (1, 2, or 3) for dogs and cats based on behavioral presentation and history.
2. Differentiate between daily and situational behavior medications and apply a systematic decision-making framework to select the most appropriate pharmaceutical intervention for a given patient.
3.Identify correct dosing ranges, onset times, key indications, and contraindications for commonly used behavior medications in dogs and cats, including Alprazolam, Clonidine, Fluoxetine, Sertraline, Gabapentin, Trazodone, and Acepromazine.
4. Recognize signs of serotonin syndrome and apply an appropriate emergency response protocol, including discontinuation and treatment drugs.
5. Describe the multimodal Chill Protocol (Gabapentin, Melatonin, Acepromazine,Trazodone)

courses.title: Veterinary Herbal Medicine Online
courses.description:
Chinese Herbal Medicine (CHM) is a major branch of Chinese Medicine. Although most associate Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) with acupuncture, the majority of cases in TCM clinics in China are treated with herbs, either with acupuncture or alone, rather than with just acupuncture. In the States, more and more TVCM practitioners are following suit by incorporating herbs in their veterinary practice. CHM therapies have their historical origins with TCM and date back 4,000 years. Herbs today are prepared with the benefits of modern technology but are still guided by the historical wisdom underlying TCM. In CHM practice, herbs are used to correct imbalance underlying a disease pattern and to promote the body's ability to heal itself. Each herb has a different effect on the body and can fall under a number of classifications such as warming, cooling, sour, or bitter and can affect a variety of organs, including the liver, lungs, or heart. TCVM utilizes herbal formulas that are a combination of single-herb ingredients to treat a specific pattern of disease.
The increasing popularity of CHM lies in the fact that it is an all-natural treatment option that is generally safe and effective when prescribed correctly. An extensive body of clinical research has shown CHM to be extremely effective in treating chronic veterinary medical issues in the fields of gastroenterology, cardiology, dermatology, endocrinology, reproduction, oncology, and animal behavior. CHM is also commonly used to treat respiratory issues and sports injuries. In addition, CHM increases the quality of life for geriatric patients, especially those diagnosed with terminal cancer, as it assists the body's ability to reduce tumor size when chemotherapy may not an option. CHM can be combined with acupuncture and/or Western Medicine to enhance clinical results.

courses.title: Psychological Health & Safety in Veterinary Hospitals
courses.description:
Psychological health and safety can be best understood as a workplace that actively works to prevent psychological harm to its employees and when harm occurs, it has the knowledge, skills, and capacity to address it. While traditional definitions of workplace safety have focused on preventing and addressing physical harm, there is now a greater appreciation that people deserve workplaces that are actively working to reduce psychological and emotional harm so they can work with greater comfort, safety, and confidence. This has a direct correlation with individual professional quality of life, healthy team dynamics and functioning hospitals with improved relationships and retention.
This session will explore the psychosocial factors required to improve professional quality of life including but not limited to organizational norms (clear leadership & expectations, employee involvement & engagement, work-life balance), ways of relating to one another (respect, equity, recognition & reward), and supports provided by employers (growth & development, workload management, psychological/social protection & support).

courses.title: Large Animal Emergency Response
courses.description:
Participants are trained to safely approach and contain large animals in emergencies from escaped horses to overturned tractors. Topics include:
Equipment Used in Large Animal Response
Slides, slip sheets, hobbles, straps, hooks and supporting hardware
Ropes and rigging for large animal response
Using mechanical equipment to assist in animal movement
Complex system creation to move animals and hazards
Equine and Farm Facilities and biosecurity
Pre-Incident Planning
Incident Command
Safe Horse Handling
Equine Behavior and Reading a Horse
Using a glide, glide belts, forward and rear pull

courses.title: AAHA Selected Endocrinopathies Guidelines Certificate Course
courses.description: The AAHA Selected Endocrinopathies Guidelines Certificate Course provides veterinary professionals with the essential knowledge and useful skills to effectively diagnose, treat, and manage common endocrine diseases in dogs and cats. Anchored in the 2023 AAHA Selected Endocrinopathies of Dogs and Cats Guidelines, the course offers a step-by-step, categorical approach to navigating endocrine cases most often seen in real-life practice. Through interactive modules and clinical case studies, learners will gain a thorough understanding of the clinical presentation and effective management strategies for these common and often challenging disorders.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: Laboratory Animal Allergy
courses.description: In the laboratory animal facility, exposure to allergens resulting from direct or indirect contact with animals is a significant concern for institutional occupational health and safety programs. However, there are many ways to prevent allergen exposure and minimize the risk of developing LAA. Environmental controls, work practices, and the use of PPE are all ways to control exposure to animal allergens.

courses.title: Strategies for a Successful Team Culture- Empathic Tools Toward Being, Building, & Belonging
courses.description: This course discusses the components of empathic leadership and the importance of fostering an environment of individuality, team collaboration, and community interfacing to promote a healthy and positive workplace culture through a concept centered on being, building, and belonging.

courses.title: Industry is NOT Destiny - Addressing Toxic Culture in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This course discusses five components leading to a toxic culture and touches on where we are today in veterinary medicine and how to identify the source of the issue. Students will learn about the importance of general wellness in the daily practice and how DEIB can help transform an unhealthy environment into a positive one. This course will cover the basic pillars of building relationships, leadership, educate/equity, navigate the unknown and diversity, inclusion and belonging.

courses.title: Seamless Referrals, Stronger Outcomes: Building Better Collaboration in Practice
courses.description: As referral volume and case complexity grow, veterinary teams must collaborate across specialties with greater coordination, empathy, and communication. This course presents the AAHA Referral Guidelines as a modern framework for navigating today's increasingly specialized care landscape. Participants will learn how to deliver client centered, well structured referrals that reduce delays, build client trust, and improve medical outcomes. The content walks through the referral lifecycle from initiating the conversation, to managing expectations, to follow up communication and emphasizes practical steps for integrating these practices into daily workflows.

courses.title: Top Ten Fallacies About Becoming a Practice Owner - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Being a small business owner comes with its list of challenges once you own the hospital. When it comes to owning a veterinary hospital there are a number of speed bumps, myths, or fallacies that frequently dissuade a potential entrepreneur from even considering taking a dive into practice ownership. From economically based concerns to time management concerns; from competition to cost; to imposter syndrome and debt; there is no shortage of mis-information and dis-information that need to be addressed.

courses.title: Front Desk as the Heartbeat of Client Retention: Training Your Team to Connect, Not Just Schedule ON DEMAND
courses.description: The front desk is far more than a scheduling hub, it is the emotional engine of your practice. In this session, we'll reframe the receptionist's role from administrative gatekeeper to the primary architect of client loyalty. By mastering the art of high-impact first impressions and empathetic communication, your front-of-house team can turn routine inquiries into lifelong relationships. We will explore how to move beyond "checking in" to truly "connecting," ensuring every client feels heard, valued, and understood. Transform your team into retention experts who drive hospital growth through the power of genuine human connection

courses.title: Advanced Practice Seminar - Anesthesia and CPR
courses.description:
The VetnCare Advanced Practice Seminar on Anesthesia and CPR is designed for both RVTs and DVMs
who want to get to the next level of expertise in veterinary anesthesia and emergency resuscitation.
Participants can expect robust theoretical content prior to the event, then problem based learning
combined with practical application of skills on the day, including emergency and CPR simulations under
the guidance of experienced supervisors.

courses.title: Don't Make These 10 Practice Ownership Mistakes Learn From Our Experiences
courses.description: Learn from the hard-earned lessons of experienced practice owners Dr. Peter Weinstein and Dr. Natalie Marks as they share the top 10 mistakes they made and how you can avoid them. From financial pitfalls to leadership missteps, this candid conversation will provide actionable insights to help you build a thriving, well-managed veterinary practice. Whether you're considering ownership or looking to improve your current practice, you'll leave with practical strategies to make smarter decisions and sidestep common challenges.

courses.title: Leading the Way to Practice Ownership
courses.description: The Veterinary Ownership Advocate (VOA) program, spearheaded by industry veterans and practice owners Drs. Peter Weinstein and Dan Markwa, is a comprehensive virtual education platform designed to fill the gap in business, leadership, and financial training for veterinarians. This program guides aspiring practice owners through the nuances of starting or buying a veterinary practice, emphasizing the development of essential skills for independent success. VOA prepares veterinarians to navigate today's competitive environment and build thriving practices.

courses.title: Introverts as Practice Owners: The How-To Guide - ON DEMAND
courses.description: In this one hour virtual live webinar, Dr. Natalie Marks and Dr. Peter Weinstein will explore two common adjectives that describe many veterinary professionals today introverts and perfectionists. They will explain why these personality traits can be valuable assets for leaders and veterinary practice owners by turning temperament into an advantage. We will reframe introversion as calm authority and deep listening, and perfectionism as high standards and systems thinking while addressing common pitfalls like overcontrol, analysis paralysis, and burnout. Attendees will learn practical tools such as a decision matrix to speed up choices, good enough thresholds and 80 20 rules, SOP and checklist development, and strategies to maintain quality without micromanaging. The session will cover hiring for complementary strengths, building psychological safety, and using feedback loops, conflict scripts, and meeting cadences to protect focus. Finally, attendees will gain insights on how to delegate confidently, align the team, enhance medical and client experiences, and lead with quiet, sustainable excellence.

courses.title: The Foundational Anesthesia Training Course
courses.description: This comprehensive training program equips veterinary professionals with the knowledge and skills to confidently manage anesthesia in various clinical settings. The program uses an evidence-based approach to enhance staff understanding and adherence to veterinary anesthesia fundamentals, including the anesthesia machine and equipment, protocol planning, perianesthetic management, and monitoring. Participants will develop a deep understanding of anesthesia machine functionality, protocol development, and evidence-based monitoring techniques through engaging lectures, interactive discussions, hands-on demonstrations, and real-world case examples. The program will also encourage a critical thinking approach to collaboration and case management between the technician and primary clinician.

courses.title: Oral Surgery 1 Oral Pathology Oral Radiology
courses.description: Through presentations using a multitude of clinical images, interactive lecturing , video technique presentations and intensive hands-on wet labs, class participants will effectively learn how to recognize normal versus disease states and employ the most current techniques in their treatment. Intraoral radiographic skill in reading and technique is the foundation of diagnosis and treatment of oral disease. It is to this end that participants will be thoroughly grounded in this discipline through a multitude of clinical case studies. Videography of surgical extractions in the cat and dog and the step by step techniques in approaching the various teeth by creating pedicle flaps will be meticulously explained in order to enhance the practitioners ability to immediately apply them in their practices.

courses.title: Hidden Infections, Better Detection: Unlocking the Power of Coproantigen Testing in Screening Populations
courses.description: This presentation explores the importance of routine fecal parasite screening and emphasizes the enhanced diagnostic value of coproantigen testing compared to traditional centrifugal fecal flotation. It highlights how antigen testing detects infections earlier including during the prepatent period and identifies significantly more clinically relevant parasites in both dogs and cats. Findings from a large retrospective study of more than 898,000 samples demonstrated that coproantigen testing provided the most actionable results and rarely missed infections that flotation alone detected. The session also reviews treatment-impacted decision making, zoonotic risks, parasite-specific trends, and guidelines for follow-up and retesting. Coproantigen testing is a highly accurate, efficient, and clinically meaningful tool for parasite management in preventive care.

courses.title: Real-Time Cytology. Real Practice Power: Automated Blood Morphology and Beyond
courses.description: This presentation discusses how revolution in-house cytology and blood morphology brings diagnostic power directly into the veterinary clinic. With automated technology, practices can make faster, informed decisions. We'll explore how this shift improves efficiency, enhances care, and increases access across diverse practice settings.

courses.title: GDV: A SURGEONS PERSPECTIVE (637-37896)
courses.description: This 90 minute lecture covers gastric dilitation-volvulus from the surgeon's point of view and focuses on surgical correction of the disease. Taught by a Diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Surgeons with over 10 years of small animal emergency surgery experience, this lecture provides an overview of stabilizing GDV patients and gives detailed descriptions and video of surgical correction of GDV. Common complications such as splenectomy and gastrectomy are covered in detail as well as incisional gastropexy.

courses.title: FELINE UPPER RESPIRATORY INFECTION (637-44569)
courses.description: Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, discusses common feline upper respiratory infections (URI) and how to diagnose, treat, and manage these diseases in and out of the hospital. This lecture is 55min and will additionally cover specific infectious agents and review case studies from DoveLewis.

courses.title: TOXICITIES IN THE ER (637-37477)
courses.description: Erika Loftin, DVM, DACVECC, discusses approach, diagnosis, decontamination and treatment plans in common toxicity cases.

courses.title: Inventory Academy
courses.description: Inventory Academy is a comprehensive, self-paced training program designed to equip veterinary support staff with the tools and knowledge needed to take control of inventory management. Through engaging video lessons, downloadable resources, and practical assignments, participants will learn proven strategies to reduce costs, streamline processes, and create a more efficient and profitable practice. Whether you are brand new to inventory or looking to level up your skills, this course empowers you to act with confidence.

courses.title: Clinical Cardiology in General Practice
courses.description: This session provides a practical approach to managing cardiac patients in general practice, emphasizing collaboration between primary care veterinarians and specialists through the Triad of Care model. Participants will learn to recognize cases that warrant referral or advanced diagnostics and to apply evidence-based strategies for the chronic management of congestive heart failure (CHF) in dogs and cats. The course also addresses co-management of concurrent renal disease, prevention of thromboembolic complications, and updates on emerging therapies- such as sirolimus for feline hypertrophic cardiomyopathy for situations where referral is not possible.

courses.title: Doesnt Every Cat Vomit?
courses.description: A case-based approach to acute and chronic feline pancreatitis discussing presentation, clinical signs, diagnostic options, treatment and management . The content will discuss challenges with diagnosis and considerations around when and how to treat this disease in both acute and chronic phases, as well as the impact of concurrent diseases related to diagnosis and management of patient outcomes.

courses.title: The Canine Thyroid Puzzle: Optimizing Diagnosis of Thyroid Disease
courses.description: IDEXX Learning Center 1 hour long recorded webinar about the diagnosis and management of diseases of the canine thyroid. This will cover basic thyroid pathophysiology, testing options, results interpretation and treatment. Case examples will be used to go through these steps.

courses.title: Diabetes, the Glycocalyx, and Kidney Disease: Mechanisms to Clinical Management in Small Animals
courses.description: This integrated session explores in separate lectures the pathophysiology and clinical implications of diabetic kidney disease in humans, dogs, and cats and introduce current understanding of the endothelial glycocalyx. Dr. Matthew Butler will introduce the endothelial glycocalyx, its role in vascular and glomerular health, and its potential as a therapeutic target. Dr. Natalie Finch will focus on diabetic nephropathy, highlighting glomerular ultrastructural changes and whether these are present in dogs and cats. Together, these talks bridge cutting-edge research with practical clinical applications.

courses.title: Anesthetic Plan Creation
courses.description:
This program will detail the process for creating individualized and multi-modal
anesthetic plans for cats and dogs. The lecture will start with pre-procedure considerations (e.g. patient
assessment, patient optimization/stabilization, goals of anesthesia, and pre-visit pharmaceuticals). From
there, the lecture will outline commonly utilized drugs and drug dosages for the four phases of general
anesthesia (preanesthesia, induction, maintenance, and recovery). Finally, audience members will be
given the opportunity to create hypothetical anesthetic plans based on real world patients.

courses.title: The Role of Biochemistry Panels in the Minimum Database Part II of the Veterinary Technicians Learning Journey
courses.description: The biochemistry panel is made up of tests that reflect the activity and function of many internal organs. When paired with electrolytes, the biochemistry panel can offer insights into the patients health that extend well beyond the physical exam, so it is a key component of the laboratory minimum database for sick and apparently healthy pets. This self guided course will use an organ system approach to study the biochemistry panel and begin to integrate findings with hematology and urinalysis results. Veterinary technicians guide quality and output of laboratory results, so we will reinforce best laboratory practices to optimize results. Learners will progress from patient preparation through sample acquisition to in house sample processing or reference laboratory submission.

courses.title: Therapeutic Apheresis in Veterinary Medicine: Current Evidence and Clinical Applications for the Specialist
courses.description: Therapeutic apheresis encompassing therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE), double filtration plasmapheresis (DFPP), cytapheresis, cytokine adsorption, and immunoadsorption has emerged as a viable extracorporeal treatment modality in small animal medicine. This lecture provides a comprehensive, evidence-based review of the current veterinary literature, translational extrapolation from human medicine guidelines (ASFA 9th Edition, 2023; EXTRIP workgroup), indications by disease category, patient selection criteria, technical considerations, and the horizon of emerging applications.

courses.title: Ear Infection Essentials: An Expert-Backed Guide to Otitis Externa
courses.description: This 3-hour self-paced, online course provides an evidence-based, practical approach to diagnosing and managing otitis externa in dogs. Built around Dr. Meagan Painter's Inflammation First philosophy and the Four Pillar Framework, this course reframes otitis as an inflammatory condition, not just an infectious one. Topics include understanding primary causes, mastering cytology, appropriate use of culture, treatment selection, and client communication. The course is delivered as a non-interactive distance program with embedded quizzes to reinforce learning.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: DIAGNOSTIC MUSCULOSKELETAL ULTRASOUND (197-35962)
courses.description: Diagnostic Musculoskeletal Ultrasound will focus on how ultrasound can be used to make musculoskeletal diagnoses more precisely, accurately and efficiently. Basic skills in ultrasonographic assessment will be covered as well as how findings can be applied clinically. This will enable a more targeted treatment approach to patients suffering from soft tissue injuries such as Achilles tendinopathy and iliopsoas myotendinopathy. The course will include live dog labs, lectures, and hands-on experience with ultrasound.

courses.title: GETTING FAMILIAR WITH THE URINALYSIS: INTERPRETING AND UNDERSTANDING THE URINALYSIS AS PART OF THE M (21-42969)
courses.description: GETTING FAMILIAR WITH THE URINALYSIS: INTERPRETING AND UNDERSTANDING THE URINALYSIS AS PART OF THE M (21-42969) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Anesthetic Considerations for Patients with Respiratory Disease
courses.description:
This program will review general anesthetic considerations for small animal
patients with respiratory disease. The lecture will begin with a brief overview of the respiratory system.
After that, common respiratory monitoring modalities will be discussed. Finally, both general and
specific anesthetic recommendations for this subset of patients will be provided and discussed.

courses.title: Hematology at a Glance: What Are You Missing without a CBC?
courses.description: The complete blood count (CBC) is a common diagnostic test; however, many times, is not included in the minimum database. This webinar will provide a rapid overview of the CBC, emphasizing what information is lost when it's not included in screening healthy animals and evaluating sick patients. The CBC is highly sensitive for identifying underlying illness, characterizing severity of disease, and providing objective information regarding the progression/regression of disease.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Canine Sports Medicine
courses.description: This three (3) day course offers both foundational and advanced knowledge about canine sporting dogs. You will learn from the world-renowned specialist Dr. Chris Zink through lectures and extensive hands-on labs. Class sessions will include observing athletic events in conjunction with the 2025 National Specialty Border Collies Society of America competition event at Purina Farms, with Dr. Zink providing narration and insights during the events. This is an incredible opportunity for those looking to enhance their skills in evaluating and treating canine athletes.

courses.title: Coproantigen Testing in Population Screening: Insights from a Fecal Dx Antigen Testing Retrospective Study
courses.description: In this session, Dr. Wade Burton will discuss a recently published retrospective clinical data study comparing fecal antigen testing and centrifugal fecal flotation. Dr. Burton will present the details of the study and the clinical utility of this study in practice. Further, Dr. Burton will review the benefits of testing with Fecal Dx antigen testing

courses.title: Radiation Safety - Texas
courses.description:
Sage Radiation Safety - Texas is a self-paced, online radiation safety and compliance course for veterinary technicians, veterinary students, and veterinarians who operate or assist with radiation-producing imaging equipment. The course addresses radiation safety fundamentals, imaging modality awareness, equipment terminology, and Texas-specific compliance requirements. Knowledge checks and a final examination are included to verify learner understanding.
At Sage Veterinary Imaging, we are passionate about imaging, and even more passionate about protecting the people who use it every day. You will learn practical safety principles, get familiar with Texas regulations, and explore how each imaging modality works, from X-ray to nuclear scintigraphy. Note that we will not cover MRI or ultrasound in this course, as they do not produce ionizing radiation.

courses.title: Blood Morphology Made Practical: Turning Insight into Action
courses.description: Comprehensive hematology goes beyond CBC numbers with blood morphology providing critical and often underutilized insight into patient health. This program explores the diagnostic value of morphology in identifying clinically relevant findings across white blood cells red blood cells and platelets while highlighting how the IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer delivers standardized slide free and AI supported morphology results at the point of care to enhance accuracy and efficiency. Participants will learn practical strategies for integrating blood morphology into routine workflows including when to run morphology alongside CBCs and how to implement consistent protocols across the care team. The session will conclude with a panel discussion featuring a veterinarian practice owner and technician who will share real world experiences implementing inVue Dx offering actionable insights on improving workflow team adoption and patient care outcomes.

courses.title: Diagnosis of GI Foreign Bodies
courses.description: This presentation will provide an overview of the imaging modalities used in the identification of GI foreign bodies. Additionally, we will discuss common types of GI foreign body obstructions and how imaging modalities can be best utilized to guide diagnosis.

courses.title: Empowering veterinary front office teams through the human-animal bond
courses.description: This webinar will feature a conversation with Debbie Boone, BS, CVPM, sharing her expertise on the critical role the human-animal bond plays in veterinary practices, particularly at the front office level. Veterinary front office staff are often the first point of contact for pet owners and play a pivotal role in shaping the client experience. This webinar will highlight the importance of empathy, active listening, and clear communication in helping pet owners feel understood and supported. By recognizing the emotional connections clients have with their pets, front office teams will be able to build trust and create a more welcoming and compassionate environment. Overall, the webinar will underscore the importance of training and empowering veterinary front office teams to recognize and nurture the human-animal bond, ultimately leading to a more positive experience for both clients and pets.

courses.title: Chronic Pain in Dogs and Cats: An Integrated Approach
courses.description: Integrative pain management speaks to an overall philosophy of caring for patients with complementary therapies, beyond just conventional pharmaceuticals. Learn from Staff Veterinarian Katherine Earl, DVM, CVA, about how to identify chronic pain in our patients, while considering multiple pain-management strategies and tools for treatment.

courses.title: From Screening to Strategy: Advancing Preventive Care with Diagnostics
courses.description:
Preventive medicine is a cornerstone of high-quality veterinary care, yet it remains underutilized in many practices. This presentation explores the value of early disease detection through comprehensive diagnostic screening, including vector-borne disease testing with 4Dx and intestinal parasite screening with Fecal Dx.
Participants will learn practical strategies to better integrate preventive diagnostics into everyday workflows, improve team alignment, and effectively communicate their value to clients. By strengthening both clinical approaches and client engagement, veterinary teams can enhance patient outcomes, increase compliance, and elevate the standard of care.

courses.title: Improving Patient Care in a Radiation Safety Culture
courses.description: This presentation reviews various aspects of a radiation safety culture and how veterinary practices can manage these to better protect the health of staff, patients, and the public. Medical imaging using ionizing radiation has grown tremendously in the last 50 years and has become a go-to diagnostic tool, revolutionizing medical practice across the globe in both human and veterinary patient care. Despite this fact, many workers in the human and veterinary health care fields have little or no training in radiation safety and protection

courses.title: LIFTERS OR LEANERS (637-41547)
courses.description: The lecture is 62 minutes and consists of a CEO Ron Morgan doing a formal presentation on employee engagement. This is the second lecture in a two-part series, targeted towards new managers in the veterinary field, or individuals who have taken on management responsibilities.

courses.title: SURPRISE! THE USE OF ANESTHESIA IN THE ER AND ICU (637-38747)
courses.description: Anesthetizing less than ideal patients, whether due to the primary disease or pre-existing co-morbidities, are common cases discussed at DoveLewis. Learn the best ways to approach and devise plans for anesthetizing challenging patients and review current literature, case examples, and different approaches to critically ill patients that require anesthesia with Staff Veterinarian Katherine Earl, DVM.

courses.title: Addisons disease dont make a crisis out of diagnosis and management
courses.description: Hypoadrenocorticism is known as the great imitator because of the often intermittent and vague nature of clinical signs. The disease can also present as a life-threatening emergency requiring prompt aggressive therapy to ensure survival. This lecture will provide updated recommendations for diagnosing and managing both forms of the disease.

courses.title: HAC easy as 123 Simplifying Cushings diagnosis and management
courses.description: Managing patients with Cushings syndrome can be a challenge for clinicians in small animal practice. This interactive session will provide practitioners with updated guidelines for screening, differentiating, treating, and monitoring this disease. Common complications and comorbidities will also be addressed.

courses.title: Pragmatic Diagnostic Needs of the Veterinary Clinical Medical Oncologist
courses.description: This course equips participants with essential knowledge and skills to navigate the evolving landscape of cancer diagnostics in veterinary medicine. By exploring previous, current, and future diagnostic tools, including tests like PetDx/OncoK9, FicoCure, and Nu.Q Vet, participants will learn to evaluate and integrate diagnostic results into therapeutic decision-making. The course covers point-of-care diagnostics for specific cancers, as well as advanced technologies. With a focus on both current clinical needs and future innovations, this course prepares veterinary oncologists to effectively use diagnostic advancements to enhance cancer care in veterinary patients.

courses.title: Management of Pancreatitis in Dogs: A Tailored Approach
courses.description: Pancreatitis remains a complex and often frustrating condition in veterinary medicine, requiring a multimodal and individualized treatment approach. This session will provide veterinarians with the latest evidence-based strategies for managing pancreatitis, including fluid therapy, analgesia, nutritional support, anti-emetic therapy, and emerging therapeutics. Emphasizing a patient-centered approach, we will discuss how to tailor treatment plans based on clinical severity and patient response.

courses.title: The SDMA is normal but everything else is high: How to manage discrepant results
courses.description: Have you ever looked at your results and wondered how to explain them to your client? Or how to answer a question that you might have about one of your results? In this session well walk through some of the frequently asked questions for IDEXX renal products as well as some scenarios in which you might find yourself scratching your head. Come prepared for an interactive session involving real-life questions to some of the thorniest issues involving renal health.

courses.title: MRI Fellowship 2025
courses.description:
Course Description:
This self-paced, 5-week online MRI Fellowship is designed to provide veterinarians with an in-depth, case-based approach to MRI interpretation. Each week, participants will review five MRI cases, with each case requiring approximately one hour to analyze images and complete a structured worksheet ("practice report"). Participants will then compare their reports to a detailed "gold standard" report authored by Dr. Jaime Sage, which serves as the rubric for self-assessment and learning.
The fellowship focuses on refining interpretation skills, enhancing diagnostic accuracy, and improving clinical decision-making in veterinary MRI. Topics include MRI physics, neuroimaging, musculoskeletal imaging, and abdominal MRI. Cases are selected to cover a broad spectrum of pathology, with structured feedback guiding participants toward mastery of MRI evaluation.

courses.title: Acute Kidney Injury in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This lecture will cover the basic pathophysiology of kidney failure based on current veterinary literature, including some of the scoring systems used to help prognosticate these cases for practitioners. Special emphasis will be placed on the most common nephrotoxins in cats and dogs. Finally, we will discuss the common treatments for AKI as well as some individual therapies for specific toxins and in cases of oliguria or anuria.

courses.title: Need for Platelet Morphologic Review: True Thrombocytopenia
courses.description: The platelet count or thrombogram is one of the three components of the CBC. A platelet morphologic review is indicated to confirm true thrombocytopenia and assess for the presence of thrombopoiesis associated with pathologic consumption or destruction of platelets or their sequestration. In this second course on platelets, Doctors DeNicola, Rebar, and Metzger revisit thrombogram basics and expound upon platelet morphology using several clinical cases of thrombocytopenia. Take home expert tips on how to assess numeric data and cytograms (dot plots) from the Procyte Dx Hematology Analyzer and how to manually assess platelet morphology on a blood smear for more confident diagnoses of thrombocytopenia.

courses.title: The FeLV Lifetime Study - Decoding FeLV: From Point-of-Care to Predicting Lifespan
courses.description: Join Dr. Julie Levy and Dr. Melissa Beall as they reveal groundbreaking findings on feline leukemia virus (FeLV) diagnostics and survival outcomes. This session will transform how you interpret test results and guide clinical decisions. Bridging cutting-edge research with real-world shelter and clinical practice, the webinar equips participants with evidence-based strategies to improve care for FeLV-positive cats. Whether you manage high-volume intake or provide specialty care, youll leave with actionable tools to optimize outcomes and client communication.

courses.title: Team Communication
courses.description: This course will review all of the roles on the veterinary team and their role in team communication. We will also discuss tough topics that each role tends to deal with and how to best handle these conversations with grace and professionalism.

courses.title: The Role of Hematology in the Minimum Database- Part I of the Veterinary Technicians Learning Journey
courses.description: Hematology is a sensitive indicator of overall health and thus occupies a central role in the laboratory minimum database for sick and well pets. It is a key area where veterinary technicians guide quality and output of laboratory results. This course will build a firm foundation in the components of the CBC and reinforce best laboratory practices to optimize hematology results. Learners will progress from patient preparation through sample acquisition to in-house sample processing or reference laboratory submission.

courses.title: Calgary Veterinary Point-of-Care Ultrasound Training Academy
courses.description: "When something is visualized, the truth of its occurrence or existence can no longer be doubted - Seeing is Believing". This proverb has particular meaning when it comes point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS); diagnostic confidence increases in 89.2% of human patients when general practitioners add bedside POCUS to patient evaluation! Forget about winter, "POCUS is coming", so get ready! Recent surveys suggest 50-80% of veterinary clinics in North America have an ultrasound machine. Unfortunately, despite POCUS revolutionizing all facets of veterinary medicine, many ultrasound machines are underutilized in general small animal practice. This should not be the case! By asking clinically relevant, often binary yes/no questions, veterinary POCUS can be rapidly and efficiently learned and applied by anyone in almost any setting! So, dust off that ultrasound machine, go beyond looking for the urinary bladder to get a urine sample, and start using ultrasound to make a difference in how you manage your daily patients! This course will cover the key concepts regarding veterinary point of care ultrasound (POCUS). POCUS techniques are rapid, easy-to-learn and practical ultrasound skills that ANY practitioner can apply in everyday practice. This co-lecture series will cover the core principles to understand and interpret sonographic findings of abdominal, pleural space and lung ultrasound (PLUS), cardiac and vascular POCUS. All clinically relevant POCUS questions currently studied in veterinary medicine will be covered! Know when to ask the right question at the right time, in a binary fashion, based on patient assessment! If you own an ultrasound machine, there is no excuse to not apply these principles on a daily basis!

courses.title: Stool as a Tool A fresh look at fecal testing in companion animals
courses.description: In this session we will review the diagnostics used to routinely screen for parasites as well as options for uncovering infectious causes of diarrhea in dogs and cats. We will also review the latest publication that highlights the utility of coproantigen testing in screening populations.

courses.title: Stick to the Point: Diagnosing Skin and Subcutaneous Masses
courses.description: Review how veterinarians can optimize fine needle aspiration (FNA) diagnostics for cutaneous and subcutaneous masses in dogs and cats by selecting appropriate lesions and providing detailed clinical history and mass descriptions, while comparing FNA to alternative diagnostic methods.

courses.title: Hidden Heartbreak: Diagnosing Early Cardiac Disease
courses.description: Early cardiac disease in dogs and cats is often clinically silent yet carries meaningful implications for monitoring, anesthesia, and client education. This course reviews practical approaches to early cardiac screening, with emphasis on myxomatous mitral valve disease and cardiomyopathies. Learners will examine commonly used screening tools including biomarkers, radiographs, ECG, and echocardiography and explore how test performance, disease prevalence, and patient risk factors influence interpretation. Case examples highlight how early detection supports informed clinical decision making, even when disease progression cannot be altered.

courses.title: From Skin to Within: Canine Endocrine Disease From the Internist and Dermatologist Perspective
courses.description: Endocrine diseases in dogs often present first through changes in the skin, yet these signs can be subtle, misleading, or confounded by concurrent dermatologic conditions. This program explores canine hypothyroidism and hypercortisolism from both internal medicine and dermatology perspectives, emphasizing how cutaneous findings can guide or complicate systemic diagnosis. Participants will review hallmark and overlapping dermatologic manifestations of endocrine disease, understand how infections, demodicosis, calcinosis cutis, and allergic disease influence diagnostic interpretation, and learn practical strategies for managing both cutaneous and systemic disease simultaneously. Through case examples and comparative discussions, this session highlights how coordinated diagnostic and treatment approaches improve outcomes in dogs with endocrine disease.

courses.title: From Manual to Masterful: Analyzer-powered cytology workflows
courses.description: In this on demand discussion, Dr. Sally Ryan and Dr. Christy Michael, IDEXX Professional Services Veterinarians, explore how inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer is changing the way ear cytology and blood morphology are performed and interpreted in clinical practice. Through practical comparisons with traditional microscopy, the presenters explain how fluid based analysis, expanded sample evaluation, integrated imaging, and diagnostic considerations can support more consistent results while reinforcing the importance of clinical context and veterinary judgment. The session highlights how inVue Dx can enhance confidence, efficiency, and insight without replacing the clinician role in patient care.

courses.title: Getting Started in Medical Acupuncture and Integrative Rehabilitation - Business Tips
courses.description: This ninety-minute, recorded conversation, among three established CuraCore VET faculty, answers many questions that new graduates have as they embark on their veterinary medical acupuncture and rehabilitation careers. Course is combined with reading requirements and an assessment.

courses.title: Alfaxalone and the Veterinarian DISTANCE
courses.description: This session explores alfaxalone to help veterinarians use it safely and effectively in practice. Dr. Carolyn McKune will review its indications, pharmacology, and use across species, with focus on dosing, storage, and controlled substance rules. Attendees will learn its pros and cons in dogs, cats, and higher-risk patients (ASA III-V), including effects on cardiovascular and respiratory systems, infusion use, and recovery. The session ends with guidance on confidently integrating alfaxalone into clinical use for those familiar with propofol protocols.

courses.title: Preventive Care: Roles and Responsibilities
courses.description: This course describes the key roles and responsibilities for each member of the practice staff in implementing and delivering a successful preventive care protocol. The course also underscores the importance of educating and getting the entire team on board with preventive care to help ensure the health of patients and practice alike.

courses.title: Feline Pancreatitis Diagnosis and Treatment for Clinicians
courses.description: Feline pancreatitis is an important disease with varied presentations and outcomes. Sometimes challenging, the diagnosis is commonly based on combining clinical judgment and minimally invasive diagnostic testing results. This course will assist clinicians with recognizing common presentations and supportive laboratory findings, differentiating and interpreting available pancreatic lipase tests, and choosing additional testing to assist with diagnosis and treatment of their feline patients with acute or chronic pancreatitis.

courses.title: Module 2: Cytology In My Practice: Its That Easy!
courses.description: Establishing best practice for sample acquisition, initial evaluation and application to cancer diagnosis using cytology

courses.title: CHALLENGING URETHRAL OBSTRUCTIONS (637-36711)
courses.description: Staff surgeon Dr. Coby Richter, DVM, DACVS, gives a case based presentation that covers ruptured urethras, ruptured bladders, stones that wont budge and stones you know are there but cannot find. This discussion targets uroliths in both dogs and cats, however many of the diagnostic or treatment techniques described in this presentation would apply to other causes of urethral obstruction.

courses.title: CANINE MEGAESOPHAGUS (637-37146)
courses.description: In this 43-minute lecture, Internal Medicine Specialist Barbara Davis, DVM, DACVIM, reviews canine megaesophagus and the conditions in which it is normally characterized. Attendees will learn about the clinical signs, patient work-up, and treatment plans.

courses.title: Pancreatitis in Cats Whats New in Diagnosis and Treatment
courses.description: Feline pancreatitis remains a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge, particularly in its chronic form. This webinar will review emerging evidence on the diagnosis and management of pancreatitis in cats, with a focus on practical applications in clinical practice. Participants will learn how to integrate and interpret available diagnostic modalities to improve diagnostic accuracy, gain a clearer understanding of the expected clinical course of chronic pancreatitis, and apply current treatment strategies to optimize long-term management. This session is designed to provide clinicians with evidence-based updates and actionable guidance for improving outcomes in cats with suspected or confirmed pancreatitis.

courses.title: An interactive introduction to the Anatomy of a Canine Echocardiogram
courses.description:
This course is a collaborative effort between Kevin Hannon, PhD, and Luís Dos Santos, DVM, PhD, DACVIM (Cardiology).
This course is designed for new learners or as a refresher for experienced users. It implements 3D segmentations, CT scans, and echocardiograms to help visualize and demonstrate the underlying anatomy, spatiality, and basics of a canine echocardiogram.
After a cardiac anatomy primer, the module introduces spatial awareness exercises and quizzes to help learners understand a complete and informative echocardiogram. The user will better understand the orientation and position of the ultrasound probe used to generate a long and short-axis echocardiogram and the underlying anatomy.

courses.title: The Art of Giving Bad News
courses.description: Delivering bad news is something that we face in daily life. In veterinary medicine, bad news can range from costs of care, timelines for care, and the often-true fact that little can be done for a beloved friend. In this lecture presented by DoveLewis Director of Client Care and Patient Access Erin Erck, we will discuss how to share bad news in an effective and compassionate manner. Focusing on client communication from the time the client arrives to when they depart, we will discuss how delivering messages (good and bad) can make a lasting impression.

courses.title: GFI #256: Where Are We Now?
courses.description: For over a year, the veterinary industry has been operating under the new normal that is post FDA's Guidance for Industry GFI 256. This course covers key components of the guidance, the practical implications for veterinarians, and the necessary changes to pharmacy processes. It aims to teach veterinary professionals how to advocate for continued access to critical compounded medications and equips them with the knowledge and skills to optimize patient care and processes within their practices.

courses.title: FELINE FOCUS JOURNAL CLUB (637-41346)
courses.description: Feline Focus Journal Club is a 50 minute lecture that follows four veterinary journal research articles dealing specifically with cats. Presented by Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, the four journal articles will be analyzed for an open discussion about results and best practices.

courses.title: PULMONARY HYPERTENSION (637-35677)
courses.description: In this 55 minute lecture, Veterinary Cardiologist Caryn Reynolds, DVM, DACVIM (cardiology), reviews pulmonary hypertension in dogs. This lecture will cover the causes, diagnosis, and treatment of pulmonary hypertension for veterinarians.

courses.title: RECOGNITION AND TREATMENT OF LIFE THREATENING ELECTROLYTE DISTURBANCES (637-42655)
courses.description: This talk by DoveLewis Criticalist Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, will focus on the importance of electrolyte monitoring in the emergent patient, how to recognize a critical value and how it relates to the patient's clinical status. Urgent treatment of electrolyte disturbances will be discussed along with long term management as it relates to certain diseases. The talk will focus mainly on sodium, calcium and potassium.

courses.title: The Every Day Acupuncture Veterinary Series
courses.description: This program is an 8-session mastermind series, including an orientation and 7 learning modules, created to bridge the gap between obtaining an education in veterinary acupuncture and effectively applying this modality in a clinical setting to improve patient lives every day. The protocols and processes delivered in this program are designed to help veterinarians who have already completed basic training in veterinary acupuncture take their learning and skills to the next level. The series will provide templates, quick reference guides and mentorship geared toward moving the veterinarian into action, making everyday use of acupuncture possible and efficient even if time is short and intensity is high. In the first module, participants will learn how to set the patient and the practice up for success, including systems to reduce patient stress and strategic outlines for scheduling and charging. The next four modules will focus on acupuncture strategies, from both the Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) and Western science perspective, to achieve improved patient outcomes when facing common conditions that afflict our companion animals. The conditions of focus are as follows: osteoarthritis and chronic pain, canine allergic dermatitis, feline cystitis and urinary tract inflammation, and feline inflammatory bowel conditions. The sixth module is dedicated to approaching senior patients with multiple medical problems and TCVM patterns, including how to prioritize and treat the patient with a focus on comfort and quality of life. The last module is designed to help the veterinarian develop best business practices around acupuncture and the integrative medical model, including goal setting strategy, to ensure long term success and sustainability. The overall purpose of this program is to improve patient care with acupuncture while achieving a healthy return on investment for the veterinarian and the practice.

courses.title: Medical Recordkeeping 101
courses.description: In this course you will learn all about the requirements of the patient's medical record, how to increase your practice's efficiency with medical records, how to avoid common medical record mistakes and how to perform regular medical record audits. Lack of attention to necessary compliance with medical record requirements can be costly, damaging to patient care and lead to further complications when legal claims are made.

courses.title: Librela (bedinvetmab injection): global scientific and medical information for veterinarians
courses.description: Bedinvetmab is the first injectable monthly antibody therapy developed to alleviate/control canine OA pain.
