This presentation is intended to provide veterinarians with and overview of scientific and medical information regarding bedinvetmab from its approval through 3 years of clinical experience. Topics to be covered include what is bedinvetmab; a review of 3 years of global clinical experience, efficacy and safety data supporting bedinvetmabs clinical use.

courses.title: Paws and Reflect: Transforming Pet Health with Nutrition for Obesity, GI, and Urinary Tract Wellness
courses.description: Nutrition is truly the nucleus of everything we do as veterinary professionals. It has its challenges when making recommendations and directions. In this 1 hour medical program, veterinary professionals will gain practical insights into utilizing nutrition as a primary tool to manage obesity, gastrointestinal (GI), and urinary tract conditions in pets as we visit a veterinary clinic in Maine. Through real-life case studies, expert discussions, and interviews with veterinary support staff and doctors, the course emphasizes how a collaborative team approach, with an emphasis on nutritional therapy, can enhance patient outcomes. Sponsored by Blue Buffalo, the program delves into the roles of veterinarians, technicians, and client service representatives (CSRs) in implementing diet protocols to address common health issues. Attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating diet recommendations into clinical practice, fostering better client compliance, and improving patient health.

courses.title: Blood Smear Evaluation: A Practical Step-by-Step Guide
courses.description: Blood smears remain one of the most valuable, accessible, and cost-effective diagnostic tools in veterinary medicine. This session provides a clear, practical approach to reading and interpreting smears in everyday practice. Participants will learn how to systematically evaluate smears, recognize key morphologic changes and infectious agents, and integrate findings into the broader diagnostic process. Additional tools for morphological evaluation will also be discussed.

courses.title: It's Sedimentary - Part 1: Red Cells and white cells and bugs ... oh my!
courses.description: The complete urinalysis is a critical component of the minimum database, Dr. DeNicola will discuss why it's important to understand and accurately preform a urine sediment analysis. In part 1 of this 3 part series on urine microscopy, you will learn about the identification of red blood cells (RBCs, while blood cells (WBC's) and bacteria as well as the clinical significance of each of the patient and the possible next steps to arriving at a diagnosis.

courses.title: Exotic Animal Radiology: How to Take Diagnostic Films and Identify Common Issues
courses.description: This presentation focuses on how to get the best diagnostic films of common exotic pets, including birds, reptiles, and small mammals. We will discuss common and avoidable radiology errors as well as common disease issues in these animals.

courses.title: Suffering in Silence: approach to feline chronic triaditis
courses.description: Feline triaditis describes a syndrome characterised by the concurrent presence of pancreatitis, cholangitis, and chronic enteropathy. Its prevalence varies, but it is reported in up to 30% to 50% of cats diagnosed with pancreatitis and inflammatory liver disease. While definitive diagnosis requires histologic confirmation of inflammation in each organ, this may not be always possible. In addition, clinical suspicion can be challenging as clinical signs vary with each individual case and are often vague, nonspecific, and overlapping with other diseases, increasing the risk of this syndrome being overlooked and appropriate management being delayed. The speaker will review the pathophysiology of this disease, discuss a practical diagnostic approach and ultimately a comprehensive, evidence-based treatment strategy with the help of real case examples.

courses.title: Practice Essentials to Managing Otitis
courses.description: In this session, we will discuss primary and secondary causes of otitis externa and best practices for treatment that address not only the current infection but also predisposing or perpetuating pathology.

courses.title: Juvenile Orthopedic Disease and Trauma - On-Demand
courses.description: This seminar provides a review of juvenile orthopedic conditions, with a focus on dysplasia and incongruity of the elbow, hip, and stifle joints, highlighting areas where surgical judgment and innovation meaningfully influence outcomes. Surgeons will examine traditional principles alongside emerging concepts, using case based discussion to compare diverse operative strategies and individual treatment philosophies. Practical emphasis is placed on how surgeons adapt techniques, refine decision making, and apply their unique perspectives to optimize joint preservation in growing patients.

courses.title: Urogenital Surgery
courses.description: In this course, your learning will focus on basic urogenital surgical procedures with strong emphasis upon surgical procedures and techniques commonly used in a general practice setting. You will learn basic principles of urethral retropulsation of uroliths, cystotomy, canine urethrotomy and urethrostomy, feline perineal urethrostomy, surgical management of pyometra, cesarian section and surgery of the prostate and more.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Breaking Down Brachycephalics
courses.description: This CE will cover the need-to-knows regarding anesthetizing a brachycephalic patient. We will discuss the key features of brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS), as well as other physiologic & anatomic differences, that impact your anesthetic care.

courses.title: Managing Chronic Enteropathies in Cats
courses.description: Chronic gastrointestinal issues can be some of the most frustrating pathologies seen by veterinarians, as these cases can be difficult to manage, often require multiple therapeutic trials--all while simultaneously testing the patience of pet owners. This course is intended to provide veterinarians with a standardized approach to the diagnosis and management of chronic enteropathies in cats. Recent novel research into the dietary management of chronic enteropathy in cats will also be presented which challenges much of the conventional wisdom related to the selection of diets for dietary therapy while highlighting a remarkable success rate of simple dietary change in these patients

courses.title: Feline Lower Urinary Tract Diseases: What the 2025 iCatCare Guidelines Tell Us
courses.description: Feline lower urinary tract signs are a common reason for presentation at veterinary clinics, and recurrent signs often prompt referral/second opinion and can be frustrating for owners and vets to manage. In 2025 the iCatCare Veterinary Society published guidelines on these conditions to attempt to provide practitioners with practical information on management and to address the many myths and misunderstandings about the condition. This webinar will cover the guidelines key points, top tips and latest updates on the most common causes of lower urinary tract signs.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: THE BUSINESS OF CANINE REHABILITATION (197-37692)
courses.description: The Business of Canine Rehabilitation features three instructors, each with busy, growing, successful rehabilitation practices. Students will learn how to write a business plan that fits their finances, space, staff, and client needs. Interactive panel discussions will present strategies for achieving profitability in a canine rehabilitation practice including design, equipment selection, services/fees, operations, staffing and marketing.

courses.title: MEDICAL ERRORS (637-44567)
courses.description: The lecture is 55 minutes and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on classifying, identifying, documenting, communicating, and preventing medical errors in veterinary medicine. Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, takes this hour to discuss medical errors. She covers classification of errors, what to do when errors occur in the hospital, owner communication, and some personal examples of medical errors and how they were handled.

courses.title: Veterinary Clinical Oncology
courses.description:
This course program provides a comprehensive and clinically oriented overview of veterinary oncology for general practitioners working with dogs and cats.
Participants can expect an in-depth review of cancer biology, diagnostic approaches, staging, and treatment modalities, surgery including, chemotherapy, metronomic therapy, immunotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapies, and supportive care.The program places special emphasis on the tumors most frequently encountered in general practice addressing both canine and feline patients.
Throughout the course, attention is given not only to tumor control but also to treatment tolerability, management of adverse effects, paraneoplastic syndromes, pain control, and ethical decision-making. By the end of the program, attendees will be better equipped to diagnose cancer, discuss prognosis and treatment options with pet owners, initiate appropriate therapies, monitor response and toxicity, and prioritize patient welfare throughout the disease course.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: RECOVER CPR Guidelines
courses.description: This CE is a 2 part lecture + lab. We will discusses what the RECOVER initiative is, contents of the RECOVER Guidelines (BLS & ALS), and apply the guidelines to a mock CPR simulation durin the lab portion.

courses.title: CPCR (637-43594)
courses.description: Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, walks viewers through the basics of CPR in this lecture. This lecture covers instruction for both doctors and technicians working together, and includes a demonstration of CPR with stuffed animals. Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, (RECOVER initiative contributor) walks viewers through the basics of CPR in this lecture, then heads to the hospital floor to demonstrate the hands on skills needed to perform CPR in your hospital.

courses.title: How to Talk About Heart Failure in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This lecture presented by Caryn Reynolds, DVM, DACVIM (Cardiology) will review the general prognosis for heart failure and how to discuss this with clients. We will discuss how we work through the disease management challenges our clients face, such as medication side effects. Chronic sequelae of heart failure will be discussed as well as how we can help our clients with quality of life assessment.

courses.title: SNAP Pro Analyzer Certificate Course
courses.description:
SNAP tests from IDEXX are used by animal practices all over the world. These easy-to-use assays were created to be used on a lab bench in the practice and visually read by the veterinarian or technician.
The SNAP Pro Analyzer takes SNAP testing to the next level with an automated work flow. The SNAP Pro even snaps the test for you. All you need to do is prepare the test, slide it into the analyzer, and walk away!

courses.title: Basic and Point-of-Care Ultrasound: Abdomen, Thorax and Cardiac!
courses.description:
Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is a rapidly evolving field in veterinary medicine, especially in Emergency Medicine. Ultrasound machines are often available to practitioners, but training is lacking. There is limited training in veterinary school, and the post-graduate training is not uniform. Unfortunately, this means your brand-new shining machine may be sitting in a corner of your clinic collecting dust or being used only for cystocentesis.
In this course, you will work with experts in emergency medicine and critical care with many years of experience teaching POCUS and you will learn how to use your machine appropriately. This course is mainly designed to use the ultrasound machine as a point-of-care in an emergency but will also teach you to use it as a tool for abdominal ultrasound. The great thing about this course is that you will learn to ultrasound the abdomen, the chest, and the heart.
You will be provided in-person lectures on the three types of POCUS in the morning, followed by a 4-hours hands-on lab on anesthetized small to medium breed dogs. The same pattern will be repeated on Day 2, which allows for repetition and building on those motor skills. This lab is a great way to learn, practice or refine your skills in POCUS. After this course, you will be set to go back to your practice and start applying your skills from Day 1.

courses.title: Telehealth Revolution: Enhancing Veterinary Care through Technology
courses.description:
This comprehensive course delves into the rapidly growing field of telehealth in veterinary medicine, providing participants with essential insights and practical strategies for adopting and implementing virtual care. Topics covered will include the importance of telehealth adoption, various virtual care platforms and models, legal and malpractice considerations, business model integration, monetization strategies, promotional techniques, best practices, and staying informed with the latest resources. Participants will be equipped to advance the quality of veterinary medicine and enhance client communication through telehealth.
This comprehensive course is designed to provide veterinary professionals with the necessary tools and knowledge to successfully implement and manage telehealth services, ultimately enhancing patient care and client satisfaction.

courses.title: From Vague to Vital: Diagnosing Josies Illness
courses.description: Dogs are notorious for eating things they shouldnt contributing to gastrointestinal GI signs such as diminished appetite vomiting or diarrhea. Severe and or persistent signs raise concerns for the possibility of foreign body ingestion with obstruction especially if the patient has a known history of indiscriminate eating. While recurrent or chronic intermittent GI signs may also attend dietary indiscretion or even partial obstruction the differential diagnosis list can be extensive and includes a host of nongastrointestinal conditions. Josies story illustrates a problemoriented approach to the diagnosis of vague and intermittent gastrointestinal signs including vomiting diarrhea and lethargy beginning with a minimum laboratory database then adding specialty tests and imaging. Her case highlights how the Catalyst Cortisol Test enables rapid inclinic screening and diagnosis supporting timely clinical decisions. Josies story emphasizes the importance of considering hypoadrenocorticism Addisons disease in dogs with nonspecific signs and demonstrates how integrated diagnostics can clarify complex cases.

courses.title: Evolving the Feline MDB: Purrfect Balance for Your Patient Assessment
courses.description: The minimum data base is a concept that many veterinarians are familiar with but should the MDB the same for all patients? Recent data studies looking at the diagnostic findings of cats across age ranges and diagnostic use case will be discussed. Additionally, the unique diagnostic behaviors of Cat Friendly Practices will be shared. This information will help pave the way to create the Purrfect diagnostic plan for the feline patients in your care.

courses.title: Recognizing and Treating Pain in Senior Cats: A Practical Clinical Approach
courses.description: Pain in senior cats is often under-recognized and undertreated, yet it can significantly impact quality of life. This practical session will guide you through identifying, assessing, and managing pain in geriatric feline patients. Learn to recognize subtle behavioral and clinical signs, choose appropriate diagnostic tools, and develop multimodal pain management strategies that combine pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic approaches tailored to the senior cat. By the end of this lecture, you will feel confident in improving comfort and overall well-being in your aging feline patients.

courses.title: 47th Annual Lake Tahoe Equine Conference
courses.description:
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: This conference will provide 20 hours of in-depth presentations with up-to-date practical clinical information for the equine practitioner or veterinary technician. Come enjoy high quality CE in a unique format that also allows ample time for recreation in beautiful Lake Tahoe.
The attendees can expect to receive high quality, practical and up-to-date lectures pertaining to equine medicine and surgery, with emphasis on material they can take back and use in their daily practice. Light breakfast and heavy appetizers with beverages will be provided prior to each morning and evening session. Between sessions, the attendees will have free time to ski or snowboard, or just relax in the beautiful Lake Tahoe region.

courses.title: The Role of Movement in Veterinary Practice: Impact on Job Performance and Well-Being
courses.description: This course explores the critical role of movement in veterinary practice and its impact on job performance, mental health, and overall well-being. Participants will gain insights into the physical demands of veterinary work, including common musculoskeletal challenges, and learn strategies for incorporating movement into their daily routines to enhance health and productivity. The course will also cover the influence of social media, veterinary influencers, and evidence-based practices on business growth and client retention. By integrating movement into both personal and professional practices, veterinarians can reduce burnout, improve job satisfaction, and boost client engagement. Participants will leave with practical tools and resources for fostering a health-conscious, productive work environment and implementing wellness initiatives within their teams.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Taking Away the Pain of Pain Scoring
courses.description:
Ouch my head hurts using these pain scoring systems...
This CE will cover the basics of what pain scoring systems are, why they matter, and how to use them to benefit your veterinary patients. This CE covers pain scoring in both small animal & exotic companion animal species.

courses.title: OMGiardia, worms and other parasites: When to screen, when to treat and when it's important
courses.description: This archived webinar reviews the importance of regular screening for common intestinal parasites, describes the risks they pose to people and pets, suggests when to treat, and explains why follow-up testing is needed for successful parasite management. We explore the risk of Giardia in companion animals, with critical evaluation of the diagnostic utility of Giardia genotyping and implications of identifying zoonotic versus host-adapted assemblages. Best practices for treatment, prevention, and human safety are shared.

courses.title: Patterns of Pulmonary Disease
courses.description: Evaluation of pulmonary patterns can be challenging. In this upcoming lecture, review the importance of obtaining high quality images and how thoracic radiographs can be used to evaluate respiratory disease.

courses.title: SMALL ANIMAL ULTRASOUND: THE BIG 5 (637-35234)
courses.description: Small animal ultrasound remains an important diagnostic tool for abdominal imaging. Although complete proficiency requires hundreds of hours of training, many clinical questions can be answered with much less training. Focusing on the major organ systems as opposed to the small abdominal structures and understanding the limitations of certain equipment can be very helpful in helping diagnose our small animal patients.

courses.title: The Greatest Pretenders: Challenging Adrenal Insufficiencies
courses.description: Adrenocortical insufficiency can be life threatening and may be difficult to identify. This is because of a multitude of factors including uncommon patient signalments, vague clinical signs, normal hemograms, co-morbidities, and variances in types of adrenal insufficiency. In this lecture presented by Veterinary Criticalist Christin Reminga, DVM, DACVECC, we'll highlight these difficulties and go through four unique cases and how they were diagnosed and successfully treated for adrenal insufficiency.

courses.title: The Jace Case Study Using the Minimum Data Base to Find Hidden Problems-Part IV of the Veterinary Technicians Learning
courses.description: This brief case study of a young dog presenting for routine ovariohysterectomy shows an integrated assessment of the minimum database and other clinical findings. Jaces story demonstrates how the complete blood count (CBC), biochemistry profile, and urinalysis provide unique insights into the patients health assessment. It emphasizes how optimizing lab operations from sample acquisition, through analysis and assessment, to reporting, and communications may significantly affect visit success.

courses.title: Management of Fulminant Liver Failure in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This lecture will cover the basic pathophysiology of liver failure based on current veterinary literature, including some of the scoring systems used to help prognosticate these cases for practitioners. We will place special emphasis on the most common liver toxins in cats and dogs and on the management of hepatic encephalopathy. Finally, we will discuss the common treatments for acute liver failure as well as some individual therapies for specific toxins.

courses.title: It's Not Always The Food . . . Or Is It? Navigating Food Hypersensitivities in Small Animals
courses.description: This course will cover how to clinically approach cutaneous adverse food reactions in both dogs and cats. We will highlight insights from the critically appraised topic on adverse food reactions of companion animals published in a nine-article series. We will weigh options and review diets available. Critically examine the best practices to maximize compliance with diet trials and communicate clear expectations with clients to accomplish shared goals. Lastly, we will review the most common missteps made during trials that lead to incomplete or inaccurate diagnoses.

courses.title: Pawsitive Anesthesia for General Practice Dentistry
courses.description: This 6-hour in-person interactive course is designed to help the general practice veterinarian and veterinary technician work together to ensure canine and feline patients are anesthetized safely and carefully monitored. Preparations are made in case of anesthetic complications or adverse events so that anesthetic emergencies can be addressed as they arise. Attendees will gain confidence and skills in various case examples that they can apply to patients in practice in the future.

courses.title: THE IMPORTANCE OF IN-HOUSE CYTOLOGY (637-39136)
courses.description: In this one hour lecture, review the importance of completing cytology in-house even if you are not a pathologist. Review the basics of staining and evaluating blood smear with Critical Care Specialist Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC.

courses.title: CANINE HYPOADRENOCORTICISM - ADDISONS DISEASE (637-37144)
courses.description: Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, explains hypoadrenocorticism (Addison's Disease) in dogs including signalment, diagnosis, and treatment.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: A New Point of View: Enhanced Care Through Acupuncture Integration
courses.description: This one-hour lecture will discuss the underpinnings of the veterinary acupuncture mechanism of action from both the neuroanatomy and traditional Chinese veterinary medicine approach, and how acupuncture helps with pain relief, tissue healing, mobility issues, and restoring health to our patients.

courses.title: A REVIEW OF REAL CASES (637-38748)
courses.description: Review recent cases at DoveLewis and discuss a practical approach for imaging emergency and trauma patients. This lecture, presented by Alan Lipman, DVM, DACVR will cover key concepts and expert tips for high-quality image interpretation, which provides better diagnoses of acute illnesses and injuries.

courses.title: SEIZURES- WHAT DO I DO (637-36708)
courses.description: Some common questions that are encountered when dealing with a new seizure patient include: When to start treatment? Drug options? Is it okay to stop at some point? How to handle at home seizure emergencies? Review these questions and more with DoveLewis Criticalist Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, in this 54 minute formal presentation on seizures in canine and feline patients.

courses.title: TRIAGING THE ACUTE ABDOMEN (637-36573)
courses.description: Acute abdomen in human medicine is defined as sudden and severe abdominal pain of unclear etiology. In veterinary medicine, it is typically a more general term used to describe a patient with any acute significant abdominal signs. Learn the pathophysiology, initial triage, and diagnostic evaluation in this one hour CE lecture by Critical Care Specialist Erika Loftin, DVM, DACVECC.

courses.title: Gut Instinct: Tips for Approaching Chronic GI Signs in Dogs
courses.description: Chronic gastrointestinal (GI) disease in dogs is a common, yet work-up and management remains challenging. In this presentation, canine chronic enteropathy (CE), an umbrella term encompassing food-responsive, steroid-responsive, antibiotic responsive, and non-responsive enteropathies. We will briefly examine the pathophysiology, while focusing on diagnostics for the canine CE using a case example. By the end, veterinary professionals should feel confident in optimizing diagnostic plans to improve chances of diagnosing (and thus treating) dogs with CE.

courses.title: Gut Check: The Microbiome's Impact on Patient Health
courses.description: This webinar will explore the fascinating world of the gut microbiome, a diverse community of trillions of bacteria, viruses, and other microorganisms that reside in the digestive tract. We will cover a brief overview of the basics of the gut microbiome, including its definition, importance, and impact on overall health. It will also discuss the potential consequences of imbalances in the gut microbiome, known as dysbiosis. Additionally, the module will explore the role of prebiotics, postbiotics, and probiotics in maintaining a healthy gut microbiome, as well as the use of fecal material transplantation (FMT) to address imbalances.

courses.title: The ABCs of CBCs: What, When and Why
courses.description: The complete blood count (CBC) is one of the most sensitive means of determining deviation from health in the patient as well as characterising severity of abnormalities in the clinically obvious sick patient. Focused discussed about the basic CBC will entail what is included in the CBC; when and why a CBC should be performed; and information about the red blood cells (erythrogram), white blood cells (leukogram), and platelets (thrombogram) to assure complete understanding; which is essential to maximize the value of the CBC. We will also discuss data and graphic presentations from the hematology analyzer and blood film microscopic evaluation.

courses.title: A Conversation on the Value of Blood Morphology
courses.description: In this session, we will discuss a recent study that highlights the value of blood morphology on blood smears submitted after a ProCyte Dx CBC. Through this data study, well review possible reasons for blood smear submission, interpretive prompts and the importance of clinically valuable comments, including what were the most common types of clinically valuable comments.

courses.title: Dot Plots, say what?
courses.description: What are the colorful dots at the bottom of my CBC results? What do they mean, and how I can I use them to better diagnose and treat my patients?

courses.title: The Role of Urinalysis in the Minimum Database- Part III of the Veterinary Technicians Learning Journey
courses.description: Urinalysis is an often-overlooked component of the laboratory minimum database for sick and well pets. Urine components and quality reflect both local urogenital conditions and systemic health. A comprehensive urinalysis helps us to assess hematology and biochemistry findings and is an area where veterinary technicians guide quality and output of laboratory results. This course will establish a firm foundation in the components of the urinalysis and reinforce best laboratory practices to optimize results. Learners will progress from patient preparation through sample acquisition to in-house sample processing or reference laboratory submission.

courses.title: Feline Hyperthyroidism: Pearls of treatment and how to improve long-term management
courses.description: This course will cover the diagnosis and treatment of feline hyperthyroidism with a focus on how to manage patients that develop adverse reactions to methimazole and how to improve compliance with medication administration. We will discuss long-term management recommendations and touch on common concurrent diseases that may affect the success of treatment such as chronic kidney disease and diabetes mellitus.

courses.title: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Advanced Abdominal Procedures (online)
courses.description: This online continuing education course provides a comprehensive overview of advanced small animal surgical procedures through engaging video lectures and interactive quizzes. Topics include diaphragmatic hernia repair, gastrectomy and gastroplasty, gastropexy, liver lobectomy, and cholecystectomy. Learners will also explore urogenital surgeries such as urethrostomy in male dogs and cystotomy tube placement, as well as feeding tube techniques including esophagostomy and gastrostomy. Additional modules cover splenectomy and cryptorchidectomy, offering practical insights into surgical indications, techniques, and postoperative considerations to enhance clinical competence and confidence in the veterinary surgical setting.

courses.title: Airway Structure and Function in Canine Bronchial Diseases
courses.description: Chronic bronchitis (CB) is the most common chronic respiratory impairment in dogs. The condition is defined as a chronic cough occurring for two consecutive months during the preceding year that is not attributable to another cause (e.g. neoplasia, congestive heart failure). The early changes are likely triggered by an inciting irritant stimulus, and include increases in airway mucus production, impairment of mucociliary clearance, and alterations in the local immune response. The cascade of events, if left untreated, results in a cycle of chronic inflammation, chronic cough, copious mucoid airway secretions, decreased mucociliary clearance, and hypoxemia. This session will provide the experienced specialist with a detailed review of normal airway structure, function, and physiology, will use this background to emphasize the consequences of the loss of these functions via bronchoscopy and advanced imaging, and ultimately will offer a rational approach to intervention for chronic bronchitis and its late-stage consequences.

courses.title: Early Cancer Diagnosis Dont Miss the Warning Signs
courses.description: This session will focus on the consideration and diagnosis of cancer earlier in the clinical course with integration into the existing clinical algorithm. The gathering of information starts from history-taking with emphasis on specific open-ended questions. A physical examination can offer several worrisome clinical signs leading to a suspicion of cancer. Armed with this information, routine blood work and diagnostics able to be performed in-house or at the reference lab starts to round out this clinical picture and helps to form a differential list for specific cancers. This differential list can be used to guide further recommendations to clients, including diagnostics (including those that can be performed at the clinic and those that are advanced), referral to specialty hospitals, or empirical therapy. The session will then close with an overview of the current offerings of diagnostics on the market which may aid in early detection of cancer in companion animals.

courses.title: Introduction to Canine Arthroscopy
courses.description:
You know that arthroscopy is your next level for your clients and as an orthopedist, but there is something that you may not know-while there are some great arthroscopists in this world, nobody was ever born with natural arthroscopy skills. That is EXACTLY why we designed this course! Excellent arthroscopy skills flow from hours of hands-on training that reinforce your knowledge of fundamental principles. We know that great hands-on training from great trainers is the only way to rapidly grow your arthroscopy skills, so that is exactly what we did.
In this course, you will learn and practice the important principles and skills in triangulation, camera head & light post positioning, portal and fluid flow management, and so much more. You will also learn to how to select great cases for you to apply and grow your new skills. You will return to your practice or training program with strong arthroscopy skills based upon sound knowledge of the foundational principles of canine arthroscopy.

courses.title: Future Landscape of Vector Borne Diseases: as vectors, people and pets move, what should we be on the lookout for?
courses.description: In this session, we will review the landscape of vector borne diseases in North America, how their geography and prevalence have changed and what pathogens that could emerge as a threat in the future.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Locoregional Techniques for GP & ER
courses.description: This CE is a 2 part lecture + lab. We will discuss the physiology behind nerve blocks, common drugs & supplies utilized, and walk through how to perform various nerve blocks easily applied in the GP & ER setting. The lecture will be followed by a lab where a few of the blocks will be practiced on cadavers.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Beating Blood Pressure Problems
courses.description: This CE will discuss the basics of hemodynamics. We will discuss how the body maintains blood pressure, the physiology behind blood pressure maintenance, as well as discuss how to troubleshoot when blood pressure is abnormal.

courses.title: The Intersection of Domestic Violence and Animal Abuse: How the Veterinary Community Can Help
courses.description: This webinar will feature Nicole Forsyth, President & CEO of RedRover, a national non-profit organization that brings animals from crisis to care and strengthens the bond between people and pets. Nicole will discuss the effort to create more pet-friendly domestic violence shelters to help people and animals in crisis. The documented link between animal abuse and inter partner violence (IPV) means that veterinarians are increasingly being called upon to respond to suspected animal abuse as an indicator of other violence in the household. This webinar will also address the role of veterinarians in responding to domestic violence and IPV, and how veterinarians and animal health professionals can help address this issue in their communities.

courses.title: 34th Northeast Dairy Production Symposium
courses.description: The mission of the Northeast Dairy Production Medicine Symposium, Inc. is to contribute to the well-being of our dairy producers by providing a unique educational experience for dairy-oriented veterinarians and veterinary students. The object of this experience is to provide motivation, information, discernment, and support for the practice of dairy production medicine.

courses.title: Crash Course in Collapse A Case of Canine Dilated Cardiomyopathy
courses.description: Veterinary professionals in general practice often feel challenged and under-resourced to appropriately manage emergent patients because they have limited experience or lack the necessary equipment, staff, or time. Adopting a standard, stepwise approach to patient assessment and preliminary treatment can improve clinical proficiency and confidence and may help to improve patient outcomes. This short crash course in collapse associated with dyspnea illustrates the ABCs of emergency care through a patient story. Learners will earn 0.25 CE credits as they follow Henry, a 5-year-old sporting breed dog, through triage, point-of-care testing, and emergency stabilization, from tentative to definitive diagnosis of canine dilated cardiomyopathy.

courses.title: Inventory Management 3: Inventory Strategies
courses.description: Dive into this inventory course to learn how to take a more strategic approach in how and when items are ordered during the billing cycle, along with reviewing (or establishing) pricing and discounting strategies.

courses.title: The SDMA is high but everything else is normal: How to manage discrepant results
courses.description: Have you ever looked at your results and wondered how to explain them to your client? Or how to answer a question that you might have about one of your results? In this session well walk through some of the frequently asked questions for IDEXX renal products as well as some scenarios in which you might find yourself scratching your head. Come prepared for an interactive session involving real-life questions to some of the thorniest issues involving renal health.

courses.title: Overview of Mast Cell Tumors
courses.description: In this course, youll deepen your understanding of mast cells and mast cell tumors a common form of cancer in dogs. Well cover essential terminology and concepts related to diagnosis, grading, and staging, giving you the knowledge to confidently support the veterinary team in managing these cases. By applying what you learn, youll be better equipped to perform or assist with diagnostic procedures, communicate effectively with the treatment team, and provide informed, compassionate care to patients and their owners.

courses.title: Patient and Practice Benefits of Comprehensive Vector-Borne Disease Testing: How to Combine Heartworm and Tick-Borne Disease
courses.description: In this session, we will discuss comprehensive vector-borne disease testing that can benefit patients and the practice. This small panel format brings together an infectious disease expert, a seasoned practice owner, and a licensed veterinary technician to share the medical evidence for regular testing of dogs for heartworms and tick-borne diseases and how to communicate this value to pet owners, even in advance of the visit. They will present practice management strategies for implementing change, optimizing workflow, and leveraging enhanced technology, such as clinical decision support to manage positive results in asymptomatic patients, that can elevate practice culture and outcomes, while enhancing patient care.

courses.title: Need for Platelet Morphologic Review: Artifactual Thrombocytopenia (Pseudothrombocytopenia)
courses.description: The platelet count or thrombogram is one of the three components of the CBC. When the platelet count is lower than the reference interval or what is expected for the patient, a platelet morphologic review is indicated to distinguish between true thrombocytopenia and artifactual thrombocytopenia, also known as pseudothrombocytopenia. Doctors DeNicola, Rebar, and Metzger review thrombogram basics and present a user friendly platelet count/mass algorithm to assess thrombocytopenia. They share their practical insights using data from a Procyte Dx Hematology Analyzer cytogram (dot plot) and manual assessment of a blood smear to identify artifactual thrombocytopenia in clinical cases with decreased platelet counts. Wheww, no treatment necessary!

courses.title: Ears - Why Do We Still Talk About Them
courses.description: In this lecture presented by DoveLewis Dermatologist Sonja Zabel, DVM, MS, DACVD, we will discuss the diagnosis and management of patients with Otitis Externa. While each patient is unique in determining the underlying cause, we will cover how to manage reoccurring Otitis with collaborative efforts from owners. Lastly, we will review communication tips for helping your team and clients successfully treat Otitis long term.

courses.title: POCUS Bootcamp; Abdominal, Cardiac, Pleural Space, Lung, and Interventional Point-of-Care Ultrasound Techniques (A)
courses.description:
Dust off that ultrasound machine, go beyond the basics in this full day hands on POCUS course!
This 8 hour lab, supported by over 8 hours of online pre course content, will build on basic ultrasound skills through practical, hands on training using live dogs. Participants will have the opportunity to learn and practice all the common veterinary POCUS techniques currently used to assess the abdomen, pleural space, lung, vascular system, and heart. Following live dog scanning participants will have the opportunity to put their newly learned skills to the test by searching for different pathologies in cadavers, including pneumothorax and pneumoperitoneum. Phantom training models will then be used to demonstrate and practice ultrasound guided procedures, using a vascular access model. A model used to replicate lymph node puncture will also be used and as a bonus, an ultrasound guided chicken vascular access Olympics will be included for those that wish to compete for prizes (which will be copies of the textbook Essentials of Veterinary Point of Care Ultrasound: Pleural Space & Lung).
This lab will focus on techniques developed by the instructors, designed to increase veterinary POCUS diagnostic accuracy, and help facilitate easier application into everyday veterinary practice. These are all techniques that can be performed by any practitioner and should be used in everyday practice!

courses.title: The RECOVER Newborn Resuscitation Guidelines: A Tour Through the Algorithm.
courses.description: The RECOVER Initiative's most recent clinical guidelines revolve around the unique aspects of resuscitation of newborn dogs and cats immediately after birth. This session will go over the newborn resuscitation algorithm. This algorithm provides a step-by-step approach to essential resuscitation measures for puppies and kittens as they transition from intra- to extrauterine life. Key questions addressed in this presentation are: Which newborns need resuscitation? How does the heart rate guide resuscitation measures? What monitoring should be used during resuscitation? Should oxygen always be supplemented? What is the single most important intervention to save non-vigorous newborn puppies/kittens? I will further point out how different newborn resuscitation is from CPR in adult dogs and cats.

courses.title: Changing the Paradigm for Canine Osteosarcoma Diagnosis, Treatment, and Monitoring
courses.description: This course on canine osteosarcoma offers a comprehensive exploration of the disease, examining its diagnostic methods, current treatment standards, and ongoing clinical trials. The course highlights the role of canine osteosarcoma as a comparative model for human osteosarcoma, emphasizing the similarities and differences in tumor biology and therapeutic responses. Participants will review key diagnostic tools, including clinical signs, imaging techniques, and histopathology, and explore advanced molecular diagnostics for prognosis and treatment planning. The course also delves into cutting-edge research focused on improving diagnostic accuracy through imaging advancements and biomarkers. Therapeutic strategies will be discussed, covering both traditional treatments and novel approaches, while the management of cancer-induced bone pain, including innovative therapies, will also be addressed.

courses.title: Driving Progress with Purpose: Change Leadership in Modern Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Change is constant in veterinary practice whether it's updating protocols, adapting to staff turnover, or shifting client expectations. But leading change well takes more than policy updates; it requires strategic, compassionate leadership. This session provides a roadmap for guiding teams through change using proven frameworks like Kotters 8 Step Model and the Kubler Ross Change Curve. Attendees will explore how to lead with clarity, manage resistance, and maintain engagement throughout transitions. Emphasis is placed on practical communication, team alignment, and emotional intelligence. Whether youre implementing new technology or restructuring your team, this session will prepare you to lead purposeful, people centered change at every level.

courses.title: Appearances Can Be Deceiving: Detecting Renal Disease in Healthy Patients
courses.description: How many times have you heard, no thanks, shes always been healthy? What about is there anything we can do? In this discussion well discuss why diagnostics are not just about baselines and how early intervention in those seemingly healthy patients really can make a difference.

courses.title: Photomedicine for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: Designed for veterinary professionals, this course instructs participants on how light heals tissue, alleviates pain, and improves function for a variety of acute and chronic clinical conditions. It includes recorded lectures, reading assignments, web-based videos, and assessments. Through this multi-media approach, the student builds a solid foundation in the physics, physiology, and clinical value of photomedicine. We also explore the value of less intense laser treatment, delivered at a slower pace, to optimize healing and maximize safety.

courses.title: We Need to Talk, Resolving Case Complications with Communication
courses.description:
Surgical complications are an unavoidable part of practice, but the way they are discussed among all parties often determines whether a challenging case becomes a source of collaboration, conflict, or fractured trust. This interactive lecture uses real-world large and small animal surgical scenarios to explore the difficult conversations that arise among surgeons, primary care veterinarians, clients, and clinical teams. Rather than focusing on the technical details of each case, the session invites residents to step back from the clinician cap and examine the communication decisions that shape client perception, referral relationships, case continuity, and professional collegiality.
Residents in both large and small animal surgery will gain practical strategies for navigating situations when expectations diverge, outcomes are imperfect, or communication is delayed, incomplete, or misunderstood. Emphasis will be placed on using the ACVS Collaborative Relationship Communication Tool to proactively clarify roles, timelines, follow-up responsibilities, client messaging, and shared decision-making between the specialist and primary care veterinarian. By examining difficult cases through a communication lens, this lecture aims to help residents build the professional habits needed to preserve trust, reduce conflict, and improve patient outcomes through stronger teamwork.

courses.title: Electrolytes in Critical Care: Navigating Complex Imbalances
courses.description: Electrolyte disturbances are common in critically ill patients and are associated with worse clinical outcomes. Although electrolytes are routinely monitored in intensive care units (ICUs), their exact prevalence and prognostic impact in medical ICU populations remain incompletely defined. Critically ill patients are particularly susceptible to both depletion and excess of key electrolytes, which may arise from underlying disease processes and can contribute to clinical deterioration. Multiple electrolyte abnormalities often occur simultaneously and may share a common underlying cause. While some imbalances are transient or asymptomatic, recognizing and addressing them is essential because uncorrected disturbances are more frequently observed in non-survivors than survivors. Management should prioritize identifying and correcting the underlying cause while adjusting electrolyte intake, clearance, or distribution as needed. Because ICU patients have complex and dynamic conditions, electrolyte therapy must be individualized and carefully monitored to avoid harm.

courses.title: Cannabinoids in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: With the ever-increasing questions clients ask about the use of cannabinoids for their pets, it's important to educate yourself on the legalities, potential benefits and administration of cannabinoids in veterinary medicine. Hear what Casara Andre, DVM, cVMA and founder of Veterinary Cannabis Education and Consulting has to say about this important topic.

courses.title: An Overview of Pancreatitis in Small Animals Clinical Features and Diagnosis
courses.description: Pancreatitis is an important disease in dogs and cats with varied presentations and outcomes. Diagnosis relies on a combination of clinical suspicion and diagnostic testing results, including a laboratory minimum database, diagnostic imaging, and targeted lipase testing. This course offers a brief overview of the clinical features and pathophysiology of pancreatitis and diagnostic options available to small animal clinicians.

courses.title: Wellness in the Workplace
courses.description:
I am a veterinarian and entrepreneur on a mission to save one veterinarian at a time, showing them how to regain their love for their profession, while following their passion and purpose work.
As a thought leader, practicing veterinarian, and owner of a thriving clinic in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Dr. Becky Krull lives to empower other veterinarians to find the equilibrium in their passion work and daily life. She speaks of the daily struggles of working in a high-paced, high-stress profession, as well as a being a mom and wife, and how she found the tools to thrive. She has lived in the trenches and walked the journey of caregiver burnout and is a testament to the personal growth work she follows daily to embrace her passion for practice life.
Dr. Krull has been a full-time small animal veterinarian at
Buddy's Vets in Green Bay, WI, since 2005. She became a partner and vice president of the cooperation in 2008, taking over full practice ownership and president of the cooperation in 2021. Beyond the scope of veterinary medicine, she has embraced roles as human resources director, marketing director and mentorship lead.

courses.title: Financial Management 1: The Flow of Money & Revenue Management
courses.description: In this introductory financial management course, we will review how finance touches all aspects of your business from inventory to human resources. Business equations, managing revenue, the importance of integrating your business model into your financial planning, and concepts such as price and volume factors and activity centers will be discussed.

courses.title: Like Water: Initial Fluid Resuscitation in the ER
courses.description: This lecture presented by DoveLewis Veterinarian Josh Cruz, DVM, will briefly cover the history, classification, and use of various fluid therapies. Current controversies and adverse risks will be explored. Practical recommendations for fluid therapy in the initial resuscitation stages of patients presenting to the ER, however, will be the goal. To better understand the arguments for these recommendations, concepts including physiologic response to trauma, end goal directed therapy, novel methods for calculating blood volume, and importance of vasopressor therapies will be discussed.

courses.title: DIABETES MELLITUS - PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND INITIAL ASSESSMENT (637-39725)
courses.description: The lecture is 55 minutes and consists of Critical Care Specialist Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, doing a formal presentation on Diabetes. She discusses the basics of diabetes, insulin types, glucose curves, and gives great tips on educating clients to manage this disease at home. The end of the lecture reviews case studies to show how diabetes management can be challenging for veterinarians and owners alike.

courses.title: SANDBOX WARS (637-41335)
courses.description: In this one hour lecture presented by Chief Administrative Officer, Monica Maxwell, we will discuss how to identify unhealthy conflict in the workplace. How to reverse unhealthy conflict and create a more cohesive team will also be reviewed.

courses.title: Speaking the Same Language- Cancer Cell Types and Behavior
courses.description: Cancer terminology forms its own lexicon and language when clinicians discuss diagnostics, treatments and outcomes with both pet owners and other veterinarians. As cancer testing becomes more frequent and part of routine care for people and animals, having a foundation in common terminology used will not only improve conversations with pet owners but also improve referral relations, making transfer of care more streamlined. Improved communication builds trust amongst all parties on the care team and improves patient care. In this module, you will learn about cancer types as they relate to tissue of origin, including how that may change your next steps and pet owner communication

courses.title: Veterinary Cytology and Hematology Crash Course
courses.description:
For the cytology component of this course we will discuss how to obtain a diagnostic cytology sample (FNA, swabs, impression smears, etc.) and sample processing (slide preparation, staining, microscopy techniques). Additionally, participants will learn an organized approach to evaluating cytologic specimens by using a cytology algorithm with cytologic examples of various neoplastic and non-neoplastic processes. Processing and evaluation of fluid samples (cavitary effusions and synovial fluid) will also be covered along with various chemistry analyses that can be performed on fluid samples (Triglycerides, Creatinine, K+, glucose, lactate, etc). The final session will be case based to solidify the knowledge gained in the other sessions.
For the hematology session we will discuss the parts of a complete blood count, RBC/PLT indices, interpretation of scatter plots and dot plots, differential counts, RBC morphologic changes, leukogram patterns, and infectious agents. This course will provide veterinarians and technicians the skills and confidence to assess CBC results in correlation with the clinical history and blood smear evaluation.

courses.title: Common Avian Procedures
courses.description: This course will begin with discussing and demonstrating how to properly capture and handle birds of various sizes. You will also learn about common procedures performed on avians such as nail, beak and wing trims and how to administer oral medications safely with step-by-step demonstrations led by avian specialist Anna Osofsky, DVM, DABVP.

courses.title: Targeted Testing for Important Intestinal Parasites of Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Intestinal parasites are an important problem for small animals, capable of causing significant morbidity and mortality. Young animals or adults with immune compromise and/or comorbidity are especially at risk. Routine deworming of puppies and kittens and year-round prevention informed by regular fecal testing are widely recommended to support healthy pets and households. Parasite prevention programs can be optimized with the use of accurate testing for earlier life stages to limit disease, reduce environmental contamination, and prevent zoonotic infections. This course reviews life cycles of the most common intestinal parasites, comparing diagnostic options and highlighting selective advantages of innovative methods, such as fecal antigen testing, and suggests management options for infected patients.

courses.title: An en-lyte-ening guide to electrolyte interpretation
courses.description: Electrolytes are an essential factor in many physiologic functions and when they are out of whack they can cause significant problems for our patients. In this lecture, we will discuss common electrolyte alterations and what to do about them in a case-based format. Topics will include when to include electrolytes as part of a complete chemistry panel, differential diagnoses for alterations and management of electrolyte imbalances in our canine and feline patients.

courses.title: Creeping Risks, Local Consequences: Emerging Parasites in Companion Animal Practice
courses.description: Emerging and re-emerging parasitic diseases are increasingly capturing national attention, but their impact extends far beyond the headlines and into everyday companion animal practice. Changes in climate, wildlife ecology, animal movement, and global commerce are reshaping parasite distribution patterns, exposing pets and their owners to risks that may not have historically existed in their region. This presentation explores the factors driving parasite emergence and examines several important threats currently affecting veterinary medicine, including the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax), and Echinococcus multilocularis. Participants will review current epidemiologic trends, clinical implications, public health considerations, and practical approaches for identifying and managing these emerging risks. The session will also highlight the veterinarian's role in surveillance, prevention, client communication, and One Health initiatives that support animal and human health. Through an evidence-based review of emerging parasite threats, attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating risk assessment, prevention, and education into daily clinical practice.

courses.title: New Thoughts on Old Diseases: Chronic Kidney Disease, Hyperthyroidism, Diabetes Mellitus, and Osteoarthritis.
courses.description: In this session, well focus on the things that affect geriatric cats the most. Older cats seem to collect diseases, which can make interpreting laboratory tests challenging. Once diagnoses are made, balancing treatments can be equally challenging! Well examine the most effective ways to use both classic and newer diagnostic tools and treatments to keep our older cats happy and healthy

courses.title: Feline Diabetes Deep Dive Managing DKA When the ER Isnt an Option
courses.description: Feline diabetes can be challenging to manage and diabetic ketoacidosis DKA adds a layer of complexity especially when referral to an emergency clinic is not an option. This lecture examines how to recognize treat and manage DKA patients in a general practice setting. We will cover how to differentiate DKA from uncomplicated diabetes interpret key clinical and laboratory findings and understand the pathophysiology driving this critical condition. Practical guidance will be provided for diagnostics that you can perform in clinic including blood glucose ketone testing blood gases and electrolyte assessments. Treatment and monitoring plans that dont require continuous insulin infusion fluid therapy electrolyte supplementation and practical insulin protocols that work in non ER practice settings will be discussed. By the end of this session you will have practical tools to manage DKA even when resources are limited.

courses.title: VACUUM ASSISTED (VAC) WOUND THERAPY (637-44767)
courses.description:
Vacuum assisted wound closure (VAC), also referred to as negative pressure wound therapy, has been utilized with growing popularity in human medicine since the mid 1980's. The basic concept is to subject a wound to subatmospheric pressure within a closed environment. Veterinary use of VAC was first seen in literature in 1997.
The lecture is 61 minutes and consists of speaker Coby Richter, DVM, DACVS, doing a formal presentation on vacuum assisted wound closure and a review of case studies. Coby Richter, DVM, DACVS, explains Vacuum Assisted Wound Closure (VAC Therapy) and its applications for veterinary patients. A case study is included.

courses.title: The Itch-hikers Guide to the Feline Galaxy vector-borne infections from fleas, ticks, and mosquitoes
courses.description: Tick and mosquito borne disease get a lot of attention when it comes to our canine friends, but dont forget about cats! Lets explore potential infectious diseases that lurk in common vectors, as well as how to recognize and manage these challenging infections.

courses.title: Choosing the Right Veterinary Software: From PIMS to Emerging Technologies
courses.description:
Technology is becoming an essential ally in optimizing operations and improving patient care. With a wide range of tools available - from practice management systems (PIMS) to appointment scheduling, inventory management, and AI solutions for imaging and client communication - finding the right veterinary software can be a daunting task. Choose wisely, and you'll see a boost in productivity, patient care, and staff satisfaction. Choose poorly, and you might face operational chaos, increased stress, and financial strain. At best, you might end up stuck with software that nobody uses.
In this session, we'll break down the essential components of veterinary software, starting with the backbone of any practice - PIMS - and exploring additional tools that can further enhance your operations. We'll discuss when it's time to update your PIMS, who should be involved in the evaluation process, how to create a checklist of essential features, and how to weigh cost versus value. We'll also cover technical considerations, such as hospital readiness for new software, and the steps for its smooth implementation. Special attention will be given to managing change effectively so your staff embraces and utilizes the new software fully.
Finally, we'll dive into evaluating AI tools, a rapidly growing area in veterinary medicine. We'll compare features, cost, integration options, and user experience while considering the impact on workflows, client communication, and administrative tasks. Key topics will include data security and the responsible use of this emerging technology.
By the end of the presentation, you'll be equipped with practical insights to navigate the software selection process and make informed choices that will enhance your practice's efficiency and effectiveness.

courses.title: LIFTERS OR LEANERS PART II (637-41410)
courses.description: The lecture is 52 minutes and consists of a speaker CEO Ron Morgan doing a formal presentation on employee engagement. This lecture is targeted towards new managers in the veterinary field, or individuals who have taken on management responsibilities.

courses.title: FELINE URETHRAL OBSTRUCTION: MYTH BUSTERS EDITION (637-42654)
courses.description: This lecture presented by DoveLewis Criticalist Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, will focus on current concepts in the management of feline urethral obstruction with an evidenced based discussion on antibiotic therapy, decompressive cystocentesis, urinary catheter size, when to recommend perineal urethrostomy and more.

courses.title: HEART MURMURS IN THE ASYMPTOMATIC CANINE AND FELINE PATIENT (637-35676)
courses.description: In this session, Caryn Reynolds, DVM, DACVIM (cardiology) will discuss the likely causes of heart murmurs in asymptomatic patients based on the history, signalment and physical exam. Based on those differentials, we will discuss the diagnostic approach to staging common heart diseases. Attendees will learn to recognize cases that require advanced diagnostics and referral.

courses.title: Veterinary Hospital Design of the Future: Building for Tech-Driven Efficiency
courses.description:
Veterinary hospital design trends have shifted to meet new client and team expectations. Today, the focus is on streamlined workflows, efficient patient journeys, and creating a modern and more compassionate experience for both pets and their owners.
In a future-oriented veterinary hospital, telehealth services are fully integrated, ensuring continuity of care beyond the practice's four walls. Cloud-based practice management software connects the entire practice, allowing seamless communication between departments, easy access from anywhere, and a more data-driven approach to managing operations.
In this session, we'll explore several key topics. We'll start with an overview of veterinary hospital layouts and workflows, highlighting the opportunities that advanced technologies can create.
For those looking to upgrade existing spaces, we'll discuss strategies for creating opportunities within the hospital design to incorporate technology to help provide better workflows for doctors and staff. We'll also cover the incorporation of technology into the patient journey, providing an improved and less stressful experience during their visit.
Implementation of technology through hospital design is an essential component of this transformation, and we'll provide examples, including images, to illustrate how these concepts come to life in practice.
Tomorrow's veterinary hospital embraces innovation, flexibility, and a patient-centric approach. Whether you are building a new hospital or renovating an existing one, this session will offer valuable insights into creating a modern, tech-ready facility.

courses.title: Premedication
courses.description: This program will take an in-depth look at the preanesthetic/premedication phase of general anesthesia for cats and dogs. After a brief discussion of basic definitions and goals, commonly utilized premedicates will be discussed in detail. Drug selection and suggested drug dosages will be provided. Finally, the lecture will answer commonly asked questions about specific premedicants.

courses.title: SDMA: Fundamentals to Expanded Clinical Utility
courses.description: This presentation provides veterinary professionals the necessary information on how SDMA can support a well pet diagnostic program.

courses.title: Structural & Functional Assessment of the Equine Spine - Zoonotic Disease
courses.description: This course module provides the foundational information needed to recognize clinical signs of contagious and zoonotic diseases as they relate to the animal chiropractic practitioner. Detailed definitions and examples of infection, contagious, zoonotic, and reportable diseases in Colorado are introduced. The clinical signs indicative of acute respiratory and neurologic disease in horses is presented with recommendations for biosecurity precautions to help recognized and limit the spread of equine herpes virus, West Nile virus and rabies. Additional information on the incidence and pathogenesis of equine influenza, strangles and vesicular stomatitis in horses is included. Infectious, contagious, zoonotic, and reportable diseases that affect dogs and cats in Colorado are discussed, which include detailed content on rabies, canine brucellosis, plague, and tularemia.

courses.title: The pathologist recommends immunohistochemistry. Should you do it?
courses.description: Specialist level exploration of the purpose of IHC in cancer diagnosis and differentiation. Using a case based approach to demonstrate approaches to use of IHC and how to be successful navigating the use of this diagnostics

courses.title: AI-Augmented Patient Care: Developing a Holistic AI Strategy for Your Practice
courses.description:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly weaving itself into the fabric of modern veterinary medicine. With the potential for increased efficiencies, better patient care, and enhanced employee experiences, veterinary practices are swiftly integrating this technology. As innovation continues to accelerate, understanding AI's role in veterinary practice is becoming crucial for those aiming to stay ahead in the field.
This session will begin with a brief introduction to the origins of AI, an umbrella term for software designed to replicate human cognitive abilities and perform complex tasks such as learning, reasoning, and problem-solving. We'll unpack its various components, including machine learning and deep learning, and explain how they function.
Moving into the current landscape of veterinary medicine, the session will present insights from a 2024 survey by Digitail in collaboration with the American Animal Hospital Association (AAHA), offering a snapshot of AI's adoption, sentiment, and the challenges faced by practitioners.
Next, we'll explore AI use cases across different roles in a hospital. Attendees will learn to identify tasks where AI can add value or take over routine tasks to free up time for more critical responsibilities. We'll also discuss how to segment tasks that AI can automate or augment and where caution is needed. Through real-world examples, the session will highlight existing AI solutions and scenarios for their effective use in practice.
Finally, we will address the key concerns and challenges to AI adoption. Participants will leave with the knowledge to develop an AI implementation strategy for their practice, including a change-management plan to help their team embrace the new technology, use it responsibly, and maximize its potential.

courses.title: From Big Headlines to Small Animal Practice: Emerging Parasite Risks in the Exam Room
courses.description: Emerging and re-emerging parasitic diseases are increasingly capturing national attention, but their impact extends far beyond the headlines and into everyday companion animal practice. Changes in climate, wildlife ecology, animal movement, and global commerce are reshaping parasite distribution patterns, exposing pets and their owners to risks that may not have historically existed in their region. This presentation explores the factors driving parasite emergence and examines several important threats currently affecting veterinary medicine, including the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax), and Echinococcus multilocularis. Participants will review current epidemiologic trends, clinical implications, public health considerations, and practical approaches for identifying and managing these emerging risks. The session will also highlight the veterinarian's role in surveillance, prevention, client communication, and One Health initiatives that support animal and human health. Through an evidence-based review of emerging parasite threats, attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating risk assessment, prevention, and education into daily clinical practice.

courses.title: Implementing CancerDX into Clinical Workflows
courses.description: This presentation introduces IDEXX Cancer Dx testing and provides a practical roadmap for integrating it into everyday veterinary clinical workflows as both an aid in diagnosing sick patients and a screening tool for at risk dogs. It explores how earlier detection of canine lymphoma can improve patient outcomes and the pet parent experience while guiding teams through change management strategies that support adoption confidence and consistency. Using real world case examples protocol development and clear implementation steps the presentation helps practices move from reactive cancer detection to proactive care creating clarity aligning teams and embedding Cancer Dx as a sustainable part of diagnostic and preventive medicine.

courses.title: From Pitfalls to Profits: Reimagining Veterinary Business Success
courses.description:
As veterinary professionals, we often find ourselves caught in a "clinical whirlwind" where the demands of the day-to-day obscure the path to true practice health and personal fulfillment. This high-impact, two-hour session, delivered by CSUVetCE, distills a comprehensive three-part series into a strategic roadmap for alumni to move beyond operational survival and toward sustainable prosperity. We begin by unmasking common "profitability pitfalls," challenging the misconception that revenue growth alone equals business health and explaining why "Normalized Net Profit" (NNP) is the only metric that truly reflects your practice's value. Participants will learn to activate powerful levers for success, from mastering Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) to transitioning from reactive reminders to proactive pre-booking systems that slash client lapse rates.
The presentation further explores how to unlock human potential by addressing the "hidden drain" on productivity: the non-technical skills gap and the "Wallet Guardian" mindset. By recalibrating your "Why" around patient advocacy, you can improve clinical outcomes and professional self-worth while reducing the stress and anxiety that lead to high attrition rates. Finally, we provide practical tools for prioritizing "on-business" leadership over "in-business" technical tasks. By utilizing strategies like the Urgent/Important matrix and effective delegation, owners can reclaim 10 to 20 hours of their week to focus on high-value strategic planning. This session offers a proven pathway to enhance patient care, increase financial stability, and ensure a longer, more fulfilling career in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: Exotics Advanced Acupuncture Certification
courses.description: The CuraCore VET Advanced program in Exotic Animal Acupuncture delivers science-based, factual information on the treatment of non-domestic species with medical acupuncture and related techniques. Students learn ways in which basic science and treatment techniques from human and small animal practice translate, with certain modifications, to birds, rabbits, reptiles, and more. Students acquire proficiency in avian acupuncture point locations by first finding these sites on a stuffed animal model of a chicken and inserting push pins. This novel instructional technique adds hand-eye coordination to the online program, along with personalized feedback through video assessment tools.

courses.title: 10 unexpected abnormalities your 'healthy' patients are hiding......and what to do about them
courses.description: This session will highlight 10 common yet unexpected physical examination and laboratory abnormalities in healthy patients discovered during preventive care assessment. Recent published guidelines for life-stage assessment in dogs and cats will be briefly reviewed. Practical tips on interpreting results and current treatment recommendations will be provided.

courses.title: Veterinary Anesthesia Nerds Symposium powered by VetBolus
courses.description: Earn up to 20.5 hours (15 hours of lecture, 5.5 hours of labs) of RACE and NYSED-approved CE while soaking in the centuries-old adobe charm of Santa Fe, NM. With over 300 days of sunshine, it's a haven for art lovers, foodies, and outdoor adventurers alike. Stroll throught he historic Plaza, explore immersive experiences like Meow Wolf, hike scenic mountain trails, and savor chile-infused cuisine that's as bold as as the landscape. Whether you're chasing sunsets or stories, Santa Fe delivers soul in every step.

courses.title: Introduction to Small Animal Laparoscopy
courses.description: Minimally-invasive surgery (MIS) is the standard of care for many human procedures and is increasingly the expectation of many of our more discerning pet-owning clients in progressive veterinary practices. Now is the time for you to reach for new professional horizons and discover the many advantages of laparoscopic organ biopsy, diagnostic techniques and surgical procedures. Your new skills will distinguish you and your practice within your community!

courses.title: What does CKD have to do with VBD?
courses.description: Two retrospective studies were performed to determine if exposure to tick-borne disease is associated with an increased risk of kidney disease. These studies identified an association between dogs with positive Lyme disease or Ehrlichia test results and an increased risk for chronic kidney disease (CKD) in endemic areas. This webinar will discuss the risks associated with tick-borne disease in your patients.

courses.title: Destination People for Vets Live
courses.description:
Destination People for Vets Live is a professional development program designed to enhance leadership, communication, and people-management skills within the veterinary profession.
Teaching the essential skills required to effectively lead teams and manage client relationships, participants will develop the knowledge, tools, and confidence to foster positive workplace cultures, improve client interactions, and sustain long-term professional fulfillment.
The absence of formal leadership training can contribute to stress, burnout, and diminished job satisfaction, with significant implications for mental health and overall career sustainability. Destination People for Vets Live addresses these challenges by:
-Providing structured approaches to leadership and team management
-Developing skills for client communication and relationship-building
-Supporting strategies that place people (both team members and clients) at the center of veterinary practice
-Creating a shared learning environment that acknowledges common professional struggles and leverages collective problem-solving.
Upon completion of Destination People for Vets Live, participants can expect to achieve measurable improvements in both professional and personal domains, including:
-Enhanced alignment between career expectations and day-to-day professional reality
-Improved work-life balance
-Increased practice efficiency, profitability, and sustainable growth with reduced stress
-Strengthened ability to empower and motivate teams
-Improved client relationships, resulting in stronger trust, adherence, and appreciation for veterinary services.
This program is delivered across 20 hours of live online learning sessions which combine training, mentoring, and coaching to create applied learning that is safe, engaging, and directly transferable to clinical and business contexts. Every session is designed with measurable objectives, real-world case studies, and evidence-based teaching methods, including blended learn

courses.title: IVPA 1st QTR 2026 Virtual Summit
courses.description: The Independent Veterinary Practitioners Association presents a half-day of practice management content.

courses.title: Introduction to Inventory
courses.description: Inventory management involves more than ordering and stocking. When done well, it contributes to a healthy top and bottom line as well as solid patient care. This course will teach the basics of inventory management including inventory terminology, roles, grading, and turnover. Moving from a historical place where one person handled all inventory all aspects of inventory to sharing the load with teammates requires an examination of all of the tasks involved in inventory management. This course includes a resource section that will get you started on the right foot to understanding the role of inventory in a practice and how to effectively manage it.

courses.title: Reducing Pain and Improving Mobility: Environmental Management for OA Patients
courses.description: Environmental modification is a critical yet often underutilized component of comprehensive osteoarthritis (OA) management in dogs. This program provides veterinary professionals with practical strategies to identify and address environmental factors that contribute to pain, impaired mobility, and increased risk of injury in canine OA patients. Participants will explore how common household challenges--such as slippery flooring, stairs, furniture access, and resource placement--can negatively impact joint health and daily function.
