The session will focus on simple, effective interventions that can be implemented to promote joint protection, improve mobility, and support safe movement within the home environment. Emphasis will also be placed on the role of caregiver education in successful OA management. Attendees will learn how to guide pet owners in recognizing environmental barriers and adopting sustainable modifications that enhance comfort, confidence, and quality of life for their dogs. Through practical, real-world applications, this program aims to reinforce the importance of integrating environmental management into multimodal OA treatment plans, supporting better long-term outcomes for canine patients.

courses.title: Rhino Dehorning Mission
courses.description:
Join our team on a week-long educational course about rhino care, management, and medicine whilst you help with an exciting dehorning mission. This is ideal for anyone wanting to support conservation, and developing clinical knowledge and skills around megaherbivore medicine. This mission is not just a training course. It's an experience that connects participants to the broader concepts of wildlife conservation, immerses them in the African wilderness, and fosters a sense of unity among those who share a passion for preserving the world's rhino population.
The majestic rhinoceros, one of the world's most iconic animals, has been pushed to the brink of extinction due to poaching, habitat loss, and the illegal trade of its horns. These magnificent creatures, revered for their strength and resilience, have become targets for poachers who seek to profit from the black-market value of rhino horn. Conservation efforts have intensified globally, and one of the most effective methods of protecting rhinos from poaching is dehorning.
Dehorning is bringing them back from the brink. This is the backdrop of the Rhino Dehorning Mission, a hands-on educational program designed to bring passionate people in the veterinary industry together in a collaborative effort to protect rhinos. For seven days, participants aim to dehorn at least 6 rhinos, whilst also carrying out practical training and immersive lectures about the science of rhino health, anatomy, physiology, and immobilization. When the sun sets, the evenings are filled with social and cultural activities, including bush walks, campfires, and traditional African dance performances so delegates can discover more about Namibian culture and history. The mission schedule may alter and change depending on the weather and animals. For example, we may do more dehornings on a single day than planned if many rhinos are found in one area. We may even dart multiple rhinos at once! In such instances, the lectures will be shifted around

courses.title: Anesthetic management of small animals with co-existing conditions and diseases
courses.description: Familiarity with the underlying disease conditions and their impact on anesthetics improves the outcome of the anesthetic procedure and is a necessary step for practicing veterinarians. In addition, controlling pain and appropriate analgesic medications and methods are essential for animals welfare and improving the outcome of the procedures. In this course, these topics will be discussed in detail to help clinicians design anesthetic and analgesic protocols tailored to the needs of the animal and the disease condition.

courses.title: Seizures in Canine and Feline Patients
courses.description: Seizure disorders are among the most urgent and stressful neurologic emergencies encountered in veterinary practice. This course introduces seizure disorders in dogs and cats with a practical, support-staff focused approach. Learners will build a foundational understanding of what seizures are and why they occur, explore common extra cranial and intracranial causes, and review how clinicians diagnose seizure disorders including the concept of idiopathic epilepsy as a diagnosis of exclusion. Emphasis is placed on recognizing seizure types and stages, understanding emergency priorities, and supporting patients during and after seizure events. Veterinary support staff will also learn key nursing-care considerations, first-line treatment concepts, and effective client communication strategies, particularly when seizures become prolonged or life-threatening.

courses.title: Mass Effect: Decoding the Suspicious Lump
courses.description: This 15-minute presentation offers a practical overview of diagnostic options for evaluating suspicious masses in veterinary patients. Attendees will learn when to pursue further testing and how to choose between cytology, histopathology, and newer diagnostic tools. The goal is to support faster, more informed decisions that improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: CURRENT CONCEPTS IN CLINICAL NUTRITION (637-43463)
courses.description: The lecture is 45 minutes and consists of speaker Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVEC, doing a formal presentation on nutrition and diet information for treating unique conditions. Nutrition intersects all types of clinical conditions including cognitive dysfunction, heart disease, hyperthyroidism, renal disease, atopic conditions and cancer. Join Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh DVM, DACVECC in this lecture regarding nutrition as it relates to certain conditions in companion animals.

courses.title: Inventory Management 2: Managing Movement
courses.description: Inventory management is a multi-faceted responsibility. There are several activities that move product through to the end user. In this course the learner will discover all of the stages of inventory movement starting with when and how much product to order, how to build orders, vendors and buying groups, placing and receiving orders, then ending with the sale and use of products.

courses.title: Through the Lens of Trauma: Experiences in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This lecture, presented by Chief Medical Officer Shana O'Marra, DVM, DACVECC, and Veterinary Well-being Program Director Debrah Lee, LCSW, will examine the concept of trauma in the veterinary world. Trauma is woven throughout many aspect of veterinary medicine and can influence the way we experience out work. Recognizing the impact of trauma can help us to better understand communication challenges and difficult team dynamics. We will discuss how trauma contributes to burnout and compassion fatigue in the individual and how trauma can influence the culture of a practice. Lastly, we will discuss how trauma-informed approaches can contribute to the mental health of your team.

courses.title: Module 4: Canine and Feline Lymphoma
courses.description: A comprehensive overview of lymphoma, diagnosing stage and treatment choices in dogs and cats

courses.title: Risk of Cancer Module 4: Environmental Risks of Cancer in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Cancer is an emotionally charged and complex topic. Recognizing the inherent cancer risks that abound can help guide clinical suspicions and/or inform type and cadence of proactive testing for cancer. This short video module outlines mechanisms of environmental damage to cells, describes key environmental risk factors for cancer in dogs and cats, and identifies recognized regional influences on cancer development. Amed with this information, veterinary clinicians can educate pet owners and recommend patient lifestyle modifications that may help prevent cancer. They can also offer routine cancer screening for pets with environmental exposures and other risk factors that may aid in early diagnosis and support better outcomes.

courses.title: Basic and Point-of-Care Ultrasound: Abdomen, Thorax and Cardiac!
courses.description:
Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is a rapidly evolving field in veterinary medicine, especially in Emergency Medicine. Ultrasound machines are often available to practitioners, but training is lacking. There is limited training in veterinary school, and the post-graduate training is not uniform. Unfortunately, this means your brand-new shining machine may be sitting in a corner of your clinic collecting dust or being used only for cystocentesis.
In this course, you will work with experts in emergency medicine and critical care with many years of experience teaching POCUS and you will learn how to use your machine appropriately. This course is mainly designed to use the ultrasound machine as a point-of-care in an emergency but will also teach you to use it as a tool for abdominal ultrasound. The great thing about this course is that you will learn to ultrasound the abdomen, the chest, and the heart.
You will be provided in-person lectures on the three types of POCUS in the morning, followed by a 4-hours hands-on lab on anesthetized small to medium breed dogs. The same pattern will be repeated on Day 2, which allows for repetition and building on those motor skills. This lab is a great way to learn, practice or refine your skills in POCUS. After this course, you will be set to go back to your practice and start applying your skills from Day 1.

courses.title: XX Southern European Veterinary Conference. SEVC 2026, Barcelona, Spain
courses.description: XX Southern European Veterinary Conference. SEVC 2026, Barcelona, Spain

courses.title: SURGICAL MANAGEMENT OF IDIOPATHIC CHYLOTHORAX (637-43302)
courses.description: The lecture is 53 minutes and consists of speaker Andrea Sundholm, DVM, DACVS-SA, doing a formal presentation on surgery management of chylothorax. Chylothorax is a primary (idiopathic) or secondary condition where chyle accumulates in the pleural space. Andrea Sundholm will discuss the typical signalment and clinical signs, etiology, diagnostic plan including advanced imaging modalities, medical management and surgical intervention, anesthesia and post-operative care for patients with chylothorax.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Aggressive Anesthesia
courses.description: This CE will discuss approaches to anesthetizing the aggressive patient. We will discuss causes of aggression in veterinary patients, non-pharmaceutical methods & pharmaceutical methods of working with these animals prior to anesthesia.

courses.title: What's New in Veterinary Trauma Literature?
courses.description: Review updates in veterinary trauma literature with Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC. In this lecture we'll specifically discuss insights gained from the VetCOT Initiative and use of the Animal Trauma Triage Score.

courses.title: CANNABIS AND PETS - FOR VETERINARY PROFESSIONALS (1429-37509)
courses.description: Cannabis has been called a pharmacological treasure trove by doctors and researchers around the world for its ability to treat pain, anxiety, inflammation, nausea, seizures, and potentially even cancer. Cannabinoid therapeutics is currently the hottest topic in medicine, and it will have a pivotal role in how medicine is practiced. While most people have heard of cannabis' benefits for human ailments, many are unaware that animals can also benefit from cannabis. Join Dr.Tim Shu, veterinarian, founder, and CEO of VETCBD, for a discussion on cannabinoid therapeutics, its role in veterinary medicine, and the exciting future of cannabis medicine. Dr.Shu will provide insight on the science and benefits of cannabis, as well as the regulatory and legal obstacles that practitioners face.

courses.title: Regenerative Medicine in Veterinary Health: PRP & Stem Cell Therapy
courses.description:
This course introduces regenerative medicine as it pertains to the veterinary health
market. We will discuss the science behind stem cell therapy and PRP, as well as
the advancements made in the field. The focus will be to highlight areas that may
have clinical relevance to practitioners and how this can be applied to their
practice.

courses.title: The Use of Bacterial Cultures in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Bacterial cultures are regularly used in the treatment of conditions such as pneumonia, sepsis, gall bladder disease, and complex wounds. When collected and evaluated properly, cultures can provide life-saving (and low cost) options for your patients. Join Critical Care Specialist Hannah Marshall, DVM, DACVECC, in this one hour lecture about the collection, interpretation, and use of bacterial cultures in emergency veterinary medicine.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Never Too Young nor Too Old for Drugs!
courses.description: This CE discusses the physiologic differences between pediatric and geriatric veterinary patients, and how those differences impact your anesthetic choices.

courses.title: Anesthesia from A-Z
courses.description:
This course provides an in-depth look at the entire perianesthetic period, from anesthesia planning and patient stabilization, premedication and induction, to the maintenance and recovery of veterinary anesthesia patients. A review of cardiopulmonary physiology and how it is affected by anesthetic agents and adjuncts will be presented. Best-practice monitoring procedures and managing common anesthesia-related complications will be discussed. The course
also includes a detailed look at pain physiology and how best to provide ideal perioperative analgesia to veterinary patients.
While this course focuses on the care of dogs and cats, the principles described are applicable across most companion animals.

courses.title: Abdominal Exploration and Gastrointestinal Surgery
courses.description: In this course, your learning will focus on basic abdominal surgical procedures with strong emphasis upon gastrointestinal procedures commonly performed in a general practice setting. You will learn basic principles of biopsy collection, enteromy, gastrotomy, intestinal resection & anastomosis, omental / serosal patching, enteroplication and esophago-gastro-enteric tube placement.

courses.title: Structural & Functional Assessment of the Equine Spine - Head
courses.description: This course module provides foundational knowledge needed to evaluate horses with temporomandibular joint and hyoid apparatus disorders. Content includes topographic features, review of muscle of mastication, and detailed descriptions of specific articular features of the temporomandibular joint and hyoid apparatus. Biomechanical insights into mandibular movement during mastication, hyoid movements, and the effects of dental occlusion on pain and dysfunction of the equine head are provided. Pathological descriptions include material on temporomandibular joint pain and the pathogenesis of temporohyoid osteoarthropathy. Physical examination skills include observations of static and dynamic behaviors and the role of active and passive joint motion in identifying sources of pain and discomfort localized to the equine head. Treatment options include discussion of conservative approaches for managing temporomandibular joint pain and dysfunction in horses

courses.title: Canine Cardiomyopathy
courses.description: Explore the causes of myocardial dysfunction in dogs and the common associated symptoms with Veterinary Cardiologist Caryn Reynolds, DVM, DACVIM (Cardiology). Learn more about diagnostic testing options and the current medical treatments available for your patients.

courses.title: CBC in cancer patients: whats worrying? whats not? and why should I care?
courses.description: How to identify hematologic changes suggestive or diagnostic for neoplasia. How to monitor cancer patients undergoing treatment.

courses.title: Inventory Management 4: Metrics & Measurements
courses.description: As with any activity in business, the inventory and pharmacy in a veterinary practice must be measured. Learn more about inventory forecast measures, budgeting and reviewing inventory, along with inventory benchmarking in this inventory management course.

courses.title: New insights into phosphate homeostasis in feline early CKD: the role of fibroblast growth factor 23
courses.description: Overview discussion of FGF-23, what it is, the relationship with CKD and how to use FGF-23 to monitor treatment in cats.

courses.title: Chronic Enteropathy
courses.description: This lecture aims to provide referring veterinarians with an overview of canine chronic enteropathy (inflammatory bowel disease) with a focus on diagnosis, management and when to refer. Real world case example is provided.

courses.title: Speaking in Dog: A Guide to Reading and Reacting to Canine Body Language
courses.description:
Understanding what dogs are saying through their body language is essential for safe, low stress handling and building trust in the clinical setting. In this informative session, a professional dog trainer will guide you through the subtle cues and signals dogs use to communicate fear, stress, discomfort, and friendliness.
Whether youre in the exam room, triage, or treatment area, this session will equip you with the tools to better understand your canine patients and respond in ways that foster safety, trust, and improved outcomes.

courses.title: Achieve Lowest-Dose Radiation: Radiation Safety Is Your Safety
courses.description: The primary challenge of Radiation Protection (RP) safety programs is to keep the radiation dose at a minimum while obtaining the highest image quality needed for accurate medical diagnosis, i.e. achieving the Optimal Dose. Optimal Dose is best accomplished when a Radiation Safety Culture is fostered. This discussion aims to review the use of the As Low As Reasonably Achievable or A.L.A.R.A. principle as well as optimization of the image and dose by applying A.L.A.R.A. Through use of ALARA guidelines including education, equipment selection, and anatomic radiographic techniques selection, we can reduce veterinary patient dose, which reduces occupational staff and general public exposure.

courses.title: Getting Started with the Catalyst One Chemistry Analyzer
courses.description: The goal of this course is to equip veterinary technicians and staff with the knowledge and practical skills needed to confidently operate the Catalyst One Chemistry Analyzer, including proper sample preparation, accurate test execution, result interpretation, and routine maintenance, to ensure reliable diagnostic outcomes and optimal patient care.

courses.title: IMPROVING THE EUTHANASIA EXPERIENCE; NON-MEDICAL OFFERINGS IN INTERACTIVES SESSIONS
courses.description: This series explores the veterinary professional's experience with euthanasia, offering ways to avoid common mistakes and bringing improved methodology to light. This series will combat the dreaded compassion fatigue and burnout by showcasing compassionate measures that can be taken efficiently and with the care of the pet, pet owner and veterinary staff in mind. A special focus is taken to cover the soft skills that Euthanasia requires, but veterinarians often lack training in. Resources for both the veterinary staff members and pet owners will be provided.

courses.title: AAHA INTRODUCTION TO RADIATION SAFETY (1007-38758)
courses.description: The AAHA Introduction to Radiation Safety course covers safety principles of radiation for traditional veterinary practices where general radiography is the most common imaging modality. This course, which is mandatory for all individuals in AAHA member practices, introduces learners to the components of ALARA, discusses proper occupational dose limits for patients during radiography, and gives additional guidance on improving radiation safety in a practice.

courses.title: CRASH COURSE IN VEHICULAR TRAUMA (637-42657)
courses.description: The lecture is 76 minutes and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on trauma caused by vehicle collisions. Josh Cruz, DVM, reviews how to triage, assess, and treat hit by car traumas in an emergency and critical care hospital.

courses.title: IV Catheter Placement and Maintenance
courses.description: This course covers intravenous and central line catheters, including tips and tricks for placement, maintenance and troubleshooting issues.

courses.title: Beyond Stressed About Hypercortisolism?
courses.description: A case-based approach to canine hypercortisolism discussing presentation, clinical signs, diagnostic options, treatment and management. The content will discuss challenges with diagnosis and considerations around when and how to treat this disease, as well as the impact of concurrent diseases when managing patient outcomes.

courses.title: Acute Kidney Injury in Practice-- The Landscapes for Diagnosis and Treatment are Shifting!
courses.description: Kidney function in health and disease is impacted by diverse risk factors, injury, and outcomes. In this archived webinar we will explore the concept of acute kidney injury (AKI) and compare with the older nomenclature of acute kidney failure. We will review traditional biomarkers of renal disease and introduce newer markers of renal injury including urinary cystatin B. Identification of acute kidney injury and indication of an active process provide the veterinary professional an opportunity to intervene earlier in the course of disease, and in some cases before changes in functional markers occur, potentially improving patient outcomes. We will briefly review peer-reviewed evidence in support of clinical applications of AKI biomarkers and demonstrate utility using clinical cases.

courses.title: Hematology Beyond the Numbers
courses.description: Hematology is more than the CBC numbers on a report. Using all the data, both visual and numeric, can help validate your CBC results and deliver more clinical insights into your patients health, whether they present for a medical concern or for preventive care. In this 60-minute presentation Dr. Kim Yore will review CBC basics and lead a study of dot plots and blood smears using several case examples. Prepare to level up and use hematology beyond the numbers for improved clinical decision-making.

courses.title: Piecing It Together - A comprehensive approach to challenging cases
courses.description: Join us for a practical, case based discussion on diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for some common yet challenging clinical presentations, such as respiratory distress (here s looking at you, old brachycephalic dogs) and acute abdominal pain with vomiting. These cases will be approached collaboratively from the perspective of an internist criticalist and a radiologist, with a specific focus on practical, accessible diagnostics and therapeutics. In this discussion we ll explore point-of-care strategies as well as advanced diagnostic and treatment options to consider so that you ll walk away with a holistic perspective on how to approach these tricky cases.

courses.title: Addisons Disease Adrenal Insufficiency: The Human Perspective
courses.description: This presentation will explore a case study of primary adrenal insufficiency (Addisons disease) in a human patient, highlighting the diagnostic process, clinical presentation, and treatment strategy. Through a comparative lens, the session will examine commonalities and differences in the pathophysiology, clinical signs, and diagnostic workup of Addisons disease in both human and veterinary medicine. Attendees will gain an understanding of current treatment protocols in each field and how species-specific considerations influence clinical decision-making. By analyzing both human and canine cases, this talk will provide a deeper appreciation for adrenal insufficiency across species and enhance diagnostic reasoning in practice.

courses.title: The Impact of the Human-Animal Bond on End-of-Life Care Experiences and Outcomes
courses.description: This panel discussion will feature practicing veterinarians and experts in end-of-life care who will explore the profound impact of the human-animal bond on enhancing euthanasia experiences and outcomes for pet owners. The experts will highlight how a strong, compassionate connection between humans and their pets can significantly influence the emotional and psychological aspects of euthanasia. The panelists will also discuss research findings showing that pet owners rely on their veterinary team to help them with end-of-life decisions and arrangements, and how this information can help guide veterinary teams efforts related to communication, care and services related to end-of-life. They will emphasize the importance of empathy and understanding in veterinary practice, noting that veterinarians and veterinary practices who recognize and honor the bond will be able to provide more supportive and personalized care during end-of-life decisions.

courses.title: The Science of High Performing Teams in Specialty Medicine
courses.description: The Science of High Performing Teams in Specialty Medicine explores the intersection of clinical excellence, leadership, communication, and systems design in modern specialty veterinary practice. This presentation examines the evidence and behavioral principles that drive high-performing medical teams, including psychological safety, trust, role clarity, cognitive diversity, accountability, and shared purpose. Drawing from specialty medicine, healthcare leadership research, and real-world operational experience, the session highlights how exceptional teams move beyond individual expertise to create scalable, resilient, and collaborative clinical environments. Attendees will gain practical insights into building team culture, improving interdisciplinary communication, reducing friction in complex medical systems, and developing sustainable models that support both patient outcomes and professional fulfillment in specialty practice.

courses.title: Optimization of Your Diagnostic Imaging Procedure for Best Patient Care Outcomes
courses.description: In this webinar you will learn important factors in taking optimal radiographs, optimizing workflows, and implementing radiation safety practices to keep patients and staff safe.

courses.title: The Power of Effective Communication Before, During and After the Visit
courses.description: The purpose of this module is to provide practice members with practical tips on how to engage clients using effective client communication during a preventive healthcare visit. This course consists of three parts before, during and after the visit.

courses.title: Distress, Diarrhea, and Dysbiosis . . . Oh, My! Updates on the Diagnosis and Management of Chronic Enteropathy in Dogs
courses.description: Chronic gastrointestinal issues can be some of the most frustrating pathologies seen by veterinarians, as these cases can be difficult to manage and often require multiple therapy trials--all while simultaneously testing the patience of pet owners. This course is intended to provide veterinarians with a standardized approach to the diagnosis and management of chronic enteropathy in dogs. Recent novel research into the dietary management of chronic enteropathy in dogs will also be presented which challenges much of the conventional wisdom related to the selection of diets for dietary therapy while highlighting a remarkable success rate of simple dietary change in these patients.

courses.title: Mandibular Canine Extractions
courses.description: Extraction of the mandibular canine tooth is the most common extraction associated with iatrogenic fracture and extraction dehiscence. It is an extraction that practitioners dread and occasionally avoid. In this course, we will review relevant anatomy, learn about recommended equipment, evaluate flap, bone removal and closure techniques. The course will finish with case discussions of mandibular extractions and a video demonstration

courses.title: Lead Like No Ones Watching: Influence without Authority
courses.description: Leadership doesnt require a title it requires initiative, empathy, and the ability to move people forward. In this session, veterinary team members will learn how to lead from any position through relationship-building, communication, and everyday influence. Attendees will explore practical tools to speak up, solve problems collaboratively, and inspire change without formal authority. The session emphasizes how trust and credibility are earned through consistent action, not job titles. Whether you're a technician, CSR, assistant, or aspiring manager, this session will help you strengthen your leadership presence and contribute to a culture of respect, accountability, and teamwork.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Introduction to Canine Rehabilitation
courses.description:
This course is the first of four modules for CCRT, CCRVT/CCRVN, and CCRA certification.
The course comprises online pre-course videos that must be watched before class and four days in class.
This course gives students a fundamental understanding of canine functional anatomy, physiology, and biomechanics. Using clay, students build relevant structures on canine skeletons and get hands-on experience palpating live dogs in class.
Common orthopedic and neurological disorders of the canine patient, including conservative and surgical treatment options. Canine rehabilitation therapies that apply traditional physical therapy techniques, including manual therapies, therapeutic exercise, and physical modalities, are taught along with ways to incorporate them into veterinary practice.

courses.title: TPLO 201- Level Up!
courses.description:
You have been trained in TPLO and you have gained experience in treating large breeds with mild stifle instability due to either early stage disease or due to chronic periarticular fibrosis, but small breeds, dogs with severe instability due to acute or complete CrCL rupture, and dogs with concurrent patellar luxation challenge you or perhaps you avoid these cases all together.
We have designed this TPLO 201 course so that you can take those next steps in your TPLO training and, perhaps, expand your patient spectrum. In this course, you will enjoy over 3 hours of online learning at your own pace and in your place as you prepare for your more intensive in-person and hands on training. In this hybrid course you will learn to:
Identify patients at risk for persistent post TPLO stifle rotational instability and treat them by integrating an InternalBrace extracapsular suture with their TPLO.
Perform the nuanced TPLO techniques needed in small breeds of dogs.
Intraoperatively assess and treat minor tibial torsional and varus conformations that contribute to rotational instability using the TPLO jig.
Assess patients with concurrent patellar luxation and CrCLD
to determine if trochleoplasty is indicated
to determine if lateral tibial tuberosity transposition (TTT) is indicated.
Identify patients with combined excessive TPA and caudal tibial long axis shift, TLAS, for whom TPLO is contraindicated and describe their treatment options.

courses.title: Poop, There It Is: Unlocking the Power of FMT in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This webinar explores Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) in veterinary medicine, particularly its role in integrative and holistic approaches. It covers the history of FMT in human medicine, its current applications in veterinary medicine, and its potential for treating various conditions in animals. The webinar features a panel discussion with veterinarians sharing their experiences and insights on using FMT, followed by a Q&A session with the audience.

courses.title: Digital Client Experience for the New Generation of Pet Parents
courses.description:
With pet ownership on the rise and spending growing, so do the expectations of a new generation of pet owners who demand seamless and convenient access to services. These tech-savvy consumers are reshaping the way we deliver care, seeking not only exceptional medical expertise but also an experience that matches the convenience of their everyday digital lives. The session will explore the technology-driven patient journey, where every step, from booking appointments to follow-up care, can deliver a WOW client experience.
Advances in veterinary innovation, from texting and mobile apps to virtual care and artificial intelligence, are setting new standards of care, enabling a more connected and personalized client experience.
By integrating tech-driven solutions that elevate the client experience at every touchpoint - from booking appointments to follow-up visits - you'll not only improve compliance but also foster deeper relationships that turn satisfied clients into enthusiastic advocates for your practice. This session will uncover how adopting a hospitality-focused mindset through technology can enhance client loyalty, boost your practice's revenue, and make your workplace more enjoyable for everyone.

courses.title: BLOOD TRANSFUSION BASICS (637-41811)
courses.description: The lecture is 56 minutes and consists of speakers doing a formal presentation on transfusion medicine in dogs and cats. Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, discusses blood types, blood components, and monitoring for transfusion reactions.

courses.title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA), Euglycemic DKA (eDKA), and Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic Syndrome (HHS) in Companion Animals
courses.description: This lecture reviews the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management of diabetic emergencies in veterinary patients, including DKA, euglycemic DKA (eDKA), and HHS. Key topics include recognition of clinical signs, diagnostic criteria, and differentiation between these conditions. Emphasis is placed on the "four pillars" of treatment: fluid therapy, insulin administration, correction of electrolyte and acid-base disturbances, and management of underlying causes. Special attention is given to emerging conditions such as eDKA associated with SGLT2 inhibitors, as well as practical clinical decision-making and monitoring strategies in critically ill diabetic patients.

courses.title: Aortic Thromboembolism in Cats
courses.description:
In this course, participants will review the pathogenesis of thromboembolic
disease in cats. We will describe the risk factors that preclude cardiac cats to this particular
complication, prevention mechanisms and treatment courses.

courses.title: Essential AI and Digital Tools for Veterinary Researchers
courses.description: This talk focuses on how to streamline academic writing using artificial intelligence (AI) and digital tools. Dr. Chu introduces a structured workflow (Acquisition, Collection, Crystallization, and Utilization) for efficiently managing literature searches, organizing references, and enhancing writing productivity. She discusses various AI-powered tools such as Perplexity, Consensus, Research Rabbit, and Zotero for literature management, as well as Heptabase for note-taking and ChatGPT for academic support. Additionally, she addresses ethical considerations in AI-assisted writing and the evolving role of AI in research. The talk provides practical insights for veterinarians in academia researchers who are looking to enhance their academic productivity with AI-driven solutions.

courses.title: A Complete Introduction to Safety-Focused TPLO
courses.description:
This hybrid course includes 3 comprehensive hours of bite sized online modules that provide valuable tips on pathophysiology of CrCL disease, diagnosis, positioning for TPLO radiographs, preoperative planning, meniscal injury and treatment, and reducing surgical site infections.
Once in our CE lab, you will develop your hands on surgical skills to perform stifle arthrotomy, meniscal treatment, and TPLO using plastic bone models and cadaveric specimens. This is the only TPLO course in North America that supports you each step of the way during and after your training. While here, you will also spend time in insightful radiographic review discussions of your TPLOs before repeating the procedure on your pathway toward mastery.
Ponder this, even if you were trained to fly a Boeing 737, would you pilot a commercial flight without the decision making support of a flight plan, a co pilot, control tower and ground crew? Of course not. So, why would you do a surgery as intricate as TPLO without using a support team to enhance the safety for your patient?
This course trains you to use patient specific pre, intra and post-operative support on your individual TPLO patients. You will learn how to receive case by case preoperative guidance and procedural planning, use patient specific instructions to perform a guided TPLO cut, and to use detailed postoperative critique to shorten your learning curve and more rapidly grow your skills. Curious what this is all about? Better check it out.

courses.title: Procedures for Productive Check-Ins and Outs
courses.description: This program will discuss procedures at the front desk during the check-in and check-out process that will help your staff increase efficiency, client satisfaction and revenue for your practice.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Management of Feline Subclinical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
courses.description: Feline Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common heart disease in cats with most showing no symptoms. Attendees will start with a review of the condition's pathophysiology and its epidemiology. We will then dive into the various diagnostic tests available and case examples and on how to properly treat and communicate effectively with patient owners. Lastly, we will discuss the most up-to-date data from clinical trial findings in hopes to improve feline patients.

courses.title: Structural and Functional Assessment of the Equine Spine- Equine Zoonotic Disease
courses.description: This course module provides the foundational information needed to recognize clinical signs of contagious and zoonotic diseases as they relate to the animal chiropractic practitioner. Detailed definitions and examples of infection, contagious, zoonotic, and reportable diseases in Colorado are introduced. The clinical signs indicative of acute respiratory and neurologic disease in horses is presented with recommendations for biosecurity precautions to help recognized and limit the spread of equine herpes virus, West Nile virus and rabies. Additional information on the incidence and pathogenesis of equine influenza, strangles and vesicular stomatitis in horses is included.

courses.title: Twisted Pathogens: Updates on Canine Lyme Disease and Leptospirosis
courses.description: This presentation will review the etiology, pathogenesis, clinical signs, and presenting complaints related to Lyme disease and leptospirosis in dogs. Detailed coverage of several algorithms for treatment and vaccination strategies for both Lyme disease and leptospirosis, as well as future testing in dogs that are Lyme positive will be presented. Practitioners will be able to describe the signs associated with Lyme infection and leptospirosis, describe testing and treatment options, and understand vaccination strategies. Learners will also explore how Lyme and leptospirosis are both wildlife associated diseases and what dogs could be at risk.

courses.title: Intro to Oncology; Nursing Considerations for the Oncology Patient
courses.description: This course will demonstrate nursing techniques with cancer patients for veterinary technicians and nurses.

courses.title: Transforming Early Lymphoma Detection: The Impact of Innovation in Cancer Care
courses.description: This educational session will focus on the innovation and impact of a new diagnostic tool for the early detection of lymphoma in canines, IDEXX Cancer Dx. Attendees will learn the scientific foundation, clinical applications and how this diagnostic tool is revolutionizing veterinary practices by allowing broader access to cancer diagnostics. This session will also highlight updates from the time of launch, showcasing its real-world effectiveness, clinical cases encountered, and the promising future of cancer diagnostics in veterinary medicine. Through this session, participants will understand both the clinical and practical aspects of incorporating this diagnostic tool into veterinary practices and its potential to impact the referral community.

courses.title: Exotic Animal Emergencies & Critical Care
courses.description: DoveLewis exotics veterinarian, Kelly Flaminio, DVM, we will provide an overview of the triage and critical care management techniques to care for a variety of exotic species, including reptiles, small mammals, and birds. Attendees can expect to learn how to assess and treat a range of common injuries that these species are susceptible to. We will also discuss cases from DoveLewis, which will allow participants to gain a better understanding of how these techniques are applied in real-life scenarios. This presentation promises to be a great resource for anyone who is interested in learning more about exotic animal care.

courses.title: FEVER OF UNKNOWN ORIGIN (637-42013)
courses.description: This lecture is 60 minutes and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on fevers in canine and feline patients in an emergency room practice. DoveLewis Criticalists Erika Loftin, DVM, DACVECC gives a lecture on the clinical signs, diagnostic considerations, and treatment strategies for veterinary patients suffering from a fever of unknown origin.

courses.title: THE GOOD, THE BAD, AND THE UGLY TRUE TALES OF MANAGEMENT TRIUMPHS AND FAILURES (637-41650)
courses.description: Management true stories from Monica Maxwell, SPHR and Megan Brashear, CVT, VTS (ECC). This lecture is 55 minutes and consists of two speakers doing a formal presentation discussing difficult management decisions and actions.

courses.title: Ear Cytology Interpretation: From Subjective to Standardized
courses.description: Ear cytology is often underused or inconsistently applied in practice, even though it can meaningfully improve diagnostic accuracy, antimicrobial stewardship, and treatment monitoring. This interactive, case-based course makes the invisible variability of traditional glass-slide cytology visible highlighting how common artifacts and interpretation differences can drive over-treatment or missed clinical insights. Learners will work through three realistic otitis cases that demonstrate (1) over-interpretation errors (e.g., melanin granules mistaken for bacteria neutrophil nuclear changes mistaken for yeast), (2) situations where cytology may not match clinical severity, and (3) how inconsistent medical record documentation complicates follow-up decisions. The course then reinforces how IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer supports a standardized workflow, consistent interpretation, and consistent diagnostic output to improve confidence, alignment, and repeatable decision-making.

courses.title: Module 1- Clinical Pathology in Cancer Patients
courses.description: Review of the fundamental elements of clinical pathology in practice and the benefits of consistently applying it to the patient diagnostic approach.

courses.title: IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer* Certificate Course
courses.description: This interactive, self-paced course helps veterinary professionals gain proficiency on the IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer, which provides automated, real-time cytology and blood morphology. Become an IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer expert and contribute to a more streamlined, efficient, and productive in-house laboratory workflow that helps you have extra time to focus on the patients.

courses.title: Hemostasis: A Review of Inherited Bleeding Disorders in Dogs
courses.description: When a canine patient presents for bleeding, the cause isn't always obvious. In this lecture presented by DoveLewis Internist Barbara Davis, DVM, DACVIM, we will review hemostasis and common inherited bleeding disorders in dogs. We will focus on a diagnostic approach, and what treatment options are available in the acute setting.

courses.title: Module 3: What can I do for my Cancer Patient?
courses.description: A focus on post-cancer diagnosis conversations around treatment, management, monitoring and the patient/pet owner bond

courses.title: From National Headlines to Local Exam Rooms: What's Creeping into Companion Animal Practice
courses.description: Emerging and re-emerging parasitic diseases are increasingly capturing national attention, but their impact extends far beyond the headlines and into everyday companion animal practice. Changes in climate, wildlife ecology, animal movement, and global commerce are reshaping parasite distribution patterns, exposing pets and their owners to risks that may not have historically existed in their region. This presentation explores the factors driving parasite emergence and examines several important threats currently affecting veterinary medicine, including the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax), and Echinococcus multilocularis. Participants will review current epidemiologic trends, clinical implications, public health considerations, and practical approaches for identifying and managing these emerging risks. The session will also highlight the veterinarian's role in surveillance, prevention, client communication, and One Health initiatives that support animal and human health. Through an evidence-based review of emerging parasite threats, attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating risk assessment, prevention, and education into daily clinical practice.

courses.title: Take a Breath! Management of Respiratory Emergencies
courses.description: Respiratory emergencies are some of the most intimidating cases that veterinary practitioners see. The critical need for oxygen, the very apparent distress these patients are in, and the need to move quickly through treatment, often with limited ability to perform much diagnostics on these patients all contribute to the stressors on the team. We will discuss logical, straightforward ways to treat and evaluate these patients. We will also discuss interventions such as thoracocentesis, nasal oxygen provision, and if time allows, tracheostomy.

courses.title: Confidence in Cancer Care: Practical Approaches to Canine Hemangiosarcoma Diagnosis and Management
courses.description: This session will provide a clinically focused review of canine hemangiosarcoma (HSA). Hemangiosarcoma remains one of the most biologically aggressive and challenging malignancies faced in veterinary practice. The primary focus will be on visceral hemangiosarcoma, including current understanding of its pathophysiology, biologic behavior, and patterns of metastasis. Typical and atypical clinical presentations will be covered, followed by a review of diagnostic and staging approaches, including currently available imaging modalities and emerging blood-based biomarkers. Currently available treatment strategies will be explored, including surgical intervention, systemic chemotherapy protocols, and the role of radiation therapy where applicable. In addition, the session will review emerging and investigational treatment strategies, including targeted therapies, immunotherapy, nutraceutical adjuncts, with consideration of their potential clinical utility and current limitations. Prognostic factors will be reviewed, including survival outcomes, key prognostic indicators and how these factors inform clinical decision making and client communication. For comparative context, the session will include a brief overview of actinic cutaneous hemangiosarcoma, with emphasis on distinguishing features in etiology, risk factors, clinical behavior, prognosis, and therapeutic considerations relative to visceral disease. By the end of this session, participants will have an evidence-based understanding of canine hemangiosarcoma, with particular emphasis on the recognition, diagnostic workup, staging, and management of visceral disease, as well as an informed perspective on how it differs biologically and clinically from the actinic cutaneous form.

courses.title: Rethinking The Management of Osteoarthritis
courses.description: Attendees will gain an understanding of the importance of recognizing and managing chronic pain, as well as the benefits of early OA diagnosis. Scientific data on multimodal analgesia options will be shared. The importance of pain assessment, intervention, multimodal treatment, and patient follow up will be points of emphasis.

courses.title: Pulmonary Hypertension
courses.description: This lecture will go through the different causes of pulmonary hypertension, diagnosis (echocardiogram and chest radiographs) as well as ancillary diagnostics which are often recommended, treatment options and some case examples.

courses.title: Exposed! Why Exposure to Infected Ticks is just the Beginning
courses.description: In this archived webinar we will review when to screen dogs for tick-borne diseases (TBD), what to do with the results when you get them, and what to do differently with exposed/infected dogs for subsequent yearly exams.

courses.title: Integrative Approach to Diabetes and Cushing's Disease in Small Animals
courses.description: This program is a 4 session learning series. It has been created to bridge the gap between obtaining an education in veterinary acupuncture and effectively applying this modality in a clinical setting as adjunctive treatment and management of diabetes and hyperadrenocorticism (Cushing's disease). TCM strategies associated with acupuncture and other holistic modalities that can add to patient quality of life will be discussed. The program also provides a review of diabetes mellitus and cushing's disease from the conventional standpoint along with current diagnostic and treatment options.

courses.title: Medical Math Mentality
courses.description: Medical math is a foundational competency in veterinary medicine that directly impacts patient safety, treatment effectiveness, and clinical efficiency. This course introduces the medical math mentality, emphasizing understanding calculations rather than memorizing formulas alone. Learners will review essential conversions, percentages, dosages, dilutions, fluid calculations, and constant rate infusions, along with practical equations used in daily practice. The course concludes with practice problems and a knowledge check to reinforce confidence and accuracy in real-world veterinary calculations. Content emphasizes clinical application, double checking techniques, and safe administration principles.

courses.title: Pawsitive Dentistry and Anesthesia Virtual Event
courses.description: This 6-hour virtual event will cover 3 hours of dentistry and 3 hours of anesthesia topics for the general DVM practitioner and the Veterinary Technician.

courses.title: Ears vs. Brain Vestibular Disease and How to Win by Teaming Up
courses.description: This lecture presented by Dr. Sonja Zabel, DVM, MS, DACVD and Dr. Sophie Petersen PhD, DVM, DACVIM, will go over vestibular disease and how to approach these cases for work up dermatologically as well as a neurologically. By using a case-based approach, we will review the neurologic work up, as well as the otoscopy, advanced imaging and medical approach

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Hormonal Anesthesia
courses.description: This CE will discuss how various endocrine disease impact basic physiology and our anesthetic choices in veterinary patients. Attendees will have a better understanding of how these endocrinopathies alter normal physiology & how this impacts anesthetics.

courses.title: Radiographic Case Studies
courses.description: In this lecture presented by DoveLewis Radiologist Alan Lipman, DVM, DACVR, multiple imaging case studies will be presented using multiple radiographic modalities. Case focus will be on routine thoracic and abdominal cases to provide the most educational benefit. Other cases such as musculoskeletal ultrasound will also be covered.

courses.title: Taking Care of You
courses.description: Increased patient counts and wait times. Decreased staffing and patience. It's likely every one of us in the veterinary industry has dealt with compounding stressors over the last year. In this lecture presented by Human Resources Manager Cheryl Latta, we will discuss the inherent difficulties of putting our own needs first, in an industry that requires us to be the caregivers of others. We will explore ways to address difficult obstacles, and how to recognize our own needs to better care for ourselves.

courses.title: Infection in Large Animal Fracture
courses.description: 90 minute webinar reviewing the implications, treatment options, and clinical decision making of infection in large animal orthopedic surgery. Discussion will focus on the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of infection in large animal orthopedic patients with internal fixation for fracture repair or arthrodesis.

courses.title: Dental Radiographic Interpretation
courses.description: Submitting the optimal number of ultrasound images, with the quality and format described, maximizes the diagnostic value of your submission, improves the efficiency with which our radiologists can provide a report, and ultimately enhances your ability to provide prompt and effective care to your patients.

courses.title: IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer Certificate Course
courses.description: This interactive, self-paced course helps veterinary professionals gain proficiency on the IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer, which provides automated, real-time cytology and blood morphology. Become an IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer expert and contribute to a more streamlined, efficient, and productive in-house laboratory workflow that helps you have extra time to focus on the patients.

courses.title: Beyond Expression: A Modern Guide to Anal Gland Health
courses.description: Beyond Expression reframes non-neoplastic anal sac disease as a chronic, inflammatory condition - frequently linked to a comorbidity like allergic disease - requiring a root-cause, evidence-based strategy. Anal sac problems are too often managed as a maintenance task, leading to serial expressions, antibiotic overuse, and frustrated clients. This course equips veterinarians to: (1) distinguish impaction, sacculitis, and abscessation along a continuum; (2) connect clinical signs to underlying allergic and gastrointestinal comorbidities; (3) rely on clinical acumen over low-yield diagnostics; (4) implement comprehensive, inflammation-first management including sedated lavage and medication infusion; and (5) recognize red flags for complex disease (e.g., perianal fistulae, neoplasia) and when to refer. This course covers 3 hours of learning content over several engaging lessons. It is a self-paced, non-interactive distance learning course offered through Dr. Meagan Painter's website dedicated to continuing education about allergic disease: www.theallergicdog.com.

courses.title: Acid-Base Disturbances - A Case Based Approach
courses.description: Do you have a blood gas analyzer but dread using it? Does the base excess make you weak in the knees and the anion gap bewilder you? In this session, a simple, clinically relevant step by step approach to evaluation of acid base status using arterial or venous blood gas samples will be presented. Clinical cases will be used to illustrate the utility of this approach. By the end of this session, you'll be ready to take on anything that the analyzer throws at you.

courses.title: TRANSLATIONAL BIOLOGICS IN VETERINARY MEDICINE: REGENERATIVE MEDICINE & IMMUNOTHERAPY (598-43522)
courses.description: TRANSLATIONAL BIOLOGICS IN VETERINARY MEDICINE: REGENERATIVE MEDICINE & IMMUNOTHERAPY (598-43522) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: C-reactive protein clinical update: getting the most from this diagnostic and prognostic biomarker of systemic inflammation i
courses.description: C-reactive protein (CRP) is a sensitive biomarker of systemic inflammation in dogs with well documented clinical utility in a wide range of commonly encountered diseases. Recent publications have highlighted new indications for its use. This lecture will provide an update and practical tips on using CRP as a diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring tool in a variety of conditions including pancreatitis, cardiorespiratory disease, immune-mediated disease, vector-borne disease, kidney disease, neurologic disease, acute abdomen, and others.

courses.title: How to Get What You Need
courses.description: This lecture presented by Human Resources Manager Cheryl Latta, will discuss how to communicate in ways which result in your needs being met, as well as how to acknowledge when others need something of you. Cheryl will review how knowing your audience, actively listening, and communicating feedback are important communication aspects in any clinic.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Catching the Waves of Capnography
courses.description: This CE will discuss the basics of capnography and it's importance in anesthetic monitoring. We will discuss indications for capnography, how it works, why it matters, and identify & troubleshoot various capnography waveforms.

courses.title: Essential Skills for Administering Supplemental Oxygen
courses.description: Ensuring adequate oxygenation is crucial for the health and well-being of our patients. This comprehensive course delves deep into the world of supplemental oxygen therapy in veterinary medicine, equipping you with the knowledge and skills to confidently manage respiratory distress in various situations.

courses.title: From National News to Local Patients: Emerging Threats in Companion Animal Practice
courses.description: Emerging and re-emerging parasitic diseases are increasingly capturing national attention, but their impact extends far beyond the headlines and into everyday companion animal practice. Changes in climate, wildlife ecology, animal movement, and global commerce are reshaping parasite distribution patterns, exposing pets and their owners to risks that may not have historically existed in their region. This presentation explores the factors driving parasite emergence and examines several important threats currently affecting veterinary medicine, including the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax), and Echinococcus multilocularis. Participants will review current epidemiologic trends, clinical implications, public health considerations, and practical approaches for identifying and managing these emerging risks. The session will also highlight the veterinarian's role in surveillance, prevention, client communication, and One Health initiatives that support animal and human health. Through an evidence-based review of emerging parasite threats, attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating risk assessment, prevention, and education into daily clinical practice.

courses.title: The Importance of Corporate Literacy for Veterinarians
courses.description: Corporate literacy is critical to a veterinarian's ability to navigate, communicate and thrive in a changing landscape where skills of non-medical professionals drive the veterinary profession's financial engine. This course provides education on skills and proficiencies needed in today's world.

courses.title: Controlled Substances in Veterinary Medicine: Inventory Management, Diversion, Preventing Abuse
courses.description: This comprehensive course, designed for veterinarians and veterinary technicians, delves into the crucial aspects of controlled substances in veterinary practice. Gain a thorough understanding of the legal framework, ethical considerations, and best practices for responsible use and management of these medications to effectively manage animal pain while mitigating risks and adhering to regulations.

courses.title: Dr. Becky Krull
courses.description: I am a veterinarian and entrepreneur on a mission to save one veterinarian at a time, showing them how to regain their love for their profession, while following their passion and purpose work. As a thought leader, practicing veterinarian, and owner of a thriving clinic in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Dr. Becky Krull lives to empower other veterinarians to find the equilibrium in their passion work and daily life. She speaks of the daily struggles of working in a high-paced, high-stress profession, as well as a being a mom and wife, and how she found the tools to thrive. She has lived in the trenches and walked the journey of caregiver burnout and is a testament to the personal growth work she follows daily to embrace her passion for practice life. Dr. Krull has been a full-time small animal veterinarian at Buddy's Vets in Green Bay, WI, since 2005. She became a partner and vice president of the cooperation in 2008, taking over full practice ownership and president of the cooperation in 2021. Beyond the scope of veterinary medicine, she has embraced roles as human resources director, marketing director and mentorship lead.

courses.title: The Good, The Bad and the Ugly: Online Criticism and How to Handle It
courses.description: With just the click of a button, a client can hurt your feelings, your business, and your team's wellbeing. Online reputations are more important than ever, so what do you do with a one star review or criticism from clients when it's out there for anyone to read? Learn from Tess Payne, DoveLewis Marketing Director, about the benefits of responding to online feedback and how to make the most of your online presence.

courses.title: Acupuncture and Integrative Veterinary Care for Cardiac Patients
courses.description:
This program is a series that includes 4 learning sessions. It has been created to bridge the gap between obtaining an education in veterinary acupuncture and effectively applying this modality in a clinical setting as adjunctive treatment and management of for veterinary cardiology patients (mainly small animals). The program also highlights additional integrative methods and supplements to support animals with cardiac dysfunction. The protocols and processes delivered in this program are designed to help veterinarians who have already completed basic training in veterinary acupuncture take their learning and skills to the next level. The series will provide templates, quick reference guides and case examples geared toward moving the veterinarian into action.
The first session is a presentation of research findings and evidence-based support for the use of acupuncture in cardiology cases. The second session focuses on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and acupuncture strategies that can be incorporated to enhance treatment and management plans for small animals suffering from cardiac dysfunction. The third session provides case examples of utilizing acupuncture, Traditional Chinese Medicine. The fourth session focuses on integrative management of various cardiac conditions in small animals along with scientific information in the area of neurocardiology, the brain-heart connection.

courses.title: Beyond Grey Muzzles: Unveiling the Science of Canine Aging
courses.description: Our canine companions bring us immense joy throughout their lives, but as they age, their needs evolve. This course delves into the complex world of canine geriatrics. You'll gain a deep understanding of the biological and physiological changes associated with aging in dogs, equipping you to provide exceptional care for your senior patients.

courses.title: A Veterinarian's practical guide to microbiology testing
courses.description: Everything you've ever wanted to know about microbiology but were too afraid to ask. In this course, you will learn when it is important to culture & present a strong argument to your client, select appropriate samples to culture, interpretation and face unusual organisms with equanimity.

courses.title: Pericardial Effusion
courses.description: In this one hour lecture presented by Veterinary Cardiologist Caryn Reynolds, DVM, DACVIM(cardiology) we will discuss common causes of pericardial effusion. We'll review cases seen at DoveLewis, and follow them from presenting symptoms to treatment options.

courses.title: Taking the Bull by the Horns: Effective Inventory Management
courses.description: This course will cover the principles of effective inventory management applicable to small, companion, food or mixed animal practices. We will also discuss marketing and other topics related to inventory turnover.

courses.title: Integrative Approach to Chronic Respiratory Conditions in Small Animals
courses.description:
This program is a 4 session mastermind learning series. It has been created to bridge the gap between obtaining an education in veterinary acupuncture and effectively applying this modality in a clinical setting as adjunctive treatment and management certain conditions that affect the respiratory tract in small animals. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) strategies associated with acupuncture and other holistic modalities that can add to patient quality of life will be discussed. There will be a brief review of the pathophysiology of chronic respiratory conditions from both the conventional and TCM perspective. The protocols and processes delivered in this program are designed to help veterinarians who have already completed basic training in veterinary acupuncture take their learning and skills to the next level.
There are 4 sessions: The first session focuses on neoplastic lung disease. The second session focuses on laryngeal paralysis and geriatric onset laryngeal paralysis and poly neuropathy. The third session is case presentations of patients who have been treated with the integrative approach. The fourth session covers chronic lung disease from the conventional and TCM perspective and integrative management of specific chronic lung conditions.

courses.title: Speaking the Same Language Conquering Chemotherapy
courses.description: General practice veterinarians play a crucial role in every step of a pets cancer journey, from diagnosis, to referral, and to management of the cancer patient. Understanding the basics of chemotherapy terminology that pet owners will encounter is important for counseling them through this journey. In this session, well dive into an overview of chemotherapy, where well cover key terminology, review cellular biology with mechanisms of action of common chemotherapy drugs, and describe the most common side effects of chemotherapy and terminology associated with side effects. This lecture is designed to build your confidence in oncology care, no matter your level of exposure to this field. Youll walk away not only with a stronger foundation but also have more confidence when counseling clients and supporting them through their pets cancer journey.

courses.title: Osteoarthritis-Not just an old dog disease
courses.description: This lecture will focus on prevention of OA and identifying the patients most at risk before OA becomes apparent. Special emphasis will be given to supplements and nutraceuticals that have evidence of efficacy for this subset of patients.

courses.title: EMERGENCY CONDITIONS
courses.description: Understanding emergency and critical care medicine is imperative to focusing on the immediate needs of a severely ill or injured animal. In this course James Barr, DVM, DACVECC and Medora Pashmakova, DVM, DACVECC discuss some of the most common critical care conditions you will see in the veterinary workplace.

courses.title: Following RECOVER Guidelines for CPCR
courses.description: We bring the training to you with a one hour, virtual CPR presentation. All positions within a clinic are encouraged to attend this virtual lecture. Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, walks viewers through the basics of RECOVER CPR and covers instruction for all team members working together.

courses.title: Reticulocytes Count: Why They Are More Important Than Just Classifying Anemia
courses.description: The absolute reticulocyte count measures bone marrow response to demand for red blood cells. The quality of the reticulocyte provides insight into relatively common diseases with or without anemia. Case material will be used as a foundation for discussion on why reticulocyte count.

courses.title: Feline Thyroid Disease: Evidence-Based Diagnostic Approaches and Treatment Strategies
courses.description: 50-minute presentation summarizing the pathophysiology, clinical signs, physical exam findings, diagnostic testing, and treatment for feline hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism for general practitioners though the IDEXX Learning Center

courses.title: HEPATIC LIPIDOSIS (637-39732)
courses.description: The lecture is 55 minutes and consists of presenter Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC doing a formal presentation on Hepatic Lipidosis. This talk will review the pathophysiology of hepatic lipidosis in cats. Diagnosis, acute and long term management will be discussed, as well as nutritional support. The emphasis will be on real life management of the disease.

courses.title: Induction Phase of Anesthesia
courses.description:
This program will provide an overview of the induction phase of general
anesthesia for small animal patients. Specific topics to be discussed include: goals, workflow,
equipment preparation, preoxygenation, commonly utilized induction agents, induction speed,
induction quality, intubation, and initial monitoring.

courses.title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation: When and Why A Case-Based Clinical Approach
courses.description: Dr. Toresson brings extensive clinical experience with FMT and has published two major studies on its use in dogs with non-responsive or partially responsive chronic enteropathies. In this case-based seminar, she will explore the rationale behind FMT, review the latest research findings, and discuss how this therapy influences clinical and metabolic parameters in dogs with acute and chronic enteropathies. Current indications for FMT will be examined, and Dr Toresson will interpret real-world cases, connecting them to emerging evidence and best practices.

courses.title: Implementation and Interpretation of Canine Genetic Screening in General Practice
courses.description: During this course, participants can expect to learn basic genetics terminology and concepts (such as penetrance, expression, and mode of inheritance). A brief overview of the various technologies utilized to determine genotype will be provided. Participants will then learn to apply these concepts through clinical case walkthroughs. Lastly, participants will learn how to communicate the benefits of genetic screening to their clients, and how to effectively relay genetic screening results.

courses.title: Purrfect Microbiomes: Decoding the Feline Gut
courses.description: This webinar study provides a detailed analysis of the key bacteria comprising the feline gut microbiome, building upon the 2022 research published in 'The Kitty Microbiome Project: Defining the Healthy Fecal 'Core Microbiome' in Pet Domestic Cats." Employing full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing, the study established a statistically defined core fecal microbiome at the species level for a cohort of 104 healthy domestic cats (Felis catus) consuming diverse commercial diets. This resultant healthy reference dataset investigated the correlations between fecal microbiome composition and factors such as age, diet, and living environment.

courses.title: Preventive Healthcare: Thriving Pets, Happy Owners, and Successful Practices
courses.description: The course is to learn about the practice of preventive medicine and the medical benefits of performing routine testing on well pets.

courses.title: High Flow Nasal Oxygen: Volumax
courses.description: This lecture discusses the use of high-flow nasal oxygen systems in veterinary medicine, highlighting a new unit adapted from human healthcare. Criticalist Christin Gooding, DVM, DACVECC describes its specialized cannulas designed to cater to veterinary patients and emphasizes its potential applications. The lecture aims to introduce this technology and its benefits for improving animal care.

courses.title: Beyond FAST; Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) for Everyday Practice!
courses.description:
When something is visualized, the truth of its occurrence or existence can no longer be doubted, seeing is Believing. This proverb has particular meaning when it comes point of care ultrasound (POCUS); diagnostic confidence increases in 89.2 percent of patients when general practitioners add bedside POCUS to patient evaluation!
In this half-day hands-on experience, you will learn to ask clinically relevant, often binary yes/no questions so that you can rapidly and efficiently utilize veterinary POCUS to make a difference in the daily assessment and management of your patients!
Through practical, hands-on training using live dogs, participants will have the opportunity to learn and practice all the common veterinary POCUS techniques currently used to assess the abdomen, pleural space, lung, and heart. Phantom training models will also be used to demonstrate and practice ultrasound guided procedures, using a vascular access model.
This lab will focus on techniques developed by the instructors, designed to increase veterinary POCUS diagnostic accuracy, and help facilitate easier application into everyday veterinary practice. These are all techniques that can be performed by any practitioner and should be used in everyday practice!

courses.title: The Anesthesia Continuum: Monitoring, Complications, and Recovery in Veterinary Practice
courses.description:
This comprehensive program explores the full spectrum of veterinary anesthesia, emphasizing patient safety and clinical decision-making from induction through recovery. Participants will gain a deeper understanding of physiologic monitoring, early recognition of anesthetic complications, and effective intervention strategies across a variety of species and clinical scenarios.
The course highlights best practices in anesthetic monitoring, including cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurologic assessment, as well as the interpretation of monitoring equipment and data trends. Attendees will learn how to anticipate, identify, and manage common and critical complications such as hypotension, hypoventilation, arrhythmias, and delayed recovery.
Special focus is placed on the recovery phase, often the most unpredictable period of anesthesia, covering pain management, dysphoria, airway management, and species-specific considerations. Through case-based discussions and practical insights, this program equips veterinary professionals with the tools needed to improve patient outcomes and enhance anesthetic safety in everyday practice.

courses.title: Understanding Owner Behavior: Driving Loyalty & Retention
courses.description: In todays competitive veterinary landscape, understanding what drives client loyalty is essential for long term success. This session will delve into Brakkes Home Delivery Study to uncover key insights on pet owner preferences, trust factors, and purchasing behaviors. We will explore strategies that enhance client retention, improve compliance, and maximize revenue. Attendees will gain practical tools to implement effective home delivery solutions that meet the evolving needs of pet owners while supporting the financial and operational goals of their practice. To bring these insights to life, our expert panel of industry leaders and veterinary professionals will engage in a dynamic discussion, sharing real-world applications and success stories.

courses.title: 2025 Yearly Conference
courses.description:
This year's theme: KNOWLEDGE, LIKE A PRECIOUS METAL IS PRICELESS.
Join us to celebrate our SILVER ANNIVERSARY providing yearly conferences.

courses.title: Chest Wall Surgery and Reconstruction
courses.description: Chest wall resection and reconstruction represent challenging cases. They require careful attention to the diagnosis, the imaging and the surgical planning. In this course, the participants will be exposed to the state-of-the-art techniques to perform with success a chest wall resection and reconstruction. Anesthesia is a critical part of the success for these cases since the pleural space will be entered. Different techniques for pain management will be documented to help the recovery of the patient. Post-operative care is paramount for the success of the procedure. The pulmonary and cardiac physiologies can be deeply affected after chest wall reconstruction. After this course, participants will have a better understanding of the techniques for chest wall reconstruction with mesh

courses.title: Idiopathic Spontaneous Pneumothorax
courses.description: This lecture will cover diagnosis, treatment and outcome for patients with spontaneously occurring pneumothorax. DoveLewis Surgeon Ashley Magee, DVM, DACVS, will review imaging, preoperative stabilization, anesthetic techniques, surgical approaches and post-operative management in a case-based format.

courses.title: Financial Management 2: Expense Management
courses.description: Learners will explore how to integrate their business model into daily practice life in this course. Expense management will include a review of fixed and variable expenses and how to navigate both of these categories.

courses.title: Understanding and Treating OA Pain: Practical Strategies for Veterinary Teams
courses.description:
Effective pain management is fundamental to improving mobility, comfort, and quality of life in dogs with osteoarthritis (OA). This program provides veterinary professionals with a practical, clinically relevant approach to recognizing and managing OA-associated pain across the disease continuum.
Participants will review the mechanisms and clinical presentation of OA pain, with an emphasis on identifying both overt and subtle indicators that may impact patient function and welfare. The session will explore commonly used oral analgesics, including their roles, benefits, and limitations, as well as considerations for when injectable therapies may be introduced to enhance pain control.
In addition, the program will examine how these therapeutic options can be integrated into a multimodal treatment plan tailored to the individual patient. Attendees will also gain insight into when surgical intervention may be appropriate to address underlying joint pathology and improve long-term outcomes.
Through practical guidance and real-world application, this session aims to support veterinary teams in making informed, evidence-based decisions that optimize pain management strategies and improve overall patient care in canine osteoarthritis.

courses.title: Itch to Answer: A Veterinarian's Guide to Allergic Dogs
courses.description: Itch to Answer is a structured continuing education program for veterinarians managing canine atopic dermatitis (cAD) and allergic dermatitis. The course teaches a methodical, evidence-based approach to allergic skin and ear disease in dogs, grounded in The Inflammation First framework. Participants learn pattern recognition, practical pathophysiology, mimicry conditions (scabies, demodicosis, flea allergy dermatitis), infection diagnostics aligned with ISCAID 2025 and WAVD 2020 guidelines, the ICADA-aligned diagnostic work-up including diet trials and timely allergen testing, and the full treatment toolkit from steroids and cyclosporine to JAK inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies, immunotherapy, antibiotics, antifungals, topical therapy, and supplements. The program is meant to elevate the practice and confidence of any small animal practitioner who sees allergic dogs.
