courses.title: Parvovirus: From Diagnosis to Recovery
courses.description: This in-depth course, led by critical care expert Amber Hart, RVT, VTS (ECC), delves into the complexities of canine parvovirus, providing veterinary staff with the latest advancements in diagnosis, treatment, and management. You'll gain the knowledge and skills to confidently navigate every stage of this highly contagious and potentially life-threatening disease.

courses.title: Module 5: Mast Cell Tumors, Osteosarcoma
courses.description: The fundamental approaches to recognition, diagnosis, treatment and monitoring of mast cell disease and canine osteosarcoma

courses.title: Diagnosis and Management of Common Cardiac Comorbidities
courses.description: This webinar will provide a practical approach to cardiac patients that have concurrent disease. Among the comorbidities covered will be renal disease, hypertension, electrolyte disturbances, and various endocrine diseases. Updated treatment recommendations will be provided. Upon completion, participants will be able to recognize, diagnose, and manage common comorbid conditions affecting cardiac patients using current, evidence based treatment strategies.

courses.title: Confidence in Cancer Care: How GPs Can Manage Oncologic Cases When Referral is Not Possible or Pursued
courses.description: General practice veterinarians play a crucial role in every step of a pets cancer journey, from diagnosis, to referral, and to management of the cancer patient. For patients that are unable to pursue referral, general practice veterinarians can safely and effectively manage these patients. In this course, we will cover the principles of chemotherapy in veterinary medicine, including common chemotherapeutics used in veterinary patients, safe handling of chemotherapy drugs, common chemotherapy side effects and how to manage the most common side effects. Participants will learn to identify veterinary patients that are suitable candidates for chemotherapy treatment that can safely be administered in general practice, communicate necessary information with those clients, and develop individualized treatment plans for their patients. This course will address potential side effects and complications of chemotherapy and provide strategies for monitoring and managing these risks. This lecture is designed to build your confidence in oncology care, and your confidence in safely administering specific chemotherapeutics in practice. Youll walk away with a stronger foundation to assist in management with chemotherapy of veterinary cancer patients that are unable to pursue referral.

courses.title: Unlocking Brakkes Home Delivery Data Engaging your Team & Clients Gamifying Home Delivery for Awareness & Compliance
courses.description: Home delivery is a growing revenue stream in pharmacy, but success hinges on team engagement, client awareness, and consistent compliance. This session explores proven strategies to empower staff as effective ambassadors of the service, communicate the value of home delivery to clients, and drive participation through the use of gamification techniques. Attendees will learn how to create meaningful incentives for both staff and clients, turning everyday interactions into opportunities for engagement and adherence. Real-world examples and practical tools will be shared to help veterinary practices implement programs that enhance compliance, increase revenue, and improve client satisfaction.

courses.title: Triage Review
courses.description: In this course, we will review the history of triage, how to initiate a triage exam, triage scoring systems, and how to evaluate respiratory, neurological, abdominal and cardiovascular systems, along with several other pertinent body systems. Lastly, we will discuss how to begin care for a triaged patient.

courses.title: Blood Morphology Matters: The Most Common Clinically Significant CBC Findings You Might Miss if You Dont Smear
courses.description: Microscopic examination of blood films is crucial for accurate diagnostic interpretation that goes beyond just the automated hematology results. In this session, we will review clinically significant abnormalities that are commonly missed if blood films are not evaluated alongside the CBC data, including red blood cell morphology changes, immature neutrophils, infectious agents, abnormal cells, and platelet clumps. Thorough evaluation of stained blood smears remains an essential diagnostic skill; however, novel technology can complement modern hematology analyzers to aid your daily workflow.

courses.title: Risk of Cancer Module 2: The Influence of Age on Cancer Risk
courses.description: Cancer is an emotionally charged and complex topic. Recognizing the inherent cancer risks that abound can help guide clinical suspicions and/or inform type and cadence of proactive testing for cancer. This short video module describes physiologic and pathologic changes associated with aging, detailing the associated cancer risk. Age-appropriate diagnostics for dogs and cats are proposed, with a focus on recommendations for cancer-screening, that can assist with clinical decision-making and inform conversations with pet owners about the needs of their aging pets.

courses.title: Investigational Treatment with Autologous Vaccine plus Immune Checkpoint Inhibition in Dogs with Osteosarcoma
courses.description: This course covers immunotherapeutic approaches in canine osteosarcoma, including a novel clinical trial undergoing USDA approval. We will discuss the immunologic background of cancer treatment, historical/current approaches to excite and awaken the immune system against cancer, and a novel checkpoint inhibitor being used in conjunction with autologous vaccination.

courses.title: A Journey into Indirect Reference Intervals: New Opportunities from Laboratory Big Data
courses.description:
Reference intervals are fundamental to the clinical interpretation of laboratory results. This presentation will take participants on a journey through historical and emerging concepts in veterinary and human reference interval development, exploring how novel indirect methods can leverage large laboratory datasets to generate representative and clinically relevant reference limits.
We will examine the principles behind indirect reference interval models and discuss how these approaches can be used to improve diagnostic accuracy through the development of breed-, age-, and sex-specific reference intervals. Practical applications will also include the use of indirect methods to verify externally sourced reference intervals within a laboratory's own patient population and support periodical refinement of existing reference limits.

courses.title: GASTROINTESTINAL FOREIGN BODIES: SURGICAL AND ENDOSCOPIC MANAGEMENT (637-43244)
courses.description: In this lecture presented by DoveLewis Surgeon Ashley Magee, DVM, DACVS, we will briefly discuss the history and clinical signs exhibited by a patient with a foreign body, the diagnostic tests that are most useful to run and how the results can help you differentiate a surgical from non surgical abdomen. We'll then concentrate on treatment methods, both with surgery and endoscopic removal, as well as post-operative care. We will review several cases treated here at DoveLewis to illustrate several key points in the diagnosis and treatment of patients with foreign bodies.

courses.title: Emerging Parasite Threats: What's Moving into Your Exam Room?
courses.description: Emerging and re-emerging parasitic diseases are increasingly capturing national attention, but their impact extends far beyond the headlines and into everyday companion animal practice. Changes in climate, wildlife ecology, animal movement, and global commerce are reshaping parasite distribution patterns, exposing pets and their owners to risks that may not have historically existed in their region. This presentation explores the factors driving parasite emergence and examines several important threats currently affecting veterinary medicine, including the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax), and Echinococcus multilocularis. Participants will review current epidemiologic trends, clinical implications, public health considerations, and practical approaches for identifying and managing these emerging risks. The session will also highlight the veterinarian's role in surveillance, prevention, client communication, and One Health initiatives that support animal and human health. Through an evidence-based review of emerging parasite threats, attendees will gain actionable strategies for incorporating risk assessment, prevention, and education into daily clinical practice.

courses.title: Urethral Obstruction What We Know and What We Dont Know Yet
courses.description: Urethral obstruction is a common and potentially life threatening emergency in small animal practice and managing these patients can be challenging. This session takes a practical evidence based approach from stabilization to ongoing care. Well cover underlying causes systemic consequences and clinical decision making including cardiovascular assessment management of hyperkalemia and acid base disturbances fluid therapy and analgesia. Procedural techniques such as decompressive cystocentesis urinary catheterization troubleshooting and short term catheter care will be reviewed along with current medication strategies. Youll leave with a clear practical framework to confidently manage urethral obstruction in real world practice.

courses.title: Evaluating Safety and Efficacy Of Acupuncture in Cancer Care
courses.description: Summarize the available literature reviewing both safety and efficacy of acupuncture for the cancer patient. Research will focus on areas where caution should be executed as well as special considerations that may be made in this patient population. Relevant research that may be referred to as cause for concern by the conventional community will be addressed, so that a dialogue for collaboration between the TCVM practitioner and conventional oncology care team may exist. The most common clinical conditions that are effectively treated with acupuncture in the cancer patient will be discussed in detail.

courses.title: Exploring IDEXX Cancer Dx Lymphoma Diagnostic
courses.description: This session will provide an in-depth exploration of IDEXX Cancer Dx and its role in diagnosing lymphoma in veterinary patients. We will discuss the diagnostic capabilities of the test, its integration into clinical workflows, and how it aids in differentiating lymphoma from other hematologic diseases. Attendees will gain a clear understanding of when and how to use this diagnostic tool to optimize patient outcomes.

courses.title: COMMON TOXICITIES SEEN IN THE ER (637-38440)
courses.description: Erika Loftin, DVM, DACVECC, discusses approach, diagnosis, decontamination, and treatment plans in common toxicity cases. Cases discussed in this article are patients that presented in the ER of DoveLewis Emergency Animal Hospital.

courses.title: SURGICAL SITE INFECTION AND SURVEILLANCE (637-42412)
courses.description: The lecture is 66 minutes and consists of surgeon Coby Richter, DVM, DACVS, doing a formal presentation on how to identify and manage surgical infections in veterinary medicine. Coby Richter walks through a review of surgical complications caused by bacterial infections, and how to prevent them.

courses.title: Don't Fear the Ear: How Cytology Makes Your Otitis Problems Easier to Solve
courses.description: The basic approach to otitis evaluation, diagnosis and identifying as well as addressing underlying primary and secondary causes. This is a multifactorial condition and many things need to be addressed to clear infection, inflammation and prevent future occurrences.

courses.title: Communicating the benefits of preventive care. A guide to improving life quality for pets and professionals!
courses.description: This webinar explores the essential role of effective communication in veterinary consultations, emphasizing strategies to enhance client trust and satisfaction while addressing concerns about money. Attendees will learn techniques to build rapport, clarify costs and the value of treatments, educate clients, involve them in decision-making. The session will highlight the importance of contextualized care in veterinary settings, providing practical tools and insights to foster a client-centered approach, ultimately improving outcomes in the consultation room and enhancing the overall client experience.

courses.title: Cutaneous Manifestations of Systemic Disease
courses.description: Patients with endocrinopathies including hypothyroidism, hypercortisolism, sex hormone dermatoses, feline hyperthyroidism, and feline acquired cutaneous fragility are presented to clinicians in part and occasionally solely for skin and ear changes. This presentation will review common cutaneous clinical signs of endocrinopathies along with management options for the cutaneous changes. Confounding changes when endocrine disease patients also have allergies will be presented. Following the endocrine section, superficial necrolytic dermatitis (hepatocutaneous syndrome) will be reviewed with a focus on the diagnosis and management of cutaneous changes. Lastly, three immune mediated diseases that often have significant skin involvement (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatitis, eosinophilic dermatitis with edema, and sterile panniculitis) will be identified. Discriminating clinical features of these immune mediated diseases will be discussed along with ways to distinguish them from infectious diseases that can appear similar.

courses.title: Foundations of Anesthesia
courses.description: A veterinary technicians role within the anesthesia team is crucial to ensuring the safety and comfort of patients undergoing surgical procedures. This comprehensive course delves into the fundamental principles of veterinary anesthesia, empowering technicians to confidently assist veterinarians and contribute to optimal patient outcomes.

courses.title: I'm Just Being Honest Incivility and Radical Honesty on the Floor
courses.description: Snarky comments. Offensive manners. Rudeness disguised and frankness. In this lecture with Director of Community Engagement Tess Payne and Chief Administrative Officer Monica Maxwell, SPHR, SHRM-SCP, MBTI, we will discuss how more and more, incivility is being treated as the norm and "radical honesty" is an excuse to be unapologetic. How are these communication trends manifesting on your team and what can you do to redirect communication to be more productive and kind?

courses.title: Multi-modality Imaging Case Studies
courses.description: Multiple radiographic modalities including radiography, computed tomography, sonography and MR imaging were used to diagnose a variety of disease processes in small animal Veterinary Medicine. Each modality has its place in the emergency/ critical care veterinary setting in order to achieve a rapid, accurate diagnosis. Cases will be presented which reflect the benefits of each of these modalities. Many of these cases will be diagnosed with radiographs alone, however, often there are indications for advanced imaging techniques.

courses.title: Big Questions about Small Things: Everything Vets Want to Know about Clinical Microbiology
courses.description: The microbiology lab can be a bit of an enigma- you send in a swab and get back a report. In this session, we will cover what actually happens to that swab, how you can improve you sample collection and submission and help to figure out why some frustrating results from the lab can happen. We will also cover antimicrobial susceptibility testing and when it can help and when it doesnt

courses.title: Structural & Functional Assessment of the Equine Spine - Thoracolumbar
courses.description: This course module provides the foundation needed to evaluate horses with back pain and dysfunction. Detailed anatomic descriptions of the soft tissue, muscular, articular, and osseous features of the thoracolumbar vertebrae and rib cage are presented. A review of thoracolumbar spinal biomechanics includes material on wither asymmetries, the role of the rib cage in weight bearing, and paired muscle function. Spinal pathology content includes the role of osteoarthritis and impinged spinous processes in the development of thoracolumbar pain and dysfunction. A structured outline for detailed evaluation of active and passive joint thoracolumbar and rib cage motion is provided. Treatment options focus on conservative methods for reducing pain and improving core stability in horses with back pain.

courses.title: Staging the Cancer patient
courses.description: This course will provide veterinary technicians and nurses with a practical understanding of cancer staging in companion animals. Topics will focus on the veterinary technician or nurses role in staging including diagnostics, treatment planning, and assessing disease progression. Attendees will explore how staging informs treatment planning, prognosis, and referral decisions. Emphasis will be placed on the technicians role in staging workflows, client communication, and ensuring high quality diagnostic sample collection and handling.

courses.title: How To Incorporate Early Functional Kidney Markers Into All Patient Evaluations
courses.description: Kidney disease is one of the most prevalent disease states in cats and dogs, especially in the senior and geriatric populations. The presence of worsening kidney function can affect the way that other chronic diseases (such as arthritis, thyroid disease, and metabolic diseases) are treated. This module explains the importance of early identification of decline in kidney function through preventive care and sick care, as well as in preanesthetic testing situations. The module also illustrates how to perform a complete evaluation of renal function and determine the best care protocols for patients.

courses.title: Pancreatitis: Lipase Is on the Case!
courses.description: Pancreatitis is an acute or chronic inflammatory condition of dogs and cats. This presentation will cover the basic physiology and pathophysiology of pancreatitis, look at risk factors and clinical signs of pancreatitis in dogs and cats, along with current methods of diagnosis, and explore new innovations in testing.

courses.title: Updates on the Diagnosis of Pancreatitis in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This webinar will focus on the diagnosis of pancreatitis in dogs and cats. We will discuss diagnostic methods such as general clinical pathology, ultrasound and advanced imaging. Additionally, there will be a discussion on the various lipase assays available on the market with attention given to historical assays and newer assays available on the market.

courses.title: Confidence in Cancer Care: Practical Approaches to Mast Cell Tumor Diagnosis and Management
courses.description: This session will provide a comprehensive overview of mast cell biology and its clinical relevance in veterinary medicine. We will begin with the normal function of mast cells in health, setting the stage for understanding their role in disease. Attendees will then review the typical clinical presentation of patients with mast cell tumors, followed by a discussion of current diagnostic approaches used in practice. The program will also cover commonly employed staging tools to assess the extent of disease and conclude with a review of treatment options currently available. By the end of the session, participants will gain a practical framework for recognizing, diagnosing, and managing mast cell tumors in clinical settings.

courses.title: Pain Management in Feline and Canine Patients
courses.description: This program will review the pain pathway, how to preemptively treat pain in patients, as well as addressing acute pain with a balanced, comprehensive pain protocol.

courses.title: Art of the Aspirate
courses.description: Fine needle aspirate (FNA) cytology is a minimally invasive, high impact diagnostic tool used routinely in veterinary medicine to guide clinical decision making. This program reviews core pathology concepts relevant to cytology, including distinctions between cytology and histopathology, and clarifies the role of FNA in diagnostic workflows. Participants will learn best practices for sample collection, preparation, and submission to maximize diagnostic yield and minimize non diagnostic results. The program also reviews cytology submission options, including slide based and slide free evaluation using the inVue Dx, and highlights the importance of structured clinical inputs and clinical pathologist image review in improving diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility.

courses.title: The Evolution of Cancer Diagnostics: An Update on Screening and Early Diagnosis of Canine Lymphoma
courses.description: Cancer remains one of the most significant health challenges faced in companion animal practice, with lymphoma representing one of the most frequently diagnosed cancers in dogs. Early detection offers the best chance to have conversations early and in some cases institute earlier treatment which improve quality of life. This case based session will explore the evolving landscape of cancer diagnostics with a focus on canine lymphoma. Using real world clinical examples, we will review how advances in screening and diagnostic tools particularly the use of IDEXX Cancer Dx are reshaping early detection strategies in practice. Attendees will gain an update on practical applications for both screening and diagnosis, and how to integrate this tool into everyday patient care.

courses.title: Diagnosing Canine Lymphoma: Choosing the Right Test, Not Just the Best One An Evidence-Based Comparison of Ancillary Diagnost
courses.description: This lecture provides a critical review of the current literature on diagnostic techniques for canine lymphoma, focusing on ancillary tests such as cytology, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, flow cytometry, and PARR. Rather than ranking tests by theoretical performance alone, the presentation compares sensitivity, specificity, turnaround time, costs, and real-world practicality. The goal is to help clinicians choose the most appropriate diagnostic pathway for each patient and clinical context, avoiding both under- and over-diagnosis.

courses.title: Telehealth - Veterinary Curbside Care
courses.description: Veterinary Curbside Care thrust the veterinary community into the world of telehealth and has left veterinary teams motivated to identify operational and client service needs when providing patient care entirely in the physical absence of the client. This unique and complimentary course focused on Veterinary Curbside Care will provide a perspective on how to identify the gaps and opportunities to create a sound curbside care plan.

courses.title: Bedinvetmab v. Meloxicam: A Randomized, Open-Label, Multi-Centre, Parallel-Group Trial
courses.description: Join us for an in-depth exploration of the latest advancements in osteoarthritis (OA) management for dogs, with a focus on comparing two critical treatments: Bedinvetmab and Meloxicam. Led by Dr. John Innes, BVSc, PhD, FRCVS, this session will examine the efficacy, safety, and impact of these treatments in improving the quality of life for dogs suffering from OA. The presentation will be based on findings from multi-center clinical trials, revealing how nerve growth factor (NGF) targeting with Bedinvetmab compares to the established NSAID therapy using Meloxicam. Attendees will gain insights into clinical outcomes, adverse events, and key metrics used to assess treatment success in managing pain and inflammation.

courses.title: An interactive primer for the Anatomy and Spatiality of a Canine Abdominal Point of Care Ultrasound
courses.description:
Focused ultrasound examinations are becoming extensions of the physical examination in the emergency setting. POCUS findings help direct immediate patient stabilization efforts, and serial studies can be used to monitor hospitalized patients.
This CE course is an interactive primer for new learners or a refresher for established ultrasound users. It uses a novel approach to highlight foundational anatomy and spatiality, allowing the user to assimilate a multifaceted comprehension of ultrasound. The user will have a better understanding of the orientation of the probe and beam for targeting structures and subsequent US images generated.

courses.title: Human Resources 5: The Finances of Human Resources
courses.description: In this human resources course, discover the financial components associated with HR and learn how to benchmark, create a budget, wage scales and a wage philosophy, along with a strategy to effectively reduce employee turnover.

courses.title: Basic Bone Plating Techniques for Tibia, Radius and Femur Fractures
courses.description: In this workshop, discussion will focus on decision-making for fracture repair of the tibia, femur and radius using bone plates. We will teach instrumentation, plate contouring and application techniques and give valuable practical tips. This course will employ lectures, clinical case presentations and a laboratory repairing created fracture on plastic bone models. Following lecture and case review, participants will repair fractures on plastic bone models.

courses.title: Chronic Complications of Canine Infectious Respiratory Disease (CIRD)
courses.description: Learners in the program will be presented a case-based approach to reviewing chronic complications of canine infectious respiratory disease. Cases will include history, clinical presentations, diagnostics including imaging, videos, and more. A review of CIRD prevention measures, CIRD case evaluation and re-evaluation timelines, including diagnostic work-up recommendations will be reviewed.

courses.title: JOURNAL CLUB 1 (637-37970)
courses.description: The lecture is 58min and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on several pieces of practical knowledge gleaned from recent veterinary journal research articles and papers. Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, does the reading work for you and discusses the most clinically practical techniques and knowledge from recent veterinary journals. Topics include: urethral obstructions in cats, toxicology, and antibiotic use in HGE patients.

courses.title: Achieve Lowest-Dose Radiation: Radiation Safety Is Your Safety
courses.description: The primary challenge of radiation protection safety programs is to keep the radiation dose at a minimum while obtaining the highest image quality needed for accurate medical diagnosis, that is, to achieve the optimal dose. Optimal dose is best accomplished when a radiation safety culture is fostered. This discussion reviews the use of the ALARA principle (as low as reasonably achievable) as well as optimization of image and dose by applying ALARA

courses.title: Feline CKD: Don't Wait for Weight Loss
courses.description: In this session, we will discuss the processes that regulate food intake and outline how these mechanisms are impacted by chronic kidney disease.

courses.title: Fecal Antigen Testing: Utilizing Diagnostics and Workflows to Benefit Your Patients and Practice
courses.description: In this session, we will discuss fecal testing that benefits patients and practices. We will review why regular screening for common intestinal parasites is important, the risks they pose to people and pets, when treatment is recommended and why follow up testing is critical for successful parasite management. We will also review the benefits fecal testing can bring to a practice through optimized workflows, enhanced technology and an elevated practice culture.

courses.title: Making Sense of CBC Dot Plots: From Technology to Clinical Action
courses.description: CBC dot plots provide critical insight into hematology results but theyre often underutilized in clinical practice. This session demystifies how dot plots are generated what normal and abnormal patterns look like and how to translate findings into meaningful diagnostic decisions. Participants will gain confidence in recognizing the limitations of automated results and applying appropriate next steps when abnormalities arise in house blood smear evaluation pathologist evaluation physical or scanned slides or slide free analysis of cellular morphology.

courses.title: Conscious Animal Lovers Movement Foundational Course
courses.description: This is a 9 module course (10 hours total) focused on incorporating veterinarians' conscious love of animals into everyday practice to create a more harmonious, enjoyable and successful veterinary space. We will heighten our ability to detect and assess energy while recognizing the impact it has on us, our clients, our patients, and the surrounding environment. Key points covered in this series are: The scientific basis behind the importance of energy and its impact on everything, the ability to tune into your own energy and that of your patients, tools for self-care and mind-body balance, how to work toward internal peace regardless of what is going on in your external world, and a pathway for sending more positive energy into the World.

courses.title: Leptospirosis: A Review of Clinical Signs, Diagnostic Testing, Prevention and Treatment
courses.description: In this lecture presented by Veterinary Internist Staci Goussev, DVM, DACVIM, we'll cover a thorough review of leptospirosis. Starting with a discussion of the etiology and epidemiology, we'll then focus on clinical presentation and confirmatory testing, including the microscopic agglutination test and PCR testing. Near the end of the lecture we'll cover prevention and treatment, and the public health risks of this zoonotic disease.

courses.title: Feline Cardiomyopathy: A Review
courses.description: Although a common disease, feline cardiomyopathy can be difficult to detect. In this lecture, explore the causes of myocardial dysfunction in feline patients and the common associated symptoms with Veterinary Cardiologist Caryn Reynolds, DVM, DACVIM (Cardiology). We will discuss the incidence and outcomes of cardiomyopathy, recommendations for physical exam and radiographic techniques, and diagnostic testing.

courses.title: Tricky Feline Case- Louise Is Not Acting Herself
courses.description: Sick feline patients often present with mild or vague clinical signs such as appetite change vomiting weight loss and or change in behavior. Since cats in a multi cat household often share food dishes and litter boxes and since cats are naturally secretive pet owners may not always notice the subtle differences exhibited by an ill cat. When owners do notice signs they may attribute their observations to increasing pet age change in household routine etc. In addition many cat owners believe that vomiting is normal for healthy cats. When cats are presented for evaluation because they are just not themselves the differential list can be extensive. The Louise story illustrates a problemoriented approach to the diagnosis of one such patient beginning with a minimum laboratory database then adding specialty tests and imaging. Incorporating a targeted fully quantitative pancreatic lipase assay such as the Catalyst Pancreatic Lipase Test into the initial phase of a comprehensive workup of a feline patient that presents with vague or mild signs of systemic illness is recommended to improve clinical efficiency and proficiency.

courses.title: Financial Management 4: Discounts, Audits & Accounts Receivable
courses.description: As veterinarians, owners, or managers, there will come a time in your career when you face situations that tug at your heartstrings. Often this is when a client cannot afford the care needed for their pet. Do you discount the services and products required for their pet? If so, do you understand how this discount will impact your business? In this course we will review the logistics of planned discounts, how to avoid unplanned discounts, the importance of auditing, and how to control accounts receivable.

courses.title: Don't Be Afraid, It's Only a Radiograph! Radiographic Positioning for Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This archived webinar is directed to both veterinarians and veterinary technicians, providing information on how to obtain diagnostic radiographic studies. The webinar will provide a basic understanding of why proper positioning is important and then demonstrate standard protocols for anatomical regions. In addition to obtaining diagnostic radiographs, there is also the opportunity for improved workflow and increased efficiency

courses.title: Proof Positive: Successful Teams Seek Psych Safety
courses.description: Psychological safety is the most important aspect of successful teams. Our ability to feel safe to share ideas, to grow from failure, and to be honest with empathy allows our team to bypass the "interpersonal mush" that can exist otherwise. A sense of belonging, ability to be vulnerable, and strong interpersonal relationships are the initial ingredients to create this environment. We can assess psychological safety in a team using different tools. If psychological safety is lacking, we can help foster it using specific interventions, including civility and growth mindset work.

courses.provider: COLEGIO DE MEDICOS VETERINARIOS DE PUERTO RICO
courses.title: Advanced Equine Medicine: Neck, Back, and Ocular Health
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of the clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, clinical pathology, and treatment strategies for equine athletes affected by neck and back pathologies. Additionally, it covers the principles of equine veterinary ophthalmology, focusing on the diagnosis and management of common ocular diseases. Designed for professionals seeking to enhance their knowledge and skills, this course integrates practical approaches with the latest advancements in equine medicine to optimize the health and performance of equine athletes.

courses.title: SWVS 2026
courses.description: The Southwest Veterinary Symposium will once again welcome those who support veterinary medicine in our region, including DVMs, Technicians, Veterinary Assistants, Practice Managers, Office Staff, Speakers, Sponsors, and Exhibitors. A maximum of 28 CE credit hours are available for the SWVS General Symposium. Additional credit hours are available through the purchase of ticketed events (Interactive Labs, Workshops, Master Classes, and CE Tours).

courses.title: Moving Forward: Practice Growth and the Important Role of Preventive Care Diagnostics
courses.description: Preventive care diagnostics are a unique opportunity to provide excellent patient and client care while positively impacting the financial outcomes of your practice. In this session, Dr. Beth Hetler discusses why the time is ideal to offer preventive care diagnostics to your clients and how this testing benefits your patients and your practice. She also emphasizes strategies for pricing and successful preventive care protocol implementation.

courses.title: How To- Small Animal Enucleation
courses.description: Are you comfortable with small animal surgical techniques, but when that enucleation case comes along you feel a bit unsure? You are not alone! Enroll in this online course to review the indications for performing a small animal enucleation, the two main enucleation techniques, common complications, and post-operative care. This course will provide videos of performing both subconjunctival and trans palpebral enucleation techniques along with advice and tips for each step along the way. It will walk you through everything from shaving and sterile preparation to retrobulbar blocks and post-operative treatment. After completing this course, you will feel ready to take on small animal enucleations!

courses.title: The Heat is On...Heat Stroke Management in Canines
courses.description: We will discuss the pathophysiology of heat stroke along with early recognition and prevention. We will emphasize immediate interventions, diagnostics, treatment and monitoring for the veterinary patient suffering from heat stroke.The lecture will also have a case to discuss.

courses.title: Use of Immunosuppressant Therapy in Dogs and Cats - Mechanism of Action and Literature Review
courses.description: In this lecture presented by Criticalist Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, we will review the immune mediating mechanisms of the most commonly used immunomodulating drugs. We will also cover a thorough literature review, demonstrating their clinical use in dogs and cats.

courses.title: To Err is Human: Bringing Humanity into Medical Error Prevention
courses.description: This lecture presented by Shana O'Marra, DVM, DACVECC, will explore how to confront medical errors in your practice in a way that leads to growth and productive change. The model of just culture will be explained as well as communication with clients and team members involved in the error.

courses.title: ENDOSCOPY IN THE ER (637-44230)
courses.description: The lecture is 1 hour and 10 minutes and consists of speaker Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, doing a formal presentation on Endoscopy in the ER. This course discusses the practical use of endoscopy in an emergency room setting.

courses.title: MEDICAL MARIJUANA FOR PETS (637-44232)
courses.description: The lecture is 60 minutes and consists of speaker Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, doing a formal presentation on Medical Marijuana for Pets. This course discusses a broad exploration of the topic of medical use of cannabinoids in pets including an introduction to the physiology of the endocannabinoid system. The current and changing regulatory climate around medical marijuana use in humans and the implications to veterinary medicine will be discussed.

courses.title: Navigating the cOAst: Current Consensus on Managing Canine Osteoarthritis
courses.description: So many tools in the toolbox for managing OA in dogs! So little guidance on what to utilize, when! Until now! Recent evidence-based Consensus Guidelines have been published to help clinicians make sense of and prioritize various interventions based upon patient risk factors and clinical signs. This presentation will summarize high-level expert opinion regarding OA treatment strategies for dogs, based on the validated Canine Osteoarthritis Staging Tool (COAST), to include a discussion of existing and new therapeutic modalities.

courses.title: Crash Course in Collapse - A Case of Acute Hemoabdomen Associated with Splenic Hemangiosarcoma
courses.description: Veterinary professionals in general practice often feel challenged and under-resourced to appropriately manage emergent patients because they have limited experience, or lack the necessary equipment, staff, or time. Adopting a standard, stepwise approach to patient assessment and preliminary treatment can improve clinician proficiency and confidence and may help to improve patient outcomes. This short crash course in collapse associated with pallor and shock illustrates the ABCs of emergency care through a patient story. Learners will earn 0.25 CE credits as they follow Jackson, an 11-year-old mixed breed dog, through triage, point-of-care testing, and emergency stabilization for hemoabdomen caused by rupture of splenic hemangiosarcoma.

courses.title: Dental Radiographic Positioning for the Dog and Cat
courses.description: This course is designed for those veterinary staff members new to dental radiology. The course has three sessions. Each session can acquaint the user with the basics needed to begin taking dental radiographs or for those who need to strengthen their skills. Because of its on-demand availability, participants can have access before or after formal hands-on training. The content of the course provides information in both written and video formats to provide a diverse experience. Along the way, the course requests user feedback to evolve the course material as needs arise. Lastly, there is an opportunity to interact with other participants through the course discussion moderated by the instructor. This community allows the participants to share images, feedback, and recommendations.

courses.title: Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery for the Small Animal Surgeon
courses.description:
You know the feeling- I amresecting a mass, but in the back of my mind I am worried about getting it closed. Complete excision versus wound closure. It is an ugly feeling that we can help you with! Better yet, the skills you learn here will help you with traumatic wound closures too!
In this intensive 2-day course, lectures will be followed by direct application of the surgical techniques in our cadaveric labs. Our instructors will support you so that you gain the most from each modular training session. You will learn simple and more complex reconstructive procedures for wounds involving the head (face, mouth, pinna), trunk (skin, thoracic and abdominal walls) and extremities (skin loss, pad reconstruction) including:
Local Skin Flaps; Tension Relieving Techniques; Axial Pattern Flaps; Free Grafts; Skin Stretching Closure Techniques; Muscle and Myocutaneous Flaps; Facial Reconstructive Surgery; Nasal Reconstructive Surgery; Paw/Pad Reconstructive Surgery and Reconstructive Surgery of the Pinna,

courses.title: A Breath of Fresh Air - Clinical Applications of Oxygenation and Ventilation in the Emergency Room
courses.description: Respiratory failure is diagnosed when there is a deficit in arterial oxygen (hypoxemia) or the accumulation of carbon dioxide (hypercapnia) due to abnormalities within the respiratory system or neurological control of ventilation. It is important to identify a decline in ventilation and oxygenation early in the course of critical illness to prevent the ensuing cascade of detrimental cellular events. In this lecture presented by Christin Reminga, DVM, DACVECC, we will discuss practical ways to identify the inciting causes and types of respiratory failure, the means behind timely diagnostic, therapeutic, and monitoring measures and the understanding for specialty transfer when ongoing efforts are required.

courses.title: Shaping Tomorrow: The Future-Ready Veterinary Workforce & Workplace
courses.description:
In the current veterinary landscape, the tables have turned - veterinary professionals hold all the cards. Employers are in fierce competition for top talent, and veterinary professionals now have the luxury of being choosy. Younger veterinarians, in particular, are looking for more than just a paycheck - they're searching for workplaces with a healthy, value-driven culture, modern equipment, and flexible scheduling. With telemedicine, virtual care, and cloud-based software on the rise, there are also more possibilities and growing demand for remote work opportunities and a solid work-life balance.
This session will begin by exploring the evolving candidate profile and shifting expectations from work, particularly among different generations of veterinary professionals. Attendees will learn about the skills that will define the future, like writing prompts for AI. We'll also explore how technology can enhance the employee experience and discuss strategies to keep your practice competitive in attracting and retaining today's modern workforce.
Whether you're a hospital leader aiming to build a strong culture and retention strategy or a veterinary professional eager to stay relevant in a tech-driven world, this session is designed with you in mind.

courses.title: Preventative Care Visit
courses.description: An in-deapth presentation on the reasons for expanding your offering during routine "healthy" pet visits, including the medical reasons and financial benefits to your business. In addition, the presentation will outline the process that is needed to make a successful change in your practice.

courses.title: Puffy Eye...Maybe it's Feline Herpesvirus?
courses.description: Feline herpesvirus (FHV-1) is a common pathogen of cats and kitten all around the world producing a wide variety of ocular manifestations from mild conjunctivitis to blinding keratitis or symblepharon. We will discuss how we reach a diagnosis of FHV-1 and how is best managed. Is there a good PCR test? Should I use a topical or systemic antiviral drug? How frequently? For how long? Do I also need to use antibiotics? Is lysine effective? How important is eye lubrication? We will address all of these questions in a logical fashion choosing only the clinically relevant material from all of the latest research.

courses.title: Abdominal Radiology: Case Review
courses.description: Dr. Graham will discuss abdominal radiograph case studies of patients presenting with vomiting. He will review the associated radiographs and discuss each image. Where applicable, Dr. Graham will discuss the effect of image quality and positioning on each case and eventual diagnosis.

courses.title: DVM Canine and Feline Extraction Course
courses.description: This 8-hour wet lab allocates 4 hours for canine patients and 4 hours for feline patients. Instruction will focus on proper flap creation, using a high-speed handpiece with dental burs to section multirooted teeth, and effective techniques for removing alveolar bone. Hand instruments for extracting single and multi-rooted teeth in dogs and cats will be used. Complications during extractions will be addressed, including root retrieval and managing ankylosed and resorbed tooth structures.

courses.title: Financial Management Module 6: Financial Protection
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss the importance of securing our hospital revenue, inventory, and assets through checks and balances that ensure financial protection. Managing opportunities, rationalization and pressure will be reviewed as three key leading factors in the financial security of your practice.

courses.provider: NORTHERN NEW ENGLAND VETERINARY ALPINE SYMPOSIUM
courses.title: NNEVAS Dermatology and Ophthalmology
courses.description: An overview and latest updates in disease recognition and treatment of dermatological and ophthalmological conditions with a feline emphasis.

courses.title: Hogwarts in the Workplace
courses.description: In this lecture presented by DoveLewis Marketing Director Tess Payne, we will cover four lessons learned in the Harry Potter series, and how they can be directly translated into a clinic and team environment. We will cover the benefits and risks of conflict, languages of appreciation, and how to communicate effectively with diverse team members.

courses.title: Foundations in Equine Ultrasound
courses.description: Foundations in Equine Ultrasound is a comprehensive course showing the attendee how to get excellent diagnostic quality ultrasound images in the field. Part 1 is a 4 session (1 hour per session) video course covering ultrasound of the equine metacarpus, fetlock, pastern, foot and stifle. It features original anatomical dissections and real-time split screen video of hand position and ultrasound feed to teach the attendee HOW to get excellent quality diagnostic images. Part 2 is 5, 1 hour sessions, covering the shoulder and elbow, carpus, neck and back, pelvis and hock. Attendees can opt to take single sessions or the entire course.

courses.title: Mastering Inventory: Strategies to Slash Costs and Optimize Pricing in Veterinary Practices
courses.description:
Efficient inventory management in veterinary practices isn't just about keeping shelves stocked - it's a key factor in maintaining financial health and operational smoothness. Balancing cost control with high-quality service is essential, yet many practices struggle with high Cost of Goods Sold (COGS), stockouts, and the frustrating time drain of managing inventory.
This session will focus on transforming these challenges into opportunities for savings and efficiency. Attendees will explore strategies to prevent excess stock and ensure products are available when needed, adopting a just-in-time approach.
We'll cover how to understand and accurately calculate COGS, setting realistic and effective targets tailored to your specific hospital's service and product mix. We'll explore methods for identifying and controlling cost drivers and strategies to tackle high COGS, such as managing overstock, reducing waste, and enhancing efficiency.
We'll pay special attention to different pricing models, including markup percentages and margin-based pricing, to help you craft an effective and flexible pricing strategy that aligns with your practice's goals and economic trends. You'll learn how to negotiate better pricing and integrate new products into your inventory smoothly, avoiding disruptions to operations. Additionally, we'll discuss how to use inventory software to streamline this process further, reduce costs, and boost EBITDA.
Gain practical knowledge and essential insights to enhance inventory management and drive financial success in your practice.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Heart Disease Basics
courses.description: This course is designed to give you a general overview of the most common canine and feline heart diseases and their effect on the cardiovascular system.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Evaluating ECGs
courses.description: This CE will walk through the basics of ECG as it applies to veterinary small animal patients. We will discuss how an ECG works, why it matters, developing a method of assessing a rhythm, and walk through common dysrhythmias that one might see.

courses.title: 2026 Foundations
courses.description:
This 24-week course provides veterinary practice managers with essential skills to support hospital success through focused development in leadership, financial literacy, and operational efficiency. Organized around three core themes: team, finances, and operations, the program emphasizes practical learning that supports sustainable performance in a veterinary hospital environment.
The curriculum follows a progressive educational lifecycle in which practice managers first develop self-awareness as leaders, then build the communication and influence skills necessary to effectively lead teams. Participants next gain an understanding of how money works within a veterinary hospital and how financial data informs decision-making. The curriculum then connects financial insight to daily operational choices, demonstrating how systems and workflows impact both financial performance and team well-being. The course culminates in real-world application, enabling participants to integrate leadership, financial, and operational concepts into practical hospital systems.
The course begins with a kickoff session to review the outline, goals, and expectations. Each week, participants will engage in interactive, one-hour online sessions, culminating in a final wrap-up discussion on goal setting and implementation. Upon completion, participants will earn twenty (20) CE hours.

courses.title: Speaking the Same Language- Cancer Biopsy Basics
courses.description: Cancer terminology forms its own lexicon and language when clinicians discuss diagnostics, treatments and outcomes with both pet owners and other veterinarians. Biopsies are often an integral part of diagnostics when managing an oncologic patient. Knowledge of not only the pertinent case details but also the different terms used to describe cancer biopsy results will help to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the patients diagnosis and improve communication with the pet owners and veterinary team. Explore the features and benefits of your biopsy report with this self-paced, interactive learning.

courses.title: Canine Sports Medicine - Level Up!
courses.description:
Whether by design or default, you see a lot of challenging canine lameness cases. You have experienced the thrill of restoring mobility, lifestyle, and comfort to many of your patients, but you have also tasted the bitterness of defeat. You wish that there was something more that you could do to develop your skills as a canine lameness diagnostician and to have a few more therapeutic tools at your disposal.
The good news is that YOU were who we were thinking about when we designed this one of a kind course in Canine Sports Medicine. In this course, you will enjoy approximately 6 hours of online learning at your own pace and in your place as you prepare for your more intensive in-person hands-on training. In this hybrid course you will learn to:
Confidently perform both a screening- and comprehensive-ortho/neuro exam.
Perform arthrocentesis for synovial fluid analysis, diagnostic joint blocks, and/or intra-articular therapy.
Perform needle arthroscopy on the elbow, shoulder, and stifle as well as describe its indications
Discuss available intra-articular therapies and the advantages/disadvantages of each
Discuss the important constituent variables in various preparations of Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP)
Process platelet rich plasma (PRP)

courses.title: How Long is the Wait Time?!: Setting Accurate Expectations for Clients
courses.description: Working in veterinary medicine, we know that setting accurate expectations is important to providing care to our clients. But what happens when even we don't know what to expect? In this lecture with Client Experience Training Specialist Breanna Gordon, we will discuss the importance of client communication amongst uncertain times. We will consider how our own expectations impact those around us, and the importance of establishing professional, caring relationships with our clients in times of uncertainty.

courses.title: Sampling for success: In clinic ear cytology and In clinic urine and sediment analysis.
courses.description: Pathology is new again! Find out the latest innovations in veterinary cytology and urine sediment analysis. Understand the role of the veterinary technician in cytology diagnostics and how time-proven and new techniques maximize your results.

courses.title: The Changing Workforce
courses.description: One in three people in the labor force is a Millennial, making them the largest generation in the current workforce. Millennials, the growing economy, and a tight labor market are changing the expectations employees have of their employers. In this lecture presented by Monica Maxwell, SPHR, SHRM-SCP, MBTI, and CEO Ron Morgan, we will discuss how the changing labor force has affected the veterinary industry (particularly private practices), our management styles, and offer tips on how to compete in this changing world!

courses.title: Foundations of Anesthesia
courses.description: A veterinary technicians role within the anesthesia team is crucial to ensuring the safety and comfort of patients undergoing surgical procedures. This comprehensive course delves into the fundamental principles of veterinary anesthesia, empowering technicians to confidently assist veterinarians and contribute to optimal patient outcomes.

courses.title: Workplace Violence in Veterinary Practices
courses.description: In this course we will address how to identify, respond to and prevent workplace violence in the veterinary workplace. While prevention and addressing workplace safety concerns is a team effort, managers will be able to utilize several helpful resources and tools that they can adapt for their practice, preparing them to train their team and provide support in a workplace violence event.

courses.title: A Radiographic Smorgasbord for Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Understand the importance of radiographs and collaborative relationships with specialists for practice efficiency.

courses.provider: UNIVERSITY OF MISSOURI COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE BSVT
courses.title: University of Missouri Small Animal Internal Medicine Shortcourse CE
courses.description:
The University of Missouri Small Animal Internal Medicine Team is offering a continuing education event on
Saturday, October 4, 2025 called the SAIM Shortcourse CE. This event is offered to all veterinarians and
veterinary technicians interested in learning about a variety of small animal internal medicine topics. We are
excited about the agenda for this upcoming event and are hoping to provide up to date veterinary information to
our attendees.

courses.title: Maximize Clinical Care and Efficiency with Technology
courses.description: This presentation provides veterinary professionals the necessary information on how VetConnect PLUS and IDEXX DecisionIQ can support a well pet diagnostic program.

courses.title: CONFLICT? NOPE! FACING CONFLICT WHEN YOUD RATHER AVOID IT (637-42407)
courses.description: Conflict isn't always an aggressive interaction, and it can take many forms. In this one-hour lecture with Cheryl Latta, DoveLewis Human Resources Manager, learn about the ways that conflict can present itself in the workplace. And, how to be comfortable addressing conflict instead of running away from it.

courses.title: THE HEPATOPATHY HEADACHE (637-42862)
courses.description: Join in on a review with Internist Barbara Davis, DVM, DACVIM, of the most common causes of elevated liver enzymes in dogs and cats. We'll address which diagnostics are most useful and empirical treatment options that can be attempted prior to the need for referral. This lecture will focus on asymptomatic patients with elevated liver enzymes as it can be difficult to know how to proceed when a patient presents with abnormal liver enzymes but no clinical signs.

courses.title: ONLINE REPUTATION MANAGEMENT (637-37893)
courses.description: The lecture is 62min and consists of Monica Maxwell and Ron Morgan doing a formal presentation on managing a veterinary clinic's online reputation. CEO of DoveLewis, Ron Morgan, and Monica Maxwell, SPHR, SHRM, speak about how to navigate the world of online reviews and social media; covering posts from both your hospital staff and your clients.

courses.title: DIAGNOSIS AND MANAGEMENT OF SPLENIC DISEASES (637-39326)
courses.description: Diagnosis and Management of Splenic Diseases is a 60 minute talk delivered by board certified veterinary surgeon Ashley Magee, DVM, DACVS, that discusses different reasons dogs and cats may present to the hospital requiring a splenectomy. Participants in this lecture can expect to learn or review various methods for spleen removal.

courses.title: Mountain to Sea Veterinary CE and Wellness Retreat - Costa Rica April 2027
courses.description: This program covers subject matter focused in small animal oncology and veterinary wellbeing and is suitable for the general practitioner. We will discuss bridging the oncology gap between general practice and specialty medicine, cytology, canine and feline lymphoma, canine mast cell tumors, measuring quality of life, and navigating emotional load and complex cases in oncology. In the wellbeing arena, this program will discuss true, pseudo-, and poor wellbeing, using practical tools to influence which branch of your autonomic nervous system is dominant, taming imposter syndrome, and converting burnout to buy in. This program will also include 6 hours of online coursework through Get MotiVETed University on topics of wellbeing and suicide prevention basics as veterinary professionals, which will be part of the overall program but will be taken through GMU (these 6 hours are already RACE approved and GMU will provide certificates).
courses.location: Encantada Ocean Cottages, Puntarenas, Costa Rica

courses.title: Ultrasound as the new stethoscope: from FAST and POCUS to Basic and Advanced Abdominal Ultrasound and Echocardiography
courses.description: Ultrasound is rapidly becoming the new stethoscope in veterinary practice. This webinar will guide veterinarians and technicians from the basics of FAST and POCUS to core abdominal imaging skills and an introduction to echocardiography. Practical case examples will highlight how ultrasound can be integrated into everyday clinical decision-making to improve patient care.

courses.title: Servant Leadership
courses.description: In the demanding world of veterinary medicine, effective leadership is more than just giving orders. This engaging course delves into servant leadership, a powerful approach that prioritizes the growth and well-being of your team while achieving exceptional patient care.

courses.title: Advanced Surgical Procedures
courses.description: Come join us for a special 2-day, hands on advanced surgery experience with cadavers. We have designed the course so that you will be able to focus upon expanding your surgical skills and refining your surgical technique. You will watch a demonstration of each procedure before you perform it yourself. Featured procedures include fore and hindlimb amputations, gastropexy, nephrectomy, diaphragmatic hernia repair, salivary gland removal, scrotal urethrostomy in the dog, perineal urethrostomy (PU) in the cat, and anal sacculectomy. We will also discuss basic skin reconstruction techniques, and you will have the opportunity to perform advancement flaps and caudal superficial epigastric flaps. Esophagostomy tube and thoracostomy tube placement will also be reviewed.

courses.title: Regional analgesia of the Head and Neck in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This course is designed to give attendees the basic understanding of local and regional anesthesia for the head and neck in dogs and cats. The didactic portion of the course will include a discussion of local anesthetic pharmacology, additives to local anesthetics and appropriate use of local anesthetics to maximize efficacy while minimizing side effects. The prevention and treatment of LAST will also be discussed. Participants will also be introduced to appropriate landmarks, techniques and complications associated with regional analgesia of the maxilla, mandible, eye, ear and neck. This will include analgesia for procedures involving the oral cavity, nose, eye, ear and neck, with a special focus on oral analgesia. Participants will also be introduced to epidural analgesia at both the lumbosacral and sacrococcygeal injection sites.

courses.title: Lymphoma? But My Dog Looks Fine!
courses.description: This 15-minute presentation will guide clinical practitioners on leveraging IDEXX Telemedicine services and Cancer Dx testing to enable earlier lymphoma diagnosis. Through case-based examples, attendees will gain a clearer understanding of how integration delivers clinical benefits. Earlier detection provides more time for intervention, supporting faster, better-informed decisions that can enhance quality of life and improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: See It Before They Show It: Cancer Dx Use in Preventive Screening
courses.description: This session introduces how Cancer Dx can be integrated into wellness visits through case examples, enabling earlier detection of cancer in clinically healthy patients and strengthening client relationships through proactive care.

courses.title: Take my breath away: Pleural and Lung Ultrasound in Emergency and Critical Care
courses.description: This webinar provides a comprehensive overview of thoracic point-of-care ultrasound (T-POCUS) techniques and their clinical utility in emergency and critical care settings. The talk begins with a review of normal thoracic ultrasound anatomy and systematically covers how to perform and interpret T-POCUS, including key artifacts and signs such as the glide sign, A-lines, B-lines, curtain sign, and the seashore vs. bar code signs. Clinical applications are emphasized, particularly for detecting pleural effusion, pneumothorax, alveolar-interstitial syndrome, and lung consolidation. It emphasizes the importance of focused ultrasound as a non-invasive, rapid, repeatable diagnostic tool that enhances patient triage, guides interventions, and enables serial monitoring. Practical tips are shared on probe handling, image acquisition, and identifying pitfalls, with an emphasis on integrating POCUS findings into clinical decision-making rather than using them in isolation. The session highlights that while T-POCUS is not a replacement for comprehensive imaging, it is an invaluable tool in the critical care clinicians diagnostic arsenal.

courses.title: THE SCREAM OF THE MALE NEUTERED CAT: OBSTRUCTIVE AND NON-OBSTRUCTIVE UROPATHIES (637-41409)
courses.description: This lecture is 70 minutes and consists of a speaker Katherine Earl, DVM, CPP, doing a formal presentation on obstructive and non-obstructive uropathies of feline patients in the ER and ICU. The purpose of this program is to review general approach and care for urethral obstruction in cats in addition to review and discussion of feline idiopathic cystitis in light of the most recent research.

courses.title: JOURNAL CLUB II (637-44766)
courses.description: The lecture is 56 minutes and consists of speaker Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, doing a formal presentation on evidence based treatment protocols published in the last years in veterinary medicine. Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, does the work for you by summarizing practical evidence based information from the last year in veterinary journals. Topics include urinary tract disease in dogs, antibiotic use in urinary tract disease, treatment for seizures, and pain management for post-op enucleation patients.

courses.title: PYOTHORAX (637-39667)
courses.description: The lecture is 81min and consists of DoveLewis Criticalist Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, doing a formal presentation on pyothorax causes, clinical signs, and treatment strategies in dogs and cats.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Canine and Feline Medical Acupuncture
courses.description:
This course is the third and final module for the CVAT certification.
The course consists of a four-day, in-person, hands-on learning session with various canine patients to learn from.
Canine and Feline Medical Acupuncture provides students with the opportunity to refine and expand their acupuncture needling skills with the addition of the feline patient. The use of acupuncture to treat common medical conditions is covered in depth. Students will work in small groups, palpating and treating live dogs and cats.
This course is open to licensed veterinarians and veterinary students who have completed Introduction to Veterinary Medical Acupuncture (Module 1) and Veterinary Medical Acupuncture for Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation (Module 2). Veterinary students must have completed their third year of veterinary school.

courses.title: Why Cant My Patient Breathe? A review of canine and feline thoracic radiographs.
courses.description: This webinar will cover thoracic radiograph interpretation and how to develop a systematic approach to reading thoracic radiographs. This course includes case examples of common causes of respiratory clinical signs in dogs and cats.

courses.title: When Pet Parents Become Human Parents: Supporting the Human-Animal Bond in Growing Families
courses.description:
As families transition from pet parents to human parents, new challenges can arise that affect pet behavior, family dynamics, and the human animal bond. This program explores the role of the human animal bond in growing families, with a focus on supporting positive relationships between pets, children, and caregivers.
Using current research and real world scenarios, the session examines how training approaches, perceived pet behavior, and family transitions influence attachment, behavior outcomes, and the risk of pet relinquishment. Participants will review evidence demonstrating the benefits of pet ownership for children while discussing common behavioral concerns that may emerge as families change.
This program equips veterinary professionals with knowledge to support informed client conversations, recognize when additional resources are needed, and help preserve the human animal bond during key life stages.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Foundations of Veterinary Acupuncture
courses.description: Foundations of Veterinary Acupuncture will teach the anatomy of the major points, including neurological, musculoskeletal, fascial, and lymphatic structures associated with each. Comprehensive patient evaluation will be discussed and practiced in depth, including orthopedic, neurological, and myofascial examination.

courses.title: Best Practices for Diagnosing and Staging Chronic Kidney Disease in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: The clinical signs associated with a decline in kidney function can be range from subtle to more severe. Determining the best next steps is important for both short-term and long-term renal health. This module explains how to best utilize early markers of decline in renal function and how particular tools, such as the IDEXX SDMA Algorithm and IRIS CKD guidelines, can help determine the best next steps for further diagnostics and care.

courses.title: Change as a Pathway to Growth
courses.description: This presentation explores change as a deliberate pathway to growth in veterinary practices focusing on why change feels difficult the hidden cost of staying stagnant and how culture ultimately determines whether new workflows succeed or fail. Using real world veterinary examples and established change management frameworks it helps teams understand the emotional and behavioral dynamics behind resistance reframe discomfort as a signal of progress and align assumptions values and daily behaviors to support adoption. Attendees leave with practical strategies to implement and sustain change building confident adaptable teams improving efficiency and patient care and embedding new ways of working into how we do things here.

courses.title: INTRODUCTION AND NURSING CARE FOR DKA (637-35438)
courses.description: The lecture is 58 minutes and consists of DoveLewis Veterinarian Christy Michaels, BVMS, doing a formal presentation on Diabetic Ketoacidosis. This course discusses the causes, symptoms, treatments, and care of the diabetic ketoacidosis patient.

courses.title: EMERGENCY SURGERY OF THE LIVER AND BILIARY SYSTEM (637-37904)
courses.description: The lecture is 59min and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on surgical techniques of the liver and biliary system. Ashley Magee, DVM, DACVS, discusses different surgical techniques and the decision-making process when performing surgery on the liver and the biliary system.

courses.title: Management of Urgent and Emergent Cases in General & Urgent Care Practice
courses.description: Some of the most common sick and urgent emergencies that present a diagnostic or therapeutic challenge to general practitioners are anaphylaxis, endocrine emergencies including hypoadrenocorticism, and urinary obstruction cases. With practical diagnostic tips, treatment guidelines and clinical examples, the lecture is presented from the perspective of a Criticalist that has years of experience working in general practice, urgent care and multispecialty referral hospitals, and currently provides 24/7 specialty consultations to veterinarians through DVM STAT Consulting.

courses.title: Feline Infectious Peritonitis: Cracking the FIP Code Diagnosis, Treatment, and Hope
courses.description: Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) remains one of the most challenging diseases in feline practice. This session will help you decode FIP by reviewing its pathophysiology, navigating complex diagnostics, and exploring current and emerging treatment strategies. Learn practical approaches to diagnosis, therapy, and patient monitoring, and gain insight into promising research that may shape the future of FIP management.

courses.title: From Overwhelmed To Optimized: Practicing With Efficiency & Innovation
courses.description: Discover how to level up your veterinary practice with efficiency and innovation. Join us for a transformative presentation that explores strategies aimed to optimize your veterinary practice, enhance patient care, and boost your bottom line. Learn how to streamline inventory management, boost client compliance, and deliver exceptional client experiences while fostering a highly engaged team in the process. Discover practical tips and real-world examples to implement these strategies in your practice.

courses.title: Cancer Risk Module 3: Breed-Related Cancer Risks in Dogs
courses.description: Cancer is an emotionally charged and complex topic. Recognizing the inherent cancer risks that abound can help guide clinical suspicions and/or inform type and cadence of proactive testing for cancer. This short video module reviews the available evidence for breed-related cancer risks in dogs, describing genetic predispositions and clinical presentations of some common cancers. Integrating this information about common breed-related conditions and sharing with pet owners may inspire vigilance for early signs of cancer. Early cancer detection and diagnosis may enable treatment that leads to better patient outcomes.

courses.title: Work Smarter, Not Harder: Catalyst SmartQC
courses.description: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. This is very true when it comes to analyzer maintenance. Maintaining analyzers in veterinary clinics is an essential step in delivering accurate and timely results for patients and the families that care for them. This webinar will provide a unique perspective on the important role of analyzer maintenance through the eyes and hands of a veterinarian, practice manager and veterinary technician. We will share tips for success and some of the less than ideal (but sometimes amusing) practices that we have experienced during our years in practice.

courses.title: Canine & Feline Breed Identification
courses.description: This course will help staff members learn common canine and feline breeds seen in the veterinary practice, along with common medical concerns for each.

courses.title: Patient and Practice Benefits of Fecal Antigen Testing for Intestinal Parasite Screening Sharing Evidence That Its Time to
courses.description: In this session, we discuss comprehensive fecal testing for intestinal parasites that can benefit patients and the practice. This small panel format brings together an infectious disease expert, a seasoned practice owner, and an experienced certified veterinary assistant to share newly published medical evidence for regular patient screening with fecal antigen testing and how to communicate the value of accurate results to pet owners. The team presents practice management strategies for implementing change, optimizing workflow, and leveraging enhanced technology that can elevate practice culture and outcomes, while enhancing patient care.

courses.title: Risk of Cancer Module 1: Risk and Etiology of Cancer
courses.description: Cancer is an emotionally charged and complex topic. Recognizing the inherent cancer risks that abound can help guide clinical suspicions and/or inform type and cadence of proactive testing for cancer. This foundational educational learning journey in four modules is designed to assist with clinical decision-making and to support having informed conversations with pet owners about the risks of cancer. The first video module defines cancer and offers an overview of cellular mechanisms of tumor formation and cancer hallmarks. Internal and external sources of DNA mutation contributing to cancer that are related to patient age, environment, and/or breed are introduced.

courses.title: Preventive Care - The biggest missed opportunity to transform vetcare for good?
courses.description: In a positive, grounded webinar, we will discuss how viewing preventive care as an integral part of routine veterinary services can significantly boost pet owner loyalty, empower clinic staff, and create growth opportunities for the clinic.

courses.title: Going Viral - What's New with FIP, Calicivirus, and FeLV
courses.description: Feline viral diseases have been part of our thought process as veterinarians forever, with not a lot of progress for how we can deal with them. Recent advances in therapy have provided hope and health for so many cats. In this session well talk about how best to approach these challenging infections and what options we have for treatment.

courses.title: Cracking Canine Cushings: A Practical Guide to Hypercortisolism in Dogs
courses.description:
Cushings syndrome (hypercortisolism) in dogs presents a complex diagnostic and management challenge for veterinary professionals. This lecture will provide an in-depth exploration of the pathophysiology of Cushings syndrome, highlighting how an understanding of adrenal function informs clinical recognition and diagnostic decision-making. Through interactive case examples, we will examine the key clinicopathologic features of Cushings and evaluate the most effective tools for diagnostic confirmation. Additionally, we will review emerging innovations and technologies that are reshaping how veterinarians identify and monitor this common endocrine disorder.
Designed for veterinarians and veterinary professionals, this session will enhance your confidence and clinical approach to diagnosing and managing canine Cushings.

courses.title: Enhanced Image Quality and Staff Safety: Understanding the Advantages of ALARA in Veterinary Radiography
courses.description: In this webinar, you will learn strategies for minimizing radiation exposure. This course explains the ALARA principle (as low as reasonably achievable) and how it guides the optimization of both image quality and radiation dose. ALARA-based recommendations for education, equipment selection, and appropriate radiographic techniques help lower radiation doses for veterinary patients, which in turn decreases exposure for occupational staff. This course also highlights the importance of ongoing staff training to strengthen accountability and safety. By the end, learners will be equipped to implement comprehensive radiation safety practices while fostering a culture of safety and efficiency.

courses.title: IDEXX Diagnostic Differentiators-Empowering Regional Thought Leaders
courses.description: This self paced online learning module introduces veterinary professionals to IDEXXs key diagnostic differentiators, including advanced biomarkers, in house analyzers, SNAP tests, and reference laboratory services. Through short lessons, interactive case scenarios, and knowledge checks, learners gain practical skills in early disease detection, diagnostic interpretation, and workflow integration. The program equips Regional Thought Leaders to confidently communicate IDEXX innovations and apply them to improve patient outcomes.

courses.title: Structural & Functional Assessment of the Equine Spine - Neurophysiology
courses.description: This course module provides a basic introduction to neurophysiologic principles related to axial skeleton pain. Content includes information of the pain sensitive tissues with the axial skeleton, spinal pain mechanisms, and subjective and objective measures of musculoskeletal pain in horses. Neuroanatomical descriptions of nociceptors and other spinal tissue receptors that contribute to acute and chronic pain syndromes are included. Spinal pain mechanisms are reviewed as they relate to peripheral and central sensitization, ganglionitis, and effects on mechanoreception and motor control issues. An introduction to the physical, functional, and behavioral aspects of pain are presented.

courses.title: Hallmarks of Cancer: Understanding the Basics of Cancer Biology
