courses.description: This presentation will outline the fundamental characteristics that are shared across many types of cancer. There will be emphasis on recognizing key genetic mutations and molecular mechanisms that promote cancer formation, growth, and dissemination. Representative examples of molecular medicines and biologics influenced by these genetic mutations and molecular mechanisms that are changing the way cancers could be treated will be highlighted.

courses.title: The remote neurologic consult
courses.description: This presentation is designed to facilitate the performance and interpretation of the canine and feline neurologic examination via a telemedicine format. A representative from the hospital requesting the consult will perform the neurologic examination under the remote direction of a board-certified neurologist. Once the consult is finished, a report will be sent to the requesting hospital. The presentation outlines both procedural aspects of telemedicine neurology consults, as well as a step-by-step description of the components of the neurologic examination. At the completion of this presentation, the attendee will feel comfortable performing the basic components of the neurologic examination and gain some level of expertise in localizing lesions.

courses.title: Speaking the Same Language: Additional Pathology Testing in Oncology
courses.description: Cancer terminology forms its own lexicon and language when clinicians discuss diagnostics, treatments and outcomes with both clients and other veterinarians. Cases can often become complicated with many specific tests tailored to distinct disease processes or case presentations. Understanding the information provided by these tests will guide communication with pet owners and case management. In this module, you will learn about additional testing offered after cytology or histopathology has been performed, with a specific focus on cancerous causes of disease.

courses.title: The Cancer Journey and Your Veterinary Care Team
courses.description: This engaging discussion delves into unique perspectives on cancer through the lens of a general practitioner, internist, oncologist and licensed veterinary technician. This panel-style conversation will examine the collaborative¿interactions between these roles, and the critical importance of client communication throughout the process, illuminating the patient referral process from the general practitioner to the specialist and oncologist, and to underscore the vital¿role of the LVT in treatment.

courses.title: Youve opened a can of worms, now what? When to screen, when to treat and when its important?
courses.description: In this session, we will review why regular screening for common intestinal parasites is important, the risks they pose to people and pets, when treatment is recommended and why follow up testing is critical for successful parasite management.

courses.title: (On Demand) Performance Horse Management and Rehabilitation - Including the Older Athlete
courses.description: In this on-demand webinar, participants will gain valuable insights into the latest updates and advancements related to diagnostics, management, and rehabilitation of performance horses, including senior performance horses. This session will be led by globally recognized experts at the forefront of research and clinical practice. These recorded lectures are tailored to provide veterinarians and horse owners with the most current, practical, and actionable insights.

courses.title: Fluid Therapy
courses.description: This program provides an understanding of the purpose and use of fluid therapy applications in the veterinary practice.

courses.title: Orthopedic and Wound First Aid- Online
courses.description: You know the story- the clinic was calm until one of your best clients comes running frantically through the door with her traumatically injury pet in her arms. You and your team responded just as you were trained and you have saved the pets life! But now it is time to assess and treat those open wounds and that hideously dangling limb. Even if you plan to refer the pet to a specialist for definitive orthopedic treatment, what you do now will profoundly affect the pets comfort, prevent ongoing damage and will initiate the healing process.

courses.title: Managing Trauma
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss how to discuss a trauma situation with a client, present an initial estimate, as well as stabilize the patient. In the role of the technician, it's crucial to learn how to provide fluids, oxygen therapy, point of care testing, and pain management. Each of these steps will be reviewed in detail throughout this course.

courses.title: NW X SW REGIONAL DISEASES OF THE SOUTHWEST (637-41820)
courses.description: The lecture is 59min and consists of a speaker discussing cases and treatments regional to the Southwest United States. Josh Cruz, DVM, takes us through case based examples of maladies common to the Southwest United States, with a focus on diagnostics, therapeutics, and interventions that are applicable to emergencies in the Southwest United States.

courses.title: HYPERADRENOCORTICISM DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT (637-42922)
courses.description: Barbara Davis, DVM, DACVIM, reviews Cushing's disease symptoms and management. This lecture is one hour and covers signalment and clinical manifestations in veterinary patients. We will also do into detail regarding testing options such as ACTH Stimulation test and Low Dose Dexamethasone Suppression Test. We will wrap up with an overview of client expectation management.

courses.title: Radiography: Proper Positioning for Dogs and Cats
courses.description: In this presentation, Dr. Constance De Haan reviews the basic concepts of radiographic positioning. She also includes an overview of techniques and protocols for successful radiographic images by practicing proper anatomic radiographic techniques, with a focus on the reduction of veterinary patient dose as well as occupational staff and general public radiation exposure

courses.title: Radiography: Proper Positioning for Dogs and Cats, Part 2
courses.description: In part 2 of this webinar, Dr. Constance DeHaan reviews the basic concepts of radiographic positioning for thoracic and pelvic limb radiographs. This online course presents an overview of techniques and protocols for successful radiographic images by practicing proper anatomic radiographic techniques, and it focuses on the reduction of veterinary patient dose and occupational staff and general public radiation exposure.

courses.title: Prolapse: What's That Under the Tail?
courses.description: In this lecture, Coby Richter, DVM, DACVS, takes a diagnostic and therapeutic look at different prolapses and discusses treatment strategies. This lecture is 59 minutes and covers the numerous types of prolapses, surgical considerations, and pain management.

courses.title: Beyond the CBC: Mastering Acute Phase Proteins in Practice
courses.description: This session explores the clinical utility of acute phase proteins (APPs) in companion animal practice. Attendees will review the most common feline and canine APPs, understand their diagnostic advantages over traditional leukograms, and learn how to apply them clinically. From early disease detection to monitoring treatment response, this session provides actionable insights to enhance your diagnostic and therapeutic efficiency.

courses.title: Canine Pancreatitis Diagnosis and Treatment for Clinicians
courses.description: Canine pancreatitis is an important disease with varied presentations and outcomes. Diagnosing severe, acute pancreatitis may be straightforward; however, canine patients with mild to moderate disease or more chronic signs may pose a diagnostic challenge. This course will help clinicians recognize common presentations and supportive laboratory findings, differentiate and interpret available pancreatic lipase tests, and plan additional testing to diagnose acute or chronic pancreatitis. Standard and novel treatments for canine pancreatitis are discussed.

courses.title: The Do's and Don'ts of Canine Otitis Externa
courses.description: Otitis externa is a commonly diagnosed abnormality, affecting up to 20% of dogs. This presentation discusses predisopsing, primary, secondary and perpetuating factors, the diagnostic approach, and rationale treatment for acute and chronic otitis. A detailed review of available treatment options will be presented.

courses.provider: VETERINARY ASSOCIATION FOR FARM ANIMAL WELFARE
courses.title: Immunocastration of Pigs: Welfare Benefits, Industry Adoption, and Practical Lessons from Latin America
courses.description: Immunocastration is increasingly recognized as an effective alternative to surgical castration in pig production, offering significant animal welfare advantages while maintaining productive performance. This webinar will provide an overview of the scientific basis of immunocastration, its welfare and production benefits, and current challenges associated with implementation. Drawing on recent research conducted in Brazil and Colombia, countries with some of the highest adoption rates worldwide, the presentation will explore the motivations, perceived benefits, and barriers influencing on-farm implementation. Practical insights from producers and thought leaders in the production chain will be discussed, highlighting key factors that can facilitate wider adoption of immunocastration in commercial swine production systems.

courses.title: DIC - HOW DO WE RECOGNIZE AND TREAT IT? (637-39727)
courses.description: The lecture is 50 minutes and consists of speaker Lee Herold, DVM, DACVECC, doing a formal presentation on Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation. Dr. Herold will review why it is a condition that occurs with other predisposing disease, and how to recognize it.

courses.title: YOU WANT ME TO PUT THE NEEDLE WHERE? (637-42014)
courses.description: The lecture is 63 minutes and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on paracentesis in dogs and cats. DoveLewis Criticalist Dr. Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, describes when and how to perform thoracocentesis, abdominocentesis, and pericardiocentesis in an emergency room.

courses.title: NUTRITION IN THE CRITICALLY ILL (637-36513)
courses.description: This talk will briefly review the metabolic processes of the ill patient and how it differs from a healthy patient. Different modes of nutritional support will be outlined from enteral to parenteral, as well as cases to demonstrate the different strategies at work. This lecture presented by DoveLewis Criticalist Ladan Mohammad- Zadeh is 50 minutes and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on nutrition both in and out of the hospital.

courses.title: TRIAGE CARE OF THE ACUTE ABDOMEN (637-38441)
courses.description: In veterinary medicine "acute abdomen" can be used as a general term used to describe patients with any acute significant abdominal signs. In this article, Erika Loftin, DVM, DACVECC, discusses approach, diagnosis, testing and treatment plans in acute abdomen cases. Medical versus surgical management is reviewed, as well as stabilizing therapies.

courses.title: Parasites Found: Results of the National DoGPaRCS Study
courses.description: Dog parks are the fastest growing segment of city parks in United States. Many dogs and their owners enjoy the exercise and social opportunities dog parks allow, but bringing dogs together can also contribute to elevated risk of parasitism. In this presentation, Dr. Susan Little shares results of a first-of-its-kind study that comprehensively evaluated parasitism in dogs at dog parks across the United States. With more than 1 in 5 dogs at dog parks in the United States infected with intestinal parasites1, the importance of comprehensive screening for infection, including fecal testing - even in dogs on preventatives - has never been clearer.

courses.title: Wrapped for Success: Veterinary Bandaging Techniques
courses.description: In this course, learners will develop an understanding of the different types of bandages, their applications, and proper selection for various injuries. We'll start off by discussing types of wounds, the purpose of bandaging, different paths of wound healing, and then we'll dive into bandaging techniques, including the use of drains, and various tips and tricks.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Anesthesia Fundamentals
courses.description: This CE covers "a little about a lot" about all basics of veterinary anesthesia! We will discuss the basics of anesthesia definitions, anesthetic machine, breathing circuits & airway supplies, monitoring, and anesthetic drugs utilized in veterinary anesthesia.

courses.title: Canine Pancreatitis: Updates and Focus on Evidence-Based Medicine
courses.description: This lecture presented by Staci Goussev, DVM, DACVIM (SAIM) will provide an overview of pancreatitis in dogs and cats with an eye toward recently published recommendations for diagnostics and management of the disease.

courses.title: A Complete Introduction to Safety-Focused TPLO
courses.description:
This hybrid course includes 3 comprehensive hours of bite sized online modules that provide valuable tips on pathophysiology of CrCL disease, diagnosis, positioning for TPLO radiographs, preoperative planning, meniscal injury and treatment, and reducing surgical site infections.
Once in our CE lab, you will develop your hands on surgical skills to perform stifle arthrotomy, meniscal treatment, and TPLO using plastic bone models and cadaveric specimens. This is the only TPLO course in North America that supports you each step of the way during and after your training. While here, you will also spend time in insightful radiographic review discussions of your TPLOs before repeating the procedure on your pathway toward mastery.
Ponder this, even if you were trained to fly a Boeing 737, would you pilot a commercial flight without the decision making support of a flight plan, a co pilot, control tower and ground crew? Of course not. So, why would you do a surgery as intricate as TPLO without using a support team to enhance the safety for your patient?
This course trains you to use patient specific pre, intra and post-operative support on your individual TPLO patients. You will learn how to receive case by case preoperative guidance and procedural planning, use patient specific instructions to perform a guided TPLO cut, and to use detailed postoperative critique to shorten your learning curve and more rapidly grow your skills. Curious what this is all about? Better check it out.

courses.title: Finding Connections with colleagues and clients; normalize NOT making assumptions on why some say the things they do.
courses.description: Dr. Maryse Osborn, an IDEXX veterinarians and Insights Discovery Client Practitioner with IDEXX and Rebeka Graham, a License Practitioner with Insights Discover will walk through the value of a deeper understanding of psychology preferences in communications along with some tools to adapt and connect more effectively in conversations with your peers and clients.

courses.title: Supportive Feeding Methods for Small Animals
courses.description: Elevate your nutritional support and feeding tube knowledge with Amber Hart, RVT, VTS(ECC). Learn to confidently implement various supportive feeding methods through this comprehensive course. Gain insights into the benefits and applications of each technique, master proper placement procedures, and explore common feeding tube options alongside effective suture trap methods for secure placement.

courses.title: Ophthalmic Emergencies in Dogs
courses.description: This program will provide foundational, clinically relevant information regarding commonly encountered ophthalmic emergencies in dogs. It is designed to equip veterinary professionals with the knowledge and confidence to recognize, assess, and manage these ophthalmic emergencies. Through a focused exploration of urgent conditions affecting the orbit, adnexa, cornea, and intraocular structures, participants will learn to rapidly identify sight-threatening problems and initiate appropriate interventions. Emphasis will be placed on conditions that are reasonable to manage in practice and when referral should be initiated, if available. The curriculum covers a wide range of critical topics, including orbital and adnexal emergencies such as proptosis and eyelid trauma, corneal ulcers and perforations, acute glaucoma, anterior and posterior lens luxations, and the diagnostic approach to sudden blindness. By the end of the course, learners will be better prepared to stabilize patients, prioritize differential diagnoses, and make timely decisions that preserve comfort and vision. This program is ideal for primary care general practice and emergency veterinarians seeking to strengthen their emergency ophthalmology skills and improve outcomes for canine patients.

courses.title: The Use of Orthobiologics in Equine Sports Medicine
courses.description: In this presentation, we will discuss the role of orthobiologics in equine sports medicine, highlighting their safety and effectiveness as a treatment option. Orthobiologics, such as autologous conditioned serum (ACS), offer promising alternatives to traditional nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or corticosteroids. We will explore the science behind these treatments to show how orthobiologics enhance the body's natural healing processes, promoting tissue repair and reducing inflammation at the injury site.

courses.title: Optimizing your Telemedicine Abdominal Ultrasound Submission
courses.description: Submitting the optimal number of ultrasound images, with the quality and format described, maximizes the diagnostic value of your submission, improves the efficiency with which our radiologists can provide a report, and ultimately enhances your ability to provide prompt and effective care to your patients.

courses.title: Taking the Pain Out of Ear Cytology Using In-House Diagnostics to Target Treatment of Otitis Externa
courses.description: This lecture will review the morphology of common otic pathogens including Malassezia, Staphylococcus, and Pseudomonas. Ear swab cytology results along with otic and full physical examination will be used to create treatment plans for canine and feline patients with both acute and chronic otitis externa. Progression of otitis externa to otitis media will be discussed along with criteria that may guide practitioners to consider advanced imaging and referral. Utilization of IDEXX InVue Cellular Analyzer will be discussed

courses.title: ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY (637-43592)
courses.description: The lecture is 68 minutes and consists of a speaker Erika Loftin, DVM, DACVECC, doing a formal presentation on acute kidney injury physiology, assessment, and treatment in dogs and cats. Erika Loftin, DVM, DACVECC, gives an in-depth lecture about acute kidney injury. After a review of renal physiology, diagnostics, patient assessment, treatment modalities, drug pharmacology, and patient monitoring for kidney disease are discussed.

courses.title: Ready, Set, Go to Surgery!
courses.description: Being prepared for surgery means good planning, communication and anticipation of potential complications. In this lecture presented by Andrea Sundholm, DVM, DACVS-SA, we will focus on the preoperative work that goes into specific surgical cases such as fracture repair, C-section, liver biopsy and foreign body retrieval. We will review recommended bloodwork, imaging, clipping and surgical prep. Example anesthetic protocols as well as special considerations for brachycephalic breeds will be shared.

courses.title: A CASE-BASED APPROACH TO UNDERSTANDING CANINE CHRONIC ENTEROPATHY (CE)/ INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE ( (21-43569)
courses.description: A CASE-BASED APPROACH TO UNDERSTANDING CANINE CHRONIC ENTEROPATHY (CE)/ INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE ( (21-43569) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: When Everything is an Exclamation Point: How to Communicate in Times of High Stress
courses.description: 2020 has been full of uncertainly with both political unrest and COVID. In this lecture, Monica Maxwell, SPHR, SHRM-SCP, will discuss communication in the time of highly emotional stress. When clients and staff are at their breaking point, the smallest amount of conflict can escalate quickly. This lecture will include tips and tools to defuse, reset and help manage stress in a stressful world.

courses.title: Cultivating Resilience
courses.description: Resilience helps us to work through challenges and empowers personal growth. Cultivating resilience through intentional effort is essential given the inherent stressors and challenges within veterinary medicine. This lecture presented by Debrah Lee, LSCW, will discuss strategies to support resilience using current knowledge around self-care, well-being and the impact of stress based on the mind-body connection.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Clinical Skills & Applications for the Rehabilitation Therapist
courses.description: A particular focus is identifying orthopedic and neurologic conditions and building an effective therapeutic patient plan. Practical applications of joint mobilization, modalities, therapeutic exercise, neurorehabilitation, pain recognition and assessment, gait patterns and lameness, and pain management are covered. Students get hands-on experience with dogs on-site as they learn how to perform a comprehensive exam and apply rehabilitation techniques.

courses.title: Cybersecurity and Hardware Setup for Veterinary Practices
courses.description:
In recent years, veterinary practices have made significant strides in embracing digital solutions - from cloud-based management software to AI tools, apps, online services, and telehealth. These innovations are enhancing workflows, client experiences, and patient care, but they also introduce a critical need for strong cybersecurity to keep your data safe.
It's easy to think that cyberattacks only target big corporations, but small and medium-sized businesses, like veterinary hospitals, are just as much at risk. In fact, around one-third of these businesses face cyber-attacks every year, which could mean that roughly 11,000 veterinary practices are affected annually. The consequences can be severe, from lost data and operational downtime to damage to your practice's reputation.
This course provides an in-depth exploration of cybersecurity threats specific to veterinary practices and the critical steps required to secure hardware and data. We'll walk through practical security measures, such as effective password management, two-factor authentication, and regular software updates, alongside key strategies for data backup and recovery planning.
Beyond cybersecurity, we'll discuss why a well-planned hardware setup is essential for ensuring operational efficiency and future scalability. Finally, we'll address the security and data privacy considerations associated with the growing adoption of AI in veterinary practices.
Human error is often the weakest link in cybersecurity, so we'll also cover the role of staff training in preventing breaches and fostering a culture of security within your practice.

courses.title: Master De-escalation and documentation of critical incidents
courses.description: With the societal rise in crime that is affecting all industries, Alpha Innovative Solutions, LLC has created a 1-hour course curriculum to focus on how veterinary office practice and staff can reduce liability increase workplace situational awareness, recognize and manage threats, and confidently ensure proper documentation after high-stress situations. Attendees will understand and identify threats in and around their clinics. Attendees will be asked to participate to enhance their learning experience. Attendees will develop an understanding of proper social distancing, learn to use spatial awareness to de-escalate tense situations while learning to establish and respect personal boundaries, while managing and interpreting verbal and non-verbal communication with abusive clients. Lastly, attendees will understand the best practice of proper documentation to memorialize critical incident reports for the protection of their practice and their staff.

courses.title: CIRDC: A new look at Prevalence, Detection, and Protection
courses.description: Description: CIRDC can be mild, moderate, or severe and potentially life threatening in canine patients. Description of the common causes and infectious agents, who often and where we commonly see each infectious agent in our canine population in north America and what available testing there is to identify the cause of disease and make treatment choices. With additional focus on prevention as a part of individual care but also for the benefit of populations of dogs.

courses.title: The Physiology of Pain
courses.description: Understanding pain physiology is essential to recognizing, assessing, and effectively managing pain in veterinary patients. This lecture provides a comprehensive overview of how pain is generated, transmitted, and perceived across species, forming the scientific basis for clinical pain management. Topics will include nociception, peripheral and central sensitization, acute versus chronic pain mechanisms, and the impact of pain on physiologic systems. Species differences and clinically relevant pathways will be highlighted to help bridge the gap between theory and practice. By strengthening their grasp of pain physiology, attendees will be better equipped to make informed analgesic decisions and improve patient welfare across veterinary settings.

courses.title: Preventive Care: Why it matters to pets, owners, and veterinarians
courses.description: This seminar will be a discussion around preventive care as a tool for optimizing health and longevity in pets. Topics will include what preventative care consists of, age-appropriate assessment, the benefits of patient-specific information that can be trended over time and strengthening the vet-patient-client bond. Updated health stage-guidelines for dogs and cats will be reviewed.

courses.title: Leadership Fatigue
courses.description: Are you feeling overwhelmed, demotivated, and drained in your leadership role? You're not alone. Leadership fatigue is a real threat, impacting your well-being, your team, and ultimately, the patients you care for. This engaging course equips you with the knowledge and tools to identify, prevent, and overcome leadership fatigue, reclaiming your passion and leading with renewed energy.

courses.title: Veterinary Botanical Medicine Consultant
courses.description: This online course teaches participants science-based information on botanical remedies, including their mechanisms of action, indications, contraindications, herb-drug interactions and, for cannabis, legal and ethical concerns. Instruction will comprise of short videos, self-paced assignments, reading, critiques, and online quizzes. Upon completion, participants should be able to confidently discuss the pros and cons of various herbal options with their clients based on science and research. Dr. Robinson encourages provides to exercise critical thinking and to separate fact from fiction when considering the use of any integrative therapy. Doing so is especially crucial in the field of herbal medicine due to the potential for harm from biochemically active products. Students learn to approach botanical medicine from a scientific, evidence-based perspective to provide the highest quality care to their patients. This is not a how-to course that will encourage you to sell and manage your patients solely on herbs. Until there is more evidence for target species, many challenges remain.

courses.title: Disease in Disguise: Unmasking Addisons disease
courses.description: Addisons disease, sometimes referred to as the great pretender, is not a common diagnosis, but the clinical signs seen with this disease imitate many other diseases such as acute or chronic GI disease, kidney disease, or parasitic disease. It is important to rule out or diagnose Addisons disease efficiently due to the severe consequences if a dog has an adrenal crisis. The availability of an accurate point-of-care cortisol assay allows veterinarians to quickly ruleout Addisons disease with a resting cortisol or diagnose the disease by performing an ACTH stimulation test.

courses.title: Initial Evaluation and Stabilization of Fractures
courses.description: Join Andrea Sundholm, DVM, DACVS-SA, as we discuss the evaluation and stabilization of fractures in veterinary patients. Our discussion will focus on the initial care of fractures including wound management and bandaging techniques. Using specific case examples, we will also review potential fixation options and long-term care recommendations.

courses.title: PET Detective: Tracking Trouble with FDG
courses.description: This hour-long lecture will serve to introduce participants to imaging with FDG PET/CT. It will explore the reasons why it is superior at staging and prognosticating veterinary cancer patients. There will also be a discussion of instances where FDG PET/CT was useful in non-oncology cases including musculoskeletal mysteries and fever of unknown origin. A brief mention of novel isotopes that may be soon available to veterinary patients will also be touched on.

courses.title: The IDEXX VetLab Station Certificate Course
courses.description: This interactive, self-paced course helps veterinary professionals gain proficiency on the IDEXX VetLab Station laboratory information management system. Become an IDEXX VetLab Station expert and help create a more streamlined, efficient and productive in-house laboroatory workflow.

courses.title: The Five Languages of Motivation
courses.description: In this lecture, Monica Maxwell, SPHR, SHRM-SCP, MBTI, will discuss how The Five Languages of Love by Gary Chapman can be used in the workplace. She will explain how the love languages relate to how employees communicate and hear value, and how understanding your employee's language is key to engagement and retention.

courses.title: Drawing a Line in the Sand: Setting Boundaries, Reducing Stress & Adjusting to the New Normal in Food/Mixed Animal Practice
courses.description: This course covers the principles of achieving healthy mental health as a practicing veterinarian/veterinary technician by setting boundaries and stress reduction. We will also discuss current topics affecting mixed/food animal practices.

courses.title: Confidence in Cancer Care: Practical Approaches to Lymphoma Diagnosis and Management
courses.description: Lymphoma is a common cancer in dogs, often presenting as painless enlargement of lymph nodes. There are several forms, with multicentric lymphoma being the most common. Diagnosis is typically made through fine needle aspiration (FNA) or biopsy, sometimes followed by advanced tests like flow cytometry to distinguish B-cell from T-cell lymphoma. Treatment usually involves chemotherapy, with CHOP protocols (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone) being most effective, and survival times averaging 12-14 months for treated dogs. Prognosis depends on factors like immunophenotype and disease stage, with B-cell lymphoma generally responding better than T-cell. Early diagnosis and treatment significantly improve outcomes.

courses.title: Unlocking Brakke's Home Delivery Data: Thriving in the Digital Age: E-Commerce & Marketing for Veterinary Practices
courses.description: Veterinary home delivery platforms provide a powerful solution to improve client compliance enhance patient care and capture revenue that would otherwise be lost to online retailers But simply offering home delivery isnt enough clients must be aware understand the value and feel motivated to use it In Part 2 of this CE series Thriving in the Digital Age we focus on how veterinary teams can effectively market their home delivery platform using proven digital marketing strategies Backed by Brakkes Home Delivery Data, this session empowers practices to build visibility trust and consistent use of their home delivery services through strategic promotion and communication

courses.title: Safe Sedation and Anesthesia of Patients with Cardiac Disease
courses.description: Patients with cardiac disease present unique sedation and anesthesia challenges. This course discusses the peri-anesthetic considerations that are useful in developing a sedation and general anesthesia plan. It also looks at planning and patient preparation from pre-hospital admission through discharge to home.

courses.title: Regenerative Medicine for Musculoskeletal Disease
courses.description: This course examines the use of regenerative medicine in treating musculoskeletal disease, including osteoarthritis, tendon, and ligament injuries. It covers how to combine regenerative medicine with other products for injection into arthritic joints, as well using a multimodal approach for treating tendon or ligament injury. This information will arm practitioners with a good understanding of how to use regenerative medicine, alone or in combination with other treatments, to address musculoskeletal disease.

courses.title: CERTIFICATE IN APPLIED ANIMAL BEHAVIOR (1296-44187)
courses.description:
Humans have been interacting with animals for millennia, observing them in homes, farms, zoos and labs. The more we understand about animal behavior, the more effective we can be at caring for them and improving their health and quality of life.
In this three-course certificate program, we'll study different principles of animal behavior and learn to apply this knowledge to animal care. You'll examine behavioral differences between animal species and how these reflect their evolution and habitat adaptation. Gain insights on evolutionary theory, learning theory and biology to provide better care for animals - particularly companion animals - and diagnose and treat a variety of behavior issues.

courses.title: Global FAST Hybrid Online course (AFAST-TFAST, and VetBLUE) with Hands On Live Scanning
courses.description:
The course covers AFAST and its image acquisition, its target-organ approach for obvious soft tissue abnormalities, and its abdominal fluid scoring system with case-based applications; TFAST and its image acquisition, its echocardiography views, its use for the accurate diagnosis of pleural and pericardial effusion and pneumothorax, its target-organ approach of the heart and pleural space for obvious soft-tissue abnormalities; and Vet BLUE and its image acquisition, its regional, pattern-based approach integrating its B-line scoring system, and 6 lung ultrasound signs. Global FAST is the term used when AFAST, TFAST and Vet BLUE are combined as a single ultrasound format used as an extension of the physical exam. The terms AFAST, TFAST, Vet BLUE and Global FAST are registered service marks for education purposes with the US Patent and Trademark Office to uphold each exam's highest degree of integrity as a standardized ultrasound exam.
The 5-lectures cover AFAST, TFAST, and Vet BLUE, combined called Global FAST, plus a 1-hour Global FAST image acquisition supplemental module (7-hours total of online lectures). Quizzes must be passed with a score of 80% to move on to the next module.
The remote online course above is followed by a live hands on scanning session (4 hour scanning session).

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Common Avian Emergencies
courses.description: Pet birds and backyard chickens are often presented on emergency with advanced disease as birds commonly hide signs of early illness, consistent with most prey species. This course reviews common avian emergencies including hemorrhage, seizures, cloacal prolapses, and dyspnea via case examples in parrots and chickens.

courses.title: Explanatory Thinking Styles: To Optimism and Beyond (On Demand)
courses.description: Explanatory thinking styles not only dictate our perception, they can promote growth, productivity and development. They can also contribute to worry, anxiety and pessimism. In the unpredictable and challenging field of veterinary medicine we can all benefit from a deeper understanding of the thinking styles available to us in our everyday encounters. A further understanding of the tools available within us will help each of us to reach for the right one as we navigate our day. Leaders and support staff alike can not only broaden their ability to expand a more positive outlook within themselves, they can cultivate this within their teams, clinics, and hospitals! In this session we will dive deeper into the variety of explanatory thinking styles and how they can directly influence mindset and wellbeing. We will explore the types of thinking styles, learn to recognize and combat thinking traps and create a more resilient way of showing up in the world. Attendees will enjoy playing with specific tools to empower them with these important, energizing skills.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Antimicrobial Stewardship in Companion Animal Medicine
courses.description: Veterinarians wish to use antimicrobials judiciously but sometimes it can be difficult to know how to refine and optimize antimicrobial prescribing. This course outlines antimicrobial stewardship practices that can be undertaken at the level of the individual practitioner and, in the process, achieve better patient outcomes.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: JPS? TPO? THR? FHO? WTFudge??? Navigating Hip Dysplasia Options
courses.description: There are numerous surgical options for managing hip dysplasia including juvenile pubic symphysiodesis (JPS), triple or double pelvic osteotomy (TPO/DPO), femoral head and neck ostectomy (FHO), and total hip replacement (THR). The decision for when these procedures may be recommended is difficult to navigate. Even if the practitioner is not performing these surgeries, it is important to be aware of factors affecting procedure selection. JPS and TPO are time and disease stage sensitive that could be relatively less expensive options to mitigate a lifetime of hip OA management. This course covers the main indications, patient selection/exclusion criteria, and ideal timing of each of these procedures.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Keep the Beat - Anesthetic Considerations for Patients with Cardiac Disease
courses.description: This course discusses anesthetic considerations and tips for patients with cardiac disease, focusing on concerns associated with specific cardiomyopathies. In addition, it reviews pharmacology in relation to cardiac disease as well as potential complications associated with anesthesia in these patients.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Bite Check - Detecting Malocclusions in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Do dogs really get braces? The answer is: sometimes. Every patient deserves a comfortable and pain-free bite. Addressing malocclusions that cause trauma is essential for their well-being. This course defines what constitutes a normal occlusion in both dogs and cats. From there, it will delve into the various classes of malocclusions, helping veterinary professionals accurately identify and differentiate these conditions. Finally, it will explore the appropriate treatment options for each class of malocclusion. This will help you help patients live a pain free life.

courses.title: Special Series: Owner-Present Euthanasia in Animal Shelters
courses.description: Animal shelters are regularly tasked with the euthanasia of animals, for a variety of reasons. In many instances, the request to euthanize a pet comes directly from a pet owner who wishes to end suffering due to age related changes, specific illnesses, or when aggressive behavior has become overwhelming. Pet owners may ask to remain with their pet during the euthanasia procedure, however this is rarely allowed in shelters due to staffing constraints, the extra skill required to euthanize a pet when owners are watching, and/or the increased risk of staff compassion fatigue from watching emotional owners say goodbye. As the cost of home and hospital euthanasia increases, shelters need to prepare for more euthanasia requests by owners. In this 4 hour short course, CAETA prepares shelter personnel to work directly with pet owners who wish to remain present for the euthanasia procedure. Hour 1 focuses on communicating with pet owners including understanding owner needs, establishing trust and answering important questions. Hour 2 highlights appointment preparations such as planning and paperwork, preparing staff and space, and owner and pet arrival. Hour 3 focuses on the euthanasia procedure itself, specifically on patient handling, describing what's happening to owners, and challenging situations. Lastly hour 4 teaches about grief support, body care and exploring case examples over a series of 3 videos. Shelter staff and all learners who complete the course will increase their confidence when performing the procedure with pet owners there for the entire appointment.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Rabbit and Rodent Dentistry
courses.description: Dental disease is one of the most common diseases of herbivorous rodents (guinea pigs and chinchillas) and of rabbits. It is vital to be aware of anatomy and disease etiology along with how to perform the oral exam. In addition, awareness of diagnostic factors and treatment options are important in providing good patient care. This course will review all these components.

courses.title: Foundational Knowledge of Referring THR
courses.description: Foundations of Referring Total Hip Replacement THR is designed to provide you with the necessary information to refer dogs and cats for THR. Traditionally, THR has been considered by many veterinarians to be complicated and challenging for vets, owners, and pets. However, technology and technique have evolved. THR is now considered a routine surgical procedure and the gold standard for treatment of hip dysplasia and severe osteoarthritis by experts in the field. Advancements in technology have made it possible for implants to last the pets lifetime. By replicating the natural ball and socket joint, THR is designed to return pets to a normal-functioning pain free life.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Recognizing and Preventing In-House Cardiopulmonary Arrest
courses.description: This course discusses how to recognize impending cardiopulmonary arrest, what to do if a patient arrests in-house, and how to continue supportive care in the post cardiopulmonary arrest patient.

courses.title: Ears and Otitis Externa: Treating the Ears/Understanding the Basics
courses.description: Otitis externa can be a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. Success requires a complete plan. The presenter will discuss each step in detail including the history, physical examination, identification of primary and secondary underlying factors, development of a treatment plan that the client can accomplish, and the need for continual follow-up.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Canine Influenza from Emergence to Outbreaks - Protecting our Patients and Clinics
courses.description: In 2015 a novel flu virus was identified in dogs in the US. This canine influenza virus (CIV) quickly spread between dogs and continues to cause outbreaks with considerable dog illness and even death. This course provides the tools needed to tackle CIV. It outlines practical steps to assist in identifying these patients before they come in the door and infect other dogs, making the diagnosis to best inform treatment, developing a dog/owner specific prevention plan, and steps every facility should take to protect themselves from dog respiratory infections and outbreaks.

courses.title: Animal Echo Collection: Four Legs, Two Legs, One Heart: Cardiac Response To Athletic Training Across Species
courses.description: Differentiating echocardiographically between an athletic heart and a heart with dilated cardiomyopathy is often very straightforward, but in some cases can be challenging. This diagnostic dilemma occurs both in human patients and in dogs. The OnDemand course will demonstrate similarities and differences between these two types of patients, to provide complementary insights to physicians, monographers, veterinarians, and veterinary technicians.¿Format: This OnDemand course will offer 1 hour prerecorded course content as well as a separate test your knowledge section that will contain 5 questions. Learners must complete the test your knowledge section with a 70% or higher to complete the course and earn their course certificate. The OnDemand course will also contain a prerecorded Q&A with each of the speakers.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: ID poo-pourri- Emerging and Evolving Infectious Disease in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: In dogs and cats, infectious diseases are emerging and evolving rapidly, such as the impacts of the tapeworm (Echinococcus spp.), roundworm (Baylisascaris procyonis), and Giardia. These changes, and new research findings, bring various One Health (animal, human, environment), antimicrobial resistance, and stewardship challenges to the forefront for veterinarians and veterinary teams. This course addresses the concerns specific to Gastro-intestinal (GI) parasites and wellness screening and provides practical resources to aid clinical management and pet-owner communication.

courses.title: Advance25 - Advanced Abdominal Surgery
courses.description: Advance25 - Advanced Abdominal Surgery is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Cardiology Series with Dr. Peter Modler
courses.description: This Anytime course includes 14 hours of lecture with Dr. Peter Modler DVM, Dipl.-Tzt, who is a leading expert on mitral valve repair. Dr. Modler has an entertaining teaching style and provides ample visual and case-based examples to help you grasp complex subject matter easily.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: The A to Z of Pharmacology - Tips and Tricks to Remember Drugs, Classifications, and Actions
courses.description: Pharmacology is a complex component of everyday veterinary practice. All medical team members need to have a strong grasp of drugs, their classifications, and their actions. The learning process does not need to be hard or boring. This course will share fun and effective tips and tricks to aid retention. Refresh your memory or pick up some new knowledge to assist as you work daily with pharmaceuticals.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Diagnostic Testing for Feline GI Disease: From Laboratory Tests to Review of Histopathology Results
courses.description: This course walks through the case of a cat presenting with chronic gastrointestinal (GI) signs in a stepwise manner, looking at diagnostic testing in each stage. It starts with the initial evaluation and tests used to both confirm primary GI disease and non-invasively assess disease severity, utilizing tools readily available to primary practitioners. The course then progresses to more focused testing to localize disease and evaluate for non-GI disease that cannot be achieved through initial screening. Finally, it culminates with a review of the case's histopathology results and tips for looking at subtle descriptors to distinguish a chronic inflammatory enteropathy from low-grade alimentary lymphoma, as well as the utility of PCR and immunohistochemistry to aid in interpretation.

courses.title: Introduction to Avian Fracture Management Online Course
courses.description: Introduction to Avian Fracture Management Course is a webinar designed to provide an introduction to avian bone structure and effective fracture procedures. Delving into individual cases and bird anatomy, including ulna anatomy, it explores strategies for selecting repair methods and utilizing pins. Additionally, the webinar covers essential topics such as stabilization methods and p

courses.title: Guiding Choices: The GPs Role in Pet Cancer Treatment and Palliative Care
courses.description: No one wants to hear the word "cancer," but sadly it is a leading cause of death in pets. Veterinarians have to give pet owners this devastating news all too often and these conversations can be challenging but necessary. This course covers how to discuss cancer with pet owners including how to explain the differences in treatments between animals and people, types of treatments, and goals with therapy. Pet owners often have lots of questions for the primary veterinarian prior to referral and this course walks through commonly asked questions.

courses.title: CTUSS; The Key to Global Diagnostic Efficiency in Veterinary Medicine ANYTIME program
courses.description: This 1-hour online CE program will discuss the differences and individual benefits of both CT and ultrasound, as well as the combined benefit for patients. When should you pick up the probe or schedule a CT depending on the symptoms, clinical signs, and other diagnostics. CT: head, spine, neck, skeleton, thorax, abdomen, pelvic canal, perineum. US: head, MSK, thorax, abdomen. Case studies with sampling and cytologic findings will be presented and discussed.

courses.title: Advance25 - Orthopaedic for Advanced Practitioners
courses.description: Advance25 - Orthopaedic for Advanced Practitioners is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Avian Anesthesia: A Bird's Eye View
courses.description: Anesthetizing birds requires understanding their basic anatomy and physiology, including the ways they differ from mammals. It is important to be familiar with the anesthesia monitoring equipment that works with birds as well as machine and basic equipment set-up. Lastly, a well-rounded avian anesthesia protocol will incorporate the appropriate medications. This course will provide an overview of all these factors.

courses.title: Feline infectious peritonitis
courses.description: This practical course will bring veterinary professionals completely up to date on the treatment of feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) and give them confidence to diagnose and manage affected cats. The course will explain differences between feline enteric coronavirus (FECV) and feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), the pathogenesis of FIP as well as most common, and unusual, clinical signs. The course will explain the different diagnostic tests for FIP available in practice with emphasis on most useful tests and any limitations. This course will also discuss new options for FIP therapy including different antivirals (dosages and adverse effects) and immunomodulatory drugs. and as well as monitoring during treatment and possible complications of FIP therapy with antivirals. We will also discuss Managing complicated cases of FIP is discussed, as well as what to do if cats are not responding to medications, relapses of FIP and management of comorbidities such as IMHA, sepsis, pneumonia etc. Last but not least the course will cover supportive care for FIP cats as well as how to best support, and communicate with, their caregivers.

courses.title: Say What You Need To: Professionally Assertive and Honest Conversations
courses.description: In this one-hour video presentation, we'll share tools to help veterinary professionals feel comfortable and confident in any conversation - with your boss, your co-workers, and your clients. Want a raise? More time off? A change in protocol? This program will help attendees gain the confidence to ask for it! We will review assertive vs passive communication, study the various responses to an assertive conversation (crying, yelling, story-telling, etc), and consider how to best adapt to each response-type.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Knock 'em Down; Wake 'em Up
courses.description: This course covers the fundamentals of veterinary anesthesia for the veterinary technician. It starts with reviewing the basics of vital parameters and the impact that anesthesia has on them. It transitions into what is needed to prepare for an anesthetic case. The course also addresses equipment needs, intubation approaches, anesthetic maintenance, and troubleshooting. Lastly, it focuses on the process of recovery. The course reviews how we traverse from knocking patients down to waking them up.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Cannabinoids in the Clinic - Practical Approaches
courses.description: The clinical data for companion animals with the use of cannabinoids, like CBD, has been growing. This course will review the current and relevant literature along with dosing for safe and effective use in practice.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Hypersomatotropism - A Common Cause of Diabetes Mellitus in Cats
courses.description: Are you treating cats with diabetes mellitus (DM)? At least 1 in 4 of those cats have concurrent hypersomatotropism (DM-HS). The treatment, prognosis, progression, and monitoring of cats with DM and HS-DM can be vastly different. Therefore, differentiating between DM and HS-DM is critical. If you are waiting for classic acromegalic phenotype or excessive insulin requirements before diagnosing, you are missing many of these cats. Diagnosis, management, treatment goals, and monitoring of cats with HS-DM are discussed.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Talking to Clients About the Most Important Appointment, the Euthanasia
courses.description:
Euthanasias are one of the most difficult appointments that we see in a veterinary hospital. It is emotional for the client and the doctors, as well as the rest of the team. Many team members are awkward and unable to convey empathy to the clients while they are making the appointment.
This course looks at commonly made mistakes in the scheduling, the handling, and the communication during a euthanasia appointment. It will explain how managers can train their team members on this difficult conversation. It includes tips to use and specific phrases for team members to say to owners during this difficult time.

courses.title: Advance25: Medical Oncology in Practice
courses.description:
Diagnosis and treatment of cancer is a large and growing part of daily veterinary practice, and clients increasingly want to provide advanced cancer care for their pets. Increasing your ability to handle your own medical oncology cases in practice offers an exciting opportunity to expand your skill set; bring in more revenue to your practice; and most importantly, improve the quality of life and survival time for the many oncology patients whose owners would like to try treating their pet's cancer, but might not be able to pursue referral to a specialist for reasons of cost or logistics.
This entirely online course in Medical Oncology in Practice is specifically designed for vets in practice who want a thorough understanding of the latest updates on oncology in dogs and cats, with a focus on what you can do in practice to improve and prolong good patient quality of life. Through recorded sessions, extensive notes and MCQs, this course will increase your ability to handle your own medical oncology cases in practice.
Enjoy unlimited access to your course materials for a full 12 months. Get the help you need to deal effectively with your oncology patients.

courses.title: On Demand: Chronic Vomiting in the Dog and Cat
courses.description: Originally presented in 2020, this on-demand course features two videos, through which veterinary internist, Dr. David Twedt, will review step by step standards for diagnosing and treating causes of chronic vomiting and regurgitation. We'll practice differentiating reflux and regurgitation from vomiting, learn the causes of esophagitis and esophageal motility disorders, and hear how to prioritize a differential list for patients with chronic vomiting.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Laser Therapy Master Class - Inflammation and Beyond
courses.description: Laser therapy has been used in medicine for a long time, yet in the last decade there has been an explosion of pertinent research. From Osteoarthritis to Syringomyelia, the laser is an amazing tool when used correctly. It is vital to know how to get the best results from your laser no matter which laser you have, Class I, III, or IV. This course looks at the physiologic effects laser has on the body as well as how and when to use laser therapy, from treating cancer, osteoarthritis, asthma, and so much more. From traumatic brain injuries to a tooth abscess, this course provides insight on more ways to utilize your laser with solid research thrown in for fun.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Pretty Poisons: Common Plant Intoxications
courses.description: This course addresses the importance of accurate plant identification as it applies to toxic exposures as well as resources that can be used to accurately obtain plant identification. It will also cover plants toxic to the gastrointestinal, renal, cardiac, and neurologic systems. Mechanism of toxicity, symptoms and how to treat the various toxins will also be reviewed.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Novel Treatments for Refractory Chronic Enteropathy Management
courses.description: This course reviews novel therapeutic approaches to treating chronic enteropathy patients. Once a patient is diagnosed and fails traditional approaches to management, how are we going to treat it? Are we implementing nutritional management in the correct scenarios? Are we managing underlying irritable bowel syndrome? Are there recently identified drug treatments available? This course provides a clinical update on the treatment of refractory chronic diarrhea.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Toxicology 101
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to toxicology for the veterinary technician. It focuses on initial presentation and obtaining a thorough history, the value of a poison control consultation, and toxic principles. It will also look at some common toxins in veterinary medicine

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Complications of Dental Extractions: Avoiding and Dealing with Them
courses.description: The old adage "it's like pulling teeth" arose for a reason. Extracting firmly rooted teeth is sometimes necessary, but there are many things that can go wrong. This course discusses the most common complications associated with dental extractions, including retrieving broken root tips, displaced roots into the nasal passage as well as mandibular canal, sialoceles, and iatrogenic mandibular fractures. It reviews how to avoid these complications and how to treat them when they do occur.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Surgical Conditions of the Equine Foot
courses.description: At times, medical conditions and trauma of the equine hoof requires surgery to fully address. Knowing when and how to approach can greatly benefit both horse and owner. This course reviews a variety of surgical conditions of the equine foot. Topics cover trauma to the hoof, septic pedal osteitis, keratoma, canker, quittor, bone cysts, and fractures. Typical presentation, diagnosis, treatment options, surgical techniques, and prognosis is discussed for each condition.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Guttural Pouch Disease in the Equine Patient
courses.description: Guttural pouch disease presents unique challenges for equine professionals and requires a nuanced understanding of its causes along with diagnostic methods and management strategies. This course explores the anatomy and function of the guttural pouches. Next it delves into the various types of guttural pouch diseases along with examining their etiology, clinical presentations, and treatment options.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Cytology for Technicians
courses.description: This course discusses why cytology is important in dermatology, will outline the parts of a microscope, and will explain how to perform cytology and microscopic identification.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Honoring Your Mental Health as a Veterinary Professional
courses.description: This course examines the most common causes of mental health difficulties currently facing the veterinary industry. It includes how to recognize the early warning signs of emerging mental health struggles such as burnout, compassion fatigue, imposter syndrome, and perfectionism. In addition, it provides tangible guidance on how to help manage chronic stress and anxiety during client interactions as well as provides tools to aid veterinary professionals in rediscovering and sustaining wellness, resilience, and contentment within the field of veterinary medicine. Participants shall discover how vital self-advocacy, self-care, mindfulness, and boundaries are when choosing a workplace environment and for protecting physical, mental, emotional, and financial health.

courses.title: On Demand: ER Anesthesia
courses.description: This course features two videos, through which we'll learn how to maximize the safety of anesthesia and sedation in an ER setting, both for patients and staff. We'll review species-specific considerations for critically ill dogs and cats, determine how to set IV fluid rates, how to choose optimal pre-anesthetic drugs, and how to manage blood pressure and other parameters in our ER patients. We'll also study the safest practices for handling fractious patients, avoiding medication errors, and responding to malfunctions in anesthesia equipment.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Master the Money Conversation and Move Your Clients to Yes
courses.description: Money conversations with clients are at best uncomfortable and at worst can lead to unhappy outcomes. These conversations are usually dreaded by team members. But it does not have to always be this way. Armed with training in communicating with clients, the practice can work to overcome resistance and misunderstandings. Converse with an elevated level of awareness and confidence so that you get more compliance and adherence while at the same time reducing team stress.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Neurodiversity and Disability Justice - Americans with Disabilities Act Includes Neurodiversity
courses.description: The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) was passed in 1990 as part of a movement to recognize the civil rights of Americans with disabilities. This legislation seeks to eliminate discrimination. It is not just for people with different physical abilities, but also includes mental and emotional conditions that limit one or more major life activity. What does the Americans with Disabilities Act mean for neurodiverse veterinary professionals in the workplace?

courses.title: IMEX External Skeletal Fixation Level 1: Distal Limb Traumatology
courses.description: An introductory workshop designed to address both routine and challenging fractures of the distal limb using linear and hybrid external skeletal fixation. The course will cover ESF principles and application techniques, patient selection, instrumentation and implants, and postoperative care. Additionally, the workshop discusses the potential complications associated with external skeletal fixation and how to recognize and manage issues that develop in the postoperative convalescent period. Current theory and practice are reinforced through laboratory exercises using plastic bones and cadavers.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: You're My Hero: Smoke Inhalation
courses.description: Picture the scene...the door to the treatment room opens and a fireman in full gear walks in, carrying a cat in his arms, oxygen mask held to its face. This everyday hero has saved the patient from the fire, but now it's up to you. What damage can be caused from smoke inhalation and thermal burns? What can you expect to see? What do you monitor for? What will you be treating for? What are the chances you can save this patient?

courses.title: International Association for Animal Hospice and Palliative Care Certification Pain Management Module 4
courses.description: This program covers the management of pain for the hospice and palliative care patient. Subjects covered include the neurophysiology of pain, understanding and using pain pharmaceuticals, managing acute and chronic pain and the use of comfort kits, recognizing and assessing pain, non-pharmacologic ways to manage pain, the role of the veterinary technician in managing the pain of a hospice and palliative care patient and understanding emerging pain management therapies.

courses.title: VETERINARY DENTISTRY FOR TECHNICIANS
courses.description: This online course focuses on instruction in veterinary dentistry for technicians in general practice including information on radiology, periodontal disease, pain management, anesthesia and client communication.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Angling for Great Intraoral Dental Radiographs
courses.description: This course outlines a logical and step-by-step approach to intraoral dental radiographs. It looks at both the why and the how, including safety considerations. The course identifies some key components of how to take diagnostic images and how to help prevent the need to repeat radiographs. It takes the geometry out of choosing angles and outlines the positioning for each view in dogs and cats.

courses.title: Steps to a Comprehensive Oral Health Assessment and Treatment (COHAT)
courses.description: Performing a Complete Oral Health Assessment and Treatment (COHAT) entails much more than removing plaque and calculus from the teeth. A thorough dental prophylaxis consists of educating the client, an oral examination, and charting the disease process, pathology and anomalies. It also includes radiographs, both supra, and sub-gingival plaque and calculus removal, hand scaling, polishing, irrigation, and home care instructions. Each step is vital to prevent or halt disease progression.

courses.title: Working Dog Toxicology - Part I:
courses.description: Toxicology is unique, because it draws upon both basic science and direct, on-the-ground practical applications. Due to the inherent duties of their job, Workng Dogs of all discplines possess an occupational risk for exposure to various hazardous material and toxins in the envrionments where they operate. Part 1 of this elective provides veterinary professionals that support the Working Dog community the awareness, understanding, and appropriate treatment measures for the following Toxicology topics: Module 1: Veterinary Toxicology Review Modules 2 - Part 1: Chemical Contaminant Risks for Working Dogs: Hydrocarbons, PCBs, metals, asbestos, gases, soaps/detergents, acids/alkalis, glycols/phenols/alcohols Module 3 - Part 2: Chemical Contaminant Risks for Working Dogs: Hydrocarbons, PCBs, metals, asbestos, gases, soaps/detergents, acids/alkalis, glycols/phenols/alcohols Module 4: Risks Associated with Floodwaters

courses.title: Obesity in Pets - A Practical Approach to Weight Management
courses.description:
Pet obesity is one of the most common and preventable conditions seen in clinical practice today, affecting over half of dogs and cats in the U.S. This course addresses the medical, behavioral, and emotional challenges of pet obesity, equipping the veterinary team with practical tools to support successful weight management plans.
It explores how obesity alters physiology, complicates comorbidities, and reduces lifespan and how veterinarians and technicians can build effective partnerships with pet owners to reverse these effects. Using real cases, the course examines the steps to create individualized diet plans, tackle begging behavior, and overcome common barriers in multi-pet households. It benefits every member of the veterinary team by improving communication, increasing client compliance, and most importantly, enhancing patient outcomes.

courses.title: Global FAST Point of Care Ultrasound Pre-Lab Online Lectures
courses.description: The course covers AFAST and its image acquisition, its target-organ approach for obvious soft tissue abnormalities, and its abdominal fluid scoring system with case-based applications; TFAST and its image acquisition, its echocardiography views, its use for the accurate diagnosis of pleural and pericardial effusion and pneumothorax, its target-organ approach of the heart and pleural space for obvious soft-tissue abnormalities; and Vet BLUE and its image acquisition, its regional, pattern-based approach integrating its B-line scoring system, and 6 lung ultrasound signs. Global FAST is the term used when AFAST, TFAST and Vet BLUE are combined as a single ultrasound format used as an extension of the physical exam. The terms AFAST, TFAST, Vet BLUE and Global FAST are registered service marks for education purposes with the US Patent and Trademark Office to uphold each exam's highest degree of integrity as a standardized ultrasound exam.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Pain Management for Chronic Disease
courses.description: Chronic pain can be very difficult to control because the chronicity itself causes changes in the pain pathway that may not resolve with the use of common analgesics. Effective treatment of chronic pain often requires administration of both traditional and "nontraditional" analgesics along with nonpharmacologic techniques. The importance of the animal's "team" (caregiver or owner, technician, veterinarian, etc.) in pain identification and management is stressed.

courses.title: Ready Vet Go Mentorship Program
courses.description: The Ready, Vet, Go, Mentorship Program For New Veterinary Graduates My 6-Step System To Help You Feel More Confident, Become a Valued and Productive Member Of The Practice, And Take Better Care Of Yourself

courses.title: Introduction to Laboratory Medicine
courses.description: Introduction to Laboratory Medicine is a 6 CE credit program that focuses on the role of pathology in veterinary medicine and how this integrates with clinical practice. This program will provide an overview of the type of diagnostics performed in the reference laboratory and the in-hospital laboratory, and how these diagnostics are performed. This program will also cover sources of error, communication between the clinician, veterinary staff, and laboratory, as well as cytology and fluid sample preparation and handling and care of biopsy specimens.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Analgesia in Small Mammals: Case Studies for Pain Management
courses.description: As prey species, most small mammals are adept at hiding signs of illness or pain until late in the disease process. Additionally, they commonly present for surgery or procedures that necessitate analgesia. Therefore, identifying a painful small mammal is important in the management of many diseases. This course discusses updates on analgesia in small mammals focusing on medication selection and practical application. As analgesia is commonly included in procedures, this course also covers aspects of small mammal anesthesia or sedation.

courses.title: Radiology of the Emergency Abdomen
courses.description:
In emergency practice, rapid and accurate imaging is often the key to stabilising patients and guiding life-saving decisions. This three-lecture short course is designed specifically for veterinarians seeking to refine their approach to abdominal radiology in urgent clinical settings.Course Outline:
Topic 1: Imaging the Vomiting Patient
Vomiting is one of the most common and challenging presentations in small animal practice. This focused session explores the role of radiography and ultrasound in evaluating the vomiting patient, guiding you through a practical, case-based approach to diagnostic imaging. Learn how to identify key radiographic signs of obstruction, foreign bodies, and gastrointestinal disease, and how to apply abdominal ultrasound to differentiate causes and refine your diagnostic pathway. With tips on technique, interpretation, and avoiding common pitfalls, this lecture will equip you with the tools to make faster, more confident decisions when faced with the vomiting dog or cat.
Topic 2: Diagnosing Intestinal Foreign Bodies
Intestinal foreign bodies are a frequent cause of acute illness in small animals, and timely recognition is critical to successful outcomes. This lecture focuses on the radiographic diagnosis of intestinal obstruction in dogs and cats, highlighting both the classic and more subtle signs that indicate the presence of a foreign body. Through practical examples and case discussions, you will learn how to distinguish obstructive from non-obstructive patterns, recognise pitfalls that can lead to misinterpretation, and apply systematic radiographic evaluation techniques, giving you greater confidence in your diagnostic evaluation.
Topic 3: The Surgical Abdomen: To Cut or not to Cut
One of the most critical challenges in small animal emergency medicine is deciding whether a patient requires surgical intervention. This lecture explores how diagnostic imaging - particularly radiography and ultrasound - can be used to guide that decision-m

courses.title: Sonographic Approach to Urology Parts 1 & 2 - ANYTIME PROGRAM
courses.description: This anytime program will teach the attendee about the most frequently imaged organ system in small animal patients. Lower Part 1: Urinary apparatus - Lower urinary ultrasound. Urethral pathology - Urinary bladder - Cysto-urethral junction -Normal v. abnormal anatomy - Stones - Bladder Polyps - Cystitis/recurrent UTIs - TCC, etc. Upper Part 2: Renal anatomy - Kidney to adrenal efficiency clip - Medullary rim kidney - Polycystic kidney disease - Perirenal pseudocyst - Amyloid kidney - Congenital renal dysplasia - Pelvic dilation/Hydronephrosis.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Converging on Consensus - New Recommendations for Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prevention of Leptospirosis
courses.description: Leptospirosis is a zoonotic disease caused by the bacterial spirochete Leptospira. Despite the availability of vaccines, outbreaks continue to occur in unvaccinated dog populations in the United States. This course reviews the importance of understanding the difference between reservoir hosts and incidental hosts, how dogs can become infected, and clinical signs that alert to leptospirosis. In addition, it discusses how new diagnostic tests should be used and the best approaches to treatment and prevention of the disease. Important recommendations provided in the 2023 ACVIM updated consensus statement on leptospirosis will be discussed, including vaccination recommendations that impact the frequency of wellness visits for all dogs; and recommendations to reduce the risk of zoonotic transmission to owners, practice teams, and veterinarians.

courses.title: Using Global FAST Point of Care for Assessment of Dogs with Pulmonary Hypertension
courses.description: This webinar will discuss using point of care ultrasound for the helping in the early detection of Pulmonary Hypertension (PH, PHT, PAH). We will review recent literature including the ACVIM Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) Consensus Statement. This webinar includes cases studies covering imaging with TFAST echocardiography techniques, use of right sided cardiac TFAST markers, imaging for heartworms and saddle thrombus in the pulmonary arteries (PA), Vet BLUE lung ultrasound for the pulmonary profile including the Wedge Sign of pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) , and AFAST for ascites and its R-CHF markers. We discuss common disease conditions that cause pulmonary hypertension in dogs including heartworm disease and using TFAST for assessing heartworm burden plus surgical heartworm extraction. Participants will see examples and illustrations of imaging the Pulmonary Artery (PA) and its Right Main PA (RPA) and Left Main PA (LPA), assessing right ventricular free wall thickness to left ventricular free wall thickness, how to measure the PA size and the right PA distensibility index.

courses.title: Veterinary Dental Composite Restoration and Bonding Online Course
courses.description: In this training we will discuss what teeth can be repaired, indications for bonding vs restoration, when to offer a referral and when to extract, step-by-step video techniques to equip you to repair tooth fractures, and how to diagnose and repair teeth through multiple case examples.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: You've Gotta Be Kitten Me - Cats Get Orthopedic Disease Too?
courses.description: This course discusses the pertinent anatomy of the feline as it pertains to orthopedic disease. Common causes of thoracic and pelvic limb lameness in cats is presented along with associated treatment methods. Particular attention will be taken in discussing the treatment of feline osteoarthritis.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Taking the Mystery Out of the Diagnosis and Treatment of Soft Tissue Orthopedic Injuries in Dogs
courses.description: Soft tissue orthopedic injuries in dogs are challenging to diagnose and treat effectively. This course takes the mystery out of some of the most common muscle and tendon injuries seen in dogs. It provides practitioners and technicians with information to assist them in identifying these complicated cases. The diagnosis, treatment, and aftercare of calcanean tendon rupture, biceps tenosynovitis, supraspinatus tendon injuries, iliopsoas muscle injuries, and more are discussed

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Time to Tick-Talk
courses.description: This course provides a review of tick-borne diseases in dogs and cats with an emphasis on clinical diagnostic challenges and treatment options. Diseases include Anaplasmosis, Ehrlichiosis, Rickettsiosis, Borreliosis, Babesiosis, Cytauxzoonosis, and Hepatozoonosis.

courses.title: Feline Stomatitis
courses.description: Feline stomatitis is a fairly uncommon finding, making up only about 3% of oral conditions that affect felines. This condition presents as an inflammation of the oral mucosal tissues. The inflammation becomes progressively worse and causes increasing levels of pain. This course looks at the etiology and predisposition of this condition, along with symptoms, diagnostics, and current treatments.

courses.title: Feline Radiology: Your Guide to Diagnostic Imaging of the Cat
courses.description: In this video course, we'll take a deep dive into the 'inner workings' of cats, as we practice identification of pathology via radiography and ultrasound. Working from nose to tail, we'll begin with a step-by-step assessment of the feline thorax. Focusing on lung pathology. Then we'll move to the hepatobiliary system, pancreas, and GI tract. In each video, begin by learning Dr. Gaschen's systematic approach to evaluating radiographs and ultrasound, learning the most important landmarks and understanding normal anatomy. Then apply this step-by-step evaluation, as you review dozens of cases with Dr. Gaschen. Repetition and habit building are part of the central mission of this course. Head back to practice feeling more confident reading images immediately.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Mast Cell Tumors: Options for the Primary Veterinarian
courses.description: This course reviews mast cell disease which can be very challenging to treat. There are many new options available making it difficult to keep up with the current trends and to know what to do next. Pet owners have many questions and not all have the same goals for the treatment of their pet. This course focuses on what the primary veterinarian can do from understanding pathology reports and testing to treatments with injectable drugs like Stelfonta and surgery.
