It also reviews prognosis and survival time with the various types of mast cell tumors and treatment pursued.

courses.title: Advance25: Cardiac Ultrasound
courses.description: This online course is specifically designed for vets who want to advance their knowledge and understanding of key areas of cardiac ultrasound. Through recorded sessions, extensive notes and MCQs, you will learn from highly regarded cardiac specialists about how to confidently interpret, measure and optimise echocardiography images. You will also learn how to evaluate and diagnose a range of cardiac patients, from common presentations to the more unusual presentations like pericardial effusion, endocarditis and pulmonary hypertension. There will be a range of cases to review and diagnose helping with your own case management. You'll be able to utilise your new knowledge from day one of the course. You will also be able to enjoy unlimited access to your course materials for a full 12 months after the course has finished.

courses.title: Feline Dentistry Online Course
courses.description: This course will teach veterinarians and technicians how to diagnose and perform crown amputations, execute proper flap techniques, client communication regarding stomatitis, as well as many other questions students might have regarding topics of discussion within this on demand course.

courses.title: ESSENTIAL ANESTHETIC SAFETY FOR THE VETERINARY DENTAL PATIENT (588-35796)
courses.description: The focus of this presentation is learning to create balanced anesthetic protocols, when to use non-opiod analgesics. Anesthesia protocols in Geriatric Patient, Obese patient anesthesia, and Peri-anesthetic decision making and lastly managing Anesthetic Events.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Purrfectly Balanced: Navigating Feline Obesity & Wellness through Nutritional Care
courses.description: Despite the knowledge that unhealthy weight gain contributes to comorbid conditions along with reduced mobility, comfort, quality of life and lifespan, the prevalence of overweight cats continues to rise in the US. The complex nature of this problem can challenge the success of treatment plans. Taking an individualized approach to weight management by partnering with pet owners and engaging and empowering the whole team are keys to successful preventive actions as well as successful weight loss and maintenance. Individualized nutritional plans will not only improve the health of the patient but also the relationship and satisfaction of clients.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Fine-tuning Your Dentistry in General Practice
courses.description: This course discusses ways to practice better such as ergonomics, instrumentation, proper PEE, and how it contributes to better patient care. Patient positioning, prevention of tracheal tears in cats, safety limitations, and what we need to know when it comes to mouth gags is reviewed. The course also looks at normal clinical anatomy and radiographic anatomy to help identify findings that may be abnormal. Radiographic anatomy, using tools such as correct image orientation and the mounting or layout of the images, will help develop a systematic approach to tooth identification. Lastly, the course outlines how to identify basic instruments in dentistry, including the periodontal probe, explorer, and different ultrasonics as well as how to properly use them.

courses.title: Fear Free Handling: When to Pause, Pivot, and Reassess
courses.description: Learn how to recognize indicators that signal the need to pause or modify, how to differentiate between situations that require continuation, adjustment, or reassessment and how to apply strategies to pivot handling techniques to support reduced stress and patient safety.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Managing Atopic Dermatitis: Why Parasite Control Matters
courses.description: Allergic skin disease in dogs and cats consist of lifelong inflammatory diseases that require proactive management with a multimodal approach. One of the major flare factors for allergic dogs and cats is infestation by ectoparasites. Even when our patients do not have a classic flea allergy, low level infestation by fleas can cause a disease flare and reduce the efficacy of our treatments. Where fleas are not common other parasites are happy to take up the slack. This course looks at isoxazolines as a key management tool for allergic pets and explains how they improve outcomes for our patients.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Corneal Opacities in Dogs
courses.description: This course provides a brief review of the normal canine corneal anatomy and a broad overview of abnormalities that can occur. The focus will be on common canine diseases that can lead to corneal opacities. The section on non-ulcerative keratitis will describe and provide treatment plans for chronic superficial keratitis (pannus), immune-mediated keratitis, pigmentary keratopathies, corneal degeneration, and corneal dystrophy. The last component will be a brief overview of medical management for complicated corneal ulcers.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Diagnosis and Management of CKD in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: In geriatric populations at referral institutions, Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) affects as many as 10% of dogs and 35% of cats. Goals for treating and managing CKD include identifying CKD early in disease, slowing disease progression, and improving quality of life. This course discusses markers for detecting CKD early in dogs and cats, including how to stage and substage CKD according to IRIS guidelines. It also looks at treatment and management of both CKD and its comorbidities with the goal of preventing progression and improving patient quality of life.

courses.title: PATELLAR LUXATION CORRECTION: WET LAB (195-37676)
courses.description: This hands-on workshop is one part of a series of programs designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn, build and refine the knowledge and techniques necessary for safe and effective treatment of medial patellar luxation in small breeds of dogs. During the workshop attendees will perform the surgical approach, trochleoplasty, tibial crest transposition and soft tissue balancing techniques on canine cadavers under faculty supervision using a step-by-step high-resolution video demonstration.

courses.provider: AMERICAN VETERINARY SOCIETY OF ANIMAL BEHAVIOR
courses.title: The Clinical Animal Behavior Conference 2026 (Recorded)
courses.description: The Clinical Animal Behavior Conference is a 2.5-day intensive event dedicated to advancing the field of veterinary behavioral medicine. Centered on the theme Evolving Together: Advancing our Understanding of Behavior, this conference provides veterinary professionals with actionable, compassionate, and science-based strategies to elevate patient care and improve outcomes. Throughout the conference, attendees will learn to identify behavioral disorders, devise treatment plans which include behavior modifications, environmental changes, the use of constructional affection, enrichment and psychoactive medications. In addition, attendees will learn strategies such as fostering a team approach and using inclusive language to build trust and empathy among the health care team and with clients in order to achieve effective and consistent long term behavioral care for patients.

courses.title: (LIVE COURSE) Oncological Emergencies in the Dog and Cat
courses.description:
Cancer patients don't just present for diagnosis associated with chronic illness - they can also present in crisis. This two-week online course will equip you with the skills to both diagnose and manage the acute complications of neoplasia in dogs and cats. You will focus on true emergencies: acute haemorrhage from tumour rupture, life-threatening electrolyte imbalances like hypercalcemia, sepsis from treatment-related neutropaenia, anaphylaxis and tumour lysis syndrome.
You will learn how to prioritize interventions for the oncologic emergency patient, interpret lab results in the context of cancer, and understand when emergency surgery or critical care is the immediate priority over a definitive cancer diagnosis. Guided by current peer-reviewed literature, this course will transform your approach to the acutely deteriorating cancer patient.

courses.title: Implementing Kitten and Puppy Socialization Programs
courses.description:
Appropriate puppy and kitten socialization at the correct age will decrease the number of pets relinquished to shelters by helping to reduce the behaviors that are often the cause. Socialization will also help puppies and kittens become less stressed during visits to the practice. This course is designed to aid in the development of socialization classes within the practice environment.
Participants will be introduced to the stages of development of both puppies and kittens including when the socialization period for each species occurs as well as basics of training. Logistics of a class, identifying client needs, and exceeding client expectations are covered at length. The goals of a socialization class are highlighted with examples and resources provided to help practice teams succeed, starting with their first class.

courses.title: THE BROAD SCOPE OF ULTRASOUND & SAMPLING FOR IN-HOUSE DIAGNOSTIC EFFICIENCY (802-41659)
courses.description:
Explore the extent to which ultrasound and ultrasound-guided procedures can be applied to nearly every organ system for a fast, efficient and accurate diagnosis. Covering all abdominal and thoracic organ systems. Course Objectives:
FNA/Tru-cut biopsy sampling for in-house procedures. Areas of focus:
Urogenital system
Adrenal pathology
Pancreatitis
Gastrointestinal tract
Liver pathology and presentations
Orthopedic ultrasound diagnosis

courses.title: Internal Medicine Series With Dr. Remo Lobetti
courses.description: An internal medicine approach to the GI, pancreas, urinary tract, liver, and endocrine disorders.

courses.title: Managing the Red Eye - Conjunctival Disease or Something Else?
courses.description: This course reviews the most common causes of a red eye in dogs and cats along with a general treatment overview. It will help participants recognize signs of conjunctival inflammation and how to sort through the many underlying causes. In addition, it explains how cats differ from dogs in causes of conjunctivitis. Lastly it will explain the use of diagnostic tests to help focus differentials.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Do You Speak Cat? Feline Communication for the Veterinary Team
courses.description:
Veterinary team members often express doubt about handling cats. The best way to know a cat's emotional state and whether they are relaxed enough to cope with the stress of veterinary procedures is to watch their body language.
This course explores how cats communicate with us and how to determine when they are fearful, stressed, anxious, or happy. This is the first step to Fear-Free and Feline Friendly handling.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: The Science of Medical Massage and Why It Belongs in Your Practice
courses.description: This course looks at the scientific basis of medical massage and reasons why it belongs in your practice. In contrast to other forms of massage, medical massage focuses on problems related to a patient's diagnosis and implements techniques to achieve specific outcomes. It complements conventional medical care by reducing stress, pain, and discomfort as well as facilitating the healing process through neuromodulation, myofascial relaxation, and improved circulation. Techniques draw from a variety of professions and philosophies, including osteopathic manual therapy. Clinical applications discussed in this presentation include approaches for post-surgical recovery, especially for orthopedic cases, as well as in critical care medicine, neurologic injury, geriatric care, palliative medicine, and more.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Emergency Triage of the Poisoned Patient: History Taking and Initial Diagnostics
courses.description: This course offers guidance on complete and thorough history taking for a poisoned patient, including a focus on what information is key to obtaining an appropriate risk assessment for a particular toxin. Common toxins will be reviewed, including fast-acting and potentially life-threatening exposures as well as "good" toxins that are of minor toxicologic concern and may be taken care of by telephone triage only. A brief overview of initial diagnostic options for a poisoned patient will be presented.

courses.title: Unlocking Comparative Cardiology: A Definitive Collection on Precision Quantification, Advanced Imaging, and Revolutionary In
courses.description:
** The sessions in this course were previously approved for AAVSB RACE CE credit as an in person course, # 20-1308763. The were recorded and will now be used in an OnDemand course shown below.
Description:
This essential five-source collection offers an in-depth, cross-species analysis of echocardiography, tackling challenges from normalizing heart size in animals spanning a "ten-thousandfold difference" (mouse to horse) to implementing cutting-edge transcatheter repairs. It synthesizes core techniques, comparative anatomy, and pioneering research, making it vital for anyone interested in advanced cardiac imaging.
Sessions include: (originally recorded during ASE 2025 Scientific Sessions).
Transesophageal Echocardiography in Pet Dogs Undergoing Mitral Valve TEER
Human-Veterinary Challenge: Stump the Experts
A Ten-Thousandfold Difference: Indexing the Left Ventricle from Mouse to Human to Horse
Veterinary Abstract Showcase
Comparative Aspects of Human and Veterinary Transthoracic Echocardiography
Learning Objectives:
Analyze the methods for indexing cardiac dimensions across diverse mammalian species
Compare and contrast fundamental anatomical and technical differences between human and veterinary transthoracic echocardiography.
Evaluate the utility of advanced imaging and quantification techniques employed to improve diagnostic accuracy and reproducibility in veterinary patients
Describe the procedural requirements and anatomical criteria for Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair (TEER) in dogs with Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease (MMVD)

courses.title: Chronic Otitis Externa: Strategies for Better Care
courses.description: Otitis externa is very common in dogs, and it is the dermatologic disease for which we are least effective, particularly when it becomes chronic. Often dogs with chronic or recurrent otitis are treated without cytology, without rechecks, without finding the underlying cause, and without establishing a proactive preventive care program to reduce relapses. Over time, many of these dogs will end up with incredibly resistant infections, stenosis, proliferative changes, and constant pain, requiring a total ear canal ablation. By this time, the owners are financially and emotionally tapped out, and their dogs suffer. This course discusses an approach to chronic or recurrent otitis that is meant to help prevent progression to the end stage ear.

courses.title: Current Concepts in Veterinary Periodontal Disease Management
courses.description: This 3-hour continuing education course explores current diagnostic and treatment protocols for periodontal disease in companion animals. Participants will learn how to apply essential periodontal techniques including closed root planing, open root planing, bone grafting, guided tissue regeneration, and flap surgery. This program will also examine key case studies, indications for therapy, and integration of appropriate periodontal therapies in general practice.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Triaging the Sick Neonatal Foal
courses.description: So, your client's mare delivered a live, apparently healthy, foal several days ago and now the newborn is deteriorating? This course focuses on the most common causes of illness in foals in the first few days of life, including sepsis, diarrhea, and more. It reviews risk factors, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and treatment for these conditions, focusing on key takeaways, including when to refer and what to do before sending the pair on their way to the hospital. Prompt intervention can greatly impact survival in critically ill foals and this course will help you to prepare to identify and triage the most likely causes of disease in equine neonates.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: The Physiology of Pain
courses.description: Pain signals travel along a certain path on their way up to the brain. By understanding this pathway, we can treat pain more effectively by augmenting the pain signal within the nervous system. This course focuses on what pain is, how bodies react to painful stimuli, and what can be done to mitigate it.

courses.title: Panel Discussion: Work-Life Balance in Equine Practice
courses.description:
Adapt or die. Do you worry about the future of Equine Practice? Why have we had no applications for our vacancy? Where have all the experienced equine vets gone? What should we do to find and retain enthusiastic vets? Can you have a work life balance in equine practice or is that an oxymoron? Can we break the mould and find new ways of working?
What can we learn from the millennials? What will practice look like in 10 years' time? The panel of experienced English equine practitioners will try to find answers to some of the difficult issues facing equine practice today. Bringing together many years of experience, they represent a broad spectrum of the equine veterinary profession - from the traditional practice to corporate ownership and also a 24/7 out-of-hours on-call service provider.

courses.title: SONOGRAPHIC APPROACH TO THE SPLEEN
courses.description: Anytime program. When is a spleen normal and what does it mean when it is not A comprehensive presentation of normal splenic parameters and every splenic pathology in cats and dogs, guidelines for imaging for a full evaluation, sampling, and review of every type of lesion, mass, disease process with illustrative imaging, and case studies, what are your differentials.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Instagram 101: How to Easily Start & Manage an Instagram Account for Your Clinic
courses.description: Are you ready to start an Instagram account for your clinic but have been intimidated by learning a new social media platform? This course provides an overview on using and navigating Instagram. It shares the difference between Facebook and Instagram, what to post to Instagram, and provides an action plan so you can launch your Instagram account asap.

courses.provider: NVA OVERLAND PARK VETERINRY EMERGENCY AND SPECIALTY
courses.title: Vestibular Disease in the Dog
courses.description:
The goal of this presentation is to help learn how to recognize which patients have vestibular disease.
Another main objective is to learn how to differentiate between peripheral and central vestibular disease based off a neurologic examination.
Another objective is following being able to provide a list of differentials causes based off the history and examination findings.
Length of Session: 1 hour
Presenter: Dr. David Weinstein, DMV, DACVIM (Neurology)

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Common Drug Interactions in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Knowing common drug interactions associated with medications given in veterinary medicine is an important component in caring for patients to ensure they have the longest, healthiest life possible. This course discusses the specifics behind drug interactions in veterinary medicine and how these interactions can be identified before they become detrimental to patients. It also looks at specific mediations and mechanisms that cause drug interactions and ways to communicate these interactions to clients.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: A Tale Of Three Tails - Abnormal Repetitive Behaviors In Dogs
courses.description: Abnormal repetitive behaviors (ARB) in animals encompass a diverse group activities characterized as repetitive, exaggerated, sustained, out of context, and without apparent function. In dogs common examples include spinning or tail chasing, light or shadow chasing, fly snapping, flank sucking, or self-injurious licking. Etiology is unclear but medical conditions and sources of distress should always be assessed. Common differentials and treatment plans, including management, medications, and behavior modification for common canine repetitive behaviors will be discussed.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Wellness in the Workplace
courses.description: This course shares the story of Dr. Becky's burnout and how she healed her way back to be the doctor, wife, mom, and leader she now is today. Her presentation focuses on what worked for her and how she has implemented these tools into her daily life as well as her business.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: It's Not Always in Their Heads - Identifying Red Flags for Physical Disease in the Behavior History
courses.description: A significant proportion of pets referred to veterinary behavior practices have an underlying physical disease either causing or contributing to their clinical signs. In most cases, once those physical illnesses are treated the behavior concerns resolve or improve significantly. Recognizing red flags for physical disease in the behavior history, and developing a complete differential diagnosis list, allows veterinarians to arrive at the correct diagnosis and implement the most appropriate treatment.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: How Old is Too Old? Anesthesia for the Geriatric Patient
courses.description: While anesthesia is never a one-size-fits-all procedure, it requires special considerations for geriatric patients. Veterinarians and their medical teams need to address the unique physiological changes and considerations in older animals. Anesthetic plans must be tailored to individual needs. Thorough history taking and physical examination coupled with pre-anesthetic assessments and risk stratification is crucial. Focusing on pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics in older patients, with specific protocols for those with concurrent diseases, is vital. The importance of intraoperative monitoring, pain management, and post-anesthetic care to ensure optimal recovery cannot be over emphasized.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: A New Way to See an Old Disease - Updates on Canine and Feline Osteoarthritis
courses.description: Osteoarthritis is not a new disease, but there are a lot of new concepts to consider in the identification, diagnosis and management of OA. This course reviews the latest information regarding OA prevalence in dogs and cats, providing tips on how to recognize and diagnose OA and OA pain as early as possible. It also addresses how to engage the entire veterinary healthcare team, including the caregiver, in the management of OA, via developing an effective plan of care.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Recruitment and Retention - Neurodiverse Individuals are Valuable Members of the Veterinary Team
courses.description: Is your practice missing an opportunity to attract and retain highly motivated and qualified people who may have some kind of disability, such as being neurodiverse? Considering that the average cost of accommodating an individual is less than $500 and the average cost per hire is $4,700, accommodating individuals is an opportunity to attract and retain dedicated talent.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Inclusive Leadership - Integrating Chronically Ill and Handicapped Professionals in Veterinary Practices
courses.description: It is important to create a supportive and inclusive environment for chronically ill and handicapped team members. This course discusses common challenges faced by these individuals in the industry and provides best practices for inclusion and integration. It includes real-life examples of successful inclusion and the impact it can have on individuals and practices. The goal is to increase awareness of the benefits of a diverse and inclusive team and to encourage veterinary professionals to adopt these practices in their own workplaces.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Euthanasia Without Pain: It Can Be Done
courses.description: Pain and euthanasia don't mix. The very definition of euthanasia includes pain-free at its core. Pain may sometimes find its way in but doing everything we can to prevent it is job #1. Ask clients what's important to them and they'll say their pet pain-free in the final moments. Vets say the same. This course lays the foundation for a pain-free passing each and every time. Special focus given to dogs and cats, though subthemes will emerge for all species. Let' say "goodbye" to pain during death.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: I Feel Your Pain: How Empathic Communication and the Human Perception of Pain Influence Our Animal Patients
courses.description: Pain is an incredibly subjective and personal experience in humans. Perception of pain is influenced by numerous factors, including age, socioeconomic status, gender, race, and more. Animal pain may be subjectively affected by these human factors, for better or worse, from standpoints of both the owners/guardians and the treating veterinarians. As we strive to determine levels of pain and appropriate treatment for our patients, we can consider these additional influences and better modulate our client communication for compliance and satisfaction. Empathic listening and understanding human perceptions of pain may improve care and compliance for our clients, our colleagues, and especially our animal patients

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Phytocannabinoids and Pain Management:
courses.description: This course discusses the basics of the endocannabinoid system and the pharmacology/pharmacokinetics of CBD. It reviews the published clinical studies that relate to the use of CBD as a pain management tool. In addition, it examines the potential of other phytocannabinoids as pain management tools and briefly discusses the human experience of using CBD to manage pain, based on the published literature.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Digital Cytology - The Past, Present, & Future of this Innovative Diagnostic Service
courses.description: This course provides participants with a robust overview of digital cytology aimed at enabling an understanding of the factors of this innovative diagnostic solution. It will cover terminology, equipment, and modalities alongside real cases that will help create successful discussions with colleagues and providers about digital cytology. The course includes digital slides to demonstrate what to expect with current technology. The end goal is to help practices successfully adopt the valuable diagnostic service for the benefit of patients.

courses.title: Emergency Euthanasias: Getting it right when time is tight (Recording)
courses.description: You have 10 minutes to provide a perfect euthanasia experience for patient and client. Can it be done? You bet it can. Being tight on time can still lead to beautiful, smooth euthanasias. It's all about leveraging the essential components and picking the right euthanasia technique. Recent studies show clients report poor satisfaction with emergency euthanasias compared to general practice. A fast euthanasia can equal a great one if we put in the effort. This session will outline what must be included and what can be left out, ensuring everyone has the experience they are hoping for.

courses.title: Updates on Common Toxicology Topics
courses.description: This course offers guidance on current topics in toxicology, including a focus on advances in understanding grape and raisin toxicosis in dogs, the emergency of different mushroom types in "magic mushroom" products, decontamination considerations with activated charcoal and chocolate, and considerations with fluid diuresis recommendations and intravenous lipid therapies. Up to date information about these topics will be discussed and treatment of toxin ingestions will be reviewed.

courses.title: Effective Topical Therapy for Your Atopic Patients: Why It Matters
courses.description: Managing a disease as complicated as atopic dermatitis and feline atopic skin syndrome can be difficult. These are life-long diseases that progress over time and there is no one way to manage them. Topical therapy has been underutilized in the management of these diseases. This course discusses the skin barrier and how its malfunction contributes to disease, how to choose effective shampoos, how to use mousses and sprays effectively, and how to select and use skin barrier repair spot-ons to improve outcomes.

courses.title: Advance25: GP Refresh - Medicine
courses.description: This online course is specifically designed for vets who want to refresh and update their knowledge and understanding of some key areas of first opinion small animal medicine. Through recorded sessions, extensive notes and MCQs, you will learn from a highly regarded internal medicine specialist about new developments in the field, and how this relates to your own case management. We'll use a logical problem solving approach to each case, interpret the results of diagnostic tests and determine optimal management strategies based on current best evidence. You'll be able to utilise your new knowledge from day one of the course. You will also be able to enjoy unlimited access to your course materials for a full 12 months after the course has finished.

courses.title: Regenerative Medicine Applications for Bacterial Infections and Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: Regenerative medicine is gaining popularity in small animal medicine for a variety of applications due to extensive research documenting the success of biologic therapies for a multitude of conditions. This treatment modality is most well-known for its use in osteoarthritis where it promotes downregulation of inflammation and regeneration of cartilage. However, there are multiple promising applications for other conditions such as multidrug resistant infections and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). This course looks at the variety of stem cell products used in research and clinical applications focusing on providing an increased understanding of what products are available and how to decide which products to choose. The use of cellular therapies in bacterial and viral infections as well as use in IBD will be discussed including the evidence supporting their use. The pathophysiology of these conditions will be discussed in light of how regenerative medical products can effect a cure or remission. This goal of this course is to help the practitioner make evidence-based decisions on the product and application of this promising novel therapy.

courses.title: Feline Chronic Gingivostomatitis Online Course
courses.description: Designed for veterinary professionals eager to stay abreast of the latest in FCGS management or those questioning their current treatment strategies, this course is crucial. Participants often find themselves uncertain about choosing the most effective treatments for their feline patients suffering from this painful condition. This course, featuring Dr Brett Beckman, aims to bridge that knowledge gap by introducing cutting edge insights and techniques for managing FCGS. Through detailed instructional videos, Dr. Beckman guides participants through the complexities of FCGS, from diagnosis to advanced treatment options, ensuring veterinarians and veterinary technicians can confidently apply modern pain management strategies tailored to the unique needs of cats with chronic gingivostomatitis. This online course not only demystifies the condition but also empowers veterinary professionals with the skills and knowledge to enhance the quality of life for their feline patients through effective pain management and treatment approaches.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Common Arrhythmias
courses.description: This practical, case-based course will help veterinarians confidently use the ECG in everyday canine and feline practice. It covers when to perform an ECG, how to obtain high-quality tracings, and how to identify common arrhythmias and conduction abnormalities. ECG waveforms, measurements, and mean electrical axis are reviewed with a focus on clinical relevance, including how findings guide diagnosis and treatment decisions. The course concludes with real ECG examples to reinforce rhythm recognition and interpretation skills.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Pharma MythBusters ECC Edition
courses.description: Do we still need to use heparin to flush peripheral IV catheters? Should we still stock doxapram in the neonatal resuscitation kit? What about administering steroids or pain medications to emergency patients? This course addresses these emergency and critical care pharmacological questions along with evidence to support recommendations.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Feline Nutrition - Special Features for Special Creatures
courses.description: The adage that cats are not small dogs is especially true when it comes to nutrition. As obligate carnivores, cats have different nutritional requirements than the omnivorous canine. Their anatomy, physiology, and behavior have all evolved around eating small prey. But what does this mean to us as clinicians? How, how often, how much to feed as well as what to feed is important for feline welfare. This presentation will include how, by using a nutritional assessment in every consultation, existing feeding practices can be assessed and, if needed, a tailored nutrition plan can be developed for a given individual.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Is That Veterinary Diet Really Too Expensive? Effective Cost Conversations
courses.description: Cost conversations regarding veterinary diets, especially those used as part of treatment plans for medical conditions, are a mainstay of client interactions for veterinary professionals. A quick internet search provides a glimpse into the misinformation surrounding the cost of veterinary diets. Unfortunately, this type of misinformation can make conversations regarding cost more challenging for veterinary professionals and prior research in companion animal hospitals has revealed that cost conversations were uncommon during appointments. Like any conversation regarding the cost of veterinary services or products, customizing the conversation to the individual pet is critical, by focusing on the value to the pet. To facilitate the ease of cost conversations, veterinary teams can be trained to utilize existing resources to have cost conversations and to apply these learnings to common scenarios in small animal veterinary practice, including elimination diet trials and effective weight loss plans.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Small Ruminants 101 for Small Animal Practitioners
courses.description: This course discusses basic small ruminant medicine, herd management, and case work up. Emphasis will be on the individual or small herd/flocks that may present to small animal practitioners. Legal drug use will also be discussed. Collection of diagnostic samples with videos will be shown.

courses.title: An Introduction to Computed Tomography for the General Practitioner-Evaluating the Head
courses.description: In this program, students will learn the advantages CT has over radiography in evaluating canine and feline diseases of the head. Proper technique will be reviewed, covering patient positioning and technique parameters that will maximize diagnostic yield. Finally, cases commonly encountered in general practice will be used to introduce normal anatomy, interpretation strategies, and the appearance of disease on CT images. Focus will be given to equipping you with the knowledge to successfully integrate CT in your small animal veterinary practice-onsite or offsite and illustrate how CT offers a more satisfactory alternative to investigate many everyday conditions in the head.

courses.title: Igniting Your Veterinary Career
courses.description: Want to know the secret to a long and successful career in Veterinary Medicine? It is not working 80 hours a week nor is it giving up your family and friends for your career. Train your mindset and use emotional intelligence to navigate your career. Inoculate yourself against some of the stresses that affect so many. No matter your role in the practice, or how long you have been in veterinary medicine, this course can help you learn key leadership skills that benefit you, your team, and the practice

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Pancreatitis
courses.description: Pancreatitis can be managed through focus on key nutritional factors and diligent owner compliance. The healthcare team's role in managing pancreatitis is crucial, beginning with proper identification of pancreatitis vs. other vomiting and diarrheic conditions. This course focuses on the healthcare team's role in identifying and managing pancreatitis and the key nutritional factors responsible for minimizing signs and symptoms associated with pancreatitis.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Intraoperative Fluid Therapy and the Hypotension Algorithm
courses.description: Fluid administration in human and veterinary patients warrants constant re-evaluation. Fluid therapy is not benign. Determining the right amount and type are key to successful patient outcomes. We've been told to hold back on fluid rates and total doses administered perioperatively in the past 10 or so years. However, the pendulum may have swung a bit too much in the other direction. Fluid therapy must always be based on patient exam and evaluation. Ways to treat hypotension need to be discussed preoperatively to help avoid fluid overload.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Analgesia - Opioids and their Alternatives
courses.description: This course provides an overview of current systemic pain management drugs, including opioids and a selection of non-opioid analgesics.

courses.title: VetCE On Demand: Powerful Client Communication through Social Media
courses.description:
Client communication is more vital than ever before but also more restricted than ever. Sharing positive news and ideas is challenging right now. Where do you begin? How do you have great communication with clients when face to face dialogue is not possible for so many? This is a great opportunity to use your practice social media platforms to communicate with clients.
Practice teams are facing stressors from every direction and so are clients. The practice that shares their day-to-day news, setbacks, and expectations can build connections with their clients. Lift the veil and help your clients view you in a new way on social media. Help reduce negative reviews that come from frustration and misunderstandings by building relationships. Let us look at some easy ways to bring the clients into the fold of your practice culture.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Anesthesia Safety - Checklists and Troubleshooting the Anesthetized Patient
courses.description: This course outlines basic anesthesia safety including the use of checklists to help prevent problems as well as troubleshooting algorithms to quickly recognize and safely treat problems in the anesthetized patient. It offers a brief review of checklist development and implementation, particularly surgical safety and anesthesia machine checklists. The course also includes discussion of peri-anesthetic troubleshooting and a logical safe approach to managing common anesthesia problems.

courses.title: Emergency Training for the Non-Emergency Clinic: Interviewing Your Team to Play Their Best Part
courses.description: Emergency patients can happen at any time in any type of clinic. The team needs to be prepared to handle whatever comes through the door. Have you ever asked the team how comfortable they are with handling those critical patients and hysterical owners? This course provides some interview questions to ask your team to help them learn what parts they like to play in emergency medicine so to work towards successful patient outcomes. It also discusses two different training styles, written and role playing, and how to use each one to benefit and train the team. Participants will come away with ideas for document creation and how to plan a real-life emergency practice with your team.

courses.title: SONOGRAPHIC ADRENAL PATHOLOGY (802-43044)
courses.description: With this online anytime program you will gain a better understanding of when adrenal changes are clinically pertinent from a clinical & sonographic perspective. Learn when sonographic changes are simply age-related and have no bearing on case work-up.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Needles and Nociception - How Acupuncture Helps Modulate Pain
courses.description: This course briefly reviews pain pathways and nociception to form the foundation for theories of how acupuncture, and associated modalities, may modulate pain. A history of acupuncture and the Five-Element Theory are introduced to outline an Eastern approach. It will compare individual case management vs. a broader-based Western treatment approach. Bi Syndromes and additional modalities, such as aquapuncture, electrostimulation, moxibustion, etc., are included to provide a more complete picture of acupuncture and pain management. Rescue points, acupuncture and anesthesia, contraindications, as well as how to get started with acupuncture are addressed.

courses.title: FVMA's On-Demand 2025
courses.description: FVMA's On-Demand 2025 offers continuing education for veterinarians and veterinary technicians through on-line lecture sessions, complete with quiz questions and answers, for the attainment of required continuing education. Lectures include a wide range of topics.

courses.title: Feline Anesthesia: Renal Disease
courses.description: Cats needing anesthesia often present with pre-existing disease. In the case of chronic renal disease, it is important to understand the basic pathophysiology and interplay with the effects of anesthesia and anesthesia drugs. Properly applied, this knowledge helps to avoid worsening of already compromised renal function and maximizes positive outcome. This course will discuss the basic approach to take when dealing with the patient with chronic renal disease in need of general anesthesia.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Unlocking the Power of Genetic Testing To Revolutionize Detection of Feline Disease
courses.description: Decoding a feline patient's DNA is another step in the pursuit of better medicine and optimal quality of life. It offers a way to identify health risks early so detection doesn't come too late. This course reviews the process of genetic testing, how to incorporate genetic testing in practice, and how to prepare caregivers with a plan when mutations are detected.

courses.title: Dental Nerve Blocks for Zen Anesthesia
courses.description: This course explores the different site and drug choices needed to perform safe dental nerve blocks in dogs and cats by identifying risk factors, adverse effects, and contraindications. It will familiarize attendees with anatomy of the dog and cat skull with regard to innervation of the face and jaw. It also defines the indications for nerve blocks and appropriate site choices with evidence-based references for good decision making. The ultimate goal is to provide multimodal pain relief and balanced anesthesia for dental procedures.

courses.title: Advance25: Complex Medicine 2
courses.description: This online course is specifically designed for vets who want to advance their knowledge and understanding on complex and often frustrating medical conditions, from challenging pyrexic cases to interpretation of confusing endocrine test. There will also be interesting discussions on topic issues including Brucella, alongside haematology, endocrinology, hepatobiliary disease and gastroenterology. This course is for you if you are an Advanced Practitioner or you're at that level, and if you want to broaden and deepen your knowledge in a variety of essential small animal medicine topics. You will also be able to enjoy unlimited access to your course materials for a full 12 months after the course has finished.

courses.title: Communication That Connects: Internally Aligned, Externally Respected
courses.description: Strengthen team collaboration and enhance client satisfaction through effective applied communication. Content includes communication frameworks, team meeting strategy, emotional intelligence, and client conversation models.

courses.title: Senior Dog Veterinary Certification Level 2
courses.description: This multisession program focuses on the fundamentals of senior and geriatric canine medicine within specialized topics including anesthesia and surgery, evaluating the healthy senior dog patient, diagnostic recommendations for senior dogs, and chronic pain management. Establishing foundations in these areas of senior dog medicine will enhance the ability of veterinary practitioners in meeting the unique needs of their elderly canine patients.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Oral Assessment of the Dental Patient Under Anesthesia
courses.description: The oral exam of veterinary patients under anesthesia entails a tooth-by-tooth evaluation. The team member must be familiar with the oral cavity's structures in order to perform an effective oral exam. The use of diagnostic instruments such as the periodontal probe to find periodontal pockets, gingival bleeding, and furcation involvement, along with the dental explorer to find pulp exposure and tooth resorption, are addressed. Also included is a basic dental charting technique which shows how the examination findings, combined with dental radiographs, are recorded on a dental chart that guides the clinician.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Dental Radiology Made Easy- Tips and Tricks for Great Rads
courses.description: This is a 24/7/365 open-enrollment self-study distance course. Dental radiographs are an essential part of the oral exam. The crown is just the tip of the iceberg. Approximately 42% of dental pathology is found subgingivally. Radiographs will help diagnose pathology that is not visible from the surface and confirm suspect pathology as well as help demonstrate the pathology to the client. Dental radiographs can improve the standard of care in your practice and increase your clinic's revenue. This course will share methods to make taking dental radiographs a dream.

courses.title: Exploring Nonclinical Career Pathways in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: In today's rapidly evolving landscape of veterinary medicine, non-clinical career avenues have gained unprecedented significance. This program is designed to guide veterinary professionals - both veterinarians and veterinary technicians - through the transition from clinical to non-clinical roles. Attendees will explore diverse opportunities in industries such as pharmaceuticals, research, academia, government, animal health companies, veterinary journalism, medical writing, and consulting. The session will cover essential strategies for identifying interests and strengths, building a strong foundation, navigating the job search and application process, excelling in interviews, and overcoming common challenges. By leveraging their expertise, veterinary professionals can successfully transition into roles that offer personal growth, professional fulfillment, and improved work-life balance. Join us to unlock new potential in your veterinary career and contribute to innovative solutions in animal health.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: It's More Than Missing Teeth: Recognizing Dental and Oral Abnormalities
courses.description: Take your dental charting to the next level. It is important to recognize both normal anatomy and abnormal dental and oral pathology. Oral pathology is often misdiagnosed and underdiagnosed due to lack of recognition. Once one can recognize what is abnormal in the mouth, correct charting may be completed. The proper treatment options for commonly seen pathology are discussed and described. Abbreviations according to the American Veterinary Dental College (AVDC) are used for commonly seen pathology and are discussed.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Battling the Bulge - Strategies for Managing Obesity in Veterinary Patients
courses.description: This course reviews current statistics of obesity in dogs and cats including prevalence, contributing factors, and comorbidities. It examines the endocrine and inflammatory components of obesity, as well as how to use tools to diagnose obesity. It also explains how to estimate ideal body weight, calculate RER and amount to feed to achieve ideal weight, important factors in weight loss diets, how to choose the right food, and how to prevent obesity in the first place. Lastly, the course outlines a 6 step process to easily guide your clients through a successful weight loss program.

courses.title: 2026 AAVA On Demand Annual Meeting
courses.description: The objective of the 2026 AAVA On Demand Annual Meeting is to provide top quality continuing education which advances the knowledge and skills of veterinarians in the areas of acupuncture, acupuncture related and East-Asian medical therapy including Chinese herbal medicine, TCVM Master Points and TCVM Review. Continuing education is provided through lectures led by presenters known as experts in veterinary acupuncture medicine. Sessions include Small/Large Animal, TCVM, Exotics, Herbal Medicine and Cardiology.

courses.title: VetCE On Demand: Beyond De-Escalation - Connecting with Calmness
courses.description: Talking with upset clients and stressed colleagues can feel like tiptoeing through a minefield. This presentation will help you learn how to be more effective and more relaxed when speaking with clients and colleagues who are experiencing strong emotions such as stress, frustration, anxiety, or anger. It reviews a theoretical framework for building trust and establishing rapport, and practice techniques to help others release their "emotional charge" to the point of being able to collaborate with you on solving the problem at hand, while strengthening your relationship.

courses.title: SONOGRAPHIC APPROACH TO THE PANCREAS (802-42351)
courses.description:
With this online anytime course, the attendee will learn about the basic pancreatic gross anatomy and how it relates to the adjacent organ systems in position and function from the sonographic perspective. Changes to this structure in the midst of pathological processes will be demonstrated.
Course Objectives:
Pancreatitis in dogs and cats along with expectations regarding sensitivities and specificities with current serum testing (amylase, lipase, PLI)
Degenerative pathologies such as fibrosis, amyloid deposition, and nodular hyperplasia compared to neoplastic patterns
Sampling the pancreas from an ultrasound-guided process
Medical and surgical approaches to pathologies will also be discussed.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Crash, Boom, Bang! Protocols for Dogs with Sound Sensitivity
courses.description: It is estimated that anywhere from one-third to two-thirds of dogs have noise aversion. Out of 12 dogs, 4 to 8 are likely to develop noise sensitivities in their lifetime. Not only can a fear of sounds be physiologically and emotionally damaging for dogs, but it can also strain the human-animal relationship. This course helps provide strategies for how to approach and prevent sound sensitivities, including teaching desired coping skills.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: PsyMed: The Science Linking Psychological Stress and Medical Symptoms
courses.description: It is well known that certain behavioral signs can identify chronic psychological stress that eventually may affect medical symptoms. This field is known as "PsyMed." This course examines why identifying these behaviors is more effective than measuring cortisol. It looks into stress-induced cell adhesion molecule disruption and introduces the "PsyMed Hypothesis" as the connection between pet behavioral health and enjoyable longevity.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: When Quality of Life Scales Aren't Enough; Counseling Clients Who Won't Let Go
courses.description: Choosing to end the life of a beloved and loyal companion is a responsibility that many people are unable to bear. This makes it particularly challenging to navigate conversations surrounding decision making for euthanasia. Dr. Cooney, an animal hospice veterinarian, outline ways to handle these difficult discussions, demonstrating leading with compassion and empathy, while still advocating for patients to prevent unnecessary suffering. It shares utilizing some leading questions and supportive statements to create an open and honest dialogue, to allow these clients to say goodbye without fear and regret but with grace and dignity.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Ethical Criteria Indicating Euthanasia in Canine Aggression
courses.description:
The stress and guilt related to performing euthanasia is recognized as one factor in the rising rate of veterinary suicide. One way to reduce this factor is if the veterinarian is not personally responsible for the decision but instead is following a consensus protocol.
Without objective and science-based guidelines, there are likely animals being euthanized inappropriately. Canine Aggression is the one of the most common reasons for behavior euthanasia. This course outlines guidelines for euthanasia related to Canine Aggression. It reviews aggression diagnosis as well as a step-by-step process for making a behavior euthanasia decision.

courses.title: TIBIAL PLATEAU-LEVELING OSTEOTOMY: WET LAB (195-36639)
courses.description: This hands-on workshop is one part of a series of programs designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn/refine the tibial plateau-leveling osteotomy technique and to understand the major advantages of PAX Polyaxial Locking TPLO Plate System. Participants will perform the TPLO technique on bone models and canine cadavers under faculty supervision. This lab is only for veterinarians who already have a thorough knowledge of the relevant stifle anatomy, extensive stifle surgery experience, and prior training in bone plating techniques and principles.

courses.title: A CLINICIANS GUIDE TO INCORPORATING RABBITS INTO YOUR PRACTICE
courses.description:
This online course provides an intensive lecture on a wide array of medicine, surgery, commonly performed techniques and procedures in rabbits. It covers aspects of how to set up your practice, rabbit anatomy, husbandry, handling, clinical techniques, common diseases, diagnostic imaging, therapeutics, anesthesia, medicine, and surgery, among other important topics.
The course is aimed at veterinarians and veterinary paraprofessionals (technician, assistant, nurse), as well as respective students with a keen interest in rabbit medicine and surgery.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Workforce Crisis- Retaining Staff
courses.description: The veterinary industry is facing a workforce crisis. Retaining and growing staff has never been more important. Employees are our most valuable assets, but do they know this? With the Great Resignation upon us, now is the time to change our focus to retention and talent management. If you don't help them grow, you will watch them go.

courses.title: Urine Trouble: Lower Urinary Tract Disorders of Cats
courses.description: This 1-hour on-demand video will review the latest research and provide novel concepts and recommendations for managing feline lower urinary tract disease (FLUTD). This course will challenge you to rethink your rationale in diagnosing, treating, and preventing lower urinary tract disease in cats.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Canine Otitis Externa- Proper Work Up for This Ear-Y Occurrence
courses.description: This course discusses the proper evaluation of Canine Otitis Externa cases from the examination, slide preparations, and microscopic observations for proper diagnosis followed by common treatments for both short-term and long-term conditions.

courses.title: Orthopedic vs Neurologic Disease: Which is it?
courses.description: Various orthopedic conditions may be confused for neurologic dysfunction. To aid the practitioner in identifying these conditions and to rule out neurologic causes, this course first provides an overview of performing and interpreting a neurologic examination. Then, notable orthopedic conditions that may be considered "neurologic imposters" are covered, with description of the causes and examination findings associated with these conditions.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Feline-Focused Anesthesia & Analgesia
courses.description: The phrase "cats are not small dogs" is true in almost all aspects. This course outline specific approaches for anesthesia and for control of acute pain in cats.

courses.title: PATELLAR LUXATION CORRECTION: WET LAB (195-37676)
courses.description: This hands-on workshop is one part of a series of programs designed for the veterinarian who wishes to learn, build and refine the knowledge and techniques necessary for safe and effective treatment of medial patellar luxation in small breeds of dogs. During the workshop attendees will perform the surgical approach, trochleoplasty, tibial crest transposition and soft tissue balancing techniques on canine cadavers under faculty supervision using a step-by-step high-resolution video demonstration.

courses.title: Avian Anesthesia Basics
courses.description: Veterinarians and technicians will benefit from demystifying the avian respiratory tract and gaining basic anesthetic and monitoring principles to guide safer, more consistent anesthesia. This course covers avian cardiovascular and respiratory anatomy, basic anesthesia equipment, principles of safe anesthesia along with some guidelines and recommendations for anesthetic and analgesic protocols.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: The Leaky Vessel: Extravasation Protocols and Antidotes
courses.description: This course discusses what to do when chemotherapy administration goes wrong. It covers the common injectable chemotherapeutics and what to do if they get outside the vein. Each drug will be explained as an irritant or vesicant, plus whether or not it has an antidote, and what the suggested protocols are if extravasated. Chemotherapy handling and administration will be addressed in terms of safety and prevention.

courses.title: DIAGNOSIS AND MANAGEMENT OF PROTEINURIA (802-42324)
courses.description: This presentation by Dr. Remo Lobetti will address the etiologies, pathophysiology, and consequences of proteinuria, as well the diagnostic approach to an animal that has unexplained proteinuria on routine urine analysis.

courses.title: 52nd Annual IVAS Congress
courses.description:
The objective of the 52nd Annual IVAS Congress is to provide top quality continuing education which advances the knowledge and skills of veterinarians in the areas of acupuncture, science of acupuncture, research, acupuncture related and East-Asian medical therapy, including Chinese herbal medicine, laser and Chinese food therapies.
Continuing education is provided through live lectures led by presenters known as experts in the field of veterinary acupuncture medicine. Session tracks include small animal and large.
courses.location: Harpa Concert Hall and Conference Center

courses.title: TRIAGE Leadership: Systems-Based Leadership for Veterinary Teams
courses.description:
TRIAGE Leadership: Systems-Based Leadership for Veterinary Teams
Veterinary hospitals operate in complex, high-pressure environments where effective communication, accountability, and coordination among clinical teams are essential for consistent patient care. Breakdowns in these areas can contribute to delayed treatments, medical errors, and reduced team effectiveness, particularly in emergency and specialty settings.
This program introduces the TRIAGE Leadership framework, a structured, systems-based approach designed to support veterinary professionals in leadership roles, including veterinarians, veterinary nurses, and non-clinical team members with supervisory responsibilities. Through case-based scenarios and applied learning, participants will examine common leadership challenges encountered in veterinary practice, including unclear role expectations, communication breakdowns, and difficulty addressing performance concerns within teams.
The course focuses on the development of repeatable leadership strategies that promote clear communication, reinforce accountability, and improve clinical workflow reliability. Participants will be provided with practical tools, including structured communication frameworks, intervention models, and decision-making strategies that can be applied directly within veterinary hospital environments.
By strengthening leadership capability across the veterinary team, this program aims to improve coordination of care, enhance communication between team members, and support more consistent execution of patient care plans within clinical settings.

courses.title: SURGICAL BILIARY DISEASE & ULTRASOUND (802-42320)
courses.description: This online anytime course program will help the individual understand the clinical and sonographic parameters of surgical biliary disease in order to recognize when medical and surgical treatment is appropriate in biliary disease processes in dogs and cats.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: No Pain is All Gain in Dentistry
courses.description: This course discusses various pain management techniques for veterinary dentistry patients. The importance of multi-modal pain management before, during, and after dentistry procedures will be covered. It also outlines the pharmacology of different agents including opioids, NSAIDs, and regional anesthesia.

courses.title: Surg'X Interlocking Nail Fracture Fixation Online Pre-lab
courses.description:
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: 2-Parts:
Preoperative Planning Using vPOP Pro (25 minutes)
Veterinary ILN; history, concept, biomechanics, evolution (55 minutes)
Surg'X ILN system; presentation, technical features, indications, clinical evaluation.
Pre-operative planning; surgical approaches, tips, tricks & practical session.
Summary of surgical technique

courses.title: The Touch of Triage - Hypoxia and Shock
courses.description: This course covers how to quickly and accurately assess emergency patients and treat for the things that will kill them the quickest which are hypoxia and shock. It then explains how triage doesn't just end in the waiting room, or ER, but even after a patient is hospitalized. Every time you enter their cage you are essentially triaging them again and again.

courses.title: TFAST Point of Care Ultrasound for Assessment of Heart Disease in Small Animal Practice
courses.description: This webinar will focus on TFAST Fundamental Echocardiography including image acquisition of the TFAST Echo Views in the standing position. We will teach the fundamental right sided and left sided echo views and how to use them for patient assessment for dogs with chronic valvular disease, dilated cardiomyopathy and pulmonary hypertension and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in cats. We will also discuss applying the EPIC guidelines from the Cardiac Education Group for management of early chronic valvular disease dogs regarding when to start therapy with pimobendan. We will also discuss imaging the caudal vena cava and lung as fallback views to assess for right sided and left sided heart failure respectively.

courses.title: The Quiet Acutely Blind Eye
courses.description: This course focuses on differentials for acute but quiet blind eyes in dogs with concepts applicable to other species. It contrasts some common more active/hot causes of ocular cloudiness and visual impairment.

courses.title: Toxicology - Rodenticides
courses.description: This course explores rodenticide toxicity in small animal veterinary medicine. Rodenticide exposure is a Top 3 call annually for the ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center and a very common presentation to the veterinary hospital. It discusses the three major types of rodenticide that are available on the market including decontamination, toxic doses with LD50's, treatment, and nursing care. It includes a look at other "less toxic" rodenticides as well. The course reviews how to tell these rodenticides apart to make sure the correct one is being treated for and what to do when one cannot identify it. Lastly, it discusses relay exposure which is the occurrence of a pet eating wildlife or a carcass that may have eaten rodenticide.

courses.title: Renal Disease: Protecting the Kidneys During Anesthesia
courses.description: Renal disease is a common co-morbidity in patients requiring anesthesia for various procedures. Understanding how the pathophysiology of renal disease intersects with the impact of anesthesia is important to developing a plan for safe delivery of anesthesia that minimizes impact on renal function. This course looks at sedation and anesthesia drugs along with patient care and monitoring for patients with renal disease.

courses.title: Current Status of Stem Cell Use in Cats
courses.description: There is significant unmet medical need for cats and regenerative therapies, including stem cells, are being evaluated as potential treatments for several feline diseases. Although there are currently no approved stem cell products for cats in the U.S., veterinary professionals can provide benefit to themselves and their patients by being aware of the regulations, unique considerations, and current evidence on the use of cell-based therapies in this species.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Diagnosis and New Treatment Options for Cats with FIP
courses.description: Diagnosing feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) can be straightforward in its effusive form but identifying dry FIP remains a clinical challenge. This course breaks down the key diagnostic tools and testing strategies available in practice to help practitioners confidently recognize all forms of FIP. It also explores the distinctions between feline enteric coronavirus (FECV) and feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), the underlying pathogenesis, and the most common clinical signs to watch for. This course helps participants gain clarity and confidence in managing this complex and often misunderstood disease.

courses.title: Safe to Soar: The Secret Sauce of Highly Effective Teams (On Demand)
courses.description: A team's capacity for reaching toward their highest potential is supported or depleted by the environment in which they work. While the nature of the work in veterinary medicine is often out of our control, the culture of a team can be crafted to support the individual and organization's wellbeing and performance. At the foundation of this is psychological safety. Decades of study by researchers such as Harvard Business School leadership professor, Dr. Amy Edmondson, and organizations such as Microsoft and Google have shown psychological safety to be the #1 factor differentiating happy, effective teams from those that are languishing. But what is psychological safety? And how can it be cultivated in veterinary teams? Attendees will learn about the team phenomenon of psychological safety including what it is and is not. We'll explore how it impacts team wellbeing and performance and discover evidence-based tools and practices for cultivating it in your hospital.

courses.title: Why Physical Health and Behavior are Inextricably Linked
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss the intersections among physical health and behavior, the impacts of stress, and the connection among immune function, the microbiome, pain, and behavior. Finally, we will offer recommendations for trainers and veterinarians working together to maximize success for the animals.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Chemotherapy Induced Sepsis
courses.description: Sepsis is often thought to be synonymous with infection. This course examines sepsis brought on from chemotherapy. It delves into how chemotherapy works on the cells of the body, specifically the white blood cells. It details symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment, as well as how to prevent a second episode.

courses.title: Dr. Cooney's Most Challenging Cases: pivoting from panic to peace (Recording)
courses.description: Someone who performs a lot of euthanasia is going to have challenging cases from time to time. They make everyone nervous during a time when calm and peace is so important. Dr. Cooney is a well-known expert in companion animal euthanasia and has helped over 10,000 animals with the procedure. She has picked out some of her toughest to review with you and help you overcome challenges of your own. When we know better, we do better.

courses.title: Reptiles: How to Approach in a Fear-Free Manner
courses.description: This program provides an overview of Fear Free approaches for treating reptiles. You will learn core concepts that are required to understand your patients and apply a Fear Free approach to their treatment. You will then learn how to do a Fear Free exam on a lizard, a snake, and a chelonian. Finally you will learn to identify signs of pain in reptiles.

courses.title: Advance25: Feline Medicine
courses.description:
This online course is specifically designed for vets who want to advance their knowledge and understanding of some key areas of feline medicine.
Through recorded sessions, extensive notes and MCQs, you will learn from a highly regarded internal medicine specialist about new developments in the field, and how this relates to your own case management.
You'll be able to utilise your new knowledge from day one of the course, and be able to enjoy access to your course materials for a full 12 months after the course has finished.

courses.title: G.I. Sonographic Pathology & Obstruction Parts 1 & 2 (online ANYTIME Program)
courses.description: Gastrointestinal normal structure and activity will be described. Deviations from the normal structure will be explained and how to recognize them sonographically. Demonstration of the tendencies of certain pathologies. What is sonographically normal and abnormal in the gastrointestinal tract. How to follow normal curvilinear structures into abnormal or obstructive presentations. How to recognizing tissue densities/masses vs. a foreign body.

courses.title: Hematuria: Clearing the Path to Urinary Health (SAIM717)
courses.description: How much should you worry about hematuria? In this course, we'll focus on top differential diagnoses, a diagnostic approach, and long-term management strategies for hematuria in dogs and cats. You'll learn how to distinguish true hematuria, utilize urine sediment analysis and point-of-care ultrasound, identify triggers, and avoid unnecessary antibiotic use, along with emergency stabilization of patients with acute, severe urinary blood loss.

courses.title: ADVANCED TWO DAY CANINE AND FELINE WET LAB
courses.description: This lecture and wet lab will provide the veterinarian with the skills needed to treat the advanced dentistry cases seen in practice. This LIVE wet lab event provides Veterinarians with equipment, specimens, etc.

courses.title: Navigating Raw Nutrition Conversations
courses.description: Nutrition has become the fifth vital assessment; therefore, confident communication about nutrition and alternative diets has become essential in the clinic. But how do you start a nutrition dialogue in the exam room and how do you navigate conversations with savvy nutrition clients? This talk will improve the practical application of nutrition knowledge about alternative feeding and raw pet foods.

courses.title: Fiber in Veterinary Nutrition
courses.description: Dietary therapy is at the foundation of all gastrointestinal disease management. The most critical nutrient in a majority of cases is dietary fiber. Despite this importance, dietary fiber is a vexing area due to the complexity of what fiber is and does. This course discusses how to assess fiber intake, strategically adjust dietary fiber supplementation, and implement it in practice. It reviews key concepts like fermentability, viscosity, and solubility and the outcomes associated with these factors.

courses.title: I Think My Dog is Pregnant
courses.description: This online/non-interactive course covers the following: History, Confirming Pregnancy, Ultrasonography, Radiology, Serologic Testing, Estimation of Whelping Date, Progesterone Testing vs Counting From Breeding Dates, Progesterone Testing Counting Days From Ovulation, Ultrasound Measurements, Technique and Interpretation, Radiographic Interpretations In Pregnant Bitch, The Non-gravid Uterus In A Bred Bitch, Ultrasound Technique, Ultrasound Findings.

courses.title: ANAESTHESIA 1: ESSENTIALS OF VETERINARY ANAESTHESIA ( On Demand Course)
courses.description: This 4 week online course is designed to provide you with the knowledge you need to help effectively and safely manage anaesthesia in your patients. We willll cover setting up your anaesthetic machine and circuits, selecting appropriate anaesthetic machine settings for your patient, and the pharmacology of common anaesthetic and sedative medications. settings for your patient, and the pharmacology of common anaesthetic and sedative medications. What's more, we will also talk about how to reduce anaesthetic risk in your patients, and will complete the course with a discussion on anaesthetic monitoring, and the management of common anaesthetic problems, such as hypotension, hypothermia, arousal during anaesthesia and much more!

courses.title: Aspects of Working Dog Reproduction For Working Dogs, PART 1
courses.description: This elective is part 1 of 2. In this elective, you will learn breeding management for working dogs. There are many factors and decisions that determine the overall success of canine breeding programs. These elective reviews the normal physiology and behavior associated with pregnancy and parturition in the female dog and the stages of fetal development and outlines the factors and causes of canine dystocia.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: The Eye is the Window - Ocular Manifestations of Systemic Disease
courses.description: Ocular lesions can be clues to underlying systemic disease. On the flip side, systemic disease can result in ophthalmic pathology ranging from incidental to vision threatening. Comprehensive physical and ophthalmic examination will lead to the most complete assessment of a patient's health. Knowledge of ocular manifestations of systemic disease will facilitate formulation of differential and definitive diagnoses as well as support patient vision and ocular health.

courses.title: Immunotherapy in Veterinary Oncology: Past Present and Future
courses.description: Veterinary oncology has seen significant advancements in immunotherapy, offering novel treatment approaches for companion animals diagnosed with cancer. Immunotherapy aims to harness the body's immune system to recognize and attack cancerous cells, reducing reliance on traditional treatments such as chemotherapy and radiation therapy. This course discusses key immunotherapeutic strategies, available products, and clinical advancements in veterinary oncology.

courses.title: MSK US - Shoulder: Protocol & Pathologies (Anytime Program)
courses.description: Learn sonographic approaches for MSK ultrasound of the shoulder region. Understand common pathologies that affect the shoulder, and how to identify them on ultrasound.

courses.title: Raw Diets 101
courses.description: Communication about nutrition is essential for wellness in companion animals, and continuing education about the potential risks and potential benefits of raw diets will improve in-clinic conversations. What are raw diets, and why are they gaining popularity? This talk will cover perceived benefits, anecdotal evidence, and a brief introduction to emerging research, as well as covering essential differences between homemade & commercially prepared raw diets.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Approach to Acute Respiratory Distress in Cats
courses.description: Being presented with a cat in acute respiratory distress can be distressing for us. This course reviews a simple and systematic approach to the diagnosis and treatment of cats in respiratory distress. The focus is on localizing the problem within the respiratory tract which allows targeted diagnostics and early treatment.

courses.title: SDEP Echo On-Demand Ultrasound Training
courses.description: This 6 CE online, anytime course includes, the SDEP 7pt Echo Lectures. An in- depth presentation of the philosophy and reasoning behind the development of SDEP and the key features; basic ultrasound terminology and knobology; the functions of the various probes, and a thorough dissection of the 7 points one by one with illustrative videos of each position, the SDEP 7pt Technique Videos. Individual training modules on each step covered in the lecture, so you can spend as much, or as little time with each position as needed. First, practice the unique SDEP probe manipulation and scanning motions detailed in the intro, then proceed to each module with your patient as Dr. Lindquist walks you through the needed probe movements on his patient with associated position videos. including a spit screen showing image acquisition too, bootcamp video sessions. Ready your patient and scan as you listen to Dr. Lindquist talk you through an entire abdomen. Each session moves you along in both speed and more challenging views, allowing progression as you are ready. Extended Training Modules. Round out the training program by addressing areas of particular difficulty for most. SDEP Echo Emergency protocol - Learn to perform a full cardiac workup in just minutes with our SDEP Emergency protocol.

courses.title: Veterinary Practice Management: A Bird's Eye View
courses.description:
This course is in a self-study format with open enrollment 24/7/365.
This course is designed to introduce the fundamentals of veterinary management and leadership. The roles of management verses leadership strategies are explored, along with different management styles.
Missions, visions and business basics are covered, along with a summary of OSHA requirements. Professionalism, communication and general organization of successful veterinary hospitals are described, and templates for an employee manual, job description and medical records audit are provided. An overview of human resources, marketing and finances helps participants identify critical areas of the veterinary practice that must be focused on, allowing ample opportunity for growth within the business.

courses.title: Thoracic Pathology & Ultrasound. When is it cardiogenic vs. other?
courses.description: This 2 hour On-Line/ANYTIME program will present the necessary actions and clinical parameters needed to dial down whether clinical signs are derived from cardiac disease/thoracic disease, or other. In depth discussions of: normal respiratory parameters, normal echo parameters and radiographic findings, cardiac parameters of left sided heart failure, pleural effusion, cardiogenic parameters vs non-cardiogenic, thoracic lesion mapping for US-guided sampling, non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema causes, thoracic causes of abdominal passive congestion, pulmonary & other thromboembolic presentations, thoracic cysts, lung consolidations, lung lobe torsions, US-guided thoracic sampling, thoracic hernia, thoracic carcinomatosis/lymphomatosis, valve disease classifications, cardio-thoracic case presentations.
