courses.title: Cardiac Measurements and View Adjustments Do's and Don'ts
courses.description: This online anytime program focuses on cardiac measurements correcting common measurement and Doppler evaluations and overall echo refinement. Secret to Functional Cardiology in Practice Echo Technique 5 Chamber Pump, and Starlings Laws, 5 reasons why we should improve our images, Measurements and Adapting To Common Pathology, LV M Mode Anatomy, DCM and M Mode, EPSS Mitral valve E Point to Septal Separation LA MAX Measurement LA AO June Boon Method, LA AO Heart base with measurement Doppler Knobology, Normal MV TV Color Flow Doppler, Pulmonary Artery Doppler, Apical 5 Chamber, Proper LVOT Alignment Whats Wrong Here and Why and How do I fix it Common mistakes and how to correct them.

courses.title: Neurological History and Exam Protocols of Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Veterinary neurology, in general, is often a difficult and confusing topic for general practitioners. The basis of clinical neurology is lesion localization. Lesion localization can only be achieved with a good neurological examination and history. This self-study course first focuses on how to obtain an accurate history from owners. Next it reviews how best to perform and interpret a neurological examination. Overall, this course helps participants develop their history-taking protocols and enhance their neurological examination skills.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: The Diet Trial is a Diagnostic Test
courses.description: This course will outline how to understand the elimination diet trial as a diagnostic test when approaching the allergic patient. Specifics will include a review of the food allergy phenotype, best practices for diet selection, strategies for improving owner compliance, and a current review of the literature. A strong focus will be placed on introducing practical solutions that help general practitioners improve diagnostic outcome after a diet trial is prescribed. Numerous case studies will be presented to highlight these concepts.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: A Peaceful Passing- Best Practices for In Home Pet Euthanasia
courses.description: This course helps explain why families choose euthanasia over natural death. It looks at setting expectations and how to communicate the process to pet owners. It covers pre-euthanasia sedation, euthanasia injection techniques, and aftercare, including memorialization options. Lastly, the course discusses on supporting pet owners through grief with resources and ongoing emotional support. This course helps the veterinarian and practice team perform in-home pet euthanasia compassionately and professionally.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Managing Canine Atopic Dermatitis With More Joy and Less Frustration
courses.description: The keys to success in managing atopic dermatitis are developing a proactive treatment plan and providing tools to empower our clients. Atopic dermatitis is a forever disease; while we can't cure it, we can manage it well. We need to set realistic expectations with our clients and partner with them to improve quality of life for themselves and their pets.

courses.title: Avoiding Common Euthanasia Mistakes at Your Clinic (Recording)
courses.description: It's easier to stick to a routine than make changes. Many veterinary teams assume their euthanasia process is "good enough", unaware that a few changes could dramatically enhance functionality, client experience, and team morale. Euthanasia work is often overlooked, but it's an area where thoughtful refinement can have an outsized impact. In this session, we'll explore the five most common euthanasia-related mistakes clinics make, spanning medical procedures, client interactions, and business standards. Attendees will gain practical insights they can implement immediately to reduce risk, elevate care, and foster a deeper love of vet med.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Navigating the Muddy Waters of Pharmacy - Improving Outcomes and Reducing Errors
courses.description: There is a growing need for veterinarians to partner with community pharmacists to maximize patient health and client satisfaction. Both professions want the best possible outcome for patients while fulfilling their legal and ethical professional duties. Because community pharmacists are not trained in veterinary pharmacology as part of their core education, problems can arise when there are large differences in dosage or side effects of the same drug in animals and humans. In this course a practicing private practice veterinarian and a licensed pharmacist discuss the current state of pharmacy issues. It looks at common sources of error, steps that veterinarians can take to prevent these errors, and techniques for building successful working relationships with community pharmacists.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Gaslighting: A Guide for Burning Your Practice Culture to The Ground
courses.description: Is your practice culture suffering, and you don't know why? Is gaslighting happening within your practice setting you and your team up for failure? It is important to realize how different gaslighting behaviors can create toxicity in the workplace. No matter how much you pay your team members, they won't stick around with a toxic culture. Our teams are more aware than ever that they are more willing to take a cut in pay or have no pay at all than work in a toxic environment. This course will look at specific examples of gaslighting in the practice that we are so used to seeing that we don't even realize it's gaslighting. It doesn't have to be the way it's always been.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Land of Confusion - Cognitive Dysfunction in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: There are over 30 million middle aged dogs and 76 million mature cats in the us, as our pets pass middle age and more into their senior years we can see sensory decline, cognitive change, physical health changes, and limitations in mobility. It is our job to recognize how these changes affect our pets and determine the best ways to help them.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Geriatric Globes - Best Practices for Treating Ophthalmic Disease in Senior Dogs and Cats
courses.description: While ophthalmic diseases may present in companion animals at any age, those affecting senior patients may be particularly challenging to manage. Common contributing factors include intolerance of ophthalmic medications and presence of comorbidities that may complicate treatment or administration of general anesthesia. However, there is an expanding range of options for managing many geriatric eye diseases in dogs and cats; and many can be administered or performed by primary care veterinarians and their animal care teams. This course lists the most common eye diseases presenting in geriatric dogs and cats, with a focus on those best practices for management and techniques to preserve vision and/or comfort in our aged small animal patients.

courses.title: The Anal Sac Dilemma: Diagnosing, Treating, and Managing Recurring Anal Sac Issues in Dogs
courses.description: This course reviews how to effectively diagnose, treat, and manage anal sac disorders in dogs. It covers key clinical signs, best-practice diagnostic techniques, and treatment strategies for both acute and chronic cases, including when to use medical management, dietary modifications, and surgical intervention. Special emphasis is placed on long-term care and prevention, including the role of allergy management, weight control, and client education in reducing recurrence. Participants should feel more confident in their approach to anal sac disease, ensuring improved patient outcomes and better owner compliance.

courses.title: Neonatal Care and Resuscitation
courses.description:
Whelping and neonatal care can be some of the most high-stakes, stressful, and rewarding moments in practice. This course walks step-by-step through the stages of parturition, recognizing normal vs. abnormal progression, and when to step in. It provides hands-on strategies for neonatal resuscitation, APGAR scoring, and managing the "big four" challenges in newborn puppies: hypothermia, hypoglycemia, hypoxia, and hypovolemia.
The course also looks at practical protocols for nutrition, tube vs. bottle feeding, fluid therapy, oxygen delivery, and early detection of congenital defects. Real-world tips, drug protocols, and clear decision points will give you confidence the next time you're called to care for a neonate.
This course provides practical tools that can be applied immediately to improve survival rates, reduce stress during emergencies, and support healthier litters. This course is a must for anyone who wants to feel more prepared and more effective when it matters.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Don't be a Pain! Analgesia for Emergency and Critical Care Patients
courses.description: After reviewing pain and pain control definitions, along with commonly used analgesia drugs in emergency and critical care settings, this course examines pain control scoring systems as well as the consequences of untreated pain. It looks at the effect of patient comfort and stress levels on pain perception. Lastly it reviews non-pharmacologic measures to help with pain control.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Zero Stars, Do Not Recommend - Handling Negative Online Reviews
courses.description: Reputation management for the practice is a necessary evil. Negative reviews create a lot of harmful emotional noise you must sift through during your already busy day. There are different types of negative reviews. This course covers practical ways to set up a review response management system and triage protocol for your reviews. It then outlines how to handle different types of negative reviews online. It will help you embrace your inner 'wet-blanket' when dealing with dumpster fire reviews online. The last thing you want to do is pour gasoline on a fire.

courses.title: Opioids: Safety, Storage, and Responsible Pain Management
courses.description: During this two-hour video course, Dr. Quandt will help veterinary practices ensure they're choosing the safest and most effective pain control options for their patients, while also shielding their team from the risks of abuse, theft, and legal challenges. Viewers will learn the legal requirements for purchasing, storing, dispensing, and disposing of controlled substances, with an emphasis on the state of Texas and DEA regulations. We will also discuss complimentary analgesic options that may help minimize a patient's need for opioid pain control.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Embracing all Interdisciplinary Team Members in the Delivery of Pet Hospice Care
courses.description: The veterinary team consists of trained, purpose-driven individuals, delivering end-of-life care with compassion. Their roles and duties in serving geriatric and terminally ill patients may be defined and enhanced. Now, let's consider the many professionals beyond the veterinary hospital walls supporting pet hospice and family caregiving. This course examines the components of an interdisciplinary team, including skill assessment and how to best leverage the team

courses.title: Canine Chagas Disease: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, and Treatment
courses.description: in this 2.5 hour video series, Dr. Roy Madigan will cover all aspects of Chagas disease, from prevalence to pathogenesis, diagnosis, novel treatments and environmental control. Upon completion of the videos and quizzes, viewers will understand how to recognize the clinical signs of Chagas disease, obtain a definitive diagnosis, initiate treatment, and monitor response to therapy. Viewers will also understand the pathophysiology and transmission of the infectious organism that causes Chagas disease.

courses.title: Global FAST Hybrid Online course (AFAST-TFAST, and VetBLUE) with Hands On Live Scanning
courses.description:
The course covers AFAST and its image acquisition, its target-organ approach for obvious soft tissue abnormalities, and its abdominal fluid scoring system with case-based applications; TFAST and its image acquisition, its echocardiography views, its use for the accurate diagnosis of pleural and pericardial effusion and pneumothorax, its target-organ approach of the heart and pleural space for obvious soft-tissue abnormalities; and Vet BLUE and its image acquisition, its regional, pattern-based approach integrating its B-line scoring system, and 6 lung ultrasound signs. Global FAST is the term used when AFAST, TFAST and Vet BLUE are combined as a single ultrasound format used as an extension of the physical exam. The terms AFAST, TFAST, Vet BLUE and Global FAST are registered service marks for education purposes with the US Patent and Trademark Office to uphold each exam's highest degree of integrity as a standardized ultrasound exam.
The 5-lectures cover AFAST, TFAST, and Vet BLUE, combined called Global FAST, plus a 1-hour Global FAST image acquisition supplemental module (7-hours total of online lectures). Quizzes must be passed with a score of 80% to move on to the next module.
The remote online course above is followed by a live hands on scanning session (4 hour scanning session).

courses.title: Dermatophytosis: Wood You Be Able to Spot This Ringer?
courses.description: Dermatophytosis is a common fungal infection in companion animals. Early recognition of signs, comprehension of diagnostic tests available, and selection of safe and effective treatment protocols are important in resolution of this contagious disease. Images and case discussion will help participants recognize common disease patterns, particularly in susceptible populations. Point of care diagnostics that can be easily performed in the clinic can speed successful treatment. A three pronged approach to eliminating this frustrating fungi and the communication tools needed to empower clients to implement the plan are reviewed.

courses.title: Less Fear, More Hope - How Research is Driving New Strategies in Hemangiosarcoma Treatment and Prevention
courses.description: Hemangiosarcoma remains one of the most challenging and devastating diseases in veterinary medicine. Its heterogeneity and aggressive nature have made meaningful therapeutic progress frustratingly slow. This course introduces a forward-thinking approach that combines cutting-edge targeted therapies with rationally designed preventative strategies, offering hope for better outcomes for patients, clients, and veterinary teams alike.

courses.title: Updates on Spay/Neuter Recommendations
courses.description: The World Small Animal Veterinary Association published Reproduction Control Guidelines in 2024. These guidelines included decision-making recommendations for reproduction control in dogs and cats that differ from the traditional recommendation to prepubertally spay/neuter. This course focuses on these decision-making recommendations in light of the most current research related to some of the long-term adverse health effects of gonad removal.

courses.title: Advanced Therapies Working Dogs Rehabilitation
courses.description: In this elective, you will learn about the uses and benefits of aquatic therapy (underwater treadmill), photobiomodulation (or laser therapy), massage techniques, kinesiology taping, and nutraceuticals as they apply to Working Dogs. This elective consists of six, one-hour online modules and is designed to be completed at your own pace. This elective is authored by Dr. Matt Brunke, a 2004 graduate of Ross University and Diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation. Dr. Brunke has been actively practicing in the field of veterinary rehabilitation since 2008. No matter what discipline of Working Dog you have or support, this elective will help you learn the fundamental techniques of canine rehabilitation to keep the Working Dog healthy and operationally sound.

courses.title: 2025 Spring into Feline Medicine eConference - On-demand
courses.description: This conference encourages attendees in various stages of their professional development to increase their feline knowledge and elevate their standard of care for cats. This conference will focus on multiple feline topics such as NSAID guidelines, paraneoplastic syndrome, pleural space disease, feline leukemia virus, toxin trends, diabetic cats, blood transfusions, comorbidity management, hypercalcemia, chronic upper respiratory infections, cat friendly neurologic exams, and hypertension, hypokalemia, and hyperaldosteronism in senior cats.

courses.title: Aspects of Working Dog Reproduction For Working Dogs, PART 2
courses.description: This elective is part 2 of 2. In this elective, you will learn breeding management for working dogs. Many factors and decisions determine the overall success of canine breeding programs. In this elective you will learn about canine semen collection and assessment; insemination techniques, and periparturient disorders and management.

courses.title: Mastering ECG Basics
courses.description: This course covers the basic principles of ECG, the anatomy of the conduction system, how and when to perform an ECG, ECG interpretation and treatment of arrhythmias. There are also 31 practice ECGs.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Comorbidities in Cats
courses.description: Nutritional management is critical in managing feline disease conditions. The diet's role in these nutrient sensitive conditions vary, as diet may be a primary intervention or hold a supportive management role. Cats presenting with multiple concurrent disease conditions exhibit an added degree of clinical complexity. These comorbidities frequently occur in senior feline patients, as multiple diseases demonstrate increased prevalence with advancing age in cats. These disease conditions include chronic kidney disease, joint disease, cognitive dysfunction, neoplasia, and endocrinopathies. Selecting the most suitable diet for a feline patient involves thoroughly evaluating their nutritional needs, understanding the nutrients involved in managing disease conditions, and knowledge of nutritional profiles available in helping to manage the disease conditions.

courses.title: VetCE On Demand: Feline Ophthalmology 101 - Taking the Mystery Out of Common Ocular Diseases
courses.description: This course examines common ocular diseases including identification, diagnostics, and treatment of these conditions that are unique to cats. It will help practitioners provide effective treatments for ocular conditions afflicting many feline patients.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Euthanasia Reimagined - The Modern Approach
courses.description: Euthanasia was ready for an evolution and much has changed in the past 10 years. Experts and practitioners alike have found ways to celebrate the bond, protect patient comfort, and elevate client pre-planning and communication. Everyone is benefitting from the advancements. Has your veterinary team joined 'The Good Death Revolution'? Dr. Kathleen Cooney, Director of Education for the Companion Animal Euthanasia Training Academy (CAETA) highlights their 14 Essential Components of Companion Animal Euthanasia. It's time to look deeper into what clients want, what patients need, and how veterinary teams can find fulfillment in euthanasia work.

courses.title: March CE Journal Articles 2025 RACE Submission
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of journal articles that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Advance25: Endoscopy for Advanced Practitioners
courses.description: This online course is specifically designed for advanced practitioner vets who want to refresh, update and advance their knowledge and understanding of some key areas of small animal endoscopy. Through recorded sessions, extensive notes and MCQs, you will learn from a highly regarded internal medicine specialist about new developments in the field, and how this relates to your own case management. We'll cover endoscopy of the gastrointestinal tract, respiratory tract and bladder; whilst discussing your approach to these cases using the most up to date research. You'll be able to utilise your new knowledge from day one of the course. You will be able to enjoy unlimited access to your course materials for a full 12 months after the course has finished.

courses.title: The Science of Creating and Achieving Meaningful Goals (On Demand)
courses.description: Setting meaningful goals can be a powerful mechanism to boost wellbeing and research shows that setting appropriate goals can help measure progress toward self-mastery, ignite motivation as well as promote self-efficacy. But how are "appropriate" goals set and met? In this session, attendees will develop a foundational understanding of the science-based process associated with setting meaningful goals. They will understand the steps necessary for change and work through the steps to identify, develop and implement achievable and meaningful professional goals. Upon completion, participants will be better prapared to implement these concepts into their unique lives.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Toxicology: Initial Approach and Decontamination
courses.description: In companion animals, toxin ingestion often leads to emergency visits, necessitating rapid and effective management strategies. The initial approach is crucial for managing intoxicated pets, enabling rapid treatment planning and optimal outcomes. A spectrum of decontamination techniques is available and there are risks and benefits associated with each technique. This course provides insights into tailoring the approach to poisoned cases, helping to ensure the best possible outcomes for their patients and their owner.

courses.title: 13th The Gulf-Atlantic Veterinary Conference 2026
courses.description: FVMAs TGAVC 2026 offers continuing education for veterinarians and veterinary technicians through lecture sessions and hands-on wet labs.
courses.location: Fort Lauderdale Marriott Harbor BEACH RESORT & SPA

courses.title: Non-Surgical Treatment Options for Pyometra and Pregnancy Termination
courses.description: This course discusses reasons for considering medical options over surgical spay for cases of canine pyometra and pregnancy termination. It reviews the available medical treatment options including protocols, efficacy, and side effects. These will include prostaglandins, dopamine agonists, steroids, and progesterone receptor blockers.

courses.title: Feline Facial Dermatitis
courses.description: There are multiple causes for feline facial dermatitis. They range from atopic dermatitis, food allergy, dermatophytosis, and auto-immune skin diseases. It is important to be able to recognize basic skin lesions and perform the proper workup to ensure the patient is diagnosed correctly and treated properly. The course includes a look at different skin lesions, diagnostics, and treatment plan options.

courses.title: Focus on Surgery (a 2 lecture series)
courses.description:
Lecture Title 1: Flat Faces and Big Problems: Review of BOAS : Lecture Abstract: This webinar provides an introduction to Brachycephalic Obstructive Airway Syndrome (BOAS), focusing on presentation, case management, an overview of a few surgical techniques and complications. This is an introduction for surgeons seeking to have an insight into these cases, their management and refine their approach to treatment. This is aimed as an introduction to the topic for you to then build upon with additional reading and/or practical CPD. Lecture 2: It's a Chole Story: Reviewing Biliary Obstruction Cases: Lecture Description
This webinar provides an introduction to extrahepatic biliary duct obstruction cases, focusing on the anatomy and physiology of the biliary system, species differences, common biliary pathologies, patient evaluation, decision-making including when to refer, and an introduction/brief overview of key procedures such as cholecystectomy. We will cover management of biliary diseases and aim to refine the initial approach to these cases. This session serves as a stepping stone for further study and skill development.

courses.title: Advance25: Abdominal Ultrasound
courses.description: This online course in Abdominal Ultrasound is specifically designed for vets in practice who want to advance their scanning skills and interpretation. The course is designed to last for 6 weeks. Each week will have 2 pre-recorded webinars; written notes; and a mandatory multiple choice quiz. The students will also have access to an online discussion forum which the course tutor will monitor for 8 weeks from the start date.

courses.title: Ultrasound Image Optimization: Sonographer Technique, Hardware, Software and Essential Physics
courses.description: This 1-hour course covers an introductory look at the main control settings of an ultrasound system, and how to utilize them in both pre- and post-processing to optimize ultrasound images for effective diagnostic purposes. In conjunction with the SDEP scanning protocol, where attendees learn the SDEP hand maneuvers, this course will help participants optimize the images while scanning by explaining how to manually adjust settings on the ultrasound machine, and the basic acoustic physics behind what those settings do. Machine hardware and software considerations and challenges will be discussed.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Rabbits in General Practice - Breaking the Exotic Spell
courses.description: This course is beneficial for all team members of a general practice which opens its doors to rabbits. It examines the rewards of serving rabbit-owning clients. The course emphasizes defining and following each team member's role and of working in unison, with the understanding that these roles and responsibilities can evolve as the team gains experience. Next, it examines building a network that comprises of other general practices that have ventured into rabbit medicine, veterinary specialists, and emergency practices that might be called upon to provide after-hours care for our rabbit patients, as well as rescue organizations/shelters. Lastly it outlines how to maximize the odds of successful outcomes of anesthesia and surgical procedures.

courses.title: No Pain is More Gain: Multimodal Analgesia in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Effective pain management is essential to improving patient outcomes, enhancing recovery, and elevating the standard of care in veterinary practice. This course explores the principles of multimodal analgesia and how to apply them throughout the peri-anesthetic period in both canine and feline patients. Participants will review pain pathways and nociception, learn how to match analgesic drugs and techniques to specific pain mechanisms, and gain confidence incorporating opioids, NSAIDs, local anesthetics, and other analgesic options into patient-centered treatment plans. Through real-world case examples, veterinarians and veterinary technicians will discover practical strategies for developing tailored analgesic protocols, optimizing peri-operative care, minimizing anesthetic risks, and improving patient comfort from admission through recovery and discharge.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Basics of Triage and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation in Zoological Companion Animals
courses.description: Do you have treatment anxiety when presented with an emergency rabbit, bearded dragon or parrot? This course reviews the basic principles of triage and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in zoological companion animal (ZCA) species. It provides information and tools to help practitioners and team members feel more comfortable handling initial triage in these species. Additionally, it discusses similarities, which are many, and differences to CPR in ZCA species, highlighting anatomic and physiologic differences between small mammals, reptiles, and birds.

courses.title: Feline Cardiac Emergencies
courses.description: Cardiac emergencies are common in the veterinary ER and, like most things involving cats, cardiac issues present special challenges. The most common cardiac emergencies in cats are feline atrial thromboembolism (FATE), congestive heart failure (CHF), and arrhythmias. This course reviews cardiac anatomy and physiology before moving on to discuss the specific disease processes. It then examines the difficulties faced in cats with cardiac disease and how to manage them.

courses.title: Ocular Emergencies
courses.description:
In emergency practice, rapid and accurate imaging is often the key to stabilising patients and guiding life-saving decisions. This three-lecture short course is designed specifically for veterinarians seeking to refine their approach to abdominal radiology in urgent clinical settings.
Course Outline:
Topic 1: Corneal Ulcers
Corneal ulcers are a common ophthalmic condition presenting to the small animal practitioner. They may be classified as "simple and uncomplicated"or "complicated/emergent".. If emergent, they typically present due to significant ocular discomfort, loss of vision, or compromised globe integrity. Causes vary from external trauma in origin ( i.e. secondary to globe prolapse, conjunctival/corneal foreign body, corneal chemical burn, corneal wound and/or perforation, iris prolapse) or other primary ocular underlying conditions (i.e. keratoconjunctivitis sicca (KCS), eyelash abnormalities (disticia, ectopic cilia), eyelid abnormalities (entropion, ectropion). Prompt intervention and proper treatment are essential to preserve vision and restore ocular comfort.
Uveitis specifically refers to inflammation of the middle layer of the eye (the uveal tract) but more commonly, it may refer to any inflammatory process involving the interior of the eye, with inflammation specifically of the uvea termed iridocyclitis. This lecture outlines the pathology, recognition and treatment of the various causes of uveitis in the dog and cat.
Topic 3: Glaucoma
Glaucoma is a heterogeneous group of clinical syndromes that are characterized by elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) ultimately leading to optic nerve damage and blindness. Glaucoma is common in the dog and is not only blinding but also painful if the IOPs are not maintained within a normal range. This lecture provides a simplified approach to diagnosis and clinical decision making in cases of canine glaucoma for the general practitioner, including a discussion of emergency and maintenance therapy.
Topic 4: The Blue

courses.title: On Demand: Treat that Toxin
courses.description: In this on demand course, viewers will review the top 15 toxins affecting dogs and cats, and mistakes to avoid when treating poisoned patients. Mechanisms of action, clinical signs, treatment, and prognosis will be discussed for each toxicant. Viewers will learn when to induce emesis (or not), when to give activated charcoal (or not), when to perform gastric lavage, how to safely sedate or anesthetize poisoned patients, and how to obtain a thorough history.

courses.title: Tricky Client Questions During Euthanasia: Responding with grace and confidence (Recording)
courses.description: Grieving clients say and do unexpected things during euthanasia appointments. Whether they're thinking clearly or lost in sorrow, their questions and expectations may not align with what the veterinary team can ethically or medically provide. Examples include asking to feed highly unusual foods, film the procedure, administer the injection themselves, or keep a piece of the body. Many clients ask if their pet knows what's happening to them and why. In this session, we'll explore what clients seek with such questions and how to respond in a way that meets their emotional needs while honoring the team's boundaries. Come prepared to share unique client experiences and leave with practical, compassionate responses.

courses.title: 21st Promoting Excellence Symposium 2026
courses.description: The Florida Association of Equine Practitioners (the equine division of the Florida Veterinary Medical Association) PES 2026 offers continuing education for veterinarians and veterinary technicians/staff through in-person lectures and wet labs to attain required continuing education.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: How to Treat What You See - Treatments of Common Pathologies Found in the Oral Cavity
courses.description: This is a 24/7/365 open-enrollment self-study distance course. What to do with what you see in the mouth? This course compares various dental presentations including periodontal diseases, tooth resorptions, overbites, under bites, mandibular maxillary asymmetry, oral masses, and fractured teeth. It illustrates the various conditions and describes the treatment for those conditions. Simplifying procedural approaches and "treating what you see" can greatly improve the health of the mouth and long-term health of the patient.

courses.title: Seizures and Brain Disease in Felines: Diagnosing Challenges
courses.description: Diagnosing the cause of seizures and other brain diseases in cats can be a challenge for the general practitioner. This course will explore the metabolic, toxic, and symptomatic causes of these conditions. In addition, it will review the testing options to aid the practitioner and medical team in reaching a diagnosis. Treatment options and prognosis will be briefly discussed.

courses.title: Updates in Reptile Dermatology
courses.description: Reptiles housed under human care , as pets or in zoological collections, are commonly presented to veterinarians for dermatologic issues, including non-infectious and infectious causes. Several reptilian dermatologic pathogens have recently been discovered with the potential for significant health implications to both wild and captive reptiles. This course reviews clinically relevant anatomy of reptile skin and adnexal structures, common infectious and non-infectious dermatologic diseases of reptiles, and recently published treatments for these disease conditions.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Feline Acute Kidney Injury
courses.description: Acute renal injury (AKI) in a cat can be a devastating condition. This course reviews the causes of AKI, its diagnosis and distinguishing differences from chronic kidney disease, and how to develop a treatment plan. It provides case examples as well.

courses.title: A Clinicians Guide to Incorporating Hystrichomorphs into Your Practice
courses.description:
This online professional training course will provide intensive lecture on a wide array of medicine, surgery, commonly performed techniques and procedures in hystricomorph rodents (guine pig and chinchilla).
The course is aimed at veterinarians and veterinary paraprofessionals (technician, assistant, nurse) as well as students with a keen interest in hystricomorph medicine and surgery.
The course will cover aspects of how to set up your practice, anatomy, husbandry, handling, clinical techniques, common diseases, diagnostic imaging, therapeutics, anesthesia, medicine and surgery, among other important topics.

courses.title: Management of Respiratory Complications During Anesthesia
courses.description: Monitoring during anesthesia is far more than recording numbers. It's about understanding what those numbers mean for the patient in front of you. An effective veterinary anesthetist doesn't just interpret data. They translate it into clinically relevant insights and use it to guide decision making in real time. This course focuses on turning ventilation and oxygenation parameters into actionable tools, with practical strategies for recognizing and managing hypoventilation and hypoxemia before they become critical events.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Feline Idiopathic Cystitis - Background and Current Therapeutics
courses.description: This course explores the challenging clinical condition of Feline Idiopathic Cystitis (FIC), focusing on its diagnosis and the range of current therapeutic options. Topics include strategies for managing stress and alleviating pain, along with an introduction to emerging treatments such as low-dose radiation therapy, supported by recent study findings.

courses.title: CLINICAL SONOGRAPHY TRICKS OF THE TRADE PARTS 1 & 2
courses.description:
Learn the significance of how blood chemistry markers, effusions, cardiac issues, abnormal patterns, and disease processes direct the sonographic study. Defining masses in the abdomen will also be covered with a focus on the origination of masses and how to follow them to the primary organ involved.
Course Objectives:
Part 1:
The albumin game
The bilirubin game
Working through ascites
Cliff notes
Multiple myeloma
Part 2:
G.I. foreign body
Cliff notes

courses.title: Intracardiac Pet Euthanasias; Your Heart's in the Right Place (Recording)
courses.description: Euthanasia is an intimate experience for many veterinary practitioners. They know which techniques they like and those they don't. While it's been known for quite some time that intracardiac injections are nerve wracking to perform, a recent study showed that 82% of veterinarians prefer not to do them with clients present, and would just as soon avoid them altogether if given the chance. There are times when an intracardiac euthanasia injection is the best option for the patient, and it's up to all veterinarians to gain the confidence and skills to perform them, especially in front of clients. In this session, we take a closer look at this euthanasia injection method and why it's so effective. Want to make it a safe and dare-we-say pleasant experience for your patient, clients and team? Join us to learn how.

courses.title: LEVEL ONE DENTAL WEEKEND VIRTUAL LAB
courses.description: This is everything that you need to perform basic dentistry in general practice. Extractions, radiology, periodontal disease & therapy, and oral pathology.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Management of Feline Hyperthyroidism
courses.description: Feline hyperthyroidism is the most common endocrine disease affecting older cats. Left untreated, the disease can cause some potentially life-threatening metabolic disturbances. This presentation will review pathophysiology, diagnosis and treatment options in cats with feline hyperthyroidism. In addition, there are sections discussing co-management with chronic kidney disease and co-management with cardiovascular disease.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Are You Keeping Score? The Importance of Pain Scoring Systems
courses.description: This course reviews current pain score scales and systems, including which ones are easiest to use and which are the most useful for dogs and cats. It also discusses why pain scoring is vital and the importance of choosing and implementing a pain scoring system for patients.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Demystifying Google's SEO Algorithm
courses.description: Veterinarians and their management teams are becoming increasingly aware of the importance of the internet and using search engine optimization (SEO) to increase revenue for their practices. Climbing to the top of Google's search engine is something almost every practice owner should want since it can exponentially increase revenue during uncertain economic times.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Stop Pain in its Tracks: Local Blocks for Every Practice
courses.description: Local anesthetic drugs are very effective analgesics. They are also largely easy to use and inexpensive. The use of local/regional blocks improves anesthetic safety and provides analgesia, even after the expected duration of action of the drug. Blocks that can be used in any practice are covered in a step-by-step description, complete with videos.

courses.title: Putting the Fun in Fundus - Evaluation of the Posterior Segment
courses.description: This course describes techniques for examination of the retina and optic nerve with a goal of differentiating pathologic changes from normal variations. A brief overview of species-specific variation in retinal and optic nerve anatomy will also be provided.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Me-OUCH! The Physiology of OA in Cats
courses.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) affects many cats over 10 years of age. Understanding the physiology of pain and the intricacy of OA is the first step to helping our feline friends feel better. This course reviews pain physiology in general and delves into the specifics of OA as well as discusses some treatment options.

courses.title: Tiny Hearts, Big Problems: Cardiovascular Disease in Zoological Companion Animals
courses.description: This course reviews a select number of cardiovascular diseases in zoological companion animal species, such as rabbits, bearded dragons, and parrots in a case based format. It focuses on the disease types, etiology, if known, and key anatomical differences of these species. It also examines any differences in diagnosis from dogs and cats as well as treatment options or preventative measures if available.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Challenging Euthanasias - Case Review and Preventing Dysthanasia
courses.description: All practice team members want euthanasia procedures to go well. This course explores euthanasia cases and looks at how pet owners and veterinarians define a good death experience. It discusses what is ideal compared to what is considered a dysthanasia, the opposite of a good death. The course then looks at determining how best to address dysthanasias when they happen, aiming to protect the mental health of pet owners and the veterinary team.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Essential Hospice and Palliative Care Strategies for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: This course helps to provide veterinary professionals with the essential tools and insights needed for navigating the delicate landscape of end-of-life scenarios. It examines the nuances of the hospice and palliative care philosophy, offering the expansion of this component of care. It reviews communication techniques that go beyond the clinical, fostering empathy and forging lasting bonds with families facing difficult decisions. The course looks at palliative care strategies to enhance the quality of life for patients. It also offers a wealth of resources within the veterinary community, ensuring the seamless continuation of care throughout the end-of-life journey.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: The Physiology and Pharmacology of Euthanasia
courses.description: Euthanasia is a process requiring more than just knowing how to give an injection. As with any procedure, it is important to know how it works and how we achieve a peaceful passing. This course examines the physiology of death and discusses how the drugs used work on the body.

courses.title: Ears and Otitis Externa: Cleaning the Ears/Understanding the Basics
courses.description: Otitis externa can be a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. Success requires a complete plan. Part of that plan is proper cleaning and ear flushing techniques. The presenter will discuss the differences between a normal and diseased ear, appropriate examination of the diseased ear, and normal and abnormal ear anatomy. Additional education points include protocol and product selection for cleaning ears and principles in ear cleaning. He'll finish with tips on managing different types of otitis, including the ear with biofilm.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Job Crafting for Veterinary Teams
courses.description:
Historically, veterinarians, technicians, and other members of the veterinary team have been expected to be generalists. But in our broad field, with a wide range of competencies, asking all veterinary workers to excel at all areas of practice is a recipe for burnout and disaster. This course will illustrate how job crafting, on both an individual and an organization level, can help veterinary practices to leverage the strengths of their workers, and achieve better outcomes.
Job crafting is the practice of taking the job you have and molding it to make it more meaningful for you. Pioneered, researched, and written about extensively by Amy Wrzesniewski, American Psychologist and Professor at the Yale School of Management, job crafting helps individuals increase their job satisfaction, grow within their field, and leverage their strengths at work. For organizations, it can help increase team efficacy, reduce turnover, and improve culture and business outcomes. In veterinary hospitals in particular, it can also improve patient outcomes and customer satisfaction.

courses.title: Adrenal Gland Ultrasound Masterclass: A Structured Approach to Reliable Identification and Interpretation in Dogs and Cats
courses.description:
This non-interactive masterclass is a recording of the original live RACE-approved webinar and includes the original audience Q&A session. A post-content quiz of 5+ questions will be added and participants must obtain 70% or higher to achieve credit.
This practical veterinary ultrasound webinar masterclass focuses on improving clinician confidence and accuracy when imaging the adrenal glands in dogs and cats. Drawing on the presenter's background in education, this course introduces a structured, repeatable approach to adrenal imaging using the L.A.D.R. and R.A.D.R. protocols. These are frameworks specifically developed by the presenter to simplify adrenal localisation and reduce cognitive overload during scanning. These protocols are designed to be easy to remember, clinically applicable and immediately implementable in practice. Participants will learn how to reliably locate and assess adrenal glands using anatomical landmarks, alongside alternative techniques for challenging cases. The course covers adrenal anatomy, scanning techniques, normal ultrasonographic appearance, measurement guidelines, and interpretation of abnormal findings including adrenal enlargement, nodules, mineralisation and small glands. The program incorporates high-quality, professionally filmed ultrasound footage, including detailed visualisation of probe positioning and hand movements, to enhance practical understanding and replicate real-world scanning techniques. Designed for general practitioners and emergency clinicians, this webinar masterclass emphasises clinical application, troubleshooting and integration of ultrasound findings with patient history and laboratory data.

courses.title: SDEP Echo Emergency Protocol (canine & feline) - ANYTIME program
courses.description: This course is targeted to sonographers who are competent in the SDEP Echo Protocol and are ready to focus, practice and apply it to emergency situations on critical patients to obtain a full cardiac image set in under five minutes. This protocol utilizes the same 7-point approach and images all of the traditional views needed to assess function, velocities, pressures, chamber sizes. It is efficient, structured, readily trainable, and is a natural advanced extension of the basic SDEP Echo.

courses.title: VetCE on Demand: Raising Resilience - How to Avoid Compassion Fatigue, Burnout, and Moral Distress
courses.description: This course focuses on the causes, symptoms of, and prevalence of moral distress, compassion, fatigue, and occupational burn out in veterinary medicine. More importantly, it reviews several strategies veterinary professionals can use to prevent moral distress, compassion, fatigue, and occupational burn out.

courses.title: Kicking Ticks to the Curb! Updates on Protecting Your Dog from These Blood-Thirsty, Disease-Ridden Parasites
courses.description: Ticks pose a significant health risk to companion animals, both as blood-feeding parasites and as vectors for numerous pathogens. Over the past few decades, tick populations have expanded and intensified due to factors such as increased globalization, greater movement of humans and animals, and climate change. In the United States, common tick species, including the blacklegged tick, lone star tick, American dog tick, and brown dog tick, have the potential to transmit a range of bacterial, protozoal, and viral pathogens. Serological data indicate that tick-borne pathogens are a persistent challenge for dogs, with U.S. canines frequently testing positive for agents of anaplasmosis, Lyme disease, and ehrlichiosis. Many of these same ticks and pathogens also pose a public health risk, as the tick species that commonly bite dogs can also transmit these same pathogens to humans. As a result, dogs can serve as valuable sentinels for tick-borne disease risks of their human families. Despite awareness of the risk ticks pose to pets, ticks are often and easily overlooked. Given that ticks are a year-round threat in most regions, annual testing and the routine use of fast-acting tick control products play a critical role in protecting pet health by killing ticks and reducing pathogen transmission risk.

courses.title: Smart Calf Rearing: Global Insights to Elevate Dairy Calf Management
courses.description: Veterinarians are key partners in optimizing calf health and welfare, and global research continues to reshape best practices. This webinar will summarize critical findings from the Smart Calf Rearing Conference, including advances in nutrition, immunity, well-being, and management strategies. Presenters will translate cutting-edge science into practical recommendations for veterinary professionals, highlighting opportunities to improve calf resilience and long-term productivity.

courses.title: Optimal Imaging at VICSD
courses.description:
VICSD Optimal Imaging - Optimal Imaging means providing our best diagnostic imaging (Ultrasound vs CT) and AI-enhanced data disease detection for your patients/pets. It's about analyzing our imaging outside the vacuum because imaging results mean much more when analyzed in the context of all the other pertinent information (from you, the referring veterinarian, pet lab results and VICSD's in-house data). Optimal Imaging is about providing better diagnostics for your pet and giving you a more complete understanding of your pet's health.
I-131 Treatment for hyperthyroid cats: I-131 therapy for hyperthyroid cats provides a cure, replacing daily methimazole therapy. I-131 therapy has been shown to increase life-span of hyperthyroid cats compared to methimazole therapy. Confirmation of hyperthyroidism is recommended via bloodwork and a thyroid scan prior to I-131 treatment. Evaluation of left ventricular wall thickness and left atrial size prior to I-131 therapy is also recommended as a baseline.
courses.location: Veterinary Imaging Center of San Diego

courses.title: CUVS 15th Annual Continuing Education Conference
courses.description: Both Veterinarian and Technician tracks are part of this program. Each is six hours in length. Each track consists of six sessions, each 1 hour long, presented by veterinarians and technicians in their respective fields. Topics cover a wide range of specialties, details of which are listed below. Details of each individual's program agenda are provided in their specific submission.

courses.title: Cornell University Veterinary Specialists Advance 2025 - 14th Annual Continuing Education Conference
courses.description: Both Veterinarian and Technician tracks are part of this program. Each is 6 hours in length. Each track is made up of 6 sessions, 1-hour each given by veterinarians and technicians in their respective fields. Topics cover a wide range of specialties, details of which are listed below. Details of each individual program agenda is provided in their specific submission.

courses.title: Antimicrobial Use in Orofacial Medicine and Surgery
courses.description: This program will guide antimicrobial use for orofacial conditions in the dog and cat. Disease processes associated with bacteria will be discussed, with a particular focus on the environment and pathophysiology involved. This basis will be used to consider which conditions may be susceptible to antimicrobial agents. For conditions responsive, suggestions will be made regarding both diagnostics to guide treatment, and responsible empirical use.

courses.title: On-Demand 2025 Talbot Veterinary Informatics Symposium
courses.description: This is the Association for Veterinary Informatics' 31st Annual Symposium! Named for professor, dean, and informatics pioneer Dr. Richard Talbot, DVM, PhD., the Talbot Veterinary Informatics Symposium began in 1995. Our mission is to guide and transform the veterinary profession in understanding, using and extending the practice of informatics. Veterinary clinical informatics is a rapidly evolving science that blends information technology, communications, social and behavioral science, and veterinary medicine to improve the quality and safety of patient care. This course covers how veterinary medical informatics is used in epidemiology, medical data management, veterinary healthcare information technology, and clinical decision support with an emphasis on MEDICINE and health care, NOT business and management.

courses.title: On-Demand 2024 Talbot Veterinary Informatics Symposium
courses.description: This is the Association for Veterinary Informatics' 30th Annual Symposium! Named for professor, dean, and informatics pioneer Dr. Richard Talbot, DVM, PhD., the Talbot Veterinary Informatics Symposium began in 1995. Our mission is to guide and transform the veterinary profession in understanding, using and extending the practice of informatics. Veterinary clinical informatics is a rapidly evolving science that blends information technology, communications, social and behavioral science, and veterinary medicine to improve the quality and safety of patient care. This course covers how veterinary medical informatics is used in epidemiology, medical data management, veterinary healthcare information technology, and clinical decision support with an emphasis on MEDICINE and health care, NOT business and management.

courses.title: Uterine-Derived Stem Cells for the Management of Refractory Feline Chronic Gingivostomatitis
courses.description: This session will include a review of the clinical signs, diagnostic findings, and possible etiologies of feline chronic gingivostomatitis (FCGS). Recommended treatment options, including surgical and medical management, will be covered. Discussion of the management of refractory FCGS will include the definition of this term, followed by presentation of the results of clinical trials using uterine-derived stem cells to treat cats with refractory FCGS.

courses.title: Palliative Care for the Cancer Patient and The Focus on Quality Over Quantity
courses.description: Patients with cancer suffer from a broad range of clinical signs both from their cancer itself and from the treatment. Palliative care focuses on the alleviation of those clinical signs in order to maintain a good quality of life. This course will help define palliation and discuss a multitude of options available to help patients and their families.

courses.title: How Am I Supposed To Breathe With No Air? Understanding Upper Respiratory Disease
courses.description: This course will cover the different common types of upper airway disease seen in veterinary medicine. It will focus on brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome, laryngeal paralysis, tracheal collapse, and feline laryngeal disease. It is important that nurses are able to identify the different types of airway crises quickly, effectively, and know first steps in stabilization.

courses.title: Feline Chronic Gingivostomatitis and Mesenchymal Stem Cells
courses.description: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) are multipotent cells and reside in most organs and tissues such as bone marrow, uterus, and adipose tissue. Furthermore, MSC has a profound regenerative ability attributed in part to their ability to modulate both innate and adaptive immunity. A major effort by our multidisciplinary group over the past 13 years investigating systemic MSC therapy for cats with FCGS yielded paradigm changes in understanding of the disease. This lecture will discuss the general concept of MSC immunomodulation therapy as well as the clinical outcome of MSC therapy for cats with FCGS. Moreover, with the emerging field of regenerative medicine, this lecture will inform the practitioners on the practicability of stem cell therapy for FCGS and the ongoing clinical trial conducted by Gallant in an effort to bring this therapy to clinical practice.

courses.title: The Professional Dental Prophylaxis: From Start to Finish
courses.description: This program will cover the details of the prophylaxis component of a COHAT (Comprehensive Oral Health Assessment and Treatment). Attendees will learn the purpose of this treatment and how it integrates into the COHAT. Details of dental prophylaxis will include both professional scaling and polishing. Within these topics; technique, instrumentation, and evaluation of treatment will be covered.

courses.title: Pharmacology and Medical Math for Technicians
courses.description: Veterinary technicians play a vital role in patient care through careful assessment, planning, implementation, evaluation, and documentation of pharmacy orders. Technicians must accurately perform calculations and conversions to ensure patient safety and drug efficacy. This course reviews algebraic functions, conversions, and common pharmacology equations used in the veterinary hospital.

courses.title: Paws and Breathe: Understanding Pulmonary Parenchymal Disease
courses.description: Disease of the pulmonary parenchyma can vary in causes, development, treatments, and outcome. It is essential that veterinary staff can recognize respiratory distress, fatigue, and failure, recognize and identify the different types of pulmonary parenchymal disease, possible treatment plans, and provide diligent nursing care. This one hour course will cover basic respiratory mechanics and physiology, control of breathing, hypoxia vs. hypoxemia, types of pulmonary parenchymal disease and pathogenesis, and possible treatments that may be performed. We will also discuss a case example and a brief overview of the mechanical ventilator.

courses.title: Advancements in Calf Scour Prevention: New Data on USDA-Labeled Polyclonal Bovine Colostrum Antibody Technology for On-Label
courses.description: This course delves into the critical role of scour prevention and explores the various prevention strategies currently available. The primary emphasis will be on the use of bovine-derived maternal colostrum antibodies to prevent neonatal calf scours. Participants will gain comprehensive insights into the production process of these antibodies, the scope of available data both published and unpublished and the level of protection they offer against scours and other neonatal calf diseases. The course will also address both on-label and off-label uses, alongside a thorough review of internal and external data sources.

courses.title: They're Heating Up - Pathophysiology and Treatment Options for Heat Stroke
courses.description: This informative lecture provides a comprehensive overview of heat stroke in companion animals. Participants will gain a deep understanding of the underlying physiological processes that occur during heat stroke, including thermoregulation breakdown, cellular damage, and multi-organ dysfunction. We will explore the clinical signs associated with heat stroke, and review the latest evidence-based approaches for diagnosis and treatment. This course will focus on practical strategies for managing these critical patients, covering fluid therapy, cooling techniques, monitoring, and supportive care.

courses.title: Management of Lower Airway Disease in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Lower airway disease is a common presenting complaint in dogs and cats presenting to the emergency room. Recognition of these diseases allows for appropriate stabilization and management. This course will discuss some of the most common lower airway diseases seen in small animals, including feline asthma, chronic bronchitis, tracheal collapse and bronchomalacia.

courses.title: Nutritional management of the Comorbid CKD Cat
courses.description: We will review basic nutritional goals & nutrients of concern for cats with CKD and a few comorbid conditions, including inflammatory bowel disease, diabetes mellitus, and obesity. This will be a case-based discussion with emphasis on practical clinical decision making.

courses.title: Disorders of Water Balance: SIADH and DI
courses.description: Disorders of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) disrupt normal water balance and can lead to life-threatening abnormalities in serum sodium. Dysnatremias have been associated with increased mortality in patients in the ICU, underscoring the importance of recognition and appropriate management of these disorders. This course will discuss the underlying pathophysiology, clinical features, and treatment of syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH) and diabetes insipidus (DI), including best practices for managing severe sodium disorders.

courses.title: Feline Chronic Gingivostomatitis - Current Concepts in Clinical Management
courses.description: Feline Gingivostomatitis (FCGS) is a debilitating, chronic inflammatory oral mucosal disease that affects 0.7%-26% of domestic cats. For over 3 decades, the etiology of feline chronic gingivostomatitis (FCGS) has been considered elusive and challenging. The current etiologic theories for FCGS include: an immune response to chronic antigenic stimulation, chronic viral infection(s), and a potential genetic predisposition. Without knowledge of the etiology of FCGS, as clinicians, we have focused on symptomatic and/or aggressive treatment options that may not lead to a cure. No single treatment has achieved a clinical success rate close to 100%, and cats that fail to respond to treatment require lifelong medical management or euthanasia. This lecture will review historical knowledge of FCGS as well as discuss the most recent updates related to the etiopathogenesis and treatment of this disease.

courses.title: Ok, It's 2025; Do we FINALLY have a perfect way to differentiate IBD vs. GI Lymphoma?
courses.description: This talk will focus on cats, but for many points, it applies to dogs. We will evaluate techniques to optimize the diagnosis of IBD vs. LGITL in cats and dogs, including advances in ultrasound interpretation, endoscopic utilization and additional testing following standard light microscopy.

courses.title: The Do's and Don'ts of Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
courses.description: This course provides a well-rounded perspective of identification of cardiopulmonary arrest, action steps to perform CPR in a successful manor in conjunction with the latest 2024 RECOVER guidelines, and anticipating which patients are at the greatest risk of experiencing cardiopulmonary arrest.

courses.title: Code Cortisol - When the Adrenal Alarm Doesn't Sound: Recognizing and Responding to CIRCI in the Critically Ill
courses.description:
This continuing education nursing CE program reviews Critical Illness-Related Corticosteroid Insufficiency (CIRCI) in dogs and cats, with emphasis on physiology, pathophysiology, and bedside recognition in the veterinary ICU. Participants will review hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis function, adrenal gland anatomy, and the role of cortisol in maintaining vascular tone, metabolic stability, and inflammatory regulation during critical illness.
The lecture will examine how critical illness disrupt cortisol signaling and contribute to vasopressor-resistant hypotension. Diagnostic considerations, interpretation of adrenal function testing, and principles of physiologic-dose hydrocortisone therapy will be discussed. Special focus will be placed on hemodynamic monitoring, blood pressure interpretation (macro- versus microcirculation), vasopressor responsiveness, urine output trends, thermoregulation, and nursing assessment strategies in patients with suspected CIRCI.
This lecture is intended for veterinary technicians and veterinary nurses practicing in emergency and critical care, as well as those working in general practice who wish to strengthen their understanding of shock physiology, endocrine stress adaptation, and monitoring in small animal patients.

courses.title: Thoracic Radiology: Pleural and Mediastinal Anatomy and Pathology
courses.description: Participants will review radiographic anatomy with special emphasis on the pleural and mediastinal spaces. Normal variations in dogs and cats will be discussed, followed by case examples illustrating classic examples of pleural and mediastinal pathologies including pleural effusion, pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, esophageal dilation, and mediastinal soft tissue masses. Special attention will be paid to normal variations that can be mistaken for pathology. If time permits, more unusual patient pathologies will be included.

courses.title: Effectiveness of USDA-Approved Scour Vaccines: Insights from Research and Practical Applications in Neonatal Calf Care
courses.description: This course provides an overview of scour prevention strategies for neonatal calves, with a particular emphasis on scour vaccines and the available data on disease prevention. It serves as a comprehensive refresher, blending established approaches to scour prevention with insights from recently published studies.

courses.title: Fluid Therapy: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
courses.description: This lecture will focus on normal physiology of body fluid, composition and fluid shifts in states of disease. Fluid therapy involving crystalloids, colloids, hypertonic saline, as well as blood products will be discussed. Side effects of fluid administration will be covered. Case examples will be given to discuss common scenarios.

courses.title: Take a Deep Breath: Respiratory Emergencies of Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This course covers physiology and action of breathing. This course also covers respiratory emergencies of dogs and cats. Lastly the course covers therapies including, oxygen therapy and medications to treat respiratory emergencies.

courses.title: From Pressure to Obstruction: Understanding Pulmonary Vascular Disorders in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This session will cover fundamentals of pulmonary vascular disorders for the for the veterinary nurse, with a focus on pulmonary hypertension and pulmonary thromboembolism. We will discuss the relevant physiology, pathophysiology, assessment, stabilization, diagnostics, treatment and monitoring of cats and dogs with these conditions.

courses.title: Ocular Adnexal Procedures: Eyelids, Third Eyelids, and Nasolacrimal Ducts
courses.description: This lecture will cover diagnosis, treatment options, owner counseling, and procedure tips for adnexal conditions including entropion, third eyelid gland prolapse, straightforward eyelid neoplasms, and nasolacrimal disease.

courses.title: Regenerative Medicine Fundamentals: Stem Cell Science for Real-World Use
courses.description: This lecture will describe the progression from the 'old way' of regenerative medicine, using stem cells sourced from the patient, toward the 'new way' of regenerative medicine, sourcing stem cells from healthy donors to provide ready-to-use, off-the-shelf therapies for any pet in need. The types, sources, and methods of administration of stem cells will be discussed. The potential mechanisms of action for stem cell modulation of the immune system and repair of tissue will be discussed.

courses.title: Practicing Sustainable Antibiotic Use in Cats
courses.description: This session will provide an overview of the principles of antimicrobial stewardship, common challenges of antimicrobial stewardship encountered in feline practice, and practical solutions to improve stewardship in your practice based on recent research. We will review antimicrobial use guidelines, the use of diagnostic testing in antimicrobial decisions, and how to interpret culture and sensitivity test results. Finally, you will leave with communication strategies to help you partner with cat owners for sustainable antimicrobial use.

courses.title: Spread Your Wings: Pelvic Radiographic Techniques and Interpretation
courses.description: The pelvis is an anatomically complex region that can be challenging to image and interpret, and which presents a range of pathologies for pets of all life stages. Acquisition of diagnostic radiographs requires anticipation of appropriate patient preparation, familiarity with correct patient positioning (and re-positioning) and radiographic technique, and an understanding of the application of specialized views. Once images are made, interpretation relies on understanding of normal anatomy, including at various stages of skeletal maturation, and the types of pathology that may arise from this region. This course will begin by addressing the unique challenges of imaging the pelvis, focusing on how to refine technique and "troubleshoot" images for maximal diagnostic quality. After a review of normal anatomy, it will then explore diagnosis of commonly encountered conditions evaluated with pelvic radiography, ranging from pediatric to geriatric dogs and cats. This will include a discussion of the widely used hip scoring systems offered by PennHIP and Orthopedic Foundation for Animals (OFA), since general practitioners may be commonly asked to submit to these organizations.

courses.title: Healing with Light: Laser Therapy for Mobility, Pain, & Beyond
courses.description: Expand your understanding of the clinical benefits of Class IV laser therapy for the veterinary rehabilitation specialist. Dr. Rachel Cain overviews the science behind laser therapy and its impact on the body's natural healing processes while offering practical information on clinical applications, including case examples from her practice.

courses.title: Advancing Veterinary Microbiome Medicine: Insights from ACVIM & Beyond
courses.description: This panel webinar focuses on highlighting cutting-edge developments in gut microbiome research and applications. Panelsists will discuss insights shared during the 2024 ACVIM conference, discuss critical studies within the realm of the microbiome in companion pets, as well as discuss next-gen technologies and the effectiveness of microbiome-focused diagnostics compared to traditional methods. This webinar aims to provide comprehensive coverage of recent advancements in microbiome medicine, including insights into diagnostic and research methodologies within the veterinary microbiome field.

courses.title: Cracking the Code: Localizing Respiratory Disorders in the ER
courses.description: This lecture is designed for veterinary nurses working in emergency and critical care settings, including veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and veterinary nurses. The course will focus on the identification, assessment, and acute management of respiratory emergencies in small animals, emphasizing rapid intervention and best practices to ensure optimal outcomes for critically ill patients in the emergency room (ER).

courses.title: Chest Wall and Diaphragmatic Disease in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth introduction to disease of the chest wall and diaphragm of the dog and cat. We will review the pertinent anatomy and physiology followed by a number of commonly encountered conditions including congenital disease, neoplasia, and trauma to the chest wall and diaphragm. Basic pathophysiology, presentation, and management of each condition will be discussed.

courses.title: SANSTEP: Spay And Neuter Surgical Training & Education Program
courses.description: A 3-day interactive, medical program with 1 day of lecture and 2 days of surgical wet-lab with attendees performing spay and neuter surgeries on live dogs and cats under the direct supervision of and training by a HVHQSN surgeon, in a HVHQSN facility, with the support of a HVHQSN veterinary team that is solely dedicated to the SANSTEP attendees.

courses.title: When Sugar Becomes Toxic: Understanding DKA & HHS
courses.description: This presentation is designed for veterinarians and veterinary nurses to strengthen their understanding of diabetic emergencies, specifically DKA and HHS, and how nursing care directly impacts patient outcomes. Participants will learn to recognize key clinical signs, understand diagnostic criteria, and participate confidently in treatment planning, including fluid therapy, electrolyte monitoring, and insulin administration. The session will highlight differences between DKA and HHS, how to identify complications early, and how to communicate patient needs effectively. By the end, participants will be better equipped to support critical diabetic patients and improve overall case management and prognosis.

courses.title: When the Pump Fails: Mechanisms of Heart Failure
courses.description: Heart failure is a very common disease process in our veterinary patients, and a common cause of respiratory distress. It is essential that veterinary staff can appropriately identify a patient that may be in heart failure and understand its treatment. This one-hour course will cover basic cardiac physiology, mechanisms of heart failure, and basic overview of the Frank-Starling curve. Types of heart failure, classification system of heart failure, and pharmacology will also be discussed.

courses.title: Aging in the Dog: Foundations for feeding and supplementing the Geriatric Canine
courses.description: There are many maladies that affect the geriatric canine in general including loss of lean mass, cognitive decline and mobility issues. The senior patient has slightly different requirements for feeding and supplementation for these common geriatric issues depending on the pathologies present that often require adjustments in protein, fat, specific fatty acid and potentially antioxidant intake to help optimize health. As musculoskeletal issues plague many geriatric patients there are food additives or supplements that can mitigate lean mass loss and potentiate better mobility long term that should be considered.

courses.title: Under Pressure: Thyroid Emergencies
courses.description: This course covers the most common thyroid emergencies in dogs and cats and review of common thyroid disorders in small animals. We will discuss the pathophysiology, diagnostics, and treatment options of thyroid crisis in dogs and cats presenting to the emergency department.

courses.title: Stuck Between a Lung and a Hard Place: Tackling Pleural Space Disease
courses.description: This comprehensive continuing education program is designed to equip veterinary professionals with in-depth knowledge and practical skills to recognize, manage and treat pleural space diseases effectively. Covering a wide range of conditions such as pneumothorax, pyothorax, chylothorax, and diaphragmatic hernias, this course emphasizes evidence-based approaches to patient care.

courses.title: Urgent and emergent medicine
courses.description: In this seminar, Drs Beltran, Maggs and Johnson will present a complete discussion of the common emergency clinical problems that they encounter in their individual practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of the problems. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common problems- both emergent and urgent care management. The three specialists will bring case examples highlighting the triage, stabilization and management of these dynamic and challenging cases.

courses.title: Feline Chronic Gingivostomatitis
courses.description: Feline chronic gingivostomatitis is a painful immune-mediated disease that can be challenging to treat. This can mean ongoing discomfort for our feline patients and frustration for our clients. This program covers diagnosis of feline chronic gingivostomatitis, step-wise treatment decision-making, as well as expected prognosis.

courses.title: Adrenal Tumors with Attitude: Pheochromocytomas in Small Animals
courses.description: This one-hour lecture reviews pheochromocytomas in dogs and cats. The relevant anatomy and pathophysiology of the adrenal glands, catecholamines, and adrenergic receptors is reviewed. This is followed by an in-depth discussion, based in relevant peer-reviewed literature, of the diagnosis and management of pheochromocytomas. It concludes with a thorough discussion of anesthetic management and post-operative management, with key points especially for technicians. Arterial blood pressure monitoring is briefly reviewed as well.

courses.title: Exotic Vet Academy: 2025 May-October Semester
courses.description:
The inspiration for the Exotic Vet Academy came from recognizing that many veterinarians worldwide cannot regularly attend the major exotics conferences in the US and Europe. This often limits their access to the latest advances and information in exotic animal medicine. As an author, I have seen firsthand how quickly textbook content can become outdated. My goal with the Academy is to create a platform that makes knowledge sharing faster, easier, and far more accessible, empowering any veterinarian, anywhere in the world, to stay current and confident in their exotic animal practice.
The Academy's curriculum is modeled after a traditional university semester, providing a structured, steady, and engaging learning experience. The 2025 May to October semester consists of 26 hours of live, interactive webinars, approximately one hour per week, each supported by supplementary materials and activities to reinforce learning and participation.
This program is designed for veterinarians seeking to improve and update their knowledge and skills in exotic animal medicine. The content is suitable for both those preparing for specialist board exams of the ACZM, ABVP or EZCM and those wishing to keep up with current best practices and research.
The objectives are to provide a comprehensive, up-to-date foundation in the medicine, surgery, and husbandry of exotic mammals, birds, and reptiles, to enable participants to apply the latest evidence-based practices to clinical cases in exotic animal medicine, to prepare attendees for advanced examinations by covering core topics and referencing the most recent peer-reviewed literature, and to foster critical thinking and peer-to-peer learning through interactive sessions, case discussions, and QA.
The curriculum covers Rabbits and Rodents for 23 hours, including Anatomy, Physiology, and Husbandry of Rabbits and Rodents for 3 hours, Anesthesia and Sedation of Rabbits and Rodents for 4 hours, Analgesia of Rabbits and Rodents for 2 hours, H

courses.title: Interventional Urinary Cases: Imaging and Different Management Options
courses.description: This lecture will focus on imaging findings and management options for ureteral and urethral obstructions. Medical and surgical management options will be reviewed, with a focus on the use of interventional therapies.

courses.title: Pneumonia in Dogs and Cats: Nothing To Cough At!
courses.description: This lecture will provide an overview of pneumonia in dogs and cats and will aim to cover pathophysiology of aspiration and community-acquired pneumonia in these species. In addition, major pathogens implicated, clinical presentation, diagnostic modalities and treatments will be discussed.

courses.title: Aggression in Dogs: Who Does It, and What Can We Do About It?
courses.description: This course covers the general topic of canine aggression.
