Specifically, it will cover the types of dogs likely to present for aggression, the safety measure that should be put in place and behavioral and pharmacological treatments that may lower aggression. The topic of euthanasia and when to recommend it will be discussed.

courses.title: Wound Healing and Wound Care: Getting back to basics
courses.description:
The variety of wound-care products out there are almost as infinite as the number of wounds we treat as veterinarians! How do you decide which materials to apply to which wounds? When's the right time to plan for surgical closure? How do we handle antibiotic resistant infections?
This video course is here to answer all these questions and more! Join Dr. Sarah Marvel for clear advice on wound care, that you'll be able to implement right away in practice.

courses.title: Fear Free Companion Animal Euthanasia Course
courses.description: Every pet's final visit to the veterinarian should be as Fear Free as the first. In this one-hour module, you will learn how to utilize pre-planning to create a meaningful and low-stress experience for pet and owner. It will cover uses of pre-euthanasia sedation and anesthesia to give the pet a gentle euthanasia and the benefits and downsides of different euthanasia techniques. Also explored will be the dangers of compassion fatigue and hot to prevent or alleviate it.

courses.title: The Path to a Great Bath
courses.description: Bath time is scary for many animals - whether it's the sound of the water, the feel of it on their skin, being restrained, or the tub itself. This one-hour module will teach you how to break down the bathing process into individual components that can be worked on separately, to allow for calmer, safer bathing experiences. We will provide step-by-step desensitization and counter-conditioning plans for every component - from introducing the shampoo bottle, to entering the tub, to introducing water, to the sound and feel of the dryer. You'll also learn what you can do to modify the bathing environment to make it more inviting and less stressful for animals.

courses.title: VetQuest Travel CE Hopsice & Palliative Care Medicine
courses.description:
This will be over 3 days and include
Saturday 1-2pm: It's Not Just Another 2:00 Euthanasia
Saturday 2:10-3pm: Making the "Comfort" Room Truly Comforting & Experiential
Saturday 5-6pm: Common (and easy!) Integrative Medicine Tools for Your Palliative Care Toolbox
Sunday 11-11:50am: Unraveling Frailty Syndrome: A Clinical Compass for Managing the Aging Patient
Sunday 12-12:50am: Translating Quality of Life: Tools to Guide Clients Through the Toughest Decisions
Monday 11-11:50am: Comfort First: Evolving Strategies for Pain Management in Hospice and Palliative Care
Monday 12-12:50pm: Ketamine in Comfort Care: Case Studies in Veterinary Hospice and Palliative Medicine

courses.title: Complete Compounding Guidance: Balancing Benefits, Managing Risks, and Choosing the Right Pharmacy
courses.description: This 2 hour course will feature two one hour lectures on common drug compounding topics covering risks, providing clinical framework, patient fit criteria and practical guidance on what to look for when partnering with a compounding pharmacy for veterinarians. Part 1 (1 Hour CE): Balancing Benefits and Risks Reviews pros and cons of commonly compounded drugs; delineates risks associated with their use. Provides a framework for evaluating when compounded products are appropriate and criteria to ensure a compounded preparation best fits an individual patient's needs. Compounded Medications, Part 2 (1 Hour CE): Risky Dosage Forms Defines characteristics that render certain dosage forms high risk, with an emphasis on additional considerations for transdermal compounds. Concludes with practical guidance on what to look for when selecting a compounding pharmacy.

courses.title: Complete Compounding Guidance: Balancing Benefits, Managing Risks, and Choosing the Right Pharmacy
courses.description: This 2 hour course will feature two one hour lectures on common drug compounding topics covering risks, providing clinical framework, patient fit criteria and practical guidance on what to look for when partnering with a compounding pharmacy for veterinarians. Part 1 (1 Hour CE): Balancing Benefits and Risks Reviews pros and cons of commonly compounded drugs; delineates risks associated with their use. Provides a framework for evaluating when compounded products are appropriate and criteria to ensure a compounded preparation best fits an individual patient's needs. Compounded Medications, Part 2 (1 Hour CE): Risky Dosage Forms Defines characteristics that render certain dosage forms high risk, with an emphasis on additional considerations for transdermal compounds. Concludes with practical guidance on what to look for when selecting a compounding pharmacy.

courses.title: From Vision to Ownership: Strategic Steps for Starting, Acquiring or Expanding a Veterinary Practice
courses.description:
If practice ownership or optimization is on your horizon whether youre considering a start-up, an acquisition, or expanding into a new location this panel is designed to help you understand what the journey actually looks like in real life. Rather than talk in generalities, our experts will walk you through concrete examples of how veterinarians like you evaluate opportunities, shape a business plan, and make decisions that support longterm success.
Drawing on more than 75 combined years of handson experience across the veterinary and healthcare industries, the panel will break down the practical steps, tradeoffs, and strategic considerations involved in moving from aspiration to ownership. Youll come away with insights you can immediately apply to your own situation and the clarity to talk with colleagues about what works, what doesnt, and how to approach your next move with purpose. This is applied learning built to support your strategic goals, not just theory.

courses.title: Invasive Aspergillosis and Other Invasive Mold Infections in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: This presentation will include discussion on the epidemiology, clinical findings, diagnosis, treatment and treatment monitoring of sino-nasal, sino-orbital, and systemic aspergillosis in dogs and cats. Other invasive mold infections will also be discussed, where appropriate.

courses.title: Behavioral Euthanasia - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Making the decision to euthanize a dog or cat for aggression can be ethically challenging for many people. We usually associate euthanasia with physically ill pets who no longer have a good quality of life and see this as a kind choice to end suffering. However, QoL is not just about physical health it is about mental health. Animals that are extremely fearful or anxious and show aggressive behavior are also ill. They have a poor quality of life because they cannot be trusted to have social interactions with people or other animals and may need to be contained in inappropriate housing. They key to a smooth and safe euthanasia for these patients is planning and communication with the owner. These appointments are often easier to do in the pet's home environment due to the difficulty of transporting them to a clinic and the additional stress and dangers involved. Once a Veterinary Client Patient Relationship is established, pre-visit drugs starting the day before the appointment are recommended and given by the owner. Drugs include gabapentin, trazodone, phenobarbital and melatonin. A hungry animal is more likely to eat food with drugs in it, choose high value food and treats, minimize noise, activity and the number of people in the area and leave the pet undisturbed after drugs have been administered. Additional sedation is usually required prior to euthanasia and this may involve more oral drugs or if the patient can be managed safely or a muzzle placed, injectable drugs. When the pet is no longer reacting to external stimuli, we can proceed with euthanasia.

courses.title: Practicing Quality Dentistry: What to Do with What you See
courses.description: Using both radiographic and photographic images, registrants will be guided through the diagnosis and management of both simple and complex clinical cases of dental disease in dogs and cats.

courses.title: Cardiac Level 1: Echocardiographic Examinations: Nuts & Bolts - Online
courses.description: : This course will cover all right sided imaging planes - the core of an echocardiographic examination - as well as the left sided right auricular view. Subjective and objective evaluation of these images are covered. At completion of this course the attendee will be able to recognize all right sided imaging planes, understand the principles of obtaining these images, obtain critical measurements and understand their usefulness in the assessment of cardiac disease. This is a Medicine, non-interactive distance class.

courses.title: 7 Strategies to Calm Angry Clients
courses.description: Your schedule is packed, your team is stretched thin, and now an irate client is raising her voice, again. Get practical, ready-to-use scripts and proven techniques to defuse tension, maintain professionalism, and turn confrontations into constructive conversations. Learn how to stay composed, set boundaries, and protect team morale, even on the toughest days.

courses.title: Wound Closure Academy III: Tips, Tricks, & Suture Resources
courses.description: This hands-on webinar will demonstrate the key approaches to the most commonly used suturing and knot-tying techniques.

courses.title: Making Sense of Mechanical Ventilation in Veterinary Anesthesia
courses.description: Mechanical ventilation is a critical component of modern veterinary anesthesia, yet many anesthesia providers lack confidence in selecting appropriate ventilator settings and troubleshooting respiratory complications. This interactive, case-based wet lab is designed to provide participants with practical experience applying mechanical ventilation principles to a variety of canine and feline anesthetic patients. Working in small groups, participants will evaluate patient signalments, anesthetic considerations, and physiologic parameters to develop individualized ventilator strategies using both volume-driven and advanced anesthesia ventilators.

courses.title: Certificate Course: Creating A Life You Love
courses.description:
This four-part certificate course is designed for anyone who wants to ditch the things that are holding you back from living a happy life, from achieving work-life balance, or from reaching your goals. Learn how to let go of whatever's in your way, figure out what you really want, and set realistic goals to get you there.
This course will introduce evidence-based methods to manage feelings of burnout, compassion fatigue, and other problems commonly encountered in a veterinary practice setting. In addition, the concepts of perfectionism and imposter syndrome will be defined, and we will discuss ways to help problems that arise from each. Finally, we'll hear advice on goal-setting, utilizing the other concepts learned throughout the course to understand more realistic ways to set and reach goals.
Attendees will actively participate in each session, through independent writing activities, guided meditations and other exercises, to solidify the concepts presented. Upon completing the workshop, attendees will have better awareness of the role that burnout, compassion fatigue, perfectionism, and imposter syndrome may play in their own life and career, and will come to understand concrete methods for managing the problems associated with each.

courses.title: WONJI- Working ON Not Just IN Your Practice
courses.description: Veterinarians and their teams are so deeply embedded in the day-to-day tasks of running a practice that they lose sight of their vision, mission, and core values. Assuming that they have them. Those practices that are most successful will WONJI. What is WONJI- -Working ON Not Just IN their practices. Learn how to WONJI to set your path for success.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Canine Parvovirus increasing survival. Updates on Vaccinations and Therapeutics
courses.description:
Canine parvoviral enteritis is a highly contagious viral disease of puppies that causes haemorrhagic diarrhoea and is still one of the most common causes of morbidity and mortality in dogs. Whilst in some individuals the symptoms can be mild, in many cases it can be fatal, especially if left untreated or caught too late. It is a significant disease in shelters and lower income areas however it is widespread, especially among unvaccinated animals. Treatment is generally supportive with variable prognosis, and vaccination remains the most effective means of preventing the disease.
One of the challenges with vaccinations is the unknown level and duration of maternal antibodies and the risk of exposure between them wearing off and the vaccinations taking effect. However, the advent of the newest vaccination from MSD breaks through maternal antibodies and may provide protection from 4 weeks old.
There have been advances in treatments too, will the recent USDA provisionally approved canine parvovirus monoclonal antibody treatment be as successful in reducing the burden of supportive care as we hope
Join us for a stimulating and informative discussion with a multidisciplinary panel of international specialists while they discuss and debate the most effective methods of increasing survival in these patients, as well as the game changing advancements that have recently been made in the vaccinations and therapeutics available for this disease

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Orthopaedics 101 - decision making for long bone fracture repair of the trauma patient
courses.description:
Long bone fractures are a common challenge in both referral and private practice, often resulting from trauma. These fractures vary widely in severity, from simple greenstick fractures in young, growing puppies to complex comminuted fractures requiring advanced stabilization.
Veterinarians must rapidly assess these cases, determine the most appropriate stabilization method, choose the right surgical techniques, and recognize when referral may be the best option. Making these critical decisions efficiently is an essential skill for any practitioner.
Join an esteemed international panel of experts from multiple disciplines as they discuss the decision making process behind fracture management. This engaging and interactive discussion will cover assessment strategies, surgical approaches, and key considerations for specific repair techniques. Audience participation is encouraged bring your questions and gain valuable insights from leaders in the field.
¿

courses.title: The ACVIM Consensus on Canine Mitral Valve Disease Management. What is new and different in 2024-25?
courses.description: This course covers an overview of the ACVIM consensus guidelines on canine mitral valve disease management, case examples, medical management, the clinical studies supporting the medical management, and what has changed or what might be different now since the last consensus statement.

courses.title: The Addisonian in Crisis: The First Few Hours
courses.description: Addison's disease is less common than other conditions that have similar clinical presentations; this makes recognizing and diagnosing dogs with hypoadrenocorticism somewhat challenging. In this webinar we will cover the common signalment, historical, physical examination, and laboratory findings in dogs in Addisonian crisis. We will discuss initial treatment, definitive diagnosis, and early "longer term" management.

courses.title: Why did my ExCap Surgery Fail?
courses.description: Extracapsular stabilization is one of the most common surgeries performed for Cranial Cruciate Ligament (CrCL) disease in general practice. Although straightforward in principle, there are many pitfalls of the procedure and patient selection that can affect outcome. This session highlights key points in patient selection and execution of the surgery to optimize success.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Nutritional Management of the Thin/Starved Animal
courses.description:
Poor condition in horses arises from a multitude of causes including those associated with direct human behavior (ranging from deliberate neglect to ignorance) as well as many clinical conditions including those associated with various gastro-intestinal, dental, renal and hepatic issues. In some cases, the underlying cause(s) are fairly obvious but for many, the veterinary clinician will be required to undertake a detailed, logical, stepwise and holistic approach to the case.
Join our international multidisciplinary team of world-leading experts as they discuss their approach to these cases and share their wealth of experience. They will discuss and debate how nutrition can be a part of the cause as well as part of the solution and how it is essential in the successful rehabilitation of these horses. This panel discussion will outline the approach to the thin/starved animal and consider how best to utilize feeds and feeding management in their short- and long-term management.

courses.title: Common Ocular Emergencies in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Ocular pathologies are commonly encountered in small animal practice and the variety of problems, and their complexity presents a constant challenge for the general practitioner. The most common causes for ocular disease are infectious or traumatic. However, many times we are challenged by autoimmune, metabolic, neoplastic, and idiopathic diseases, many of which can present with ocular pain or significant discomfort, loss of vision and/or compromise in the integrity of the eyeball and/or its adnexa. Inappropriate management can lead to rapid permanently impaired vision. This course will provide the basic knowledge and necessary tools to address the most common ophthalmic presentations and emergencies in small animal practice, explore potential differential diagnoses, describer appropriate first line therapy and provide guidelines on when to refer patients to a specialist. Further, indicated diagnostic tests the initial prognosis will be discussed.

courses.title: Webinar - Vomiting and Diarrhoea - Triage and Approach in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: Dogs and cats presenting with acute vomiting, diarrhea, other gastrointestinal signs and abdominal pain are some of the most common complaints for patients presenting for emergency care. On presentation, it is important to differentiate between a likely self-limiting case versus a more concerning patient which requires further diagnostics immediately. A thorough history and a good clinical exam will allow the clinician to differentiate these cases and allow for the correct decisions to be made. Join us for this interactive panel discussion where our multidisciplinary group of internal medicine and emergency & critical care specialists and experienced general and emergency room (ER) veterinarians will discuss and debate these concepts including how they approach more challenging presentations in their different clinical settings, and from their different perspectives

courses.title: Advanced Dental Procedures
courses.description: Tooth extraction is not necessarily the optimal solution to many dental diseases. Learn multiple options for treatment beyond tooth extraction.

courses.title: From Microscope to Medication: Using Ear Cytology for Ingredient-Based Treatment of Otitis
courses.description: In this non-interactive webinar we will be discussing Topical therapy is the treatment of choice for most cases of otitis. Higher concentrations of medication are achieved through topical administration compared to systemic routes. Topical therapy also delivers the medication directly to the affected area. With resistant bacteria constantly on the rise, it is essential to be judicious about the use of antibiotics in cases of skin and ear infections. This includes using otic cytology to know what organisms are causing the infection. Learn the importance of working up cases of otitis and how product selection is key based on your cytology findings.

courses.title: Take a Walk on the Wild Side: A review of poisoning risks and cases involving wildlife and non-traditional pets
courses.description: Beyond dogs and cats, this webinar will focus on the other animals, non-traditional pets and wildlife that share our indoor and outdoor spaces. We will examine toxicity risks for these species, including pesticides and rodenticides, human medications, toxic foods, and cleaning products, typically because of their interactions with humans. We will discuss mitigation of these risks and using a case-based approach, will discuss assessment and treatment of exposures.

courses.title: Bovine Artificial Insemination and Embryo Transfer Training Course
courses.description: Topics covered during this 6 day course are conventional ET and AI techniques, superovulation of donors and synchronization protocols, lab protocols, evaluation of embryos, freezing, thawing and transfer of embryos as well as nutrition and genetics. Students who choose the AI/ET combined option will attend the complete duration of the course. The option for students to just come for the embryo transfer course is available for those that are already proficient in AI, in which they would only attend Wednesday through Saturday.

courses.title: Titer Testing in Practice: Understanding Immunity and Guiding Vaccination Protocols
courses.description: In this lecture, participants will explore the clinical applications of antibody titer testing for core vaccines in dogs and cats. The session will review key immunologic principles, including secondary and sterilizing immunity, vaccine types, and duration of immunity (DOI) studies for modified-live vaccines. Attendees will gain an understanding of titer testing for CPV, CDV, CAV and FPV and how these tests can be integrated into current vaccination protocols. Special consideration will be given to puppies and kittens (maternal antibody interference), vaccine risk groups (autoimmune disease, immunosuppressive therapy, adverse vaccine reactions), and senior pets (immunosenescence). The session will emphasize how titer testing supports individualized vaccination strategies The lecture will also compare laboratory-based and in-house titer testing methods, outlining their advantages, limitations, and clinical applications. Finally, will conclude with practical answers to common clinical questions.

courses.title: How to Maximize Your Dental Practice ON-DEMAND
courses.description: This lecture provides a practical, actionable framework for elevating veterinary dentistry by walking participants through an optimal dental practice checklist that highlights the key elements of an efficient, profitable, and high-quality dental service. It will cover essential equipment and medical recommendations, along with targeted training strategies for both veterinarians and support staff. Attendees will learn how to leverage their PIMS for scheduling, communication, and workflow efficiency. The session will also address pricing considerations that reflect value and sustainability, and will conclude with practical methods for measuring success so practices can track clinical quality, efficiency, and financial impact over time.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Management of Acute Pancreatitis in Dogs
courses.description: This webinar will focus on the clinical presentation of acute pancreatitis in dogs, including pancreatitis-associated bile duct obstruction (PABDO), describe the optimal diagnostic approach to the disease, the value of different diagnostic tools, and provide an update on current treatment options.

courses.title: Gaining Dental Compliance
courses.description: Over 80% of adult dogs and cats have some form of oral disease. Is your practice currently performing dental procedures on that percentage of your patients? Learn ways to explain and communicate the importance of good oral health to your clients and to take dentistry to the next level in your practice and fill those tables!

courses.title: Prescribing with Purpose: How to Manage Ear-rational otitis
courses.description: Topical therapy is the treatment of choice for most cases of otitis. Higher concentrations of medication are achieved through topical administration compared to systemic routes. Topical therapy also delivers the medication directly to the affected area. With resistant bacteria constantly on the rise, it is essential to be judicious about the use of antibiotics in cases of skin and ear infections. Learn the importance of working up cases of straightforward and difficult otitis. Also, how product selection is key for the cases you see today and in the future.

courses.title: Managing common medical problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with common medical problems. The combination of two Internal Medicine Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in their daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Fur Real! Weekly skin care secrets from Veterinary Dermatologist
courses.description: In this lecture skin care recommendations for maintenance and prevention of dermatological conditions will be reviewed.

courses.title: Dog longevity 301: The ultimate deep dive into metabolic health, clinical lab monitoring, and extending healthy lifespan
courses.description: This program will take a detailed look at metabolic dysfunction, one of the major drivers of the age-related decline in health and quality of life in dogs. We will examine how changes in insulin sensitivity, body fat, and blood lipids affect both routine clinical lab values and both healthspan and lifespan in dogs. We will also compare the existing evidence for dogs and humans to identify similarities, differences, and knowledge gaps. Finally, we will consider the clinical implications of these processes for monitoring and treating senior dogs.

courses.title: Implementing a Successful Weight Loss Program (On Demand)
courses.description: This talk will cover the process of designing specific weight loss programs for pets, assessing the effectiveness of ongoing recommendations to maintain long-term success, and developing strategies to address common barriers to weight management. Additionally, it will explore client preferences for communication in various clinical decision-making contexts and identify key weight-related attributes during veterinarian-client conversations.

courses.title: Don't forget the diet: Incorporating diet into daily dermatology case management (On Demand)
courses.description: This Purina Institute Collaborative Care webinar will explore the role of nutrition for dermatology cases commonly seen in clinical practice. The speakers will emphasize the importance of obtaining a thorough diet history, even when adverse food reactions are not on the differential diagnosis list, and provide guidance for evaluating the pet's current diet and recognizing opportunities to improve nutrition to optimize clinical results. They will also provide tips for effective communication regarding diet recommendations, whether it involves switching to a therapeutic diet, a different commercial diet, or a need for an elimination diet trial.

courses.title: Telemedicine and Vaccine Clinics in California, What Veterinarians Need to Know About Legislative Updates for 2025
courses.description:
This course, Telemedicine and Vaccine Clinics in California: What Veterinarians Need to Know About Legislative
Updates for 2025, provides a comprehensive overview of recent legal and regulatory changes affecting veterinary
practices. It highlights critical updates, including the redefined roles of veterinarians (DVMs), registered veterinary
technicians (RVTs), and veterinary assistants (VAs) under California law. Participants learn about the implications of
SB 669 and AB 1399, which expand the scope of practice for RVTs in vaccine clinics and enable telemedicine to
establish veterinary-client-patient relationships (VCPRs) for animals through audio-video communication. The course
also emphasizes the distinction between direct and indirect supervision and the integration of these updates into
best practices for veterinarians.
Focusing on practical applications, the course outlines best practices for delegation, documentation, and leveraging
telemedicine to improve care access and efficiency. It addresses how to run public vaccine clinics, provided specific
protocols are followed, and explores scenarios where telemedicine is effective. By adopting these updates,
veterinarians and shelters can increase community outreach, enhance animal welfare, and address veterinary
shortages, ultimately improving health outcomes for animals under their care.

courses.title: An update on managing common cardiac and renal problems
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian/technician with practical information on the current thoughts on diagnosis and management of common canine and feline medical problems (cardiac and renal) that they encounter in their daily practice. Dr. Oswald will also discuss how he manages clinical problems encountered with the canine and feline patient. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of diagnosis and management available for their patients.

courses.title: Yes- you can do that surgery in your practice
courses.description: This seminar will be technique- and patient-centered around common surgical techniques that can be done in general practice. These topics will be presented by an academic surgeon and a private-practice surgeon, guided by an anesthesiologist/pain-management specialist to help frame the entirety of each procedure

courses.title: Taking the Bite Out of Performing Intra-oral Dental Radiographs and the Oral Exam: The Foundation of Veterinary Dental Care
courses.description: This half day, primarily lab-based session (listed below as repeated on the same day to another group of attendees) is designed to provide resources and confidence regarding the procurement of diagnostic intra-oral radiographs and oral exam techniques. Participants will rotate through a circuit training style laboratory practicing regional dental radiographs on feline and canine specimens as well as a hands-on oral exam curriculum. Training will be provided by a combination of either board certified veterinary dentists and/or certified veterinary technicians working full time in dentistry/oral surgery specialty practice.

courses.title: Efficient Team Communication in Vet Emergencies: Tools for Every Role
courses.description: While patient care is prioritized above all else during a pet emergency, a strong communication plan takes these events to the next level. Learn how every single member of the hospital team plays a role in saving lives, ensuring pet owners feel included and cared for. Learners will also understand the importance of a brief post-event huddle where teams can acknowledge what went well, identify helpful adjustments, and strengthen confidence for the next emergency.

courses.title: Tips and Tricks for Successful Dental Extractions
courses.description: This one-hour lecture format course is designed to introduce the equipment and techniques needed to be successful with dental extractions. Through images and video, flap design, tissue handling and lever principles are described. Dental radiographic techniques and interpretation are discussed where relevant. Common complications, such as root fracture and retrieval, are highlighted.

courses.title: Economic Principles and Financial Strategies for Veterinary Practices
courses.description: Economic Principles and Financial Strategies for Veterinary Practices is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Microbiome Forum Round Table 2025: First-Line Approach to GI Disease in Dogs and Cats (On Demand)
courses.description:
Veterinary medicine is undergoing a paradigm shift in our understanding of gastrointestinal disease in dogs and cats, and a multimodal approach is vital to success. How does this shift affect clinical decision-making in acute and chronic GI disorders? In this roundtable discussion with Q&A, a panel of gastroenterologists and nutritionists to discuss the ongoing evolution of gastrointestinal case management, including the foundational role of nutrition and addressing dysbiosis. Specific topics that will be addressed include dietary modification as the first-line approach to diarrhea; the impact of macronutrient composition on the microbiome; appropriate diet selection for GI disease; the current evidence against the use of antibiotics for acute diarrhea or chronic enteropathy; and practical approaches to fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT).
This presentation does not contain any brand or product promotion.

courses.title: AALAS 2026 District 8 Meeting
courses.description: This program is a live and interactive, annual educational symposium for laboratory animal science professionals employed within one of the American Association for Laboratory Animal Science (AALAS) District 8 states. District 8 AALAS unites laboratory animal research professionals across Alaska, Arizona, California, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, Utah, and Washington. It aims to provide professional development for animal technicians, animal scientists, veterinary technicians, veterinarians, research specialists and investigators. Continuing education provided in this event will include improved animal welfare practices, anesthesia techniques, improved pain management practices, improved health surveillance, and application of the 3Rs (replacement, reduction, and refinement) in various lab animal species. Continuing education will also be provided on improved personnel welfare and promoting a culture of care within the vivarium, as well as leadership growth in the laboratory animal science field. Also included will be an Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) workshop which will be a comprehensive introduction to the humane care and use of laboratory animals led by respected leaders in the field of animal welfare.

courses.provider: ADVANCED VETERINARY CARE THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE
courses.title: Cardiovascular Anesthesia
courses.description:
This 1 hour CE lecture is designed for veterinary doctors, technicians, and tech assistants. It will cover an overview of: Cardiac physiology, Physiology of blood pressure, Cardiac safe pre-medications, induction agents, anesthetic maintenance,
Complications with cardiac anesthesia, and Drug MOAs.
LEARNING OBJECTIVES:
Understand cardiac physiology
Understand reactions and consequence of drugs on the cardiovascular system
Develop a cardiac safe anesthetic protocol
Gain an understanding of cardiovascular anesthesia

courses.title: 2025 Academy of Veterinary Consultants Winter Conference
courses.description:
This Course Includes to following: Health and Performance Outcomes of Heifers Administered Two Different Deworming Programs Upon Entry into a
Commercial Feedyard - Dr. Mark Alley BRD Diagnostics: What weve been seeing at ISU-VDL - Dr. Drew Magstadt and Dr. Shane Terrell New World Screwworm Update - Dr. Lewis Dinges Banana cows and more: Theileria orientalis Ikeda genotype in North America Dr. Kevin Lahmers Cattle welfare from the perspectives of the people who take care of the animals - Dr. Lily Edwards Callaway Environmental Stress Management in Feedlot Cattle - Dr. Terry Mader Language of Antimicrobials - Dr. Michael Apley Therapuetics for New World Screw Worm - Dr. Michael Apley Swapping out antimicrobials. A spectrum review for when an antibiotic is not available - Dr. Michael Apley
Viral Shedding Pattern following MLV Intranasal Vaccination - Dr. Jennifer Rice Gallo Update on hemotrophic mycoplasmas in Missouri cattle - Dr. Celeste Morris Applying epidemiology to clinical reasoning - Dr. David Smith
Handling Cattle Truck Emergencies in Practice - Dr. Pat Gorden Digital Dermatitis in Feedyards - Dr. Terry Engelken

courses.title: Using ChatGPT in Clinical Practice: Time-Saving Tools for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description:
This program teaches licensed veterinarians how to effectively integrate generative AI (ChatGPT) into clinical workflows. Attendees will explore real-world techniques for using ChatGPT to draft SOAP medical records, create client education materials in multiple languages, and retrieve rapid clinical support during appointments. This live webinar is ideal for practitioners seeking efficiency, productivity, and digital fluency in modern practice.
Keywords: Veterinary AI, SOAP records, ChatGPT, veterinary CE, clinical documentation, client education, generative AI in practice, veterinary software tools

courses.title: Eyes, ears & beyond
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients presented to their clinic with a dermatologic or ocular problem. The combination of a Dermatologist and an Ophthalmologist will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists

courses.title: Boviteq Difference Conference 2025
courses.description: This conference is for Boviteq Accredited veterinary partners to understand the latest innovations related to bovine oocyte pick up and in vitro fertilization. Topics will include global updates, leveraging data to enhance performance, tools to show value of an IVF program to producers, timing non-stimulated OPUs, continuous improvement updates, media composition and calf viability and health, recipient and calf management, trace mineral and nutritional impacts on recipients and calves, per embryo pricing model, and an overview of AI embryo grading.

courses.title: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery in Veterinary Patients: Fracture Repair and Tumor Management
courses.description: This is a 4-hour, LIVE Seminar presented by Christopher Snyder, DVM, DAVDC, DEVDC. This program provides an advanced overview of oral and maxillofacial surgery in small animal patients, focusing on fracture repair and surgical management of oral tumors. The session begins with an exploration of craniofacial growth and mandibular biomechanics, emphasizing how embryologic development, tooth position, and maxillary buttresses influence fracture patterns and fixation strategies. Participants will review contemporary methods of mandibular stabilization, including intraoral splinting, cerclage wiring, maxillomandibular fixation, and plating systems, with attention to preserving dental structures while achieving biomechanical stability. The lectures then transition to the surgical management of oral tumors, covering diagnostic approaches, biopsy and staging techniques, and imaging modalities such as cone beam and medical CT. Surgical planning principles, including margin assessment, osteotomy approaches, and tissue handling, are presented for mandibulectomy, maxillectomy, and tongue resections. Potential complications, such as hemorrhage, mandibular drift, and fistula formation, are reviewed with strategies for prevention and management. Throughout the program, emphasis is placed on integrating diagnostic accuracy, surgical precision, and client communication to optimize both clinical outcomes and quality of life for veterinary patients.

courses.title: Myths and Misperceptions about Pre-, Pro-, and Postbiotics
courses.description:
The use of pre- and probiotics in veterinary medicine is common and awareness of postbiotics is increasing, but many myths and misperceptions remain concerning their definitions, characteristics, and indications. This presentation from the Purina Institute Microbiome Forum Virtual Event 2025 will address these common myths and misperceptions to help veterinary professionals make informed decisions regarding biotic use.
Note: This presentation was part of the Purina Institute Microbiome Forum Virtual Event 2025, held 12-13 November 2025 (Course number 20-1329191) and approved as a full program for RACE CE. This submission is for on-demand viewing of this individual presentation.

courses.title: IACUC Training Workshop - Pittsburgh
courses.description:
This in-person training will continue to provide high quality educational material and information to members of the animal research community, veterinarians, veterinarian technicians and members of Institutional Animal Care and Use Committees about better humane and responsible care of research animals.
IACUCs are mandated by the Animal Welfare Act to oversee the welfare, care and use of animals used in research, testing and teaching. IACUC members include veterinarians, community members, scientists from the institution and nonscientists. IACUCs play a very significant role in research animal well-being. SCAWs in-person training will provide IACUC members and animal researchers and laboratory staff with an opportunity to learn new information, to discuss complicated protocols with the faculty and their peers, and to keep current with new and developing events.
This in-person training will help meet the requirement stated in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals 8th edition, 2011 All personnel involved with the care and use of animals must be adequately educated, trained, and/or qualified in basic principles of laboratory animal science to help ensure high-quality science and animal wellbeing. It will also address USDA/APHIS/AC Policy 15.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Trigeminal-Mediated Headshaking: Latest & Future Perspectives on Management
courses.description: A panel of leading international specialists will debate the latest evidence and future possibilities in managing trigeminal-mediated headshaking. The discussion will explore emerging therapies such as cannabinoids, electroacupuncture, and blue light therapy, alongside updates on other established therapeutic options. With diverse expertise and perspectives, the panel will critically examine current practices, challenge assumptions, and open new avenues for investigation and clinical application.

courses.title: The 41st Muller-Ihrke-Kwochka Veterinary Dermatology Seminar, The 26th Veterinary MEDicine Seminar & The JOINT Meeting
courses.description: VETS presents 13.5 CE Units in Dermatology from Board Certified DVMs and 13.5 CE Units in Internal Medicine (also Board Certified DVMs)-- this year with an emphasis on Brachycephalic Issues, Small Animal Ophthalmology and Diseases and Aging of the Cat. Attendees may choose the Dermatology Track or the MEDicine Track or BOTH-- which is what we call The JOINT Meeting.

courses.title: Improving Diagnostic Confidence: Case-Based Applications of Thoracic & Abdominal Radiography
courses.description: This CE webinar aims to help strengthen your diagnostic confidence by sharing improved radiographic techniques and offering collaborative insights from board-certified radiologists. In this session, expert panelists will review the diagnostic pathway for 2 unique cases from start to finish, including imaging decisions, interpretation challenges, and final diagnoses. Attendees will discover the value of high-quality image acquisition, the role of reference image libraries, and how teleradiology services can help support timely, accurate case management. Attendees will leave the session with practical strategies for integrating specialist input into everyday practice to enhance patient care.

courses.title: Biennial Inventory: Your DEA Recordkeeping Baseline
courses.description:
If the Drug Enforcement Administration ("DEA") shows up to conduct an inspection or audit, one of the FIRST documents they will request to review is your most recent biennial inventory. Your ability to produce a current, accurate, biennial inventory documentation upon request has the power to start a DEA visit off with success...or distress (if you have not completed one).
Completing a biennial inventory is a federal requirement and matter of regulatory inspection readiness that ALL DEA registrants ordering and maintaining a controlled substance inventory must adhere to every two years (at minimum). The Biennial inventory sets the baseline for all controlled substances on hand. Still, confusion persists over the biennial inventory process, what it is, why it matters, and how to properly perform and document it.
This 50-minute webinar provides a practical overview and step-by-step guide to understanding and properly executing upon DEA biennial inventory requirements to ensure regulatory inspection readiness. Participants will learn why conducting "inventory" and "DEA biennial inventory" are not synonymous processes, including what constitutes "on-hand" stock, when to count, how to properly document biennial inventory, and how to avoid common, costly mistakes. Navigating proper separation of drug schedules and state-only scheduled drugs on inventory documentation will also be covered, followed by best practices for implementing processes and systems that support a stress-free, consistent biennial inventory trail. Webinar content will be presented in the following four key areas:
1. DEA Registrant: Who is required to physically conduct biennial inventory. What aspects of biennial inventory are "delegable". Understanding the role of witnesses and individuals to whom power of attorney has been granted within the biennial inventory process.
2. Biennial Documentation (Paper): The DEA provides biennial inventory regulatory requirements, not a template. How biennial inventor

courses.title: Product Primer: Nutritional Management of Canine Calcium Oxalate Urolithiasis -On Demand
courses.description: Calcium oxalate uroliths frequently recur, with recurrence in high-risk breeds approaching 100% in some studies. Because calcium oxalate stones can not be dissolved, physical removal utilizing surgery or minimally invasive techniques must be pursued in affected patients, followed by proactive management to help delay stone recurrence. Nutritional management should include the use of diets shown to promote urine with RSS in the metastable range for calcium oxalate, and the patient response to nutritional therapy should be closely monitored. Through careful monitoring, adjustments in the treatment plan can be made to help reduce recurrence, and recurrent stones may be caught early, thus enabling removal via non-invasive means such as voiding urohydropropulsion. In this session, we will discuss factors contributing to calcium oxalate RSS, diet selection, and monitoring. Strategies to further reduce USG in refractory patients will also be discussed.

courses.title: Complications of Tooth Extraction: Avoidance and Management
courses.description:
This webinar will address the avoidance and management of common complications that can occur during tooth extraction including excessive bleeding, jaw fractures, incomplete tooth removal, and inadvertent trauma to adjacent tooth structures.
Management strategies to be discussed will include use of hemostatic agents to control bleeding, application of coat buttons to stabilize mandibular fractures, techniques to identify and remove residual root fragments, and criteria to determine when extraction of an iatrogenic injured adjacent tooth is necessary.

courses.title: Understanding the Impact of Pain on Behavior in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This presentation explores how pain affects behavior in dogs and cats, with a focus on identifying the subtle signs of both acute and chronic pain. Participants will examine the physiological and emotional effects of pain, including its relationship with the stress response and its influence on body language, movement, and social interaction. The session will provide practical guidance on distinguishing pain-related behaviors from those linked to fear, anxiety, frustration, or training difficulties. Strategies for treatment and ongoing management will be discussed to address both physical discomfort and associated behavioral changes. Attendees will gain the skills to recognize the impact of pain and to incorporate pain assessment into every patient visit, regardless of age.

courses.title: Attack the Scratch! Approach to Allergy in the Itchy Kitty
courses.description: This course will equip veterinary professionals with an in-depth understanding of how to systematically approach and manage pruritic feline cases. Attendees will learn to recognize the clinical signs associated with feline atopic syndrome, such as overgrooming, miliary dermatitis, alopecia, and pruritus. The course will guide participants through the process of developing a comprehensive diagnostic workup plan, ruling out common differentials, and exploring the latest treatment options for feline atopy. With a focus on both immediate and long-term management, practical strategies will be provided to help improve the quality of life for allergic felines. Attendees will leave with the knowledge and skills to confidently address and manage feline atopic syndrome in clinical practice.

courses.title: Crash, Boom, Bang! Addressing Noise Aversion in Dogs
courses.description: It is estimated that a third of dogs suffer from some form of noise aversion. If you saw 12 dogs yesterday, four of them are likely to develop noise sensitivities in their lifetime. Not only can a fear of sounds be physiologically and emotionally damaging for dogs, but it can also strain the human-animal relationship. This session will provide you with strategies for how to approach, prevent, and treat sound sensitivities, including teaching desired coping skills.

courses.title: Everyones Least Favorite Appointment: The Cat Whos Urinating Out of the Box
courses.description: Is it the cats bladder or brain? In this session, well discuss the best ways to approachout of box urination. From signalment to diagnostics and treatment, youll leave this session ready to face thenext cat presented for this problem, armed with tools to make the most effective and appropriate treatmentrecommendations.

courses.title: I Really Don't Want to Get Bit Today On-Demand
courses.description: Most adult dogs and cats exhibit some level of fear and/or anxiety in the veterinary setting, and almost 30% of dogs and more than 40% of cats display some degree of veterinary-related aggression. With a focus on these fearful and fractious patients, this lecture will outline the benefits and limitations of preveterinary visit pharmaceuticals, offer sedation protocol considerations based on severity of veterinary related aggression, and provide practical tips for handling patients with veterinary-related aggression in a manner than enhances safety and reduces stress for patients, clients, and staff.

courses.title: Veterinary Ethics in Equestrian Sports
courses.description:
PANEL DISCUSSION DESCRIPTION
Public concern about the use of animals in sport and the challenge to the social licence for that use have been increasing in recent years. Events in the run-up to the Paris 2024 Olympics put equestrian sport under even more scrutiny. Some (including some within the Veterinary Profession) have started to challenge the traditional view of equine Vets as safe guarders of equine welfare, and to suggest instead that they are facilitators of the human use of animals which should no longer be considered acceptable.

courses.title: Congestive Heart Failure and Arrhythmia management in the ER
courses.description: This presentation will provide an overview of assessment, diagnosis and treatment of congestive heart failure and common arrhythmias.

courses.title: Essentials of Anaesthesia By Dr Kristi Kobluk DACVAA. 6-week online course
courses.description:
Course Format:
A 6-week, self-paced online program with 12 hours of structured video lectures, downloadable notes, drug charts, and interactive quizzes. Learners have 12 weeks access and can complete modules at their own pace.
Target Audience:
Veterinarians and final year veterinary students seeking to improve confidence and competence in small animal anaesthesia, including general practitioners, emergency clinicians, and new graduates.
Course Overview:
Anaesthesia is a critical component of veterinary practice that demands both technical skill and sound clinical judgment. Essentials of Anaesthesia provides a structured, evidence-based approach to every phase of the anaesthetic process from patient assessment to safe recovery. The course bridges theory and practice through case examples, protocol development exercises, and instructor-guided discussions designed to strengthen real-world application.
Learning Objectives:
By the end of this course, participants will be able to:
Perform comprehensive pre-anaesthetic evaluations, identify patient risk factors, and assign ASA status.
Select and administer appropriate sedatives and premedications, understanding drug mechanisms, contraindications, and reversal agents.
Execute smooth induction and intubation, manage airway and equipment setup, and troubleshoot complications.
Monitor physiological parameters (ECG, blood pressure, ventilation, temperature) and interpret changes in anaesthetic depth.
Recognize and manage common complications including hypotension, hypoventilation, arrhythmias, and hypothermia.
Apply individualized protocols and fluid/drug plans for high-risk or emergency patients.
Ensure safe anaesthetic recovery and postoperative monitoring.
Educational Methods:
The course combines short, focused video lectures (5 to 20 minutes each), printable workbooks, case-based learning, and multiple-choice quizzes for reinforcement. A final comprehensive assessment (minimum 70% to pass) confirms knowledge integration.
