courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Periodontal Therapy for the Busy GP (On-Demand)
courses.description: This on-demand discussion will include a practical focus on periodontal therapy designed for the busy general practitioner. Attendees will review the anatomy of the periodontium, along with the pathogenesis and stages of periodontal disease, to build a clear understanding of how this condition develops and progresses. The discussion will include how to identify periodontal disease on radiographs and outline treatment options appropriate for each stage. Common misconceptions will be addressed, with guidance on how to provide effective, realistic care using the tools and resources typically available in general practice.

courses.title: Product Primer Nutritional Tips for Urinary, GI, and Derm Cases
courses.description: In this program, we will review three of the most common indications for therapeutic nutrition in veterinary patients including feline idiopathic cystitis, acute gastroenteritis, and allergic dermatitis, and summarize top nutritional tips that can help practitioners leverage nutrition effectively in patients affected by these conditions. Attendees will learn how to go beyond the bladder to address common nutritional risk factors for FIC, discover the benefits of going beyond bland in the management of gastroenteritis and finally, learn how targeted nutrition can promote healthy skin from within, via allergen avoidance, strengthening of the skin barrier, and modulation of the immune system.

courses.title: Aging Gracefully: Understanding the Nutritional Needs of Senior Dogs and Cats (On Demand Webinar)
courses.description: This webinar will focus on strategies for providing specialized nutrition for older pets. It will emphasize the need to adapt diet plans and nutraceutical supplements to meet the unique health needs of geriatric cats and dogs. The presentation will include strategies for weight management, joint health, general wellbeing, and diet enhancements for finicky patients.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Catastrophic Injury Prevention in Thoroughbred Racehorses
courses.description:
PANEL DISCUSSION DESCRIPTION
Catastrophic fractures of horses are a major threat to the racing industry. This has driven racing authorities to explore and, in specific cases, implement methods for managing the risk of horse deaths on racetracks. However, evidence-based practices are challenging to establish and implement. Despite this, the ability to identify pre-existing pathology has driven the use of imaging as an important risk management tool while supporting evidence continues to be gathered.
We have been able to assemble an international panel of experts to address the following critical questions:
Which racehorses are at risk of catastrophic injury on the track and how do we identify them?
What is the value of radiography for risk assessment?
Can computed tomography (CT) determine if a horse is at risk of injury?
What role does / could MRI and positron emission tomography (PET) play?
Beyond imaging: Is it possible to determine injury risk through analysis of stride patterns and race performance?
Reflecting on the Australian injury reduction strategy for specific high-profile races: what have we learnt and how will this inform future approaches to equine welfare in high-stakes racing events?

courses.provider: PURPLE MOON HERBS AND STUDIES, LLC
courses.title: Wholistic Pain Management and Rehabilitation
courses.description: This course will introduce an integrative approach to pain management and rehabilitation. We will learn to incorporate herbal medications, acupuncture, and other rehabilitation modalities in addition to conventional allopathic pharmaceuticals. We invite you to join us in the beautiful Outer Banks of North Carolina and enjoy the beach while learning about pain management and rehabilitation in animals. The beaches are beautiful and serene, wonderful restaurants abound and there are plenty of other activities throughout the barrier islands. Visit the Corolla Wild Horses or Jenette's Pier, walk through one of the nature preserves or on the beach, or just sunbathe and shop. Continental breakfast is included each morning. Lectures include an overview of the multimodal approach to pain management in which we look at the whole animal - body, mind, and spirit. The wholistic exam including the history and findings are the stepping off point that will help guide patient recommendations and treatments. We will have more in-depth discussions regarding the theory behind common modalities found in rehabilitation medicine as well as how and when to utilize these for your patients. There will be in depth discussions on herbs that are utilized in pain management and palliative medicine specifically, but also in the general support of chronically ill and geriatric animals. There will be an organoleptic portion to these lectures to see and taste the herbs in tea, dried and tinctured forms. We will discuss how the herbs can be used as safe, effective alternatives to non-steroidals and the differences in the body's physiologic response to both. To tie everything together, we will review specific cases of various conditions, as well as cases that incorporate a variety of the above modalities

courses.title: Panel Discussion End of Life Decision Making
courses.description: End of life decision making is an integral aspect of veterinary medicine. While the process may be straightforward in certain cases to prevent prolonged and unnecessary suffering, determining the most appropriate course of action in end of life situations can be challenging. Approaches often vary among veterinarians based on their experience, background, and geographic location, with the latter influenced by societal and cultural factors, professional codes of conduct and rules legislation. Further, navigating the interests of multiple stakeholders as well as the complexity of ascertaining whether a horses life is worth living, may lead to misalignment and lack of consensus. In this panel discussion, four handpicked distinguished experts will debate where and why these differences exist, the contributing factors, and share their knowledge, experience and perspectives on this important subject.

courses.title: The More you Gnome: Gardening Hazards in Pets
courses.description: As spring blooms around us we'll take time to evaluate the hidden hazards of the garden shed, the flower bed, the vegetable patch, and the growing lawn. This webinar will follow a case-based approach in evaluating the potential poisonous hazards including common fertilizers and plant feeds, pesticides, herbicides, and a few of the more dangerous plants.

courses.title: On Demand: Diagnosis and Treatment of Acute Pancreatitis
courses.description: Originally presented in 2023, this on-demand course features practical updates on diagnosing and managing pancreatitis. Dr. Mark Acierno reviews the latest recommendations for effective treatments and discusses how to decide which diagnostic test to run and when, in a world where the variety of options are always expanding. We'll also study the roles of pain medication, antiemetics, and nutrition in treatment.

courses.title: Evidence-based spotlight: Antibiotic therapy
courses.description: Collaborating with VIN, the EBVMA data-mined some of the most common antibiotic questions that populated VIN message boards with a goal of bringing practitioners the most current treatment recommendations for a variety of common clinical scenarios. With the help of 4 recognized experts in this area, a round-table discussion format will be used to highlight the clinical research and studies underpinning these recommendations. Gaps in the medical literature will also be identified. The presenters will bring a practical but evidence-based approach to help veterinarians optimally treat their patients while being good antibiotic stewards.

courses.title: The 7M's of Treating Any Behavior Problem
courses.description:
OVERVIEW OF THE ISSUE: When clients are faced with behavior problems in their pets, they want to be able to trust their veterinarians as a source of information for treatment. Many general practitioners feel overwhelmed when faced with a behavior problem which may be a result of the paucity of behavior education in veterinary school.
OBJECTIVES OF THE PRESENTATION: In this presentation, clinicians will learn how to systematically think about treating any behavior problem-from nuisance behaviors (jumping, counter-surfing, etc) to severe anxiety and aggression.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Feline & Canine How To - Extraction Lab Focused (On-Demand)
courses.description: This two-hour on-demand discussion will walk attendees through the principles and practical steps of performing extractions in both feline and canine patients. The feline portion begins with a review of surgical fundamentals, including proper suture selection, knot placement, and spacing, before moving into the instruments best suited for feline dentistry such as elevators, periosteal elevators, burs, and root tip picks. A step-by-step guide will cover how to approach full-mouth extractions when indicated, with an emphasis on recognizing and preventing potential complications. High-quality video demonstrations will provide a clear visual of techniques for several types of feline extractions. The canine portion builds on these same principles, with discussion of the specialized equipment required for canine extractions and a focused look at more advanced procedures, including extraction of the canine teeth and maxillary fourth premolars. Throughout, the session emphasizes efficiency, precision, and patient safety, ensuring that participants leave with a solid foundation to approach complex extractions in practice.¿

courses.title: Join the Local Block Party!
courses.description:
This lecture is essential for veterinary team members to select better and place drugs into the local oral
block sites. At a minimum, attendees will understand the anatomical landmarks for the four major local blocks - the infraorbital, caudal maxillary, mental, and inferior alveolar blocks. Tips for placement, alternative approaches, drug choices, and volumes will be reviewed. Contraindications and complications that have been reported in the literature will be used to learn from others mistakes in order to more likely have good outcomes with local block placement in practice.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Malocclusions in Dogs and Cats expert insight on diagnosis, management and treatments
courses.description:
Malocclusions or misalignments of the teeth may simply result in a crooked grin. However, they also have the potential to significantly affect the daily lives of our patients. They can have an impact on their overall health and comfort. Amongst other things they can play a role in their ability to eat, increase their risk for periodontal disease and result in excessive wear on other teeth.
Discomfort can result in irritability and other behavioural changes and, in general, reduce their potential quality of life. The options for treatments can range from simple minimally invasive procedures to more advanced Facio-maxillary surgeries. The challenge can sometimes be in recognising if and when the more advanced or invasive procedures should be considered, and which of the malocclusions that can be picked up during the first few puppy vaccinations have the capacity to cause harm if left untreated.
In this discussion, our multidisciplinary panel of international experts will discuss how to recognise these conditions in time, their tips and tricks for correcting them and their insights into managing some of the more challenging cases.

courses.title: Case Rounds: Diagnostic Strategy for the Vomiting Dog and Cat ON Demand
courses.description: In this course learners will work through acute and chronic vomiting presentations in dogs and cats while strengthening clinical reasoning, prioritizing differential diagnoses, interpreting diagnostic findings, developing treatment plans, and navigating client communication. The program emphasizes practical decision-making and evidence-based approaches that participants can immediately incorporate into everyday small animal practice.

courses.title: Veterinary Anaesthesia and Analgesia Mentorship Program
courses.description:
The Veterinary Anaesthesia and Analgesia Mentorship Program is a comprehensive, postgraduate-level continuing education course designed to guide small-animal veterinarians from foundational principles of safe anaesthesia to confident clinical application.
The program runs from September 2026 through May 2027 and is delivered across multiple European locations. It combines on-site teaching, simulation-based training, supervised practical experience, and continuous online mentorship to ensure progressive learning, consolidation of skills between modules, and durable clinical competence.
Across five modules, participants progress from equipment checks, monitoring, thermoregulation, and ventilation to pharmacology and protocol design, peri-operative pain management and cardiopulmonary cerebral resuscitation (RECOVER-based), loco-regional techniques, and the recognition and management of anaesthetic complications in patients with common comorbidities. The program concludes with a summative theory and practical examination using a simulator-based format.
Practical training is delivered through an ethically robust framework, including high-fidelity simulation scenarios (e.g., changes in heart rate, blood pressure, capnography, and oxygenation), task training using phantoms, cadaver-based anatomical and block technique training, and a welfare-positive live clinical module involving routine canine castration of shelter animals in collaboration with local partners. All live-animal practical activities are performed under direct veterinary supervision and in accordance with local legislation and welfare standards.
The overarching goal of the program is to enable veterinarians to plan and conduct anaesthesia safely, interpret monitoring trends accurately, anticipate and manage complications promptly, and implement effective analgesic strategies and resuscitation protocols aligned with current best practice.

courses.title: DNM Therapeutic Nutrition for Adverse Food Reactions
courses.description: This course explores common food allergies and intolerances and discusses the mechanisms behind food allergy reactions, the body's immune response to food allergens, and the diagnosis and nutritional management of these conditions

courses.title: The Complete Oral Exam: From Consultation to Surgery Table
courses.description: This fundamental level discussion will cover the conscious (awake) oral examination in front of the client, including estimation and client communication, and then move onto complete sedated exam including imaging and periodontal probing.

courses.title: The Hospital Environment, Part 1: Exploring Sensory Exposure
courses.description: This is the first lecture in a two-part series that does a deep dive into real, physical, objective environment in which we work as veterinary professionals. We will explore the external environment in terms of sensory exposure, and the internal environment in terms of culture.

courses.title: The Equine Practice Company Ophthalmology Program
courses.description:
A comprehensive, self-paced program that begins with the fundamentals of the ophthalmic examination and guides you through diagnostic procedures, interpretation of findings, treatment planning, and case management, all grounded in evidence-based practice.
Designed for real-world application, the program includes step-by-step demonstrations, case-based discussions, and practical guidance to help you approach ophthalmic cases with greater confidence and clarity. Whether you're refreshing your skills or building new ones, this course gives you the tools to make informed decisions and deliver effective care when it matters most.

courses.title: Forages in Equine Diets
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with information about forages in equine diets, including how plant physiology affects equine nutrition, types of forages available, and interpretation of a forage analysis.

courses.title: Matching Diet to Disease: Dietary Strategies for Gastrointestinal Disease
courses.description:
This webinar will focus on discussing the different nutritional strategies for the management of gastrointestinal disease, focusing on acute gastroenteritis and pancreatitis. We will also talk about the different dietary options for these conditions and how to choose the right diet for each case.
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: Hydrolyzed Diets in the Management of Dermatologic Diseases
courses.description:
In this webinar, Dr. Noli will discuss many aspects of hydrolyzed diets, including how they are produced; why, how, and when they should be used; how to choose the best diet; and the expected benefits for both the skin and the gut.
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: Water in Equine Diets
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with information about water in equine diets, including water physiology, equine drinking behavior, and water quality for horses.

courses.title: On Demand Webinar:Itchy Patients, Better Outcomes: How RVTs Shape Dermatology Success
courses.description: Itchy patients are some of the most common and most challenging cases in veterinary practice. This webinar puts Registered Veterinary Technicians at the center of dermatology success, showcasing how RVTs drive better outcomes through strong diagnostics, nutrition guidance, and client communication. From high quality sample collection to supporting allergy diagnostics, participants will explore the RVT's role in managing atopic dermatitis, food allergy, and patients affected by both. The session will also demystify diet trials, including hydrolyzed versus novel protein diets, key nutritional considerations such as omega-3 fatty acids, and strategies to improve client compliance. Designed to be practical and empowering, this webinar equips RVTs with tools they can use immediately to elevate dermatology care.

courses.title: Dentistry Spotlight: Oral Diseases of the Dog and Cat
courses.description: In this 2-hour video series, Dr. Sara Gonzalez drills us on dental diseases! We'll review pathogenesis of common feline and canine oral disorders and learn the most up-to-date treatment recommendations for anything you unearth. If tooth resorption, stomatitis, and oronasal fistulas make you grind your teeth, you're not alone. This course is perfect for anyone performing dentals - DVM and tech alike.

courses.title: 5 Technology-Powered Efficiencies Every Practice Needs
courses.description: When you run an efficient practice, profits and client satisfaction will soar. Learn how to use AI-powered tools to rapidly answer texts and emails from clients. Get best practices for online and app booking. Send online forms with appointment confirmations to save 10 to 15 minutes every appointment. Complete records faster with AI-powered tools for SOAP notes. Summarize calls to capture and complete clients' requests with AI tools.

courses.title: Food as Medicine for Feline OA: Weight Management & Nutrition Strategies to Support Mobility
courses.description: Feline osteoarthritis (OA) is common, underdiagnosed, and frequently complicated by comorbidities such as obesity, chronic kidney disease, diabetes mellitus, and gastrointestinal disorders. As part of a multimodal management strategy, nutrition and weight management are among the most impactful and modifiable interventions available to veterinary teams. This session explores the pathophysiology and clinical presentation of feline OA, the principles of multimodal management, and the critical role of nutrition as therapeutic intervention. We will review the evidence supporting targeted nutritional strategies (including caloric restriction, macronutrient balance, and omega-3 fatty acids), and develop practical approaches for selecting appropriate diets in cats with OA and concurrent diseases. Attendees will leave with actionable strategies to implement nutrition-forward OA plans that support mobility, reduce pain, and improve quality of life while maintaining a caregiver-centered approach.

courses.title: What Are You Looking At? Dental Radiograph Anatomy and Interpretation ON DEMAND
courses.description: This lecture reviews normal dental radiographic anatomy in dogs and cats and provides a practical approach to identifying key landmarks and interpreting common findings on dental radiographs.

courses.title: Building Better Dental Packs: Instrument Selection and Care for Periodontal and Oral Surgery Procedures ON DEMAND
courses.description: This 1-hour course focuses on veterinary dental instrument selection, organization, and care for periodontal therapy and oral surgery. Participants will learn how to choose appropriate dental instruments, assemble periodontal and oral surgery packs, and implement proper cleaning, sharpening, sterilization, and storage protocols to improve efficiency, patient outcomes, and instrument longevity.

courses.title: Charting a Course to Feline Fabulous
courses.description: This is a virtual, interactive module centered around learning more about managing feline chronic kidney disease and associated weight loss and inappetence with capromorelin.

courses.title: How to Really Read Intraoral Radiographs
courses.description: Once diagnostic intraoral radiographs are delivered then the challenge comes to read them and act on what you see. Using radiographic images of common oral lesions of dogs and cats a step-by-step approach to interpretation will be taught to ensure complete and accurate radiographic diagnoses.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Equine Asthma
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage equine asthma cases in the field.

courses.title: Rewriting Rapid Testing: 10 POC Tests Flying Under the Radar
courses.description: Point of care diagnostic analyzers are rapidly evolving to meet the need of veterinary clinicians for easy to use, accurate testing available on the clinic's schedule, not the reference lab's timeline. New analyzers bring more tests to the clinic, increasing our ability to manage complex diseases and critical patients while the patient is in the hospital and ready for treatment. Join us for a rapid and succinct review of tests now available at point of care and how they can be used in general practice.

courses.title: DNM Therapeutic Nutrition for Neurologic Disease
courses.description: This course gives you a solid foundation in specific neurologic diseases in dogs, namely epilepsy and cognitive dysfunction syndrome, and discusses the management of these diseases, including the use of targeted nutrition.

courses.title: Extending lifespan with nutrition -- science vs speculation
courses.description: This session will explore the impact of dietary interventions on the mechanisms and manifestations of aging, considering research evidence from lab animal models, humans, and companion animal species. Directions for future research, clinical implications, and popular misconceptions about diet and aging will also be discussed.

courses.title: New therapies in development for canine lifespan
courses.description: Come learn about recent advances in the field of canine aging and explore new science-driven, evidence-based research to extend lifespan in dogs. Treating aging as a modifiable risk factor allows us to take a preventative approach to age-associated diseases.

courses.title: Steps to a COHAT: Comprehensive Oral Health Assessment & Treatment - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Performing a Complete Oral Health Assessment and Treatment (COHAT) entails much more than removing plaque and calculus from the teeth. A thorough dental prophylaxis consists of educating the client, an oral examination, charting disease process, pathology and anomalies, radiographs, both supra and sub-gingival plaque and calculus removal, hand scaling, polishing, irrigation and home care instructions. Additionally, hyaluronic has indications in both a prophylactic and early periodontal disease treatment setting.

courses.title: Urethrostomies in Cats and Dogs: Indications and Technique Tips
courses.description: This webinar will review indications for urethrostomy surgery in cats and dogs. Key anatomic differences between canine and feline patients will be highlighted as well as surgical technique tips for successful outcomes. Emphasis will be placed on strategies to minimize both intraoperative and postoperative complications.

courses.title: Webinar - Diagnosing & Management of Oral Injuries (incl. Intra-Oral Foreign Bodies & Bitting Injuries)
courses.description: Webinar - Diagnosing & Management of Oral Injuries (incl. Intra-Oral Foreign Bodies & Bitting Injuries) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Certificate of Veterinary Compassionate Care Proficiency (CVCCP)
courses.description: End-of-life care for pets and compassionate work with pet owners is an important category of veterinary medicine that requires a comprehensive understanding of social and emotional communication. This course details recommendations for providers at all levels of veterinary service to employ when addressing this common and yet complicated area of care.

courses.title: ER Procedures
courses.description: In this 2.5-hour video course, ECC experts Dr. Justine Lee and Dr. Stuart Walton will guide our scalpels and demonstrate life-saving measures to address common emergency cases. Registrants will review step-by-step tips for central lines, feeding tubes, and tracking the progress of your critically ill patients. We'll also untangle cannulas and catheters of all kinds and discuss ways to make centesis less scary. Gain confidence in practical application with lessons from world-renowned speakers!

courses.title: Reach for Zen: New Relief for Dogs with Atopic Dermatitis_1.0CE
courses.description: Controlling allergies in dogs can be frustrating for veterinarians and clients. This presentation will introduce a new treatment that provides effective, continuous relief from pruritus and skin inflammation. By exploring expert management guidelines for allergic dermatitis and the concept of clinical remission for atopic dogs, attendees will learn how to achieve more Zen for a variety of allergic patients.

courses.title: A year in review: Pet Poison Helpline Toxin Trends
courses.description: This lecture will discuss the top trends regarding calls received from an international animal poison control center. This includes the top toxins, species, breeds, most common exposures based on age, and how these factors affect exposures, clinical signs and outcomes. We will also discuss several of these toxins in a case based review.

courses.title: 2024 AAV Conference ON DEMAND
courses.description: This on demand course features a selection of recorded sessions previously presented at the 45th Annual AAV Conference & Expo. Sessions will cover avian veterinary techniques and avian medicine. This conference was hosted by the Association of Avian Veterinarians (AAV). The program will focus on advancing avian health, welfare, and conservation through education, advocacy, and science.

courses.title: The Intersection of Nutrition and Rehabilitation for Orthopedic Patients (On Demand)
courses.description: We define pet well-being as the freedom for pets to pursue the world around them unlimited by pain and immobility. The dreaded duo of osteoarthritis and obesity, which slowly robs millions of pets of those freedoms, may go un-noticed by the pet owner. Starting what otherwise can be a difficult conversation is eased by identification of owner aspirations for their pet and linking treatment recommendations to their goals. In this session, we'll explore together what that can look like within the context of clinical case discussion.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Surgical Management of Stifle Injuries in Cats
courses.description:
An international panel of world-renowned experts in the field of feline orthopaedics will be discussing and debating feline stifle injuries consisting of ligamentous injuries (cruciate disease & rupture of multiple ligaments), patellar luxations and other stifle injuries. With cats not equivalent to small dogs, different aetiologies need to be taken into account. However, could certain stifle injuries be treated similarly to equivalent problems in canine patients?
The panel will furthermore address Patellar Fracture & Dental Anomaly Syndrome (PADS) and discuss critically how to differentiate it from a traumatic patellar fracture and how to best treat it.
As part of this interactive exchange panelists will share many useful tips & tricks and attendees will have ample opportunity to ask questions and share their own experiences with the group.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Urinary Incontinence: Managing the Drips and Drops
courses.description:
Urinary incontinence occurs commonly, particularly in older, female dogs and may even result in euthanasia in some cases. Join us for this exciting panel discussion with multidisciplinary world-renowned experts who will discuss normal physiology of micturition and disorders associated with urinary incontinence including the approach to disorders of storage and disorders of voiding. This will lead on to therapy of urinary incontinence which will include medical, surgical, and interventional modality discussions. Additionally, we will explore the management of comorbidities.
Our international panel representing internal medicine, neurology, and surgery will share their wealth of experience with their diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to dogs and cats with urinary incontinence. During the session we will present cases, show examples and welcome audience questions to address additional points of interest and prompt healthy professional debate.

courses.title: Panel Dicussion Genetics - Current Clinical Applications and Whats on the Horizon
courses.description:
With more and more genetic tests becoming available there is an increased need for equine veterinarians to provide horse owners with genetic counseling. Yet, are all commercially available genetic tests valid What is the difference between the many genetic testing laboratories and is there regulatory oversight How do genetics play a role in athletic performance Should it be recommended to guide breeding related decision making What is the latest in genetics research on OCD cervical compressive vertebral myelopathy Wobblers disease equine recurrent uveitis and other common conditions
The international panel consisting of worldrenowned equine veterinarians and geneticists will address these and many other clinically relevant questions and provide insight into how to provide genetic counseling to your clients. This exchange will be highly interactive with attendees able to contribute and ask questions.

courses.title: DNM THERAPEUTIC NUTRITION FOR LOWER URINARY TRACT SIGNS
courses.description: This course explores lower urinary tract signs sin both cats and dogs. It explores the risk factors, common urinary conditions and the diagnosis and management of these conditions. It will help you discuss lower urinary tract signs with your clients, including how therapeutic nutrition can be used to improve their pets' urinary tract health.

courses.title: Join the Local Block Party
courses.description: Oral and dental diseases are known to be painful, though the pain is often hidden. The pain pathway will be reviewed. How to use local block drugs to treat and prevent pain will be the main focus. Types of blocks, different approaches, drug dosages, and methods of delivery will be addressed.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Navicular Syndrome What's the current thinking
courses.description: Navicular syndrome or palmar foot pain remains the most common cause of performance limiting lameness in many equestrian disciplines. Instead of routinely diagnosing navicular disease, we now know that different osseous and soft tissue injuries may result in a set of associated symptoms that we have collectively named navicular syndrome. The different sub-categories of this syndrome, however, may present with slightly different clinical characteristics and generally require very different treatment approaches. It is true that improved diagnostic abilities have not always been met by progress in treatment success. The discussion will review the current thinking regarding the limitations of the clinical examination, the role of advanced imaging and the best choice of treatment strategies for the successful management of a sports horse with navicular syndrome.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - The many ways of fixing broken bones in dogs and cats
courses.description:
Science and art meet when dealing with the many different presentations of fractured jaws. In the advent of recently developed dental materials as well as the advancement in 3D printing the days of simply choosing the correct plate size and plating it are long gone or are they
An international panel of worldrenowned dentistry specialists and surgeons will discuss this fascinating topic from multiple angles and perspectives and will debate the many different ways to fix broken jaws. The fundamental biomechanics that need to be considered and respected will be discussed and how they dictate which techniques are appropriate or optimal. The highly experienced panel will share the decisionmaking criteria that they personally apply and many helpful tips tricks and pearls of wisdom.
Even though the panel might have different preferred techniques to fix the jaws of their patients they are united in their goal to rapidly restore the dog or cats jaws back to fully function and by doing so rapidly improving their patients quality of life.
If you are fascinated by this topic and are wondering how things have changed over the last decades, join us for a very interesting and illuminating journey where attendees will have plenty of opportunity to ask questions and share their own experiences.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Salmonella Infection From the Individual Horse to Outbreak Situations
courses.description:
Salmonella infection in the horse can result in clinical signs ranging from none to fatal colitis and septicemia. The prompt diagnosis of Salmonella infections is important in reducing the risk of pathogen spreading to other animals and people, as well as to direct optimal treatment. Outbreaks of salmonellosis can occur in both farm and hospital settings, can result in costly mitigation strategies and losses due to impact on the horses, as well as loss of business while resolving the outbreak.
An international panel of world-renowned internal medicine clinicians and biosecurity experts will be discussing ongoing monitoring to detect Salmonella, which has become common practice in equine hospitals to allow for prompt detection of pathogen spread and thus keep the impact to a minimum. They will furthermore debate methods for diagnosing and treatment of equine salmonellosis in individual horses, as well as how to investigate and mitigate outbreaks. Equine practitioners need to be knowledgeable in biosecurity practices that reduce the risk of Salmonella introduction and spread in equine populations, both on farms and in equine hospitals.

courses.title: Disease Progression - ON DEMAND
courses.description: This program is designed to prepare doctors within Lap of Love for the various diseases typically encountered within a hospice and palliative care setting. It is separated by body system and covers the most common diseases from which these patients suffer. It reviews the clinical course of those diseases to prepare doctors for the varied conversations that occur within the home, and reviews the palliative treatment options available to optimize quality of life within this setting in which diagnostic options are unavailable, including medications, dietary interventions, and environmental changes.

courses.title: TeamSTEPPS for Veterinary Teams
courses.description: This course adapts the TeamSTEPPS framework, an evidence-based teamwork system originally developed for human healthcare, to veterinary practice settings. Participants will learn structured communication tools including SBAR, Call Out, Check Back, and Handoff/I-PASS for transferring critical patient information accurately between team members. The course covers team leadership behaviors, including Brief, Huddle, and Debrief structures, situation monitoring and shared mental models, and mutual support tools such as task assistance, patient advocacy and assertion (CUS), and structured feedback (DESC). Participants will also review research evidence linking structured team communication to improved safety outcomes and will learn a practical framework for implementing TeamSTEPPS tools within their own practice. Searchable keywords: TeamSTEPPS, team communication, patient safety, SBAR, veterinary teamwork, situation monitoring, communication tools.

courses.title: NAVC Certified Veterinary Business Leader
courses.description:
Unleashing the full potential of veterinary professionals extends beyond their love for animals; it entails arming them with essential business expertise. Acknowledging this imperative, the North American Veterinary Community (NAVC) introduces an innovative certification program meticulously designed for veterinary professionals aiming to enhance their leadership and business acumen.
The NAVC Certified Veterinary Business Leader certificate program is meticulously crafted to delve into the intricacies of successful veterinary practice management, encompassing business principles, leadership strategies, and technical competencies essential for sustained growth and excellence. Whether you're a veterinarian, technician, practice manager, or part of the veterinary team, this comprehensive program is designed to empower you to navigate the complexities of veterinary business with confidence and expertise.
Our unique curriculum equips you with the tools and knowledge needed to lead, strategize, and propel your veterinary practice toward long-term success. Through a blend of theoretical insights and practical applications, you'll gain a deep understanding of business fundamentals while honing your leadership capabilities.
It's worth noting that our program stands distinct from the CVPM certification course offered by the VHMA. With NAVC, you're embarking on a transformative journey tailored specifically to the dynamic needs of the veterinary industry, setting you on the path to becoming a proficient and respected Veterinary Business Leader.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Improving Pain Management of the Front Limb using Regional Analgesia
courses.description:
Surgeries involving the forelimb are commonly performed in small animal practice. The use of regional anesthesia has revolutionized hospital flow, case throughput and, in particular our ability to provide perioperative analgesia and optimal care for patients undergoing these painful procedures. Its use is also expanding beyond simply using nerve blocks to manage surgical pain, with new applications being appreciated for managing chronic pain resulting in lameness or from cancer. The list of possible regional anesthetic techniques that can be used has expanded over the last 20 years and there is often confusion over which technique to use and when to use it. Many veterinarians may find themselves asking Which block should I perform for a particular procedure Is one approach clinically better than another Do the benefits outweigh any potential risks Can I perform blocks blindly or is it worth learning how to use ultrasound to perform my blocks
Join our panel of internationally renowned anesthesia and pain management specialists for an interactive discussion covering the ins and outs of delivering regional anesthesia for forelimb procedures. We will discuss what information experts in the field use to decide which technique to perform on a patient how to select which drug and dose to administer what equipment to use the pros and cons of the various techniques that are possible e.g. blind nerve stimulatorguided ultrasoundguided and their personal preferences. Differences in decision making between cats and dogs will be discussed as will controversial aspects of the various blocks and what types of new techniques are in development and on the horizon.
Whether you are new to the idea of using regional anesthesia for forelimb procedures and simply want to improve your level of patient care or are a seasoned practitioner of nerve blocks and want to refine your approach by hearing what experts are doing and how they got there you will find this session invaluable to your pro

courses.title: Overcoming the I Can't Afford It Objection
courses.description: Before conversations even start, 58 percent of veterinarians anticipate client objections to treatments. Why are we so terrified to talk about money? Every employee must talk to clients about money, from presenting treatment plans to explaining fees to phone shoppers. Get training on how to confidently talk about money.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Readiness for birth Prediction of parturition
courses.description:
The art and science of prediction of parturition will be discussed and debated by four internationally renowned experts in equine reproduction. There is a marked variability in physiological equine gestation length making prediction of parturition in this species especially difficult. On the other hand foaling in horses must be surveilled to avoid loss of mares and their foals due to dystocia or other parturition related emergencies.
In this webinar different methods for prediction of parturition in mares as well as risks and opportunities associated with augmentation of parturition will be compared. The influence of mare breed age parity housing and management practices and the impact of pathological conditions on the onset of parturition and the decision-making process will be discussed.
This panel promises to provide valuable insights and expert opinion through a robust exchange of experiences and ideas. Register now to learn from the worlds leading minds in the field and submit your questions in advance or during the live event to contribute to the discussion on improving outcomes for mares and foals.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Heart Murmur Case-Discussions - Assessing their Importance for Performance & PPE
courses.description: Cardiac murmurs are commonly identified in horses but determining their significance might be challenging especially in a pre-purchase exam setting. Physiological murmurs are absolutely innocent and do not require further investigation but what about pathological murmurs Can we trust our stethoscope to triage which cases need further investigation .Although careful auscultation usually allows us to pinpoint which valve is leaking echocardiography is often needed to assess regurgitation severity Based upon clinical cases the international panel consisting of a group of world-renowned cardiologists will share tips and tricks and provide rules of thumb on how to deal with specific cardiac murmurs regarding diagnosis risk assessment and decision-making in a PPE setting.

courses.title: New Concepts in Minimally Invasive and Interventional Approaches to Chylothorax
courses.description: This 1.5-hr course will present the newest information in minimally invasive surgery (MIS) and other interventional approaches regarding small animal chylothorax from two experts in the field. This will be an interactive webinar with designated a questions and answers session.

courses.title: Tackling Fungal Keratitis Without A Blade
courses.description: Fungal keratitis is a challenging and often frustrating disease to treat in horses, especially in field conditions. In this lecture, I'll walk you through practical, farm-friendly strategies for managing these complex cases. We'll cover the available medications, how to choose them, how to use them effectively, and discuss additional procedures that can enhance medical therapy. Fungal keratitis doesn't have to be a losing battle. With the right approach, you can improve outcomes and give your patients a fighting chance.

courses.title: Webinar - Introduction to Clinical Governance - Just because you've always done it that way?
courses.description:
Clinical governance* is rising in prominence as its relevance is being increasingly recognised by practices and governing bodies alike, but what exactly is it? How can it be applied in first opinion practice and what are the benefits? In this webinar we will look at practical things you can start doing in your practice to improve both clinical and non-clinical outcomes. We will also explore how the entire practice team can be involved.
* Clinical Governance: A system through which veterinary practices/clinics are continuously improving the quality of their services, which safeguards high standards of care and encourages clinical excellence.

courses.title: Improving Mobility in the Aging Patient
courses.description: This lecture will focus on the aging canine and feline patient, and how to assess for sarcopenia and mobility impairment with an emphasis on preserving muscle health, mobility, and quality of life. Multimodal therapy and client education related to the aging patient will be emphasized.

courses.title: Pericardial disease: Neoplastic, Idiopathic, and Left atrial rupture
courses.description: In this 2-hour, LIVE seminar, Gordon Peddle, VMD, DACVIM (Cardiology) will explore the various causes of pericardial effusion in dogs in cats, with a particular focus on malignancy and left atrial rupture secondary to degenerative mitral valve disease

courses.provider: INTERNATIONAL SYMPOSIUM ON EQUINE REPRODUCTION TRUST
courses.title: West Coast Equine Reproduction Symposium (WCERS-VII)
courses.description:
The West Coast Equine Reproduction Symposium is a continuing educational event for veterinarians. The meeting has been held once every 4 years since 2001 in Solvang, CA. Speakers at the symposium are amongst the world leaders in the field of equine reproduction, with a majority of speakers Board Certified in either the American College of Theriogenologists, European College of Animal Reproduction or board certified in both Colleges. The symposium also serves as an important fund-raising event for the International Symposium on Equine Reproduction (ISER), which will be held in Dublin, Ireland, in July of 2027. The WCERS VI will be an in-person meeting with two days of lectures and one day of wet-lab. The lecture part of the Symposium will be divided into 8 sessions, including Stallion Management, Reproductive Diagnostics I, Reproductive Diagnostics II, In Vitro Embryo Production (IVP) and Embryo Transfer, Pregnancy Health and Diagnostic Monitoring, Peripartum Emergencies, Foaling and Postpartum Management, and Sick Foal Management and Treatments.
A series of 36 Lectures, totaling 840 minutes, within two full days. All Lectures will be eligible for CE credit.
On the third day, there are three hands-on, wet-labs modules, each participant can choose one module.
Module 1 - General Stud Farm
Pregnant mare ultrasound fetal evaluation and sexing
Hands on transabdominal ultrasonography with rectal demo in mid-gestation mares; identification of viability parameters (heartbeat, bone maturity, placental thickness) and fetal sexing
Foal resuscitation dummy and placental examination
Protocols for neonatal airway management, ventilation and chest compressions on a mannequin; systematic gross placental exam of frozen samples
Cytology and culture prep biopsy interpretation
Collection of uterine samples; on-farm Gram and Diff-Quik smears; plating for bacterial culture; interpretation of inflammatory versus infectious findings
Semen evaluation
Manual assessment of motility, concentrat

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Neurologic Disease
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage neurologic disease in the field.

courses.title: How I Manage Acute Kidney Injury
courses.description: This webinar will cover the diagnostic approach to AKI and medical treatment including management of hyperkalemia, discussion of fluid therapy, nutritional support, and prognosis.

courses.title: The 90 Day Startup: Launching an In-Home Euthanasia Practice for Veterinarians
courses.description: This 12-week Masterclass, hosted by Kindred.Vet, equips licensed veterinarians with the clinical, business, and ethical skills required to launch a new in-home euthanasia practice. Participants receive guided instruction on compliance, patient care, client communication, marketing, pricing, and emotional resilience specific to end-of-life care. Through paced modules, live sessions, and case-based learning, attendees will move from concept to operational readiness, completing their first client interaction within 90 days. Each week of the program includes a 2-hr workshop and activities outside of the workshop designed to take an additional 2 hours of project work to complete (2.5 credits total per week for 12 weeks).

courses.provider: PACIFIC NORTHWEST PET ER & SPECIALTY CENTER
courses.title: Get Your Thinking Cat On! - A deep dive into feline referral cases
courses.description: What patients are you referring to internal medicine? This lecture will summarize the presenting complaints and outcomes of outpatient and inpatient cats presenting to a specialty internal medicine service after referral. A further deep dive into specific complex cases will help veterinary professionals improve their differential diagnoses, improve diagnostic accuracy, educate owners, and ultimately, better patient outcome.

courses.title: Case Rounds: Diagnostic Strategy for the Vomiting Dog and Cat LIVE
courses.description: In this course learners will work through acute and chronic vomiting presentations in dogs and cats while strengthening clinical reasoning, prioritizing differential diagnoses, interpreting diagnostic findings, developing treatment plans, and navigating client communication. The program emphasizes practical decision-making and evidence-based approaches that participants can immediately incorporate into everyday small animal practice.

courses.provider: CITY OF NEW ORLEANS MOSQUITO, TERMITE AND RODENT CONTROL BOARD
courses.title: Vector Control and Disease Risks for Veterinarians
courses.description:
This comprehensive training is designed for veterinarians and industry professionals seeking to enhance their understanding of vector biology, disease risks, and control strategies in veterinary settings. Participants will learn from leading experts in the field of medical and veterinary entomology about the distribution of vectors in Florida, pre- and post-disaster, the biology and behavior of key vector species, and practical approaches to vector management for veterinary facilities.
The training combines cutting-edge research with applied strategies to address the growing challenges posed by vectors to animal and public health.

courses.title: Managing common skin problems
courses.description: : Dr. Bonenberger will present a complete discussion of the many common dermatologic problems that she encounters in her referral practice. It is Dr. Bonenberger's intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of these common problems- both canine and feline. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common skin diseases and disorders.

courses.title: Rehabilitation, Exercise, and Manual Therapy for Osteoarthritis
courses.description:
This webinar will discuss rehabilitation treatments for osteoarthritis and their complementary role in managing the most common musculoskeletal condition in dogs.
Specifically, the role of rehabilitation modalities, such as extracorporeal shockwave treatment, therapeutic laser, thermal modalities and transcutaneous electrical stimulation will be reviewed. Prescription of therapeutic exercise programs will also be discussed for the arthritic patient. The appropriate use of manual therapy programs, such as stretching and basic joint mobilizations, will also be reviewed.

courses.title: VetQuest Glacier Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
courses.description: This conference will be over 3 days and cover topics related to Orthopedic Medicine & Surgery as well as Physical therapy/Rehab for small animals

courses.title: AAV Avian Veterinary Clinical Competency Program: Tier 1 Avian Anatomy and Physiology
courses.description:
The goal of the AVCCP is to improve, promote and expand avian veterinary medicine in companion avian species* through a program of learning modules taught by specialists in avian practice. The modules are a compilation of 3 progressive tiers containing interactive, self-directed content, case scenarios and quizzes throughout the modules to solidify key learning points.
The AVCCP Will Provide:
Day-one clinical competency avian medicine education for students and early career veterinarians looking to expand their depth of practice in avian medicine.
A foundational review of current literature and research with updated standards of avian medicine care for seasoned practitioners.
A solid foundation for those wishing to further explore specialization in avian medicine.
*Psittacines, passerines, backyard poultry
Tier 1 is available to licensed veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and currently enrolled veterinary students.

courses.description: Event horses face extraordinary physical demands across three distinct but interrelated phases: dressage, cross-country and showjumping, pushing the boundaries of agility, strength, endurance, resilience, and precision. This discussion in the Discipline-Specific Performance Challenges Series unites leading veterinarians and a physiotherapist from across the globe to explore the specific challenges they encounter at different levels of eventing and their different approaches to management and prevention. From young horses stepping up the levels to elite competitors, join the conversation on early recognition of injury, injury treatment, and horse management using a team approach, to optimise the chances of a successful return to training and competition.

courses.title: 4 Ways to End No-Shows
courses.description: No-shows can cost your practice $66,000 per doctor annually in lost business. The average no-show rate for veterinary practices is 11%. Discover four strategies to curb no-shows, setting clear expectations for clients while protecting future practice revenue. This course includes a sample no-show and cancellation policy.

courses.title: Dental Radiography: Positioning with Perrone
courses.description: We can all relate to the pitfalls we encounter when taking dental radiographs. These challenges can cause anxiety and frustration when providing dental patients with the best care. This session will explore three areas you need to develop to decrease your retakes and improve your success rates. I call these the Triple-A - Anatomy, Angulation, and Alignment. I will teach you how to use the Triple-A concepts as a checklist when positioning for the best possible outcome or assessing your unsuccessful results to determine the next steps.

courses.title: Relax PRN London's Calling; Neuro and Surgical Oncology
courses.description: Come across the pond with us and earn 15 CE hours while you enjoy all that London has to offer. This program is catered to the small animal practitioner interested in better knowledge and approach to Neurology and Surgical oncology. Learn all things brain/spine and surgical approaches to cancer. In your down time explore London's history, culture, art, food and fashion scenes.

courses.description: This program is a comprehensive webinar designed for veterinary professionals eager to deepen their knowledge of compounding within animal health. This session will explore the essentials of various dosage forms, regulatory insights for 503 A and 503 B pharmacies, and foundational guidance on navigating the veterinary compounding business. We will also introduce Bova GS 441524, a first line treatment for FIP, and discuss how it fits within patient specific care. Perfect for those looking to strengthen their understanding and practice in the veterinary compounding space.

courses.title: Enhancing Your VETSPAN: Maximize Your Health and Career Longevity Through the Five Pillars of Healthspan

courses.title: Chronic Pain for the General Practitioner: Identification, Monitoring, and What's New in Treatment Options for Dogs and Cat
courses.description: This lecture is designed to introduce the General Practitioner to pain management in companion animals. Specifically, it will address the difficulties and nuances in identifying pain in dogs and cats, methods to obtain history and utilize clues from the physical exam to confirm the existence of pain and help localize it, and the selection of appropriate treatments. Furthermore, the general practitioner will gain insight into how to set up a pain management game plan with owners. This "treat and track" approach helps to ensure early intervention and knowing when to refer. Physiology of pain, the nociceptive pathway, and how to design a pain management protocol utilizing this knowledge will be discussed. Currently available pharmaceuticals as well as physical modalities will be presented.

courses.title: Prevent and Protect: Boosting Your Shelter Vaccination Protocol
courses.description:
Vaccination remains one of the most important tools for minimizing disease and preventing outbreaks in our shelters and communities. Recommendations for vaccinating these populations of animals are different than those for privately owned pets. New products and strategies require continuous review of shelter practices. During this session we will explain everything you need to know about making sure your vaccination protocols are as effective possible.
Audience: Shelter staff, management, leadership; Veterinary technicians and assistants; General veterinary practitioners working with shelters/serving as veterinarian of record; Veterinarians new to shelter practice

courses.title: Learning to Love New Technology: A Friendly Guide for Veterinary Teams
courses.description: New tools and the use of AI have permeated our profession for good, and the payoff in efficiency and accuracy has been umatched. But if you find yourself feeling left behind or overwhelmed, it can diminish your job satisfaction and cause tension in your clinic. Whether it's a gap in understanding, lack of good process documentation, or just a fear of change, knowing what's holding you back is half the battle. Learn how to identify and overcome your won hesitance around new technology - and for managers and team leads, help your teams do the same.

courses.title: Pre-Euthanasia Sedation Protocols at Their Best - ON DEMAND
courses.description:
The 2020 edition of the American Veterinary Medical Association's guidelines for the euthanasia of animals states that "pre-euthanasia sedation or anesthesia should be provided whenever practicable," making euthanasia a two-step process. Performing this step prior to euthanasia reduces stress for all stakeholders, reduces the need for physical restraint, increases safety, and allows the caregiver to witness their pet at peace before the final farewell.
It is important to differentiate between sedation and anesthesia. Sedation is a state from which the patient can be aroused with sufficient stimulation to a conscious state and become aware of what is happening. Anesthesia is a state of unconsciousness where arousal by noxious stimuli does not occur. The latter expands the techniques we can use for administering euthanasia drugs beyond the intravenous route; for example, drugs can be given intracardiac, which is not acceptable under sedation alone.
In this session, the drugs or combinations of drugs that can be used to sedate or anesthetize dogs and cats will be discussed. Choices are based on the pet's personality and their physical or psychological status. Some drugs can alter cardiovascular function and delay the onset of euthanasia agents; however, the benefits of a two-step process outweigh using intravenous euthanasia drugs alone.

courses.title: Equine Pastern Dermatitis: Expert Insights into a Common Clinical Conundrum
courses.description: Equine Pastern dermatitis (EPD) is a non-specific cutaneous reaction pattern affecting the pastern region. Although common, it can be a debilitating condition and pose a real challenge to even experienced veterinarians. The underlying causes of EPD may be many and varied and in some cases multiple aetiologies combine to create a confusing clinical picture. This international panel of experts will explore the different forms of EPD, risk factors, and compare their experience and knowledge of therapeutic approaches.

courses.title: Managing the lame dog and cat

The combination of two world renowned Veterinary Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. courses.description: Dental radiographs are an essential part of the oral exam. The crown is just the tip of the iceberg. The majority of dental pathology is found sub gingivally or below the gumline. Radiographs will help diagnose pathology that is not visible with the naked eye, confirm suspect pathology, as well as help demonstrate the pathology to the client. Dental radiographs can improve the standard of care in your practice and increase your clinics revenue. Learn trouble shooting for common errors.

courses.title: Challenging Extractions and Extraction Complications in Dogs and Cats ON DEMAND

courses.title: Panel Discussion Retinal Diseases - Diagnosis & Treatments
courses.description:
Small animal retinal diseases are more common than many pet owners and veterinary practitioners may realize and can be devastating to an individual animal or breeding line. We are excited to have a diverse panel of internationally recognized veterinary ophthalmologists who will briefly review clinically useful examination and diagnostic techniques to facilitate canine and feline fundus evaluation. The group will then discuss various topics to include pathological changes consistent with retinal disorders, thoughts on inherited retinal disease screening tests, maximizing retinal reattachment surgery success, and novel therapeutics.
This panel discussion will be aimed at the level of an experienced general practitioner, although those with a more advanced interest in ophthalmology will also find it very useful. During the session we will present cases, show examples and welcome audience questions to address additional issues of interest and prompt healthy professional debate.

courses.title: Stabilization of the ECC Patient in General Practice
courses.description: This lecture will discuss common emergencies that present to general practice. It will include stabilization, diagnostics and immediate interventions and treatments of these emergencies and when the ideal time is to transfer to a referral hospital. It will also discuss a team approach to these situations between doctors and veterinary technicians. Examples of the common emergencies that will be discussed include patients that have sustained trauma, GI foreign bodes and other GI diseases, pyometra, GDV, and spontaneous hemorrhage (hemoabdomen/pericardial effusion).

courses.title: Vacuolar Hepatopathy in Dogs
courses.description: Increases in serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity are a common finding in dogs with or without clinical illness. These increases often signal the presence of vacuolar (glycogen and/or lipid ) in the liver. This lecture will provide an algorithm to use in investigating the underlying cause of vacuolar change in the liver with range from endocrine disorders, acquired liver disease, drug induction or as a consequence of primary gastrointestinal disease or neoplasia in the splanchnic bed. Special attention will be given to the consequences of corticosteroid induction of vacuolar changes. Finally what is known about the pathology and clinical sequela of the idiopathic vacuolar hepatopathy that occurs in Scottish Terriers, Miniature Schnauzers, Shih Tzus and occasionally mixed breed dogs will be discussed.

courses.title: Behavior Challenges in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: In this 3-hour, LIVE seminar, Lisa Radosta, DVM, DACVB, will address the multifaceted challenges of canine and feline behavior. The session combines interdog aggression, generalized anxiety, and behavior changes linked to discomfort or pain. With a focus on risk factors, prognosis, and treatment strategies, attendees will learn a spectrum of care approach ranging from environmental management to medical intervention. Real-world examples will help practitioners confidently manage these cases and improve the welfare of both pets and families.

Lecture topics include management of complicated and long bone fractures as well as external fixation techniques. Time for discussion and radiographic review of complicated cases will be provided. The hands-on laboratory exercises include plate fixation of radial, ulnar and metacarpal fractures as well as fetlock arthrodesis. Dr Wininger and Dr Hackett will bring case examples highlighting the triage, stabilization and management of these dynamic and challenging cases.

courses.title: Patching the Petechiae: Consensus Statement Highlights on Diagnosis and Treatment of Immune Thrombocytopenia in Dogs and Cats
courses.description:
This program is designed to provide veterinary professionals with a comprehensive, evidence-based overview of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) in dogs and cats. Attendees will gain an understanding of the pathophysiology of ITP, learn how to apply diagnostic and treatment algorithms from the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine (ACVIM) consensus guidelines, and develop practical strategies for managing both routine and complex cases in clinical practice.
In this session, we will take a case-based approach to the diagnosis and management of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) in dogs and cats. Specifically, this session will review recent insights into the pathophysiology of ITP, describe how a diagnosis of ITP can be reached, and discuss the management of this disease. We will review the recently published ACVIM consensus statements on the diagnosis and treatment of ITP and examine the clinical algorithms that accompany these guidelines.
This session will also explore the use of immunosuppressive therapies and blood product transfusion in the treatment of ITP, including practical considerations for clinical decision-making. Novel and emerging therapeutic strategies will be introduced, with a focus on their application in more severe or refractory cases.
This program is intended for veterinarians and registered veterinary technicians/technologists and assumes a foundational knowledge of small animal medicine. The content is designed to enhance clinical decision-making and improve patient outcomes through the application of current evidence-based guidelines.

courses.title: Molly Angel DVM FAVD DAVDC
courses.description:
Feline Dentistry and Extractions with Wet Lab
This program consists of 4 hours of lecture presentations followed by 4 hours of wet lab using feline cadavers that will focus on basic oral evaluations, diagnostics and therapeutics including in-depth instruction with extraction techniques. The lecture presentation will begin with normal anatomy of the feline adult and pediatric patient, normal radiographic positioning of the feline patient, review of principles and positioning of standard imaging including digital radiographic and cone beam computed tomography, general and individual patient care with respect to the anesthetic process, fundamental anesthetic protocols and patient care for the feline dental patient, applications of local anesthesia and techniques appropriate for the feline patient, as well as standard oral surgical flap and extraction techniques. Patient aftercare and follow-up recommendations will also be discussed as well as appropriate post-operative instructions.
Lecture will also include basic necessities of the dental practice including equipment needs, logistic and regulatory requirements in regard to radiation safety, hand and power instrumentation specific to feline oral surgery suture materials as well as appropriate use and maintenance of the above noted equipment.
The wet lab segment of this day will include the application of the aforementioned lecture topics to be applied to feline cadavers. Participants will practice local nerve block applications, general oral flap techniques, closure of tissues, use of high-speed instrumentation as well as hand instrumentation to complete general therapeutics and extraction techniques on cadaver samples.
The learning objectives of this course should provide the participants with a better understanding of the dental operatory, equipment used, diagnostic procedures and the entire anesthetic dental process for a feline patient. The participants should also expect to have individual instruction during the w

courses.title: Hearts in Crisis: Case Discussions on Cardiopulmonary Arrest, Including Anaesthesia-Related Incidents
courses.description: Cardiopulmonary Arrest (CPA) is uncommon in veterinary practice, but a well-prepared team trained to recognize and respond to sudden CPA can save many of these patients with good quality Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR). Although there is strong evidence that peri-anesthetic CPA is often associated with a good prognosis, the signs of CPA may be subtle under anesthesia, underscoring the need for vigilant monitoring and early action.

courses.title: The Legal Building Blocks of Californias RVT Profession
courses.description: In this informative session, the speakers will cover a broad range of statutes and regulations that define the scope of practice and breadth of skills in which California licensed Registered Veterinary Technicians engage. The session will include tips on maximizing the training and education of RVTs, as well as clarification of the relationship between RVTs and their supervising veterinarians. The session is intended to encourage veterinarians and RVTs to increase the tasks undertaken by RVTs, and educate with respect to how the law governs and regulates these activities.

courses.title: Diabetes Mellitus in the Cat: Diagnosis, prevention and management
courses.description: Feline overweight and obesity (O&O) continues to be a common health problem affecting more than 50% of domestic cats worldwide, with obesity being considered a major risk factor for the development of diabetes mellitus. Appropriate nutrition plays a key role in prevention and management of O&O as well as management of diabetes. In this seminar, we will examine the challenges associated with diagnosis and monitoring of diabetes, focusing on how strategies for prevention can also be beneficial in disease control.

courses.title: CKD Therapy - Beyond Diet and Fluids
courses.description: The goal of this one-hour CE course is to review chronic kidney disease therapeutic options, outside of diet and fluids. IRIS diagnosis and staging will briefly be reviewed, as well common treatments for symptoms of kidney disease for both dogs and cats, including hypertension, proteinuria, and gastrointestinal signs. The main advantages and disadvantages of renal diets will also be summarized. The focus will then turn to the gut kidney axis and dysbiosis that occurs in chronic renal failure and the possible benefit of probiotics to support kidney health. The importance of phosphate management in chronic kidney disease will be described and research presented on the longevity of patients and phosphate target levels. Attendees will learn how to incorporate FGF-23 testing for improved phosphate control in feline patients. Different phosphate binding options, beyond renal diets, will be discussed. Hypokalemia management will also be presented.

courses.title: The Metro Section: Moving Beyond Antibiotics for Diarrhea
courses.description: In this on demand webinar, we will be discussing how Antibiotics such as Metronidazole have long been prescribed as a first line treatment for acute diarrhea. Antibiotics have negative effects including dysbiosis, gastrointestinal upset, and induction of antibiotic resistance. Alternative therapies such as probiotics and prebiotics such as Pro Pectalin can result in similar improvements in diarrhea while minimizing adverse effects. In addition, these treatments, the appropriate care for patients with diarrhea also includes supportive care for dehydration, hypovolemia and electrolyte derangements. In this lecture, we will discuss the various treatments for patients experiencing acute diarrhea to maximize response and minimize adverse effects.

courses.title: Better Client Conversations About Parasite Protection
courses.description: Learn how to have a consistent team message about parasite protection. Get strategies to increase preventative dispensing. Follow up client conversations with text and email refill reminders.

courses.title: AO VET NA Blended Course - Surgical Management of Pelvic Fractures and Periarticular Trauma of the Pelvic Limb
courses.description:
Spotlight Series Module 1: Surgical Management of Pelvic Fractures
This new module aims to provide participants with all the required knowledge and skills to address pelvic fractures in dogs. Following the use of precourse case-based discussion, participants will be able to devise and interpret a comprehensive diagnostic plan for patients with pelvic fractures. This will include the use of advanced imaging and planning software, as required, in order to formulate an appropriate therapeutic plan. Following the on-site portion of the course including hands-on laboratory sessions, participants will be able to compare the advantages of different surgical approaches to the pelvis and use these to expose fractures of the ilium, acetabulum or sacrum. Participants will be able to discriminate between different reduction techniques and fixation methods allowing them to choose the most appropriate options for any given scenario, with an emphasis on complex situations such as those where bone stock is minimal, or where multiple injuries have been sustained. Through the use of case discussions, participants will develop an ability to critique postoperative images, anticipate complications and develop strategies to avoid these in the future.
Spotlight Series Module 2: Periarticular Trauma of the Pelvic Limb
Joint injury and subsequent instability are common problems in pets, athletes and working dogs subjected to excessive trauma. Joint injury leads to poor function, pain and osteoarthritis. In this Master's Spotlight Series course, we will discuss the diagnosis and management of luxations and articular / periarticular fractures of the pelvic limb excluding fractures of the Pelvis / SI Luxations and Achille's tendon injury. In addition, we will build on surgical skills developed in the AO VET NA Principles of Fracture Management and AO VET NA Advanced Fracture Management courses to manage fractures of the distal extremity, as well as articular/periarticular fractures of the stif

courses.title: Traveling Vet Retreats Paris France 2026
courses.description: Traveling Vet Retreats provides destination continuing education conferences for veterinarians. We host small group lectures with boarded specialists in unique, once in a lifetime locations. Attendees also have the opportunity to participate in group yoga sessions and a relaxing group trip after completing 15 hours of continuing education.

courses.title: Home Hacks to help pets with Mobility Issues - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Mobility issues are something that plagues a large percentage of geriatric dogs. Whether the cause is arthritis, sarcopenia, disc disease, cancer, neuropathy, etc. - the owner will struggle with ways to keep their dogs moving and also comfortable in the home. This lecture will cover the practical tips, tricks and home hacks that families need while managing a mobility impaired pet!

courses.title: DNM NUTRITION MYTHS & FACTS: Part 1
courses.description: The challenge for veterinary professionals today is that the Internet has made it harder, not easier, to educate pet owners about what to feed their pets. Because of the abundance of misinformation, proper pet nutrition counseling by veterinary practices is more important than ever. The Nutrition Myths & Facts: Part 1 course explores the problem of and solutions to nutrition myths, how owner misconceptions can arise, and debunks myths about raw food diets, protein, such as animal digest, by-products and low protein diets for seniors , and food coloring and preservatives.

courses.provider: PHOENIX VETERINARY SURGICAL SPECIALISTS & ACUTEVET KANSAS CITY
courses.title: Veterinary Electrochemotherapy: Scientific Training & Clinical Applications
courses.description: This 24.0 hour online seminar series will feature 24 online powerpoint sessions, 24 quizzes, over 36 chapters and articles required reading materials, and four two-hour interactive practical online sessions. The course will provide a comprehensive overview of electrochemotherapy (ECT) in canines and felines.

courses.title: How To Really Read Intraoral Radiographs ON DEMAND
courses.description: Intraoral radiography is essential for the practice of quality canine and feline dentistry. This class will cover the essentials of dental intraoral radiography acquisition and interpretation.

courses.title: Let's get practical: clinical care for senior dogs
courses.description: This session will provide a quick overview of the special healthcare needs of senior dogs and how clinicians can develop a systematic, evidence-based approach to assessment and management of these complex cases. We will also review key resources to help with senior dog care, including validated clinical assessment tools and important clinical practice guidelines.

courses.title: On Demand: Multimodal Management and the Importance of Nutrition for the Treatment of Feline Osteoarthritis
courses.description:
This session discusses the diagnosis and non-surgical management of feline osteoarthritis. Multimodal management and other treatment options will be discussed. The importance of nutrition in managing feline osteoarthritis will be emphasized. This session is for all small animal practitioners who see older cats in their practice.
Practitioners will learn about the differences between the presentation of arthritis in dogs and cats, the principles of pain management for arthritic cats, and multimodal management.

courses.title: Common Feline and Canine Oral Pathology ON DEMAND
