courses.description: This lecture thoroughly reviews common oral pathology found in feline and canine dental patients. Common oral pathology will include, but not be limited to, malocclusions, periodontal disease stages, gingival enlargement and recession, tooth resorption types, furcation exposure classes, gingivostomatitis, etc. This training will also stress the importance of having a complete dental chart and understanding the modified trident numbering system for primary and secondary teeth.

courses.title: Management of CKD in Dogs
courses.description: This webinar focuses on the diagnosis, staging, and management of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in dogs, emphasizing early detection, slowing disease progression, and improving quality of life.

courses.title: Feline Enrichment Unleashed: Creative Strategies for a Healthier Cat
courses.description: This session will explore a variety of non-food-based enrichment techniques designed to keep feline patients active, mentally stimulated, and engaged. We'll delve into creative enrichment strategies that can help manage weight and support overall wellness. Additionally, we will cover practical tips for administering oral medications, including strategies to ensure a low-stress experience for both cats and their caregivers. You will learn valuable insights and tools that will enhance your approach to feline care, promoting healthier and more fulfilling lives for your feline patients.

courses.title: Periodontal Disease in Dogs and Cats - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Periodontal disease occurs when plaque and tartar accumulation lead to inflammation and destruction of the teeth's supporting structures. Periodontal disease is one of the most common conditions affecting over 80% of dogs by age three. Attendees will learn to understand the importance of anesthetized oral exams and dental radiographs for accurate diagnosis, and review treatment options ranging from professional cleanings to extractions. The session will also introduce indications for hyaluronic acid (HA) and discuss the research supporting HA products in periodontal disease.

courses.title: Online Forms Made Easy
courses.description: Digital forms have become the standard in veterinary care, evolving into tools that support both client expectations and better medicine. Forms are sent with confirmations for clients to complete and submit before appointments or procedures. Whether you are just beginning to explore digital forms or looking to refine your current process, this course will teach you practical ways to elevate your use of online forms.

courses.title: Golden Years: Tackling Aging and Arthritis in our Senior Felines
courses.description: This program will review aging changes in cats and present the difference between normal physiologic aging and pathologic changes. There will be a general overview of feline osteoarthritis (OA) including epidemiology, prevalence and risk factors. Diagnostic tips- including exam strategies and unique radiographic features of feline OA will be presented. Participants will gain knowledge on multi-modal treatment strategies including pharmacologic medications, supplements, diet and environmental modification. Finally, participants will learn exercise interventions and home programs for senior cats focused on improving strength, mobility and quality of life.

courses.title: Updates & Treatments of Equine Pastern Dermatitis ON DEMAND
courses.description: Pastern dermatitis and the other 'colloquial' terms above represent a disease complex rather than a specific condition. Differential diagnoses include vasculitis, contact irritant dermatitis, bacterial folliculitis, chronic progressive lymphedema (CPL), and others. Clinical signs, empiric treatment options diagnostic tools such as biopsy will be covered.

courses.title: A Spectrum of Care Approach to Canine Heartworm Disease
courses.description: Open Door Veterinary Collective and American Heartworm Society jointly created this course to support learning how to apply a spectrum of evidence-based care approach to the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of canine heartworm disease and increase access to veterinary care for more client-patient pairs. One hour of continuing education credit available.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Oncological emergencies
courses.description:
Oncological emergencies in dogs and cats are relatively common yet decision making can be highly challenging. A multidisciplinary panel of internationally renowned specialists consisting of a surgeon and two medical oncologists (USA & UK) will discuss the best approaches to a variety of oncology emergencies and how to get the best outcomes for your patients. The discussion will focus on the immediate diagnostic and therapeutic steps for these complicated patients and will include management of common emergency presentations of tumors and acute chemotherapy complications.
Attending veterinarians will have plenty of opportunity to ask questions and share their own experiences with the group.

courses.title: Flapping Wounds
courses.description: This lecture will cover all facets of subdermal plexus flaps, axial pattern flaps and myocutaneous flaps. We will discuss indications, surgical techniques, post-operative management and referral. The program will be tailored to general practitioners and will serve as both a refresher as well as deliver up-to-date information.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Canine Chronic Nasal Discharge Challenging Cases approach, workup, differential diagnoses and management
courses.description: The dog that presents over and over with a chronic nasal discharge can be challenging and frustrating to treat. Join us as our international panel of world-leading experts walk us through the differentials to consider, the work up from imaging to sampling techniques interpretation of results, and therapeutic challenges. Using a selection of cases, they will delve into interesting but challenging cases. As they share their tips and tricks along with their extensive experience, they will work through the differentials to consider such as:¿infectious causes (bacterial versus fungal), inflammatory disease (such as lymphoplasmacytic rhinitis), trauma, parasites, foreign bodies, tumours and tooth root abscesses which can all cause rhinitis and sinusitis. We will welcome questions from the attendees.

courses.title: Dog longevity 101: Aging fundamentals that every vet should know
courses.description: This course will cover the basic elements of aging biology in dogs, focusing on mechanisms that lead to aging-associated disease and potential targets for therapeutic interventions. We will explore the concept of aging as a modifiable risk factor for common diseases occurring in older dogs and look at existing and future preventive medicine options that can slow the aging process and extend healthy lifespan by delaying disease and preserving good quality of life.

courses.title: Challenging Cases & Innovative Clinical Approaches
courses.description: In this webinar, explore new clinical approaches to common veterinary surgical cases using clinical evidence. Attendees will also review the challenges associated with hemostasis and how to tackle its related risk factors, among others.

courses.provider: ZERO PAIN PHILOSOPHY - ACE VETS LIMITED
courses.title: Zero Pain Philosophy Dental Pain Course
courses.description: This course gives the learner the knowledge required to ensure optimal analgesia is provided to all patients being treated for dental pain

courses.title: Mastering Cruciate Disease in Dogs: Surgical and Non-Surgical Approaches
courses.description:
This advanced course offers a deep dive into the complexities of managing cranial cruciate ligament (CCL) disease. Designed as a continuation of CCL 101, it focuses on advanced diagnostic tools, including imaging techniques such as radiographs, CT, and MRI. Participants will explore surgical options, regenerative therapies like stem cells and PRP, and rehabilitation strategies tailored to enhance patient recovery. With practical, research-backed content, this course equips veterinary professionals with the skills to address CCL disease comprehensively and confidently.
Keywords: advanced CCL management, canine rehabilitation, surgical options, regenerative medicine, stem cell therapy, PRP, diagnostic imaging, joint stability, patient recovery, veterinary continuing education.

courses.title: Just Keep Swimming: What To Do When You're Drowning at Work and in Life
courses.description: 300 to 1,000 words of self-talk enter in your mind every minute of every day. You can allow this self-talk to drive your emotions & behaviors, or you can take control of your self-talk and grow your resilience. Stories from people like Simon Sinek and Kobe Bryant will illustrate how conscious decisions to become more present can help us to narrate our own stories, reduce stress, build executive function and self-regulation, and improve our ability to cope with, adapt to and even prevent adversity.

courses.title: Extraction Dissatisfaction
courses.description: The ins and outs of common complications of oral surgical dental extractions will be covered. The most appropriate selection and use of dental equipment will be reviewed. Diagnosis and treatment of retained tooth roots, management of different types of tooth resorption in cats and dogs, treatment of oro-nasal fistulas, and handling lost root tips will be covered. The importance of pre- and post-intraoral radiographs including the role they play in ethical dental procedures will be emphasized.

courses.title: Techniques for Tension-Free Wound Closure
courses.description: Using a series of clinical cases, we will discuss techniques for achieving cosmetic, tension-free wound closure while preserving blood supply. Topics will include proper undermining, the use of walking sutures and releasing incisions, closing oddly shaped defects, and eliminating dog-ears. We'll also discuss how to create subdermal plexus flaps, such as the sliding pedicle advancement flaps, plastic surgery techniques (H, V-Y, and Z), and both axial and inguinal skin folds.

courses.title: Using Fear Free Principles to Improve Anesthetic Safety In Complicated Patients
courses.description: Decreasing fear, anxiety, stress (FAS), and pain leads to safer anesthesia by allowing a lower dose of sedative and anesthetic drugs needed for anesthesia premedication, induction, maintenance, and recovery. Lower drug dosages are especially critical in complicated patients with underlying disease and physiologic compromise. In this discussion, Tamara Grubb DVM, PhD, DACVAA, will explore the role of Fear Free principles in anesthetic safety, especially in the compromised/complicated patient.

courses.title: Multimodal Management of Canine Osteoarthritis ON-DEMAND
courses.description: This seminar will provide a review of osteoarthritis pathophysiology, with a focus on therapeutic targets. It will introduce screening tools for the general practitioner to detect canine arthritis earlier, as well as monitoring tools to evaluate treatment efficacy and patient progression. Evidence-based multimodal management options will be thoroughly discussed, including pharmaceutical, nutraceutical/ nutritional, rehabilitative, sports medicine, and surgical interventions.

courses.title: Fixing the fallout: Debriefing animal care workers after a difficult encounter or adverse event
courses.description: Animal care facilities are often seen as the place for quality animal care and pet owner support. Unfortunately, there are also instances of adverse events and negative outcomes. When a highly stressful event occurs, it can affect members across a team, sometimes resulting in longer term symptoms of burnout, compassion fatigue and challenges to mental health. A debriefing post event can be critical in reducing these potential outcomes. This presentation Fixing the Fallout: Debriefing Animal Care Workers after a Difficult Outcome or Adverse Event will focus on helping a facility debrief its workers after a potentially negative occurrence, in the hopes that a team can build resiliency and diminish long term effects of traumatic incidents.

courses.title: The Intersection of Diet and Behavior (On Demand)
courses.description:
Nutrition plays a fundamental role in behavior and cognition by influencing neurodevelopment and nervous system functioning across life stages. Diet is the primary source of critical active ingredients like vitamins, fatty acids, proteins, and fiber, which either directly act on the nervous system or indirectly regulate important systems such as the microbiota gut-brain axis. Another critical aspect of maintaining optimum nutrition in our patients is recognizing the impact of past experiences and learning on feeding behavior.
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: Managing common abdominal problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with abdominal problems The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common Hepatic, urinary & gastrointestinal problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Rediscover Meaning and Purpose Beyond the Daily Grind of Practice
courses.description: This webinar aims to assist veterinary professionals to reclaim inspiration lost to the daily grind. It will explore how compassion fatigue and emotional residue turn passion into duty, describe practical tools, like reflection and group support to lighten the load, reconnect emotionally, and strengthen client relationships. Real-world examples will highlight veterinary chaplaincy's role in reviving purpose and supporting the human-animal bond.

courses.title: Initial management of common clinical problems cranial to the diaphragm
courses.description:
In this seminar, Drs Butler, Maggs and Johnson will present a complete discussion of the common emergency clinical problems that they encounter in their individual practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of the problems. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common emergencies.
The three specialists will bring case examples highlighting the triage, stabilization and management of these dynamic and challenging cases.

courses.title: Communication in Practice
courses.description: This course covers a non-medical, interactive presentation/training to educate veterinarians, veterinary technicians, veterinary nurses and other professional veterinary staff in communication skills to enhance their interactions with clients and team members. Effective communication is key to ensuring clear understanding between veterinary teams, clients, and pet owners, ultimately leading to improved patient care and client satisfaction. This course is based on an existing training approach in Europe, described in writing by Dr. Roeland Wessels, Dr. Jolanda Janssen and Professor Theo Lam ("Communication in Practice"). The training has been adapted for application in the US with materials from additional references "Handbook of Veterinary Communication Skills" by Carol Gray and Jenny Moffet, "Developing Communication Skills for Veterinary Practice" by Jane Shaw and Jason Coe, and "Let them" by Mel Robbins.

courses.title: ESTRUS SUPPRESSION AND PROGESTIN SUPPLEMENTATION (1190-38769)
courses.description: ESTRUS SUPPRESSION AND PROGESTIN SUPPLEMENTATION (1190-38769) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.provider: ANDREA VAN DE WETERING, DVM, FAVD
courses.title: Good Bite or Bad Bite: Pediatric Dentistry and malocclusions
courses.description: This course will cover an overview of common pediatric dental issues and treatment decisions regarding malocclusions and common pediatric trauma.

courses.provider: BOB RACICH DVM / LAKE VIEW EQUINE VETERINARY CLINIC
courses.title: 16th Philippe Benoit Progressive Lameness Diagnosis, Imaging and Treatment Lectures and Wetlab
courses.description:
Our 17th of 22 year Equine Lameness Conference with Dr Philippe Benoit
covers Back, Neck, Pelvis Diagnostics and Treatments, as well as a section on Orthobiologics, primarily PRP and PPP

courses.title: NAVC Veterinary Microbiome Certification
courses.description:
Welcome to Microbiome Basics! You might have noticed an increasing discussion about the microbiomes of dogs and cats, and your clients might be asking you questions about this topic. While there is a wealth of knowledge to uncover regarding the microscopic communities living within our patients, this course offers practical information on microbiomes to enhance your discussions with clients, improve patient care and promote overall health.
The NAVC Veterinary Microbiome Certification course comprehensively analyzes the microbes in the various systems of cats and dogs, focusing on their contributions to digestion, immune function and overall wellness. You will learn to distinguish between diagnostic tests, assess gut health with emerging technologies, and grasp the connections between the microbiome and critical organ systems, including the gut-brain and gut-skin axes.
Uncover how factors such as diet, birthing practices and responsible use of antimicrobials affect microbiome balance and health outcomes. Acquire knowledge about microbiome-related therapies, from probiotics and prebiotics to innovative techniques such as fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). Emphasizing clinical applications, you will assess current protocols and discover strategies that support microbiome health to improve patient care.
Once you complete this certification, you will have the skills and confidence to implement microbiome science in your daily veterinary practice. This will enhance the outcomes of your patients and position you at the cutting edge of this swiftly evolving field.

courses.title: Updates in CCL Disease in Dogs: What You Need to Know from Prevention to Treatment
courses.description: This presentation provides a comprehensive update on cranial cruciate ligament (CCL) disease in dogs, covering its pathophysiology, risk factors, diagnostic strategies, and treatment options. It emphasizes that CCL disease is a chronic, degenerative condition often presenting acutely, and outlines both surgical and non-surgical approaches to management. Strategies for potential prevention - including delayed gonadectomy, maintaining lean body condition, and regular conditioning - are also discussed.

courses.title: (On Demand Webinar)(English): INTRODUCTION TO SUSTAINABLE EATING: MAKING A DIFFERENCE ONE MEAL AT A TIME
courses.description:
Our eating habits can shape a greener future for our planet, protecting the environment, marine life, and biodiversity. In this conference, we'll explore:
- The urgent need to talk about sustainable food choices
- Navigating the landscape of sustainable agriculture
- Debunking the myth: is organic always the healthiest option?
- Practical tips and tricks to reduce the ecological footprint of meals
- Looking to the future: insect farming to meet growing food demand
- Pet food as a solution to food waste

courses.title: Radiation Safety Training
courses.description: This course provides a foundational overview of ionizing radiation, its health effects, regulatory dose limits, contamination control, ALARA principles, and proper use of dosimeters and protective equipment. Participants will learn how to maintain safety, compliance, and competency when working with or around radiation in veterinary and research environments

courses.title: Panel Discussion - LASER Therapy for the Management of Musculoskeletal Injuries
courses.description:
The use of LASER therapy for musculoskeletal (MSK) injuries in horses has and continues to grow across the globe. With several LASER types, specifications and protocols available, we have assembled an international panel featuring four leading and highly experienced experts to discuss and debate the clinical applications of LASER therapy in horses.
Valuable for both experienced LASER users and those wanting to explore the potential of this technology, this interactive session will offer insights grounded in the latest scientific research and clinical experience.

courses.title: Certificate Program: Master Clinical Neurology
courses.description:
Our much-loved Master Clinical Neurology course has been upgraded! With 3 new topics and a refresh on seizure management, Neuro 2.0 now offers 10 hours of CE credit. If you ever diagnose back pain, treat seizures, or feel like your neuro exams could use a tune-up, this workshop is for you!
Through this three-part series, Dr. Bill Bush and his colleague, Dr. Martin Young, will share practical tips and real case examples on localizing lesions, managing inflammatory brain disease, vestibular disease, acute and chronic seizure management, and more. We'll also discuss current recommendations for disc disease, identify the most commonly seen congenital CNS anomalies, and enjoy a session devoted entirely to feline vestibular disease. Last but not least, review seizure identification and management with video case studies and get all the latest on anticonvulsant drugs.

courses.title: Feline Vaccinology & the Zen of Cats
courses.description: Feline medicine is good business and represents a significant, and often underutilized, opportunity in companion animal practice. In this webinar, Dr. W. Mark Cousins will review how understanding today's feline market, including the unique expectations and decision-making behaviors of cat owners, can help practices deliver higher-quality care while strengthening financial performance. Dr. Cousins will also explore how the feline market segment differs from the general mix of private practice and how preventive strategies, including feline vaccinology, can support better clinical outcomes, improve client compliance, and increase average transaction value. Attendees will discover practical ways to create a more cat-friendly practice environment that can enhance the client experience.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Geriatric Dentistry: Decision-Making & Challenging Case Discussions
courses.description: This interactive panel brings together equine dental experts to openly explore decision-making in older patients with dental disease and unique age-related conditions, including quality-of-life considerations. Through the discussion of challenging real-world cases, the panel will share and debate their approaches to diagnosis, treatment planning, and client communication to optimise outcomes in this unique patient population.

courses.title: Spill the proTEIn. An Update on Proteinuria Management
courses.description:
This will provide a review of current management protocols for
proteinuria. We will discuss the pathophysiology and etiologies of proteinuria development as well as recommendations for adjunctive diagnostics, dietary management, medication protocols, and follow up guidelines.

courses.title: DNM Feeding Dogs
courses.description: As you know, there's more to keeping dogs healthy than regular visits to the veterinarian. The right diet matched with the right feeding plan can help maintain health and mitigate disease, so dog owners and veterinary professionals need to choose foods and feeding plans that are appropriate for each individual pet.

courses.title: DNM Therapeutic Nutrition for Kidney Disease
courses.description: This course explores key topics in canine and feline kidney disease, including the diagnosis of common conditions affecting the kidneys of dogs and cats and the medical and nutritional management of these conditions. It will help you educate clients about the connection between nutrition and the upper urinary tract health of their pets.

courses.title: DEVELOPING THE FEAR FREE PLAN OF ACTION FOR PATIENT CARE (1135-42824)
courses.description: Many of the procedures we perform on canine and feline patients are uncomfortable and unpleasant. Debbie Martin, LVT, CPDT-KA, KPA CTP, VTS (Behavior), shows how you can use body language knowledge, touch gradient, considerate approach, and gentle control to get your procedures done with limited injury or stress to your team or your patient.

courses.title: RVG Symptom Masterclass: Vomiting Edition
courses.description:
A dynamic three-part on-demand series designed to give newer veterinary professionals a confident, systematic approach to one of the most common presenting complaints in small animal practice. Vomiting seems straightforward- until it is not. This masterclass cuts through the noise with a practical, progressive framework that starts with acute cases in dogs and cats and builds to the more complex world of chronic vomiting and its underlying systemic causes.
Across three focused sessions, learners will sharpen their ability to distinguish vomiting from regurgitation, recognize red-flag presentations, apply a stepwise diagnostic approach, and make confident treatment decisions -including when and how to use maropitant citrate (Cerenia, Zoetis) as a first-line antiemetic in both dogs and cats. Each session is packed with clinical pearls across four key areas: presentation, diagnostics, treatment, and client communication - so learners walk away with tools they can use immediately in practice.

courses.title: Cat-astrophic airways: Managing inflammatory airway disease in cats
courses.description: In this lecture, a series of clinical cases will be presented in cats with large and small airway disease highlighting the clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, and therapeutic considerations (when applicable). Awareness of the similarities and differences in these disorders will help provide optimal management, and for the bronchiolar disorders, aid in their classification, which in turn may provide useful for future investigation of optimal treatment strategies.

courses.title: Bad Breath Is a Really Big Deal!
courses.description: One of the first things veterinarians learn is that the whole body is connected--even poor oral health can have lasting impacts on a dog's longevity and quality of life. Fighting smelly breath before it starts by implementing (easy!) at-home dental routines can ensure your patients have more wags and fewer worries. Join Jan Bellows, DVM, DAVDC, as he discusses the importance of canine dental care.

courses.title: Foundations in Reproductive Medicine
courses.description: The landscape of animal reproductive health has changed over time, and it's time to move past old "one size fits all" mentalities. This 3-part video series will answer the many questions asked of practitioners every day: Should I wait to spay this dog? Is this prostate normal? Does a pyometra always need to be cut? Join our expert panel of specialists for a tour in theriogenology foundations. We'll discuss the impacts of ethical breeding practices, heritable disease screening options, practice neonatal care, and cover all the options for dystocia and pyometra treatment. With a few lectures on surgical tips for c-sections, spays, and neuters, this course is a perfect package for producing perfect puppies (and kittens)!

courses.title: Hyaluronic Acid: A Review of Clinical Applications in Human and Veterinary Dentistry ON DEMAND
courses.description: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a naturally occurring biomaterial that stabilizes and hydrates the extracellular matrix. Exogenous HA has been used in a wide variety of human and animal settings, including in joints, ophthalmology, wound care, and dermatology. While available for years in human dentistry, HA has recently emerged as an important new tool for improving clinical outcomes in both routine and specialty dentistry. This lecture provides an overview of HA, its mechanism of action, broad clinical applications, and specific data and studies in dentistry.

courses.title: Equine Gait Analysis Society - online program
courses.description:
In the EGAS online program, you will learn the theory and all aspects of the clinical application of quantitative gait analysis.
In this multi-session program, we start with the basics of gait analysis, basics of equine biomnechanis and the differences between validated and non-validated technologies. We then dive deeper into specific applications of gait analysis in clinical practice with a special emphasis on topics such as the application of gait analysis when performing diagnostic analgesia, flexion tests and pre-purchase examinations.
This program includes clinical cases and recorded interviews from world-renowned experts in each topic. We also cover specific aspects related to back kinematics and the use of gait analysis in the rehabilitation program of horses.
The program is lectured by academic and clinical experts from around the world, and is based on evidence-based content.

courses.title: Purrfect Mobility: A Practical Guide to Feline Rehabilitation
courses.description: This lecture introduces the fundamentals of feline rehabilitation, defining what feline rehabilitation is and its role in improving mobility, comfort, and quality of life. Attendees will learn about the key benefits of rehabilitation, which therapies cats are most receptive to, and practical strategies to keep cats engaged in physical activity. Emphasis will be placed on low-stress handling, positive reinforcement, reading feline body language, and incorporating play-based and home-friendly exercises to encourage participation.

courses.title: Panel Discussion -Feline Leukaemia Virus Infection - the Outcomes and Management
courses.description:
Feline leukaemia virus (FeLV) was first described in 1964 by William Jarrett and colleagues, following their observation of retrovirus particles budding from the membrane of malignant lymphoblasts from a cat with lymphosarcoma. FeLV infections occur worldwide in domestic cats and progressively infected cats can develop lymphosarcoma, leukaemia and immunosuppression. In many countries the prevalence of infection has decreased to low levels thanks to the development of reliable diagnostic tests and effective vaccines. A good understanding of the disease process and the identification of FeLV-infected cats is important for their management and to prevent further transmission.
Join us for an exciting panel discussion where our international panel of world-leading experts will discuss and debate this topic. They will enlighten us on the newest advances in the research and ensure we are up to date in the diagnosis and management of these cats and share extra tools and ideas to help us improve the prognosis for these cases.

courses.title: Periodontic Therapy Getting to the Root of the Problem
courses.description: Veterinarians are often confronted by their dental patients with the decision to either extract their teeth or to save them. This webinar will discuss the latter from the perspective of the patient's initial presentation on the physical oral evaluation, accompanying anesthetic evaluation and diagnostics and the therapeutic modalities in saving teeth.

courses.title: The Taste of Success: Mastering the Diagnostic Diet Trial
courses.description: This webinar will cover the ins and outs of the dermatologic diagnostic diet trial. From choosing the right patient and counseling owners to selecting a diet and creating a realistic follow-up plan, participants will leave this session feeling confident about how to tackle food allergies in dogs and cats. With so much information out there, Dr. Julia Miller will distill how to perform an appropriate diet trial and share practical tips veterinary professionals can implement in practice.

courses.title: Exciting Developments in the Treatment of Canine and Feline Diabetes Mellitus
courses.description: During this webinar we will discuss changes in the way we treat diabetes mellitus. This includes changes in the cost of available insulins, potential insulin options for the future, and the new class of oral medications for feline diabetes, SGLT2-inhibitors.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: Llama Medicine Through a Case Study
courses.description:
This webinar will review common concerns and veterinary needs in the llama industry by following a case study. Veterinarians will be presented with an overview of basic medical care unique to practicing on llamas.
Learning Objectives:
1. Viewers will gain an understanding of what llama producers are needing and expecting from their veterinarian.
2. Participants will be provided with a basic knowledge to start practicing on llamas and adding them to their general practice.
3. Participants will learn common illnesses and conditions seen in general llama practice

courses.title: Beyond the Basic Periodontal Flap
courses.description: This lecture is intended to go beyond the fundamentals of periodontal treatments to review all types of periodontal flaps except those that are created for routine oral surgical tooth extractions. The conditions for which periodontal therapy will be shown include closed and open root planing, gingivectomy, the proximal wedge technique, oral nasal fistula repair, a lateral sliding flap, and type 2 crown lengthening. Guided tissue regenerative techniques will also be reviewed along with some bone augmentation choices.

courses.title: A Crash Course to RECOVER CPR
courses.description: CPR updates

courses.title: Mouth Maintenance Through Dental Home Care
courses.description: Clients frequently want a home care solution that prevents the need for anesthetic dental procedures. All types of dental home care are reviewed as well as the tooth location of action and research study illustrated benefit. This information helps all understand that dental home care is not a replacement for an anesthetic dental procedure but should reduce the degree of problems between anesthetic dental procedures.

courses.title: Leadership in the Trenches: Managing Up and Down
courses.description: Middle managers in veterinary medicine face the unique challenge of balancing the needs of their team with the expectations of higher up hospital leadership. This lecture discusses the communication skills, consistent expectations, frequent feedback needs and understanding of both the team and hospital leadership in order to succeed in the role. Effective leadership depends on balancing both directions: advocating for the team while contributing to hospital-wide goals, fostering collaboration, and maintaining transparency.

courses.title: DNM Choosing a Pet Food
courses.description: This course will teach you how to distinguish between different commercial pet food forms and categories, how to read and understand pet food labels and how to select the right food for a patient.

courses.title: Nutritional Management for Colic Prevention
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage colic-prone horses in the field.

courses.title: 2026 EDPA CONTINUING EDUCATION CONFERENCE
courses.description: Annual continuing education program structured for veterinarians, vet techs, and equine dental practitioners.

courses.title: Certificate of Social Media Strategies for Veterinary Practice Proficiency (CSMSVPP)
courses.description: Welcome to the Certificate of Social Media Strategies for Veterinary Practice Proficiency, where you will learn to translate your passion for animal care into a powerful online presence. This comprehensive course guides you from foundational principles and ethical guidelines to mastering key social media platforms for your practice. You will develop critical skills in strategic content creation, empathetic copywriting, and online community management, including how to handle challenging feedback with professionalism. We will demystify social media advertising, teaching you how to target local pet owners and measure the success of your campaigns using analytics. In today's digital world, an effective social media strategy is essential for educating clients, promoting preventative care, and building lasting trust within your community. By the end of this program, you will construct a complete social media blueprint, equipping you to confidently grow your practice's reach and impact.

courses.title: Feline Low Stress Handling in a Shelter Environment (LIVE)
courses.description: Cats are not small dogs. They have a lower tolerance for frustration and a much shorter window before physical restraint stops helping and starts causing harm. Feline Low Stress Handling meets cats where they are. This session offers practical, in-the-moment applications for shelter veterinary exams: reading the feline communication signaling, from fear to frustration, applying the 2-second rule and the least-restraint principle, adjusting the examination approach to the individual, and creating a low stress environment.

courses.title: VetQuest Grand Cayman Anesthesia & Neurology
courses.description: This conference will be over 3 days and cover anesthesia & neurology topics in small animals.

courses.title: The Role of Fiber in Dietary Management in Dogs & Cats
courses.description: Dietary fiber is commonly used in the nutritional management of dogs and cats, but not all fiber sources behave the same way. This CE article reviews fiber classification, physiology, and key functional properties and examines how these characteristics influence clinical outcomes. Readers will gain practical guidance for selecting appropriate fiber sources to support patients with conditions such as obesity, diarrhea, and constipation.

courses.title: The Microbiome: What to Make of This Mess
courses.description: Dr. Craig Webb, a professor of small animal medicine at Colorado State University, explains the significance of the gut microbiome in various health conditions. He discusses the impact of dysbiosis, an imbalance in the gut microbiota, and how it can lead to diarrhea, inflammation, and other problems. Dr. Webb explores alternatives like probiotics, prebiotics, fiber, and diet to restore balance. The conversation covers topics such as the inflammasome, fecal transplants, and the role of diet and nutrition in tackling dysbiosis.

courses.title: Introduction to Veterinary Small Animal Rehabilitation (DRIP154)
courses.description: Give your patients the chance to move, heal, and thrive! This introductory course is designed to help you discover the power of veterinary rehabilitation and its ability to transform your practice and patient outcomes. Youll be equipped with foundational knowledge in rehabilitation and the latest evidence-based techniques to restore mobility, speed recovery, reduce pain, and enhance quality of life.

courses.title: All Paws In: Why Inclusive Teams Are More Resilient, Skilled, and Connected
courses.description: Even strong team members can falter when they feel they don't belong, their contributions don't matter, or they aren't safe asking questions or sharing ideas. These situations are rarely intentional, but their impact is real. Step into the shoes of a team member who's quietly struggling and explore the key moments shaping their experience. Identify what went wrong, what could have gone differently, and which inclusive behaviors help lift the whole team. Discover how to create a workplace where everyone feels welcome to learn, grow, and thrive.

courses.title: Old Dog New Tricks Part 2- Clinical Application of Ketamine in Chronic Pain Patients
courses.description: In this hour we will cover the logistics of integrating ketamine into chronic pain management. While most veterinarians are comfortable using ketamine for sedation and in the perioperative setting, clear guidance on its use in the chronic pain patient is not readily available. Based on the review of ketamine pharmacokinetics and also chronic pain the previous lecture (part 1) we dive deeper into using ketamine with a case based and systematic approach. We discuss case/patient selection, dose and frequency selection, route of administration, outcome measures, and risk considerations. We follow a selection of patients we have managed with ketamine to illustrate the concepts highlighted above. Attendees should leave feeling ready to start safely and effectively using ketamine in their chronic pain patients.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Positron Emission Tomography PET Clinical Applications & Case Discussions
courses.description: This international panel will bring together the worlds leading experts in equine Positron Emission Tomography PET to explore its growing role in musculoskeletal imaging for racehorses and sports horses. As technological advancements improve access to PET, the panel will discuss both the advantages and limitations of the modality. They will debate optimal scenarios for PET application, shedding light on its clinical utility. Attendees will gain insight into the latest research and practical considerations. This session is essential for those looking to expand their knowledge of cuttingedge imaging techniques in equine medicine.

courses.title: Assessment of Upper Airway Problems in Brachycephalics
courses.description: To be a competent surgeon when operating on brachycephalic breeds, we must be familiar with the anatomy and function of the pharyngeal chiasma, including nasopharynx, oropharynx, laryngopharynx, larynx and immediate infra-glottal region. The nasal cavity, auditory system and swallowing are also integrally involved with the upper airway and should be evaluated. This talk will cover an anatomical review of the region and demonstrate how to perform a thorough upper airway examination, including how to record findings systematically. It will also cover appropriate imaging that assists in fully characterizing airway issues in brachycephalic dog breeds. Finally, we will discuss how important it is to be familiar with performing a temporary tracheostomy and how to maintain one.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Surgical Considerations for Emergency and Elective C-Sections & Techniques for Successful Neonatal Resusci
courses.description:
This interactive panel discussion will cover decision making regarding anaesthetic protocols for routine and emergency C-section and suggestions to minimize risks for brachycephalic breeds, bitches with large litters, or bitches carrying high-risk pregnancies such as hypoluteoidism, anasarca, placentitis, concurrent pyometra and pregnancy, etc. Basic surgical procedures will be covered briefly, with particular emphasis highlighting tips for preventing concerns like intra-operative hypotension, excessive blood loss, preventing uterine lacerations, and other common complications during the surgical procedure.
Neonatal resuscitation protocols will be included as well as post-operative pain management, lactation induction or augmentation for the dam. We will discuss improvement of maternal behaviour towards her neonates particularly regarding the maiden bitch undergoing elective C-section.
There will be plenty of opportunity for attending vets to ask questions, make comments and share their own experience with the group.
This is part 2 of our C-section panel discussion. See part 1 covering indications for and against elective and emergency C-section in dogs and cats and factors that should be considered in preparation for surgery.

courses.title: Dog longevity 301: The ultimate deep dive into metabolic health, clinical lab monitoring, and extending healthy lifespan
courses.description: This program will take a detailed look at metabolic dysfunction, one of the major drivers of the age-related decline in health and quality of life in dogs. We will examine how changes in insulin sensitivity, body fat, and blood lipids affect both routine clinical lab values and both healthspan and lifespan in dogs. We will also compare the existing evidence for dogs and humans to identify similarities, differences, and knowledge gaps. Finally, we will consider the clinical implications of these processes for monitoring and treating senior dogs.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Chronic Enteropathies in Dogs andCats Novel Insights into Causes, Diagnostics & Treatments
courses.description:
The consultation of a dog or cat with chronic diarrhoea .Do you dread it or wait for it in eager anticipation Do you love discussing diet trials with your clients or do you feel overwhelmed by the thought Do you effortlessly go through a checklist of diagnostics or is making a diagnostic plan for these patients a struggle Are you confused about guidelines regarding treatments or the blurry lines between inflammation and neoplasia, particularly in cats Do you want to know all there is about novel treatment strategies
Fear not Regardless of whether you are a small animal gastroenterology enthusiast or not, this panel discussion is for you! Join our international panel of worldrenowned experts with a particular passion and expertise in gastroenterology and nutrition for a lively discussion focused on chronic enteropathies CE
In a relaxed collegiate atmosphere, using clinically relevant case examples, the group will be discussing the advances that have been made in understanding what causes or contributes to the development of CE; how to spot the typical cases a good diagnostic plan; further tests including scoping; dietary management and treatment including probiotics and faecal microbiota transplants and much more.

courses.title: Panel Discussion The Jaundiced Cat - liver disease (inflammatory disease and hepatic lipidosis) including feline triaditis
courses.description:
Liver disease is common in cats, but it can be a challenge to diagnose. Clinical signs are usually non-specific, and laboratory testing may identify few abnormalities. However, early diagnosis is critical to ensure that appropriate management strategies are employed.
Inflammatory liver diseases are common in cats, and include neutrophilic cholangitis and cholecystitis, lymphocytic cholangitis and, in some countries, chronic cholangitis associated with flukes. Hepatic lipidosis is also a very common feline liver disease in certain geographical regions, and chronic storage hepatopathies are occasionally seen. Some cats present with concurrent pancreatic and small intestinal disease, which is commonly referred to as feline triaditis. Diagnosis of these conditions involves clinical pathology, diagnostic imaging, and ultimately sampling and analysis of liver tissue and or bile. Ultrasonography is commonly used to detect key features of hepatobiliary disorders, and may aid in identifying biliary tree anatomical variation that can predispose to biliary diseases. Ultrasonography can also be used to guide sample collection, but a number of other techniques exist. Pre-sampling procedures are essential to reduce the associated risk.
In this exciting panel discussion where world-leading experts will come together to discuss these sometimes-complex cases. We will talk about the expected clinical signs, signalment and history, as well as clues to help in the specific diagnosis. Aspects of clinical pathology, imaging and tips and tricks of biopsy techniques and deciphering the histopathological report will be debated. We will cover the latest and tried-and-tested treatments and nutritional management of acute and chronic cases. The factors affecting prognosis will be addressed. We will welcome comments and questions from attendees.

courses.title: Don't Get Wrapped Up! Mastering Placement of a Subpalpebral Lavage Tube
courses.description: Placing a subpalpebral lavage tube is one thing-making it last in the real world is another. In this lecture, I'll show you a battle-tested technique designed to withstand the challenges of the barn, not just the controlled environment of a clinic. As a field ophthalmologist, I've refined a method that prioritizes durability, practicality, and ease of placement. This isn't what you've seen before-it's simpler, more effective, and will make you question why you ever did it differently. After this, you'll never place a lavage tube the old way again.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Regional Anaesthesia for Procedures of the Head in Dogs and Cats
courses.description:
Surgeries and other procedures of the head are commonly performed in small animal practice and the use of regional anesthesia has revolutionized our ability to provide perioperative analgesia for patients undergoing these painful procedures. The list of possible regional anesthetic techniques for the eye, the nose, the ear, and the oral structures that can be used has expanded over the last 10 years and there is often confusion over which technique to use and when to use it. Many veterinarians may find themselves asking Is there a block that I could use for this procedure Is one approach clinically better than another Do the benefits outweigh the potential risks and Can I perform my blocks blindly or do I need special equipment to do them
Join our panel of internationally renowned anesthesia and pain management specialists for an interactive discussion covering the ins and outs of delivering regional anesthesia for the head. We will discuss what information experts in the field use to develop new blocks decide which techniques to perform on their patients how to select which drug and dose to administer what equipment to use, the pros and cons of the various techniques that are possible eg blind, ultrasound-guided and their personal preferences for different regions of the head. Differences in decision making between cats and dogs will be discussed, as will controversial aspects of the various blocks and what types of new techniques are currently in development or on the horizon.
Whether you are new to the idea of using regional anesthesia for procedures involving the head and simply want to improve your level of patient care or are a seasoned practitioner of nerve blocks and want to refine your approach by hearing what experts are doing and how they got there, you will find this session invaluable to your professional development.

courses.title: The Power or Four: Protection Against Common and Emerging Parasite Threats
courses.description:
This comprehensive program provides veterinary professionals with a deep dive into the world of canine parasitology, exploring common and emerging threats, and introduces a recently approved comprehensive parasiticide protection product for dogs. Attendees will gain practical knowledge and insights to enhance their ability to diagnose, treat, and prevent parasitic infections in dogs.
The program begins with a foundational review of common internal (hookworms, roundworms, tapeworms, heartworms) and external parasites (fleas and ticks) affecting dogs, covering disease states, and key features. It then focuses on emerging threats, particularly Echinococcus tapeworms, providing recent research updates and public health implications. Attendees will also review other important cestodes such as Taenia spp. and Dipylidium spp., including transmission, and diagnostic considerations.
Lastly, attendees will receive an introduction to a recently approved parasiticide product for dogs, including detailed information about indications, safety and unique features.
1. Enhanced understanding of common and emerging canine parasites.
2. Latest research updates on Echinococcus and other tapeworm species.
3. Practical insights into the indications, safety, and features of a new, comprehensive parasiticide product.

courses.title: Managing Obesity in Patients with Comorbid Conditions: A Case-Based Approach
courses.description: This case-based course reviews the management of obesity in dogs and cats with concurrent disease. Participants will follow two patients from initial assessment through long-term management. The program will discuss species-specific considerations in weight management, selection of appropriate therapeutic diets, necessary calculations, and monitoring strategies. Emphasis will be placed on developing individualized weight-loss plans, implementing nutritional interventions, and troubleshooting common challenges encountered during treatment. Attendees will gain practical strategies for managing obesity in medically complex patients and optimizing long-term outcomes.

courses.title: Aging Gracefully: Update on Canine and Feline Cognitive Dysfunction Syndrome
courses.description: In part due to the excellent veterinary care that we deliver to our patients, we are presented with more geriatric cats and dogs now than we were 10 years ago. Most of us didn't learn much about how to recognize and treat cognitive dysfunction syndrome (CDS) in dogs and cats. In this session, attendees will learn the most up to date prevention strategies and treatments of CDS in dogs and cats.

courses.title: Happier Cats and Happier Clients: Diagnosing and Treating Feline OA
courses.description: In this webinar, Michael Petty, DVM, CVPP, CVMA, CCRT, CAAPM, covers how fear, anxiety, and stress can impact pain and vice versa, along with a team- and case-based approach to diagnosing and treating feline OA. A new treatment option, recently approved for controlling the pain associated with feline OA, is also discussed.

courses.title: Update on Canine Atopic Dermatitis and Food Allergies ( On Demand webinar in French)
courses.description: The webinar focuses on the pathophysiology of canine atopic dermatitis and its recent advances (immunological mechanisms, skin barrier, genetics), as well as the diagnosis of food allergy. We'll then take a brief look at the mechanisms of action of standard medications. Finally, we'll look at the benefits that food and supplements can bring to the management of canine atopic dermatitis.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - The Management of Twin Pregnancies
courses.description:
Twinning remains a common issue to deal with in equine reproductive practice. Nature provides the circumstances for twin triplet and rarely quadruplet pregnancy and sometimes when multiple pregnancies are presented dealing with them and successfully reducing them to a healthy singleton can be a challenging task. There is no perfect formula to deal with twins in all cases and so twin pregnancy remains an important topic for discussion amongst equine practitioners.
In this panel world renown equine reproductive experts from the USA Europe and Australia will discuss their approaches to managing twin pregnancy from early first detection through to midgestation they will aim to discuss the evidence to help both beginners and experienced colleagues to deal with the next case they are presented with. The basics are just as important as cuttingedge techniques and this group of highly experienced clinicians will discuss them all based on decades of personal experience. There will be ample opportunity for attending veterinarians to ask questions and share their own experiences.

courses.title: Successful Medication Strategies in a Fear Free World
courses.description: In this webinar, Sharon Minninger, DVM, discusses how we can modify our thoughts and actions to improve the "just medicate my pet" problem. She also addresses what other medication forms can be considered and how to develop strategies to train your team and your clients for success.

courses.title: Five Fascinating Veterinary Radiology Cases with Specialist and AI Insights
courses.description: This session presents a series of five small animal radiology cases that illustrate a range of conditions, including a greenstick fracture, congestive heart failure, pregnancy, small intestinal mechanical obstruction, and an aggressive bone lesion with degenerative joint disease. Each case includes both AI-generated and/or specialist radiology reports, allowing participants to explore how findings are identified and described across different approaches. The session will walk participants through the case history, imaging findings, and specialist assessment, encouraging critical thinking around interpretation and next steps. The goal is to enhance confidence in radiographic assessment, understanding of diagnostic possibilities, and familiarity with how both specialist insight and technological tools can support clinical decision-making in general and referral practice.

courses.title: An update on cranial cranial cruciate ligament disease and the TPLO advantage.
courses.description: With cranial cruciate ligament disease being a common ailment in dogs, understanding the most effective treatment options is crucial for veterinarians to provide the best possible care. This presentation aims to enhance clinical knowledge and improve outcomes for canine patients.

courses.title: Nutritional Management for Chronic Diarrhea
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage large and small intestinal diarrhea cases in the field.

courses.title: Emergency and urgent care medicine
courses.description: In this seminar, Drs Beltran, Stern and Li will present a complete discussion of the common emergency clinical problems that they encounter in their individual practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of the problems. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common problems- both emergent and urgent care management. The three specialists will bring case examples highlighting the triage, stabilization and management of these dynamic and challenging cases.

courses.title: Medical and surgical management of common abdominal problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with common medical problems. The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common urinary & gastrointestinal problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the three specialists.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Equine Metabolic Diseases
courses.description: This one-hour course explains how nonstructural carbohydrate or NSC content of equine feedstuffs is determined and its effects in the horse. Discussion of feeding recommendations, major symptoms, affected breeds and feeding examples of horses diagnosed with Equine Metabolic Syndrome, Polysaccharide Storage Myopathy Type 1, Polysaccharide Storage Myopathy Type 2, Polysaccharide Storage Myopathy Type 2 Myofibrillar Myopathy and Recurrent Exertional Myopathy will be provided.

courses.title: Step by Step: Efficient Wellness Appointments
courses.description: Have timely, efficient wellness appointments that encourage client compliance. Before appointments, learn when to send scheduling notices, confirmations, and online health forms. During appointments, discover technician and veterinarian roles in explaining and delivering wellness services. After appointments, forward book the next checkup and follow up with clients who decline care.

courses.title: AAV Avian Medicine Virtual 2024 - ON DEMAND
courses.description: 1. This virtual event will provide a full day of online learning that will bring you the latest developments in avian medicine. Topics include Training the King of the Sky; A Wing and a Prayer: Supporting Birds with Neoplastic Diseases; Practical Avian Blood Transfusions; Avian Anesthesia Doesn't Have to Be Scary; Conservation from the Clinic to the Field; Common Pet Bird Toxicities; Avian Orthopedics: Complications and Complex Cases; and Management of Vent and Cloacal Disease in Pet Birds.

courses.title: Radiosurgery: An Advanced Surgical Tool
courses.description: The course will outline the most important things to know when using radiosurgery for small animal surgical procedures.

courses.title: Lap of Love Webinar Series - ON DEMAND
courses.description: This program is presented to help provide support to the veterinarians of Lap of Love when dealing with in-home appointments for pets with behavioral disorders, specifically fear and aggression. It will cover everything from the physiology of behavioral disorders as well as the barriers to treatment and associated conversation with clients. It will help the doctors recognize the body language of these pets and the best ways to approach these appointments. It will conclude with case discussions as well as medications and tools to ensure a peaceful process

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Small Animal - Regional Anesthesia for the Upper Pelvic Limb and Chronic Pain Conditions
courses.description:
Regional anaesthesia has revolutionized hospital flow, case throughput and, in particular, our ability to provide perioperative analgesia and optimal care for patients undergoing these painful procedures. The list of possible techniques has grown exponentially over the last 20 years and there is often confusion over which technique to use and when to use it. Many veterinarians may find themselves asking Which block should I perform? Is one approach better than another, Should I just perform an epidural, Should I use nerve stimulation or can I just do the block blindly or Is it worth learning how to use ultrasound to perform my blocks
Join our panel of internationally renowned anaesthesia and pain management specialists for an interactive discussion covering the ins and outs of delivering regional anaesthesia for proximal pelvic limb and chronic pain conditions. We will discuss what information experts in the field use to decide which technique to perform on a patient, how to select which drug and dose to administer, what equipment to use, the pros and cons of the various techniques that are possible e.g blind, nerve stimulator-guided, ultrasound-guided, and their personal preferences. Differences in decision making between when working with different species will be discussed, as will controversial aspects of the various blocks and what types of new techniques are in development and on the horizon.
Whether you are new to the idea of using regional anaesthesia for hindlimb procedures and simply want to improve your level of patient care, or are a seasoned practitioner of nerve blocks and want to refine your approach by hearing what experts are doing and how they got there, you will find this session invaluable to your professional development.

courses.title: Managing common cardio-respiratory problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with a cardiac or respiratory problem. The combination of a Respiratory Internist and a Cardiologist will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.provider: ADVANCED VETERINARY CARE THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE
courses.title: What's Under The Pulmonary Hypertension Tree?
courses.description: This 1 hour CE lecture is designed for veterinary doctors, technicians and veterinary support staff. It will cover the clinical signs, causes diagnostic steps and treatment options associated with pulmonary hypertension. At which point in the process, would referral be indicated or how much of these work ups can be managed in a general practice or emergency care setting.

courses.title: The Links Between Consumer Flea and Tick Control and Aquatic Toxicity
courses.description: Pesticides for ectoparasite control such as topicals, collars, foggers, and sprays are making their way down indoor drains, through wastewater treatment plants and into our local waterways, sometimes at concentrations that exceed the US Environmental Protection Agency's benchmarks for chronic exposure to aquatic invertebrates. This course will present: (1) scientific evidence regarding the fate and transport of indoor pesticide use, (2) the linkages between indoor pesticide use and aquatic toxicity in local water bodies, and (3) alternatives analyses for both flea and tick control.

courses.title: Managing common respiratory and ocular problems
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian/technician with practical information on the current thoughts on diagnosis and management of common canine and feline respiratory and ocular problems that they encounter in their daily practice. Both specialists will also discuss how they manages clinical problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of diagnosis and management available for their patients.

courses.title: RECOVER 2024: Revamping and Reviewing Current Recommendations
courses.description: The RECOVER 2024 guidelines have recently been released and its an exciting time for the veterinary movement as this release is the first update that has been provided with context and feedback from the initial launch 10 years ago. This program will review the foundational recommendations of the initiative, explore new recommendations and alterations of the updated guidelines, and review theory behind the new initiative CPR algorithm. Please note, there will NOT be any practical demonstrations of CPR during the lecture.

courses.title: Medical Decisions and Their Behavioral Impacts
courses.description: In this 3 hour, LIVE seminar, Lisa Radosta, DVM, DACVB, will explore how medical decisions shape behavioral outcomes in veterinary patients. The program reviews the behavioral and medical implications of gonadectomy, examines how chronic pain drives behavior changes, and provides practical tips, tricks, and hacks for integrating behavior into everyday clinical practice. Participants will leave with evidence-based strategies to guide decision-making and enhance patient outcomes.

courses.title: Certificate of Veterinary Telehealth Program Proficiency (CVTHPP)
courses.description: As modern veterinary medicine evolves, offering virtual care has become essential for expanding service reach and enhancing client service. This course provides a comprehensive roadmap, guiding learners from the core principles and legal considerations through to selecting the right technology and developing a sustainable business model. Learning objectives include how to design a service menu, integrate telehealth into daily workflow, and effectively train teams for their new roles. We will master the techniques of the virtual examination, establish best practices for documentation, and outline clear protocols for remote prescribing and emergency triage. Upon completion, learners will have established skills to create a strategic framework with practical tools needed to confidently launch and grow a successful telehealth service.

courses.title: Fixing the Fix: Navigating Through Common Variations and Complications of Spay/Neuter Surgeries
courses.description: "It's JUST a spay!" "It's ONLY a neuter" How many times are spay/neuters dismissed as simple common procedures when, in fact, they're actually major surgeries- that can have significant variations and even greater complications! Sadly we often feel ill-equip and less confident handling such complications- but we don't need to! In this lecture, you will join your peers in a safe, open conversation where you will learn skills to quickly and efficiently recognize and address spay/neuter variations. You'll also learn confidence and tools needed to work through common spay/neuter complications for successful outcomes. Let this lecture help you "Fix the fix" when you need it most.

courses.title: Minerals in Equine Diets
courses.description: This course provides veterinarians with key information about minerals in equine diets, including their physiologic roles, dietary recommendations, and diagnosis of mineral disturbances.

courses.title: Efficient Use of Technicians/Nurses in your Practice
courses.description: How well does your hospital utilize technicians/veterinary nurses and how does this compare to other practices and current standards? Optimal utilization of veterinary nurses (and all team members) is linked to better patient care, team member fulfillment, manageable workload, increased practice revenue, and team wellness. This session will investigate reasons for poor utilization, identify obstacles to reaching higher standards, identify solutions to aid in increasing team utilization, and discuss how to have the difficult conversation with hospital leadership.

courses.title: The Constipated Cat: From Backed up to Back on Track
courses.description: A comprehensive discussion on acute and chronic management strategies for feline constipation. Techniques including the use of polyethylene glycol (PEG 3350) administered as a constant rate infusion via nasoesophageal tube in the acutely obstipated patient will be shared. Additionally, using a case-based approach, we will discuss how the use of fiber and diet therapy can help with chronic management and prevention.

courses.title: Clinical Tips for the Management of Heart Failure
courses.description: Heart failure is frequently seen in small animal practice, posing a perpetual challenge for veterinarians. Mitral valve disease in dogs and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in cats are the primary causes. Recognizing congestive heart failure signs and selecting appropriate diagnostic tests and treatment are crucial for successful management. This session will offer clinical insights into heart failure management in small animals, covering the spectrum from physical examination to treatment strategies.

courses.title: Anesthetic Monitoring and ECG Interpretation: Basics to Common Arrhythmias
courses.description: This one-hour lecture will discuss the importance of ECG monitoring for anesthetized patients and cover the basics of the cardiac electrical pathway and how it relates to the parts of an ECG waveform. We will also go through how to evaluate an ECG and discuss normal waveforms as well as abnormal waveforms. In addition, we will discuss common arrhythmia encountered under anesthesia and treatment options for those arrhythmias.

courses.title: Cardiac Level 2: Doppler Echocardiography
courses.description:
This course is designed for the attendee to obtain an accurate and diagnostic
Echocardiographic study that incorporates color flow and spectral Doppler. All topics will focus on accuracy of the Doppler information and optimizing image quality. Topics covered will
include: understanding the physical principles of Doppler echocardiography as it applies to the
accuracy and quality of an echocardiographic exam, correct placement of Doppler cursors and gates, and recognition of normal and abnormal color flow Doppler. Hands on sessions will focus on equipment controls that affect image quality, image optimization and measurement of the Doppler echocardiogram. This is a Medical program that is in a lecture/wetlab format.

courses.title: Dental Anesthesia, Pain Management & Dental Nerve Blocks
courses.description: Treatment for dental disease can create extremely painful stimuli for our veterinary patients. This discomfort can extend well beyond the procedure and into recovery. This course discusses management of oral surgical pain through regional nerve blocks and multimodal pain control. Considerations for patients with comorbidities affecting anesthetic risk are presented.

courses.title: Dietary Management of Chronic Enteropathies
courses.description: This session will focus on both commercial and home cooked diet options available for dogs and cats with chronic enteropathies (CEs), and how to best prioritize micro and macronutrients during CE stabilization and maintenance. Updates on the literature will be emphasized regarding the standard of care for fat, fiber, and protein content, as well as maintenance of a healthy body condition score.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Veterinary Therapies for Chronic Pain Management in Practice - A Comparison of Acupuncture, Chiropractic, La
courses.description: Join us for this insightful panel discussion on veterinary therapies for chronic pain management in horses. Featuring an international team of experts, the panel will explore a range of treatments, including chiropractic, regenerative laser therapy, and western acupuncture. The evidence-base for these therapies, how and when they could be employed as part of a management plan will be discussed and debated openly. This event promises to provide a comprehensive overview of holistic and integrative approaches to managing chronic pain in horses.

courses.title: Surgical Extractions Gentle Dentistry at its Best
courses.description: Participants will be empowered in the exam room when talking to clients of the necessity to extract teeth in their patients and the successful techniques of surgical exodontia without performing "Brutalectomies" whereby patients are worse off after the procedure than before.

courses.title: FEAR FREE NAIL TRIMS: BEHAVIORAL CONSIDERATIONS TO TRIM AWAY THE TERROR (1135-39520)
courses.description:
For humans, nail trims are mundane experiences. But for pets, nail care can cause stress by imposing on their personal space, restricting their freedom to move, and sometimes causing discomfort or even pain.
Successful nail care encompasses more than just being able to physically maintain nails. True success is found in gaining calm participation and trust from the animals you're working with.

courses.title: Corneal Ulcers: Diagnosis and Treatment
courses.description: This webinar will review the anatomy and physiology of the ocular surface. The classification of corneal ulcers will be described with corresponding clinical pictures to aid in the recognition and accurate diagnosis of the various types of corneal ulcers. The participant will learn how to execute the first line of treatment for each specific classification of corneal ulcer in addition to gaining helpful insights regarding client education, prognosis for the eye and vision, and when referral is recommended.

courses.title: Practical Management of Acute Diarrhea in Dogs: The Role of Probiotics and Fiber
courses.description: This course reviews practical approaches to managing acute diarrhea in dogs with an emphasis on the use of probiotics and fiber supplementation. Participants will learn when to consider these therapies and what outcomes to expect in general practice. The session highlights current evidence, clinical recommendations, and real-world case applications.

courses.title: Introduction To Custom Leg Braces And Prosthetic Devices
courses.description: Learn how custom veterinary orthotics and prosthetics aid in canine rehabilitation and provide non-surgical patients with additional options and quality of life. Through this one hour course, we will review the types of devices available and the specific injuries in the stifle, hock, carpal and elbow that benefit from this conservative management modality. Special emphasis on stifle braces for CCL injuries.

courses.title: The role of nutrition and feeding strategies for cats with FIC (On Demand)
courses.description:
Using clinical case examples, this Collaborative Care webinar will focus on nutrition as a component of multimodal management of feline idiopathic cystitis (FIC), including research related to dietary strategies used in the management of FIC, as well as hydration and feeding behavior strategies that optimize the indoor environment. Topics will include an overview of FIC pathophysiology and its impact on the human-animal bond, along with evidence-based nutritional strategies that support cats with chronic lower urinary tract disease. Discussion will focus on the role of therapeutic urinary diets, practical methods for increasing hydration, and feeding and environmental strategies that align with Multimodal Environmental Modification (MEMO).
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: Aspire UCS Companion Animal Abdominal Ultrasound Survey 2 day interactive workshop
courses.description:
The Aspire UCS team have many decades of ultrasound experience, (scanning and teaching) in both the human and veterinary worlds of medicine.
It is essential that you understand how to drive your ultrasound machine so the workshops have been developed to ensure that you get a good mixture of lectures combined with plenty of hands on practical time. we have numerous workstations and a low delegate to mentor ratio so you will be learning in small groups.
Our many years of teaching hundreds (possibly even thousands between us) of human medics and sonographers and hundreds of veterinarians and vet techs means we know exactly what works and what doesn't.
No matter the profession or experience of delegates in our different workshops, ultrasound is ultrasound so we teach everyone the basic principles and how to drive the machine in an engaging and interactive format. We understand that, as individuals we all take on board information in slightly different ways and our teaching methods coupled with small groups ensures that no matter your preferred method of learning, you will have a solid knowledge base to take back to practice to enable you to drive your own ultrasound machine.
Once you understand the machine controls and how to use them to improve the image quality we will teach our systematic approach to scanning the abdomen to build your confidence step by step - yes even the adrenals and pancreas can be mastered!
We teach an eight step technique for scanning the abdomen so that each step can be practiced and mastered without being overwhelming and as you become more confident and your competence improves you will find yourself automatically bringing all the steps together to complete the abdomen without having missed any structures. The ability to recognise normal and normal variants is what makes it easy to recognise abnormal!
Our unique way of sharing our skills and knowledge will make your learning experience the best you will have ever had (according to our 80+ 5 s

courses.title: Immune Mediated Hemolytic Anemia (IMHA)/Immune Mediated Thrombocytopenia (ITP)
courses.description:
Program Outline
Course Description: In this 2 hour long, in-person lecture based meeting, a case based presentation of immune mediated hemolytic anemia will be discussed. There will be emphasis on the pathophysiology of the disease, along with an ACVIM Consensus Statement guided review of the recommended diagnostics, treatment options and long-term monitoring . Additionally, immune mediated thrombocytopenia will be reviewed with recommendations guided by the ACVIM Consensus Statement on diagnosis and treatment of ITP.
Course Objectives:
Following this presentation, the attendee will be able to:
