Recognize the clinical presentation of canine and feline IMHA and ITP
Accurately differentiate IMHA from various other causes of anemia
Prioritize diagnostics for investigating associative/secondary causes of IMHA and ITP
Initiate therapy (both acute setting and chronic management)
Recognize when remission has been achieved and how to taper immunosuppressants

courses.title: Strength in Practice: Ergonomics and Body Mechanics for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: Veterinary healthcare work is physically demanding and often unpredictable. This live course provides essential training on ergonomic techniques and body mechanics tailored specifically for veterinarians and the veterinary healthcare team. Along with practical ergonomics, this course incorporates strength and mobility exercises to build resilience and reduce injury risks. Participants will gain actionable insights and engage in a guided physical demonstration to prepare for the varied physical demands of their daily work.

courses.title: You mean the party's over? A review of recreational and illicit poisonings in the dog and cat
courses.description: Let's face it, people like to party, and pets seem to have more access to recreational and illicit drugs now more than ever before. We will discuss cases involving poisonings centered around toxins that may be found at the scene of the party including nicotine, hops, alcohol, marijuana, methamphetamine and cocaine.

courses.title: Behavioral or Medical: Are They One in the Same?
courses.description: This presentation examines the medical contributors to common behavioral presentations in dogs and cats. A change in behavior is often the first sign of an underlying medical condition. Using a case-based approach, this 90-minute presentation will cover common behavior conditions such as aggression, separation-related behaviors, noise phobias, compulsive behaviors and age-related behavioral changes along with how to diagnose and treat them.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Regional Anaesthesia for Spinal and Thoracic Procedures in Dogs and Cats
courses.description:
Thoracic and spinal surgeries are commonly performed in small animal specialty and referral practice and the use of regional anesthesia has revolutionized our ability to provide perioperative analgesia for patients undergoing these procedures. The list of possible regional anesthetic techniques for the lateral and ventral chest and the structures associated with different approaches to the thoracic and lumbar spine has expanded over the last five years and, unless you follow the literature closely, may not be aware of these new analgesic techniques or the pros and cons of each of them. Many veterinarians may find themselves asking s there a block Do the benefits outweigh the potential risks?, and Can I perform my blocks blindly or do I need special equipment to do them?
Join our panel of internationally renowned anesthesia and pain management specialists for an interactive discussion covering the ins and outs of performing regional anesthesia to facilitate spinal and thoracic surgeries. We will discuss what information experts in the field use to develop new blocks, decide which techniques to perform on their patients, how to select which drug and dose to administer, what equipment to use, the pros and cons of the various techniques that are possible (e.g. blind, ultrasound-guided), and their personal preferences for different regions of the body. Differences in decision making between cats and dogs will be discussed, as will controversial aspects of the various blocks and what types of new techniques are currently in development or on the horizon.
Whether you are new to the idea of using regional anesthesia for these surgical procedures and simply want to improve your level of patient care or are a seasoned practitioner of nerve blocks and want to refine your approach by hearing more about what the experts are doing and how they got there, you will find this session invaluable to your professional development

courses.title: The Role of Compounding in Contemporary Veterinary Practice
courses.description: Extemporaneous pharmacy compounding has been part of veterinary medicine for decades. With complex issues such as quality control, ever-changing regulatory issues, and greatly refined pharmacy capabilities, this program is designed to acquaint the veterinary practitioner with technical enhancements, various dosage forms, accreditation, and regulatory trends on the horizon. Additionally, veterinary health care providers will be familiarized with the impact compounding brings to dosing accuracy and therapeutic compliance.

courses.provider: SAINT FRANCIS VETERINARY SPECIALTY AND EMERGENCY
courses.title: Recover CPR: Recent Updates & Guidelines for Neonatal Resuscitation
courses.description: A recap of the three Recover CPR guidelines including 2024 updates and the 2025 guidelines for neonatal resuscitation.

courses.title: Approach to the Poisoned Patient
courses.description: This webinar will cover how to approach to the poisoned patient including decontamination, administration of antidotes and supportive measure. Additionally, blood purification strategies using extracorporeal therapy will be introduced.

courses.provider: AMANDA ENSOR, DVM | VETERINARY LEADERSHIP & WELLBEING
courses.title: Mentorship in Action: Turning Early Career Veterinarians Into Your Practice's Greatest Strength.
courses.description: This 120-minute continuing education program explores mentorship as a critical leadership skill in veterinary practice. Participants will examine the mindset, behaviors, and structures required to effectively mentor early-career veterinarians while maintaining high standards of patient care. The course addresses generational context, communication strategies, on-boarding frameworks, trust-building behaviors, and feedback techniques that support engagement, retention, and professional growth. Practical tools and case-based discussions will equip veterinary leaders with actionable strategies to create psychologically safe, adaptable mentorship relationships that benefit clinicians, clients, and teams.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: Approaches to Treating Subclinical Mastitis in US Dairy Goats: Considerations of Efficacy and Influence on Antimicrobial Resi
courses.description: This webinar will cover recent research in the treatment of the most common kind of subclinical mastitis in dairy goats. The material will talk about the efficacy of products, pharmacokinetics and withdrawal intervals following treatment, factors to consider when implementing these strategies, and the risk for the development of antimicrobial resistance when utilizing these therapies.

courses.title: Comprehensive Look at Pet Aftercare: From Final Disposition, Memorialization, to Pet Bereavement
courses.description:
Comprehensive Look at Pet Aftercare: From Final Disposition, Memorialization, to Pet Bereavement course meets the non-medical definition for veterinarians and veterinarian technicians for continuing education requirements specifically in pet aftercare and pet bereavement. This course may be presented in multiple settings and media including: An onsite interactive workshop, at conference as either a seminar or keynote, as an interactive workshop online, or through video presentation.
Description of Workshop: Pets are now considered important members of our families more than ever, especially since COVID. Many families usually have more than one pet. Some couples choose pets over having children. Pets provide us with unconditional love and support, waiting for us and greeting us when we come home from work or school, cuddling with us, caring for us in many ways including as therapeutic and protective dogs. There are many health benefits of having a pet family member. When our pet family members pass away, there may be intense and overwhelming grief that can bring with it depression and a loss of direction. Where do our pet family members turn?
Research has shown that veterinarians and their staff are many times the first professionals pet families look to for trusted pet aftercare options once a pet passes. Therefore, it is important for veterinarians and veterinarian technicians to provide informed guidance to their pet families based on sound knowledge of pet aftercare options and bereavement. This course is to help to understand roles in the veterinarian field in being a part of ultimately fostering a healthy grief journey through the areas outlined.
About the Presenter: Dr. Ruth Ann Wood-Humiston, licensed funeral director for over 30 years, certified pet funeral director, certified pet bereavement specialist, certified crematory operator, second-generation owner of a human funeral home and crematory, founder and owner of a full-service pet funeral home and cremat

courses.title: Managing common clinical problems: medical & surgical management
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with common problems. The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common clinical problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Paws and Plan: Mastering Time and Delegation in Veterinary Medicine LIVE
courses.description: Few of us have extra time within our days. This session aims to help veterinary professionals enhance time management and delegation skills for improved efficiency and wellness. You will learn key strategies, including prioritization, scheduling, and using tools such as the Eisenhower Matrix and Pomodoro technique. Delegation is addressed as a crucial part of time management, with a focus on choosing the right person, providing clear expectations, and fostering empowerment through shared responsibility. The importance of operational efficiency is highlighted, showing that streamlining processes can lead to higher productivity and revenue. The presentation encourages participants to reflect on their current practices, overcome resistance to delegation, and create systems to ensure long-term success.

courses.title: V & T - The basics of veterinary dental radiography
courses.description: The theme is to have a veterinary specialist and RVT co-present to share relevant and practical knowledge that would appeal to both veterinarians and RVTs in general practice. The goal is to help empower Veterinary Technicians, as well as showcase how the veterinarian and Tech can best work together and leverage each other's skillsets and expertise. 1) 50-minute plenary session (all attendees are veterinarians and Techs) providing an overview of dentistry. 2) Attendees would then be sent to one of two break-out rooms for a 50-minute workshop (Part 1) -Virtual Breakout Room #1 (this workshop is aimed at GP veterinarians) -Virtual Breakout Room #2 (this workshop is aimed at Techs) 3) Break, followed by a second 45-minute workshop (Part 2) -Virtual Breakout Room #1 (this workshop is aimed at GP veterinarians) -Virtual Breakout Room #2 (this workshop is aimed at Techs) 4) Wrap-up plenary session (all attendees) for a 15-minute closing session with q&a

courses.title: Canine Orthopedic Examination Video
courses.description: Refine your orthopedic examination skills through this instructional video led by canine orthopedic pain expert, Dr. Duncan Lascelles and sponsored by Elanco Animal Health. This video covers: observation of posture and motion, overall assessment of muscle mass and sensitivity, detailed assessments of the forelimbs and hindlimbs, utilizing tools for measuring muscle mass and atrophy, and putting it all together with a real-time demonstration exam.

courses.title: Defend Puppies. Defeat Parvo: Updates in the Treatment of Canine Parvoviral Enteritis
courses.description: This program provides an overview of canine parvovirus (CPV) and associated treatment. This discussion includes disease state for CPV, standard of care inpatient and outpatient treatment options, and a review of treatment options discussed in recent literature. An introduction and overview of Elanco's Canine Parvovirus Monoclonal Antibody will be discussed.

courses.title: Ultrasound and Echocardiography Techniques of Veterinary Practice
courses.description: This interactive course provides veterinarians with a comprehensive approach to performing and interpreting echocardiograms and abdominal ultrasounds. Covering both fundamental techniques and advanced imaging skills, the course will help veterinarians confidently identify, diagnose, and manage a variety of cardiac and abdominal conditions in companion animals. With hands-on practice and expert guidance, participants will improve their diagnostic abilities and enhance patient care.

courses.title: The Equine Lameness Program
courses.description: An in-depth course on lameness in the horse for veterinarians with an additional module consisting of The Equine Practice Company's Lameness Workshop in Ocala, Florida

courses.title: Managing common GI and Urinary problems
courses.description: The three doctors will present a complete discussion of common problems that they encounter in their individual practices. The combination of a Two surgeons and an Internist will provide a unique approach to the canine and feline patient management. The problems presented will be everyday common clinical disorders that veterinarians manage in their practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of these common problems. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of the clinical diseases and disorders.

courses.title: Word Makeovers that End Client Confusion
courses.description: When clients are confused, they decline care. Learn to recognize body language that signals confusion or worry, show empathy and confidence, and get word makeovers for top blunders.

courses.title: NAVC Certified Veterinary Client Service Representative RACE Submission
courses.description:
The Certified Veterinary Client Service Representative course is a comprehensive and engaging program designed to equip client service representatives with the skills, knowledge and confidence to excel in veterinary clinic settings. As the primary point of contact for clients, veterinary client service representatives set the first impression, manage appointments, address concerns, and ensure smooth communication between clients and the veterinary team. This pivotal role significantly impacts client retention and the overall practice experience, making them the face of the clinic and essential to client care and practice operations.
Participants will explore interactive videos, scenarios and activities to develop strategies for navigating client concerns, managing challenging interactions and building lasting relationships. The curriculum emphasizes core principles of customer service excellence, including effective communication, empathy and cultivating a client-centered approach. Key topics include veterinary clinic operations, basic medical terminology, scheduling and payment processes, and approaches to handling euthanasia with empathy and professionalism.
This program also addresses the emotional challenges inherent in the role, offering strategies for self-care, stress management and professional growth. With a focus on teamwork, collaboration and maintaining confidentiality, participants will be empowered to contribute to a supportive and efficient workplace environment.
Upon completion, participants will be prepared to deliver exceptional service, support veterinary teams effectively, and enhance the overall client experience in any veterinary practice.

courses.provider: MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: 2025 Great Lakes Regional Dairy Conference
courses.description: The Great Lakes Regional Dairy Conference (GLRDC) has been dedicated to helping dairy veterinarians learn new ways of increasing farm profitability by doing more with less. Thanks to support from generous industry supporters, the GLRDC has earned a reputation as a top educational conference. Leading experts will present on topics ranging from nutrition and genetics to the dairy industry's future and dairy sustainability and economics.

courses.title: NUTRITIONAL MODULATION OF THE GASTROINTESTINAL MICROBIOME-WHAT IS THE EVIDENCE? (155-37891)
courses.description: NUTRITIONAL MODULATION OF THE GASTROINTESTINAL MICROBIOME-WHAT IS THE EVIDENCE? (155-37891) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Managing the Critically Ill Blocked Cat
courses.description: This webinar will cover how to stabilize and treat a critically ill blocked cat including a discussion of treatment for hyperkalemia, pain and post-obstructive management. Current evidence of treatment and prevention options will be emphasized.

courses.title: RVG Symptom Masterclass: Limping Edition
courses.description:
This in-depth session explores the common symptom of limping in dogs and cats, providing veterinary professionals with a structured, diagnostic approach to addressing this complex and frequently encountered issue. The program reviews common causes of lameness, from developmental disorders in young animals to chronic degenerative conditions in seniors. The course emphasizes the importance of thorough history-taking, physical examination, and gait assessment to localize the cause of the limp, with clear guidance on when to pursue diagnostics, treatment, or referral. Special attention is given to recognizing systemic causes, including immune-mediated diseases and infectious conditions, which may present as lameness.
Participants will walk away with practical strategies for managing limping patients, understanding when advanced diagnostics and referrals are necessary, and knowing how to treat the most common causes of limping in small animals effectively.

courses.title: SMALL ANIMAL ULTRASOUND IN-CLINIC TRAINING SESSIONS
courses.description: During those one-on-one in clinic training sessions, the attending veterinarian will be presented the technique on how to perform a thorough abdominal ultrasound and / or explained how to perform a full echocardiogram (including Doppler Study)- depending on selected topic. The attendee will be given to scan under the guidance of a veterinary ultrasonographer instructor and get to polish his/ her scanning technique. Image interpretation will also be covered.

courses.title: Focused In-Clinic Focused Ultrasound, Radiography, and Computed Tomography Training
courses.description: This course will provide personalized in-clinic instruction for basic through advanced ultrasound, radiography and computed tomography to veterinarians and veterinary technicians. Each day session will allow attendees to complete abdominal, non-cardiac and musculoskeletal ultrasounds, thoracic, abdominal, spinal and musculoskeletal radiography, and computed tomography (skull, spine, thorax, abdomen, musculoskeletal) under the guidance of an ACVR Diplomate. Participant skill level will be confirmed by the instructor and targeted guidance to refine and improve diagnostic ultrasound, radiography and computed tomography skills will be provided.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Hyperkalemic Periodic Paralysis
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage hyperkalemic periodic paralysis cases in the field.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Recurrent Exertional Rhabdomyolysis
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage recurrent exertional rhabdomyolysis cases in the field.

courses.title: Treating the Itch that Won't Quit On-Demand
courses.description: We will explore a case-based approach to the itchy pet. How to prioritize diagnostics based on clinical presentation, lesion distribution and onset of symptoms. Pathogenesis of common pruritic diseases will also be discussed along with treatment options.

courses.title: Dog longevity 101: Aging fundamentals that every vet should know
courses.description: This course will cover the basic elements of aging biology in dogs, focusing on mechanisms that lead to aging-associated disease and potential targets for therapeutic interventions. We will explore the concept of aging as a modifiable risk factor for common diseases occurring in older dogs and look at existing and future preventive medicine options that can slow the aging process and extend healthy lifespan by delaying disease and preserving good quality of life.

courses.title: : Pathophysiology and treatment of congestive heart failure and pulmonary hypertension in dogs and cats
courses.description: In this 4-hour, LIVE seminar, Gordon Peddle, VMD, DACVIM (Cardiology) will discuss the pathophysiology of pulmonary edema, management of congestive heart failure in dogs and cats with an in-depth focus on diuretic therapy, and review the causes, diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: Neonatal disease management in sheep, goats, and camelids
courses.description:
This course provides a focused overview of neonatal disease management in sheep, goats, and camelids. Participants will learn to recognize, diagnose, and treat the most common infectious and non-infectious conditions affecting newborn lambs, kids, and crias. Practical guidelines for prevention, colostrum management, environmental hygiene, and herd-level strategies will be emphasized. Attendees will leave with clear, evidence-based tools to improve neonatal survival and clinical outcomes in small ruminants and camelids.
Learning Objectives:
1. Identify the most common infectious and non-infectious diseases affecting neonatal sheep, goats, and camelids, including early clinical signs and key risk factors.
2. Develop effective diagnostic approaches for neonatal diseases
3. Implement evidence-based treatment protocols tailored to field and hospital settings for critically ill neonates.
4. Apply practical preventive strategies for neonatal diseases

courses.title: FEAR FREE VETERINARY CERTIFICATION PROGRAM: AVIAN (1135-38750)
courses.description:
Many bird species live for decades longer than their mammalian counterparts. This not only provides opportunity for improvement through traning; it emphasizes the importance of preventing our patients from experiencing repeated, unnecessarily stressful events over the course of their lifetime. by embracing the Fear Free approach, we have the power to not only ensure excellent health over their long lifespans, but to increase hospital revenue in a significant way.
The Veterinary Certification Program - Avian teaches you how to use Fear Free concepts to ensure that avian veterinary visits go as smoothly as possible. Video clips and slides show you how to recognize signs of stress in Avian patients, how to use simple tools to provide Gentle Control, how to train cooperative behaviors and more!

courses.provider: ADVANCED VETERINARY CARE THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE
courses.title: Splinting & Bandaging
courses.description:
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: This 1 hour CE lecture is designed for veterinary doctors, technicians, and tech assistants. It will cover an overview of:
Basic bandage layers
What to put over different wounds
How to make a custom splint
Troubleshooting common bandage problems
LEARNING OBJECTIVES:
Understand how to place a basic bandage
Gain an understanding of bandage related wounds and how to manage them
Learn how to make a custom splint using different materials

courses.title: WHEN CLIENTS BITE (80-44863)
courses.description: WHEN CLIENTS BITE (80-44863) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF VETERINARY ANESTHESIA AND ANALGESIA
courses.title: American College of Veterinary Anesthesia and Analgesia Annual Scientific Meeting
courses.description: This event is the annual scientific meeting for the American College of Veterinary Anesthesia and Analgesia. Continuing education will be provided at a level appropriate for specialists, and this with a special interest in anesthesia and analgesia. Topics will include cutting edge anesthesia as provided in human medicine, leading topics in veterinary anesthesia/analgesia, and research in these areas.

courses.title: Paroxysmal Dyskinesia in Dogs: Response to a Gluten-free, Hydrolyzed Diet
courses.description:
Paroxysmal dyskinesia (PD) is a well-known pathological condition in dogs that has shown interesting developments in recent years. This presentation provides an overview of PD and discusses the results of a prospective study aimed to evaluate the reduction in frequency of PD episodes after introducing a gluten-free hydrolyzed diet. The presentation will also address the role of antibodies such as gliadin peptide immunoglobulin G and tissue transglutaminase-2-immunoglobulin A as biomarkers of the clinical condition in Border Terriers.
Note: This presentation was part of the Purina Institute Microbiome Forum Virtual Event 2025, held 12-13 November 2025 (Course number 20-1329191) and approved as a full program for RACE CE. This submission is for on-demand viewing of this individual presentation.

courses.provider: CITY OF NEW ORLEANS MOSQUITO, TERMITE AND RODENT CONTROL BOARD
courses.title: An innovative approach for reducing the incidence of dog heartworm (Dirofilaria immitis)
courses.description: This lecture will cover mosquito biology, management, and the mosquito's role in vectoring Dirofilaria immitis. Potential control strategies and future case reporting to vector control agencies will be discussed.

courses.title: Sit. Stay. Upgrade. The future of veterinary technology.
courses.description: Current and future technology that veterinary practices will need to stay current. Dig into the technology that is shaping veterinary medicine today, look to the future, and leave with an action plan to bring change to your business.

courses.title: Emergent and urgent care medicine
courses.description: In this seminar, Drs Wininger, Stern and Li will present a complete discussion of the common emergency clinical problems that they encounter in their individual practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of the problems. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common problems- both emergent and urgent care management. The three specialists will bring case examples highlighting the triage, stabilization and management of these dynamic and challenging cases.

courses.title: Creating an Excellent Euthanasia Experience
courses.description: This course covers medical skills, technical skills, and soft skills that will help veterinarians and veterinary support staff to create an excellent euthanasia experience for their patients and clients. We will discuss ways to set up for success, best practices, and how to handle when things don't go according to plan.

courses.title: Traveling Vet Retreats Maine
courses.description: Traveling Vet Retreats provides destination continuing education conferences for veterinarians. We host small group lectures with boarded specialists in unique, once in a lifetime locations. Attendees also have the opportunity to participate in group yoga sessions and a relaxing group trip after completing 15 hours of continuing education.

courses.title: Radiography at Yearling Sales What really matters
courses.description:
Interpretation of radiological findings at bloodstock sales can be a minefield for clinicians and may have a huge impact on the realised sale price of yearlings yet, there is no rulebook and nobody gets it right all of the time. Beyond the science, many factors feed into the final determination of relative importance of any given radiological blemish, including variables relating to horse, client, racing jurisdiction and clinician experience. What types of imperfections are most important, and for whom What weight should be attributed to conformation, physical exam and pedigree when viewing a defect What are the most appropriate ways to communicate findings in terms of risk How should one approach quality control of radiographs, and when and how should additional projections be taken Which are the most important projections
This panel discussion will draw on the experience of three highly respected vets on the international yearling sales circuit from Europe, North America and Australia. Covered topics will range from key pathologies including imaging nuances, unusual cases, tricky situations and unexpected outcomes. Expect to learn far more than can be found in any textbook!

courses.title: Nutrition in Equine Health and Performance
courses.description: Nutrition for the healthy horse is fairly straightforward; however, in the equine patient, a more scientific and clinical case approach is often needed. This presentation will offer an overview of the science behind nutrition and medical conditions of the horse, offer case studies of certain clinical conditions, as well as focus on the specific needs of the performance horse including guidelines to assist the equine veterinarian or veterinary technician in determining the best feeding options. Discussions will explore the pathophysiology of these conditions to better understand the role that nutrition can play in not only helping the athletic performance horse, but also our everyday equine companions and patients.

courses.title: Certificate of Veterinary Practice Marketing Skills Proficiency (CVPMSP)
courses.description:
The Certificate of Veterinary Practice Marketing Skills Proficiency (CVPMSP) course provides training to help veterinary professionals build an in-depth modern marketing plan. Marketing is essential for veterinary practices because it helps them to grow their client list, build trust with clients, and stand out in a competitive field. The hands-on AI exercise tool allows learners to complete a comprehensive analysis of their current business to help frame a strategic marketing plan.
At the completion of this course, the learner should be able to:
- Define and describe veterinary practice marketing principles
- Identify potential marketing audiences
- Explain how to build a successful marketing brand
- Outline potential marketing channels
- Demonstrate an understanding of AI resources in marketing
- Create a basic veterinary practice marketing assessment and plan

courses.title: How to Deal with Jerks
courses.description: Emotions may escalate during conversations with veterinary clients. Learn the right words and body language to use when responding to difficult pet owners. Get tips on being a confident communicator. Find out how to manage clients' emotions so patients get needed medical care. Learn how to deal with High-Maintenance Helen, F-Bomb Frank, Just-Do-Everything Ed, Price-Sensitive Paula, Dental Dodging Dan, and No-Money Nancy.

courses.provider: CITY OF NEW ORLEANS MOSQUITO, TERMITE AND RODENT CONTROL BOARD
courses.title: Emergency Preparedness for Veterinary Staff
courses.description: This course is designed to familiarize veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and other animal welfare personnel with types of disasters and responses, laws that affect veterinarians during emergencies, emergency plans, and continuation of practice post-event.

courses.title: Let's get practical: clinical care for senior dogs
courses.description: This session will provide a quick overview of the special healthcare needs of senior dogs and how clinicians can develop a systematic, evidence-based approach to assessment and management of these complex cases. We will also review key resources to help with senior dog care, including validated clinical assessment tools and important clinical practice guidelines.

courses.title: The Canine Gallbladder Cholecystitis and Mucoceles
courses.description: ¿Canine gallbladder mucoceles and cholecystitis are common. Silent progression of gallbladder mucoceles often precede an emergent event where costly diagnostics, surgical intervention and post-operative critical care are required. While advancements in diagnostic imaging have led to earlier detection of a spectrum of gallbladder disease in dogs, many questions remain regarding causal aetiologies, diagnostic methodologies, the effectiveness of medical therapy, and when cholecystectomy is warranted.

courses.title: Making Gains: The Importance of Maintaining Muscle Mass in Aging Canines
courses.description:
While it is often overlooked, muscle physiology and synthesis of skeletal muscle plays a critical role in the health of veterinary patients. Loss of muscle can have a significant impact on a multitude of functions, reduce quality of life and be a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. Loss of muscle mass from disease and injury is commonly seen in the clinic. Age-related loss of lean body mass has significant impacts on frailty in older dogs.
Many of us have not thought critically about these mechanisms since we left vet school. When presented with these cases, we are often at a loss of what to do, or feel that there is little that can be done. With improved understanding of these complex mechanisms, key strategies and treatment options can be identified, leading to earlier intervention, and ultimately improving the quality and quantity of life of our patients.

courses.title: DNM Therapeutic Nutrition for Dental Disease
courses.description: This course focuses on common dental diseases in dogs and cats, such as periodontal disease, and explores the impact, etiology, diagnosis and management of these diseases, including the use of targeted nutrition and dental chews.

courses.title: Ovariohysterectomy; Preventing and treating surgical complications
courses.description: This lecture will discuss surgical principles and how they should be routinely applied to ovariohysterectomy. Appropriate surgical technique for OHE will be discussed as well as how to avoid and treat OHE complications such as hemorrhage, infection, ovarian remnant and stump pyometra.

courses.title: Energy Sources in Equine Diets
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with information about energy sources in equine diets, including the basics of energy and how it is produced, sources of energy, and the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.

courses.title: Advanced Abdominal
courses.description: Advanced Small Animal Ultrasound is designed for veterinarians and technicians with an intermediate level of ultrasound experience. Emphasis is on advanced ultrasound of the abdomen with particular focus on small and superficial structures, the use of Doppler, and optimization of technical parameters to maximize image quality. Limited enrollment and 3 participants per ultrasound station ensure dedicated instruction and ample scanning time. The highest quality ultrasound equipment will be used for the course.

courses.title: Veterinary Dental Ergonomics: Preventing Injury and Enhancing Clinical Efficiency ON DEMAND
courses.description: Veterinary dental procedures place significant physical demands on practitioners and technicians, often leading to chronic musculoskeletal injuries. This course provides evidence-based ergonomic strategies tailored to dental workflows in veterinary practice. Attendees will learn proper operator positioning, patient setup, instrument handling techniques, and preventive strategies such as microbreaks and stretching routines. Real-world case examples will demonstrate how small ergonomic adjustments can significantly reduce discomfort and improve clinical performance.

courses.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma
courses.description: This CE reviews the most common solitary, primary hepatic tumor with a review of anatomy, clinical signs, diagnostics, and treatment options including liver lobectomy and embolotherapy.

courses.title: GI Emergencies in Small Mammals
courses.description: This lecture will focus on the rapid assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of gastrointestinal emergencies in exotic small mammals. Participants will review species-specific GI conditions and their pathophysiology. The course will cover diagnostic approaches, medical and surgical interventions, and critical care techniques for conditions such as GI stasis, foreign body obstructions, and acute enteritis. Veterinary professionals will learn to implement prompt, effective treatment protocols and appropriate supportive care to improve outcomes in these challenging cases.

courses.title: RVG Symptom Masterclass: Diarrhea Edition On Demand
courses.description: This on-demand session focuses on real-world, practical diarrhea cases that new graduate veterinarians are most likely to encounter in clinical practice. Using a life-stage approach, the course highlights the most common differentials for young, adult, and senior pets, outlines a diagnostic work-up for each group, and provides communication pearls to support effective client discussions. By emphasizing practical application, this session equips early-career veterinarians with tools to confidently approach one of the most frequent clinical presentations in practice.

courses.title: Trace Minerals - Small, But Mighty!
courses.description:
1. Program Title:
Trace Minerals: Small, But Mighty
2. Program Description:
This course will further discuss trace minerals and how their composition, inclusion levels, and interactions affect the bones and soft tissues in canines. We will discuss how trace minerals work together in a synergistic relationship and how the composition of the trace mineral affects quality.
3. Learning Objectives:
a. Be able to identify the different forms of trace minerals,
b. How the minerals work together and against each other
c. The role of trace minerals in soft tissue and joint health
4. Program Agenda:
a. Length of session: 50min
b. Presenter Name: Shana Winkel, MS, PhD
c. CE Credit: 1
d. Cost: Free

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Anaesthetic Challenges of the Brachycephalic Patient Including Emergency Resuscitation
courses.description:
There are at least 24 recognised dog breeds with brachycephalic conformation. With the rise in popularity of a number of these breeds, veterinary surgeons are seeing these dogs with increasing frequency for routine surgical and medical treatment as well as for signs of brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome BOAS. This can place them at higher risk of complications before, during and after general anaesthesia including complete airway obstruction. This panel will discuss multiple aspects of anaesthetising these patients including
Anatomy of brachycephalic patients
Identifying which patients may be more at risk during anaesthesia
Preoperative interventions to help mitigate potential issues
Drug selection for premedication, induction and recovery from anaesthesia
Recognising problems and how to treat them
Join us for this exciting panel discussion as the worlds leading experts come together to discuss this important relevant topic

courses.title: On Demand webinar: Demystifying Myths in Animal Nutrition: Communicating with Confidence and Clarity (in FRENCH)
courses.description:
Communicating about animal nutrition can sometimes be challenging when speaking with pet owners. How can we ensure we speak their language and effectively convey information? In this webinar, you'll have the opportunity to build confidence in addressing these sensitive topics.
We will begin with an overview of current trends and influences in animal nutrition. Then, we will break down the most persistent myths in three steps. Each belief will first be presented as perceived by the pet owner; next, we will explore the reality and science behind it; and finally, we will discuss the best ways to communicate this information clearly and convincingly to clients

courses.title: Metabolic dysfunction in dogs: The hidden driver of aging
courses.description: This webinar will introduce the insidious process of metabolic dysfunction and how it promotes disease, frailty, and declining quality of life in senior dogs. We will describe the elements of metabolic dysfunction and the main clinical laboratory indicators of declining metabolic health, and we will discuss potential strategies for preserving metabolic health and thereby extending health lifespan in dogs.

courses.title: Dog longevity 201: Improving senior dog care by applying what we know about aging
courses.description: This session will provide a comprehensive review of how aging impacts senior dogs, from disease and physical impairment to changes in behavior and quality of life. We will then explore a comprehensive strategy for how to evaluate and manage these complex cases. We will discuss an evidence-based approach to integrating the needs of the patient and their caregivers with the many available diagnostic and treatment options we can offer. We will also look briefly at the future or preventative medicine and how we can potentially extend health lifespan and good quality of life by targeting the aging process directly before age-related disability and disease occurs.

courses.title: Practical Supplement Strategies for Everyday Cases in General Practice
courses.description:
Supplements are often part of a general practitoner's daily toolkit, but knowing when and why to use them can make all the difference in patient care. In this session, attendees will explore common supplement categories relevant to small animal practice, with practical guidance grounded in clinical reasoning and real-life cases such as options for mobility support and urolithiasis. Additionally, the lecture will cover lesser-discussed yet impactful supplements so attendees will broaden their treatment toolkits on solutions for common issues.
By blending supplement science with case-based learning, this lecture offers practical, clinically relevant strategies to support general practitioners in making confident, evidence-guided supplement choices.

courses.title: Fighting CIRDC on Multiple Fronts
courses.description: Attendees will learn about the causative viral and bacterial agents responsible for CIRDC, associated lifestyle and patient risk factors. Updated industry guidelines are presented pertaining to vaccination strategies for CIRDC.

courses.title: Thoracic & Abdominal Radiography: Case Studies
courses.description: Understanding the common errors and pitfalls that can be encountered when assessing images is a pivotal part of accurate radiographic interpretation. In this webinar, Dr. Lisa Ziemer will present multiple abdominal and thoracic imaging cases to demonstrate some of the common difficulties that can occur in the evaluation of radiographs and how to overcome them.

courses.title: Practical Oncology for General Practice: Common Tumors in Dogs and Cats: What to Do, When to Refer, and How to Help
courses.description: This presentation will provide a practical, general-practice-focused approach to managing common tumors in dogs and cats, including mast cell tumors, urothelial tumors, mammary tumors and soft tissue sarcomas. For each tumor type, it will review typical presenting signs, appropriate diagnostics and staging that can be performed in GP, and guidance on case management when referral is not pursued. Emphasis will be placed on supportive care, quality-of-life discussions, clear referral decision points, and effective client communication around diagnosis, prognosis and treatment options.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Sedation Techniques for Cats & Dogs - From Frisky to Zen...
courses.description:
Sedation plays a pivotal role in veterinary medicine, ensuring the safety and comfort of both patients and personnel. Sedation is often necessary to complete procedures, as a preparation for general anesthesia, to facilitate examinations and to ensure the patient has a positive experience visiting the clinic. Selecting the appropriate sedation technique requires careful consideration of numerous factors such as patient disease status, behaviour, client interactions, clinic setting, the specific procedure, and a host of other variables which may have a influence on drug type, dose, and route selection.
This engaging panel discussion involving world-leading specialists will delve into a myriad of sedation approaches, considering diverse patient populations, various disease states, and clinical scenarios. We will discuss drugs options as well as new drugs and strategies and review the pros and cons of the previously accepted techniques. Any practitioner involved in sedation or general anesthesia will benefit from joining us as we will offer invaluable insights, practical strategies, and the latest advancements in sedation techniques for dogs and cats.

courses.title: Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis Can You Identify and Treat This Novel Syndrome (DRIP146)
courses.description: In recent months, sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have become available for the treatment of insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus in feline patients. One of the rare potential side effects of this class of medication is euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (eDKA). Learners will review relevant pathophysiology of, as well as diagnostic testing and therapeutic interventions for cats suspected or confirmed to be living with eDKA.

courses.title: Bandaging 101: Mastering the Basics of Veterinary Bandaging
courses.description: This webinar will provide veterinary professionals with the foundational skills needed to confidently apply common bandages in clinical practice. Participants will learn the purpose and application of basic bandaging techniques, understand the materials required, and gain insights into troubleshooting common issues such as slippage or patient discomfort. Designed for veterinary technicians, assistants, and clinicians, this course uses practical examples and step-by-step instruction to build confidence in one of the most essential skills in veterinary care. Keywords: veterinary bandaging, bandage application, small animal care, wound management, veterinary technician training, continuing education.

courses.title: Nutraceuticals for Mobility. What Does the Latest Evidence Say
courses.description: This lecture will cover current supplements for joint and muscle health, examining key ingredients, their benefits and drawbacks, supporting evidence, and how to incorporate them into clinical practice.

courses.title: Skin Infections: Latest Insights on Therapy for Quick Resolution and Long-term Success
courses.description: In this one-hour video course, we're itching to solve derm disasters! Dr. Pieper reviews presentation and diagnosis of pyoderma and discusses what underlying conditions may be hindering recovery. Then, we'll compare systemic vs topical treatment options, when to consider culture testing, and how to improve owner compliance. After this course, you'll know exactly how to stop vicious skin cycles in their tracks.

courses.title: Soft Tissue Level 1 Ultrasound - The Fundamentals - Online Class
courses.description: This course covers how to recognize an ultrasound case, incorporate ultrasound into their practice, and how to create a study for someone to interpret, which covers the five main abdominal organs. This is accomplished through learning the basic knobs necessary to create a diagnostic image, how to tweak that image, do basic measurements, and following the ACVR recommended scanning protocol. Recognizing artifacts will be covered, as well as how to quickly assess a trauma case with ultrasound. This is a non-interactive, anytime class. It is a Medical class.

courses.title: Low Stress Handling of Cats: Minimizing Fear, Pain, Frustration, and Discomfort in Veterinary Settings
courses.description: This presentation focuses on applying Low Stress Handling techniques to feline patients, with particular attention to recognizing and minimizing pain. Cats often exhibit subtle signs of fear and discomfort that can significantly affect their behavior and response to handling during veterinary visits. Participants will learn to interpret feline body language, understand how pain influences handling tolerance, and implement strategies to reduce both environmental and procedural stressors. The session will cover the use of towels, supportive handling positions, and previsit medications, along with methods for adapting handling approaches to account for pain. Emphasis will be placed on improving the comfort and safety of feline patients, their caregivers and the veterinary team.

courses.title: Top Tips for Diagnosing Canine OA
courses.description: This lecture will provide an overview of how to screen for and diagnose osteoarthritis in dogs. Participants will learn how to utilize client questionnaires and how to perform screening orthopedic and neurologic exams with low-stress handling techniques. We will review common differential diagnoses for canine osteoarthritis.

courses.title: Managing common clinical problems: cardiology & emergency medicine.
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with common problems (cardiac and emergency problems). The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common clinical problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists

courses.title: Relax PRN's Excuse my French; Anesthesia and Ophthalmology
courses.description:
An in depth continuing education retreat on small animal anesthesia and pain management as well as ophthalmology.
15 cumulative CE hours presented by two wonderful specialists; Dr. Kimberly Hassen, MA DVM CVA DACVAA and Dr. Andréa L. Minella, DVM, PhD, DACVO. The goal of this CE is to make the small animal practitioner and nurse feel more confident in their approach to anesthesia and all things eyes. This event is hosted in the French Alps.

courses.title: Book Now: Get New Clients to Schedule
courses.description: Your goal is simple. Convert every phone inquiry into a booked appointment. If your client service representatives are not asking the right questions, you are losing potential revenue. Packed with ready-to-use scripts and scenarios, this session shows your team exactly how to apply these techniques in everyday calls. Turn conversations into commitments and phone shoppers into loyal clients.

courses.title: Can we extend dogs' lives - and their quality of life?
courses.description: This course will summarize what we know about current interventions that extend lifespan and healthspan in dogs, and also touch on targets for future therapies.

courses.title: Reptiles: Things Every Veterinarian Should Know
courses.description: This webinar will provide an overview of some of the more common husbandry, diagnostic and treatment challenges in reptiles.

courses.title: VetQuest Puerto Rico Emergency & Critical Care Conference 2027
courses.description: This conference will cover 3 days on topics related to Emergency Critical Care in small animals.

courses.title: Tricks and Treats: Tasty Tales from the Palatable Pharmacy
courses.description: As the human-animal bond has evolved through time, so too has veterinary care and creative patient management. Among other practice evolutions, our veterinary pharmacies have grown to include a myriad of well targeted drugs in an array of formulations to accommodate ease of administration for our animal owners. Through a case-based approach, this presentation will discuss the toxicological consequences of palatable and flavored veterinary pharmaceutical overdoses. We'll more closely assess the consequences and management of flavored or chewable oclacitinib maleate (Apoquel), NSAID, antibiotic, phenylpropanolamine (PPA, Proin), and joint supplement overdose ingestions.

courses.title: Nutritional management of acute vomiting and diarrhea
courses.description: Vomiting and diarrhea are two of the main reasons owners bring their pets to the hospital. It is important for veterinary team members to identify these clinical signs and ascertain a complete history and evaluation regarding these frequent signs in presenting pets. Nutritional management is a crucial part of therapy in the management of vomiting and or diarrhea. Specific key nutritional factors play a role in managing vomiting and diarrhea in cats and dogs through enteral and parenteral nutrition and veterinary technicians should recognize the circumstances and reasoning for the KNFs to ensure a positive outcome for the vomiting and diarrheic patient.

courses.title: After the Error: How Veterinary Teams Respond and Recover
courses.description:
This program gives veterinary hospital leaders a practical framework for responding to medical error within their teams. Grounded in just culture and patient safety research from both veterinary and human medicine, the session treats error as a team and system event rather than an individual failing. Participants will learn to lead the response in the first hours after an error is identified, disclose to clients honestly while protecting the client relationship, support the team member involved (often called the second victim), and build the psychological safety and reporting culture that helps prevent the next error. The session is anchored by a take-home response playbook and quick-reference checklist that leaders can adapt and use in their own hospitals.
Keywords: medical error, just culture, patient safety, psychological safety, error disclosure, second victim, root cause analysis, error reporting, veterinary teams, leadership.

courses.title: Extraction in Action
courses.description: This presentation on surgical tooth extraction in small animal patients will cover the different types and uses of dental extraction tools, the importance of dental radiographs, and steps in extraction including gingival flap techniques, removal of minimal alveolar bone, sectioning, elevation, curettage, alveoloplasty, post-extraction radiographs, release, and suture of flap.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Radiographic Interpretation (On-Demand)
courses.description: This two-hour on-demand discussion is dedicated to developing confidence and precision in reading and interpreting dental radiography, an essential skill for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning in veterinary dentistry. The session begins with a practical review of how to properly orient radiographs and identify which tooth is being examined, ensuring attendees feel grounded in the basics of interpretation. From there, participants will move into a detailed discussion of normal radiographic anatomy, building a clear picture of what healthy structures should look like. With that foundation in place, the focus shifts to identifying radiographic pathology, including how to recognize subtle changes and understand their clinical significance. Common conditions such as periodontal disease will be explored in depth, with attention given not only to diagnosis but also to treatment options. By the conclusion of this two-hour session, clinicians will be equipped with the knowledge to interpret dental radiographs with confidence, distinguish between normal and abnormal findings, and apply these skills directly to patient care.¿

courses.title: Anesthesia for the Aging Pet - ON DEMAND
courses.description: It is estimated that as many as 45% of pets in clinic databases qualify as seniors. The number of senior dogs in homes has increased from 42 to 52% in the past 10 years. Older pets may require anesthesia for multiple reasons (e.g., dental procedures are important to maintain overall health) and there are age-related physiological changes that must be considered to ensure a good outcome. Frailty assessment is an important factor in predicting the outcome of anesthesia and surgery in humans and it is becoming clear that this is true in dogs and cats. Age related physiological changes, frailty and comorbidities must all be considered when devising an anesthesia and analgesic plan for aging patients. Drug choices, drug doses and administration techniques must be adjusted for older pets. This webinar will help attendees feel more confident when performing anesthesia in older patients.

courses.title: Pet Travel Regulations. Yes, it's Regulated
courses.description: This session will take the attendee through regulations regarding the transportation of pets via air. Additionally, we will discuss the process of preparing pets for domestic and international travel.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Equine Gastric Ulcers
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage both squamous ulcers and glandular ulcers in the field.

courses.title: Global Horizons: Exploring International Veterinary Opportunities
courses.description:
As veterinary medicine becomes increasingly global, opportunities for veterinarians to work, volunteer, and collaborate across borders are expanding. However, success in international veterinary roles requires more than clinical expertise- it demands cultural intelligence (CQ), adaptability, and an understanding of diverse societal, legal, and ethical frameworks.
This lecture will explore a wide range of international veterinary career paths, with a focus on clinical practice, including private practice, nonprofit veterinary work, and high-demand regions for veterinary services. Attendees will gain insights into real-world case studies, ethical dilemmas, and cross-cultural communication strategies that are critical for working effectively in diverse global setting.

courses.title: AAV Avian Medicine Virtual 2025 (ON DEMAND)
courses.description: This virtual event will provide 8 hours of online learning that will bring you the latest developments in avian medicine. Topics include: Ramphastidae Medicine, Veterinary Management of Birds in Fire Disasters, Understanding HPAI: Everything You Wanted to Know, Avian Wound Management, Avian Behavior Cases, Antimicrobial Stewardship, and Parrot Conservation in the USA.

courses.title: Managing the Emotions Around the Human-Animal-Bond
courses.description: Taking time to understand and develop the skill for conflict management in vet med is critical to the path in truly honoring the human-animal-bond. The emotions related to the human-animal-bond can be strong. These emotions are repeatedly the fuel in which drive individuals through great sacrifice to be a part of the veterinary profession. While also being the reason for clients, and ourselves, to be triggered thereby creating these moments of conflict. When individuals feel they are failing to support the bond, they often look on where to send the shame. Frequently leading people into a space of judgment, both internally and externally. Unfortunately, when clients follow this path, the veterinary professional is not uncommonly on the receiving end of an undeserving focus of anger and frustration. Learning to navigate these moments is imperative in partnering with others in the shared end goal of helping animals. Understanding the emotions related to conflict is the first step in recognizing the path to a common solution through these conflicts. Finding ways to embrace the emotions from both ourselves and the other party involved, brings sustainability within the profession. Staying connected to a common goal to support the human-animal-bond allows for longevity in the well-being of all involved.

courses.title: AAV Avian Veterinary Clinical Competency Program: Tier 2
courses.description:
The goal of the AVCCP is to improve, promote and expand avian veterinary medicine in companion avian species* through a program of learning modules taught by specialists in avian practice. The modules are a compilation of 3 progressive tiers containing interactive, self-directed content, case scenarios and quizzes throughout the modules to solidify key learning points.
The AVCCP Will Provide:
- Day-one clinical competency avian medicine education for students and early career veterinarians looking to expand their depth of practice in avian medicine.
- A foundational review of current literature and research with updated standards of avian medicine care for seasoned practitioners.
- A solid foundation for those wishing to further explore specialization in avian medicine.
*Psittacines, passerines, backyard poultry
Tier 2 is available to licensed veterinarians and currently enrolled veterinary students.

courses.title: Approaching Aggressive Pets - ON DEMAND
courses.description: This module is dedicated to helping with the emotional and physical difficulties of aggressive pet appointments. It covers Lap of Love's philosophy on aggressive pets and behavioral euthanasia as well as the various methods of handling these appointments. After successful completion, doctors will have the tools necessary to be able to set appropriate expectations for the owners as well as complete these appointments in the safest and most peaceful manner.

courses.title: Managing Mitral Valve Disease in GP
courses.description: This presentation will provide an overview of common presenting history, signalment and examination findings of patients presenting with mitral valve disease as well as a discussion of appropriate diagnostic and treatment.

courses.title: What Do I Put on This Wound? Use of Moisture Retentive Dressings and Topical Agents to Accelerate Wound Healing
courses.description: Moist wound healing, the standard for wound care, creates an environment that allows the body's cells to function at their best and results in faster healing, lower infection rates, and increased comfort compared to traditional techniques (say goodbye to wet-to-dry dressings!). Using clinical cases, we'll discuss how to select and use interactive moisture retentive dressings (e.g., calcium alginate, hydrophilic foam, hydrocolloid, hydrogel) and topical agents (honey, electrolyzed saline, silver and zinc products, etc.) to best support the needs of the wound at that point in the healing process.

courses.title: Financial Triage for Veterinary Practices
courses.description: Do you struggle with how to expand access to affordable care for your clients? This on-demand, self-paced, online certificate course prepares students with the knowledge, values and skills necessary to incorporate the Open Door veterinary business model into their practices. This course is intended for the entire veterinary-care team who works in a for-profit, nonprofit or hybrid setting. The Open Door business model increases access to veterinary care for all clients while enabling clinics to remain profitable and boosts the well-being and job satisfaction of staff. By the end of the course, you will understand the practical strategies that can be used to build a profitable practice model centered on offering a spectrum of treatment and payment options matched to the financial needs of your clients, thus increasing both staff and client satisfaction. Successful completion of this online training can be followed by onsite consultations and mentoring for those clinics that desire additional coaching for success.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Neck Problems: Recent Advances & Latest Thinking in Diagnostic Imaging
courses.description:
PANEL DISCUSSION DESCRIPTION
This interactive and multidisciplinary discussion among four world-leading experts will address recent advances in neck related problems with regards to recognized clinical presentations, diagnosis, and treatment options with a focus on imaging. Cervical vertebral compressive myelopathy (CVCM) causing ataxia, proprioceptive deficits, tetraparesis and dysmetric gait has been the focus of study for years with the earliest reports in horses since 1968. However, it has become apparent that other clinical manifestations related to neck pathology are also an important cause of impaired performance, pain, and compromised quality of life. Other manifestations of disease include thoracic limb lameness with no concurrent ataxia, thoracic limb lameness with concurrent ataxia, neck pain, and stiff neck, among others. Equally important is to rule out other problems that can cause lameness and neurologic dysfunction as differentials for neck pathology.
Diagnostic modalities such as imaging and neuroelectrodiagnostics are important aids for diagnosis and further understanding of underlying pathophysiology, as well as forming part of some prepurchase examinations. Therefore, it is essential to determine what imaging findings might be clinically relevant. Most recent studies have focused on Warmblood breeds with controversial results. This session will discuss some of these issues.

courses.title: Integrative Strategies for Canine Stifle Injuries: A Nutritional Focus
courses.description: Cranial cruciate ligament injuries are among the most common musculoskeletal issues in dogs. Although conventional practice for addressing these injuries is often surgery, which can be costly, an integrative approach can offer nonsurgical solutions. In this webinar, Dr. Shelby Watson will review how, by focusing on a diet rich in essential nutrients, combined with a variety of other complementary therapies such as strategic supplements and herbs, the odds of a successful nonsurgical outcome can be significantly improved.

courses.title: Case Rounds: Diagnostic Strategy for the Itchy Dog and Cat ON-Demand
courses.description:
Pruritus is one of the most common presenting complaints in small animal veterinary practice, yet chronic dermatology cases frequently fail due to diagnostic misclassification and incomplete workups. This case-based learning session builds upon foundational dermatology principles by walking participants through real-world itchy dog and cat cases.
Through guided clinical discussion, participants will analyze presenting complaints, lesion distribution, behavioral clues, diagnostic findings, and treatment responses to determine appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
Cases emphasize pattern recognition, the role of cytology and diagnostic databases, common causes of pruritus such as flea allergy dermatitis, infection, food allergy, and atopic disease, and common clinical mistakes that delay resolution. Participants will also evaluate treatment planning, medication selection, and communication strategies for chronic pruritus management.
The goal of this session is to strengthen diagnostic reasoning and improve confidence in managing dermatologic cases commonly encountered in general practice.

courses.title: Monoclonal Antibodies (DRIP153) Self-Study
courses.description: Monoclonal antibodies are not our grandparents drugs. Monoclonal antibodies (mAb) offer therapeutic interventions for a variety of diseases by targeting specific antigens, from infectious organisms to cellular structures to mediators of inflammation. As a class, the large molecular size of mAb removes many of the risks for adverse effects that characterize small drug molecules. However, as large proteins, many of the principles of pharmacology that we learned do not apply at least in the way we were taught. In this course, learn what you need to know to safely use and educate clients about this game-changing group of drugs, including how and when to report adverse events.

courses.title: Providing Confident Dietary Recommendations for Pets with Renal or Gastrointestinal Diseases (On-Demand)
courses.description: This webinar program will cover the basic tools and processes for providing dietary recommendations. Individualized nutritional assessment, including data collection and evaluation, will be covered. Resources for clinical decision making and diet selections will be presented.

courses.title: The 41st Muller-Ihrke-Kwochka Veterinary Dermatology Seminar, The 26th Veterinary MEDicine Seminar & The JOINT Meeting
courses.description: VETS presents 13.5 CE Units in Dermatology from Board Certified DVMs and 13.5 CE Units in Internal Medicine (also Board Certified DVMs)-- this year with an emphasis on Brachycephalic Issues, Small Animal Ophthalmology and Diseases and Aging of the Cat. Attendees may choose the Dermatology Track or the MEDicine Track or BOTH-- which is what we call The JOINT Meeting.

courses.title: The Power of the P&L: Unlocking the Financial Story of Your Practice
courses.description: Your Profit and Loss (P and L) statement is more than just numbers. It's a story about your veterinary practice's performance, priorities, and potential. In this session, we'll break down the key components of the P and L and explore how to interpret the data to better understand your revenue, expenses, and profitability. Whether you're new to financials or looking to sharpen your analysis skills, this course will give you practical tools to ask smarter questions and make informed decisions.

courses.title: Periodontal Disease and Oral Wound Healing ON DEMAND
courses.description: This session will provide a brief overview of periodontal disease and oral anatomy. Medical and surgical treatment options will be reviewed, along with current strategies to support oral wound healing.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Discipline-Specific Performance Challenges Series Western Performance Horses
courses.description: This exciting panel brings together leading specialists to examine the unique performance challenges faced by Western performance horses, from orthopaedic to respiratory conditions. The international group of experts will explore the musculoskeletal, cardiorespiratory and training-related issues most relevant to these athletes, offering insights into prevention and management from decades of combined experience at the top levels. Through case discussions and open debate, the panel will highlight practical strategies to optimize performance and welfare in this demanding discipline.

courses.title: A Surgeon's Perspective on Current Trends for the Management of Osteoarthritis
courses.description: This 1-hour lecture provides disease and management information on canine osteoarthritis. Canine osteoarthritis is a complex disease that impacts quality of life for many of our canine patients. Effective management requires development of a baseline treatment plan that is customized to the individual patient and includes a plan for managing flare-ups. This presentation will provide attendees with a systematic, evidence-based approach that can be implemented in general practice.

courses.title: Beam Me Up, Scotty: A Guide to Intraoral Radiographic Positioning
courses.description: Intraoral radiographs are essential to veterinary dentistry. Due to breed and size variations as well as tooth shape and other anatomical characteristics, veterinary intraoral radiography can be challenging. This lecture is designed to walk participants through the steps in acquiring intraoral radiographic imaging, showing how to acquire each view as well as review the Triadan tooth numbering of dogs and cats. Pitfalls and tips to more easily acquire better radiographic images are addressed without the need to memorize angles. Utilization of these techniques will allow those new to this area of veterinary medicine to decrease frustration while seasoned team members can learn to increase the speed of image acquisition which decreases anesthesia time.

courses.title: DNM THERAPEUTIC NUTRITION FOR OBESITY & WEIGHT MANAGEMENT
courses.description: Obesity is a significant health problem affecting companion animals. A few extra pounds can add a lot of stress to bones and organs and may even shorten a pet's life. It is clinically important to determine if a pet is overweight because obesity is associated with the development of serious health conditions. Overweight cats and dogs have different nutritional needs than healthy animals, and therapeutic veterinary diets are formulated to help manage this condition. An effective weight management program allows you to work with owners to attain effective weight loss for their pets, reduce the risk of obesity related health conditions and improve pet health and quality of life.

courses.title: The Coughing Dog: Assumptions and the Role of Imaging
courses.description: During this webinar, interpretation of thoracic imaging, primarily radiography, will be discussed in the context of dogs with chronic cough. The focus will be airway related imaging findings as they apply to this common clinical sign with a focus on the appearance of specific pulmonary changes as they relate to coughing and the approach to a case when no observable changes are detected on radiography, "the dreaded normal thorax."

courses.title: Extraction in Action
courses.description:
This is an oral surgical extraction lecture on our small animal patients. In this hour, we will begin with discussing the different types and uses of dental equipment, pre-operative protocols to follow, the importance of pre-operative dental radiographs.
We will also discuss the steps in extraction which include gingival flap techniques, removal of
minimal alveolar bone, sectioning, elevation,

courses.title: Feeding for Equine Fertility
courses.description: This course provides an evidence-based overview of feeding horses to improve their fertility. Participants will learn about feeding strategies for both breeding stallions and broodmares. This course is designed for veterinary professionals seeking to enhance their understanding of equine nutrition and apply tailored nutritional protocols in clinical practice. Veterinarian quick reference sheets and client handouts are also available to participants.

courses.title: House Soiling in Cats Undesirable Elimination and Marking Causes and Management Options
courses.description:
One of the most common reasons cat owners reach out to veterinary behavior specialists is house soiling of one kind or another. This umbrella label covers both urine/feces marking and urine spraying and not using the litter box/tray to urinate and/or defecate.
An important fact to keep in mind about this topic is that these are normal feline behaviors. There is nothing magic about a typically sized litter box tray filled with litter, ground-up clay, walnuts, shredded paper, pine pellets, wheat, or corn These are not substrates that cats normally eliminate in. When we, as humans, decide to share our lives, our homes, and our furniture with cats we need to remember: These are CATS and they have behaviors that are innate and normal for them. As a result, we very often need to find the balance between normal feline behaviors and our desire to keep our homes urine and feces free
During this very topical panel discussion, our panel of world renown experts will discuss and debate the various causes of undesirable elimination and marking. Treatment and management options include the multi pronged approach of environmental considerations, health concerns, and pharmacological interventions very often thinking and working outside the box

courses.title: Dentistry Topic Rounds ON-DEMAND
courses.description: Topics include common presentations, diagnostics, and treatment of TMJ disorders, maxillofacial fractures, neoplasia, contact mucositis, feline chronic gingivostomatitis, periodontal disease, and masticatory muscle myositis.

courses.title: How to Discuss Dentistry with Clients ON DEMAND
courses.description: This lecture will provide veterinarians and team members with practical communication strategies for discussing dentistry with clients in a way that is clear, confident, and compelling. Participants will learn how to explain the significance of dental disease and overcome common client misconceptions. The session will also cover how to present treatment plans, discuss costs transparently, and frame dentistry as essential medical care rather than an elective service. Attendees will leave with techniques to improve client compliance and increase acceptance of recommended dental procedures through effective, empathetic communication.

courses.title: Antibiotics in Veterinary Dentistry - ON DEMAND
courses.description: This lecture will explore the principles of antibiotic resistance, why systemic antibiotics are generally ineffective for treating dental disease, and when their use is actually indicated, taking into consideration the current ADA, AAHA, and AVDC guidelines. The session will also introduce practical applications for hyaluronic acid as a local, targeted adjunct that supports periodontal treatment without contributing to resistance.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Feline Infectious Peritonitis (FIP) Hope Where There Was None...
courses.description:
Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) is one of the most important infectious diseases, especially in cats less than 2 years of age. Every practitioner has seen these cases and, until recently, most of these cases were fatal. Now, there is hope available, but this means the diagnosis and treatment options offered are critical. In the ever-changing world of research and clinical trials and the dynamics of the availability of legal treatment options it is even more critical that clinicians are up to date and can offer a ray of hope in treating a previously untreatable and devastating feline disease.
Join us for this fascinating panel discussion where our international multidisciplinary experts will come together to debate these important points. Some regions (like Australia and the UK) have had more treatment options available for a longer period whereas in the US, treatment has only recently become available or in some cases, is still hard to come by. Our world-renown experts will come together to share their expertise and experience and to guide us to a better future.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Breeding Ethics: Broodmare Selection for Quality Progeny
courses.description: Join our hand-picked expert panel for a thought-provoking discussion on broodmare selection, not just for so-called breeding soundness which focuses on the capability of the mare to sustain a pregnancy to term, but for the quality and athletic longevity of offspring. The group will explore and debate heritability, performance traits, and ethical considerations in breeding decisions.

courses.title: Equine Basics Horse Handling, Sterile Techniques, Blood Draws and Medications, and Bandaging
courses.description: This online class is designed to teach equine Veterinarians or technicians basic skills on handling horses, sterile technique, drawing blood and medication administration, and basic bandaging skills. This is a Medical non-interactive online class.

courses.title: AAV Avian Medicine Virtual 2026 ON DEMAND
courses.description: This virtual event will provide 8 hours of online learning that will bring you the latest developments in avian medicine.
