Topics include: pelican medicine, emergency and critical care, avian radiology, coelomic ultrasound, pectoral girdle anatomy and disease, neoplasia, and behavior.

courses.title: Ears and Otitis: What your Dermatologist wants you to know (On Demand Webinar)
courses.description: Otitis is annoying! It is truly incredible how much owners can tolerate lameness, weight loss, even massive lumps growing out of their pets. But when it comes to scratching or smelly ears, it's an emergency. Dr. Ward will teach you how to manage cases as a busy practitioner, which will keep both clients and patients happy. He will discuss how to manage them in the clinic, and when to turf them to a dermatologist. He will look at some of the rhetoric that has hampered the management of some of these cases, and review literature how how we can better control ears.

courses.title: Feeding Donkeys and Hybrids
courses.description: This course provides an evidence-based overview of feeding donkeys and hybrids. Participants will learn about the nutritional requirements for donkeys and nutrition-associated diseases common in this species.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - The Canine Gallbladder: Cholecystitis and Mucoceles
courses.description:
Canine gallbladder mucoceles and cholecystitis are common. Silent progression of gallbladder mucoceles often precede an emergent event where costly diagnostics, surgical intervention and post-operative critical care are required. While advancements in diagnostic imaging have led to earlier detection of a spectrum of gallbladder disease in dogs, many questions remain regarding causal aetiologies, diagnostic methodologies, the effectiveness of medical therapy, and when cholecystectomy is warranted.
This panel discussion connects a group of internationally renowned specialists in diagnostic imaging, internal medicine, and surgery to provide insight on canine gallbladder mucoceles and cholecystitis from three unique vantage points. We will discuss the relationship, if any, between these two diseases with special focus on current medical consensus and points of contention in the management of gallbladder mucoceles and cholecystitis in dogs.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Sinus Surgery Case-Discussions
courses.description:
Horses affected by sinonasal disease for an extended time seldom respond to medical treatment. This can be due to inspissation of exudate, the presence of an infected cheek tooth, an intra-sinus benign growth (e.g. a sinus cyst or progressive ethmoid haematoma), a malignant tumour, or mycotic infection. Additionally, most sinus diseases are accompanied by infection of the nasal conchal bullae that can also cause continuing nasal discharge.
A panel of world-renowned surgeons with extensive experience with sinonasal surgery will be discussing and debating the best diagnostic and therapeutic approaches through the presentation of routine and less common cases.

courses.title: What Lies Beneath - Radiographic Interpretation 1
courses.description: Intraoral radiographs are essential for setting a standard of care in veterinary dentistry. This lecture has valuable information on the interpretation of radiographs and the steps to follow to obtain an accurate radiographic assessment. Within this hour participants will learn the important role radiographs play to address the hidden issues our patients can not tell us about, as well as how essential radiographs are for providing an appropriate standard of care.

courses.title: Navigating Veterinary Practice Finances
courses.description: In this dynamic lecture, veterinarian Dr. Dani Rabwin and entrepreneur Martin Traub-Werner join forces to tackle the critical yet often overlooked aspect of veterinary medicine: financial literacy for veterinarians. Combining Martin's data-driven and entrepreneurial approach with Dani's empathetic and clinical perspective, they explore the importance of understanding the financial intricacies of clinic operation. From uncomfortable conversations to the allocation of revenue, they delve into why grasping the numbers is essential for both veterinarians and practice owners. Through real-life examples and practical strategies, they aim to empower attendees to navigate the financial landscape with confidence and compassion.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Guttural Pouch Mycosis Update on Conservative and Surgical Therapies
courses.description: Guttural pouch mycosis is not common but when it happens you better recognize it and be ready. While all of us might not be equipped to treat a mycosis early recognition and referral could be the most critical step in managing the condition successfully. How and why does guttural pouch mycosis develop What are the different presentations Are there any conservative treatment options or is surgery the only viable therapy? What are the pros and cons of the different available surgical techniques The international panel of experts will let you in on all their experiences, good and bad and will share many useful tips and trick to help you maximize your success rate with these challenging cases.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Diseases of the Feline Oral Cavity
courses.description: Three common inflammatory oral diseases in feline patients are periodontal disease, tooth resorption, and stomatitis. Knowing that they can display similar pathogenic behavior at various stages of the disease process is essential when working up inflammatory oral diseases. Hence, diagnosing these diseases requires multiple diagnostic tests and a thorough patient history. Treatment of these conditions requires a multimodal approach involving medical therapy, surgical intervention, and home care. With the support of our specialists, these conditions can be diagnosed and treated in general practice. This webinar will review the presentation, diagnosis, and treatment of feline periodontal disease, tooth resorption, and stomatitis.

courses.title: Update on Canine Osteoarthritis: Recognition, Assessment and Management 2026
courses.description: Stay current on the latest evidence-based approaches to diagnosing and managing canine osteoarthritis in this live veterinary CE webinar. This session reviews the most up-to-date concepts in osteoarthritis recognition, assessment, staging and treatment. Learn how to effectively apply the Canine Osteoarthritis Staging Tool (COAST) in clinical practice, optimize NSAID use for long-term patient management, and explore anti-NGF monoclonal antibody therapy, including current applications and ongoing controversies. Gain practical strategies you can immediately implement to improve mobility, comfort and quality of life for your canine patients.

courses.title: Webinar Series - Rapid practical Ultrasound for everyday General & Emergency Medicine
courses.description: This 8-hour webinar series focuses on introducing the concept of point-of-care ultrasound for trauma, triage, tracking, treatment & total systemic evaluation (the 5 T's of POCUS) to the general small animal practitioner (even without any experience with ultrasound). The specialists will show how point-of-care ultrasound differs from the complete ultrasonographic examination performed by diagnostic imaging specialists and how any small animal practitioner can acquire the necessary skills to use point-of-care ultrasound in everyday practice. This series covers the following topics that have conveniently been split up into four 2-hour sessions that cover: The Essentials of Point-of-Care Ultrasound Abdominal Point-of-Care Ultrasound Examinations How to Examine the Lung & Pleural Spaces Pneumothorax, Pleural Effusion & Lung Pathology Cardiac Ultrasound Made Easy Vascular Ultrasound - Estimating Fluid Status, Fluid Responsiveness & Fluid Overload Point-of-Care Ultrasound Case-Discussions & Self-Assessment

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: Small ruminant neurology including clinical management and therapeutic strategies of cerebrospinal nematodiasis.
courses.description: This presentation will review neurologic diseases in small ruminants with a focus on diagnosis, treatment, and management of Parelaphostrongylus tenuis cases. Common differential diagnoses for neurologic presentations will be discussed including congenital, infectious, metabolic and nutritional causes. An in-depth diagnostic approach to working up neurologic disease in small ruminants will be presented along with multiple aspects of treatment ranging from medical management and supportive care.

courses.title: Vetoquinol Rehabilitation Business Solution: VeRBS - An Introduction to Rehabilitation
courses.description: This course is designed to provide an overview of the basics of rehabilitation, medical forms overview, outcome measurements, equipment and tool/device introduction.

courses.title: Cardiovascular Conditions (Part 2): Practical Arrhythmia Management
courses.description: Cardiovascular disease is the 3rd most common cause of loss of performance and lurking beneath the surface there is always a fear that clinicians might misinterpret a clinical finding which represents a risk factor for exercise-associated collapse or even death. Clients expect their vets to be able to predict the future when a cardiac rhythm disturbance is picked up in prepurchase exams and thats a challenge we may or may not be able to take on. In this panel discussion the second on this theme an international group of internists will present practical solutions to clinical challenges and use a case-based approach to discuss current practice in arrhythmia management.

courses.title: Heritage Vet Partners Cattle First Summit
courses.description: This program is being offered to provide a range of continuing education topics to practitioners in the Heritage Vet Partners Group. Topics will include research updates on transboundary animal diseases, bovine respiratory updates, clinic best practices in relation to necropsies, and personnel management issues specifically related to bridging generational gaps in practice teams.

courses.title: From Itch to Insight: Practical Updates on Food Allergies
courses.description: This continuing education program provides an evidence-based review of adverse food reactions and food allergies in dogs and cats. The lecture will discuss common clinical presentations, diagnostic approaches, elimination diet trials, and long-term management strategies for veterinary patients with suspected food allergies. Additional focus will be placed on improving client compliance, reducing caregiver burden, and selecting appropriate dietary therapies using current veterinary dermatology literature and clinical recommendations.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: USDA APHIS VS Sheep and Goat Health Programs
courses.description: This webinar will cover an overview of the National Scrapie Eradication Program including what is scrapie and a brief scientific history on the disease, surveillance and testing of sheep/goats for the scrapie program, and how to help our program eradicate the disease. Additionally, this webinar will discuss other sheep, goat, and camelid disease programs that we can assist veterinarians within their daily roles. These diseases might include tuberculosis, brucellosis, q-fever, and other zoonotic diseases. Lastly, the webinar will provide resources for where to find out additional information on our scrapie program and other reportable diseases.

courses.title: Doppler Echocardiography and Pressure Gradients
courses.description:
This program is to help the student understand the principals of Doppler
and pressure gradients by examining the Spectral Doppler tracing and what affects it, what
affects flow velocities, learn what normal systolic and diastolic pressures within the chambers & vessels of the heart are, and understanding and applying pressure gradient information. This is
a Medicine class delivered in a non-interactive distance format.

courses.title: DNM THERAPEUTIC NUTRITION FOR GASTROINTESTINAL DISEASE
courses.description: Gastrointestinal (GI) disease is a frequent problem in dogs and cats. GI conditions can vary from a mild loss of appetite to difficulty swallowing, constipation, excess gas, severe vomiting and diarrhea. Some conditions are of short duration, while others may persist for years. Dietary management is often an important tool in helping dogs and cats recover from GI distress

courses.title: Don't Poison Man's Best Friend: Medication Poisonings in Canines
courses.description: While many pharmaceuticals are used in multiple species, they do not always provide themsame effects or have the same margin of safety. This session will provide veterinarians and veterinary technicians information regarding unique characteristics of the canine species in regards to ADME and therapy needs. With this, attendees will be able to better recognize differences in prescribing methods. We will also discuss 3-4 common human medication poisonings in canines through case examples.

courses.title: Practical cardiology for the general practitioner
courses.description: In this CE qualified 60 minute lecture we make veterinary cardiology easy to understand and fun. Cardiac issues are very common in pets with approximately 1o percent of the dogs veterinarians evaluate experiencing heart disease. We will discuss many of the common cardiology scenarios that pets present in everyday practice. We will provide you easy to understand and executable plans to help pets live long and happy lives. Our goal is for everyone involved in the case to truly understand the big picture of what is going on, what signs to look for and what to expect. Some of the specific cardiology scenarios we will be discussing include congestive heart failure in little dogs, big dogs and feline patients, degenerative valve disease vs DCM, HCM, pulmonary hypertension and common arrhythmias. And we promise to make cardiology fun

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Adverse Drug Actions, Reactions and Interactions
courses.description:
Adverse reactions to drugs, although rare, are a cause for concern and sometimes confusion among equine veterinarians.
We have assembled a panel of highly experienced veterinarians from around the world with specialisms spanning internal medicine, clinical pharmacology, anaesthesiology and emergency and critical care to exchange their experiences and knowledge of drug reactions, side-effects and drug-drug interactions.
Together they will explore what can be predicted, prevented or avoided. They will debate the management of everything from idiosyncratic collapse, chronic or dose-related effects, to allergy and anaphylaxis, including life support, enhanced elimination, use of antidotes, and reporting.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Regenerative Medicine - intra-articular injection techniques and therapeutics in working dogs
courses.description:
The term regenerative medicine was coined in a human medicine conference in 1999 in an effort to describe the interventions that aim to restore normal tissue and function when it has been damaged by disease, trauma or degeneration. Since then, the field has grown dramatically, and it is also making notable strides in the Veterinary world.
The term regenerative medicine now incorporates three main concentrations 1cellular therapies, 2tissue engineering and biomaterials and 3 medical devices. For this segment, we will be focusing on the options and outcomes of using biotherapeutics in working canine patients. Cellular therapies can contribute significantly to maintaining the working canines ability to participate in search and rescue, law enforcement, and other service roles. However, how much do we truly know How applicable and usable are these potential treatments in most of our patients
In this exciting discussion, our international experts will discuss the advancements in their field and debate the options and treatments available across their disciplines. Questions from the audience are encouraged.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Mechanical Lameness Case-Discussions - Shivers Stringhalt Fibrotic Myopathy Nordic Horse Polyneuropathy,
courses.description:
Subtle mechanical lameness peripheral neuropathies, and movement disorders such as Shivers and Stringhalt can be challenging to diagnose. Recognition of the key clinical signs is the first step toward selecting optimal diagnostic tests which is followed by the challenge of devising effective management strategies.
The international panel of worldrenowned equine specialists and researchers will present and discuss the clinical signs of mechanical lameness, Shivers, Stringhalt, Nordic Polyneuropathy and other conundrums. The current understanding of their underlying basis diagnostic options and their impact on performance will be discussed. Optimal use of surgery and rehabilitation therapy will be another focal points for discussion.

courses.title: Risk factors for osteoarthritis in dogs
courses.description:
Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common and often debilitating condition in senior dogs. Multiple variables contribute to the development of OA in an individual patient. Some of these risk factors are immutable and others are modifiable, providing clinicians an opportunity to recommend preventative measures to reduce the chances of OA.
In this session, we review the results of a recent large, retrospective cohort study evaluating important OA risk factors, including age, weight, neuter status, and others. These data add to our understanding of the factors that contribute to the development of this important disease. This new evidence, integrated with previous research and the specific circumstances of each case, can also help clinicians determine the level of risk for OA in specific patients and counsel owners appropriately.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Abdominal POCUS in Equine Practice: Decision Making & the Role of Telemedicine
courses.description:
Point of care ultrasound POCUS is advanced diagnostic ultrasound that is performed and interpreted by the attending clinician as a stableside test. POCUS is a rapid diagnostic tool that is especially helpful in emergency equine practice. Join us for an in-depth session exploring the range of uses of POCUS in equine practice.
How does POCUS make a difference to our certainty of a diagnosis in colic
How do clinicians work through their protocols
In what contexts does POCUS make a difference
What can we measure and when is that helpful
Hear how our international and multidisciplinary panel of experts use ultrasound to navigate challenges in diagnosing abdominal disease; tricks to abdominocentesis, interpreting gas, understanding gastric dimensions, and confirming intestinal perforation.

courses.title: Yes, You CAN Perform a Fear Free Canine Orthopedic Exam
courses.description: In this webinar, Kristin Kirkby Shaw, DVM, MS, PhD, DACVS-SA, reviews the importance of diagnosing osteoarthritis (OA), how to perform canine exams, and pain management. Dr. Shaw also provides resources from the New Science of OA Pain website, which has canine and feline OA checklists, feline exam videos, and chronic pain teaching tools that can be provided for pet owners.

courses.title: Managing common feline medical problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, cats presented to their clinic with a medical problem. The combination of two world renowned Veterinary Internists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: AAEP XP Series 2025--Ophthalmology in Lexington, Kentucky
courses.description: This course provides lectures and hands on learning for veterinarians including: Ophthalmologic Exams; Ophthalmologic Diagnostics including: Sub-Palpebral Lavages (SPLs) placement, Orbital blocks; Adnexal Disease, Ulcerative Keratitis as well as Non-Ulcerative Keratitis; Equine Recurrent Uveitis (ERU); Glaucoma; Surgical procedures including: lid repairs, Enucleation. Wet labs are part of the educational process with this program.

courses.title: Small Animal Radiology: Level 1
courses.description: This class is designed for the student to be able to recognize and consistently scan the small animal patient in a Radiology environment using the safest and most diagnostic means possible. They will be able to understand the pathology they are looking for, properly position the patient for top diagnostic results, image the patient safely, and create diagnostic image. This is a Medical Class in a Wetlab format. 8 CE

courses.title: The Canine Microbiome
courses.description: Participants will learn about the gut microbiome in animals, with a focus on the canine microbiome. This course includes the concept and definition of dysbiosis, the difference between methodologies used to study the microbiome, and key bacteria present in healthy dogs. This includes looking at how the gut microbiome changes over a dog's lifetime and external factors that may cause these changes. In addition, the presenter will discuss the meaning of microbiome diversity, and why diversity is important.

courses.title: Managing common feline problems in practice
courses.description: This course to be presented by Dr's Butler and Coleman is focused on providing the attendee with updated information on the diagnosis and management of common feline problems. The combination of a Criticalist and a Surgeon is sure to provide a comprehensive and practical discussion. In this course, the speakers will emphasize how they manage common feline problems.

courses.title: Dermatology in practice today
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian/technician with practical information on the current thoughts on diagnosis and management of common canine and feline dermatologic problems that they encounter in their daily practice. The two Dermatologists will emphasis the diagnosis of common problems, along with appropriate clinical management. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of diagnosis and management available for their patients.

courses.title: Basic Pet Aftercare Principles and Options: Simple Cremation and Beyond
courses.description:
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: Basic Pet Aftercare Principles and Options - Simple Cremation and Beyond course meets the non-medical definition for veterinarians, veterinarian technicians, and other veterinarian staff, for continuing education requirements specifically in pet aftercare. This course is designed to be presented in multiple settings and media including: An onsite interactive workshop, at a conference as either a seminar or keynote, as an interactive workshop online, or through video presentation.
Description of Workshop: Pets are now considered important members of our families more than ever, especially since COVID with everyone being at home more. Many families usually have more than one pet. Some couples choose to have pets as their kids instead of children. Pets provide us with unconditional love and support, waiting for us and greeting us when we come home from work or school, caring for us in many ways including being therapeutic and protective dogs. There are many health benefits of having a pet family member. When our pet family members pass away, there may be overwhelming grief that can bring with it depression and a loss of direction.
Research has shown that veterinarians and their staff are many times the first professionals pet families look to for trusted pet aftercare options once a pet passes. Therefore, it is important for veterinarians and veterinarian technicians to provide informed guidance to their pet families based on sound knowledge of basic pet aftercare principles and available options.

courses.title: Mastering Veterinary Phone Communication: From Etiquette to Effective Triage ON DEMAND
courses.description: No matter who answers the call this is often the first point of contact for clients, making phone communication a critical part of delivering excellent service. Setting a great first impression and getting the call started on a positive note are key. The next step is leading the conversation and directing the client to where they need to go, essentially triaging each call and determining the next steps. Reasons for the call can vary. It's our job to actively listen in order to uncover the main concern then direct them to where they need to be. Before triaging the call, we need to master a few basic skills to help us deliver clear, confident communication, in order to build client trust. Because when our clients trust us, they treat us better AND they are more likely to follow our recommendations. This webinar will cover essential phone etiquette to ensure every client interaction is professional, compassionate, and efficient. We'll also dive into more advanced skills, including phone triage techniques, to help team members confidently assess urgent situations, provide clear guidance, and support both clients and veterinary teams effectively.

courses.title: Why Did This Not Work Troubleshooting Missteps in Otitis Cases
courses.description: Otitis externa is one of the most common conditions in small animal practice, yet treatment failures are frequent due to diagnostic and therapeutic missteps. This non-interactive/anytime lecture reviews the most common pitfalls in the management of canine otitis, including owner compliance, failure to address primary and perpetuating factors, and creating a sustainable maintenance protocol. Attendees will learn practical strategies to correct these issues and implement more effective treatment plans. This session aims to help veterinarians reduce recurrence, improve patient comfort, and achieve more consistent long-term outcomes.

courses.title: Advanced Echocardiography
courses.description:
This is an immersive three-day course focused on advanced echocardiography. Lectures cover scanning, echocardiographic diagnosis, using Echo for disease staging, and principles of patient management. It will cover advanced aspects of imaging and cardiovascular medicine. Two scanning laboratory periods will help participants with their own imaging challenges or learn new techniques. The course does not review ultrasound basics or physics (aside from how these relate to instrumentation, obtaining quality images, and recognizing artifacts).
Participants will learn how to integrate imaging with aspects of medical management, while building a stronger understanding of clinical cardiology and echocardiographic diagnosis.

courses.title: Practical Use of Mindfulness for Veterinary Professionals: Improve Performance, Enjoy More, and Stress Less
courses.description: In this 2-hour on-demand session, you will go on a journey of what mindfulness and meditation is and is not. We will debunk preconceived notions and explain the key benefits that come as a result of adopting a mindfulness-based practice such as fewer mistakes, less stress, and improved performance. You will discover how this set of skills can translate to leading a fuller, happier life as you turn destructive negative stress into something to help you grow. Most importantly, you will learn practical and immediately implementable skills that will aid in communication, self-compassion, good habit cultivation, and fostering meaningful connections with your clients, patients, family, friends, and team members! Lastly, we will deliver strategies for maintaining consistency to ensure that mindfulness and meditation aren't something that you do today and forget about tomorrow.

courses.title: Veterinary Burnout Preparedness Training: A New Strategy for Confidently Navigating the Challenges of Life and Vet Med
courses.description: Benjamin Franklin once said, "By failing to prepare, you are preparing to fail." In fact, preparation is one of the major keys to having a lengthy and enjoyable veterinary career that's not plagued by things like burnout. Like many things on planet Earth, veterinary medicine has its challenges, and these challenges are leading to mental, physical, and emotional exhaustion for some veterinary professionals. However, we still believe that veterinary medicine is one of the most rewarding and prestigious professions on the face of the planet, and with the right tools, strategies, tactics, resources, and principles you can create a veterinary experience that you can truly enjoy! In this 60-minute presentation, you will discover the foundational basics of wellbeing and veterinary burnout preparedness and how this knowledge can be applied to decrease burnout and increase wellbeing for individuals! Remember: Burnout in veterinary medicine is a very REAL thing, but it doesn't have to be your REALity!

courses.title: Navigating Feline Chronic Enteropathy
courses.description: Vomiting, diarrhea, dysorexia, and weight loss are signs of feline chronic enteropathy (CE) and are common reasons for cats to be presented to veterinary practitioners. A wide range of diseases can lead to symptoms that mimic an enteropathy. The practitioner is first challenged with evaluating if the cause of symptoms is systemic, such as with pancreatic or hepatobiliary disease, or the result of a true enteropathy. Common causes of feline CE include food-responsive disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or low-grade intestinal lymphoma. In this webinar, we will use a case-based approach to review the diagnostic and therapeutic approach and answer the most common practitioner questions about feline CE.

courses.title: Hyaluronic Acid: Clinical Application in Human and Veterinary Dentistry
courses.description: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a naturally occurring biomaterial that stabilizes and hydrates the extracellular matrix. Exogenous HA has been used in a wide variety of human and animal settings, including in joints, ophthalmology, wound care, and dermatology. While available for years in human dentistry, HA has recently emerged as an important new tool for improving clinical outcomes in both routine and specialty dentistry. This lecture provides an overview of HA, its mechanism of action, broad clinical applications, and specific data and studies in dentistry.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Dentistry Faux Pas (On-Demand)
courses.description: Participants will learn how to distinguish normal radiographic anatomy from pathology, properly diagnose and close an oronasal fistula, and perform extractions of the canine tooth and maxillary fourth premolar while avoiding common mistakes. The discussion will also cover the causes and treatment options for feline chronic gingivostomatitis, equipping clinicians with strategies for one of the more challenging conditions in feline dentistry.

courses.title: AO VET NA Webinar-Non-Traumatic Lameness Originating from the Feline Stifle
courses.description:
This webinar will cover three main causes of pelvic limb lameness in cats originating from the stifle cranial cruciate ligament failure patellar luxation and patellar fractures. We will discuss treatment options focusing on the challenges of managing cranial cruciate ligament failure the controversy around patellar luxation surgeries and the increasing recognition of patellar fracture syndrome.
Learning Objectives
1. Review the pathogenesis of cranial cruciate ligament rupture in cats and how this compares to dogs
2. Discuss the respective prognoses for non-surgical and surgical treatment of cranial cruciate ligament rupture in cats, including consideration of intra-articular mineralization and meniscal injury
3. Detail the clinical presentation of cats with patellar luxation including potential concomitance of cranial cruciate ligament rupture
4. Discuss treatment options for patellar luxation in cats and review the prognosis following surgical intervention
5. Review pathogeneses, treatment options and associated prognoses for non-traumatic patellar fractures in cats

courses.title: 2024 AAEP Virtual Convention
courses.description:
Cannot take time away from your practice and need some CE credits? Interested in learning more about equine specific veterinary medicine topics? The 2024 AAEP Virtual Convention is for you. The AAEP Virtual Convention offers educational opportunities for equine veterinarians and equine veterinarian technicians offering over 80 CE credits in various categories. CE credits are provided via recordings of lectures, seminars, workshops and facilitator lead discussions on specific topics that are presented at the live 2024 AAEP 70th Annual Convention.
These virtual sessions can help attendees gain knowledge in the areas of Sports Medicine, Rehabilitation, Lameness, Imaging, Theriogenology, Infectious and Non-Infectious Medicine, General Medicine, Cervical/Spine Disease, Dentistry, Wound Care, Podiatry, Ethics and non-medical topics including Recordkeeping for Veterinarians, Understanding Compensation, Retirement Planning, Legal Aspects, Social Licensing, Empowering Staff, Work Life Balance, as well as Diversity. Recordings vary from reminders, updates, new education for experienced veterinarians to material suited to those new or returning to equine practice.

courses.title: Assessing Quality of Life
courses.description: Assessing the quality of life of a family pet is a delicate balance between managing client emotions, the progression of the disease, and the happiness of the pet. These key issues are not always in harmony and it is the job of the veterinary professional team to manage and balance each party's interests with the natural developments of biology. Understanding common trends in both people and their pets helps better identify their needs, address their concerns, and make a decision that does the "most good" for all involved.

courses.title: AS100e - Surviving Active Threats & Shooters
courses.description:
This course provides practical guidance and real-world strategies to help individuals effectively respond to active threat and shooter situations. Participants will gain a deeper understanding of active shooter behavior, learn how to identify early warning signs, and develop the confidence to act under pressure.
Through guided instruction, case-based exercises, and scenario-driven discussions, learners will strengthen their situational awareness, enhance decision-making in high-stress situations, and apply the nationally recognized Run, Hide, Fight model. The course also includes focused modules on mental preparedness, including how to manage tunnel vision and build a survivor mindset.
Designed for staff and organizations seeking to improve readiness, this course delivers clear, actionable content applicable in the veterinary industry.

courses.title: Helping Owners Assess Quality of Life - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Assessing the quality of life of a family pet is a delicate balance between managing client emotions, the progression of the disease, and the happiness of the pet. These key issues are not always in harmony and it is the job of the veterinary professional team to manage and balance each party's interests with the natural developments of biology. Understanding common trends in both people and their pets helps better identify their needs, address their concerns, and make a decision that does the "most good" for all involved.

courses.title: How We Use Minimally Invasive Surgery to Improve Outcomes in Patients With Orthopedic Disease
courses.description: This talk will discuss minimally invasive options that can be utilized to treat orthopedic disease in dogs and cats. The use of arthroscopy will be described as a means to treat joint disease minimally invasively as well as to guide minimally invasive fracture repair. The use of fluoroscopy to guide minimally invasive orthopedic surgery and allow surgery to be performed more precisely through smaller incisions will be covered. The combined use of arthroscopy and fluoroscopy will also be discussed.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Challenging Imaging Rounds: Proximal Metacarpus/Metatarsus
courses.description: Pain causing lameness or poor performance is often localised to the proximal metacarpal or metatarsal regions. Whether using conventional or advanced imaging modalities, interpreting findings in these areas can be challenging, even for experienced veterinarians. This session brings together an international panel of imaging specialists who will share their approaches across different imaging modalities and techniques, present challenging and interesting cases, and debate the impact of recent advances in knowledge, understanding, and technology. With audience participation highly encouraged, this interactive, round-table discussion offers a unique opportunity to learn alongside world leaders in the field.

courses.title: Wrap It Up: A Hands-On Guide to Bandages, Splints, Casts, and Hobbles
courses.description: This hands-on laboratory provides a practical review of coaptation in small animal practice, including soft padded bandages, splints, casts, and hobbles. Participants will review indications and contraindications for each modality, work through proper layering and tension, and practice application on canine models. The session also covers common complications such as bandage sores, swelling, slippage, and patient interference, along with strategies for prevention, monitoring, and client communication around at-home care.

courses.provider: FORTUNE MANAGEMENT - VETERINARY DIVISION DBA VETERINARY MASTERY
courses.title: Strong Systems and Structure Skills for Peak Practices
courses.description: Learn how to build the systems and organizational structure that create consistency, efficiency, and sustainable practice growth. Participants will explore workflow design, importance of standard operating procedures (SOPs), accountability systems, role clarity, scheduling, and performance measurement. By the end of the course, attendees will be able to implement effective systems that improve productivity, reduce errors, streamline operations, enhance the client and patient experience, and empower team members to perform at a high level while supporting a scalable, profitable veterinary practice.

courses.title: Dog Behaviour & Pharmacology - Which drugs to reach for, when and why
courses.description: This panel discussion promises to be exciting and informative as our world-leading specialists come together to share their knowledge and experience as they debate the therapies and tools available to address behavioural concerns in dogs. Medication can be a very helpful tool when addressing various behavioural issues. Most of the medications used by veterinarians to help modify behaviour target anxiety and reactivity. The more common medication classes include selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors SSRIs, tri-cyclic antidepressants TCAs, benzodiazepines, and azapirones. But there are other less common medications and supplements at our disposal as well. Knowing what tools are available, how to use them correctly and which of them to use when will be the focus of this inspiring interactive panel discussion.

courses.title: Hill's 2025 State of Shelter Pet Adoption Report: Trends and Opportunities
courses.description: This 1 hour webinar will provide an overview of insights from Hill's 2025 State of Shelter Pet Adoption Report. The session will explore current trends and opportunities in animal sheltering, discuss challenges facing shelter professionals, and touch on innovative approaches being adopted across the industry. The program is designed for veterinary professionals and others interested in the landscape of shelter pet adoption. A portion of the session will be dedicated to participant questions and discussion.

courses.title: Green is the New Black: Using the Concept of Sustainability to Prevent Burnout
courses.description: "When a flower doesn't bloom, you fix the environment in which it grows, not the flower." This saying by Alexander Den Heijer is an excellent analogy for how we, as veterinary teams, should be thinking about managing burnout in our hospitals. More than ever, team members are facing emotional exhaustion, disengagement, and a low sense of personal accomplishment, and the root of the issues lies in their environment (i.e., workplace). Like plants without water or sun, employees without the necessary resources to do the job that they aspire to will never survive. Join Dr. Debbie Stoewen as she sticks her green thumb into this important issue, and shares ways that burnout can be prevented by promoting a sustainable workplace, one in which everyone can thrive (flora or fauna).

courses.title: Clarity in Compounding: Navigating Tailored Treatment in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Have you ever felt like the available standard treatment options for a particular case don't quite fit? This webinar will equip you with the necessary compounding knowledge and tools to customize patient care and understand liability. Kory Muto, PharmD, FAPC, will share where compounded medications come from and review the regulations that impact veterinary practice before diving into strategies to help maximize benefits, minimize risks, and mitigate common prescription errors.

courses.title: Treatment of Iliopsoas Injuries Manual Therapy, Focused Shockwave Therapy
courses.description: This course will provide attendees with; 1)Multiple strategies to treat Iliopsoas injuries. 2) A basic understanding of the iliopsoas muscle anatomy and its function. 3) The role of soft tissue injury in lameness 4) Common indicators and identification of iliopsoas injuries . 5) Presentation of several case studies on the treatment of iliopsoas injury. 6) Review a multimodal approach to treatment approaches. 7) Review of the available treatment modalities proven to be effective in treating soft tissue injuries. Link to Course https://youtu.be/UHXYxQcecF0

courses.title: Postgraduate Diploma in Animal Veterinary Osteopathy (PG AVO)
courses.description: This program curriculum teaches classical structural osteopathy, highlighting the significance of the structure-function relationship in maintaining animals' health. Endorsed by the veterinary community, you will learn specialized manual techniques to restore mobility and improve conditioning and performance in hoses and dogs of all ages and breeds. Flexible learning format for canine osteopathy and equine osteopathy with individual mentorship

courses.title: Psychopharmacology for the General Practitioner
courses.description: In this 4-hour, LIVE seminar, Lisa Radosta, DVM, DACVB, will provide a comprehensive overview of veterinary psychopharmacology. Building from a quick reference guide through stepwise exploration of drug classes, dosing, and monitoring, this seminar equips practitioners with confidence in prescribing and managing behavior medications. Case-based discussions will illustrate when and how to use medications as part of multimodal treatment plans.

courses.title: Diarrhea! Case Rounds: From Puppies to Geriatrics: ON DEMAND
courses.description: Join Dr. Gershon Alaluf for a case-based discussion exploring the diagnostic and treatment approaches to diarrhea across various life stages. Using real-world examples, participants will refine their clinical reasoning, improve client communication, and strengthen decision-making skills for patients with acute and chronic diarrhea.

courses.title: Old Dog New Tricks Part 1- Ketamine and Chronic pain Management
courses.description: Ketamine is a well known medication in the veterinary field, used commonly for sedation and pain management in the peri-operative setting. Ketamine is an NMDA receptor antagonist that can also alter brain and spinal cord plasticity in patients who have developed central sensitization, a complex sequelae to chronic and neuropathic pain. There is growing use of ketamine as part of a comprehensive multimodal acute pain management plan in animal hospitals, but rarely is it used for the management of chronic pain. Ketamine is now showing significant promise as a sole agent in the management of chronically painful conditions and depression/anxiety disorders in humans with a compelling body of evidence. Because the parallels between central sensitization in humans and animals are strong, it is promising that ketamine could be used for veterinary patients with chronic pain. Chronic pain management remains a challenge in veterinary medicine and ketamine offers a tool that is available to most clinicians and has an existing level of comfort with use. In this lecture we will review ketamine and its current applications in human pain management. We will review of central sensitization and chronic pain in our veterinary patients and illuminate the potential to use ketamine in its management.

courses.title: Supplements and multimodal management of arthritis
courses.description:
This 60-minute course is divided into 6 parts, covering various aspects of arthritis in dogs and its management with a focus on supplements:
Arthritis in dogs: We discuss the impact of arthritis on the quality of life for both dogs and owners, emphasizing the importance of early detection and treatment. We explore the multifactorial origins of arthritis, including primary and secondary causes, and identify dogs at higher risk. Visual aids, such as X-rays and 3D videos, illustrate the characteristics of arthritic joints.
The multimodal approach to arthritis: We present a comprehensive approach to managing osteoarthritis (OA), utilizing a combination of treatment options at different stages of the disease. We provide objective classification methods of ingredients, including the quality of the evidence pyramid. We also discuss using tools such as Client-Specific Outcome Measures (CSOM) to assess pain and engage clients effectively.
Supplement case study: Using Jope Hip & Joint Dog Chews as a case study, we guide participants in understanding how to read supplement labels and make informed recommendations. We highlight the importance of evaluating active ingredients, assessing quality and palatability, and interpreting dosing information.
Focus on UC-II: We delve into the unique mechanism of action of Undenatured Type-II Collagen (UC-II) and its proven efficacy in improving comfort in arthritic dogs. Studies, including ground force plate gait analysis, demonstrate UC-II's ability to downregulate the immune system and reduce joint inflammation.
Curcumin, Omega-3, and Glucosamine: We explore the natural approach to combating inflammation and promoting joint health using curcumin, omega-3 fatty acids, and glucosamine. We examine their impact on the inflammatory cascade, including their effects on reducing inflammation and supporting cartilage repair, supported by a review of relevant studies.
Inflammation in the joint: We discuss the four pillars of inflammation and prese

courses.title: Urgent or emergent- medical & surgical management
courses.description: In this seminar, Drs Marvel and Hackett will discuss handling those walk-in, same-day cases that challenge practitioners with an already busy schedule. They will discuss strategies used to manage high case-load, telephone triage and how to differentiate urgent care vs emergent cases. Drs Marvel and Hackett will bring case examples highlighting the triage, stabilization and both medical and surgical management of these dynamic and challenging cases.

courses.title: PROPER PRESCRIBING AND COMPOUNDING FOR EQUINE PRACTITIONERS (1190-36272)
courses.description: PROPER PRESCRIBING AND COMPOUNDING FOR EQUINE PRACTITIONERS (1190-36272) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: ELBOW ARTHRITIS - MEDICAL MANAGEMENT AND LASER THERAPY (409-41641)
courses.description: ELBOW ARTHRITIS - MEDICAL MANAGEMENT AND LASER THERAPY (409-41641) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Valley Fever in Dogs and Cats: Think Outside the Desert
courses.description: Coccidioidomycosis, also known as "Valley Fever," is a systemic fungal disease caused by the Coccidioides spp. soil fungi, C. posadasii and C. immitis. Coccidioidomycosis causes a great deal of morbidity and mortality in affected patients and can also infect humans. Although it is primarily found in the arid southwestern United States and northern Mexico, human cases have been recently reported as far north as Washington state. Pets living in and those who travel to endemic regions are at risk, so it is important for the practitioner to include this on the differential list based on clinical and travel history. In this presentation, the participant will learn more about the fungus, including its biology, clinical disease manifestations, diagnosis, differentials, and treatment as well as promising work towards development of a preventive vaccine.

courses.title: Dermatology in practice today
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian/technician with practical information on the current thoughts on diagnosis and management of common canine and feline dermatologic problems that they encounter in their daily practice. The two Dermatologists will emphasis the diagnosis of common problems, along with appropriate clinical management. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of diagnosis and management available for their patients.

courses.title: Certificate of Preventative Veterinary Care Proficiency (CPVCPP)
courses.description: PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: Welcome to this comprehensive guide designed to transform your practice by shifting the focus from reactive treatment to proactive wellness. Throughout this course, we will embark on a journey that covers every facet of building and expanding a successful preventative care program. We will begin by establishing the core philosophy and economic case for preventative medicine before diving into its essential clinical components, including advanced diagnostics, nutrition, proactive dental care, and behavioral wellness. From there, we will explore the practical business strategies necessary for implementation, from designing tiered wellness plans and pricing models to optimizing team workflow and client communication. You will also learn to customize programs for different life stages, leverage technology for engagement, and measure your success with key performance indicators. By the end of our journey, you will be equipped with a complete blueprint to not only launch or enhance your preventative care offerings but also to effectively communicate their profound value, fostering healthier patients and a more robust practice.

courses.title: Dental Extractions - ON-DEMAND
courses.description: This lecture discusses the essential knowledge needed for performing dental extractions in dogs and cats, beginning with how to accurately diagnose conditions that require extraction (from severe periodontal disease to fractured teeth). Emphasis is placed on understanding species-specific dental anatomy. The session discusses prevention of complications, including hemorrhage, oronasal fistulas, and jaw fractures. The session will also introduce indications for hyaluronic acid in extraction sites, such as in bone regeneration as well as analgesia.

courses.title: How I manage common medical problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with common medical problems. The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common medical diseases with emphasis on endocrine, cardiac and urinary problems. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to differentiate, diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Nourishing Bonds: How to Prevent and Address Food Aversions in Pets (On Demand)
courses.description: This Collaborative Care webinar brings together a veterinary nutritionist and a feeding behavior specialist to discuss the causes of food aversion in dogs and cats and provide strategies for preventing and managing food aversion in veterinary patients. This session will include communication tips for clients and the veterinary care teams about ways of balancing the risk of food aversion while getting sick patients to eat.

courses.title: 2024 APHA Annual Meeting & Expo
courses.description: Public health is inherently future-focused, looking toward prevention and promotion to enable populations to live longer, healthier lives. But recent political polarization, underfunding and distrust of scientific research threaten our ability to create optimal, equitable health and well-being for all. The promise and effectiveness of public health is challenged by pseudoscience. Given this discord, this meeting will showcase ways to rebuild trust in public health and science.

courses.title: How to Deal With Anesthetic Complications (On-Demand)
courses.description: Anesthetic complications are an inevitable challenge in veterinary medicine, but early recognition and effective management can significantly improve patient outcomes. This lecture delves into five of the most common complications encountered during anesthesia: hypotension, bradycardia hypoventilation, hypothermia, and arrhythmias. We'll explore the underlying causes, clinical manifestations and evidence-based strategies to address each of these complications.

courses.title: Making Effective Nutritional Recommendations - Helping Clients with Diet Choices ( On Demand Webinar)
courses.description: Proper nutritional management is one of the most important factors in managing health and disease in pets. As clients become more aware of the importance of nutrition in their own health, they expect this same higher standard of nutritional care for their pets. The veterinary healthcare team should be the preferred, expert source of the best nutritional information for pets. Veterinary teams that understand and promote clinical nutrition and demonstrate in-clinic behaviors consistent with this conviction will benefit their patients, their clients, and their practices. Proper nutritional management is one of the most important factors in maximizing health, performance, and longevity in addition to managing disease conditions. The healthcare team should be educated and proactive when discussing nutrition with clients. There are differences amongst manufacturers, products, and life stages, and team members should not be afraid to ask the questions. This presentation will allow the team to present a researched and educated nutritional recommendation to clients.

courses.title: Oral Soft Tissue Surgery and Complex Case Management in Veterinary Dentistry
courses.description: This is a 3-hour, LIVE Seminar presented by Christopher Snyder, DVM, DAVDC, DEVDC. This lecture series focuses on surgical strategies and case management for challenging oral conditions in veterinary patients, combining principles of soft tissue flap design, management of feline chronic gingivostomatitis (FCGS), and surgical repair of congenital cleft palates. The course begins with essential techniques for creating and advancing oral surgical flaps, emphasizing instrumentation, mucogingival versus envelope flap selection, and methods to prevent and repair oronasal fistulas. Case-based examples highlight strategies to improve flap viability, manage palatal defects, and ensure tension-free closures. We will explore the pathophysiology and management of FCGS, including differential diagnosis, the role of viral and immune factors, and advances in both medical and surgical treatments. Special attention is given to full-mouth and quadrant-based extractions, long-term medical management strategies, and emerging therapies such as immunomodulation, laser therapy, and regenerative medicine. Finally, participants will examine the diagnosis and repair of cleft lip and palate, with review of classification systems, surgical timing, and techniques such as modified von Langenbeck, hinge flaps, and auricular cartilage grafts. Postoperative care, including feeding tube management, revision surgery planning, and client counseling, will be emphasized to improve patient outcomes. Together, these topics provide a comprehensive approach to oral soft tissue surgery and the management of complex, high-morbidity oral conditions in small animal practice.

courses.title: AAEP XP Series NeuroXP
courses.description: This intensive two-day program provides equine practitioners with practical, clinically focused training in the diagnosis and management of neurologic disease in horses. Through a combination of preparatory materials, targeted lectures, interactive case discussions, and extensive hands-on laboratory sessions, participants develop a structured approach to neurologic examination, neurolocalization, diagnostic planning, and treatment decision-making. Learning will include foundational concepts, diagnostic interpretation, and hands-on skills using live horses, cadavers, and imaging modalities with advanced case-based discussions, procedural training, and real-world clinical scenarios, including client communication and risk management. Small-group laboratories and expert faculty guidance ensure individualized instruction and immediate clinical applicability, enabling participants to confidently assess, diagnose, and manage complex equine neurologic cases in practice.

courses.title: UNDERSTANDING THE LAW FOR VETERINARIANS: VACCINE CLINICS AND TELEMEDICINE IN 2025
courses.description: Participants will gain valuable insights from industry experts on navigating and optimizing telemedicine and vaccine clinics in light of the new laws introduced in 2024. The session will cover key aspects of operating vaccine clinics while ensuring full legal compliance, as well as the parameters, conditions, and limitations of veterinary telemedicine. By the end of this discussion, attendees will be equipped with practical strategies to implement these services effectively, maximize their benefits, and achieve the greatest value for their practice and clients.

courses.title: RVG Diarrhea! Case Rounds: LIVE
courses.description: Join Dr. Gershon Alaluf for an interactive case-based discussion exploring the diagnostic and treatment approaches to diarrhea across various life stages. Using real-world examples, participants will refine their clinical reasoning, improve client communication, and strengthen decision-making skills for patients with acute and chronic diarrhea.

courses.title: Totally Topical Dude! ON DEMAND
courses.description: This program from Dr. Julia E. Miller, a diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Dermatologists, will cover how to use topical therapy for a variety of dermatologic conditions, including allergies, Malassezia dermatitis, multidrug-resistant pyoderma, and wound healing. We will focus on case selection, improving owner compliance, and determining which specific products are beneficial beyond traditional shampoos. Let's improve your multimodal approach, help your dermatologic cases resolve faster, and develop a long-term preventive game plan!

courses.title: Prescribing Movement: How to design a safe exercise plan for dogs with OA
courses.description: This presentation reviews the role of therapeutic exercise in the management of canine osteoarthritis (OA) and provides practical guidance for designing safe and effective exercise plans for affected patients. Participants will explore the physiologic benefits of exercise, including improvements in pain, strength, mobility, and overall quality of life. The session will discuss how to select exercises based on functional limitations and patient specific goals, emphasizing low-impact activities and gradual progression of frequency, intensity, duration, and type of exercise. Practical examples of therapeutic exercises used in OA patients, including strengthening, proprioception, endurance, and flexibility exercises, will be presented along with strategies for teaching caregivers to implement home exercise programs. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for prescribing movement as part of a multimodal OA management plan.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Discipline-Specific Performance Challenges Series: 2. The Flat Racehorse
courses.description: Flat racehorses are among the most finely tuned equine athletes, subject to intense training and competition demands that place significant stresses to their systems. This second discussion in the Discipline-Specific Performance Challenges series brings together leading veterinarians from around the world to explore the performance challenges they encounter specific to the flat racehorse. The panel will examine performance-limiting factors and challenges commonly encountered in flat racing and debate the similarities and differences in their approaches to prevention and management. From young horses entering training to seasoned campaigners, join the discussion on strategies in maintaining soundness, optimizing performance, and setting realistic expectations for flat racehorses at every stage of their careers.

courses.title: How to Grow Your Own Managers
courses.description: How do you help an employee become a team leader or hospital manager? Discover resources for veterinary management training, networking, organizations, and mentorship. Veterinarians and managers share their experiences of promoting staff from within their hospitals.

courses.title: Otitis Made Manageable: A Tiered Topical Treatment Roadmap
courses.description: This anytime lecture provides veterinarians with a practical framework for tiered topical product selection in the management of otitis externa. We will discuss common etiologies of otitis, including bacterial, yeast, and mixed infections, and learn how cytology findings guide rational topical therapy choices. The session will outline a tiered approach to treatment, progressing from first-line broad-spectrum products to targeted therapies based on organism type, inflammation severity, and chronicity.

courses.title: TRIAGE AND RESUSCITATION OF THE CANINE AND FELINE NEONATE (1600-44549)
courses.description: TRIAGE AND RESUSCITATION OF THE CANINE AND FELINE NEONATE (1600-44549) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: The role of nutrition and feeding strategies for cats with FIC
courses.description:
Using clinical case examples, this Collaborative Care webinar will focus on nutrition as a component of multimodal management of feline idiopathic cystitis (FIC), including research related to dietary strategies used in the management of FIC, as well as hydration and feeding behavior strategies that optimize the indoor environment. Topics will include an overview of FIC pathophysiology and its impact on the human-animal bond, along with evidence-based nutritional strategies that support cats with chronic lower urinary tract disease. Discussion will focus on the role of therapeutic urinary diets, practical methods for increasing hydration, and feeding and environmental strategies that align with Multimodal Environmental Modification (MEMO).
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion

courses.title: Is it urgent or emergent?
courses.description: In this seminar, Drs De Laforcade and Butler will discuss handling those walk-in, same-day cases that challenge practitioners with an already busy schedule. They will discuss strategies used to manage high case-load, telephone triage and how to differentiate urgent care vs emergent cases. Drs De Laforcade and Butler will bring case examples highlighting the triage, stabilization and management of these dynamic and challenging cases.

courses.title: Clinical Utility of Screening Tests in Companion Animal Practice
courses.description: Many clinicians fail to understand what screening tests are, what populations they should be applied to, and what information they provide. Additionally, the epidemiological considerations of screening tests largely determine their utility and accuracy. Finally, clinicians should understand that even if all the conditions for screening tests are met, other variables might impact their application. This seminar will discuss the uses and abuses of screening test and help clinicians reassess their desires or inclinations to run tests that might not be warranted. Specific examples of a common clinical screening test will be provided.

courses.title: Certificate of Veterinary Practice Technology Proficiency (CVPTP)
courses.description:
The Certificate of Veterinary Practice Technology Proficiency (CVPTP) course provides a high-level overview of current veterinary technology tools and resources. The veterinary field has experienced a technological revolution in recent years, greatly enhancing diagnostic precision, treatment efficacy, and patient outcomes. Innovations such as electronic record management, artificial intelligence, telehealth, advanced imaging modalities, and automated laboratory analyzers have reshaped the landscape of veterinary medicine.
The learner will also have the opportunity to engage with an interactive AI pet owner for a mock telehealth appointment using suggested communication skills. They will then execute electronic veterinary record documentation for the visit

courses.title: Personal Resilience Influencers
courses.description: This on-demand course explores the key influences that determine how resilient you are, both personally and professionally, in challenging situations. You can see how certain factors, such as our personal traits (like positivity or negativity), coping skills, habits, and social circle, can influence our level of resilience. Sometimes these influences are powerful, and sometimes they are subtle. And they will either move us toward greater resilience or away from it.

courses.title: Too Aggressive to Care For? ON-DEMAND
courses.description:
A presentation about why some patients cannot counter condition to the veterinary
experience; do not sedate well, and are a safety risk for veterinary care in a clinic, shelter or
house call setting. A guide to objectively assessing this patient for safe handling, creating a safe exam environment and assessing the welfare of the animal, client and staff is included.

courses.title: What's the Link Between Chronic Pain and Changes in Behavior? - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Chronic pain adversely impacts the wellbeing of dogs and cats and has a far-reaching impact on their quality of life. Chronic pain (e.g., osteoarthritis) presents in multiple ways including changes in behavior such as increased fearfulness, noise sensitivity, disrupted sleep patterns, house soiling and aggression. In many cases the presenting behavioral complaint is a direct manifestation of underlying pain. Behavioral changes can precede the more obvious signs we associate with musculoskeletal pian including stiffness, lameness, and changes in gait. Pain assessment should be integral to any behavioral consultation. Validated questionnaires and equipment such as activity monitors can track the success of interventions.

courses.title: Comprehensive Management of Feline CKD, Part 2 (On Demand webinar)
courses.description:
This webinar brings together a boarded nutritionist and internist who will discuss how veterinarians can manage feline chronic kidney disease (CKD) using a comprehensive, evidence-based approach that includes a sound nutritional plan. Using clinical cases, the panelists will discuss the appropriate nutritional assessment, and medical and nutritional management of CKD in cats. Differences and similarities in the clinical presentation, diagnostic approach, and nutritional management of cats with CKD will be discussed. The speakers will discuss the current state of the science of CKD; the role of the gut-kidney axis; and nutritional management of CKD and its potential sequelae.
This webinar is a sequel to a previous Collaborative Care webinar from 2024 and will build on that webinar's content, but will also be suitable as a standalone webinar.

courses.title: Eyes, ears & beyond
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients presented to their clinic with a dermatologic or ocular problem. The combination of a Dermatologist and an Ophthalmologist will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists

courses.title: AAIV PRESENTS: INVESTMENTS, MARKET VOLATILITY, MEDIA NOISE AND YOU! (1055-43669)
courses.description: AAIV PRESENTS: INVESTMENTS, MARKET VOLATILITY, MEDIA NOISE AND YOU! (1055-43669) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Proudly Independent: Why the Conditions Are Right for a Renaissance of Independent Veterinary Practice Ownership ON DEMAND
courses.description: This course explores the evolving landscape of veterinary practice ownership, providing a compelling perspective on why independent practice ownership is not only viable but poised for resurgence. Attendees will gain insight into the economic, structural, and market conditions that have shaped the rise of corporatization, and learn about the opportunities, tools, and strategies available to support private veterinary ownership today. Keywords: veterinary economics, practice ownership, independent practice, corporatization, veterinary business strategy.

courses.title: Meeting the Challenge of Cognitive Decline in Older Pets
courses.description: Cognitive dysfunction syndrome (CDS) is a progressive neurodegenerative condition affecting aging dogs and cats, often compared to Alzheimer's disease in humans. Despite its prevalence, CDS remains underdiagnosed due to overlapping symptoms with other age-related conditions and a general under recognition of behavioral signs. This webinar will provide veterinary professionals with a comprehensive overview of pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic approach, and current treatment strategies for CDS. Emphasis will be placed on practical tools for recognizing cognitive decline, client communication strategies, and evidence-based management techniques to enhance the quality of life for both patients and their caregivers.

courses.title: Derm disasters got you down? Let us talk about how to use multimodal therapy to increase your successes!
courses.description: This course covers in detail the diagnostic and treatment approaches to your complicated small animal dermatology cases.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Oral Cavity Internal Trauma Case Discussion
courses.description:
Oral Cavity Internal Trauma: Case Discussions
PANEL DISCUSSION DESCRIPTION
In this Panel Discussion, four leading experts discuss their experience of, and approach to trauma to the oral cavity including injuries to the tongue, buccal and lingual mucosa, palate, foreign body complications, and iatrogenic dental trauma. While certain types of damage, such as those associated with bit fit / position or fractured teeth, have been previously explored, the broader spectrum of internal oral injuries warrants further discussion. These cases often present unique diagnostic and treatment challenges, with approaches varying based on the nature of the injury, the veterinarian's experience, and available resources. In this discussion, the panellists will share insights from their own cases, and trade practical strategies to enhance diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

courses.title: Practice Management for Success
courses.description: Hour 1: Resilience Strategies and tools to stay resilient, healthy and happy in veterinary medicine Hour 2: Communication Optimizing communication and conflict resolution with your team and pet parents Hour 3: Client Service and Patient Care Learn how going above and beyond is not all that hard when it comes to customer service and how small tips, tricks and tools can set your hospital apart from the rest Hour 4: Social Trends Consumer expectations of your veterinary team; current trends changing the veterinary industry

courses.title: Managing the cancer patient in your practice
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with problems associated with cancer. The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in their daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.provider: US ARMY PUBLIC HEALTH COMMAND EUROPE
courses.title: 71st International Military Veterinary Exchange
courses.description: The target audience is military veterinary personnel. The theme this year is Combined Veterinary Services, Stronger Together in Large Scale Combat Operations. The objective is to discuss a variety of veterinary public health concerns, exchange ideas and share best practices, and work collaboratively with international military veterinarians to address mutual interests in the areas of food safety, biosurveillance for emerging health threats, zoonoses, transboundary disease prevention and mitigation, hazards to military working animals in an operational environment, and military working animal welfare.

courses.title: Gastrointestinal medicine update
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian/technician with practical information on the current thoughts on diagnosis and management of common canine and feline gastrointestinal problems that they encounter in their daily practice. Emphasis will be placed on the diagnosis of common problems, including what tests are appropriate and what tests are not. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of diagnosis and management available for their patients.

courses.title: Managing the geriatric patient
courses.description: This course to be presented by Dr's Pike and Oswald is focused on providing the attendee with updated information on the diagnosis and management of common geriatric problems. In this course, the speakers will emphasize how use diagnostic tests and interpret the results along with current initial and ongoing therapeutic recommendations for the canine and feline patient. This combination of a Behaviorist and an Internist will provide a comprehensive discussion of the age related topics.

courses.title: Optimizing Use of Hydrolyzed and Amino Acid-Based Diets
courses.description:
This Collaborative Care webinar will provide an overview of how hydrolyzed and amino acid-based pet foods are produced, including variations in base protein, type, and degree of hydrolysis and how this may affect digestibility, and the gastrointestinal immune response. An overview of how amino acid-based diets differ from hydrolyzed diets will also be discussed. Presenters will then discuss clinical cases for which hydrolyzed, or amino acid-based diets are indicated, discussing the indications for each. The cases will reinforce the applications of hydrolyzed diet, the scientific basis for more than one hydrolyzed diet trials for specific cases (such as suspected food allergies), and when amino acid-based diets are indicated.
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: Regional Nerve Blocks for Dental Patients ON DEMAND
courses.description: Regional anesthesia is a cornerstone of modern veterinary dentistry, improving patient comfort, reducing general anesthetic requirements, and enhancing procedural safety. This presentation provides a comprehensive, clinically focused review of the most commonly used regional nerve blocks in dogs and cats. Attendees will learn the anatomical landmarks, indications, contraindications, and step by step techniques for infraorbital, maxillary, mental, and mandibular blocks. Emphasis is placed on safe needle handling, appropriate local anesthetic selection, dosage considerations, and strategies to minimize complications. Practical tips, case examples, and visual aids help participants confidently integrate regional anesthesia into everyday dental practice. This session is designed for veterinarians and technicians seeking to elevate their dentistry skills and improve patient outcomes through effective multimodal analgesia.

courses.title: Identifying & Recommending the Best Supplements for Clients
courses.description: The pet supplement market is growing, and today's pet parents are eager to use supplements, not just for managing their pet's health reactively but also proactively. Surveys have shown that clients want veterinarians to recommend supplements for their pets. To answer this demand, veterinarians need to understand the pet supplement market and how to identify and recommend safe, quality supplements for their patients.

courses.title: (On Demand) Demystifying Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency ( Dmystifier l'insuffisance du pancras exocrine) French lecture
courses.description: This lecture aims to break down exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI) in dogs and cats. The following aspects will be covered: the main causes in companion animals, the different clinical presentations in dogs and cats, diagnostic methods, concurrent diseases, as well as treatment options (necessary supplementation, implementation of digestive enzymes, diet, etc.)

courses.title: 2025 AAEP Virtual Convention
courses.description: Cannot take time away from your practice and need some CE credits? Interested in learning more about equine specific veterinary medicine topics? The 2025 AAEP Virtual Convention is for you. The AAEP Virtual Convention offers educational opportunities for equine veterinarians and equine veterinarian technicians offering over 80 CE credits in various categories. CE credits are provided via recordings of lectures, seminars, workshops and facilitator lead discussions on specific topics that are presented at the live 2025 AAEP 70th Annual Convention. These virtual sessions can help attendees gain knowledge in the areas of subjects include Lameness/Sports Medicine, Theriogenology, Infectious and Non-Infectious Diseases, Dentistry, Dermatology, Nutrition, Imaging, Tech in Practice, Surgery and Medicine, as well as Business, Ethical and Social concerns.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Anaesthetic Complications of the Gastrointestinal Tract Vomiting, Regurgitation, Stricture and Dysmotilit
courses.description:
Anaesthesia has a profound effect on the gastrointestinal tract. There are many potentially concerning complications related to the gastrointestinal tract such as nausea reflux and regurgitation ileus and gut stasis.
