Join us for this interesting panel discussion where the worlds leading experts will come together to share their wealth of experience and opinions. There are many drugs one can consider to prevent or mitigate these complications and to make our patients feel better. There are questions related to the ideal fasting regimens and timings and periods which will be included with the latest evidence available. We will also delve into the control of nausea including whether antiemetics should be a standard part of our protocols as well as the evidence around the use of gastroprotectants. Brachycephalic anaesthesia will be discussed with their unique challenges.

courses.title: Optimizing Use of Hydrolyzed and Amino Acid-Based Diets (On Demand)
courses.description: This Collaborative Care webinar will provide an overview of how hydrolyzed and amino acid-based pet foods are produced, including variations in base protein, type, and degree of hydrolysis and how this may affect digestibility, and the gastrointestinal immune response. An overview of how amino acid-based diets differ from hydrolyzed diets will also be discussed. Presenters will then discuss clinical cases for which hydrolyzed, or amino acid-based diets are indicated, discussing the indications for each. The cases will reinforce the applications of hydrolyzed diet, the scientific basis for more than one hydrolyzed diet trials for specific cases (such as suspected food allergies), and when amino acid-based diets are indicated.

courses.title: Expanding Your Veterinary Practices Horizons: The Multifaceted Values of Working with Californias Shelters in Need
courses.description: Presented by the San Francisco SPCA and the California Veterinary Medical Association (CVMA), this informative and inspiring webinar is designed to highlight the rewarding opportunities available for veterinarians within Californias animal shelters. California shelters are in urgent need of veterinary support. A significant number of shelters across the state currently lack regular access to veterinary care, resulting in a critical gap in animal welfare services. This webinar will explore how veterinarians and RVTs can play a vital role in improving outcomes for shelter animals, whether as a full-time career path or as a supplement to private practice.

courses.title: Beyond the Dental: Hyaluronic Acid and the Future of At-Home Periodontal Care ON DEMAND
courses.description:
Periodontal disease remains the most common clinical condition diagnosed in companion animal practice, yet maintaining oral health between anesthetic dental procedures continues to be a major challenge for veterinary teams and pet owners. Gingivitis represents the earliest and only reversible stage of periodontal disease, making early intervention and consistent home care essential components of effective management.
This lecture explores the emerging role of hyaluronic acid in veterinary dental medicine, including its biologic mechanisms, clinical evidence, and practical applications in both in-clinic and at-home settings. Participants will review current research evaluating hyaluronic acid therapies, including randomized controlled studies demonstrating improvements in gingival inflammation in dogs. The session will also discuss strategies for integrating simple, technician-driven home care solutions into dental protocols to support periodontal health between COHAT procedures.
Attendees will leave with practical tools for improving client compliance, enhancing periodontal care plans, and expanding preventive dentistry protocols within their practices.

courses.title: Elevating Senior and Geriatric Canine Care Part 1
courses.description: This multisession program covers different senior and geriatric canine topics with a focus on enabling practitioners to elevate their day-to-day practice with aging dogs for easier management of geriatrics in practice and the common ailments that accompany them. Topics range from implementing senior dog care programs, managing chronic pain in senior dogs, managing chronic cough in senior dogs when to work up bloodwork abnormalities, managing sarcopenia in elderly canines and novel strategies for appetite stimulation in senior dogs.

courses.title: Supporting Painful Dogs and Cats Through Veterinary Visits: A Guide to Comfort and Cooperative Care
courses.description: This presentation addresses strategies for preparing dogs and cats experiencing pain for veterinary visits, focusing on minimizing stress and discomfort both at home and within the hospital environment. The session covers home - based preparation techniques, environmental modifications in the clinic, handling approaches based on Low Stress Handling and Sophia Yin's 10 General Handling Principles, and the application of cooperative care techniques. The presentation will examine the use of medication protocols, sedation options, and handling tools to support safer and more comfortable experiences for both patients and veterinary teams. Participants will learn how to integrate these strategies into daily practice to improve outcomes for painful patients.

courses.title: Concentrates in Equine Diets
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with information about concentrates in equine diets, including types of concentrates available, commercial feed products, and interpreting a feed label.

courses.title: From Positioning to Perception: A Practical Guide to Orthopedic Radiographs
courses.description: In this 3-hour, non-interactive, online CARE CE webinar, board-certified orthopedic surgeon Dr. Kristin Kirkby Shaw will review practical principles for obtaining and interpreting orthopedic radiographs in dogs and cats, with emphasis on osteoarthritis and common orthopedic diseases of the thoracic and pelvic limbs. This course will cover the prevalence of radiographic joint disease, limitations of radiographs in patients with joint disease and chronic pain, strategies for optimizing image quality, and a systematic approach to image interpretation. Participants will also review joint-specific positioning considerations for the shoulder, elbow, carpus, digits, hip, stifle, and tarsus, and learn when radiographs may help narrow a diagnosis versus when advanced imaging may be indicated.

courses.title: Embrace Your Feline Diabetics: A Novel Strategy to Remove Fear, Anxiety, & Stress from Patients, Clients, & Veterinary Teams
courses.description: This program reviews clinical presentation and diagnostics with a new feline diabetic, including the impact on emotional health for the patient and pet parent. Much of the lecture will focus on our options with this patient, specifically the new SGLT2 inhibitor Bexacat. Attendees will learn about the mechanism of action, dosing, possible adverse events (and how it differs from insulin therapy), case selection, and monitoring guidelines. The final aspects of the webinar will focus on this alternative option and ways to remove fear, anxiety, and stress in our diabetic patients and families.

courses.title: Health and Wealthness: Financial Wellness Basics for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: In this course, Get MotiVETed and Florida Veterinary Advisors bring you this financial wellness basics for veterinary professionals! Finances are at the top of most people's minds, which can lead to day-to-day unhappiness, overwhelm, divorce and at times, worse. Not only does this apply to people in the general public, but it also applies to us as veterinary professionals. When you approach your wellbeing in a holistic sense, finances emerge as an integral part of that. Your level of peace, safety, comfort and success can be measured to an extent based on your financial picture. Here's the good news: no matter what your financial picture is now, it can be improved, and in this course, we'll show you how! You will learn whether or not money really does buy happiness. In addition, we explore the most powerful motivators to improving your financial wellbeing, so you can get out of survival mode which means you get to build wealth and comfort as a veterinary professional! Together, we work to help you find clarity and purpose in the areas of your life that are most important and highly influenced by your relationship with money. You will know the best habits to cultivate or change in order to build your asset column, and when you can release the budget! We cover different options of where to put your money, and we touch on budgeting with a reluctant spouse. Ultimately, we teach you the mindset and skill set you need to bring freedom and joy into your life through enhancing your financial security.

courses.title: Psychological Safety in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This session will cover psychological safety and how veterinary professional team members and leaders can survive and thrive through education, resources, and support.

courses.title: Veterinary Laser Therapy in Clinical Practice: Science, Safety, and Applications in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description:
Photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) is a type of laser therapy increasingly utilized in veterinary medicine as an adjunctive modality in a variety of situations, including pain management, inflammatory conditions, wound healing, and rehabilitation. This continuing education course provides a practical overview of PBMT and its clinical application in veterinary patients.
Participants will review the biologic and physics of PBMT, including wavelength, power density, energy dosage, and proposed mechanisms of action at the cellular and tissue levels. Current veterinary literature will be discussed to evaluate the indications and therapeutic effects of PBMT across common clinical scenarios.
The course will address practical considerations for clinical use of PBMT, including patient selection, treatment protocols, safety standards, and contraindications. Common applications such as musculoskeletal pain, osteoarthritis, wound management, and post-operative care will be presented to illustrate appropriate integration into veterinary practice. Additionally, the course shares newer modalities for the use of PBMT, including internal medicine usage, allergic dermatitis, as well as dental disease.
Designed for both veterinarians and veterinary technicians, this course emphasizes safe, ethical, and informed use of PBMT while supporting interprofessional collaboration within the veterinary healthcare team.

courses.title: Communication Strategies for Improved Patient Outcomes
courses.description: This course teaches veterinary team members how to apply the Calgary-Cambridge Guide, a structured communication framework, to client interactions across the full clinical visit. Participants will learn to initiate appointments effectively, gather complete client histories through active listening, build trust through empathy and partnering language, deliver clear recommendations, convey the value of recommended services, and create space for client questions and concerns. Learning is reinforced through applied practice scenarios and a final knowledge assessment.

courses.title: Pet Fish Medicine
courses.description: This lecture will provide an in-depth exploration of veterinary care for pet fish species. Attendees will learn about aquarium water quality management, physical examination techniques, and diagnostic sampling methods specific to fish patients. The course will cover common diseases, treatment options, and drug administration routes in aquatic species. Veterinary professionals will gain practical skills in fish handling, anesthesia, and surgery, enabling them to confidently manage fish patients in both home aquarium and pond settings.

courses.title: Can we influence aging? Learn the fundamentals of aging in dogs
courses.description: This program will introduce fundamentals of aging biology in dogs, with an emphasis on clinical impact and targets for prevention and treatment. We will examine what goes wrong as dogs age, how this damages their health and quality of life, what approaches have been shown to extend healthy lifespan, and what new treatments are on the horizon.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - The Equine GI Microbiome and Dysbiosis: What do we Know & What Should we be Doing?
courses.description: We have assembled an expert and multidisciplinary panel to discuss the current and clinically applicable understanding of the equine gastrointestinal microbiome and dysbiosis. There will be a focus on what defines a healthy microbiome, factors that disrupt it, and its potential clinical relevance. Key topics include the clinical use of faecal microbiomics, faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and practical use of prebiotics, probiotics, and dietary strategies to modify, influence, or support intestinal microbiota populations. The panel will discuss clinical scenarios where the microbiome should be considered, address methods for assessing microbiome status, practical approaches to maintain or restore balance, and the potential impact on equine patients.

courses.title: Refractory Equine Glandular Gastric Disease Morbidity and Mortality Case Discussions
courses.description:
This interactive panel discussion brings together internationally recognised internal medicine specialists from Europe and the United States to discuss the challenges of treating Equine Glandular Gastric Disease EGGD, and specifically, how best to manage horses that are refractory to treatment. The discussion will focus primarily on pharmacological management but will also touch on other management and feeding strategies that can be used to improve healing rates and mitigate against reoccurrence.
Whilst recognising the limitations surrounding availability of certain drug formulations in different countries, the panelists will debate what they consider to be first line and second line drugs for treatment of EGGD how they use them to maximise efficacy and how they would modify their approach in the case of a non-responder. The panelists will contribute a wealth of clinical experience and anecdote to the discussion but will be encouraged to justify their approaches based upon current evidence where available.

courses.title: Certificate Course: Master Foundations in Reproductive Medicine
courses.description:
The landscape of animal reproductive health has changed over time, and it's time to move past old "one size fits all" mentalities. This 5-part video series will answer the many questions asked of practitioners every day: When should I spay this dog? How do I fix a pyometra on a near zero budget? What can I do to save fading puppies? Join our expert panel of specialists for a tour in theriogenology foundations, covering everything from breeding soundness screening, to surgical advice, neonatal and puppy care, and even a lesson on cats!
We'll discuss ethical breeding practices, heritable disease screening options, practice neonatal care through weaning, and cover all the options for dystocia and pyometra treatment. Receive in-depth spay/neuter and c-section surgical tips, learn about feline reproduction and often overlooked male reproductive issues. With over 16 hours of training, this course offers a wide variety of insights that will benefit litter-ally every general practitioner's clinic!

courses.title: Advanced imaging of the chest and abdomen - when does it enhance patient care vs. just owner cost?
courses.description:
Accessibility to advanced imaging has been ever growing for both general and specialist veterinarians. Advanced imaging of the thorax is often a huge complement to radiographs and ultrasound for numerous types of pathology, not only limited to pleural, pulmonary, thoracic wall and even cardiac imaging. For the abdomen applications are even more extensive with improved visualization of all organs, vasculature and surrounding musculoskeletal structures.
Despite how much advanced imaging has enhanced diagnostics in the veterinary patient, as with all medical imaging advances there are also numerous occasions in which advanced imaging may be unnecessary, may not provide further information or even be the less ideal modality for patient signs.
An international panel of world-renowned imaging specialists with extensive experience with advanced imaging will be discussing indications, the numerous benefits but also the limitations of and alternatives to advanced imaging. The different discussion points will be debated via case presentations to keep the discussion focused on clinical decision making.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Hepatic and Urinary Disease
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage hepatic and urinary disease cases in the field.

courses.title: DNM Nutrition Myths & Facts: Parts 1 & 2
courses.description: The challenge for veterinary professionals today is that the Internet has made it harder, not easier, to educate pet owners about what to feed their pets. Because of the abundance of misinformation, proper pet nutrition counseling by veterinary practices is more important than ever. This course explores the problem of and solutions to nutrition myths, how owner misconceptions can arise, and debunks myths about raw food diets, protein, such as animal digest, by-products and low protein diets for seniors, and food coloring and preservatives. You've heard the adage, "A little knowledge can be a dangerous thing." This saying certainly applies to misinformation about pet nutrition, which often persists despite scientific information that disapproves it. While nutrition myths may initially be based on facts, over time the accurate data becomes distorted with inaccuracies.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Polysaccharide Storage Myopathy
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage polysaccharide storage myopathy cases in the field.

courses.title: PANEL DISCUSSION - Common Complications of Routine Surgical Procedures - UG Tract (Castrations, Spays etc.)
courses.description:
Routine urogenital surgeries are frequently required and commonly undertaken in small animal general practice (spays, castrations, cystotomies, urethrostomies, etc..).
Join our team of world-leading multidisciplinary specialists in this exciting panel discussion where they will discuss and debate the commonly encountered pitfalls and management of postoperative complications following routine surgical procedures of the urogenital tract, including haemorrhage, urine leakage, urinary tract infection, haematuria, urethral stricture, ovarian remnant syndrome, scrotal swelling, and much more.
Case examples will be used to highlight key points and share useful tips. This is a unique opportunity for attending veterinarians to share their experience and ask questions of our experts.

courses.title: Stronger for Longer: Maintaining Muscle & Mobility in the Aging Feline
courses.description: We're all familiar with the "cut the snacks" message for cats with double digit scale numbers. But what about the quiet creep of weakness that follows senior pet weight loss? In this free, one-hour video course, we're joining feline specialist Dr. Ashlie Saffire in exploring the types and consequences of muscle loss in geriatric felines. We'll discuss feline age stages, the effects of frailty, and ways to slow sarcopenia that preserve mobility and quality of life.

courses.title: Small Animal Programme part 1
courses.description: This programme includes 23 hours of world-class CPD, delivered by experts in the field. The main objective is to keep veterinarians up to date with the latest insights into small animals. The Programme will outline the typical approach to investigating and managing cases in order to optimise the outcome. Topics covered range from dermatology, nutrition, behaviour, oncology, among others.

courses.title: Exam Communication Mastery
courses.description: When clients decline vaccines, blood work, or preventatives, patient care and revenue suffers. Get strategies and scripts to increase compliance for preventive services, products, and procedures. Understand body language and how to use it during exam conversations. Learn how to present treatment plans so clients will accept care.

courses.title: Confident Canine Care: Masterclass In Exercise Therapy For Every Practice
courses.description: This course covers why canine exercise is important, how to evaluate a dog before and after exercises are done, how to choose and perform appropriate exercises. The exercises we chose to teach are designed for dogs of all ages. The purpose is for veterinary professionals, whether they have had rehabilitation training or not, to be able to implement these exercises into their medical recommendations for improved quality of life, cognitive function and longevity for their canine patients.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Heatstroke and Collapse
courses.description:
Heatstroke in dogs is seen more frequently these days due to record high temperatures thanks to climate change and extreme weather patterns.
Heatstroke is an acute, progressive and potentially life-threatening clinical emergency secondary to a severe temperature increase due to the inefficiencies of heat dissipation mechanisms and or dogs which havent been acclimated to higher temperatures. Canine athletes and military working dogs may develop exertional heatstroke especially in extremes of temperatures. It causes a multitude of problems including central nervous system dysfunctions and hypoxia, which may lead to multiple organ dysfunction syndrome and even if rapid treatment is performed, it may still be fatal. There can be other factors such as dehydration, electrolytes disturbances, clotting abnormalities, heart dysfunction and signs related to organ failure. exertional or non-exertional.
Many questions may arise related to this syndrome What are the risk factors Why do these patients deteriorate so rapidly What can we do better to improve their prognosis How can we educate clients How should a dog be effectively cooled without causing vasoconstriction in the skin and or hypovolaemia What medical support is needed Is there a place for routine oxygen therapy, plasma transfusions, anti-seizure and anti-arrhythmic medication How should these patients be monitored
Join us for this exciting, relevant panel discussion where four hand-picked experts will share their experiences and tips and tricks to improve the outcome of these dogs, debate the best course of action for prevention an management, and explore challenging cases.

courses.title: From Chaos to Control: Strategic Planning for Veterinary Practices; Part 3
courses.description:
From Chaos to Control: Strategic Planning for Veterinary Practices is a three-part, live webinar program designed to help veterinary leaders transition from reactive daily operations to intentional, sustainable practice leadership. Delivered as a progressive learning series, each session builds upon the previous to guide participants through the foundational elements of strategic planning, team alignment, operational accountability, and long-term organizational resilience.
Veterinary medicine often operates in a constant state of urgency, leaving little time for proactive planning or leadership development. This program provides practical frameworks and actionable strategies to help veterinary professionals clarify priorities, improve communication, strengthen culture, enhance team utilization, and create measurable organizational goals that support both financial health and team well-being.
Participants will learn how to identify barriers that prevent practices from achieving strategic alignment, translate vision into daily operational behaviors, and develop systems that create accountability, adaptability, and long-term sustainability. The program is designed specifically for veterinary professionals seeking practical tools that can immediately be applied within clinical practice settings.
Attendees must complete all three sessions to receive continuing education credit, as each session builds upon the concepts and application work introduced in prior sessions.

courses.title: Modern Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approaches to Musculoskeletal Conditions
courses.description: This course is intended to provide participants with an on-demand continuing education program in regenerative medicine and other modern diagnostic & therapeutic approaches to musculoskeletal conditions to maximize case success(es).¿

courses.title: Changing Outcomes, Saving Lives
courses.description:
"How lucky to be in Veterinary Medicine! You get to play with puppies and kittens all day." We have all heard that and we all know that is not even close to being true.
Even if we do have puppy or kitten patients, they are not always healthy. Parvo is a disease that destroys wellbeing in all - the puppy, the owner, and the veterinary team. Fighting to save the life of a sick puppy has not only physical demands, but also significant mental strain and emotional drain. Adding cases like this to an already overwhelmed and overworked staff can deplete morale, stamina, and resources.
How can we change the outcome for the better when a puppy is diagnosed with parvo? Elanco's new CPMA treatment for Parvo is not only saving the lives of puppies but is also improving the lives of the people who care for them. This single dose of Compassion goes a long way in helping to energize the veterinary team to care for the lives of their patients, their clients, and their own lives.

courses.title: FDA, XCA, RXE: What Does the Alphabet Soup of Conditional Drug Approval Really Mean for Veterinarians?
courses.description:
In the last few years, some really useful new drugs have become available to veterinarians through the new pathway of conditional approval, such as Laverdia and Panoquel.
This session explains this relatively new pathway for veterinary drugs and lays out a road map to help clinicians understand:
- the safety and effectiveness of conditionally approved products
- what rules there are for how we can and should use them
- how we can explain to clients the difference between conditionally approved veterinary drugs, fully approved veterinary drugs, off-label use of human and veterinary drugs, and dietary supplements.

courses.title: Understanding and measuring frailty in geriatric dogs
courses.description: Frailty is a routine clinical measure of the impact of aging and age-associated disease on health and wellbeing in geriatric humans. A number of frailty instruments have been developed to assess this measure in companion dogs as well. Measuring frailty can help clinicians assess risk and make decisions about the best treatment plan for older dogs. Frailty can also be useful in research to evaluate the effects of new treatments. This session will explore the causes of frailty, the tools used to measure, and the practical uses of frailty assessment in canine practice.

courses.title: Fur Real! Weekly skin care secrets from a veterinary dermatologist
courses.description: On this lecture skin care recommendations for maintenance and prevention of dermatological conditions will be reviewed.

courses.title: What to Say When You Raise Prices
courses.description: Inflation is hitting the veterinary profession hard, with vendor price hikes reaching up to 12 percent, and everyday costs climbing from fuel to food. If your hospital has not adjusted its fees yet, it is time to act. But raising fees is only half the battle. The real challenge is communicating those changes to clients with clarity, confidence, and compassion. Get the language, strategies, and mindset needed to navigate fee conversations without losing trust or loyalty. Learn how to frame your message, anticipate client reactions, and turn a potentially awkward moment into an opportunity to reinforce the value of your care.

courses.title: Feline Fine: How to recognize and manage arthritis in cats
courses.description: This lecture equips veterinary professionals to recognize and manage feline osteoarthritis (OA) by blending behavior-centered detection with practical, multimodal treatment. We review why radiographs underestimate the burden of DJD in cats and emphasize caregiver-sourced home videos and checklists to close the diagnosis gap. Attendees will learn to develop a multi-modal management plan based on the CARE Comprehensive Care Quad pain pharmacology, nutrition/weight, lifestyle/environmental modification, and rehabilitation. We also cover cat-friendly, low-stress visit strategies (including pre-visit pharmaceuticals) to improve assessment and outcomes.

courses.title: The ABCs and 123s of Veterinary Dentistry; Pre-anesthesia to Procedure
courses.description: This lecture is designed to engage participants while broadening their understanding of the importance of veterinary dentistry. During this session, participants will recall practical steps of the pre-anesthetic work up and review communication tools to aid in explaining the value of dental procedures to clients. The session will finish by beginning to prepare the veterinary team for anesthesia monitoring during dental procedures, a most requested topic. As veterinary technicians and assistants become more confident in their abilities to recognize issues and respond to them, their confidence will show in the exam room when talking with clients as they approach dentistry conversations and advocate for the pet.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: State of the Sheep Industry
courses.description:
This course will discuss the current situation and outlook for the sheep and lamb sector. Main topics to be discussed will be current economic conditions in the US, supply and demand market fundamentals, and driving factors that could affect the sheep and lamb industry.
Learning Objectives:
1. The attendee will gain insights into market fundamentals driving the sheep and lamb industry.
2. Attendees will better understand the market dynamics at play in the sheep and lamb industry that are potentially driving production decisions.

courses.title: Veterinary Ventures CE Acadia 2026
courses.description: This course covers two specialty topics commonly encountered by the general practitioner & ER veterinarian - Emergency/Critical Care and Internal Medicine. Dr. Megan McClosky will discuss CKD, FIP, and managing comorbidities in older patients. Dr. Katie Mauro will discuss AKI and maternal and neonatal emergencies. This will be an interactive medical presentation. This is a 3 day conference that will provide 15 hours of RACE approved CE credits.

courses.title: DNM Therapeutic Nutrition for Cardiovascular Disease
courses.description: Cardiac disease is a common disorder in dogs and cats. Depending on the species and breed, cardiomyopathies, such as hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy, and myxomatous mitral valve disease, are heart conditions typically seen by veterinarians. Heart disease progression can be unpredictable, and pets often appear normal in the early stages of heart disease. Management of heart disease includes medication and specially formulated diets, as certain nutrients can have a positive impact on heart health. Throughout this module, you will briefly review healthy heart anatomy and physiology. Following, a more in-depth discussion will be provided surrounding Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease (MMVD): its pathophysiology, diagnosis of including staging, and management of. Further discussion will be had on targeted beneficial nutrients for dogs and cats with cardiac disease including cachexia

courses.title: Recognizing the Top 15 Dog and Cat Dental Diseases
courses.description: Of the many dental diseases affecting our patients' mouths, learn how to recognize the top 15 including abrasion, attrition, caries, contact mucositis, complicated and uncomplicated crown exposures, dentin dysplasia, enamel hypocalcification, enamel hypoplasia, furcation involvement and exposure, gingival enlargement, hairy tongue, oronasal fistulae, and periodontal disease.

courses.title: Everything You Need to Know About Reminders
courses.description: Discover the science and strategy behind effective reminders. Find out which methods yield the highest response rates, how to time and tailor your outreach, and what language motivates timely action. Learn how to boost appointment bookings, reduce no-shows with confirmations, and drive prescription refills using smart, action-oriented messaging.

courses.title: FAT RESPONSIVE CONDITIONS IN DOGS AND CATS (On Demand Webinar)
courses.description: This lecture will focus on practical approaches to diseases in the dog (mainly) and cat which are responsive to treatment at least in part to a low-fat diet. We will cover vacuolar hepatopathy, hyperlipidemia, pancreatitis and some forms of gastrointestinal disease.

courses.title: The Role of Nutrition in Diabetes Management (On Demand)
courses.description:
This Collaborative Care webinar will provide an overview of diabetes mellitus in cats and dogs, including species differences. Although it will focus on the role of nutrition in the management of feline and canine DM, presenters will also address comprehensive management (including monitoring and weight loss).
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this webinar will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: More Than a Cleaning: Elevating Dental Care & Patient Outcomes
courses.description: This interactive webinar will reframe the concept of a "routine dental cleaning" as a vital medical procedure that can help improve patient health, comfort, and longevity. Dr. Jennifer R. Mathis will review the incidence and hidden nature of periodontal disease, the anatomy of the gingival sulcus, and the clinical difference between pocket depth and attachment loss. She will also discuss radiographic assessment of periodontal staging and treatment planning, including closed versus open root planing and proper use of hand and ultrasonic instruments. An overview of anesthesia considerations and healing-focused, tooth-preserving therapies will reinforce how every team member can meaningfully contribute to successful patient outcomes, improving client trust, and overall practice success.

courses.title: Infection Control: New Thoughts on Old Ideas in Veterinary Surgery ON DEMAND
courses.description:
Surgical site infections (SSIs) continue to impact patient outcomes, client satisfaction, and practice efficiency in veterinary medicine. This evidence-based webinar reviews foundational infection control principles alongside emerging insights into antimicrobial resistance, biofilm formation, and perioperative protocols.
Participants will explore risk factors associated with SSIs, evaluate current aseptic and sterilization techniques, and identify practical strategies to improve infection prevention. Emphasis will be placed on antimicrobial stewardship, patient preparation, surgical environment management, and postoperative care.
This session is designed to provide actionable recommendations that veterinary teams can implement immediately to enhance patient safety and surgical outcomes.

courses.title: The 41st Muller-Ihrke-Kwochka Veterinary Dermatology Seminar, The 26th Veterinary MEDicine Seminar & The JOINT Meeting
courses.description: VETS presents 13.5 CE Units in Dermatology from Board Certified DVMs and 13.5 CE Units in Internal Medicine (also Board Certified DVMs)-- this year with an emphasis on Brachycephalic Issues, Small Animal Ophthalmology and Diseases and Aging of the Cat. Attendees may choose the Dermatology Track or the MEDicine Track or BOTH-- which is what we call The JOINT Meeting.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Hoof and Skin Conditions
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage hoof and skin conditions in the field.

courses.title: PURRfecting the Feline Exam: Expert Tips for Smooth and Successful Visits
courses.description: Join us for an insightful session with Dr. Margaret Gruen, where she will share valuable tips, tools, and strategies to improve feline veterinary visits. This program will emphasize the vital role of all practice team members in ensuring a positive experience for both cats and their owners.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Management of Feline Lower Urinary Tract Diseases
courses.description: This webinar will describe common lower urinary tract diseases in cats including stones and idiopathic cystitis, discuss diagnosis including common mistakes, and cover management focusing on nutrition.

courses.title: Right Size, Right Species: the Role of Compounding Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Is your clinic compliant with recent legal changes? In this one-hour video course, we breakdown regulations and best practices for medical compounding. Dr. Rae Hutchins, the first Chief Veterinary Officer for Wedgewood, guides us on partnering with compounding pharmacies to best suit your clinic and patient needs. Find out what new methods are available to make medicating a breeze for clients, and learn what new regulatory changes might affect your practice. This session won't leave a bad taste in your mouth!

courses.title: AI for Network and Cybersecurity: What Veterinary Practices Need to Know
courses.description:
Technology is changing quickly, and artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming part of everyday IT, especially when it comes to keeping networks and data secure. In this webinar, Baran from Schultz Technology will explain how AI is being used today to help protect veterinary practices from cyber threats and network issues.
This session is designed for veterinary practice managers who want to understand AI without confusing technical terms. We will focus on what AI actually does behind the scenes, how it helps catch problems faster, and where human oversight is still critical. Attendees will walk away with a clear, practical understanding of how AI fits into modern network and cybersecurity and what questions they should be asking their IT partner.

courses.title: Dental and Oral Care Impacting Quality of Life ON- DEMAND
courses.description: Once a patient enters the hospice/compassion care realm, the chance for appropriate oral and dental care with general anesthesia may no longer be an option, or at least a risky one. That is why it is critical to provide good oral care and procedures to our senior pets prior to this stage whenever possible. In fact, by removing the inflammation of chronic dental disease, the quality of life and healthspan of these patients can be maximized and help make these final stages more comfortable.

courses.title: MasterClass Objective Gait Analysis From Technology to Clinical Application
courses.description:
Objective gait analysis is transforming how equine clinicians assess lameness, monitor performance, and guide rehabilitation strategies. This series provides a comprehensive introduction to the different technologies, interpretation, and real-world application of systems such as Sleip, Equinosis Q, Lameness Locator, EquiMoves, Consteed and many more...
The carefully curated sessions will benefit a wide audience from equine practitioners new to gait analysis, maybe currently considering which system to purchase, to those looking to critically evaluate and refine their use of these invaluable tools.
The Program
This threepart online series has been designed to give you a solid understanding of objective gait analysis and its role in modern equine practice
Foundations and Frameworks
Explore the principles behind objective gait analysis, from inertial sensors force plates motion capture to AI based, and compare the leading systems to understand how they work and where they fit into practice.
Systems in Practice SidebySide Comparison
Learn how to confidently apply objective gait analysis in real-world settings including interpreting the data, responses to diagnostic anaesthesia, and recognising normal variations or conflicting results.
Clinical Applications and Future Directions
Go beyond lameness diagnosis to see how objective data supports pre purchase examination performance monitoring fitness to compete decisions and rehabilitation. Ethical challenges like subclinical asymmetries, over reliance on numbers and managing client expectations will be discussed and debated.
A Unique Interactive Format
Each module is designed in VetPDs signature format to transform your clinical practice and gain actionable skills:
Two to three leading specialists with complimentary experience, acting as both speaker and discussant
The latest evidence based information, followed by discussion of real cases
Friendly and dynamic environment where speakers explore the topic honestly, not shyin

courses.title: Tailoring Treatment: Implementing Genetics in Small Animal Practice
courses.description: Genetic screening has gained prominence in veterinary medicine for dogs and cats, offering insights into health, breed predispositions, and traits. These powerful tools have the potential to improve the quality of care delivered by veterinary professionals. To harness the full potential of genetic testing in practice, it is important to grasp essential genetic terminology and concepts. Additionally, proficiency in interpreting test results, integrating genetic insights into clinical care, and effectively communicating findings to clients is crucial. This presentation is designed to equip veterinary clinicians with the skills and knowledge needed to confidently utilize genetic tools and engage in productive conversations with pet owners. Through engaging case presentations and practical examples, attendees will gain experience in applying genetics to real-world scenarios, ultimately fostering a more personalized approach to veterinary care.

courses.title: DNM Therapeutic Nutrition for the Microbiome
courses.description:
Intestinal problems are one of the most common reasons dogs and cats are brought to their veterinarians and behavioral problems, like anxiety, are prevalent. Research has found that there is an influenceable connection between pet health and behavior and the gut microbiome.
The gut microbiome consists of both beneficial and potentially harmful microorganisms, such as bacteria, which affect energy balance, metabolism, intestinal cell turnover and behavior. An imbalance within the microbiome is associated with health and behavior related problems. Pets with intestinal upset often experience an imbalance of these bacteria, which can contribute to diarrhea, soft stools, or excessive gas. Chronic stress has been linked to gastrointestinal distress, predisposition to inflammatory bowel disease, suppression of the immune system, and may lead to increased incidences of integumentary diseases, and negatively impact the reproductive system.
This course explores what the gut microbiome is, why it is important, and how this microbiome affects pet health and pet behavior, such as anxiety.

courses.title: Fear Free Dermatology: Exams that won't make your patients' skin crawl
courses.description: Many small animal dermatology patients require long-term treatment for chronic diseases. The patient's fear of the veterinarian and the clients perception of distress during exams are barriers to clinical success, impeding the clinician's ability to evaluate lesions during difficult exams as well as lack of exams when clients forgo recheck visits. This discussion presents techniques and videos for maximizing your dermatologic and otoscopic exams and procedures, improving communication with clients, and minimizing the anxiety level of patients, clients, and staff alike.

courses.title: To Extract or Not to Extract...Radiographic Interpretation 2
courses.description: This lecture is intended to walk participants through understanding the signs of periodontal disease radiographically. Intraoral radiographs are an essential tool in providing appropriate care for our patients. This lecture reviews radiographic interpretation of periodontal disease and suggested treatment approaches. Participants should be able to appropriately interpret intraoral radiographs, recognize the signs of periodontal disease radiographically, and use their knowledge combined with a patient oral exam to provide an accurate plan for treatment.

courses.title: Understanding Aging in Dogs: From Principles to Practice
courses.description: This session connects geroscience and geriatrics, introducing the principles and underlying biology of canine aging, describing the key clinical impacts of this process, and discussing strategies for how to assess and manage geriatric canine patients and show to set up a senior care program for dogs in your practice.

courses.title: A New Look at Old Labs: Familiar Lab Values as Potential Indicators of Unhealthy Aging
courses.description: Many clinical lab values change with aging in dogs. When these changes aren't clearly linked to a specific disease, we often dismiss them as "normal aging." However, new research is suggesting that small changes in some of these values, even when still within the reference range, may be indicators of insidious processes that ultimately lead to clinical dysfunction and disease. Understanding these changes can help guide a preventive approach to aging that reduces the negative impact on health.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Comorbidities in Cats
courses.description:
Nutritional management is critical in managing feline disease conditions. The diets role in these nutrient sensitive conditions vary, as diet may be a primary intervention or hold a supportive management role. Cats presenting with multiple concurrent disease conditions exhibit an added degree of clinical complexity. These comorbidities frequently occur in senior feline patients, as multiple diseases demonstrate increased prevalence with advancing age in cats. These disease conditions include chronic kidney disease, joint disease, cognitive dysfunction, neoplasia, and endocrinopathies.
Selecting the most suitable diet for a feline patient involves thoroughly evaluating their nutritional needs, understanding the nutrients involved in managing disease conditions, and knowledge of nutritional profiles available in helping to manage the disease conditions.

courses.title: Clinical approach to chronic enteropathy in the dog
courses.description:
Chronic GI disease is common in dogs and can be a frustrating issue for both owners and veterinarians. This lecture will discuss updates from the recent ACVIM-endorsed guidelines on chronic inflammatory enteropathy in dogs. Attendees will develop an understanding of diagnostic testing and therapeutic trials for management of chronic
inflammatory enteropathy.

courses.title: Communication Principles
courses.description: This training is designed to equip veterinary professionals and leaders with foundational communication knowledge and skills to improve collaboration, team effectiveness, and workplace interactions within veterinary practice settings. Participants will review core communication principles, learn techniques to improve clarity and engagement, and explore strategies to strengthen professional communication in high-paced veterinary environments.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: Online Webinar: Guidelines for therapeutic drug use and residue avoidance in small ruminants
courses.description:
In the United States, there are fewer FDA-approved drugs for minor species (such
as sheep and goats) than for the major species so the small ruminant practitioner must be familiar with the
laws and regulations related to extra-label use in multiple species. This presentation will discuss the laws
and regulations around extra label drug use, clinical use of different therapeutics in small ruminants, with
a focus on commonly used antimicrobials, analgesic drugs and intramammary products. This presentation
will also discuss the importance of residue avoidance and how to get advice about a meat or milk
withdrawal interval from the Food Animal Residue Avoidance Databank Program.

courses.title: Navigating Parvovirus: Updates, Challenges, and Innovations
courses.description: This lecture will provide a comprehensive update on parvovirus, focusing on recent research, diagnostic advancements, and evolving treatment strategies in critical care settings. Topics will include epidemiological trends, emerging variants, novel therapeutic approaches, and the latest clinical guidelines for managing severe cases. Attendees will gain valuable insights into recognizing and treating parvoviral infections, particularly in immunocompromised patients and high-risk populations. Case studies and real-world applications will be discussed to enhance clinical decision-making and patient outcomes.

courses.title: DNM NUTRITION MYTHS & FACTS: Part 2
courses.description:
You've heard the adage, "A little knowledge can be a dangerous thing." This saying certainly applies to misinformation about pet nutrition, which often persists despite scientific information that disproves it. While nutrition myths may initially be based on facts, over time the accurate date becomes distorted with inaccuracies.
The Nutrition Myths & Facts Part 2 course continues from where Part 1 left off. In Part 2, we tackle myths about carbohydrates, gluten-free and grain-free diets, corn, soy and wheat, food allergens and pet food labels.

courses.title: DNM Feeding Cats
courses.description: Cats are not small dogs, they are carnivores not omnivores and they do not participate in rigorous activities, such as sled pulling or jogging. They have different feeding styles and unique dietary needs. We'll explore the unique nutritional requirements of cats and the importance of feeding cats in accordance with their life stage, lifestyle, and individual needs as these also affect ideal nutritional plans. Providing appropriate quantities of high-quality, easily digestible food can contribute to a cat's overall health and help prevent disease.

courses.title: Panel Discussion
courses.description:
Equine practitioners commonly encounter head trauma in horses, with many injuries being relatively benign. Some wounds or abrasions may at first glance appear to be trivial, but upon further investigation might turn out to be associated with damage to neurovascular structures, the orbit, the eye or with facial bone fractures.
Whilst ocular and orbital trauma will be the focus of another exchange, the international panel consisting of 4 internationally renowned equine surgeons with decades of experience with wound care and head trauma specifically, will be discussing soft tissue injuries and facial bone fractures. Which wounds should be closed and which best left open When should sinus lavage be considered? What are the best methods to reposition/repair facial bone fractures

courses.title: Tricks and Treats: Tasty Tales from the Palatable Pharmacy
courses.description: As the human-animal bond has evolved through time, so too has veterinary care and creative patient management. Among other practice evolutions, our veterinary pharmacies have grown to include a myriad of well targeted drugs in an array of formulations to accommodate ease of administration for our animal owners. Through a case-based approach, this presentation will discuss the toxicological consequences of palatable and flavored veterinary pharmaceutical overdoses. We'll more closely assess the consequences and management of flavored or chewable oclacitinib maleate (Apoquel), NSAID, antibiotic, phenylpropanolamine (PPA, Proin), and joint supplement overdose ingestions.

courses.title: Derm disasters got you down Let us talk about how to use multimodal therapy to increase your successes
courses.description: This anytime course covers in detail the diagnostic and treatment approaches to your complicated small animal dermatology cases.

courses.title: Senior Pet Con
courses.description: Senior Pet Con is the first event to bring the whole world of senior pet care together: pet parents and the veterinarians who care for their animals. It's virtual and runs across two days. Day One is built for pet parents, so they can learn from expert vets without leaving their pet's side. Day Two is continuing education for veterinarians so they can get better at caring for nearly half their patients without travel, cost, or missed time in clinic. It's led by Dr. Monica Tarantino, a senior dog veterinarian and co-founder of the Senior Dog Veterinary Society, and Adam Greenbaum, founder of WhiskerCloud and Love, Baxter. Nearly half the pets in this country are seniors. This is the event built for them.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Feline Hyperthyroidism - What's New in Diagnostics & Treatment
courses.description:
Hyperthyroidism is the most diagnosed feline endocrinopathy. In this engaging panel discussion, esteemed world-renowned experts will converge to share their invaluable insights, diverse perspectives, and evidence-based approaches regarding when and how to screen cats for this condition, pre-treatment evaluation, selection of an appropriate treatment modality, and considerations regarding long term follow-up for affected cats. Issues related to common comorbidities such as chronic kidney disease and inflammatory bowel disease will also be discussed and debated.
This illuminating panel discussion promises to equip attendees with a comprehensive understanding of feline hyperthyroidism diagnosis and management, empowering them to deliver optimal care and improve the quality of life for their feline patients. Join us as we unravel the complexities and chart the course towards better outcomes for these cats.

courses.title: Thoracic Radiographic Interpretation: A Review
courses.description: This course is composed of a series of modules covering normal and abnormal interpretation of canine and feline thoracic radiology. Objectives of this course include review and assimilation of normal and abnormal aspects of the pulmonary parenchyma, mediastinum, pleural space, body wall, and heart. After completing this course, the participant will develop more confidence and expertise in interpretation of daily patient thoracic radiographs. This is a Medical non-interactive distance online class.

courses.title: Panel Discussion
courses.description: An international panel of world-renowned equine reproductive and neonatal clinicians from all corners of the world will discuss both normal and abnormal findings and management of the postpartum mare and foal. Expert opinions will be shared and debated on topics including breeding management for the post-foaling mare, conditions that affect reproductive efficiency (and sometimes mortality!) of mares after foaling, as well as recognizing and managing routine and unusual conditions that afflict equine neonates. Participants will be encouraged to share their own experiences with the panel and contribute to a vibrant learning session.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Biosecurity in Equine Practice From the Farm and Event to the Hospital
courses.description:
Vaccination is key in reducing the risk of some equine infectious diseases, whilst equine veterinarians play a crucial role in protecting their patients from infectious diseases. The effectiveness of vaccination protocols can be significantly augmented with strategies to reduce the risk of exposure to disease agents through biosecurity practices. For some diseases there is a lack of effective vaccination tools and therefore biosecurity protocols are the most useful avenue for reducing the risk of exposure and disease caused by these agents. Biosecurity protocols rely on a combination of activities that reduce the overall risk of exposure of equids to infectious disease agents in various settings.
An international panel of world-renowned practicing equine veterinarians will provide an overview of the advances in biosecurity practices within the equine hospital setting as well as the role of the veterinarian in providing individualized biosecurity guidance to clients managing farms and equine events. The international panel will share many practically applicable tips and procedures, provide key lessons learned in developing and refining biosecurity protocols, investigating and resolving disease outbreaks and discuss opportunities for improving the level of biosecurity across the equine veterinary and equestrian sector worldwide.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Equine Procedure Avoidance Needle-Shyness, Loading Travel Medicating etc
courses.description: Join us for what promises to be an exciting panel discussion with an international panel of worldleading equine experts with extensive experience in equine behavior. This panel discussion will explore how we might make the lives of our clients staff and ourselves easier and safer as well as positively impacting equine welfare. Training horses is subject to many unqualified approaches and opinions. We are fortunate to have 3 of the worlds leading specialists and researchers who will offer their experiences opinions and evidence of how we should consider, prevent and approach tricky behavioral issues in horses. The focus will be on aversions to common healthcare procedures injections, clipping, eye medications etc and making horses more comfortable and accepting of veterinary care. Problems encountered with loading for transport will also be discussed. The research underlying recommended approaches will be covered as well as offering practical guidance when faced with such problematic situations. Our panelists will share tips and tricks and will welcome comments or questions from attending vets.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Sports Horse Pre Purchase Exam X Rays Foot Pastern Fetlock
courses.description:
Sport horse pre-purchase examinations are a difficult yet common component of equine practice. Radiograph interpretation is frequently involved in the overall pre-purchase examination. In veterinary medicine, strong guidelines on the significance and impact of various lesions are lacking and clinicians often rely on their own experience to make assessments regarding outcome. Join this panel discussion to see various different viewpoints on radiographs in the pre-purchase examination.
This exchange focusses on the following anatomic regions:
The Foot - P3, Navicular Bone, Collateral Cartilages & Hoof Conformation
Pastern Joint incl. subchondral defects of P1 / proximal P2
Fetlock - Proximal Sesamoid Bones
Cervical Spine

courses.title: Fear Free for Relief Vets
courses.description: This Certification Course is for Certified Professional veterinarians considering relief work and relief vets considering Fear Free certification who have an opportunity to positively impact the profession but also face unique challenges. Throughout this course, you will learn how to practice Fear Free as a relief vet and address different types of communication unique to this role. In addition to bringing Fear Free to general relief practice, we'll also cover some of the situations you may encounter in emergency or shelter relief practice. You'll also learn tips for identifying compassionate clinics who share your Fear Free philosophy

courses.title: Panel DiscussionNavigating Feline Conjunctivitis
courses.description: Although conjunctivitis is one of the most common clinical problems seen in cats worldwide, this condition continues to present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges for general practitioners and specialists alike. Navigating the aetiology of feline conjunctivitis can often be a complicated and frustrating process for both the cat owner and the veterinarian. Our panel of world-leading experts will share how they attempt to work out the aetiology of, and treatment course for, both acute and chronic inflammation of this vulnerable mucous membrane in their feline patients. Evidence-based, up-to-date information on diagnostic and medical advances will be presented and details debated.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Radiography at Yearling Sales What really matters
courses.description:
Interpretation of radiological findings at bloodstock sales can be a minefield for clinicians and may have a huge impact on the realised sale price of yearlings yet there is no rulebook and nobody gets it right all of the time. Beyond the science many factors feed into the final determination of relative importance of any given radiological blemish, including variables relating to horse, client, racing jurisdiction and clinician experience. What types of imperfections are most important, and for whom? What weight should be attributed to conformation physical exam and pedigree when viewing a defect What are the most appropriate ways to communicate findings in terms of risk? How should one approach quality control of radiographs, and when/how should additional projections be taken? Which are the most important projections
This panel discussion will draw on the experience of three highly respected vets on the international yearling sales circuit from Europe, North America and Australia. Covered topics will range from key pathologies including imaging nuances unusual cases, tricky situations and unexpected outcomes. Expect to learn far more than can be found in any textbook

courses.title: ( On Demand Webinar) Cat-astrophic Gut Feelings: Unraveling the Mysteries of the Feline Gastrointestinal Microbiome
courses.description: This lecture provides an exploration of the feline gastrointestinal microbiome, focusing on its composition, function, and impact on feline health. We will examine the latest research findings on the diversity and roles of microbial communities within the feline gut, highlighting their contributions to digestive processes, immune function, and overall well-being. We will discuss the implications of microbiome research for veterinary medicine, particularly in the context of dietary interventions and disease management. This lecture aims to offer an understanding of the feline gastrointestinal microbiome with the current state of knowledge, fostering a deeper appreciation for the complex interplay between host and microbial populations.

courses.title: Fear Free Certification Level 2
courses.description: The Level 2 course is designed for Fear Free Certified Professionals who are ready to take their knowledge to the next level. Modules in this course are a result of direct feedback we received from many of our professionals voicing their need for more in-depth education in the areas of patient handling, advanced handling techniques, in-hospital care, communications, marketing and finance. In addition to step by step procedures, the modules feature numerous videos detailing procedures, handling techniques and client communication examples.

courses.title: DNM Therapeutic Nutrition for Liver Disease
courses.description: This course will provide you with a basic understanding of acute and chronic liver diseases in dogs and cats, including clinical signs, key diagnostic tests and how it can be managed through medication, supportive care, and targeted nutrition.

courses.title: There is No Eye in Enucleation: A Review of Treatment Options for Blind, Painful Eyes
courses.description:
This presentation will review the various surgical options for eyes that are blind and painful.
Learning Objectives
1. When should you try to save an eye and when should you stop?
2. Signs and causes of ocular pain, causes of vision loss, and when they occur together.
3. Review of enucleation/exenteration
4. Review of ciliary body ablation
5. Review of ocular evisceration and intrascleral prosthesis placement

courses.title: Patient-Specific Care for Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Learn to offer a spectrum of evidence-based care and payment options that meet the standard of care. Help more clients accept treatment plans so their pets get care, our practices remain sustainable, and the care teams have less moral distress.

courses.title: Urinary And Kidney Pearls In The Caribbean
courses.description: This course covers kidney and urinary pathologies and treatment from the perspective of a double boarded internal medicine and nutrition specialist and boarded ECC specialist. This will be an interactive Medical presentation. Dr. Markovich will discuss kidney disease, feline lower urinary tract disease, inappetence, proteinuria/hypertension, and enteral feeding. Dr. Mauro will discuss acute kidney injury, urinary obstruction in cats, reproductive emergencies, and neonatal emergencies.

courses.title: Comprehensive Oral Health Assessment and Treatment
courses.description: A complete oral examination including dental probing and charting is the most important part of a dental procedure. It is more than just cleaning teeth. This class explains instrument handling, the importance of proper cleaning technique, probing and charting. A detailed, wet lab provides instruction on the proper way to do a complete dental prophylaxis and oral examination including correct charting. Learn how to properly and safely handle dental instruments to perform supragingival and subgingival hand scaling to remove plaque and calculus, polishing, and irrigation.

courses.title: #5 COMMIT TO CARE: SOCIAL NETWORKING (155-42215)
courses.description: #5 COMMIT TO CARE: SOCIAL NETWORKING (155-42215) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Managing common behavioral problems in practice
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian/technician with practical information on the current thoughts on diagnosis and management of common canine and feline behavioral problems that they encounter in their daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of diagnosis and management available for their patients.

courses.title: Canine Ocular Emergencies
courses.description: "Canine Ocular Emergencies" will cater to primary care and emergency veterinarians in their evaluations of and management of ocular conditions seen in dogs. It will help to guide them in terms of parsing out what constitutes an ocular emergency versus an urgent ophthalmic case. A quick recap of an ophthalmic evaluation and minimum database testing will be discussed, followed by a series of the most frequent and pertinent types of emergencies seen in practice. This will include medical management, alleviating procedures and surgical intervention. In addition, a major goal of this presentation will be to cover what can be addressed in clinic versus what needs to be referred to an ophthalmologist on an emergent basis for evaluation.

courses.provider: INTERNATIONAL SYMPOSIUM ON EQUINE REPRODUCTION TRUST
courses.title: West Coast Equine Reproduction Symposium (WCERS-VII) - Wet-Labs
courses.description:
The West Coast Equine Reproduction Symposium is a continuing educational event for veterinarians. The meeting has been held once every 4 years since 2001 in Solvang, CA. Speakers at the symposium are amongst the world leaders in the field of equine reproduction, with a majority of speakers Board Certified in either the American College of Theriogenologists, European College of Animal Reproduction, or both Colleges. The symposium also serves as an important fund-raising event for the International Symposium on Equine Reproduction (ISER), which will be held in Dublin, Ireland, in July of 2027. The WCERS VI will be an in-person meeting with two days of lectures and one day of wet-lab.
For the Wet labs, there are three hands-on modules; each participant can choose one module. Module 1 - General Stud Farm Pregnant mare ultrasound fetal evaluation and sexing Hands on transabdominal ultrasonography with rectal demo in mid-gestation mares; identification of viability parameters (heartbeat, bone maturity, placental thickness) and fetal sexing Foal resuscitation dummy and placental examination Protocols for neonatal airway management, ventilation and chest compressions on a mannequin; systematic gross placental exam of frozen samples Cytology and culture prep biopsy interpretation Collection of uterine samples; on-farm Gram and Diff-Quik smears; plating for bacterial culture; interpretation of inflammatory versus infectious findings Semen evaluation Manual assessment of motility, concentration and morphology; extender preparation; use of the VetMotl microfluidics device Module 2 - OPU TVA IVP Equipment and media set up Assembly and priming of transvaginal aspiration systems; comparison of available platforms; checklist preparation for aseptic oocyte collection TVA demonstration on full reproductive tracts and ovum pick-up under ultrasound guidance; discussion of techniques to optimize oocyte recovery and minimize contamination Oocyte search and packing Filtration of aspiratio

courses.title: Multimodal Pain Management
courses.description: Discussion based lecture on pain physiology and pathophysiology. We will discuss both pharmacological intervention and non-pharmacologic modalities for pain.

courses.title: AAEP XP Series: DentistryXP (TX)
courses.description: This intensive two-day program provides equine practitioners with practical, clinically focused training in the diagnosis and management of neurologic disease in horses. Through a combination of preparatory materials, targeted lectures, interactive case discussions, and extensive hands-on laboratory sessions, participants develop a structured approach to neurologic examination, neurolocalization, diagnostic planning, and treatment decision-making. Learning will include foundational concepts, diagnostic interpretation, and hands-on skills using live horses, cadavers, and imaging modalities with advanced case-based discussions, procedural training, and real-world clinical scenarios, including client communication and risk management. Small-group laboratories and expert faculty guidance ensure individualized instruction and immediate clinical applicability, enabling participants to confidently assess, diagnose, and manage complex equine neurologic cases in practice.

courses.title: From Pregnancy to Lactation: Understanding the Transition Cow Challenge (LAMS304)
courses.description: Postpartum disease conditions continue to be the scourge of the dairy industry. Research to identify pathophysiology, risk factors, and methods of disease prevention for the cow transitioning from pregnancy into lactation has been ongoing for more than five decades, with only moderate successes. Part of the transition cow challenge is the complex interaction among nutrition, animal management, and environment, or what we can term the transition challenge triad, and how this impacts animal physiology, health, and performance. This course will provide a detailed discussion of cow physiology and metabolism as it is impacted by the transition challenge triad to better understand fundamental concepts of postpartum disease pathogenesis and their prevention. Information presented will assume some foundational understanding of dairy cattle physiology, nutrition, and management. Participants successfully completing the course should be capable of providing comprehensive suggestions to their clients for improving herd performance.

courses.title: Own Your Mentorship Experience
courses.description: Mentorship is a relationship and requires the input of both mentor and mentee for success. If you want a great mentoring experience, you need to become an active participant in the process. In this session, we will review the skills you need to be an effective mentee and empower you to advocate for your needs as a mentee, set goals for your development, and learn how to leverage relationships with both your in-clinic mentor, your clinical team, and your external mentor to make your first year in practice the best it can be.

courses.title: Veterinary Drug Diversion: Protecting Patients, Staff, and Your Practice
courses.description: Veterinary drug diversion is a growing concern that threatens patient safety, staff well-being, and the integrity of veterinary practices. This session will explore the scope of the problem, including in-hospital diversion and client-driven vet shopping. Attendees will learn how to recognize red flags, identify common diversion methods, and implement effective prevention strategies. We'll cover regulatory requirements, reporting obligations, and practical steps for investigating suspected diversion. Through real-world case examples and actionable tips, this webinar will empower veterinary professionals to protect controlled substances, maintain compliance, and foster a culture of accountability and safety.

courses.title: Managing common feline problems.
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage the feline patient who are presented to their clinic with a variety of clinical problems. The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the three specialists.

courses.title: Disseminated Idiopathic Myofasciitis (DIM) in a Ferret
courses.description: This course covers clinical signs, diagnosis, and treatment of Disseminated Idiopathic Myofasciitis (DIM) in ferrets. We will discuss the case of an individual ferret diagnosed with DIM, including a detailed description of history reported by the owner, physical exam findings, blood work results, supportive care treatments and specific treatment of DIM.

courses.provider: PACIFIC NORTHWEST PET ER & SPECIALTY CENTER
courses.title: When It Hits the Fan: stabilizing ECC cases in the primary care setting
courses.description: A case-based discussion on common emergency situations that may present to the primary care provider. The focus of discussion will be on early goal directed therapy to aid in patient stabilization prior to transfer or prior to further treatment in clinic. Pathophysiology of shock states, the value and interpretation of different diagnostic and monitoring capabilities, and multimodal stabilization will be discussed for various emergency cases. Recommended discussion points for owners to ensure institution of best care for pet and family will also be discussed.

courses.title: Hoof Care Clinic | Split-Shoe Approach | Education & Demonstration
courses.description:
This clinic will educate and familiarize the attendees with how to gain all the benefits of a barefoot hoof while still achieving the protection, installation ease, and low cost of traditional nail-on steel horseshoes.
The importance of providing the horse with as much natural hoof mechanism flexibility as possible will be accomplished through highlighting five critical factors driving healthy hooves (Hoof Mechanism, Blood Circulation, Hoof Growth/Quality/Shape, Shock Absorption, and Biomechanics).
Attendees will gain firsthand knowledge of real-world split-shoe usage through a live-horse demonstration. The practical, interactive demonstration will cover recommended hoof mapping, trimming, shoe fitting, nailing, and final splitting techniques.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Dental Disease
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to nutritionally manage dental disease cases in the field.

courses.title: Management of Seizures in Dogs
courses.description: This webinar will provide an evidence-based discussion of current concepts in the management of epilepsy in dogs. Topics to be discussed include updates to epilepsy terminology, principles of treatment (focused on both maintenance therapy and emergency treatment), and drug resistance.

courses.title: Shifting from Survival: Nervous System Health for Animal Care Professionals
courses.description: This course provides animal care professionals with essential knowledge and practical tools to support nervous system health and sustainable wellbeing in high-stress, trauma-exposed environments. Recognizing that survival mode is a protective response to the realities of this work, not a personal failing, participants will learn how chronic stress and trauma shape the body, emotions, and behaviours. They will explore somatic awareness, grounding techniques, and simple, effective practices to help restore internal safety, foster connection with themselves and others, and support their wellbeing to sustain their purpose-driven work.

courses.title: Managing common medical problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with common medical problems The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common urinary & gastrointestinal problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Use Technicians as Physician Assistants
courses.description: Despite signing bonuses, student-loan payoff assistance, shortened workweeks, and enticing salaries, private and corporate practice owners are grappling to hire associate veterinarians. Just as physician assistants are fulfilling the gap in human healthcare, veterinarians should consider the same strategy. Learn how to leverage technicians and assistants to work at the top of their licenses and skillsets. Find out how to charge for technician appointments and show value to clients.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Investigation of the sub Fertile Mare
courses.description:
Most horses are fertile however, approximately 10-15% of mares can be classified as sub-fertile, and establishing and maintaining pregnancy in these animals can be challenging and frustrating.
Although there are many potential causes of subfertility, the various forms of endometritis are among the most common. Fortunately, in recent years several novel diagnostic procedures and treatments have been developed to aid detection, prevention and resolution of the different forms of endometritis. However, it can be difficult to determine which of the available tests or treatments are the most appropriate in a specific clinical situation.
Suring this panel discussion, our team of international experts will help you decide which tests and/or preparatory treatments are most appropriate for diagnosing infectious and chronic degenerative endometritis, and what to bear in mind when translating the results of the diagnostic tests into a treatment plan or breeding soundness advice. The panel will outline their decision-making process when selecting interventions that may help to prevent, ameliorate, treat or resolve the various forms of endometritis, and what to do next should the chosen treatment plan fail.

courses.title: On Demand: Widening the Lens: A Broader Understanding of OA-Associated Pain
courses.description: In this video session, we will explore the quiet epidemic of feline OA pain, uncovering the complexity of OA pain and its impact beyond the joint. Feline OA pain is a common and often underdiagnosed condition. The signs are often hidden, making diagnosis challenging.
