Cats being cats, are cryptic with showing overt signs of pain, which can complicate diagnosis and management of this debilitating disease. Innovations in veterinary medicine have led to the development of screening tools and new treatments to effectively control feline OA pain. Explore why cats tend to hide their pain and discuss the significance of early diagnosis and intervention.

courses.title: Clinical Dentistry Lab for Veterinarians - Day 2
courses.description: Clinical Dentistry Lab for Veterinarians Day 2 will provide extended training in dental radiograph interpretation and applied oral surgery in cats and dogs

courses.title: Small Animal MRI: Level 1
courses.description: This class is designed for the student to be able to recognize and consistently scan the small animal patient in an MRI environment using the safest and most diagnostic means possible. They will be able to understand the pathology they are looking for, properly position the patient for top diagnostic results, image the patient safely, and create diagnostic image in the environment of an MRI scanner. This is a Medical Class in a Wetlab format. 8 CE

courses.title: 2025 Academy of Veterinary Consultants Summer Conference
courses.description:
This course includes the following: Introduction to Huvepharmas commitment to portfolio development investing in a Vaccination Program for
Lifelong Immunity-Dr. Jeff Hall Phenotypic and genetic characterization of Bovine Congestive Heart Failure in beef and beef x dairy cattle Topic Description - Presentation of our current knowledge of both the genetic and phenotypic characteristics of bovine congestive heart failure. - Dr. Scott Speidel
Vaccination and resistance to BRD: What the heck are we doing?
Topic Description - This presentation will review current
evidence regarding bovine immune responses that are
related to health in feedlot and stocker cattle, and whether
vaccination against BRD agents affects these responses.
- Dr. Amelia Woolums Outcomes of Liver Abscesses -Topic Description - Identifying the harvest floor and carcass outcomes associated with the liver abscess
condition in fed cattle - Dr. Dale Woerner Liver Abscesses in Cattle: Anything new on the etiology and pathogenesis? Topic Description - Sharing recent research on the bacteriology of liver abscesses and source of the bacterial pathogens - Dr. TG Nagaraja Equine Lameness for the Feedlot Veterinarian Topic Description - Equine Lameness for the Feedlot Veterinarian - Dr. Joe Carter A retrospective evaluation of feedlot mortality using a closeout database Topic Description - A feedlot closeout database was utilized to evaluate mortality trends and explore correlations with an array of factors to identify opportunities for mitigation strategies or guide the development of research programs to reduce mortality going forward - Dr. Jacob Hagenmaier Evolution of Yield Grade and Red Meat Yield Topic Description - Will discuss the current progress being made towards replacing USDA Yield Grade with improved
measures of red meat yield - Dr. Dale Woerner
Evaluation of 3-, 6-, and 9-day post-treatment intervals following pradofloxacin for treatment of bovine respiratory disease in stocker cattle Topic Descrip

courses.title: Advanced SUB placement Lecture & Wet Lab
courses.description: This 3 hour lecture will describe in detail how to diagnose feline ureteral obstruction, stabilise, treat and provide post-operative care, follow-ups and troubleshooting complications following SUB placement. Following the lecture, a 3 hour hands-on lab will provide training in fluoroscopic and ultrasound-guided SUB placement and SUB flusing on cadavres. Small groups and one-on-one training will be provided. This workshop will put theory into practise

courses.title: How to Drive In-Clinic Pharmacy Sales
courses.description: Your team spends three hours a day processing prescription requests from third-party pharmacies. The task robs revenue from your practice and puts stress on your overworked and short-staffed team. Up to 30% of hospital revenue comes from your pharmacy. Your staff needs to lead clients to buy medications from you. Find out how to do it.

courses.title: Compassionate Communication - ON DEMAND
courses.description:
As veterinarians, we have two parties to serve in almost all areas of our profession; first, the owner/client, and second, the patient. Our clients serve as proxy for their pet's wishes in almost every interaction they have with a veterinarian. Legally, the clients are in fact owners of the patient and our communication and established rapport with that owner is imperative if we are to gain the trust such that our medical knowledge will be used for the betterment of the pet and/or the treatment of a disease. Learning how to gain that rapport is where the rubber meets the road!
In this program, tips on how to start a difficult conversation about a serious diagnosis, or euthanasia will be discussed; this includes engaging with the owner(s), gaining trust and rapport, verbal priming, supporting the owner/family, understanding the difference between
empathy and sympathy, focusing on the pet's needs and being non-judgmental. Owners may direct their grief and anger at you, and it is important to interpret this correctly and redirect the conversation.
Much attention is placed on non-verbal communication, and rightly so. By unknowingly appearing disinterested, forceful, or unsure of yourself in the exam room you are giving up your position of influence and losing ground with your client. The way you walk into the room, hold the patient's chart, and shake the client's hand may determine compliance before you even speak. The way you address an unconvinced, impatient, or unresponsive client may determine if the lifesaving surgery you recommend will be performed. In this talk, we will illustrate various aspects of nonverbal communication that may occur within the practice of veterinary medicine. Being aware of these unspoken subtleties can offer a clinician the chance to discern, confirm, then reshape the attitude a client may be feeling without putting the change into words.

courses.title: From Science to Practice: Integrating Hypochlorous Acid in Veterinary Care
courses.description: This program describes hypochlorous acid, a powerful and safe disinfectant with broad-spectrum antimicrobial properties often used in wound care, infection control, and various applications in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: Shake It Off. Shake It Off! Toxic Effects from Topical Flea and Tick Products
courses.description: This lecture will focus on topical flea and tick products in both dogs and cats. Early in the lecture a focus will be made on how to differentiate paresthesia from true neurologic disease after application of permethrin and etofenprox in both dogs and cats using case examples and quizzes to encourage participation. Further case examples will be used for discussions involving the list of active ingredients in the learning objectives below. The discussion will be case based and include clinical signs, exam findings, if radiographs of flea and tick collars are helpful and treatment recommendations including a conversation of using intravenous intralipids in feline patients exposed to canine pyrethrin containing topicals.

courses.title: New Tricks for the Diagnosis and Treatment of CHF in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: This webinar will discuss newer diagnostic and treatment options for canine and feline congestive heart failure. Diagnostic options will focus on combining the use of newer point-of-care tests with traditional imaging modalities to increase diagnostic confidence. Current treatment options will be discussed, including newer drugs for more challenging CHF cases.

courses.title: The Hidden Cost of Masking: Neurodiversity, Mental Health, and Being Unseen LIVE
courses.description: Veterinary professionals are often expected to be calm under pressure, highly capable, emotionally resilient and endlessly adaptable. But for many neurodivergent individuals, meeting these expectations can require a tremendous amount of invisible effort through masking. Masking can help people stay employed, avoid judgment, and feel safer in environments that were not built with their needs in mind. Over time, though, masking can come at a significant cost. This CE webinar explores why neurodivergent professionals feel forced to hide their true selves, how this obscures mental health struggles, and how we can redesign our teams to be truly supportive, safe spaces where everyone can thrive without pretending. The program is especially relevant in the context of suicide prevention and awareness.

courses.title: Introduction to Veterinary Hospice - ON DEMAND
courses.description: This course is designed to help provide an overview of veterinary hospice - what it is and what it is not. It will set the stage for doctors to be able to enter the home confidently prepared to help families navigate this sensitive season of their pets' lives. The course will provide an overview of palliative and comfort care and stress the importance of performing a thorough observational exam. It will also start the conversation on what measures can be taken to help improve overall quality of life for those owners no longer seeking diagnostics and curative measures.

courses.title: Endoscopy CE training program
courses.description: Provide endoscopy training to veterinarians and their veterinary technical staff. This training will be done on-site at a Veterinary Hospital for hands-on training with actual patients. The course will cover the use of a gastroscope, otoscope, rhinoscope and their respective accompaniments. The course will cover the most common endoscopy procedures, recommended maintenance and troubleshooting.

courses.provider: VETERINARY URGENT CARE OF THE DESERT
courses.title: Taking TIME for wound management; applying the TIME concepts to improve your wound management
courses.description: A review of the pathophysiology of wounds and wound healing. Introduction and instruction on the utilization of the TIME acronym for wound categorization based on the wound bed preparation concept. Decision making regarding primary vs delayed primary vs secondary closure. Wound management in the acute and subacute phases. Hypochlorous acid usage in wound management, how it works, and the evidence behind its usage.

courses.title: From Early Care to Lifelong Health: Diarrhea Management in Puppies and Kittens (MFRT2026 On Demand)
courses.description:
This Microbiome Forum Round Table brings together panelists with expertise in veterinary nutrition, gastroenterology, dermatology, microbiome science, and clinical case management to discuss the lifelong impacts of early-life gastrointestinal disease in puppies and kittens. The pathophysiology of relevant diseases will be discussed with the lens of gastrointestinal and microbiome health, as well as the evidence supporting the role of early-life experiences on the development of chronic disease in adulthood. Panelists will discuss how these early-life conditions should be addressed to mitigate the risk of later-life conditions such as chronic enteropathy and atopic dermatitis.
In accordance with Purina Institute policies, this presentation does not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: Insightful.vet 2024
courses.description: Insightful.vet brings together practice owners in an intimate setting where they can connect, learn, and apply new knowledge to help their hospitals achieve their vision of success.

courses.title: Purina Dairy Enterprise Veterinarian Conference 2025
courses.description: Purina Dairy Enterprise Veterinarian Conference 2025 is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Oral Anatomy and Terminology
courses.description: The first step to providing proper dental care to our patients is learning to identify normal oral anatomy and terminology. This lecture describes the normal oral, skull, and tooth anatomy. We need to be able to determine what healthy periodontium is, know the number of tooth roots, and the normal structure of the head and mouth are. Using the Triadan tooth numbering system and directional terminology of the mouth will help you to be able to perform more efficient dental charting. This lecture includes an introduction to charting and preparing for the dental cleaning. One will learn proper terminology and charting techniques along with being comfortable with the anatomy of the mouth, skull, and teeth.

courses.title: Advances in vaccine technology - pioneering a preventive for Valley Fever in dogs (On Demand)
courses.description: Coccidioidomycosis, also known as "Valley Fever," is a systemic fungal disease caused by the Coccidioides spp. soil fungi, C. posadasii and C. immitis. Coccidioidomycosis causes a great deal of morbidity and mortality in affected patients and can also infect humans. To date, the only available prevention for this disease is avoidance of endemic areas. Progress is being made towards development of a viable systemic vaccine against Coccidioides spp. in the dog. In this program, we will review the increasing geographic spread of Valley Fever, our current understanding of the protective host immune response to Coccidioides spp. infection and review scientific studies leading us towards a potential vaccine to prevent the disease in dogs.

courses.title: The New Calcium Tartrate Tetrahydrate Stone and Updates on Struvite and Calcium Oxalate
courses.description: The emergence of calcium tartrate tetrahydrate uroliths has introduced a new layer of complexity to the diagnosis and management of urinary stone disease in dogs. This session will explore the origin of tartaric acid within the body, why its presence can become clinically significant, and the current treatment options available for managing calcium tartrate-associated disease. In addition, the lecture will provide practical updates on struvite and calcium oxalate urolithiasis, with particular attention to the clinical implications of identifying calcium oxalate stones in young dogs. Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of this evolving urolith landscape and the decision-making considerations needed in everyday practice.

courses.title: Management of Glaucoma
courses.description: This lecture, titled "Management of Glaucoma," provides an overview of glaucoma, including its different types (primary and secondary) and the effects of high intraocular pressure (IOP) on the eye. It covers both medical and surgical treatment options, including medications to lower IOP and procedures like gonioimplants, laser therapy, and enucleation, with guidance on case selection. The lecture also emphasizes practical tips for diagnosing glaucoma, managing treatment plans, and improving client communication to ensure the best outcomes for patients.

courses.title: Abdominal Ultrasound Techniques of the Veterinary Patient
courses.description: This on-site hands-on abdominal ultrasound instruction is given to veterinarians and/or technicians providing the information and technical ultrasound skills to acquire images for diagnostics. At the end of the presentation the participant should be able to recognize the value of the ultrasound as a complement diagnostic imaging tool and will be able to recognize major organs within the abdominal cavity.

courses.title: On Demand: Taste of Science
courses.description: Taste is an important element of pet nutrition as a food that isnt enjoyed by dogs and cats will not be eaten willingly and therefore not be effective. Hills conducts extensive research into what tastes good to dogs and cats and has identified several key factors to making pet foods taste good.

courses.title: JPS? TPO? FHO? THR??? Hip Dysplasia Surgeries Demystified
courses.description: There are numerous surgical options for managing hip dysplasia including juvenile pubic symphysiodesis (JPS), triple or double pelvic osteotomy (TPO/DPO), femoral head and neck ostectomy (FHO), and total hip replacement (THR). Even if the practitioner is not performing these surgeries, the decision for when these procedures may be recommended is difficult to navigate. JPS and TPO are time- and disease stage sensitive procedures that could be relatively less expensive options to mitigate a lifetime of hip OA management. This session will cover the main indications and ideal timing of each of these procedures.

courses.title: Evaluation of Pet Crematories
courses.description:
Many pet families look to their veterinarian for trusted guidance for pet aftercare. Many families choose cremation for their cherished pets. Since most all veterinarians utilize and contract with a third-party/wholesale pet crematory, it is very important for veterinarians to know how to evaluate a trustworthy pet crematory that operates ethically and with integrity to protect consumer confidence, practice reputation, and to help avoid possible litigation. There is no government oversite of pet crematories unlike human crematories. Anyone can purchase a cremation retort, apply for a business license, and set up for business.
Due to lack of oversite and adverse experiences, pet families are becoming more enlightened about the unscrupulous practices of pet crematories. Veterinarians can no longer afford to do business as usual. Pets are very important family members and as pet families are learning that sometimes the cremains they have been given may not be of their actual pet or with other pet cremains, they are severely emotionally traumatized. Now court cases are appearing where pet families are suing veterinarians similar to the human crematory business, even with the human crematories being heavily regulated and inspected by government officials regularly. How can veterinarians protect themselves?
This course is intended to allow veterinarians not to just learn about a tool to evaluate a pet crematory, but more that is involved instead of just going through the paces afterwards when a pet is euthanized. To realize the associated emotion of pet families. The course learning objectives may be presented as an in-person workshop, keynote address, or online.
About the Presenter: Dr. Ruth Ann Wood-Humiston, licensed funeral director for over 30 years, certified pet funeral director, certified pet bereavement specialist, NFDA certified crematory operator, second-generation owner of a human funeral home and crematory, founder and owner of a full-service pet funeral home

courses.title: Urgent care medicine
courses.description: In this seminar, Dr.s Wininger and Hackett will present a complete discussion of the common urgent clinical problems that they encounter in their individual practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of the problems. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common problems requiring urgent care management. The two specialists will bring case examples highlighting the triage, stabilization and management of these dynamic and challenging cases.

courses.provider: DBA VETERINARY DENTISTRY EDUCATION AND CONSULTING SERVICES
courses.title: Veterinary Dentistry for Technicians and Veterinarians
courses.description: This 8-hour CE course (4 hours of lecture and 4 hours of laboratory) is for technicians and veterinarians and is designed for technical aspects of veterinary dentistry in the dog and cat. It is instructed by two Board Certified Veterinary Dentists. The 4-hour didactic course curriculum will start with canine and feline nomenclature and examination, periodontal probing, and dental charting for medicolegal documentation. Intraoral dental radiology for anatomy and common pathology will be presented. Regional nerve blocks for analgesia will be presented. Dental operatory and equipment maintenance, sharpening, and care will be present. Periodontal disease and complete periodontal cleaning will be presented. The laboratory portion will be hands on wet lab (canine cadavers and teaching models) with regional nerve block administration, intraoral radiographic positioning, surgical extraction of teeth with mucoperiosteal flaps, and subgingival crown amputation with intentional root retention. The course will provide canine and feline dentistry education and skills for primary care veterinary practice.

courses.title: Periodontal Disease Review
courses.description: This will be a 1 hour lecture to veterinarians with an emphasis on periodontal disease diagnosis and treatments in dogs and cats. We will review current theory and also discuss new treatments available.

courses.title: Certificate of Revenue Recovery & Medical Collections Proficiency (CRRMCP)
courses.description:
The Certificate of Revenue Recovery & Medical Collections Proficiency program is
designed to navigate the critical intersection of compassionate veterinary care and financial sustainability. This course will guide you through the entire veterinary revenue cycle, from establishing ethical legal frameworks and proactive financial policies to mastering the psychology of client financial conversations. We will equip you with structured internal workflows for managing overdue accounts, including effective communication, negotiation strategies, and de-escalation tactics. You will also learn the necessary criteria for escalating accounts, how to partner with external agencies, and the fundamentals of small claims court. Throughout this journey, you will develop the skills to create transparent, empathetic, and effective financial processes that protect your practice's health. By the end of this course, you will be able to implement a robust revenue recovery strategy that strengthens client relationships and secures your clinic's financial future.

courses.title: Emotionally Intelligent Euthanasia
courses.description: Emotionally Intelligent Euthanasia (EIE) is born of the idea that maintaining personal control of emotions is beneficial to one's mental health and well-being. It is useful to understand what we are feeling during euthanasia and what other around us are experiencing. Such knowledge guides our communication with pet owners and makes end-of-life work much more enjoyable and fulfilling. This lecture explores concepts like self-awareness, social skills, and empathy to build lasting EIE. Ideal for students, those new to veterinary medicine, and those who may be feeling dissatisfied with euthanasia-related work.

courses.title: Nutrition News 2024
courses.description: This course provides an overview of equine nutrition research from 2024. The goal of this presentation is to provide equine veterinarians with up-to-date information on equine nutrition that is applicable to veterinary practice.

courses.title: Bridging the Gap Between Practice Owner and Buyer Expectations
courses.description: Bridging the Gap Between Buyer and Seller Expectations explores the realities behind veterinary practice valuations and why buyer and seller expectations do not always align. This presentation examines the differences between Fair Market Value and corporate value models, along with the expectations and capabilities of individual buyers compared to corporate consolidators. Attendees will learn what truly drives a practice's salability and desirability, from location and services offered to quality of medicine and operational structure. Practice owners will gain actionable strategies to strengthen their position and maximize value at the time of ownership transition while prospective buyers will learn how to navigate common acquisition challenges and position themselves for success.

courses.title: The Purr-fect Balance of Nutrition and Weight Management in Cats
courses.description: Feline obesity is a common and preventable nutritional disorders in veterinary medicine. This lecture will provide an overview of the pathophysiology of obesity, emphasizing the metabolic, hormonal, and behavioral factors that contribute to excessive weight gain. This presentation will review the nutritional requirements and formulation principles underlying effective feline weight loss strategies, including caloric restriction, macronutrient balance, and satiety management. The session will also examine commercially available therapeutic diets, highlighting their key nutritional features, indications, and clinical outcomes. By integrating physiological understanding with practical dietary planning, participants will be equipped to develop individualized and sustainable weight management programs for feline patients.

courses.title: Hill's 2025 State of Shelter Pet Adoption Report: Trends and Opportunities ON-DEMAND
courses.description: This 1-hour webinar will provide an overview of insights from Hill's 2025 State of Shelter Pet Adoption Report. The session will explore current trends and opportunities in animal sheltering, discuss challenges facing shelter professionals, and touch on innovative approaches being adopted across the industry. The program is designed for veterinary professionals and others interested in the landscape of shelter pet adoption. A portion of the session will be dedicated to participant questions and discussion.

courses.title: PETLOSS PARTNERS PET LOSS BEREAVEMENT SPECIALIST CERTIFICATION COURSE (1459-38405)
courses.description:
This 10- week online course is designed for veterinarians and their staff to have the knowledge necessary to support clients going through anticipatory bereavement or those who have lost a beloved pet.
This course provides specific and usable tools for students to take away to support their clients.

courses.title: Flip It or Clip It: Eyelid and Adnexal Surgery in General Practice
courses.description: Eyelid and adnexal disorders are among the most common ophthalmic conditions encountered in general practice, and many can be successfully managed without referral when appropriate case selection and surgical techniques are employed. This lecture will provide a practical, case-based approach to diagnosing and treating common eyelid and third eyelid abnormalities as well as periocular masses in dogs and cats. Participants will learn how to determine when an eyelid or third eyelid should be "flipped" through corrective reconstructive procedures such as cherry eye or entropion repair, and when it should be "clipped" through surgical excision of eyelid and adnexal masses. Surgical planning, instrumentation, tissue handling, reconstruction principles, and postoperative management will be emphasized, along with recognition of cases that warrant referral to a veterinary ophthalmologist. Attendees will leave with practical techniques and increased confidence in managing common eyelid surgical conditions in everyday practice.

courses.title: The ins and outs of shock
courses.description: During this lecture we will discuss the pathophysiology of shock. We will also cover the various types of shock such as hypovolemic, cardiogenic and distributive shock.

courses.title: Host Modulation, The New Way to Put Out Periodontal Fires
courses.description:
The course introduces the participant to and defines the new treatment concept of Host Modulation Therapy (HMT) as it relates to Periodontal Disease. The course provides an in-depth understanding of the Pathogenesis of Periodontal Disease which is critical to understanding this novel solution to periodontal disease treatment and prevention. It compares and contrasts the old verses the new concept of periodontal destruction.
The course does a deep dive into the neutrophil function and migration, and the immune balance between health and disease, discussing modulation of arachidonic acid metabolites, bone remodeling, signaling pathways, nitric oxide synthase activity and how HMT promotes periodontal regeneration.
It concludes with a comprehensive chart which summarizes all of the HMT actions as they relate to the periodontium.

courses.title: CPR in Accordance with RECOVER Guidelines (Lecture/Lab)
courses.description:
This course will provide a 1 hour review of the latest RECOVER guidelines for veterinary CPR as well
as 1 hour of practice using CPR simulations and a static canine mannequin

courses.title: Advances in Veterinary Dentistry: Radiography, Periodontology, Extractions, and Regional Anesthesia
courses.description: This is a 3-hour, LIVE Seminar presented by Christopher Snyder, DVM, DAVDC, DEVDC. This comprehensive program provides veterinary professionals with an integrated approach to advanced small animal dentistry, emphasizing diagnostics, treatment planning, surgical technique, and pain management. The course begins with intraoral radiography, highlighting positioning strategies, interpretation of normal versus pathologic findings, and their impact on clinical decision-making. Building on this diagnostic foundation, participants will review the etiology, staging, and management of periodontal disease, with discussion of both preventive care and advanced interventions such as root planing, guided tissue regeneration, and locally delivered antimicrobials. Extraction techniques are presented in detail, including mucogingival flap design, bone removal, tooth sectioning, and tension-free closure, with a focus on minimizing complications and optimizing healing. Finally, the program explores the use of regional anesthesia for dentistry patients, covering pharmacology, anatomic landmarks, and safe injection techniques to reduce anesthetic risk and enhance recovery. Through practical examples, step-by-step instruction, and evidence-based recommendations, this course equips practitioners with the skills necessary to improve patient outcomes, strengthen client communication, and confidently integrate advanced dentistry into daily practice.

courses.title: CKD: Therapy Beyond Diet and Fluids
courses.description: The goal of this on demand one-hour CE course is to review chronic kidney disease therapeutic options, outside of diet and fluids. IRIS diagnosis and staging will briefly be reviewed, as well common treatments for symptoms of kidney disease for both dogs and cats, including hypertension, proteinuria, and gastrointestinal signs. The main advantages and disadvantages of renal diets will also be summarized. The focus will then turn to the gut kidney axis and dysbiosis that occurs in chronic renal failure and the possible benefit of probiotics to support kidney health. The importance of phosphate management in chronic kidney disease will be described and research presented on the longevity of patients and phosphate target levels. Attendees will learn how to incorporate FGF-23 testing for improved phosphate control in feline patients. Different phosphate binding options, beyond renal diets, will be discussed. Hypokalemia management will also be presented.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Vector-Borne Diseases on the Move: West Nile Virus & African Horse Sickness
courses.description: As vector-borne diseases like West Nile Virus and African Horse Sickness expand into new regions, equine practitioners worldwide are facing unprecedented challenges. This international panel discussion brings together leading infectious disease experts with research and clinical backgrounds from across the globe to explore how these threats are shifting, what they mean for equine health, and what strategies can mitigate the risks. From diagnostics to vaccination and biosecurity, join this global conversation on staying one step ahead of these emerging challenges.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Discipline Specific Performance Challenges Series 1. The Showjumper
courses.description: Showjumpers are subject to unique athletic demands that can test the limits of their physical ability. This first discussion in the Discipline-Specific Performance Challenges Series brings together leading veterinarians and world-class physiotherapists to explore how to identify, manage and prevent injuries in these elite athletes. The panel will discuss the performance-limiting factors and challenges they regularly encounter at different levels of the sport and openly debate the similarities and differences in their approach to management and views. From amateur-produced horses to seasoned professionals, join the discussion on how to optimise soundness, enhance performance, and set realistic expectations for showjumpers at all levels

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Equine Sleep Disorders Deprivation, Narcolepsy & Fragmented Sleep Patterns
courses.description: This interactive panel discussion brings together the worlds leaders in equine sleep explore and discuss the causes, impact and management strategies of sleep deprivation, narcolepsy and fragmented sleep patterns. The discussion will delve into the latest research on sleep cycles in horses, the impact of management practices and environment on sleep quality, and the links between sleep deprivation, health, and performance. Live attendees will have the opportunity to engage with the panel and gain practical insights to support the welfare and athletic potential of their patients.

courses.title: Traveling Vet Retreats Thailand
courses.description: Traveling Vet Retreats provides destination continuing education conferences for veterinarians. We host small group lectures with boarded specialists in unique, once in a lifetime locations. Attendees also have the opportunity to participate in group yoga sessions and a relaxing group trip after completing 15 hours of continuing education.

courses.title: Initial Surgical Approach to wound repair and fracture stabilization
courses.description: This 1 hour CE course will describe basic would repair and basic fracture stabilization and basic surgical fracture consolidation techniques

courses.title: Intervertebral Disc Disease
courses.description:
In this lecture we will cover intervertebral disc disease as it relates to dogs and cats. We
will briefly talk about the pathophysiology of IVDD, discuss the signalment and history with
the disease, point out distinguishing features of the exam that help build the differential list,
discuss how radiographs are used in diagnosis, and discuss treatment options with a focus
on medical and at home care.

courses.title: Webinar - The difficult Synovial Sepsis Case
courses.description: Septic arthritis cases can be among the most frustrating of our equine cases. This webinar will give an overview of diagnosis and treatment, focusing on common pitfalls and difficulties of diagnosis and treatment. Case studies will be used to illustrate the concepts.

courses.title: Helping Our Feline Friends Feel Fear Free with Dr. Tony Buffington
courses.description: In this webinar, Tony Buffington, DVM, PhD, Clinical Professor UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine, will remind participants "who cats are" and why they are particularly prone to fear in confined situations (i.e., hospitals, shelters, homes, etc.) After defining fear and stress in cats, Dr. Buffington will explain what people can do to minimize their fear, particularly in caged contexts--including how to enrich the cat's surroundings, both inside and outside of the cage, and how to recognize both red and green flags by "asking" the cat. Resources for training staff and where to learn more about effective environmental enrichment for cats will also be provided.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Business Leader Recertification
courses.description: The recertification for the Certified Veterinary Business Leader course includes 3 hours of inventory management and 2 hours of leadership content. The first three hours of content focus on inventory management. Veterinarians have many choices of drugs and diets to treat patients. Yet carrying every wonderful medication and diet that is available ties up a lot of cash and creates confusion for the staff and for clients. Doctors - unite! We will discuss tips to effectively manage your inventory without running out of needed drugs and diets, learn the difference between margin and markup, calculate inventory turnover rates, and gain an understanding of how a weekly inventory budget will help reduce your in-house inventory costs. We will also review some simple steps for identifying opportunities to continue to grow revenue. The second portion of this course includes two hours of content emphasizing on quality leadership skills. Leadership from the point of view of "Leading Within the Day", exemplifying leadership, your team looks to you to see, feel, and experience leadership, along with giving and receiving valuable feedback, which everyone on the team can benefit from.

courses.title: Intentional Well-Being (On Demand)
courses.description: This webinar is designed for new graduates and early career veterinarians and focuses on intentional well-being strategies to support mental health

courses.title: Management of Weight and Appetite Loss in the Aging Feline
courses.description: This course will cover the recognition and sequential monitoring of diseases that are commonly recognized in geriatric felines, with a focus on feline cognitive dysfunction, osteoarthritis and disorders affecting the gastrointestinal tract. An emphasis will be placed on the preservation of weight and muscle mass, differences in presentation between cats and dogs, published scoring systems, and recent advances in diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for these disorders.

courses.title: Bleeding Disorders and Hemostasis (DRIP144)
courses.description:
This course focuses on relevant pathophysiology and diagnostic testing regarding bleeding disorders and hemostasis and discusses potential therapies.
To earn a certificate of completion the participant must complete all learning modules and score 80% or better on the end-of-course test. Participants must complete the participation requirements to be eligible for a certificate.

courses.title: Knowing your dental instruments and how to use them
courses.description: Providing optimal dental care for your patients can be very challenging if you don't have the right tools to provide the best level of care. There are a wide range of dental instruments, with a variety of choices in each category, from periodontal curettes to extraction elevators and luxators, to even dental burs. Knowing their proper use and care will allow you to have less frustration and better results with your oral and dental procedures.

courses.title: Toxicology Essentials of Essential Oils
courses.description: This course will cover clinical signs, monitoring, treatment, and prognosis of toxicosis from common essential oils including tea tree oil, oil of wintergreen, peppermint oil, and others. We will also discuss metabolic and decontamination concerns in dogs and cats.

courses.title: Feline Idiopathic Cystitis: A New Era of Novel Management
courses.description: Feline Idiopathic Cystitis is a leading cause of lower urinary tract disease in cats, and often involves recurrent flare ups of lower urinary tract signs in affected cats. Traditional management strategies including analgesia, environmental modification, and nutrition will be reviewed, along with a novel treatment strategy involving low-dose radiation therapy that is showing promising results.

courses.title: Beyond the Buzzwords: How AI Is Actually Helping Veterinary Practices Today
courses.description:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into healthcare environments to help manage complex workflows, reduce administrative burden, and support clinical teams. In veterinary medicine, AI is emerging primarily as an assistive technology that helps capture, organize, and structure information allowing veterinarians and technicians to spend more time focusing on patient care and client communication.
This course will introduce the practical role of AI in veterinary medicine, including where it is most effective and where human oversight remains essential. Participants will learn how AI systems can assist with documentation, workflow organization, and communication tasks while maintaining clinician control over medical decisions. Real-world examples will demonstrate how veterinary AI assistants - such as medical scribes and workflow tools - can be integrated into everyday practice.
Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how to evaluate AI tools, implement them responsibly, and use them to improve efficiency, reduce cognitive load, and support a healthier work-life balance in veterinary practice.

courses.title: Case Rounds: Diagnostic Strategy for the Limping Dog and Cat ON DEMAND
courses.description:
Limping is a common presenting complaint in small animal veterinary practice, with causes ranging from minor injuries to systemic disease. This case-based learning session builds upon foundational orthopedic and neurologic principles by guiding participants through real-world limping dog and cat cases.
Through guided clinical discussion, participants will analyze presenting complaints, gait abnormalities, lesion distribution, and diagnostic findings to determine appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
Cases emphasize pattern recognition, the role of physical examination and diagnostic testing (e.g., radiographs, bloodwork, advanced imaging), and the importance of early diagnosis and appropriate management. The session will also address common diagnostic pitfalls that delay resolution, including missed fractures, misdiagnosed ligament injuries, and systemic conditions presenting as lameness.
The goal of this session is to strengthen diagnostic reasoning and improve confidence in managing limping cases commonly encountered in general practice.

courses.title: Certificate of Managing Difficult Client Conversations in Veterinary Care Proficiency (CDCCVCP)
courses.description: Welcome to your comprehensive training on mastering difficult client conversations in veterinary care. This course moves beyond clinical knowledge to build expertise in the nuanced art of human communication. We begin by establishing foundational skills in active listening and empathy before exploring the deep psychology of the human-animal bond and diverse client perspectives. You will gain structured frameworks for navigating high-stakes topics, including delivering unwelcome news, discussing the cost of care, and guiding families through end-of-life decisions. Additionally, we address modern challenges like managing online criticism and de-escalating conflict while emphasizing strategies for building personal resilience and preventing burnout. By the end of this program, you will improve confidence and build practical skills to lead these essential conversations with compassion, clarity, and professionalism.

courses.title: Psychoactive - Practical Veterinary Psychopharmacology
courses.description:
This course provides an overview of psychopharmacological agents for canine and feline veterinary practice, enabling the attendee to use these medications for the management of chronic behavioral presentations as well as fearful, anxious and stressed patients coming into the veterinary setting.
The course also provides foundational neurobiological information such as overviewing neurotransmission, neurotransmitters, and pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamics of psychotropic agents.
The course furthermore provides a framework for patient assessment, decision making and safe and effective choices around the use of psychopharmaceutical medications in practice.
Attendees will learn about neurotransmission and neurotransmitters and neuromodulators relevant for the understanding of psychopharmaceutical agent use.
Important aspects of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics are discussed, as well as receptor types, the agonist-antagonist spectrum and medication interactions and contraindications.
Choice of suitable patients, contexts and presentations for psychopharmacological use are discussed as well as the constraints of psychopharmacological use and why treatment failures arise and how they can be managed.
The importance of client communication and building a trust-based relationship with clients is addressed.
Attendees will learn about the most commonly used long-acting psychopharmacological agents such as SSRIs, TCAs, SNRIs, MOAIs, Imepitoin and some others. The neurotransmitter profiles, mechanisms of action, adverse effect profiles and contraindications are discussed for each medication class.
Attendees will learn about the most commonly used short-acting / event psychopharmacological agents such as Gabapentinoids, SARIs, Alpha 2 Agonists, Benzodiazepines and some others. The neurotransmitter profiles, mechanisms of action, adverse effect profiles and contraindications are discussed for each medication class.
Attendees will learn how to make medication choices based on

courses.title: Maddie's Insights: Implications of Weeklong Fostering and Co-Housing on Shelter Dog Welfare (On Demand)
courses.description: Meeting both the physical and psychological needs of dogs living in animal shelters is a challenging proposition. Negative environmental inputs, such as excessive noise, restrictive kenneling, and social isolation, contribute to compromised canine welfare. Human-animal interaction, such as a temporary stay in a caregiver's home, has been shown to reduce dogs' cortisol levels and increase their rest. What is not well understood, though, is if longer durations of foster care could extend those benefits. In addition, co-housing in the animal shelter has been even less explored scientifically, but previous studies suggest that dogs' behavior can be improved through living with another dog. In this webcast, I will present our findings from our recently published study about weeklong fostering and co-housing, place these results in context with our previous work investigating various durations of fostering, and discuss the implications of these findings for how we utilize foster care and co-housing in the animal shelter.

courses.title: Dog longevity 201: Improving senior dog care by applying what we know about aging
courses.description: This session will provide a comprehensive review of how aging impacts senior dogs, from disease and physical impairment to changes in behavior and quality of life. We will then explore a comprehensive strategy for how to evaluate and manage these complex cases. We will discuss an evidence-based approach to integrating the needs of the patient and their caregivers with the many available diagnostic and treatment options we can offer. We will also look briefly at the future or preventative medicine and how we can potentially extend health lifespan and good quality of life by targeting the aging process directly before age-related disability and disease occurs.

courses.title: Managing the emergency patient
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian/technician with practical information on the current thoughts on diagnosis and management of common canine and feline emergency problems that they encounter in their daily practice. Emphasis will be placed on the diagnosis of common problems, including what tests are appropriate and what tests are not. The combination of a Surgeon and an Emergency medicine Specialist will provide a unique approach to the patient management. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of diagnosis and management available for their patients.

courses.title: Managing common dental & senior care problems
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian/technician with practical information on the current thoughts on diagnosis and management of common canine and feline dental problems that they encounter in their daily practice. Dr. Lobprise will also discuss how she manages clinical problems encountered with the senior patient. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of diagnosis and management available for their patients.

courses.title: Cats are not Small Dogs: Tackling Diabetes the Feline Way
courses.description: Feline diabetes is not just "small animal diabetes" - cats play by their own rules. From their unique metabolism and obligate carnivore diet to distinct risk factors and treatment responses, managing diabetes in cats demands a species-specific approach. This seminar will explain what makes feline diabetes different from etiology, key risk factors, and the metabolic quirks that influence everything from diagnosis to long-term outcomes. We will compare treatment options - traditional insulin therapy versus emerging SGLT2 inhibitors - and explore strategies to achieve remission and set realistic diabetic goals. Whether you want to refine your approach to feline nutrition, learn when to reach for newer therapies, or simply better understand what makes cats so different, this session will give you the tools to optimize care and improve outcomes for your diabetic patients.

courses.title: On Demand: Feline Anxiety - When Enrichment isn't Enough
courses.description: Join us for a video session on scaredy-cats! Behaviorist Dr. Megan Herron gives us a clear view on the manifestation of feline anxiety and methods of treatment. She'll review the value in nutritional adjustments for managing anxiety, nutraceutical supplements, and show us when to reach for psychopharmacology. With ample discussion on how to better meet feline behavioral needs, this session will help you soothe cat-astrophes of all kinds and make for kinder kitty care.

courses.title: Why Cats Are Not Small Humans: Medication Poisoning in Felines
courses.description: While many pharmaceuticals are used in multiple species, they do not always provide the same effects or have the same margin of safety. This session will provide pharmacists and pharmacy technicians information regarding unique characteristics of the feline species in regards to ADME and therapy needs. With this, attendees will be able to better recognize differences in prescribing methods. We will also discuss 3-4 common human medication poisonings in felines through case examples.

courses.title: Taming the Itch: Harnessing the Power of AI to Optimize Patient Care and Efficiency
courses.description: In this one-hour video course, the future is now! We take a moment to review the challenges of dermatological conditions for pets, owners, and veterinary teams. Then we join Dr. Jones to implement practical technological solutions that save time and treatment. Using AI-powered diagnostics and automated communication systems, we'll work on improving owner compliance, eliminating frustrations, and providing relief to pets suffering from ear and skin issues.

courses.title: Emerging Roles of Hyaluronic Acid Bioscaffolds in Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Dentistry ON DEMAND
courses.description: Hyaluronic acid (HA), a naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan, is increasingly recognized for its regenerative potential in veterinary dentistry. This session explores the structural characteristics, biological mechanisms, and clinical applications of HA in small animal patients, highlighting its role in periodontal regeneration, guided tissue and bone healing, and post-extraction management.

courses.title: The Complete Plan for the Periodontal Patient
courses.description: Learn how to properly conduct and oral examination, perform dental cleaning, administer perioceutic treatment, and develop home care instructions on dogs and cats.

courses.title: Dealing with Grief - ON DEMAND
courses.description:
The death of a pet is, for many, the worst personal loss they have ever experienced. Complicate the event with the possibility of euthanasia and the emotions can be too much for some pet parents to bare. How, when, and why veterinary professionals can make a difference at such an important time is essential to maintaining not only the human animal bond, but the doctor-client bond as well. There is no better time to show your clients you care than by helping through the difficult journey of pet loss.
We cannot discuss the different ways clients face death without first understanding what grief is and how it can look. An important part of ministering to the grief is knowing that grief can present in many ways. There are many styles to grief, and it does not follow any particular timeline. Grief is often said to have different stages, however, they aren't concrete. This talk will go over a number of different presentations of grief and tips on how to handle them!

courses.title: Microbiome-Informed GI Care for the Growing Puppy (On Demand Webinar)
courses.description: This webinar provides veterinarians and veterinary professionals with a practical approach to gastrointestinal cases in growing puppies. Focusing on the period from weaning until the end of growth the session reframes how the early-life gut microbiome shapes clinical outcomes and how everyday decisions in the consultation room can either support or undermine it. Drawing on recent canine microbiome research, the lecture equips clinicians to take a clearer and more confident approach to gastrointestinal health in growing puppies. Particular emphasis is placed on revising outdated reflexes, including routine antibiotic prescribing, fasting a puppy presenting with gastrointestinal signs, and generic homemade recommendations, and replacing them with biologically justified choices grounded in current science. Attendees will leave with clear, practice-ready decision frameworks, monitoring cues, and nutrition-based strategies to support gut resilience, reduce avoidable medical escalation, and protect long-term gastrointestinal health during this vulnerable developmental window.

courses.title: Clinical Animal Nutrition Academy
courses.description:
This 3-Tier certification equips you to confidently recommend diets and supplements, customize nutrient plans, and address specific health challenges in dogs, cats, and horses.
Unlock new revenue streams, including consultations, lab tests, supplement sales, and follow-ups, while utilizing proven tools like the Clinical Animal Nutrition Survey and Fur Tissue Mineral Analysis.
Join live bi-monthly Zoom sessions offering the ultimate key to growing your practice and delivering exceptional care.
Proven methods such as the Clinical Animal Nutrition Survey and Fur Tissue Mineral Analysis empower practitioners to transform animal health. With these science-backed tools, you can confidently address the unique needs of dogs, cats, and horses.

courses.title: (On Demand) Caught Between a Rock and a Hard Place: Bladder Stone Prevention (Adieux Cailloux: Prvention des calculs vsicau
courses.description: This case-based talk will discuss practical strategies for stone prevention with a special focus on calcium oxalate, struvite and cystine stones. Lots of practical and easily to implement options will be presented.

courses.title: The Heart of the Matter: Managing Complex Congestive Heart Failure
courses.description: In this Non-Interactive Distance course, the audience will be understanding complex CHF cases in dogs and cats

courses.title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation: Why, When, and How?
courses.description: This webinar will focus on the use and potential benefits of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in dogs and cats. This webinar will focus on the use and potential benefits of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in dogs and cats. Based on current evidence from the literature and on the author's experience, the various indications for this treatment modality will be reviewed. In addition, the selection of fecal donors and the various techniques for the in-hospital preparation of fecal slurry and the administration of FMT will be discussed so that participants can utilize the method in their hospital. In addition, the selection of fecal donors and the various techniques for the in-hospital preparation of fecal slurry and the administration of FMT will be discussed so that participants can utilize the method in their hospital.

courses.title: MythBusting: Anesthesia Edition
courses.description: This course will focus on some commonly held anesthesia misconceptions that persist in veterinary medicine. Six myths will be presented followed by the facts and outstanding questions still present regarding these topics today using evidenced-based medicine and the most current literature available.

courses.title: Conversational Spanish in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This course was designed by a bilingual Veterinarian and is geared toward Veterinarians, Veterinary Technicians, Veterinary Assistants but is helpful for the whole team! It is designed for people who have studied some Spanish in the past. A comprehensive, self-paced modular course that will give you the most important Spanish words and phrases in addition to the most useful grammar in communicating with your Spanish speaking clients in our Veterinary profession. The course consists of lectures, videos, and listening practice and consists of 11 modules. You have one year to complete the course but you will get partial credit for any modules you complete. Direct one on one communication with the course creator is available when needed.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Common Oral Pathology (On Demand)
courses.description: This one hour, on-demand discussion will expand into common oral pathology, highlighting conditions that veterinarians are most likely to encounter in daily practice. Topics will include the identification and treatment of discolored teeth, enamel defects, fractured teeth, granulomas, tooth wear, persistent deciduous teeth, unerupted teeth and dentigerous cysts, oral tumors, feline tooth resorption, and maxillofacial trauma triage. The importance of a thorough oral exam will be emphasized throughout as the cornerstone of diagnosis and treatment.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: Ho Ho Ho: What every small ruminant veterinarian should know about reindeer.
courses.description:
Program Description:
This webinar will familiarize the attendees with the species Rangifer tarandus and will provide the common conditions that are found in this unique species.
Learning Objectives:
1. Participants should feel comfortable providing veterinary services for this species following this webinar.
2. We will discuss the anatomy and physiology of reindeer. Participants will learn about common medications used for general anesthesia, best practices when dealing with antler injuries, heard health, theriogenology and parasitology.
3. We will discuss assisted reproduction techniques in male and females of this species. WE will also discuss gestation length, dystocias, and neonatology.

courses.title: ECG Rounds
courses.description: This course will review how to interpret and treat common arrhythmias

courses.title: Product Primer Nutrition as a first-line treatment for acute diarrhea
courses.description: Diarrhea is one of the most common disorders seen in dogs and cats. Dietary management is often recommended as part of the treatment strategy, often in conjunction with antimicrobial therapies and probiotics. However, recent research has called into question our reliance on antimicrobials in the treatment of these patients, revealing limited patient benefits with this approach, and potential adverse effects for patients, including sustained dysbiosis. In this program we will review the evolving research on the role of the gastrointestinal microbiome and the use of antimicrobials, synbiotics, and nutrition as it pertains to modernizing our therapeutic approach to diarrhea. Dietary management is often recommended as part or all of the treatment strategy for pets with acute diarrhea. The traditional advice of simply recommending a bland diet is problematic due to the potential for nutritional deficiency and safety issues of this approach. Moreover, it can be challenging for practitioners to choose amongst the many gastrointestinal diet options available to them in order to make an individualized nutritional recommendation for their patients. This program will help practitioners understand the benefits of utilizing a complete and balanced gastrointestinal diet in the support of patients with gastrointestinal disease, while providing a systematic framework from which they can make rational diet choices based on unique patient needs.

courses.title: ON DEMAND: Vet Your Voice Online: Mastering Best Practices for a Standout Social Media Profile
courses.description: This lecture explores essential strategies for veterinarians to establish a compelling social media presence, distinguishing between a personal profile, a personal brand, and your practice's digital identity. We will delve into the importance of defining your "why," appreciating the investment in content creation, and leveraging audience insights--including feedback from your most influential contacts--while also covering best practices and must-have strategies to create profiles that are secure, effective, and truly stand out.

courses.title: Feline Anesthesia Techniques
courses.description: This webinar will cover species specific challenges of feline anesthesia, the relevance those challenges have to anesthetic outcomes, and techniques for the anesthetist to overcome these challenges including anesthetic care from the time that the patient leaves home to the time the patient returns home.

courses.title: Management of Chronic Pain
courses.description: Chronic pain is a significant quality of life issue for small animals. Recognizing chronic pain, developing treatment options, owner education, and staff teamwork in pain management will be the focus of this talk.

courses.title: ON DEMAND: Diabetic Pearls from 2025...New insulins, new products, and how's it going with SGLT2 inhibitors?
courses.description:
This lecture will discuss:
Newer tools (and how to use them) in the diagnosis and management of diabetes mellitus in both species.
Newer therapies:
An insulin update : Toujeo and Degludec
SGLT2 drugs a year in...
Nutrition, diabetes, and comorbidities: How to make diet decision making less painful

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: Basic camel medicine tips for the dromedary and Bactrian camel
courses.description: An overview of commons diseases of dromedary and Bactrian camels in the U.S. and how to manage them. Touching on, amongst other things, gastrointestinal parasitism, other gastrointestinal diseases, nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism, neonatal care, and nutrition, as well as what lab tests to use for diagnoses. How to do a physical exam on a camel. A brief summary of medications used in camels, and which commonly used medications can be toxic in camels, such as banamine and bute. An introduction into camel restraint, including use of the hobble and lip twitch. And a demonstration of how to draw blood from camels.

courses.title: Commit to Care: Pet Food Labels 101 (On Demand)
courses.description: In a world filled with misinformation about pet foods, it is essential for veterinarians to have the knowledge and confidence to engage in meaningful nutritional discussions with pet owners. This 1-hour webinar will empower veterinarians to take control of the conversation about pet nutrition by breaking down and understanding pet food labels. From decoding nutritional adequacy statements to understanding the role of by products, this session will provide practical tips for interpreting packaging and communicating effectively with clients about the foods their pets are consuming. Veterinarians will leave this session with the tools needed to make informed dietary recommendations based on pet food labels.

courses.title: Keeping Up with the Kidneys: Updates in Renal Disease Management
courses.description: In this video series, we're joining Dr. Mark Acierno through a comprehensive review of acute and chronic kidney disease. Learn to care for acute kidney injury, practice IV fluid therapy calculations, cover common nephrotoxins, and discuss the increasing prevalence of leptospirosis and methods to manage it safely in your practice. Finally, we'll look at a long-haul approach to CKD and hypertension, starting with defining at-risk pets you might already be seeing.

courses.title: Navigating Feline Chronic Enteropathy: A Comprehensive Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approach
courses.description: Vomiting, diarrhea, dysorexia, and weight loss are signs of feline chronic enteropathy (CE) and are common reasons for cats to be presented to veterinary practitioners. A wide range of diseases can lead to symptoms that mimic enteropathy. First, the practitioner is challenged with evaluating if the cause of symptoms is systemic, such as with pancreatic or hepatobiliary disease, or the result of a true enteropathy. Common causes of feline CE include food-responsive disease, inflammatory bowel disease, or low-grade intestinal lymphoma. In this webinar, we will use a case-based approach to review the diagnostic and therapeutic approach and answer the most common practitioner questions about feline CE.

courses.title: Diet Formulation and Evaluation
courses.description: This course provides an evidence-based overview of diet formulation and evaluation for horses. Participants will learn about taking a nutritional history, factors to consider when formulating or evaluating a diet, and diagnosis of nutritional imbalances. Veterinarian quick reference sheets and client handouts are also available to participants.

courses.title: Feline Low Stress Handling in a Shelter Environment (On Demand)
courses.description: Cats are not small dogs. They have a lower tolerance for frustration and a much shorter window before physical restraint stops helping and starts causing harm. Feline Low Stress Handling meets cats where they are. This session offers practical, in-the-moment applications for shelter veterinary exams: reading the feline communication signaling, from fear to frustration, applying the 2-second rule and the least-restraint principle, adjusting the examination approach to the individual, and creating a low stress environment.

courses.title: DNM PET FOOD INGREDIENTS
courses.description: There is a lot of misinformation and many misunderstandings about commercial pet food ingredients and their nutritional value. This course explores how ingredient quality is defined and regulated, the four main sources of ingredients, how these ingredients typically appear on pet food labels, and the most common ingredients used in commercial pet foods. Understanding pet food ingredients is a crucial step in determining which diet is best for a specific pet.

courses.title: LOV Self Study Program
courses.description:
The LOV Self Study Program is a self guided online program made up of five video segments with post course test questions, including:
The Art of Euthanasia
Assessing Quality of Life
Old Age is Not a Disease
Anticipatory Grief and Pet Loss Preparation
Veterinary Hospice - Comfort Beyond a Cure

courses.title: Canine Low Stress Handling in a Shelter Environment (On Demand)
courses.description: This session offers practical, in-the-moment applications of Low Stress Handling of dogs for shelter veterinary exams: reading the canine communication signaling, applying the 3-second rule and the least-restraint principle, adjusting the examination approach to the individual, and creating a low stress environment.

courses.title: Periodontal Disease: Treatments, Adjuncts, and an Exciting New Option - ON DEMAND
courses.description: This CE session provides a comprehensive overview of periodontal disease in companion animals, with emphasis on current therapies and emerging adjunctive treatments. Participants will gain foundational knowledge in disease pathogenesis, diagnostic staging, and standard treatment protocols, including closed and open root planing. The course then introduces PerioVive, a novel hyaluronic acid-based biomaterial shown to promote wound healing, reduce inflammation, and support tissue regeneration in periodontal and post-extraction sites. Clinical applications, supportive studies, and guidelines for practical integration are included to help improve clinical outcomes in veterinary dentistry.

courses.title: Pruritus: Diagnostic Approach and Management
courses.description: This webinar will focus on the diagnostic approach to the pruritic patient and how to rule in or rule out the most common differential diagnoses. The strategy of how to work through various triggers for allergic skin disease will be presented as well updates on food allergies, food trials and the pros and cons of current treatments for pruritus.

courses.title: Snap, Send, Solve: Decoding Real-World Dental Dilemmas
courses.description: Texted dental questions have become a routine part of veterinary practice, often arriving with a single photo and a quick request for advice. While these messages can be constructive, they can also be unclear or incomplete, making case assessment challenging. This webinar provides a friendly, practical overview of genuine "Snap and Send" dentistry, presenting multiple anonymized cases that highlight common diagnostic dilemmas and the decision-making steps necessary to reach an informed conclusion.

courses.title: Management of Coxofemoral Luxations
courses.description: Coxofemoral luxations occur frequently in dogs and cats. In most instances, reduction is preferable to salvage procedures such as femoral head and neck excision or total hip replacement. Closed reduction should be attempted and can yield acceptable clinical outcomes in the lion's share of cases. Open reduction is associated with a high degree of success in appropriate cases. This lecture will offer perspective on non-surgical and surgical management of coxofemoral luxation.

courses.title: Nutrition News 2023
courses.description: This course provides an overview of equine nutrition research from 2023. The goal of this presentation is to provide equine veterinarians with up-to-date information on equine nutrition that is applicable to veterinary practice.

courses.title: Primary Layers - Made Easy
courses.description:
In this one- hour presentation on primary bandage layers we will say goodbye to the gauze of old and say hello to a plethora of advanced primary wound dressings! This presentation reviews the number one goal of wound care which is to cultivate a clean and moist wound environment. Also, we will move forward with a historical deep dive into wet-to-dry bandages and their place in modern day wound care. Recommended primary layer products will be discussed along with additional wound focused resources provided. Finally, some new wound products will be reviewed including the cutting-edge product: The Vetlen Pouch.
Learning Objectives:
Review the goals of wound care.
To review Wet - To - Dry bandages and their place in modern day wound care.
Examine recommended primary layer products including cutting edge research.

courses.title: Hop on Up: Rabbit Medicine
courses.description: Are you intimidated by the thought of a bunny hopping through your door? Fear not! After this presentation you will be familiar with the clinically relevant anatomy and physiology of the domestic rabbit, husbandry and preventative medicine, methods of restraint and physical examination, treatment techniques, and some common disorders of the domestic rabbit including differential diagnoses, diagnostic techniques, recommended treatment(s), and prognosis.

courses.title: Weight Reduction in Cats: Tips, Tricks, and Tools to Make it Successful
courses.description: This presentation explores the latest scientific insights into feline obesity pathophysiology, practical dietary interventions, and long-term management strategies to sustain weight loss. Case studies provide real-world applications, demonstrating the importance of individualized treatment plans and owner education in achieving successful and sustainable outcomes.

courses.title: Mastering Non-Surgical Periodontal Therapy: Scaling, Root Planing, and Beyond ON DEMAND
courses.description: This lecture will begin with an introduction to periodontal disease, including its identification and progression. Participants will review the clinical indicators used to diagnose and classify periodontal conditions. The lecture will then explore the role of therapeutic dental cleaning that precedes root planing, emphasizing effective biofilm and calculus removal. This segment will also briefly review ultrasonic scaling fundamentals, including the differences between piezoelectric and magnetostrictive (ferrite rod) units, proper tip selection, and the role of cavitation in disrupting biofilm. The presentation will then transition into non-surgical treatment approaches, with a particular focus on closed root planing and curettage techniques. The lecture will conclude with an exploration of emerging research surrounding the incorporation of hyaluronic acid into periodontal treatment protocols. Together, these topics will provide attendees with both foundational knowledge and practical insight into innovative approaches aimed at improving treatment outcomes.

courses.title: Judicious Use and Antimicrobial Stewardship in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Abstract: Judicious Use and Antimicrobial Stewardship in Veterinary Medicine Presented by Dr. Lauren Forsythe, PharmD, DICVP This course provides a comprehensive framework for implementing effective antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary practice. Focusing on the core principle of "using the right antibiotic, at the right time, right dose, for the right duration," the program emphasizes evidence-based medicine and practical risk assessment to optimize clinical outcomes while minimizing resistance development. The course covers critical areas including treatment decision frameworks, FDA-approved uses, and prevention strategies. Participants will learn essential protocols for diagnostic confirmation, culture and susceptibility testing, and documentation of treatment rationales. Special attention is given to implementing required elements such as valid VCPR, proper documentation, treatment protocols, and staff training. Key topics include: - Evidence-based treatment decision making - FDA-approved therapeutic uses versus prohibited production uses - Prevention strategies including vaccination and biosecurity - Implementation requirements and best practices - Resource utilization and quality assurance programs - Documentation and compliance requirements The course addresses the growing global health threat of antimicrobial resistance, which causes over 2 million resistant infections yearly and has a $55B economic impact. Participants will gain practical strategies for: - Implementing diagnostic testing protocols - Developing written treatment guidelines - Maintaining detailed records - Monitoring outcomes - Educating staff and clients Special emphasis is placed on utilizing available resources from professional organizations (AVMA, species-specific groups), government agencies (FDA, USDA, CDC), and quality assurance programs (BQA/PQA) to support decision-making and ensure compliance with current guidelines. Duration: 1 hour CE Credit: Meets state requirements for antimi

courses.title: 37th Annual Southern Veterinary Conference On-Demand
courses.description: This is an Annual Veterinary Conference that occurs in August in Birmingham, Alabama located at the The Hyatt Regency/Wynfrey Hotel in front of the Galleria Mall. This will be a continuation of the in-person sessions recorded live at the conference August 6th to 9th, 2025 . Each session made available will be edited for and will link to questions at the end of each session for a RACE approved certificate. You will be emailed a certificate for each hour completed. These sessions will end in December 31st.

courses.title: DNM Therapeutic Nutrition for Dogs with Osteoarthritis
courses.description: This course explores the mechanisms and management of osteoarthritis in dogs, the most prevalent canine joint disorder. It will help you educate clients about the risk factors for osteoarthritis, such as obesity, and the importance of a multimodal approach, including targeted nutrition, to manage dogs with this condition

courses.title: Ticks Do Not Check the Calendar. When You Cannot Predict, PROTECT.
courses.description:
Dr. Victoria Wagner will highlight the unpredictable reality of ticks in Canada, where evolving patterns are making it increasingly difficult to anticipate risks. She will also review relevant updates on ticks and tick-borne diseases, providing practical insights to help you stay ahead in this dynamic landscape.
Discover tips for the successful implementation of tick control strategies with Dr. Scott Stevenson. Dr. Stevenson will explore key learnings, successful approaches, and measurable outcomes, while addressing common hurdles such as prescription barriers and the broader ONE Health implications for both pets and their owners.

courses.title: Tackling Feline Chronic Kidney Disease and Comorbidities with a Pawsitive Approach ( On Demand Webinar)
courses.description: In this 1-hour webinar, feline specialist Susan Little, DVM, DABVP will discuss management of cats with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and concurrent conditions (multimorbidity). Practitioners routinely see middle-aged and senior feline patients with multimorbidities and a strategy must be found to minimize the burden on patient and caregiver. One such strategy (Ariadne Principles) will be discussed in the context of a CKD case to illustrate how to work with owners to make the best treatment choices.

courses.title: Technology Tools Every Practice Needs
courses.description: You are short-staffed with excessive appointment demands, 800 calls a day, and clients who are more demanding than ever. Get advice from veterinarians and hospital managers who discovered game-changing technology tools that improve efficiency and employees cannot do without.

courses.title: 2025 AAV Conference ON DEMAND
courses.description: This on demand course features a selection of recorded sessions previously presented at the 46th Annual AAV Conference & Expo. Sessions will cover avian veterinary techniques and avian medicine. This conference was hosted by the Association of Avian Veterinarians (AAV). The program will focus on advancing avian health, welfare, and conservation through education, advocacy, and science.

courses.title: Navigating Renal Nutrition: From Physiology to Practical Management (On-Demand)
courses.description: This presentation provides a brief review of renal physiology and the essential functions of the kidney. Through some case-based discussions, participants will develop an understanding of nutritional requirements in patients with kidney disease and concurrent comorbidities. The program will help participants strengthen their understanding of the diet product guides, enabling them to evaluate nutrient composition and make specific nutritional recommendations for patients. The program will conclude with a practical focus on how to introduce therapeutic diets and optimize patient acceptance and compliance.

courses.title: Updates on Sterilization Recommendations age, breed specifics, OVE vs OVH vs chemical implants
courses.description:
