This panel discussion will delve into the evolution of surgical sterilization procedures for dogs and cats, since the inception in the 1930s. Initially, ovariohysterectomy was the primary method performed in females, with proposed benefits, along with population control, including a reduced risk of mammary neoplasia. Over time, there has been a shift towards pre-pubertal neutering with some preferring pre-pubertal ovariectomy, and laparoscopic ovariectomy and some have even considered the ovary-sparing hysterectomy. Furthermore, there have been significant advances in hormonal methods for long term sterilization, especially with the development of depot GnRH agonists.
However, research has highlighted that the benefits of these procedures may not be as straightforward as once believed, with potential associations with increased risks of non-reproductive neoplasia and increased joint disease in some dog breeds. The impact of neutering on the risk of urinary incontinence and development of obesity cannot be ignored. Given these complexities, veterinarians, breeders, owners, and shelter managers face challenges in making evidence-based decisions regarding the most effective sterilization methods and timing, especially considering the influence of animal breed on disease risks.
An esteemed international panel of world-renowned specialists will explore the benefits and risks of various sterilization procedures performed in dogs and cats, aiming to navigate the current evidence landscape, providing insights to guide clinical decision-making.

courses.title: How you can help aging dogs -- options for today and tomorrow
courses.description: This session will address the role of aging as a modifiable risk factor for most of the health problems seen in geriatric dogs and what vets can do about it. Our understanding of the biology of aging has reached the stage where we can take a preventative approach to age-associated diseases. Vets already have tools to prolong healthy lifespan in our patients and more solutions are rapidly emerging from ongoing research. We will cover what you can do today, and what you may be able to do tomorrow, to help your patients live longer, healthier lives.

courses.title: Beyond Healing: Real-World Use of Hyaluronic Acid ON DEMAND
courses.description: This lecture examines the evolving role of hyaluronic acid, highlighting its application beyond conventional wound healing in veterinary dental patients. While traditionally valued for its hydrating and protective properties, hyaluronic acid is now recognized as a bioactive agent that supports tissue regeneration, modulates inflammation, and enhances post-procedural outcomes. Attendees will gain insight into the mechanisms of action that make hyaluronic acid effective in practice and discuss positive real-world case examples which have provided meaningful benefits to healing.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Developmental Orthopedic Disease
courses.description: This course provides an evidence-based overview of nutritional management of developmental orthopedic disease. Participants will learn about the pathophysiology of select orthopedic diseases, how nutrition can play a role, and feeding strategies for affected farms. This course is designed for veterinary professionals seeking to enhance their understanding of equine nutrition and apply tailored nutritional protocols in clinical practice. Veterinarian quick reference sheets and client handouts are also available to participants.

courses.title: Triaditis from Exam Room to Food Bowl: Integrating Nutrition into Clinical Case Management
courses.description: This lecture provides a practical, case based overview of feline triaditis, integrating diagnostic evaluation, clinical decision making, and nutritional management. Participants will review clinical case examples, with discussion centered on diagnostic choices and treatment strategies. The program emphasizes applying nutritional intervention as part of comprehensive case management.

courses.title: X-ray Vision- Secrets to Mastering Dental Radiographs ON DEMAND
courses.description: This lecture provides a comprehensive overview of veterinary dental radiography. Participants will review the importance of dental radiographs as the standard of care in small animal practice and explore indications for intraoral imaging. The session will cover essential equipment, radiation safety protocols, and step-by-step positioning strategies, including parallel and bisecting angle techniques. Common challenges such as patient anatomy variations, positioning errors, and image quality issues will be addressed, along with troubleshooting strategies to improve diagnostic accuracy. Attendees will leave with increased confidence in acquiring and evaluating high-quality dental radiographs in clinical practice.

courses.title: Sedation as an Alternative to Anesthesia in the Avian Patient
courses.description: Birds often benefit from sedation or anesthesia for procedures ranging from general handling (for very stressed individuals), and diagnostics to surgery. Several drugs have been investigated for sedation in birds, and in combination with local analgesia can even be considered for minor surgical procedures. Sedation should be considered any time general anesthesia is not specifically indicated.

courses.title: Effective Candidate Engagement and Successful Hiring
courses.description: The webinar will cover ideas on how to better engage with candidates, develop a strong interview process and successful hiring, on-boarding and continued engagement.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: Beyond Vesicles: Reportable Diseases of Sheep and Goats
courses.description:
Program Description:
This presentation will provide an overview of reportable diseases of small ruminants, how to identify reportable diseases for your location, the logistics of reporting and the consequences. Anthrax, coxiellosis (Q fever), tularemia, Rift Valley fever, and screwworm will be reviewed in more detail with an emphasis on key takeaway points about the clinical presentation, diagnosis, zoonotic potential, and response.
Learning Objectives:
1. Identify location-specific and national resources for reportable disease lists, reportable disease questions, and actual disease reporting for small ruminants
2. Increase awareness and recognition of zoonotic risks of specific reportable diseases of small ruminants
3. Recognize preventive measures to avoid or reduce animal disease and prevent human infections

courses.title: VetQuest Travel CE Oncology & Oncologic Surgery
courses.description: These lectures will be over 3 days and cover topics related to diagnosing neoplasia in small animals, diagnostics for treatment planning and outline non-surgical and surgical therapies.

courses.title: DNM DIGESTION & NUTRIENTS
courses.description: As you know, nutrition plays a vital role in the overall health and well being of cats and dogs. In this course we'll explore the organs involved in digestion, the nutrients contained in food, how energy is derived from certain nutrients, and the energy requirements of cats and dogs. You will also learn the metabolic differences between dogs and cats and how this plays a role in formulation of pet food. As you progress through he course, you'll learn new terminology and explore real life scenarios, which will help you apply new nutritional knowledge to your daily practice.

courses.title: 1099 Unleashed: The Relief Vets Complete Tax Game Plan
courses.description: A comprehensive A-to-Z framework for independent veterinarians who want to take control of their finances, master their taxes, and keep more of what they earn.

courses.provider: CORNELL UNIVERSITY, COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: VetTEAMS: Master Trainer Course
courses.description: VetTEAMS is an evidence-based team training course adapted for veterinary medicine from the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality's TeamSTEPPS framework. This course equips all members of the veterinary healthcare team - veterinarians, veterinary technicians and technologists, facilities and animal care personnel, and customer service representatives - with practical tools and strategies to enhance teamwork, improve communication, and strengthen patient safety in clinical settings.

courses.title: From Recruitment to Retention: Cultivating a Resilient Veterinary Team
courses.description: Building and maintaining a resilient veterinary team is essential for the sustained success and excellence of any veterinary practice. This lecture explores the continuum of team development, from initial recruitment to long-term retention, focusing on strategies to foster resilience and cohesion within the veterinary workplace. The lecture addresses the multifaceted challenges and opportunities encountered at each stage of the employee lifecycle. Key topics include effective recruitment practices to attract diverse talent, onboarding strategies to integrate new team members seamlessly, fostering a supportive workplace culture that values collaboration and professional growth, and implementing proactive retention initiatives to nurture long-term commitment and loyalty. Furthermore, the lecture examines the pivotal role of leadership in fostering resilience, providing mentorship, and navigating inevitable setbacks and challenges within the veterinary team. By cultivating a resilient and cohesive team, veterinary practices can enhance staff satisfaction, improve client experiences, and ultimately elevate the standard of care provided to animal patients.

courses.title: CERTIFIED VETERINARY BUSINESS LEADER
courses.description: CERTIFIED VETERINARY BUSINESS LEADER is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Feeding the Endurance Horse
courses.description: This course provides an evidence-based overview of feeding endurance horses. Participants will learn about the challenges endurance horses face and how they can be nutritionally managed. This course is designed for veterinary professionals seeking to enhance their understanding of equine nutrition and apply tailored nutritional protocols in clinical practice. Veterinarian quick reference sheets and client handouts are also available to participants.

courses.title: Veterinary Ultrasound and Radiography Mentorship Program
courses.description:
The SkillVet Veterinary Radiology and Ultrasonography Mentorship Program is a 9-month postgraduate continuing education program designed for small animal veterinarians who wish to develop a structured, clinically applicable approach to diagnostic imaging. The program combines radiology, ultrasonography, case-based learning, supervised practical training, and longitudinal mentorship to help participants progress from foundational interpretation skills to confident clinical application in daily practice.
The program is delivered across five in-person modules between October 2026 and June 2027, taking place in Prague, Warsaw, Bucharest, and Cluj. The curriculum begins with thoracic and abdominal radiology, including normal anatomy, lung patterns, pleural and mediastinal disease, thoracic masses, cardiac radiology, gastrointestinal and genitourinary radiography, and abdominal mass interpretation. The radiology component then progresses to musculoskeletal imaging, including aggressive versus non-aggressive bone lesions, diseases of the growing and mature patient, trauma, and extensive case-based revision.
The ultrasonography component introduces ultrasound physics, artefacts, machine optimisation, and scanning technique before progressing through a systematic small animal ultrasound curriculum. Participants receive supervised training in abdominal ultrasonography, including the liver, biliary tract, spleen, gastrointestinal tract, pancreas, urinary tract, reproductive tract, adrenal glands, and lymph nodes. Advanced practical sessions also cover ultrasound-guided fine needle aspirates and biopsies, ocular ultrasound, thyroid and parathyroid ultrasound, neck ultrasound, salivary glands, larynx and trachea, lymph nodes of the head, and selected musculoskeletal ultrasound applications such as tendon scanning.
The teaching format combines structured lectures, live demonstrations, case-based discussions, small-group practical sessions, guided image interpretation, and continu

courses.title: Panel Discussion Interventional Therapy for Equine Corneal Disease Morbidity Rounds
courses.description:
This interesting panel discussion will focus on the diagnosis, therapeutic approach, and clinical and surgical management of corneal diseases and syndromes in equine patients as well as the potential pitfalls which should be considered.
Join the panel of internationally renowned specialist ophthalmology clinicians as they discuss and debate how to approach multiple challenging cases. The case discussions will address the approach to cases of misdiagnosis; therapeutic and surgical mistakes; complications following surgery; and those with frustrating outcomes despite therapy.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Dental Radiography - Indications, Findings & Interpretation
courses.description: Dental radiography although complex is an essential diagnostic tool in the workup of equine dental cases. With good radiographic technique and careful interpretation dental radiographs can be diagnostic for most equine dental problems including incisor cheek teeth and sinus conditions. An international panel of worldrenowned equine dentistry specialists will discuss case selection for dental radiography and radiographic interpretation in light of the remainder of the workup. A good mix of common and interesting cases examples will be used to discuss all aspect of dental radiography and when more advanced imaging modalities should be considered.

courses.title: Canine Musculoskeletal Disorders - Focus on the Working Dog
courses.description:
Musculoskeletal disorders and injuries are a common-place problem in dogs from all walks of life. However, they have an added impact on working dogs when the outcome of the injuries affects not only their quality of life but also whether they will be able to return to function :be it that of a high-level agility athlete or a highly specialised service dog.
This fascinating panel discussion will address some of the common musculoskeletal injuries, with a focus on the working dog, including the recognition and diagnosis of specific injuries, as well as the possible approaches to their treatment and correction and options for management going forward.
Join this multidisciplinary panel of internationally renowned specialists as they discuss and debate the most recent advances in diagnostics, surgery, rehabilitation and therapeutics for our canine athletes

courses.title: On Demand Webinar: Pet Care for Seriously Ill and Homebound Adults
courses.description: This presentation will help you learn about Pet Peace of Mind's turnkey solution to help patients with their pet care needs and the importance of the role veterinarians play in building a successful program within the community. However, there will be significant exploration in the value of the human-animal bond and other important learning objectives

courses.title: Panel Discussion
courses.description:
The use of assisted reproductive techniques has, and continues, to increase in equine breeding. These technologies may reduce wastage, with increased progeny and the potential for genetic improvement.
This panel discussion will provide a truly unique, global insight into the clinical use of ICSI and OPU, with the worlds leading minds. As well as sharing their personal knowledge and case experiences, with panellists encouraged to share their failures as well as successes, this group will appraise the current knowledge base, discuss the potential future of assisted reproduction in equine breeding across the world and at practice level, and contextualise these techniques with responsible breeding practices.
With audience participation highly encouraged, this interactive panel discussion will be a key event for veterinarians worldwide with an interest in equine breeding.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Pain Assessment in the Ridden Horse
courses.description: This panel discussion brings together five internationally renowned experts to explore the identification and assessment of pain in horses during ridden exercise. Key points of debate and discussion will include why and when ridden evaluation as part of a clinical workup may provide additional useful information, and how pain-related behaviours can be identified using tools such as the Ridden Horse Pain Ethogram. Potential influencers such as saddle fit, rider weight, height, or skill on the behaviour of ridden horses will also be explored by the group.

courses.title: Efficacious Use of Acid Suppressants in General Practice
courses.description: This session explores use of gastric acid suppressants (histamine-2 receptor antagonists (H2RA) and proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) in canine and feline patients. Optimal selection of drugs and duration of treatment to address conditions that require acid suppressant therapy will be explained including GI ulceration, bleeding, chronic kidney disease, portosystemic shunt disease, gastroesophageal reflux, mast cell tumors, and thrombocytopenia. The potential impact of co-administration of certain medications with acid suppressants (e.g., antifungals, antacids, antiplatelet drugs) and concerns regarding chronic administration will be covered.

courses.title: Orthopedic Exam- How to be Efficient, but Thorough
courses.description: One of the greatest challenges of the orthopedic examination is confident localization of lameness. This session focuses on visual and manual tips that help with more efficient localization through the gait evaluation, standing and manipulative portions of the orthopedic exam.

courses.title: Avian Emergency and Critical Care (On-demand Webinar)
courses.description: As the field of veterinary medicine continues to advance and specialize, there is a growing demand for veterinary technicians with specific areas of expertise. This lecture will focus on enhancing participants' skills in assessing critically ill avian patients. Topics covered include initial triage and stabilization, establishing venous access, and how to place an intraosseous catheter and air sac cannula.

courses.title: DVM Inc; Incorporating Yourself, Protecting the Corporate Veil and Shielding Personal Assets
courses.description: This class is designed to provide participants with a comprehensive understanding of the benefits of incorporating oneself and the crucial strategies to avoid piercing the corporate veil. This program will explore the legal and financial advantages of forming a corporation or limited liability company (LLC) for professionals. Additionally, it will delve into the potential risks associated with personal liability and the techniques to safeguard personal assets by maintaining the integrity of the corporate veil.

courses.title: Resource Guarding in Dogs: A Fear Free Approach
courses.description: Resource guarding is a common problem in dogs with a wide variety of behavioral presentations. The condition is sometimes referred to as possessive aggression, and it poses a serious risk of injury when aggression is directed toward humans or other animals. Resource guarding can negatively affect the human-animal bond and the dog's social relationship with other animals. In this webinar, Kenneth Martin, DVM, DACVB, will discuss prevention, establishing a diagnosis, and treatment recommendations.

courses.title: Neurology in practice today
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian with practical information on the current thoughts on anesthesia along with acute and chronic pain management in their practice. The combination of two Anesthesiologist/pain management specialists will provide a unique approach to the patient management. Dr's Grubb and Robertson will discuss their approach to management of patients requiring anesthesia along with their assessment and management of pain in practice today. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of anesthesia and pain management available for their patients.

courses.title: Veterinary Practice Pricing & Principles
courses.description:
In this program we will discuss the differences between service and inventory pricing, markup strategies
for inventory items and services that have a direct cost, margin pricing strategies and how that can be
applied, price increase strategies and protocols and lastly the cost of not knowing or not having a pricing
strategy. With all of the changes we have had in the marketplace over the recent years with regard to
online retailers as well as COVID some of the old set pricing strategies likely have changed or need to be
updated. In this program we will discuss some of the changes and how we can create a strategy that
keeps practices both profitable and competitive based on their mission.

courses.title: Dermatology in practice today
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian/technician with practical information on the current thoughts on diagnosis and management of common canine and feline dermatologic problems that they encounter in their daily practice. Dr. Outerbridge will emphasize the diagnosis of common problems, along with appropriate clinical management. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of diagnosis and management available for their patients.

courses.title: Purina Institute Global Summit 2026 (On Demand)
courses.description:
Proactive, Not Reactive: Changing the Care Paradigm
Veterinary medicine is experiencing a pivotal shift as pet owners place growing importance on the human-animal bond and expect more personalized, preventive veterinary care. This shift offers veterinarians an opportunity to move from reactive, illness-focused interventions to proactive, long-term preventive care that supports better outcomes and longer, healthier lives for pets. What was once conceptual is now essential - practical, urgent, and increasingly achievable.
The Purina Institute Global Summit 2026 brings together global leaders in veterinary medicine, nutrition science, behavioral science, and human health care. Over two days of evidence-based presentations, experts will share the latest research, practical frameworks, and communication strategies that help veterinary teams strengthen client relationships and deliver more effective preventive care plans.
In accordance with Purina Institute policy, this event will not include any product or brand promotion.

courses.title: The Acid Test: HPP and Lactic Acid For Raw Food Safety
courses.description: Considering the health risks associated with raw meat pet foods to pets and humans, High Pressure Processing (HPP) has shown promise in significantly reducing pathogens like Salmonella, E. coli STEC, and L. monocytogenes refrigeration. Since L. monocytogenes is more resistant to HPP, further formulation and process optimization are needed to ensure long-term safety. Chicken based raw diet pet food was inoculated with 7-8 log CFU/g cocktails of Salmonella spp., E. coli STEC or L. monocytogenes and stored at 4*C for 24 hours before the addition of either 0.7% or 1.0% w/v lactic acid fermentate (LAF) and HPP treated at 586 MPa for 2, 3 and 4 min after 24 or 72 hours storage at 4*C. HPP treated products were stored frozen up to 21 days and analyzed microbiologically. This study clearly demonstrates that when both LAF and HPP are employed, a full 5-log reduction of Salmonella spp., E. coli STEC, and L. monocytogenes is consistently achieved. The use of LAF appears to be instrumental in enhancing the lethality of the treatment. Qualitative enrichment further highlights that LAF not only boosts the immediate log reduction but also contributes to a more comprehensive inactivation profile during post-HPP frozen storage. The optimal combination in this study was found to be 1% LAF with HPP at 586 MPa for 4 minutes. The combo hurdles not only maximize pathogen inactivation but also provide both formulation and processing controls, serving as a robust strategy against potential re-growth during storage.

courses.title: RVG Symptom Masterclass: Itching Edition
courses.description:
This three-part lecture series focuses on improving diagnostic accuracy and clinical reasoning in small animal dermatology, specifically addressing acute and chronic pruritus in dogs and cats. The program emphasizes pattern recognition, logical case progression, common diagnostic failure points, and strategic management of chronic itch.
Rather than focusing on pharmacologic details or long-term allergy management plans, this course strengthens early diagnostic classification and clinical strategy to reduce misdiagnosis, inappropriate escalation of therapy, and unresolved chronic cases.
Participants will leave with improved confidence in distinguishing common pruritic patterns in dogs and cats and in managing chronic itch cases using structured clinical reasoning.

courses.provider: NEW JERSEY ASSOCIATION FOR BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH
courses.title: 2026 3Rs Sharing Conference
courses.description: The 2026 3Rs Sharing Conference, our 10th 3Rs conference, will include a variety of content addressing issues related to the refinement, reduction, and replacement of animals in biomedical research. This year's conference will include a variety of 3Rs content with a focus on improving rigor and translatability in biomedical research through the robust incorporation of the 3Rs. We will explore opportunities for the robust incorporation of 3Rs in institutional research, as well as the use of machine learning and new technologies to advance rigor and translation of laboratory animal research. Presentations will address the use of current and emerging technologies to help guide future drug development strategy to advance next steps. In addition, the conference will discuss study design, animal methodology, and, as always, best practices to promote laboratory animal welfare for a variety of species.

courses.title: Pet Therapeutic Nutrition Coach Certification
courses.description:
This sequel to our Pet Nutrition Coach certification will provide therapeutic pet nutrition education for the veterinary healthcare team. The goal is to empower and enable veterinary professionals with an understanding of the importance and application of nutrition in managing
disease conditions in dogs and cats.

courses.title: Compassion Fatigue 101: What Veterinary Professionals Need to Know
courses.description:
Compassion fatigue is quickly becoming a term that members of the veterinary community are becoming familiar with. While the awareness of compassion fatigue is increasing, how to notice, prevent, and overcome the affliction remains a seeming mystery. In this 2-hour course, you will learn strategies, tools, principles, and tactics for preventing compassion fatigue, recognizing it, and overcoming it.
This course is intended for veterinary professionals of all roles and will cover the basics of compassion fatigue along with specific strategies for combating compassion fatigue.
The first half of the course features mental health professional Dr. Barry Feldman, and the second half of the course is a discussion between Dr. Feldman, Dr. Hawley (DVM), and Renee Machel (veterinary technician).
This course is going to provide you with much of what is needed to cultivate and maintain a life and veterinary career that is free of compassion fatigue!
If you're passionate about veterinary medicine and if you want to enjoy your career mentally and emotionally then we highly suggest that you take this course. Your ability to understand and prevent compassion fatigue will be directly related to your level of resentment, animosity, and regret about the veterinary profession and your job!
By the end of this course, you will feel confident and competent in your ability to recognize and prevent compassion fatigue.

courses.title: Updates on Elbow OA: What You Need to Know from Prevention to Treatment
courses.description: This presentation offers a comprehensive overview of canine elbow osteoarthritis (OA), from understanding its developmental causes - such as elbow dysplasia, incongruity, and humeral intracondylar fissures - to practical approaches for diagnosis and both surgical and non-surgical management. Emphasis is placed on early recognition through observation, palpation, and imaging, as well as on building an individualized multimodal treatment plan. Rehabilitation, therapeutic exercise, NSAID therapy, intra-articular treatments, and environmental modifications are discussed.

courses.title: Conventional Embryo Flushing Training Course
courses.description:
Conventional Embryo Flushing Training Course
Topics covered during this 4-day course are Embryo Transfer, Other topics include nutrition, protocols, donor selection, donor and recipient selection, grading of embryos, freezing, thawing and transfer of embryos. During this course students will have a combination of classroom, lab, and chute time with live cattle. (Thawing and Implanting Included)

courses.provider: COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE, UTAH STATE UNIVERSITY
courses.title: Mountainlands Utah Veterinary Summit 2025
courses.description: Continuing education event for veterinarians and veterinary technicians in the state of Utah and surrounding areas. Hosted by Utah State University College of Veterinary Medicine and Utah Veterinary Medical Association. Topics ranging over small and large animal practice, medical and non-medical topics.

courses.title: Managing common medical problems in practice
courses.description: Dr. Twedt will present a complete discussion of the many common gastro-intestinal problems that he encounters in his referral practice. It is Dr Twedts intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of these common problems- both canine and feline. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common gastro-intestinal diseases and disorders.

courses.title: Vitamins in Equine Diets
courses.description: This course aims to provide veterinarians with the tools they need to understand vitamins in equine diets, and apply this knowledge to formulating diets for their clients.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Hindlimb Lameness and Diagnostic Analgesia When Horses Dont Read the Rule Book
courses.description:
In most horses diagnosing the cause of hindlimb lameness is straightforward lameness is abolished by diagnostic analgesia and diagnostic imaging reveals significant pathology. However not all horses read the rule book and reaching a conclusive diagnosis in these cases can be a real challenge even to the most experienced clinician.
Topics that will be debated by an international panel of experts consisting of lameness clinicians and radiologists include
Unexpected response to diagnostic analgesia lameness that does not improve or gets worse after diagnostic analgesia
How to deal with the dangerous horse
Approach to multilimb lameness
The role of advanced diagnostic imaging in diagnosing challenging hindlimb lameness
What shall we do when the diagnostic imaging results dont match clinical findings and the results of diagnostic analgesia
When the cause of hindlimb lameness is not in the hindlimb

courses.title: Innovations in Small Animal Surgery
courses.description: In this webinar, attendees will explore various techniques and medical devices used in surgical procedures performed in small animals.

courses.title: When Words Fail, Numbers Talk (On Demand Webinar)
courses.description: In this lecture participants will learn to use two tools developed in partnership with the University of Tennessee to determine ideal body weight for dogs and cats: morphometric measurements and body fat indexing

courses.title: VetQuest Travel CE Brachycephalic Conference Nashville 2026
courses.description: These lectures will be over 3 days and cover topics related to brachycephalic anesthesia, surgery, and ophthalmology.

courses.title: Top 3 Technology Strategies to Address Modern Veterinary Practice Challenges
courses.description: In today's fast evolving veterinary landscape, practices are challenged to do more with less and serve more clients, deliver better care, and remain financially sound, all while navigating staffing shortages and growing client demands. This session will highlight the tangible benefits veterinary professionals can unlock by adopting a modern, connected approach to their workflows. Attendees will explore how streamlining key touchpoints across the care journey, from pre appointment preparation to post-visit follow up can lead to significant time savings, enhanced client satisfaction, and improved patient outcomes. Discover how leading practices are boosting profitability, creating operational consistency, and standing out in a crowded marketplace by aligning their teams, tools, and processes around efficiency and service excellence. Whether you are a veterinarian, technician, or practice manager, this session offers practical insights to help your team focus on what matters most, delivering high quality, compassionate care while building lasting loyalty with your clients.

courses.title: Change Management
courses.description: Leadership and professional development training focused on change management strategies for veterinary professionals. This course will provide practical tools for communication, adaptability, team engagement, and leading organizational change within veterinary healthcare environments.

courses.title: Missoula Fall 2025 DVM Symposium
courses.description: This meeting will offer a comprehensive overview of the latest developments in oncology and critical care, highlighting breakthroughs in cancer diagnostics, treatment strategies, and recovering from CPR in small animals. We will discuss new and current medications that can enhance patient care in critical cases.

courses.title: Reach for Zen: New Relief for Dogs with Atopic Dermatitis_0.5CE
courses.description: Controlling allergies in dogs can be frustrating for veterinarians and clients. This presentation will introduce a new treatment that provides effective, continuous relief from pruritus and skin inflammation. By exploring expert management guidelines for allergic dermatitis and the concept of clinical remission for atopic dogs, attendees will learn how to achieve more Zen for a variety of allergic patients.

courses.title: Help! Troubleshooting in the Real World (On Demand)
courses.description: Achieving successful weight loss in pets can be challenging, even with the best-laid plans. In this 30-minute webinar, we will tackle common obstacles veterinarians face in real-world weight management cases, from poor owner compliance to medical conditions that hinder progress. Through practical case-based discussions, we will explore troubleshooting strategies, including adjusting caloric intake, selecting appropriate diets, overcoming behavioral feeding challenges, and managing multi-pet households. By the end of this session, veterinarians will have a toolkit of solutions to help patients stay on track and achieve sustainable weight loss

courses.title: Surgery and Diagnostic Imaging with Katy Townsend and Andrew Gendler
courses.description: Earn CE on Diagnostic Imaging and Surgery

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Dystocia & Foaling Emergency Management - Considering Options & Consequences
courses.description: Join our international panel of multidisciplinary experts consisting of an obstetricians soft tissue surgeon and neonatologist who will discuss management approaches for equine dystocia. Different strategies and tips and tricks will be discussed with an emphasis on rapid resolution of dystocia and optimal survival for mare and foal. Having faced a large number and variety of parturition challenges the highly experienced specialists will contribute their unique viewpoints providing a global perspective on the topic. Skilled in controlled vaginal delivery fetotomy and cesarean section bthis team is prepared to address your worst case scenario for foaling that has gone wrong

courses.title: Next Level Dentistry for the Family Practitioner:Finding Confidence with Advanced Extractions, ONF Repair, and Retained Roots
courses.description: This two-day course is designed to provide resources and confidence regarding challenging and worrisome extractions. A primarily lab based, hands-on, tailored lab will focus on the techniques and thought processes necessary to undertake the more advanced dental extractions. Participants will practice the individualized surgical techniques used when repairing oronasal fistulas, retrieving retained root segments, and extraction of multi-rooted teeth, maxillary molars, with careful extraction of the mandibular canine.

courses.title: Approaching New Murmurs in Asymptomatic Dogs
courses.description: The program will focus on how to stage and treat dogs with acquired heart disease (particularly focusing on degenerative valve disease) while being cognizant of client financial concerns. If there is time, we will also discuss new acquired murmurs in cats.

courses.title: Feline Fine 101: Protective Emotions, De-escalation and Sedation Techniques in the feline patient
courses.description: Learn to understand positive and negative emotions cats portray in the clinic. Understand these emotions are NORMAL, and how to safely navigate these appointments working with cats.

courses.title: The Art of Euthanasia - ON DEMAND
courses.description: The euthanasia appointment is unparalleled in emotion and sentiment. There are few things in veterinary medicine, or life moreover, that require as many outward displays of empathy, compassion, and commiseration from a doctor. The tone of voice, delivery of words, bedside manner with both patient and client, and the medical procedure itself become a delicate dance around death that doctor and staff should carefully choreograph and continually improve.

courses.title: Cranial Cruciate Disease 101 - Diagnostics, Management, and Care
courses.description: Cranial Cruciate Disease 101 - Diagnostics, Management, and Care is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: DEA Registrant Responsibilities
courses.description: Becoming the DEA registrant of record at a facility carries significant written and implied responsibilities. While some registrants may choose to personally oversee every compliance task, others may delegate specific duties to trained associates or facility team members. Regardless of the approach, it is essential to have a thorough understanding of all required obligations to make informed decisions. Ultimately, state officials and the DEA hold the registrant accountable for any compliance deficiencies or errors, reinforcing the importance of diligent oversight and adherence to regulatory requirements. This course is designed to help registrants know what is expected of them so they can better prepare for regulatory inspections, and ensure smooth audits.

courses.title: Managing Complexities in Internal Medicine: Focus on Aging Canine and Feline Patients
courses.description: This EUVETCE Experiences seminar is meticulously crafted to equip veterinarians and technicians, with practical and contemporary knowledge on managing intricate internal medicine challenges in aging feline and canine patients. This seminar focuses on a practical approach to adrenal disease, and investigating and managing hypercalcemia. It presents a species-specific perspective on thyroid disease, examines common neoplasias in the elderly pet, including management strategies, discusses idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, chronic hepatitis, and addresses inappetence, nausea, and vomiting, including the selection of feeding tubes. Furthermore, the seminar provides up-to-date insights on managing complex comorbidities, an introduction to the cardiorenal syndrome, and engages in a discussion on the latest Antimicrobial stewardship 2026 guidelines. Additionally, the seminar concludes with a group discussion on end-of-life care.

courses.title: Chronic Pain Management in the Senior Dog
courses.description:
Chronic pain management in canine patients often involves a multimodal
approach, combining pharmacologic agents alongside lifestyle changes, environmental aides, and
other physiotherapy-related modalities. This one-hour lecture will focus on chronic pain management
from a pharmacologic standpoint, specifically covering multiple drug classes and their utility in the
chronic pain patient. Specific coverage of newer canine products, such as Librela
and Galliprant will be included. Supporting literature as well as clinical efficacy will be
discussed for all drug classes, and recommendations for drug combinations and contingency plans
will be emphasized during this discussion.

courses.title: Hospice: Symptom Management - ON DEMAND
courses.description:
The program overview is broken down into each individual lecture. The first session will review new additions to the feline and canine pain management toolbox. This includes a new assessment tool for acute pain in cats, drugs for acute pain management in cats and monoclonal antibodies for alleviation of pain related to osteoarthritis in dogs and cats.
The next session will discuss ketamine's role as a perioperative agent and its potential role for treating chronic (maladaptive) pain. Many clinicians are giving low doses subcutaneously to animals with long term pain and the evidence for this practice will be discussed.
Next will be a session to describe the differences between nausea, vomiting and retching and describe pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic approaches to treatment. There are multiple causes of inappetence in dogs and cats and this session will review these and discuss the rational approach to incorporating capromorelin into a treatment plan. Key acupuncture points used to prevent vomiting and to stimulate appetite will be discussed.
Afterwards we will focus on GOLPP - Geriatric Onset Laryngeal Paralysis and Polyneuropathy, which affects a large population of dogs but sadly many go undiagnosed, or if diagnosed, do not have access to optimal treatment options. Owners require education on the treatment options so they can make informed decisions and regardless of what they choose (surgical or non-surgical). We as veterinarians should be familiar with the course of clinical disease, how to discuss options with owners, deliver appropriate interventions or where to refer these patients.
The next session will focus on the many environmental management tips that can help improve mobility as well as quality of life, but owners are often unaware of the products and strategies available to them. Being aware of the many options to provide to owners is important in improving quality of life in these hospice patients.
Osteoarthritis (or degenerative joint disease) is

courses.title: Performance Horse Nutrition
courses.description: This course presents the nutritional management of performance horses, beginning with a review of the anatomy and physiology of the equine digestive system, nutrient requirements, and nutritional evaluation of horses. Optimal performance horse diet formulation will then be discussed, with emphasis on special nutritional considerations for equine athletes, including provision of digestible energy, current research and nutritional strategies for the support of muscle development and recovery, and prevention of digestive disturbances.

courses.title: From Detection to Diagnosis: Mastering Cancer Screening in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: In this comprehensive webinar, explore the latest in cancer screening and diagnostic innovations with Dr. Sue Ettinger. This session will equip you with cutting-edge advancements and practical applications for cancer screening in veterinary practice. Dr. Sue will dive into the details regarding the NuQ Vet Cancer Test designed to detect systemic cancers such as lymphoma and hemangiosarcoma at early stages and its capability to identify additional cancer types. She will also touch on how to use in-house testing with the Element i+, which can provide results in just 6 minutes, and introduce the Cadet BRAF test, a noninvasive urine test specifically aimed at detecting and monitoring urothelial carcinoma in dogs. Real-world case studies will underscore how these tests can be integrated into practice to enhance early detection and patient care.

courses.title: From Anatomy to Abnormality: Navigating Small Animal Pulmonary Radiographs
courses.description: This course offers an in-depth, systematic review of small animal pulmonary radiographic anatomy, covering both normal and pathological states. It guides participants through identifying common diseases as they appear radiographically, enhancing diagnostic accuracy in clinical settings. Through detailed explanations, attendees will learn to distinguish between normal anatomical variations and pathological findings, as well as recognize disease manifestations and their unique radiographic patterns.

courses.title: Building Resilience in Veterinary Healthcare: Actionable Exercise and Nutrition Strategies for Career Longevity
courses.description: This interactive course is tailored to meet the unique physical and nutritional demands faced by veterinarians and their healthcare teams. Participants will gain practical insights and science-backed strategies on exercise and nutrition that are easy to adopt and aim to enhance durability, energy levels, and resilience. This session is designed to provide immediate, actionable steps, helping attendees integrate small but impactful habits into their daily routine for sustainable health and career success.

courses.title: The Basics of Small Intestinal Surgery: Enterotomy, Resection and Anastomosis
courses.description: This webinar will focus on intra-operative decision making and specific surgical techniques for enterotomy and resection and anastomosis of the small intestine in dogs and cats. Procedures that minimize the risk of dehiscence and other complications will be emphasized. Discussion will also include how much bowel can be resected, reinforcement of the repair site, antibiotic protocol, and special considerations for different conditions such as intestinal biopsies, linear foreign bodies, intussusception, and intestinal neoplasia.

courses.title: ON-DEMAND - 25th VSC Veterinary Education Conference
courses.description:
This course is a recording of the 25th VSC Veterinary Education Conference and will be offered On-demand.
The 25th Annual VSC Veterinary Education Conference will provide 6 hours of continuing education on separate learning tracks for both technicians an veterinarians. The lectures on the tech side will cover Feline Respiratory Disease; Cardiomyopathy in Cats; the Treatment of GI Lymphoma in Cats; Urethral Obstruction in Cats; Rehabilitation for Senior Dogs; Difficult Anesthetic Recovery; Complete Urinalysis for the Lab; Troubleshooting Difficult Anesthetic Recovery and the removal and treatment of anal tumors. The lectures for Veterinarians will cover the following: Troubleshooting Difficult Anesthetic Recovery; A Case Study on Bubbles (a difficult recovery); the removal and treatment of anal tumors; Rehabilitation in Senior Dogs; Screening for Cardiac Disease in Cats; Advances in the Treatment of Chronic Kidney Disease; Fly Catcher Syndrome in Dogs; Understanding Soft Tissue Sarcoma's; Updates in Treatments of Lymphoma in Dogs and Cats; An update on domestic violence and what to look for in animal abuse cases and Using CT Scans to Diagnosis Medical Problems.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Neoplasia of the Eyelids and Globe incl enucleation techniques and tips
courses.description:
Neoplasia of the eye and eyelids are common and can have a significant effect on vision, comfort, and systemic health in dogs and cats. Join us for this interesting panel discussion bringing together multidisciplinary experts from around the world to unpack and explore this topic. Amongst many other points, we will discuss laser ablation versus surgical removal of intraocular tumours and different therapeutic approaches for eyelid neoplasia in dogs including mass debulking with cryoablation versus complete surgical excision. Various approaches and options for treating cats with diffuse iris melanoma and mast cell tumours will be reviewed. Recent advancements in the use of advanced imaging techniques to assist in the clinical management of ocular surface masses will be presented.
Additionally, the experts will share their surgical tips and tricks relating to enucleation to ensure a good cosmetic result as well as fast healing time with lowest risk of complications. Questions and queries from the attendees will be welcome.

courses.title: Its Not Just a Phase Mom: The 4 Phases of Anesthesia
courses.description: This presentation will cover the 4 phases of anesthesia: premedication, induction, perioperative and recovery. It will cover common anesthetic considerations, drugs, analgesia and monitoring needed for each phase in order to ensure your patient has the safest anesthesia possible.

courses.title: Snowbird Veterinary CE May 2025
courses.description: This course will cover feline and canine dermatology for the general practitioner. Additionally, there will be an in-depth review of common challenges of radiology in general practice.

courses.title: Rational Approach to Chronic Diarrhea in Dogs
courses.description: Attendees will gain practical insight on the most recent categorization of chronic enteropathies in dogs with a focus on food-responsive enteropathies, corticosteroid-responsive enteropathies, antibiotic-responsive enteropathies, and non-responsive enteropathies. The webinar will be case-based to highlight practical tips for rapid differentiation of the different types of chronic enteropathy. In addition, the seminar will highlight the limited role of antimicrobials in most dogs with chronic enteropathy, the side-effects of injudicious antimicrobial administration, and how to determine when antimicrobials are warranted.

courses.title: Guided steps on echocardiography
courses.description: This course is designed to provide general veterinary practitioners with a solid foundation in small animal echocardiography. By the end of the program, participants will understand the different echocardiographic modes, along with their potential sources of error and limitations, and will be able to obtain the main right and left parasternal views. The course also aims to equip veterinarians with the skills to recognize the primary indications for performing echocardiography and to carry out a basic to intermediate-level assessment in a systematic and consistent manner. Finally, practitioners will learn to identify and interpret the most important echocardiographic findings associated with the most common cardiac and pericardial diseases in dogs and cats, enabling them to formulate a diagnosis using a structured approach.

courses.title: How CSRs Can Save 6+ Hours a Day
courses.description: Get tips to shorten call times. Set up text and email templates to reply to common client questions. Identify ways to sort and organize emails. Use online forms to gather client information before appointments. Discover ways to streamline checkout.

courses.title: How I manage common medical problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with common medical problems. The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common medical diseases with emphasis on endocrine, gastro-intestinal, cardiac and urinary problems. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to differentiate, diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series: Oral Exam
courses.description: The opening session of the series will provide a strong foundation in the fundamentals of the oral exam, beginning with the instruments and equipment needed, along with proper patient positioning for dental procedures. Attendees will review dental anatomy in detail, including tooth structure, the components of the periodontium, and surrounding paradental structures, before learning the tooth numbering system and root configurations. Malocclusions will be introduced, and a step-by-step demonstration will highlight how to conduct a thorough oral exam in just five to seven minutes.

courses.title: Insightful.vet 2025
courses.description: Insightful.vet brings together practice owners and managers in an intimate setting where they can connect, learn, and apply new knowledge to help their hospitals achieve their vision of success.

courses.title: ECC, it's all Greek to Me;Emergency & Critical Care Medicine: Foundations Through Advanced Practice
courses.description:
15-Hour Continuing Education Series for Small Animal Veterinarians and Vet Nurses
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION:
This 15-hour continuing education program provides small animal veterinarians with a progressive, clinically relevant understanding of small animal emergency and critical care. Delivered by Dr. Christina Fernandez, DVM, DACVECC, MRCVS, this course builds from foundational concepts, such as triage, stabilization, and early diagnostics, to advanced ECC topics including shock optimization, pediatric emergency management, trauma, respiratory emergencies, transfusion principles, and urgent toxicology case
management. Attendees will learn evidence-based approaches for emergencies commonly encountered in small animal practices.

courses.title: Antibiotics, probiotics, and fecal transplant for canine microbiome restoration (Anytime course)
courses.description: Participants will learn about diseases that have been associated with alterations in the microbial composition of the canine gut and current methods of manipulating the microbiome. Topics include the use of antibiotics and their consequence on the canine microbiome and the efficacy of probiotics. This course also includes in-depth look at fecal microbiome transplants (FMT), including donor selection and screening; protocols for processing, storage, and delivery of FMT; risks and limitations; and other common questions.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Bit by Bit: Unravelling the Influence of Bridles and Bits on Welfare & Performance
courses.description:
y Clayton BVMS, PhD, DACVSMR, FRCVS - Private Consultant, USA
PANEL DISCUSSION DESCRIPTION
Bits and bridles have been used and developed over thousands of years. From bit related lesions, so-called bridle lameness to the impact on performance, understanding the influence of bits and bridles and having the skillset to identify and troubleshoot issues is essential for the equine vet. Four distinguished clinicians and researchers explore the relationship between bridles and bits with equine performance and welfare. The panel will appraise the evidence base and share their experiences on how issues relating to the bridle or bit can manifest. They will collectively explore when and how to intervene, and how practitioners could apply an evidence-based approach to optimizing performance and welfare. Topics explored will include:
Bit induced lesions a logical approach to evaluating and decision making for bit adjustment
The impact of bridle and bit design and or fit on performance
Going bitless what do we know?
Exploring the tack-rider interface through the relationship between rein tension and kinematics

courses.title: Eyes, ears & beyond
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients presented to their clinic with a dermatologic or ocular problem. The combination of a Dermatologist and an Ophthalmologist will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Hypercortisolism (Cushing's Disease) in Dogs
courses.description:
Section 1 will explore some of the less common clinical signs that suggest the presence of hypercortisolism. The array of available diagnostic tests and tools and their application and accuracy in various situations will be presented.
Section 2 will focus on the treatment of hyperadrenocorticism using trilostane. Monitoring strategies, including the use of the pre-medication plasma cortisol levels, will be explained.

courses.title: Spay-Neuter Research Review: Evaluating the Evidence (ON DEMAND)
courses.description:
This continuing education session provides a comprehensive and critical
review of the current scientific literature on the health impacts of spay and neuter
(gonadectomy) in dogs and cats. The program examines benefits, risks, and controversies
associated with sterilization, with an emphasis on breed, age, sex, and size-specific outcomes.
Drawing from landmark studies including the UC Davis cohort, the Golden Retriever Lifetime
Study, and Banfield Health data, participants will explore correlations between spay-neuter and
the incidence of orthopedic disorders, neoplasia, urinary incontinence, and longevity. The
session also addresses biases and limitations in existing research, helping attendees apply an
evidence-based approach to sterilization decision-making.

courses.title: The Purr-fect Balance of Nutrition and Weight Management in Cats ON-DEMAND
courses.description: Feline obesity is a common and preventable nutritional disorders in veterinary medicine. This lecture will provide an overview of the pathophysiology of obesity, emphasizing the metabolic, hormonal, and behavioral factors that contribute to excessive weight gain. This presentation will review the nutritional requirements and formulation principles underlying effective feline weight loss strategies, including caloric restriction, macronutrient balance, and satiety management. The session will also examine commercially available therapeutic diets, highlighting their key nutritional features, indications, and clinical outcomes. By integrating physiological understanding with practical dietary planning, participants will be equipped to develop individualized and sustainable weight management programs for feline patients.

courses.title: Urology Unleashed: From Medicine to Surgery
courses.description: In this seminar we will review the clinical spectrum of urological diseases amenable to interventional procedures We will review traditional treatment modalities while also reviewing novel treatments such as subcutaneous ureteral bypass placement and laser lithotripsy We will also be joined by a Hills representative who will discuss the nutritional management of urinary stones

courses.title: Top 5 Human Medications Ingested by Pets
courses.description: This course covers the top 5 human medications most commonly ingested by pets. Mechanism of action, clinical signs, and general treatment recommendations for these medications will be discussed.

courses.title: How Immunotherapy Can Make a Difference for Your Patients
courses.description: Osteosarcoma accounts for up to 85 percent of all primary bone tumors in dogs. Yet, there have been relatively few advancements in treatment options to improve patient outcomes. Until now, treatment options have been limited to therapeutic amputation to relieve pain and remove tumor burden. Without further medical intervention such as 4-6 dose carboplatin, median survival time for dogs with no metastatic disease at diagnosis has been shown to be 134 days -4 months. With carboplatin, median survival time has been shown to be 9 months. The American Cancer Society website defines Immunotherapy as treatment that uses certain parts of the immune system to fight diseases such as cancer. Immunotherapies that have achieved considerable success in the human health arena include checkpoint inhibitors and adoptive cell therapies such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapies and TIL (tumor infiltrating lymphocytes). These are finally becoming available in veterinary medicine. In this program we will discuss the history and background of immunotherapy development, learn how to identify and distinguish between current cancer immunotherapy technologies, and discuss the conduct of the ELIAS Cancer Immunotherapy adoptive cell therapy protocol.

courses.title: Managing common gastro-intestinal problems
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with a gastro-intestinal problem. The combination of two world renowned Gastro-intestinal Internal Medicine Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Becoming a Dream Team
courses.description: This course covers a non-medical, interactive presentation/training to educate veterinarians, veterinary technicians, veterinary nurses and other professional veterinary staff on communication skills and people management skills to enhance their interactions with other team members and to provide optimized care for their patients.

courses.title: Managing the Brachycephalic patient
courses.description: Ever since Winston took home the trophy at Westminster, you have been seeing a lot of Frenchies, not to mention all of their smooshed-faced friends. Those short noses, bulgy eyes, and prickly skin are keeping you busy. This all-new seminar will focus on recognition and management of common clinical problems associated with all the brachycephalic breeds that you see in your daily practice. The combination of an Internist, a Dermatologist, and an Ophthalmologist is sure to provide you with plenty of practical information that you can put into use as soon as you return to your hospital.

courses.title: Evaluating Brachycephalic Obstructive Airway Syndrome (BOAS) Dogs in General Practice
courses.description: With over 200 articles published on BOAS in the last 10 years, there is a vast amount of information worth reviewing. This webinar will discuss using flexible and rigid endoscopy to evaluate key areas of the BOAS respiratory system and discuss the validity of currently recommended therapies. Pre- and post-operative therapies will be briefly discussed as well as common surgical procedures, and how to select an appropriate patient.

courses.provider: SCHOOL OF VETERINARY MEDICINE, FAC OF MED SCI, UNIV W INDIES
courses.title: Small animal Soft tissue surgery Webinar
courses.description:
This webinar will consist of two one-hour lectures delivered via zoom platform. The lectures will be delivered by a Diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Surgeon. The primary purpose of the webinar is to improve the surgical skills of the veterinary clinicians with two of the most encountered problems, namely, gastrointestinal surgery and cystotomy in dogs. The objectives are:
1. To educate Veterinarians about the management of gastrointestinal surgical affections and urolithiasis.
2. To improve knowledge, self-confidence, and technical competence for managing surgical repair.
3. To provide clear knowledge of the deleterious effects of each condition.
4. To demonstrate knowledge of the surgical principles and planning the relevant treatments
5. To attain the competency in the said surgical procedures by learning important tips

courses.title: Part 1: The Artistry to Ophthalmic Surgery. Part 2: Acute Blindness: Glaucoma, Retinal Detachments, Optic Neuritis and SARDS
courses.description:
Part I: In the first part of this seminar, we will review the basics of ophthalmic surgery, including instrumentation, techniques, and important clinical pearls. The surgeries discussed will be geared towards a general practitioner/emergency veterinarian. Attendees will be presented with images and videos to help guide appropriate surgical intervention.
Part II: In the second part of this seminar, we will discuss the most common causes of acute blindness, including etiology, diagnosis, and therapeutic recommendations.

courses.provider: BEHAVIOURAL MEDICINE, ATLANTIC VETERINARY COLLEGE, UPEI
courses.title: Behaviour at the Beach - Karen Overall AVC UPEI
courses.description: This course provides 4.5 days of lectures an evidence based case discussions on clinical behavioural medicine. Because of this emphasis on questions and cases, this course is suitable for veterinarians ranging from novices through those who see behavioural medicine cases in practices. Our goal is to give practicing veterinarians the tools to help care for their patients' mental health at the same level they care for their physical health throughout their lifetimes. Behavioural complaints and problems remain the biggest cause of pet death and relinquishment. Early intervention at both the general practice and specialty practice level is essential, but you have to know what to do. Special focus is on taking an informative history, understanding behavioural pharmacology and using it effectively, and understanding and treating a range of conditions driven by anxiety and fear.

courses.title: Feline Abdominal Ultrasound Workshop
courses.description: This is an immersive two-day workshop focused on feline abdominal ultrasonography. Morning lectures cover image optimization, scanning technique, and interpretation of feline abdominal anatomy, using canine ultrasound as a comparative reference. Afternoon lab sessions provide extensive hands-on practice with live feline models, guided by experienced sonographers from diverse clinical backgrounds.

courses.title: Guided steps on abdominal ultrasound
courses.description: This course is designed for general veterinary practitioners seeking to enhance their diagnostic capabilities through the effective use of abdominal ultrasound in canine and feline patients. With a focus on both theoretical understanding and practical application, the program offers a structured and clinically relevant approach to mastering abdominal ultrasonography in daily practice. Participants will first gain a solid foundation in ultrasound principles, including image generation, probe handling, and optimisation of settings. Emphasis will be placed on developing the ability to perform a systematic abdominal examination, ensuring a thorough and repeatable assessment of all major abdominal organs. The course will then guide participants through the normal ultrasound anatomy of the abdomen, helping them visualise, memorise, and recognise the sonographic appearance of healthy abdominal structures. This anatomical understanding serves as the basis for identifying deviations from normal and recognising pathological changes with greater confidence. Building on this knowledge, the program focuses on developing the skills required to identify key ultrasonographic findings in the most common abdominal diseases of dogs and cats. Participants will learn how to correlate ultrasound images with clinical signs and laboratory data, enabling them to formulate accurate diagnoses or generate meaningful differential diagnosis lists in a variety of clinical scenarios. Through a combination of lectures, and image interpretation sessions, this course empowers general practitioners to confidently incorporate abdominal ultrasound into their diagnostic routine, ultimately improving patient care and clinical outcomes.

courses.title: Mentee Skills for Lifelong Learning
courses.description: This online asynchronous course covers the basic skills needed by new veterinarians to be active and effective mentees. It is structured around the principles of Self Directed Learning and will teach new vets how to take ownership of their own Professional Development learning activities while working with a mentor. We will discuss how to identify and enlist mentors, how to create and utilize personal learning objectives and how to effectively evaluate one's own skills and reflect on new learning strategies to accomplish professional goals. Course participants will practice proven communication techniques that will help them make the most of their mentor-mentee relationships. The course will utilize short lectures, modeling, written assignments, journaling, role playing, and quizzes.

courses.title: Managing common surgical problems
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian with practical information on the current thoughts on the diagnosis and management of dogs and cats that present with a problem that will require surgery. Dr. Marvel will discuss her approach to management of many different surgical problems. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of management available for their patients

courses.title: Dysbiosis in Canine & Feline Chronic Enteropathies & Role of Diet Therapy (On-Demand)
courses.description:
Gastrointestinal microbiome dysbiosis is a characteristic of chronic inflammatory enteropathies (CIE) in dogs and cats. Diet therapy is a cornerstone of CIE treatment in both species, and the impact of diet on GI dysbiosis is a continuing topic of investigation.
In this presentation, we will review the fundamentals of dysbiosis in dogs and cats with CIE, as well as current evidence for diet therapy as it pertains to dysbiosis and how to practically apply this knowledge to diet selection for CIE patients.

courses.title: Procedures for Airway Problems in Brachycephalic Breeds
courses.description: The popularity of brachycephalic breeds around the world has soared, and their accompanying upper airway issues can be challenging to manage. This talk discusses the surgical techniques that are indicated following accurate characterization and grading of the upper airway. Different techniques for addressing the nares, the palate, tonsils, cuneiform processes, epiglottic cartilage, piriform recess and laryngeal ventricles will be described. The immediate post-operative and final outcome of any surgical intervention on the upper airway is dependent not only on the surgical procedures, but also on optimal pre-, intra- and post-operative care. This talk will cover preparation of the patient including drug selection to minimize reflux, and intra-operative techniques to minimize swelling and regurgitation/aspiration. It will also discuss what post-operative management can be performed in all cases, to mitigate complications.

courses.title: Navigating Generation Gaps in the Veterinary Staff
courses.description: One of greatest strengths of any team is diversity. Whether its educational level, race, gender identity or age, chances are weve worked alongside people with life experiences different from our own. This presentation will look at generational differences in the workplace including Baby Boomers, Gen X, Millennials and Gen Z. The goal of this presentation is to bridge generations together and highlight the importance of collaboration in a clinical setting.

courses.title: MAKING THE ROUTINE REMARKABLE: TURNING CLINIC CACOPHONY INTO HOSPITAL HARMONY A FEAR FREE PRESENTAT (369-39696)
courses.description: MAKING THE ROUTINE REMARKABLE: TURNING CLINIC CACOPHONY INTO HOSPITAL HARMONY A FEAR FREE PRESENTAT (369-39696) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: The Science Behind Dental Products (On-Demand)
courses.description:
Oral disease is one of the most prevalent diseases in dogs and cats. 80-85% of adult dogs and cats have some form of oral disease. Dental problems are among the top three concerns for pet owners of dogs and cats. Calculus and gingivitis are the most common conditions diagnosed by veterinarians in all ages of animals.
Successful treatment of periodontal disease requires a multi-modal approach, including thorough professional examination and periodontal therapy, and the recommendation and application of an effective home care plan. Over the years, many products have been developed and marketed for dental care in pets. The range of claims and the research evidence supporting them is highly variable, making the decision for pet owners difficult. The objective of this presentation is to assist technicians in understanding the emerging concept in decision-making, termed home-based medicine, and to apply this concept in a review of the evidence supporting various home care products for the prevention and/or treatment of periodontal disease in companion animals.

courses.title: On-Demand: Shelter Success - The Magic Formula Everyone Needs to Know
courses.description: This program provides a practical and strategic framework for effective shelter management with an emphasis on population control, humane care, and operational efficiency. Participants will explore key shelter management principles, including the Five Freedoms of animal welfare, capacity for care, length of stay optimization, and resource assessment (financial, manpower, and facility). Using real-world examples and formula-based models, the course introduces tools for evaluating and improving shelter flow, maximizing lifesaving capacity, and aligning practices with organizational mission and resources. Attendees will leave with actionable strategies to reduce crowding, increase adoptions, and improve animal and staff welfare in diverse sheltering environments

courses.title: How Early Home Toxicity Treatment Can Make Veterinarians Look Like Heroes in the ER
courses.description: Pet intoxication is one of the most common veterinary emergencies, yet current treatment paradigms often fail to address the most critical variable in successful outcomes: time to intervention. Traditional approaches rely heavily on in-clinic decontamination methods such as emesis induction, gastric lavage and activated charcoal: Procedures that are increasingly shown to be both ineffective and delayed. This presentation challenges long-standing veterinary norms and explores how immediate at-home administration of adsorbing agents like activated charcoal can dramatically improve patient outcomes, reduce toxin absorption, and enhance the effectiveness of veterinary intervention upon arrival at the hospital. Drawing parallels from human medicine's use of at-hole emergency treatments like EpiPens and Narcan, this session highlights the growing body of evidence supporting rapid home decontamination, particularly with a new, user-friendly activated carbon formulation, as well as the deficiencies of classic decontamination techniques in hospital. These interventions not only mitigate the severity of toxicosis but also help bridge the critical gap between exposure and professional care.

courses.title: A Close Look at Canine Enrichment: What, why and how?
courses.description: True enrichment goes way beyond simply providing dogs with food puzzles each day. For instance, a comprehensive enrichment strategy incorporates all types of enrichment: social, occupational, physical, nutritional, and sensory. This course will show you how to engage all the senses, as well as how to thoughtfully determine which enrichment activities are most appropriate for individual dogs, how to enrich the lives of dogs in a veterinary clinic, and those who are recovering from an injury and on restricted exercise.

courses.title: FEAR FREE DERMATOLOGY (1135-40088)
courses.description:
Dermatologic conditions, such as otitis externa, allergic dermatitis, and bacterial skin infections, are among the most common reasons clients bring patients to veterinarians. Additionally, dermatologic diseases are often chronic and recurrent, so procedures may be repeated on the same patient multiple times. This course provides tools for incorporating a Fear Free approach to common dermatologic techniques used in the clinic, including ear exams and cytology, skin scrape and cytology, and biopsy.
In addition, in-home bathing and ear treatments can also be a source of stress for both pets and clients. By providing suggestions for decreasing FAS during bathing and ear treatments, we can help increase compliance for topical therapy.
This course consists of four lessons:
Lesson 1: Classical Conditioning and Conditioned Emotional Responses
Lesson 2: The Ears: Exams and Procedures
Lesson 3: The Skin: Diagnostic Tests and Procedures
Lesson 4: Bathing: At Home and In Clinic

courses.description: This presentation goes over core and non-core vaccinations for dogs and cats per AAHA and AAFP vaccine guidelines, individual risk factors and helps determine clinic vaccination protocols. courses.description: Dental radiology is a critical and important diagnostic tool for recognizing oral pathology and developing treatment plans in the dog and cat. Common indications for dental radiology and case presentations of common problems seen clinically, followed by radiographic interpretation and treatment options will be discussed.

courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive review of transfusion medicine in small animal practice. Safe administration, monitoring, and recognition of transfusion reactions will be emphasized. Case examples highlight practical decision-making for both general practitioners and emergency clinicians. The program also reviews unconventional transfusion strategies such as auto-transfusion, Xeno transfusion, and massive transfusion protocols.

courses.title: Certified Equine Rehabilitation and Performance Veterinarian Online
courses.description:
A good veterinarian is able to diagnose the source of the lameness and get the horse back to competition quickly; a great veterinarian is able to see variations in gait and performance before they lead to lameness and correct them as well as rehabilitate the horse after injury.
In this program, we will explore how the equine athlete functions. Beginning with the powerful way the muscles, bones, and tendons work together for high-level performance we will go on to develop skills to spot small performance deficits and learn ways to correct them, and then we will investigate the etiology of injury, the process of healing, the use of rehabilitation tools and case management.
