courses.description: In this presentation, we will discuss the implications of bacteria found in a urine sediment analysis. We will cover some of the common pitfalls of accurately identifying and classifying bacteria while highlighting proper techniques and protocols, as well as walk through several confirmatory methods. Additionally, in a case-based approach we will highlight the bacteria results, the clinical significance to the patient, and the possible next steps to arriving at a diagnosis.

courses.title: Veterinary Herbal Medicine Onsite
courses.description:
Chinese Herbal Medicine (CHM) is a major branch of Chinese Medicine. Although most associate Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) with acupuncture, the majority of cases in TCM clinics in China are treated with herbs, either with acupuncture or alone, rather than with just acupuncture. In the States, more and more TVCM practitioners are following suit by incorporating herbs in their veterinary practice. CHM therapies have their historical origins with TCM and date back 4,000 years. Herbs today are prepared with the benefits of modern technology but are still guided by the historical wisdom underlying TCM. In CHM practice, herbs are used to correct imbalance underlying a disease pattern and to promote the body's ability to heal itself. Each herb has a different effect on the body and can fall under a number of classifications such as warming, cooling, sour, or bitter and can affect a variety of organs, including the liver, lungs, or heart. TCVM utilizes herbal formulas that are a combination of single-herb ingredients to treat a specific pattern of disease.
The increasing popularity of CHM lies in the fact that it is an all-natural treatment option that is generally safe and effective when prescribed correctly. An extensive body of clinical research has shown CHM to be extremely effective in treating chronic veterinary medical issues in the fields of gastroenterology, cardiology, dermatology, endocrinology, reproduction, oncology, and animal behavior. CHM is also commonly used to treat respiratory issues and sports injuries. In addition, CHM increases the quality of life for geriatric patients, especially those diagnosed with terminal cancer, as it assists the body's ability to reduce tumor size when chemotherapy may not an option. CHM can be combined with acupuncture and/or Western Medicine to enhance clinical results.

Description of the common causes and infectious agents, who often and where we commonly see each infectious agent in our canine population in north America and what available testing there is to identify the cause of disease and make treatment choices. With additional focus on prevention as a part of individual care but also for the benefit of populations of dogs

courses.title: Integrative Approach to Behavior Issues in Dogs, Cats and Birds
courses.description: This course builds upon the fundamentals of TCVM and include a new focus on the treatment of behavioral disorders with a holistic approach including Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine integrated with lifestyle recommendations for all species and science-based behavior analysis and certified professional dog training for behavior disorders in dogs when indicated. Students will learn real world implementation of an approach to Behavior through Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (including Zang-fu physiology (which element(s) is/are involved) and the importance of the TCVM Constitution in Pattern Diagnosis) and professional dog training for behavior disorders in dogs. This course will focus on commonly seen behavioral disorders in veterinary practice including separation anxiety in dogs; noise and storm phobia in dogs and cats; inter-dog, inter-cat and human-directed aggression in dogs and cats; house soiling in cats; geriatric dog and cat issues and behavioral issues in caged birds including therapies for such conditions. In addition, instructors will share clinical experience via case presentations.

courses.description: In this presentation, we will discuss the medical need for and the diagnostic value of imaging in accurately diagnosing pets' conditions. We'll talk about effective ways to educate pet owners about imaging and review best practices in communication skills that will help you increase client compliance and your practice's imaging revenue.

Understand current advancements in atopic dermatitis diagnosis, treatment and long-term case management in a very informative Archived Webinar hosted by Dr. Terri Bonenberger

The on-site portion is held on the Chi Campus. The course can be taken by small animal, mixed, and equine veterinarians. Lectures and labs cover treatment for both small animals and horses. Hands-on learning is heavily emphasized in the Tui-na course, and wet labs take up most of the on-site session. In wet labs, students can practice Tui-na techniques on live animals, and they can choose to work on either small animals (cats and dogs) or horses.

courses.description:
The Integrative Approach to Veterinary Oncology course is designed for the veterinarians wishing to integrate Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) and other integrative medicine for their cancer patients. The course teaches evidence informed approach to integrative veterinary oncology. This course discusses the use of acupuncture, herbs, nutrition, and nutraceuticals and reviews the etiology of cancer from a TCVM perspective. This course is taught by two board certified veterinary oncologists with extensive experience in the combination of TCVM and conventional therapy, and a senior Chi faculty and clinician with a TCVM Master's degree.
The course will also review common cancer and treatment protocols in general as well as include a deeper look into the mechanisms of action of anticancer herbs as well as evidence to support safety and efficacy of an integrative approach.

The general concepts of integrative veterinary medicine, including history, definitions, context, and evidence-based application are also discussed.

courses.title: Basics of Rabbit Medicine: Setting the Stage for Success in Practice
courses.description: Rabbits are one of the most common exotic mammals seen in practice, yet many clinical frustrations stem from husbandry. This session lays the groundwork for better outcomes by covering the essentials: understanding the rise in rabbit ownership, how client perception shapes care, and common pitfalls in diet, obesity, water intake, and housing. Well walk through practical husbandry counseling that actually sticks, strategies for improving clinic design to be more rabbit friendly, and how to approach a low stress physical exam from carrier to recovery. The goal is simple: set rabbits up for success before they ever get sick, and make the veterinary visit feel safe and efficient for both patient and team.

courses.title: Recordkeeping: Do You Know Where Your Controlled Drugs Are?
courses.description:
Controlled substance recordkeeping isn't just a regulatory requirement-it's a critical safeguard for your veterinary practice. In Part 2 of the controlled substance series, we dive into the essential "what, why, and how" of controlled drug documentation. From understanding the DEA inspection process to identifying common recordkeeping violations, this session will equip you with the knowledge and tools to stay compliant and confident.
Well walk through where to find federal requirements, review the full range of required records-from DEA Forms 222 and 41 to waste logs and client pickup logs-and discuss how to tailor your recordkeeping system to your practice's needs. You'll also explore the pros and cons of electronic versus paper logs, get practical template suggestions, and learn how to audit your records to ensure accuracy and completeness.
Whether you're new to controlled substance compliance or looking to tighten up your current system, this session will help you take control of your controlled drug records.

courses.title: Evaluating Automated Thrombograms
courses.description: In this module, learn about platelet parameters that are reported from automated hematology analyzers. These parameters provide a quantitative assessment of different aspects of platelets, such as platelet mass and platelet indices.

courses.title: Stones, Cysts, Cystitis: Urinary Tract Pain as a Cause of Anorexia in Guinea Pigs
courses.description: Guinea pigs with urinary tract disease often present with decreased appetite instead of typical urinary signs, making these cases easy to mistake for GI stasis. This session highlights how to identify urolithiasis, bacterial cystitis, chronic interstitial nephritis, and cystic ovarian disease as causes of anorexia in guinea pigs. Attendees will learn how to detect subtle exam clues, properly position for radiographs, and make practical medical or surgical decisions for case management. Recurrence prevention, pain management strategies, and effective owner communication will also be covered to improve long-term outcomes in these challenging cases.

courses.title: Its Sedimentary Part 3 Crystals and Miscellaneous Gems Found in Liquid Gold
courses.description: The complete urinalysis is a critical component of the minimum database. Dr. DeNicola will discuss why it's important to understand and accurately perform a urine sediment analysis. In part 3 of this 3-part series on urine microscopy, you will learn about the identification of many crystals routinely found in urine, crystals that are rarer, and other organisms and artifacts that could be found; the clinical significance of each to the patient; and possible next steps for arriving at a diagnosis.

courses.title: Integrative Veterinary Medicine for Pain Management
courses.description: The Integrative Veterinary Medicine for Pain Management course is designed for veterinarians wishing to integrate Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) and other integrative medicine for their patients. The course is a comprehensive review of the most contemporary concepts of veterinary pain management, including neurobiology, neuropharmacology, physical modalities, herbals, acupuncture, and rehabilitation therapy. Applications for pain management across a broad spectrum of clinical presentations will be presented. Relevant literature on the topic, principles of pain management, and the multimodal management of complex pain syndromes in dogs and cats will also be discussed. Information on treating pain from many different perspectives will be highlighted.

courses.title: Sit. Stay. Heal: Designing PTS Comfort with Care
courses.description: This session explores the emotional impact of pet loss, and the role veterinary professionals can play in supporting clients and each other through grief. Participants will learn how to create an environment that acknowledges and validates bereavement, enhances client loyalty, and fosters a compassionate clinic culture through a DEIB lens.

courses.title: Structural & Functional Assessment of the Equine Spine - Sacropelvic
courses.description: This course module provides the foundation needed to evaluate horses with pelvic asymmetries and sacroiliac joint pain and dysfunction. A review of the unique articular and ligamentous features of the sacroiliac joint and muscles acting on the lumbosacral junction are discussed. Biomechanical topics include muscles responsible flexion and extension of the lumbosacral joint and the structural-functional relationships of individual sacroiliac ligaments. A review of the pathological process affecting the pelvis and sacroiliac joint is presented. A detailed description of the skills needed to evaluate sacropelvic pain and dysfunction is provided. Treatment options for managing sacroiliac joint pain and dysfunction include medical and rehabilitation methods.

The three parts are titled: -Report Goals, Searching For and Running Reports -Frequently Requested Reports and Why Information Varies -Exploring Reports and custom reporting.

courses.title: Equine Acupuncture Deep Dive
courses.description: The Equine Acupuncture Deep Dive Course brings you to a higher level of understanding acupuncture and how to use acupuncture effectively in treating your equine patients. The course is intended for equine practitioners who have learned and are familiar with equine acupuncture points and respective indications.

courses.title: Common Diagnostic Issues in Pathology: Submitting Samples and Getting to Know Your Pathologist
courses.description: This presentation discusses the innovations of pathology testing and provides practices with answers to the most frequently asked questions from the IDEXX Medical Consulting Services. We will also include details on the value of proper sample submissions and benefits of open communication between the clinician and pathologist

courses.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Traumatized Immature Permanent Teeth in Dogs and Cats
courses.description:
Management of traumatized immature permanent teeth in dogs and cats presents unique clinical challenges for the veterinary practitioner. These teeth are characterized by thin dentinal walls, incomplete apical development, and unfavorable crown-to-root ratios, all of which complicate treatment planning and long-term prognosis.
This online lecture will review the principles of pulp vitality, including how to differentiate between vital and non-vital teeth based on clinical and diagnostic findings. Participants will learn to evaluate fractured immature permanent teeth and select appropriate treatment options based on fracture classification, degree of pulp exposure, and pulpal status.
Treatment strategies, including vital pulp therapy and management options for non-vital teeth, will be discussed with emphasis on preserving tooth structure and function whenever possible. Case-based examples will be used to support clinical decision-making and improve confidence in managing these challenging cases in general practice.

courses.title: Managing Itchy Pets in a Shelter Environment
courses.description: Sarcoptes (scabies) and dermatophytes (ringworm) are common in shelter environments and are considered high-risk diseases because of their contagious nature. Ruling out other underlying causes of itching is important to determining a course of action and treatment. This presentation focuses on common causes of itching, diagnostic options, sample collection methods, understanding of results, and therapeutic monitoring. Also included in the presentation is a cost-analysis case study of the 1- to 3-day polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test for Sarcoptes and dermatophytosis versus the traditional ringworm culture

courses.title: New insights into phosphate homeostasis in feline early CKD: the role of fibroblast growth factor 23
courses.description: Overview discussion of FGF-23, what it is, the relationship with CKD and how to use FGF-23 to monitor treatment in cats.

courses.title: Integrative Approach to Emergencies
courses.description: This course offers an overview of updates to the Western and TCVM approaches to common emergency medical conditions in dogs, cats, horses, ruminants, birds, and other exotic animals. Students learn how to integrate these two medical modalities for a comprehensive approach to common emergencies presented in general practice.

courses.title: The IDEXX Guide to Hematology (Module 2): The White Blood Cells
courses.description: This three-part course will help veterinary professionals gain the basic knowledge they need to understand and interpret small animal hematology results, including using an automated hematology analyzer and performing a confirmatory blood film. This second module is focused on the second component of the hemogram: the white blood cells. it also includes basic terminology, the components of the complete blood count (CBC) and common hematologic abnormalities The first module focuses on and introduction to hematology and the red blood cell and the third on platelets and the blood film.

courses.title: Structural and Functional Assessment of the Equine Spine: Cervical
courses.description: This course provides the foundation needed to evaluate horses with neck pain and dysfunction. Content includes detailed anatomical studies that describe and illustrate individual muscles within the cervical region. Biomechanical descriptions provide insights into the functional features of the cervical muscles, ligaments, articulations, and vertebrae. Detailed characterization and examples of soft tissue, neurologic, and articular pathology affecting the cervical region are provided. A structured outline is presented for comprehensive physical examination of the cervical region. Evidence-based treatment approaches are discussed based on currently available research.

courses.title: Help Avoid Anesthetic Complication
courses.description: Help Avoid Anesthetic Complications -- Run a Complete Blood Count on Every Preanesthetic Patient. Thanks to increased client awareness and compliance, preanesthetic testing is not only practical and accepted, it is also expected. The results benefit everyone as they decrease client anxiety, improve anesthetic safety, establish baseline data and increase a practice's financial health.

courses.title: Anesthesia Essentials
courses.description:
Anesthesia Essentials is a 12-hour interactive online training program designed to strengthen the knowledge and clinical decision-making skills required for safe anesthesia and sedation in veterinary patients. Designed and reviewed by board-certified anesthesiologists, this course is intended for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, veterinary nurses, and other veterinary professionals involved in anesthetic patient care.
The program follows the anesthetic process from patient assessment through recovery, with an emphasis on patient safety, physiologic understanding, clinical reasoning, and early recognition of complications. Rather than focusing on memorization of anesthetic protocols, participants learn to assess patient-specific risk, develop individualized anesthetic plans, use anesthetic equipment safely, interpret physiologic monitoring data, recognize developing problems, and select appropriate interventions.
Course content includes pre-anesthetic assessment and risk stratification; anesthesia machines and breathing systems; anesthetic and analgesic pharmacology; balanced anesthesia; development of individualized anesthetic plans; patient preparation and induction; airway management; fluid therapy; cardiovascular, respiratory, and temperature monitoring; interpretation of blood pressure, pulse oximetry, capnography, and other monitoring data; recognition and management of common anesthetic complications; and safe recovery.
The course emphasizes integration of monitoring parameters with the patient's overall clinical condition, recognition of trends and early deterioration, and identification of the physiologic causes of abnormalities. Systems-based approaches to anesthesia safety are also addressed, including equipment checks, emergency preparedness, appropriate monitoring, team communication, and structured recovery practices.
Course Overview:
Module 1 (1.5 hours): Introduction to Safe Anesthesia and Risk Management
Principles of anesthesia and sedation, a

courses.title: Blending Old and New Marketing and Client Communication Strategies
courses.description: Learn how to identify the right marketing plan for your practice based on assessment of key performance indicators, then implement and execute an effective marketing and client communication plan. Participants will leave knowing specific action steps to take to execute marketing initiatives, which will increase service utilization and attract new clients.

courses.title: Everyday Emergencies
courses.description: Vomiting patient emergencies happen 24 hours a day. Is your practice equipped to properly handle them? You don't have to be a specialty practice to successfully diagnose and treat common emergencies. Dr. Bill Saxon, a board-certified internist and emergency and critical care specialist, will review proper triage, emergency diagnostics and treatment options to better prepare your clinic to handle vomiting patient emergency

courses.title: Veterinary Anesthesia from A to Z
courses.description:
This online course provides an in-depth look at the entire perianesthetic period, from anesthesia planning and patient stabilization, premedication and induction, to the maintenance and recovery of veterinary
anesthesia patients. A review of cardiopulmonary physiology and how it is affected by anesthetic agents and adjuncts will be presented. Best-practice monitoring procedures and managing common anesthesia-
related complications will be discussed. The course also includes a detailed look at pain physiology and how best to provide ideal perioperative analgesia to veterinary patients. While this course focuses on the
care of dogs and cats, the principles described are applicable across most companion animals.

courses.title: Testing for Tick-borne Diseases: Conversations Made Easy
courses.description: With advances in technology, we are discovering new tick-borne disease (TBD) agents and have more tests available to us than ever. It is getting harder to know which patients to test, which tests to run, what to do with the results, and how to communicate this to our clients. We will review some indications for testing sick dogs, discuss the benefits of screening healthy dogs for exposure to or infection with TBD agents, and explain how to provide this information to pet owners.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: Working Up the Ruminant with Abdominal Disease
courses.description: Our clients consider any abdominal dissension "bloat" but we know there are many things other than rumen gas bloat that can cause abdominal dissension in ruminants. In this session, we will work through the process of localizing the cause of the distension and then figuring out how to move forward to definitive diagnosis and treatment. We will go through a differential list for the specific abdominal shapes, interpretation of bloodwork, and review the process and interpretation of procedures such as rumen fluid collection and evaluation and abdominocentesis.

courses.title: An Update on Management of Furcation Lesions in Dogs On Demand
courses.description: This lecture provides an update on the prognosis and management of furcation lesions in dogs. Emerging evidence suggests that teeth previously considered to have a poor prognosis may be successfully maintained with appropriate periodontal therapy. Participants will review treatment options including closed and open debridement, furcation plasty, tunneling, root resection techniques, regenerative therapies, and exodontia, with emphasis on clinical decision-making and long-term patient comfort.

courses.title: Keep the Pace: The Bradyarrhythmia Breakdown
courses.description: In this 1-hour, recorded, online VETgirl CE webinar, Dr. Gordon Peddle, DACVIM (Cardiology) will discuss pathologic bradyarrhythmias in dogs and cats. Electrocardiographic recognition of the most common bradyarrhythmias in dogs and cats will be reviewed, along with therapy options and indications for pacemaker implantation.

courses.title: Advanced TCVM Approach to Neurological Disorders
courses.description: TCVM plays a vital and indispensable role in the treatment of neurological disorders in small animals and horses. This course focuses on Pattern Diagnosis and Treatment of the most commonly encountered neurological conditions in veterinary medicine through acupuncture, herbal medicine, and Tui-na therapy

courses.title: Canine Musculoskeletal Ultrasound and US-Guided Injections Bootcamp Online
courses.description: This immersive is designed to build expertise in musculoskeletal ultrasound for accurate diagnosis and ultrasound-guided interventional procedures, with a primary focus on soft tissue injuries of the thoracic and pelvic limbs. The course features a combination of in-depth lectures, live scanning demonstrations, and hands-on practice.

courses.title: Understanding and Treating Periodontal Disease in Companion Animals - On Demand
courses.description: Periodontal Disease is defined as an infectious disease caused by plaque and the resulting inflammatory response. If left untreated, periodontal disease will progress, resulting the destruction of the structures surrounding the tooth and can contribute to systemic concerns for the pet.

courses.title: The Benefits of Screening with SDMA: What You Don't Know Can Hurt You
courses.description: The Benefits of Screening with SDMA: What You Don't Know Can Hurt You is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: When the Tinkle Gets Tough, the Tough Get Em Tinkling: How to Manage Complex Feline Urethral Obstruction
courses.description: In this lecture, we will examine the less common complications of a common disease, feline urethral obstruction. We will discuss the management of hyperkalemia, post obstructive diuresis, uroabdomen, urethral tear, and patients that you struggle to catheterize. We will discuss the mechanisms behind atrial standstill and how to manage it, and why some hyperkalemic patients may in fact be tachycardic.

courses.title: Stabilizing the Patient with Non-Traumatic Hemoabdomen
courses.description: In this lecture, we will take a case-based approach on managing the non-traumatic canine hemoabdomen patient, from initial triage and stabilization, through diagnostics, and into the operating room. Participants will gain an understanding of common cardiovascular and hemostatic disturbances in these patients and how to manage them. Beyond the physiology, we will discuss the overall approach to these patients and how to manage owner conversations and expectations.

courses.title: ECGs in your Practice
courses.description: In this webinar, you will gain understanding of electrocardiogram (ECG) generation, including the action potentials of the cardiac myocytes. We will discuss ECG use cases, including preanesthetic use cases and the percentage of ECG abnormalities noted on preoperative ECGs through IDEXX Telemedicine Consultants. We will also cover case examples of ECG abnormalities, including treatment for specific arrhythmias.

courses.title: Engaging Staff to Ensure a Successful Preventive Care Diagnostic Initiative: A Scenario-Based Course for Practice Managers
courses.description: This scenario-based course is designed to support practice managers gain the skills and confidence to successfully launch a preventive care diagnostic initiative in their hospital.

courses.title: Neonatal Calf Diarrhea
courses.description:
In this session, we will review common causes of neonatal diarrhea in calves. We will focus our time on clinical
evaluation of the sick calf, determining the need for fluid therapy, fluid therapy formulation and the use of ancillary
therapies for calf scours.

courses.title: Business Management for an Integrative Veterinary Practice
courses.description: When running your own practice management skills can be as critical as clinical skills. Business Management for an Integrative Veterinary Practice is a course designed to introduce students to all aspects of managing their own integrative practice and developing their professional skills. Students will learn from practice owners and managers with many years of experience how to organize staff, manage finances and client relationships, understand common legal issues, keep up in a changing marketplace and more while running their individual practices with maximum efficiency and profitability.

courses.title: Quiet Pain, Big Impact: Chronic Pain in Exotic Companion Mammals
courses.description: This lecture examines the often-overlooked area of chronic pain in exotic companion mammals, including rabbits, guinea pigs, chinchillas, and ferrets. Participants will learn to identify subtle signs of ongoing discomfort, understand the underlying mechanisms of persistent pain, and develop effective multimodal treatment approaches. The focus will be on common conditions and practical dosing guidelines.

courses.title: Itchy Patients: How to Set Expectations and Create Successful Client Experiences
courses.description: This course was developed with the entire practice in mind. Our goal is to provide everyone in your practice with tools to support better outcomes for itchy patients.

courses.title: Thoracic Radiology: Extrathoracic Structures
courses.description: In this archived webinar, Dr. Ringold reviews thoracic radiographs with an emphasis on extrathoracic structures. Where applicable, we will discuss the effect of image quality and the importance of positioning

courses.title: Less Stress, Better Medicine: Pain Recognition in Exotic Companion Mammals
courses.description: This session emphasizes the connection between pain recognition and low-stress handling in exotic species. Participants will develop skills in using validated tools like the Rabbit Grimace Scale, CANCRS, Bristol Pain Scale, and interpreting subtle behavioral changes in ferrets, rodents, and lagomorphs. The lecture will also explore evidence-based approaches to reduce fear and restraint-related stress in clinical settings, including handling techniques, environmental adjustments, and recovery room strategies. Attendees will leave with practical methods to improve patient welfare and increase diagnostic accuracy by minimizing stress.

courses.title: Common Food Animal Toxicants
courses.description: In this session, we will review common food animal toxicants, including nitrates, cyanide, copper, sulfur-induced polio, lead, urea and ionophores. Using photos and videos we will review clinical signs and discuss treatment options, documentation of toxicity and preventative strategies.

courses.title: Musculoskeletal Imaging: Diagnosing the Causes of Lameness
courses.description: This case series reviews orthopedic disorders of the thoracic and pelvic limbs that can present as lameness. Topics to be discussed include the University of Pennsylvania Hip Improvement Program (PennHIP) test versus the Orthopedic Foundation for Animals (OFA) hip joint scoring system, as well as elbow evaluations

courses.title: SDMA Testing: When, Why and What to do Next
courses.description: SDMA testing is not just for patients that have been diagnosed with or are suspected to have chronic kidney disease (CKD). Did you know that 81% of pets with a one or more mildly increased SDMA results had creatinine within the reference interval when SDMA was first increased? Or that half of cats and dogs had an increased creatinine within one year after a mild increase in SDMA? SDMA concentration increases with on average as little as 40% loss of functioning renal tissue as compared to approximately 75% loss before creatinine levels rise. Identifying potential changes in kidney function early and instituting proper therapy has been shown to extend patient survival. In this session we will discuss when to include SDMA in a patient profile, why monitoring SDMA is important, and next steps toward ensuring long term health in your patients.

courses.title: The IDEXX Guide to Chemistry: Endocrine System Profile
courses.description: This course includes an introduction to the endocrine system and will cover common areas of confusion when interpreting blood work. During this course, we will discuss the principal laboratory tests used to assess physiologic functions and possible diseases of the endocrine system. We will organize these tests into primary and secondary diagnostic screening panels for each of the major endocrine glands and will demonstrate the use of these diagnostic panels to characterize the presence of Cushing's syndrome, Addison's disease, diabetes mellitus, hyperinsulinism, hypo- and hyperthyroidism, and hyper- and hypoparathyroidism

courses.title: It's Sedimentary Part 2 Epithelial Cells and Casts of Thousands
courses.description: The complete urinalysis is a critical component of the minimum database. Dr. DeNicola will discuss why it's important to understand and accurately perform a urine sediment analysis. In part 2 of this 3-part series on urine microscopy, you will learn about the identification of squamous epithelial cells, nonsquamous epithelial cells, hyaline casts, and nonhyaline casts; the clinical significance of each to the patient; and the possible next steps to arriving at a diagnosis.

courses.title: What does CKD have to do with VBD?
courses.description: Two retrospective studies were performed to determine if exposure to tick-borne disease is associated with an increased risk of kidney disease. These studies identified an association between dogs with positive Lyme disease or Ehrlichia test results and an increased risk for chronic kidney disease (CKD) in endemic areas. This webinar will discuss the risks associated with tick-borne disease in your patients.

courses.title: Certified Myofascial and Manual Therapy Veterinarian Onsite
courses.description:
The Certified Myofascial and Manual Therapy program is a comprehensive course designed to train veterinarians in a wide range of manual and myofascial therapy styles and techniques. The program integrates foundational science, evidence-based practice, and extensive hands-on application to address soft tissue dysfunction, movement restriction, and pain, while promoting overall patient well-being. Participants will develop advanced palpation skills and learn to select and apply appropriate techniques based on individual patient presentation and clinical goals.
This program emphasizes real-world clinical integration, teaching veterinarians how to incorporate myofascial and manual therapy into diverse practice settings, including general practice, acupuncture/TCVM, rehabilitation and sports medicine, and integrative medicine services. In addition, the course also addresses practical considerations for building, integrating, and sustaining myofascial and manual therapy services within a successful veterinary business model.

courses.title: Tying it All Together -Pathology Case Submissions in Action
courses.description: This course reviews a case that highlights important factors in pathology sample submissions

courses.title: Rabbit Practice Essentials: Sedation, Sampling, Imaging, and Medications
courses.description: This session covers the essential practical skills needed to confidently manage rabbit patients in general practice. We will go through when and how to safely use sedation, tips for venipuncture and catheter placement, and how to build a minimal database without overhandling. Attendees will receive a clear overview of radiographic positioning that produces diagnostic images, quick interpretation tips for common lab patterns and errors, and a real-world discussion of medication routes and drug choices; focusing on what to use, what to avoid, and why. Designed as a foundational lecture, this session emphasizes efficient diagnostics, safe drug administration, and practical workflow to set the stage for successful case management.

courses.title: TCVM Palliative and End-of-Live Course
courses.description: The Certified TCVM Palliative and End-of-Life Practitioner (CTPEP) Course introduces palliative and end-of-life care as a recognized field of veterinary medicine. The integration of palliative and end-of-life care with TCVM (Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine) will give the veterinary professional more options to treat the clinical signs of disease and preserve a longer and better quality of life in pets struggling with aging, chronic and life limiting illnesses

courses.title: Integrative Approach to Equine Pain Management
courses.description: This course provides an integrative overview of equine pain mechanisms, pathophysiology, and management. Students will explore holistic approaches, including pharmacology, acupuncture, herbal medicine, medical manipulation, and rehabilitation therapy, to develop a comprehensive understanding of equine pain care and performance optimization.

courses.title: 27th Annual International Conference on TCVM Online
courses.description: The International Conference on TCVM (Annual Conference) has been conducted every year since 1999. It provides a great opportunity for veterinarians to learn from the top TCVM experts and meet TCVM practitioners from all over the world. The theme of the 27th annual International Conference on TCVM (ICTCVM) is TCVM for Feline, Exotic Animals, Behavior, and Infectious Diseases.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: Eyes and Endocrine: Recognizing Ocular and Hormonal Disease in Rabbits
courses.description: Rabbits often present with ocular disease, and many cases are missed or mismanaged without a structured diagnostic approach. This session covers practical recognition and treatment of common eye conditions, including glaucoma, dacryocystitis, infectious blepharitis, with a note on managing syphilis when procaine penicillin G is hard to obtain, conjunctival overgrowth, cataracts, corneal ulcers (superficial, deep, and indolent), lipid keratopathy, and intraocular neoplasia. The session will also include a brief overview of the most relevant endocrine conditions seen in practice, primarily adrenal disease and insulinoma, with a focus on clinical presentation and what can realistically be worked up in a general practice setting.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: Understanding Spectrum of Care
courses.description: As veterinarians struggle to keep up with the demand for veterinary services, the animal welfare field needs to embrace new ways of meeting the needs of animals and their people. Embracing a Spectrum of Care approach to common conditions is one concrete way every veterinary practitioner can play their part.

courses.title: Equine Veterinary Medical Manipulation Online
courses.description:
The Certified Medical Manipulation Practitioner Course trains and certifies licensed veterinarians in Equine Veterinary Medical Manipulation (EVMM). This program is offered exclusively to veterinarians or veterinary school students, providing them with the opportunity to learn EVMM more efficiently and effectively, while taking their skills and knowledge to a deeper level. This program is split up into 6 sessions, 3 online sessions and 3 on-site sessions.
The lab groups are small with 4-6 students per group to ensure that each student receives the maximum amount of individual attention and hands-on experience to practice EVMM. This structure ensures that students will be confident to start clinical practice after the first on-site session.

courses.title: Implementing inVue DX into Clinical Workflows
courses.description: This presentation guides veterinary teams through successfully implementing the IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer into everyday clinical workflows with a focus on blood morphology and ear cytology. It explores why adopting new technology can be challenging how inVues slide free AI supported approach improves consistency efficiency and clinical confidence and how these benefits translate into better patient care team wellbeing and client experience. Through practical workflow examples case studies and action oriented checklists attendees learn how to align doctors and staff reduce subjectivity save time and build sustainable protocols that stick in busy practices ultimately creating clarity confidence and more effective standards of care.

courses.title: Evaluating Automated Leukograms
courses.description: In this module, learn about white blood cell parameters that are reported from automated hematology analyzers and how they provide insight into both pathologic and physiologic conditions commonly encountered in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: Platelet Morphology
courses.description: In this module, learn about normal and abnormal platelet morphology. Additionally, examples of cytograms are provided to show how cytograms can be impacted by platelet morphological changes.

courses.title: Inside the Hive: Fundamental Honey Bee Biology and Beekeeping Practices for Veterinarians
courses.description: Veterinarians play an important role in the management of honey bee colony health and in advancing the health of both managed and wild bee populations. Effective engagement with this species requires a foundational understanding of honey bee biology, behavior, and husbandry. This presentation provides an introduction to core principles of honey bee biology, standard beekeeping practices, and the fundamentals of the hive inspection.

courses.title: The Basic Echocardiographic Exam
courses.description: A complete basic echocardiographic examination can provide crucial information about a patient quickly and noninvasively. This lecture will outline the requirements for a complete basic echocardiogram in dogs and cats. Time will be spent reviewing the standardized images and measurements, while highlighting common mistakes to avoid.

courses.title: Nuts and Bolts: The Why, What, and How of Getting Preventive Care Going in Your Practice
courses.description: How can preventive care work in the era of pandemic? If there's anything this virus should be teaching us, it is that we need to be as proactive as possible in keeping our animal population healthy to minimize impacts on human health. Prevention makes sense ethically, and driving preventive care also drives bonds with clients and patients during these uncertain times. Join Nancy Drumm, general manager of four veterinary practices in New York's Capital District, as she covers the nuts and bolts of a successful preventive care implementation, from pricing strategies to team engagement.

courses.title: Business Management for an Integrative Veterinary Practice
courses.description: When running your own practice management skills can be as critical as clinical skills. Business Management for an Integrative Veterinary Practice is a course designed to introduce students to all aspects of managing their own integrative practice and developing their professional skills. Students will learn from practice owners and managers with many years of experience how to organize staff, manage finances and client relationships, understand common legal issues, keep up in a changing marketplace and more while running their individual practices with maximum efficiency and profitability.

courses.title: Integrative Approach to Chronic Eye Disorders in Small Animals
courses.description: The primary objective of this course in veterinary ophthalmology is to improve the ophthalmic diagnostic and surgical skills of veterinary practitioners in order that they can provide higher levels of care to animals with eye problems. This will begin with a review of ophthalmic terminology, anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology of the animal eye. Basic and advanced ophthalmic examination and diagnostic techniques of animals, and the diagnosis and treatment of common ophthalmic disorders of animals will be covered in detail. Discussions on how to perform basic and advanced ophthalmic diagnostic procedures will be taught.

courses.title: Certified Myofascial and Manual Therapy Veterinarian Online
courses.description:
The Certified Myofascial and Manual Therapy program is a comprehensive course designed to train veterinarians in a wide range of manual and myofascial therapy styles and techniques. The program integrates foundational science, evidence-based practice, and extensive hands-on application to address soft tissue dysfunction, movement restriction, and pain, while promoting overall patient well-being. Participants will develop advanced palpation skills and learn to select and apply appropriate techniques based on individual patient presentation and clinical goals.
This program emphasizes real-world clinical integration, teaching veterinarians how to incorporate myofascial and manual therapy into diverse practice settings, including general practice, acupuncture/TCVM, rehabilitation and sports medicine, and integrative medicine services. In addition, the course also addresses practical considerations for building, integrating, and sustaining myofascial and manual therapy services within a successful veterinary business model.

courses.title: Optimizing Your Telemedicine Ultrasound Submission
courses.description: This archived webinar provides guidance for optimal telemedicine submission of ultrasound studies. We also discuss appropriate patient preparation as well as organ normals and possible pathology.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: TVCU Business & Practice Management On-Demand Series
courses.description: The TVCU Business & Practice Management CE Series offers veterinary professionals practical strategies to strengthen both operations and client care. Covering topics such as risk reduction and insurance savings, effective client complaint management, and disaster preparedness, these webinars provide actionable tools to improve efficiency, build stronger teams, and enhance overall practice resilience. Each session is designed to translate everyday challenges into opportunities for long-term growth and success.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: Challenges in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Feline Hyperthyroidism
courses.description: Feline hyperthyroidism is commonly encountered in small-animal practice. Feline hyperthyroidism typically responds well to treatment, so it is important for the clinician to routinely screen patients with suspected or potential hyperthyroidism. This archived webinar will discuss the available diagnostic tests for feline hyperthyroidism and the current treatment and monitoring recommendation

courses.title: Feline Integrative Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This course utilizes the 5 branches of TCVM: acupuncture, herbal medicine, Tui-na, food therapy, and lifestyle in the clinical approach to common disease issues in the common house cat. The feline species has unique metabolic and energetic attributes, which can make clinical treatment both challenging and rewarding since they can be very responsive to appropriate treatment. The integration of TCVM principles and treatment with Western medical approaches are discussed, and problem solving for managing various maladies is addressed. Various treatment options are presented for each topic so that the practitioner has a list of potential choices to consider when devising a treatment plan.

courses.title: Improve Your Patient's Experience: Putting Standards of Care and Processes in Place
courses.description:
In veterinary medicine, standards of care are guidelines typically created to define standard protocols or treatment plans on appropriate treatment for different stages in a pet's life for commonly seen illnesses or diseases. They are a set of guidelines that define the proper treatment for a particular health issue or disease at your practice. In other words, standards of care define what is medically appropriate for your patients according to your best practices, evidence-based medicine, and patient outcomes to ensure the delivery of high-quality client and patient care. Standards of care can be specific or general depending on practice needs and they tend to vary from practice to practice.
Proven processes are a five-step or less outline of how to complete a task. Processes are instrumental and vital to upholding standards of care in a veterinary practice. In this webinar, we will discuss standards of care and how proven processes will support those standards.

courses.title: Compounding Confidence: Choosing the Dosage Form and Pharmacy Partner
courses.description:
Selecting the right dosage form and compounding pharmacy is critical to ensuring safe, effective, and high-quality medication use in veterinary and human healthcare. This session provides a practical, in-depth look at the pros and cons of oral, transdermal, and sterile dosage forms, including how to determine which medications are appropriate for each route and how to mitigate sterility risks.
Participants will also learn how to critically evaluate compounding pharmacies. Through real-world website evaluation examples, we'll explore the differences between 503A and 503B facilities, the significance of PCAB accreditation, and the key questions to ask when selecting a pharmacy partner.
Whether you're prescribing, dispensing, or simply aiming to improve patient outcomes, this session will give you the tools to make informed, confident decisions about compounded medications.

courses.title: Improving Emotional Well-Being by Setting Appropriate Boundaries
courses.description: Boundaries are not learned they are taught. We are not given boundaries but, rather, we adopt the boundaries of our role models, parents, and peers. Boundaries (or lack thereof) are behaviors and therefore they must be practiced. This session examines what boundaries are at a veterinary hospital and how to navigate and implement professional and personal boundaries.

courses.title: Small Animal Veterinary Medical Manipulation Online
courses.description:
The Certified Veterinary Medical Manipulation Practitioner (CVMMP) small animal track is a program (approved by AAVSB RACE) that trains and certifies veterinarians in Small Animal Veterinary Medical Manipulation (SAVMM). This program is offered only to licensed veterinarians and 3rd or 4th year veterinary school students, providing them with the opportunity to learn SAVMM more efficiently and effectively, while taking their skills and knowledge to a deeper level. The Veterinary Medical Manipulation (VMM) certification course is comprised of 3 hybrid sessions, with 3 online modules and 3 on-site visits at the Chi University campus in Reddick, Florida, USA.
The lab groups are small with 4 - 6 students per dog to ensure that each student receives the maximum amount of individual attention and hands-on experience to practice SAVMM. This structure ensures that students will be confident to start clinical practice after the first on-site session.

courses.title: Advanced Integrative Approach to Small Animal Neurology
courses.description:
True integration of conventional (Western) veterinary medicine and Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) requires the ability to treat these two seemingly disparate conceptual entities as two interrelated and synergistic parts of an indivisible whole. From pathophysiology to treatment, conventional veterinary and TCVM principles are typically mutually translatable. This course covers key aspects of diagnosing and treating small animal neurologic disorders from this inclusive integrative standpoint. As such, this course provides a complete and clinically relevant overview of localizing lesions, generating differential diagnosis lists, creating targeted diagnostic plans, and devising effective treatment protocols-all from the standpoint of combining conventional veterinary medicine and TCVM at each step. At the end of the course, the practitioner will feel confident in diagnosing and developing treatment strategies for the most common neurologic disorders encountered in small animal practice.
This class will be ideal for anyone who wishes to feel comfortable diagnosing and treating small animal neurology patients from both western and eastern standpoints. This course will both simplify small animal neurology and offer insights into integrative diagnosis and treatment.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: Critical Connections in Feline Patients
courses.description: Critical Connections in Feline Patients discusses key topics in the pathology of hypertension in feline patients. Within this course, participants will explore the disease of hypertension and its associated risks, steps to take in treating hypertension, and additional resources available. In doing so, veterinarians will be better equipped to comprehensively help cats lead healthier, longer lives.

courses.title: Principles of Communication: A Guide for Change Management
courses.description: Are you capable of recognizing and minimizing resistance to change with your team before it takes over and completely highjacks your plans? Implementing change with your team can be done in a way that is effective and minimizes fear and resistance. Learn the basic principles of communication. Recognize how these principles affect our teams' willingness to engage and see the step-by-step process to successfully implement change while resolving conflict in your practice.¿Learn and recognize what effective change looks like on a day-to-day basis and the ways your culture can affect that change.

courses.title: The Pressure is On: The Ins and Outs of Blood Pressure and Management
courses.description: Understanding blood pressure values fairly straightforward, but interpreting abnormal readings, their implications, and appropriate treatments can be challenging. This course will explain what blood pressure is, various methods for monitoring it, and provide detailed insights into systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressures. Hypotension, in particular, is complex, and with this knowledge, you will be better equipped to identify what your patient needs to address it effectively. We will also explore case-based examples to clearly illustrate the appropriate treatments and the reasons behind them.

courses.title: From Foreign Bodies to ECE: Pinpointing GI Causes of Ferret Anorexia
courses.description: When a ferret stops eating, GI disease should be at the top of the¿differential¿list. This focused session walks through a practical approach to anorexia in ferrets, highlighting high-yield differentials such as foreign bodies, Helicobacter associated gastritis, inflammatory and eosinophilic enteropathies, coronavirus syndromes, and GI neoplasia. Attendees will learn how to use small exam cues, bruxism, posture, stool character, abdominal¿palpation, to guide diagnostics and decide when to treat medically, when to scope, and when to move straight to surgery. Nutritional considerations, biopsy strategy during exploratory, and avoiding common diagnostic pitfalls will be emphasized to help streamline case management in general and emergency practice.¿

courses.title: Evidence Based Veterinary Acupuncture
courses.description: The course addresses the scientific basis of acupuncture, including relevant literature on the topic, the principles of acupuncture in pain management, the clinical application of trigger points, the indications, and contraindications of acupuncture, and how to apply acupuncture in general practice for neurological, gastrointestinal, renal and respiratory disorders in small animals, as well as lameness, laminitis, and navicular diseases in horses. How to integrate acupuncture in a conventional practice through a simple set of cookbook rules is also discussed.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: Neurodiversity in Veterinary Medicine: Embracing Minds That Work Differently
courses.description: This module explores neurodiversity in the veterinary profession through the lens of lived experience, education, and leadership. Learners will deepen their understanding of neurodivergence (such as ADHD and autism) and discover practical ways to support themselves, their teams, and the broader community through inclusive leadership and communication practices

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: Certified Equine Rehabilitation and Performance Veterinarian Online
courses.description:
A good veterinarian is able to diagnose the source of the lameness and get the horse back to competition quickly; a great veterinarian is able to see variations in gait and performance before they lead to lameness and correct them as well as rehabilitate the horse after injury.
In this program, we will explore how the equine athlete functions. Beginning with the powerful way the muscles, bones, and tendons work together for high-level performance we will go on to develop skills to spot small performance deficits and learn ways to correct them, and then we will investigate the etiology of injury, the process of healing, the use of rehabilitation tools and case management.

courses.title: Veterinary Balance Method Acupuncture Online
courses.description: Acupuncture has been practiced for thousands of years. It continues to evolve and improve to this day. MRI studies have shown how quickly the stimulus from an acupuncture needle can travel to the brain. When it comes to pain relief, the effects can arrive almost instantaneously. Pursuing this fast response is what characterizes the Balance Method from traditional acupuncture. When correctly and strategically placed, the bodys response is immediate, within minutes or even seconds of treatment.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: Less Pressure, More Persuasion: Leading Change with Empathy and Influence
courses.description: This 1-hour interactive session explores how veterinary leaders and team members can guide organizational change more effectively by addressing the emotional side of resistance. Through a modern approach grounded in empathy and influence, attendees will learn how to create team buy-in, reduce friction, and lead with emotional intelligence.

courses.title: Backyard Poultry and Small Flocks: A Practical Guide for Veterinarians
courses.description:
This course offers an essential overview of backyard poultry and small flock medicine for veterinarians, with a focus on
real-world clinical scenarios. Attendees gain practical insights into husbandry best practices, disease prevention,
diagnostic approaches, nutrition, pharmacology, and common conditions encountered in small flocks. From examining
chickens and collecting blood to managing egg production issues and parasite control, this program prepares
veterinarians to confidently support backyard poultry clients in general and mixed animal practice.

courses.title: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly of Making good Radiographs
courses.description: The talk covers technical aspects of radiography to optimize image quality and radiation safety.

courses.title: TCVM Fundamental Theories
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce those new to Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) to its fundamental theories.

courses.title: Building Your Feline Dentistry Practice
courses.description: In this online course, veterinary technicians/staff learn how to improve patients' overall health through an understanding of good feline dental care, identify the most common and problematic oral diseases affecting cats, apply good oral examination and treatment guidelines to your feline patients and take advantage of information that will help build a feline dentistry practice

courses.title: Compounding Clarity: Answering the Tough Questions About Veterinary Compounds
courses.description:
Veterinary professionals and pharmacists alike face a growing number of questions, and frustrations, when it comes to compounded medications. This session is designed to cut through the confusion with a practical, question-driven format that delivers clear answers, evidence-based reasoning, and actionable recommendations.
Each frequently asked question is addressed in four parts:
1. A concise, one-sentence answer
2. The reasoning behind that answer, including clinical, legal, and regulatory context
3. Supporting data or examples (e.g., AMDUCA, GFI #256, USP revisions)
4. A recommended action for veterinary professionals to apply in practice
Topics include why commercial products should be prioritized over compounds, who is responsible for ensuring a compound will work, why pharmacists often fill compound prescriptions without pushback, what's limiting access to previously available compounds, and what veterinarians should expect from a high-quality compounding pharmacy.

courses.title: Radiographic Assessment of Canine Lameness
courses.description: The objective of this Archived Webinar is to present radiographic examples and principles of interpretation of common causes of lameness in dogs

courses.title: Common Dermatological Diseases of Pet Rabbits
courses.description: Dermatologic issues are among the leading reasons rabbits visit the exam room, accounting for nearly a quarter of primary care cases. This session offers a practical overview of the most common skin conditions seen in pet rabbits, starting with ectoparasites and effective treatment protocols used in general practice. We will discuss pharmacologic options, dosing considerations, and safety tips for medications often adapted from other species. Next, we will examine key infectious causes, including dermatophytosis, myxomatosis, Shope papillomavirus, and Shope fibromas, focusing on recognition, diagnostics, and client communication. The session concludes with an in-depth look at ulcerative pododermatitis, including medical and husbandry-based management strategies you can implement immediately in your practice.

courses.title: Cytology Techniques
courses.description: Have you ever been frustrated by seeing "Nondiagnostic" on your pathology report? Have you felt like the microscope is your worst enemy? Would you like more confidence in looking at cytology specimens? If you answered yes, this is the session for you! We'll explore how to get the most from your pathology samples and establish a collaborative relationship with your pathologist. A few "tips and tricks" not seen in textbooks will be offered. We will review of basic principles for interpretation of cytology samples as well as review of inflammation, criteria of malignancy, dysplasia vs. neoplasia and Lymphoid neoplasms. Lastly, we'll discuss new technology providing rapid turnaround time on cytology reports.

courses.title: Advanced Equine Veterinary Medical Manipulation Online
courses.description:
The Advanced Equine Veterinary Medical Manipulation (Chiropractic) is the advanced equine adjusting techniques, to veterinarians exclusively.
Students will refine their manipulation (chiropractic) skills, get more from their physical exams and learn new adjusting techniques. The course is open to veterinarians who are graduates of any veterinary spinal manipulation or chiropractic course.

courses.title: Canine Acupuncture Deep Dive
courses.description: The Canine Acupuncture Deep Dive Course helps solidify your grasp of acupuncture points and to become more confident in treating your patients with acupuncture. The course is intended for small animal practitioners who have learned and are familiar with canine acupuncture points and respective indications.

courses.title: January 2024 Modules
courses.description: This course includes 56.5 hours of veterinary and veterinary technician/nurse continuing education in cattle, sheep, goat, camelid, and swine topics. Medical themes covered for these species include parasite control, surgical topics, herd health and emergency care. One of these hours is related to the nonmedical topic of managing difficult client situations.

courses.title: Certified Veterinary Acupuncture Onsite
courses.description: The program begins with an overview of fundamental aspects of Chinese Medicine, including Yin-Yang and Five Elements theory, which serves as a foundation for case diagnoses and treatment. A variety of acupuncture techniques are taught, including electro-acupuncture and moxibustion, in addition to conventional "dry" needling. Students will learn acupuncture points on animals during hands-on practice in the wet labs.

courses.title: Integrative Veterinary Medicine for Pain Management
courses.description: The Integrative Veterinary Medicine for Pain Management course is designed for the veterinarians wishing to integrate Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) and other integrative medicine for their patients. The course is a comprehensive review of the most contemporary concepts of veterinary pain management including neurobiology, neuropharmacology, physical modalities, herbals, acupuncture, and rehabilitation therapy. Applications for pain management across a broad spectrum of clinical presentations will be presented. Relevant literature on the topic, principles of pain management, and the multimodal management of complex pain syndromes in dogs and cats will also be discussed. Information on treating pain from many different perspectives will be highlighted.

courses.title: The Intersection of Domestic Violence and Animal Abuse: How the Veterinary Community Can Help
courses.description: This webinar will feature Nicole Forsyth, President & CEO of RedRover, a national non-profit organization that brings animals from crisis to care and strengthens the bond between people and pets. Nicole will discuss the effort to create more pet-friendly domestic violence shelters to help people and animals in crisis. The documented link between animal abuse and inter partner violence (IPV) means that veterinarians are increasingly being called upon to respond to suspected animal abuse as an indicator of other violence in the household. This webinar will also address the role of veterinarians in responding to domestic violence and IPV, and how veterinarians and animal health professionals can help address this issue in their communities.

courses.title: Watch Your Step! A Playground for Parasites
courses.description: In this 60-minute presentation, Elanco and IDEXX collaborate to bring you the results of a groundbreaking study that shows parasites are more common than you may think. As pets have become active members of the family, the popularity of dog parks, along with pet travel and pet activities, has exploded. Given recent lifestyle changes, people are spending more time with their dogs at home and outside, including more frequent walks and visits to parks. While dog parks fulfill the need for pet and human socialization, they also involve an elevated risk of exposure to intestinal parasites. A recently published, first-of-its-kind study, explored intestinal parasitism at dog parks in 30 major metropolitan areas across the continental United States. This study demonstrated that more than 1 in 5 dogs visiting dog parks was infected with at least one intestinal parasite, highlighting the importance of regular screening- even in dogs on preventives -combined with a comprehensive parasite prevention strategy

courses.title: Integrative Approach to Chronic Eye Disorders in Equine
courses.description: The primary objective of this course in veterinary ophthalmology is to improve the ophthalmic diagnostic and surgical skills of veterinary practitioners in order that they can provide higher levels of care to animals with eye problems. This will begin with a review of ophthalmic terminology, anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology of the animal eye. Basic and advanced ophthalmic examination and diagnostic techniques of animals, and the diagnosis and treatment of common ophthalmic disorders of animals will be covered in detail. Discussions on how to perform basic and advanced ophthalmic diagnostic procedures will be taught.

courses.title: Equine Introduction
courses.description: This course is an introductory seminar which covers the Fundamental Principles of Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) and the two major branches of TCVM: Veterinary Acupuncture and Chinese Herbal Medicine. These seminars take place throughout the year in multiple locations. Veterinary Medical Spinal Manipulation (VMM) techniques are also covered this program.

courses.title: Urinary Catheter Placement in Cats and Dogs (Male and Female)
courses.description: Urinary catheterization is a common procedure in veterinary medicine, essential for managing urinary tract obstructions, monitoring urine output, and facilitating diagnostic sampling. This presentation will provide a comprehensive overview of urinary catheter placement in both male and female cats and dogs. Topics include indications, equipment selection, aseptic technique, step-by-step catheterization procedures and troubleshooting complications. Emphasis will be placed on minimizing patient discomfort, preventing infection and ensuring accurate placement through anatomical understanding and practical tips.

courses.title: Allyship in Mental Health
courses.description: Sometimes it can be difficult to know when and how to help our colleagues when they are struggling. This course will teach learners what it means to be a mental health ally, including how to recognize the signs when someone is struggling with their mental health, being prepared to point them towards services, learning how to actively listen and make yourself available, while also creating healthy boundaries for your own well-being.

courses.title: Equine Restraint
courses.description: Participants will learn general concepts of equine restraint, including safety concerns and considerations. Learn to identify and properly use common restraint equipment through hands-on demonstrations.

courses.title: HIRING AND FIRING
courses.description: This course provides the tools needed to create effective job ads that stand out from competitors and attract the type of candidates desired. Whether conducting telephone, in-person, or working interviews, learn how to establish protocols and standardize the interview process for prospective employees. Gain an understanding of progressive discipline, while learning how to prepare and conduct disciplinary and termination meetings effectively. The information in this series will also cover topics such as questions to avoid during interviews, violations of the Fair Labor Standards Act during discipline, and traps that prevent management from terminating employees.

courses.title: Effective Strategies for Time Management
courses.description: his course will give you core strategies to tackle the problem of making the most of the time we have each day. First, you will learn the basic principles of time management, along with some symptoms that could uncover poor uses of time. Then, you will learn how better time management will improve your daily life and get tips to start managing your time more effectively.

courses.title: Foundation Essentials for Digital Marketing
courses.description: Think of digital marketing as a marketing car. Just as a car needs four wheels moving at the same speed to motor down the road, a business marketing strategy needs four major components to gain traction in the electronic world. All four components need to be running simultaneously, at the same speed, to gain the maximum benefit of an online marketing program. These four wheels are: website, search engine optimization, social media, and reputation management/branding. Finally, the chassis of the car is held together by blogs. Ready? Start this course to delve into the process of understanding how online marketing works today.

courses.title: Marketing Management 1: Introduction to Marketing
courses.description: In this introductory course to marketing, we will explore the contributing factors to your practice's reputation: everything from the communications that you send out to your clients to the way you design your logo that's on your signage outside. You will begin to understand the building blocks to a solid reputation, plus the importance of involving the entire team throughout this process of reputation building and maintenance. We will also discuss the role of leadership in modeling these behaviors for the team and ensuring employees are aligned.

courses.title: Marketing Management 5: Quantifying Reputation
courses.description: In this course we will discuss the final piece of authentic reputation management: quantifying. A manager must understand how well reputation management and marketing efforts are working so gaps and future initiatives can be appropriately planned. Cycle of service metrics and reputation formulas will be reviewed to understand how marketing efforts can be effectively measured.

courses.title: Operational Efficiency
courses.description: Are you a veterinary practice owner or manager feeling overwhelmed by the daily grind? Do you find yourself constantly running in circles, putting out fires, and struggling to keep up? You're not alone! Many veterinary practices operate with high effectiveness. Things get done but with low efficiency. This leads to stress, burnout, and a feeling of constantly being in "survival mode." This course is designed to help you break free from this cycle and unlock the full potential of your practice by mastering the Four P's of veterinary practice efficiency: Physical Plant, Products, People, and Processes.

courses.title: Veterinary Practice Data
courses.description: Your veterinary practice data is most valuable to you. The biggest mistake made by veterinary practice leadership is how data backups are managed, which leads to costly downtime and lost data. Learn how to prioritize data management in your veterinary practice. This course is composed of two modules. Module 201: Understanding Data Backups Beginning with the key concepts of RTO and RPO, what they mean, why they are important, and how to implement them into your practice properly. Then learn how to leverage both local and cloud backups that would make any IT professional jealous. Module 202: Data to Protect in Your Practice Now that you understand how to create a proper backup plan, you need to know what in your practice needs to be protected. Key data areas in the practice that are often overlooked, learn the steps to protect them.

courses.title: Workplace Emergency & Evacuation Plans
courses.description: This course is designed to equip employees with essential knowledge to prepare for, respond to, and recover from workplace emergencies. Participants will explore the types of emergencies that may occur, from weather events to workplace violence and hazardous material incidents. The course will guide learners in developing tailored emergency action and evacuation plans, ensuring a proactive approach to safety. By the end of this course, learners will be better prepared to protect themselves and others during critical incidents.

courses.title: Clinical Techniques I
courses.description: This course is designed to equip veterinary assistants and technicians with the essential laboratory skills necessary for accurate and efficient sample collection. Learners will gain an understanding of how to perform venipuncture on both canine and feline patients, incorporating various techniques to minimize stress and maximize blood draw success. Additionally, the course will delve into urine collection methods, covering both cystocentesis and free-catch techniques, as well as the importance of proper sample handling and storage. Understanding the intricacies of ear cytology will be emphasized, including sample collection and slide preparation. Furthermore, learners will be able to identify and utilize a wide range of sample collection tubes after this course, having gained knowledge of their specific additives and applications. By the end of this course, learners will be proficient in these fundamental laboratory techniques, enabling them to contribute effectively to patient diagnosis and treatment.

courses.title: Marketing Management 2: Branding
courses.description: Who you are, collectively, isnt where your reputation starts and stops. There are other contributors to reputation. It is often said to never judge a book by its cover.
