But the truth is, we do. In this course, we will discuss the impressionable areas of your practice from a consumer perspective and how to build your tangible and intangible brand.

courses.title: Florida Veterinary Jurisprudence & Ethics
courses.description: This 2-hour continuing education course provides Florida-licensed veterinarians and technicians with a comprehensive understanding of the legal, ethical, and regulatory framework governing veterinary medical practice in the state. Through case studies, interactive scenarios, and regulatory analysis, participants will strengthen their ability to make informed decisions in compliance with Florida statutes and administrative codes. The course covers standards of care, record keeping, supervision, informed consent, telemedicine, and the disciplinary process. Designed to meet Floridas jurisprudence CE requirement for license renewal, the course empowers veterinary professionals to uphold the highest standards of professional accountability and client service

courses.title: Recumbent Patient Care
courses.description: Recumbent patients require special considerations, care and monitoring. Learn the effects that remaining in recumbency has on the body systems and how to care for these types of patients.

courses.title: Performance Management: Removing Bias & Having Essential Conversations
courses.description: In this course learners will overcome the common dread of performance review cycles and master preparation, conversations and follow through, removing potential bias and common pitfalls experienced during the process.

courses.title: Pain Assessment in Feline & Canine Patients
courses.description: ¿Identifying pain in animals poses a difficulty due to their inability to communicate in the same manner as humans. Nevertheless, canine and feline patients exhibit distinct behaviors that can serve as indications of pain, aiding in its recognition. Learn more about pain pathways, signs of pain, how to assess and rate pain in these patients, and the technicians role in being an advocate for pain management.

courses.title: Bridging the Divide: What to Do When Your Veterinary Team Feels Divided
courses.description: As a veterinary practice manager, you're the cornerstone of cohesive and high-performing team. But what happens when rifts merge, and your team feels divided? This intensive course equips you with the essential skills and strategies to understand team division, your role in communication in division and unity, how to rebuild trust and team cohesion, intervention tools, conflict prevention and team culture maintenance.

courses.title: Handling Exotic Mammals
courses.description: Small mammals and other nontraditional pets present unique handling challenges that directly affect diagnostic quality, patient welfare, and team safety. In this rapid, case focused microcourse, learners compare low-stress restraint options and red-flag contraindications across common exotics seen in general practice such as rabbits, ferrets, guinea pigs, small rodents, hedgehogs, chinchillas, and prairie dogs then close with practical guidance on wildlife kept as pets: legal, zoonotic, and triage considerations. Emphasis is placed on species-specific stress signals, thermoregulation, safe anatomy, escalation to chemical restraint, and bite and zoonosis risk mitigation so clinical tasks such as exam, sampling, imaging, administration can be completed safely and effectively.

courses.title: Marketing Management 3: Marketing Tactics
courses.description: In this course, we will review how building a solid team and optimizing your cycle of service is the first step before embarking on marketing activities. From there, we will introduce key marketing tactics including findability, website design, social media, email, mobile apps, videos and blogs so that you may learn how to implement these elements into your marketing strategy.

courses.title: VETERINARY DENTISTRY PROCEDURES
courses.description: This program discusses the process for performing efficient dentistry procedures. Participants will begin learning how to obtain patient history and perform an oral examination on awake patients that sets the foundation for a successful dentistry plan. You will then proceed to understand how to position anesthetized patients for dentistry, efficient dental charting and anesthetized oral examination. Finally, you will see a demonstration explaining how to properly scale and polish the teeth. The knowledge gained in this program will aid in communication, documentation and efficiency in performing dentistry procedures.

courses.title: Leadership and Planning
courses.description:
In this program, Amanda Donnelly, DVM, MBA, will help explain how critical strategic planning is for a
successful business. Learn how to conduct a SWOT analysis and combine your information with Key
Performance Indicators to set and achieve practice goals. Discover time management skills that will help
prioritize job tasks and increase productivity. Learn how establishing hospital procedures and protocols
will improve efficiency and consistency within your practice. The tools discussed in Leadership and
Planning will help with business growth, increase profitability, and improve practice culture.

courses.title: Colorado Jurisprudence Course
courses.description: This 2 hour continuing education course provides Colorado-licensed veterinarians with a comprehensive understanding of the legal, ethical, and regulatory framework governing veterinary medical practice in Colorado. Through case studies, interactive scenarios, and regulatory analysis, participants will strengthen their ability to make informed decisions in compliance with the Colorado Veterinary Practice Act and the State Boards administrative rules. The course covers standards of care, recordkeeping, supervision, informed consent, telehealth, and the disciplinary process. Designed to meet the Colorado jurisprudence CE requirement for license renewal, the course equips veterinary professionals to uphold the highest standards of ethical conduct, legal compliance, and client-centered care.

courses.title: Feline Behaviors & Handling
courses.description: Veterinary Behaviorist Meghan Herron provides insight into creating low-stress visits for felines by understanding their body language, proper handling techniques and how to provide the best environment for your feline patients.

courses.title: Journal Club Potpourri
courses.description: In this lecture presented by Ladan Mohammad-Zadeh, DVM, DACVECC, will be reviewing new pertinent journal articles from JAVMA, JVIM and JVECC relevant to general practitioners. Subjects include reviewing risk factors for feline squamous cell carcinoma, utility of prazosin for prevention of recurrent urethral obstruction, and risk factors for development of acute kidney injury after administration of furosemide.

courses.title: Marketing Management 4: Building Community Connection
courses.description: In this course, we will encourage you to consider taking your approach to caring to another level: creating a community presence for the practice and the people in it as another layer of care. This can be done though community involvement. Opportunities and how to get started in your community will be reviewed in this course.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: In this course, learners will discover the path technological advances have paved for radiological artificial intelligence today. Accuracy in terms of sensitivity and specificity will be reviewed along with the ability for artificial intelligence to improve itself with increased collected measurements. Potential benefits to the practice in light of current caseload demands will be highlighted while learners brainstorm how technology may improve their workflows. Case studies comparing radiologist and AI review will help the learner gain a stronger understanding of AI's capabilities within the realm of veterinary radiology.

courses.title: Phamiliar Pharmacology
courses.description:
Phamiliar Pharmacology is a focused, two-hour course designed to enhance the foundational knowledge of veterinary pharmacology for veterinary professionals and students. This course equips learners with the essential terminology, classifications, administration protocols, and ethical considerations necessary to safely and confidently navigate drug use in clinical practice.
Through a series of concise, high-impact modules, participants will explore the names and categories of commonly used medications, prescription labeling standards, and routes of administration. Additionally, the course highlights regulatory guidelines, ethical principles, and effective client communication techniques. Interactive reviews and a final knowledge check ensure the learner can apply pharmacological knowledge in both clinical documentation and real-world client education.
Whether preparing for certification or improving in-practice accuracy, this course empowers learners to handle veterinary medications with a deeper understanding of safety, communication, and compliance.

courses.title: Stress Management in the Veterinary Industry
courses.description: The discussion focuses on stress management and sharing strategies to gain perspective during stressful times. The session offers self-reflection opportunities and tools for managing difficult moments in the veterinary industry. Key influences include the book "Burnout" and a Harvard Business Review article on recovering from work stress. DoveLewis Veterinary Wellbeing Director Debrah Lee, LCSW, emphasizes that managing stress is an ongoing effort and aims to provide practical, continuous techniques for dealing with stress.

courses.title: Optimizing the OR Workflow
courses.description: This course will guide you through developing a strategic vision for managing your veterinary practice's operating room (OR) and surgery schedule. We'll explore key concepts, practical steps, and tools to optimize efficiency, improve patient care, and enhance team satisfaction.

courses.title: Elevating Your Vocabulary with Advanced Medical Terminology
courses.description: The Elevating Your Vocabulary with Advanced Medical Terminology course is designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of the advanced medical language used in the veterinary field.

courses.title: Feline Neurology: When Cats Don't Follow the Textbook
courses.description: This lecture provides an updated, practical review of feline neurology, highlighting how cats often present with neurologic conditions that do not follow traditional textbook patterns. Attendees will learn how to approach the feline neurologic exam, recognize unique clinical diseases, and identify key decision points before pursuing advanced diagnostics such as MRI. The session will also outline treatment strategies following imaging and offer case-based insights to help veterinary professionals feel more confident managing feline neurologic patients.

courses.title: Harmony in the Clinic: Strategies for a Happy Veterinary Team
courses.description: Harmony in the Clinic: Strategies for a Happy Veterinary Team is designed to empower veterinary professionals to cultivate a positive and supportive work environment. By focusing on essential elements such as kindness, respect, accountability, encouragement, and teamwork, this course provides practical strategies to enhance team dynamics and overall job satisfaction. From setting a positive tone at the start of the day to fostering a culture of open communication and mutual support, learners will develop valuable techniques to create a harmonious clinic where everyone feels valued and motivated.

courses.title: Marketing Management 6: Protecting Reputation
courses.description: When youve worked hard to build an authentic reputation, youll want to protect what youve built. In this course, we will review reputation risk management techniques, including how to monitor and respond to online reviews.

courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Develop a better understanding of the science of thermodynamics and its impact on animal health with this course. With Amber Hart, RVT, VTS (ECC) as our guide, we will delve into the complex world of thermodynamics, equipping you with the knowledge and skills to effectively manage your patients body temperature in various situations.

courses.title: Addressing Chronic Pain in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: Maladaptive pain is an important topic of conversation as better treatments are becoming available in pet pain management. Internationally double board-certified in Analgesia and Animal Welfare, Dr. Sheilah Robertson shares a host of new ketamine research that earns it a spot in your peri-operative protocols to reduce and prevent "wind up" pain. Then, we'll switch gears to integrate effective non-drug therapies that are tried and true.

courses.title: IMMUNE-MEDIATED HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA (802-42307)
courses.description: In this online program, Dr. Remo Lobetti will address the pathophysiology, types, etiologies, diagnostic approach, and therapeutic management of immune-mediated hemolytic anemia in the dog and cat.

courses.title: 2026 VetFolio Skillshop Prework
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: STRESS FREE PETS FOR VETERINARY PROFESSIONALS
courses.description: Stress Free Pets is an animal handling and behaviour education program, certification and community for Veterinary and Pet professionals. We aim to enrich the lives of our patients through delivering world class education, tools and networks.

courses.title: Restful Nights: Managing Sleep Disruption in Dogs with Canine Cognitive Dysfunction
courses.description: This seminar covers the treatment of sleep disturbances in dogs with canine cognitive dysfunction (CCD). We will discuss medical and behavioural differentials, behaviour modification as well as treatment with psychopharmacological medications

courses.title: Nutrition of the Geriatric Dog and Cat
courses.description: The aging organism undergoes a 'normal' series of dysregulation events that are further compounded when diseases of aging develop. Even healthy geriatric pets present nutritional challenges due to changes in organ system functions, and the sick senior presents more significant challenges to obtaining even adequate levels of essential nutrients. The focus of the senior pet's owner is to slow or mitigate the clinical signs associated with obvious age-related disease, but it may be just as important to manage the subclinical effects of inflammaging, sarcopenia, and microbiome shifts. This talk presents nutrients of interest in senior dogs and cats, advice on when to use senior diets and how to choose them, and recent news about certain key nutrients.

courses.title: What makes dogs tick: The impact of evolution and domestication on their genes and the human-animal bond
courses.description: Dogs and humans have co-evolved over many millennia in a mutualistic relationship. The close bond humans developed with dogs is evident in the archeological record dating back at least 14,000 years. As these two species evolved together, they both adapted to their environments and lifestyles. Genes involved in digestion, neurological processes, and even diseases like cancer show parallel evolutionary changes in both dogs and humans. This presentation will discuss the fascinating evolutionary history of mans best friend and how their genetic adaptations have altered key aspects of the species impacting everything from the human-animal bond to nutrition to disease predispositions. Understanding the unique physical and psychological needs of dogs can improve our ability to care for and bond with them.

courses.title: Updated Guidelines for Atopic Dermatitis: Strategies and Solutions
courses.description: We've all dealt with the daily frustrations of managing atopic dermatitis (AD) and the toll it takes on both dogs and owners. That's why we're joining Dr. Frane Banovic as he gives an insightful overview of the evolving landscape of canine AD treatments and trends. After reviewing current treatments in human and canine AD, we'll break down what strategies to prioritize for both reduction AND prevention of flare-ups.

courses.title: (On Demand) Insects and Insults: Tick Borne Disease, Anaphylaxis, and other Outdoor Offenders
courses.description: Originally presented in 2025, this 5.5 hour lecture series takes a bite out of a variety of environmental hazards. We'll start with a deep dive into tick-borne disease, covering the most important organisms for both dogs and cats. Next, we'll move on to things that sting - bees, fire ants, spider bites, and more! Learn rapid recognition of hypersensitivity and anaphylactic reactions, so you can quickly reverse the process before things turn life-threatening. We'll close out this course with a lesson on a variety of other outdoor offenders - from cane toads to porcupines to fish hooks.

courses.title: November 2024 RACE Submission
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Master Heartworm Disease
courses.description: Our classic Master Heartworm Disease program gets an update! With an added lecture to recap the new 2024 American Heartworm Society guidelines, Heartworm Disease 2.0 now includes 9.5 hours of CE credit dedicated to these heartache causing parasites. Does skipped prevention make your heart skip a beat? This seven-video series will instill confidence in all aspects of heartworm prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. Train your practice team to be ready for any client question and treat heartworms at all stages.

courses.title: Feline Diabetes Made Easy
courses.description: Diabetes is a treatable disease, yet many cats are euthanized shortly after diagnosis. A significant factor in the decision to euthanize is the effect of the disease on the owner's finances and quality of life. In this lecture, we will compare old dogmas of complicated treatment for feline diabetes with new opportunities; these options make it a simpler disease to treat, reducing the owner's treatment burden.

courses.title: Fresh, New Possibilities: How Fresh Pet Food Can Expand Nutritional Solutions
courses.description: This learning module is designed to equip learners with the knowledge and confidence to support pet owners who are considering fresh pet food as an option for their pets.

courses.title: Anaphylaxis Uncovered: Understanding Triggers, Risks, and Blind Spots in Canine Allergic Reactions
courses.description: This lecture will explore anaphylaxis in dogs, focusing on identifying, diagnosing, and managing this life-threatening allergic reaction. Participants will learn to recognize common and rare triggers such as storage mites and unexpected allergens that may lead to anaphylaxis. The session will cover the clinical signs of anaphylaxis, methods for differentiating it from other conditions, and the diagnostic tools used to confirm the diagnosis. Emphasis will be placed on immediate interventions, including epinephrine administration, as well as client education to manage at-risk dogs and prevent future episodes. By the end of the lecture, attendees will be equipped with practical strategies to quickly respond to anaphylactic emergencies and better manage allergic reactions in their canine patients.

courses.title: Compounding Confidence: Choosing the Dosage Form and Pharmacy Partner
courses.description: Selecting the right dosage form and compounding pharmacy is critical to ensuring safe, effective, and high quality medication use in veterinary and human healthcare. This session provides a practical, in depth look at the pros and cons of oral, transdermal, and sterile dosage forms, including how to determine which medications are appropriate for each route and how to mitigate sterility risks. Participants will also learn how to critically evaluate compounding pharmacies. Through real-world website evaluation examples, we will explore the differences between 503A and 503B facilities, the significance of PCAB accreditation, and the key questions to ask when selecting a pharmacy partner. Whether you are prescribing, dispensing, or simply aiming to improve patient outcomes, this session will give you the tools to make informed, confident decisions about compounded medications.

courses.title: January 2026
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: TPLO
courses.description: This CE provides an overview of cranial cruciate ligament disease with a focus on surgical treatment including TPLO, arthrotomy, and arthroscopy. Information regarding potential complications and expected outcomes is also reviewed.

courses.title: Surgical Insights Unlocked: Interactive Learning Through Video Analysis
courses.description: This engaging webinar is designed to enhance your surgical skills and knowledge through interactive video analysis. Participants will view a series of surgical procedures, followed by multiple-choice questions that encourage critical thinking. Each segment will be accompanied by in-depth discussions and evidence-based explanations, drawing from current scientific studies and literature.

courses.title: 50 Dental Hacks to Smile About
courses.description: This comprehensive collection of dental hacks encompasses innovative strategies for maintaining exceptional dental hygiene, drawing insights from veterinary and human dental practices. The compilation covers a wide range of techniques from practical daily care to professional interventions designed to revolutionize dental maintenance. Key areas of focus include preventive care, cleaning techniques, natural remedies, and professional strategies that can be applied by both dental professionals and individuals seeking to improve their oral health.

courses.title: From Observation to Diagnosis: How to Detect Canine OA and Other Mobility Impairments
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive approach to diagnosing mobility impairment in dogs, focusing on early identification of primary joint disorders that lead to secondary osteoarthritis (OA) and associated maladaptive pain. Participants will explore differential diagnoses for impaired mobility, including concurrent musculoskeletal conditions that may affect a dog's quality of life. Veterinarians will learn screening and examination techniques, including orthopedic and neurologic exams with low-stress handling, as well as high-quality radiographic practices. The course aims to equip veterinarians with the confidence and skills to diagnose conditions like cranial cruciate ligament disease, hip dysplasia, and osteochondrosis, and make informed decisions regarding additional diagnostics and advanced imaging.

courses.title: Maintaining healthy weight in senior cats with chronic disease
courses.description:
Good body condition of cats is associated with overall health, whilst there are risks to cats both when they are above and significantly below their ideal condition. Although maintaining ideal weight can promote health and wellbeing in cats, this can be challenging in senior cats. Obesity is a problem of increasing importance and almost half of call cats are overweight, including many senior cats. This can affect quality of life in the older cat mainly through the comorbidities that may arise. Other senior cats may be prone to weight loss, often as a result of chronic diseases that are prevalent in this age group. These cats tend to lose bodyweight.
This lecture will focus on how veterinary professionals can assist their senior feline patients to maintain a healthy weight, both in terms of maintaining weight in cats prone to weight loss, and modest weight loss in those that are overweight. In both instances, preserving lean body mass (LBM) is key to ensuring health and wellbeing

courses.title: Pain Busters - Why Care?
courses.description:
In these four videos you will learn how todays controlled drug laws were shaped by a series of drug crises that unfolded over more than a century. We trace how opioids sedatives and stimulants moved from common medical tools to tightly regulated substances and how politics class enforcement and pharmaceutical influence shaped the rules veterinary teams now work under. Along the way you will see why diversion happens quietly why DEA schedules look the way they do and how past decisions still create real risk in modern practice. This series is essential viewing for anyone who handles controlled drugs and wants to understand not just the rules, but the system behind them.
Part 1 VIDEO 1 - In this video, you will learn why controlled drug laws are so complicated and how history shaped the rules you follow every day. We break down real cases of diversion in veterinary practice and show how these issues can happen quietly in any clinic. You will also understand the key difference between dependence and addiction and why that distinction matters for patient care and compliance. This is a must-watch if you handle controlled drugs and want to protect yourself, your team, and your license.
Part 1 VIDEO 2 - In this video, you will learn how the first opioid crisis shaped the divide between medicine and drugs that still drives controlled substance laws today. We unpack how opioids and stimulants were once freely used, why addiction became politicized, and how regulation split along lines of access, class, and enforcement. You will see how these early decisions led to prescription rules, white markets, and criminalized drug use. This is a must watch if you want to understand why modern controlled drug regulations exist and why they still create real risk in veterinary practice today.
Part 1 VIDEO 3 - In this video, you will learn how the second major drug crisis shifted misuse from opioids to sedatives and stimulants and how that directly shaped todays controlled substance sched

courses.title: Product Primer: A Synergistic Approach to Canine Osteoarthritis
courses.description: The management of canine osteoarthritis involves a multi-modal approach. Medical management and nutraceuticals are commonly recommended, but nutrition remains an underutilized and often overlooked part of the treatment plan. While there is extensive evidence supporting the efficacy of omega-3 fatty acids for patients with osteoarthritis, the evidence regarding the effectiveness of glucosamine and chondroitin remains mixed. In this presentation, well discuss the importance of incorporating nutrition into the overall treatment plan for patients with osteoarthritis. Additionally, well discuss the research supporting the use of turmeric extract, hydrolyzed collagen, and green tea extract in canine patients with osteoarthritis as a novel and synergistic approach to the disease.

courses.title: THE NEUROBIOLOGY OF TOXIC STRESS
courses.description:
In this one-hour course, you'll learn about the different types of stress and how stress impacts the brain. You will develop an understanding of learned helplessness, the range of behaviors commonly associated with toxic stress, and the connection between those behaviors and changes to the brain. The course will finish with a discussion of the benefits of giving an animal more control and how that changes the brain. By the end of this course, you should have a strong understanding of why Fear Free principles are important for promoting both physical and behavioral health and wellbeing.
This course contains six lessons:
Lesson 1: Types of Stress
Lesson 2: Learned Helplessness
Lesson 3: Toxic Stress and Trauma
Lesson 4: The Power of Agency
This course was written by Kristina Spaulding, PhD, CAAB.

courses.title: November 2025
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: An Update on the Use of Bisphosphonates in Horses
courses.description: This presentation will review our current understanding of bisphosphonate drugs in equine practice and introduce recently available scientific data. Topics will include clinical efficacy data, pharmacokinetic studies, equine safety studies, and recently discovered effects in non-bone cells. To conclude, it will provide an overview of relevant non-nitrogenous bisphosphonate clinical trials.

courses.title: Recertification 2024 & 2025
courses.description: Online course providing 16 modules of which 12 have existing RACE approval. Participants are required to complete 4 modules to maintain their Stress Free Pets certification.

courses.title: Boundaries: Your boundaries: fences, gates or open spaces?
courses.description: Boundaries: It is said that when resentment is felt towards a person, a boundary has been crossed. Boundaries are what help us keep our personal life and our practice life separate and fulfilling. This presentation will explain what boundaries look like in veterinary practice. It will also help viewers understand their creation, effective use and tactful communication of them to the people we deal with.

courses.title: What Oncologists Wish GPs Knew and Did
courses.description: In this presentation, a board-certified oncologist will discuss how general practitioners and oncologists can collaborate on cancer cases. She'll discuss what cancer presentations are of concern, the critical diagnostic tests for making the diagnosis, staging and grading, appropriate treatment, and working with an oncologist.

courses.title: Anesthesia Ventilators 101
courses.description: Many practices may at some point find it necessary to provide temporary or short-term ventilatory support for their patients. Learn the basic principles behind ventilatory support during this presentation, utilizing mechanical ventilation with the Hallowell 2000 Anesthesia Ventilator as a demonstration model. Capnogram interpretation and troubleshooting tips will also be discussed.

courses.title: Invironmeant: Building a Resilient Team
courses.description: A resilient team is built upon culture and decisions. What skills and knowledge are needed to support and strengthen your team against the difficulties of that work that you do daily? This workshop goes over key elements of building a resilient team for a healthy and happy practice. Leaders live the values and set the vision of their team. What is it that the team aligns around? The elements of a successful team are shared and measured during the presentation. Elements include creating an inviting and invincible culture, supporting, and strengthening your team and defining your hospital's meaning and purpose.

courses.title: Strength in Practice: Ergonomics and Body Mechanics for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: Veterinary healthcare work is physically demanding and often unpredictable. This course provides essential training on ergonomic techniques and body mechanics tailored specifically for veterinarians and the veterinary healthcare team. Along with practical ergonomics, this course incorporates strength and mobility exercises to build resilience and reduce injury risks. Participants will gain actionable insights and engage in a guided physical demonstration to prepare for the varied physical demands of their daily work.

courses.title: Fear Free Pain Management
courses.description: This course will discuss chronic pain, its causes, and its impact on animals' wellbeing. It will include case studies, as well as a discussion of alternative and complementary treatment.

courses.title: Spread of the Spirochetes: Update on canine leptospirosis and Lyme disease
courses.description:
As the geographic range of continues to expand and reservoir wildlife have more access to dogs, the threat of spirochetal diseases like leptospirosis and Lyme disease is no longer confined to rural settings. Today's veterinary teams face the dual challenge of diagnosing these "great pretenders" - which often present with vague clinical signs or subclinical infections - and addressing the rising risk in urban and small-breed populations.
This session provides a comprehensive update on the epidemiology of Leptospira serovars and Borrelia burgdorferi. We will dive into latest ACVIM consensus guidelines for diagnosis and treatment. Finally, we will explore the science behind vaccine technologies and how highly purified, 1/2 mL combinations can provide protection and minimize vaccine injections.

courses.title: Assessment of Cats with CKD: What's Important and Why?
courses.description: The instructor will discuss her steps for approaching and assessing cats with CKD. This includes the history, physical exam, medical and nutritional assessment, and caregiver experience. From that information, she determines a care plan, including a medical, nutritional, and monitoring plan.

courses.title: On-Demand | AI in Veterinary Medicine: Tools, Risks, and Clinical Applications
courses.description: When there's simply not enough minutes in an hour, it's time to use every tool you have to your advantage. AI technology is fast improving and increasingly relevant in easing the strains of day-to-day clinical practice. This one-hour power session provides a practical overview of artificial intelligence systems and their applications for veterinary professionals. We'll begin by understanding how machine-learning works, then evaluate benefits, limitations, and responsible oversight parameters to integrate AI tools that support you exactly how you want them to. Reclaim your valuable attention and delegate the tedious tasks so you can focus on what matters most!

courses.title: Acupuncture for Neurological Diseases in Diverse Veterinary Species
courses.description:
Acupuncture is now a recognized treatment for spinal cord conditions, and is covered by medicare for lower back pain in humans. This very high bar has been achieved because acupuncture has been demonstrated to provide analgesia, reduce chronic pain and addiction, and improve outcomes when used in addition to, or in place of opioids.
Acupuncture points are neuroanatomically rich, especially for modification of neurological diseases. This includes: myelinated and unmyelinated nerves, low-threshold mechanoreceptors, mast cells and microcirculatory complexes. With needle placement, nerve stimulation occurs directly, and/or secondary to mechanical forces applied by the fascia in the region surrounding the point, which is a form of mechano-transduction.
Mechano-transduction modifies the fibroblasts in a repeating loop of metabolic activity that last for up to 36 hours. Mechanical pull on mast cells and keratinocytes is detected by mechano-sensitive TRP channels causes the release of chemicals: histamine and purines (in part) that contribute to modifying the electrical and chemical signals in the region of the acupuncture needle. Additionally, microcirculation is modified by the exchange, generally with vessel dilation via nitric oxide, and increased fluid flux through lymphatic channels that are formed by the fascia
This series of changes alters homeostasis via sympathetic/parasympathetic input, modification of axonal flow and dorsal root ganglion transcription, spinal neurotransmitter modulation, modification of reflex loops, and influences on immune function and balance.
Subsequently, central nervous system modification occurs in the form of stress reduction and increase in analgesic and calming neurotransmitters from the periaqueductal grey and rostroventral medulla (pain regulation regions). This also contributes to improved descending inhibition of pain signals, and improved enteric homeostasis.
There is evidence in the literature for use of acupuncture for spinal pa

courses.title: Effective Pain Relief in Senior Dogs
courses.description:
This session will focus on effective methods for improving pain management in
senior dogs. Many senior dogs suffer from chronic pain that is either unrecognized or not treated appropriately. Participants will learn key physiologic changes that take place during aging that impacts drug metabolism and how this may influence drug choice and dosing. We will review the current evidence for oral pain management in dogs and present practical strategies for choosing the most effective pain medications and supplements. Finally, non-pharmacologic strategies (including rehabilitation modalities, weight loss, exercise and acupuncture) will be briefly reviewed as well. These strategies augment and complement pharmacologic approaches.

courses.title: Veterinary Dentistry 101: Foundations & Techniques
courses.description:
A high percentage of pets suffer from periodontal disease - which can lead to significant pain and discomfort, impact overall health and negatively affect quality of life-making dental care a crucial part of routine veterinary practice. To be effective, the veterinary team must possess extensive knowledge of anatomy, periodontal probing, dental scaling and intraoral radiography. Veterinary Dentistry 101: Foundations & Techniques is a comprehensive certificate course that equips veterinary professionals with a solid grounding in the basic fundamentals vital to the oral health of their patients. Learners will delve into key aspects of dental anatomy, including the skull, types of teeth, periodontium and gingiva/mucosa, utilizing detailed diagrams and engaging visual aids. They will also familiarize themselves with the terminology and systems for identifying teeth, such as the Triadan and Anatomical tooth identification methods. The course incorporates hands-on learning through videos and practical demonstrations that cover essential equipment use, instrument maintenance and ergonomic techniques.
By the end of this course, participants will possess the skills and knowledge needed to perform thorough dental assessments, including charting, probing periodontal pockets, and evaluating oral health in dogs and cats. They will also be prepared to obtain dental radiographs, adhere to radiation safety protocols and troubleshoot common imaging issues.
This course is essential for any veterinary professional aiming to enhance their capacity to provide high-quality dental care and improve overall patient health.

courses.title: When Bandages Go Wrong: Managing Slips, Sores, and Owner Conversations
courses.description:
Join Brian Goleman for an engaging and practical session focused on one of the most common and potentially harmful procedures performed in veterinary medicine bandaging. While bandages are essential tools for wound management, post-operative care, and orthopedic support, improper application or monitoring can quickly lead to serious complications for patients.
In this presentation, participants will explore real world examples of bandage complications, including pressure sores, impaired circulation, swelling, moisture related skin damage, delayed healing, and patient discomfort. Brian will walk attendees through the why behind common bandage failures and provide actionable strategies to improve bandage application, monitoring, client communication, and patient outcomes.
Designed for veterinary technicians, assistants, students, and veterinary teams, this session combines clinical insight, practical tips, and case-based learning to help attendees build confidence in recognizing risks before they become problems.

courses.title: Product Primer: From Chihuahua to Great Dane: The Case for Customized Breed Specific Canine Diets
courses.description:
The pure breed population is growing. With over 340 different breeds recognised by canine breed organisations worldwide they make up over 50% of the pet dog population.
Breed Health Nutrition is important because pure breed dogs are unique and have specific nutritional needs. For example,
Multiple specificities and characteristics.
Different jaw morphology's and eating behaviours.
Specific needs at each life-stage from growth through to ageing.
The breeding of pure breed dogs had led to defined standards for size, morphology and temperament, along with many other characteristics and specificities some of which can be supported by adapted nutrition. Some of the specificities on which breed specific diets are based are listed below.
Body type: Every breed has their specific body type, size and shape. For example, The Boxer has a high proportion of lean muscle mass (fat free mass) at around 85% while The Labrador Retriever has a much lower percentage of lean mass at 65%. Therefore, energy content in the diets need to be formulated based on the body composition.
Bones and joints: Many of our small breeds, including the Pomeranian and Chihuahua, are affected by the condition patella luxation or as it is commonly known - slipping kneecaps. The risk of this condition in small breeds is approximately 12 times that of large dogs. Breeds such as the Bulldog and Rottweiler are heavy for their size, which places daily pressure on their bones and joints. These breeds therefore benefit from support to help maintain joint health.
Coat type: The skin is the largest organ in the body and has many important roles to play, not just as a defensive barrier between the body and the external world. Whether the dog has a water-resistant coat like the Labrador Retriever, a curly coat that grows continuously like the Poodle or a long hair-like coat that doesn't shed like the Maltese, nutrition can be adapted to support its specific needs. A sensitive skin can affect many breeds for many diff

courses.title: Tube Tactics: Mastering Placement and Troubleshooting of Feeding Tubes
courses.description: Nasoesophageal tubes (NE), nasogastric tubes (NG) and esophageal tubes (E) are useful tools in the supportive care of veterinary patients. In addition to providing access for nutritional support, they can provide stress free access for administration of medications, removing excess saliva and gastric fluids that occur with megaesophagus and GI stasis, or excess gas from dysbiosis. Though placement of these tubes is common, complications can occur, such as malposition, irritation, infection and dislodgement. In this presentation, we will explore the indications for each type of tube, the step-by-step procedure for placement, common complications associated with each tube type, and troubleshooting strategies to manage issues that may arise during placement and use. Mastery of this procedure can significantly improve patient care by ensuring that patients receive appropriate nutritional and therapeutic support while minimizing risks associated with these medical devices.

courses.title: Tie-Over Bandaging Techniques
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of tie-over bandages an essential technique for managing wounds located in areas where traditional bandages are impractical. Participants will learn indications, benefits, materials selection, application steps, common pitfalls, and modifications for challenging anatomical regions.

courses.title: IBD vs IBS: Key Differences for an Important Differential
courses.description: In this Royal Canin Continuing Education Event, Dr. Adam Rudinsky, MS, DACVIM reviews the problem of irritable bowel syndrome in dogs and cats. We will discuss our current understanding as well as how prevalent, concerning, and important this differential is to the health and well-being of our small animal patient population. Will specifically focus on the current literature supporting the existence of this disease as well as new information related to potential causes and treatment approaches. Tune in to get a clinical update on appropriate strategies to screen, diagnose and treat your irritable bowel patients.

courses.title: A Gentle Goodbye: Euthanasia Principles for Exotic Pets
courses.description: From anatomical differences and species-specific protocols to sensitive client communication, euthanasia in exotic pets poses special difficulties. This session provides practical guidance for veterinarians who are new to treating birds, reptiles, amphibians, and exotic mammals, with a focus on low-stress handling and methods compliant with the AVMA 2020 Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals. Participants will leave this session with the tools to carry out humane, compassionate euthanasia in the most common exotic species seen in general practice.

courses.title: Metronidazole: Friend or Foe? Battling Acute Diarrhea
courses.description: In this Royal Canin online veterinary CE, Dr. Adam Rudinsky, DACVIM reviews canine acute diarrhea management and major changes to common clinical approaches. This course covers how a small animal patient with acute diarrhea is diagnosed and treated based on current literature and new findings from recent research. Begging the question - is prescribing metronidazole truly helping our patients? Are there more effective and beneficial treatments available? Worse yet, could we be making things worse?

courses.title: Webinar - Titre testing and its role in more sustainable veterinary practice and personalised care.
courses.description: This webinar will discuss titre testing in dogs and cats where it is most useful and when it may not be appropriate. We will also be taking a wider look at why it could be an important step in more personalised veterinary care and a move away from blanket vaccination and other preventative health measures. As a profession, should we be changing our attitudes and wellness plans We will also discuss all of this with regards to sustainability.

courses.title: 5 Elements of Veterinary Hospice - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Veterinary hospice care is a unique case approach centered around education, preparation, and support for the pet and the client. Understanding what this service includes and what it does not include will help veterinary professionals solidify their role as animal advocators, strengthen the human animal bond, and maintain the highest level of client care.

courses.title: Essential Skills in Surgery & Ophthalmology
courses.description:
This EUVETCE Experiences seminar offers veterinarians and technicians a combined program in soft tissue surgery and ophthalmology for canine and feline patients.
The surgical sessions include practical approaches to abdominal exploratory procedures and organ biopsies, decision-making in gastrointestinal obstruction, and a review of core principles in gastrointestinal and urinary tract surgery. Emergency management is also addressed, with dedicated sessions on urinary obstruction, uroabdomen, thoracic trauma, chest tube placement, and feeding tube placement.
The ophthalmology sessions cover the diagnosis and management of deep and non-healing corneal ulcers, corneal lacerations, and ruptured globes. Other topics include practical approaches to glaucoma, conjunctivitis in dogs and cats, and acute-onset blindness. Surgical techniques such as entropion correction, cherry eye repair, eyelid tumor excision, and enucleation are discussed. Additional lectures offer updates on cataract management, long-term treatment strategies for keratoconjunctivitis sicca, and a review of essential ophthalmic medications for daily practice. The program ends with case discussions on complex ophthalmic conditions and guidance on referral decisions.

courses.title: Whats the Magic Formula? Treatment Framework for Every Behavior Case!
courses.description: Behavior cases are complex but treatment planning doesnt have to feel overwhelming. In this engaging and practical session, Dr. Christopher Pachel introduces a structured, flexible framework that guides clinicians and behavior professionals through the process of developing treatment plans for virtually any fear or anxiety-based condition in dogs and cats. Attendees will learn how to apply this magic formula across a range of clinical presentations, including canine separation anxiety, noise phobia, and leash reactivity, as well as feline house soiling, fear based aggression, and overstimulated play behavior. Clinical case examples, video demonstrations, and decision making strategies will illustrate how to individualize care within a repeatable, effective framework.

courses.title: Product Primer: Beyond One-Diet Fits All: Exploring Size-Based Canine Nutrition
courses.description:
The physical features of small and large dogs are obvious. However, among others, research has revealed gastrointestinal differences that could lead to the softer stool in the large sized dogs as compared to smaller sized dogs.
While formulating food for dogs of different size, considerations should be given to:
Kibble size and texture based on jaw structure & strength of the dogs.
Energy content in the food. Energy content in food for smaller dogs generally contains higher energy because of the higher proportion of active metabolic tissues per unit of the body as compared to larger dogs.
The body composition. Energy content in the food for the dogs weighing the same will vary based on their body composition. For example, Boxers and Labrador Retriever (Lab) weighing 60 lbs., energy content in the Boxer diet will be higher than Lab because Boxers are muscular as compared to Labs who contain higher proportion of adipose tissues.
Differences in gastrointestinal (GI) physiology of the small & large dogs. Food transit time and intestinal permeability varies based on the size of the dog.

courses.title: Microchipping Companion Animals: What Veterinary Professionals Need to Know
courses.description: A microchip for a pet is a tiny, injectable transponder that is implanted under the skin. It is such a small thing (about the size of a grain of rice), but it serves a crucial purpose in the event of a lost pet and proof of ownership is required. Each chip has a unique code is stored in a national database and can be traced back to a pet owner. Of course, we veterinary professionals are aware of the benefits of microchipping a pet, as long as the chip is registered and kept up to date. But do you know everything you need to know about microchipping your patients? Learn the ins and outs of this vital practice.

courses.title: Treating Contagions in the 21st Century: CIRDC and Antimicrobial Resistance
courses.description: In this video course, we take a look through the microscope and see the current state of microbe management. When do pets with a cough need antibiotics? How can we use antibiotics responsibly in this and other situations? Dr. Jennifer Chatfield will provide evidence-based responses and case studies to bring us all up to speed. We unmask the top pathogens causing respiratory illnesses today, discuss treatment and prevention, and learn best practices for juggling antimicrobial resistance with sick patients in a practical way.

courses.title: AETA Anytime CEs
courses.description:
The American Embryo Transfer Association (AETA) aims to present a unified voice for those involved in the embryo transfer industry in the promotion of mutual interests and objectives, provide continuing education and information regarding current issues in the embryo transfer industry for members. AETA embraces its responsibility as the resource for embryo transfer in the United States. This authority is developed and supported through our commitment to excellence in several broad areas: education and standards of quality.
These anytime, distance learning, online offerings will be available to AETA members and non-members to ensure they have access to timely, relevant, and cutting-edge ET information.

courses.title: Urinary Tract Surgery: let's get pumped for cleaning the pipes
courses.description: Urinary Tract Surgery: let's get pumped for cleaning the pipes is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: TPLO
courses.description: This CE provides an overview of cranial cruciate ligament disease with a focus on surgical treatment including TPLO, arthrotomy, and arthroscopy. Information regarding potential complications and expected outcomes is also reviewed.

courses.title: January 2025 RACE Submission
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Equipment Controls and Protocol for Soft Tissue Ultrasound - Intermediate to Advanced - Scan Only
courses.description: This program will cover machine functions and measurements needed for a complete abdominal exam. We will discuss the purpose of the different probes. We will cover how to scan the liver, spleen, kidneys, and bladder, pancreas, adrenals, and GI following a scanning protocol for these organs, so that the attendee can create a complete soft tissue ultrasound exam. This will be a Medical Program, that is hands-on scanning in a wet lab format for 8 hours of RACE CE.

courses.title: How to cope with sadness, grief and non-closure
courses.description: This is a PowerPoint lecture that addresses the sadness that affects so many veterinary staff members and examines the types of grief and lack of closure.

courses.title: Transitional Cell Carcinoma Diagnosis and Treatment
courses.description: The program will cover the TCVM herbs and medication that have been used in the 8 clinical cases. This will include the canine breeds, environmental factors and laboratory testing for Transitional Cell Carcinoma

courses.title: Slow, Stiff and Sore Dogs: Optimizing Comfort and Quality of Life - ON DEMAND
courses.description: Osteoarthritis intervertebral disc disease, degenerative myelopathy, and geriatric onset laryngeal paralysis polyneuropathy are conditions that impact on mobility in dogs. Osteoarthritis is the most common cause of long-term pain and mobility impairment in dogs. Currently there is no cure, therefore patient care is focused on managing pain and improving mobility and quality of life. Due to the complexity of the disease, a multimodal individualized plan is required for success. This approach includes pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment modalities. This webinar will use a case-based approach to demonstrate long-term management of an aging patient with mobility impairment.

courses.title: Rapid Thoracic Diagnostics: ECG and POCUS
courses.description: Originally recorded in 2025, this on-demand course will walk us through ECG and POCUS execution and interpretation. First, we'll identify abnormal waveforms, and the little details that point to chamber enlargement. Then follow the experts' guide to getting clear cardiac and thoracic images. These patient-side diagnostics are crucial to differentiate disease processes and treat quickly; every second counts when your patient can't breathe. Practice quick recognition of arrhythmias and irregularities with real case studies, and be ready to lung-e into action during cardiac crisis!

courses.title: PPID in Horses: Essential Steps for Diagnosis, Treatment, and Lifelong Management
courses.description: This course provides equine veterinarians with a practical, evidence-based approach to Pituitary Pars Intermedia Dysfunction (PPID) in horses. Participants will learn how to identify clinical signs, perform and interpret endocrine testing, and implement current treatment protocols including pharmacologic therapy and supportive care. The session also covers long-term management strategies, monitoring treatment response, and addressing common comorbidities such as insulin dysregulation and laminitis. Attendees can expect guidance to improve diagnostic accuracy, optimize therapeutic decisions, and enhance lifelong outcomes for horses with PPID.

courses.title: August 2025 RACE Submimssion
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Tube-Tastic! The Journey From Critical Care To Recovery
courses.description:
This live lecture empowers veterinary technicians to take an active, confident role in the nutritional management of critically ill dogs and cats. Participants will learn how nutrition functions as a therapeutic intervention, not just supportive care, and how timely, appropriate nutritional support can directly impact recovery, healing, and survival in hospitalized patients.
The program focuses on identifying patients at risk for malnutrition, appropriate timing for nutritional intervention, and strategies to reduce complications such as refeeding syndrome. Attendees will review evidence-based principles of enteral nutrition, including when to utilize the gastrointestinal tract, selection of feeding tube types, and considerations for cardiovascular stability and electrolyte balance.
Participants will walk through how to calculate and monitor resting energy requirements (RER), evaluate liquid, semi-elemental, polymeric, and blended diets, and assess feeding tolerance in hospitalized patients. Emphasis is placed on the veterinary technicians role in ongoing monitoring, communication, and advocacy to support healing, recovery, and improved outcomes in critical and recovering patients.
Searchable keywords: critical care nutrition, hospitalized patient nutrition, enteral feeding, feeding tubes, malnutrition in dogs and cats, RER calculation, refeeding syndrome, veterinary nursing care

courses.title: Anal Sacs: How to Help Patients Who Scoot, Lick, Leak, or Smell
courses.description:
Anal sac disease is one of the most common reasons dogs present with scooting, licking, odor, and perianal discomfort - yet the pathophysiology, diagnostic approach, and long-term management remain poorly understood.
This 60-minute, evidence-based lecture provides a clear, practical, and up-to-date framework for diagnosing and treating non-neoplastic anal sac disease, using current research and clinical insights from a veterinary dermatologist. Attendees will learn to differentiate impaction, sacculitis, and abscessation; identify key comorbidities including allergies and gastrointestinal disease; apply diagnostic decision-making (including when cytology and culture are - and are not - useful); and implement effective treatment strategies ranging from expression to infusion.
The session emphasizes inflammation-driven pathophysiology, antimicrobial stewardship, long-term prevention, and communication strategies for improving client understanding and adherence. Participants will leave with actionable protocols they can apply immediately in general practice to improve patient comfort and reduce recurrence.

courses.title: Keep Calm and Carry on: A comprehensive approach to FIC
courses.description: This lecture will focus on feline lower urinary tract diseases (FLUTD), with main focus on feline idiopathic cystitis. We will cover the main clinical signs as well as diagnosing cats with FLUTD. This lecture will focus on management of cats with FIC. We will be discussing medical management, multimodal environmental modification (MEMO) for cats and how to best implement MEMO and nutrition for FIC. We will also cover the AAFP/ISFM Environmental Needs Guidelines for cats.

courses.title: Be True to Your Teeth or They will be False to You: Canine and Feline Oral Disease in Chinese Medicine
courses.description:
Within the oral cavity, we see much disease in veterinary medicine. From malocclusion to periodontitis to cancer, it is an organ system that we treat from birth to death in animals. Its impacts on the rest of the body are large, from chronic inflammation and infection to heart, liver and kidney disease.
It is for this reason that Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine can help us with prevention, diagnosis and treatment ideas. In a nation where a 70-90% of our patients have oral disease by age two, it behooves us to take extra care and thought in our wellness and treatment plans in an integrative way.
This lecture aims to assist in this by addressing the following:
- the normal and balanced structure and function of the Spleen and Stomach channels in dogs and cats
- the pathologies that can affect the Spleen and Stomach channels
- nutritional, herbal and acupuncture treatments that can help treat these pathologies
- 2-3 case studies that exemplify the importance of the oral cavity treatment in integrative medicine

courses.title: Product Primer - FIC: Addressing the Risk Factors that Matter Most
courses.description: Feline idiopathic cystitis (FIC) is a complex disease process resulting in bladder pain and dysfunction secondary to an abnormal neuroendocrine response to stress. There are many documented risk factors for FIC, including both nutritional and environmental risk factors that have the potential to be modified for the benefit of these patients. In this seminar, we will briefly review FIC pathogenesis and risk factors. The five pillars of a health feline environment will be discussed in detail, with the goal of helping learners identify environmental deficiencies that can be addressed for their FIC patients. Finally, the role of nutrition will be discussed, with a special focus on nutritional risk factors such as obesity and low water consumption.

courses.title: Mastering Rabbit Spays and Neuters
courses.description: This lecture will walk participants through anatomical and physiological characteristics, indications for spay & neuter, pre- and post-operative management, and a step-by-step photographic approach to surgical ovariectomy, ovariohysterectomy, and both open and closed orchiectomy of companion rabbits with the goal of equipping veterinarians with the knowledge and skills needed to successfully perform reproductive surgeries in rabbits while optimizing patient outcomes and minimizing risks.

courses.title: Stronger for Longer: Maintaining Muscle & Mobility in the Aging Feline
courses.description: Are you missing the subtle signs of muscle loss and pain in your senior feline patients? In this free, one-hour session, Dr. Ashlie Saffire delves into the critical, yet often underdiagnosed, issues of feline mobility and muscle health. Attendees will learn how to differentiate between disease-associated cachexia, age-related sarcopenia, and frailty. The presentation emphasizes the crucial role of utilizing both Body Condition Score (BCS) and Muscle Condition Score (MCS) during every senior exam to catch early downward trends. Discover how to implement environmental modifications, structured mobility exercises, tailored nutritional support, and the science behind an innovative supplement to inhibit muscle atrophy and keep your feline patients stronger for longer!

courses.title: Comprehensive Weight Loss Strategies: Beyond Initial Feeding Calculations
courses.description: This lecture will explore the essential aspects of implementing a successful weight loss plan for cats and dogs, beyond the initial feeding calculations. Attendees will learn how to develop specific diet, environmental, and exercise modifications aimed at improving owner adherence to what are often significant lifestyle changes. Key topics include managing routine recheck appointments, monitoring weight loss rates, and adjusting feeding amounts as needed. The session will cover common barriers to success such as households with multiple pets, food-seeking behavior, and preventing unintended access to food. By attending this lecture, participants will gain valuable strategies to support their clients through every stage of their pets weight loss journey for long-term success and improved health.

courses.title: Executive Functioning Management and Mental Health
courses.description: The veterinary profession is demanding, both mentally and emotionally, leading to increased risk of stress and burnout among veterinarians and veterinary staff. Executive functioning (skills like planning, organization, time management, and emotional regulation) plays a critical role in managing these challenges. Executive functioning abilities are influenced by our mental health, emotional states, and our overall stress levels, potentially impacting effectiveness in managing those challenges. This module will explore how enhancing executive function can help veterinary professionals maintain mental health and well-being. By focusing on executive functioning skills, participants will learn strategies to effectively manage personal and professional demands, while simultaneously enhancing well-being.

courses.title: Periodontal case study. Putting out the fire
courses.description: In a case study titled "Putting Out the Fire," a mature Dachshund named Fifi presented with symptoms of periodontal disease, including inflamed gums and bad breath. A review of what causes periodontal disease, how it's treated and how prevented will be covered as well as the different treatments as they apply to Fifi's dental maladies.

courses.title: Go with the Flow: Navigating Fluid Therapy in Equine Critical Care
courses.description: The presenter will discuss the general principles for fluid therapy in equine critical care cases. Topics will include types of fluids, rate and volume of administration, goals and end points, and safety limits. Additionally, the physiologic parameters of fluid compartments will be assessed including total body water, extracellular fluid, and intracellular fluid.

courses.title: Standards in Small Animal Radiology Positioning and Safety
courses.description: Amber's veterinary career spans 15 years as she has been the lead diagnostic imaging tech at a specialty practice, a hospital manager at a general practice and is now a veterinary sonographer splitting her time between Boone and Atlanta. Amber's passion for mentorship and imaging led to the creation of ARADVETTECH, a company dedicated to empowering support staff to pursue formal education and strengthen the foundation of the veterinary community. Through ARADVETTECH, she helps teams enhance radiographic efficiency and diagnostic quality while also exploring ways to integrate ultrasound into general practice. In her free time you won't find Amber as she finds her peace and inspiration on dirt roads exploring in her 4Runner. The year ahead Amber is pursuing her VTS and hosting networking events thru ARADVETTECH to connect technician students to mentors within the community.

courses.title: Bowl Before Biopsy: The Value of Dietary Intervention Before Invasive Diagnostics in Feline Chronic Enteropathy
courses.description: A discussion on the most common causes of chronic enteropathies in cats will be provided. There will be a focus on how dietary intervention and feeding trials can be used as part of the diagnostic work-up prior to more invasive diagnostics such as biopsies and histopathology and ultimately acting as a potential therapeutic at the same time. We will discuss the difference between available diets (including hydrolyzed, novel protein, high fiber, and highly digestible) and when we should select one over another. We will work through an example case that can be used as a reference for similar cases in the future.
