courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Equine Ultrasound-Guided Joint Injections, Objective Gait Analysis & Rehabilitation Workshop
courses.description:
COURSE DESCRIPTION
This intensive and hands-on, one-day programme is designed for equine practitioners who want to advance their diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities in sports medicine and rehabilitation with the world's leading specialists, and apply these skills immediately in their daily clinical work.
With a strong emphasis on hands-on workshops and clinical panel discussions, this course provides a unique opportunity to learn and refine practical techniques under the guidance of international key opinion leaders in equine sports medicine and rehabilitation.
From ultrasound-guided joint injections to objective portable gait analysis using Consteed's revolutionary Smart Sneaker measuring ground reaction forces in real time, and the clinical application of modern rehabilitation modalities, each component of the programme is focused on delivering skills that can be implemented from day one after returning to practice.
Morning Lecture Sessions
The morning lecture sessions offer a concise, clinically focused overview of:
Practical tips and techniques for ultrasound-guided injections
New roles and applications of objective gait analysis
Matching the most appropriate rehabilitation modalities with specific lesions
Development of structured treatment plans and effective therapeutic monitoring
Clinical Case Panel Discussions
One of the highlights of the course is the Clinical Case Panel Discussions, where participants will engage directly with several world-leading specialists from diverse backgrounds.
These highly interactive sessions explore real-life clinical cases in an open and frank atmosphere, focusing on critical decision-making, treatment strategies, and optimisation of outcomes in everyday practice.
Afternoon Practical Sessions
The afternoon is dedicated to small-group practical sessions on live horses and high-fidelity anatomic replica simulators, ensuring a high level of individual hands-on participation and detailed instructor feedback.
Participants will

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Refractory Equine Glandular Gastric Disease Morbidity and Mortality Case Discussions
courses.description:
This interactive panel discussion brings together internationally recognised internal medicine specialists from Europe and the United States to discuss the challenges of treating Equine Glandular Gastric Disease EGGD and specifically how best to manage horses that are refractory to treatment. The discussion will focus primarily on pharmacological management but will also touch on other management and feeding strategies that can be used to improve healing rates and mitigate against reoccurrence.
Whilst recognising the limitations surrounding availability of certain drug formulations in different countries, the panelists will debate what they consider to be first line and second line drugs for treatment of EGGD how they use them to maximise efficacy and how they would modify their approach in the case of a non responder. The panelists will contribute a wealth of clinical experience and anecdote to the discussion but will be encouraged to justify their approaches based upon current evidence where available.
When do you consider a lesion healed
How long should you wait before deciding a horse is a non-responder?
Is there any value or science in determining intragastric pH in non-responders
Should you biopsy lesions that are refractory to treatment? If so, how do you interpret the results
What are the alternatives when acid suppression is not effective? When do you reach for corticosteroids
Should competition horses be rested during treatment Are there any other management strategies that might be effective
What is the role of the microbiome in horses with EGGD? Are antibiotics ever indicated
Are there any nutritional risk factors that could potentially delay or prevent healing

courses.title: Let's Go Tubing! Intubation, Extubation and Beyond!
courses.description: Every veterinary technician performing general anesthesia is responsible for securing an airway in a variety of small animal patients. Discussion includes an overview of the various types of endotracheal tubes and how to ensure proper cuff inflation. Learn to identify potential complications and avoid tracheal trauma during this essential task. Finally, we will explore extubation criteria and the value of a recovery checklist during the postoperative period.

courses.title: Enhancing Your VETSPAN: Maximize Your Health and Career Longevity Through the Five Pillars of Healthspan
courses.description: This course will introduce the veterinary community to the concept of VETSPAN, emphasizing how prioritizing health and well-being through the five pillars of Healthspan can increase career longevity, vitality, and emotional well-being. The session will empower participants with actionable strategies to improve their physical and emotional resilience, enabling them to thrive in a demanding profession.

courses.title: Product Primer: Obesity: A Growing Problem
courses.description: The obesity epidemic in cats and dogs continues to grow. Therapeutic weight loss diets and weight loss plans are the standard of care for most veterinarians, but there is still resistance from pet owners. This presentation focuses on communication techniques to help veterinarians identify stages of change in their clients. This presentation also discusses research that describes factors that would motivate a client to pursue a weight loss plan for their overweight pets, and strategies to help overcome difficult weight-related conversations. There is also a small section on weight loss diets and Royal Canins Satiety Support diet.

courses.title: Addressing Fear & Aggression in Avian Patients: A Constructional Approach
courses.description:
Veterinary visits can be very challenging for many animals, especially avian patients.
This short course will cover a novel technique for minimizing stress to birds, while also comparing this technique to past concepts covered in the original course. We will teach you an alternative, advanced approach to reinforcing desired behavior in avian patients displaying fear or aggression that are not responding to other Fear Free training techniques, in addition to providing several examples of F2F used to teach useful behaviors, and recommendations associated with the client and team communication surrounding the use of F2F.

courses.title: Fear Free Veterinary Certification Program: Equine
courses.description:
Fear Free and good horsemanship go hand in hand: Communication is the essence of both. Horses are large, powerful animals and injuries to equine veterinarians are common. Fear Free helps reduce injuries to veterinary staff and horses, improve the health and wellbeing of patients, save you time, create more manageable patients, and earn your clients lasting trust and commitment.
The Veterinary Certification Program - Equine teaches you how to use Fear Free concepts to ensure that barn visits and hospital visits go as smoothly as possible. Video clips and slides show you how to examine equine patients safely by using gentle techniques, perform routine procedures in a non-threatening way, recognize signs of stress in equine patients, help owners train their horses to cooperate in medical care, hoof care, and more.

courses.title: On Demand: Skin and Ears: Updated Clinical Thinking on Pyoderma and Otitis Externa
courses.description: Dermatology cases can snowball into recurring nightmares - chronic skin infections, purulent ear discharge, and switching antibiotics again. When skin and ears aren't getting better, it's our least favorite type of follow-up visit. That's why we're teaming up with a real derm-namite duo, Drs. Pieper and Santoro to learn what actually works and why. Viewers will learn a tiered framework to guide initial antibiotic selection, with stepwise escalation for severe and resistant cases. We'll review the epidemiology of resistant skin infections, as well as strategies for long-term control of atopy and otitis. With a fresh framework and insider tips, you'll have the perfect plan the next time a client asks, "What else can we do?"

courses.title: Unlocking the Gut-Kidney Connection: Innovative Approaches to Managing Chronic Kidney Disease in Cats
courses.description: This seminar will explore the emerging science behind the gut-kidney axis and its implications for feline practice. We will delve into how gut health impacts kidney function in cats, discussing the latest research and clinical evidence that connects gastrointestinal health with renal outcomes. Key topics will include the mechanisms of gut-kidney interactions, diagnostic approaches, and management strategies for optimizing both gut and kidney health. Participants will gain practical insights into how to apply this knowledge in clinical settings to improve patient care and treatment outcomes for cats with chronic kidney disease (CKD).

courses.title: Veterinary Recordkeeping Compliance: Florida Laws, Best Practices, and Risk Management
courses.description: Accurate and compliant medical recordkeeping is essential to patient care, continuity of treatment, regulatory compliance, and risk management in veterinary practice. This course provides an overview of Florida statutes and administrative rules governing veterinary medical records, including documentation requirements, ownership, confidentiality, retention, and telehealth recordkeeping obligations. Participants will learn how complete and defensible records support quality patient care, protect veterinarians during client disputes and board investigations, and improve overall practice efficiency. Real-world examples and common recordkeeping mistakes will be discussed, along with practical strategies to strengthen recordkeeping processes.

courses.title: Multifaceted Approach to Feline CKD
courses.description: This session will discuss utilizing a multifaceted approach to the management of Feline CKD. It will include perfusion/hydration as well as medical management of anemia, hypertension, proteinuria and other symptoms of CKD. The nutritional management of CKD will be discussed as adjunctive therapy. Finally the speaker will discuss individualizing the management plan to the patient and when it becomes time to consider quality of life.

courses.title: Not Who, But What: Changing the narrative around medical mistakes
courses.description: Medical errors are an inevitable part of healthcare, but how we respond to them can make all the difference for patients, clients, and veterinary teams. This session challenges the traditional blame focused approach to medical mistakes and advocates for a systems based mindset that prioritizes learning, accountability, and improvement. Through real world case studies we will explore how narratives around medical errors are shaped and how shifting from who is to blame to what is to blame can foster a culture of safety and transparency. Participants will examine error statistics in both human and veterinary medicine, learn how to identify and respond to mistakes effectively, and understand the psychological and organizational factors that influence outcomes. We will also delve into the nuances of human behavior distinguishing between human error, at risk behavior, and reckless conduct and discuss how to apply root cause analysis RCA and failure mode and effects analysis FMEA to strengthen internal systems. By the end of this session, attendees will be equipped with practical tools and a new mindset to approach medical errors constructively and compassionately.

courses.title: Splints and Scalpels: Soft Tissue and Orthopedic Trauma Repair
courses.description: Managing wounds is often complicated, a marathon littered with infectious and inflammatory hurdles along the whole way. In this series, Drs. Goh and Marvel are our guides through the tensions of wound reconstruction and fracture repairs. We'll start with a list of dressing options and opinions, recap bandaging foundations, and follow step-by-step flap tutorials. Then take a sharp turn into proper bone support using casts, splints, and surgery to achieve best results. This dynamic duo tag-teams the final lecture with real case examples, so you know what to do when they limp into your practice.

courses.title: May 2025 Monthly RACE Packet
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Principles of Fracture Stabilization
courses.description: Are you interested in learning or improving your approach and reduction of long bone fractures? Are you interested in learning simple techniques designed for the general practitioner to stabilize the most commonly seen fractures in dogs and cats? This laboratory is the one for you! The participant will learn reliable techniques and valuable practical tips helpful in repairing simple and more challenging comminuted fractures of the long bones. New implant designs have made fracture repair much simpler and more affordable. In addition, postoperative management of patients has also been simplified, and complications are rare if the principles of fracture repair are followed. This course will familiarize participants with fracture repair techniques, including IM pin/cerclage, tension band, bone plating, and External Skeletal Fixation (ESF), through lecture and clinical case presentations. Following the lecture and case review, participants will repair fractures on plastic bone models and cadavers. Postoperative radiographs will be taken to evaluate the participants' repair technique

courses.title: Periodontal Disease, Tooth Resorption, and Stomatitis
courses.description: This comprehensive lecture focuses on three critical dental conditions in veterinary medicine: Periodontal Disease, Tooth Resorption, and Stomatitis. Designed for veterinary professionals, the course will provide in-depth knowledge and practical skills to diagnose, treat, and manage these common oral health issues in small animals. Key topics include the etiology and pathogenesis of periodontal disease, clinical signs and stages, diagnostic techniques such as periodontal probing and dental radiography, as well as treatment strategies ranging from professional cleaning to advanced periodontal procedures. Additionally, the lecture will cover the types and classification of tooth resorption, risk factors, prevalence in different species, and the importance of radiographic diagnostics. Stomatitis will also be addressed, focusing on its causes, clinical presentation particularly in feline patients diagnostic criteria, and evidence-based treatment approaches. Participants will develop proficiency in diagnosing these conditions through clinical examination and radiography while formulating appropriate treatment plans based on disease stage and patient factors. The course will also provide practical knowledge on surgical techniques, including extractions and periodontal treatments, along with post-treatment care and long-term management strategies for affected patients. By combining theoretical knowledge with practical case studies, this lecture ensures that attendees can apply their learning to real-world clinical scenarios, ultimately enhancing their skills in dental diagnostics and treatment to improve the quality of dental care in veterinary practice.

courses.title: Behavior and Chronic Pain in Dogs: A Clinical Guide to Recognition and Management
courses.description: This course covers the physiological and anatomical base of the development of chronic pain conditions in dogs, behavioural signs of pain-related disorders, as well as diagnostic steps, treatment, and management of the behavioural side of chronic pain in dogs.

courses.title: Belly-aching babies: gastrointestinal issues in kittens
courses.description: Having a kitten in the home is meant to be a time of fun and wonder. Gastrointestinal issues such as vomiting or diarrhea can pose unexpected challenges, hampering growth and wellbeing and interrupting vaccination protocols as well as training. This course will review common causes of vomiting and diarrhea in the juvenile cat, exploring key concepts in diagnostic testing and therapeutics. Preventive measures such as appropriate deworming and age-appropriate nutrition will be discussed.

courses.title: Breed Phenotypes of Dermatologic Disorders in Canines: Understanding Variations and Clinical Implications
courses.description: This lecture is a 50-min lecture designed to provide a deeper understanding of the role that breed plays in the manifestation of various dermatologic conditions in dogs. This information will provide a veterinarian with an improved set of skills for disease recognition and diagnosis for common dermatologic conditions such as allergic diseases, sebaceous adenitis, non-inflammatory alopecic conditions, otitis externa, keratinization and follicular disorders, and more. Strategies for treatments will also be provided from a breed-specific angle. This talk is meant to be practical and engaging, allowing general practice veterinarians to increase their pattern recognition skills to improve their clinical outcomes.

courses.title: Introduction to Canine and Feline Osteopathy
courses.description: The webinar is an introduction to osteopathy for dogs and cats. It will cover basic principles of history, philosophy, anatomy and neurophysiology. It will highlight the common neurologic and musculoskeletal conditions commonly treated with osteopathic techniques. The webinar will demonstrate the diagnosis and treatment of spay/neuter adhesions and other internal visceral -fascial restrictions that lead to basic misalignment patterns in the musculoskeletal system.

courses.title: Rewards For All: Creating Meaningful Team Rewards
courses.description: The veterinary industry has a history of ignoring our team members in pursuit of higher profits and new equipment to care for patients. However, our team is the best tool we have to care for our patients. Imagine a practice where teams come to work day after day and actually ENJOY their practice. They get along with their team members and work well together. They are empathetic towards each other and supportive of personal problems that may be happening outside of the workspace. Taking care of your team through better rewards above and beyond basic wages will create a culture of loyalty and retention, leading to better outcomes and profitability.

courses.title: Surgical Procedures for General Practitioners: Urinary, Gastrointestinal and Basic Oncology Techniques
courses.description: During this course, participants will receive the most up-to-date information on urinary tract and gastrointestinal diseases with a focus on surgical management of both benign and malignant conditions. Lectures will be followed by laboratories that focus on having participants perform the same procedures that were highlighted during the lectures. At the end of this course, participants will be comfortable with many different urinary tract and gastrointestinal procedures, with a focus on procedures such as cystotomy, cystostomy tube placement, urethrostomy, gastrotomy, biopsy, enterotomy, intestinal resection and anastomosis, local flaps, digit amputation, and vulvoplasty.

courses.title: Pain Is Inevitable, Suffering Is Optional: Managing the Painful Patient Beyond Anti-Inflammatories
courses.description: This session will explore modern strategies for managing pain in veterinary patients beyond traditional anti-inflammatories. It will review the different types of pain, highlight syndrome-specific approaches, and place special emphasis on neuropathic pain management. Attendees will gain insight into emerging therapies and practical tools to improve comfort and quality of life in their patients.

courses.title: Well begun is half done - Giving puppies a good start!
courses.description: Raising a puppy from birth to adulthood is a critical period marked by rapid physical and physiological changes. Proper nutrition is essential to ensure healthy growth and development. Mistakes in feeding - such as providing diets with inappropriate energy content, allowing unrestricted (ad lib.) feeding, or switching to adult food too early - can hinder proper growth. Overfeeding, even when done out of affection (e.g., excessive puppy food, table scraps, treats, or supplements), can lead to early weight gain, obesity, and increase the risk of orthopedic and other diseases later in life.

courses.title: Nutrition and Enteral Feeding for the Critical Cat
courses.description: Nutritional support is crucial to the outcome of critical patients, and can be successfully implemented in general practice. In this seminar, we will engage in a practical discussion of how to implement assisted feeding in inappetent cats. Integrating common case examples, participants will learn when to consider assisted feeding, the approach to client communication, and practical tips and resources to make feeding tube placement and management easier. Anyone who cares for cats can learn to place a feeding tube and elevate their feline medicine techniques.

courses.title: A Veterinary Team Members Guide to Financial Conversations with Pet Owners
courses.description:
In the rapidly changing economy and landscape of veterinary care, cost of care is a growing and critical discussion. While veterinary clients are struggling to afford the rising costs of care, patients may receive less care or sometimes no care at all. Veterinary team members are often stuck in the middle of providing care for a client within the limitations of pet families. The emotional, mental, and moral distress that veterinary teams are facing due to the growing client limitations highlight the need for a new approach to veterinary care.
A wide variety of financial tools exist that can assist owners in affording veterinary care for their beloved pets. These tools include pet insurance, credit based financing solutions, payment plans, grant options, and more. The tricky part is knowing how they can all work together in your practice to create the best outcomes for the patients and their owners. Paraprofessionals often shoulder the majority of the burden when it comes to financial conversations, though they receive limited education on the topic.
With proper understanding of the financial tools that exist within the veterinary profession, veterinary teams can turn some of these very emotionally charged conversations into a supportive partnership that improves the culture within the hospital, client retention, and patient outcomes.
This lecture will explore available financial tools in the veterinary industry and empower veterinary team members to discuss these options with clients. Understanding these tools and how to most appropriately use them can improve team culture and wellbeing by minimizing situations of moral distress and lead to healthier veterinary-client-patient relationships.

courses.title: Mind Over Money: Financial Wellness for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: Originally presented in 2024, this lecture series is back to help us transform our financial future! Too often, busy veterinary professionals are left unsure and confused on how to make good financial decisions regarding their budget, savings, and debt payoff. Dr. Grace Kim and certified Life Coach Julie Squires will lead us through a systematic, thoughtful approach to money. It's more than just crunching numbers and spreadsheets - this course helps reframe our thoughts on financial burdens by inviting self-compassion and personal goals to the party. It's time to stop working for money, and make your money work for YOU!

courses.title: Barking Up the Right Tree: Creating your 6-Star Dental Practice
courses.description: This presentation will provide veterinarians with the knowledge and skills needed to evaluate and improve their dental practices. It will focus on the integration of equipment, education, and staffing relevant to dental procedures within their general practices.

courses.title: The Anti-Inflammatory Diet: Does it Exist in Pet Food?
courses.description: In human nutrition, anti-inflammatory diets contain a variety of nutrient dense, fresh foods. For pets, minimally processed raw and lightly cooked diets offer some similarities. These characteristics will be described in this talk, along with selected clinical studies that may demonstrate an anti-inflammatory effect from feeding them.

courses.title: Panel Discussion - Equine CT vs MRI
courses.description: With the tremendous growth of options in equine CT and MRI, it can be difficult to know when to use which modality. Join us for what promises to be an exciting panel discussion with an international panel of world-leading experts with extensive experience in this field. The pros and cons of the various types of CT and MRI systems, including low field and high field MRI, cone beam and fan beam CT and standing sedated and anesthetized studies will be discussed. The panel will cover what to expect from the information gained in these studies and how to best use it as part of your diagnostic toolbox. We will provide case examples to illustrate and discuss the merits, benefits and limitations of the modalities

courses.title: The Tree Pose Philosophy: Strong Roots (GPs) + Reaching Branches (Specialists)
courses.description: Strong patient care depends on strong collaboration. The Tree Pose Philosophy: Strong Roots (GPs) + Reaching Branches (Specialists) explores how intentional partnerships between general practitioners and specialists lead to better outcomes for patients, clients, and veterinary teams. In this session, Jessica Larson, DVM, DACVIM-SAIM, will share practical, real-world insight into building effective collaborative care relationships- focusing on clarity, communication, and trust across primary and specialty care.

courses.title: Movement as Medicine: How Exercise can Help Alleviate Pain
courses.description: This presentation explores the role of physical activity in managing and reducing pain in dogs. Drawing on current research from humans and animals, as well as clinical experience, we'll examine how tailored exercise programs can improve mobility, reduce inflammation, and enhance quality of life in dogs. Attendees will learn about the physiological mechanisms behind exercise-induced pain relief, common therapeutic exercises, and practical considerations for designing safe, effective movement plans. This session highlights how movement can be a powerful, non-invasive tool in canine pain management.

courses.title: Uncharted Leadership Essentials 2023 Submission
courses.description:
This program delves into crafting an inspiring vision, nurturing a shared sense of purpose, and striking the delicate balance between the needs of the veterinary team, clients, and patients. Additionally, participants are introduced to the powerful DiSC model for enhancing communication and leadership capabilities. Understanding behavioral tendencies and practicing flexible communication are essential skills taught to build stronger relationships and more effective teams.
Participants learn tools to achieve team buy-in as well as provide impactful coaching and feedback, breaking through barriers and fostering a culture of continuous improvement within their veterinary practices. Lastly, this program is rounded out with action-oriented modules on not only setting priorities but getting them done!
This program equips veterinary professionals with the tools to effectively engage their teams, drive collaboration, and successfully implement positive changes, ultimately ensuring a prosperous and fulfilling veterinary career for themselves and the teams they lead.

courses.title: Nuts and Bolts Part 2: Anesthesia Monitoring- Troubleshooting and Treating
courses.description: This program will review the standard anesthesia monitors including pulse oximetry, capnography, noninvasive blood pressure, electrocardiography, and temperature. The presenter will then discuss when to worry about the results, how to troubleshoot those problematic parameters, and potential treatment options for various situations. The presenter will pay particular attention to correcting hypotension, hypoxemia, and bradycardia.

courses.title: The Critical Kitten Window: Practical Microbiome Medicine Protocols (On Demand Webinar)
courses.description: This webinar provides veterinarians with a practical, evidence-informed framework for applying microbiome medicine during the critical early-life period in kittens. Focusing on the post-weaning and early pediatric window, the session explains how diet transitions, stressors, antibiotics, and growth demands interact to shape gut function, resilience, and clinical outcomes. Drawing on recent kitten studies and relevant feline and comparative data, the lecture introduces decision-making protocols to help clinicians distinguish expected transitional GI signs from situations requiring nutritional intervention. Particular emphasis is placed on when a standard kitten diet is appropriate versus when a therapeutic GI diet is biologically justified, including post-antibiotic recovery and multi-stressor contexts. Attendees will leave with clear, practice-ready decision frameworks, monitoring cues, and nutrition-based strategies to support gut resilience, reduce unnecessary escalation, and improve outcomes during this vulnerable developmental window.

courses.title: September 2025
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: PES On-Demand 2024
courses.description: The Florida Association of Equine Practitioners (the equine division of the Florida Veterinary Medical Association) PES On-Demand 2024 offers continuing education for veterinarians and veterinary technicians/staff through on-line lecture sessions (complete with quizzes) to attain required continuing education.

courses.title: Rethinking Deworming: A New Approach to Equine Parasite Control Involving the Gut Microbiome
courses.description:
Equine parasite control is evolving from a primarily drug-based approach toward a more integrated understanding of the gastrointestinal tract as a complex ecosystem. This session examines the interactions among the equine host, intestinal microbiome, and cyathostomin populations, with emphasis on their implications for clinical management.
Cyathostomin life stages, including encysted larvae and larval emergence, are associated with changes in mucosal integrity and inflammatory responses that may influence microbial stability. Conversely, alterations in the gut microbiome resulting from anthelmintic administration, dietary change, stress, or pasture management practices may affect parasite dynamics and disease risk in susceptible horses.
Participants will review current evidence regarding these interactions and discuss how they inform sustainable parasite control strategies, including targeted deworming and management practices aimed at maintaining gastrointestinal health and microbial diversity.
Emerging research on nematode-associated microbiota will also be introduced, including its potential role in parasite development and host interaction, and the implications for future control strategies.

courses.title: Three Ds of Antimicrobial Stewardship: Minimizing Resistance While Enhancing Therapeutic Success
courses.description: This course is a case-based approach to focus on the clinical use of antimicrobials in the era of stewardship. Case studies will include skin, urinary tract, uterine, surgical, dentistry, and use during gastroenteritis. The cases will focus on the impact of antimicrobial use for the acute infection and the after-effects of using them appropriately or inappropriately.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Oral Anatomy and Positional Terminology
courses.description: Whether a new graduate or a seasoned practitioner, veterinarians and their team will learn about or review oral anatomy and positional terminology from a veterinary dentist. The presenter will use high-quality images to clarify his teaching points.

courses.title: On Demand: Keep Moving: Optimizing Mobility Requires a Whole Body Approach
courses.description: In this 2 credit hour webinar, we'll break outside the box of NSAID-only OA protocols and consider a broader picture for maintaining mobility and muscle mass in aging cats and dogs. Learn to incorporate muscle condition scoring into our standard exams, implement rehab exercises and activity-based treatment, and evaluate commonly recommended supplements for improving joint health, muscle mass, and mobility in both dogs and cats.

courses.title: Practical Blood Banking and Donor Programs
courses.description: This presentation provides a practical overview of blood banking in veterinary medicine, covering donor sourcing, screening, blood collection, processing, and storage. Attendees will learn how to ensure donor and recipient safety through proper selection criteria, blood typing, and crossmatching to prevent transfusion reactions. The session also explores strategies to maintain blood quality, manage storage challenges, and recruit donors through community engagement. Practical guidance will help participants implement or enhance effective blood banking protocols in their practices.

courses.title: NAVIGATING CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE IN CATS AND DOGS BEYOND THE NUMBERS
courses.description: In this lecture, well explore chronic kidney disease (CKD) in dogs and cats, with a focus on key insights to enhance patient management. Topics include the role of FGF23 in early CKD, phosphorus targets, IRIS guidelines, the connection between the microbiome and CKD, nutritional support strategies, and practical clinical pearls to simplify treatment.

courses.title: Striving Toward Antimicrobial Stewardship: The Role of Culture and Susceptibility Testing. The Best Bang for your Bugs
courses.description: This course will discuss antimicrobial stewardship and explain how to interpret culture and susceptibility testing. The presenter will discuss empirical choice antibiotics for various scenarios and the pitfalls we may see when dosing without culture. She will then utilize two case examples to explain culture and susceptibility and how to interpret the data given by the reference laboratory. Ultimately this should set up the listener to understand how a culture can be utilized to determine the correct antibiotic for a given infection.

courses.title: F is for Fatigue
courses.description:
Description: This presentation on mental wellness uses a mnemonic device of important words that begin with the letter f. The words:
Fatigue
Flame on (Burnout)
perfectionism
Fooled you (Cognitive Distortions)
Filtering
Feelings
Fictitious thoughts
Frustration
Failure
Findings
Flame off (Combatting Burnout)
Flexibility
Focus
SelF Care
are important to remember when dealing with a mental crisis as is so common in veterinary medicine today.

courses.title: Antimicrobial Stewardship: Designing the Antimicrobial Dosing Regimen: the MIC is the KEY
courses.description: This course will discuss antimicrobial stewardship and considering the correct choices of drug for a given infection. Differences in bactericidal vs bacteriostatic drugs will be discussed. The presenter will also discuss time-dependent vs concentration-dependent drugs. She will use case examples and explain how pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics can be used to design your dosing regimen.

courses.title: Rehabilitation of the Aging Patient
courses.description: The participant can expect to go through the process of aging, senior versus geriatric and the expected life stages based on breed/size. There will be a basic outline going through each organ system and the changes that occur as dogs age then a case study on management of multi joint degenerative joint disease in an older dog.

courses.title: Nutritional Management of Pancreatitis
courses.description: Pancreatitis can be managed through focus on key nutritional factors and diligent owner compliance. The healthcare teams role in managing pancreatitis is crucial, beginning with proper identification of pancreatitis vs. other vomiting and diarrheic conditions. This webinar will focus on the healthcare teams role in identifying and managing pancreatitis and the key nutritional factors responsible for minimizing signs and symptoms associated with pancreatitis.

courses.title: Fear Free Animal Trainer: Preventive and Proactive Training
courses.description:
In this module, you will learn ways in which the Fear Free Animal Trainer can partner in Fear Free efforts to keep animals calm during veterinary care, procedures, and even on the day of surgery. This includes teaching animals the concept of a Treat-Ment station, training them to accept passive restraint, and acclimating them to sounds and equipment used during common diagnostic procedures.
While it's impossible to train for every possible scenario, general training strategies can be practiced, such as training a dog to lie on this side while being handled, preparing him for an injection, or teaching him to indicate his willing consent for handling or care.
Through several in-hospital and at-home video tutorials, you will learn step-by-step how to proactively prepare animals for procedures such as ECGs, radiographs, ultrasounds, surgery, and more.

courses.title: Building Resilience in Veterinary Healthcare: Actionable Exercise and Nutrition Strategies for Career Longevity
courses.description: This virtual course is tailored to meet the unique physical and nutritional demands faced by veterinarians and their healthcare teams. Participants will gain practical insights and science-backed strategies on exercise and nutrition that are easy to adopt and aim to enhance durability, energy levels, and resilience. This session is designed to provide immediate, actionable steps, helping attendees integrate small but impactful habits into their daily routine for sustainable health and career success

courses.title: Nutrition in Equine Health and Performance
courses.description: Nutrition for the healthy horse is fairly straightforward; however, in the equine patient, a more scientific and clinical case approach is often needed. This presentation will offer an overview of the science behind nutrition and medical conditions of the horse, offer case studies of certain clinical conditions, as well as focus on the specific needs of the performance horse including guidelines to assist the equine veterinarian or veterinary technician in determining the best feeding options. Discussions will explore the pathophysiology of these conditions to better understand the role that nutrition can play in not only helping the athletic performance horse, but also our everyday equine companions and patients.

courses.title: INFECTIOUS CONDITIONS: WHAT TRAINERS NEED TO KNOW
courses.description: In this module, we will review the signs and risk factors associated with infectious diseases in dogs and cats. We will cover how to minimize disease risk when training pets as well as how to properly disinfect and manage the training environment.

courses.title: A Gentle Goodbye: Euthanasia Principles for Exotic Pets
courses.description: From anatomical differences and species-specific protocols to sensitive client communication, euthanasia in exotic pets poses special difficulties. This session provides practical guidance for veterinarians who are new to treating birds, reptiles, amphibians, and exotic mammals, with a focus on low-stress handling and methods compliant with the AVMA 2020 Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals. Participants will leave this session with the tools to carry out humane, compassionate euthanasia in the most common exotic species seen in general practice.

courses.title: The Anatomy of an Error: Dissecting Mistakes to Build Safer Systems
courses.description: Behind every medical error lies an opportunity not just for accountability, but for transformation. This session takes a deep dive into the anatomy of medical mistakes, using a real world case involving alfaxalone and ketamine to illustrate how even small missteps can have significant consequences. Participants will explore the foundations of a just culture, learning to distinguish between reckless and at risk behavior while shifting the focus from individual blame to systemic improvement. Through hands on tools like Root Cause Analysis (RCA), the 5 Whys, fishbone diagrams, and the Swiss cheese model, attendees will learn how to uncover the true root causes of errors. The session also introduces Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) as a proactive strategy to prevent mistakes before they happen especially when introducing new medications or protocols. Attendees will leave with a framework for building a Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) plan, implementing risk reduction strategies using the Plan Do Study Act (PDSA) cycle, and navigating common pitfalls in system redesign. With a focus on practical solutions and cultural change, this session empowers veterinary professionals to take meaningful action even when perfection is not possible.

courses.title: Bandaging 102 Advanced Bandaging Techniques
courses.description: This program provides an in depth overview of advanced small animal bandaging techniques including fiberglass casts, SPICA splints, external fixator bandaging, Ehmer slings, and the use of vacuum-assisted closure (VAC) systems. Participants will learn clinical indications, materials selection, application steps, and key troubleshooting points. Keywords: veterinary bandaging, casts, SPICA splints, external fixators, VAC therapy, orthopedic support, wound care.

courses.title: Canine Diabetes Made Easy
courses.description: Diabetes is a treatable disease, yet many dogs are euthanized shortly after diagnosis. A significant factor in the decision to euthanize is the effect of the disease on the owner's finances and quality of life. In this lecture, we will compare old dogmas of complicated treatment for canine diabetes with new opportunities; these options make it a simpler disease to treat, reducing the owner's treatment burden.

courses.title: Emergency Techniques for the General Practitioner
courses.description:
This cadaver-based course covers emergency management of penetrating thoracic and abdominal trauma through hands-on practice and discussion. Procedures include thoracostomy tube placement, tracheostomy, laryngeal foreign body removal, cardiopulmonary resuscitation and defibrillation, abdominocentesis, nasoesophageal tube placement, and endoscopic foreign body removal.
By the end of this course, participants will be able to:
- Perform Abdominal and Thoracic FAST (AFAST/TFAST) examinations to identify free fluid
- Perform thoracocentesis and abdominocentesis using appropriate technique and landmarks
- Place and manage nasogastric (NG) tubes and esophagostomy (E) tubes
- Perform urinary catheterization in male and female patients
- Demonstrate central venous catheter placement and surgical cutdown techniques
- Perform nasotracheal oxygen supplementation and basic airway management
- Perform emergency tracheostomy and chest tube placement
- Deliver high-quality CPR using current BLS and ALS principles
- Select and prioritize appropriate emergency procedures based on clinical presentation

courses.title: Gait Changes in Senior Pets - Arthritis? Or something more?
courses.description:
Mobility changes in senior pets can be challenging to differentiate between
orthopedic or neurologic origins, and are often a combination of both. This program provides education from history taking to exam findings to help facilitate the veterinarian's clinical ability to detect neurologic
symptoms and pain as well as provide treatment recommendations and client education with the overall goal of improving the quality of life for neurologic senior pets.

courses.title: Beyond the Break: Mastering Canine and Feline Jaw Fractures
courses.description: This presentation on diagnosing and treating jaw fractures in dogs and cats will cover a comprehensive range of topics. The agenda includes an introduction to jaw fractures, basic anatomy and physiology of the canine and feline skull, common causes of jaw fractures, clinical signs, diagnostic imaging techniques, classification of fractures, treatment options, and case studies. The presentation begins with defining jaw fractures and their prevalence, then delves into the anatomical structures involved. It discusses various causes of jaw fractures in dogs and cats, including trauma from accidents and falls. Clinical signs and diagnostic methods, particularly radiographic imaging, will be explored in detail. The presentation would then cover fracture classification and treatment options, ranging from conservative management to surgical repair techniques. Real-world case studies will be presented to illustrate the diagnostic process, treatment plans, and outcomes. The presentation would conclude with a recap of key points and emphasize the importance of early intervention in jaw fracture cases.

courses.title: Certificate Program: Master Behavioral Medicine
courses.description: In this course, we break down the language barrier between pets and people. Certified veterinary behaviorists, Drs. Pike and Learn, share proven methods to rule-out medical concerns, identify and modify unwanted behaviors, and prevent escalation. We'll discuss low-stress handling, cooperative care, and pharmaceutical options in depth, including alternative and adjunctive therapies like nutraceuticals. For anyone dealing with problematic puppies, fractious felines, or white-coat syndrome, this certificate program has it all!

courses.title: Dental Escape Room: Daisy and Sherlock's Excellent Adventure
courses.description: This interactive course will walk the participant through two dental case scenarios. One involves a cat with dental resorptive lesions, and the other involves a senior dog with a dental slab fracture and underlying health issues. The participant must select the optimum diagnostic, treatment, and home care regimens to complete the cases.

courses.title: Genetic Testing Unleashed: Practical Applications in Small Animal Medicine
courses.description: From the beginning of life to their senior years, our patients DNA remains constant, but the technology for genetic testing is continually evolving. This session will explore effective strategies for implementing the latest advancements in genetic testing within small animal practice. We will also discuss how to interpret health-related results and how to use this information to develop proactive care plans.

courses.title: Leave no stone unturned when it comes to stranguria, hematuria and FLUTD
courses.description: Undiagnosed urolithiasis can lead to chronic pain in the feline patient and frustration for both the veterinarian and pet parent. As point of care ultrasound (POCUS) ultrasound technology is becoming more accessible and user friendly in veterinary general practice, it is now easier than ever to incorporate into everyday use. Learning how to scan the feline bladder will improve the veterinarians diagnostic capabilities and elevate the level of care for cats with feline lower urinary tract disease (FLUTD). The participants will learn basic scanning skills and how to diagnose common lower urinary tract diseases with a focus on urolithiasis. There will also be a discussion on dissolution options and recommendations on when its time to pursue surgery.

courses.title: Master Canine and Feline Endocrine Disorders
courses.description:
Originally presented in 2025, we've brought together a Master course for everything endocrine! The consequences of hormonal changes are often difficult to confirm and tricky to treat, especially in general practice. Celebrated speaker Dr. Andrew Bugbee simplifies updated approaches to screening, diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring of disorders commonly referred to specialty care. He'll break down Addison's disease, Cushing's syndrome, diabetes, and thyroid dysfunction with clear distinctions. Then, we'll close up with practical management guidance for diabetic ketoacidosis from Dr. Stuart Walton.
If you have questions on new oral medications for diabetes, wearable glucose monitors for pets, or simplified monitoring of Cushing's and Addison's disease, this course is for you!

courses.title: VetAhead - Small Mammal Exotics
courses.description: These courses are devoted to rabbit medicine we delve into understanding and treating these cuddly but delicate patients, from proper handling and examining techniques to helpful diagnostic tools, common illnesses and performing anesthesia. You will gain valuable knowledge, crucial skills and indispensable tips that you will be able to put to use immediately in your practice, clinic or hospital.

courses.title: December 2024
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Itch Happens: New Help for Atopy
courses.description: Dermatology cases are very common and identifying and treating the root cause is critical to relieve the patients irritating clinical signs. Nutrition plays a key role in the health of the epidermal barrier; thus, many dermatologic diseases may respond to specific dietary interventions. This presentation reviews the main causes of skin issues in dogs and how to diagnose the underlying condition as we work toward a rule-out diagnosis of canine atopic dermatitis. We will then delve deeper into the treatment of atopic dermatitis with a focus on the nutrients that can support the skin barrier and immune system to help manage atopic dogs in practice.

courses.title: FIC: Treating the Risk Factors that Matter Most
courses.description: Feline idiopathic cystitis (FIC) is a complex disease process impacted by many factors. The role of stress as a factor in FIC is abundantly clear. As a result, a deep dive into the patients history and environment is essential to understanding and managing their disease. This seminar will review and highlight the importance of the 5 Pillars of a Healthy Feline Environment in the management of FIC, guiding participants on how to identify and correct deficiences in the 5 pillars. Other factors impacting FIC including diet will be explored.

courses.title: Name that Skin Lesion!
courses.description: This interactive course will walk the participant through multiple common dermatology lesions with accompanying patient photos. Questions will be asked about each lesion, and the answers will include information on the presentation, diagnostic tests, underlying conditions, and recommended treatments.

courses.title: The Itchy and Scratchy Cat: how to provide relief when options seem limited
courses.description: Cats can have unique presentations of their allergies including oral lesions, overgrooming, asthma, etc. Eosinophilic granulomas and rodent ulcers can be missed on exam if the oral cavity is not carefully evaluated. This presentation will show the workup of an allergic cat based on history and clinical presentation. Treatment options will be discussed including off-label options in tough cases. Also, break down the clinical presentations of the eosinophilic granuloma complex.

courses.title: Brachycephalic Upper Airway Surgery - Optimizing Outcomes
courses.description: This course delivers hands-on training for managing brachycephalic patients requiring upper airway surgery. Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) is common, and careful perioperative assessment and management is essential for good outcomes. Anesthesia can be challenging and requires several peri-operative considerations and interventions. Concurrent and related aerodigestive disorders are also critical to understand and diagnose appropriately. Led by a world-renowned soft tissue surgeon, an internal medicine specialist focused on airway disease, an anesthesiologist and experienced resident, this team will guide you through their approach to brachycephalic patients, using case-based scenarios and proven methods, so you leave with the confidence and tools for your next pug or bulldog surgery.

courses.title: Introduction to Animal Biomechanical Medicine
courses.description: This program introduces veterinarians and other animal health professionals to the foundational principles of Animal Biomechanical Medicine (ABM). Participants will explore how the musculoskeletal and nervous systems work together to produce healthy movement, how dysfunction in one area creates compensatory changes throughout the body, and how ABM integrates with conventional veterinary care to support injury prevention, rehabilitation, and performance medicine. Through case studies, movement assessment principles, and an overview of treatment approaches, this program provides a practical and evidence-informed foundation for understanding biomechanical dysfunction and the value of interdisciplinary animal care.

courses.title: The 92nd FVMA Annual Conference - On-Demand
courses.description: The 92nd FVMA Annual Conference offers continuing education virtually for veterinarians, veterinary technicians and other members of the small animal veterinary care team through lecture sessions and hands-on wet labs. Lecture tracks include Ophthalmology, Surgery Clinical Pathology, Anesthesia, Practice Management, Dentistry, Cardiology, Emergency and Critical Care, Medicine, Neurology, Dermatology and more.

courses.title: Pediatric Dermatology
courses.description: This lecture will provide an in-depth overview of some of the common dermatological conditions affecting puppies and young dogs, with a focus on identifying, diagnosing, and managing pediatric dermatology diseases. Diseases discussed will include parasitic infection, allergic disease, juvenile cellulitis and congenital diseases and will discuss treatment options safe for puppies.

courses.title: Beating the Odds: Updates in Feline Infectious Peritonitis
courses.description: We are sure you've heard about the novel antiviral therapy saving cats with FIP - GS-441524 - but can it be obtained legally? And how effective is this therapy for dry vs wet FIP? Dr. Cerna has the answers. Originally presented in 2024, this one-hour video course reviews the often-fatal Feline Infectious Peritonitis and recent updates in successful treatment. We'll cover clinical signs, diagnosing, and prevention, as well as define forms of FIP and the relationship with feline enteric coronavirus (FECV).

courses.title: Equipment Controls and Protocol for Soft Tissue Ultrasound - The Fundamentals
courses.description: This program will cover basic machine functions and measurements for those that are new to ultrasound. We will discuss the purpose of the different probes. We will cover how to scan the liver, spleen, kidneys, and bladder, and following a scanning protocol for these organs, so that the attendee can create a basic soft tissue ultrasound exam. We will also cover scanning a grid of the abdomen, artifacts, and different probe uses. This will be a Medical Program, that is hands-on scanning in a wet lab format for 8 hours of RACE CE.

courses.title: (On Demand) Treating Snakebites in Small Animal Practice: Pit Vipers and Elapids
courses.description: Originally presented in 2025, this new on-demand series deals with the aftermath of certain serpent encounters. Join ECC enthusiasts Drs. Gerken and Kuo as we slither through current envenomation treatment practices in the United States, covering geographic distribution and access to care. After identifying venomous species, get the expert's advice on adjunctive and anecdotal therapies (even the weird bacon trick your cousin swore by). We'll review nuances of antivenom types so you can choose what works for your practice, and then close with a conversation on special considerations for coral snake cases.

courses.title: Exotic Companion Mammal Dentistry Essentials
courses.description: Exotic Companion Mammal Dentistry Essentials will provide participants with an overview of dental anatomy and physiology, etiology of dental disease, how to perform an oral exam, effectively utilizing diagnostic tools, and the basic tenets of treatment of common exotic mammal dental problems seen in practice.

courses.title: VetFolio Skillshop Avian Prework RACE Submission
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Effective Communication in the Veterinary Clinic
courses.description: Poor or lack of adequate communication between veterinarians and their clients is commonly the cause for lawsuits and negative social media posts. By learning the basics of communicating with clients, we can achieve not only better understanding and solidify relationships with our clients as well as better outcomes for our patients.

courses.title: From wildcat to domestic cat: Veterinary perspectives on the evolution of cats
courses.description: Domestic cats have been an important part of human society for thousands of years by initially helping humans successfully transition from hunter-gatherers to a more agrarian lifestyle. Cats as we know them today evolved from a felid species, Felis libyca libyca, in the desert regions of North Africa and the Near East which can shed some light on their interesting, and sometimes challenging, physiological characteristics. Since those early days, both cats and humans have adapted genetically and developed a close and unique relationship built on a premise of mutual benefits. While many cats no longer need to earn their living clearing pests, understanding their evolutionary history and genetic adaptations can help veterinarians improve our therapeutic and nutritional care of cats and support for the human-animal bond.

courses.title: Respiratory Fungal Infections in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: The majority of fungal infections have respiratory involvement, but how can you tell what's brewing in those chest rads? Join us as Dr. Hanzlicek identifies suspicious presentations and diagnostic strategies for pulmonary and intranasal changes. We'll cover the top offenders causing diffuse and focal patterns on radiographs, and differentiate fungal organisms from neoplasia using targeted antigen testing. Then, flash through case studies that highlight practical steps to determine your own clinical blueprint.

courses.title: Welcome to the Block Party! Local anesthetics in veterinary dentistry ON-DEMAND
courses.description: A review of the use and benefits of local anesthesia in veterinary dentistry and oral surgery. Discussion of local anesthetic agents, adjuncts, and doses. A detailed review of locations and techniques for administering local anesthetics.

courses.title: Tackling Diabetes the Feline Way
courses.description:
Feline diabetes isnt just small animal diabetes cats play by their own rules. From their unique metabolism and obligate carnivore diet to distinct risk factors and treatment responses, managing diabetes in cats demands a species-specific approach.
This seminar dives into what makes feline diabetes different: its etiology, key risk factors, and the metabolic quirks that influence everything from diagnosis to long-term outcomes. Well compare treatment options traditional insulin therapy, nutrition, emerging SGLT2 inhibitors and explore strategies to achieve remission and set realistic diabetic goals.
Whether you want to refine your approach to feline diabetes, learn when to reach for newer therapies, or simply better understand what makes cats so different, this session will give you the tools to optimize care and improve outcomes for your diabetic patients.

courses.title: Raw Feeding: Are the Anecdotes on to Something?
courses.description: Raw feeding of dogs and cats is growing - both in popularity and as a matter of concern for veterinarians. Are pet owners really seeing the benefits they claim? There are studies appearing in the literature that show possible benefits to feeding raw. Epidemiologic and prospective studies comparing raw to conventionally processed foods will be reviewed. These findings and the health changes reported by pet owners may be explained at least partially by biochemical differences in minimally processed vs ultra-processed foods. The biochemical features of raw and minimally processed foods with also be reviewed.

courses.title: Fear Free for Humans
courses.description: This course is dedicated to helping animal care professionals learn and practice skills to promote a more positive personal welfare. Throughout this course, you will learn how to care for yourself--and the humans around you--to create an environment and a lifestyle that is Fear Free for people as well as for pets! Through thought-provoking material, tips, and engaging content, you'll learn healthier habits by challenging old ways of thinking and learning how to better protect human emotional welfare just as we do for animals!

courses.title: The Feline Genome: A Guide for Veterinary Practice
courses.description: Discover how the feline genome can transform veterinary care. Genetic screening is becoming a commonly used tool in veterinary medicine, offering insights into health, breed ancestry, genetic blood typing, and traits. This session simplifies genetic terminology, interpretation, and application, using case examples to illustrate. Gain confidence in integrating genetic tools into practice and effectively communicating with clients. Join us to unlock the potential of the feline genome in elevating veterinary care.

courses.title: Antibiotic Stewardship in Veterinary Medicine: From Policy to Practice
courses.description: Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health threat that impacts both human and animal populations. This one-hour continuing education session will explore the principles of antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary medicine and its critical role in the One Health approach. Attendees will learn strategies for responsible antibiotic use, including diagnostic decision-making, regulatory requirements, and implementation of stewardship programs in practice. The session will also cover extra-label drug use regulations, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and practical case-based scenarios to guide evidence-based prescribing. By the end of this lecture, participants will be equipped with resources and actionable steps to optimize antibiotic therapy while minimizing resistance development.

courses.title: Senior Cats and Dental Care- The Challenges
courses.description: As cats age, many changes occur, from body and muscle condition to organ function and disease occurrence. The oral cavity can also undergo changes, sometimes an extension or continuation of existing disease such as tooth resorption or periodontal disease, and sometimes previously unreported issues such as oral tumors. Anesthetic concerns may increase with comorbidities, but being able to provide adequate care under general anesthesia can be critical to the overall quality of health and life in these patients.

courses.title: Nutrition and Liver Disease: To Feed or Not to Feed
courses.description: In this RC Live online veterinary CE event, Dr. Adam Rudinsky, MS, DACVIM reviews the conundrum of when and how to use liver diets in dogs and cats. We will discuss the most prevalent, concerning, and important indications related to nutritional management of liver disease and how to effectively translate this information into management plans for chronic liver patients. In a world where there is a litany of prescription diets, we will demystify the nutritional approach to liver patients in a practical patient centered approach.

courses.title: October 2025
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Practical Parasitology for Exotic Pets
courses.description: This one-hour lecture will provide participants with an overview of parasites found in exotic pet companion mammals, reptiles, and avian species. Dermatological and gastrointestinal parasites will both be discussed, along with a few outliers that affect other systems. Details including clinical signs, diagnosis, and treatment of the most common parasites will be covered.

courses.title: Deep Dive into Prevention for Oral Wellness
courses.description:
Oral health is a crucial aspect of overall well-being for dogs and cats, and preventive care is vital in maintaining their dental wellness. By prioritizing preventive measures, veterinary professionals can effectively mitigate the risk of severe oral diseases, discomfort, and potential systemic complications in dogs and cats.
Oral diseases like periodontal and dental infections can have far-reaching consequences beyond the mouth. The bacteria in these conditions can enter the bloodstream and travel to major organs like the kidneys, liver, and heart, causing significant health issues. Preventive oral care promotes a healthy mouth and contributes to our canine and feline companions' overall longevity and quality of life.

courses.provider: SOUTH CAROLINA VETERINARY SPECIALISTS & EMERGENCY CARE
courses.title: Canine Cruciate Ligament Rupture: Is Surgery Needed?
courses.description: This presentation will discuss cranial cruciate ligament disease in dogs. It will cover ways to identify a cranial cruciate ligament injury, pathophysiology of CCL disease, pros and cons of various surgical treatment options, non-surgical treatment options, and recent literature on CCL disease

courses.title: From diagnosis to diet: managing triaditis in cats with confidence
courses.description: Triaditis concurrent inflammation of the pancreas, liver, and small intestine is a common and often complex syndrome in feline patients. This presentation will equip general practitioners with a practical, confidence-building approach to diagnosing and managing feline triaditis, with a special focus on the pivotal role of nutrition in recovery and long-term control. Attendees will learn to recognize clinical signs, interpret diagnostic findings, initiate targeted treatment, and implement effective nutritional strategies including techniques for feeding hospitalized patients who are anorexic or critically ill. Case examples will be used to bring clarity to this often daunting condition.

courses.title: The Hospital Environment, Part 2: Exploring Culture
courses.description:
This is the second lecture in a two-part series that does a deep dive into the real, physical, objective environment in which we work as veterinary professionals. We will explore the external environment in terms of sensory exposure, and the internal environment in terms of culture.
In this second part, we tackle veterinary workplace culture. Culture, by its simplest definition, is everything that is thought of by a group of individuals. It contains all of our ideas, modes of expression, values, hopes, fears, assumptions, and misconceptions as they affect our living and working together. The quality of each of those items (and countless others) gives a sense of the health of a culture and where changes ought to occur. From an organizational perspective, the quality of leadership determines the quality of the culture, and in turn the health of the workforce.

courses.title: Seeing Clearly: Master Ophthalmology Certificate Course
courses.description: In this certificate course, we'll review ocular diseases of all kinds. Study species-specific differences in ocular disease presentations, optimize your ophthalmic pharmacy, and see how eyes can be a window to the rest of the body. Dr. Fritz will review methods of ophthalmic examination and which tools work best in your clinical setting, as well as common ocular emergencies. Then, feel more confident managing eye problems after hearing Dr. Hauessler's tips and tricks for treating corneal ulcers, keratitis, epiphora, glaucoma, uveitis, retinal detachment, and more.

courses.title: Feline Dermatology: A Different Kind of Beast
courses.description: This Florida Veterinary Medical Association-sponsored webinar explores the unique challenges associated with diagnosing and managing dermatologic disease in cats. Feline skin disorders often present differently than those seen in dogs, requiring a species-specific approach to diagnosis, treatment, and long-term management. Participants will review the most common feline dermatologic conditions, including hypersensitivity dermatitis, eosinophilic granuloma complex, infectious skin diseases, immune-mediated disorders, and parasitic conditions. The course will emphasize practical diagnostic strategies, evidence-based treatment recommendations, and current and emerging therapies for feline allergic skin disease. Through clinical case examples and treatment discussions, attendees will gain confidence in developing effective management plans that improve patient comfort and quality of life.

courses.title: Anal Sac Apocrine Gland Retention Syndrome: Expression or Excision
courses.description: The lecture will focus on the indications for anal sacculectomy, anal sacculectomy techniques, possible complications, and anal sac retention syndrome.

courses.title: Reversing Canine Cognitive Dysfunction in Elderly Dogs
courses.description:
Canine Cognitive Dysfunction, also known as Sundowner Syndrome, is a common complaint that is very difficult for both the dog and the owner to live with. Although the drugs most commonly prescribed are seemingly appropriate to the pacing and anxiety affected dogs exhibit, the reality is the medications often don't work at all.
New research on CCD now tells us that this is because the drugs target the wrong pathways, and that CCD is actually a form of Alzheimer's Disease. While this news may seem just as disheartening, rapid progress is being made using herbal medicine.
Chinese herbal formulas contain some of the most effective treatments for CCD and Alzheimer's. This lecture will equip the attendee with the knowledge to be able to choose the most effective formulas to treat a patient, so that the pathology of CCD can be reversed in the patient and the relationship between the dog and owner can be restored.

courses.title: Decreasing Occupational Stress in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Stressed and looking for strategies to Improve your wellbeing? Come learn about the link between environmental stress, occupational stress and personality. In this webinar will give you a brief overview of the dimensions of wellbeing, and dive into factors that affect occupational stress in veterinary medicine. Finally, we will have an overview of long-term success strategies to combat occupational stress. While you cannot always fix environmental stress in the workplace, combating perfectionism and fostering a growth mindset can

courses.title: Bereavement: Saying a Good Bye
courses.description:
Euthanasia is a procedure in Veterinary Medicine that can be a gift, but it also causes a lot of grief, in owners and in the veterinary team. This talk goes over what bereavement is, how to help clients handle it, and how make sure the pet gets the most respectful passing.
It also discusses how the veterinary team needs to care for themselves after any loss of a patient.

courses.title: The Impacts of Vaccination on Fertility and Profits
courses.description: This presentation discusses the concept of "Lifetime Immunity" and how sequence of vaccination may be critical for a robust immune response. We will also discuss how vaccination of cattle must not only be about risk mitigation, but also immune system development. This includes the idea that some vaccine presentations may not be appropriate for all cattle ages or production phases. We will reference the concept of heterologous prime-boost. Further discussions will remind the attendee about the intricacies of the relationship between the immune system and the reproductive system of cattle.

courses.title: Pain Busters Certificate
courses.description:
The Pain Busters Certificate is a comprehensive, multi part educational series designed to help veterinary professionals understand, manage, and safeguard controlled substances in modern practice.
This program goes beyond basic compliance training. Participants will explore
The historical forces that shaped todays controlled drug laws
How and why diversion happens in veterinary settings
The mechanics of DEA compliance and inspection readiness
Practical systems for airtight record keeping
Real world prevention strategies for both in hospital and client-driven diversion
By the end of the program, participants will not only understand the rules they will understand the system behind the rules and how to build defensible, inspection ready processes that protect patients, teams, practices, and professional licenses.

courses.title: Speak the Same Language: Strategies to Help Clients Understand Recommendations
courses.description: This presentation examines the barriers to adherence (compliance) in veterinary hospitals. Strategies to help increase acceptance of clinical recommendations, including how to communicate value and the importance of clear, consistent protocols will be explored. Attendees will learn actionable tips that can be implemented in a use it today manner.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF SMALL RUMINANT PRACTITIONERS
courses.title: Online Webinar: Break a leg Treating long bone fractures in small ruminants
courses.description:
This webinar will discuss long bone fractures in small ruminants and what factors impact the prognosis. We will differentiate which types of fractures can be managed medically and which require surgical intervention. Finally, we will discuss complications of fracture healing and alternative salvage options.
Learning Objectives:
Determine the appropriate diagnostics needed to diagnose long bone fractures in small ruminants
Understand what factors impact prognosis in cases of long bone fractures
Know what surgical options are available for long bone fractures in small ruminants

courses.title: Core Surgical Skills 1: Basic Instrument Use
courses.description: Whether performing a routine spay or dealing with an emergency trauma, veterinary surgeons need to master core surgical skills. This online VetFolio premium content course teaches specific surgical procedures using a skills-based training method that breaks surgery down into a series of core surgical skills. It is your essential guide to what matters most in the operating room.

courses.title: Nuts and Bolts Part 1: Understanding and Using Your Anesthesia Monitors
courses.description: This program will discuss the usage and parameters of standard anesthesia monitors, including pulse oximetry, capnography, noninvasive blood pressure, electrocardiography, and temperature. The presenter will also discuss tips and tricks for making monitors function in various situations.

courses.title: Whats new with Feline Constipation: Acute & Chronic Treatment Modalities
courses.description: A comprehensive discussion on acute and chronic management strategies for feline constipation. Techniques including the use of polyethylene glycol (PEG 3350) administered as a constant rate infusion via nasoesophageal tube in the acutely obstipated patient will be shared. Additionally, we will discuss how the use of fiber and diet therapy can help with chronic management and prevention.

courses.title: CERTIFICATION IN VETERINARY WESTERN HERBAL MEDICINE (682-44363)
courses.description: CERTIFICATION IN VETERINARY WESTERN HERBAL MEDICINE (682-44363) is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Chronic Disease and the Geriatric Feline: Empowering the Caregiver at home
courses.description: As ageing cats and cats with chronic disease become a growing segment of the veterinary patient population, engaging caregivers more actively in their care has never been more critical. Caregivers are increasingly savvy about their cat's care, willing and able to obtain accurate body weights, monitor condition scores, measure food intake and determine food intake requirements. They can assess levels of pain using the many validated scoring systems now available. This seminar will focus on the rol of the caregiver in their cat's care, with options for improving monitoring and care at home.
