courses.title: On-Demand: Update on Equine Asthma: Current Strategies for Diagnosis and Management by Kelsey Hart, DVM, PhD, DACVIM (LAIM)
courses.description: Sponsored by Kentucky Performance Products and the Florida Association of Equine Practitioners, this 1-hour On-Demand Session will provide an in-depth discussion of Equine Asthma Syndrome, with specific focus on approaches to EAS diagnosis and currently available management options. The audience will be invited to participate by bringing questions about specific EAS cases in their practice to discuss at the end of the session.

courses.title: Life-Saving Alternatives in Veterinary Transfusions: Autotransfusions and Xenotransfusions
courses.description: This presentation explores two advanced transfusion techniques, autotransfusion and xenotransfusion, focusing on their principles, applications, benefits, and risks in veterinary medicine. Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of these life-saving procedures, with an emphasis on when and how they should be implemented. Using real-world case studies, we will discuss scenarios in which these methods serve as last-resort options, including severe anemia, trauma, or when species-compatible blood is unavailable. Through this session, veterinary professionals will learn practical tips, decision-making criteria, and ethical considerations to optimize patient outcomes in critical care settings.

courses.title: Dental Exam Room Gems
courses.description: Veterinary dental exam rooms are specialized spaces designed to facilitate comprehensive dental procedures and diagnostics for animal patients. These rooms typically provide ample space, allowing for approximately eight feet in width to ensure that technicians can maneuver easily around the treatment table. Essential equipment includes a periodontal probe for assessing dental health, specialized dental X-ray units, and an anesthetic machine to manage patient comfort during procedures. The design also incorporates adjustable LED lighting for precise examinations and features like a wet table or collection type table to enhance functionality. In addition to the critical equipment, the infrastructure of veterinary dental exam rooms is carefully considered to promote safety and efficiency. This includes an exhaust fan for negative air pressure, a waste anesthesia gas disposal system, and dedicated storage for instruments and supplies. The room is designed with ergonomic features to support staff comfort and workflow efficiency while enabling comprehensive assessments such as periodontal depth measurements, gingival health evaluations, and dental X-rays. By integrating these elements, veterinary dental exam rooms become sophisticated environments that ensure thorough, precise, and compassionate dental care for animals.

courses.title: Sorting Through a Jungle of Pet Foods
courses.description: This lecture will discuss how to choose a pet food. There are over 5,000 brands and 200 manufactures of pet food. This lecture will discuss where to find reliable sources of information, how to read a pet food label and how to compare current foods on the market. Information will be discussed to show what standards are recommended for pet food companies to follow. Where to find this information easily will also be discussed. Pet food labels will also be discussed. Information will be provided on what is required to be on a label and how to decipher what that information means. A variety of ingredients will also be discussed as well as the specific nutrients each of those ingredients provides. A case study will be presented to tie all the information provided together.

courses.title: Investment Basics A No-Bull Guide for Beginners
courses.description:
One of the key elements of success in long-term investing is starting early. But often, getting started is difficult because we havent been taught the basics of how investing works and/or our experience with financial advisers hasnt been good.
This course will provide a foundational understanding of investing, beginning with how investing works. We will learn some general key principles about investing and then review common of types of investments. Well conclude with practical tips on how to get started investing and how to choose an investment adviser.

courses.title: NAVC Pet Nutrition Coach Certification Hybrid
courses.description: Nutrition is a cornerstone of patient health and preventive care. The entire veterinary healthcare team should be a trusted source of nutrition information for clients. Educating pet owners on the importance of nutrition strengthens the human-animal bond and encourages regular veterinary visits. This program empowers team members to confidently discuss proper nutrition with every client, supporting better outcomes and stronger client relationships. Good nutrition is not a trend, it is good business and great medicine.

courses.title: Obesity Prevention in Puppies and Kittens
courses.description: This presentation emphasizes the significance of early obesity prevention in pets. Effective communication is essential in addressing and preventing pet obesity. When initiating conversations, veterinarians should state the problem clearly, ask for permission to discuss weight management, and assess the owners readiness to change. Tailored, specific advice such as exact food amounts, feeding frequency, and calorie intake helps ensure practical, actionable steps. Preventive strategies highlight the role of pet owner education on maintaining an ideal body condition and the use of growth curves to monitor and guide appropriate weight management during the developmental stages. Growth curves help predict a pets ideal adult weight, allowing for adjustments in feeding to prevent excessive weight gain as the pet matures. By tracking growth patterns, veterinarians and owners can intervene early when deviations occur. Accurate calculation of Resting Energy Requirements RER and feeding recommendations based on life stage and physiological needs are crucial. Diets with higher protein, lower calorie density, and appropriate feeding methods are recommended, while treats should be limited to less than 10 percent of daily caloric intake. Incorporating feeding enrichment to slow food consumption and engage pets is also encouraged.

courses.title: Companion Animal Euthanasia Training Academy 2025
courses.description: These courses seek to provide education in companion animal euthanasia to improve the overall experience. We will explore what clients, patients and your team need when it is time to say goodbye to a beloved pet.

courses.title: Modern Pet Diets: Risks, Rewards & Real Talk
courses.description: Pet owners are increasingly turning to raw, homemade, and fresh diet formats. These diets may be a part of a veterinary teams daily clinic conversations. Are these feeding strategies better than traditional kibble or canned pet food? Are there risks to these diet formats? This session will equip veterinary professionals with the tools to critically evaluate and discuss these popular diet formats. This session will deliver an evidence-based overview of raw, homemade, and fresh diets. Well unpack the science, explore the risks and benefits, and provide practical tips to help guide client decisions. Whether youre skeptical or supportive, this talk will help you engage confidently no matter whats in the bowl.

courses.title: Veterinary Pediatrics Revisited !
courses.description: If we change the beginning of the story, we change the whole story. This quote is often used in human pediatrics and we now have evidence that the exact same applies to the canine and feline species. Every event that takes place during puppy kittenhood has long lasting health consequences; this period therefore represents an opportunity for veterinary clinics, as the best pediatric care they provide, the healthier later in life the animals will be. Through clinical cases, this presentation will provide you with the opportunity to learn about the new knowledge, new tools and new protocols that are now available in veterinary pediatrics. We will discuss preventive care, nutrition, spaying and neutering and share with you plenty of actionable tips you can quickly implement in your veterinary clinics. Equipped with all this, you will be able step up your game in veterinary pediatrics.

courses.title: Navigating Kidney Health in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: In this on-demand CE module, well explore acute and chronic kidney disease (CKD) in dogs and cats, with a focus on key insights to enhance patient management. This module features 3 cases that participants will work through to dive deeper into nutritional support strategies and practical clinical pearls to simplify treatment. There is a focus on distinguishing when to use different diets from Royal Canins Renal Support line.

courses.title: Hiring 2.0: Hack the Process, Ditch the Bias, and Build a Veterinary Dream Team (On Demand)
courses.description: Your gut instinct has served you well in past hiring decisions, hasn't it? Think again! In Hiring 2.0: Hack the Process, Ditch the Bias, and Build a Veterinary Dream Team, we'll uncover the sneaky ways cognitive biases influence everyone's hiring decisions, spoiler: they're everywhere! Backed by solid science, this presentation will arm you with simple, practical strategies to outsmart bias, sharpen your process, and make stronger hiring decisions. You'll walk away with a step-by-step plan to build your dream team, boost success rates, and maybe even save a few headaches along the way!

courses.title: Pain Management
courses.description: Attendants will be expected to learn how to better assess pain in veterinary patients, better recognize and treat chronic pain in pets, localize painful lesions and use pharmaceutical and other modalities for pain management.

courses.title: Relevant Aspects of Antimicrobial Resistance in Backyard Poultry
courses.description: Relevant Aspects of Antimicrobial Resistance in Backyard Poultry is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Boundary Basics for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: The veterinary profession is facing unprecedented stressors and demands. Workload, short-staffing, and client demands are fueling burnout and turnover. Many veterinary professionals feel a strong sense of pride and dedication, and as a result, have difficulty saying no and taking time for themselves. Now, more than ever, veterinarians and veterinary team members need to learn to set healthy boundaries with kindness and compassion. In this course, we will define boundaries and discuss how healthy boundaries can improve patient care. We will cover types of boundaries, effective and ineffective approaches to boundary-setting, mentoring early career veterinary professionals through the process of setting boundaries effectively, and common misconceptions about boundaries.

courses.title: Top Tips for Managing Urinary Emergencies
courses.description: Learners will review the basics of diagnosis and management of common emergencies affecting the lower urinary tract, namely urethral obstruction, urethral rupture, and uroabdomen.

courses.title: Sedation and Anesthesia of Exotic Species
courses.description: Sedation and anesthesia are essential tools in exotic animal medicine not only for surgery but for safe, low stress handling. This presentation will give general practitioners the tools to approach sedation confidently in parrots, exotic companion mammals, and reptiles/amphibians. We will evaluate species-specific considerations, practical protocols and tips for safe monitoring and recovery. Whether you are performing your first sedated parrot blood draw or looking to improve anesthetic outcomes, this lecture will offer actionable guidance for better patient care.

courses.title: Flexible and Rigid Endoscopy
courses.description:
This 4-day course combines flexible GI endoscopy and rigid endoscopy to create a comprehensive course comprised of lecture and hands-on lab covering the following areas:
Basic Flexible Endoscopy: Introduction to endoscopy, including indications, endoscopic instrumentation, techniques for examining the upper and lower GI tract, plus a 7-hour wet lab to provide hands-on experience in both upper and lower endoscopy.
Intermediate Flexible Endoscopy: One-day course (lecture, demonstration, & laboratory session) on intermediate endoscopy techniques, including canine airway exam, additional experience in gastrointestinal examination, and foreign body retrieval and biopsies. This lab will also include a gastrointestinal examination of cats.
Rigid Endoscopy: One-day course (lecture, demonstration & laboratory session) on rigid endoscopy, including laparoscopy, rhinoscopy, video-otoscopy, and urethroscopy/cystoscopy.

courses.title: Feline the Future: Innovations in Diabetes Management OnDemand
courses.description: Diabetes management in cats is evolving with new therapeutic options, a better understanding of comorbidities, and a growing appreciation for individualized care. This lecture will explore current treatment strategies for feline diabetes, including the importance of patient selection for the integration of insulin or SGLT2 inhibitors, dietary management, and the impact of underlying diseases on treatment success. This lecture will use a case-based approach to discuss practical insights to optimize outcomes and improve quality of life for diabetic feline patients. We will conclude with practical PURRLS for managing our feline diabetic patients while being mindful of caregiver and team burden!

courses.title: Transfusion Complications: When Blood Components Go Bad!
courses.description: Transfusion reactions in veterinary patients can be life-threatening if not promptly recognized and addressed. This presentation delves into the complexities of transfusion complications, categorizing them as immunologic or non-immunologic, and explores their underlying mechanisms, clinical manifestations, and management strategies. We will highlight examples to provide a practical understanding of allergic reactions, hemolytic transfusion reactions, febrile non-hemolytic reactions, and rare complications like TRALI and TACO. Attendees will gain insights into evidence-based prevention methods, including the use of compatibility testing, leukoreduction, and meticulous patient monitoring. This session is designed to empower veterinary professionals with the knowledge and tools to provide safer and more effective transfusion care.

courses.title: Meow-ch! Addressing Acute Pain in Cats and Dogs
courses.description: How do we know when our patients are in pain? Join Dr. Robertson, an internationally celebrated specialist in anesthesia and animal welfare, as we discuss validated tools for measuring pain consistently and create treatment plans to satisfy individual patient needs. We'll also give some special attention to new feline analgesics that meet a variety of clinical needs, from safe NSAIDs to high compliance, easy-to-give opioids.

courses.title: June 2025 with August 2023 RACE Submission
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Pandemic Puppies: Where are We Now?
courses.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, a surge in puppy adoptions occurred as people sought companionship and emotional support during lockdowns. With remote work and social isolation, many saw an opportunity to raise a dog, expecting benefits such as reduced stress and increased outdoor activity. However, these puppies often experienced limited socialization, reduced exposure to new environments, and inconsistent training. Now, five years later, many of these pandemic puppies exhibit behavioral challenges like separation anxiety, fearfulness, and reactivity, leading to a rise in behavioral consultations as owners adjust to post-pandemic life. Managing these issues often requires structured training, behavioral therapy, and, in some cases, medication. Understanding the long-term effects of pandemic puppy-raising is crucial for supporting both dogs and owners while reinforcing the importance of proper socialization and training for future generations of pets.

courses.title: DNM THERAPEUTIC NUTRITION FOR DIABETES MELLITUS
courses.description: Just as in humans, both dogs and cats can succumb to diabetes mellitus However, unlike humans that may succumb to both Type 1 and Type 2, dogs usually have insulin-dependent, while cats typically have non-insulin-dependent diabetes. Medication, therapeutic nutrition and exercise all play important roles in managing this disease. The goal is to maintain blood glucose within a safe range throughout the day and night and to avoid further complications. Because obesity can be a complicating factor in diabetes, nutritional management of overweight dogs and cats may be an important first step in controlling it. Through this course you will learn the pathophysiology of diabetes development in both species as well as management strategies, especially when it comes to nutrition. Nutrients important for the management of patients with diabetes mellitus will be covered in detail with examples of different case management examples.

courses.title: Veterinary Dentistry 102: Pathology & Procedures
courses.description:
Veterinary Dentistry 102: Pathology & Procedures builds upon foundational dental knowledge to explore common oral diseases, advanced treatment techniques, and the vital role technicians play throughout the surgical and recovery process. This course delves deeper into oral pathology, providing a detailed review of dental fractures, tooth resorption, periodontal disease, malocclusions, oral tumors, and other related conditions, paired with clinical insights into treatment planning and decision-making.
Participants will gain confidence in assisting with oral surgery by learning how to properly prepare surgical packs, administer dental nerve blocks, and provide intraoperative support. The course also covers post-operative care, including pain management, patient recovery, and effective client communication for discharge and home care instructions.
Through detailed diagrams, procedural videos, and case-based scenarios, learners will elevate their skills in identifying complex pathology, supporting surgical interventions, and delivering high-quality dental care. This CE course is ideal for veterinary professionals seeking to improve their clinical skills and enhance patient outcomes in dentistry.

courses.title: Canine Healthspan Advocate: The Essential Role of Veterinary Technicians in Management of Canine Mobility and Chronic Pain
courses.description: This course empowers veterinary technicians with the knowledge and skills to improve quality of life in dogs with osteoarthritis (OA) and chronic pain. Participants will learn proactive approaches to preserving mobility, reducing chronic pain, and extending a dog's healthspan through multimodal management techniques. The course covers critical topics such as weight management, tailored exercise, environmental optimization, and caregiver education. By the end, veterinary technicians will be prepared to serve as OA and Healthspan Advocates within their practice, enhancing both patient outcomes and client satisfaction.

courses.title: Raw Food: Can it be Made Safe?
courses.description: Most veterinarians consider all raw pet foods to present the same major risks of pathogen contamination and nutritional inadequacy. In truth, homemade pet foods generally the deserve this reputation. However, commercial raw pet food companies employ a variety of measures to ensure safety - some more than others. This talk will cover the range of safety procedures that can be employed and end with a set of questions that should be asked of any raw food company being considered by the pet owner.

courses.title: Ear Cytology: A Quick, Simple Way to Maximize Success in Otitis Management
courses.description: Topical therapy is the treatment of choice for most cases of otitis. It allows targeted treatment in the problematic anatomical location. Also, higher concentrations of medication are achieved through topical administration compared to systemic routes. To ensure success with topical therapy, cytology of the ear canal is important to identify which treatment is necessary and what ingredients will be beneficial for the pet. With antimicrobial resistance continuing to increase, it is imperative to select therapy based on appropriate identification of the organisms. Learn the appropriate way to interpret ear cytology and treatment recommendations for otitis externa.

courses.title: The Cost of Care
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to discuss common barriers to veterinary care and ways to eliminate them. Focusing primarily on cost, this course provides proactive conversational tools that veterinary professionals can use to inform pet parents about budgeting for their pets' care. Medical costs can often stand in the way of a pet's access to care due to their family's inability to afford unexpected out-of-pocket expenses. When these costs exceed what's known as the stop-treatment threshold (the average maximum out-of-pocket expense that families in Canada and the US can afford) pet parents are forced to make impossible decisions, and these situations can unfortunately lead to economic euthanasia. Pet parents are often uninformed about the potential for such incidents, such as injuries from accidents and illnesses due to genetic predispositions. By taking this course, veterinary professionals will learn how to prepare pet parents for these situations, thereby increasing access to care because when prepared, pet parents can have peace of mind to agree to the gold standard care their pets deserve and veterinary professionals can focus on what matters most -- treating patients.

courses.title: Equine Surgical Congress 2026
courses.description: Morbidity and mortality reporting of equine lameness surgical cases through presentations of case studies and case series by each presenter attendee in an open discussion round table format. Each attendee and presenter are Diplomates of the American College of Veterinary Surgeons. See below for summaries of each attendees presentations and specific learning objectives. Each presentation will last 60 minutes for a total of 14 hours of class time and 14 CE credits.

courses.title: May 2026
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Think Like a Dermatologist: Step by Step Approach in Real World Cases
courses.description: As a clinician is evaluating the skin in a dog or cat, it should be considered how the skin reacts. What lesions are present? What is the distribution of lesions, etc.? There are many details that can be discovered when cases are evaluated with critical thinking. Then, the appropriate diagnostic tests and treatment can be implemented for the benefit of the pet and owner. This lecture will review numerous real life clinical pictures to help simplify this process.

courses.title: Your Clients: Distressed or De-stressed?
courses.description: This course will take a close look at the stress response in humans and why this matters in a veterinary setting. A case study will be followed throughout the course to demonstrate realistic scenarios that could either distress or de-stress a client. This course is for veterinary professionals of all levels and backgrounds who want to strengthen their understanding of how to prevent and intervene on pet owner stress and to reinforce a positive relationship between pet owners and vet staff.

courses.title: On Demand Webinar: EVIDENCE-BASED POST-OPERATIVE NUTRITION FOR THE VETERINARY PRACTITIONER
courses.description: Post-operative fasting remains common in veterinary practice, despite growing evidence that it may delay recovery. This webinar reviews evidence-based post-operative nutrition strategies that replace outdated feeding practices with safer, more proactive protocols. Attendees will explore the gastrointestinal effects of common anaesthetic and analgesic drugs, including opioid-associated ileus and nausea, and how these influence feeding decisions. Practical discharge feeding plans for routine procedures such as gonadectomies will be discussed, with an emphasis on obesity prevention. The role of Early Enteral Nutrition (EEN) in gastrointestinal surgery and recovery from trauma, mass excisions, cancer cachexia, and cystotomy for urolithiasis will be addressed

courses.title: Short Procedures, Big Decisions: Sedation in Everyday Canine Care
courses.description: Participants will dive into the art and science of canine sedation through five real-world clinical scenarios. This session uses interactive case studies to guide clinicians in crafting tailored sedation protocols that prioritize patient comfort, procedural efficiency, and safety.

courses.title: Tackling the dogs and cats with obesity and concurrent disease
courses.description:
Obesity is now a major health and welfare concern in companion animals. Overweight dogs and cats are at increased risk of developing comorbidities including: diabetes mellitus, musculoskeletal disease, neoplasia, oral cavity disease skin disease, and urinary tract disease. Increased adiposity can also adversely affect respiratory function, cause metabolic derangements including insulin resistance, and also affect renal function and health. Although weight management programmes can be successful, outcomes are often disappointing with many animals either failing to reach target weight or regaining weight subsequently.
This talk will consider obesity as a disease and provide guidance on clinical priorities for weight management when other diseases are present. The concept of tailoring weight management to the individual be considered, whereby the target for weight loss is set according to individual circumstances. Case examples will be used to illustrate the concepts covered.

courses.title: The Science of Lasting Relief: A Deep Dive into Befrena (tirnovetmab)
courses.description: This program provides a comprehensive overview of¿Befrena¿(tirnovetmab), a caninized anti-IL-31 monoclonal antibody indicated for the treatment of canine allergic and atopic dermatitis. Participants will explore how this fast-acting, long-lasting therapy starts controlling pruritus within 24 hours and provides at least 6 weeks of relief from a single, vet-administered subcutaneous injection. The session covers key clinical efficacy and safety data. By examining the practical aspects of the product along with all of the information available to date, the webinar provides Befrena's role within Elanco's broader dermatology portfolio. This program equips veterinary professionals with the insights needed to provide "lasting itch relief" for their patients.

courses.title: Personality Traps: Perfectionism, People-Pleasing, the Imposter Phenomenon, and the Big Five
courses.description: Several personal attributes that likely contribute to the objective success of veterinary professionals in school and may continue to contribute to their effectiveness in practice have a dark side. Perfectionism and people-0pleasing tendencies each mean that someone else is receiving an individual's best, with little left over to invest in their own mental health or wellbeing. The imposter phenomenon amplifies this imbalance by driving a need to perform at maximum capacity or else risk being found out as incompetent or unworthy. As one of the most popular personalities profiles, the Big Five is also discussed. This presentation will examine each of these personality traps: how to recognize them, their effect on mental wellbeing, and what can be done to mitigate their impact.

courses.title: NAVC: Captivate & Connect- A Speakers Guide to Impact
courses.description: The NAVC Speaker Certification equips veterinary professionals with the skills to deliver clear, engaging, and impactful presentations. This program covers public speaking techniques, storytelling, executive presence, visual design, and audience engagement to enhance communication and presentation effectiveness. Participants will also learn to craft compelling session descriptions, design effective slides, and translate conference insights into action. Whether new to speaking or looking to refine existing skills, this certification provides practical tools to enhance delivery and audience connection.

courses.title: Obesity in 2024: What are the challenges and where are the solutions?
courses.description: Obesity now a major and highly prevalent medical disease affecting health and wellbeing of cats throughout the world. Although the focus of much ongoing research, obesity remains a challenging condition to manage. This talk will discuss many of the current challenges that that veterinary professionals face when attempting to address obesity and make suggestions on how these can be overcome.

courses.title: March 2025 RACE Submission
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Shortcuts to Chinese Medical Diagnosis via TCVM History Taking
courses.description: This program will show the attendee how asking the caregiver basic questions in a standard Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) protocol can in some cases easily give important clues as to the TCVM diagnosis for the patient.

courses.title: Unleash the Power of VOHC in Your Veterinary Practice
courses.description:
Join Dr. Elizabeth Lowrey, director of the Veterinary Oral Health Council (VOHC), and Dr. Jan Bellows, board-certified veterinary dentist, in this informative podcast the VOHC's origins in the late 1980s, its official launch in 1997, and its mission to review and recognize effective plaque and tartar control products for pets.
Dr. Lowrey delves into the rigorous review protocols required for products to earn the prestigious VOHC Seal of Acceptance, including multiple trials and statistical validation.
Veterinarians can confidently recommend VOHC-accepted products to their clients, knowing these items have been scientifically proven to reduce plaque and tartar in dogs and cats by at least 20%.
This podcast is a resource for veterinary professionals seeking to improve their patients' oral health and pet owners looking to make informed decisions about their furry friends' preventative dental care.

courses.title: The Diabetic Dilemma tailoring nutritional approach for each DM kitty
courses.description: This course will discuss and review manifestations of diabetes mellitus in the feline patient. Specifically, we will review pathophysiology predisposing conditions and diagnosis, as well as, appropriate nutritional support for the individual patient. An emphasis is also placed on client communication throughout the entirety of the lecture.

courses.title: September 2024
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Medical and Interventional Management of Urolithiasis
courses.description:
This lecture will focus on struvite and calcium oxalate treatment and prevention in dogs. Specifically, medical dissolution of struvite uroliths will be discussed along with prevention strategies for both struvite
and calcium oxalate stones. The 2014 ACVIM Consensus Recommendations on the Treatment and Prevention of Uroliths in Dogs and Cats will be highlighted. By the end of this lecture, practitioners will be able to recognize cases that may be candidates for dissolution of uroliths.

courses.title: Facing Your Personal Finance Monster First Steps to Take Control of Your Money
courses.description: Getting control of your financial situation can be a daunting subject. We know we need to do it but we often put it off because we dont know where to start. This course is a foundational personal finance course that will help learners begin to understand their financial situation and to get started managing it with practical first steps.

courses.title: Lumbosacral Hyperextension Connections with Hip Dysplasia, Cruciate Ligament, & Intervertebral Disc Diseases
courses.description: This webinar will describe the signs associated with various etiologies of low back and hip pain in the dog and will describe the use of myofascial meridians to treat these conditions (Integrative Veterinary Fascial Therapy- IVFT).

courses.title: NAVC Human-Animal Bond Certification RACE Submission
courses.description:
Research studies have proven that owning a pet improves someones physical and mental health. Given the events of the last several years, the human-animal bond has never been stronger or more important to pet owners. We designed this course in partnership with the Human-Animal Bond Research Institute (HABRI), with educational support from the American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA), to help explain what the bond is, how it works, and to demonstrate the role of the veterinary healthcare team in supporting and strengthening its effects. We have also enhanced the program with content that includes after-euthanasia, access to care, and the veterinary nurse perspective.
This certification covers foundational lessons where learners will develop an understanding of the neurological mechanisms fundamental to the bond, the specific scientific benefits of owning a pet, and the health benefits generated by distinct types of human-animal interactions. It includes content provided by our educational sponsor, AVMA, on the three domains of animal welfare, how to perform certain assessments and the important role that animal welfare plays in the human-animal bond.

courses.provider: CORNELL UNIVERSITY, COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: Acid-Base and Blood Gas Analysis in Small Animals
courses.description: This interactive online course teaches a systematic approach to blood gas analysis, including an assessment of acid-base disturbances, oxygenation and ventilation. Differential diagnoses for common metabolic and respiratory disturbances that can be identified on blood gases are discussed, and a series of cases are presented to illustrate the clinical correlates of these concepts.

courses.title: THE RIGHT TOOL FOR THE RIGHT JOB: THE BENEFITS OF BLOOD COMPONENT THERAPY
courses.description: A patient comes to your practice, presents as anemic, and requires a transfusion. What blood product do you use? If whole blood is the answer, the benefits of component therapy are being missed. The ability to split whole blood into specific components improves the safety, utility, and benefits of blood products, and in turn, can save more lives.

courses.title: Foundations of Anesthesia and Sedation
courses.description: This asynchronous online program is designed for veterinary assistants, on-the-job trained technicians, and newly graduated veterinary technicians seeking to build or strengthen their foundational knowledge in anesthesia and sedation to enhance patient safety. Participants will gain a thorough understanding of critical principles; including pharmacology, patient monitoring, safety protocols, and proper equipment use, while working through engaging topic modules, case studies, and practical applications.

courses.title: Understanding the Long-Term Health Consequences of Gonadectomy in Dogs and the Emerging Role of Hormone Replacement Therapy
courses.description: This one-hour CE lecture examines the systemic, whole-body health consequences of routine spaying and neutering in dogs, with a focus on the chronically elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) that follows gonadectomy and the broad distribution of LH receptors throughout non-reproductive tissues.

courses.title: A Technicians Guide to Epithelial Cancers
courses.description: Round cell tumors are among the most common cancers seen in veterinary practice and include lymphoma, mast cell tumors, plasma cell tumors, histiocytomas, and transmissible venereal tumors. This lecture will review their distinguishing features, common presentations, and typical treatments. Technicians will learn to interpret basic cytology findings, understand criteria of malignancy, and appreciate the nuances of diagnosing these cancers. The course emphasizes the technicians vital role in staging, sample collection, client communication, and treatment of the different diseases.

courses.title: Aortic Thromboembolism in Cats
courses.description:
In this course, participants will review the pathogenesis of thromboembolic disease in cats. We will describe the risk factors that preclude cardiac cats to this particular complication, prevention mechanisms and treatment courses.
Learning Objectives:
* Identify how to prevent aortic thromboembolism in cats
* Determine prognostic indicators that help dictate client conversation and expectations
* Learn various courses of treatments for aortic thromboembolism cases

courses.title: Understanding the Connection Between Health and Behavior
courses.description: We constantly assess and monitor our patient's physical health but what if any decline in health jeopardized their social relationships and wellbeing? Every action of every individual is the result of genetics, development, learning history, and health. We can actively help our patients stay healthy both physically and mentally.

courses.title: Radiographic Techniques of the Veterinary Patient
courses.description: This on-site hands-on radiograph instruction is given to technicians and/or veterinarians providing the information and technical radiographic skills to acquire images for diagnostics. At the end of the presentation/lab the participant should be able to understand the importance of radiation safety, how to operate an x-ray machine properly, and recognize the value of well positioned radiographs as a diagnostic tool for the veterinary patient.

courses.title: Small Animal Ophthalmology: Ophthalmic Examination and Surgical Techniques
courses.description: Ophthalmology does not have to feel foreign. This course equips general and emergency practitioners to recognize and manage common eye conditions. We will begin with a thorough ophthalmic exam, taught via lecture and live animal labs, then tour key diagnoses and their medical and surgical treatments. In cadaver labs, you will practice techniques for entropion, cherry eye, eyelid masses, proptosis, eyelid lacerations, and enucleation. You will leave ready to perform these procedures confidently in everyday practice.

courses.title: Small Animal Ophthalmology: Ophthalmic Examination and Surgical Techniques
courses.description: Ophthalmology does not have to feel foreign. This course equips general and emergency practitioners to recognize and manage common eye conditions. We will begin with a thorough ophthalmic exam, taught via lecture and live animal labs, then tour key diagnoses and their medical and surgical treatments. In cadaver labs, you will practice techniques for entropion, cherry eye, eyelid masses, proptosis, eyelid lacerations, and enucleation. You will leave ready to perform these procedures confidently in everyday practice.

courses.title: Feline Osteoarthritis Pain Management: NGF Signaling, Anti-NGF Antibodies, and Practical Clinical Decision-Making
courses.description:
Osteoarthritis affects up to 60% of cats over the age of six - yet most go undiagnosed because cats mask pain in ways that are subtle and easily overlooked. For many feline patients, chronic OA pain is quietly diminishing quality of life long before it is recognized in the exam room.
In this session you will learn how to recognize feline OA earlier, explore the role of NGF in perpetuating OA pain, and be introduced to the science of long-acting monoclonal antibodies. We'll cover new safety data and clinical evidence regarding the use of antiNGF mAbs in cats and understand how to apply proper patient selection criteria.
By the end of this session, participants will be able to identify OA in feline patients earlier and more consistently and confidently integrate monoclonal antibodies into their pain management protocols to improve outcomes for cats living with chronic OA.

courses.title: guidED 2026 | Edmonton Alberta
courses.description:
guidED Veterinary Leadership Conference is a comprehensive leadership development program designed specifically for veterinary practice leaders, including practice owners, managers, medical directors, and emerging leadership team members.
Scheduled for September 26-28, 2026, in Edmonton, Alberta, guidED provides an integrated learning experience focused on strengthening leadership effectiveness, team performance, organizational culture, client experience, and long-term practice sustainability.
The program is built around three interconnected learning components that support knowledge acquisition, practical application, and implementation of learning within veterinary practice settings.
Virtual, Online (On-Demand / Self-Paced)
What we call our Integral Learning Experience
The first phase is a virtual self-paced learning experience delivered approximately four weeks before the conference through the Octopoda learning platform. Developed in collaboration with subject matter experts, this component introduces foundational concepts, encourages early engagement, and helps identify participant questions and learning needs before the live event.
Classroom, Face-to-Face (Real Time)
What we call our Immersive Learning Experience
The second phase is the in-person conference experience. Participants engage in interactive workshops led by experts in leadership, professional wellbeing, communication, organizational development, client experience, and practice performance. All attendees participate in a shared curriculum with no concurrent sessions, creating a consistent learning journey and encouraging collaboration among veterinary leaders from diverse practice environments. Educational methods include facilitated discussion, reflective exercises, practical application activities, and peer learning opportunities designed to support immediate translation into practice.
Virtual, Online (Real Time)
What we call our Implementation Experience
The final phase is a live virtual impleme

courses.title: From Rookie to All-Star: Designing the Veterinary Excellence Operating System LIVE
courses.description:
Veterinary clinics everywhere are investing in CE, onboarding, and skills training, yet many still struggle with inconsistent competency levels, staff frustration, leadership fatigue, and a revolving door of support team turnover. The missing piece isn't more information - it is structure.
Rookie to All-Star: Designing the Veterinary Excellence Operating System is a six-week, implementation-focused hybrid program designed for veterinary leaders ready to build a sustainable team through an intentional, tiered development program. This program emphasizes purposeful team design, progressive skill development, competency validation, and a culture of excellence.
Participants will learn how to evaluate their current team structure, identify training breakdowns, design progressive learning pathways, integrate adult learning principles, build measurable competency systems, and create recognition programs that drive engagement and retention - leaving with a fully built Veterinary Excellence Operating System ready to launch in their practice.

courses.title: Practical Assessment and Stabilization of Polytrauma in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Polytrauma patients present unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges that require quick prioritization and decisive action. This lecture, led by DoveLewis Critical Care Specialist Dr. Marie Min, DVM, MS, DACVECC, focuses on a systematic, evidence-based approach to the initial assessment and stabilization of dogs and cats with multiple traumatic injuries. The focus will be on identifying life-threatening conditions, implementing effective stabilization strategies, and avoiding common pitfalls in early trauma management. Practical case examples will illustrate real-world decision-making relevant to both general and emergency practice.

courses.title: Offense Versus Defense: How to Play the Dermatology Game
courses.description: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic, multifactorial disease that can be frustrating for both veterinarians and owners. This lifelong condition requires long-term management specially tailored to each patient. In this webinar, learn how shifting from purely reacting to flares and infection to managing proactively can help patients and decrease frustration. Dr. Amy Schnedeker will discuss current strategies in managing atopic dermatitis, including systemic and topical therapies, and show how intervening between flares can help improve the quality of life of your dermatology patients.

courses.title: Is Your Osteoarthritis Patient Still a Puppy? Rethinking Pain, Behavior, & Early Intervention
courses.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is not limited to senior dogs. Developmental orthopedic disease, joint instability, abnormal conformation, and injury can initiate OA during puppyhood, when pain may appear only as subtle changes in play, activity, posture, and/or movement. This webinar will help clinicians identify at-risk young dogs, recognize early pain behavior and functional change, and implement a practical multimodal plan that preserves joint health, muscle function, and mobility while establishing sustainable lifelong care.

courses.title: 38th Annual Southern Veterinary Conference On-Demand
courses.description: This is an Annual Veterinary Conference that occurs in August in Birmingham, Alabama located at The Hyatt Regency/Wynfrey Hotel in front of the Galleria Mall. This will be a continuation of the in-person sessions recorded live at the conference August 5th to 8th, 2026. Each session made available will be edited and will link to 5 questions at the end of each session for a RACE approved certificate. You will be emailed a certificate for each hour completed. These sessions will end on December 30th.

courses.title: Canine Infectious Respiratory Disease Complex: 5-Star Care on a 2-Star Budget
courses.description: In this webinar, Dr. Carol Reinero will provide a practical framework for diagnosing and managing canine infectious respiratory disease complex (CIRDC) in a variety of patients and clinical settings, including the otherwise healthy dog with acute respiratory signs, dogs with pneumonia, and groups of dogs affected by large outbreaks. Emphasis will be placed on recognizing the different clinical presentations of CIRDC and selecting diagnostic tests that provide meaningful information while considering case severity, diagnostic yield, and financial constraints. Dr. Reinero will explore strategies for delivering high-quality patient care without unnecessarily increasing diagnostic and treatment costs, with an overall goal of helping clinicians make thoughtful, cost-conscious decisions that maximize patient outcomes while remaining practical and accessible in real-world settings.

courses.title: Managing common abdominal problems in practice today
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients (both dog and cat) who are presented to their clinic with common abdominal problems The combination of Specialists will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common gastro-intestinal, splenic and urinary problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: The B2 Dog: What Every General Practitioner Should Know About Preclinical Heart Disease With Dr. Visser
courses.description: A newly ausculted heart murmur is a common encounter in general practice, but navigating what comes next isn't always straightforward. In this episode of the Partner Podcast, Dr. Lance Visser, board-certified veterinary cardiologist, breaks down the essentials of myxomatous mitral valve disease, including staging and diagnostic criteria, the landmark EPIC trial data, and what the recent approval of VETMEDIN (pimobendan) by the FDA for the preclinical B2 dogs means for clinical practice.

courses.title: Assessing the Cardiac Size and Shape
courses.description: Assessing the cardiac silhouette in radiographs is an important skill for veterinary teams. Radiographic signs of cardiac remodeling include generalized cardiomegaly and left atrial enlargement, which can be assessed by subjective observation and by objective measurements such as VHS (Vertebral Heart Size) and VLAS (Vertebral Left Atrial Size). This course aims to provide a practical learning experience in both subjective and objective cardiac assessment, including exercises in assessing cardiomegaly and cardiac shape, measuring VHS and VLAS, and an introduction to the clinical signs and staging of Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease.

courses.title: A Breath of Fresh Air: Perioperative Care of Brachycephalic Patients
courses.description: When you hear snorting in the lobby during the morning surgical check-ins, do you start to sweat a little? Brachycephlic breeds are more popular than ever, but their signature aesthetic complicates routine procedures and often requires corrective surgery. This free, 90-minute session shares new, proven techniques to improve anesthetic success for our stout snout patients, both canine and feline! We'll discuss physiological obstacles and ways to mitigate disaster with easy preventive strategies.

courses.title: INVENTORY MANAGEMENT CERTIFICATION
courses.description: See attached

courses.title: Functional Mushrooms in Animal Health
courses.description:
Functional mushrooms are increasingly incorporated into companion-animal supplements and integrative veterinary care, yet clinicians often encounter inconsistent terminology, variable product formats, and differing interpretations of the available evidence. This course provides a practical, evidence-informed overview of functional mushrooms and their use in animal health.
The session will cover a brief background of fungi, including the mushroom life cycle and examples of the historical use of mushrooms in traditional medicine. Participants will review commonly used functional mushroom species and the major classes of bioactive compounds associated with them.
This webinar will provide an overview of commercial mushroom products, including insights into how different types of mushroom-derived ingredients are manufactured and what quality considerations are important to consider when selecting a mushroom-based supplement.
The course will explore proposed and evidence-supported relationships among mushroom-derived compounds, the gut microbiome, immune signaling, and host physiology. Attendees will learn practical guidance on how to better evaluate product quality and safety, dosing considerations, applications, and how to best integrate functional mushrooms into patient care plans.

courses.title: Sleeping Beauty; Pre-euthanasia sedation protocols
courses.description:
When you picture Sleeping Beauty from the classic fairytale, you likely see a state of
pure tranquility, without a care or cause for concern. Clients want their pets sleeping in
their final moments; peaceful and pain free. In this session, we discuss how using
sedatives and anesthetics help patients let the world around them go and prepare for
death. The benefits are numerous, the downsides minimal. Join us as we talk about
how we look beyond just propofol before pentobarbital, and really dive into combination
protocols we can use for a wide variety of species.

courses.title: Gut Microbiome and Canine Behavior
courses.description: This Florida Veterinary Medical Association-sponsored webinar explores the growing body of research demonstrating the connection between the gastrointestinal microbiome and canine behavior through the gut-brain axis. Participants will examine how the intestinal microbiome influences neurologic development, immune function, stress responses, cognition, and emotional regulation, as well as the impact of gastrointestinal health on behavioral disorders. The course reviews current evidence linking dysbiosis to anxiety, fear, aggression, and cognitive dysfunction while discussing the role of nutrition, probiotics, prebiotics, and gastrointestinal therapies as adjuncts to behavior modification. Through evidence-based discussion and clinical examples, attendees will gain practical strategies for incorporating microbiome health into comprehensive behavioral case management.

courses.title: Medical Math and CRIs: Removing the Fear Factor (TECH432)
courses.description: Does the thought of performing medical math, especially calculating a Continuous Rate Infusion (CRI), fill you with dread? It doesn't have to be that way! You have the power to master medical math! This lecture will illuminate the essential role of math in your practice, provide a brief review of key medications whose use often involves math, and guide you through each step of the calculation process with confidence.

courses.title: Nutrigenomics & Obesity: It's About Prediction, Not Restriction
courses.description: The field of nutrigenomics is a growing science that holds promise for health management in people and pets. A therapeutic weight loss food for pets was developed using nutrigenomic technology; the steps needed to create such a food using this advanced science will be reviewed. Clinical studies in dogs and cats using a nutrigenomic approach to weight loss will be discussed.

courses.title: Mechanical Ventilation During Anesthesia: Hands-On WorkshopOn-Demand
courses.description: This hands-on, interactive workshop guides attendees through the equipment set-up, operation, and troubleshooting for mechanical ventilation during anesthesia. Attendees learn about the importance of monitoring and maintaining normal ventilation of anesthetized patients. The anatomy and physiology involved with respiration and ventilation will be reviewed in detail, along with how capnography gives an indirect assessment of ventilation, cellular metabolism, and perfusion. Scenarios for common complications and troubleshooting during mechanical ventilation are reviewed in detail, allowing for hands-on correction and comprehensive understanding.

courses.title: The Burnout Conversation We Should Be Having
courses.description: Burnout remains one of the most significant challenges facing the veterinary profession, yet it is often oversimplified as a workload issue. This session rethinks the conversation around burnout by exploring organizational influences, individual responses, compassion fatigue, and self-awareness. Participants will explore practical strategies to recognize burnout earlier, respond more effectively, and build a more sustainable career in veterinary medicine.

courses.title: Stopping Bleeding; A Brief History of Methods and Techniques, and what we can do better.
courses.description: The need to control bleeding in human and animal surgeries and traumas has existed for centuries. Galen documented common methods in the second century AD, and this lecture will briefly review the changes and development in hemostatic methods form then until now. The latter part of the lecture will focus on hemostatic products, how they work, and the pros and cons of the various types available. Participants will have a better understanding of the options available to control bleeding, how they evolved, and what current best practice is.

courses.title: Small Animal Programme part 2 (2024)
courses.description: This programme includes 21 hours of world-class CPD, delivered by experts in the field. The main objective is to keep veterinarians up to date with the latest insights into small animals. The Programme will outline the typical approach to investigating and managing cases in order to optimise the outcome. Topics covered range from dermatology, nutrition, behaviour, oncology, among others.

courses.title: What does the changing landscape for accessible veterinary care mean for general practice?
courses.description: The idea that the veterinary industry as a whole has an obligation to provide care for all companion animals in the United States, regardless of their owner's ability to pay, is gaining acceptance. The veterinary oath requires us to use our skills and abilities for the betterment of society and the protection of animal health and wealth regardless of the animals' circumstances. For veterinarians confronting the daily economic realities of private practice and/or for any veterinarian who wants to practice high quality medicine, it can be difficult to understand how to balance owner limitations with the desire to provide care. The growing field of accessible veterinary care recognizes that for our profession to meet the professional obligations to provide care for all companion animals the industry needs to change. These changes involve rethinking the way care is delivered and developing new models for care. For veterinarians in practice who want to expand services to underserved clients, key strategies include offering flexible treatment plans and/or accepting alternative payment options.

courses.provider: TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY OFFICE OF VETERINARY CONTINUING EDUCATION
courses.title: 2026 Foundations of Avian Medicine and Nutrition
courses.description: A Continuing Education Course offered by the College of Veterinary Medicine, Texas A&M University, College Station TX. This one-day, virtual symposium is designed for veterinarians ranging from those new to working with birds to those already holding board certifications. The symposium will provide a practical progression through the foundations of avian medicine and nutrition. We will begin with an overview of avian care and clinical decision-making, followed by a nutrition primer covering the most important dietary considerations for captive psittacines and other avian species. A dedicated session on avian emergency medicine will focus on patient assessment, stabilization, and other essential techniques for managing critical cases. A lunch session will include information about captive parrot diets, supporting parrot wellbeing and aiding avian conservation. After lunch, participants will explore how research on wild and captive parrot foraging behavior and welfare can inform husbandry and nutritional management. The symposium will conclude with a practical feeding session focused on translating these concepts into clear, actionable dietary recommendations.

courses.title: It's Not the Injection, It's the Selection: Optimizing 2.5% iPAAG Outcomes in Canine OA
courses.description:
As the management of canine osteoarthritis continues to evolve, veterinarians are seeking therapies that provide long-term improvements in mobility, comfort, and quality of life. While intra-articular 2.5% iPAAG offers a novel approach to joint management, achieving optimal outcomes begins with selecting the right patient and setting appropriate client expectations.
This webinar will review the clinical considerations that support successful use of 2.5% iPAAG in canine patients, including patient selection criteria, diagnostic workup, joint-specific considerations, and treatment planning. Through real-world case examples and practical insights, attendees will learn how to identify ideal candidates, recognize factors that may influence outcomes, and integrate 2.5% iPAAG into a multimodal osteoarthritis management strategy.
Participants will leave with a framework for improving case selection, enhancing client communication, and maximizing the likelihood of positive clinical outcomes.

courses.title: Advances in Canine Urinary Incontinence Management: Understanding Bulking Therapies and what makes Mictamid different
courses.description:
Urinary sphincter mechanism incompetence (USMI) remains a common challenge in veterinary medicine, and advances in bulking agent technology continue to expand treatment options for affected patients. Join Dr. Roger Dmochowski, a recognized leader in female urology and reconstructive outcomes, and Dr. JD Foster, a veterinary specialist in nephrology and urology, for an in-depth discussion of the evolution of urethral bulking therapies.
This webinar will review the history and classification of bulking agents, exploring their mechanisms of action, benefits, and limitations. The faculty will discuss how Mictamid differs from traditional bulking agents, including its clinical application and potential role in managing canine urinary incontinence. Attendees will gain practical insights into patient selection, treatment positioning within current therapeutic strategies, and considerations for integrating procedures and documentation into everyday clinical workflows through electronic medical record (EMR) systems.
Designed for veterinary practitioners seeking to enhance their understanding of interventional options for urinary incontinence, this session will provide evidence-based perspectives and actionable takeaways for clinical practice.

courses.title: Why Are Veterinary Teams So Exhausted by People? Using Cultural Intelligence to Reduce Conflict and Build Trust (On-Demand)
courses.description:
Veterinary professionals spend much of their day navigating emotionally charged conversations with clients, collaborating across diverse teams, and making complex medical decisions under pressure. While burnout is often attributed to workload and compassion fatigue, the cumulative impact of interpersonal friction is frequently overlooked.
This session introduces Cultural Intelligence (CQ) as a practical, evidence-based framework for improving communication, strengthening relationships, and reducing unnecessary conflict in veterinary practice. Using real-world veterinary case examples, participants will explore how assumptions, cultural perspectives, and communication styles influence client interactions, team dynamics, and patient care. Practical strategies for applying the four capabilities of Cultural Intelligence (CQ Drive, CQ Knowledge, CQ Strategy, and CQ Action) will be presented to help attendees build trust, navigate challenging conversations, and foster stronger collaboration with both clients and colleagues.

courses.title: The Before, During, and After of Obtaining a Veterinary Technician Specialty Nutrition
courses.description: Veterinary Technician Specialties (VTS) provides an opportunity for credentials technicians to enhance their skills and knowledge in specific areas of practice. Obtaining these credentials include gathering experience, increasing knowledge and skills mastery through case development, practical skill exposure, and validated accreditation testing which can take anywhere from 3-5 years. The question many pre-applicants have is, and then what? Is there a guaranteed pay increase? What career opportunities are there? This session will discuss the story of a VTS Nutrition applicant from the preparing years, the application year, and what possibilities lie ahead.

courses.title: Managing Uncertainty: Four Ways to Optimize Practice Success
courses.description:
Throughout the world, this is a time of radical uncertainty. Wave after wave of disruption creates continual changes to the global economy, resulting in shrinking paychecks as costs continue to increase in all parts of life. Due to economic stressors, pets are receiving less veterinary care and the costs of operating a practice continue to increase.
Course corrections are necessary when turbulence sets in. What are four areas that practice leaders can map out today to help them weather this storm?

courses.provider: SOUTH CAROLINA VETERINARY SPECIALISTS & EMERGENCY CARE
courses.title: The Overzealous Thyroid: A review and update on hyperthyroid management and associated comorbidities in cats.
courses.description:
Hyperthyroidism is the most common endocrine disease in cats, affecting senior to geriatric
cats. Feline hyperthyroidism is typically a progressive, slow growing condition that, left
untreated, can result in deleterious reversible and irreversible changes in the body. Four
treatment modalities have been described for feline hyperthyroidism, which come with various
risks versus benefits. This course aims to highlight current literature discussing each of these
treatment modalities, along with the diagnosis and management of comorbidities associated
with or as a consequence to hyperthyroidism in cats. State regulatory protocols involving
radioiodine treatment in cats will also be briefly discussed

courses.title: Resident & Specialists Only: Soft Tissue Ultrasound Camp
courses.description: This course will cover a basic to intermediate level of the abdomen, emphasis on anatomy, physics, principles, knobology, image acquisition and protocols, normals, abnormals, case studies, scenarios, and touch on basic Doppler. This course is designed for Residents and Specialists with an interest in 40 hours of abdominal ultrasound with a Board Certified Radiologist to build their level of proficiency and satisfy the requirements of the ACVIM. Taught by Martha Larson, DVM, MS, DACVR

courses.title: Shaping the Diagnosis Series: Morphology Mystery
courses.description: Automated hematology analyzers provide powerful quantitative data, but important diagnostic insights can be missed when blood morphology is not assessed. This presentation explores the clinical value of blood morphology assessment as a complement to automated CBC results. Through one canine case study, participants will examine how morphology findings altered diagnostic pathways, improved interpretation of laboratory data, and influenced patient management. Practical guidance will be provided on when morphology review is most important and how morphology findings can be integrated into everyday clinical decision-making.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Field Castration: Morbidity & Mortality Case Discussions
courses.description:
Castrations are one of the most commonly performed elective surgeries in equine practice, frequently being performed outside of a controlled surgical suite, and with minimal or no support i.e. in the field
Complications are not uncommon, and can range from mild to life-threatening. Join our highly experienced, leading panel of experts who will share their experiences, debate the different anaesthetic and surgical approaches, and discuss their approaches to management and prevention of complications.

courses.provider: PARACHUTE VET - YOUR SAFETY NET FOR ECC
courses.title: Triage in Small Animal Emergency and Critical Care
courses.description: This lecture provides a practical approach to triage in small animal emergency and critical care. Participants will learn how to rapidly identify unstable canine and feline patients using the ABCDE triage framework, perform focused physical examinations, recognize life-threatening abnormalities, utilize bedside diagnostics, and initiate immediate stabilization. The course also covers effective phone triage, preparation for incoming emergencies, and the Veterinary Triage List to improve patient prioritization and outcomes.

courses.title: Essentials of Small Animal Ophthalmology by Dr Jennifer Sheahan DVM, DACVO
courses.description:
Course Format:
A six-week guided online program offering approximately 12 hours of structured video lectures, downloadable notes, ophthalmology protocols, clinical checklists, case studies, and interactive quizzes. Lessons are presented in short 5 to 20 minute videos. A new module unlocks each week, and learners retain access to all course materials for six months.
Target Audience:
Veterinarians and final-year veterinary students seeking to improve confidence and competence in the examination, diagnosis, initial treatment, and referral of common and urgent small animal ophthalmic conditions.
Course Overview:
Essentials of Small Animal Ophthalmology provides a structured, evidence-based approach to the ocular examination and the management of ophthalmic conditions commonly encountered in general and emergency practice. The course progresses from ocular anatomy, examination techniques, and diagnostic testing to glaucoma, ophthalmic emergencies, corneal disease, ulcers, posterior segment disease, retinal disease, and acute blindness.
With guidance from board-certified veterinary ophthalmologist Dr Jennifer Sheahan DVM, DACVO, participants develop practical clinical reasoning and learn when a patient can be managed in general practice and when urgent referral is required. The course emphasises accurate examination, correct interpretation of diagnostic tests, timely treatment, preservation of vision, and effective client communication.
Educational Methods:
The course combines short, focused video lectures, downloadable workbooks, clinical protocols and checklists, pre and post module multiple-choice quizzes, and realistic case-based exercises. Participants may ask clinical questions within The Vet Tribe Community and receive guidance from the specialist mentor. The final module includes a comprehensive online MCQ examination with a minimum pass mark of 70 percent.

courses.title: Advanced TPLO
courses.description:
This course is for the experienced TPLO surgeon that wants to expand their understanding of TPLO and stifle surgery.
Prerequisites:
1. Online Tibial Plateau-Leveling Osteotomy series*
*Tibial Plateau-Leveling Osteotomy Series

courses.title: Is it Neoplasia or Not? The oncology world from the clinical sonographer's perspective.
courses.description: Attendees of this live lecture course should expect to learn their imaging responsibilities and expectations regarding a local vs. a multi-centric clinical presentation. What is overtly surgical, potentially surgical, or non-surgical. What meets neoplastic criteria, diagnostic sampling vs. surgical intervention, and sampling types depending on clinical presentations; FNA for cytological pathology and core biopsy for structural pathology.

courses.title: FiberMaxxing: When should pets do it?
courses.description: In this online CE event, Dr. Adam Rudinsky, MS, DACVIM reviews the properties of dietary fiber and how they can be implemented in small animal practice with specific focus on case based application of fiber diets and supplements and dosing protocols. The systemic health of animals and maintenance of gastrointestinal tract (GIT) homeostasis heavily relies on influences from dietary fiber. Dietary fiber includes a diverse assortment of non-digestible carbohydrates. Primary roles of dietary fiber in the GIT include physically altering the digesta, modulating appetite and satiety, regulating digestion, and acting as a microbial energy source through fermentation. Beyond the GIT, dietary fiber also has widespread systemic effects throughout the body. This review will focus on how to modify fiber in dogs and cats with gastrointestinal disease. The goal being to provide clinically relevant information for practical application in clinical practice. Join us to get a clinical update on appropriate strategies to identify and manage your fiber-responsive gastrointestinal patients.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Choosing the Right Rehab Modality for Soft Tissue and Bony Injuries Laser vs Shockwave Therapy
courses.description:
Selecting the most effective rehabilitation modality is one of the most important clinical decisions when treating soft tissue and bony injuries. This online panel discussion explores the comparative strengths, mechanisms, and ideal use cases of therapeutic laser and extracorporeal shockwave therapy ESWT two of the most widely used and evidence supported technologies in modern musculoskeletal care.
The discussion breaks down how each modality interacts with biological tissues, highlighting the differences between photobiomodulation laser and mechanotransduction (shockwave). Attendees will gain clarity when to choose laser for cellular-level healing, inflammation control, and acute injury management, and when shockwave becomes the superior option for chronic tendinopathies, calcifications, delayed bone healing, and tissue remodeling.
Key topics include
Brief overview of the science behind laser therapy wavelengths, dosages, and how light energy accelerates tissue repair
How shockwave therapy stimulates neovascularization, collagen restructuring, and analgesia
Clinical decision making for acute vs chronic injuries
Contraindications, treatment parameters, and safety considerations
Case examples illustrating modality selection in real world scenarios
How combining laser and shockwave can enhance outcomes in complex or stubborn injuries
By the end, practitioners will have a clear, practical roadmap for choosing the right modality or combination of modalities to optimize healing timelines, reduce pain, and improve functional outcomes for both soft tissue and bony pathologies.

courses.title: Unlocking MDR1 Mutations in Cats: Prevalence, Perils, & Protocols
courses.description: Join us for an evidence-based update on the feline multidrug sensitivity gene (MDR1 gene, also known as ABCB1 gene). Dr. Jeba Chelladurai will discuss the feline ABCB1 1930_1931del TC variant, a key loss-of-function mutation that can cause neurotoxicity following exposure to certain antiparasitic and other commonly used drugs. Dr. Chelladurai will review the MDR1 essentials, including how this 2-base pair deletion may place cats carrying 2 copies of the variant at high risk, and share new data from the largest screening study to date of 12,000 US domestic cats. Actionable takeaways will include how to identify which feline patients warrant genotyping and how to approach prescribing decisions with confidence.

courses.title: Certification in Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine
courses.description: The Certification in Veterinary Western Herbal Medicine enables practitioners to develop competency in utilising Western herbal medicine and Western herbal medicine principles in the assessment, treatment and management of animals in their care. Successful completion of this course will enable practitioners to safely and effectively integrate a core group of 40 important herbs into a veterinary practice. The course is orientated towards applied theory, which can be implemented in a veterinary practice almost immediately. Practitioners will be able to develop confidence and competence over time during the course, with continuous case support, guidance and feedback from tutors with both simulated and active case forums and subsequently their own clinical cases.

courses.title: Hormone Therapy in Broodmare Practice
courses.description: Hormone Therapy in Broodmare Practice is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: A Fresh Perspective: A Discussion on Feeding Fresh
courses.description: This course provides veterinary professionals with a balanced, evidence-based look at fresh pet food diets compared to fresh-homemade and traditional dry food. Topics include a review of pet food safety; effective strategies for navigating popular nutrition trends; the practical benefits of fresh feeding; and key considerations for tailoring to a patients needs. Attendees will leave equipped to objectively counsel clients on fresh versus dry feeding options.

courses.title: Open Wound Management - What's New and What Works?
courses.description: This lecture provides a practical update on open wound management in veterinary patients, with an emphasis on current evidence and techniques that can improve wound healing. Topics will include wound assessment, debridement, wound bed preparation, lavage, topical therapies and dressings, negative pressure wound therapy, and decision-making for delayed or definitive wound closure. Participants will review what is new in veterinary wound care, which traditional approaches remain effective, and how to select appropriate management strategies for challenging wounds encountered in clinical practice.

courses.title: VetCE Virtual: Beyond Bad Behavior - Understanding Canine and Feline Behaviour Disorders
courses.description: This VetCE Virtual set of 3 live distance presentations includes topics of interest presented by experts. The presentations are held on separate dates. Attendees enroll in all three and must attend all to earn the completion certificate. The first presentation is on September 14, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Easy as one, two, pee: Solving Feline Housesoiling. The 2nd is on September 21, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Resource Guarding of Food. The 3rd and final presentation is on September 28, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Addressing the Medical Components of Behavior Cases. The VetCE Virtual series of micro-conferences are a convenient alternative to in-person events and are designed to deliver multiple RACE and/or CVPM approved CE credits in a virtual format with three one-hour presentations. They provide educational sessions presented by expert speakers, and an easy way to learn and earn credits in the comfort of your home or office.

courses.title: Management 2: Advanced
courses.description: This course offers an in-depth exploration of advanced management and financial strategies, designed for those pursuing the AALAS Certified Manager of Animal Resources (CMAR) certification and preparing for the M2 exam, as well as anyone seeking to enhance their advanced management and financial skills. Participants will gain a deep understanding of value chain management, organizational structure, human resources, motivation, financial decision-making, and more, equipping them with the expertise needed for high-level management roles. Key topics include: - Implementing value chain management for superior quality and efficiency - Designing effective organizational structures and cultures - Utilizing strategic human resources management for competitive advantage - Motivating and enhancing employee performance - Leveraging accounting information for informed decision-making - Conducting financial analysis and budgeting for operational success Participants will engage with practical applications of these concepts, preparing them for both the M2 certification exam and complex managerial challenges.

courses.title: From Cells to Signals: Innovations Transforming Cancer Diagnostics in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: Recent advances in artificial intelligence, computer vision, and biomarker science are transforming the way cancer is detected, characterized, and monitored in veterinary patients. This presentation will explore emerging technologies that enhance diagnostic testing and clinical decision-making, including AI-enabled cytology interpretation, novel statistical approaches that objectively quantify diagnostic confidence, and blood-based biomarkers that support cancer screening, diagnosis, and disease monitoring. Together, these innovations are creating new opportunities for earlier detection, more informed clinical decisions, and improved patient care across the cancer journey.
