courses.title: Instrument Care Essentials: Surgical Instrumentation Cleaning Protocols for Clinical Teams
courses.description: This presentation is designed to educate clinic team members responsible for cleaning and maintaining surgical instruments. The program focuses on the importance of proper instrument care to help extend instrument life, maintain performance, and support optimal surgical outcomes.

courses.provider: THE AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF FISH VETERINARIANS
courses.title: ISAAH AAFV SESSION:Fish Veterinary Medicine in North America: Diversity in Production and Practice
courses.description: AAFV is hosting a session during ISAAH Norway with the topic Fish Veterinary Medicine in North America: Diversity in Production and Practice.

courses.title: The Balance Between Art and Science in Seizure Management (NEUR101-1026)
courses.description:
The primary purpose of this course is to improve the ability and comfort of participants to manage seizure patients by providing an in-depth understanding of diagnostic workflows and approaches, how various anticonvulsants work, and how contextual factors of the patient and pet owner affect decisions regarding drug selection, monitoring, and alteration. The course will include a discussion of seizure definitions and classification, formulating a diagnostic plan for the seizure patient based on signalment and history, and general principles of seizure management. This course will focus on three major domains:
1. Classification and Diagnostic Approaches to Seizures, Medication Selection and Monitoring
2. Non-pharmacological Interventions
3. Discussion of Real-Life Cases and Approaches

courses.title: Panel Discussion Cardiology as Part of PPE Case Discussions
courses.description: This interactive panel brings together the leading minds in equine cardiology from around the world to explore the role of cardiac assessment in the prepurchase examination. Through sharing cases, the panel will discuss and debate the interpretation of murmurs, arrhythmias, and echocardiographic findings, and how these influence decision making and risk assessment. With a focus on grey zone case examples, this will be a lively debate on when further diagnostics are warranted, how to assess risk, and how to effectively communicate findings to prospective purchasers.

courses.title: Canine Veterinary Ophthalmology: Adnexa, Cornea, and Intraocular Disease
courses.description: This 4-hour continuing education program provides veterinarians and veterinary technicians with a practical review of common adnexal, corneal, and intraocular disorders in dogs. The adnexal section addresses eyelid conformation and hair disorders, eyelid masses and lacerations, and third-eyelid disease. The corneal section reviews systematic assessment and management of simple, indolent, infected, melting, deep, and ruptured corneal ulcers as well as other clinically important corneal disease. The intraocular section covers examination techniques and the recognition and management of uveitis, glaucoma, cataracts, lens luxation or subluxation, retinal disease, and blindness.

courses.title: Dental Radiographs (TECH343)
courses.description:
Even for technicians experienced in radiography, dental radiographs are a whole different animal - and these images play a crucial role in conducting thorough oral exams on every patient.
This course will empower veterinary technicians and assistants with the essential skills needed to obtain diagnostic dental radiographs. Together, we will explore the normal anatomy and terminology of the mouth before embarking on the journey of mastering full mouth radiographs for both canine and feline companions. We will discuss and demonstrate proper positioning techniques to ensure the highest-quality images, while also addressing common challenges you may encounter and providing invaluable tips and tricks for capturing dental radiographs in brachycephalic breeds. Finally, we will delve into the various types of dental radiography equipment and the importance of radiation safety, equipping you with the knowledge to excel in this vital aspect of veterinary care.

courses.title: Spectrum of Care: Steering the Conversation to Navigate for Better Outcomes
courses.description: As veterinary professionals, we are trained to offer and plan for the highest level of care for our patients. While that is what we ideally want to offer to every client and patient, the reality is that not every client can pay for or even manage such "Ideal" care. This lack of adherence to our recommendations for care contributes to meaning burnout and moral injury within the profession. Spectrum of Care refers to discovering what the client can or can't do for their pet - financially, physically, and emotionally. Understanding this enables an honest and non-judgmental conversation between the veterinary team and the client so that a mutually agreed upon treatment plan can be made for the shared focus of both - the Pet. Embracing a Spectrum of Care strategy with our clients means that we can help more patients and clients, and ultimately, can help ourselves by finding more fulfillment and satisfaction in our work.

courses.title: Level Up: 2026 Veterinary Nurses and Technicians LIVE
courses.description: Veterinary nurses and technicians are the heartbeat of every practice - and this summit is built for you. Join our annual Level Up: Veterinary Nurses and Technicians Summit to learn while sharpening your clinical knowledge and fueling your professional growth. From emesis and Cushings disease to periodontal care, senior wellness, traumatic burn injuries, radiologic positioning, neurodiversity, burnout, and more, you will come away with clinical updates, new skills, fresh confidence, and ideas you can use on your very next shift. Because the future of veterinary medicine is not waiting - and neither should your career!

courses.title: Ethical disagreements in veterinary practice settings
courses.description:
Ethical disagreements are common in veterinary practice and arise when members of the veterinary team, clients, or other stakeholders hold differing views about what ought to be done in a particular situation. These disagreements may occur in relation to animal welfare, treatment decisions, resource limitations, financial constraints, client preferences, workplace policies, or professional responsibilities. When unresolved, ethical conflict can contribute to moral stress, moral distress, and reduced wellbeing among veterinary professionals.
This webinar will examine the nature and sources of ethical disagreement in veterinary practice settings. Participants will be introduced to common factors that contribute to differing ethical viewpoints, including variations in professional roles, values, ethical frameworks, experiences, and perceptions of animal welfare. Through discussion of practical veterinary scenarios, attendees will explore how ethical disagreement can reveal underlying welfare concerns and competing obligations that require careful consideration.
The webinar will also provide a structured approach for identifying and analyzing sources of ethical conflict within veterinary teams. Emphasis will be placed on recognizing disagreement as a potentially constructive component of ethical decision-making and as an opportunity to improve communication, support team wellbeing, and enhance animal welfare outcomes.

courses.title: Antibiotics and the Eye: Pharmacology, Stewardship, and Best Clinical Practices (OPHT211)
courses.description: Inappropriate use of antibiotics is a leading contributor to increasing antimicrobial resistance in both human and veterinary medicine. The principles of ocular antibiotic therapy differ from systemic treatment for many reasons, including differences in pharmacokinetics, available formulations (e.g., eyedrops vs orals), and classes of antibiotics commonly available for treating the eye. The risk of resistance is also different when treating topically compared with systemically. Unfortunately, antibiotic stewardship is often not considered when treating ophthalmic disease, and overuse of antibiotics is common (e.g., using a topical steroid that contains antibiotics for a non-infectious disease or using a topical fluoroquinolone for prophylactic treatment of a simple corneal ulcer). This course will discuss ocular antibiotic treatment principles and the mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance - highlighting the specifics as they relate to the eye. It aims to also improve attendee familiarity with ocular antibiotic treatment principles. It will also discuss the use of "best" practices to avoid the emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance, from an international perspective, giving specific strategies for minimizing antibiotic use in ophthalmic disease, including identifying situations when antibiotics are not necessary and suggesting alternatives to antibiotics.

courses.title: Kidneys and adrenals: Diagnostic challenges and therapeutic interventions in chronic kidney disease and canine hyperadrenocor
courses.description: In this 4-hour, LIVE seminar with Dr. Christina Marino, DVM, DACVIM (SAIM), participants will review advanced diagnostic and management strategies for complex endocrinopathies, polyuria/polydipsia (PU/PD), and chronic kidney disease in dogs and cats. The program re-evaluates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, covering diagnostic innovations for canine hyperadrenocorticism, atypical Cushing's disease, and alternative monitoring protocols that move beyond the traditional ACTH stimulation test. It provides a structured diagnostic approach to PU/PD, including the step-by-step execution and interpretation of a modified water deprivation test. Finally, the seminar details the pathophysiology and progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), providing updated therapeutic strategies including novel phosphate binders and erythropoietin-stimulating agents.

courses.title: Foundations of Vaccination
courses.description: This educational program provides a comprehensive overview of the core principles of veterinary immunology and vaccinology. Designed for veterinary professionals, the session explores the physiological mechanisms of immune protection, the classification of modern vaccine technologies, and best practices for implementing effective vaccine protocols. Participants will gain the foundational knowledge necessary to support evidence-based vaccination strategies and confidently communicate the vital role of vaccination in lifelong pet wellness.

courses.title: APV 54th Annual Workshop
courses.description: Each fall since 1973, the Association of Primate Veterinarians has held its annual Workshop. During the four days of the meeting, members and nonmembers come together to enjoy the lectures, poster sessions, case reports, and roundtables. The program is designed to have topics relevant to the entire membership. The workshop will be held in Houston, Texas from Wednesday, October 21st to Saturday, October 24th.

courses.title: Shockwave Therapy for Post-Surgical Treatment
courses.description: This course will provide attendees with: 1. A basic understanding of the various applications and techniques for delivering therapeutic shockwave 2. A review of conditions treated with shockwave therapy and specific positioning of the device and patients that optimize treatment outcomes 3. In-depth focus on palpation skills and advanced treatment techniques. 4. Provide the post-surgical indications for shockwave therapy, with particular attention to TPLO and non-healing bone cases. 5. Provide hands-on positioning and treatment practice for post-surgical patients using the PiezoWave Vet.

courses.title: Leading With Intention: Building the Career and Culture You Want
courses.description:
Your first position after graduation will shape you but it should never define you.
Veterinary hospitals vary widely in their cultures, expectations, workflows, and utilization of team members. Learning to recognize those differences and intentionally choosing environments that align with your values and professional goals is an essential skill that is rarely taught in school. This session prepares participants to navigate the realities of veterinary practice with confidence, professionalism, and discernment while understanding how every member of the veterinary team contributes to exceptional patient care.
Participants will explore how to become a positive influence regardless of title by leading themselves first. Topics include understanding interdisciplinary roles, building professional credibility, advocating respectfully, navigating workplace dynamics, recognizing healthy versus unhealthy workplace cultures, and contributing to solutions rather than drama.
Discussion will also include strategies for evaluating prospective employers, establishing healthy boundaries, and maintaining professionalism in environments that may not always reflect the kind of veterinary medicine they hope to practice.
Through practical examples and guided reflection, participants will leave with a framework for making intentional career decisions, strengthening the teams they join, and becoming the kind of colleague who elevates the people and culture around them. Rather than simply adapting to veterinary medicine as it exists today, attendees will be challenged to become part of the profession they hope to create for tomorrow.

courses.title: Performing and Communicating Around Euthanasia With Compassion
courses.description:
Few moments in veterinary medicine require greater presence than guiding a family through the end of a beloved pet's life. While clinical skills are essential, the experience is equally shaped by communication, compassion, professionalism, and the ability to create an environment where families feel supported during one of their most difficult moments.
This session explores practical strategies for preparing both the physical space and your professional presence before, during, and after euthanasia appointments. Participants will learn techniques for creating a calm environment, clear energy, developing authentic communication scripts, and utilizing body language that conveys empathy and confidence.
Equally important, this webinar addresses what happens after the appointment ends. Repeated exposure to grief can quietly accumulate over time, making intentional recovery practices essential to a sustainable veterinary career. Participants will explore practical approaches for honoring each experience through protective practices, brief personal resets, structured team debriefs, and meaningful end-of-day rituals that acknowledge the emotional weight of the work while supporting long-term professional well-being.
By integrating compassionate behavior with intentional recovery practices, participants will leave with a framework for caring not only for patients and their families, but also for themselves and their colleagues.

courses.provider: DBA VETERINARY DENTISTRY EDUCATION AND CONSULTING SERVICES
courses.title: Intermediate Canine Dentistry Beyond the Fundamentals in Practice
courses.description: This 16-hour CE course (8 hours of lecture and 8 hours of laboratory) is for veterinarians only. It is recommended that registrants have completed a fundamental course with us, or equivalent course with another Diplomate of the American Veterinary Dental College, as basic fundamental concepts are presumed and built upon. It is instructed by two Board Certified Veterinary Dentists. The 8-hour didactic course curriculum will start with a visual photographic and radiographic tour of hidden canine oral pathology. Step-by-step oronasal fistula repair will be presented. Fractured teeth and bonded resin sealants will be discussed and covered step-by-step. Surgical extraction of the maxillary molars and surgical site closure will be presented. Surgical complications, prevention, and management will be presented. Periodontal treatments beyond periodontal cleaning, including but not limited to, bone augmentation, guided tissue regeneration, osseous resective surgery, open root planing, and periodontal treatments will be presented. The course will provide canine dentistry education and skills for primary care veterinary practice.

courses.title: The Fresh Food Alternative: Nutritional Strategies for Dogs with Protein-Losing Enteropathy
courses.description: For dogs with protein-losing enteropathy (PLE), commercial dry and canned diets don't always deliver the results patients need. Pet parents and the veterinary team are often left searching for alternatives. This webinar explores the role of fresh food diets as a therapeutic option when conventional commercial diets fall short. Attendees will learn how to approach diet selection for PLE patients, key nutritional considerations (fat restriction, protein source and digestibility, caloric density), and how to monitor response to fresh food interventions. Whether you're a veterinarian, veterinary nutritionist, or technician looking to expand your toolkit for managing difficult GI cases, this session will provide actionable guidance for incorporating fresh diets into a PLE treatment plan.

courses.provider: MELISSA SHAPIRO, DVM, PIGLET INTERNATIONAL INC
courses.title: A Veterinarian's Guide to Disabled Pets and Their People: Caring for the Disabled Patient
courses.description:
Pet parents of disabled animals face a unique hurdle, finding a veterinary team willing to embrace and partner in the care of their disabled pets. This might be due to differences in perceptions of quality of life and a lack of experience working with pets who are disabled.
This 60 minute session offers an empowering overview showing that disabled pets share the same foundational medical needs as typical patients, and that general and specialty practices are fully equipped to manage them. Through real life examples of disabled pets in authentic photos and engaging videos, attendees will start to reframe traditional quality of life conversations around a pets capacity for adaptation and happiness.
Attendees will learn to leverage external community resources and build an in clinic peer mentorship network to alleviate client stress and prevent premature euthanasia. The SHIFT Framework for Care of Disabled Pets will be introduced to give veterinarians, vet techs, and vet students an action plan for welcoming disabled pets into their practice.
The audience will leave feeling inspired, with a better understanding of the veterinarians role in supporting and guiding clients who choose to care for profoundly disabled pets.
The SHIFT Framework for Care of Disabled Pets
Secure appropriate medical care
Honor relative quality of life
Implement in home accommodations for individual needs
Find external online guidance and support networks
Tap into client base for peer mentorship

courses.title: Understanding Client Communication in Real-World Practice
courses.description:
Exceptional veterinary care extends beyond medical knowledge it requires the ability to connect with people. Every client brings their own experiences, emotions, expectations, and unseen circumstances into the exam room. By learning to meet people where they are, veterinary professionals can build trust, strengthen rapport, and create a shared vision for their pet's care.
This practical session explores communication strategies that empower and educate pet parents while supporting optimal patient outcomes. Participants will learn how to guide conversations with confidence, simplify complex medical information without sacrificing accuracy, and bridge the gap between recommendations and understanding. Discussion will include navigating emotionally charged conversations, financial limitations, difficult diagnoses, and other challenging interactions with empathy and professionalism.

courses.provider: PARACHUTE VET - YOUR SAFETY NET FOR ECC
courses.title: Something s brewing in this belly: diagnosis & stabilization of dogs with septic peritonitis
courses.description:
This clinically focused, case-based course guides veterinarians through the recognition, diagnosis, and initial stabilization of dogs with septic peritonitis. Participants will learn to recognize hyperdynamic and hypodynamic presentations of sepsis, and prioritize bedside diagnostics that identify immediately life-threatening abnormalities. The course reviews the interpretation of venous blood gas results, lactate, glucose, ECG findings, global POCUS, abdominal-fluid cytology, and blood-to-fluid glucose and lactate differences. Practical stabilization strategies include early broad-spectrum IV antimicrobial therapy, individualized fluid resuscitation, vasopressor support, analgesia, glucose and electrolyte correction, and management of clinically significant ventricular arrhythmias. Emphasis is placed on serial reassessment, preparation for anesthesia, and proceeding efficiently to definitive surgical source control.
Keywords: Canine septic peritonitis, septic abdomen, sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, systemic inflammatory response syndrome, SIRS, multiple organ dysfunction syndrome, MODS, acute abdomen, abdominal effusion, abdominocentesis, abdominal fluid cytology, intracellular bacteria, degenerate neutrophils, blood-to-fluid glucose difference, blood-to-fluid lactate difference, bacterial culture, antimicrobial therapy, fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine, vasopressors, venous blood gas, metabolic acidosis, hyperlactatemia, hypoglycemia, ventricular arrhythmias, POCUS, emergency surgery, source control, veterinary emergency medicine, veterinary critical care

courses.title: Small Animal Theriogenology Basics
courses.description:
This course is intended for veterinary students and practicing veterinarians. This is a review of the basics of small animal theriogenology that should permit the average practitioner to address concerns that are common in small animal practice.
It is a completely on-line course with interactive components. To complete the course, participants must complete the following:
Seven modules, associated with video lectures and course notes, completion of a study guide, and a quiz
A final examination, on which they must achieve a score of 70% or higher to gain access to the final project
A capstone project, which requires them to work through five of fifteen possible cases, demonstrating ability to use the course information for clinical decision making. This project will be graded by the instructor and participants will receive feedback.

courses.title: Feline Hyperthyroidism: Clinical Updates in Diagnosis, Treatment, & Management
courses.description: Join Dr. Ashlie Saffire for this webinar on hyperthyroid disease in cats. Dr. Saffire will review how to identify classic and "apathetic" presentation types and explore new diagnostic options, including how to use thyroid-stimulating hormone. The risks and rewards of the 4 treatment methods (ie, medical management, radioactive iodine, surgical thyroidectomy, and dietary restriction) will also be discussed. The presentation will conclude with how to adjust monitoring plans to meet the needs of common comorbidities so every cat gets the individual care they deserve.

courses.title: The Art & Science of the Neurologic and Orthopedic Exam from a Practical Perspective
courses.description: This live, interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will review methods for identifying the source of lameness. Case presentations will highlight orthopedic and neurologic evaluation, plus feature practical tips that are invaluable when determining surgical or conservative treatment for various disabling conditions. This course will also include methods drawing on techniques passed down from renowned practitioners of veterinary orthopedics and neurology.

courses.provider: DAVIS-THOMPSON DVM FOUNDATION FOR VETERINARY PATHOLOGY
courses.title: 36th Southcentral Davis-Thompson Meeting
courses.description: This 2 day meeting will feature 3 guest speakers and 20 veterinary pathology short case reports with a Friday lunch and dinner for in-person attendees. Zoom participation is also welcome.

courses.title: Preparing for Anesthesia: Lowering the Blood Pressure of Everyone in the Room While Raising the Patient's
courses.description: This webinar will focus on improving confidence, consistency, and patient safety through thoughtful anesthesia preparation. Suzanne McKenzie, RVT, VTS (Anesthesia/Analgesia), will emphasize the importance of evaluating each patient's history, signalment, physical examination findings, blood work, procedure needs, and individual risk factors before anesthesia and will walk participants through the stages of anesthesia planning, from preanesthetic evaluation and preparation to monitoring, response, and recovery. A central message of the presentation will be that anesthesia should never be approached with a "cookie cutter" protocol; instead, each patient should have an individualized plan that anticipates complications, supports physiologic stability, and helps the veterinary team feel prepared before the procedure begins.

courses.provider: THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE SPECIALISTS NORTH SCOTTSDALE
courses.title: Arthrocentesis and Joint Injection Wet Lab
courses.description:
2. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: In this cadaver wet lab, participants will learn and practice arthrocentesis and joint injection techniques for the hip, stifle, tarsus, shoulder, elbow, and carpus.
3. LEARNING OBJECTIVES:
1. Understand the indications for arthrocentesis and joint injections
2. Be able to confidently and successfully perform arthrocentesis and joint injection of the hip, stifle, tarsus, shoulder, elbow, and carpus.
4. PROGRAM AGENDA:
1. Divide participants into small groups, 4 per instructor and cadaver
2. Discuss the indications for arthrocentesis and joint injections
3. Demonstrate proper patient positioning and arthrocentesis and joint injection (using saline) technique for the hip, stifle, tarsus, shoulder, elbow and carpus. Participants to follow after instruction of each joint.

courses.title: Reach for Zen: New Relief for Dogs with Atopic Dermatitis_1.0CE
courses.description: Controlling allergies in dogs can be frustrating for veterinarians and clients. This presentation will introduce a new treatment that provides effective, continuous relief from pruritus and skin inflammation. By exploring expert management guidelines for allergic dermatitis and the concept of clinical remission for atopic dogs, attendees will learn how to achieve more Zen for a variety of allergic patients.

courses.title: Fetch Encore - NAVLE - Preparation, Placement & Professional Growth For the Vet Student and New Grad
courses.description:
Passing the NAVLE is one thing but being ready for real practice is another! This Fetch Encore virtual symposium focuses on the professional skills veterinary students and veterinary technician students need but rarely get taught:
Start making stronger calls with case-based learning, including:
- Managing the transition into practice
- Testing strategies
- Clinical reasoning
Expect honest conversations about confidence, imposter syndrome, and how to think like a doctor under pressure.

courses.title: Increased Liver Enzyme Activities in a Dog: Help! What Should I do Next?
courses.description: This presentation focuses on a practical, stepwise approach to dogs with persistently elevated liver enzyme activities. Common diagnostic tests used in evaluation of canine hepatic disease will be reviewed, with emphasis on their appropriate application and interpretation. A staged diagnostic framework will be presented, including when to pursue advanced testing such as liver biopsy and how to maximize diagnostic yield from the procedure.

courses.title: Equine Acupuncture: Locating Big Points on the Live Horse
courses.description: This short presentation on the locations and innervation of equine acupuncture points is designed as an introduction and/or refresher for those who seek to learn, with confidence, the topographical locations of select acupuncture points on the horse.

courses.provider: AMERICAN KENNEL CLUB CANINE HEALTH FOUNDATION
courses.title: Protecting the Aging Brain: IGF-1 and Canine Cognitive Dysfunction
courses.description: Older dogs often develop a form of dementia that is similar to Alzheimer's disease. We currently know little about this condition which limits our ability to prevent or manage it. IGF-1 is a hormone that regulates body size in dogs. In studies with humans and other animals, this hormone has been shown to protect the aging brain. This webinar will explore research investigating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), a hormone that regulates body size in dogs and has been associated with protective effects on the aging brain in humans and other animals. Attendees will learn how researchers are evaluating whether lower IGF-1 levels are associated with increased risk for cognitive dysfunction in dogs and what this could mean for future research and treatment.

courses.title: When Weight Loss Stalls: Practical Strategies for Challenging Cases
courses.description: Obesity management is often complicated by challenges such as inconsistent weight loss, food-seeking behaviors, multi-pet households, feeding inaccuracies, and declining owner adherence. This case-based presentation will explore practical strategies for overcoming common barriers encountered when weight loss stalls in dogs and cats. Through real-world clinical examples, participants will review methods for assessing weight loss progress, identifying factors limiting success, and implementing evidence-based interventions, including gram-scale feeding, feeding enrichment, automated feeders, and individualized nutritional adjustments. Presented from both the veterinarian and veterinary nurse perspectives, the session will emphasize the collaborative team approach needed to support successful weight management and long-term client engagement. Effective communication strategies, client preferences for decision-making, and practical methods for improving adherence will also be discussed. Attendees will gain tools to troubleshoot challenging cases and improve weight management outcomes in companion animals.

courses.title: Practice Management Software Administration
courses.description: Learn how to manage your practice via your practice management software, Covetrus Pulse. Better manage inventory, paperless/paperlight medical records, financials reporting and comprehension, daily workflow processes to assist the veterinarians and staff through their day. This course includes inventory management, paperless medical records, daily workflow processes to assist the staff, Pulse roadmap initiatives, and time to roundtable with your colleagues.

courses.title: Urine Trouble: Navigating Urethral Obstruction in Cats & Dogs
courses.description: Urethral obstruction is a common and potentially life-threatening urinary emergency requiring rapid recognition, stabilization, and relief of obstruction. This lecture will review clinically relevant urinary anatomy and physiology before providing a practical approach to the diagnosis and management of urethral obstruction in cats and dogs. Feline urethral obstruction will be discussed with emphasis on pathophysiology, diagnostic evaluation, stabilization, urinary catheterization, and management of associated metabolic complications. The canine section will address common causes of urethral obstruction, diagnostic investigation, and treatment options. Practical tips and techniques for managing challenging obstructions and reducing complications will be incorporated throughout the lecture.

courses.title: Becoming a Veterinary Technician Specialist (VTS): Pathways, Possibilities, and Passion
courses.description: Veterinary technicians are increasingly seeking advanced recognition for their knowledge, skills, and impact on patient care. The National Association of Veterinary Technicians in America (NAVTA) responded to this need by establishing the Committee on Veterinary Technician Specialties (CVTS), which provides the framework for creating and maintaining veterinary technician specialty academies. This webinar will walk you through the VTS journey--from understanding the history and structure of veterinary technician specialties, to deciding which discipline aligns with your passion, to navigating the application, examination, and recertification processes. We'll explore all currently recognized VTS academies, and outline what it takes to start a new specialty when one doesn't yet exist. Blending practical guidance with real-world experience, including a personal case example in veterinary nutrition, this session is designed to help you determine whether a VTS is right for you, how to prepare, and how specialization can advance both your career and your practice.

courses.provider: PARACHUTE VET - YOUR SAFETY NET FOR ECC
courses.title: Chest Trouble: The Dirty Secret of Pyothorax
courses.description:
Pyothorax can rapidly become both a respiratory and septic emergency. This practical, case-based course follows a dyspneic dog from initial presentation through stabilization, diagnosis, hospitalization, and discharge. Participants will learn to recognize pleural-space disease, prioritize oxygen supplementation and thoracocentesis, and use thoracic POCUS and pleural fluid cytology to answer immediate clinical questions. The course reviews appropriate culture submission, empiric antimicrobial selection, thoracic tube placement and lavage, and monitoring of treatment response. Medical and surgical management are compared, with emphasis on the use of radiographs, thoracic ultrasound, CT, and bronchoscopy to investigate underlying causes and guide intervention.
Keywords: Pyothorax, septic pleural effusion, dogs and cats, thoracic POCUS, thoracocentesis, thoracostomy tube, pleural fluid cytology, empiric antimicrobial therapy, thoracic lavage, thoracic CT

courses.title: VSC Veterinary Nutrtition Conference
courses.description: This five hour continuing education program will cover a wide variety of topics related to nutrtion for dogs and cats including - how to read pet food labels; healthy pet loss; evaluating raw, home-made and natural diet options; role of diet in pet allergies; and the role of diet in treating common diarrhea.

courses.title: Beyond the Dental: Hyaluronic Acid and the Future of At-Home Periodontal Care
courses.description:
Periodontal disease remains the most common clinical condition diagnosed in companion animal practice, yet maintaining oral health between anesthetic dental procedures continues to be a major challenge for veterinary teams and pet owners. Gingivitis represents the earliest and only reversible stage of periodontal disease, making early intervention and consistent home care essential components of effective management.
This lecture explores the emerging role of hyaluronic acid in veterinary dental medicine, including its biologic mechanisms, clinical evidence, and practical applications in both in-clinic and at-home settings. Participants will review current research evaluating hyaluronic acid therapies, including randomized controlled studies demonstrating improvements in gingival inflammation in dogs. The session will also discuss strategies for integrating simple, technician-driven home care solutions into dental protocols to support periodontal health between COHAT procedures.
Attendees will leave with practical tools for improving client compliance, enhancing periodontal care plans, and expanding preventive dentistry protocols within their practices.

courses.title: Canine Atopic Dermatitis - Is it the Perfect Situation for a Spectrum of Care Approach?
courses.description: One hour discussion session with Christina M Gentry, DVM, DACVD, Craig Teller, MD and Lori Teller, DVM, DABVP along with the moderator, Kristin Jankowski, VMD, CCRP. During the hour we will discuss their publication, How does canine atopic dermatitis provide a unique opportunity to study spectrum of care? as well as the related JAVMA publication, Multiple factors, including client financial constraints, play a role in clinician decisions for canine atopic dermatitis: spectrum of care in a chronic and relapsing disease. We will review barriers to care, care burden clients experience when managing dermatologic conditions in their pets, spectrum of care dermatology, as well as strategies that can be used in veterinary medicine aligned with the human dermatology field to manage costs with good outcomes. There will be 10-15 minutes of the session where attendees will ask the panelists questions related to the topic.

courses.title: Expert Panel Review of Musculoskeletal Adverse Events associated with Librela(TM) (bedinvetmab injection)
courses.description: This presentation summarizes findings from an independent, external, multidisciplinary panel of veterinary specialists, published in the Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association (JAVMA). The panel reviewed the past five years of adverse events reported in association with the administration of Librela with a goal to describe any consistent patterns of clinical-radiographic signs of musculoskeletal adverse events reported in a small subset of dogs receiving bedinvetmab for osteoarthritis (OA)-associated pain.

courses.provider: MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE
courses.title: Practice with Confidence: Leveling Up Veterinary Teams
courses.description: Practice with Confidence: Leveling Up Veterinary Teams is a collaborative CE experience designed to help veterinary professionals strengthen team utilization, improve workflow efficiency, and practice with greater confidence through a clearer understanding of licensure and scope of practice. Bringing together veterinarians, veterinary nurses, and team members for a shared learning experience, the program focuses on practical, real-world knowledge and strategies that empower individuals to work to their full potential and practice to the full extent of their license. Through sessions focused on delegation, leadership communication, risk management, workforce sustainability, and emerging animal health threats, participants will explore evidence-based approaches to optimizing team performance while maintaining high standards of patient care. Participants will leave with actionable tools and follow-up opportunities to support long-term implementation and success.

courses.title: Hands-On, Ears Up: Mastering the Physical Exam in Exotic Companion Mammals
courses.description: Physical exams can be your most powerful diagnostic tool, if you know what to look for. This session focuses on refining your approach to exotic mammals, with tips for minimizing stress, recognizing subtle abnormalities, and adapting techniques for various species.

courses.title: Urgent or emergent
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian with practical information on the current thoughts on the initial management of patients that require either urgent or emergent care. Dr's Lee and Hackett will discuss their approach to deciding on the initial management of these patients along with deciding when to transfer to emergency care

courses.title: Hyaluronic Acid in Practice: A Veterinary Dental Case Round Table LIVE
courses.description:
This is a case-based round table exploring the use of hyaluronic acid as an adjunct to a variety of dental and oral procedures.
Through a series of canine and feline cases, our panelists will share their clinical experiences using hyaluronic acid alongside established dental treatments, including closed root planing, gingival curettage, bone grafting, guided tissue regeneration, and full-mouth extractions. Cases will highlight applications involving advanced periodontal disease, furcational bone loss, feline chronic gingivostomatitis, and significant oral inflammation.
Participants will see how hyaluronic acid has been incorporated into treatment plans to support soft-tissue healing, manage local inflammation, promote periodontal and alveolar bone regeneration, and, in select cases, help preserve teeth that may otherwise have required extraction.
This interactive discussion will go beyond the theory and into the clinical decision-making behind each case, including patient selection, treatment techniques, outcomes, and practical considerations for incorporating hyaluronic acid into veterinary dental procedures.

courses.title: Comparative Speed of Kill of the Lone Star Tick (Amblyomma americanum)
courses.description: This presentation considers the importance of speed of tick kill to safeguard pets against tick-borne diseases and protect the human-animal bond. Tick-borne disease transmission and the unique characteristics and geographical expansion of Amblyomma americanum (lone star tick) will be reviewed. Details of a recent study on A. americanum comparing the relative immediate and residual speed of tick kill following administration of three monthly-use isoxazoline-containing products will be discussed, including methodology and key study findings. This new data will be utilized to highlight the importance of rapid and consistent speed of tick kill.

courses.title: UROGENITAL SURGERY
courses.description: Let Dr. Berg help you eliminate the stress with your veterinary surgery cases by providing a blueprint for success. Feel at ease with each and every procedure by incorporating the lessons, tips and tricks learned in this course.

courses.title: Zennovation in Sedation: Rethinking What is Possible
courses.description: In this educational presentation, we will discuss sedation in dogs. The foundation will be set by reviewing the basic physiology behind commonly used sedatives in dogs. We will discuss the most commonly used sedatives and reversal agents, and introduce the novel sedative Zenalpha (medetomidine and vatinoxan hydrochlorides).

courses.provider: ACCESS SPECIALTY ANIMAL HOSPITAL PALM BEACH COUNTY
courses.title: Introduction to Interventional Radiology
courses.description: This course offers a concise review of key interventional radiology procedures and their indications. Topics include tracheal, nasopharyngeal, urethral, and ureteral stenting (including SUBS), treatment of intrahepatic shunts, and percutaneous laser disc ablation. Post-procedure care and complication management are also covered.
courses.location: ACCESS Specialty Animal Hospital Palm Beach County

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Dentistry Faux Pas
courses.description: The second hour of our eight-part series will review dentistry faux pas that practitioners commonly encounter. Participants will learn how to distinguish normal radiographic anatomy from pathology, properly diagnose and close an oronasal fistula, and perform extractions of the canine tooth and maxillary fourth premolar while avoiding common mistakes. The discussion will also cover the causes and treatment options for feline chronic gingivostomatitis, equipping clinicians with strategies for one of the more challenging conditions in feline dentistry.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Feline & Canine How To - Extraction Lab Focused
courses.description: This two-hour discussion (of our eight-part series) will walk attendees through the principles and practical steps of performing extractions in both feline and canine patients. The feline portion begins with a review of surgical fundamentals, including proper suture selection, knot placement, and spacing, before moving into the instruments best suited for feline dentistry such as elevators, periosteal elevators, burs, and root tip picks. A step-by-step guide will cover how to approach full-mouth extractions when indicated, with an emphasis on recognizing and preventing potential complications. High-quality video demonstrations will provide a clear visual of techniques for several types of feline extractions. The canine portion builds on these same principles, with discussion of the specialized equipment required for canine extractions and a focused look at more advanced procedures, including extraction of the canine teeth and maxillary fourth premolars. Throughout, the session emphasizes efficiency, precision, and patient safety, ensuring that participants leave with a solid foundation to approach complex extractions in practice.

courses.title: Updating Your Ocular Surgery Techniques.
courses.description: This program will review the ophthalmic surgical procedures that can be performed by a general practitioner or an emergency clinician. Each procedure will be discussed in detail and time will then be given to perform them on cadaver pig eyes. This will be a lecture plus wetlab

courses.title: CKD: Therapy Beyond Diet and Fluids
courses.description: The goal of this one-hour CE course is to review chronic kidney disease therapeutic options, outside of diet and fluids. IRIS diagnosis and staging will briefly be reviewed, as well common treatments for symptoms of kidney disease for both dogs and cats, including hypertension, proteinuria, and gastrointestinal signs. The main advantages and disadvantages of renal diets will also be summarized. The focus will then turn to the gut kidney axis and dysbiosis that occurs in chronic renal failure and the possible benefit of probiotics to support kidney health. The importance of phosphate management in chronic kidney disease will be described and research presented on the longevity of patients and phosphate target levels. Attendees will learn how to incorporate FGF-23 testing for improved phosphate control in feline patients. Different phosphate binding options, beyond renal diets, will be discussed. Hypokalemia management will also be presented.

courses.title: (LIVE COURSE) Updates in The Diagnosis and Management of Sepsis
courses.description: This 3-week online course covers current approaches to recognising and managing severe systemic illness and sepsis in dogs and cats. We will move from the initial systemic inflammatory response through septic shock and into multiple organ dysfunction. Each week addresses practical diagnostics, fluid and vasopressor therapy, antimicrobial selection, and organ-specific support. This course is ideal for anyone seeing patients with severe illness, and provides a sound, evidence-based approach to patient management based on the very latest literature - all designed to optimise patient outcome.

courses.title: Innovate with Intention 2026 Virtual Conference
courses.description: This year's conference offers more than 49 hours of RACE-eligible CE content across medical and non-medical categories. Medical sessions cover evidence-based clinical topics including pharmacology and analgesic protocols for dogs, cats, exotic companion animals, birds, and small mammals; palliative nutrition for patients with kidney and gastrointestinal disease; physical rehabilitation and therapeutic exercise for geriatric and hospice patients; management of endocrinopathies, respiratory conditions, and degenerative disease at end of life; cannabinoid therapy; rational NSAID use; and the latest research in euthanasia protocols and decision-making. Non-medical sessions address professional development, practice management, and professional wellness topics including communication strategies for end-of-life conversations, cultural competency, grief theory and bereavement support, ethics, technician career pathways, practice management and workflow systems, and mental health for veterinary professionals.

courses.title: Intro to TPLO
courses.description: TPLO has become a favorite technique of general and specialty veterinarians to treat CrCL tears in all sizes of dogs. TPLO stabilizes the stifle by eliminating cranial tibial thrust. TPLO is an excellent technique for treating partial and complete tears of the CrCL. This interactive course includes lectures and laboratories to teach participants the theory and method of tibial plateau leveling osteotomy TPLO. Participants will perform TPLOs on plastic bones and cadavers using state of the art equipment and implants. Participants will use locking plate technology to simplify increase precision and reduce complications of the procedure. Participants should have a basic knowledge of anatomy and surgical approach to the stifle and principles of bone plate application. Postoperative radiographs will be taken to assess the participants' repair technique. Postoperative management will also be discussed.

courses.title: Hands-On, Ears Up: Mastering the Physical Exam in Exotic Companion Mammals
courses.description: Physical exams can be your most powerful diagnostic tool, if you know what to look for. This session focuses on refining your approach to exotic mammals, with tips for minimizing stress, recognizing subtle abnormalities, and adapting techniques for various species.

courses.provider: FISH HEALTH SECTION, AMERICAN FISHERIES SOCIETY
courses.title: ISAAH 2026 - Fish Nutrition Workshop
courses.description: The continuing education program "Fundamentals of Nutrition: Better Feeds for Healthier Fish" will offer veterinary and fish health professionals a working knowledge of fish nutrition and guidance for achieving better outcomes in the field. The workshop will cover core nutritional principles, common nutritional diseases, interactions between nutrition and infectious diseases, and practical strategies for improving fish health and performance.

courses.title: Itching for the truth - the ins and outs of how to choose the best management plan for your environmentally allergic dogs
courses.description:
1. Program Description (Abstract Overview): In this session with Dr. Julia, we will cover the ins and outs of managing canine allergies. From topical products to which oral or injectable is best for your patient to when to consider immunotherapy, you will leave this session confident in your approach to the ever-so-common atopic dog.
2. Learning Objectives:
a. Recognize when topical therapy is beneficial and be able to council owners on how to use it effectively
b. List all of the available treatments for canine atopy and why/when to use each
c. Create a comprehensive treatment plan for environmentally allergic dogs
d. Develop a streamlined approach to these cases including handouts and communication tid bits

courses.title: Ocular Emergencies (OPHT206)
courses.description: In this course, we will discuss how to tackle the dreaded red eye that shows up on the emergency schedule and much more. Topics covered will include the most common ophthalmic emergencies in veterinary practice, how to triage them, treatment and management options available, and what to tell the owner in a crisis.

courses.provider: THE WORLD SMALL ANIMAL VETERINARY ASSOCIATION (WSAVA)
courses.title: 51st World Small Animal Veterinary Association Congress
courses.description: The WSAVA-PSAVA-FECAVA World Congress will take place in Warsaw, Poland, from 13 to 15 October 2026. The event will unite the WSAVA World Congress, the PSAVA Congress, and the FECAVA European Congress, offering an international scientific program focused on companion animal health and welfare. The congress will feature expert-led lectures, professional development opportunities, and networking among veterinary professionals from around the world.

courses.title: Management of Common Anesthesia Complications (part 1 of 2)
courses.description: Anesthetic complications are common, predictable, and often caused by the very drugs used to provide safe anesthesia. This lecture reviews the most frequent peri-anesthetic complications, including hypotension and bradycardia, and provides practical, case-based strategies to recognize them, understand their physiologic causes, and intervene effectively to support safer outcomes from induction through recovery.

courses.title: There's No Such Thing as Just Behavior
courses.description: There's No Such Thing as "Just Behavior" explores the critical connection between physical health and behavior, challenging the assumption that behavior problems exist in isolation. Using current research and real-world case studies, Dr. Lisa Radosta demonstrates how gastrointestinal, dermatologic, and endocrine disease can contribute to changes in behavior and how recognizing these underlying medical conditions can lead to more successful patient outcomes. Participants will also learn practical strategies for discussing the relationship between medical and behavioral health with clients, helping them understand why a comprehensive diagnostic approach is essential to effective Fear Free care.

courses.title: Techniques for Managing Behavior in the Treatment area
courses.description: Fear Free doesn't stop at the exam room door. In this session designed for the entire veterinary team, we'll explore what it takes to manage fear, anxiety, and stress in the treatment area -- from reading stress signals and building a calmer environment, to creating team workflows that keep patients at the lowest possible FAS throughout their visit. With real-world examples, attendees will leave with practical tools and a shared framework for advocating for patient emotional health at every step of the back-of-house experience.

courses.title: Upper Airway Complications and Revisions-On-Demand
courses.description: This seminar provides brief discussions on how to best prevent, minimize, and/or address complications arising from a variety of upper airway conditions and optimize patient outcomes.

courses.title: Selecting Therapeutic Diets for GI and Skin Disease: An Iterative Approach to Nutritional Management
courses.description: This course reviews the nutritional strategies available for common GI and skin disorders and provides practical guidance on when and how to use them. Participants will learn how to obtain a diet history, perform a nutritional assessment, and use this information to guide diet selection. The course emphasizes an iterative approach to dietary management, helping clinicians evaluate patient response and fine-tune nutrition plans to achieve optimal outcomes.

courses.provider: FISH HEALTH SECTION, AMERICAN FISHERIES SOCIETY
courses.title: ISAAH 2026 - Fish Pathology Workshop
courses.description: The Fish Pathology Workshop will take place, in conjunction with the 10th ISAAH, on Monday September 21 2026 at The Noatun laboratory building is a new, modern laboratory facility at the Bodo campus of Nord University. Lectures and laboratories will be delivered by Dr. David Groman Section Head of the Aquatic Diagnostic Services at the Atlantic Veterinary College in Prince Edward Island, Canada, Dr. Jeff Wolf Senior Pathologist from Experimental Pathology Laboratories, Inc. (EPL) located in Sterling, Virginia, USA, and Dr. Ginevra Brocca Fish Pathology Consultant from Glasgow (UK). The workshop is designed for entry and midlevel fish health researchers and workers, as well as students. Demonstrations on diagnostic necropsy protocol with reference to diagnostic lab submissions will be the focus in the morning, using Atlantic salmon and Wolffish specimens. The afternoon session will include sessions on Zebrafish histo-anatomy and physiology as well as case studies of unusual Atlantic salmon and Wolffish pathologies. Scanned slides of diagnostically interesting cases will be available for participants to follow during afternoon lectures and as such participants are encouraged to bring laptops.

courses.title: What's the deal with pre- and pro-biotics? How nutrition can influence the treatment of gastrointestinal disease
courses.description: This lecture will describe the nutritional management of patients with chronic and acute gastrointestinal symptoms. Nutritional assessment of patients will be discussed. There will be discussion of the wide range of commercially available gastrointestinal diets and their applications. There will also be a focus on fibre classification, prebiotic vs non-fermentable fibres, and their adjunctive use in gastrointestinal disease. Finally, there will be a discussion on the different varieties of probiotics available and when they are best used in the treatment of gastrointestinal disease.

courses.title: Pet Insurance Misconceptions
courses.description:
Pet insurance has never been more relevant to veterinary practice - yet misconceptions about how it works continue
to create friction at the exam table and erode client trust. This session addresses the most common myths veterinary
professionals encounter, from beliefs about pre-existing condition exclusions and claim complexity to the idea that pet
insurance "never pays out." Drawing on nearly two decades of veterinary medicine experience and six years inside a
leading pet insurance company, speaker Britni Bardin offers a perspective on where the industry falls short in
communicating its value, and how veterinary teams can guide clients toward coverage decisions that serve their pets.
Attendees will leave with a practical understanding of how pet insurance policies work, what to look for when
comparing plans, and how to have more confident, accurate conversations with clients about coverage.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF LABORATORY ANIMAL MEDICINE
courses.title: Building A Culture of Care Through a Formal Global Strategy
courses.description: In 2023, Comparative Medicine initiated a strategy to build an active and robust Culture of Care at all US Pfizer sites conducting animal research. It consists of three pillars: intentional, consistent progress in animal care and welfare while maintaining study quality, colleague care and wellbeing, and openness and transparency internally and with the public. This presentation will include how activities and goals under each pillar were prioritized and resourced over the past three years as well as how we utilize tools such as formal colleague surveys to gauge our progress in building our Culture of Care.

courses.title: The Definitive Veterinary Extraction Protocol
courses.description: The Definitive Veterinary Extraction Protocol is an in-depth, evidence-based surgical training program designed to elevate the standard of veterinary dental extractions. Through over 8 hours of comprehensive instruction, Dr. Brett Beckman guides participants through diagnosis, extraction prevention, simple and surgical extractions, multi-rooted teeth, feline dentistry, regional anesthesia, tooth resorption, complication management, and practice efficiency. Featuring real clinical cases, radiographic interpretation, step-by-step surgical demonstrations, and practical techniques that can be implemented immediately, this course provides veterinarians with the knowledge and confidence to perform safer, more predictable extractions while improving patient outcomes and practice success.

courses.title: Held Together by Heroes: Redesigning Inventory, Compliance, and Technology in the Veterinary Hospital
courses.description: Held Together by Heroes: Redesigning Inventory, Compliance, and Technology in the Veterinary Hospital is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Feeding Management for Pets with Kidney Disease
courses.description:
This lecture will discuss feeding management and strategies for pets with kidney disease. Attendees will learn how to compare products on the market to make the
best choice for their patient to help slow the progression of the disease and keep pets feeling well for as long as possible. Technicians should be familiar with the specific nutrient modifications in a renal-friendly diet so that information can be shared with clients. Being able to educate clients that food is the medicine for pets with renal disease will help clients feel better about feeding the recommended diet and sticking to the recommended treatment plan. Feeding management tips and tricks will also be covered. Pets with renal disease often have selective appetite, and different feeding management strategies need to be used to help keep pets eating
the proper diet will be shared. A discussion on various ingredients in the diets will also be covered. When technicians remember that pets do not need ingredients, they need nutrients, they can better educate their clients on why a specific diet was selected.

courses.title: A Picture Is Worth 1,000 Words
courses.description: A Picture Is Worth 1,000 Words is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Oh Sew Easy! Understanding Suture Materials (TECH463)
courses.description: Suture selection is a crucial and integral factor to ensuring successful surgical outcomes. Suture materials are considered surgical implants because they remain inside in the patient's body upon discharge. Suture material choices must be based on the anticipated wound healing times and tissue types as well as considerations unique to each patient. Using the wrong suture material may lead to unintended consequences such as wound dehiscence, abscess formation or tissue reaction. This session will enable veterinary technicians to understand the basis for suture material selection and usage.

courses.title: Reducing Burnout in Veterinary Medicine: Practical Strategies for Sustainable Wellbeing
courses.description:
Burnout remains one of the most significant wellbeing challenges facing veterinary care providers, affecting one-third to one-half of individuals working in the profession. While burnout is often discussed as an individual struggle, research increasingly recognizes it as a complex workplace phenomenon influenced by factors such as workload, psychological safety, team culture, autonomy, and organizational practices. Addressing burnout requires more than individual resilience; it requires meaningful strategies at both the personal and organizational levels.
In this 1-hour webinar, participants will explore the current evidence on burnout in veterinary medicine and examine the contributing factors that influence wellbeing in clinical practice. Through a practical, solutions-focused approach, attendees will learn strategies that veterinary professionals can implement to support their own wellbeing, as well as approaches that leaders and organizations can use to create healthier, more sustainable workplaces.
Participants will leave with actionable tools to reduce burnout risk, strengthen protective factors, and foster a culture where veterinary teams can thrive while continuing to provide compassionate care.

courses.title: Equine Distal Interphalangeal Joint ArthrodesisOn-Demand
courses.description: This hybrid laboratory discusses an open dorsal approach to the distal interphalangeal joint, debride the articular cartilage, and prepare the dorsal surface of the middle phalanx and the dorsal proximal surface of the distal phalanx for application of a custom arthrodesis plate. Under radiographic guidance, the plate will be applied along with transarticular screws in lag fashion. The custom designed plate will be applied through a single skin incision without penetration of the hoof wall.

courses.title: VetQuest Anesthesia, Dentistry & Oral Surgery
courses.description: These lectures will be over 3 days and cover topics related to anesthesia, dentistry & oral surgery in small animals.

courses.title: 2026 Surgery Summit
courses.description: The American College of Veterinary Surgeons (ACVS) defines the standards of veterinary surgical excellence, promotes advancements in veterinary surgery, and provides surgery continuing education programs. The ACVS Surgery Summit features seminars focused on all areas of patient care, from diagnosis, pain management and anesthesia, to surgery, postoperative care, and rehabilitation. The entire practice team can gain invaluable skills and exceptional continuing education.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Current & Future Perspectives on Management of Large Open Wounds
courses.description:
Treating large equine skin wounds remains a significant challenge in veterinary practice, especially when primary closure is not possible and healing must occur by second intention. With a wide array of potential management strategies and a growing number of novel treatments the decision making process can be complex and case dependent.
In this discussion, the expert panel will share their approaches and case experiences in managing large open wounds and burns. The session will explore the current evidence behind treatment protocols and foster debate around emerging therapies and future directions in equine wound management. The panel will be sharing interesting cases, and the many practical tips and tricks they have picked up along the way
Discussion topics will include a range of treatment options such as LASER therapy, infrared and red monochromatic light, medical-grade honey, strategies for managing biofilms, cell therapy, platelet-rich plasma, and biological dressings

courses.title: Chrysalis
courses.description: Non-Clinical junior and intermediate leader development program held over 12-14 months. Starting with 4 days of face to face training in a residential style followed by either a) 11 months of monthly face to face webinars (90 minutes each) for corporate veterinary groups, or 12 x monthly webinars called "Sprints" (90 minutes) for non corporate veterinary groups.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Endometritis and Biofilms Breaking Down Barriers to Treatment
courses.description: Endometritis remains a major cause of subfertility in mares, particularly as they age, with diagnosis and treatment often complicated by the presence of biofilms and the varying forms of the disease. This panel brings together leading experts to explore novel approaches managing mares with biofilm associated endometritis. This discussion will focus heavily on the population of mares that biofilms affect, current and future diagnostic tests, and the current best treatments for restoring fertility in these mares. Join this interactive session to stay at the leading edge of understanding of endometritis pathophysiology and learn how advances in diagnostics and therapeutics are helping to overcome barriers to effective management.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Subclinical Laminitis Shedding Light on an Under-Diagnosed Condition
courses.description:
Subclinical laminitis may be underdiagnosed compared with the more well-recognised form of laminitis, with acute onset of clinical signs. Subclinical laminitis is typically insidious in onset and can contribute to poor performance, bilaterally shortened forelimb step length or loss of extravagance of forelimb movement. Unrecognised subclinical laminitis may precede apparent acute-onset laminitis.
This international and world-leading group will discuss and debate the impact of subclinical laminitis, the horses at risk, how they approach the investigation of these cases, and the imaging findings that may indicate the presence of laminar pathology. They will share their experiences of managing this condition, and how they address challenging presentations or situations.

courses.title: Performance Challenges Series The Dressage Horse
courses.description: An international panel will explore and debate the distinct performance demands of dressage horses from amateur to elite The panel will discuss common musculoskeletal training and management issues alongside strategies for injury prevention rehabilitation and long term soundness Through evidence based debate and a wealth of case driven insights, this hand picked group of experts will share practical approaches to optimize both performance and welfare in this discipline

courses.title: Managing common surgical problems in practice
courses.description: This seminar has been designed to provide the attending veterinarian with practical information on the current thoughts on the diagnosis and management of dogs and cats that present with a problem that will require surgery. Dr. Coleman will discuss her approach to management of many different surgical problems. Upon completion of the seminar, attendees will have gained a greater understanding of the current methods of management available for their patients.

courses.provider: SHREIBER SCHOOL OF VETERINARY MEDICINE OF ROWAN UNIVERSITY
courses.title: When They Can't Just Shake It Off: A Practical Approach to Status Epilepticus and Cluster Seizures in Dogs
courses.description: What do you do when a dog's seizures will not stop? Status epilepticus in dogs (continuous seizure activity of greater than 5 minutes or greater than 2 generalized seizures without recovery of consciousness) is one of the most challenging neurological emergencies veterinarians encounter. Recent advances in our understanding of the mechanisms underlying prolonged seizure activity have challenged traditional approaches and reshaped treatment protocols. This practical talk will discuss how to prevent and treat cluster seizures and status epilepticus in dogs.

courses.provider: AMERICAN COLLEGE OF LABORATORY ANIMAL MEDICINE
courses.title: Anesthesia and Analgesia of Laboratory Fish
courses.description:
This session will focus on anesthesia and analgesia of laboratory fish. Included in this session is discussion of species-specific anatomical, physiologic, and behavioral considerations as it relates to the anesthetic event and pain management. Available health and welfare monitoring tools and different types of analgesic drugs and techniques will be covered. Learning objectives include:
-Review fish-specific considerations for anesthesia provision.
-Discuss available methods and protocols for anesthesia.
-Discuss available methods for assessing pain.
-Determine analgesia protocols for management of pain.
After completing this webinar, participants will have had the opportunity to refine species-specific knowledge, to advance understanding of animal assessment, and to enhance the quality and safety of fish anesthesia and pain management

courses.title: Diamonds in the Ruff
courses.description:
Those of us in the veterinary profession constantly find ourselves under significant pressure from self and others. The effect of that stress can either be unfortunate or of value to us. Like Diamonds, the stress that we endure can aid us in developing into brilliant and valuable caregivers.
This conversation goes over the 4 C's of being in the veterinary profession and how to use them to shine and succeed in practice.

courses.title: Is it Neoplasia or Not? The oncology world from the clinical sonographer's perspective.
courses.description: Online attendees of this course should expect to learn their imaging responsibilities and expectations regarding a local vs. a multi-centric clinical presentation. What is overtly surgical, potentially surgical, or non-surgical. What meets neoplastic criteria, diagnostic sampling vs. surgical intervention, and sampling types depending on clinical presentations; FNA for cytological pathology and core biopsy for structural pathology.

courses.title: Mobility, Obesity and Pain
courses.description:
Learners will understand the role of obesity on its role in pain management and mobility.
Program Agenda:
Highlight clinical pain assessment
Role of cytokines with pain and joint health and changes that occur with obesity.
Highlight means to address nutritional aspects of obesity and the role of the veterinary team.
Learning Objectives:
Understand pain assessment
Clinical approach to pain exam.
Role of cytokines in obesity and pain
Nutritional options for obesity

courses.title: Human Grade Pet Food: Understanding the Highest Standard for Integrity, Quality, and Food Safety
courses.description:
Pet owners are increasingly seeking "Human Grade" diets for
their pets, but what does this claim actually mean? Is it simply a marketing term, or does it represent a
meaningful difference in ingredient quality, manufacturing, and food safety?
This presentation explores the regulatory definition of Human Grade Pet Food and the rigorous standards
required to legally make this claim. Attendees will learn how Human Grade products differ from conventional
pet foods in ingredient sourcing, manufacturing practices, facility requirements, documentation, and regulatory
oversight. The seminar will also examine why quality systems-including supplier qualification, sanitation,
traceability, preventive controls, and testing-play a critical role in ensuring product integrity.
Rather than focusing solely on nutrition, this session provides veterinarians with a behind-the-scenes look at
how pet food is produced and why manufacturing standards matter when evaluating food quality. Participants
will leave with a practical framework for interpreting Human Grade claims and confidently discussing ingredient
quality and food safety with clients.

courses.title: Certified Equine Ergonomist Program (CEE)
courses.description: The Certified Equine Ergonomist (CEE) program, hosted by Saddlefit 4 Life, is an advanced 60-hour continuing education curriculum designed specifically for veterinarians and credentialed veterinary technicians. Delivered through 40 hours of self-paced digital theory, incorporating interactive modules, graded quizzes, and reviewed coursework, and 20 hours of hands-on field case studies, this program provides an evidence-based framework for evaluating the biomechanical and pathological impacts of saddle fit on the ridden horse. Attendees gain clinical expertise in diagnosing tack-induced musculoskeletal restrictions, localized tissue inflammation, and secondary gait compensations. The curriculum covers equine functional anatomy, top-line quantitative measurements, anatomical mapping of 14 key reflex points, and standardized diagnostic tools such as Dr. Sue Dyson's Ridden Horse Pain Ethogram. Participants master a step-by-step 80-Point Saddle Fit Diagnostic Framework across static standing and dynamic movement assessments. During the practical externship, each submitted case study receives individualized feedback from experienced evaluators, culminating in a comprehensive final review led by program founder and German Certified Master Saddler Jochen Schleese before participants graduate with their CEE certification.

courses.provider: INTERNATIONAL SOCIETY FOR COMPANION ANIMAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE
courses.title: Companion Animal Antimicrobial Stewardship and Infection Control 2026-2027 Seminar Series
courses.description: This seminar series provides ten (10) approximately monthly, one (1) hour-long seminars led by an expert in the field of veterinary antimicrobial stewardship and/or infection prevention and control over the course of eleven (11) months beginning in September 2026 and concluding in July 2027. Participants are not required to attend every seminar and can attend seminars of interest, earning credit for only the seminars attended. Seminars deliver clinically relevant information and cutting-edge research updates on topics surrounding antimicrobial resistance, antimicrobial stewardship, and infection control within companion animals. Seminars are designed to support the implementation and expansion of antimicrobial stewardship and infection control programs within general practice and specialty veterinary hospitals.

courses.title: Beyond the Scratch: The Real Story Behind Itchy Patients
courses.description: LIVE Panel Discussion CE program focused on the role of nutrition in dermatology. We will discuss ways to incorporate nutrition in the multimodal management of pruritus and atopic skin disease. Gain further insight on the intersection of the immune and gastrointestinal systems and the importance in balancing the gut flora.

courses.title: 2026 AETA - CETA/ACTE Joint Annual Convention
courses.description: The AETA & CETA/ACTE 2026 Joint Convention aims to present a unified voice for those involved in the embryo transfer industry in the promotion of mutual interests and objectives, provide continuing education and information regarding current issues in the embryo transfer industry for members. The American Embryo Transfer Association embraces its responsibility as the resource for embryo transfer in the United States. This authority is developed and supported through our commitment to excellence in several broad areas: education and standards of quality.
courses.location: Monona Terrace Community and Convention Center

courses.title: A Pain in the Gut: A Discussion on Managing Chronic Canine Enteropathies
courses.description: This course will discuss and review primary enteropathies in the canine patient. Specifically, we will review pathophysiology/ predisposing conditions and diagnosis. Furthermore, while focusing on common comorbidities, developing an appropriate nutritional support based on the individual patient will be discussed. An emphasis is also placed on client communication throughout the entirety of the lecture.

courses.title: Management 1: Essentials
courses.description: This course provides comprehensive training in essential management skills, designed for those pursuing the AALAS Certified Manager of Animal Resources (CMAR) certification and preparing for the M1 exam, as well as anyone looking to enhance their foundational management skills. Participants will gain a deep understanding of effective management practices, team dynamics, communication strategies, change management, individual differences, and conflict resolution. Key topics include: - Identifying the core functions and roles of exceptional managers - Understanding the development and management of groups and teams - Enhancing communication skills and overcoming communication barriers - Applying strategies to manage organizational change and stress - Leveraging individual differences and emotional intelligence for improved performance - Developing conflict management and negotiation skills Participants will explore practical applications of these concepts, preparing them for both the M1 certification exam and real-world managerial challenges.

courses.title: June 2026
courses.description: All VetFolio courses within this packet are comprised of webinars, certificate courses, journal articles and podcasts that are created by the NAVC and VetFolio for on-demand education.

courses.title: Confident Conversations: Communication Strategies for Increasing Trust and Wellness Compliance
courses.description: Helping clients understand the value of preventive care isn't always easy. Questions about vaccines, parasite prevention, and other wellness recommendations can lead to difficult conversations that leave veterinary professionals feeling discouraged. Join Dr. Donnelly as she shares practical approaches for navigating these everyday communication challenges. Using real-world wellness appointment scenarios, attendees will learn how to help clients feel heard, respond to concerns with empathy, and communicate recommendations in ways that foster trust and improve compliance.

courses.title: Beef Cattle Carcass Ultrasound Scanning and Image Interpretation
courses.description: This three-day program trains veterinarians and field technicians to collect and interpret ultrasound images used in beef cattle genetic evaluation. The program is offered to two audiences: (1) veterinarians who wish to add carcass ultrasound scanning and image interpretation as a diagnostic-imaging service they can offer to cattle-producing clients, building on their existing training in anatomy, physiology, and diagnostic imaging; and (2) non-veterinarian field technicians who perform this scanning role directly for breed associations and processing labs.
