By the end of this session, attendees will be equipped to implement safer radiographic protocols, make informed equipment decisions, and consistently produce diagnostic dental radiographs in practice.

courses.provider: MIDWEST ANESTHESIA CONSULTING VETERINARY SERVICES LLC
courses.title: Understanding the 5th Vital Sign: Pain Physiology & Pharmacology
courses.description: Pain is a complicated physiologic process that is difficult for many veterinary professionals to understand on both the microscopic (e.g. mechanistic pathways) and macroscopic (e.g. outward or physical indications of pain) levels. This lecture will walk through the basics of pain physiology and analgesic pharmacology as it applies to small animal veterinary professionals. The mechanisms and application of certain analgesic agents will be the main focus of the lecture, rather than specific analgesic protocols.

courses.title: Start Smart - Understanding & Preparing for a Veterinarian of Record Relationship (On Demand)
courses.description:
This program introduces the veterinarian of record (VOR) relationship in the context of animal shelters and animal welfare organizations. Participants will explore the purpose and value of establishing a veterinary partnership, the roles and responsibilities of both veterinarians and shelter leadership, and factors that contribute to an effective working relationship.
For veterinarians, the program will address the veterinarian-client-patient relationship (VCPR) within a shelter setting, differences between shelter medicine and traditional private practice, and considerations for determining interest and capacity to serve an animal welfare organization. Participants will also examine characteristics to consider when evaluating a potential shelter partner.
For shelter and animal welfare leaders, the program will provide guidance for identifying their organization's veterinary needs, distinguishing between a veterinarian-of-record arrangement and a more comprehensive veterinary partnership, and assessing organizational readiness to work effectively with a veterinarian.
Through discussion of expectations, capacity, communication, and partnership structure, participants will develop a framework for evaluating potential veterinarian-shelter partnerships and identifying appropriate next steps toward establishing or formalizing a veterinarian of record relationship.

courses.title: Start Smart - Understanding & Preparing for a Veterinarian of Record Relationship (LIVE)
courses.description:
This program introduces the veterinarian of record (VOR) relationship in the context of animal shelters and animal welfare organizations. Participants will explore the purpose and value of establishing a veterinary partnership, the roles and responsibilities of both veterinarians and shelter leadership, and factors that contribute to an effective working relationship.
For veterinarians, the program will address the veterinarian-client-patient relationship (VCPR) within a shelter setting, differences between shelter medicine and traditional private practice, and considerations for determining interest and capacity to serve an animal welfare organization. Participants will also examine characteristics to consider when evaluating a potential shelter partner.
For shelter and animal welfare leaders, the program will provide guidance for identifying their organization's veterinary needs, distinguishing between a veterinarian-of-record arrangement and a more comprehensive veterinary partnership, and assessing organizational readiness to work effectively with a veterinarian.
Through discussion of expectations, capacity, communication, and partnership structure, participants will develop a framework for evaluating potential veterinarian-shelter partnerships and identifying appropriate next steps toward establishing or formalizing a veterinarian of record relationship.

courses.title: A Gut Feeling: Understanding Liver Abscesses in Beef x Dairy Cattle
courses.description: Liver abscesses are an important challenge in beef x dairy cattle, with reported prevalence exceeding 50% in some populations and occurring at substantially higher rates than in native beef cattle. But why are beef x dairy animals seemingly more susceptible and what can be done to reduce the risk? This webinar will explore the connection between gut health and liver abscess development, including how damage and disruptions to the gastrointestinal epithelium can allow Fusobacterium necrophorum and other bacteria to enter the portal circulation and reach the liver. The presenter will examine current industry trends and the growing importance of liver abscesses in beef x dairy production, including their potential impact on animal performance, carcass value, and profitability.

courses.title: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Wound Management
courses.description: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Wound Management is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Wound Management
courses.description: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Wound Management is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.title: Diagnosis and Management of Degenerative Mitral Valve Disease in Your Practice
courses.description: This session will discuss the approach to management of a small breed, older dog presenting with a heart murmur. In addition, there will be a review of how thoracic radiographs can be used to help stage a patient within the current ACVIM staging for degenerative mitral valve disease

courses.title: Confident Conversations: Communication Strategies for Increasing Trust and Wellness Compliance
courses.description: Helping clients understand the value of preventive care isn't always easy. Questions about vaccines, parasite prevention, and other wellness recommendations can lead to difficult conversations that leave veterinary professionals feeling discouraged. Join Dr. Donnelly as she shares practical approaches for navigating these everyday communication challenges. Using real-world wellness appointment scenarios, attendees will learn how to help clients feel heard, respond to concerns with empathy, and communicate recommendations in ways that foster trust and improve compliance.

courses.title: Shaping the Diagnosis Series: Differential Decoded
courses.description: Automated hematology analyzers provide powerful quantitative data, but important diagnostic insights can be missed when blood morphology is not assessed. This presentation explores the clinical value of blood morphology assessment as a complement to automated CBC results. Through one canine case study, participants will examine how morphology findings altered diagnostic pathways, improved interpretation of laboratory data, and influenced patient management. Practical guidance will be provided on when morphology review is most important and how morphology findings can be integrated into everyday clinical decision-making.

courses.title: Fetch Encore - NAVLE - Preparation, Placement & Professional Growth For the Vet Student and New Grad
courses.description:
Passing the NAVLE is one thing but being ready for real practice is another! This Fetch Encore virtual symposium focuses on the professional skills veterinary students and veterinary technician students need but rarely get taught:
Start making stronger calls with case-based learning, including:
- Managing the transition into practice
- Testing strategies
- Clinical reasoning
Expect honest conversations about confidence, imposter syndrome, and how to think like a doctor under pressure.

courses.title: Whats that Sound? Approach to Puppies and Kittens with a Heart Murmur
courses.description: Heart murmurs are commonly detected during routine exams in young dogs and cats yet determining whether a murmur is innocent or pathologic can be challenging. This session will present a practical approach to evaluating murmurs in puppies and kittens, with emphasis on differentiating normal from abnormal findings using auscultation, physical exam, and breed-specific predispositions. Learn how to apply diagnostic tools such as thoracic radiographs, NT-proBNP, point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), and echocardiography to guide next steps. Special consideration will be given to congenital heart disease in both species, including when advanced imaging or referral is warranted.

courses.title: Avoiding Mishaps: Selecting and Preparing Anesthetic Equipment
courses.description: This 1-hour presentation focuses on selecting the patient breathing circuit and setting up the anesthetic machine in preparation for a procedure. Learn how to perform appropriate anesthetic machine check out procedures to ensure equipment is assembled correctly and functional before applying to a patient.

courses.title: Everything But the Kitchen Sink, Utilizing All Parts of the Anesthetic Protocol
courses.description: This presentation will discuss how utilizing the anesthetic protocol in its entirety can help mitigate potential negative side effects associated with using individual portions of the protocol alone. The presentation will cover pre-appointment medications, premedications, induction and co-induction, maintenance, MAC reducers including injectable anesthetics and local or regional blocks, and recovery. Emphasis will be placed on how each phase of anesthesia contributes to patient comfort, analgesia, smoother transitions between anesthetic phases, and reduction of anesthetic drug requirements. Patient-specific considerations and the benefits and limitations of commonly used anesthetic techniques will also be discussed.

courses.title: Hyaluronic Acid in Practice: A Veterinary Dental Case Round Table ON DEMAND
courses.description:
This is a case-based round table exploring the use of hyaluronic acid as an adjunct to a variety of dental and oral procedures.
Through a series of canine and feline cases, our panelists will share their clinical experiences using hyaluronic acid alongside established dental treatments, including closed root planing, gingival curettage, bone grafting, guided tissue regeneration, and full-mouth extractions. Cases will highlight applications involving advanced periodontal disease, furcational bone loss, feline chronic gingivostomatitis, and significant oral inflammation.
Participants will see how hyaluronic acid has been incorporated into treatment plans to support soft-tissue healing, manage local inflammation, promote periodontal and alveolar bone regeneration, and, in select cases, help preserve teeth that may otherwise have required extraction.
This interactive discussion will go beyond the theory and into the clinical decision-making behind each case, including patient selection, treatment techniques, outcomes, and practical considerations for incorporating hyaluronic acid into veterinary dental procedures.

courses.provider: FORTUNE MANAGEMENT - VETERINARY DIVISION DBA VETERINARY MASTERY
courses.title: Culture: Building and Retaining the Unstoppable Team
courses.description: Learn how to create a thriving workplace culture that attracts, develops, and retains exceptional team members. Participants will explore leadership behaviors, hiring strategies, onboarding, communication, accountability, recognition, and employee engagement that foster trust and collaboration. By the end of the course, attendees will be able to build a strong, values-driven culture, reduce turnover, improve team performance, increase employee satisfaction, and develop practical strategies that inspire ownership, accountability, and long-term commitment while supporting outstanding client/patient care and practice growth.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.title: Understanding Empathy and Its Application Via the Heart-Head-Heart Model
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.

courses.title: Wild About Eyes 2026
courses.description: This continuing education event brings together a variety of clinically relevant topics designed to help veterinary professionals strengthen their diagnostic and treatment skills. Sessions will cover feline infectious peritonitis (FIP), ophthalmic manifestations of systemic disease, ocular and orbital neoplasia, and non-ulcerative keratitis in dogs. Through practical, case-based discussions, attendees will gain current, applicable knowledge they can use to recognize complex disease, select appropriate diagnostics, develop treatment plans, and determine when referral or advanced care is indicated.

courses.title: Degenerative Lumbosacral Stenosis in a Working Dog Diagnosis, Treatment & Shockwave Mechanisms
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of degenerative lumbar sacral stenosis. The participant will be presented with a review of degenerative lumbosacral stenosis (DLSS) in dogs, covering pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnostics (radiographs, CT, and MRI as the gold standard, including the importance of dynamic imaging), and treatment options ranging from activity modification and medications (NSAIDs, gabapentin, amantadine) to epidural therapies (steroids, PRP, and a stem cell case report) and surgical approaches. Also, participants are introduced to shockwave mechanisms and device differences and are then presented with a case study.

courses.title: Understanding Empathy and Its Application Via the Heart-Head-Heart Model
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.

courses.provider: ACCESS SPECIALTY ANIMAL HOSPITAL PALM BEACH COUNTY
courses.title: Veterinary Applications of Hemopurification
courses.description: This talk will provide basic information on purification of the blood using extracorporeal therapies including hemodialysis, therapeutic plasma exchange and hemoperfusion. The lecture will include an overview of each of the modalities and a case example will be provided for each.
courses.location: ACCESS Specialty Animal Hospital Palm Beach County

courses.title: When Bandages Go Wrong: Managing slips, sores, and owner conversations
courses.description:
This lecture dives into the most common complications that can occur with veterinary bandages, from slipping and unraveling to pressure sores and moisture damage. Attendees will learn how to identify early warning signs, correct mistakes, and effectively communicate with pet owners when issues arise. Practical tips and real-world case examples will help veterinary technicians feel more confident in preventing and managing bandage failures, ensuring better outcomes for both patients and clients.
Learning Objectives:
* Recognize and troubleshoot common bandage complications such as slipping, pressure sores, and moisture-related damage through early detection and intervention.
* Apply practical correction strategies to improve bandage security, comfort, and effectiveness, using real-world case examples and technician-focused techniques.
* Develop effective communication skills for guiding pet owners in monitoring bandages at home, addressing concerns, and ensuring compliance for better patient outcomes.

courses.title: SDEP Anatomy, Pain Points & Tips
courses.description: This presentation provides an overview of general anatomy and how it pertains to the sonographic presentation while scanning. Anatomical terms, ultrasound terminology, anatomical diagrams, and step by step scanning instructions are discussed in detail. Probe positioning, tips, and scanning techniques, trouble shooting, and efficient imaging are conveyed to the attendees. Cine loops and stills of proper scanning are also utilized. Interactive questions and answers are encouraged during this 2-hour presentation.

courses.title: Equipment Controls and Protocol for Soft Tissue Ultrasound - The Fundamentals
courses.description: This program will cover basic machine functions and measurements for those that are new to ultrasound. We will discuss the purpose of the different probes. We will cover how to scan the liver, spleen, kidneys, and bladder, and following a scanning protocol for these organs, so that the attendee can create a basic soft tissue ultrasound exam. We will also cover scanning a grid of the abdomen, artifacts, and different probe uses. This will be a Medical Program, that is hands-on scanning in a wet lab format for 8 hours of RACE CE.

courses.title: Tackling Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency
courses.description: In this course, we will review the causes, clinical signs, diagnosis, and management of exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI). The session highlights current evidence, clinical recommendations, and real-world case applications.

courses.title: Triage and Common Presentations in Exotic Companion Animals
courses.description: Exotic patients are fragile and often mask illness until advanced. This lecture reviews efficient, low-stress triage techniques, key history elements, and species-specific stabilization steps. Common emergency and appointment presentations in ferrets, rabbits, small mammals, birds, and reptiles are outlined with practical, actionable protocols to improve outcomes and client education.

courses.title: Dentistry Webinar Series - Radiographic Interpretation
courses.description: This two-hour discussion (of our eight-part series) is dedicated to developing confidence and precision in reading and interpreting dental radiography, an essential skill for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning in veterinary dentistry. The session begins with a practical review of how to properly orient radiographs and identify which tooth is being examined, ensuring attendees feel grounded in the basics of interpretation. From there, participants will move into a detailed discussion of normal radiographic anatomy, building a clear picture of what healthy structures should look like. With that foundation in place, the focus shifts to identifying radiographic pathology, including how to recognize subtle changes and understand their clinical significance. Common conditions such as periodontal disease will be explored in depth, with attention given not only to diagnosis but also to treatment options. By the conclusion of this two-hour session, clinicians will be equipped with the knowledge to interpret dental radiographs with confidence, distinguish between normal and abnormal findings, and apply these skills directly to patient care.

courses.title: Stop Reacting, Start Controlling: A Simple Step-by-Step Plan for Inventory Success
courses.description:
Inventory is the second largest - and often most mismanaged - expense in a veterinary practice. Whether it's overstocking, understocking, or spending excessive time on manual counts, these missteps can drain your time, money, and energy. This webinar will address the real challenges that veterinary professionals face when managing inventory and provide practical strategies to take control.
We'll dive into the concept of inventory on hand (IOH) and how carrying excess stock ties up valuable capital. The webinar will explore the importance of formulary optimization to boost margins and reduce waste, and we'll walk through the benefits of cycle counting as a streamlined solution. Participants will gain hands-on advice for conducting full hospital counts, cleaning up old inventory, and organizing a system for ongoing success. The session includes a project plan, broken into small, manageable tasks, to help participants start improving their inventory practices right away.
No more relying on guesswork, post-it notes, or reacting to inventory shortages at the last minute. This webinar will provide actionable steps to regain control of inventory, reduce costs, and improve your practice's financial health.

courses.title: Veterinary Medicine: Radiology For Bone Lesions and Fractures in the Dog and Cat
courses.description:
Diagnostic work up of musculoskeletal disorders frequently includes radiographic examination and/or other diagnostic imaging procedures. The imaging modalities are used to further characterize clinically localized problems and to differentiate disease processes.
Aggressive and nonaggressive bone lesions are very common. Diagnostic imaging plays an important role in diagnosing and differentiating these pathologic processes. Radiology is considered the first technique to implement to try to establish a diagnosis.
Diagnostic imaging is a vital component in the diagnosis and management of fractures. At initial presentation, fractures can be identified and classified to permit planning of optimal treatment. Fractures can be monitored to assess healing and identify developing complications. Fracture identification and radiographic description of fractures along with evaluating fracture healing and complications of fracture repair, are of paramount importance for a successful treatment.

courses.title: (LIVE COURSE) Updates in Management of Neurological Emergencies
courses.description: This 3-week online course reviews current evidence and practical approaches to three common neurological emergencies in veterinary patients. We will cover traumatic brain injury, status epilepticus, and spinal trauma and acute disc disease. Each week focuses on triage, diagnostic decision-making, medical and surgical options, and monitoring. The content is designed for veterinarians who want the latest updates, with clinically applicable protocols you can use in practice.

courses.provider: ADVANCED VETERINARY CARE THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE
courses.title: The ABC SECTION'S Of Dystocia and Delivery Management Improving Your Outcomes
courses.description: This 1 hour CE lecture is designed for veterinary doctors, technicians, and tech assistants. It will cover an overview of neonatal resuscitation / care. Successful management of dystocia and neonatal resuscitation requires rapid assessment, effective teamwork, and timely intervention to optimize outcomes for both the dam and neonates. This presentation will review the recognition and management of dystocia, decision-making surrounding medical versus surgical intervention, and evidence-based approaches to neonatal stabilization and resuscitation. Attendees will gain practical knowledge of delivery room preparation, neonatal assessment, resuscitation techniques, and post-delivery care that can be immediately applied in clinical practice. Through case-based discussion and real-world scenarios, participants will learn strategies to improve survival rates and enhance patient care during obstetrical emergencies.

courses.title: Strategic Advancements in Wound Therapy: Evidence-Based Pathways
courses.description:
Challenging wounds are among the most common and most demanding cases in veterinary practice. From degloving injuries and burns to chronic non-healing and oncologic wounds, successful outcomes require more than basic bandaging skills. They demand strategic decision-making grounded in anatomy, physiology, and surgical principles.
In this case-based session, Dr. Justin Ganjei, DACVS-SA, walks attendees through real-world examples that highlight the clinical reasoning behind effective wound management. Participants will revisit the critical role of skin anatomy and vascular supply, review the phases of wound healing and how they guide timing of intervention, and explore how wound classification directly influences treatment strategy.
The session will move step-by-step through immediate management stabilization, lavage, debridement, and temporary protection before advancing to definitive closure options including primary and delayed closure, second intention healing, flaps, grafts, and adjunctive therapies such as negative pressure wound therapy and biologic dressings.
Attendees will leave with a practical, structured approach to evaluating and managing complex wounds while balancing patient factors, owner expectations, and available resources to optimize functional and cosmetic outcomes.
Learning Objectives. Upon completion of this session, participants will be able to:
1. Describe the relevant layers of skin anatomy and vascular supply and their influence on wound healing and surgical planning.
2. Explain the inflammatory, proliferative, and remodeling phases of wound healing and how these phases guide timing of intervention.
3. Classify wounds based on contamination level, duration, and tissue viability to determine prognosis and management strategy.
4. Apply evidence-based principles of immediate wound management, including stabilization, hemorrhage control, lavage, debridement, and temporary bandaging.
5. Differentiate between primary closure, delayed primary closu

courses.title: Refractory Congestive Heart Failure: Diagnostics and New Therapies in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: A detailed clinical exploration of feline and canine congestive heart failure diagnostics, focusing on radiographic interpretation and echocardiography while highlighting the vertebral heart score's diagnostic value. The session will evaluate conventional gold-standard management strategies alongside innovative pharmaceutical developments within the field of veterinary cardiology.

courses.title: The Real-Life Approach to Osteoarthritis Management: A Case-Based Discussion
courses.description: This program is a case-based discussion of osteoarthritis and building a general guideline for approaching the management of patients. OA is a complex and complicated process with no cookbook approach that works the same every time. It is a vicious cycle starting with joint pain and inflammation; it is the number one cause of chronic pain in dogs in the US. This talk will provide the presenters thoughts/opinions on managing patients with the goal being to have attendees make their own decision on how to manage their patients. We will discuss appropriate history taking, use of technicians, staging tools and at-risk patients. In addition, there will be a review of gait evaluation, examination, palpation and radiographs. Finally management options and multimodal approach.

courses.title: Perioperative Surgical Patient Care: Honoring the Bond
courses.description: A veterinary patient's perioperative experience is based on so much more than the surgeon's skill. Veterinary technicians play a vital role in the care of perioperative patients and educating pet owners. Strategies for supporting patient comfort and emotional wellbeing while assuring successful surgical outcomes will be discussed, such as the importance of Fear Free handling techniques, perioperative analgesia, and nutrition tactics for the veterinary team. Join this lecture for practical ideas that elevate the perioperative experience by nurturing the human-animal bond and exceeding client expectations.

courses.title: The Canine (and Feline) Knee: Old Problem, Newest Solutions
courses.description:
In this focused lecture, DoveLewis Small Animal Surgeon Dusty Spencer, DVM, DACVS-SA, will explore the anatomy of the canine and feline stifle as it relates to cranial cruciate ligament disease and medial patellar luxation.
Attendees will learn about the surgical goals for CCL and MPL repairs, comparing traditional techniques with innovative advancements in stifle stabilization. Dr. Spencer will also review the Off-Set TPLO procedure, discussing its benefits and indications for enhancing joint stability and recovery in affected animals.

courses.title: Down and Out: A Case-Based Review of Patients That Just Can't Walk
courses.description: This Florida Veterinary Medical Association-sponsored webinar provides a practical, case-based approach to evaluating dogs and cats that present with an acute inability to walk. While intervertebral disc disease is a common cause of non-ambulatory patients, numerous neurologic, orthopedic, cardiovascular, metabolic, and systemic disorders can present with similar clinical signs. Participants will learn a logical, stepwise approach to patient assessment, neurologic localization, differential diagnosis, and clinical decision-making. Through real-world clinical cases, attendees will gain practical strategies for prioritizing diagnostics, initiating appropriate stabilization and treatment, and recognizing when referral is indicated to optimize patient outcomes.

courses.title: Reading Canine Body Language: How It Could Save Your Life
courses.description: This Florida Veterinary Medical Association-sponsored webinar provides veterinary professionals with practical skills for recognizing and interpreting canine body language to improve patient safety, reduce stress, and prevent injuries in the veterinary setting. Every interaction with a canine patient begins with communication, and subtle behavioral cues often provide early warning signs before fear, anxiety, or aggression escalates. Participants will learn to recognize facial expressions, posture, movement, vocalization, and other body language signals that communicate a dog's emotional state. Through real-world examples and clinical scenarios, attendees will gain practical techniques for safer patient handling, reducing fear and anxiety during veterinary visits, and fostering positive experiences for patients, clients, and the veterinary team.

courses.title: How to Effectively Use Apoquel and Cytopoint
courses.description: This Florida Veterinary Medical Association-sponsored webinar provides a practical, evidence-based approach to using Apoquel and Cytopoint for the management of canine allergic dermatitis. Pruritus is one of the most common reasons dogs are presented to veterinary practices, and selecting the appropriate therapy requires more than simply controlling itch. Participants will review the mechanisms of action, indications, benefits, limitations, and clinical applications of Apoquel and Cytopoint while learning how these therapies fit within a complete diagnostic and treatment plan. The course also addresses common reasons for treatment failure, management of flare-ups, and long-term strategies that improve patient comfort, client compliance, and overall success in managing canine atopic dermatitis.

courses.title: The Role of the Human-Animal Bond in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: The human-animal bond influences pet parent behaviors when making health care decisions for their pets. This course will cover the meaning of the human-animal bond, its significance for pet parents, its role in veterinary care, and strategies for maintaining and strengthening the human-animal bond.

courses.title: AAEP XP Series: NeuroXP (LEX)
courses.description: This intensive two-day program provides equine practitioners with practical, clinically focused training in the diagnosis and management of neurologic disease in horses. Through a combination of preparatory materials, targeted lectures, interactive case discussions, and extensive hands-on laboratory sessions, participants develop a structured approach to neurologic examination, neurolocalization, diagnostic planning, and treatment decision-making. Learning will include foundational concepts, diagnostic interpretation, and hands-on skills using live horses, cadavers, and imaging modalities with advanced case-based discussions, procedural training, and real-world clinical scenarios, including client communication and risk management. Small-group laboratories and expert faculty guidance ensure individualized instruction and immediate clinical applicability, enabling participants to confidently assess, diagnose, and manage complex equine neurologic cases in practice.

courses.title: Animal Health Canada Forum 2026
courses.description:
Animal Health Canada Forum brings together senior leaders from government, animal agriculture, and from across the animal health and welfare system to share experience, exchange knowledge, and learn from one another.
The Forum 2026 theme is, 'Turning Insight into Action for Canada's Animal Health and Welfare System.'
Forum will focus on rising animal welfare expectations, evolving biosecurity risks, and the growing impact of misinformation and disinformation.
Participants will leave with practical insights to support decision making and action across Canada's animal health and welfare system.

courses.title: 2026 VHA Expo
courses.description:
Program Description: Our 2026 conference features 5 compelling speakers, including opening keynote Sarah Wooten, DVM. The breakout sessions will be guided by industry leaders who will cover topics of Neurology, Hematology, Practice Management, and Spectrum of Care. We will conclude the day with closing keynote Paul Burke.
The objective of the 2026 VHA Expo is to elevate medicine practiced in the clinics attending through networking, education, professional development, new products and services, and industry trends and insights. The veterinary field is constantly evolving, with new research, techniques, and technologies emerging. Attending the 2026 VHA Expo can help veterinary professionals stay updated on the latest developments.
courses.location: Double Tree Hilton Bloomington Minneapolis South

courses.title: Canine Mast Cell Tumors
courses.description: Mast cell tumors (MCT) are one of the most common skin tumors of dogs. Join us to learn how to better detect, evaluate, and treat this cancer as a general practitioner. In this webinar, a board-certified clinical pathologist and a board-certified medical oncologist will discuss this disease, focusing on understanding grading, staging, prognostic factors, and basic treatment options. Gain confidence deciphering pathology reports, better understand what factors affect the prognosis of MCT so you can better counsel your clients, and learn how to best treat your MCT patients. Finally, see how you can quickly move these MCT cases forward in your hospital, even when referral is needed.¿

courses.title: Low Stress Handling and Restraint of Large Dogs (BHVR908)
courses.description: Have you ever struggled to get a dog into position, or to keep them there for an exam or procedure? Too often, we reach for force to restrain an uncooperative dog when a little finesse would work far better. With Low Stress Handling(R) techniques, you learn to control a dog's movement in all six directions while giving them the support and guidance they need to feel secure. A comfortable dog is a still dog, and this course shows you how to earn that stillness rather than force it, across the everyday tasks of moving, positioning, examining, and drawing blood from large dogs.

courses.title: NAVC Human-Animal Bond Certified Company Training
courses.description:
Research has shown that owning a pet improves both physical and mental health - and the human-animal bond has never been more important to pet owners than it is today. This course explores the science behind that bond: how it works, why it matters, and the role your team plays in supporting and strengthening it.
Completing this training is more than a certificate or course - it is a signal of your organization's commitment to advancing research and education that support the well-being of people, animals, and the professionals who care for them.
In one hour, you will gain a foundational understanding of the neurological mechanisms behind the bond, review key research on its measurable health benefits, and explore the three domains of animal welfare and their connection to the human-animal relationship.

courses.title: Percardial Effusion: Diagnosis and Management
courses.description: Patients frequently present to the emergency department in tamponade with significant hemodynamic compromise. Early recognition and appropriate management are critical to improving patient outcomes. During this session, we will discuss the immediate management of patients in tamponade, as well as long-term planning and therapy options to achieve the best results for our patient populations. We will also discuss pericardial effusion in the feline, which carries a different long-term complication and survival outcome when compared to the canine patient

courses.title: Developing and Utilizing a Parvo Champion in Your Practice LIVE
courses.description:
Come join the conversation with Open Door Veterinary Collective consultant Dr. Kathleen Babbitt, DVM, as we explore Developing and Utilizing a Parvo Champion in Your Practice.
Managing canine parvovirus presents unique hurdles for veterinary clinics, particularly regarding staffing, communications, and client financial constraints. Implementing a dedicated Parvo Champion mitigates team burnout while ensuring high-quality, compassionate patient and client care.
This session demonstrates how to integrate individualized patient care with practical, cost-effective treatment paths and go-home communication resources. Attendees will gain actionable tools for every stage of the patient journey - from intake to discharge - enabling teams to elevate clinical outcomes, alleviate workplace fatigue, and maintain financial sustainability.

courses.title: Managing common skin and behavioral problems
courses.description: Doctors Bourgeois and Pachel will present a complete discussion of the common dermatologic and behavioral problems that they encounter in their individual practices. It is the speakers intent to provide the participants with the most up to date concepts for both diagnosis and management of the problems- both canine and feline. Upon completion of the seminar the participants will have a greater understanding of what is needed for the management of common behavioral and skin diseases and disorders.

courses.title: Continuing education evening with Vision Vets For Pets and East Tennessee Veterinary Dentistry
courses.description: This course will provide 1 hour of ophthalmology continuing education and 1 hour of dentistry continuing education. The ophthalmology portion will provide information on the diagnosis and treatment of glaucoma, and the dentistry portion will cover basic and advanced dentistry techniques for use in small animals.

courses.title: Easy to Swallow: Utilizing Contrast Radiography to Evaluate the Gastrointestinal Tract
courses.description: Contrast studies remain a valuable diagnostic tool for evaluating gastrointestinal disease. This lecture will discuss practical techniques for performing oral and rectal contrast studies, as well as interpretation of findings associated with disorders of the esophagus, stomach, small intestine, and colon. Attendees will gain a better understanding of when contrast radiography is indicated and how these studies can contribute to clinical decision-making.

courses.title: Understanding and Navigating the Companion Animal Practice Marketplace : A Review of Current Dynamics
courses.description: This program is a 60-minute prepared lecture that introduces the attendee to the major dynamics in the companion animal marketplace, and how these recent shifts are driving changes in the practice of veterinary medicine. Included in this lecture are an overview of the recent growth and/or decline of the major segments of companion animal practice, including wellness & preventive medicine, parasite prevention, surgical and procedural volume, as well as chronic disease management. Intended for all positions within the veterinary hospital including owners, associate clinicians, technical support staff and administrative support staff/management, this program utilizes a nationwide data set of both product sales/consumption data and practice information management system (PIMS) data to present nationwide, regional and even subgroup detail.

courses.provider: ACCESS SPECIALTY ANIMAL HOSPITAL PALM BEACH COUNTY
courses.title: Minimally Invasive Orthopedic Surgery
courses.description: This lecture will review the advantages of minimally invasive orthopedic surgery and review the indications and minimally invasive orthopedic techniques.

courses.title: VSPN/AIMVT Elevate - Online Conference - Advance. Specialize. Inspire (AIMVT 010-2026))
courses.description:
This online conference will help the attendee in meeting their professional goals. As the title says, Advance, specialize, and inspire: the attendee will learn how to leverage their Veterinary Technician Specialist (VTS) credential, handle challenging communication issues, create a supportive learning environment in the clinic, and use critical thinking skills effectively.
Learning Objectives
-Compare multiple career pathways available to Veterinary Technician Specialists beyond traditional clinical practice.
-Recognize transferable leadership, communication, and educational skills that can be developed through obtaining a VTS credential.
-Apply strategies for leveraging advanced credentials to pursue opportunities in leadership, education, industry, consulting, and professional organizations.
-Create an individualized action plan to support continued professional growth and career advancement after earning a VTS credential.
-Review coaching techniques to ensure that information is taken to heart
-Review best practices for offering suggestions and feedback
-Identify tone and tenor that will color a conversation negatively
-Discuss next steps if medical standards are not met even after addressing them
-Understanding the basics of psychological safety and team communication and the role of Veterinary Technician Specialists in creating and supporting psychological safety on the hospital floor
-Prioritize communication between teams amongst all other responsibilities on the hospital floor and model this to other employees
-Integrate critical thinking exercises and train the trainer learning activities on the hospital floor
-Define critical thinking and distinguish it from passive skepticism or contrarianism within a professional clinical context.
-Identify at least three cognitive biases that commonly influence clinical decision-making in veterinary nursing practice and describe one concrete mitigation strategy for each.
-Apply a structured framework to evaluate a peer-

courses.title: Fetch National Harbor 2026, part 1
courses.description: Fetch, a dvm360 conference, at National Harbor, MD is a live interactive, in-person conference with a combination of both medical and non-medical programs created for veterinarians, veterinary technicians, and practice managers to achieve their continuing education in veterinary medicine. Educational content tracks include: Artificial Intelligence, Behavior, Cardiology, Communication, Critical Care, Dentistry, Dermatology, Endocrinology, Ethics, Feline Medicine, Geriatrics, Infectious Disease, Internal Medicine, Laser Therapy, Marketing, Nutrition, Oncology, Ophthalmology, Orthopedics, Pain Management, Parasitology, Practice Management, Practice Ownership, Preventive Medicine, Rehabilitation, Surgery, Technician Anesthesiology, Technician Critical Care, Technician Feline Medicine, Technician Medicine, Technician Neurology, Technician Pain Management, Wound Management.

courses.title: Dermatology Symposium
courses.description: The continuing education program will include two parts. Part I will be a single didactic lecture on modern pet diets. Part II will be a 2-topic lecture series with interactive elements.

courses.provider: ACCESS SPECIALTY ANIMAL HOSPITAL PALM BEACH COUNTY
courses.title: Advances in Total Hip Replacements
courses.description:
2. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: Provide updates on new techniques and procedures available for total hip replacements.
3. LEARNING OBJECTIVES:
a. Review of anatomy
b. Review of hip dysplasia and pathophysiology
c. Arthroscopic techniques
d. Discuss candidates for surgery
e. Review of post-op care and complications Review of post-op care and complications

courses.title: Focus on Dentistry ( a 3 lecture series)
courses.description:
Lecture 1: Dentistry in the Patient with Oro-Facial Trauma
Lecture Abstract
The patient with oro-facial trauma can present a significant challenge, with injuries ranging from fractured jaws, tooth fractures and displacement, to significant soft tissue injuries. This lecture gives clinicians a clear, practical approach to patient stabilisation, analgesia, and dentistry planning, staging and execution, providing a sound framework for approaching these cases.Lecture 2: Local Anaesthesia for Small Animal Dentistry
Speaker: Dr Aaron Forsayeth BVSc (Hons) MACVSc (Veterinary Dentistry)
Lecture Abstract
Effective pain management is a crucial component in small animal dentistry. This lecture provides a practical, step-by-step guide to performing regional nerve blocks of the maxilla and mandible. Dr. Forsayeth will review relevant skull anatomy, the pharmacology of commonly used local anaesthetics, and techniques to ensure a successful block every time. Learn how to achieve profound intra- and post-operative analgesia, reduce general anaesthetic requirements, and provide a smoother, more comfortable recovery for your patients.Lecture 3: The Approach to Management of Fractured Teeth
Speaker: Dr Aaron Forsayeth BVSc (Hons) MACVSc (Veterinary Dentistry)
Lecture Abstract
This lecture reviews a practical, evidence-based framework for diagnosing and managing crown and root fractures in canine and feline patients. We will discuss key decision points, including endodontic versus extraction considerations, and the role of restorative materials in preserving tooth structure. The session aims to equip clinicians with a systematic approach to triage, treatment planning, and long-term monitoring of these common dental injuries.

courses.provider: THRIVE PET HEALTHCARE SPECIALISTS NORTH SCOTTSDALE
courses.title: 2026 Thrive North Scottsdale Specialists Desert Summit: Advanced Multi-Disciplinary Case Management & Clinical Diagnostics
courses.description:
This comprehensive, single-track, day-long continuing education program provides primary care veterinarians and emergency clinicians with practical, evidence-based approaches to multi-disciplinary case management across key specialty areas.
Following a logical anatomical and physiological progression throughout the day, participants will cover:
Neurology: Fundamentals of performing a thorough neurologic examination and establishing an accurate neuroanatomic localization.
Cardiology: Clinical utility of cardiac biomarkers, including NT-proBNP, in dogs and cats to differentiate cardiac vs. non-cardiac disease and guide targeted management.
Anesthesiology: Tailored anesthetic protocols, premedication/induction choices, and hemodynamically stable fluid management strategies for patients with co-existing cardiac and renal disease.
Emergency & Critical Care: Pathophysiology of hemorrhagic shock and practical execution of emergency autotransfusion during acute blood loss.
Soft Tissue Surgery & Internal Medicine: Diagnostic workup, imaging, and management of surgical acute abdomens, peritonitis, and the perioperative anatomy, physiology, and complications associated with adrenal gland surgery ("Adrenal Squeeze").
Oncology: Practical diagnostic workups, staging plans, biopsy considerations, and clinical decision-making for common canine and feline neoplasms encountered in general practice.
Through case-based discussions and review of current literature, attendees will gain actionable strategies to optimize patient outcomes, preserve future treatment options, avoid common diagnostic pitfalls, and navigate timely specialty referrals.

courses.title: Eyes, ears & beyond
courses.description: This seminar will provide the participants with the skills needed to diagnose and then manage, patients presented to their clinic with a dermatologic or ocular problem. The combination of a Dermatologist and an Ophthalmologist will provide the attendee with a comprehensive discussion of the common problems encountered in daily practice. Upon completion of the seminar, the attendee should have a greater understanding of how to diagnose and clinically manage the disorders and diseases that have been presented by the two specialists.

courses.title: Integrative Neuroacupuncture
courses.description: This course explores acupuncture from a modern, evidence-based perspective, with discussion of the use of acupuncture, explained through a neuro-physiological perspective, for a range of common veterinary medical conditions in small animals. In this rapidly developing area, effective evaluation and validation of research is important and will also be discussed.

courses.title: The Intersection of Nutrition and Behavior in Veterinary Care
courses.description:
Nutrition and behavior are closely connected components of comprehensive veterinary care. Feeding recommendations made during puppyhood and kittenhood can influence growth, health, and lifelong wellness. Routine nutritional assessments provide veterinary teams with opportunities to identify nutritional risk factors early, allowing for development of nutrition support plans.
In this webinar, participants will explore practical strategies for feeding growing puppies and kittens, including calculating daily energy requirements (DER) and applying the 10% rule when incorporating unbalanced foods (e.g., treats, human foods, chews, etc.). Participants will also review the importance of routine body weight, body condition scoring (BCS), and muscle condition scoring (MCS) monitoring, with consideration for how these assessments can be performed in ways that support positive, reduced-stress, veterinary experiences. Veterinary professionals will gain practical strategies they can incorporate into routine puppy and kitten appointments to support both health and positive veterinary experience.

courses.title: 2026 Saratoga Equine Practitioners Conference
courses.description: The NAEP is back in Saratoga for the Saratoga Equine Practitioners Conference from September 23-26th, 2026. This conference will include presentations in the following areas: Lameness, Podiatry, Internal Medicine. There will also be a full day of Wet Labs in the following areas: Lameness, Podiatry, Internal Medicine, and Ultrasound.

courses.title: FiberMaxxing: When should pets do it?
courses.description: In this online CE event, Dr. Adam Rudinsky, MS, DACVIM reviews the properties of dietary fiber and how they can be implemented in small animal practice with specific focus on case based application of fiber diets and supplements and dosing protocols. The systemic health of animals and maintenance of gastrointestinal tract (GIT) homeostasis heavily relies on influences from dietary fiber. Dietary fiber includes a diverse assortment of non-digestible carbohydrates. Primary roles of dietary fiber in the GIT include physically altering the digesta, modulating appetite and satiety, regulating digestion, and acting as a microbial energy source through fermentation. Beyond the GIT, dietary fiber also has widespread systemic effects throughout the body. This review will focus on how to modify fiber in dogs and cats with gastrointestinal disease. The goal being to provide clinically relevant information for practical application in clinical practice. Join us to get a clinical update on appropriate strategies to identify and manage your fiber-responsive gastrointestinal patients

courses.title: Beyond the Diarrhea: Harnessing the Canine Gut Microbiome for Better Clinical Outcomes
courses.description: In this lecture, we will explore the crucial role of the intestinal microbiome in maintaining digestive health and resilience in dogs, with a focus on evidence-based strategies to preserve, support, and restore microbial balance in clinical practice. Using clinical cases of dogs with acute diarrhea, we will discuss the importance of a systematic diagnostic and therapeutic approach tailored to the severity of the clinical signs, highlighting interventions that minimize disruption of the microbiome whenever possible. Participants will gain practical guidance on when to consider fecal microbiota transplantation, how to select appropriate fecal donors, and how to safely and effectively perform fecal microbiota transplantation procedures.

courses.title: Human Grade Pet Food: Understanding the Highest Standard for Integrity, Quality, and Food Safety
courses.description:
Pet owners are increasingly seeking "Human Grade" diets for
their pets, but what does this claim actually mean? Is it simply a marketing term, or does it represent a
meaningful difference in ingredient quality, manufacturing, and food safety?
This presentation explores the regulatory definition of Human Grade Pet Food and the rigorous standards
required to legally make this claim. Attendees will learn how Human Grade products differ from conventional
pet foods in ingredient sourcing, manufacturing practices, facility requirements, documentation, and regulatory
oversight. The seminar will also examine why quality systems-including supplier qualification, sanitation,
traceability, preventive controls, and testing- play a critical role in ensuring product integrity.
Rather than focusing solely on nutrition, this session provides veterinarians with a behind-the-scenes look at
how pet food is produced and why manufacturing standards matter when evaluating food quality. Participants
will leave with a practical framework for interpreting Human Grade claims and confidently discussing ingredient
quality and food safety with clients.

courses.title: The Modern Veterinary Pharmacy: Integrating In-Hospital and Online Care
courses.description:
Consumer expectations have fundamentally changed the way veterinary clients purchase medications, prescription diets, and preventive products. Convenience, home delivery, automatic refills, and digital ordering have become standard expectations rather than competitive advantages. As a result, veterinary hospitals are invited to revisit how online pharmacy services fit within an overall strategy for patient care, client service, and hospital profitability.
This presentation explores the evolving role of online pharmacies as an extension of veterinary healthcare rather than simply another retail channel. Participants will examine how consumer purchasing behavior has shifted, the operational advantages and challenges of online pharmacy integration, and strategies for maintaining strong client relationships regardless of where products are dispensed. Discussion will explore the factors practices should consider when evaluating an online pharmacy partner, from inventory management and operational efficiency to client compliance, convenience, and practice profitability. Lastly, the presenter will touch upon ways to garner staff buy-in to an online pharmacy and how to integrate and promote the pharmacy within the hospital's daily workflows.

courses.title: Rethinking the Insulin Reflex: SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy for Feline Diabetes Mellitus
courses.description: This course reviews the 2026 AAHA Diabetes Management Guidelines for Cats and critically evaluates four objections commonly raised against SGLT2 inhibitor (bexagliflozin/Bexacat, velagliflozin oral solution/Senvelgo) therapy for newly diagnosed feline diabetes mellitus: perceived monitoring complexity, owner administration burden relative to insulin injections, cost, and the risk of euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis compared with insulin-associated hypoglycemia. Attendees will leave with a practical, evidence-based framework for selecting SGLT2 inhibitor versus insulin therapy in newly diagnosed diabetic cats.

courses.title: Open Wound Management - What's New and What Works?
courses.description: This lecture provides a practical update on open wound management in veterinary patients, with an emphasis on current evidence and techniques that can improve wound healing. Topics will include wound assessment, debridement, wound bed preparation, lavage, topical therapies and dressings, negative pressure wound therapy, and decision-making for delayed or definitive wound closure. Participants will review what is new in veterinary wound care, which traditional approaches remain effective, and how to select appropriate management strategies for challenging wounds encountered in clinical practice.

courses.title: LACE Summer 2026 Courses
courses.description:
This course includes 110.25 hours of veterinary and veterinary technician/nurse
continuing education in cattle, sheep, goat, swine, and poultry topics. Medical themes
(107.25 hours) covered include general medicine, foot trimming, diagnostic testing,
metabolic disease, fluid therapy, legal drug use, respiratory disease, blood transfusion,
neurologic disease, pain management, neonatal care, pot bellied pig medicine,
dermatology, pinkeye, urinary, reproductive, respiratory, musculoskeletal and
gastrointestinal surgery. Nonmedical topics (3 hours) of medical decision making, herd
consultation and client communication will also be included.

courses.title: VetCE Virtual: Beyond Bad Behavior - Understanding Canine and Feline Behaviour Disorders
courses.description: This VetCE Virtual set of 3 live distance presentations includes topics of interest presented by experts. The presentations are held on separate dates. Attendees enroll in all three and must attend all to earn the completion certificate. The first presentation is on September 14, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Easy as one, two, pee: Solving Feline Housesoiling. The 2nd is on September 21, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Resource Guarding of Food. The 3rd and final presentation is on September 28, 2026 at 8PM Eastern: Addressing the Medical Components of Behavior Cases. The VetCE Virtual series of micro-conferences are a convenient alternative to in-person events and are designed to deliver multiple RACE and/or CVPM approved CE credits in a virtual format with three one-hour presentations. They provide educational sessions presented by expert speakers, and an easy way to learn and earn credits in the comfort of your home or office.

courses.title: Communication Skills to Make Clients LOVE You
courses.description: Excellent communication skills are crucial to develop trusting client relationships and improve both client compliance and patient outcomes. These skills should be developed by all team members. It has been shown that veterinarians with excellent bedside manner and communication skills are more likely to have a satisfied client and less likely to receive board complaints or malpractice claims. During this lecture, we will review basic communication tools and then discuss their application in various situations in the clinic, including making diagnostic and treatment recommendations, talking to upset clients, managing complications, and discussing finances.

courses.title: Code Brown: Updates in Fecal Diagnostics & Emerging Parasites in Cats & Dogs Near You
courses.description: This case-based session will provide updates on recent advances in fecal diagnostics and summarize key diagnostic and management components of "moving GI experiences" (ie, feline and canine diarrhea). An overview of common day-to-day causes of infectious diarrhea, with a focus on canine and feline GI parasites, including those of One Health and emerging importance (eg, Echinococcus multilocularis, drug-resistant hookworms, Giardia spp) and relevant antimicrobial stewardship aspects, will be provided. Pet owner communication, recent research pearls, and contextualized clinical strategies will be incorporated to provide actionable insights for attendees.

courses.title: A Journey into Indirect Reference Intervals: New Opportunities from Laboratory Big Data
courses.description:
Reference intervals are fundamental to the clinical interpretation of laboratory results. This presentation will take participants on a journey through historical and emerging concepts in veterinary and human reference interval development, exploring how novel indirect methods can leverage large laboratory datasets to generate representative and clinically relevant reference limits.
We will examine the principles behind indirect reference interval models and discuss how these approaches can be used to improve diagnostic accuracy through the development of breed-, age-, and sex-specific reference intervals. Practical applications will also include the use of indirect methods to verify externally sourced reference intervals within a laboratory's own patient population and support periodical refinement of existing reference limits.

courses.title: STP Virtual Modular Education Course: Digestive System Pathology
courses.description: The objective of the STP Modular Education Course, Digestive System Pathology, is to provide a practical framework for evaluating pathology of the gastrointestinal tract and associated digestive organs in nonclinical toxicology studies. The course emphasizes histology, species differences, spontaneous and treatment-related findings, and interpretation of lesions. Participants will strengthen their ability to distinguish background from treatment-related changes and integrate histopathology with clinical pathology, biomarkers, and mechanistic context. Emerging topics, including translational relevance, cutting- edge molecular pathology tools, and artificial intelligence in toxicologic pathology, are also included. The course will be a mixture of didactic lectures and case studies. Topics covered include: Overview of digestive system anatomy, physiology, and INHAND terminology; Contemporary approaches for evaluating digestive system structure and function; Digestive system considerations across therapeutic modalities, regulatory, translational, and case-based perspectives on interpreting digestive system findings in safety assessment. Course Chair: Kristofer Michalson, DVM, PhD, DACVP, (Bristol Myers Squibb); Course Co-Chair: Dinesh Bangari, BVSc, MVSc, MS, PhD, DACVP, (Sanofi); Course Scientific Advisors: Alys Bradley, BVSc (Charles River Laboratories); Ingrid Cornax, BS, DPhil, DVM (Altos Lab); Odete Mendes, DVM, PhD, DACVP, DABT (Merck & Co. Inc); Jagannatha (Jay) Mysore, MVSc, PhD, DACVP (Asklepios); and Jerrold Ward, DVM, PhD, DACVP, FIATP (Global VetPathology)

courses.title: Improving Outcomes for Clients with Financial Limitations Using a Spectrum of Care Approach
courses.description: Cases limited by client finances are a daily occurrence for many small animal practitioners. As pets are considered part of the family, conversations between pet owners and the veterinary team can become emotionally charged, especially when finances are limited and decisions about care become life or death. These cases and the discussions that go with them can create moral distress and contribute to burnout for many veterinarians. But it doesn't have to be this way. This lecture will explore the concepts of spectrum of care and incremental care in the context of client financial limitations and provide tools that can be used in financial conversations to maximize patient outcomes in clinical practice.

courses.title: IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer* Certificate Course
courses.description: This interactive self paced course prepares veterinary professionals to confidently operate the IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer for automated real time blood morphology ear cytology and FNA cytology testing. Across five modules Getting Started Blood Morphology Ear Cytology FNA Cytology and Maintenance learners will practice preparing and running samples interpreting results and maintaining the analyzer with a final assessment required to earn the certificate. By course completion learners will be equipped to integrate the IDEXX inVue Dx Cellular Analyzer into a streamlined efficient in house laboratory workflow.

courses.title: Panel Discussion Close, Impinging & Overlapping Spinous Processes: Advances in Diagnosis & Treatment
courses.description: Diagnosis and management of close, impinging and overriding spinous processes, so-called kissing spines, remain subjects of ongoing debate, particularly regarding when or if surgical intervention is truly necessary. With disciplinary and geographical variation in opinions, this panel discussion brings together specialists and experts in surgery, sports medicine and diagnostic imaging, from around the world. Through open debate and case-based insights, the panel will examine advances in diagnostics, rehabilitation strategies, surgical management and our current understanding of prognosis, with audience participation highly encouraged.

courses.title: AAV Avian Veterinary Clinical Competency Program Tier 3
courses.description: The goal of the AVCCP is to improve, promote and expand avian veterinary medicine in companion avian species* through a program of learning modules taught by specialists in avian practice. The modules are a compilation of 3 progressive tiers containing interactive, self-directed content, case scenarios and quizzes throughout the modules to solidify key learning points. The AVCCP Will Provide: - Day-one clinical competency avian medicine education for students and early career veterinarians looking to expand their depth of practice in avian medicine. - A foundational review of current literature and research with updated standards of avian medicine care for seasoned practitioners. - A solid foundation for those wishing to further explore specialization in avian medicine. *Psittacines, passerines, backyard poultry. Tier 3 is available to licensed veterinarians and currently enrolled veterinary students.

courses.title: Exotic Technical Animal Rescue: Principles and Preparedness- Anytime Course
courses.description: Exotic Technical Animal Rescue (ETAR) addresses complex rescue situations involving zoological species that require specialized equipment, training, and coordination between veterinary and operations teams. This webinar introduces ETAR concepts and highlights their role in supporting animal welfare, staff safety, and emergency preparedness. Participants will gain an overview of ASAR Training & Response, the development of exotic animal rescue capabilities, and practical considerations for implementing ETAR within their organizations.

courses.provider: SOUTH CAROLINA VETERINARY SPECIALISTS & EMERGENCY CARE
courses.title: Use of Intraarticular Therapies for Management of Canine Osteoarthritis
courses.description: In this session we will review the pathophysiology of canine osteoarthritis, degenerative joint disease and synovitis. Then we will compare various intra-articular therapies. We will review the mechanism of action of each product, efficacy of each product based on current research, labeled usage of each product, side effects, duration of action, tolerance, etc. The products to be reviews include but not limited to synovetin, arthromeid, platelet rich plasma, osteocushion, hyaluronic acid, corticosteroids.

courses.title: Health Certificates Are Not Enough: What Veterinary Teams Need to Know About Pet Travel Readiness
courses.description: Pet travel is increasingly showing up in veterinary practice, yet many veterinary teams are being asked to manage these cases without standardized training, consistent workflows, or confidence in key areas of travel preparation. Using preliminary insights from the When Pets Fly Veterinary Pet Travel Education Interest Survey, this webinar will explore where pet travel preparation commonly breaks down, including how clinics handle travel appointments, the types of requests veterinary teams receive, and the areas where teams report the least confidence when advising clients. Participants will learn why a health certificate does not automatically mean a pet is ready to travel and why veterinary teams need to be involved before the final paperwork appointment to achieve earlier, more informed, welfare-centered travel preparation. Veterinary Air-Travel Medicine and the When Pets Fly Pet Travel Readiness Assessment, will be introduced as an emerging approach that moves pet travel conversations beyond health certificate completion and toward safe, consistent, and welfare-centered pet travel case management.

courses.title: Feline Ophthalmology: Comprehensive Clinical Update
courses.description: This 2-hour continuing education program provides veterinarians and veterinary technicians with a feline-specific review of common anterior and posterior segment eye disease. The first segment addresses feline conjunctivitis, corneal ulceration, corneal sequestrum, eosinophilic keratitis, bullous keratopathy, eyelid masses, and entropion. The second segment reviews feline uveitis, glaucoma, hypertensive retinopathy, iris melanoma, and practical enucleation decision-making and surgical pearls for general practitioners.

courses.title: How We are Shooting Ourselves in the Foot: Veterinary Professionalism
courses.description:
While we often parallel ourselves with human medical counterparts, many in our ranks need some self-reflection and objective feedback before calling themselves professionals.
Everyone, from medical directors to kennel workers, should be representing the veterinary medical profession adequately to ensure appropriate public perception while commanding respect. What is veterinary professionalism and how do we obtain it?

courses.title: How We are Shooting Ourselves in the Foot: Veterinary Professionalism
courses.description:
While we often parallel ourselves with human medical counterparts, many in our ranks need some self-reflection and objective feedback before calling themselves professionals.
Everyone, from medical directors to kennel workers, should be representing the veterinary medical profession adequately to ensure appropriate public perception while commanding respect. What is veterinary professionalism and how do we obtain it?

courses.title: Performing and Communicating Around Euthanasia With Compassion
courses.description:
Few moments in veterinary medicine require greater presence than guiding a family through the end of a beloved pet's life. While clinical skills are essential, the experience is equally shaped by communication, compassion, professionalism, and the ability to create an environment where families feel supported during one of their most difficult moments.
This session explores practical strategies for preparing both the physical space and your professional presence before, during, and after euthanasia appointments. Participants will learn techniques for creating a calm environment, clear energy, developing authentic communication scripts, and utilizing body language that conveys empathy and confidence.
Equally important, this webinar addresses what happens after the appointment ends. Repeated exposure to grief can quietly accumulate over time, making intentional recovery practices essential to a sustainable veterinary career. Participants will explore practical approaches for honoring each experience through protective practices, brief personal resets, structured team debriefs, and meaningful end-of-day rituals that acknowledge the emotional weight of the work while supporting long-term professional well-being.
By integrating compassionate behavior with intentional recovery practices, participants will leave with a framework for caring not only for patients and their families, but also for themselves and their colleagues.

courses.title: Common Misconceptions in General Practice: Unpacking Assumptions About Cancer Screening for Lumps & Bumps
courses.description: Cutaneous and subcutaneous masses are among the most common reasons patients are presented in canine general practice, yet how these masses are evaluated varies widely from clinic to clinic. For some, fine-needle aspiration (FNA) is performed on as many lumps as possible. For others, the reality of daily practice means FNA is avoided. This real-world complexity has necessitated a change in first-step cancer screening diagnostics to help practitioners better detect cancer. In addition, new innovations in cancer screening like heat diffusion imaging have raised a lot of questions, and been met with skepticism from veterinary teams, about where they fit alongside existing tools like cytology and histopathology and in everyday decision-making.

courses.title: Navigating Construction, Design, and Financing Challenges for Veterinary Hospitals
courses.description:
This should briefly describe what a participant can expect during the course. This will be used in the CE Broker website search for upcoming CE/CME, and should have searchable keywords, so an attendee is able to locate the course based on their interest. For example, if this program was about the RACE Standards, I might state, "This course covers who qualifies to give a Medical presentation based on the 2023 RACE Standards. We will discuss when letters of reference are needed and what may disqualify an individual from being accepted as a presenter of a RACE program".
This course covers the construction, design, and financing decisions veterinary practice owners face when starting up, expanding, or relocating a hospital. We will discuss how to evaluate real estate and buildout options, assemble the right team of real estate, lending, and construction partners, compare SBA, conventional, and 504/504 Green loan structures, and build realistic project budgets. Attendees will also learn how lenders evaluate borrowers using the five C's of credit so they can prepare stronger, better-supported loan applications.

courses.provider: PARACHUTE VET - YOUR SAFETY NET FOR ECC
courses.title: The Domino Effect: From GI Obstruction to Metabolic Crisis
courses.description:
This 30-minute, case-based webinar follows a vomiting dog presenting with hypovolemic shock, and severe electrolyte and acid-base abnormalities caused by an intestinal foreign body. Participants will work through a practical emergency approach integrating perfusion assessment, ECG, POCUS, venous blood gas analysis, and abdominal imaging. The session translates acid-base physiology into immediate bedside decisions, including fluid resuscitation, safe potassium supplementation, and sodium-aware monitoring. Emphasis is placed on recognizing the metabolic consequences of gastrointestinal obstruction, prioritizing the abnormalities that affect immediate patient safety, and using serial reassessment to guide treatment before, during, and after surgery.
Keywords: Canine gastrointestinal foreign body; intestinal obstruction; vomiting dog; metabolic alkalosis; chloride-depletion alkalosis; hypochloremia; hypokalemia; hyponatremia; hypovolemic shock; tachycardia; venous blood gas; electrolyte disorders; point-of-care ultrasound; POCUS; fluid resuscitation; potassium chloride supplementation; abdominal radiography; emergency surgery

courses.title: Understanding Empathy and Its Application Via the Heart-Head-Heart Model
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how in our work with clients, connecting with empathy supports wellbeing and the care process. We discuss the 3 types of empathy and how they manifest in our daily work. "Heart-Head-Heart," a 3-step model for connecting with empathy, is then applied to a series of client communication scenarios. Attendees work in groups, receive feedback and can begin using the model immediately.

courses.title: Service Recovery and the L.A.S.T. Method
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program will review how Service Recovery is the process of "making right what went wrong" (Berry, 1995). Following an overview of Service Recovery theory, we introduce the L.A.S.T. Method, a proven service recovery communication model which is then applied in large and small-group breakouts to our most common veterinary service breakdowns.

courses.provider: PARACHUTE VET - YOUR SAFETY NET FOR ECC
courses.title: Hemolysis in a Hurry: Rapid Recognition & Management of IMHA in Dogs
courses.description:
Immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA) is a life-threatening emergency requiring rapid recognition, stabilization, and prevention of thromboembolic complications. Using a practical, case-based approach, this program guides veterinarians through the emergency assessment of an anemic dog, from bedside diagnostics and differentiation of hemorrhage versus hemolysis to confirmation of immune-mediated destruction. Participants will learn when to initiate transfusion, how to select appropriate immunosuppressive therapy, and how to implement thromboprophylaxis. Emphasis is placed on clinically applicable decision-making that can be used during the veterinarian s very next shift.
Keywords: immune-mediated hemolytic anemia, IMHA, canine anemia, hemolysis, regenerative anemia, saline agglutination test, spherocytes, blood transfusion, immunosuppressive therapy, thromboprophylaxis

courses.provider: PARACHUTE VET - YOUR SAFETY NET FOR ECC
courses.title: Under Pressure: Recognizing and Characterizing Shock in Dogs and Cats
courses.description:
This clinically focused course provides a physiology-driven approach to recognizing and characterizing shock in dogs and cats. Participants follow oxygen delivery from the respiratory system through hemoglobin, the heart, the circulation, and cellular utilization to identify where it is failing. Through practical examples, learners differentiate hypovolemic, distributive, cardiogenic, obstructive, hypoxemic and metabolic shock while recognizing compensated and decompensated presentations and important species differences. The course emphasizes rapid integration of perfusion parameters with lactate, PCV/TP, glucose, blood gas analysis, blood pressure, ECG, pulse oximetry, and global POCUS. Serial reassessment is used to refine the shock classification and guide immediate clinical priorities.
Keywords: veterinary shock, oxygen delivery, tissue perfusion, hypovolemic shock, distributive shock, cardiogenic shock, obstructive shock, metabolic shock, hypoxemic shock, lactate, POCUS, bedside diagnostics

courses.title: Biosecurity Considerations for Zoological Operations and Wildlife Confiscations in Aquatic and Terrestrial Settings- Anytime
courses.description: Infectious disease prevention and management are critical considerations in zoological facilities. Veterinary professionals at zoos and aquariums are leaders in establishing biosecurity protocols for routine zoological operations, including pre-shipment testing and quarantine procedures. Biosecurity is particularly essential in practice situations that incorporate the interface between well-established animal collections in managed care, wildlife rehabilitation, and notably, confiscations. Animals confiscated from the illegal wildlife trade present some of the highest biosecurity risks for a rescue facility.
