Presenting with little or no medical history, potential severe illnesses, and the possible presence of infectious, zoonotic, or foreign animal diseases, these cases require rapid assessment and strict protocols to protect both animal and human health. This lecture will discuss veterinary risk management and biosecurity practices in AZA accredited zoological institutions, focusing on the care of aquatic and terrestrial taxa, respectively. Discussion will include unique examples of risk assessment and applied biosecurity from aquatic and terrestrial species perspectives. The session will also review how to evaluate a facility's capability to manage confiscated wildlife safely, effectively, and with the highest standards of biosecurity, considering resources, staffing, species experience, veterinary capacity, and access to experienced consultants.

courses.title: Heritage Vet Partners Cattle First Summit
courses.description: This program is being offered to provide a range of continuing education topics to practitioners in the Heritage Vet Partners Group. Topics will include research updates on transboundary animal diseases, bovine respiratory updates, transcriptomics, clinic best practices in relation to necropsies, and personnel management issues specifically related to bridging generational gaps in practice teams.

courses.title: PIMS is NOT a Four-Letter Word -Pick It More Strategically with Help LIVE
courses.description:
Your practice information management system touches every part of your hospital, from scheduling to invoicing to medical records. Join Veterinary Ownership Advocates for a webinar with PIMS expert Adam Wysocki on how to choose the right system for your practice.
Whether you're launching a new practice or evaluating an acquisition, this session will cover:
For startups: how to identify what you actually need and match it to the right PIMS
For existing hospitals or acquisitions: how to assess whether your current PIMS is meeting your needs, and if not, how to choose and convert to a better option

courses.provider: PARACHUTE VET - YOUR SAFETY NET FOR ECC
courses.title: The Morning After: Navigating Post-Op Septic Abdomen Care
courses.description:
Dogs recovering from surgery for septic peritonitis remain at risk for hemodynamic instability, fluid imbalance, arrhythmias, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, aspiration pneumonia, and gastrointestinal dehiscence. This case-based course focuses on the practical postoperative management of these critically ill patients. Participants will learn to formulate individualized fluid and hemodynamic support plans, provide multimodal analgesia and early enteral nutrition, use culture results to guide antimicrobial de-escalation, and interpret serial physical examination, laboratory, ECG, drain, and POCUS findings. Emphasis is placed on recognizing early signs of clinical decline and initiating timely interventions to optimize recovery.
Keywords: canine septic peritonitis, postoperative management, fluid therapy, hemodynamic support, postoperative monitoring, POCUS, pain management, enteral nutrition, antimicrobial de-escalation, gastrointestinal dehiscence

courses.title: Medical Colic in the Adult Horse
courses.description:
This talk will cover the anatomy of the equine gastrointestinal tract and explore the subject of colic. There are many reasons for a horse to exhibit abdominal pain and most horse owners are well versed to spot the signs of colic. Many bouts of colic can be managed at the farm with an ambulatory veterinarian and will never need to be hauled into a referral hospital. Those cases that cannot be managed at the farm due to access to care, owner preference or severity can be managed medically or surgically depending on the reason for the abdominal pain.
Medically managed colic can range from a gastric impaction, an Ileus, or disruption in motility, to a displacement of the large colon into the nephrosplenic space. Treatment options include fluids, given in various ways, gastric decompression, specific medications such as phenylephrine, and pain management.

courses.title: Mission Possible: Beating FIP
courses.description: The objectives include recognizing that FIP is no longer 100% fatal, identifying the wide range of clinical presentations, and developing individualized diagnostic and treatment plans. Early recognition and intervention are emphasized as critical factors influencing treatment success. The main focus will be clinical presentations, diagnostic testing, and case review.

courses.title: Optimum Laser Therapy
courses.description: Optimum laser therapy is a course designed to teach veterinary professionals everything they need to have optimal results with any laser they use. There are 45 modules each with goals and quizzes. The first half dives into laser didactics. The second half reviews disease processes, goals for treatment, and treatment specifics for multiple lasers. Below is the module breakdown.

courses.title: The Fresh Food Alternative: Nutritional Strategies for Dogs with Protein-Losing Enteropathy
courses.description: For dogs with protein-losing enteropathy (PLE), commercial dry and canned diets don't always deliver the results patients need. Pet parents and the veterinary team are often left searching for alternatives. This webinar explores the role of fresh food diets as a therapeutic option when conventional commercial diets fall short. Attendees will learn how to approach diet selection for PLE patients, key nutritional considerations (fat restriction, protein source and digestibility, caloric density), and how to monitor response to fresh food interventions. Whether you're a veterinarian, veterinary nutritionist, or technician looking to expand your toolkit for managing difficult GI cases, this session will provide actionable guidance for incorporating fresh diets into a PLE treatment plan.

courses.title: Veterinary Instructional Development
courses.description:
This is a course for DVM and veterinary technical program instructors and others wishing to improve their instructional skills.
It is a completely on-line course with interactive components. To complete the course, participants must complete the following:
Five modules, associated with video lectures and course notes, completion of a study guide, and a quiz. Modules 1 and 2 are extensive and are required of all participants. The other three modules may be completed by choosing any of modules 3-6, which are included in the course, or as a series of equivalencies, as in the course.
Examinations on modules 1 and 2, on which they must achieve a score of 70% or higher to gain access to the final project
A capstone project, which requires them to create a teaching portfolio. This encourages thoughtful deliberation about choices made as an instructor and helps prepare participants for promotion and tenure and certifications within external bodies, for example, regional or national teaching academies.

courses.title: Dental Radiography
courses.description:
Dental radiography is the most important diagnostic tool in veterinary dentistry, yet it is often underutilized or performed with technique that compromises image quality and safety. This lecture reviews core radiation safety principles the ALARA principle, personal protective equipment, and proper positioning of personnel relative to the primary beam along with regulatory considerations relevant to veterinary practice.
Attendees will compare available radiography systems, including conventional film, phosphor plate, and digital sensors, weighing image quality, workflow, durability, and cost to help determine the best fit for their practice. The lecture concludes with practical guidance on obtaining diagnostic quality radiographs, covering parallel and bisecting angle positioning, sensor placement for maxillary and mandibular arcades, and common technique errors and how to correct them.
By the end of this session, attendees will be equipped to implement safer radiographic protocols, make informed equipment decisions, and consistently produce diagnostic dental radiographs in practice.

courses.title: 2026 AAHA CON Conference
courses.description: The American Animal Hospital Association has been setting the standard for small animal veterinary care for over 90 years. Every year, AAHA CON brings together veterinary professionals from across the country to learn, connect, and celebrate the future of veterinary medicine. In 2026, we're heading to Portland, Oregon for three unforgettable days of inspiration, education, and community. Immerse yourself in transformative learning experiences in an intimate setting designed for your personal growth. This year's conference celebrates the strength, stability, and growth that comes from being firmly grounded in veterinary medicine while reaching upward to explore new possibilities.

courses.title: From Instruments to Incision: Veterinary Ophthalmic Surgery
courses.description: This live, interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will review common ophthalmic surgical procedures performed in general practice. This course will provide an overview of surgical anatomy, instrumentation, indications, and techniques. Common pitfalls for eyelid surgery will be highlighted, as well as key procedural steps to improve outcomes in ophthalmic procedures.

courses.title: Acupuncture And Western Herbs for Senior Pets.
courses.description: This two-session program provides a practical overview of integrative approaches to supporting the health and well-being of senior pets. One one-hour session focuses on the use of acupuncture to enhance comfort, mobility, and quality of life in aging dogs and cats. The second one-hour session explores the role of Western herbal medicine in supporting common age-related conditions and promoting healthy aging. Together, these sessions offer veterinary professionals an introduction to complementary therapies that can be integrated with conventional care to optimize outcomes for senior patients.

courses.title: Feline Triaditis in Practice: Understanding the Tricky Triad
courses.description: This presentation explores feline triaditis, a complex syndrome involving concurrent disease of the gastrointestinal tract, pancreas, and hepatobiliary system. Current understanding of the etiopathogenesis will be reviewed, along with practical approaches to diagnosis and clinical evaluation. Attendees will also learn to develop effective treatment strategies while considering how therapies for one component of the triad may impact others.

courses.title: To Spay or Not to Spay, That is the Question
courses.description: Plan to discuss previously accepted recommendations for castrating dogs based on age and breed/size and how recommendations have changed based on new research over the last two decades. Within the presentation there are also correlations between animals and humans with similar disease processes. At the end of the presentation guidelines will be provided to help veterinarians educate their clients about this topic as well as the different surgical options available today.

courses.title: Feline Lower Urinary Track Disease-FLUTD
courses.description:
In this 2 hour long, in-person lecture based meeting, an in-depth review of
feline lower urinary tract disease along with practical case review will occur. Emphasis on the
pathophysiology of the main causes of FLUTD and recommended diagnostics will be discussed.
Both medical and interventional therapies will be discussed, with particular emphasis on feline
idiopathic cystitis

courses.title: Senior Cats and Hidden Disease: The Impact of Early Detection
courses.description: Senior cats are often affected by hidden diseases that go undetected until advanced stages. This session will explore the findings of the Mortier study to highlight gaps in feline preventive care and examine key conditions that may be improved through early detection. Emphasis will be placed on the latest diagnostic data, and the role of regular wellness assessments in improving outcomes. Attendees will also gain strategies for practice- and client-level change management to better support feline health through proactive care.

courses.title: Frustrating Felines: The Inappetent Cat
courses.description: How do we get a sick cat to eat? Surely, this is one of the greatest challenges in feline practice. This session will explore the mechanisms that regulate appetite in healthy cats and emphasize the importance of identifying and addressing underlying causes of inappetence through appropriate diagnostic evaluation. A multimodal approach to managing inappetent cats will be discussed, including dietary and environmental modifications as well as pharmacologic options to support food intake.

courses.title: Thoracic Pathology and Ultrasound. When is it cardiogenic vs. other? (LIVE/LECTURE)
courses.description: This 2 hour Live/On-site lecture program will present the necessary actions and clinical parameters needed to dial down whether clinical signs are derived from cardiac disease/thoracic disease, or other. In depth discussions of: normal respiratory parameters, normal echo parameters and radiographic findings, cardiac parameters of left sided heart failure, pleural effusion, cardiogenic parameters vs non-cardiogenic, thoracic lesion mapping for US-guided sampling, non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema causes, thoracic causes of abdominal passive congestion, pulmonary & other thromboembolic presentations, thoracic cysts, lung consolidations, lung lobe torsions, US-guided thoracic sampling, thoracic hernia, thoracic arcinomatosis/lymphomatosis, valve disease classifications, cardio-thoracic case presentations.

courses.title: CARES VetMed Fall 2026 Virtual Conference
courses.description: This live, virtual conference is provided by 12 individual Veterinary Technician Specialists in either Anesthesia & Analgesia or Emergency and Critical Care. Topics to be presented include: Heart Rate of the Anesthetized Patient: The Chronotropic Effects of Autonimic Tone and Anesthetic Agents, ECG in the ER: Rapid Rhythm Recognition for Critical Patients, Fresh Frozen Facts: Blood Transfusions in Veterinary Medicine, Triaging Trauma, Pheochromocytoma - What Do I Do?, Riding the Waves of Capnography, "The Inordinately Protected Airway" Brachycephalic Anesthesia, Sedation in the ER, When Sugar Hits the Fan: Recognizing HHS, Emergency and Critical Care of Exotic Companion Animals, Prioritize, Assess, Intervene: Understanding What it Means to Triage, and Cardiology for the Anesthetist.

courses.title: NT-proBNP in Practice: From Cardiac Signal to Clinical Decision
courses.description: This session reviews the clinical use of NT-proBNP as a cardiac biomarker in dogs and cats. Attendees will learn the physiologic basis of NT-proBNP release and its role as a marker of myocardial stretch. Practical applications in general and specialty practice will be discussed, including differentiation of cardiac versus non-cardiac disease, triage of clinical signs, and support of referral decisions. Emphasis will be placed on appropriate test selection, interpretation within clinical context, and limitations of NT-proBNP testing.

courses.title: Heart Healthy Anesthesia for the Small Animal Cardiac Patient
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary professionals will review the challenges of anesthetizing a small animal with cardiovascular conditions. This course will focus on alterations and adaptations to anesthetic techniques, plus feature practical strategies and protocols for a safe anesthetic episode. An overview will also be provided on the current literature regarding heart healthy anesthesia for cardiac patients.

courses.title: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Complete Urinary System in the Dog and Cat
courses.description:
Urinary problems in dogs and cats, whether they are acute, chronic, or genetic, can diminish the health and happiness of patients and their owners. We understand that urinary surgery can be stressful. If urine trouble feels like you are in trouble inside your operating room, let this course get you back in the flow of things. That is why we designed this course, to help you develop & refine new surgical skills to ease your anxieties with future cases. You will perform nephrectomy, cystotomy, and canine & feline urethrostomies.
After this course, you will feel confident in performing surgery in the urinary system, including surgical planning, execution, and troubleshooting unexpected challenges.

courses.title: Next Level Soft Tissue Surgery: Complete Urinary System in the Dog and Cat
courses.description:
Urinary problems in dogs and cats, whether they are acute, chronic, or genetic, can diminish the health and happiness of patients and their owners. We understand that urinary surgery can be stressful. If urine trouble feels like you are in trouble inside your operating room, let this course get you back in the flow of things. That is why we designed this course, to help you develop & refine new surgical skills to ease your anxieties with future cases. You will perform nephrectomy, cystotomy, and canine & feline urethrostomies.
After this course, you will feel confident in performing surgery in the urinary system, including surgical planning, execution, and troubleshooting unexpected challenges.

courses.title: Off to See the Wizard: A Journey to Reliable Itch Control
courses.description: Managing chronic canine itch can feel like being caught in a tornado--frustrated clients, flaring patients, and treatment plans that never quite stick. In this fun, practical, Wizard-of-Oz-themed webinar, Dr. Ali Diesel guides veterinarians along a clear 'yellow brick road' to more reliable long-term itch control. Participants will learn how IL-31 drives pruritus, why committing to a structured three-dose approach matters, how to manage common confounders, and how simple workflow strategies like forward booking support long term success. Through real-world cases and interactive discussion, attendees will leave with a confident, Monday-morning-ready framework for managing chronic itch in practice.

courses.title: Winning with Senior Pets and Nutrition
courses.description:
Seminar diving into what data and clinical evidence tells us about aging pets, their diseases, and how we can elevate the standard of care for senior pets through nutrition and home delivery
Program Agenda:
Review of Senior pet demographic data and what is changing
Introduction of a Framework for better senior care appointments
Review of the prevalence and treatment data for 3 common diseases of aging- Renal disease, Arthritis, Cognitive decline
Show how more proactive recommendation of nutrition and more proactive use of vet sponsored home delivery can elevate care for senior pets
Learning Objectives:
The changing demographics for senior pets and the prevalence of disease
How to plan and execute more effective senior pet visits
How large the patient care opportunity is with arthritis, renal disease, and cognitive decline
See the impact that home delivery can have on patient compliance and business outcomes

courses.title: (Live Webinar) The Secret of Pee: Myths and Realities of Urinary Health in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Urinalysis is a valuable but often misunderstood diagnostic tool in small animal practice. This session will explore the clinical significance of two commonly encountered urinary findings, crystalluria and bacteriuria, and help clinicians distinguish clinically relevant abnormalities from incidental findings. The webinar will discuss the different types and causes of crystalluria, when treatment is warranted, and practical approaches to management. It will also address the interpretation of bacteriuria in dogs and cats, including how to differentiate true urinary tract infection from contamination or subclinical bacteriuria, and when antimicrobial treatment is appropriate. Through a practical, case-based approach, participants will gain a clearer understanding of how to interpret these findings and make evidence-based treatment decisions in everyday clinical practice.

courses.title: Oral Tumors in Canines & Felines: Adjuvant Therapies and Surgical Resection
courses.description:
This course covers common neoplastic tumors that are encountered in veterinary medicine for dental and
oral cases. The oncology team will discuss detail information on behavior of the tumors, prognosis for
patients, as well as options of adjuvant therapy. The dental & oral surgery team will then discuss
different surgical resection options for these tumors and examples with case reports.

courses.title: (On Demand Webinar) The Secret of Pee: Myths and Realities of Urinary Health in Dogs and Cats
courses.description: Urinalysis is a valuable but often misunderstood diagnostic tool in small animal practice. This session will explore the clinical significance of two commonly encountered urinary findings, crystalluria and bacteriuria, and help clinicians distinguish clinically relevant abnormalities from incidental findings. The webinar will discuss the different types and causes of crystalluria, when treatment is warranted, and practical approaches to management. It will also address the interpretation of bacteriuria in dogs and cats, including how to differentiate true urinary tract infection from contamination or subclinical bacteriuria, and when antimicrobial treatment is appropriate. Through a practical, case-based approach, participants will gain a clearer understanding of how to interpret these findings and make evidence-based treatment decisions in everyday clinical practice.

courses.title: 2026 AETA - CETA/ACTE Joint Annual Pre-Conference Sessions
courses.description: The AETA & CETA/ACTE 2026 Joint Convention aims to present a unified voice for those involved in the embryo transfer industry in the promotion of mutual interests and objectives, provide continuing education and information regarding current issues in the embryo transfer industry for members. The American Embryo Transfer Association embraces its responsibility as the resource for embryo transfer in the United States. This authority is developed and supported through our commitment to excellence in several broad areas: education and standards of quality.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION FOR LABORATORY ANIMAL SCIENCE
courses.title: 77th AALAS National Meeting
courses.description: Each fall since 1950, the American Association for Laboratory Animal Science has held its annual National Meeting. During the five days of the meeting, members and non-members come together to enjoy the workshops, lectures, poster sessions, and exhibits. The program is designed to have topics relevant to the entire membership. Exhibitors have an opportunity to interact with AALAS members from the academic community, research institutions, government organizations, and commercial companies. The AALAS National Meeting is the largest gathering in the world of professionals concerned with the production, care, and use of laboratory animals. The meeting will be held at the George R Brown Convention Center in Houston, Texas from October 25 - October 29, 2026.

courses.title: The Curvilinear Approach for Consistent Recognition of Sonographic Pathology (LIVE/Lecture)
courses.description: This program focuses on following the natural external and internal curvilinear patterns in all organ systems, when interrogating ultrasound or any imaging modality, allows a cognitive flow pattern that: recognizes deviation from normal, evaluates degree of deviation, identifies neoplastic criteria or NEEDLE CRITERIA, ensures methodical approach to organ interrogation minimizing risk of lesion omission, provides clinical-pathological insight to Normal vs. Age-related vs. Inflammatory vs. Neoplastic states.

courses.title: Practical Pruritus: Making the Right Drug Choice for Dogs in Everyday Practice
courses.description: In this presentation, we will cover changing client perceptions and treatment options for managing allergic dogs. Current concepts surrounding diagnosis and treatment considerations will be covered. We will focus on currently available therapeutic options and where they fit with managing allergic dermatitis in dogs and how clinical presentation and client desires may affect treatment decisions.

courses.title: Ophthalmology Surgery - Common GP Techniques
courses.description: In this 3-hour, LIVE seminar, Shelby Reinstein, DVM, MS, DACVO will present numerous ophthalmic conditions which are typically managed surgically, including eyelid masses, prolapsed gland of the third eyelid, and glaucoma.

courses.title: Skin Cytology: How and Why
courses.description: This lecture will teach the Veterinarians and their Technicians the importance of skin cytology along with lesion identification, skin sampling techniques, and microscopic evaluation of obtained samples. The microscopic evaluation section will help in identifying common findings including bacteria, yeast, inflammatory cells, and more. We will also discuss bacterial skin cultures and why they are such an important part of treating skin infections and how to use cytology to help your course of treatment.

courses.title: SDAALAS Symposium 2026
courses.description:
During this full day symposium AALAS members and non-members come together to experience lectures and networking. The program is designed to have topics relevant to the entire membership
.Sick to Solved: Identifying and Addressing Morbidity & Mortality in Rodent Colonies, When Things Go Sideways: Lessons Learned for Vivarium Leaders, From Manager to Coach: An Introduction to Coaching Skills, Life Lessons from the Animals in Our Care, Think in Color: Using Six Thinking Hats to Drive Decisions, : Leadership Development Coaching: Building Influence, Engagement, and Impact,

courses.title: Infectious Disease Hot Topics and Vaccination Strategies
courses.description: This presentation goes over core and non-core vaccinations for dogs and cats per AAHA and AAFP vaccine guidelines, individual risk factors and helps determine clinic vaccination protocols. The course focuses on leptospirosis, Lyme disease, Feline Calicivirus, Feline Leukemia Virus and vaccine safety principles.

courses.title: 2nd Annual Veterinary Burnout Preparedness Summit of the Year
courses.description:
The 2nd Annual Veterinary Burnout Preparedness Summit of the Year is a two-day continuing education program for veterinarians, veterinary technicians and technologists, practice managers, and veterinary support staff. The program addresses burnout preparedness, compassion fatigue, compassion satisfaction, moral distress, workplace communication, leadership, psychological safety, grief in end-of-life care, anxiety, and team wellbeing. Across eleven one-hour sessions delivered by veterinarians and allied subject matter experts, participants examine both individual and organizational contributors to burnout and learn practical, evidence-informed strategies for personal recovery and team-level culture change. Sessions cover foundational wellbeing terminology and burnout preparedness frameworks, compassion satisfaction as a protective factor, expectation-setting and its effect on retention and client compliance, career design and sustainability, physical durability and ergonomics in clinical work, anxiety recognition and management, sustainable organizational wellbeing systems, burnout as an occupational risk addressed through upstream organizational and regulatory strategy, learned helplessness and employee silence, and cumulative grief in end-of-life care. The program is delivered live and interactive online, with presenter interaction available throughout each session.
Attendees may select from the available sessions. CE credit is awarded on the basis of documented per-session attendance, and hours earned are reported per licensee.

courses.title: Regional Dental Anesthetic Blocks Lab
courses.description: This lab will introduce participants to the tips and techniques for applying regional dental anesthetic blocks for pain management during oral surgery cases. It will include hands on practice, as well as discussions on patient considerations and how to manage recovery.

courses.title: Advanced Vascular Access: Cut Downs, Ultrasound Guidance, and More
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary technicians will review difficult venous access, including advanced catheter and line placement, plus alternative sites. In addition, this program will include cut down and ultrasound guided catheter placement, intraosseous cannulation (IO) and jugular catheters, peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) lines, plus central line placement tips and tricks.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1242060.)

courses.title: Husbandry! It's a Life Saver
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary technicians will review basic husbandry needs of reptiles including bearded dragons, geckos, turtles, and snakes. This course was previously presented live and RACE-approved (#20-1102580) and this version will be accessible anytime online on medvet.com.

courses.title: Having a Ruff Day: All About Canine Parvovirus
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for technicians will review the presentation, diagnosis, and management of canine parvovirus. This course was previously presented live and RACE-approved (#20-1006044) and this version will be accessible anytime online on medvet.com.

courses.title: CPR: A Near Breath Experience
courses.description: This program for technicians will review the Reassessment Campaign on Veterinary Resuscitation (RECOVER) guidelines for cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and how to implement and perform them.

courses.title: Fur Real Math: Calculations and Dilutions
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will provide practical guidance on common veterinary calculations and dilution techniques. This course will review how to accurately calculate dosages based on dose and weight conversions, prepare dilutions for medications, plus calculate appropriate additive volumes.

courses.title: Abdominal Ultrasound: A Technicians Perspective
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary technicians will review abdominal ultrasounds so that they may provide better assistance to ultrasonographers in order to obtain the best diagnostic images. The presentation will focus on the preparation of the patient, an overview of the anatomy included in a full abdominal ultrasound, and how the ultrasound image is created.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1100136.)

courses.title: Pick Your Poison: Toxins in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) program is a recording of a live virtual webinar. This medical program for veterinary technicians will review the clinical signs, pathophysiology, and progression of toxicity in common toxic exposures encountered in small animal practice with an emphasis on how toxin dose, species differences, and time to presentation influence clinical outcomes. In addition, this session will review appropriate diagnostic plans for suspected toxin exposures based on case presentation and toxin type, plus how to apply treatment strategies and emergency interventions for a variety of toxin-related emergencies. This course will also review how to assess prognosis and provide follow-up care based on toxin class and severity of clinical signs.

courses.title: Calling all Vet Techs. Answers from the frontlines
courses.description: Peter Carlos, AKA Vet Tech Pete, has garnered a huge following on TikTok for his light-hearted perspective on the reality of daily life as a veterinary technician. Join us in this exclusive interview as Peter reveals what fuels his passion as an RVT and how the simple idea of making a few videos to brighten up his colleagues days escalated into a viral sensation that brings joy to millions of veterinary professionals all around the world.

courses.title: AVST (Academy of Veterinary Surgical Technicians) Orthobiologics Webinar
courses.description: This 1-hour webinar covers the application of biologics in veterinary practice. This program is specifically designed for the veterinary technician, covering the what, why & how of biologics, troubleshooting, application in practice, and success stories. The remaining time will be used for live Q&A.

courses.title: A-Z Veterinary Dentistry & Anesthesia for Veterinary Technicians
courses.description: Online 2-hour training brings the essentials of indispensable tricks to dental charting, radiographs and general COHAT principles together with anesthetic dynamics. Added confidence/efficiency boosters to make procedures faster and easier.

courses.title: Suturing for Veterinary Technicians Level 2
courses.description: This is a four-session progressive workshop series bringing the scope of skin closure into the hands of Veterinary Technician. Each in-person course provides 3-hours of learning for tissue handling, instrument use, and essential skin sutures.

courses.title: AAHA Diabetes Educator Certificate Course
courses.description:
Successful management of diabetes mellitus takes nothing less than a team effort. While technicians have always had a role in diabetes management, completion of this course will empower them to be the team's "go-to" supporter of diabetic pets and the people who care for them.
In this course, learners will experience the following modules:
- Module 1: An Introduction to Diabetes
- Module 2: Preparing Owners of Diabetic
- Module 3: Feline Diabetes
- Module 4: Canine Diabetes
- Module 5: Diabetes Education for the Veterinary Team
- Module 6: Navigating Diabetes
This comprehensive course empowers Veterinary Technicians to support their patients, clients, and teammates in the treatment of companion animal diabetes.

courses.title: BRisky Business: Brachycephalic Anesthesia
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will review congenital issues common to brachycephalic breeds and focus on utilizing brachycephalic risk (BRisk) scoring to assess anesthetic dangers. In addition, this course will include methods to improve safety under anesthesia by implementing brachycephalic protocols plus review best practices to manage brachycephalic patients to optimize peri-operative safety.

courses.title: My Pet has Diabetes
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will review the clinical signs leading to the diagnosis and management of diabetes mellitus in dogs and cats. This course will review the underlying etiologies, appropriate glucose monitoring techniques, and evidence-based treatment options.

courses.title: Suturing for Veterinary Technicians Level 3 (Advanced)
courses.description: This workshop is designed for veterinary technicians to the next level with real tissue handling. This advanced workshop provides access to cadavers to further develop experience with skin apposition. Additional suturing tips, hemostasis and ligature techniques help prepare the veterinary technician for more surgical support.

courses.title: Radiographic Excellence: Essentials for Small Animal Veterinary Teams
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary technicians will provide an overview of the essentials needed to safely and efficiently produce diagnostic radiographs of dogs and cats in small animal veterinary medicine including proper setup, planning the exam, positioning, evaluating the image, and common adjustments for optimal image quality.
(This course was previously presented live in 2025 and was RACE-approved # 20- 1288998.)

courses.title: Letting Go with Love: Euthanasia Loss and Healing
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) program is a recording of a live virtual webinar. This non-medical program for veterinary technicians reviews the emotional impact of euthanasia on pet families and provides tools to support them through the process with empathy and professionalism. In addition, resources to support caregivers with compassion fatigue are presented as well as ways to improve the physical space and procedures for a more compassionate experience.

courses.title: Comfy Kittens: Hospitalized Care of the Obstructed Cat
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) program is a recording of a live virtual webinar.
This program for veterinary technicians reviews the physiology and presentation of feline urinary tract disease and the accompanying obstructed state, in addition to common signalment. This session focuses on emergent stabilization and treatment for both hospitalized patients plus prevention at home.
This course was previously RACE-approved program # 20-1323495.

courses.title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA): The Not So Sweet Side of Diabetes
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) program is a recording of a live virtual webinar. This medical program for veterinary technicians will provide a comprehensive review of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) including pathophysiology, clinical signs, diagnostic approach, treatment protocols, and the critical role technicians play in monitoring and supportive care to improve patient outcomes. This session will also provide practical tips to support both the medical team and patients through this critical condition.

courses.title: Sterile Processing
courses.description: This live interactive non-medical program for veterinary technicians will provide an overview of sterile processing practices focusing on the principles of sterility and infection prevention. This course will examine key sterilization methods, including the differences in types of sterilizers for clinical applications, plus review the use of chemical and biological indicators to ensure effective sterilization and patient safety.

courses.title: Anesthetic Induction of General Anesthesia
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) program is a recording of a live virtual webinar.
This medical program for veterinary technicians reviews the process of induction to general anesthesia. This session includes induction setup, equipment, managing difficult intubations, and detail rapid sequence inductions.
This course was previously RACE-approved program # 20-1323522.

courses.title: Wink at Me & I'll Wenkebach: ECG Interpretation of Anesthetized Patients
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary technicians will review the use of an electrocardiogram (ECG) to monitor patients undergoing sedation and general anesthesia. It is an incredibly useful and necessary tool but can be challenging to read to the untrained eye. In addition, this course will provide an overview on the use of electrocardiograms (including their limitations), the cardiac conduction system and how it correlates to an ECG, plus arrhythmia identification and response.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1242004.)

courses.title: Suturing for Veterinary Technicians Level 1
courses.description: Essentials of skin and how it relates to the body as a whole. This 2-hour webinar covers anatomy and physiology of tissues with a focus on the skin, its growth and repair cycle and the healing process. Includes an overview of suturing knowledge and techniques.

courses.title: Bleeding Disorders: Testing, Treatment, and Transfusions
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary technicians will highlight the clotting cascade, as well as disease processes that affect the cascade and how to test for them. In addition, this program will review the types of transfusions and which disorders respond to which blood products.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1242108.)

courses.title: Dental Emergencies
courses.description: This non-interactive distance (On Demand) program is a recording of a live virtual webinar. This medical program for veterinary technicians reviews multiple types of dental emergencies, including trauma, tumors, and more. This session will also cover clinical presentation, causes, and treatments. This course was previously RACE-approved program # 20-1323504.

courses.title: Equine Emergency First Aid
courses.description: EMERGENCY FIRST AID FOR HORSES PROVIDES AN INTRODUCTORY OVERVIEW OF HOW TO MANAGE COMMON MEDICAL EMERGENCIES WHEN THEY OCCUR IN HORSES. Topics include: Transporting and restraining sick and/or injured horses, how to prepare an emergency plan and first aid kit for your farm, how to perform triage, physical assessments, obtaining vital signs, managing traumatic injuries such as wounds and fractures, how to apply an emergency splint, how to use safety ropes and halters. We will discuss the important supplies that should be found in the equine first aid kit and how to use them as well as how to administer first aid for severe bleeding, burns, eye injuries, digestive Issues, emergencies that happen on the trail and horse shows and more.

courses.title: Understanding and Interacting with the Pain Pathway
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will introduce the pain pathway and its role in patient care. This course will review pain pathway components, how protocols interact with each stage, and the importance of multimodal analgesia in comprehensive pain management for veterinary patients.

courses.title: Blood Pressure Measurements: How Accurate Are Our Numbers?
courses.description:
This non-interactive distance (On Demand) medical program for veterinary technicians will focus on the methods currently available to measure blood pressure (BP), including various methods to measure non-invasive and invasive BP. This program will also provide an overview regarding the pros and cons of measuring non-invasive blood pressure (NIBP) using Doppler and oscillometric blood pressure. In addition, this course will review the research on the accuracy of blood pressure measurement.
(This course was previously presented live in 2024 and was RACE-approved # 20-1242072.)

courses.title: Perfect Pawsition: Mastering Small Animal Radiographs
courses.description: This in-depth lecture and hands-on wet lab will cover advanced techniques for radiographic positioning of the thorax, abdomen, spine and joints of dogs and cats.

courses.title: TOTAL IV ANESTHESIA (637-43304)
courses.description: The lecture is 33 minutes and consists of speaker Kristin Spring, CVT, VTS, CVPP, doing a formal presentation on total IV anesthesia. The accepted best practice for anesthesia has been to induce the patient with and injectable drug, intubate, and maintain on inhalant anesthetics. The alternative to this is total IV anesthesia or TIVA. Learn from Kristin Spring about ideal patients for TIVA, equipment needed, and drug compatibility.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: The Raw Pet Food Diet Trend
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of raw pet food diets by examining the differences between commercial and homemade options, as well as various preservation methods like freeze-drying and high-pressure pasteurization. It outlines the potential health benefits some owners associate with raw feeding while critically evaluating the scientific evidence supporting these claims. The course also highlights significant risks, particularly microbial contamination and nutritional imbalances, which can endanger both pets and humans. Participants will gain tools for informed client communication and learn why veterinary professionals must engage pet owners in balanced, evidence-based discussions about raw diets.

courses.title: Monitoring: What Vitals Really Tell Us (TECH418)
courses.description: Everyone can look at a monitor and document numbers, but how well do you really know what those numbers represent? This self study course provides an in-depth look at manual and equipment monitoring in small animals and what each vital tells us about our patients. As you learn how to interpret these vitals, you can appreciate changes or trends more rapidly, which allows you to intervene appropriately and feel more confident in your decisions.

courses.title: VTNE Review (TECH430)
courses.description: This course reviews the veterinary technicians essential skills, tasks, and knowledge base as outlined in the guidelines set forth by the AVMA CVTEA for approved veterinary technology programs. The material is divided into modules, each with an associated resource library containing poll questions, charts, study guides, interactive games, and videos, to help you organize your study time and improve your competency and test-taking skills in preparation for the VTNE. While this is a self study course, you will benefit the most by engaging actively with the modules and associated resources. As many topics as possible are included to help you identify levels of competency as an aid to focus your study efforts.

courses.title: A Survival Guide: When Veterinary Medicine Kicks you in the Teeth
courses.description: In this course, Dr. Carrie Jurney, DVM, DACVIM (Neurology) tackles the difficult topic of mental health in veterinary medicine. Through this video training, you will learn how to build resiliency as you deal with the day to day tasks of your job. You will also learn the difference between problem based coping and emotional based coping and how these coping tools can help you to manage workplace stress while maintaining a strong mental health.

courses.title: Compassion Fatigue and Mental Health in Veterinary Care: Building a Supportive Culture
courses.description: Have you ever felt emotionally drained after a tough day caring for animals or supporting clients? This course is designed for veterinary staff and technicians who face the unique emotional and mental health challenges of animal care.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF EQUINE VETERINARY TECHNICIANS AND ASSISTANTS
courses.title: AAEVT AAEP Annual Convention 2025 Virtual - 2026
courses.description:
Our 2025 AAEVT Annual Convention, held in conjunction with the AAEP Annual Convention, is a 3 and one half day stand-alone CE event offering multiple medical and non-medical tracks to include scientific, anesthesia and leadership / career enhancement topics. Throughout the convention, participants will have opportunities to choose from 47.5 hours of focused CE sessions led by prominent veterinary medical experts. Beginning with a distinguished keynote speaker followed by a full complement of lectures, roundtable discussions, breakfast / lunch talks, case study presentations as well as a full day of hands-on wet labs, we have organized an event that offers something for everyone at all levels of expertise. Our goal is to provide best practices knowledge, techniques, updates and reviews in all areas for veterinary technicians, assistants and support staff working in equine veterinary practices. Our partnership with AAEP also helps to facilitate many golden opportunities to network and share ideas with other professionals in our industry. All participants will be provided online proceedings and resource materials for reference and sharing with others once they return. Open interaction with speakers will be available throughout the convention for any questions that may arise. Information gained from sessions and networking with fellow participants will be immediately applicable to clinics upon participant return.
Medical topics to include: Anesthesia protocols, tips and tricks, reproduction, nutrition, podiatry, medicine, surgical, care and treatment protocols, and treatment or diagnostic modalities currently available.
Non-Medical topics to include: Team / Practice communications, leadership, engagement, wellness, responsibilities relating to cost of care discussions as well as skill sets for future financial planning and self-advocacy.
In our fourth year offering a virtual component for the AAEVT AAEP Annual Convention 2025, we are proud to present twenty pre-recorded

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: The Veterinary Nurse's Guide to Diagnosis and Management of Feline Infectious Peritonitis
courses.description: This course provides veterinary technicians with an in-depth overview of FIP, crucial to understanding this complex disease. Multiple facets of FIP are discussed including pathogenesis, signalment, manifestation of clinical signs, routine and advanced diagnostics, prognosis, prevention, and treatment. Veterinary technicians need to be prepared to educate clients confronted with an FIP diagnosis, which will enhance the quality of care and support they can provide to them and their cats.

courses.title: Veterinary Team Telehealth
courses.description: This program prepares veterinary healthcare team members to provide telehealth services to patients and clients in a virtual environment. Students will learn key terminology, legal regulations, communication strategies for telecommunication, how to apply those communication skills when performing teletriage, and the importance of effective workflows and standard operating procedures.

courses.title: KYON: Total Hip Replacement THR for Veterinary Technicians
courses.description: KYON Total Hip Replacement THR for Veterinary Technicians Online Course is designed to prepare veterinary technicians to assist in a KYON THR procedure. First the course defines hip dysplasia and describes indications for total hip replacements. It reviews correct positions and techniques for pre and postoperative radiographs. The course summarizes the surgical procedure from a veterinary technicians point of view, highlighting important steps where the veterinary technician plays a vital role. Finally, the course summarizes recovery, discusses risks of THR, and reviews considerations for a successful THR veterinary technician.

courses.title: Some like it Hot! Heatstroke in Dogs (TECH413)
courses.description: Heatstroke is a common problem during the summer months and can affect any breed of dog. Heatstroke is a life threatening condition that requires quick treatment. Knowing what to look for and how to treat animals in heatstroke can make a difference between life and death.

courses.title: Orthopedics for Veterinary Technicians Online Course
courses.description: Orthopedics for Veterinary Technicians Online Course is designed to provide technicians with a foundation in orthopedic patients, preoperative and postoperative managing of a surgery, the importance of sterilization, and how to assist an orthopedic surgeon. It also covers critical responsibilities such as sterilization, instrument care, and radiology safety. By the end of this course, learners will be prepared to contribute to orthopedic surgical teams and provide optimal care for orthopedic patients.

courses.title: CPR
courses.description: The purpose of the course in the CPR program is to help participants recognize and respond appropriately to cardiac, breathing and first aid emergencies to know to give immediate care to a suddenly injured or ill animal until more advanced medical personnel arrive and take over.

courses.title: RACE I: Equine Sociology, Physiology and Gastrointestinal Health
courses.description: This course is divided into four sections, all of which are relevant to the gastrointestinal health and overall well-being of the horse. The first two sections, Equine Sociology and Equine Physiology, provide the student with knowledge of equine social structure and physiological adaptions to grassland ecology. The various components of equine internal anatomy relevant to the general physical examination of the horse are discussed. In the third section, Equine Nutrition, the intricacies of digestion and hindgut fermentation are further examined as well as pathology of the gastrointestinal tract related to diet. Forage, grains, and supplements are discussed. The final section of this course, Equine Dentistry, covers the anatomy and eruption of equine teeth. Normal and abnormal occlusion is discussed with regard to diet. Equipment necessary for and the role of the veterinary technician and the veterinarian in dental maintenance and correction procedures is discussed.

courses.title: Aseptic Skin Preparation for Canine and Feline Surgery: A Practical Guide
courses.description: Are you ready to master the essential skills for preparing canine and feline patients for surgery? In this course, you'll learn the evidence-based steps and best practices for aseptic skin preparation, helping you minimize the risk of surgical site infections and support optimal patient outcomes. Through clear explanations, practical demonstrations, and real-world scenarios, you'll gain confidence in selecting supplies, performing safe clipping and antiseptic techniques, and adapting protocols for special cases. By the end, you'll be equipped to apply safety checklists and quality controls, ensuring every surgical prep is performed to the highest standard.

courses.title: Advances in Nutrition
courses.description:
This online course for veterinary nurses and veterinary technicians will cover a range of clinical nutritional issues commonly encountered in first opinion practice. These will include patients with diabetes mellitus, cardiac disease, liver compromise, and dermatology conditions. We will investigate how nutrition plays a vital role in each of these conditions, and how specific nutrients can exacerbate or improve clinical signs in our veterinary patients.
This is an on-demand four module course with unlimited lifetime access, where each module consists of a tutorial, quiz and further reading.
Module 1: Diabetes Mellitus
Module 2: Cardiac Disease
Module 3: Hepatic Disease
Module 4: Dermatological Disease

courses.title: Sweet Dreams - Veterinary Anesthesia for Nurses
courses.description:
5 modules that include a 1 hour webinar, handouts and a 25 MCQ test on completion.
Got the basics down but ready to advance your anesthesia knowledge? In this anesthesia course Jennifer will present the following modules. Be prepared to take a deep look into the pathophysiology of disease processes, to learn about advanced regional blocks, and feel confident monitoring anesthesia and developing anesthetic protocols for any patient.
Modules as follows:
Anesthesia Waveforms: Interpreting the Monitor
Feline Friendly Anesthesia
Anesthesia for Pediatrics and Pregnancy
Anesthesia and Systemic Disease
Anesthesia and Analgesia for Thoracic Surgery

courses.title: Introduction to ECG Interpretation - Just the Basics Please (TECH414)
courses.description: Understanding electrocardiogram waveforms can be overwhelming; sometimes, it is even difficult to know if what you are seeing is normal or not! This lecture will describe five simple steps to recognize if a waveform is normal or abnormal. We will review the movement of electrical impulses through the heart and how that is reflected on the ECG monitor. Examples will be shared to practice interpreting common arrhythmias.

courses.title: Arizona Veterinary Technician Annual Conference
courses.description: The Arizona Veterinary Technician Association meets annually to provide CE credit to our members as well as conduct our annual meeting and awards.

courses.title: Veterinary Anesthesia Refresher Certificate: Course 1 Anesthetic protocols
courses.description:
The Veterinary Anesthesia Refresher Certificate is a comprehensive anesthesia refresher program primarily targeted to Registered Veterinary Technologists and Technicians (RVTs). The certificate program consists of 4 stand-alone courses each a prerequisite for the next. The first 3 courses are online-asynchronous, and the 4th course is a 4 day in-person SIM-based wet lab (location: Douglas College, British Columbia, Canada). Courses 1-3 must be completed with a grade of 75 percent or higher on the final exam, prior to taking the 4th wet lab course.
Topics included in course #1 are: a review of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, anatomy and physiology of the nervous system, anesthetic and analgesic drugs, and a team approach to safe anesthesia through the development of safe effective anesthetic protocols.
Each of the 5 unit includes 45-90 minutes recorded lecture, 30 minutes reading, 30-60 minute student activity (e.g. case studies, assignments etc), plus an end of unit quiz (30 minutes).
Keywords: anesthesia, patient care, analgesia, pharmacology, drugs, fluid therapy, critical thinking, problem solving.

courses.title: Veterinary CPR and Resuscitation: Best Practices for Animal Care Teams
courses.description: Preparation, organization, and teamwork are the foundation of successful veterinary CPR. When every second counts, having a well-organized resuscitation area and a fully stocked crash cart can make the difference between life and death. Readiness ensures that the team can respond rapidly and efficiently, minimizing delays and maximizing the chances of a positive outcome for the patient.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Immunizations or Vaccines?
courses.description: Vaccinating and immunizations are often used interchangeably; however, they are pretty different. Vaccinations are the actual physical action of immunizing a patient against disease. Immunizations are the pharmacological agents introduced into the body to prevent disease through an immune response of the patient.

courses.title: KYON: Total Hip Replacement (THR) for Veterinary Technicians Online Course
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare veterinary technicians to assist in a KYON THR procedure. First the course defines hip dysplasia and describes indications for total hip replacements. It reviews correct positions and techniques for pre and postoperative radiographs. The course summarizes the surgical procedure from a veterinary technicians point of view, highlighting important steps where the veterinary technician plays a vital role. Finally the course summarizes recovery, discusses risks of THR, and reviews considerations for a successful THR veterinary technician.

courses.title: Small Animal Radiographic Imaging Fundamentals for Veterinary Technicians
courses.description: In this course, you'll gain the essential knowledge and hands-on techniques needed to confidently and safely perform small animal radiographs.

courses.title: BioMedtrix: Total Hip Replacement (THR) for Veterinary Technicians Online Course
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare veterinary technicians to assist in a BioMedtrix THR procedure. First the course defines hip dysplasia and describes indications for total hip replacements. It reviews correct positions and techniques for pre and postoperative radiographs. The course summarizes the surgical procedure from a veterinary technicians point of view, highlighting important steps where the veterinary technician plays a vital role. Finally, the course summarizes recovery, discusses risks of THR, and reviews considerations for a successful THR veterinary technician.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Golden Years: Treasuring the Senior Years of Our Furry Friends
courses.description:
The 2023 AAHA Senior Care Guidelines for Dogs and Cats provide veterinary teams with a thorough framework to enhance the quality and longevity of life for aging pets. Recognizing that aging itself is not a disease, the guidelines stress the importance of individualized wellness care, proactive health screenings, tailored nutrition, and routine communication with pet owners.
Senior pets are defined as those in roughly the last quarter of their expected lifespan, with age thresholds adjusted for species and size. The guidelines recommend regular comprehensive exams, including lab work, pain assessments, and behavioral screenings, to detect and manage age-related conditions early. A senior-friendly clinic environment, equipped with accessible facilities and staffed by professionals trained in low-stress handling, helps encourage routine care visits.
Nutritional management is emphasized, both for healthy seniors and those with chronic illnesses, with diet plans adjusted to medical status, and guidance provided for safe food transitions. As pets approach the end of life, compassionate communication, palliative care, and support for both pets and families are highlighted as crucial to maintaining comfort and dignity. Overall, the AAHA's approach centers on collaboration, prevention, and emotional support, ensuring that senior pets remain cherished family members throughout their lives.

courses.title: Anesthesia Considerations
courses.description:
This online course for veterinary nurses and veterinary technicians aims to highlight patients that require specific consideration and individual planning prior to general anesthesia. These patients include the paediatric and senior patient, the underweight and overweight patient, patients with chronic renal disease and hyperadrenocorticism. The final module to complete the course is cardiopulmonary resuscitation, a subject that is always a common request, which includes the updated RECOVER guidelines from 2024.
This is an on-demand four module course with unlimited lifetime access, where each module consists of a tutorial, quiz and further reading.
Module 1: The Young, The Old, and Anesthesia!
Module 2: Anesthesia Considerations for Overweight and Underweight Patients
Module 3: Renal, Adrenals and Anesthesia!
Module 4: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Obesity in Companion Animals; A Kaleidoscope View from Veterinary Technician Specialists
courses.description: As with people, pets suffer from being overweight and obese. Increased body weight leading to obesity causes decreased quality of life and increased risk for comorbidities. Given the occurrence of obesity in our companion animal patients, primary care veterinary professionals are faced increasingly with having to manage obesity as an additional consideration when providing care. In this course veterinary professionals gain unique perspectives from veterinary technician specialists about their top concerns and considerations when providing care to an overweight or obese patient. Understanding others' unique perspectives can improve the overall care veterinary professionals provide for their patients.

courses.title: Alternative Veterinary Diets
courses.description:
This online course for veterinary nurses and veterinary technicians will discuss the various different alternative diets available for our pets.
The pet food industry is vastly varied which makes choosing a suitable, safe diet hugely challenging, particularly in the face of overwhelming amounts of information, misinformation, and strong divided opinion. This course will separate fact from fiction by evaluating the latest available evidence for four of the common alternative diets types which are increasingly being fed to dogs and cats:
Module 1: Grain free diets
Module 2: Home-prepared cooked diets
Module 3: Raw meat-based diets
Module 4: Plant-based diets
As with all veterinary medicine, it is vital that a recommendation should be evidence based and so for each diet type the course will evaluate the evidence for and against its use, alongside highlighting where further work is required. Each of the four diet types have associated risks, but also associated potential benefits which should be carefully considered.
Our role as veterinary professionals is not to dictate what pet owners should feed their pet, but to provide support through information and education by becoming a reliable resource a pet owner can trust. Our aim is to support pet owners so that in the full knowledge of the facts they can make informed decisions when they choose a diet to feed their pet. Ultimately some pet owners will continue to wish to feed a diet which is not recommended. The course will therefore examine ways in which safety can be improved and will detail where to find specialist help and reliable information, so support is always given to every pet.
This is an on-demand four module course with unlimited lifetime access, where each module consists of a tutorial, quiz and further reading.

courses.title: Advanced Veterinary Nursing of Rabbits
courses.description: This program is designed for experienced veterinary nurses and technicians seeking advanced knowledge and skills in the care and management of rabbits. The course covers a comprehensive range of topics from basic husbandry and care to advanced medical procedures, challenging participants to deepen their expertise in exotic pet nursing. Emphasizing evidence-based practices, this course prepares attendees to deliver high-quality care to rabbits in various clinical settings.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF EQUINE VETERINARY TECHNICIANS AND ASSISTANTS
courses.title: AAEVT AAEP Annual Convention 2024 Virtual - 2025
courses.description: Our 2024 AAEVT AAEP Annual Convention held in conjunction with the AAEP Annual Convention, is a three and one half day stand-alone CE event offering multiple medical and non-medical tracks to include scientific, anesthesia and leadership / career enhancement topics. Throughout the convention, participants will have opportunities to choose from 48 hours of focused CE sessions led by prominent veterinary medical experts.Beginning with a distinguished keynote speaker followed by a full complement of lectures, roundtable discussions, breakfast / lunch talks, case study presentations as well as a full day of hands-on wet labs, we have organized an event that offers something for everyone at all levels of expertise. Our goal is to provide best practices knowledge, techniques, updates and reviews in all areas for veterinary technicians, assistants and support staff working in equine veterinary practices. Our partnership with AAEP also helps to facilitate many golden opportunities to network and share ideas with other professionals in our industry. All participants will be provided proceedings and resource materials for reference and sharing with others once they return. Open interaction with speakers will be available throughout the convention for any questions that may arise. Information gained from sessions and networking with fellow participants will be immediately applicable to clinics upon participant return. Medical topics to include: Anesthesia protocols, tips and tricks, reproduction, nutrition, podiatry, medicine, surgical and treatment protocols, and treatment or diagnostic modalities currently available. Non-Medical topics to include: Team / Practice communications, leadership, engagement, wellness, responsibilities relating to cost of care discussions as well as skill sets for future financial planning and self-advocacy. In our third year offering a virtual component for the AAEVT AAEP Annual Convention 2024, we are proud to present twenty pre-recorded sessions

courses.title: Nutrition for Life
courses.description:
This online course for veterinary nurses and veterinary technicians will cover life stage nutrition in our canine and feline patients. From birth, correct nutrition is vital for a puppy or kitten's health and survival, shaping their well-being throughout their entire life. This course explores the evolving nutritional needs at each life stage, providing an in-depth understanding of key dietary considerations. Participants will gain the knowledge, confidence, and skills to make tailored, dynamic nutritional recommendations for pets of all ages. Additionally, the course covers essential strategies for preventing overfeeding, guiding pet owners in maintaining a healthy weight for their pets, and teaching participants fundamental clinical examination techniques needed to identify health concerns.
This is an on-demand six module course with unlimited lifetime access, where each module consists of a tutorial, quiz and further reading.
Module 1: From Conception to Weaning
Module 2: Growth
Module 3: Adult Maintenance
Module 4: Senior Pets
Module 5: Diet Choices
Module 6: Maintaining an Ideal Weight

courses.title: Surgical Monitoring of Wildlife: Avian Anesthesia
courses.description:
With a focus on monitoring wild avian species for surgical procedures, attendees will first strengthen their understanding of avian anatomy and physiology while connecting these unique features to their anesthetic impacts. This application of knowledge lends to being able to safely monitor wildlife avian anesthesia from induction through to recovery. Further, discussing the technical aspects behind the skills necessary to safely support avian patients makes the connection between knowledge and application seamless.
Anesthesia on wildlife avian patients is not inherently more dangerous than working with mammalian patients. Grow your confidence and learn how to be a medical advocate for wildlife avian species.

courses.title: Blood Draw
courses.description: Drawing blood correctly from animals is crucial for obtaining accurate diagnostic results, minimizing animal distress, and ensuring the safety of both the animal and the personnel involved. Proper technique prevents contamination, hemolysis (blood cell damage), and other factors that can skew test results. In this course, you will learn how to perform a correct blood draw.

courses.title: Veterinary Anesthesia Refresher Certificate: Course 2 Safe Anesthetic Administration
courses.description: The Veterinary Anesthesia Refresher Certificate is a comprehensive anesthesia refresher program primarily targeted to Registered Veterinary Technologists and Technicians (RVTs). The certificate program consists of 4 stand-alone courses each a prerequisite for the next. The first 3 courses are online-asynchronous, and the 4th course is a 4 day in-person SIM-based wet lab (location: Douglas College, British Columbia, Canada). Courses 1-3 must be completed with a grade of 75 percent or higher on the final exam, prior to taking the 4th wet lab course. Topics included in course #2 are: patient assessment, anesthetic equipment, anesthesia and the cardiorespiratory system, introduction to anesthetic monitoring, anesthetic case studies and protocols. Each unit includes 45-90 minutes recorded lecture, 30 minutes reading, 30-60 minute student activity (e.g. case studies, assignments etc), plus an end of unit quiz (30 minutes). Keywords: anesthesia, anesthetic equipment, anesthetic monitoring, patient care, analgesia, pharmacology, drugs, fluid therapy, CPR, critical thinking, problem solving, emergency care.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Why the Microbiome Matters for Pet Health Microbiome Science
courses.description: Microbiome science is an exciting and evolving field in veterinary medicine. However, it is an emerging field with a lot of ongoing research that will likely shape the future of veterinary microbiome science. This article covers some of the main concepts about veterinary microbiome science and medicine as well as some of the challenges in this field.

courses.title: The Room is Spinning! Vestibular Disease in Companion Animals (TECH412)
courses.description:
Course Information:
Vestibular disease is a fairly common problem in small animals that can have a very dramatic presentation. This lecture will cover the pathophysiology of vestibular disease, and the signs associated with it. We will also discuss treatment and nursing considerations for patients who feel like their world is spinning.
Learning Objectives:
Upon completion of this course, the participant should be able to:
1. Examine the anatomy of the vestibular system
2. Describe the signs associated with vestibular disease
3. Discuss peripheral and central localization of vestibular disease
Level and Prerequisites: This intermediate CE course will be open for enrollment to veterinary technicians/technologists, support staff, veterinary teams, actively interested in vestibular disease.

courses.title: Smooth Delivery: Anesthetic Management of Emergency Cesarian Sections
courses.description: Emergency cesarean sections present unique anesthetic challenges that require rapid assessment, efficient stabilization, and careful balancing of maternal and neonatal outcomes. This lecture is designed for veterinary technicians and will provide practical, evidence-based approaches to the anesthetic management of canine and feline emergency C-sections. Participants will also learn essential techniques for neonatal assessment, resuscitation, and immediate post-delivery care to improve neonatal survival. Emphasis will be placed on rapid decision-making, effective team communication, and practical skills that veterinary technicians can confidently apply in both emergency and general practice settings.

courses.title: Certificate in Emergency and Critical Care Nursing
courses.description: The Veterinary Technician Certificate in Emergency and Critical Care has been designed to expand the emergency and critical care nursing knowledge and skills, improving their confidence in this area and is appropriate for general practice and referral nurses. Delegates will learn the fundamental principles of nursing patients that present as emergencies and how best to nurse them to optimise their care and welfare.

courses.title: Veterinary OR Setup and Infection Control: Best Practices for Technicians
courses.description: In this course, you'll learn how to efficiently and safely prepare a veterinary operating room, mastering infection control and ensuring every procedure starts with confidence. Through step-by-step lessons, you'll discover how to identify infection control zones, implement rigorous cleaning and sterilization techniques, assemble equipment, apply PPE and hand hygiene, and perform critical equipment checks.

courses.title: THR for Veterinary Surgical Technicians Workshop
courses.description:
The Total Hip Replacement for Veterinary Surgical Technicians Workshop will provide a full day of hands-on instruction. Participants of this workshop will learn recommended pre-op and post-op patient care, how to take well-positioned x-rays, surgery-day preparation, and responsibilities including proper patient clipping, positioning, and draping for THR. Additional topics will include Inventory Management as well as suggested communication and relationship-building with both pet parents and the referring veterinarian.
Course participants will also have the opportunity to experience both sides of the operating table, along with time for Q&A throughout three THR procedures; Cemented, Cementless, and a Hybrid THR

courses.title: RACE II: Equine Musculoskeletal Anatomy, Physiology and Lameness Diagnosis
courses.description: his course is divided into six lessons all of which are relevant to musculoskeletal structure, function and pathology. The first two lessons discuss normal anatomy. Lesson 1, Equine Musculoskeletal Anatomy, covers the anatomical and common names for the structures and regions of the horse. Lesson Two, The Equine Hoof, covers the anatomy and biomechanics of a healthy equine hoof and the evolutionary and environmental influences on hoof structure. Included is a discussion on the barefoot versus the shod horse and guidelines on how to assess the quality of trimming and shoeing. The third lesson educates the student in evaluating conformation to determine for what discipline a horse's conformation is best suited, to understand how physical issues may arise from less than ideal conformation, to recognize conformation faults that may lead to unsoundness. Lesson Four, The Equine Lameness Exam, discusses how to recognize lameness and the steps necessary to pinpoint the source of the lameness. The steps of the systematic exam are discussed as well as the roles of the veterinarian and the assistant in the lameness evaluation. Once the source of lameness is identified, it is necessary to visualize the affected structures. In the fifth lesson, the student learns how to assist in taking radiographic images. Proper radiographic safety and techniques and common nomenclature and equipment used for lameness diagnostics is covered. Once the lameness exam and diagnostic imaging is complete, the veterinarian often makes a diagnosis. The sixth lesson covers many of the most common musculoskeletal diseases diagnosed in the horse.

courses.title: VetTechnicalities: Triage
courses.description: Evaluate the patient. Calm the clients. Notify the team. Treat the patient. Repeat! Veterinary technicians and nurses are the first responders in the ER, and triaging requires more than a brief once-over. This course covers every aspect of an ER veterinary triage, from input to intake, and informs you how to implement effective triage into your practice. Useful for general practices and specialty centers, via telemedicine and in-person. You won't just be reading a temperature; you will be reading the whole room.

courses.title: Orthopedic Instrumentation for Veterinary Technicians
courses.description: Short description: Orthopedic Instrumentation for Veterinary Technicians Online Course is designed to give a comprehensive overview of commonly used veterinary instrumentation with a focus on instrumentation used in orthopedic procedures. The course reviews instrument anatomy, key features, and outlines preoperative and postoperative instrument handing, cleaning, sterilization, maintenance, and care.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF EQUINE VETERINARY TECHNICIANS AND ASSISTANTS
courses.title: AAEVT AAEP Annual Convention 2023 Virtual
courses.description:
Our 2023 AAEVT AAEP Annual Convention, held in conjunction with the AAEP Annual Convention, is a three and one-half day stand-alone CE event offering multiple medical and non-medical tracks to include scientific, anesthesia and leadership / career enhancement topics. Throughout the convention, participants will have opportunities to choose from 46 hours of focused CE sessions led by prominent veterinary medical experts.
