In our second year offering a virtual component for the AAEVT AAEP Annual Convention 2023, we are proud to present sixteen pre-recorded sessions. These sessions have been carefully selected from our current speaker roster to cater to those who are unable

courses.title: Elevate Emergency Nursing Program
courses.description: The Elevate Emergency Nursing Program is the solution for veterinary nurses and veterinary techs who want to be confident in their management of emergency patients, enhance their current knowledge and take their emergency skills to the next level. The Elevate Emergency Program has been designed and developed by a team of Animal Emergency Service Nurses, Technicians and Vets. The team have years of combined clinical emergency experience and know-how in fast paced AES hospitals across Australia and have helped mentor nurses and techs across the practices in becoming fully confident and valued emergency colleagues. The Elevate program grew from the need to bridge the knowledge gap between general practice and emergency and critical care nursing. The Elevate Nursing Program is built with relevant, practical and case-based care in mind and, in plain nurse speak.

courses.title: Clinical Nutrition
courses.description:
This online course for veterinary nurses and veterinary technicians will cover a range of clinical nutritional issues commonly encountered in first opinion practice. These will include those animals (feline and canine) with renal disease, liver compromise, gastrointestinal disturbances, pancreatitis and urinary issues. We will investigate the root cause of inappetence and how pharmaceutical and nutritional support can aid in increasing calorific and nutrient intake. In all these cases we will be looking at the evidence base behind the claims of diets and supplements and whether they are of benefit to our patients. We will look at nutritional fashions and how to talk to clients about new trends that seem to be highlighted on-line almost continually. In order to do this, we will have some case studies to work through where we can discuss different options for nutritional management.
This is an on-demand four module course with unlimited lifetime access, where each module consists of a tutorial, quiz and further reading.
Module 1: Nutritional Assessment and Calculations
Module 2: Renal, Urinary, Liver and Cardiac Nutrition
Module 3: Gastrointestinal and Pancreatic Nutrition
Module 4: Nutritional Supplements and Trends

courses.title: Neurology in Practice
courses.description:
This online course for veterinary nurses and veterinary technicians will cover a range of neurological conditions commonly encountered in general practice. Although neurological patients may seem daunting initially, by working step-by-step from the patient's history, through the diagnosis, to their treatment and nursing care, we can make these cases less daunting and more rewarding.
Each module will look at a different aspect of veterinary neurology so that you gain a full picture of how and why certain treatment options are preformed/required. Following the course, you can apply the knowledge of various conditions and how these will affect the nursing care requirements of the patient, to produce successful nursing care plans, as well as fully support your clients that have pets with on-going neurological needs at home.
This is an on-demand six module course with unlimited lifetime access, where each module consists of a tutorial, quiz and further reading.
Module 1: Patient History and Assessment
Module 2: Diagnostics
Module 3: Spinal Conditions
Module 4: Brain Disease
Module 5: Neuromuscular Disease
Module 6: Nursing the Neurological Patient

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Otitis: Weighing All the Factors
courses.description: This course provides a review of ear anatomy and an explanation of how the four factors of ear disease play a role in otitis. It also discusses the successful treatment of ear disease.

courses.title: Veterinary Anesthesia Refresher Certificate: Course 3 Anesthetic Emergencies
courses.description: The Veterinary Anesthesia Refresher Certificate is a comprehensive anesthesia refresher program primarily targeted to Registered Veterinary Technologists and Technicians (RVTs). The certificate program consists of 4 stand-alone courses each a prerequisite for the next. The first 3 courses are online-asynchronous, and the 4th course is a 4 day in-person SIM-based wet lab (location: Douglas College, British Columbia, Canada). Courses 1-3 must be completed with a grade of 75% or higher on the final exam, prior to taking the 4th wet lab course. Topics included in course #3 are: Fluid therapy and shock, prevention and treatment of anesthetic emergencies, recognition and treatment of arrhythmias, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation - preparation, crash kit and case scenarios. Each unit includes 45-90 minutes recorded lecture, 30 minutes reading, 30-60 minute student activity (e.g. case studies, assignments etc), plus an end of unit quiz (30 minutes). Keywords: anesthesia, anesthetic equipment, anesthetic monitoring, patient care, analgesia, pharmacology, drugs, fluid therapy, CPR, critical thinking, problem solving, emergency care.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Modernizing Pet Food Labels
courses.description: Pet food labels have been updated. Four major changes have been communicated. The major changes were the addition of an intended use statement, a pet nutrition facts box, a voluntary handling & storage statement, and updates to the ingredient statement. There were also some minor changes to definitions and terms, the label format & labeling, feeding directions, and descriptive terms. Pet food companies have 6 years from 2024 to update their packages, so for the next 6 years both labels may be found on pet food packages. From a nutritional and regulatory standpoint, the final regulations may be difficult for pet parents to understand. It is important that the health care team understands the new regulations and can help the pet parent understand the changes and how it may affect their decision to purchase the food.

courses.title: The Nutritional Assessment
courses.description:
The importance of nutrition in health and well-being has long been recognized. In fact, nutrition is recognized as the fifth vital assessment, but may be an untapped opportunity in practice promoting optimal nutrition. A nutritional assessment should be a part of every pet's visit to the practice and is an excellent opportunity for a veterinary technician to operate at the top of their license.
During this webinar we will discuss the step-by-step approach to completing a nutrition assessment including nutritional factors to consider when making a diet selection and creating a feeding plan. That can reveal that an adjustment may be needed from their current feeding routine. Next, we will dive into how to calculate a pets Ideal Body Weight, energy needs and how to create a feeding plan.

courses.title: A Step-By-Step Approach to Canine and Feline Weight Loss
courses.description: More and more pets are tipping the scale. Obesity, described as excess body weight that contributes to impaired health and body function, is the most common nutritional disease seen in companion animals. Obesity can result from animal factors, such as breed or spay/neuter status, or from considerations related to their owners, such as diet choice or feeding methods. This presentation reviews the adverse consequences of obesity and discusses treatment strategies that can help with healthy and successful weight loss in overweight dogs and cats. Cases will also be shared to further understanding of these strategies.

courses.title: How to Read a Pet Food Label - On Demand
courses.description: By participating in this lecture, you will learn what is required on a pet food label, what agencies in the US are responsible for pet food label regulations and rules associated with pet food labels.

courses.title: Medical Nursing Academy Library Club
courses.description: The medical nursing academy's on-demand library club provides a hub of interactive and relevant on-demand virtual CPD/CE for veterinary nurses and technicians in the field of internal medicine.

courses.title: TCVM for Veterinary Technicians Online
courses.description: TCVM for Veterinary Technicians is a course designed to teach veterinary technicians to support and promote TCVM services in your practice. Through the course, technicians are given the tools to speak knowledgeably about the purpose and value of TCVM and to teach clients how to care for their animals with food therapy and Tui-na techniques. Tailored for veterinary technicians working in clinics and hospitals where TCVM is practiced, this course concentrates on TCVM theoretical principles as well as practical techniques to allow vet techs to best assist TCVM veterinarians. A reference letter from a licensed veterinarian is required to enroll in this course. Please note that no information about TCVM diagnosis or locations of acupuncture points will be covered in this course.

courses.title: Getting Cats to eat: It is More than Pouring Food into a Bowl
courses.description: Proper nutritional management is one of the most important factors in maximizing health, performance, and longevity in cats, in addition to managing disease conditions. Proper nutrition and care throughout a cat's life maximizes health, longevity, and quality of life. Domestic cats and other members of the superfamily Feloidea are strict obligate carnivores. This difference from dogs is supported by specific behavioral, anatomic, physiologic, and metabolic adaptations of cats to a strictly carnivorous diet. This presentation will investigate the unique nutritional needs of cats. The veterinary healthcare team should be the preferred, expert source of the best nutritional information for pets. This session will review the physiology and behavior of feeding cats, along with tips to ensure cats are getting the nutrients they need.

courses.title: VACCINES: WHY ARE WE VACCINATING? (637-36396)
courses.description: Vaccines offer protection against infectious diseases for individual pets and for herd immunity. When vaccines lapse, outbreaks occur. AAHA (American Animal Hospital Association) and AAFP (American Association of Feline Practitioners) have created guidelines for veterinarians based on scientific research. The guidelines include Core, Noncore, Conditionally Licensed Vaccines as well as vaccines that are not recommended. This lecture is 60 minutes and consists of speaker Becky Smith, CVT, VTS (Clinical Practice Canine/Feline) doing a formal presentation on the AAHA/AAFP guidelines for vaccines in dogs and cats.

courses.title: ZOONOTIC DISEASES PROTECTING YOURSELF AND YOUR CLIENTS (637-36954)
courses.description: The lecture is 63 minutes and consists of a speaker Becky Smith, CVT, VTS (Clinical Practice) doing a formal presentation on zoonotic diseases. This course discusses common zoonotic diseases, their modes of transmission, and how to educate staff and clients on how to prevent these diseases from spreading.

courses.title: RECORDED SESSIONS for 45th Annual Meeting of the Association of Zoo Veterinary Technicians (AZVT)
courses.description: The Annual Meeting of the Association of Zoo Veterinary Technicians (AZVT) offers a variety of educational workshops, presentations, and posters on topics that relate to general medical and non-medical topics in veterinary medicine as well as specific topics associated with wildlife, zoo, or aquarium animals and their medical care. This meeting offers continuing education for veterinary technicians working in a zoo, a quarium, or wildlife setting. These presentations were recorded and will be available to the AZVT membership for a limited time following the conference. There are 24 presentations covering a range of topics (see Agenda and Objectives) for the RECORDED 2025 conference.

courses.title: RESPIRATORY REVIEW NURSING STRATEGIES FOR OXYGEN ADMINISTRATION (637-36190)
courses.description: Respiratory distress is one of the most commonly seen emergencies in veterinary medicine. These patients present with a variety of clinical signs and diseases that are the insult initiating the crisis event. Review the technician's role in supporting respiratory emergencies with Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS (ECC).

courses.title: BUGS, WOUNDS, AND YOU (637-36602)
courses.description: This 55 minute lecture is presented by Kristin Spring, CVT, VTS (ECC, Anesthesia), CVPP and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on the physiology of wound healing. Learn about the different classes of wound, MRSA, and bandaging techniques.

courses.title: Blood Collection
courses.description: This course covers venipuncture techniques and restraint methods used in the process of obtaining blood samples from commonly used canine and feline veins.

courses.title: ANESTHETIC COMPLICATIONS (637-39671)
courses.description: The lecture is 1 hour presented by Kristin Spring CVT, VTS (ECC, Anesth), CVPP and includes a formal presentation on anesthetic complications and solutions for veterinary technicians in the emergency and general practice field.

courses.title: Preventive Medicine and Client Care in the Age of COVID
courses.description: What can staff do to help reassure clients about what is happening inside the clinic during a pandemic? In this lecture presented by Technician Becky Smith, CVT, VTS (Clinical Practice Canine/Feline) we will discuss how we can interact and educate clients on preventive care (including oral health, vaccines and monthly preventives) from a distance.

courses.title: The Technician's Role in the Assessment and Treatment of Hypoperfusion
courses.description: Fluid therapy is a hot topic in veterinary medicine, specifically with a focus on individual patient response to volume resuscitation. The veterinary technician plays an integral role in assessing hydration and closely monitoring patients who are receiving fluid therapy. This lecture presented by Patient Care and Educational Specialist Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS(ECC), we will include a review on hypoperfusion, hypotension, understanding perfusion parameters and a variety of treatments to consider.

courses.title: Emergency Bandaging Essentials for Dogs and Cats
courses.description:
Emergency Bandaging Essentials for Dogs and Cats is a course designed for veterinary staff seeking to strengthen practical wound management and stabilization skills in small animal patients. This course reviews the principles of effective bandage application, including the structure and function of the standard three-layer bandage system (primary, secondary, and tertiary layers) and its role in hemorrhage control, wound protection, edema reduction, and temporary immobilization.
Participants will evaluate appropriate material selection for various clinical and field scenarios, including use of non-adherent dressings, padding, conforming gauze, cohesive bandages, and improvised support materials. Emphasis is placed on proper technique to minimize complications such as vascular compromise, pressure necrosis, bandage slippage, and impaired lymphatic return.
The course includes step-by-step application techniques for common bandages (distal limb, paw, and supportive wraps), introduction to temporary splinting for suspected fractures, and use of slings for patient stabilization and transport. Clinical decision-making is reinforced through discussion of indications, contraindications, and limitations of field bandaging, with clear differentiation between temporary stabilization and definitive veterinary care.
This course is appropriate for veterinary technicians in clinical, shelter, and field settings who require competency in rapid, safe, and effective bandaging techniques as part of emergency patient management.

courses.title: COMMON TOXICITIES (637-39724)
courses.description: This lecture, presented by certified veterinary technician Megan Brashear, CVT, VTS, is 60 minutes and consists of a formal presentation on common toxicities seen in both the emergency room and the general practice animal hospital.

courses.title: DOUBLE VISION (637-36238)
courses.description: Veterinarians and technicians rely on one another every day to perform their jobs. Learn from veterinarian Christy Michael, BVMS, and Megan Brashear, CVT, VTS (ECC) about how to improve communication, simplify hospital processes, and have an overall better experience in day to day roles.

courses.title: URINE TROUBLE: UNDERSTANDING DIAGNOSTIC MARKERS OF RENAL DYSFUNCTION (637-43252)
courses.description: Kidney disease is very common in companion animals. Clinical signs of renal disease don't occur until kidneys have lost at least 75% of their function, making routine diagnostics key in early recognition of disease. This lecture presented by DoveLewis Technician Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS(ECC), will provide a review of available diagnostics, how they work, and what they tell us.

courses.title: Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN) in Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: In this 16min demonstration and discussion, DoveLewis Technician Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS (ECC) walks viewers through total parenteral nutrition (TPN). Speaker discusses equipment, techniques, safety considerations, and patient nursing care.

courses.title: GETTING STARTED WITH DENTAL CHARTING (637-39325)
courses.description: This is a 63 minute lecture presented by Becky Smtih, CVT, VTS (Clinical Practice Canine-Feline) about the importance of dental charting in the small animal practice. First covered are the reasons why dental charting is important as well as some examples of different charts available to use.

courses.title: Exotic Animal Triage and Stabilization
courses.description: Interested in learning how to properly triage and provide care for exotic animal species that come to your clinic? In this lecture provided by DoveLewis Exotics Technician Jamie Michaelis, CVT, we will discuss how to gather patient history and basic vitals for exotic animals in an emergency room setting. You will learn techniques for observing the patient and identifying when they are in distress or discomfort. We will also cover basic husbandry needs that can be provided by the technician team during triage. Finally, we will discuss CPR options for each species.

courses.title: Technician Multidisciplinary Rounds: Blood Gases
courses.description: This lecture presented by Director of Patient Care Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS (ECC) will go over the fundamentals of acid-base balance and blood gas analysis, which are essential for healthcare professionals across various specialties. It revolves around understanding pH as a measure of acidity or alkalinity in bodily fluids like blood and urine. Knowledge of acid-base balance and blood gas analysis is crucial for assessing patient health, guiding treatment decisions, and interpreting test results effectively in clinical practice.

courses.title: ETCO2- WHAT EVERY TECHNICIAN SHOULD KNOW (637-38569)
courses.description: DoveLewis Technician Manager Chantal Faraudo provides a practical overview to using end-tidal CO2 monitoring in practice. She covers different types of equipment, what ETCO2 is telling us, how to troubleshoot problems with our patients, and why this is such an important monitoring tool.

courses.title: LOCAL ANESTHESIA TECHNIQUES FOR TECHS (637-41822)
courses.description: Pain management is an important facet of any treatment plan, especially surgical procedures. Kristin Spring, CVT, VTS (ECC, Anes.), CVPP, walks you through simple and inexpensive local anesthesia procedures you can start using tomorrow to benefit your patients. The lecture is 60 minutes and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on local anesthesia techniques. The speaker covers local blocks and basic pain management knowledge for technicians.

courses.title: ECG INTERPRETATION (637-37481)
courses.description: Megan Brashear, CVT, VTS(ECC), gives you the basic skills to begin interpreting dysrhythmias. Cardiac drug classes are discussed as well as when to give which drug for which dysrhythmia. Video from DoveLewis patients on ECG monitors illustrates common dysrhythmias and the audience is encouraged to participate to help decipher the ECG.

courses.title: Canine and Feline CPR for Veterinary Staff
courses.description: Megan Brashear, CVT, VTS(ECC), presents the DoveLewis yearly canine/feline CPR staff training, starting with updated information from the RECOVER initiative and then practicing CPR with various staff members. The most important aspect of any veterinary emergency is being prepared. This video is useful for all veterinary staff, as teamwork during CPR is vital.

courses.title: Livestock First Aid and Wellness Care
courses.description: This course provides an introductory overview of how to provide initial emergency first aid and perform triage on cattle, small ruminants, and swine until veterinary care can be ascertained. The curriculum also teaches how to maintain proper herd management utilized in both companion and food animal husbandry environments. Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) disaster plan curriculum for livestock will also be discussed.

courses.title: EMERGENCY MEDICINE IN GENERAL PRACTICE: THE TECHNICIANS ROLE (637-42395)
courses.description: The technician plays a crucial role in managing emergency cases in veterinary medicine. In this one hour lecture with DoveLewis Technician Training Specialist Jessica Waters-Miller, CVT, learn how to be the best advocate for your patients even if you're not at an emergency clinic.

courses.title: LOW STRESS HANDLING FOR YOUR PATIENTS AND YOU (637-42658)
courses.description: The lecture is 52 minutes long and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on low-stress handling of dogs and cats. In this lecture, Jenn Fiendish, CVT, VTS (Behavior), discusses low stress handling techniques and why they are important.

courses.title: PASS ON THE GAS (637-41972)
courses.description: Total intravenous anesthesia techniques and protocols when inhalant anesthesia may not the best option for patients with co-existing disease. This lecture presented by Morgan McCann, CVT, VTS (Anesthesia & Analgesia), will include patient assessment and selection, basic pharmacodynamics of isoflurane and sevoflurane, pharmacology of injectable anesthetic agents, and continuous rate infusion calculations.

courses.title: Practical Knowledge in Emergency and Critical Care for the Veterinary Technician
courses.description: In this short lectures series you will learn the process of the triage exam as outlined by the VetATLS, the properties of solutes in water and how that corresponds to fluid shifts in the body, the anatomy of the heart, blood flow through the heart and heart chambers and corresponding valves and also covers some of the most common arrythmias such as ventricular premature contractions (VPC), atrial fibrillation, AV block and ventricular fibrillation. You will also learn where and how to obtain an arterial blood gases and discuss indications and the process of placing IO catheters. At the end of this series you will have strong familiarity with these processes and their indications.

courses.title: ANXIOUS AND AFRAID: HELPING FRIGHTENED PATIENTS RELAX (637-42656)
courses.description: The lecture is 93 minutes long and consists of a speaker doing a formal presentation on treating fear and anxiety in cats and dogs. Jenn Fiendish, CVT, VTS (Behavior), discusses fear and anxiety in cats and dogs. Common presentations, management techniques, treatment strategies are covered.

courses.title: Going Viral: Canine Distemper
courses.description: Canine distemper virus is found around the world with domestic dogs serving as the reservoir species. Learn from Liz Hugston, RVT, CVT, VTS (SAIM, ECC) about the etiology, epidemiology, and pathology of this virus.

courses.title: Too Little Too Much Too Late: Starvation and Refeeding Considerations
courses.description: Refeeding syndrome is a rare, but severe complication that occurs after reintroducing food in patients experiencing states of malnutrition and starvation. In this lecture presented by Nursing Care and Quality Administrator Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS (ECC), we will discuss the physiologic consequences a patient experiences from starvation to refeeding syndrome. Additional discussion will be had regarding recognition and treatment, as well as appropriate approaches to refeeding.

courses.title: THE TROUBLE WITH TEETH (637-41569)
courses.description: The lecture is 53 minutes and consists of speaker Becky Smith, CVT, VTS (Clinical Practice Canine/Feline), doing a formal presentation on dental complications and challenges in the general practice. Reviews case summaries of patients with dental complications, learn the difference between normal and abnormal radiographs, dental charting, and periodontal disease.

courses.title: SHOCK TALK (637-41348)
courses.description: The lecture is 60 minutes and consists of a speaker Megan Brasher, CVT, VTS (ECC) doing a formal presentation on shock in the ER and ICU. This talk will help other technicians learn to recognize, treat and monitor shock from the technician and support staff perspective.

courses.title: 45th Annual Meeting of the Association of Zoo Veterinary Technicians (AZVT)
courses.description: The 2025 Annual Meeting of the Association of Zoo Veterinary Technicians (AZVT) offers a variety of educational workshops, presentations, and posters on topics that relate to general medical and non-medical topics in veterinary medicine as well as specific topics associated with wildlife, zoo, or aquarium animals and their medical care. This meeting offers continuing education for veterinary technicians working in a zoo, aquarium, or wildlife setting. There are five wet labs (two offered twice), one workshop, and 24 presentations covering a range of topics (see Agenda and Objectives below) for the 2025 conference.

courses.title: Inviting Everyone to the Party Recognizing the Systemic Consequences of Anaphylaxis
courses.description: Anaphylaxis can happen anywhere without warning. Multi-organ involvement is one of the key differences between anaphylaxis and an allergic reaction. In this lecture presented by Technician Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS(ECC), review how anaphylactic reactions are becoming more common in veterinary medicine, making it even more important for technicians to understand the process key for recognition and treatment.

courses.title: PAIN IS THE FIFTH VITAL SIGN (637-41652)
courses.description: DoveLewis surgery technician Kristin Spring, CVT, VTS presents a lecture on monitoring pain, and treating pain as the fifth vital sign. The lecture is 54 minutes including a formal presentation on pain management in dogs and cats, pain recognition, and identification, are discussed in detail.

courses.title: When the Bad Gets Worse: Oncologic Emergencies
courses.description: Cancer is a common and often fatal diagnosis in veterinary medicine. However, cancer isn't the death sentence it once was. More and more owners are seeking treatment for their pets because they not only tolerate cancer treatments, but they often are able to maintain a good quality of life. This means we are likely to see and treat animals when they experience the sequela of emergencies that can occur secondary to cancer. In this lecture, a variety of oncologic emergencies will be discussed including hematologic, cardiopulmonary and extravasation emergencies, tumor lysis syndrome, and more.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Concepts & Therapeutic Exercise for the Rehabilitation Team
courses.description: A foundational understanding of functional canine anatomy, therapeutic modalities, exercise, hydrotherapy, massage, and basic neurological rehabilitation. It emphasizes how exercise influences tissue physiology and trains students to evaluate, select, and progress exercises through various healing stages. Students will develop and practice detailed, case-specific rehabilitation programs for orthopedic, neurological, post-operative, geriatric, and canine athlete cases, with exercises tailored for both clinical and at-home settings. Students get hands-on experience with dogs on-site.

courses.title: Expanding knowledge base in emergency and critical care for Veterinary Technicians
courses.description: In this training you will learn the importance and significance of a complete physical exam, the steps necessary to gather and collate the information to assess the patient beginning from the first phone call. The basics of triage, physical exam, shock, system basics; cardiology, liver, renal and gastrointestinal systems will be covered, as well as fluid therapy and blood gas interpretation will be covered. At the conclusion of this course, you will have the skills and information to perform a thorough examination and triage evaluation.

courses.title: You're So Vein; You Probably Think This Talk is About You
courses.description: Venous access is a primary skill practiced by all technicians. One-size-fits-all approach does not account for patient variability, comfort, and longevity. In this lecture presented by Surgery Technician Joanie Abrams CVT, VTS (ECC), attendees can expect to learn about creative and adaptable approaches to obtaining vascular access. Key points will include individual patient considerations, tips and tricks, and an introduction to advanced techniques. Discussion will cover what proper and improper catheter placement looks like, and how to identify potential complications.

courses.title: Seizures in Veterinary Patients
courses.description: When working in emergency veterinary care, you encounter a diverse range of patients. Seizures are a common and challenging condition, prompting questions about terminology, manifestations, and treatment with anti-seizure medications. This article delves into the basics of seizures, their stages, various types, and offers insights into diagnostics, emergency management, and ongoing treatment strategies for veterinary professionals.

courses.title: The Far-Reaching Effects of Hypothermia
courses.description:
Hypothermia is a common finding in veterinary medicine, but often the negative impacts are greatly underestimated. In this lecture presented by Patient Care and Education Specialist Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS(ECC), we will discuss the potential causes of hypothermia, the systemic consequences, and safe prevention and correction options.
Attention will be given to at-risk patients including the critically ill, surgical, geriatric, neonatal, and exotic species. This lecture will provide learning opportunities for both beginning and advanced technicians wanting a review on the thermoregulatory system and how to better provide for our patients.

courses.provider: CANINE REHABILITATION INSTITUTE (AKA THE ANIMAL REHABILITATION INSTITUTE)
courses.title: Concepts for the Rehabilitation Team
courses.description: This course gives veterinary technicians and assistants a fundamental understanding of functional canine anatomy, therapeutic modalities, therapeutic exercise, and massage. It also introduces the basics of neurological rehabilitation. Participants get hands-on experience with dogs on-site. Outcome measurement, documentation, patient education, and legal and ethical issues related to canine rehabilitation are also covered.

courses.title: DONT DRINK THE WATER - LEPTOSPIROSIS IN DOGS (637-41651)
courses.description: The lecture is 57 minutes long and consists of a speaker Megan Brashear, CVT, VTS doing a formal presentation on Leptospirosis in dogs. The speaker will cover the concerns of zoonotic diseases, and how to care for these critical patients while in a veterinary clinic. Megan discusses at risk populations, the disease progression, and treatment. Heavy emphasis is placed on proper barrier nursing care and zoonosis.

courses.title: EMERGENCY TRIAGE (637-37595)
courses.description: Emergencies are stressful enough without having to wonder when to do what. In this hour Megan Brashear, CVT, VTS(ECC), will guide you through how to recognize and organize emergency cases, getting started with treatment and walks through some real emergency cases seen at DoveLewis. We'll review the important details to consider when receiving emergencies, performing triage, and treating emergencies.

courses.title: Veterinary CPR Training
courses.description: We'll bring the training to you with a one hour, virtual CPR presentation. All positions within a clinic are encouraged to attend this lecture to learn about their role in CPR. Technician Trainer Jessica Waters, CVT, walks viewers through the basics of CPR and covers instruction for team members working together, equipment needed, and roles. Learn how to set up your crash cart, practice closed-loop communication, and set your team up for CPR events, no matter how often they happen.

courses.title: Handling Avians
courses.description: This program will introduce you to the principles in safely handling avian patients, along with discussions on common diseases and conditions related to poor-husbandry.

courses.title: Lessons from Loss: A Reflection on the Cases That Change Us
courses.description: We all have those cases that stick with us long after our shifts end. Stress and trauma are inherent in the work we do, but we can begin to combat this by creating a nurturing environment to process both medically and emotionally challenging cases. Some of the hardest cases provide the most immense learning opportunities. Burnout, compassion fatigue, imposter syndrome and second-victim syndrome impact our ability to connect with and care for patients in a sustainable way. In this lecture, two cases will be studied taking into account both the medical review and the psychosocial well-being of the staff involved. Attendees will learn about morbidity and mortality case reviews, grand rounds, and debriefings and how they can help all veterinary professionals process loss. This lecture is geared towards veterinary technicians, but applications can benefit all team members.

courses.title: CANINE AND FELINE INFECTIOUS DISEASES IN THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST (637-40014)
courses.description: In this one hour lecture with Technician Becky Smith, CVT, VTS (CP), review some of the most common infectious diseases of dogs and cats in the northwest, as well as some that are new and on the rise.

courses.title: Just Take a Chill Pill: Pre-Admit Oral Sedation
courses.description: Reducing stress and anxiety in the veterinary setting for both canine and feline patients have become a hot topic in veterinary medicine. This lecture presented by Morgan McCann, CVT, VTS (anesthesia) we will discuss various oral sedation protocols that owners can administer at home prior to their arrival at the veterinary clinic for procedures or surgery. These protocols for the anxious, nervous or fractious patients can ultimately reduce MAC and improve healing and recovery from general anesthesia.

courses.title: Blocked: Urethral Obstructions in the Male Cat
courses.description: What steps does the ER Tech need to take in a urethral obstruction emergency? This lecture presented by DoveLewis Technician Training Specialist Jessica Waters-Miller, CVT, will discuss a general overview of recognition and treatment as well as tips and tricks from the ER technician's role.

courses.title: Confident Communication with Clients: Engaging Owners in Patient Care
courses.description: Caring for patients is truly a collaborative effort with clients. As technicians, our role is critical to ensuring that patients receive the best care not only while they are in the hospital, but especially once they leave. In this lecture presented by DoveLewis Blood Bank Coordinator Kelsey Reinauer, CVT, and Training Specialist Jessica Waters-Miller, CVT, we will discuss strategies and tips for improving your client communication in the exam room. We will review the importance of building relationships with clients so that everyone, from the hospital to the home, feel included and supported in patient care.

courses.title: BRACYCEPHALIC PATIENTS IN CLINICAL PRACTICE (637-38746)
courses.description: Brachycephalic patients are some of the most popular breeds in the U.S. so it's important to recognize the risks that they face in a veterinary hospital. Explore the special needs of the brachycephalic patients. Learn to prevent distress in a clinic environment, and discover the important role support staff play in patient comfort. Becky Smith, CVT reviews common concerns, handling tips, and anesthesia considerations for taking the best care of brachycephalics in your clinic.

courses.title: The PU/PD Workup- a rational approach to frustrating cases!
courses.description: Polyuria and polydipsia are common client complaints. There are many underlying causes that can result in pu/pd, which can lead to a lengthy list of differentials. Choosing the appropriate tests can help eliminate client costs and lead to the underlying diagnosis faster.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Mosquitoes - It's Not Just About Heartworms Anymore
courses.description: This course examines the broader impact of mosquito-borne diseases beyond just heartworm, including their effects on a wide range of animals such as horses, livestock, and poultry. It emphasizes the economic implications for production animals and highlights the importance of discussing mosquito control during veterinary farm visits. It also explains the role of different mosquito species in transmitting diseases and the significance of understanding their life cycle to aid in prevention.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Recognition and Assessment of Pain in Dogs, Cats and Exotic Pets
courses.description: This course provides coverage of pain physiology, recognition, and management in animal patients. It differentiates between types of pain, including acute, chronic, maladaptive, and neuropathic, as well as exploring their physiological and behavioral manifestations across species. The course will help technicians hone the skills necessary to identify signs of pain and distress and apply effective treatment strategies in clinical practice.

courses.title: Veterinary Nursing: The Language of Veterinary Medicine
courses.description: This course will help the participant develop the skills to understand and interpret veterinary terminology used daily at their practice. The course material begins with the dissection of medical terms continuing on to anatomical positioning, medical abbreviations, and will then take the student through the vocabulary of the various body systems. Wordlists, images, and an audio glossary aid the student in absorbing their newly acquired knowledge.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Those Eyes Look Sweeter Than Candy: Development and Management of Diabetic Cataracts in the Canine Patient
courses.description: This article is designed to help the reader understand why diabetic patients get cataracts, how they can be managed, and what cataract surgery entails. It also addresses complications seen with medical management or surgical intervention, along with an appreciation of some of the increased risks associated specifically with the diabetic patient.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Utilizing Continuous Glucose Monitors in the Diabetic Patient
courses.description: Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs) are transforming the management of diabetic pets. This course discusses how CGMs compare to traditional blood glucose testing, how these devices work, and how their data can guide treatment plans. It also explains how veterinary staff can assist pet owners in obtaining, placing, and using CGMs effectively. Overall, the course highlights how CGMs improve monitoring accuracy, convenience, and comfort for both pets and their owners.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Reproductive Emergencies in the Dog and Cat
courses.description: Life threatening disorders of the reproductive system can occur in both male and female dogs and cats. Veterinary professionals must recognize these emergencies quickly because delays in treatment may threaten the life of the animal or the survival of the offspring. Veterinary professionals must also be familiar with medical and surgical interventions used to treat these conditions. This course seeks to educate professionals on prompt stabilization, early recognition, and appropriate options to significantly improve outcomes for both the patient and the offspring.

courses.title: Advance15 - Physiotherapy for Nurses
courses.description: Advance15 - Physiotherapy for Nurses is listed in CE Broker's official AAVSB RACE-approved catalog.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Wolbachia - The Silent Partner in Heartworm Infection
courses.description: Clients often present with canine family members that are suffering from heartworm. While this is a somewhat common parasite to treat, another silent organism is lurking within the diagnosis. Wolbachia must be addressed with clients and throughout the heartworm treatment protocol as well. Understanding the symbiotic relationship that exists between heartworm and Wolbachia is important for technicians who may be faced with clients seeking answers. It is essential to treat animals for Wolbachia prior to beginning the heartworm protocol-driven treatment in order to recognize a positive outcome for pets.

courses.title: Clinical Techniques II
courses.description: This secondary level of the clinical techniques course is designed to equip veterinary technicians and assistants with the knowledge and skills necessary to perform laboratory procedures. Learners will develop an understanding of blood smear preparation and analysis, including red blood cell morphology, white blood cell differential counts, and platelet estimation. Additionally, the course will cover hematology, focusing on complete blood counts and their clinical significance. Techniques for determining total solids, including packed cell volume and total protein, will be explored. The importance of ear cytology in diagnosing ear infections will be emphasized, along with microscopic examination. Learners will also gain an understanding of how to perform urinalysis, including physical, chemical, and microscopic examination of urine samples. Blood chemistry analysis, covering a range of biochemical tests, will be discussed, and the interpretation of results will be highlighted. Finally, the course will delve into fecal analysis, including parasite identification and fecal flotation techniques.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Exploring the Ins and Outs of Zoonoses in Reptiles and Amphibian Pets
courses.description: Reptiles and amphibians continue to trend as popular pets and have found a niche with those who may not have the space or time to dedicate to a dog or cat. It is important that medical personnel as well as owners are aware of the potential health hazards and risks that are associated with these species in order to have a positive experience.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Getting Cats to Eat: Its More Than Pouring Food in a Bowl
courses.description: Proper nutritional management is one of the most important factors in maximizing health, performance, and longevity in cats, in addition to managing disease conditions. Proper nutrition and care throughout a cat's life maximizes health, longevity, and quality of life. Domestic cats and other members of the superfamily Feloidea are strict or obligate carnivores. This difference from dogs is supported by specific behavioral, anatomic, physiologic, and metabolic adaptations of cats to a strictly carnivorous diet. This course investigates the unique nutritional needs of cats. The veterinary healthcare team should be the preferred expert source of the best nutritional information for pets. This course reviews the physiology and behavior of feeding cats, along with tips to ensure cats are getting the nutrients they need.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: Pet Obesity: Tackling a Growing Crisis with Realistic Expectations
courses.description: This course addresses the growing concern of pet obesity, emphasizing the need for veterinary professionals to recognize, assess, and openly discuss weight-related health issues with pet owners. It outlines key tools such as Body Condition Score (BCS), Muscle Condition Score (MCS), and nutritional assessments to guide diagnosis and treatment. It also explores the serious health risks of obesity in pets and advocates for a collaborative, informed approach to tackling pet obesity through education, compassion, and proactive care.

courses.title: Advance15: Anaesthesia
courses.description: This online course is specifically designed for vet nurses/technicians who want to advance their knowledge and understanding of anaesthesia and analgesia. Through recorded sessions, extensive notes and MCQs, you will learn from a highly regarded veterinary anaesthesia specialist about new developments in the field, and how this relates to your own cases. You'll be able to utilise your new knowledge from day one of the course. You will also be able to enjoy unlimited access to your course materials for a full 12 months after the course has finished.

courses.provider: NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF VETERINARY TECHNICIANS IN AMERICA (NAVTA)
courses.title: A Crashing Course Through Antiarrhythmics
courses.description: Antiarrhythmic drugs are powerful tools that veterinary technicians are often charged with administering. Gaining intelligence in how these medications affect various conditions broadens the technician's understanding of not only the pharmacology, but also the pathophysiology of the diseases that are being treated.

courses.title: Pyometra: The Unwanted Guest in the Womb
courses.description: Canine pyometra is a life-threatening reproductive emergency frequently encountered in general practice and emergency medicine. This lecture provides veterinary technicians an in-depth understanding of the pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and treatment options for pyometra with an emphasis on nursing responsibilities and patient care and monitoring. Participants will learn to identify key diagnostic patterns, understand stabilization goals, decipher between medical management and surgical intervention for optimizing patient outcomes and how to educate clients on preventative and postoperative care.

courses.title: Sweet Dreams Are Made of This: Hypoglycemia in Small Animals
courses.description: Hypoglycemia is a common emergency seen in veterinary hospitals and can be life-threatening. It is essential that veterinary support staff are able to quickly identify clinical signs of hypoglycemia, identify laboratory tests to give further information, and understand treatment options to provide in a timely manner. This 1 hour course will cover basic pathophysiology of glucose absorption, mechanisms of glucose homeostasis, how to define neuroglycopenia, and clinical signs and consequences of hypoglycemia. Additionally, we will also discuss diagnostics, different disease processes that can cause hypoglycemia, and treatment options for most disease processes.

courses.title: Whelping...or Yelping? When Things Go Wrong at the End of Gestion
courses.description: This course covers reproductive management of the female small animal. This course also covers the stages of estrous and what can go wrong at the end of gestion.

courses.title: From Hunger Games to Healthy Gains: Feeding Tubes 101
courses.description: This course covers a basic review of various feeding tubes, including indications/contraindications, management, potential complications, troubleshooting techniques, and client education.

courses.title: Dental Charting: How to Perform a Complete and Thorough Orofacial Exam
courses.description: This program will cover what it means to perform a complete and thorough orofacial exam, and that it does not just start and stop with the dentition. Attendees will learn what is included in the extra and intra oral exam along with how to document those findings using AVDC terminology and abbreviations on the dental chart. An overview of some of the most common dental abnormalities along with how to identify and chart them will be covered.

courses.title: Deep Breaths: Anesthesia Wins, Woes, and What We Did Next
courses.description: This course covers the good, the bad and everything in between for our small animal patients in all phases of anesthesia. We will discuss what went right initially, anesthetic choices, the unexpected events, interventions and patient outcomes.

courses.title: What's the Plan? Anesthesia Protocols That Don't Stink
courses.description: This course reviews the 2025 JAVMA and ACVAA anesthesia guidelines to help veterinary technicians lead in protocol creation. We will discuss the 10-step design process, multimodal analgesia, and locoregional techniques. Participants will learn to use cognitive aids and advanced monitoring trends to enhance patient safety and collaborative communication with the attending veterinarian.

courses.title: Addisonian Crisis
courses.description: This course covers the basics of hypoadrenocorticism, also known as Addison's disease. We will discuss how to recognize a crisis situation and what to do to stabilize a patient in that situation. This lecture will also go over some basic anatomy to better understand this endocrine disease.

courses.title: (OnDemand)(French): REDUIRE NOTRE EMPREINTE ECOLOGIQUE UNE ASSIETTE A LA FOIS; INTRODUCTION A L'ALIMENTATION DURABLE
courses.description:
Our eating habits can shape a greener future for our planet, protecting the environment, marine life, and biodiversity. In this conference, we'll explore:
- The urgent need to talk about sustainable food choices
- Navigating the landscape of sustainable agriculture
- Debunking the myth: is organic always the healthiest option?
- Practical tips and tricks to reduce the ecological footprint of meals
- Looking to the future: insect farming to meet growing food demand
- Pet food as a solution to food waste

courses.title: Dental x-ray positioning made simple in the dog and cat.
courses.description: Attendee will learn how to keep it simple in taking dental x-rays in the dog and cat. I will also be reviewing basic dental scaling and polishing, tools used in dentistry and dental charting.

courses.title: The Heart of Anesthesia: ECG and arrhythmias
courses.description: i. An interactive course designed to teach the parts of the ECG waveform and how they relate to the heart's function, as well as learn to identify common arrhythmias such as VPCs, AV block, AV dissociation, and escape beats. It begins with the normal waveform and identifies the parts of the waveform as they relate to the heart. Then we look at how this waveform can vary and what various arrhythmias mean for heart function. This course also discusses the best way to treat these various arrhythmias. The last 15-20 minutes consists of a variety of real-world ECGs that attendees can practice identifying and treating.

courses.title: Nurse Programme 2025
courses.description: The 2025 Veterinary Nurses Programme offers expert-led webinars designed to empower veterinary nurses, equipping them with practical skills and knowledge across diverse topics. From nurse consultations to anaesthesia, cardiology, and feline care, this comprehensive programme supports career growth and enhances patient outcomes.

courses.title: A Breath of Fresh Air: Getting the Most out of Your Capnography
courses.description: Capnography is becoming more and more prevalent in veterinary hospitals and is a monitoring tool that aids in the assessment of patient ventilation under anesthesia and during CPA. This course will define capnometry and capnography followed by a series of abnormal capnographs commonly seen in practice and concluding with utilization of capnometry and capnography during CPR including the most recent updates from RECOVER.

courses.title: Hot Topics for Avian Veterinary Technicians
courses.description:
This on demand course features a selection of recorded sessions previously presented at the 45th Annual AAV Conference & Expo specifically geared toward technicians. Sessions will cover avian veterinary techniques and avian medicine. This conference was hosted by the Association of Avian Veterinarians (AAV). The program will focus on advancing avian health, welfare, and conservation through education, advocacy, and science.
- Learn how to assist owners of poultry in providing appropriate housing, biosecurity, understanding pharmaceutical use, and how to advise clients about husbandry, nutrition, behavior, and vaccinations.
- How to safely and effectively administer avian intravenous and intraosseous catheter placement. Learn anatomy, placement sites and techniques, maintenance, troubleshooting, and tips.
- Client education and teaching avian husbandry are vital roles of veterinary technicians. Gain an understanding of avian nutrition, techniques for psittacine dietary conversion, and contraindications for dietary conversion.
- Learn about the origin of the current high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) outbreak and its significance to wildlife, poultry, and humans. Clinical signs of disease and testing are reviewed. Learn about in-hospital precautions to take when treating poultry during an HPAI outbreak.
- Learn why ultraviolet light is recommended for pet birds, what safety issues may arise, and how to encourage and support clients who want to include it in their bird-care routine.
- Learn training methods you can implement to ensure your team is well-prepared to care for new patients and how to teach skills to new technicians without increasing risk to a sick bird.

courses.title: Canine and Feline CPR and Advanced Life Support for Veterinary Professionals
courses.description: This course provides an overview of how to manage a life-threatening emergency when it arrives at a veterinary hospital. The skills and topics covered in this class include how to communicate effectively during an emergency situation both with clients and other staff members, how to triage a patient and determine medical need, develop an emergency plan for your hospital, how to function as an ICU team during an emergency, how to recognize and manage cardiac arrest, how to properly use monitoring equipment in the ICU, utilize fluid therapy, how to perform manual and ventilated CPR.

courses.title: Veterinary Nursing Playbook: Comprehensive Care for Every Patient part 3, Level III Patients
courses.description: This is part 3 of a four-part course designed to help educate veterinary assistants and technicians in providing optimal patient care to patients with increasingly complicated needs. In this third lecture, we will focus on the care of patients in respiratory distress including different methods to provide oxygen and how to monitor these patients for signs of decline as well as improvement. We will also be discussing high needs patients with infectious or contagious diseases that require hospitalization. And finally, when and how to transfer patients from the general practice setting to a 24/7 facility.

courses.title: Is My Patient Painful? Moving From A Subjective To Objective Assessment
courses.description: Assessing pain objectively in our veterinary patients can be challenging. This course will introduce the Glascow Composite Measure Pain Scale and through the use of images and videos guide veterinary technicians in the use of the scale to measure pain in our canine and feline patients. We will introduce the SF - GCMPS as a validated tool for measuring pain in canine and feline patients. We will show a short video of a pain assessment of a canine followed by a breakdown of each section of the SF-GCMPS with signs of pain in picture/video form. We will show a short video of a pain assessment of a feline followed by a breakdown of each section of the SF-GCMPS with signs of pain in picture/video form. This will allow technicians to practice using the form.

courses.title: Certificate of Veterinary Site Staffing Proficiency (CVSSP)
courses.description: Effective staff management is not merely an administrative task; it is a cornerstone of success for any veterinary practice. A well-managed team directly impacts patient care quality, client satisfaction, operational efficiency, and ultimately, the financial health of the clinic. When staff members are engaged, supported, and appropriately utilized, the entire practice thrives, creating a positive ripple effect throughout the community it serves. Understanding the intricate dynamics of human resources within a veterinary setting is the first step towards building a resilient and high-performing team. This course will illuminate the pathways to achieving such an environment, ensuring your practice stands out for its excellence. By focusing on strategic staffing, you can transform potential challenges into opportunities for growth and innovation. Embracing these principles allows for a more harmonious and productive workplace. Ultimately, investing in your staff's well-being and professional growth is an investment in your practice's future. The Certificate of Veterinary Site Staffing Proficiency (CVSSP) course provides the learner with a clear understanding of best practices and models for effective staffing in professional veterinary environments.

courses.title: Serving Up a Food Trial: A Recipe for Improved Outcomes
courses.description: Allergic food responses can stir up trouble for pets, owners, and veterinary clinics alike. It's time to whip up the perfect blend of resources to alleviate discomfort and dispel confusion. Prepare to 'Serve Up' an effective food trial with a focus on educating pet owners. From shedding light on their pet's internal workings to guiding them through each step of the trial, emphasizing the benefits of therapeutic diets. Through clear and empathetic communication, empower yourself to have meaningful discussions with pet owners. Finally, cement your role as a crucial partner in their pet's health journey, providing invaluable guidance and practical tips for successful trial execution.

courses.title: Certified Canine Rehabilitation Veterinary Technician Online
courses.description: Certified Canine Rehabilitation Veterinary Technician (CCRVT) is a hybrid course with 3 online and 2 onsite sessions. CCRVT includes hands-on labs in canine anatomy, objective assessments, manual therapies, and rehabilitation modalities. It is necessary to finish the internship with a small animal rehabilitation therapist after completion of sessions 1-4 and within 6 months of completion of the course are necessary to receive certification.

courses.title: From Estimates to Empathy: The Technician's Role in the Spectrum of Care
courses.description:
Have you heard about the spectrum of care? This style of medicine is not new, though the term has gained wider recognition in recent years. Providing a spectrum of care allows veterinarians to present a range of treatment options to their clients that vary in cost, invasiveness, and intensity. When done well, spectrum of care medicine maximizes patient quality of life within the individual goals and limitations of the pet family while meeting the moral, ethical, and legal obligations of our profession.
Have you ever wondered what your doctor was thinking when they created a certain treatment plan? That's okay! Often, our technicians are not present for the whole conversation and may not hear how client and veterinarian arrive at a decision. Veterinarians who practice spectrum of care think carefully about the best way to meet the needs of each individual pet family and patient. Just because a treatment plan isn't what you are used to seeing for a given condition doesn't make it poor medicine.
Have you wanted to get more involved In practicing spectrum of care? Veterinary technicians are an essential part of client communication and should be included in these care conversations. And that doesn't mean just reviewing the financial estimate. You should have a role in identifying Barriers to Care and client goals of care.
Join a practicing veterinarian to explore the spectrum of care using a case-based approach. We will discuss what spectrum of care looks like in practice and unpack the thought process doctors have when deciding which options are appropriate. Then we will explore the essential role technicians play in client communication when practicing a spectrum of care, including key tools and phrases you can take back to your practice and implement right away.

courses.title: Certified Food Therapy for Veterinary Technicians Online
courses.description: This course is intended for veterinary technicians or assistants to create diets under the supervision of a licensed veterinarian. Tailored for veterinary technicians working in clinics and hospitals where TCVM is practiced. This course is intended for veterinary technicians or assistants to create diets under the supervision of a licensed veterinarian.

courses.title: Certified Canine Tui-na Technicians Online
courses.description: Certified Canine Tui-na Technicians (CCTT) is a hybrid course with 1 online and 1 onsite sessions. CCTT includes hands-on labs in Canine and Tui Na (Chinese Medical Massage and Manipulation) techniques, Contraindications for manual therapy, Soft tissue assessment, how to teach Tui-Na to clients, TCVM diagnoses.

courses.title: Certified Companion Animal Palliative and End-of -Life Care for Veterinary Technicians
courses.description: The Certified Companion Animal Palliative and End-of-Life Care for Veterinary Technicians course prepares veterinary technicians to effectively support veterinarians providing compassionate hospice care. The lectures highlight the technicians crucial role, emphasizing integrative care, quality-of-life assessments, comfort care techniques, and emotional support for caregivers and their pets during end-of-life.

courses.title: Administering & Dispensing Medications
courses.description: This course, specifically designed for veterinary technicians and assistants, focuses on medication administration techniques, as well as how to properly dispense medications. Learners will develop a detailed understanding of various routes of administration including oral, topical, subcutaneous (SQ), intramuscular (IM), and intravenous (IV). Patient well-being, effective client communication, needle selection for injections, proper animal restraint for medication administration, and aseptic techniques to prevent infection during injections will also be reviewed.

courses.title: Critical Care Management of the Exotic Patient (Part One): Avian and Reptiles
courses.description: Companion animals come in all shapes and sizes; feathers, scales and fur. Part one of this two part series will focus on the critical avian and reptile patient. Presented by Patient Care and Educational Specialist Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS(ECC), you will learn basic assessment, stabilization, nursing requirements and common presenting illnesses.

courses.title: Critical Care Management of the Exotic Patient (Part Two): Rabbits, Ferrets and Other Small Mammals
courses.description: Small mammals seeking veterinary care are not limited to cats and dogs. The final part of this series will focus on the exotic small mammal patient. Presented by Patient Care and Educational Specialist Sarah Harris, CVT, VTS (ECC) you'll learn basic assessment, stabilization, nursing requirements and common presenting illnesses.

courses.title: Take a Bite Out of Periodontal Disease: Nutritional Considerations For Dental Heath
courses.description: Benjamin Franklin once said, An ounce of prevention is worth a pound cure. When it comes dental health, veterinary technicians educating our pet owners on how to be proactive can make a mouth of difference. This webinar will highlight nutritional factors that may help benefit a pets dental health and will discuss the Veterinary Oral Health Council (VOHC) two seals of acceptance.

courses.title: Wounds, Wounds, Wounds
courses.description: This engaging webinar explores the fundamentals of veterinary wound management, from initial assessment through healing. Participants will learn how to evaluate different wound types, recognize factors that impact healing, select appropriate wound care strategies, and apply practical techniques to support optimal patient outcomes. Through real-world case examples, Brian shares evidence-based approaches to wound treatment, bandaging considerations, complication prevention, and client communication tips. Attendees will leave with increased confidence in managing challenging wounds and promoting successful healing in veterinary patients.

courses.title: That was Awkward: Tips to Improve Client Communication
courses.description: Communication is a two-way process that awkwardly at times can feel like a dead-end road. This webinar will explore communication styles and how we can adapt our own style to improve our client interactions leading to better patient care and hopefully fewer awkward moments.

courses.title: Managing and Monitoring Diabetes Mellitus- Empowering technicians
courses.description: Diabetes management and monitoring can be a complex and daunting subject. Throughout this module we will focus on different management and monitoring techniques for diabetes mellitus. Highlighting key areas of communication to focus on.

courses.title: Your Pet Got Into What?? Asking the Right Questions when Assessing an Animal Poisoning
courses.description: Wow, animals get into some crazy things! Did you know that not every animal should be treated simply based on the toxin? This lecture will discuss the basics of properly assessing a poisoned patient in order to understand both the risks presented by the toxin and the risks associated with specific species, breeds, and pre-existing conditions.

courses.title: Onsite Dental & Anesthesia Workshop for the Veterinary Technician
courses.description: Hands-on, limited-number attendees (16) offering the essentials of indispensable tricks to dental prophylactic care and dental radiographic skill sets. Anesthetic insights for drugs, physiologic responses and other factors affecting the patient safety. Overall approaches to taking away the fear and making dental procedures faster and easier.

courses.title: My Pet has Diabetes
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will review the clinical signs leading to the diagnosis and management of diabetes mellitus in dogs and cats. This course will review the underlying etiologies, appropriate glucose monitoring techniques, and evidence-based treatment options.

courses.title: Stall to Table, When its time to cut
courses.description: This program will discuss 5 core areas of the surgical colic. These areas are most common types of surgical colics, why surgery is an option, indicators that warrant surgery while touching on Anesthesia and discussing the prognosis whether good or bad.

courses.title: Fall VTNE Preparation Class (TECH120)
courses.description: This course is designed to provide a review of the veterinary technicians essential skills tasks and knowledge base as provided by the guidelines set forth by the AVMA CVTEA for approved veterinary technology programs. Active engagement in the entire course should help organize study time and allow for better competency and test-taking skills. The course library will contain a variety of handouts, study guides, charts, interactives, slide shows, and flashcards. Note: This class does not guarantee passage of the exam; we will approach as many topics as possible in an effort to help the student identify levels of competency as an aid to focus study efforts. In-depth and advanced topics will NOT be covered.

courses.title: Your Pet Got Into What?? Asking the Right Questions when Assessing an Animal Poisoning
courses.description: Wow, animals get into some crazy things! Did you know that not every animal should be treated simply based on the toxin? This lecture will discuss the basics of properly assessing a poisoned patient in order to understand both the risks presented by the toxin and the risks associated with specific species, breeds, and pre-existing conditions.

courses.provider: AMERICAN ASSOCIATION OF EQUINE VETERINARY TECHNICIANS AND ASSISTANTS
courses.title: AAEVT Fall Anesthesia Society Event 2026
courses.description:
This equine anesthesia program is designed to expand the knowledge and practical skills of veterinary technicians at varying levels of experience who are involved in, or interested in, the anesthesia and perioperative care of equine patients. Through a combination of lectures and hands-on wet labs, participants will explore advanced concepts in cardiovascular and respiratory monitoring, arterial blood gas analysis, mechanical ventilation, pain physiology and multimodal analgesia, anesthetic emergency management, airway management, and vascular access.
Hosted at Rood & Riddle Equine Hospital in Lexington, Kentucky, the program provides participants the opportunity to learn and practice advanced anesthesia techniques within a leading equine referral hospital and clinical setting.
Lecture sessions will emphasize interpretation and clinical application of physiologic and monitoring data, recognition and management of anesthetic complications, and development of appropriate interventions to support patient safety throughout anesthesia and recovery. Hands-on wet labs will reinforce these concepts through practical experience with arterial catheterization, invasive blood pressure monitoring, arterial blood gas sampling, mechanical ventilation equipment and troubleshooting, advanced airway techniques, and alternative vascular access methods.
The combination of advanced didactic instruction and practical application will provide participants with knowledge and skills that can be incorporated into equine anesthesia protocols and patient management within their clinical practice.

courses.title: Exam Room Basics
courses.description: Becoming a patient advocate and a veterinary asset for pets and their pet parents.

courses.title: Build It or Buy It? The Realities of Veterinary Practice Ownership
courses.description:
For veterinarians dreaming of practice ownership, there are two primary paths: build a clinic from the ground up or purchase an existing practice. But which option is the better fit for your goals, finances, timeline, and vision for the future?
In this panel-style webinar, experienced veterinary industry professionals will explore the realities of both approaches--from start-up costs, financing, and time to profitability to existing goodwill, established client bases, operational risks, and long-term value. Attendees will gain practical insight to help determine which path makes the most sense for their own ownership journey.

courses.title: Paws & Unwind Wellness Retreats
courses.description: In this conference we aim to provide an opportunity for wellness and rejuvenation as well as continuing education for veterinary technicians. We will feature a variety of CE sessions focused on internal medicine, grief, burn out, compassion fatigue, and overall wellness.

courses.title: Beyond the Bleed: Understanding Small Animal Blood Products
courses.description: The participant can expect to learn common blood types of dogs/cats, common blood products used in veterinary medicine, the importance of crossmatching, how to correctly monitor patients for transfusion reactions, and the breakdown of each blood product any why they are used.
courses.location: Bay State Veterinary Emergency and Specialty Services

courses.title: Stall to Table, When It's Time to Cut
courses.description: This program will discuss 5 core areas of the surgical colic. These areas are most common types of surgical colics, why surgery is an option, indicators that warrant surgery while touching on Anesthesia and discussing the prognosis whether good or bad.

courses.title: Bite-Sized Wisdom: Dentistry for Veterinary Technicians
courses.description: This workshop is for technicians and assistants only and will empower them by increasing their knowledge in many aspects of veterinary dentistry and implement a higher level of dental care in a general practice setting. Covered topics will include a compete professional dental cleaning using ultrasonic scalers and hand instruments, performing and correcting diagnostic radiographs, instrument care and sharpening, regional anesthesia, ergonomic in veterinary medicine, treatment plans and home care tips. All the discussed items will be implemented during the hands-on wet lab portion. This course is limited to 10 technicians or assistants with one instructor and one assistant.

courses.title: From Assessment to Action: Improving Pain Management in Veterinary Patients.
courses.description: Effective pain management is a critical component of high-quality veterinary patient care, and veterinary technicians play an essential role in recognizing, assessing, and advocating for appropriate analgesia. This lecture is designed to enhance technicians' understanding of pain physiology, improve confidence in pain assessment, and provide practical tools for supporting multimodal pain management in clinical practice.

courses.provider: CVETS - COLUMBIA VETERINARY EMERGENCY TRAUMA AND SPECIALTY
courses.title: Turning on the Lytes: Electrolyte Basics for Nurses
courses.description: This course will cover the basics of electrolytes, their normal values, and nursing considerations for patients with electrolyte derangements. The focus will be on the common electrolytes tested using point-of-care blood gas machines (EPOC, GEM 5000, Nova etc.) that nurses will often times be reviewing before the attending doctor. The goal is to help nurses be more confident interpreting basic electrolyte values to improve patient advocacy, as well as being able to anticipate potential treatment changes.

courses.title: Dental Radiograph Positioning Training
courses.description: Learn how to take efficient full mouth diagnostic dental radiographs with positioning techniques. Participants will get hands-on practice with feline/canine skulls or cadaver heads. There will be three workstations set up with Midmark x-ray generators and both Progeny and ScanX films available. A Zoom video lecture will be sent prior to the hands on training.

courses.title: Basic Anesthesia for Veterinary Technicians
courses.description: This lecture with Outreach Coordinator Jessica Waters, CVT, provides veterinary technicians with a review of anesthesia and monitoring in general practice settings. The focus is on patient preparation, equipment setup, monitoring interpretation, and early recognition of anesthetic concerns. Emphasis is placed on understanding normal versus concerning trends, effective communication with the veterinary team, and technician advocacy to support anesthetic safety.

courses.title: BRisky Business: Brachycephalic Anesthesia
courses.description: This live interactive medical program for veterinary technicians will review congenital issues common to brachycephalic breeds and focus on utilizing brachycephalic risk (BRisk) scoring to assess anesthetic dangers. In addition, this course will include methods to improve safety under anesthesia by implementing brachycephalic protocols plus review best practices to manage brachycephalic patients to optimize peri-operative safety.
